Authors: Liu S.; Wu P.; Zeng S.; Zhu H.; Bao X.; Duan S.; Wang N.; Chen X.D.
Title: Combined effects of Ca2+ crosslinking and microsphere size on network disintegration and digestion of DHA-loaded calcium alginate-whey protein gel microspheres
Abstract: Docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) delivery by alginate-based gel carriers is strongly influenced by gel network architecture, yet the combined effects of network crosslinking and particle size on digestion behavior remain poorly understood. In this study, DHA-loaded calcium alginate-whey protein isolate composite gel microspheres (DHA-CA-WPI) were prepared by extruding a DHA-loaded sodium alginate-whey protein isolate (SA-WPI) emulsion through syringe needles of different gauges into CaCl2 solutions via external ionic gelation. Ca2+ concentration (0.05, 0.10, and 0.30 M) and microsphere size (2.61-4.28 mm) were varied systematically to examine their combined effects on gel structure and in vitro digestion. Needles of 10, 12, 16, and 20 G yielded mean microsphere diameters of 4.28, 3.75, 3.30, and 2.61 mm, respectively. Increasing Ca2+ concentration produced denser gel networks with reduced pore size, whereas decreasing microsphere size promoted more uniform crosslinking and shortened diffusion pathways. During gastric digestion, all formulations remained structurally stable, with protein hydrolysis below 10%, suggesting limited proteolytic degradation of the embedded protein network. Following transfer to intestinal conditions, microsphere size and Ca2+ concentration affected hydration, enzyme accessibility, matrix degradation, and FFA release. Small microspheres (20 G, 2.61 mm) prepared with 0.05 M Ca2+ underwent rapid structural breakdown and exhibited the highest FFA release (63.92 ± 0.96%), whereas large microspheres (10 G, 4.28 mm) crosslinked with 0.30 M Ca2+ showed slower degradation and the lowest FFA release (32.87 ± 2.06%). These findings suggest that microsphere size and Ca2+-dependent network structure can influence digestion kinetics through their effects on digestive transport and matrix resistance, providing a basis for designing alginate-protein gel carriers with tunable gastrointestinal behavior for oxidation-sensitive lipophilic nutrients. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Miao W.; Shang T.; Wen Y.; Ye C.; Zhang C.; Qiu C.; Jin Z.; Quek S.Y.
Title: Engineering dual-network oleogels based on OSA starch/chitosan complexes for enhanced astaxanthin stability: Effects of beeswax and β-sitosterol crystal networks
Abstract: To improve the stability of emulsion-templated oleogels and enhance astaxanthin protection, dual-network oleogels based on OSA starch/chitosan complexes (OS/CS) were fabricated by incorporating crystalline networks formed by beeswax or β-sitosterol. The effects of different crystalline networks on the microstructure, stability, and astaxanthin retention of OS/CS oleogels were systematically investigated. The incorporation of both crystalline networks significantly (p < 0.05) enhanced the oil-binding capacity of OS/CS oleogels under various processing and storage conditions, with beeswax exhibiting the most pronounced improvement. After storage at 25 °C for 56 days, astaxanthin degradation was observed in all oleogel samples; however, the OS/CS oleogels containing 6% beeswax or β-sitosterol showed relatively lower astaxanthin degradation of 19.32% and 21.05%, respectively. In vitro digestion revealed that astaxanthin bioaccessibility in the dual-network oleogels (23.92-43.04%) was higher than that of bulk oil (20.97%). Overall, beeswax exhibited superior synergistic effects in promoting the formation of a dense dual-network structure and enhancing the oil-binding capacity of OS/CS oleogels, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving oleogel stability and astaxanthin retention. Authors: Cui J.; Li S.; Cui F.; Zhang A.; Wang H.; Wan Z.; Meng J.; Zhang M.
Title: Unraveling silkworm pupa polysaccharide structure and its impact on the glass transition and processing characteristics of dough
Abstract: Animal polysaccharides have high biological activity and are easily absorbed and utilized. This study investigated the structural characteristics of silkworm pupa polysaccharide (SWP) and its dose-dependent impact on the glass transition behavior of dough. The molecular weight of SWP was 4.84 × 105 Da, with its main chain likely comprising →3)-α-D-Glcp-(1→ and side branches possibly composed of →6)-α-D-Galp-(1→, →4)-α-D-Glcp-(1→, and α-L-Fucp-(1 → . Upon SWP incorporation into dough, the glass transition temperature (Tg’) of dough increased by up to 49.36%. Results indicated the glass state of the dough is easier to achieve by changing water distribution and forming a continuous and uniform gluten network. The finding was attributed to the increased proportion tightly bound water (TBW), β-sheet, hydrogen bond and covalent bond content via forming hydrogen-bond network in SWP's hydrophilic groups. Rheological and texture analyses further suggested that SWP fortifies dough elasticity and hardness. Therefore, SWP emerges as a promising animal-derived polysaccharide for elevating the storage stability of frozen dough. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Yan R.; Zhu X.; Dong Q.; Zhang M.; Yin Z.; Zhao Z.; Chen X.
Title: Industrial robot fault detection and diagnosis for intelligent maintenance: A review of data, methods, and emerging trends
Abstract: Industrial robots are widely used in intelligent manufacturing due to their high efficiency, flexibility, and repeatability. However, long-term operation under complex working conditions inevitably leads to performance degradation and various faults across mechanical, transmission, and electrical subsystems. Owing to the structural complexity of industrial robots, strong coupling among subsystems, and heterogeneous monitoring data, fault detection and diagnosis has become a challenging yet crucial task for ensuring system reliability and enabling intelligent maintenance. Despite considerable progress, existing studies remain fragmented across different robot subsystems, data modalities, and diagnostic paradigms, and a systematic review dedicated to industrial robot fault detection and diagnosis is still lacking. To address this gap, this paper presents a comprehensive and structured review from three complementary perspectives: fault characteristics and data resources, diagnostic methodologies, and emerging trends. Specifically, the review summarizes typical fault types and data acquisition strategies, organizes existing diagnostic methods into a structured taxonomy, and discusses key challenges and emerging directions such as multimodal fusion, trustworthy deployment, and digital-twin-driven diagnosis. This review provides a structured reference for advancing both theoretical research and engineering applications of industrial robot fault detection and diagnosis in intelligent manufacturing systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Author full names: Benkhira, EL Hassan (44460930300); Yamouni, Ouiame El (59780942300); Fakhar, Rachid (44461128300); Mandyly, Youssef (57208573772)
Title: Mixed double-hemivariational analysis of piezoelectric contact with multiplier-coupled nonmonotone friction
Abstract: We introduce and analyze a static piezoelectric contact model for Hencky-type materials in which the nonsmooth interface response depends on the tangential displacement, the electric potential jump, and a regularized representation of the normal contact reaction through the Lagrange multiplier. This yields a genuinely multiplier-dependent double nonsmooth coupling on the contact boundary. The model is formulated as a mixed problem in which a Lagrange multiplier is associated with the unilateral Signorini-type contact constraint and, through its regularized representation, also enters the nonsmooth interface response. The resulting boundary functional is expressed in hemivariational form through Clarke’s generalized directional derivative with respect to both the primal interface variables and the regularized multiplier variable. Under standard assumptions on the constitutive operators and suitable growth, compactness, and upper semicontinuity conditions on the coupled superpotential, we prove the existence of weak solutions. The proof combines a truncation procedure, a Fan–KKM argument with a Minty-type reformulation, a uniform multiplier estimate based on an inf–sup property for the normal trace, and a weak compactness argument. We also establish a sequential stability result showing the robustness of weak solutions under perturbations of the loadings and of the foundation data. Finally, a numerical illustration is provided to highlight the influence of the regularized normal reaction on the effective frictional and electrical interface responses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: He S.; Liu Q.; Ma J.
Title: Möbius disjointness conjecture for Furstenberg's flow on Tω in short intervals
Source title: Communications on Pure and Applied Analysis
Abstract: Furstenberg's flow on the infinite-dimensional torus Tω is defined by T(x1, x2, …, xv, …) = (x1 + α, x2 + h(x1), …, xv + h(x1 + (n - 2)β), …) with α∈R satisfying certain Diophantine conditions, β∈R\Q, and h: R→R being 1-periodic and analytic. This flow is a generalization of Furstenberg's irregular flow on T2. In this paper, we obtain a short-interval version of the Sarnak's Möbius disjointness conjecture on (Tω, T). © 2027, American Institute of Mathematical Sciences.All rights reserved.

Title: Effects of Balangu seed mucilage and plant proteins on the rheological and structural properties of gluten-free bread: A mixture design approach
Abstract: The absence of gluten weakens the structure of gluten-free bread systems, resulting in poor batter stability, limited gas retention, and reduced crumb porosity. To overcome these limitations, plant proteins and hydrocolloids are commonly incorporated to restore viscoelastic properties. In this regard, batter rheology plays a critical role in regulating gas-cell stability during fermentation and baking, thereby determining the final crumb structure and bread quality. This study used a mixture design to evaluate the effects of two protein isolates (soy protein isolate, SPI; faba bean protein isolate, FPI) and two hydrocolloids (carboxymethyl cellulose, CMC; Balangu seed mucilage, BSM) on the rheological properties of gluten-free batters and bread quality. The aim was to compare SPI and FPI and assess the performance of BSM relative to CMC, considering both individual and interactive effects. Results showed that batter viscoelastic behavior was strongly affected by both protein source and hydrocolloid type. BSM enhanced structural strength and stability more effectively than CMC, indicating a greater ability to promote network formation in the batter matrix. Appropriate protein–hydrocolloid combinations improved gas-cell stability and crumb porosity, whereas excessive hydrocolloid levels produced overly rigid matrices that restricted expansion. Optimization using a desirability function identified an optimal formulation (SPI 0.897%, FPI 3.60%, CMC 0.00%, BSM 0.498%), yielding bread with a specific volume of 4.37 mL/g and porosity of 31.5%. Overall, the results highlight the potential of BSM as a bio-based alternative to CMC and demonstrate the importance of optimizing protein–hydrocolloid ratios to improve gluten-free bread structure. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Wang B.; Liu S.-Q.; Yang Y.; Xu X.-Y.; Wang J.-W.; Li L.-L.; Zhang G.; Ma C.-M.; Zhang N.
Title: Effects of four modifiers on the protein network in gluten-free bread: Insights into disulfide bonds and non-covalent interactions
Abstract: Although rice dough is a promising gluten-free alternative to wheat dough, it lacks gluten's robust protein network—formed via hydrogen bonds and intermolecular interactions—resulting in poor viscoelastic properties. This study selected four modifiers with different functional mechanisms: 0.5% glyceryl monostearate (GMS, an emulsifier binding starch and proteins), 1% hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC, a hydrocolloid simulating gluten viscoelasticity and improving water retention), 0.6% trypsin, and 9% whey protein. Circular dichroism (CD), SDS-PAGE, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) were adopted to characterize protein conformational shifts, intermolecular forces, and dough microstructure integrity. Whey protein most effectively improved network integrity by supplying exogenous subunits to reconstruct continuous protein matrices, whereas HPMC, although it improved water-holding capacity, failed to construct a stable continuous protein network structure. Trypsin caused excessive endogenous protein hydrolysis and structural deterioration, whereas GMS exhibited only moderate viscosity improvement with inferior regulatory efficacy compared to whey protein. Collectively, whey protein and HPMC are identified as superior modifiers, trypsin requires precise dosage control to avoid quality degradation, and GMS can serve as a supplementary functional agent. This work provides targeted strategies for overcoming textural defects in gluten-free rice dough, facilitates industrial production of high-quality gluten-free cereals, and offers fundamental insights into molecular interaction mechanisms between functional modifiers and cereal protein networks in gluten-free matrices. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Sun Z.; Liu Y.; Hettinga K.; Wang S.; Luo J.; Liu C.; Zhou P.
Title: Comparative analysis in the structural and functional properties of sunflower seed protein prepared by isoelectric precipitation and salt extraction-dialysis
Abstract: Developing novel and green extraction methods for sunflower protein concentrate (SPC) from defatted sunflower seed meal is vital to the food industry. This study systematically compared the molecular structure, functional properties, and in vitro bioactivity of sunflower seed proteins prepared via a novel salt-extraction dialysis (SD-SPC) process and conventional isoelectric precipitation (IP-SPC). The results showed that the optimal extraction parameters for SD-SPC were a NaCl concentration of 1.5 mol/L and three extraction cycles. SD-SPC achieved higher protein recovery (80.02% vs 57.10%) and yield (66.40% vs 39.02%) than IP-SPC, although its purity was lower (70.82% vs 86.02%). In terms of molecular structural characteristics, SDS-PAGE and spectral analyses verified that SD-SPC possessed a higher proportion of albumins and a more unfolded molecular conformation. SD-SPC exhibited superior thermal stability (Td = 86.46 vs 74.77°C) and brighter color, and SEM observation confirmed its fine and uniform flaky microstructure. In contrast, IP-SPC formed large lamellar aggregate structures with inferior structural homogeneity. Functionally, SD-SPC showed higher solubility and foaming capacity. Furthermore, in vitro assays demonstrated that SD-SPC exerted stronger antioxidant capacity (DPPH IC50 = 1.72 vs 13.28 mg/mL) and higher inhibitory activity against α-amylase, α-glucosidase and lipase, showing potential as a functional food ingredient, though further in vivo validation is still needed. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Preparation, characterization, and application of soluble dietary fiber-rich kiwi peel pomace: Fiber-fortification of bread
Abstract: Kiwifruit processing generates large amounts of peel pomace rich in dietary fibers and polyphenols, but these by-products are usually discarded or underutilized. In this study, an optimized cellulase/β-glucosidase treatment was developed to valorize kiwifruit peel pomace. The treatment converted insoluble dietary fiber (IDF) into soluble dietary fiber (SDF), increasing SDF to 14.83%, and simultaneously enhanced total phenols, flavonoids, antioxidant activities, and volatile compounds. When assessed as a functional ingredient in bread, the treated pomace improved dough properties by elevating α-amylase activity, reducing free sulfhydryl groups, and increasing disulfide bonds, thereby promoting gluten cross-linking and the formation of a continuous gluten network with embedded starch granules. This mechanism was associated with improved farinograph parameters, dough extensibility, and viscoelasticity. In bread, the treated pomace improved loaf volume and texture, raised resistant starch to 54.61%, lowered the estimated glycemic index to 63.16, and prolonged gastric emptying, while antioxidant capacities and sensory scores were also improved. Overall, enzymatic conversion of IDF to SDF effectively enhanced dough processability and bread nutritional quality. These findings demonstrate that enzyme-assisted valorization of kiwifruit peel pomace is a sustainable strategy for producing a functional bread ingredient, with benefits mechanistically linked to gluten network reinforcement and modulated starch digestibility. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Mao S.; Li M.; Wang W.; Han P.; Li H.; Zhang T.; Lu C.
Title: Carrageenan based hydrogel systems with artificial compartment for probiotics microcapsules and tannic acid to preserve perishable food
Abstract: In this study, microcapsules of Lactococcus lactis in whey protein isolated/sodium alginate was co-encapsulated with tannic acid in the carrageenan hydrogel. This design created compartments via the microcapsules and prevented the activity loss with direct contact of the components. The structural analysis results indicated that tannic acid and microcapsules strengthened the network structure through hydrogen bonding. The incorporation of microcapsules into the hydrogel provided physical support, improving the mechanical properties of the carrageenan-based composite hydrogel by 36.5%. Furthermore, the acidic microenvironment created by Lactococcus lactis and the protective network formed by tannic acid mutually enhanced stability and demonstrated synergistic effects. The composite hydrogel exhibited excellent antioxidant activity with scavenging rates exceeding 80% for ABTS, DPPH and superoxide anion radicals. Meanwhile, it significantly inhibited the growth of bacteria and fungi, including Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, Salmonella enteritidis, Aspergillus niger and Botrytis cinerea. Biocompatibility assessment showed that the composite hydrogel exhibited virtually no cytotoxicity or hemolytic activity, and could promote plant growth after degradation in water. Practical storage tests confirmed that composite hydrogel significantly delayed browning of fresh-cut apples and potatoes, maintaining acceptability after 1 and 8 h storage. Besides, it slowed the accumulation of total volatile basic nitrogen and deterioration of sensory quality in refrigerated chicken, extending shelf life by 2 days. In summary, the composite hydrogel possessed outstanding functionality and practicality, providing a promising strategy for the design of highly efficient and safe active food packaging. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Lu M.; Sun H.; Wang Z.; Wang Z.; Liu L.; Sun B.; Huang Y.; Zhu Y.; Qu M.; Zhu X.
Title: Ion-specific modulation of hierarchical assembly in hemp protein-carrageenan composite hydrogels: from conformational relaxation to distinct network topologies
Abstract: Modulating the hierarchical assembly of plant proteins and polysaccharides is crucial for designing functional hydrogels, yet ion-specific multiscale mechanisms remain ambiguous. This study systematically resolved the salt-mediated conformational shifts and gelation of hemp protein isolate (HPI) and carrageenan (CA) complexes using monovalent (Na+) and divalent (Ca2+) cations. Spectroscopy revealed that optimal ionic strengths (100 mM NaCl or 150 mM CaCl2) enabled controlled structural relaxation of HPI hexamers, maximizing the exposure of reactive anchoring sites, facilitating a 2.5-fold increase in surface hydrophobicity (as indicated by bound BPB, reaching 35.2 μg) and available sulfhydryl content (to 10.9 μmol/g). Non-reducing electrophoretic profiles showed that the network was mostly stabilized by non-covalent physical cross-links rather than macroscopic disulfide polymerization. Thus, macroscopic mechanical integrity and water holding capacity (WHC) were at maximums of 680 g and 85.0%, respectively. Low-field NMR and SEM quantitative analyses elucidated that optimal salt additions resulted the densest topologies, minimizing apparent porosity to 24.62% (NaCl) and 26.94% (CaCl2) to firmly entrap immobilized water. Morphologically, Na+ promoted a homogeneous, fine-stranded matrix, while Ca2+ induced compact particulate-like assembly via specific calcium-bridging. Over-ionic strengths (>200 mM) resulted chaotic over-aggregation and steric hindrance, disrupting the capillary network (porosity >41%) and strong synergy. These quantitative insights provide a robust theoretical framework for precisely tailoring the micro-topology and hydration properties of hemp protein-based composite hydrogels for advanced food applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Huang Z.; Wang R.; Fei X.; Gong D.; Hu X.; Zhang G.
Title: Modulation of interfacial stability for potato protein-gallic acid-sodium carboxymethyl cellulose conjugates: Structural modification and assembly behavior
Abstract: Protein–polyphenol–polysaccharide ternary conjugates represent a promising class of high-efficiency emulsifiers. However, their assembly behavior and stabilization mechanism at the oil–water interface has not yet been systematically clarified. In this study, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) was covalently grafted onto potato protein isolate–gallic acid (PPI–GA) conjugate by dry-heating Maillard reaction, and the structural evolution and interfacial functional mechanisms of the resulting conjugates were systematically investigated. The structural characteristics of the conjugates were characterized by SDS-PAGE, fluorescence spectroscopy, FT-IR spectroscopy, circular dichroism, and scanning electron microscopy. The results showed that CMC was successfully introduced by Maillard glycosylation, which significantly altered the secondary structure and micromorphology of PPI–GA conjugate. Consequently, the emulsifying properties, surface hydrophobicity and thermal stability were improved, with the denaturation temperature reaching 109.08 °C. The PPI–GA–CMC conjugate prepared at a 1:1 mass ratio of PPI–GA to CMC exhibited optimal interfacial performance with the highest rearrangement rate (Kr = 16.33 s−1) and formed the most stable elastic interfacial film (ΔE/π = 2.548), and a thick, highly hydrated, and mechanically robust interfacial layer (ΔF = −36.62 Hz, ΔD = 22.52 × 10−6) was formed, verified by quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation (QCM-D) analysis. These superior interfacial properties may provide a theoretical basis for designing high-performance plant protein-based emulsifiers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Zhao X.; Zhang H.; Wang K.; Li J.; Tian B.; Wang S.
Title: pH-shifted potato protein/carboxymethyl chitosan-based water-in-oil-in-gel emulsions: physicochemical properties and controlled release
Abstract: Water-in-oil-in-gel (W/O/G) emulsions were developed using pH-shifted potato protein (PP) and carboxymethyl chitosan (CMCS) composite gels as the external aqueous phase for epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) delivery. The external gel phase was prepared by combining pH-shift-modified PP with CMCS under a fixed Ca2+ crosslinking condition. PP was modified by alkaline (pH 12) or acidic (pH 2) pH-shifting, and EGCG-loaded W/O/G emulsions with different W/O:G ratios (4:6, 3:7, and 2:8) were prepared. The structural characteristics, rheological properties, physicochemical stability, and release behavior of the emulsions were systematically investigated. Results show that alkaline pH-shifting significantly enhanced the structural and functional properties of PP, promoting stronger interactions with CMCS and yielding a more robust external gel network. All W/O/G emulsions exhibited typical gel-like rheology. The alkaline-treated group displayed the best physical stability at the same phase ratio. Specifically, under alkaline treatment with a W/O:G ratio of 2:8, the emulsion showed optimal freeze-thaw stability, retaining a solvent retention rate > 87.28% after six cycles. This formulation also achieved the slowest EGCG release during simulated gastrointestinal digestion, and the zero-order model provided the best fit for the overall cumulative release data among the tested kinetic models. This research provides a novel approach for developing delivery systems based on modified plant proteins. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Edible tea polyphenol oxidation self-assembled zein films for fruit preservation
Abstract: Tea polyphenols (−)-epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG) oxidation self-assembled nanocomposites (ENP) were synthesized through a one-step self-assembly process without templating or seeding agents and incorporated into zein-based edible films for the purpose of fruit preservation. The ENP nanocomposites maintained the core structural characteristics of EGCG and demonstrated excellent antioxidant activity, and antibacterial properties against E. coli and S. aureus. As a coating, ENP significantly reduced strawberry decay, weight loss, and nutrient degradation during storage. When integrated into zein films, ENP improved structural density, mechanical properties, water vapor permeability, antioxidant capacity, and light transmittance, without affecting the crystallinity of the zein-based films. The zein-based ENP edible films effectively extended the shelf life of strawberries and fresh-cut apples, surpassing the performance of both pure zein and polyethylene films. Mechanistic investigations have demonstrated that ENP compromised bacterial biofilm and structure integrity, leads to the leakage of intracellular contents, and inhibited ATPase activity. Biological safety assessment showed that the ENP nanocomposites exhibited negligible toxicity to zebrafish and seed germination, and the zein-based ENP film has ideal degradation performance. Taken together, zein-based films incorporating ENP offer a sustainable, effective, and safe approach for packaging in fruit preservation. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wang Z.-S.; Li G.-F.; Li S.-Y.
Title: A metric-compatible positivity-preserving compact scheme for degenerate time–space fractional reaction–diffusion with variable delay
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: We develop a metric-compatible positivity-preserving compact scheme for a degenerate time–space fractional reaction–diffusion equation with variable delay. A fourth-order Riesz discretization and the second-order L2-1σ formula produce a candidate, which is projected onto the nonnegative cone in the inverse-diffusion metric. The same metric converts the nonlinear diffusion into a monotonicity product and transfers the candidate error to the accepted state with unit constant. We prove unique candidate solvability and exact nonnegativity of accepted states. Under explicit smoothness, zero-extension compatibility and causal step restrictions, complementary-kernel estimates yield an O(τ2+h4) error bound, with parameter dependence stated and no positive lower bound on the solution. A nonuniform Alikhanov implementation supports graded startup refinement, while the general nonsmooth convergence question remains separate from the smooth theorem. Numerical tests include analytical solutions, oscillatory and discontinuous delay reconstruction, 27 mesh–parameter contact configurations, a 576-case activation scan, and a published direct implicit baseline on a shared model. They distinguish correction distance from solution-error amplification: metric projection is nonexpansive for a fixed candidate, but is not uniformly more accurate than clipping over separately advanced trajectories. Dual active-set and full-solver benchmarks also separate inversion-free projection and fast operator actions from end-to-end runtime. These results delimit the accuracy, admissibility and computational scope of the proposed metric-compatible construction. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Li X.; Huang R.; Li M.; Zhang L.; Qian X.; Sun B.; Ma S.; Li L.
Title: Unveiling the impact of mixed-strain solid-state fermentation on wheat bran dietary fiber: gluten protein structure evolution, dough rheological modulation and steamed bread quality enhancement
Abstract: Wheat bran dietary fiber (WBDF) helps enhance the nutrition of dough products, but its direct incorporation triggers quality deterioration. In this study, a mixed-strain solid-state fermentation strategy involving Basidiomycetes, Candida utilis, and Lactobacillus plantarum was employed to modify WBDF. The underlying mechanisms by which modified WBDF affects dough and steamed bread quality were systematically investigated across a range of addition levels (0, 3, 6, 9, 12, and 15 %). Results showed that unfermented WBDF (UWBDF) disrupted the gluten network, reducing dough and steamed bread quality. In contrast, fermented WBDF (FWBDF) effectively mitigated these adverse effects. At the gluten protein level, FWBDF promoted disulfide bond cross-linking (free sulfhydryl groups content decreased from 8.16 to 7.36 μmol/g), and increased the glutenin macropolymer content from 0.47 to 1.92 g/100 g. Besides, FWBDF optimized water distribution within the dough, improving water availability for starch and gluten proteins. These changes enhanced the pasting, extension, and dynamic rheological properties of dough, ultimately improving steamed bread quality-characterized by increased specific volume (from 1.71 to 2.30 mL/g), texture (hardness from 3209 to 2670 g; springiness from 0.81 to 0.84), and antioxidant capacity. Notably, the beneficial effects of FWBDF were closely dependent on its addition level. At 3-6 % addition, the modifying advantages of WBDF were fully realized; however, at 12-15 %, excessive FWBDF exacerbated gluten network disruption, leading to quality deterioration of dough and steamed bread. This study provides a theoretical foundation for the fermentation modification of WBDF and its application in steamed bread production. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Improved differential-linear attacks on round-reduced forró
Abstract: At ASIACRYPT 2022, Coutinho et al. proposed the stream cipher Forró as a successor to ChaCha. ChaCha is a well-known ARX-based cipher widely deployed in many practical applications, including TLS 1.3, SSH, Noise, S/MIME 4.0, and Google Chrome. The goal of the Forró design is to achieve a security level comparable to ChaCha while requiring fewer operations. Although Forró follows a structure similar to ChaCha, its modified round function provides stronger diffusion. The designers claim that 14 rounds of Forró offer a security level comparable to ChaCha20. In this work, we study the security of Forró using MILP-based differential-linear cryptanalysis. We model the ARX structure of the cipher using Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) and automatically search for optimal differential trails. Using the best one-round trail, we construct a 3-round differential-linear distinguisher. Furthermore, we introduce the concept of probabilistic neutral vectors (PNVs), which improves the selection of effective neutral key-bit positions compared to traditional probabilistic neutral bit (PNB) methods. By combining our MILP-derived trails, the newly found differential-linear distinguisher, and the proposed PNV technique, we obtain improved key-recovery attacks on 5 and 5.5 rounds of Forró, improving the attack time by approximately 2^5 and 2^30, respectively. In addition, to the best of our knowledge, we present the first key-recovery attacks on 5.75, 6^*, and 6 rounds. © 2026 American Institute of Mathematical Sciences

Title: A PRIMAL-DUAL SPLITTING ALGORITHM FOR MONOTONE INCLUSIONS WITH APPLICATIONS
Abstract: In this paper, we study a broad class of structured monotone inclusion problems in real Hilbert spaces. We propose a novel primal-dual splitting algorithm for solving such inclusions, which accommodates multiple monotone operators and cocoercive terms, as well as a composite monotone operator involving the linear map. The algorithm combines forward evaluations for the cocoercive components with backward resolvent steps for the monotone operators and employs a dual update for the linear composition term. Title: Neural-network learning and identifiability for mobility-based SEAIR epidemic models
Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a mobility-based SEAIR epidemic model that addresses two limitations of existing heterogeneous compartmental models: the neglect of pre-symptomatic transmission, and the absence of symptom-driven mobility reduction. Title: Generalized complex Itô-type Hermite polynomials: properties and applications

Title: Neural network model for mathematical programming problems with complementarity constraints

Title: Synergistic modification of okara insoluble dietary fiber by hydrothermal alkaline treatment and ball milling reinforces casein gel properties

Title: LEARNED ALTERNATING DESCENT ALGORITHM WITH EXTRAPOLATION FOR DUAL-DOMAIN CT RECONSTRUCTION
Abstract: Sparse-view and limited-angle Computed Tomography (CT) are important accelerated imaging techniques with reduced X-ray radiation dose. Title: Concentration - dependent rheology of chia seed mucilage across shear and extensional deformation
Abstract: Chia seed mucilage (CSM) is a plant-derived heteropolysaccharide with potential as a natural thickener, yet its structure–function relationships under combined shear and extensional flow remain unclear. In this study, CSM dispersions (0.01–2.0 g dL−1) were characterized under pH 3 and pH 7 buffered conditions using Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, steady shear, small-amplitude oscillatory shear, and dripping-onto-substrate (DoS) extensional rheometry. Title: Mechanistic investigation of covalent interactions between 11S soy glycinin and genistein following thermal treatment using benchtop testing and molecular modelling
Abstract: The effect of thermal treatment on the molecular interactions between soy glycinin (11S) and genistein (GNE) at 95°C was explored utilising a combination of spectroscopic and in-silico techniques. UV-vis analysis revealed substantial alterations to absorption spectra following ligand addition and heat exposure, suggesting a covalent interaction may have occurred. Heat exposure significantly enhanced binding affinity, with the association constant increasing from 2.5 x 104 M−1 at ambient temperature to 1.0 x 105 M−1, when quantified on a binding-site basis appropriate for this multivalent system. FTIR and CD analysis demonstrated that GNE addition resulted in only minor increases to alpha helix and beta sheet components of 11S. Title: AI-Driven Surrogate Modeling and Inverse Design of Type-II Superlattice Infrared Detectors
Source title: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics
Abstract: The conventional design of Type-II superlattice (T2SL) infrared detectors relies on iterative physics-based simulations, which can make broad exploration computationally costly. Here, we develop an AI-driven surrogate workflow for InAs/GaSb T2SL detectors. Title: Taming the boundary effect: Femtosecond laser slicing of 4H-SiC enabled by side scribing for improved processability
Abstract: The 4H polytype of silicon carbide (4H-SiC) has excellent properties such as high electron mobility and high saturation electron velocity; ithas therefore become an important material for high-power and high-frequency devices. The simulations revealed boundary regions that resist laser modification because of the coupling between asymmetricfocusing and spherical aberration, which degrades the slicing quality of conventional laser processing. Systematic parametric experimentswere then used to investigate the influence of the laser processing parameters on the formation of the modified layer. Targeted experimentsperformed using the optimized processing parameters provided a quantitative characterization of the hard-to-modify regions and guided theapplication of the side-scribing process. Title: Fish skin collagen improves ostrich myofibrillar protein heat-set gels through hydrophobic interaction-driven network formation
Abstract: This study developed a fish skin collagen (FSC) and ostrich myofibrillar protein (OMP) composite system to investigate how FSC affects the gel properties of OMP when heated. The analysis focused on structural and gel-related properties, including solubility, particle size, surface hydrophobicity, and water-holding capacity. At 0.75% FSC, the composite gel formed the most compact and continuous three-dimensional network, as evidenced by microstructural imaging and corroborated by the maximum hydrophobic-interaction contribution, the strongest network elasticity, and the highest cooking yield and water-holding capacity. Compared to the control, cooking yield and water-holding capacity rose by 16.71% and 25.96%, respectively, with notable improvements in hardness, elasticity, and chewability. Mechanistic analysis showed that hydrophobic interactions mainly drove gel network formation, while hydrogen bonds enhanced water retention and stability. However, adding 1% FSC led to excessive aggregation, disrupting network continuity and gel properties. Thus, 0.75% FSC was optimal for enhancing OMP gel properties within the 0–1.0% addition range. Title: Physicochemical properties of hydroxypropylated short-chain glucan aggregates
Abstract: Short-chain glucan aggregates (SCGA) is a starch-derived hydrocolloidal material with great potential. Title: Pulsed electric field pretreatment modulates heat-induced rheological properties of plant-based milks through protein conformational changes
Abstract: Plant-based milks are attractive ingredients for developing structured foods; however, their proteins often exhibit limited structuring ability under mild thermal processing, restricting the formation of desirable rheological properties. In this study, pulsed electric field (PEF) pretreatment was investigated as a strategy to modify protein conformation and modulate heat-induced rheological behavior in complex plant-based milks. PEF pretreatment induced matrix-dependent protein conformational changes, evidenced by secondary structural rearrangements and increased exposure of hydrophobic regions, while the extent of protein association differed among botanical sources. Collectively, the results demonstrate that PEF pretreatment modifies protein conformation in complex plant-based milks, facilitating intermolecular interactions during subsequent mild heating and modulating their rheological properties. Title: Eigenvectors of the De Bruijn graph Laplacian: A natural basis for the cut and cycle space
Source title: Journal of Combinatorial Theory. Series A
Abstract: We study the Laplacian of the undirected De Bruijn graph over an alphabet A of order k. This is done by developing an analogue of the Fourier transform on the De Bruijn graph, which acts to diagonalize the undirected Laplacian. Title: Deep-learning–based automated multimodal fusion network using multiphoton imaging for predicting lymph-node metastasis in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma

Title: Gelation and positivity of solutions to the discrete Oort–Hulst–Safronov coagulation equation
Source title: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
Abstract: Motivated by the recent deterministic approach of Fournier [16] to gelation for the continuous Smoluchowski coagulation equation, we adapt his method to the discrete Oort–Hulst–Safronov (OHS) coagulation system. Title: Conditional interval distortion risk measures: Stochastic comparisons and applications
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: This study is motivated by the need for systemic risk measures that can capture risk transmission under different levels of financial stress. Comparative theorems for CoID and its contribution measures are systematically established under various stochastic orders, showing that, under reasonable tail dependence assumptions, the stochastic ordering of marginal distributions effectively propagates to the comparative assessment of risk vectors. Title: Finite element approximation of a hemivariational inequality for steady-state heat conduction: double-limit convergence of penalization and discretization
Abstract: In this paper we study the numerical approximation and convergence analysis of a steady-state heat conduction problem with mixed boundary conditions. The physical model is governed by a hemivariational inequality depending on a heat transfer parameter α > 0. We consider the finite element approximation of this penalized problem, as well as its corresponding limit problem with a prescribed constant temperature on a part of the boundary. The main theoretical result establishes the strong convergence of the discrete solutions. Specifically, we prove the double-limit convergence of the finite element approximations to the limit solution as the mesh size h tends to zero and the penalization parameter α tends to infinity, independently and simultaneously. We further complement the convergence analysis with an error estimate of optimal order for the discrete limit problem, and we explain why an estimate uniform in the penalization parameter cannot be expected. The theoretical results are illustrated by numerical simulations on four examples verified by the method of manufactured solutions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Kobayashi T.; Nakasato R.
Title: Analyticity and asymptotic behavior of solutions to the compressible Navier-Stokes-Korteweg equations with the zero sound speed in scaling critical spaces
Abstract: We consider the initial-value problem in the d -dimensional Euclidean space Rd ( d ≥ 3) for the compressible Navier-Stokes-Korteweg equations under the zero sound speed case (namely, P′(ρ*)=0, where P=P(ρ) stands for the pressure). The system is well-known as the Diffuse Interface model describing the motion of a vaper-liquid mixture in a compressible viscous fluid. The purposes of this paper are to obtain the global-in-time solution around the constant equilibrium states ( ρ *, 0) ( ρ * > 0) satisfying the estimate on the analyticity as established by Foias-Temam (1989), and investigate the Lp−L1 type time-decay estimates in scaling critical settings based on Fourier-Herz spaces. In addition, we also derive the first order asymptotic formula with higher derivatives for solutions as the application of the analyticity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Author full names: Djaoué, Séraphin (57219198213); Damakoa, Irépran (56652300000); Perasso, Antoine (36473706300); Richard, Quentin (57196036446)
Title: Global stability in an age-structured SIRS malaria transmission model
Abstract: This paper proposes and analyzes a malaria transmission model structured by the chronological age of the human host population. The model couples an age-structured SIRS system for humans, incorporating waning immunity, with an SI system for mosquitoes under mass-action transmissions. Using integrated semigroup theory and spectral analysis, we establish the well-posedness of the model, derive the basic reproduction number, and prove the global asymptotic stability of the parasite-free equilibrium by using a Lyapunov functional when R0≤1, thereby excluding the possibility of backward bifurcation. Numerical simulations suggest the global stability of the endemic equilibrium when R0>1, while the analytical proof remains an open problem. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Jiao P.; Liu Y.; Luo J.; Song Y.; Wang M.; Cai X.
Title: A four-shank 32-channel microelectrode array integrated with FPGA-based online processing for multichannel neural recording
Abstract: Multichannel neuralrecording requires not only microelectrode arrays(MEAs) with sufficientspatial coverage but also stable front-end acquisition and online signal processing hardware. In this work, a four-shank 32-channel MEA and a field-programmable gate array (FPGA)-basedonline processing module are developed for multichannel neural recording. The four-shank structure is designed to provide broader spatialcoverage while maintaining a compact probe footprint. Platinum nanoparticles (PtNPs) are modified on the electrode surfaces to improvethe electrical interface of the recording sites. Electrochemical measurements demonstrate that PtNPs modification significantly improves theinterfacial properties of the electrodes. An FPGA-based module is employed to enable communication with the front-end chip and performonline signal processing. Post-implementation verification further demonstrates that the FPGA design satisfies the timing constraints whilemaintaining acceptable power consumption. The end-to-end performance of the electrophysiological recording chain is evaluated throughgain/bandwidth testing and simulated neural signal detection. The system exhibits an average gain of 45.57 dB within the main passband, witha bandwidth ranging from 4.28 to 2.36 kHz. In addition, simulated spike tests demonstrate stable online detection and waveform extraction.In addition, in vivo recordings from the hippocampal CA1 region demonstrate that the proposed system simultaneously acquires clear spikeand local field potential signals from multiple channels, with representative spike waveforms exhibiting good consistency. The combinationof a four-shank MEA with PtNPs-modified recording sites and FPGA-based online processing supports stable neural signal acquisition bothin vitro and in vivo and provides a useful foundation for future neural interface applications. © 2026 Author(s).

Authors: Pradhan S.; Das S.K.
Title: An anthraene-threaded phenanthroimidazolate-based fluorescent room temperature ionic liquid and its low-dimensional materials: Implications as photoluminescence ink and dextran Sulphate detection
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: A novel anthracene-coupled phenanthroimidazolate-based fluorescent room-temperature ionic liquid (ILs), PHIL , is synthesized and subsequently processed via reprecipitation to obtain its microstructured form, mPHIL . Detailed spectroscopic and microscopic characterizations confirmed the successful formation of the ILs and microstructure. Neat PHIL has been used as fluorescent photoluminescence ink. Microstructured PHIL ( mPHIL) has been utilized for the selective detection of the anticoagulant agent dextran sulfate (DSS) in aqueous media. The intrinsic fluorescence of mPHIL is relatively low in aqueous medium but is greatly amplified upon association with DSS. The system enables sensitive detection with a limit of detection (LOD) in the nanogram per milliliter (ng/mL) range. To facilitate field applicability, a portable detection kit is fabricated to enable rapid, sensitive detection of DSS. The detection of DSS in various serum samples highlights its effectiveness in challenging biological media. This work demonstrates a promising approach for developing an IL-derived photoluminescent ink as a security ink and microoptode for medical diagnosis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Xie L.; Yang J.; Song B.
Title: Exploring 2D Isotope Heterostructures for Atomic-Scale Control of Thermal Radiation
Source title: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics
Abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) materials with their characteristic layered structures and weak van der Waals interlayer interactions provide a versatile platform for manipulating emergent phenomena and engineering novel functionalities in the thermal near field. Recently, it has been revealed that the energy-momentum dispersions and photonic density of states of 2D materials can be effectively modulated by isotope engineering. Here, we explore the impact of isotope composition on thermal radiation for 2D heterostructures based on hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). By systematically varying the number of layers, we discover that few-layer hBN amplifies the isotope-induced spectral match and mismatch between the hyperbolic phonon polaritons. The largest isotope effect is observed in monolayer hBN, where the ratio of the heat transfer coefficient between isotopically identical and maximally distinct hBN pairs reaches approximately 300. Interestingly, for emitters and receivers of different layer counts, the heat flux between isotopically distinct hBN pairs can surpass that for identical pairs. Furthermore, we reveal that thermal transport is highly sensitive to the stacking order at sub-10 nm gap sizes, as demonstrated by bilayer isotope heterostructures. Finally, to facilitate experimental study, the substrate and temperature dependence of the isotope effect are investigated. Our findings highlight the unique potential of 2D materials for isotopically engineering near-field thermal radiation with single-atomic-layer precision.  © 1995-2012 IEEE.

Authors: Gao F.; Hou X.; Wang Z.; Li Z.; Wang J.; Liu J.
Title: Thermo-reversible bigels stabilized by soluble dietary fiber extracted from microwave-treated okara: Molecular interactions, network rearrangement, and application in mayonnaise
Abstract: This study investigates the preparation and structural regulation of thermo-reversible bigels composed of soluble dietary fiber from microwave-treated okara (M-SDF) hydrogels and carnauba wax/sunflower seed oil oleogels, evaluating their application in low-fat mayonnaise. Carnauba wax was introduced as the oleogelator to structure the oil phase, with its crystalline matrix largely determining the mechanical properties and thermal reversibility of the bigels, while M-SDF served as a macromolecular stabilizer to structure the hydrogel phase and enhance interfacial stability. Microwave pre-treatment altered the molecular characteristics of okara SDF, leading to altered monosaccharide composition, enhanced thermal stability and increased crystallinity, driven by strengthened hydrogen bonding and a more ordered network arrangement. Using variable-temperature FTIR and rheological temperature sweeps, the microstructure and phase transition of the bigels were systematically characterized. The spectral and structural responses were highly dependent on the oleogel-to-hydrogel ratio, with the 7:3 bigel exhibiting pronounced thermal reversibility. Temperature elevation intensified bands at 3677 and 1041 cm−1, indicating the progressive weakening of intermolecular interactions and interfacial rearrangement. Rheological measurements confirmed that the optimized bigels possessed elevated storage modulus (G′ up to 4.65 × 103 Pa) and high phase transition temperature (Tgel of 85.87 °C), supporting a mechanically robust matrix. Incorporating these bigels into mayonnaise significantly improved textural properties and viscoelastic behaviors, demonstrating their effectiveness as a clean-label structuring and stabilizing agent. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Jiang F.; Fan C.; Dang M.; Wei F.; Liang L.; Fu L.; Xu C.; Lin B.
Title: A novel edible, all-biomass Pickering emulsion coating based on Lys/Alg composite nanoparticles for curcumin delivery and active fruit preservation
Abstract: The integration of nano-encapsulation with edible coatings holds great potential for active fruit preservation. However, conventional emulsions often rely on chemical surfactants, posing safety risks and limited functionality. Here, we developed an edible, all-biomass-derived Pickering emulsion (CLAPE) coating stabilized by amphiphilic lysozyme/alginate composite nanoparticles (Lys/Alg). The Lys/Alg were fabricated through electrostatic self-assembly followed by Ca2+ cross-linking, forming a robust interfacial layer that effectively encapsulates curcumin (Cur). Molecular docking simulations revealed a strong binding affinity between Lys and Cur (binding energy: −87.2 kcal/mol), which significantly enhances the aqueous dispersibility and stability of Cur. The resulting Pickering emulsion enables sustained release of curcumin over 60 h, with a peak cumulative release of 94.0%, approximately twice that of the unencapsulated control. This release profile follows Fickian diffusion, extending the bioactive duration and increasing the total released amount, thereby enhancing curcumin's bioavailability. Moreover, CLAPE exhibits excellent thermal stability, maintaining high stability indices under varied accelerated storage conditions. It also exhibited high antioxidant (99.02%) and broad-spectrum antibacterial activity. Additionally, the application of CLAPE on strawberries, bananas and grapes has led to a doubling of their shelf life while maintaining the freshness and nutrient content of the fruits. The edible active preservative material, based entirely on biomass, not only forms a multifunctional protective coating that prevents spoilage but can also be easily washed off. This study presents an innovative strategy for the designs of active preservation materials utilizing all-natural plant-derived components. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Author full names: Li, Jinghong (58725677000); Zhao, Minghui (58766582200); Zhang, Nan (59343453200); Liu, Mengzhuo (58111135000); Li, Hanyu (57218770262); Zhang, Huajiang (59655693900)
Title: Fibrillation-induced compositional remodeling of egg white protein: Differential glycerol regulation of cryogel networks and thermomechanical performance
Abstract: Cryogels constructed from food proteins derive their macroscopic properties from the structural organization and intermolecular interactions established in the precursor gel network. This study investigated the structural and compositional changes in egg white protein (EWP) during acid–heat-induced fibrillation and how these changes influence the subsequent effects of glycerol (Gly) on the protein network. Acid-heat treatment converted native globular EWP into β-sheet-rich fibrillar assemblies while simultaneously inducing protein hydrolysis, redistribution of protein components, and reorganization of surface interaction sites. These changes resulted in a heterogeneous composite gel network containing native proteins, fibrils, and remodeled protein components rather than a network dominated by globular protein aggregates, thereby modifying the available intermolecular contacts and load-bearing junctions. Gly consequently exhibited distinct concentration-dependent effects in the two networks. In native EWP cryogels, a relatively low Gly level was sufficient to maximize network stiffness, whereas the EWPF-containing system required a higher Gly level to achieve its maximum Young's modulus and bending load-bearing capacity. This shift in the optimal Gly concentration was associated with the greater heterogeneity of the hydrogen-bonding environment and the stronger structural constraints imposed by fibrillar and protein interfaces. Excessive Gly increased molecular mobility and heat transfer, ultimately reducing network stiffness and thermal-insulation performance. These findings show that fibrillation regulates EWP cryogels not only through fibrillar reinforcement but also through compositional and interaction-site remodeling, which in turn redefines the way Gly interacts with and regulates the resulting protein network. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Liang Y.; Yu X.; Zhang P.; Xing W.; Zhao J.; Wang X.; Liu H.; Wang J.
Title: Fabrication of bioactive hydrogels stabilized by gluten amyloid fibrils and ε-polylysine: Effects of fibril morphology and blending ratios
Abstract: The introduction of ε-Polylysine (PL) provides additional functional activities for hydrogels. However, it simultaneously impairs their mechanical properties to a certain extent. To address this trade-off, we hypothesized that gluten protein amyloid fibrils (GAFs) with distinct topological morphologies—long rigid fibrils (LRF), long flexible fibrils (LFF), and fibril networks (FN) differentially modulate PL hydrogels through site-specific molecular bridging and spatial cross-linking. Driven by strong electrostatic attraction and hydrogen bonding, GAFs and PL underwent ratio dependent systemic reorganization and assembly. The physicochemical properties of GAFs/PL hydrogels were primarily governed by the combined regulation of GAFs morphology and blending ratios. Specifically, at the same GAFs/PL ratio, FN exhibited superior spatial connectivity, contributing to enhanced water immobilization within the hydrogel network. Meanwhile, LRF and FN were more effective in constructing continuous force transmission pathways, thereby improving hardness and dynamic viscoelasticity. These findings demonstrate that the functional performance of GAFs/PL hydrogels can be tailored by selecting appropriate fibril morphologies and blending ratios according to specific application requirements. However, the network formed by LFF was more susceptible to deformation, resulting in a relatively limited mechanical reinforcement effect on the hydrogel skeleton. Ultimately, this study aims to clarify the assembly pathway driven by the cooperative contribution of GAFs and PL. This study provides a theoretical foundation and design strategies for developing food-grade composite materials with tunable mechanical properties and bioactive functionalities. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Boravelli J.A.R.; Vir A.B.
Author full names: Boravelli, Joseph Abhisheka Rao (58971957900); Vir, Anil B. (55963697700)
Title: Millifluidic-assisted internal gelation of tunable hydrogels: Mechanistic insights into gelation and enhanced betanin encapsulation
Abstract: Ionotropic gelation of polysaccharide-based hydrogels offers a versatile approach for encapsulating and controlling the release of bioactive compounds. However, conventional external ionotropic gelation can result in substantial losses of highly hydrophilic solutes through diffusion during gel formation, limiting encapsulation efficiency. In this study, internal gelation integrated with a continuous-flow millifluidic platform was employed to generate monodisperse, tunable alginate hydrogel particles for the encapsulation of highly hydrophilic bioactive betanin. The influence of biopolymer (sodium alginate), crosslinker carrier (Ca-EDTA), and acid trigger (acetic acid) concentrations on the structural and viscoelastic properties of hydrogel particles was systematically investigated. A regime map relating alginate and acid-trigger concentrations to the extent of gelation was developed. The influence of crosslinker carrier concentration on viscoelastic properties of hydrogel particles was elucidated using rheological characterization and deconvoluted FT-IR spectroscopy, providing mechanistic insights. The continuous-flow millifluidic platform enabled the controlled generation of spherical and rod-shaped hydrogel particles with tunable dimensions by varying the channel diameter, flow rate ratio, and alginate concentration. The integrated continuous-flow millifluidic internal gelation approach achieved significantly higher encapsulation efficiency for betanin (96.35 ± 1.11%), than the external gelation approach (45.35 ± 1.62%). The synthesized hydrogel particles also exhibited enhanced storage stability, retaining approximately 95% of the encapsulated betanin after six days of storage in the dried state. The release kinetics of encapsulated betanin were analysed at different pH values (3.8, 5.5, 6.8, and 8.03), using the Korsmeyer–Peppas model for swelling-associated release at pH 3.8 and 5.5 and the Hopfenberg model for dissolution-associated release at pH 6.8 and 8.03.Overall, this study demonstrates continuous-flow millifluidic internal gelation as an effective strategy for high-efficiency encapsulation, improved storage stability, and controlled release of highly hydrophilic food bioactives, while providing mechanistic insights into the relationship between crosslinking, hydrogel viscoelasticity, and bioactive release behavior. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Sun Y.; Jin H.; Zhang Y.; Ali S.; Wang R.; Ma J.; Yao X.; Shan Y.; Jin G.; Sheng L.
Title: pH-dependent foam stability of egg white protein-sodium alginate-eggshell powder systems: Roles of soluble calcium availability, bulk structuring, and interfacial behaviour
Abstract: Egg white protein (EWP)-based foams are widely used in aerated foods, and their stability depends on bulk-phase structure and air-water interfacial behaviour. This study investigated how initial pH conditions regulate soluble calcium availability, structural assembly, interfacial behaviour, and foam stability in EWP-sodium alginate (SA)-eggshell powder (EP) systems. EWP-SA dispersions were initially adjusted to pH 5.0, 7.0, or 9.0 before EP incorporation. Wet ball milling reduced EP to a submicron particle size of 0.41 μm while preserving the calcite CaCO3 crystalline structure. The pH 5.0 group showed the greatest pH increase after EP addition and the highest SWeibull plateau values for soluble calcium measured colorimetrically (21.52-24.22 mM), consistent with enhanced CaCO3 dissolution under the initially acidic condition. This group also exhibited enhanced EWP-SA association, possible Ca2+-mediated alginate crosslinking, broader particle-size distributions, higher β-Sheet contents, stronger bulk viscoelasticity, greater aggregation, and improved long-term foam retention during standing. Although the pH 7.0 and 9.0 groups generally exhibited higher dilatational moduli under the applied oscillatory conditions, the pH 5.0 group showed a faster initial adsorption response, with a maximum Kdiff of 2.359 mN m−1·s−1/2. Moreover, the 1.5% SA-1% EP and 1.5% SA-2% EP systems in the pH 5.0 group retained 100% and 95.63% of their foam volumes after 12 h, respectively. Foam stability was associated with changes in soluble calcium availability, bulk viscoelasticity, and interfacial behaviour. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for constructing stable EWP-SA-EP foams by regulating initial pH to coordinate bulk-interfacial coupling processes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Bartosz K.
Title: Vanishing viscosity method for a class of second order Clarke subdifferential inclusions
Abstract: We study a coupled system consisting of a second-order subdifferential inclusion, in which the multivalued term is given by the Clarke subdifferential of a locally Lipschitz function and an ordinary differential equation (ODE). The studied system arises from a contact problem involving a viscoelastic body and involves two operators related to viscosity and elasticity effects. The coercivity of the viscosity operator plays a crucial role in establishing the existence result for the viscoelastic problem. In addition, we consider an elastic case in which the viscosity operator is absent, leading to a loss of coercivity. To address this difficulty, we introduce a vanishing viscosity regularization and analyze the associated approximating problem. Using known results in the coercive setting, we establish existence for the regularized system, derive uniform a priori estimates, and pass to the limit to obtain a solution to the noncoercive problem. The approach extends previous results on hemivariational inequalities (HVIs) to a coupled HVI–ODE system and provides an alternative to discretization methods, with applications in contact mechanics and systems with evolving internal state variables describing adhesion. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Tao D.; Zhao Y.; Li M.; Liu H.; Li X.; Zhang J.; Du B.; Zhang B.; Ma F.
Title: Effect of oxygen-assisted solution pulsed plasma on the physicochemical properties of chitosan and mechanisms of action
Abstract: Oxygen-assisted solution pulsed plasma (SPP/O2) was employed to improve the physicochemical properties of chitosan. The effects of key process parameters on the degradation effect, rheological properties, antioxidant activity, thermogravimetry, and structural characteristics of chitosan were investigated. The results showed that after SPP/O2 degradation, the molecular weight and degree of deacetylation decreased, while the reducing sugar content increased. The shear thinning behavior, viscoelastic behaviors, and antioxidant activity of chitosan were enhanced, while its thermal stability decreased. The results of FTIR, 1H NMR, laser particle size, SEM, and XRD analysis revealed that the primary chemical backbone of chitosan was largely retained. The morphology structure became rougher, and the average particle size, PDI, and crystallinity decreased. Above all, SPP/O2 degradation effectively improved the physicochemical properties of chitosan. The reduction in molecular weight evidently played a key role in the improvement, and the oxygen flow rate, discharge voltage, and degradation time were positively correlated with the improvement. Compared with air, O2 promoted greater production of reactive species. Increasing the discharge voltage favored the production of •O2−, while increasing the O2 flow rate promoted the generation of •NO. These findings demonstrated the feasibility of SPP/O2 for chitosan degradation and provided new insights into the preparation of modified chitosan. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Raouf I.; Kim H.S.; Wang P.
Title: Cross-robot open-set fault detection via normal-only adaptation and residual latent-space alignment
Abstract: Reliable fault detection and health monitoring of industrial robots are important for smart manufacturing in Industry 4.0. However, robotic platforms differ in their mechanical design, sensing characteristics, and operating conditions. These differences make it difficult for data-driven models to generalize to unseen robots and working conditions. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a cross-robot framework for open-set fault detection using only normal data from the target robot. The framework uses a condition-normalized residual adaptation mechanism in the latent space. First, a structured representation is learned from the source robot. The learned representation is then adapted to the target robot using only normal samples. Compactness-based constraints and statistical modeling of normal behavior are used to detect unknown faults as deviations from the normal representation. The framework is evaluated on two industrial robots under variations in load, speed, and motion. Two evaluation strategies are also considered: sequential normal-only adaptation to welding motion and direct open-set detection without further adaptation. The results show consistent fault detection across different robots and operating conditions. A comparative benchmarking analysis further demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach and its ability to maintain reliable fault detection performance under different loading and motion conditions. This demonstrates the potential of the framework for practical industrial health monitoring. This is an open access article under the CC BY-NC license. http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/

Author full names: Khireddine, Houd (60155796700); Benabderrahmane, Benyattou (55672201400); Boukhatem, Yamna (55214958100); Feng, Baowei (55261404400)
Title: A fully dynamic frictional contact problem for viscoelastic materials with long-term memory and simplified Coulomb’s friction law
Abstract: We study a mathematical model describing the dynamic behavior of a viscoelastic body in frictional contact with a rigid foundation. The contact is governed by simplified Coulomb’s friction law, and the material exhibits a nonlinear constitutive law incorporating long-term memory effects. We present the model, specify the assumptions on the data, and derive a variational formulation in terms of the displacement field. We first establish a local existence and uniqueness result, then the global existence result is proved via energy methods. Finally, we prove the exponential stability of energy solutions using the multiplier technique. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Ullah A.; Amin A.
Title: Hydrocolloid microgels as programmable fat mimetics in food systems: Linking particle mechanics, tribology, rheology, and sensory perception
Abstract: Hydrocolloid microgels are emerging as programmable soft particles for designing low-fat and plant-based foods with improved texture, lubrication, water retention, and sensory quality. Unlike conventional hydrocolloid thickeners, microgels are discrete, hydrated, and deformable particles whose size, swelling behavior, stiffness, internal network density, surface properties, and water mobility can be tuned to reproduce selected functions of fat droplets. This review evaluates hydrocolloid microgels as fat mimetics and oral lubrication modulators by linking particle architecture, rheology, tribology, oral processing, digestion, and real-food performance. Major hydrocolloid materials, including alginate, pectin, gelatin, whey protein, casein, soy protein, pea protein, starch, cellulose derivatives, carrageenan, chitosan, gellan-like systems, and protein–polysaccharide blends, are discussed together with fabrication strategies such as ionic gelation, thermal gelation, acid gelation, enzymatic crosslinking, emulsification-gelation, shearing of bulk gels, spray drying, antisolvent precipitation, and microfluidics. Particular emphasis is placed on how microgel concentration, particle packing, deformability, swelling, surface charge, and interparticle interactions control viscosity, yield stress, shear thinning, viscoelasticity, thixotropic recovery, and weak-gel behavior. The review further highlights the role of microgels in reducing oral friction, improving creaminess, enhancing smoothness, modulating flavor release, and supporting juiciness in low-fat dairy, sauces, dressings, desserts, plant-based dairy analogues, meat analogues, emulsions, encapsulation systems, and 3D-printed foods. Future progress requires standardized characterization, tribology-guided formulation, digestion-aware design, and validation in real food matrices using both instrumental and sensory approaches. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Kim H.D.; Ye Y.J.; Kong M.; Lim W.S.; Chao C.; Kim Y.J.; Kim H.W.; Lee M.H.
Title: Structural reinforcement of O/W bigels by incorporating soy protein isolate–gellan gum complex and beeswax: Enhancing 3D printing precision and freeze-thaw stability
Abstract: This study developed a freeze-thaw stable bigel system optimized for extrusion-based 3D food printing using soy protein isolate (SPI), high acyl gellan gum (GG), and beeswax (BW). Physicochemical screening identified the SPI–GG0.2 complex, containing 4.0% w/v SPI and 0.2% w/v GG in the complex dispersion, as the optimal formulation. Rheological profiling revealed that SPI–GG complex bigels exhibited superior viscosity, a tunable loss tangent and a thixotropic recovery above 70% even at the highest BW content. After repeated freeze-thaw cycles (FTCs), the flagship formulation (SPI–GG_BW6) demonstrated superior cryo-resistance, maintaining macrostructural integrity with minimal syneresis, uniform droplet distribution, and the smallest color change of all formulations, whereas SPI-only controls suffered catastrophic phase separation. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and low-field nuclear magnetic resonance analyses revealed that physical compression from the crystallized BW oil core forced the interfacial SPI–GG complex into an ultra-dense arrangement. Furthermore, this structural reinforcement translated into superior printing performance. The SPI–GG complex inks reproduced the designed geometry far more faithfully than the SPI-only inks at all three structural levels, namely one-dimensional (fiber diameter), two-dimensional (grid area) and three-dimensional (cylinder height). Among them, SPI–GG_BW6 was the greatest resistant to repeated FTCs, showing a significantly smaller height loss than every other formulation and essentially unchanged grid area. Ultimately, this co-structuring strategy of aqueous and oil phases successfully resolves the rheological trade-off between fluid extrudability and post-printing freeze-thaw stability, offering a viable blueprint for cryo-resistant food fabrication. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Liu S.; Chen Z.; Pan Q.; Li X.; Gan X.; Chen G.
Title: AK-BHS: adaptive kriging with bisection-guided hyperspherical shell for reliability analysis
Abstract: To tackle the computational challenges in structural reliability analysis characterized by strong non-linearities and small failure probabilities, existing Kriging methods often incur redundant evaluations due to the lack of a rapid localization mechanism for the most probable point, as well as a well-defined adaptive exploration domain and effective boundary criteria. To address these issues, an adaptive Kriging method with bisection-guided hyperspherical shell is proposed. First, a bisection search mechanism coupled with a spherical boundary exploration function is introduced to rapidly lock onto the critical MPP hypersphere. Next, a closed hyperspherical shell is adaptively constructed to delineate a rigorous exploration boundary. Stratifying the shell according to the Kriging spatial autocorrelation scale, the limit-state boundary is efficiently refined using triple-filtering criteria. Finally, five benchmark and engineering examples involving multiple design points, small failure probabilities, and implicit limit states demonstrate the superior accuracy, computational efficiency, and robustness of the proposed method. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Authors: Campbell P.J.
Title: On the existence of integers with at most 3 prime factors between every pair of consecutive squares
Abstract: We prove an explicit analogue of Legendre's conjecture for almost primes. Namely, for every integer n≥1, the interval (n2,(n+1)2) contains an integer having at most 3 prime factors, counted with multiplicity. This improves the previous best result of Dudek and Johnston, who showed that every such interval contains an integer with at most 4 prime factors. The proof is divided into two ranges. For n2≤1031, we use prior computational results on primes in short intervals between consecutive squares, together with explicit bounds on maximal prime gaps. For n2>1031, we give a sieve-theoretic argument with explicit constants, adapting Richert's logarithmic weights to intervals between consecutive squares and employing an explicit linear sieve of Bordignon, Johnston, and Starichkova. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Knowledge-grounded multimodal cognitive decision-making for aerospace machining: A physics-aware reasoning framework for generative process planning of special-shaped features
Abstract: Complex aerospace products encompass numerous special-shaped features (SSFs), whose machining processes rely on highly customized process planning. Traditional data-driven discriminative models predominantly operate as physics-agnostic "black boxes." Moreover, applying general-purpose Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to manufacturing often causes "physical hallucinations", generating linguistically plausible but mechanically infeasible process plans. Title: Recovering noise-buried low-rank tensors in high dimensions: Accuracy estimates using Gaussian width bounds
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: The goal of this paper is the development of theoretical support for noise filtering properties of low-rank tensor approximations. Empirically, assuming that a given tensor with an exact low-rank structure is subjected to an additive noise, some widespread low-rank approximation algorithms can recover it quite accurately - even if the Frobenius norm of the noise exceeds that of the raw tensor. In this work, a rigorous recovery accuracy bound is proved for rank-one tensors with arbitrary dimensionality for the case of additive Gaussian noise: the analysis is based on the framework of Gaussian width of the set of tensors with rank 2. Title: Formation of soy protein isolate–xanthan gum eutectogels induced by natural deep eutectic solvents: Effects of hydrogen-bond donor type and acceptor-to-donor molar ratio

Title: Ultrasonically modified coconut protein hydrogel-sunflower seed oil oleogel bigels: Effects of hydrogel/oleogel ratios on physicochemical properties and freeze-thaw stability

Title: Adzuki bean starch: A review of its extraction, composition, structure, properties, modification and applications

Title: High internal phase Pickering emulsions stabilized by plant protein and polysaccharide composite particles: Construction, stability, application, and research advance

In contrast, at a lower saturation (S = 4%), the paste retained sensory attributes indistinguishable to the control while substantially enhancing physical stability, presenting a promising balance for practical application. Title: Compact relative-ordering models for interpretable EEG-based dementia classification
Abstract: Most EEG dementia classifiers rely on absolute feature magnitudes. We assessed whether pairwise relative-ordering methods, widely used in omics, support compact, interpretable EEG classifiers. We analysed eyes-closed (EC) and eyes-open with photic stimulation (EO/photo) recordings from the same Alzheimer's disease (AD), frontotemporal dementia (FTD), and cognitively normal (CN) OpenNeuro cohort (N = 88). Top Scoring Pair and k-Top Scoring Pair models were evaluated against standard machine-learning classifiers and fixed EEG-ratio controls across amplitude-decile and PSD/bandpower representations using repeated subject-wise cross-validation with training-fold-only model selection. Spectral representations most consistently supported relative-ordering models. Across six prespecified disease-versus-control task–condition settings, the main k-TSP models were broadly competitive with the strongest setting-specific standard machine-learning comparators (macro-F1 differences −0.030 to +0.035). Age and sex were examined in complementary sensitivity analyses; results were moderately sensitive to demographic adjustment, whereas repeated matching produced no consistent directional loss. Participant-level permutation localised the strongest recurrence evidence at the level of broader prespecified spectral–regional patterns (motifs): these motifs exceeded corrected nulls in specific AD-related settings, although no individual exact pair did so.
