Title: A temperature-coupled Cahn-Hilliard-Stokes-heat model for thermally driven phase separation
Abstract: We study a diffuse-interface model for thermally driven phase separation in viscous incompressible mixtures. The system couples a convective Cahn-Hilliard equation for the order parameter with a Stokes subsystem for the velocity-pressure field and a heat equation for the temperature. Temperature enters the bulk free energy through a Landau-type coefficient, while the phase field feeds back on the flow through concentration-dependent density and viscosity, yielding a phenomenological temperature-coupled Cahn–Hilliard–Stokes–heat system. The model serves as a proxy for temperature-triggered condensation-like phase separation and does not include humidity, latent heat, vapor pressure, or capillary forcing; these effects are absorbed into the choice of the threshold temperature Θ S . We motivate the chemical potential by a temperature-dependent Landau free energy and derive a priori estimates for the regularized subproblems. On the analytical side, we prove local-in-time existence of weak solutions for a regularized auxiliary model of the coupled system. This regularized formulation serves as an auxiliary analytical model for establishing local existence. On the numerical side, we use a first-order sequential finite-element discretization of a simplified quasi-static formulation. The heat equation is advanced by an implicit diffusion step, the variable-coefficient Stokes problem by a Taylor–Hood discretization, and the Cahn–Hilliard bulk derivative is evaluated at the previous time level, so every algebraic subproblem is linear. An isothermal diffusive test confirms mass conservation to roundoff and exhibits monotone discrete-energy decay for the tested parameter set. Time-step and mesh-refinement studies show first-order temporal and approximately second-order spatial behavior. The remaining computations are qualitative, parameter-specific illustrations, and no global discrete energy law is claimed for the non-isothermal sequential scheme. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Cinnamaldehyde-lactic acid deep eutectic solvent modified chitosan composite film and its application in grape preservation
Abstract: To address the issues of non-degradability in traditional petroleum-based packaging materials and the limitations of chitosan (CS) films (e.g., poor mechanical properties, insufficient water resistance, and single functionality), this study incorporated a deep eutectic solvent (DES) composed of cinnamaldehyde (CIN) and DL-lactic acid (LA) into the CS matrix to fabricate high-performance composite films. FTIR and XPS analyses suggested that a fraction of the aldehyde groups of CIN participated in Schiff base formation with the amino groups of CS. Together with hydrogen-bond reorganization and LA induced protonation of CS amino groups, these interactions contributed to the regulation of the CS network. When the DES content was 60% of the dry weight of CS, the resulting CS(CIN:LA)60 film exhibited the optimal comprehensive performance: its tensile strength (TS) reached as high as 41.57 MPa; the water contact angle (WCA) was approximately 100°, indicating good hydrophobicity; the water vapor transmission rate (WVTR) was reduced to 560.2 g/(m2·24h); meanwhile, it possessed excellent ultraviolet (UV) shielding ability, remarkable anti-fogging performance, and good antibacterial activity. Grape preservation experiments demonstrated that the CS(CIN:LA)60 film could effectively inhibit microbial growth, reduce water loss, and delay fruit softening and the degradation of nutritional components. Compared with commercial polyethylene (PE) cling film, the composite film showed advantages in antibacterial activity, anti-fogging performance, and the maintenance of several grape quality attributes. Title: Similarity solution and asymptotic analysis of a multi-phase Stefan problem with a convective boundary condition at the fixed face
Abstract: In a one-dimensional multi-phase Stefan problem occurring within a semi-infinite, homogeneous material, a convective (Robin-type) boundary condition is applied at the fixed boundary x=0. The evolution of the problem is governed by heat diffusion equations that are connected through Stefan conditions at the free boundaries, describing a phase-change process involving n distinct phases separated by moving boundaries. Under appropriate assumptions about the physical parameters and the heat transfer coefficient the existence and uniqueness of a similarity-type solution are established. The locations of the free boundaries and the temperature profiles in each phase are explicitly identified. It is shown that the nonlinear system of equations used to determine the free boundary coefficients has a unique solution. Additionally, the asymptotic behavior as the heat transfer coefficient approaches infinity is analyzed. The similarity-type solution of this Stefan problem with a convective boundary condition approaches the similarity-type solution of the multi-phase Stefan problem with a fixed-temperature boundary condition in this limit. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Feng X.; Wang Y.; Wu X.; Hu X.; Ren T.
Title: Structural-function relationship of β-cyclodextrin derivatives in regulating encapsulation and humidity-triggered release of essential oils
Abstract: Understanding how cyclodextrin cavity microenvironment and key physicochemical properties of guest molecules govern the encapsulation and release behaviors of essential oils is critical for designing efficient delivery systems, yet the relevant mechanisms remain unclear. In this work, we systematically investigated this structure-function relationship using three β-cyclodextrin variants (native, methyl-β-cyclodextrin and hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin) and four representative essential oil molecules (cinnamaldehyde, carvacrol, eugenol and terpinyl acetate). We find that the relative contributions of guest hydrophobicity and molecular size to encapsulation efficiency are not intrinsic, but are dictated by the substituents on the cyclodextrin rim. Multiscale characterizations including XRD, FTIR and 1H NMR verified stable 1:1 inclusion complexes across all systems. Release kinetics exhibited a pronounced humidity-triggered pattern, governed by a balance between cyclodextrin hydrophilicity and crystallinity that linked water-mediated cavity hydration and diffusional resistance. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that hydrophobic interactions dominate host–guest binding, while substitution enhances cavity flexibility and alters guest embedding depth, thereby modulating the encapsulation and release of essential oils. This work establishes a structure, microenvironment and release framework for cyclodextrin-based delivery systems, providing mechanistic insights for rational design of controlled release carriers in food preservation applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Effects of salt ion identity and concentration on the acid-heat-induced aggregation behavior of lysozyme and the stability of the resulting emulsions
Abstract: The formation, structure, and functional properties of protein aggregates are highly sensitive to the ionic environment. In this study, lysozyme was heated at pH 2.0 and 90 °C in the presence of varying concentrations of Na+, K+, Ca2+, and Mg2+ to investigate how ion identity and concentration affect its aggregation characteristics and emulsion-stabilizing performance. Salt addition markedly altered the temporal evolution of lysozyme aggregation and the structures of the resulting aggregates, with the extent of these effects depending on both ion identity and concentration. Compared with monovalent ions, divalent ions more strongly promoted the formation of β-sheet-rich structures and the assembly of lysozyme aggregates. Ca2+ primarily accelerated fibril accumulation during the intermediate stage of heating and promoted fibril bundling at later stages, whereas Mg2+ favored the early formation of β-sheet-rich structures and subsequent aggregate growth. Moreover, emulsions stabilized by aggregates obtained after 72 h at the highest Mg2+ concentration exhibited the greatest storage stability. These findings clarify how ion identity and concentration modulate lysozyme aggregate structure and emulsion performance, providing a theoretical basis for regulating lysozyme aggregation using common salts and broadening its potential applications in food emulsion systems. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Plant protein flour microgels: new generation Pickering stabilisers for oil-in-water emulsions
Abstract: We present a novel plant-based particle i.e. lentil flour-based microgels (LFBMs) to serve as effective Pickering stabilisers for oil-in-water emulsions. The LFBMs were successfully synthesised using a top-down approach, employing a thermal treatment to form an initial flour-based gel, that was broken down to microscopic gel particles using high pressure homogenisation. Investigation via confocal laser scanning microscopy confirmed the formation of microgel-laden films at the droplet surface, protecting the droplets from coalescence. Cryogenic scanning electron microscopy was also performed using high pressure freezing (HPF) and plasma focused ion beam (pFIB) milling techniques, this being the first instance that HPF has been used to image microgel-stabilised emulsions. These images confirmed the attachment of LFBM particles to the droplet surfaces, substantiating that the LFBMs stabilise the emulsions via a Pickering-type mechanism. Title: TIMOSHENKO-VOLTERRA SYSTEMS WITH WEAK EXPONENTIAL KERNELS

Abstract: The existence, uniqueness and exponential stability of solutions to a fully dissipative Timoshenko-Volterra system with weak memory kernels are investigated. Title: Multimodal enhancement and multiscale sparse fusion framework for congenital heart disease detection
Abstract: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is one of the most common congenital structural abnormalities in children, and early detection is important for improving patient prognosis. Phonocardiogram (PCG) signals and echocardiographic images provide complementary hemodynamic and anatomical information, respectively. However, most automated CHD methods rely on a single modality, and the joint use of these modalities remains limited. In addition, PCG signals are susceptible to environmental and device noise. Pediatric CHD can involve small structural defects that are difficult to identify in echocardiographic images, and echocardiographic analysis requires both global cardiac structure and local structural details. During cross-level feature fusion, standard cross-attention may also introduce responses from irrelevant regions. In this study, we propose the Multimodal Enhancement and Fusion Network for Congenital Heart Disease (MEF-CHDNet), which takes both PCG signals and echocardiographic images as inputs. The proposed framework is designed for supporting computer-aided diagnosis of CHD when both modalities are available. A Convex-constrained Channel Enhancement (CCE) module adaptively reweights feature channels under a convex constraint to improve PCG feature representation. We also design a Multi-Scale Convolutional Sparse Cross-Attention (MSCSC) module. It combines multiscale convolutions with dual-branch Top-K sparse cross-attention to integrate multilevel and multiscale structural information while reducing the influence of irrelevant information during cross-level feature fusion. We evaluate MEF-CHDNet on a multimodal pediatric dataset from Sichuan Provincial Maternity and Child Health Care Hospital using stratified five-fold cross-validation. Title: Differential hemivariational inequalities with fractional-order derivatives and applications to contact problems
Abstract: This paper investigates the existence results for a hybrid system that couples a differential evolution inclusion with a fractional hemivariational inequality. Within the study, by employing a variable substitution technique applied to the fractional derivative, the original problem is reformulated into an equivalent system. Building upon this reformulation, the mild solution of the transformed form is subsequently defined. The Rothe method is utilized to discretize this problem and construct a corresponding iterative system, and the results for the discrete approximate problem are established. Title: An adaptive algorithm for complete quenching phenomenon of semilinear diffusion equations over nonuniform grids
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: This paper presents a novel study that investigates complete quenching phenomena in a two-dimensional (2D) semilinear diffusion equation, which arises in the context of catalytic and enzymatic reactions. A numerical scheme that utilizes a nonuniform spatial discretization is employed to effectively resolve the steep gradients encountered at the time of quenching. Further, an adaptive time mesh is implemented to optimize time-step and accurately measure both single-point and complete quenching across the entire domain. The stability of the numerical scheme is analyzed under specific constraints on the time step. Simulations are conducted numerically for both 1D and 2D problems to investigate critical domain sizes. The time of single-point quenching and complete quenching is compared and analyzed to understand their relationship with initial conditions, as well as the dynamics of parameter control related to the source term. Finally, the numerical results are validated by comparing the computed outcomes of quenching with existing findings in the literature. Title: A WEIGHTED NONLINEAR DIFFUSION EQUATION-BASED MODEL FOR MULTI-FEATURE IMAGE DENOISING

By using a weight function to combine integer-order and fractional-order derivative operators, the proposed model adaptively controls the diffusion type according to the regional features of the image. We also analyze the theoretical and numerical properties of the proposed model. Title: Thermal destabilization mechanisms of multi-component egg white protein blends: Selectively deficient aggregation behavior and analysis of gelation differences

Title: Meta-operation-assisted optimization for execution-parameterized robotic disassembly sequence planning
Abstract: Existing robotic disassembly sequence planning (RDSP) studies mainly optimize operation ordering under precedence constraints, whereas robot configurations and local operation parameters are typically treated separately or represented by fixed or simplified operation costs. To bridge this gap, this paper formulates an execution-parameterized robotic disassembly sequence planning (EP-RDSP) problem that jointly considers disassembly sequencing, robot configuration selection, and disassembly operation parameter optimization. In contrast to task-level RDSP, EP-RDSP evaluates a plan through the coupled effects of its operation sequence, selected inverse kinematics (IK) configurations, joint-space transitions, and local operation parameters. EP-RDSP contains heterogeneous and tightly coupled decisions, making direct optimization of the full mixed decision space computationally challenging. To address this challenge, a meta-operation-assisted (MOA) optimization framework is proposed to support multiobjective evolutionary algorithm (MOEA)-based search. The framework exploits meta-operation knowledge for operation-parameter generation before online optimization, allowing MOEA to focus on globally coupled planning decisions such as operation ordering, IK candidate selection, and joint-configuration and speed-ratio decisions. Experiments on 15 generated problem instances show that, across the four underlying optimizers and three instance scales, the MOA variants reduce the mean online runtime required to reach the target hypervolume (HV) by 16.45%–83.01%. Title: Selective photocatalytic reduction of 4-nitrophenol to 4-aminophenol over Ru-modified TiO₂: Effect of Ru loading and operating conditions

Abstract: Ru-modified TiO₂ photocatalysts with different Ru loadings (0.05, 0.1, and 0.2 mol%) were synthesized and investigated for the selective photocatalytic reduction of 4-nitrophenol (4-NP) to 4-aminophenol (4-AP) under UV irradiation. The 0.05 mol% Ru–TiO₂ sample exhibited the highest photocurrent response and the fastest 4-NP conversion kinetics, whereas the 0.1 mol% Ru–TiO₂ photocatalyst showed the highest selectivity toward 4-AP. The latter also exhibited the highest specific surface area (160 m2 g−1), the smallest crystallite size, enhanced surface hydroxylation, and the lowest band-gap energy. Title: Noise-resilient meta-learning on the Grassmann manifold for few-shot fault diagnosis of industrial robots

Thus, they are highly vulnerable to noisy perturbations, resulting in suboptimal discriminative power and unstable prototype estimation. To address these challenges, we propose a noise-resilient meta-learning (NRML) framework on the Grassmann manifold. Specifically, a noise-aware damped distance (NADD) is developed to provide a robust similarity measure under varying noise levels. Furthermore, an energy-thresholded subspace prototype (ETSP) is designed for adaptive and compact class representation on this manifold under extremely limited and noisy support samples. Comprehensive experiments on a public bearing dataset and a homemade industrial robot dataset demonstrate that NRML consistently outperforms multiple classical and state-of-the-art few-shot diagnosis methods. Title: A SIMPLE RANGE CHARACTERIZATION FOR SPHERICAL MEAN TRANSFORM IN ODD DIMENSIONS AND ITS APPLICATIONS

Title: CONSTRUCTION AND DECODING OF CONVOLUTIONAL CODES WITH OPTIMAL COLUMN DISTANCES

Title: Novel classification framework for stroke analysis using FBSE-EWT decomposition from EEG signals
Abstract: This paper presents a novel classification framework for stroke analysis that utilizes electroencephalogram (EEG) signal decomposition using a Fourier–Bessel series expansion and empirical wavelet transform (FBSE-EWT) method. Title: Modulating the microstructure and rheological properties of low-fat cheese: Combined effects of emulsion gel formulation, phase state, and coagulation mechanism

In contrast, W/O emulsion gels reconstituted into complex W/O/W double emulsions within the cheese milk, forming a multi-compartmentalized physical barrier that achieved the protection of the active ingredients. Title: A fully discrete nonlinear method for approximating spatially fractional-order quenching-combustion equations

Title: Weakly-C1 solutions to the biharmonic problem on multi-patch domains

Abstract: Solving fourth-order problems typically requires C1-smooth splines. While straightforward on cuboidal patches, constructing these spaces on complex multi-patch geometries is challenging, often leading to complex and restrictive implementations, limitations on spline degrees, or reliance on constrained non-conforming approaches. Title: A sequence-to-sequence U-Net based network for annotating overnight polysomnography
Abstract: Sleep is essential for maintaining both mental and physical health. Title: User-friendly spreadsheet for implementing international guidance on the evaluation of measurement uncertainty
Abstract: The objective interpretation of quantitative chemical parameters determined in an analysed item or sample requires probabilistic modelling of how close the measured value is to the “true” value of the quantity. Recently, a new Eurachem/CITAC guide on the evaluation of measurement uncertainty has described how data collected during in-house method validation, namely precision and recovery data, can be used to accurately assess the impact of all relevant effects on the measurements. The guide covers how to model the variation of measurement uncertainty with the measured value and how to handle inconsistencies in recovery observed in the analysis of various reference materials. The guide presents a comprehensive framework for evaluating the uncertainty of measurements in chemistry, in which tools for optimising the measurement can be used to meet the most demanding requirements for accuracy and uncertainty. To promote the dissemination and easy application of this relevant guidance, a user-friendly MS Excel spreadsheet is provided. Application examples of the spreadsheet for different types of tests in chemistry, namely the determination of soil pH and fluoranthene in river sediments, are presented. Title: INVERSE SOURCE PROBLEMS WITH REDUCED INTERIOR DATA FOR A COUPLED REACTION-DIFFUSION SYSTEM

Title: Synergistic biofabrication of structured dual microbial protein meat analogs via integration of yeast protein 3D printing and controlled mycelial growth

Title: WELL-POSEDNESS ANALYSIS OF A UNILATERAL CONTACT PROBLEM
Source title: Communications on Pure and Applied Analysis
Abstract: We consider a mathematical model that describes the equilibrium of a nonlinear elastic membrane which can come into contact with a rigid obstacle, the so-called foundation. We use a Weierstrass-type minimization argument to prove the unique weak solvability of the model. Then we turn to the well-posedness analysis of the problem, which represents the main novelty of this manuscript. Thus, we introduce three well-posedness concepts, compare them, and state and prove strong and weak well-posedness results. We also discuss the problem of finding an optimal well-posedness concept. Title: Mycelium morphology modulates the structural and functional properties of Hericium erinaceus–soy protein composite gels: From continuous reinforcement to phase separation
Abstract: Controlling mycelial morphology is critical for tailoring the structure and functionality of fungal–protein composite gels. Title: A COMMUTATIVE GROUP ACTION-BASED FRAMEWORK FOR ASYMMETRIC ANAMORPHIC ENCRYPTION
Abstract: Anamorphic encryption is a cryptographic paradigm that allows covert messages to be hidden inside ordinary ciphertexts of a public-key encryption scheme. Even if an adversary coerces the receiver into revealing the secret-key, the hidden communication remains undetectable without the double-key. The resulting scheme is secure in the standard model. Our construction combines a hybrid encryption scheme, built under the GA-DDH assumption and entropy smoothing of hash functions, with a second independent group-action instance that carries the covert message. The resulting scheme satisfies anamorphic security, sender indistinguishability under chosen-plaintext attack security and colluder indistinguishability under chosen-plaintext attack security. Authors: Wang D.; Jiao X.; Gou W.; Zhang S.; Huang J.; Kang Y.; Dong R.; Yu H.; Wu H.
Title: Distinct proteomic responses of Zygosaccharomyces rouxii to functional protein and palmitoleic acid supplementation under salt stress
Abstract: Zygosaccharomyces rouxii is a salt-tolerant yeast found in high-salt fermented foods; nevertheless, the proteome changes caused by dietary treatments are poorly characterized. This study investigated the proteome responses of Z. rouxii supplemented with functional protein or palmitoleic acid (FA C16:1) to 120 g/L NaCl stress. Proteomic analysis revealed 155 differently expressed proteins in the functional protein versus FA C16:1 comparison, including 30 proteins with increased abundance and 125 with decreased abundance. Functional enrichment analysis indicated variations in oxidative phosphorylation, ribosome-related processes, lipid metabolism, proteasome activity, peroxisomal functions, and cellular maintenance pathways. Protein-protein interaction and gene set enrichment analyses revealed distinct patterns of pathway representation in the two treatments. Overall, functional protein supplementation showed a greater representation of proteolytic and peroxisomal pathways, whereas FA C16:1 supplementation was more strongly associated with mitochondrial, translational, and lipid-related activities. These results provide a comparative proteomic view of the distinct cellular processes associated with the two supplementation conditions under high-salt stress. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Liu F.; Ren J.; Chen X.-L.; Lei Y.-T.; Cui H.-L.; Yang H.; Wang J.-J.
Title: Modulating excited-state dynamics in RhB@Cd-MOF composites: spectroscopic elucidation of PET-driven quenching and ACQ- suppressed radiative enhancement for differential fluorescence sensing
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Tuning host–guest interactions in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) provides a powerful strategy for regulating the photophysical pathways of encapsulated chromophores. Herein, a dual- emissive composite (RhB@ 1 ) was constructed by encapsulating rhodamine B (RhB) within a Cd-MOF ( 1 ). Under 350 nm excitation, RhB@ 1 exhibits two well-resolved emission bands at 433 nm (MOF host) and 585 nm (RhB guest) via efficient host-to-guest energy transfer, enabling a rare differential fluorescence behavior: a selective “turn-off” response to Fe3+ and a distinctive “turn-on” response to o-nitrobenzaldehyde (o-NBA). Time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy reveals that the fluorescence lifetime decreases from 2.22 ns to 1.68 ns upon Fe3+ addition, confirming dynamic quenching through a photoinduced electron transfer (PET) pathway, while Stern-Volmer analysis further supports this mechanism. In stark contrast, the turn-on effect for o- NBA is attributed to the suppression of aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) via supramolecular rigidification of RhB molecules, which restricts intramolecular rotation and enhances radiative decay. The composite also demonstrates outstanding photostability and recyclability, benefiting from efficient host-to-guest energy transfer. The practicality of the method was verified by visual detection of Fe3+ using test strips, Fe3+ recovery by standard addition in Yanhe River water, and o-NBA recovery by standard addition in tap water. Overall, this work not only provides a dual-responsive sensing platform but also offers direct spectroscopic evidence for how MOF nanoconfinement dictates the excited-state dynamics of guest dyes. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Wu Q.; Deng M.; Li F.; Qin S.
Title: Benzophenone Schiff base photoinitiators for efficient radical polymerization under visible LED irradiation up to 470 nm
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: This study describes the benzophenone Schiff base as visible photoinitiators for free radical polymerization and as photosensitizers for bis(4- tert -butylphenyl)iodonium salt. Two derivatives, BPN and BPN1, were synthesized and characterized. The photopolymerization kinetics of various acrylate monomers were monitored by real-time FTIR upon LED irradiation in the 385–470 nm range. The radical photochemistry mechanisms were investigated using fluorescence quenching, photolysis, cyclic voltammetry, and electron spin resonance experiments. Additionally, density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) calculations were performed to gain insight into the photophysical and photochemical processes. The results indicated that excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT) reaction occurs in the BPN system upon irradiation. The ESIPT process may accelerate the generation of initial radicals, which accounts for the nearly negligible induction period observed in the BPN system. Independently, the photolysis products act as electron donors and form charge transfer complexes (CTCs) with the iodonium salt as the electron acceptor. These CTCs exhibit a reduced HOMO-LUMO gap and enable efficient photoinitiation even under LED@470 nm irradiation. These findings provide a rational design for novel salicylaldehyde Schiff base-based visible photoinitiating systems. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Duan W.; Xie Y.; Ding K.; Tang Q.; Xu S.; Zhang Y.; Qiao X.; Jiang N.; Shan Y.; Ding S.
Title: Starvation trap strategy: An amylase-responsive potato starch-based Pickering emulsion for inhibiting foodborne microorganisms and preserving starchy foods
Abstract: Inspired by microbial carbon-source uptake, we developed polysaccharide-based intelligent responsive cinnamaldehyde (CIN) nanoemulsions (NEs) stabilized by the metal–phenolic network (MPN)-modified potato starch particles (PSEF). This system achieved amylase-responsive CIN release and inhibition of Bacillus cereus in starchy foods, while continuously releasing CIN to control other foodborne microorganisms. The results confirmed that the prepared 5% CIN NEs showed high encapsulation efficiency (98.66%), sustained release, and reliable biosafety (relative hemolysis rate <5%), effectively inhibiting Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, Listeria monocytogenes, Bacillus cereus, Burkholderia gladioli, and Aspergillus niger. Co-incubation with Bacillus cereus further supported the amylase-responsive release behavior of the system. Finally, the 5% CIN NE coating extended the shelf life of fresh-cut kiwifruit, lotus root, and rice noodles by 1.5–2.0-fold, showing better preservation performance than the commercial preservative ε-polylysine hydrochloride (ε-PLH). This safe and intelligent responsive coating may provide a sustainable solution for extending the shelf life of starchy foods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Torokhti A.; Howlett P.; Pudney P.
Author full names: Torokhti, Anatoli (35617274900); Howlett, Phil (7004973130); Pudney, Peter (6602936109)
Title: On a performance improvement of distributed data processing
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: Distributed filters/systems enable to process data across multiple sensors to provide an efficient estimation of source data x. Recently, several computational techniques for the distributed data processing (DDP) have been proposed and applied to various practical tasks. Inspired by these, this paper provides a further insight into the numerical estimation of distributed random data. The method we develop combines models of noisy data recognizers, preconditioning filters, and optimal sensors that are ingredients of each channel of the proposed DDP filter. The recognizer transmits observed data for the further estimation or blocks the observed data if noise is less or overcomes, respectively, a prescribed level. The preconditioning filter reduces noise that corrupts the observed data. The optimal sensors process outputs of the preconditioning filters to reconstruct x from observed data with a minimal associated error. The described procedure is formalized as an optimization problem for a numerical determination of the optimal sensors. The provided direct solution allow us to achieve fault and heavy noise tolerance, and process large amount of data fast. Numerical examples show the effectiveness of the proposed method. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Explicit construction of spherical 5- and 7-designs
Source title: Journal of Combinatorial Theory. Series A
Abstract: This paper develops an explicit and implementable framework for constructing spherical designs by lifting point sets from tight fusion frames. By combining existing ingredients, we obtain, in every dimension, explicit spherical 5-designs with |X|=O(d3). As a core component of the method, we give an explicit construction of simplex 3-designs realized as orbits of the symmetric group. Title: On k-arc-transitive inner-automorphic Cayley graphs
Source title: Journal of Combinatorial Theory. Series A
Abstract: A Cayley graph Cay(G,S) of a group G is called inner-automorphic if S is a union of conjugacy classes of G. In this paper, we prove that a connected inner-automorphic Cayley graph is 3-arc-transitive if and only if it is isomorphic to a cycle or a balanced complete bipartite graph, thereby answering a 2020 question of Pan. We also classify 2-arc-transitive inner-automorphic Cayley graphs of diameter at most 2. In addition, we construct an infinite family of 2-arc-transitive inner-automorphic Cayley graphs of diameter 4 and valency p2 of nonabelian groups having order 2p3, where p is an odd prime. Furthermore, we investigate 2-distance-transitive inner-automorphic Cayley graphs of nonabelian simple groups, and show that no such graphs exist for alternating groups, sporadic simple groups, or projective special linear groups. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Arós Á.; Fernandes C.
Title: Numerical analysis of elastic elliptic membrane shells in frictional contact with wear
Abstract: We consider a family of linearly elastic and elliptic membrane shells, all sharing the same middle surface, with thickness 2ε, clamped along their entire lateral face, which upon deformation may enter in frictional contact with a moving foundation along its lower face. As a result of friction, material might be removed from the interface, thus causing wear. In this paper, we focus in the numerical analysis of our model and provide a priori error estimates for displacements, stress and wear fields. We have implemented the fully discrete scheme with the FreeFEM++ programming environment, by using an intrinsic (basis free) formulation, reduction of order, penalization and Newton method. We carried on a series of numerical simulations to demonstrate the capabilities of our code, providing experimental evidence of our theoretical results regarding the convergence with respect to the thickness parameter ε and mesh size h . As a practical application, we have also included the results of a simulation of the wear that undergoes the tyre of a vehicle braking on a road. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Geometric digital twin for additive manufacturing (gDT-AM): In-process part surface reconstruction and shape monitoring
Abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) faces critical challenges, particularly in achieving real-time quality control and precision. These challenges are heightened in complex geometries and high-deposition-rate robotic AM (HDR-RAM) processes such as robotic cold spray. Traditional quality control methods generally detect defects after the entire part is produced, leading to material waste and increased lead time and cost. The lack of real-time insight during production limits the ability to identify and correct the process variations as they occur. To address this, digital twin technology has emerged as a powerful tool within the intelligent manufacturing paradigm. This study proposes a novel geometric digital twin (gDT) framework, gDT-AM, specifically designed for HDR-RAM. It continuously captures and maps the part’s geometry in real-time during printing. It incorporates two experimentally validated alternative methods for precise, fast surface reconstruction from sparse spatio-temporal 2D laser profiler scans. This supports the monitoring of geometric anomalies during deposition by providing timely, actionable information for intervention to reduce material waste and process inconsistency. The proposed framework provides a basis for online process-parameter optimization and toolpath correction. Ultimately, integration of the digital twin aligns with the principles of intelligent manufacturing through connectivity, automation, data-driven decision-making, and adaptive process control. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Wang Y.; Zhang J.; Wang Z.; Peng Z.; Xu X.; Zhao L.
Title: Learning vascular continuity for faithful liver vessel segmentation
Abstract: Spatial continuity is the primary characteristic of liver vessels, which can be helpful in bridging gaps between vessel segments and locating very thin vessels in liver scans. As liver images are typically acquired in the transverse plane, vessels appear as a mixture of blob-like and tube-like structures, making their continuity difficult to preserve. We therefore employ recurrent modeling to infer vessel continuity from the three orthogonal anatomical views, enabling long-range directional information propagation within each view. The inferred continuity is used in two-fold: (1) shaping feature learning on vessel-like regions and (2) balancing the skewed distribution of vessels against others. Comprehensive experiments on three well-established datasets, namely 3D-IRCADb, MSD, and LiVS, show that the proposed model achieves relative improvements of up to 4.02% in Dice and 3.27% in centerline Dice over the corresponding second-best methods. Furthermore, our method improves the recovery and continuity preservation of ambiguous and fragmented vessels, providing a computationally efficient solution for liver vessel segmentation. © 2026

Authors: He D.; Liu Z.; Yin X.; Zhang C.; Shi Y.; Liu H.; Gao W.; Fu Y.
Title: SRTD-Net: Decoupling Spatial Reliability from Temporal Dynamics for endoscopic video segmentation under instrument–tissue interactions
Abstract: Real-time segmentation of surgical instruments and anomalies in endoscopic videos is essential for image-guided surgery, yet remains challenging due to high temporal heterogeneity, frequent occlusions, and complex non-linear instrument–tissue interactions that often lead to temporal inconsistency and visual ambiguity. We present SRTD-Net, a Spatial Reliability and Temporal Dynamics Network that explicitly targets spatiotemporal reliability via a dual-stream design that decouples feature refinement from interaction modeling. The Spatial Reliability Stream performs diffusion-inspired feature refinement using an Energy-Calibrated Wavelet Decomposer and a Diffusion Feature Refinement module, suppressing dynamic noise and restoring corrupted representations. In parallel, the Temporal Modeling Stream integrates Dynamic Kernel Attention to retrieve historical context under occlusion and an Interaction-Gated Temporal Dynamics unit to capture non-linear scene evolution while promoting temporal consistency across frames. To facilitate systematic evaluation under challenging interactions, we further introduce the EndoPolyp-Instrument Dataset (EPID), curated with diverse instrument–tissue and instrument–anomaly interaction scenarios. Extensive experiments on three benchmarks demonstrate that SRTD-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance and shows improved robustness in zero-shot generalization. Code and dataset are available at https://github.com/hedongdong6060/SRTD-Net. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Iqbal A.; Asghar S.
Title: An ultrasound spectrum-to-graph (US2G) framework with multi-feature graph attention networks for automated lesion classification in B-mode ultrasound imaging
Abstract: Automated classification of lesions in B-mode ultrasound images remains challenging due to speckle noise, irregular lesion boundaries, and variable echo intensity distributions. Existing convolutional neural networks (CNNs), Vision Transformers (ViTs), and ultrasound foundation models share a critical limitation: all represent regions of interest (ROIs) as regular pixel grids, failing to exploit the irregular spatial topology of acoustic energy diffusion patterns that encode diagnostically relevant tissue microstructure. We propose US2G, a three-stage spectrum-to-graph framework that (i) extracts an adaptive Acoustic Energy Diffusion Region (AEDR) via multi-level Otsu thresholding, without manual annotation; (ii) constructs a multi-feature weighted graph with six heterogeneous node features and a composite three-term edge similarity function combining intensity affinity, spatial proximity, and textural coherence; and (iii) classifies variable-topology graphs using edge-conditioned multi-head GATv2 with differentiable hierarchical pooling. Experiments on the BUSI (breast), DDTI (thyroid), and CAMUS (cardiac) datasets yield classification accuracies of 91.47%, 93.82%, and 89.63%, respectively, corresponding to absolute gains of 5.60, 8.82, and 6.13 percentage points over the strongest CNN baseline and 3.97, 5.49, and 3.88 points over a GCN operating on an identical graph. The proposed US2G achieves this with 48.7 K parameters and 6 ms per-ROI inference, more than two orders of magnitude below the parameter count of contemporary ultrasound foundation models. Attention visualisations align with radiologist-interpretable sonographic features, supporting clinical interpretability. We also explicitly delineate the assumptions and applicability constraints of the framework, including its dependence on ROI quality, its single-frame scope, and the limited scale of the benchmarks currently available. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Author full names: Lim, Ming Y. (57409137300); Xu, Yuan (56399566100); Shewan, Heather M. (55817201300); Stokes, Jason R (7202786124)
Title: Influence of structure and non-Newtonian rheology on the lubrication of emulsion gels in soft contacts
Abstract: The microstructural complexity and rheology of emulsion gels significantly influences their lubrication behaviour in soft contact tribology, resulting in experimental observations that are difficult to interpret. To investigate this, model emulsion gels (acidified milk gels) were prepared with systematic variations in protein to fat ratio, total solid content, and fat particle size. The lubrication of these multiphasic gels with semi-solid rheology deviates notably from the typical Stribeck “master curve” by showing the existence of a secondary transition in mixed lubrication (ML) regime. This behaviour generally occurs for shear-thinning lubricants, and we show how this secondary transition in ML relates to the presence of a yield stress, which relates to the strength and integrity of gels’ microstructure and the fat content. This distinct tribological behaviour of emulsion gels diminishes as the system enters the elasto-hydrodynamic lubrication (EHL) regime due to the enlarged interfacial separation so that the response depends on high-shear viscosity. For systems where there is a significant amount of free fat (i.e. the fat is not strongly associated with the protein network), local phase separation can occur whereby the fat phase dominates tribological response at low entrainment speeds (narrow gaps). By systematically decoupling the effects of composition, rheology, and microstructural integrity within a common emulsion-gel platform, this study establishes a mechanistic framework for interpreting the lubrication behaviour of complex multiphasic food gels. The findings demonstrate how structural evolution during oral processing influences tribological response in complex foods. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. Title: Stability of the critical constant steady state of a Keller–Segel model
Abstract: In this paper, we prove the asymptotic stability of the critical constant steady state for a simplified parabolic–elliptic Keller–Segel system in RN ( N ≥ 3), which admits a one-parameter family of constant steady states. Although the stability threshold for constant steady states is known, the critical case has remained open. Title: Ni-Pi-Ni Based Asterisk Shaped Highly Efficient Solar Energy Harvester
Source title: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics
Abstract: This article presents an asterisk shaped ultra-wideband absorber designed with nickel (Ni) as conducting layers and polyimide substrate to form a three-layered structure. Symmetricity of asterisk’s geometry leads to polarization insensitivity while having Aavg > 90% for 0°≤incident angle(θ) ≤ 60°. Title: Impact of gamma irradiation as a non-thermal technology on the structural, digestive, and rheological properties of rice bean (Vigna umbellata) protein isolate and its application in the development of 3D printable food ink
Abstract: This study aimed to analyze the effect of gamma modification on the functional properties of rice bean protein isolate (RBPI) at doses of 3, 5, and 10 kGy. Both native and gamma-irradiated RBPI were characterized through structural, molecular, functional, rheological, and digestive analyses to evaluate the influence of different irradiation doses and identify a suitable dose for 3D food ink formulation. Gamma irradiation induced dose-dependent structural modifications, as evidenced by FTIR and UV–visible spectroscopy, particle size analysis, SDS–PAGE, and SEM, suggesting irradiation-induced structural modifications, alteration in particle organization, and microstructural changes without evidence of extensive protein degradation under the studied conditions. These structural modifications significantly (p < 0.05) improved solubility and water-binding capacity, particularly at moderate irradiation doses (3-5 kGy), whereas the highest in vitro protein digestibility was observed at 10 kGy. Rheological evaluation revealed enhanced shear-thinning behaviour, elastic dominance (G′ > G″), and improved viscoelastic stability in gamma-irradiated RBPI, reflecting stronger protein–protein interaction networks. Based on its favourable functional and rheological characteristics relevant to 3D printing, the modified RBPI was further applied to develop a fruit-based 3D-printable ink formulated with agar and guar gum. The rheological behaviour of native and gamma-irradiated RBPI-based inks was characterized, revealing enhanced shear-thinning, elastic dominance, and viscoelastic stability, which are considered favourable for extrusion-based 3D food printing. Textural analysis further indicated higher mechanical strength, cohesiveness, and structural integrity of the gamma-irradiated RBPI food ink, suggesting its potential as a component of a composite formulation for extrusion-based 3D food printing. Representative self-supporting printed structures were obtained under the selected printing conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Asymmetric discrete-time Hopfield neural networks: Orientation selectivity
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: This paper introduces and formalizes the concept of orientation selectivity in asymmetric discrete-time Hopfield neural networks (ADHNNs). It demonstrates that networks with asymmetric synaptic weight matrices exhibit fundamentally different dynamic behaviors depending on whether the network states are interpreted as row or column vectors, leading to distinct left-side and right-side dynamics. The paper provides a comprehensive analysis of ADHNN dynamics with rank-one asymmetric weight matrices and introduces a novel recording rule based on convex optimization for programming ADHNNs for associative memory tasks. Computational experiments show that ADHNNs programmed with this new method exhibit superior noise tolerance and memory capacity compared with symmetric Hopfield networks with the pseudo-inverse rule, particularly when storing large numbers of patterns. These findings align with recent advances in modern Hopfield networks and dense associative memories, suggesting that weight asymmetry is not only biologically plausible but also computationally advantageous for memory storage and retrieval applications. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Jena U.; Barman M.; Pradhan A.; Khuntia P.
Title: Topological spin freezing in frustrated quantum materials
Abstract: Competing interactions, non-trivial electronic band topology, quantum fluctuations, and the interplay between emergent degrees of freedom in frustrated quantum materials can lead to a myriad of exotic phenomena, potentials for addressing recurring themes in contemporary condensed matter, while offering immense promise for quantum technologies. Glassy dynamics, originally explored in amorphous materials and biological systems, has gained significant attention in quantum condensed matter physics, particularly in the context of collective behavior of electrons, slow spin dynamics, emergent low-energy excitations, and exotic topological or constraint-driven spin textures. Here, we provide a comprehensive overview of the manifestation of unconventional glassy spin dynamics in a broad class of frustrated magnets, where the underlying mechanisms of spin freezing exhibit distinct signatures in thermodynamic and microscopic experiments. We discuss the key experimental signatures of topological spin glass behavior in frustrated quantum materials through a comprehensive suite of experimental probes, including thermodynamic measurements, nuclear magnetic resonance, muon spin relaxation, and inelastic neutron scattering. These complementary techniques collectively reveal unconventional spin dynamics, short-range spin correlations, emergent low-energy excitations, and glassy behavior emerging from magnetic frustration, topological defects, and local constraints, thereby distinguishing the resulting topological spin freezing from conventional spin glasses and disordered magnets. Furthermore, we discuss the emergence of spin jam states and the role of topological and emergent constraints in stabilizing non-trivial spin freezing in frustrated magnets. Together, these insights provide a comprehensive framework for understanding unconventional spin freezing, slow spin dynamics, and exotic low-energy excitations in frustrated quantum materials, while bridging experimental observations with representative phenomenological frameworks. The current review aims to broaden our understanding of collective many-body phenomena stemming from competing interactions, topological degrees of freedom, collective excitations and their interactions, perturbations, and underlying symmetry in frustrated quantum materials. This may aid in the discovery, design, and investigation of novel quantum materials to address some of the fundamental questions in contemporary condensed matter, with potential significance for future quantum technologies. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Zhang Q.; Wang S.; Yang S.; Bai J.; Zhou X.; Xu Z.; Lan T.; Sui X.
Title: Yielding behavior and intracycle viscoelastic evolution of transglutaminase-induced soy protein isolate-sesbania gum gels revealed by nonlinear rheology
Abstract: Structured food systems, including plant-based and 3D-printed foods, often undergo large deformation during processing, making nonlinear rheology important for controlling shape stability and deformation performance. Transglutaminase (TGase)-induced soy protein isolate (SPI) gels containing sesbania gum (SG; 0-0.50%, w/v) were prepared to determine the effects of SG on yielding behavior and intracycle viscoelastic evolution. Rheological tests, multi-criterion yield stress analysis, large amplitude oscillatory shear (LAOS) coupled with sequence of physical processes (SPP) analysis, compression tests, and SEM were integrated. SG increased the consistency coefficient from 25.37 to 95.94 Pa·sn and the apparent elastic modulus ((Formula presented) ) from 0.45 to 1.56 kPa, indicating enhanced flow resistance and initial compressive stiffness. Yield stress also increased across different criteria; for example, static ramp yield stress increased from 24.8 to 62.8 Pa and LAOS-derived elastic bifurcation stress from 12.2 to 48.8 Pa. Notably, SG-containing gels departed from the linear viscoelastic regime at lower strain amplitudes despite exhibiting higher yield-related stress thresholds, indicating an apparent distinction between strain sensitivity and yield resistance. They also showed reduced short-term recovery and stronger strain-dependent nonlinearity. LAOS-SPP analysis revealed a progressive intracycle pathway involving an initially elastic-dominated response, local viscoelastic transition, increased viscous dominance, and partial recovery. Overall, SG strengthened TGase-induced SPI gels but increased their strain sensitivity under large deformation. These findings provide a nonlinear rheological basis for designing plant protein-polysaccharide gels with controlled deformation behavior. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Hu X.
Title: Exponential decay estimates for the surface wave problem of micropolar fluids with surface tension
Abstract: We investigate a fully dissipative micropolar fluid in a finite-depth, horizontally periodic domain of two and three dimensions, featuring a free-moving boundary and a fixed solid boundary. The fluid dynamics are governed by gravity-driven incompressible micropolar equations, and the surface tension is considered on the free surface. The main result of this paper is to prove the global well-posedness of the surface wave problem when the surface tension is considered. Meanwhile, we prove that the solution decays to equilibrium at an exponential rate. This is achieved by taking advantage of the gain of regularity for the free interface caused by the existence of surface tension. Compared to the author’s previous results [1], we find that the surface tension of the micropolar fluid not only increases the regularity of the free interface but also increases the decay rate of the solution to the surface wave problem of micropolar equations. Meanwhile, the restriction of the viscosity required in [2] has been removed in this paper by using a good structure of the equation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Hui L.; Runxin G.; Lingyun S.; Xiaomei Z.; Bing S.
Title: Influences of dissolved organic matter and halide ions on the photodegradation of amitriptyline: Kinetics and characterization of transformation products
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Amitriptyline (AMT), a widely used tricyclic antidepressant, is frequently detected in both freshwater and marine environments, where its photochemical fate may differ. In this study, the photodegradation of AMT was investigated in reservoir water and seawater, and dissolved organic matter (DOM) and halide ions were identified as the key factors controlling its photolysis. The photodegradation behavior of AMT was systematically examined in the presence of humic acid (HA) and halide ions. HA promoted AMT photodegradation, and higher HA concentrations led to more pronounced enhancement. In halide-containing systems, both ionic strength and specific halide effects jointly influenced AMT photodegradation. When HA coexisted with halide ions, the excited triplet state of HA (3DOM) and the resulting reactive halogen species (RHS) were identified as the key drivers promoting AMT photodegradation. In freshwater, AMT was photodegraded mainly through ROS-mediated oxidation and hydroxylation, whereas in saline water it reacted with RHS to form a halogenated intermediate that was further oxidized and hydroxylated into low-toxicity final products. Overall, AMT photodegraded faster under saline than under freshwater conditions, and the toxicity of its major transformation products decreased accordingly. These findings improve our understanding of the photochemical fate of AMT in freshwater and saline waters and provide valuable insights for the ecological risk assessment of AMT and structurally analogous pollutants in estuarine and coastal systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Controlled Alcalase hydrolysis of mealworm protein: Structure-driven modulation of techno-functional and interfacial properties, emulsion stability, and digestibility
Abstract: Mealworm protein (MP) is a sustainable alternative protein source; however, its limited solubility and interfacial performance restrict its use in emulsion-based food systems. This study investigated the effects of Alcalase hydrolysis at different enzyme levels and hydrolysis times on the structural, techno-functional, emulsifying, and digestion properties of MP hydrolysates (MPHs). Alcalase hydrolysis reduced molecular size and altered protein conformation, as indicated by decreases in α-helix content and intrinsic fluorescence intensity. As enzyme level and hydrolysis time increased, the MPH samples exhibited improved solubility, wettability, and radical scavenging activity, along with reduced tropomyosin-related immunoreactivity. At the oil–water interface, hydrolysis accelerated initial adsorption but reduced the amount of protein retained and the dilatational modulus. In oil-in-water emulsions, all MPH samples formed smaller droplets than native MP. The hydrolysate prepared using 0.5% Alcalase for 15 min showed the smallest droplet size, a low Turbiscan stability index, and improved stability during storage and under environmental stress conditions. However, increasing the degree of hydrolysis did not proportionally improve emulsion stability or lipid digestion. More extensive hydrolysis increased protein digestibility, whereas emulsion stability and lipid digestion showed no further improvement. Multivariate analysis further showed that MPH functionality was associated with changes in structural, surface-related, emulsion, and digestion properties, rather than the degree of hydrolysis alone. These results indicate that appropriate control of enzyme level and hydrolysis time is required to obtain MPH samples with balanced solubility, interfacial functionality, emulsion stability, and digestion performance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Loveday S.M.; Homer S.; Fitzgerald A.; Logan A.
Author full names: Loveday, Simon M. (18437732200); Homer, Stephen (56121620600); Fitzgerald, Adam (57221925420); Logan, Amy (55829585900)
Title: Protein-fibre-water interactions in thermally-treated Lupin fractions
Abstract: The functionality of protein concentrates depends on structural and physicochemical interactions between protein and non-protein fractions. We examined the protein-fibre-water interactions in heated blends of lupin protein isolate and fibre-rich co-product, tailored to cover typical protein concentrations in protein concentrates: 84.2-29.1% protein and 1.3-60.9% w/w fibre (dry basis). Blends were hydrated at 10-15% solids and heated to 120 °C for 2.5 min in a rapid visco-analyser. Heated samples were examined with oscillatory and rotational rheometry, confocal microscopy, nuclear magnetic resonance relaxometry and dynamic water vapour sorption analysis. The fibre fraction had monolayer moisture content 10-14% higher than the isolate, and microscopy showed fibre particles expanding and solubilising as a result of the heat treatment. Rheometry revealed that fibre content dominated rheological properties. Isolate-only samples (8.4-12.6% protein) had viscosity <0.5 Pa s at 100 s−1, and viscosity increased uniformly as isolate was replaced with fibre fraction. Rheological properties appeared to be controlled by two structuring phenomena: solubilised fibre exerting a shear rate-dependent viscosifying effect on the aqueous phase, and lupin kernel tissue particles (up to 500 μm) jamming together to an extent that depended on phase volume. In high-solids samples water availability set the ceiling to the extent of solubilisation and particle swelling that could occur during RVA heating. Equivalent textures could be achieved with different compositions and microstructures, as shown by convergence of rheological parameters from 10, 12.5 and 15% solids samples. Process-mediated interactions between protein, fibre and water are the key to understanding and optimising protein concentrate functionality. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Yin L.; Song Y.; Chen S.; Hu S.; Dai M.; Zhang W.; Chen C.; Lin Y.; Yan T.; Wang P.; Sun Y.; Du Z.
Title: Comparative structuring of goat, yak, and camel casein isolates in moldable emulsions via calcium-mediated association, TGase crosslinking, and ultrasound-assisted emulsification
Abstract: Acid-isolated caseins from goat, yak, and camel milk were compared within a common processing framework to evaluate differences in the structuring of moldable oil-in-water emulsions among the three casein sources. Casein preparations were subjected to sequential calcium-mediated association and microbial transglutaminase (TGase) crosslinking, followed by ultrasound-assisted emulsification at an oil-to-aqueous-phase volume ratio of 2:1. Calcium source, Ca2+ concentration, TGase activity, redispersed casein concentration, sonication duration, and ultrasound set power were screened in independent one-factor series. Processing responses were generally nonlinear and differed markedly among the three casein sources. Within the tested formulation space, CaCl2 supplying 5 mmol/L Ca2+, 3% (w/v) redispersed treated casein, and an ultrasound set power of 2.0 kW provided the most consistent overall balance of oil incorporation, macroscopic homogeneity, physical stability, low apparent flowability, and moldability. The selected TGase activities were 4, 8, and 4 U/g casein for goat, yak, and camel caseins, respectively, with corresponding sonication durations of 15, 15, and 10 s. Maximum apparent viscosity did not consistently predict the selected formulation: low-shear viscosity reached approximately 240 Pa s for goat casein and approximately 300 Pa s for camel casein under intermediate treatment conditions, whereas higher treatment levels could markedly increase instability, with TSI values exceeding 20 in the camel system. Confocal microscopy further showed a comparatively fine and densely interspersed goat emulsion, large incompletely dispersed casein-rich aqueous domains in the shape-retaining yak emulsion, and a broader heterogeneous domain-size distribution in the camel emulsion. These findings demonstrate that macroscopic moldability can emerge through different multiscale structural pathways and does not necessarily imply microscopically uniform emulsification or elastic gel formation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Li B.; Ma Y.; Pang C.; Zhang R.; Lu R.; Lyu L.
Title: BMANet: Boundary-aware Multi-Scale Attention Network for medical image segmentation
Abstract: Medical image segmentation remains challenging across modalities because weak object boundaries, scale-varying anatomical structures, and heterogeneous appearances often degrade feature representation and prediction accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose BMANet, a Boundary-aware Multi-scale Attention Network for accurate and efficient medical image segmentation. BMANet is built upon a lightweight encoder–decoder architecture and consists of four complementary modules. First, the Multi-scale Contextual Aggregation Module (MCAM) combines pyramid dilated convolutions with a large-kernel branch to capture hierarchical contextual information while reducing spatial information loss caused by repeated down-sampling. Second, the Edge Contour Enhanced Attention Module (ECEA) integrates low-level edge cues with high-level semantic representations to enhance edge-sensitive feature learning. Third, the Adaptive Channel-aware Spatial Attention Module (ACSA) dynamically calibrates channel and spatial responses, improving feature discrimination under varying contrast and texture conditions. Finally, the Prior Multi-scale Feature Refinement Decoder (PMFR) employs reverse attention and progressive feature refinement to emphasize hard-to-segment regions and recover fine spatial details. Extensive experiments on seven publicly available datasets covering polyp, nuclei, skin lesion, and cell segmentation demonstrate that BMANet achieves competitive or superior performance compared with state-of-the-art methods while maintaining favorable computational efficiency. These results indicate that BMANet provides an effective and practical framework for robust medical image segmentation across diverse imaging scenarios. © 2026

Authors: Cheng X.; Hu T.; Xie Y.; Chen W.; Yuan Y.; Hu H.
Title: Soy protein isolate composite gels fabrication via short-term high-intensity ultrasound
Abstract: Dual-protein systems offer advantages for improving soy protein isolate (SPI) gelation. However, conventional gelation approaches still rely on complex procedures and prolonged heating, resulting in high energy consumption. Herein, short-time high-intensity ultrasound (HIU; 20 kHz, 400 W, 4-6 min) was used to directly fabricate SPI composite gel without additional heating, with ovalbumin (OVA), peanut protein isolate (PPI), and pea protein isolate (PAPI) serving as added proteins. The results indicated that SPI-OVA gel at a mass ratio of 2:4 exhibited the highest gel strength (183.02 g), the strongest viscoelasticity, and the greatest water immobilization (T22 = 54.789 ms), corresponding to a highly compact and dense network. Importantly, intermolecular force analysis revealed that OVA promoted the formation of a highly compact network dominated by hydrophobic interactions and disulfide bonds. The SPI-PPI composite gel network was mainly maintained by ionic bonds, while the dominant forces in the SPI-PAPI composite gel network shifted from ionic bonds to hydrophobic interactions and disulfide bonds as PAPI concentration increased. Furthermore, free sulfhydryl and surface hydrophobicity results indicated that HIU thermal effects facilitated protein unfolding and sulfhydryl exposure, while excessive hydrophobic aggregation in SPI-PPI and SPI-PAPI gels partially buried hydrophobic groups and weakened network formation. This study reveals mechanistic insights into HIU-induced fabrication of SPI composite gels and supports the rational design of high-performance dual-protein gel systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Hydrocolloid–polyphenol Co-assemblies for food structure design: Linking molecular binding, network mechanics, oxidative stability, and bioaccessibility
Abstract: Hydrocolloid–polyphenol co-assemblies are emerging as multifunctional food matrices that can integrate texture control, antioxidant protection, interfacial stabilization, active packaging, and bioactive delivery. Although polyphenols are commonly regarded as antioxidants, pigments, or nutraceutical compounds, their capacity to act as molecular regulators of hydrocolloid structure and performance remains less systematically addressed. This review evaluates hydrocolloid–polyphenol systems through a structure–function perspective, focusing on how protein and polysaccharide hydrocolloids interact with phenolic acids, flavonoids, anthocyanins, tannins, catechins, curcumin, resveratrol, and polyphenol-rich extracts. Particular emphasis is placed on how hydrocolloid molecular architecture, polyphenol structure and dose, pH, ionic strength, processing history, and interactions with coexisting matrix components influence whether reversible association or persistent covalent/oxidative coupling produces reinforcement, controlled release, or undesirable aggregation. The review further examines gelation, rheology, water mobility, interfacial behavior, oxidative stability, oral lubrication and astringency, edible films and coatings, and gastrointestinal release. Quantitative formulation windows are highlighted where primary studies provide them, while the limits of transferring simplified-model observations to real foods are considered explicitly. Applications are evaluated across dairy and plant-based systems, gels, beverages, emulsions, sauces, edible coatings, active packaging, and delivery platforms. The resulting framework emphasizes application-specific binding regimes, sensory-aware formulation, standardized characterization, and validation in compositionally realistic food matrices. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Liu T.; Zhang X.; Xu H.; Wu X.; Fan Y.; Jiang H.; Pan X.; Ma R.; Liu C.; Tian Y.
Title: The structure-function relationship of resistant starch from its molecular structure to gut microbiota interactions
Abstract: Resistant starch (RS) is the starch fraction that escapes hydrolysis in the small intestine within physiological transit time and is fermented by gut microbiota, with its health effects (e.g., blood glucose regulation, gut health improvement) fundamentally determined by the hierarchical structure of its subtypes. These subtypes (RS1-RS5) are characterised by distinct structural features. For example, RS1 relies on physical encapsulation, RS2 and RS3 depend on native or retrograded crystallinity, respectively, RS4 gains resistance through chemical modification, and RS5 arises from different V-type inclusion complexes formed with guest molecules such as lipids, aliphatic alcohols, and polyphenols. These features influence enzymatic resistance through molecular reorganisation or hydrophobic interactions. This structural diversity largely determines glucose-release patterns and substrate specificity for gut microbes. While previous studies have summarized RS types, modification methods, and functional properties, the comprehensive relationship between RS structure and nutritional outcomes remains incompletely understood. This review systematically explores the structure–function relationships of RS by examining methods for evaluating its structural properties, elucidating the interactions among RS, gut microbiota, and key digestive enzymes, and further discussing how food components, including proteins, lipids, and polyphenols, regulate starch digestibility through their interactions with RS. By integrating these perspectives, this review aims to provide a theoretical foundation for understanding the mechanisms underlying the health benefits of RS and to support its application in precision nutrition and functional food development. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Guo Y.; Tan C.S.
Title: Beyond passive mixing: Geometric evolution and multifunctional applications of staggered herringbone microfluidic devices
Abstract: Staggered herringbone microfluidic chips are widely used passive systems for enhancing transport and interaction under laminar flow conditions, and have been extensively applied in chemical synthesis, biosensing, and cell-related studies. The performance of these systems is fundamentally governed by their geometric design, which determines mixing efficiency, mass transfer, and flow-induced stimulation. Despite their widespread adoption, the design logic connecting geometric parameters, fabrication constraints, and functional applications has not been systematically clarified. In this review, we summarize and organize the key geometric features of herringbone microstructures and their influence on fluid behavior, fabrication feasibility, and application performance. Representative design strategies are discussed across different application scenarios, ranging from homogeneous reactions and nanoparticle synthesis to surface-interaction enhancement and cell functional regulation. By integrating design principles with practical implementation and application-driven requirements, this review aims to provide a critical overview of the design logic and application-dependent optimization strategies of staggered herringbone microfluidic chips. Passive microfluidics can be tuned for bioanalysis, cell manipulation, and material production. © 2026 Author(s).

Authors: Bohorquez P.
Title: Two-dimensional stability analysis and nonlinear simulation of roll waves in large-scale spillways: The case of Oroville dam
Abstract: Spillway flows are nonuniform and supercritical, which can cause surface instabilities called roll waves. This study analyzes the nonlinear development of real-scale roll waves on the Oroville Dam spillway and shows consistency with two-dimensional linear stability theory at Froude numbers of 4.3-11 and width-to-depth ratios of 60-500. The approach uses the depth-averaged two-dimensional Saint-Venant equations, which neglect vertical velocity, to describe the three-dimensional shape of the free surface. Linear stability analysis proves that higher-order transverse modes are as unstable as the standard one-dimensional mode, with nearly equal phase velocities and frequencies at a given wavenumber, thereby producing multiple trains of roll waves. Numerical simulations and the nature of convective instability show that the growth of specific modes depends on the inlet boundary conditions at the spillway chute’s flood-control section. Fully open-gate releases generate pier-induced standing crosswaves in the tailwater that are consistent with Ippen’s classical theory of supercritical flows, excite higher-order transverse modes, and develop roll waves even at discharges where one-dimensional models predict stability. In contrast, with the lateral gates closed, the supercritical abrupt expansion triggers macroscopic oblique shock waves that can delay or prevent roll waves by disrupting the balance between frictional and gravitational forces. The wavelengths and phase velocities of the numerically simulated roll waves closely match the solutions of the algebraic dispersion relation, confirming the solver’s performance and the correctness of the linear stability theory, and demonstrating that the two-dimensional framework overcomes the limitations of the one-dimensional approach for studying roll waves. Authors: Liu J.; Zhang Y.; Li Z.; Wang Z.; Liu J.
Title: Dynamic regulation of β-lactoglobulin amyloid fibrillation by hydroxytyrosol: Structural and functional insights
Abstract: β-lactoglobulin amyloid fibrils (LGF) are promising emulsion stabilizers, while their limited antioxidant activity restricts wide applications. In this study, hydroxytyrosol (HT) was introduced at different stages of β-lactoglobulin (LG) fibrillation to investigate its effects on fibril structure and emulsifying function. HT introduced at the initial stage inhibited nucleation and β-sheet accumulation, while HT at the end of the lag phase interfered with fibril elongation, producing shortened fibrils. HT added at the end of the growth phase remodeled complexes structure, preserving the typical fibrillar architecture. Moreover, the LGF-HT complex prepared with 100 μM HT at the end of the growth phase (LGF8-HT100) showed the best emulsifying performance (EAI: 14.28 m2/g; ESI: 71.36%), and enhanced the resistance of LGF-stabilized emulsions to lipid oxidation, decreasing TBARS value from 68.03 μM to 28.74 μM. LGF8-HT100 stabilized emulsions also exhibited the highest interfacial protein adsorption percentage, and reduced intestinal FFA release from 75.67% to 62.04%, indicating enhanced resistance to enzymatic hydrolysis. Accordingly, surface hydrophobicity analysis showed that HT intervention at this stage retained a higher H0, indicating that the hydrophobic driving force stabilizing the fibrillar structure was largely preserved. Molecular dynamics simulations further revealed that HT formed stable hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions within a buried LG pocket, and engaged a distinct surface groove on the LGF core. These findings provide new insights into the mechanisms by which HT regulates protein fibrillation and lay a theoretical foundation for the design of LGF-based emulsion stabilizers with enhanced antioxidant capacity and stability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Beyond molecular hydrophilicity: ice recrystallization inhibition and matrix-level hydrophilicity in cellulose-derivative cryoprotection of fresh wet rice noodles
Abstract: Cellulose derivatives are widely selected as food cryoprotectants based on their molecular hydrophilicity, yet whether this property reliably translates into a more hydrophilic food matrix and effective cryoprotection remains unclear. This study investigated three structurally distinct cellulose derivatives, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), methyl cellulose (MC) and hydroxypropyl methyl cellulose (HPMC), as cryoprotectants for fresh wet rice noodles (FWRN) over seven freeze-thaw cycles. Only HPMC provided substantial protection, as it uniquely combined ice recrystallization inhibition (IRI) activity with enhanced matrix-level hydrophilicity. Its IRI activity was evidenced by a 44% reduction in mean ice-crystal grain area in a sucrose model system and supported by smaller ice-derived voids in the FWRN matrix observed by Cryo-SEM. Its matrix-level hydrophilicity was reflected by the lowest contact angle (37.4°) and freezable water content (38.9%), which contributed to reduced free-water accumulation, lower syneresis, and better preservation of noodle hardness and integrity. Although HPMC delayed early-stage starch retrogradation by retarding amylose-related short-range reordering, this anti-retrogradation effect played only a secondary role in its cryoprotection, as long-range starch crystallinity remained unaffected by all derivatives. In contrast, CMC, despite having the highest molecular hydrophilicity, generated the least hydrophilic FWRN matrix, accompanied by the highest contact angle (50.7°) and freezable water content (50.9%), thereby aggravating freeze-thaw damage. MC lacked IRI activity and exerted little influence on matrix-level hydrophilicity, resulting in limited cryoprotection. These findings demonstrate that molecular hydrophilicity alone does not predict the cryoprotective performance of cellulose derivatives, as hydrocolloid–starch–water interactions can substantially alter their functionality at the matrix level. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Lead-adaptive self-supervised ECG representation model for multi-scenario ECG monitoring
Abstract: Background: Electrocardiogram (ECG) is a critical non-invasive tool for the early detection of cardiovascular diseases. However, ECG interpretation remains challenging because of signal complexity, limited medical resources, and heterogeneous monitoring settings. Most deep learning models are still designed for specific tasks and fixed lead configurations, limiting their transfer across clinical and wearable ECG scenarios. Objective: This study aims to develop a lead-adaptive self-supervised ECG representation model that supports transferable analysis across representative tasks and lead configurations. Methods: The proposed model follows a two-stage framework. First, a VQ-VAE-based ECG tokenizer converts raw ECG segments into morphology-aware waveform tokens and integrates patch and lead-time positional encodings to retain spatiotemporal context. Second, a Masked Autoencoder (MAE) extracts rich representations from unlabeled data, empowered by a novel adaptive-lead training algorithm to generalize across varying lead configurations. Results: After pretraining on 178,602 multi-center ECG records, the model was evaluated on nine downstream ECG tasks under representative 1-, 3-, 8-, and 12-lead settings. Compared with a plain MAE baseline, it improved average macro-F1 by +2.56, +4.85, and +12.80 points on broad multi-label, morphology-related, and rhythm-related classification, respectively. Ablation analyses further supported the contributions of ECG tokenization and lead-adaptive pretraining. Conclusions: The proposed model improves representation transfer across the evaluated ECG monitoring scenarios. By providing a robust representation backbone for intelligent ECG analysis, it offers a transferable technical solution for clinical ECG interpretation and wearable ECG monitoring, and may reduce the need to develop separate models for each task and lead configuration. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd
