Authors: Du Z.; Lin Y.; Hu X.; Pang K.; Cao L.; Lin B.; Huang Y.; Yang S.
Title: Microfluidic system and method for synchronous simulation of periodic pulsatile blood flow velocity and pressure in local human microvessels
Abstract: Accurately reproducing complex blood flow environments in vitro remains challenging, with the key difficulty lying in precise regulation of blood flow velocity, pressure, and periodic pulsatile characteristics. To address this issue, this study proposes a regulation method for complex microvascular blood flow environments to achieve controllable simulation of velocity, pressure, and pulsatile features within local microvessels. The feasibility of a cooperative regulation strategy, combining upstream flow-rate control with downstream hydrodynamic resistance regulation, was first demonstrated through theoretical analysis and computational fluid dynamics simulations. A fluidic regulation platform was then established to investigate the discrepancy between theoretically predicted and experimentally measured pressures under constant-flow conditions, based on which a pressure correction strategy was proposed. To improve pulsatile blood flow simulation, fluid dynamic analysis and structural optimization were performed to reduce pressure response lag and waveform distortion, thereby enhancing the accuracy of pulsatile pressure waveform reproduction. Finally, modular polyether ether ketone (PEEK) microtubes were integrated to replace on-chip hydrodynamic resistance, improving the flexibility and convenience of dynamic blood flow microenvironment regulation. Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) experiments were further conducted to validate the proposed strategy. By introducing a fluid interface isolation mechanism, the system effectively prevented the non-Newtonian behavior of PRP from interfering with linear pressure regulation in the hydrodynamic resistance channel. This method provides a convenient, efficient, and accurate strategy for in vitro blood flow regulation and may facilitate studies of blood flow-related physiological, pathological, and pharmacological mechanisms. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Wang W.; Yang Z.
Title: Sign-aided unlimited sampling for robust line spectral estimation
Abstract: The unlimited sampling framework, which employs modulo analog-to-digital converters (ADCs), has recently been introduced to mitigate the information loss caused by the dynamic range limitations of traditional ADCs. In this paper, we evaluate the performance of line spectral estimation with modulo ADC by deriving the Cramér–Rao bound (CRB) and show that it can be sensitive to noise. To address this issue, we propose a sign-aided unlimited sampling paradigm that integrates modulo ADC with the sign information of the pre-folding samples. We compare the CRBs of different unlimited sampling frameworks and show significant improvements in estimation accuracy achieved by the sign-aided approach. We further develop a least-squares (LS)-based algorithm for line spectral estimation under the sign-aided unlimited sampling framework by formulating the estimation problem as a rank-constrained structured matrix recovery problem. The proposed algorithm relies solely on spectral sparsity and does not require oversampling. Extensive numerical results are provided that validate our analysis and demonstrate improved robustness to noise and reduced dependence on oversampling of StruMER-SUS as compared to the state-of-the-art methods. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Qiu J.; Xu F.; Ren Y.; Cheng P.; Tang X.
Title: SemiET: Semi-supervised fundus enhancement with efficient Transformers
Abstract: Retinal fundus imaging is essential for the screening, diagnosis, and management of ocular diseases. High-quality fundus photographs are a prerequisite for reliable clinical interpretation and automated analysis. However, in real-world acquisition, image quality varies widely due to defocus, illumination, motion blur, and sensor noise, making robust enhancement necessary. Traditional enhancement methods often fall short by either over-enhancing images or losing vital details. Similarly, deep learning approaches, especially CycleGAN-based models, struggle with preserving structural details and bridging domain gaps. To address these limitations, we introduce SemiET, a novel semi-supervised fundus enhancement framework that utilizes an efficient Transformer structure. SemiET jointly leverages paired synthetic degradations for pixel-level reconstruction and unpaired real low-quality images for distribution alignment. To make high-resolution Transformer enhancement efficient, SemiET adopts Restormer-inspired channel-wise attention, avoiding a large spatial-affinity map while preserving global-context modeling. To assess utility beyond PSNR and SSIM, we develop a comprehensive evaluation framework that spans quality grading, vessel and optic disc/cup segmentation, fovea localization, and held-out DDR lesion-preservation detection. Across multiple datasets, SemiET achieves leading full-reference image-quality results, competitive structural downstream-task performance, and the highest mAP@0.5 among the evaluated enhancement methods in the DDR probe, while retaining the smallest parameter count among the compared methods. © 2026

Authors: Thanh Phong D.
Title: Explicit formulae for the confluent hypergeometric and Bessel functions of the second kind with Hermitian matrix argument
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: In a recent work published in Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics 457: 116258 (2025), exact expressions were derived for the hypergeometric function of a Hermitian matrix argument, motivated in part by applications in multivariate statistics and engineering sciences. Building upon these results, the present paper develops explicit formulae for the confluent hypergeometric and Bessel functions of the second kind with Hermitian matrix argument. The derivations are based on determinant representations and special function techniques. These results provide computationally tractable formulae that facilitate numerical evaluation in multivariate statistics and related applications. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Liu D.; Yu Z.; Liu X.; Yu J.; Gu T.; Xue Y.; Xue C.
Title: Fibrous structure formation in Alaska pollock surimi induced by sodium alginate or carrageenan during high-moisture extrusion: Effects of sodium alginate M/G ratio and carrageenan type
Abstract: In recent years, high-moisture extrusion (HME) has become one of the primary processing technologies for producing meat analogs. Both polysaccharide addition and protein blending are key strategies for improving the texture of extrudates. In this study, Alaska pollock surimi and soy protein isolate (7:3, w/w) were used as raw materials in an HME system, and the mechanisms by which sodium alginate with different guluronic acid/mannuronic acid (G/M) ratios and three types of carrageenan (κ, ι, and λ) regulate the fibrous structure and textural properties of extrudates were investigated. The results showed that G-rich sodium alginate led to the formation of a more continuous, stable, and well-oriented fibrous structure. The textural properties of extrudates were significantly improved. G-rich sodium alginate improved water retention and enhanced the apparent contributions of ionic interactions and disulfide bonds, thereby restricting disordered water migration and stabilizing the protein network. These changes were accompanied by a conversion of random coil and β-turn structures into more ordered β-sheet structures. In contrast, carrageenan showed relatively limited effects on improving the structure and physicochemical properties of extrudates, and the effects of different carrageenan types were not significantly different. Overall, this study revealed the important role of polysaccharide structural characteristics and associated physicochemical properties in high-moisture extrudates and provided a theoretical basis for the precise regulation of the overall quality of meat analogs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Peng H.; Ma F.; Zhang J.; Kang F.; Zheng X.
Title: UV–vis light driven photo-Fenton degradation of tetracycline over flower-like Bi2WO6 microspheres decorated with Cu2(OH)3Br nanosheets
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Photo-Fenton oxidation is a promising wastewater remediation technique, but its practical application is limited by the severe charge recombination, low charge separation efficiency and acidic-induced metal leaching. Z -scheme Cu2(OH)3Br/Bi2WO6 heterojunction was thus fabricated by anchoring Cu2(OH)3Br nanosheets on flower-like Bi2WO6 microspheres for the efficient UV–vis light induced photo-Fenton degradation of tetracycline hydrochloride (TCH) in alkaline medium. The intimate heterojunction interface accelerated the charge transfer and provides the abundant active sites for TCH adsorption and light harvesting. The Cu+/Cu2+ couples effectively activated H2O2 and O2 to generate •O2− and •OH radicals for the oxidization of TCH into harmless small molecules, which was confirmed by the degradation pathway and intermediate toxicity evaluation. Compared with Cu2(OH)3Br and Bi2WO6, Cu2(OH)3Br/Bi2WO6 exhibited the prominent photo-Fenton performance. The optimized 3-Cu2(OH)3Br/Bi2WO6 achieved the removal efficiency of 98.80% (100 mg L−1 TCH) within 120 min, while decreased to 85.35% after eighth-cycling test. The decayed activity originated from the metal leaching and valence states variation of surface components. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Tian J.; Chen H.; Dong Q.; Xu C.; Xu J.; Zhang L.; Liu D.; Wang W.
Title: Ultrasonically textured engineering of protein amyloid fibrils-tannic acid composite hydrogels for dysphagia management
Abstract: Dysphagia severely affects the quality of life in elderly and neurological patients. Conventional carbohydrate-based dysphagia-oriented foods, which have insufficient nutritional richness, tend to fragment during oral processing, increasing aspiration risk. Protein amyloid fibrils offer high protein supplement and robust mechanical properties, which can form stable hydrogels with polyphenols, suggesting potential for dysphagia-oriented foods. However, the effect of the protein amyloid fibril structure on related hydrogel properties and its International Dysphagia Diet Standardization Initiative (IDDSI) classification remain unclear. In this case, we used ultrasonic pretreatment to modulate the β-lactoglobulin fibril structure, and then induced fibril-tannic acid (TA) interactions to form composite hydrogels. Transmission electron microscopy showed that ultrasound accelerated fibrillation kinetics and induced fibril shortening, and excessive treatment (U50-10, 4.80 W/mL, 10 min) resulted in predominantly short fibrillar species. Title: Effects of fish skin collagen peptide and freezing on structure, rheology, water distribution, and digestibility of starch within wheat dough

Title: HCS-Net: A Hybrid ConvNeXt-Nano-Swin Transformer-Tiny with bottleneck fusion and residual MLP for patient-wise skin cancer classification

Title: Spreading properties of a predator-prey model in a shifting environment: Locked front case
Abstract: This paper is devoted to the study of spreading speeds for a predator-prey system in a shifting environment driven by the conversion efficiency of predation, which models the invasion of predator into the habitat already occupied by prey. Title: On the Mordell-Weil rank of certain CM abelian varieties over anticyclotomic towers

Title: Convergence analysis of the randomized Kaczmarz method with anchoring hyperplanes

Abstract: We propose an improved randomized Kaczmarz method, named the randomized Kaczmarz method with anchoring hyperplanes (RKM-AH), for solving large systems of linear equations. Our method originates from a variance reduction idea: choosing one or several hyperplanes, called anchoring hyperplanes, and forcing the iterative sequence generated by the method to belong to these hyperplanes through projections, thereby reducing the oscillation amplitude of the iterative sequence and accelerating the convergence rate. Title: Buckling Analysis of Functionally Graded Beams under Combined Loadings
Source title: Advances in Applied Mathematics and Mechanics
Abstract: This paper investigates the buckling behavior of axially functionally graded (FG) material beams subjected to combined loads with various boundary conditions. For functionally graded beams with a fixed parameter np, the critical buckling load exhibits a nonlinear increase with the gradient index. Title: Global stability of the 2D magnetohydrodynamic equations with horizontal fractional dissipation

Title: An exact penalty difference-of-convex approach for solving inverse optimal value problems in linear programming
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: This paper develops an exact penalty difference-of-convex (DC) algorithm for solving inverse optimal value problems (IOVP) in linear programming. Title: Entropic chaos of mixed mean-field jump processes

Title: Stable approximation to the solution of a sideways problem for a time-fractional advection-dispersion equation

Title: CONVERGENCE ANALYSIS OF THE RANDOM ORDINATE METHOD FOR MITIGATING THE RAY EFFECT

Title: Preference-guided graph reinforcement learning for multi-objective quality-aware hybrid flow shop scheduling with multilevel assembly

Title: Fourier neural operators with least-squares readout refit for learning random obstacle-to-solution maps
Abstract: We study operator learning for random obstacle-to-solution maps arising from elliptic variational inequalities with finite-band self-affine random obstacle fields. Title: Symmetry breaking for the planar Lane–Emden equation with Robin boundary conditions

Title: Transient aware EEG representation for sleep apnea subtype classification using adaptive segmentation
Abstract: Accurate sleep apnea subtype classification is important because obstructive, central, and mixed apnea reflect different physiological mechanisms and may require different clinical management. Title: Photonic Quantum Gates Using OAM and MPLC

Title: Rb₂ZrCl₆:Mo4+–A near-infrared lead-free perovskite phosphor for high-efficiency imaging
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: In this study, Mo4+-doped vacancy-ordered double perovskite Rb2ZrCl6:Mo4+ was synthesized for the first time, and its near-infrared (NIR) luminescence properties were systematically investigated. Title: Protease-specific effects of limited enzymatic hydrolysis on the structure, air-water interfacial adsorption, and foaming properties of jackfruit seed protein
Abstract: Jackfruit seed protein (JSP) is an underutilized plant protein with promising nutritional and functional value, but its limited foaming performance restricts its application in aerated foods. In this study, JSP was subjected to limited hydrolysis with Alcalase, bromelain, papain, and trypsin within a narrow low-DH range (approximately 6-7%). The study aimed to determine how protease-dependent molecular and colloidal changes under comparable hydrolysis extents were associated with stage-dependent air-water interfacial adsorption and foaming performance. Limited hydrolysis altered molecular-weight distribution, secondary structure, Trp microenvironment, surface hydrophobicity, particle size, ζ-potential, solubility, and interfacial adsorption behavior. Among the hydrolysates, Alcalase-treated JSP (JSP-A) exhibited the smallest particle size, highest solubility, lowest dynamic surface tension, and largest absolute rearrangement slope (|Kr|), together with the highest foaming capacity and foam stability and the lowest foam drainage. In contrast, although JSP-B showed relatively high surface hydrophobicity and rapid apparent diffusion and penetration, it did not exhibit the best foaming performance, indicating that early-stage interfacial adsorption alone was insufficient to determine foam functionality. Authors: Dai J.; Dong Y.; Wang H.; Lan T.; Sui X.
Title: Deep eutectic solvent-protein interactions regulate hydrogen-bond network reconstruction and mechanical properties of soy protein isolate eutectogels
Abstract: Soy protein isolate hydrogels are characterized by highly hydrated and fragile networks, which often limit their mechanical strength and stability under environmental conditions. In this study, SPI-based eutectogels were constructed by replacing water in heat-induced SPI hydrogels with three deep eutectic solvents (DESs), including betaine-glycerin, choline chloride-glycerin, and choline chloride-urea. DES-mediated solvent exchange remodeled the hydrogen-bonding environment and strengthened protein-solvent/protein-protein interactions, thereby reducing water mobility and forming more compact gel networks. As a result, the eutectogels exhibited improved mechanical and thermal properties. Notably, the choline chloride-glycerin eutectogel showed the highest hardness, storage moduli, and thermal stability, while the choline chloride-urea eutectogel exhibited superior deformation recovery. These results highlight the effectiveness of DES-mediated solvent exchange in modulating SPI hydrogel networks through solvent-phase regulation, providing a feasible approach for designing protein-based eutectogels with tunable mechanical properties and enhanced stability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Wang H.; Zou F.
Title: A Mixed Finite Element Method for Elliptic Interface Problems on Local Anisotropic Hybrid Meshes
Source title: Advances in Applied Mathematics and Mechanics
Abstract: We propose a mixed finite element method for solving second-order elliptic interface problems. The method is based on a fitted hybrid mesh, constructed by connecting the intersection points of the interface with an underlying unfitted triangulation. The resulting mesh consists of anisotropic triangles and quadrilaterals aligned with the interface. On this mesh, we define a pair of finite element spaces of type RT0–P0, designed to preserve the commutativity between the interpolation operator and the divergence operator. This structure ensures that the discrete inf-sup condition is satisfied without the need for additional stabilization. We establish optimal convergence rates in the L2-norm for both the velocity and pressure approximations. Numerical experiments are presented to confirm the theoretical results. © 2027 Global Science Press.

Title: Existence and necessary optimality conditions for nonlinear inverse problems governed by quasi-hemivariational inequalities with parameter-dependent constraints
Abstract: This paper investigates nonlinear inverse problems governed by a class of evolutionary quasi-hemivariational inequalities featuring constraints that depend simultaneously on parameters and unknowns. We begin by establishing the well-posedness of the parametric forward problem within the framework of evolution triples, providing existence, uniqueness, and a priori estimates for the state system. The associated inverse problem is subsequently formulated as a Tikhonov-regularized output-least-squares optimization problem, where the existence of at least one optimal parameter is proved utilizing the direct method of the calculus of variations. A primary analytical contribution of this work is the derivation of necessary optimality conditions in the presence of both nonsmoothness and state constraints with potentially empty interiors. To overcome these inherent challenges, we employ a rigorous double-approximation strategy combining smoothing and penalization techniques. This methodology leads to the derivation of an adjoint system and a first-order variational inequality associated with a singular Lagrange multiplier. Finally, to demonstrate the utility and applicability of our abstract theoretical framework, we apply our results to a nonlinear parabolic quasi-obstacle problem. Within this context, the abstract framework is verified in appropriate Sobolev spaces, and explicit optimality conditions are successfully derived. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Alfakih A.; Xia Z.; Mamoon S.; Ali B.; Lu J.

Title: Dynamic causal graph representation learning for neurological disorders recognition
Abstract: The effectiveness of dynamic brain networks in diagnosing neurological disorders, which represent a worldwide threat to human health, is increasingly recognized. Numerous Graph Neural Network (GNN) models have been created to autonomously detect aberrant integration patterns related to specific neurological conditions in brain graphs. Nevertheless, most existing approaches exhibit primary drawbacks. These methodologies typically either employ predetermined statistical metrics (e.g., Pearson correlation) or depend on static brain networks. Moreover, the process of constructing dynamic brain networks/graphs concentrates on static or temporally invariant effective connectivity, resulting in a substantial knowledge gap about the dynamic aspect of dEC. Although statistically-specific brain networks are extremely efficient in identifying certain disorders, their performance may lack robustness when applied to other neurological diseases. To address these issues, we introduce a novel model termed the Dynamic Causal Graph Inference Graph Neural Network (DCGI-GNN), which can estimate brain networks and learn graph representation within a two-stage pipeline, facilitating the optimization and interpretability of each stage. The term “causal” in this work refers to directed, time-varying functional influence relationships, not intervention-based causality. Our model initially deduces the task-relevant graph structures directly from the data and later utilizes them to improve downstream task performance. We conducted extensive experiments to diagnose three brain diseases: autism spectrum disorder (ASD), Alzheimer's disease (AD), and Parkinson's disease (PD) using data from the ABIDE, ADNI, and PDD datasets. Our findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. Beyond its superior performance, the model is highly interpretable, and its conclusions align largely with existing literature. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Li J.; Li H.; Chen H.; Sheng H.; Zhang S.; Fu L.; Zhang J.
Title: Subcritical water-induced soy protein isolate nanofibrils with tailored interfacial architecture enhance the stability and intestinal release of resveratrol-loaded Pickering emulsions
Abstract: In the present study, subcritical water treatment (SWT) was employed to precisely regulate the fibrillation of soy protein isolate (SPI), and a stable resveratrol-loaded Pickering emulsion was subsequently constructed using the resulting SPI nanofibrils. The effects of different processing temperatures (105, 110, 120, 130, 140°C) and treatment times (20, 30, 40, 50, 60 min) on the structural and functional properties of SPI nanofibrils were investigated. The results showed that treatment at 120°C for 40 min represented the optimal processing condition. Under these conditions, the protein nanofibrils showed a regular short rod structure, the smallest particle size (about 369 nm), and the ζ-potential was approximately −25 mV. Compared with the conventional hydrothermal method (85°C for 12 h), SWT markedly shortened the fibrillation time while improving fibrillation efficiency. The Pickering emulsion stabilized by subcritical water (SW)-induced SPI nanofibrils showed excellent encapsulation performance for resveratrol, with an encapsulation efficiency (EE) of approximately 91%. In vitro digestion experiments showed that the delivery system effectively inhibited the premature release of resveratrol during the gastric phase and achieved controlled release in the small intestine stage. The delivery system significantly improved the recovery rate of resveratrol (about 80%), which was markedly higher than that of the hydrothermal control (about 58%). Release kinetic modeling demonstrated that the release behavior of resveratrol at different digestion stages followed different mechanisms. This study proposes a possible mechanism by which SWT-induced SPI nanofibrils stabilize the oil–water interface and modulate resveratrol release, based on experimental intermolecular force quantification, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and release kinetics. Title: Construction of Z-scheme heterojunction via in-situ growth of nano zero-valent iron from natural hematite: Efficient sunlight-driven photocatalysis for PFOA removal
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Nano zero-valent iron (NZVI) has already demonstrated its broad application potential towards the removal of organic pollutants in water bodies. However, the passivation of NZVI still remains a significant challenge for its practical application. Herein, in-situ growth of NZVI from the surface of natural hematite was realized, and heterojunction structures were constructed by activating the passivation layer (FeOOH as the main component). The composites, denoted as HeFex, were employed in the photocatalytic removal of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) under simulated sunlight irradiation. Notably, the HeFe20 composite exhibited the highest photocatalytic activity, achieving 92.2% PFOA degradation and 39.2% defluorination within 80 min. The remarkably high catalytic efficiency was attributed to the extended light absorption range, excellent charge separation capacity, significantly high optical responsiveness, and various efficient adsorption pathways. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy valence band analysis, quenching experiments, electron spin resonance, and density functional theory calculations confirmed the successful fabrication of a Z -scheme heterojunction. It is worth noting that h+ and the Fe(III) were identified to be the dominant species, driving a stepwise process of decarbonization and defluorination. Title: Synthesis and photophysical properties of 3-azinyl-7-aminocoumarins: tuning solvatochromism, HLCT excited state, and static fluorescence quenching by picric acid

Abstract: A series of new coumarin-azine fluorophores based on 1,2,4-triazinyl and pyridinyl substituted derivatives of 7-aminocoumarin was synthesized via a nucleophilic substitution of hydrogen (SNH) reaction followed by an inverse electron-demand Diels–Alder transformation. Thus, the emission of the fluorophores in acetonitrile solution covers the range from blue to green-yellow with emission maxima from 470 to 547 nm with absolute quantum yields (QYs) of up to 85%. The emission in toluene solution covers only blue region and QYs values decreased to 60%. A study of the solvent effect using the Lippert-Mataga equation showed that two derivatives of 3-triazinyl coumarin are solvatochromic and demonstrate hybrid local and charge transfer exited state, while 3-pyridyl coumarins turned out to be non-solvatochromic. Six fluorophores were tested as sensors for detecting nitroaromatic compounds. Title: Engineering a naphthalene diimide-derived dual-mode chemodosimeter for cyanide with an ultralow nanomolar detection limit and food sample applications
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: A unique fluorescent sensor, NDI-TCF , was developed and found to be highly effective at identifying CN− ions over the presence of different anions. Furthermore, it exhibited a Stern-Volmer constant of 2.97 × 105 M−1 and strong anti-interference properties. Additionally, cyanide detection was investigated in six food items to demonstrate the practical applications of the sensor. Methods such as visual eye detection and paper strip tests were employed to assess the effectiveness of the sensor for rapid CN− detection in real-world scenarios. Title: Feedback-Free Photonic Reservoir Computing via Time-Concatenated Dimensional Expansion and Hybrid Pruning
Source title: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics
Abstract: Reservoir computing (RC) offers an efficient framework for temporal processing by combining nonlinear mapping with short-term memory. However, conventional implementations are often hindered by the high hardware costs of spatial arrays or the speed and integration bottlenecks associated with feedback delay lines and input masking in time-delayed RC. In this paper, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a single-node photonic reservoir computing system without physical delay lines and input masking operations. To enhance the representational capability of the single-node system, we introduce a time-concatenated dimensional expansion technique to construct a high-dimensional state space. Furthermore, a hybrid pruning strategy is employed to quantitatively optimize the trade-off between computational resources and forecasting performance. Our results demonstrate a feedback-free photonic reservoir computing framework that combines physical photonic feature generation with digital state construction and optimization for temporal processing tasks with diverse dynamical characteristics.  © 1995-2012 IEEE.

Title: Rational design of a quinoline-derived Schiff base for dual-mode detection of zinc and copper ions
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Rapid industrialization and urbanization have led to the widespread release of copper and zinc into the environment through mining, smelting, electroplating, galvanization, battery manufacturing, electronics production, and other metallurgical processes. Upon complexation, QUO-QUO displays distinct color changes from yellow to pink for Cu2+ at 519 nm and to light orange for Zn2+ at 480 nm. This probe demonstrates high sensitivity, with detection limits reaching as low as 0.67 μM using spectrophotometric methods for Cu2+ and 28 nM using spectrofluorometric methods for Zn2+ ions. Title: Some Structure-Preserving Schemes for Fractional Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation in Two Dimensions
Source title: Advances in Applied Mathematics and Mechanics
Abstract: In this paper, we develop some structure-preserving schemes to solve two-dimensional fractional nonlinear Schrödinger system, which preserve one or more analytical properties of the fractional system. First, the Crank-Nicolson scheme and the relaxation scheme are applied to deal with time derivative, and the resulting semi-discrete systems can exactly preserve the semi-discrete mass and energy conservation laws. However, the obtained semi-discrete systems are of nonlinear systems. Then, we show a equivalent form of fractional nonlinear Schrödinger system by introducing some new auxiliary variables. The new system is discretized by the scalar auxiliary variable scheme in time, and a linear semi-discrete system is obtained, which can conserve the energy conservation law of the system. Second, the resulting semi-discrete systems are discretized by compact difference scheme with zero boundary condition and periodic boundary condition. We find that the compact difference scheme preserves only energy conservation law very well for periodic boundary condition, which is different from the integer order case. Title: Nonlinear Vibration Analysis of Fractional Viscoelastic Timoshenko Nanobeams Considering Nonlocal and Surface Effects
Source title: Advances in Applied Mathematics and Mechanics
Abstract: This study proposes a non-classical Timoshenko beam model that incorporates von-Kármán geometric nonlinearity and a fractional Kelvin-Voigt viscoelastic model, based on nonlocal strain gradient theory and surface elasticity theory. The model captures the effects of microstructure, surface energy, and nonlocality, with governing equations and boundary conditions derived using Hamilton’s principle to describe fractional viscoelastic nanobeams under transverse harmonic excitation. Numerical simulations reveal that fractional order significantly modifies the nonlinear vibration characteristics of structures and enhances damping as the fractional order increases. Furthermore, due to the correlation between fractional order and excitation frequency, the effects of fractional order on nonlinear time responses differ between free and forced vibrations. Title: Segmented variable impedance controller with trajectory adaptive adjustment for robotic polishing tasks
Abstract: In robot contact force control, adaptive variable impedance control reduces force tracking error compared to constant impedance control, but there is a collision between the end effector and the environment, resulting in overshoot of the contact force. To reduce contact-force overshoot and further improve force-tracking accuracy, an adaptive reference trajectory-based adaptive variable impedance control (ART-AVIC) method is proposed. The controller’s reference trajectory is adjusted in real time based on the magnitude of the force error. Meanwhile, the damping parameters are updated in a segmented manner according to the contact force error in contact stage. This approach effectively reduces the system’s steady-state error and significantly reduces overshoot and settling time during robotic polishing. In the simulations that account for environmental changes, desired force variations, and practical factors, the ART-AVIC method exhibits better overall performance. In curved surface polishing experiments, compared with other control methods, ART-AVIC reduces the contact-force overshoot by 13.61%-54.93% and the steady-state contact-force RMSE by 11.11%-61.90%. In addition, polishing experiments on blade and cage have demonstrated the potential of the ART-AVIC method for industrial applications. Title: How methyl esterification patterns shape pectin structure and functionality: From controlled modification to function
Abstract: Pectin function depends not only on the degree of methyl esterification (DM), but also on the spatial distribution of methyl esters along the homogalacturonan (HG) backbone. DM remains the primary descriptor of pectin esterification, but does not describe how methyl esters are distributed along the HG backbone. The importance of this distribution has long been recognized. Enzymatic fingerprinting and multistage mass spectrometry provide information on methyl-ester distribution beyond that captured by DM. This review integrates the historical fundamentals and recent advances in the modification and analysis of pectin methyl esterification patterns. It evaluates how DM and methyl-ester distribution affect pectin structure, physicochemical properties, intermolecular interactions, bioactivities, and food applications. By distinguishing established principles from emerging evidence, this review highlights the need for better characterization of methyl-ester distribution, improved control of structural variables, and testing under real food conditions. Such efforts could provide a clearer basis for understanding how DM and methyl-ester distribution influence pectin performance in gelled foods, emulsions, dairy systems, delivery systems, and other food applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Bifurcation of periodic solutions for a free boundary problem modeling 2-dimensional tumor growth
Abstract: For a simple tumor model with a periodic supply of external nutrients σ=ϕ(t) on the boundary, a unique radially symmetric T -periodic positive solution ( σ *( r, t ), p *( r, t ), R *( t )) was established by [1, 2]. Title: Xylo-oligosaccharides modulate retrogradation in high-moisture rice starch gels: Insights from molecular interactions to multiscale ordered structures
Abstract: High-moisture rice products are susceptible to rapid textural deterioration during storage, as starch chains remain sufficiently mobile to reassociate within the gel matrix. Moreover, DP3 and DP4 XOS formed multipoint contacts with starch, but DP4 showed a much more stable association, whereas DP2 mainly formed single-point contacts. Title: β-Lactoglobulin fibrils: An effective modulator of lotus seed starch–lauric acid complexation
Abstract: Starch–fatty acid complexation represents a major route for producing functional resistant starch. The results showed that the incorporation of 30% BLG fibrils markedly increased the V-type diffraction intensity of the IC system by approximately threefold, while the engineered nanofibrils had no significant effect on IC formation. Moreover, both BLG fibrils and nanofibrils inhibited starch retrogradation, as evidenced by the reduced proportion of B-type polymorphs and double helices. Title: An integrated framework for breast cancer diagnosis using adaptive DeepLabv3+ for segmentation and attention-based multiscale EfficientNetB7 for classification

Title: Elucidating the contributions of alginate and fucoidan to algal cell wall structure and rheology using bacterial cellulose gels

Title: Mobility-tunable water-soluble starch nanoparticles reinforce whey protein gels for IDDSI-aligned dysphagia foods

Title: Iterative reweighted framework based algorithms for sparse linear regression with generalized elastic-net penalty

Abstract: The elastic net penalty is frequently employed in high-dimensional statistics for parameter regression and variable selection. It is particularly beneficial compared to lasso when the number of predictors greatly surpasses the number of observations. However, empirical evidence has shown that the ℓq-norm penalty (where 0 < q < 1) often provides better regression compared to the ℓ1-norm penalty, demonstrating enhanced robustness in various scenarios. Title: Preference-guided phase-conditioned residual admittance control for physical human–robot collaboration
Abstract: Flexible manufacturing is shifting robots from fixed-process automation toward physical human–robot collaboration (pHRC), where robots share workspaces, decisions, and task execution with human operators. The method uses nominal admittance as the baseline control structure, represents collaboration quality through a demonstration-quality-calibrated preference reward, embeds soft confidence values for the free and constrained phases into the policy state, and combines behavior cloning (BC) initialization with soft actor-critic (SAC) learning using dual replay buffers to learn damping residuals. Compared with the BC policy and randomly initialized SAC, task completion time also shows a decreasing trend. Title: Free boundary problems for the two-dimensional Euler equations in exterior domains
Abstract: In this paper we present some classification results for the steady Euler equations in two-dimensional exterior domains with free boundaries. Title: Rheo-tribological measurements and trained sensory panel texture perception across size-controllable whey protein microgels
Abstract: Protein microgels have gained attention as potential fat replacers and texture modifiers due to their ability to modulate viscosity and lubrication. Title: Effects of structure flexibility of glucan on molecular conformations of gluten proteins under freeze stress
Abstract: Frozen storage and freeze-thaw cycles cause cold denaturation of gluten proteins, significantly compromising frozen dough quality. Title: Steric hindrance engineered through-space conjugation for the emission wavelength control of organic room-temperature phosphorescence

Title: Graphs with constant links and induced Turán numbers

Abstract: A graph G of constant link L is a graph in which the neighborhood of any vertex induces a graph isomorphic to L. Given two different graphs, H and G, the induced Turán number ex(n;H,G-ind) is defined as the maximum number of edges in an n-vertex graph having no subgraph isomorphic to H and no copy from G as an induced subgraph. Our main motivation in this paper is to establish a bridge between graphs with constant link and induced Turán numbers via the class of t-regular, k-uniform (linear) hypergraphs of girth at least 4, as well as to present several methods of constructing connected graphs with constant link. We show that, for integers t≥3 and k≥3, ex(n;Ck,K1,t-ind)≤(k−2)(t−1)n/2 and that equality holds for infinitely many values of n. This result is built upon the existence of graphs with constant link tL with restricted cycle length, which we prove in another theorem. More precisely, we show that, given a graph F with constant link L and circumference c, then, for all integers t≥2 and g>c, there exists a graph with constant link tL which is free of cycles of length l, for all c<l<g. We provide two proofs of this result using distinct approaches. We further present constructions of graphs with constant links tL, t≥2, and restricted cycle length based on Steiner Systems. Finally, starting from a connected graph of constant link tL, for t≥2, having order n and restricted cycle lengths, we provide a method to construct an infinite collection of connected graphs of constant link tL that preserves the cycle length restriction, and whose orders form an arithmetic progression qn, q≥1. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Enhancement of chitosan coating properties by carrier-free self-assembled coptisine-cinnamic acid nanoparticles and their application in cherry tomato preservation
Abstract: Chitosan is an important hydrocolloid for edible films; however, its strong water affinity, swelling tendency, and limited moisture-barrier capacity restrict its application in high-humidity food storage. In this study, we synthesized carrier-free coptisine–cinnamic acid nanoassemblies (COP–CA NPs) and incorporated them as active nanofillers into chitosan coatings. The optimized nanoparticles had an average particle size of 55.09 nm, a PDI of 0.205, and a relatively narrow particle size distribution, while retaining good in vitro free radical scavenging and antibacterial activities. Strong antibacterial functionality was also maintained after incorporation into the CS matrix. The incorporation of COP–CA NPs reduced the water wettability, water solubility, and swelling degree of the chitosan film, while simultaneously enhancing its moisture barrier properties and mechanical strength. The water vapor permeability of the 0.20% composite coating film (0.20% CS@NPs) decreased by 56.1%, while its tensile strength increased by 53.5%, without markedly affecting elongation at break. Physical characterization and multiscale simulations indicate that COP–CA NPs form multisite interfacial associations with chitosan through hydrogen bonding, local electrostatic interactions, aromatic contact, and van der Waals forces, thereby limiting water absorption, swelling, and water migration within the film. After 14 days of storage, the 0.20% CS@NPs coating reduced the weight loss of cherry tomatoes from 14.75% to 6.89%, and better maintained fruit firmness and total soluble solids. The COP–CA carrier-free nanoassemblies can effectively enhance the water resistance, moisture barrier properties, and fruit preservation capacity of the chitosan coating. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Enhancing robotic interoperability: An approach for ROS 2-driven system integration
Abstract: Reconfigurable manufacturing requires robotic workcells that can adapt to changing products, processes, and equipment without extensive redesign or manual reprogramming. This paper presents the R3M framework, a ROS 2 driven integration architecture that connects model based manufacturing knowledge with execution level robotic control. Product, process, and equipment information is formalised through UML domain models and serialised in AutomationML(AML), enabling automated correspondence between assembly requirements, available skills, and executable recipes. The framework integrates automated programme generation, reinforcement learning based recipe optimisation, and a modular CAD informed six degree of freedom perception layer to support both technical and semantic interoperability across simulated and physical workcells. The approach is evaluated through Cube Kitting and Cylinder Stacking use cases implemented on distinct robotic platforms, including ABB and Universal Robots systems. Experimental results show high reliability, with environment launch performance reaching up to 99.93%, standard skill sequences achieving 100% execution success, and full use case trials exceeding 97% success in simulation and reaching 100% on physical hardware. These findings demonstrate that R3M provides a scalable foundation for adaptive robotic manufacturing, reducing programming effort while supporting modular substitution, robust perception, and simulation to real deployment. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Characterization of single-step and two-step OSA-modified chitosan and performance of thermo-compression moulded films
Abstract: Chitosan is a promising alternative to petroleum-based plastics. However, their limiting mechanical and barrier properties have made its chemical modification a spot of interest nowadays. This work evaluates the effect of different degrees of octenyl succinic anhydride (OSA) modification, including single- and two-step functionalization, on the physicochemical properties of chitosan and its behaviour during compression moulding. FTIR analysis confirmed the successful grafting of OSA onto both amino and hydroxyl groups, achieving degree of substitution (DS) values ranging from 0.124 to 0.585, which resulted in changes in the internal molecular organization observed by XRD. These structural rearrangements contributed to matrix free volume and increased chain mobility, which led to improved thermo-mechanical processability and enabled the production of uniform and flexible films. Films prepared from single-step OSA-modified chitosan exhibited enhanced mechanical performance compared to native chitosan, with tensile strength increasing from 20.68 to 36.42 MPa and elongation at break from 5.36 to 11.48%. In contrast, two-step OSA-modified samples displayed higher elasticity (up to 34.05%) but significantly reduced tensile strength (13.28-14.32 MPa), indicating that high degrees of modification lead to an excessive plasticization and decreased matrix cohesion. Moreover, OSA modification improved water vapour barrier properties by up to 67% compared to native chitosan, attributed to the hydrophobic character of the alkenyl side chains. Overall, the combination of OSA modification and compression moulding represents a feasible strategy for the scalable production of chitosan-based bioplastics suitable for food packaging applications. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Mizusawa Y.; Mouhib A.
Title: Real quadratic fields with metacyclic 2-class field towers over their Z2-extensions
Abstract: Abstract. We consider the maximal unramified pro-2-extension over the cyclotomic Z2-extension of a real quadratic field, which is the union of 2-class field towers along the Z2-extension. By using cyclotomic units in finite fields, we give a complete classification of real quadratic fields such that the unramified pro-2 Galois groups over their Z2-extensions are metacyclic. We also give a general formula on the 2-rank of the unramified Iwasawa module which is the abelianization of the unramified pro-2 Galois group. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Commercial enzyme-assisted extraction of structurally tailored okra pectin for enhanced emulsion stabilization in reduced-egg and plant-based mayonnaise
Abstract: The emulsifying functionality of okra pectin is highly dependent on its molecular structure. However, tailoring its structure has largely relied on post-extraction modification using purified enzymes, limiting industrial applicability. In this study, commercially available multicatalytic enzyme preparations were investigated as a one-step strategy to simultaneously extract and structurally tailor okra pectin with enhanced emulsion-stabilizing functionality. Among the enzyme preparations evaluated, Rohament® CL produced enzyme-optimized okra pectin (EOP) with the highest extraction yield (13.9%) and superior emulsion-stabilizing performance. The improved functionality was associated with greater RG-I branching, higher molecular weight, increased degrees of acetylation and methylation, and a higher abundance of neutral sugar side chains, confirmed by macromolecular characterization, and 1D/2D NMR analyses. The applicability of EOP was evaluated in vegan, egg-reduced (up to 90%), and fat-reduced (up to 40%) mayonnaise formulations. EOP effectively stabilized concentrated oil-in-water mayonnaise emulsions, producing finer and more homogeneous oil droplets, shear-thinning behavior, elastic gel-like networks (G′ > G″), and excellent thixotropic recovery (86.9-98.2%). At sufficient concentrations, EOP, as the sole stabilizing agent, successfully stabilized vegan mayonnaise, while formulations containing 50% egg reduction or combined 50% egg and 20% fat reduction exhibited physicochemical, rheological, storage, and sensory properties comparable to conventional mayonnaise. In addition, EOP improved storage stability by reducing phase separation, color change, and lipid oxidation during storage. These findings demonstrate that commercial enzyme-assisted extraction provides a practical one-step strategy for tailoring the structure and emulsion-stabilizing functionality of okra pectin, supporting its application as a multifunctional plant-derived stabilizer for reduced-egg, reduced-fat, and clean-label mayonnaise formulations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Wang X.; Tian X.; Ma Y.; Liu Y.; Li C.; Wang C.; Wang Q.; Yuan N.; Wang W.
Title: Synergistic effects of deamidation and heat treatment on protein thermal aggregation: Structural rearrangement and flavor-binding behavior
Abstract: Off-flavors limit the application of alternative proteins in foods. This study systematically investigated the synergistic effects of deamidation pretreatment combined with thermal treatment (65, 80, 95, and 120 °C for 30 min) on the conformational changes and flavor-binding and release behaviors of chickpea protein (CP), oat protein (OP), and Pleurotus eryngii protein (PEP). Following protein-glutaminase (PG) treatment, the corresponding deamidated proteins (DCP, DOP, and DPEP) exhibited deamidation degrees of 57.67%, 55.44%, and 48.24%, respectively, which further increased to 68.90%, 62.79%, and 53.84% after heating at 120 °C, indicating that heating further promoted protein deamidation. Thermal treatment decreased the α-helix proportion and increased the β-sheet content of CP, OP, and PEP, accompanied by a gradual reduction in intrinsic fluorescence intensity, indicating heat-induced rearrangement of protein secondary and tertiary structures. Deamidation increased electrostatic repulsion between protein molecules and partially inhibited heat-induced aggregation, as evidenced by increased solubility, reduced particle size, and a lower proportion of high-molecular-weight components. Furthermore, flavoromics analysis integrated with release kinetics revealed that deamidation combined with thermal treatment significantly inhibited volatile compound release. Specifically, at 120 °C, deamidation reduced the release rate of 2-pentylfuran by 28.51%, 30.96%, and 21.98% in the CP, OP, and PEP systems, respectively, relative to their corresponding non-deamidated controls. Among the identified volatile compounds, decanal and nonanal showed higher retention, whereas 2-pentylfuran was more readily released. Overall, deamidation pretreatment effectively limited volatile compound release by mitigating heat-induced protein aggregation. These findings provide new insights into flavor regulation in alternative protein-based foods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Zhou Z.; Wang Y.; Guo Y.; Gao S.; Dai O.; Ma A.; Zhang H.
Title: Molecular characterization and nonlinear rheology of native and carboxymethylated carrageenans
Abstract: Carrageenans are important marine polysaccharides extracted from red algae and are widely used for their ability to form ion-induced hydrogels. In food and pharmaceutical applications, these hydrogels are often subjected to large-amplitude, rapid shear deformations, making the study of their nonlinear rheological responses highly relevant. Herein, carboxymethyl derivatives with varying degrees of substitution (DS) were prepared from κ-, ι-, and λ-carrageenans. Structural characterization using FT-IR, NMR, elemental analysis, and gel permeation chromatography confirmed successful carboxymethylation, accompanied by partial desulfation and changes in molecular weight. Steady and dynamic shear tests revealed shear-thinning behavior in the solutions; carboxymethylation converted the original gel-like response to a more liquid-like viscoelasticity by altering chain conformation and electrostatic interactions. Large amplitude oscillatory shear (LAOS), combined with Fourier-transform and Chebyshev analyses, showed that κ-carrageenan gels exhibit weak strain overshoot and a narrow linear viscoelastic region, whereas ι-carrageenan and most carboxymethylated derivatives display strong strain overshoot and a broader linear region. Notably, increasing DS progressively enhances resistance to nonlinear deformation. These findings elucidate transient network dynamics and establish a structure–rheology relationship for carboxymethylated carrageenans, guiding the design of soft, tough hydrogels for food and biomedical applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Arrepu P.; Zhou H.
Title: STABLE DETERMINATION OF COEFFICIENTS IN NONLINEAR DYNAMICAL SCHRÖDINGER EQUATIONS BY CARLEMAN ESTIMATES
Abstract: We consider the inverse problem of recovering stationary coefficients in a class of dynamical Schrödinger equations with locally analytic nonlinear terms. Upon treating the well-posedness for small initial data and trivial boundary data, we proceed to establish stable and unique determination provided knowledge of the coefficients near the boundary and the measured Neumann data of the solution. We discuss both the case of measurement on a subset of the boundary satisfying a certain geometric condition and, under stronger assumptions on the regularity and size of the coefficients, the case of measurement on arbitrary subsets of the boundary. Our argument relies on high-order linearization and Carleman estimates for the linear Schrödinger equation. © 2026, American Institute of Mathematical Sciences. All rights reserved.

Authors: Kalia V.; Kumar B.
Title: On traces of cycle integrals attached to harmonic weak Maass forms
Abstract: Bringmann, Guerzhoy and Kane introduced the notion of traces of cycle integrals of harmonic weak Maass form of negative weight in terms of traces of weak Maass form of weight 0. They proved that these traces coincide with the traces of cycle integrals of the associated classical cusp forms. Their result applies to the case of positive discriminants d,δ such that dδ not a square. In this paper, we define traces of cycle integral of weak Maass forms of weight 0 in the case of negative discriminants d,δ such that dδ not a square and prove the similar result. Further, we define modified traces of weak Maass forms of weight 0 in the case of discriminants d,δ such that dδ a square and prove that for a given harmonic weak Maass form of negative weight, the modified traces of cycle integral of the associated weak Maass form of weight 0 coincide with the twisted central L -values of the associated classical cusp forms. As an application of our result, we classify all weakly holomorphic modular forms lying in the space of harmonic weak cusp forms in terms of vanishing of modified traces (twisted central L -value). © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Fang Y.; Zhao Z.
Title: Gelatin-based hydrogels modified by transglutaminase and acid-heated ovalbumin aggregates: Experimental characterization
Abstract: Conventional cold-set gelatin hydrogels have limited mechanical strength and thermal stability. This study examined gelatin (GEL)-based formulations modified with transglutaminase (TGase) and acid-heated ovalbumin aggregates (AHOA). Short-time characterization of acid-heated ovalbumin showed spectroscopic changes consistent with amyloid-like aggregation and an increased elastic response. AHOA prepared by an 8-h acidic heat treatment was incorporated into gelatin formulations. At a common TGase reaction time of 6 h, the GEL:AHOA volume ratio of 6:4 gave the highest hardness and springiness among the tested formulations. Because changing this ratio also changes protein concentrations, the maximum describes a formulation-dependent response. TGase-treated gelatin hydrogels exhibited higher moduli and altered hydration behavior than the untreated control. In the extended in vitro digestion test, treated groups showed lower early but higher final cumulative betacyanin release, and a higher fraction of endpoint-recovered betacyanin in the liquid phase. The storage tests showed higher betacyanin retention at 8 days and lower loss at 28 days for the TGase-treated groups than for GH in the respective series. These results distinguish the mechanical response to AHOA incorporation from the hydration and pigment-release properties measured for gelatin hydrogels with and without TGase. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Han X.; Wu L.; Wang L.; Zheng L.
Title: Bioactive nanocomposite-reinforced biopolymer films for multifunctional food packaging
Abstract: Developing sustainable food packaging materials with mechanical strength, antibacterial activity, and biodegradability remains challenging. In this study, a multifunctional konjac glucomannan (KGM)/quaternized nanocellulose (QNC)-zinc oxide (ZnO) composite film was fabricated through a triple interfacial synergistic reinforcement strategy using KGM, QNC, and ZnO nanoparticles. The incorporation of QNC and ZnO enhanced film performance via strong interfacial interactions. The optimized film exhibited a tensile strength of 139.6 MPa and elongation at break of 21.7%. Moisture resistance improved, with a water vapor transmission rate of 78.2 g m−2·day−1 and a water contact angle of 88.6°. The composite exhibited strong antibacterial activity against E. coli and S. aureus with antibacterial rates of 99.75% and 99.99%. The composite also showed good biodegradability and excellent cytocompatibility. Grape preservation tests indicated a weight loss of only 15.49% after 18 days. This study provides a green and feasible strategy for constructing biodegradable multifunctional packaging films with enhanced mechanical properties, antibacterial activity, and preservation functionality. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Comparative study of curcumin- and limonene oil-encapsulated Pickering emulsions stabilized by pH-Responsive chitosan nanoparticles: Structural, rheological, and controlled release properties
Abstract: Curcumin and limonene oil, bioactive compounds with therapeutic potential, are vital for human health but face limitations due to poor solubility, stability, and bioavailability. Chitosan (CS), a pH-responsive natural polysaccharide, serves as an effective stabilizer in Pickering emulsions (PEs), thereby enhancing their delivery. This study focuses on preparing stable CS nanoparticles (CSNPs) via a pH-responsive self-assembly method for encapsulating bioactive compounds. Optimal stability of CSNPs was observed at pH 6, as indicated by a higher contact angle reflecting enhanced hydrophobicity. At pH 6.5, the contact angle decreased due to the formation of large, unstable aggregates that settled out, resulting in a reduced hydrophobicity of CS. Curcumin-loaded PEs prepared at pH 6 exhibited uniform droplet size and distribution, which can be attributed to the strong hydrophobic interactions of the CSNPs. Below pH 6, the CSNPs became hydrophilic, resulting in the phase separation of the PEs. Increasing the concentration of CSNPs and oil content promoted the formation of interconnected networks, resulting in elastic gels that are stable at 35°C. At elevated temperatures (70°C), the enhanced kinetic energy of CSNPs induced a gel-to-semi-gel transition, while elevated ionic strength further liquefied PEs. Limonene oil-encapsulated PEs were stable at pH 5.5 and 6.0, differing from curcumin systems due to limonene's lower viscosity and the pH-sensitive behavior of CSNPs. This study demonstrates that slight pH variations in CSNPs have a significant impact on bioactive encapsulation and stability. Curcumin- and limonene-loaded PEs achieve high efficiency, capacity, and controlled release, providing a versatile method to improve bioactive delivery in food and pharmaceutical systems. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: You K.-M.; Sha X.; Soni M.; Liceaga A.M.; Ilavsky J.; Chen D.
Title: Pea protein hydrolysate aggregates in fat-free cream cheese: influence by degree of hydrolysis in fat-mimicking capacity
Abstract: Plant protein hydrolysate aggregates have emerged as promising fat replacers. However, the influence of degree of hydrolysis (DH) on their fat-mimicking behavior and the underlying mechanism remains unclear. In this study, pea protein hydrolysate aggregates (PPHA) with DH values of 3.0% (PPHA-3.0), 4.5% (PPHA-4.5), and 7.0% (PPHA-7.0) were prepared. Among the samples, PPHA-4.5 exhibited higher apparent viscosity and lower friction coefficient (μ) than PPHA-3.0 and PPHA-7.0. Incorporation of PPHA into skim milk to produce fat-free cream cheese decreased the storage modulus (G′) from ∼35 kPa in the control cheese to ∼15 kPa in PPHA-3.0 containing cheese and further to ∼9 kPa in PPHA-4.5 and PPHA-7.0 containing cheese. Stress relaxation showed the characteristic relaxation time (τ) decreased from 2.0 s in the control cheese to ∼0.96 s in PPHA-containing cheeses. Tribological analysis showed that μ within the mixed lubrication regime decreased from ∼0.50 in the control cheese to ∼0.21 in PPHA-3.0 cheese and further to ∼0.15 in PPHA-4.5 and PPHA-7.0 counterparts. Confocal laser scanning microscopy and cryo-SEM showed that PPHA-3.0 cheese maintained a relatively compact protein network, whereas PPHA-4.5 and PPHA-7.0 produced more open and heterogeneous structures. Ultra-small and small-angle X-ray scattering further showed enlarged mesoscale scattering domains after PPHA incorporation, with the radius of gyration increasing from ∼390 nm in the control cheese to ∼505 nm in PPHA-4.5 containing cheese. These findings suggest that PPHA with DH-4.5 and 7.0 are promising fat replacers in reducing viscoelasticity and friction coefficient of cream cheese by limiting aggregation of casein micelles. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: NPR-NLMMI hybrid mode-locked fiber laser with an SMF-PCF-GIMF-SMF saturable absorber
Abstract: This study demonstrates a hybrid mode-locked fiber laser by incorporating a single-mode fiber-photonic crystal fiber-graded-index multimode fiber-single-mode fiber (SMF-PCF-GIMF-SMF) structure as a saturable absorber (SA) into a nonlinear polarization rotation cavity.The SA exhibits a modulation depth of 5.8% and a saturation intensity of 59.8 μJ/cm2. Stable fundamental mode-locking is achieved at acenter wavelength of 1555 nm with a 3 dB spectral width of 7.2 nm. Compared to the hybrid mode-locked laser employing a conventionalSMF-GIMF-SMF SA, the proposed SA reduces the fundamental-frequency mode-locking threshold from 120 to 50 mW, improves the signalto-noise ratio of the RF spectrum from 35 to 48 dB, and decreases the pulse width from 580 to 493 fs. Harmonic mode-locking up to the eighthorder is achieved by adjusting the pump power and polarization controllers. The long-term stability of the laser is confirmed by the powerfluctuation of the fundamental-frequency pulse train over an 8-h period. This compact, low-cost laser exhibits a high damage threshold andgood stability, highlighting its significant potential for both fundamental ultrafast photonics research and industrial applications. © 2026 Author(s).

Title: Alginate-induced structural modification of high-moisture extruded soy and pea protein scaffolds for cultivated meat applications
Abstract: Producing plant-based scaffolds through high-moisture extrusion offers a promising approach for cultivated meat. However, the influence of hydrocolloid incorporation on scaffold structure and functionality remains insufficiently understood. This study investigated alginate incorporation during high-moisture extrusion of pea and soy protein concentrates and evaluated its effect on structure, material properties, and cell distribution.Protein source was associated with differences in processing behavior and extrudate appearance, with soy exhibiting higher specific mechanical energy and darker extrudates than pea. Increased directional alignment was observed in pea extrudates upon alginate addition, whereas soy extrudates only showed moderate structural changes. Mechanical characterization of soy extrudates showed increased stiffness and cohesion compared to pea extrudates, while alginate-containing formulations generally reduced stiffness and increased deformability, potentially reflecting both alginate incorporation and the associated reduction in protein content. Protein extraction differed between pea and soy protein and was altered by alginate addition, indicating changes in protein accessibility, potentially reflecting both altered protein-polysaccharide interactions and the decreased protein content. Scaffold preparation altered surface morphology, with observed increased porosity upon ethanol treatment, especially in alginate-containing scaffolds. Cell experiments showed heterogeneous cell distribution, with observed localized cell accumulation in grooves and cavities.Overall, differences between protein sources were observed in processing behavior, structure, mechanical properties, and protein solubility, while alginate addition altered these properties to varying extents. These findings provide first insights into how formulation composition and scaffold preparation may influence scaffold architecture and cell distribution, for cultivated meat applications. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Lemoine C.
Title: A quantum manifestation principle for the classical–quantum boundary
Abstract: We propose an organizational principle for the classical–quantum boundary that focuses on the conditions under which non-classical effects become operationally manifest and experimentally certifiable. Standard decoherence theory explains why quantum signatures become latent in generic environments; we complement this by making explicit the physical conditions that render quantum manifestation robust. Building on Haroche’s cavity-QED experiments as a paradigmatic case, we show that measurable mode properties, namely frequencies, lifetimes, and couplings, depend on boundary conditions, environment, and preparation–measurement protocols. We formalize this through the framework (Ω,C,Ωeff(C),W,W∗(C)), where Ω denotes a reservoir of dynamical degrees of freedom, C the physical and protocol conditions, Ωeff(C) the context-induced effective modal structure, W a manifestation witness tied to the quantum effect under consideration, and W∗(C) a context-dependent certifiability threshold. A quantum effect is manifest when W(C)>W∗(C). We illustrate this principle with cavity QED, the Casimir effect, atomic clocks, and molecular matter-wave interferometry. The framework reformulates the classical–quantum boundary as a boundary of conditional manifestability rather than a dichotomy between system types. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Chapman University 2026.

Title: Fermentation-driven remodeling of whey macromolecules: Mechanisms, functional outcomes, and industrial implications
Abstract: Whey, a protein- and carbohydrate-rich dairy byproduct, presents significant valorization potential yet remains largely underutilized due to the high cost and energy intensity of conventional fractionation technologies. Fermentation offers a biologically driven, scalable alternative that fundamentally remodels whey macromolecules through microbially mediated enzymatic and metabolic cascades. This review critically examines fermentation-induced structural, conformational, and interactional modifications of whey proteins, glycoproteins, and associated carbohydrate fractions. We delineate how strain-specific proteolytic systems, pH-dependent conformational unfolding, and non-proteolytic transformations (e.g., glycation, phenolic–protein complexation, and microbial transglycosylation) govern macromolecular hydration, interfacial behavior, and network assembly. Integrated proteomic and metabolomic evidence demonstrates that optimal bioactivity and matrix stability emerge at a substrate-dependent degree of hydrolysis: 8–12% for sweet whey (native protein conformation), 6–10% for acid whey (partially denatured proteins), and 10–15% for pre-heat-treated whey (exposed hydrophobic domains). Beyond these thresholds, excessive cleavage compromises functional epitopes, triggers bitterness via hydrophobic 3–8 residue peptides, or exposes neo-allergens. By establishing a structure–function framework for fermentation-mediated whey remodeling, this work positions microbial bioprocessing as a precision tool for engineering next-generation hydrocolloid-functionalized dairy matrices, aligning with circular bioeconomy and sustainable food system objectives. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Formulation, physicochemical characterization, stability, and in vitro antioxidant and antidiabetic properties of chitosan-coated delphinidin-3-O-galactoside-loaded nano-nutriosomes
Abstract: The application of delphinidin-3-O-galactoside (D3Ga) in functional foods is limited by its environmental instability. This study formulated chitosan-coated nano-nutriosomes (CS-D3Ga-NS) using water-soluble dietary fiber and natural phospholipids through water-based self-assembly of the nano-nutriosome core followed by CS coating from dilute aqueous acetic acid. CS-D3Ga-NS exhibited 92.02% encapsulation efficiency, a particle size of 198.70 nm, and a ζ-potential of +41.23 mV, confirming successful CS deposition. Thermal analyses showed that CS coating increased the decomposition peak temperature to 270.83 °C and the residual mass to 18.2%, indicating enhanced thermal resistance. CS-D3Ga-NS maintained favorable physicochemical characteristics across pH 2.5–7.5 and ionic strengths up to 300 mM NaCl and exhibited an apparent D3Ga release of 10.08% at 24 h in PBS (pH 7.4) under the applied spectrophotometric conditions. During simulated gastrointestinal digestion, CS-D3Ga-NS showed significantly higher DPPH (10.69%) and ABTS (26.83%) radical-scavenging activities at the end of the intestinal phase than the uncoated formulation. The CS coating reduced post-digestion enzyme inhibition relative to the uncoated formulation (47.35% for α-glucosidase and 37.90% for α-amylase). Qualitative cellular uptake imaging using RH123 as a fluorescent surrogate showed stronger intracellular fluorescence for CS-coated than uncoated nano-nutriosomes in Caco-2 cells. These findings support CS-D3Ga-NS as a promising delivery platform for anthocyanin-based functional-food applications. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Convergence analysis of an asymptotic expansion regularization method for coefficient inverse problems in singularly perturbed time-periodic Burgers-type equations

Abstract: This article investigates time-periodic singularly perturbed reaction-diffusion-advection equations with internal transition layers and the associated coefficient inverse problems. We consider two benchmark reconstruction settings: recovery of a spatial coefficient F(x,t)=f(x) from snapshot-type data and recovery of a temporal coefficient F(x,t)=f(t) in the time-periodic solution setting from boundary data and transition-layer positions measured over one period. In the latter formulation, measurements are taken on one full periodicity interval only. In the numerical implementation, the noisy data are periodically extended before applying the link equation, and the resulting pointwise coefficient values are then smoothed. No additional independent measurements are used outside the measured period. The main contribution is a rigorous convergence analysis of asymptotic-based inversion algorithms for these two settings. We derive explicit error estimates that separate the effects of the asymptotic approximation, spatial or temporal discretization, and measurement noise. The analysis is supported by a sharp estimate for the transition-layer location. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted convergence behavior and illustrate the stability of the proposed reconstructions under noisy data. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Source term identification for a class of history-dependent quasi variational-hemivariational inequalities
Abstract: This article is devoted to the study of inverse problems related to the identification of the source term in a class of evolutionary history-dependent quasi-variational–hemivariational inequalities with constraints introduced in [S. Migórski, Y. Bai, S. Zeng, A new class of history-dependent quasi–variational–hemivariational inequalities with constraints, Commun. Nonlinear Sci. Numer. Simul. 114 (2022), 106686]. We establish the existence of solutions to the considered inverse problem. Furthermore, we illustrate the theoretical results by investigating a quasistatic frictional contact problem. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately recovering the unknown source term. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Li L.; Peng H.; Xia Y.; Huang M.
Title: Convergence analysis of Reshaped Wirtinger Flow with random initialization for phase retrieval
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: This paper investigates phase retrieval using the Reshaped Wirtinger Flow (RWF) algorithm, focusing on recovering a target vector x∈Rn from magnitude measurements yi=|〈ai,x〉|,i=1,…,m, under random initialization, where ai∈Rn are measurement vectors. For Gaussian random measurements, we prove that when m ≥ O(nlog2nlog3m), the RWF algorithm with random initialization achieves ϵ-accuracy within O(logn+log(1/ϵ)) iterations, thereby attaining nearly optimal sample and computational complexities. Moreover, we show that the RWF algorithm with random initialization remains stable under additive noise. Numerical experiments further demonstrate its robustness to initialization randomness and its stability even with relatively large step sizes. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: He W.; Xu Z.; Meng H.; Zhang J.; Zhu Q.; Liu H.; Liu Y.; Ying X.; Kang J.; Cui S.W.; Guo Q.
Title: Molecular structure governs intermolecular interactions and rheological properties of three seed mucilage polysaccharides
Abstract: Seed mucilage polysaccharides are promising plant-derived hydrocolloids. This study selected three seed mucilage polysaccharides: chia seed gum (CSG), Artemisia sphaerocephala Krasch polysaccharide (ASKP) and Plantago ovata seed mucilage (POSM), and elucidated the relationships between structure, intermolecular interaction and rheological relationship through structural characterization, chain conformational analysis and steady shear/oscillatory rheological measurements. Although all three samples consisted of two molecular fractions, they exhibited significant differences in molecular weight, degree of branching and uronic acid content. POSM has the highest molecular weight, exhibited the highest viscosity and the strongest intermolecular association, which was related to its highly branched structure promoting intermolecular hydrogen bonding. CSG had a lower molecular weight but a high terminal uronic acid content, causing its rheological behavior to be strongly influenced by electrostatic repulsion. ASKP exhibited weaker network formation, linked to weaker intermolecular interactions resulting from differences in its composition. These results indicate that molecular weight, branching structure, uronic acid content and intermolecular interactions collectively govern the rheological behavior of seed mucilage polysaccharides. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Author full names: Pastrana, Ester F. (59333942500); Mota-Santiago, Pablo (55102860000); Lillevang, Søren K. (7004682336); Krasowska, Marta (8581638300); Ahrné, Lilia (6701342068)
Title: Multi-scale structural fingerprinting of dairy emulsion gels using advanced X-ray scattering
Abstract: Understanding the structural evolution of dairy emulsion gels during storage is essential for controlling cheese quality and processing efficiency. This study presents a comprehensive multi-scale investigation of skimmed milk curd emulsion gels containing dairy fat during two weeks of cold storage, employing synchrotron-based ultra-small-angle, small-angle, and wide-angle X-ray scattering techniques combined with confocal laser scanning microscopy. This integrated approach bridges length scales spanning four orders of magnitude, from macroscopic fat globule arrangement to nanoscale protein-lipid interactions.Processing temperature strongly affected structural organisation: higher temperatures (85–90 °C) produced smaller, more monodisperse fat droplets (2 ± 1 μm versus 35 ± 25 μm at 70 °C) and increased lipid crystallisation intensity by a factor of 3–4. This behaviour contrasts with classical nucleation theory, which predicts reduced crystallisation in smaller droplets, and indicates that casein interfaces act as efficient heterogeneous nucleation sites rather than passive stabilisers. Crystalline lipid reflections persisted at 25 °C in the emulsion gels, i.e. 10 °C above the melting point of bulk milk fat, highlighting the strong stabilising effect of protein-lipid interfacial interactions on fat crystal thermal behaviour.Emulsion gels processed at 85 °C exhibited superior stability, with β′ polymorphic peaks (q ≈ 1.47–1.66 Å−1) remaining essentially unchanged in intensity over two weeks of storage, constant lamellar spacing (4.12–4.14 nm), and minimal change in colloidal calcium phosphate domains (≤2% change versus 11–55% at other temperatures). Title: Error Analysis of the Stabilized Finite Volume Method for Time-Dependent Incompressible MHD Equations with Rotational Velocity Correction
Source title: Advances in Applied Mathematics and Mechanics
Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a fully decoupled numerical method for solving the time-dependent incompressible magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) equations. The method features a rotational velocity correction technique, which is combined with the finite volume method to ensure both the local conservation of physical quantities. Using the lowest equal-order mixed finite element pair (P1 −P1 −P1 ) to approximate the velocity, magnetic field, and pressure, we address the inf-sup condition through pressure projection stabilization. A semi-implicit method is used to handle the nonlinear terms, and the rotational velocity correction method decouples the MHD system into three subsystems, thereby simplifying the computation and solution process. By selecting appropriate test functions and applying the Gronwall inequality, the stability of the numerical solution and optimal error estimates for velocity, magnetic field, and pressure are established. Finally, numerical results are presented to validate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the performance of the proposed method. © 2027 Global Science Press.
