Authors: Du Z.; Shou L.-Y.; Yao L.; Zhang Y.
Title: INCOMPRESSIBLE LIMIT FOR A NON-CONSERVATIVE COMPRESSIBLE TWO-FLUID MODEL
Source title: Communications on Pure and Applied Analysis
Abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for a non-conservative compressible two-fluid system, focusing on the stability of the incompressible limit in the regime of large bulk viscosity. A key challenge in this research lies in overcoming the mathematical difficulties induced by the non-conservative nature of the system and the strong coupling between the two fluids, especially when dealing with large initial data. In two dimensions, we address this challenge by constructing a unique global strong solution in Sobolev spaces for arbitrarily large initial velocities, provided that the bulk viscosity coefficients are chosen sufficiently large—this result breaks through the restriction of small initial data commonly required in related studies. In three dimensions, global well-posedness is established under an additional scaling-invariant smallness condition on the incompressible parts of the initial velocities, which is a necessary refinement to handle the more complex spatial structure in higher dimensions. To the best of our knowledge, we establish the first result on the global existence of large solutions for the high-dimensional non-conservative compressible two-fluid model without Korteweg terms. Furthermore, we rigorously justify the global-in-time convergence of large solutions from the compressible two-fluid system to the corresponding incompressible Navier–Stokes equations as the bulk viscosity coefficients tend to infinity, and explicit convergence rates are derived. In particular, we identify a novel diffusive initial-layer profile for the compressible velocity components and establish improved convergence rates for the remainder. © 2027, American Institute of Mathematical Sciences. Title: Interfacial bi − S bridging S-scheme Bi4O5Br2/In2S3 heterojunction for boosted photocatalytic CO2 reduction
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Photocatalytic CO2 reduction is constrained by sluggish CO2 activation and rapid photocarrier recombination. Herein, an interfacial Bi-S bridged S-scheme Bi4O5Br2/In2S3 heterojunction is constructed, in which the Bi-S bonds function as atomic-scale charge transfer channels that reinforce the built-in electric field and enable efficient S-scheme charge migration. The optimized BIS-6 delivers CO and CH4 evolution rates of 6.12 and 1.54 μmol g−1 h−1, which are 4.28 and 2.17 times higher than those of pristine Bi4O5Br2. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the S-scheme pathway spatially separates charge carriers while retaining high-energy electrons for CO2 reduction. In situ DRIFTS further identifies *COOH, *CO, *CHO and *CH3O as key intermediates, delineating a stepwise proton-coupled electron transfer pathway to CO and CH4. This research illustrates that the integration of interfacial chemical bonding with S-scheme charge migration provides a strategic approach for the design of efficient heterojunction photocatalysts. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Behavior of radially symmetric classical solutions to a chemotaxis system with spatially heterogeneous diffusion sensitivity
Abstract: This paper is focused on a parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel system with spatially dependent diffusion sensitivity {ut=∇·(|x|β∇u)−∇·(uα∇v),0=Δv−μ+u,μ=1|Ω|∫Ωu, with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions in a radially symmetric domain Ω=BR(0)⊂Rn(n≥1), and the initial data is radially symmetric Hölder continuous. Authors: Malau D.; Sopade P.A.
Title: Kinetics of starch digestion in Australian pigeonpea [Cajanus cajan (L.) Millsp.] genotypes and consequences for nutrient asynchrony
Abstract: In view of pigeonpea global food importance, the in-vitro starch digestibility of Australian genotypes ICPLs 14425, 86022, 88039, 90048, 91039, and 98011 was investigated, objectively revealing monophasic and biphasic digestograms. The digestograms were adequately modelled (r2 > 0.89, p < 0.001) by the 1- and 2-term exponential and non-exponential plus the recommended sequential modified first-order kinetic model. Genotypes ICPLs 86022, 88039, and 91039 were monophasic with digestion rates (KST x 10−3 min−1) 6.9-11.3. The biphasic genotypes ICPLs 14425, 90048, and 98011 exhibited a rapid-slow digestion phenomenon with KST 13.8–30.8 for the rapid first phase and 0.5–5.2 for the slow second phase. The maximum digestible starch (D∞, g/100g dry starch) ranged from 8.4 to 100.0, indicating remarkable genotypic differences (heterogeneous amylolysis), also revealed in the very rapidly (2.7–4.2), rapidly (3.9-9.8), and slowly (2.0–4.9) digestible and resistant (85.4–92.7) starches. Moreover, the genotypes significantly (p ≤ 0.05) differed in their low glycaemic indices (eGIAVG, 22.1–38.9%) and loads (eGL, 6.7–11.8%) relative to white wheat bread. The relative release (nutrient asynchrony) of amino acids and glucose during digestion was examined by comparing the starch hydrolysis index (HISTARCH) and eGIAVG (current study) with their protein parameters (HIPROTEIN, in-vitro protein digestibility [IVPDAVG], Malau & Sopade [2026]. Food Science and Processing 2 {2}: 8). The nutrients could be comparably released in ICPL 90048, but amino acids could be released slower in ICPL 14425 and faster in ICPLs 86022, 88039, 91039, and 98011. These results, hereby first reported, are valuable for global uses of pigeonpea. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Peng Y.; Lian L.; Tang Y.; Hong G.; Jiang J.
Title: Reversing the structural failure of reduced-salt meat protein gels via collagen: A clean-label physical-filling strategy
Abstract: Sodium reduction in meat products has been a long-standing challenge due to impaired myofibrillar protein functionality. This study investigated collagen as a clean-label filler to mitigate structural deterioration in reduced-salt (0.2 M NaCl) lamb myofibrillar protein - sarcoplasmic protein (MP-SP) emulsion gels. Collagen was incorporated at 1%–4%, with interfacial, microstructural and gelation properties evaluated against a 0.6 M NaCl benchmark. Optimal 2% collagen addition notably alleviated low-salt matrix degradation, bringing properties closer to regular-salt levels via enhanced hardness (+41.5%, P < 0.05) and water-holding capacity (+17.9%). Thermal unfolding of collagen exposed hydrogen-bonding sites to reinforce the low-salt network, elevating emulsifying activity index from 6.6 to 7.9 m2/g. Consistently, SDS-PAGE and microstructural analyses confirmed collagen acted as a non-covalent filler rather than inducing cross-linking. Excessive 4% collagen caused steric hindrance, impeding the degree of disulfide-mediated protein cross-linking (evidenced by fading 45–50 kDa bands) and compromising gel integrity. These findings suggest that collagen functions as a promising natural ingredient for enhancing the structural and water-binding properties, offering a viable strategy for premium reduced-salt meat emulsions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Methanobactin-Cu mediated ferulic acid dimerization in starch helical cavities for constructing highly stable starch-ferulic acid complex
Abstract: Traditional starch–ferulic acid composites fabricated via physical blending generally suffer weak intermolecular binding affinity and loose microstructures, while conventional catalytic agents only act on starch exterior and cannot realize efficient FA transformation within starch internal hydrophobic regions. In this work, a natural copper chaperone methanobactin-Cu (Mb-Cu) was used to mediate in-situ oxidative dimerization of ferulic acid (FA) in gelatinized starch matrix. Multi-scale structural characterizations confirmed that the possibility of FA dimer formation facilitated by Mb-Cu catalysis, which further interact with starch chains to reorganize short-range ordered conformation and build a dual supramolecular network containing V-type inclusion structures and intermolecular hydrogen-bonded crosslinks. Systematic physicochemical tests proved that this catalytic modification optimizes the pasting properties, viscoelasticity, freeze-thaw stability and anti-retrogradation performance of starch hydrocolloids. Meanwhile, the DPPH and ABTS radical scavenging capacities of modified starch were distinctly enhanced due to the production of FA dimers. In vitro digestion assays illustrated that Mb-Cu treatment reduces the proportion of rapidly digestible starch and raises slowly digestible as well as resistant starch fractions, along with decreased hydrolysis index and estimated glycemic index. This mild, food-grade bio-inspired catalytic method provides a feasible strategy to prepare stable, antioxidant and slow-digesting starch-FA complex, which exhibits promising prospects for functional food manufacture. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Wang Z.; Liu X.; Chen F.
Title: A graded-mesh adaptive Chebyshev spectral collocation method for fractional-order weakly singular integro-differential equations
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: This paper investigates the high-precision numerical solution of a class of weakly singular integro-differential equations involving Caputo fractional derivatives. For fractional-order weakly singular integro-differential equations, this paper adopts a graded-mesh adaptive method to partition the solution domain and separates the inherent weak singularity via variable transformations. On each subinterval of the graded-mesh adaptive partition, we construct a piecewise Chebyshev spectral collocation scheme to achieve high-order discretization of the equation. Furthermore, by exploiting the properties of fractional operators and the interpolation approximation error estimation theory, we rigorously analyze the convergence and stability of the proposed numerical method and establish the corresponding error estimates. Finally, several numerical examples are presented to verify the validity and high-order accuracy of the proposed method for solving fractional integro-differential equations with weakly singular kernels. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Peng C.; Jing Q.; Zhang R.; Chen M.; Yu R.
Title: Hierarchical contrastive learning for multi-modal representation in Alzheimer's disease diagnosis
Abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) diagnosis increasingly relies on the integration of multi-modal data, including structural magnetic resonance imaging, positron emission tomography and cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers. However, existing methods often inadequately explore the discriminative information within each modality and fail to fully capture complementary interactions between modalities. In this paper, we propose a hierarchical contrastive learning method which can fully utilize the intra-modal and inter-modal information, guiding the model to learn a well-structured feature space to improve the performance of diagnosis. Specifically, our method first introduces intra-modal alignment, which enforces supervised contrastive constraints within each modality, thereby effectively exploiting discriminative information between different clinically diagnosed groups. Secondly, we innovatively propose a clinical label-guided inter-modal alignment method to exploit the complementary interactions between modalities, leading to more discriminative and coherent representations. Furthermore, a dynamic learning strategy is employed between the intra-modal and inter-modal alignments to ensure the stability of the training process and achieve the comprehensive hierarchical contrastive learning. Experimental results on multiple datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches, validating its efficiency in learning discriminative multi-modal representations for AD related diagnosis. Title: Adaptive accelerated proximal gradient for controlled autoregressive moving average models with outliers in outputs
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: This paper develops an efficient approach for parameter estimation in controlled autoregressive moving average models. Outliers are detected by formulating the problem as Robust Principal Component Analysis, after which an adaptive accelerated proximal gradient algorithm is employed to reconstruct the uncontaminated information matrix. To accommodate large-scale data and obtain unbiased estimates, parameter identification is then performed using the recursive extended least squares algorithm. The simulation studies are provided to demonstrate the robustness and favorable performance of the proposed adaptive accelerated proximal gradient recursive extended least squares method. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Bag S.S.; Roy S.
Title: Fluorimetric detection of ethanol and discrimination from methanol using thioflavin T analogue substituted naphthalene diimide probe
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: The design of fluorescent probes capable of selectively detecting ethanol among common organic solvents and structurally similar alcohols, particularly methanol, remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report two core-substituted naphthalene diimide (NDI)-based fluorescent probes incorporating 4-(benzo[ d ]oxazol-2-yl)aniline ( ThT  O ), a thioflavin T analogue, at the NDI core, with either 2-ethylhexylamine (probe 1 , ThT  O  -NDI-EHA ) or N , N -dimethylethylenediamine (probe 2 , ThT  O  -NDI-DMEDA ) as the imide substituent. Comparative photophysical studies revealed that probe 1, bearing bulky and hydrophobic 2-ethylhexylimide groups, exhibited substantially higher selectivity toward ethanol than probe 2 . In ethanol, probe 1 displayed enhanced and red-shifted fluorescence emission, whereas common organic solvents and other alcohols, including methanol, predominantly caused fluorescence quenching with negligible spectral changes. This discrimination arises from distinct solvent-dependent microenvironmental effects and hydrogen-bonding-mediated aggregation, which modulate the excited-state dynamics of ThT  O  -NDI-EHA . Probe 1 showed excellent photostability in ethanol, with no significant variation in fluorescence intensity over 60 min of continuous monitoring. It also maintained a stable and reproducible absorption and fluorescence response over the pH range of 2–7, while preserving the characteristic emission difference between ethanol and methanol. This operational pH range encompasses that of common alcoholic beverages. In aqueous media, the progressive addition of ethanol produced an approximately 25-fold fluorescence enhancement relative to pure water, with a limit of detection of 0.181% (v/v), a limit of quantification of 0.72% (v/v), recoveries of 96–104%, and relative standard deviations of 2.89–6.02%. Probe 1 also enabled ethanol detection in commercial petroleum fuel, providing a limit of detection of 0.20% (v/v), a limit of quantification of 1.14% (v/v), recoveries of 98.61–105.50%, and relative standard deviations of 0.91–2.14%. Furthermore, the probe retained its sensing ability in the solid state, enabling ethanol-vapour detection. These findings establish probe 1 as a sensitive, selective, stable, and versatile fluorimetric platform for ethanol detection and methanol discrimination in solution, aqueous alcoholic matrices, petroleum fuel, and the vapour phase, highlighting its potential for portable and rapid on-site sensing applications. Authors: Yan J.; Li R.
Title: State-enhanced surrogate environment and multi-time-scale deep reinforcement learning for robotic grinding optimisation
Abstract: Robotic grinding parameter optimisation requires reliable evaluation of how candidate parameter actions affect grinding performance. Experimental construction of the evaluation relationship is costly, as each candidate parameter combination must be physically executed and measured. Surrogate environments can support virtual performance evaluation and reinforcement-learning-based optimisation. However, most existing approaches directly map pre-processing variables to final indicators, neglecting informative but difficult-to-measure intermediate process responses. This study proposes a state-enhanced surrogate environment and a multi-time-scale deep reinforcement learning (MTS-DRL) framework for robotic grinding optimisation. The surrogate environment estimates intermediate process responses to enrich the grinding-state representation and then evaluates action-conditioned grinding indicators through a multi-objective performance-estimation component. On this basis, the proposed MTS-DRL framework assigns temporal information according to the different roles of parameter generation, value feedback and environment-side performance evaluation, rather than using a single shared temporal horizon. The functional allocation enables parameter decisions to respond to recent process variations while incorporating longer-context effects on multiple grinding indicators. Robotic grinding experiments show that the proposed surrogate environment improves indicator-estimation reliability, and the MTS-DRL strategy achieves a better balance between surface quality and processing efficiency than representative baselines. Physical grinding trials further confirm the effectiveness of the learned policy for robotic grinding parameter recommendation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Shape optimization for the Stokes hemivariational inequality with slip boundary condition
Abstract: In this paper we study a shape optimization problem for a variational-hemivariational inequality describing the steady-state Navier-Stokes model of an incompressible fluid of the Bingham type in a bounded domain with a nonmonotone slip boundary condition. First, we provide results on the stability of solutions to the variational-hemivariational inequality on variations of the domain. Then, an existence result is proved for an optimal shape design problem for the variational-hemivariational inequality. Finally, we discuss the convergence of shape optimization problems for the regularized variational-hemivariational inequality when the regularization parameter tends to zero. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Tian A.-Y.; Song Y.-Y.; Meng F.-Y.-H.; Liu Y.-Y.; Yu H.-M.; Li L.-H.
Title: Emission-wavelength-associated interfacial electronic structure of biomass-derived full-color CDs@TiO2 for broad-spectrum photocatalytic degradation of organic pollutants
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Biomass-derived full-color carbon dots (BM-CDs) with tunable emission wavelengths are promising sustainable materials for constructing high-performance photocatalysts, yet the relationship between their emission characteristics and photocatalytic behavior remains unclear. To reveal how the emission-wavelength-dependent full-color BM-CDs relates to the interfacial electronic structure and photocatalytic behavior of BM-CDs@TiO2 composites, four BM-CDs emitting blue, green, yellow, and red light were combined with TiO2 via an impregnation-calcination method, and the resulting products were named Bl-, Gn-, Yl- and Rd-CDs@TiO2, respectively. All the obtained photocatalysts achieved over 85% degradation efficiency for various organic pollutants. Particularly, the Rd-CDs@TiO2 composite can achieve a degradation rate of 94.5% for tetracycline hydrochloride (TC) as the model pollutant within 120 min. The varying emission wavelengths of these BM-CDs are associated with distinct surface, structural and electronic properties, which govern the charge transfer and photocatalytic performance of the composites. Except for dual-emission Gn-CDs, the emission wavelength correlates with oxygen content and graphitization degree, yielding narrower bandgaps and more favorably aligned Fermi levels. Photoelectrochemical characterization confirmed that Yl-, Gn-, and Bl-CDs@TiO2 exhibit straddling-type structures. Interestingly, driven by the abundant oxygen-containing groups and the highly graphitization structure of Rd-CDs, Rd-CDs@TiO2 shows an interfacial charge-transfer pathway consistent with the S-scheme mechanism and thereby exhibits the best photocatalytic performance. Radical trapping experiment, density functional theory calculation, and mass spectrometric analysis identified that ·O2−, h+, and ·OH are the main active species in Rd-CDs@TiO2, and they revealed the free radical attack sites of TC and two degradation pathways. Ecotoxicity assessments and wheat seed germination tests indicated that Rd-CDs@TiO2 has reduced potential ecotoxicity. The stability test showed that after 10 cycles, the degradation efficiency of TC by Rd-CDs@TiO2 remained above 90%. This work elucidates how the property differences among homologous biomass-derived CDs affect the photocatalytic behavior of the composites, providing theoretical support for the design of green and highly efficient S-scheme heterojunction photocatalysts. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zhang T.; Gao C.
Title: Accelerated Bregman proximal point algorithm for solving the maximal monotone inclusion problem
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: We propose an Accelerated Bregman proximal point algorithm for solving maximal monotone inclusion problems. Unlike existing accelerated methods that are restricted to the Euclidean setting, our approach accommodates general Bregman distances, enabling broader applicability and avoiding costly subproblem computations in non-Euclidean settings. The algorithm achieves O(1/k) (k represents the iteration count) convergence rate in terms of a residual measure. In the Euclidean case, it recovers known inertial methods and reveals connections to Halpern iteration. Numerical experiments demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed method. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Lei L.; Zeng G.; Zhang Q.; Fan L.; Zhang D.
Title: KAN-MIFuseNet: pathological feature segmentation of myocardial infarction in LGE cardiac magnetic resonance imaging
Abstract: Late gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (LGE-MRI) is the gold standard for clinical diagnosis and quantitative assessment of myocardial infarction (MI). Accurate segmentation of myocardial scar and edema is essential for clinical decision-making and prognosis evaluation. However, challengs such as complex cardiac anatomy, blurred lesion boundaries, small target sizes, and low tissue contrast present significant difficulties for automatic segmentation. We propose KAN-MIFuseNet, a dual-branch encoder–decoder network. The SAM2 encoder extracts global semantic features, and the RegNet encoder captures local fine-grained details. A Unified Feature Alignment Module (UFAM) achieves dimensionality unification of the dual branches, while the Dual Attention Fusion Module (DAFM) performs adaptive multi-scale feature fusion. The Fast KAN Convolution Layer (FKCL) is a plug-and-play module that enhances nonlinear modeling capabilities. The decoder incorporates FKCL and CBAM with deep supervision to stabilize training. On the MyoPS 2020 dataset, this method achieved a scar segmentation Dice coefficient of 0.703 ± 0.315 and a combined scar and edema segmentation Dice coefficient of 0.723 ± 0.239, with an average score of 0.713, demonstrating significantly superior performance compared to traditional and advanced segmentation models. Ablation experiments confirmed the efficacy of DAFM and FKCL individually, while their synergistic application enhanced small target capture capability. Generalization experiments exhibited excellent performance on both the LGE-LVP and True datasets.The proposed network yields high accuracy and strong generalization, providing reliable support for clinical quantitative analysis of myocardial infarction. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Long J.; Wang S.; Liu C.
Author full names: Long, Jingyi (60081200300); Wang, Shengnan (54788634900); Liu, Chunlei (59538341100)
Title: Interfacial regulation of okara nanocellulose-reinforced chitosan films for enhanced mechanical performance and Larimichthys crocea preservation
Abstract: The increasing environmental burden caused by petroleum-based plastic packaging has accelerated the development of biodegradable food packaging materials. However, chitosan-based films still suffer from insufficient mechanical strength and barrier performance, and the role of okara-derived nanofibers in regulating film structure and functionality remains unclear. Therefore, this study developed pH-responsive chitosan (CS) composite films using okara nanofibers (OF) as reinforcing agents and ε-polylysine (EPL) and anthocyanins (Ant) as functional additives to elucidate their effects on interfacial interactions, network architecture, and preservation performance. The incorporation of effectively optimized the microscopic network architecture and enhanced the mechanical and hydrophobic properties of films. At a chitosan-to-OF ratio of 1:1, the water contact angle increased from 66.7° to 102.4°, corresponding to a 53.5% improvement in surface hydrophobicity. The optimal mechanical reinforcement was achieved at a CS/OF ratio of 2:5, where tensile strength increased from 2.25 MPa to 11.41 MPa, while elongation at break decreased. Meanwhile, water vapor permeability decreased from 6.1 × 10−12 to 3.6 × 10−12 g cm/(cm2·s·Pa), and oxygen permeability was reduced by 13.6%. Authors: Li C.; Li Z.; Yang B.; Wang S.; Liu J.; Wang J.; Wu D.; Huang J.; Ni Y.; Cao L.; Wang Z.; Chen L.
Title: Hierarchical food hydrogels for co-delivery of bioactives: Structure design and gastrointestinal fate
Abstract: Hydrogels are increasingly used as food-grade soft-matter matrices to improve the stability, dispersibility, and digestive performance of bioactive compounds. However, conventional single-network hydrogels often fail to meet the demands of multicomponent functional foods, especially when bioactives differ in polarity, stability, sensory impact, and digestion-related release behavior. This review considers hierarchical hydrogels as structurally organized food matrix systems and systematically discusses their roles in bioactive co-delivery. First, the assembly functions of major food-grade building blocks are summarized, including polyelectrolyte polysaccharides, amphiphilic proteins and polysaccharides, neutral and structural polysaccharides, and functional small molecules. Then, molecular, nanoscale, microscale, and macroscale architectures, such as double networks, interpenetrating networks, nanocomposites, emulsion-filled gels, bigels, core-shell systems, multilayer structures, and anisotropic hydrogels, are analyzed in terms of their contributions to mechanical stability, compartmentalized loading, interfacial stabilization, texture modulation, and digestion-responsive release. Particular attention is paid to the co-delivery of hydrophilic and hydrophobic bioactives, where hierarchical compartmentalization improves component compatibility, reduces premature loss, and supports combined functional performance in food systems. Beyond encapsulation and protection, this review further links hydrogel structures with oral processing, gastric swelling and retention, intestinal enzyme accessibility, lipid digestion, bioaccessibility, and colonic fermentation, emphasizing that hydrogel architecture not only affects bioactive protection and release, but also determines sensory quality, digestive behavior, and nutritional functionality. Finally, future perspectives are proposed regarding predictable structural design, scalable food processing, dynamic digestion evaluation, clean-label formulation, and the development of consumer-acceptable functional foods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Electro-assembly of soy protein and konjac glucomannan into biomimetic scaffolds for cultured meat: Structural and biological performance
Abstract: Anisotropic porous scaffolds for cultured meat were fabricated by freeze-dried soy protein isolate (SPI) and konjac glucomannan (KGM) hybrid hydrogels aligned under a low-voltage electric field. The scaffolds exhibited well-defined oriented pore structures with porosity exceeding 80%, where freezing temperature governed pore architecture: scaffolds prepared at −20 °C produced pores of 50–200 μm, while −80 °C generated finer pores (0–100 μm). SEM analysis revealed an ordered lamellar structure, and mechanical testing further demonstrated higher transverse strength than longitudinal strength. Optimal KGM content (1.0–1.5 wt%) enhanced stiffness (up to 160 kPa), whereas excessive KGM (2.0–2.5 wt%) reduced mechanical strength to 40-80 kPa. The scaffolds displayed excellent water absorption (800%–1147%) and maintained structural integrity after swelling (KGM concentrations: 1.0–2.5 wt%). C2C12 myoblasts showed high seeding efficiency (up to 90%) with enhanced robust adhesion, proliferation, and differentiation. Scaffolds prepared at −20 °C, with pore sizes of 50–200 μm, provided a more favorable microenvironment for cell growth, whereas the overly dense structure formed at −80 °C likely limited cell proliferation and nutrient diffusion. Notably, constructs fabricated at −80 °C with 1.5 wt% KGM achieved excellent mechanical properties (∼56 kPa). This study established an in-house, laboratory-scale, low-voltage direct-current electric-field system and provides a potential sustainable strategy for designing anisotropic scaffolds for cultured meat and highlights the potential of hydrogels in next-generation food and biomedical applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Extruded cornmeal improves freeze-thaw stability of wheat dough by restricting water mobility
Abstract: In frozen cereal-based foods, water is not only a structural plasticizer but also a destructive phase-change medium. Temperature fluctuations during frozen storage promote water migration and ice recrystallization, which weaken the gluten-starch matrix and lead to cracking, water loss, and textural deterioration. Existing strategies mainly rely on gluten reinforcement or hydrocolloid addition, whereas starch-rich non-gluten ingredients are often regarded as formulation diluents because they disrupt dough network formation. This study investigated whether extrusion can convert cornmeal into a functional water-state regulator that improves the freeze-thaw stability of wheat dough. Wheat flour (CK), wheat flour containing 15% native cornmeal (NC-15) and wheat flour containing 15% extruded cornmeal (ECM-15) were compared. ECM-15 significantly reduced freezable water content (from 71.85% in CK to 51.63%, a reduction of 28.14%) and melting enthalpy, and showed the lowest water loss throughout five freeze-thaw cycles. Low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (LF-NMR) analysis revealed restricted water mobility in ECM-containing dough, indicating that extrusion-modified starch immobilized water fractions that would otherwise contribute to freezing and migration. Consistently, ECM-15 exhibited higher water-holding capacity, swelling power and farinograph water absorption, together with lower pasting viscosity and setback. X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, and Raman analyses indicated that these effects arose from extrusion-induced amorphization and short-range disordering of starch, rather than simple cornmeal addition. Notably, this improvement was achieved despite reduced dough mixing stability, indicating that extrusion-induced water-state regulation offers a label-friendly strategy for frozen dough improvement, distinct from conventional gluten reinforcement. Title: Importance of complex type for structure and stability of pectin-gelatin assemblies: precipitates, coacervates, soluble, and co-soluble complexes
Abstract: Protein-polysaccharide complexes can be classified into four types based on structural characteristics and phase behavior: precipitates (PPT), complex coacervates (CC), soluble complexes (SC), and co-soluble polymers (CSP). However, the majority of studies focused primarily on their preparation and characterization without clearly distinguishing these four categories, leading to inconsistent conclusions and potential ambiguity. In this study, the structural differences among PPT, CC, SC, and CSP were systematically compared at three mixing ratios (1:1, 1:3, and 1:6). Confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM) results revealed significant differences in microstructure, with PPT exhibiting large, irregular aggregates. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) analyses indicated stronger interactions in PPT and CC than in SC and CSP. Fluorescence measurements showed that PPT exhibited the highest fluorescence intensity, while CC displayed the lowest, suggesting a highly folded gelatin conformation in PPT. The curcumin encapsulation efficiencies of PPT and CC (>96%) were significantly higher than those of CSP (48.6%-67.9%). The formation of pectin-gelatin complexes markedly improved curcumin thermal stability and photostability. CC prepared at a 1:1 ratio exhibited the highest thermal stability (75.08%) and photostability (71.98%) for curcumin. All four complexes exhibited pH-responsive color changes, with CSP showing the fastest response. Title: A pre-deployment framework for simulation-driven optimization of robotized manufacturing tasks
Abstract: The pre-deployment configuration of robotic workcells encompasses layout design, task allocation, motion planning, and safety assessment. Despite their strong interdependence, these aspects are still largely addressed through expert knowledge and empirical rules, often in a sequential manner and without a formal optimization framework. This paper proposes a simulation-driven optimization framework that jointly optimizes these interdependent domains during the early design stages. To ensure general applicability, we formulate the overall problem as a hierarchy of nested optimization layers, each dedicated to a specific domain of the robotic task, while accounting for the coupling between them. The overall problem is treated as a black-box iterative optimization, where the unknown underlying function is replaced by a high-fidelity digital model, allowing to evaluate system performance through simulation rather than analytical cost functions. By decoupling domain-specific decisions while preserving their inter-dependencies, the proposed approach can be flexibly applied to heterogeneous scenarios, ranging from fully autonomous robotic operations to human–robot collaborative assemblies within the same manufacturing cell. The framework is evaluated on representative robotic tasks, including both collaborative and human-free scenarios, and its performance is compared against experience-based design solutions. The results show that the proposed method consistently attains better performances than the benchmark strategies enforced as a baseline, demonstrating its effectiveness as a systematic alternative to traditional heuristic-driven design practices. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Single-channel wearable EEG for ADL recognition in Healthy and Epileptic cohorts using MODWT-MRA and machine learning
Abstract: Wearable single-channel EEG is increasingly used to monitor epileptic patients outside the clinic, but the physical activity of daily living (ADL) continuously shapes the recorded signal. This activity-coupled variability is typically discarded as noise, even though it holds recoverable contextual information. Until now, EEG-based human activity recognition (HAR) has been studied almost exclusively in healthy participants under controlled lab conditions, leaving ADL recognition in clinical epileptic populations unaddressed. Title: Elliptic quasivariational-hemivariational inequalities in the Beppo-Levi space
Abstract: In this paper, we study elliptic quasivariational-hemivariational inequalities in the Beppo–Levi space D1,p(RN), where both the constraint set and the associated energy functional depend on the unknown solution. Title: Physical and oxidative stabilization of high internal phase emulsions using flaxseed press cake powder as a direct-use ingredient: An extraction-free shortcut
Abstract: Flaxseed press cakes (FPCs), a by-product of cold-pressed oil extraction, are a rich source of bioactive and functional compounds. However, their valorization relies on costly and time-consuming extraction processes. This study evaluated powdered FPC as a scalable, dual-functional ingredient for the physical and oxidative stabilization of high internal phase emulsions (HIPEs), as a basic food model system for potential future formulations. Title: pH-dependent structural properties, air–water interfacial behavior, and foam stability of fibrillated egg white protein
Abstract: Fibrillation is an effective approach for enhancing the interfacial functionality and foam stability of egg white protein (EWP). Title: Gallic acid modulates the balance among network structure, water stability, and antioxidant function in corn peptide-konjac glucomannan gels
Abstract: Plant-based gels increasingly need to reconcile mechanical integrity, water stability and bioactivity, yet most designs still rely on intact proteins whose folded or aggregated structures limit molecular accessibility. Corn peptide (CP) offers a distinct but underused route: a short-chain, mobile and chemically exposed plant-peptide fraction with intrinsic antioxidant potential, but limited ability to form self-supporting networks. This study treated CP as an interaction-active, network-modulating component within a konjac glucomannan (KGM) scaffold and examined how gallic acid (GA) concentration translated peptide-associated reactivity into macroscopic gel performance. At 0.3% GA, the gel combined low syneresis and freeze-thaw water loss, shorter water-relaxation times, high cohesiveness, rapid stress relaxation, and greater microstructural continuity. Higher GA levels further enhanced ABTS and T-AOC responses but were associated with larger operational hydrophobic-association indices and reduced network uniformity. Operational extraction indices and FTIR changes were consistent with concentration-dependent reorganization of non-covalent association. Title: pH-dependent thermal assembly of β-lactoglobulin colloids regulated by chlorogenic acid and cyanidin-3-O-glucoside with exploratory evaluation in a mulberry fruit powder matrix

Colloidal differences were most evident after the 105 °C treatment; at pH 7, similar zeta potentials but distinct particle-size distributions indicated that apparent surface charge alone did not account for colloidal organization. Functional responses were likewise condition specific. CQA showed the clearest positive deviation from the calculated additive ABTS expectation at pH 7, whereas enzymatic accessibility and antibody recognition varied with ligand identity, pH, and processing condition. Title: A fast adaptive finite element method for nonlocal diffusion problems on octree-based adaptive Cartesian multilevel mesh formulation
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: We propose a novel adaptive finite element method (AFEM) algorithm for nonlocal problems discretized on an n-dimensional Cartesian mesh. We prove that when the nonlocal kernel function is radially symmetric, the number of distinct entries in the stiffness matrix on the Cartesian mesh depends only on the mesh depth. Based on this property, a fast assembly algorithm is designed to reduce the computational cost of solving nonlocal problems with AFEM. Numerical experiments successfully implement adaptive solutions for 2D and 3D nonlocal problems, verifying the effectiveness of the new AFEM algorithm. © 2026

Title: La3+-Doped Bi3NbO7: mechanisms of morphological–lattice–electronic structure synergistic reconstruction and enhanced photocatalytic performance

Abstract: Solar-driven water treatment has attracted increasing attention as energy transition and environmental remediation continue to advance. La3+ incorporation altered the crystal growth, morphology, and electronic structure of Bi3NbO7. Among these, 9%La-BNO exhibited the best photocatalytic activity, achieving a TC removal rate of 95.7% within 90 min, with a degradation rate 4.58 times that of pure Bi3NbO7. Further analysis combining LC–MS, molecular electrostatic potential, and Fukui function theoretical calculations identified the potential reaction sites for TC and inferred its degradation pathway. Title: Retinal Recombination: A robust augmentation and synthesis of retinal images with annotation fusion
Abstract: Medical image synthesis has become a crucial research topic for enhancing image analysis software. The relatively small size of available datasets, the lack of ground-truth annotations, and the poor quality of registered images are among the driving reasons for the development of novel algorithms. Recently, neural network architectures for image generation, such as generative adversarial networks, have achieved high fidelity in this domain. However, the remaining problems include high computational cost, low output resolution, and inconsistent synthetic features. To address these limitations, we propose a novel retinal image augmentation and synthesis algorithm that decomposes real images, augments their components, and recombines them into new, unique samples. Further, we introduce a method for optic disc transfer based on image statistics and blood vessel geometry augmentation based on entropy maximisation. Our approach works at a scalable resolution on standard personal computers, transfers the annotations from the original images, and enables the fusion of features from labelled and unlabelled datasets. Two ophthalmologists evaluated the synthetic image quality, and we validated our method using four publicly available datasets, showing the ability to preserve segmentation masks, statistically significant improvements in optic nerve head segmentation, and the impact on pathology classification. Title: Sr2InSbO6:Er3+ phosphor: A versatile dual-functional platform for non-contact thermometry and CO2 Photoreduction

Abstract: In this paper, Sr2InSbO6:Er3+ up-conversion phosphors for multifunctional applications were successfully prepared by high-temperature solid-phase reaction in air atmosphere. First-principles calculations based on density-functional theory (DFT) are utilized to determine the crystal structure, phonon composition, and electron distribution. The crystal structure and optical properties of the materials were also investigated using infrared spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, and UV–vis diffuse reflectance spectroscopy. Luminescence spectra demonstrate that Sr2InSbO6:Er3+ emits bright orange light under excitation by 980 nm near-infrared light, and further investigation has been conducted into the luminescence properties and thermal stability. Title: The effect of methoxypectin on the permeation of cyanidin-3-O-glucoside through the mucus layer and its in vivo absorption and distribution
Abstract: The low absorption of anthocyanins limits their health benefits. This study investigated the effects of low-methoxy citrus pectin (LCP) on the aggregation structure and mucin-interface behavior of the cyanidin-3-O-glucoside (C3G) complex, and how these factors influence its mucus/barrier migration and in vivo exposure. Among different LCP:C3G mass ratios, PC-1-1 (1:1) exhibited a higher binding rate, smaller particle size, and a relatively uniform rod-like aggregate structure, and demonstrated the highest permeability in both the mucin model and the Caco-2/HT29-MTX co-culture model, with Papp values 52.10% and 81.9% higher than those of free C3G, respectively. Three-phase analysis revealed that PC-1-1 has a lower contact angle, higher apparent diffusion rate, and lower bioadhesion. Thermodynamic and disruptor experiments indicated that at pH 5.2, LCP-C3G interacts with mucin primarily through hydrophobic interactions, whereas at pH 7.4, both hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions are involved. In vivo studies in mice showed that LCP-C3G increased systemic exposure of the prototype C3G and reduced its excretion in urine and feces. Overall, changes in the aggregate structure of the complex and its interfacial behavior with mucin, induced by different LCP:C3G composition ratios, were closely correlated with its mucus/trans-barrier migration and in vivo exposure profiles. Specifically, a 1:1 ratio forms smaller, relatively uniform aggregate structures and exhibits better wetting, faster diffusion, and lower adhesion—consistent with its higher migration and in vivo exposure levels. This supports the correlation between the complex structure and its migration and absorption properties, providing a basis for the rational design of pectin-based anthocyanin delivery systems. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Akhbari M.; Nazmdeh V.
Title: High-performance brain tumor classification via transfer learning with fully fine-tuned and modified CNN architectures
Abstract: Accurate and timely brain tumor diagnosis remains challenging due to the limitations of manual MRI interpretation. This study introduces a transfer learning framework using six fully fine–tuned and modified CNN architectures DenseNet169, InceptionV3, Xception, ResNet50, InceptionResNetV2, and EfficientnetB0 each equipped with a redesigned classification head. The proposed head combines global average pooling with four dense layers (1024, 512, 256, 128 neurons) incorporating ReLU activation, Batch Normalization, and Dropout to enhance generalization. The models were trained on the Kaggle Brain Tumor MRI dataset containing 7,023 images across four tumor classes, using data augmentation and five–fold stratified cross–validation for robust evaluation. Results show that the modified CNNs achieve state–of–the–art performance, with InceptionResNetV2 obtaining the highest accuracy (98.7%) and F1–score (98.7%) with minimal overfitting. Xception and DenseNet169 also demonstrated strong performance with lower computational cost. Overall, the proposed fully fine–tuned architectures provide an efficient and reproducible solution for automated brain tumor classification, supporting radiologists and improving diagnostic workflow efficiency. © 2026

Title: EMG-SegNet: rethinking the U-shaped paradigm with efficient multi-scale feature aggregation and global coordinate attention for medical image segmentation
Abstract: U-shaped architectures have become the dominant framework for medical image segmentation and have achieved remarkable performance across various tasks. However, their reliance on complex encoder–decoder designs and progressive resolution recovery leads to high computational costs, limiting their applicability in resource-constrained scenarios. To address this issue, we propose a lightweight E-shaped segmentation framework, termed EMG-SegNet, which improves segmentation performance while significantly reducing model complexity. In the decoder, Multi-scale Dilated Feature Aggregation is designed to enlarge the effective receptive field during feature fusion without introducing additional spatial downsampling, thereby enhancing multi-scale contextual modeling on the reconstructed high-resolution feature representation. In addition, a Global Grouped Coordinate Attention module is designed to adaptively recalibrate feature representations by leveraging global spatial dependencies, thereby enhancing discriminative capability. Extensive experiments conducted on three 2D medical image segmentation benchmarks, including Synapse, ACDC, and a self-collected ear canal dataset, demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art U-shaped models across multiple evaluation metrics while using significantly fewer parameters. These results indicate that our approach achieves a favorable balance between accuracy and efficiency, providing a promising direction for lightweight medical image segmentation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: DARE: Domain-Aware Representation Enhancement for data-efficient histopathological tissue classification
Abstract: Deep learning (DL) has achieved remarkable progress in medical image analysis. However, its success critically depends on large-scale, expert-annotated datasets, which are costly and impractical to obtain in clinical practice. This limitation is further aggravated by the inherent heterogeneity of medical imaging across institutions, making it even more challenging to curate reliable and consistent datasets. Therefore, DL models trained on a single dataset often exhibit limited generalizability and poor transferability especially under the limited training data scenario. To address these challenges in the Histopathological Tissue classification task, we propose a novel framework named Domain-Augmentation via Representative Enrichment (DARE), which integrates two data augmentation strategies within an advanced lightweight deep broad learning system for targeted domain adaptation. First, we analyze the source-domain dataset in the feature space and argue that, a single global statistic is insufficient to fully characterize the source-domain distribution under limited training data scenario. Therefore, we introduce DARE†, a pseudo-domain partition-based feature-space augmentation strategy. By partitioning the limited source-domain data into multiple pseudo-domains via the thought of sampling, DARE† extracts diverse statistical representations that enrich domain variability and thereby improve generalization to the target domain. Second, recognizing that the original image space fundamentally shapes the feature space, we further design DARE*, an image-level augmentation scheme. DARE* directly increases the diversity of source-domain images, complementing the feature-space augmentation and further enhancing the model's robustness to domain shift. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our proposed methods achieve consistent performance improvements on target domains under extremely limited source-domain training scenarios. Title: Threshold dynamics of a reaction-diffusion population model with seasonal succession, periodic delays and mating behaviors
Abstract: We investigate a reaction-diffusion, stage-structured model for amphibian populations that incorporates seasonal succession, temperature-dependent maturation delays, and a mating-based birth function. The model captures the joint effects of seasonal fluctuations, spatial heterogeneity, and mating behaviors on long-term population dynamics. Since the system cannot be linearized at zero, we introduce a linearizable auxiliary system on an appropriate quotient space and establish its strong monotonicity. Title: Consensus and flocking with transmission and reaction delays
Abstract: We investigate consensus formation and flocking behavior in multi-agent systems subject to two distinct types of delay: a transmission delay accounting for information exchange between agents, and a reaction delay representing the processing time before agents adjust their states. For a simplified linear two-agent system, we analyze how these delays affect asymptotic stability. We then derive sufficient conditions for asymptotic consensus and flocking in the general multi-agent setting with a nonlinear, globally positive influence function. These conditions require the delays to be sufficiently small relative to the initial data and the decay rate of the influence function. The analysis is based on a Lyapunov functional approach combined with a Grönwall–Halanay-type inequality. Our results establish rigorous sufficient conditions under which collective behavior emerges in delayed multi-agent systems where both communication and reaction lags are non-negligible, with applications to biological, social, and engineered systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A free boundary analysis of tumor invasion driven by angiogenesis
Abstract: We discuss a free boundary model for tumor invasion that describes a cloud of cells that diffuse and, at the same time, are drifted along the vector field of the chemotactic direction. Title: A deep learning approach for pricing convertible bonds with path-dependent reset and call provisions

Abstract: This paper develops a deep learning framework for pricing convertible bonds with path-dependent downward reset and issuer call provisions governed by rolling-window triggers. Title: Projection graph convolution and variable-granularity feature shuffling with spatiotemporally separated feature enhancement: A lightweight 3D GCN for human action recognition

Title: Effect of atmospheric cold plasma treatment on the structural characteristics and gel properties of hemp protein isolate
Abstract: Hemp protein isolate (HPI) is a promising plant protein source owing to its balanced amino acid composition and low allergenicity; however, its propensity for aggregation severely limits its functional and gel properties. Title: Emulsion-stabilizing properties of sorghum protein ingredients with various tannin contents

Title: Near-field 3-D SAR imaging with periodically selected array elements via sparse reconstruction
Abstract: Sparse reconstruction has been widely adopted in near-field three-dimensional (3-D) synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging, as it reduces the amount of array-domain measurements while maintaining high imaging quality. However, existing sparse reconstruction methods are mostly developed under random, nonuniform, or specifically designed sparse acquisition strategies, which may complicate system implementation or require modifications to the acquisition mechanism. Such sampling pattern complicates the position-control logic and requires tighter position-control accuracy during scanning, which limits its practical application. To address this, this study proposes a sparse reconstruction method for near-field 3-D SAR imaging from periodically selected array elements. Specifically, the aliasing mechanism is first analyzed, and then an explicit expression for the location-dependent nonlinear distortion aliasing is formulated. Subsequently, we construct a frequency-domain aliasing reduction regularization for range-slice reconstruction within the considered imaging range. Based on this, a corresponding optimization model is established for the range-slice image reconstruction. Finally, we unfold the sparse reconstruction procedure into a deep network with fixed layers and learnable parameters. Experimental results on both simulated and measured data demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method in aliasing reduction and sparse imaging for periodically selected array-domain data. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Stage-aware and roughness-constrained diffusion policy for multi-stage robotic polishing
Abstract: Polishing is a critical finishing process in high-end manufacturing fields such as aerospace, where surface quality directly affects the service performance and reliability of components. Robotic imitation learning provides a flexible solution for such tasks, but current methods remain limited in industrial polishing because of long-horizon dependencies, uncertain stage transitions, and the difficulty of modeling and regulating coupled process parameters. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Stage-Aware and Roughness-Constrained Diffusion Policy (SRDP) for robotic polishing. SRDP infers the process-stage posterior from multimodal observation histories and uses it to condition the shared reverse denoising process, enabling stage-consistent action generation without external stage labels during execution. Furthermore, a roughness-oriented process-constrained diffusion sampling method is incorporated to generate constrained feed speed and normal contact force under stage-wise preset spindle speeds, thereby improving process consistency and physical feasibility. Systematic experiments are conducted on two representative scenarios, namely spacecraft cabin coating-surface polishing and inner-cavity structural surface finishing. Comparisons with advanced baselines, ablation studies, and real-robot validations comprehensively evaluate the proposed method. The results show that SRDP improves stage-transition stability, process-parameter consistency, and final surface quality across different polishing scenarios. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: LLM-agent-based explicit-implicit interaction fusion for human-robot collaborative Assembly
Abstract: In human-robot collaboration (HRC), explicit and implicit interactions typically follow distinct workflows: explicit interactions are actively initiated by the operator to convey task objectives, while implicit interactions are continuously perceived and responded to by the system to adapt robot behavior to the current collaboration context. Existing HRC systems often handle these interaction types separately, lacking a unified cognitive and decision-making mechanism, which can lead to interaction conflicts, execution interruptions, or delayed safety responses in complex scenarios. Although large language models (LLMs) demonstrate tremendous potential in reasoning, they have yet to effectively integrate explicit and implicit interactions into robotic decision-making. To address this, this paper proposes an LLM-Agent-based framework for explicit-implicit interaction fusion, which models both types of input within a unified semantic space and incorporates a two-stage fusion decision mechanism in LLM reasoning. This framework helps robots maintain consistent responses to task objectives and mitigate potential collaborative safety risks. Preliminary small-scale experimental results on representative HRC tasks reveal favorable trends in task completion ratio, collaborative safety performance and decision consistency when compared with the baseline scheme without explicit-implicit fusion. The proposed method provides an interpretable and scalable approach for deploying LLM-based HRC systems in real-world settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Controlled ball milling enhances the lubrication performance of proso millet flour dispersions
Abstract: Proso millet flour (PMF) is a sustainable cereal ingredient with significant potential for nutritional and functional food applications. The improved hydration increased the bulk apparent viscosity and promoted the formation of a soft, hydrated, and viscous adsorbed film, thereby reducing friction through the development of a load-bearing lubricating layer. Title: Divalent cation-mediated regulation of the hierarchical structure and rheological properties of ovalbumin fibrils
Abstract: Metal ions can regulate the structural organization and macroscopic properties of protein fibrillar assemblies. Although previous studies have extensively examined ion-mediated regulation of protein fibrillation, the effects of divalent cations on the hierarchical organization of preformed egg-protein fibrils remain poorly understood. In this study, OVA fibrils were prepared by heating the protein at pH 2.0 and 90 °C for 8 h, after which Mg2+, Zn2+, Ca2+, or Fe2+ was added to evaluate the effect of each ion on the post-formation organization and properties of the preformed fibrils. Divalent-cation treatment caused ion-dependent changes in the secondary-structure distribution, colloidal properties, microscopic morphology, and rheological behavior of the preformed OVA fibrils. These changes were attributed to post-formation interfibrillar association, aggregation, and structural reorganization rather than enhanced fibril formation. All OVA fibril systems showed partial precipitation at 500 mM, indicating loss of colloidal stability rather than homogeneous hydrogel formation. ICP-MS revealed ion-dependent differences in apparent metal retention. Collectively, these findings demonstrated that divalent cations regulated the hierarchical organization and rheological properties of preformed OVA fibrils through ion-dependent post-formation structural reorganization, providing a basis for controlling the functionality of egg-protein fibrillar materials. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Effect of soy protein aggregate morphology on interfacial behavior and stability of plant-based emulsion foams
Abstract: This study investigated the structure-function relationship of soy protein isolate (SPI), soy protein fibrous aggregates (SPF), and soy protein aggregates (SPA) in modulating three-phase emulsion foams under varying oil volume fractions (10%–30%). Consequently, SPF formed a continuous, mechanically robust viscoelastic network at the oil–water interface, exhibiting superior complex dilatational moduli and low energy dissipation in nonlinear Lissajous analysis. In contrast, the rigid, compact conformation of SPA severely restricted molecular mobility and steric unfolding, resulting in compromised surface activity. Under whipping, SPF-stabilized systems exhibited extraordinary structural integrity and stability (96.95%), driven by enhanced interfacial protein concentration and controlled partial coalescence of fat globules, which established a resilient skeletal network that immobilized bubbles and retarded drainage. Conversely, SPA foams exhibited low firmness, minimal overrun, and severe coalescence. Viscosity and dynamic rheology further confirmed that SPF-stabilized emulsions possessed enhanced deformation resistance, maintaining a uniform droplet architecture even at a 30% oil fraction. Title: Effect of low - methoxy pectin, heat treatment and pH on interfacial properties of purified cricket protein
Abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of cricket protein isolate at A/W and O/W interfaces on their interfacial rheology. Title: On set-like sunflower-free families of subspaces over finite fields
Abstract: The Erdos–Rado sunflower problem admits two natural analogues in finite vector spaces, corresponding to two different ways of generalizing the set-theoretic notion of a sunflower. The first, used by Ihringer and Kupavskii [FFA 110 (2026) 102746], requires the petals to be in general position over the kernel; the second, used in the subspace codes literature (cf. Etzion–Raviv [DAM 186 (2015) 87-97], Blokhuis–De Boeck–D’haeseleer [DCC 90 (2022) 2101-2111]), requires only that the kernel equals the pairwise intersection of distinct petals. We refer to the second version as a set-like sunflower, following Blokhuis, De Boeck, and D’haeseleer [4]. In this note, we focus on the set-like setting. We first observe by illustrations that general-position sunflower-freeness does not imply set-like sunflower-freeness. We then present a construction of set-like s-sunflower-free families of k-spaces in F_q^n for ⌈(n+1)/2⌉≤ k≤ n-1, of size (and for even q), based on a manipulated version of the lifting construction; to our knowledge, this is the first systematic construction tailored to this setting. Finally, we compare the size of the construction with the exact optimum for small parameters, computed by exhaustive search. © 2027 American Institute of Mathematical Sciences

Title: The complex Ginzburg-Landau equation on a finite interval and chaos suppression via a finite-dimensional boundary feedback stabilizer
Abstract: In this paper, we study the well-posedness and boundary stabilization of the initial-boundary value problem for the complex Ginzburg-Landau (CGL) equation on a finite interval. First, we establish a local well-posedness theory for the open-loop model in L 2-based fractional Sobolev spaces in the case of Dirichlet-Neumann type inhomogeneous mixed boundary conditions. This local well-posedness result is based on linear estimates derived by using the weak solution formula obtained via the unified transform (also known as the Fokas method). Next, we study the global well-posedness properties of the open-loop model in presence of inhomogeneous boundary conditions. Then, we turn our attention to the rapid boundary feedback stabilization problem and design a nonlocal controller which uses a finite number of Fourier modes of the state of solution. This design relies on the fact that solutions of the CGL equation can be separated into a slow, finite-dimensional component and a rapidly decaying tail, with the former primarily governing long-term behavior. We determine the necessary number of modes required to stabilize the system at a specified rate. Additionally, we identify the minimum number of modes that ensure stabilization at an unspecified decay rate. These theoretical results are validated by numerical simulations. The spatiotemporal estimates established in the first part of the paper are also employed to obtain local solutions of the controlled system. The existence of global energy solutions follows from stabilization estimates, while uniqueness follows from the uniqueness of an associated initial-boundary value problem with homogeneous boundary conditions whose solutions are in correspondence with the solutions of the original system through a bounded invertible Volterra-type integral transform on Sobolev spaces. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Nonregular graphs with a given maximum degree attaining the maximum spectral radius

Title: An unconditionally energy-dissipative compact scheme with a convergent two-grid solver for the Swift-Hohenberg equation
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: The Swift-Hohenberg equation is a fourth-order nonlinear parabolic partial differential equation with a gradient flow structure, widely used to model pattern formation in nonequilibrium systems. To overcome the drawbacks of existing unconditionally stable schemes, which rely on auxiliary variables or artificial stabilization terms that deviate from the original energy dissipation law and incur high computational costs, we propose an efficient numerical scheme that directly preserves the original energy dissipation law. The Crank-Nicolson scheme is used for temporal discretization to achieve second-order accuracy, while a fourth-order compact finite difference method is used for spatial discretization to accurately capture complex spatial structures. To overcome the computational bottleneck of implicit schemes, a two-grid acceleration strategy with H=h is introduced, in which the nonlinear system is solved on the coarse grid and only linearization corrections are performed on the fine grid. Numerical experiments verify second-order temporal and fourth-order spatial convergence rates, the original energy dissipation property, and the acceleration effect of the two-grid strategy. The proposed method provides an effective approach for long-time, large-scale, high-precision simulations of the Swift-Hohenberg equation, achieving both physical rigor and computational economy. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: The existence and instability of blowing-up steady states for the Shigesada-Kawasaki-Teramoto competition model with cross-diffusion

Title: Intelligent brain tumor classification using a Bi-level optimized stacking ensemble with metaheuristic feature selection and Bayesian hyperparameters

Title: Cross-graph learning based mating interface identification for CAD-assisted assembly design
Abstract: During CAD model exchange and reuse, explicit assembly metadata may be incomplete even when the geometries of candidate parts remain available. Title: Wavelet-based inversion of Abel equations in two unknowns for spherically symmetric sources

Abstract: This paper presents a wavelet-based numerical approach for inverting a system of Abel integral equations in two unknowns arising in spherically symmetric physical systems. Title: A novel approach to prevent conflicts in industrial human–robot tool sharing through motion and eye tracking
Abstract: Seamless human–robot interaction is one of the main research challenges for the industrial robotics community. Title: Time–space adaptive finite element method for the FitzHugh–Nagumo equations

Title: Multiscale structural characteristics and functional properties of Angelica dahurica starches from different origins
Abstract: Although the demand for novel starch resources continues to grow, starch derived from Angelica dahurica remains largely underexplored, particularly with respect to how structural variations translate into differences in functional performance. Title: Optimization and validation of a green analytical method for determining bixlozone herbicide in water

Title: A new Dixon resultant algorithm for solving parametric polynomial systems using sparse multivariate rational function interpolation
Abstract: Elimination methods such as Gröbner bases and triangular sets have been employed to address the growing demand for solving parametric polynomial systems in practice. However, experiments have shown that when used in Computer Algebra Systems such as Maple and Magma they often struggle with systems that have many parameters. To address this problem, we present a new interpolation algorithm for solving parametric polynomial systems over Q using the Dixon resultant. The Dixon resultant is a multiple of the unique generator of an elimination ideal of a polynomial system. It can be expressed as the determinant of a matrix of polynomial entries called the Dixon matrix.In practice, the Dixon resultant R often has many repeated factors and a large polynomial content. To avoid computing these unwanted factors of R, our new algorithm interpolates the rational function coefficients in the parameters of the monic square-free factors of R from monic univariate images of R. It does this using our newly developed sparse multivariate rational function interpolation method. By not computing R in expanded form, our approach often dramatically reduces the number of images needed to interpolate the monic square-free factors of R over Q[jls-end-space/].We have implemented our new Dixon resultant algorithm in Maple with many parts of the algorithm coded in C for increased efficiency. Our benchmarks show that our new Dixon resultant algorithm can solve many parametric polynomial systems that other algorithms for computing R are unable to solve. Our new algorithm is probabilistic; it may fail to produce an answer, and even when successful, it may return an incorrect answer, but with provably low probability. In this work we identify and classify all the causes of failure in our new algorithm, and we give a detailed failure probability analysis. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Sonication at pH 12 improves dispersibility, interfacial properties, and emulsifying functionality of a soy-yeast protein blend without post-sonication alkaline holding

Title: Bifurcation analysis of the tangential switching mode in a non-monotonic tumor growth model
Abstract: The study of tumor growth is a classic topic in mathematical biology. Title: Optimized machine learning models for identification of autism spectrum disorder

Title: An iterative knowledge extraction and dual-channel fusion framework for clinical differential diagnosis
Abstract: For common diseases in the cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, and respiratory systems that present with overlapping clinical manifestations (for instance, chest tightness and shortness of breath), accurate identification is critical for formulating effective treatment plans. Title: A new partial differential system involving evolutionary variational-hemivariational inequalities arising in contact mechanics

Title: On some hypergeometric modularity conjectures of Dawsey and McCarthy
Abstract: In recent work, the author, in collaboration with Allen, Long, and Tu, developed the Explicit Hypergeometric Modularity Method (EHMM), which establishes the modularity of a large class of hypergeometric Galois representations in dimensions two and three. In this article, we introduce an analogous family of eta-quotients, which we call the K3 functions. These K3 functions are constructed using the theory of weight one cubic theta functions originally developed by Jonathan and Peter Borwein. We then use the K3 functions in the EHMM to resolve several hypergeometric modularity conjectures of Dawsey and McCarthy. Further, we provide applications to special L -values of the K3 functions and to the study of generalized Paley graphs. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: TFP-WAN: Prompt-guided imperceptible watermark attack network based on transformer architecture
Abstract: Although interference with the correct extraction of watermarks is caused by traditional watermark attack method, noticeable degradation in the visual quality of watermarked images is often caused. Title: Axially symmetric Réthy flows in a finite nozzle with an obstacle inside
Abstract: In this study, we show that there exists a unique solution to the axially symmetric incompressible Réthy flow for the steady three-dimensional Euler system, and that the free boundaries converge to a certain direction as the flow goes to infinity. Title: Discrete energy consistency for dynamic finite-strain frictional contact models with inelastic transformation
Abstract: This paper presents a thermodynamically consistent framework for the numerical treatment of finite-strain contact problems involving frictional interaction and inelastic material transformations, with particular reference to plastic or superelastic materials. Title: Non-covalent interactions between pectin and volatiles modulate flavor formation in goji berry (Lycium barbarum L.) during pulsed vacuum drying
Abstract: Pectin plays a crucial role in modulating the flavor attributes of goji berry. NVOCs involving soluble sugars, organic acids and amino acids affected VOC profiles. CSP exhibited substantial nanostructural rearrangement and interconnected network reconstruction, showing strong negative correlations with key aroma-active compounds such as acetic acid and octanal. It was further revealed that CSP interacted with acetic acid predominantly through hydrogen bonding, while octanal binding likely involved both hydrophobic interactions and hydrogen bonding. These non-covalent interactions inhibited pectin aggregation, reduced particle size, and promoted the formation of stable porous fibrous microstructure that may facilitate flavor retention. Title: Comparison of VUV/ozone and VUV/H2O2 processes for the degradation of aniline in water: Performance evaluation and oxidation mechanism

Abstract: Residual aniline in water is highly toxic and poses a threat to the aquatic environment. Title: Multiscale modeling of heat and mass transfer problems in unsaturated permafrost soils

Abstract: This paper studies multiscale model reduction for coupled heat and mass transfer in unsaturated permafrost soils using the Generalized Multiscale Finite Element Method (GMsFEM). Title: TF-HyperNet: Sleep apnea detection using dual-stream time–frequency fusion and a soft-margin hyperbox decision head
Abstract: Sleep apnea (SA) is a prevalent sleep-related breathing disorder that poses a substantial threat to public health. Deep learning-based ECG detection methods hold considerable promise for clinical applications. For classification, a multi-center mapping module partitions abnormal samples with high intra-class variability into multiple subsets. Title: Hybrid regularizers and a nonconvex fidelity model for impulse noise image restoration

Title: Functional protein extracts and colouring co-products from Chlorella fusca: Towards integrated microalgal bioprocessing

Title: Multiscale structure-function design of modified fish gelatin for gels, interfaces, films, and printable food matrices: A comprehensive review

Physical treatments, enzymatic crosslinking, phenolic reinforcement, Maillard-type glycosylation, targeted chemical modification, protein-polysaccharide complexation and composite strategies are evaluated according to their effects on chain conformation, molecular weight distribution, aggregation, crosslinking density, water distribution, interfacial behaviour and rheological properties. These structural changes are further linked to food-relevant applications, including edible films and coatings, active and intelligent packaging, emulsion gels, structured oils, fat-replacement systems, 3D-printable matrices and food-grade delivery systems. The key challenge is not to maximise a single property, but to match each modification route with the structural bottleneck of a specific food matrix. Title: Complete reduction for derivatives in a transcendental Liouvillian extension

Title: Polarization-guided flow-matching reconstruction of orthogonal polarization components from speckle transmission through biological tissue

Title: Numerical Investigation of Flow Control Around Three Cylinders using a Passive Method
Source title: Advances in Applied Mathematics and Mechanics
Abstract: This study investigates the flow behavior around three cylinders with attached splitter plates arranged in an equilateral triangular configuration using the lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) at low Reynolds numbers (Re). Although previous research has focused on flow around bluff bodies without splitter plates, this study examines the effects of splitter plates on flow control. Title: Diffusive limit of the Vlasov-Maxwell-Landau system

Title: Learning conjugate fringe decomposition for single-shot fringe projection profilometry

Traditionally, in fringe projection profilometry (FPP), depth is not measured directly but inferred from the phase of a projected fringe, so demodulating phase from a single image is the central step. The classical single-shot FPP demodulator, Fourier transform profilometry (FTP), demodulates the carrier fringe in the frequency domain to retrieve the phase, but it degrades on complex surfaces and is sensitive to spectral separation. Instead of regressing depth, it decomposes one fringe into a background intensity and the real and imaginary parts of a complex baseband field and retrieves phase from that field. Title: Low-distortion planar embedding of rod-based structures

Title: Dynamic aspects of tumor-immune interaction under dual immunotherapy (effector cells and IL-2)

We analyze tumor size oscillationsto explain long-term phenomena, such as tumor elimination or recurrence, under the influence of cellular immunotherapy. The model captures the nonlinear dynamics of immunogenic tumors. In particular, we show that the trajectories are bounded and defined for all positive time, invariant subsets exist, and under certain parameter conditions, the system admits at most five equilibrium points in the first octant: one tumor-free and up to four coexistence states. Our analysis reveals that the model exhibits rich dynamical behavior, significantly influenced by the parameters μ 1 (death rate of effector cells) and p 1 (production rate of effector cells stimulated by IL-2).
