Title: A clinical rule-guided neuro-symbolic network for interpretable diabetic retinopathy grading with limited data
Abstract: Diabetic retinopathy grading from fundus images remains challenging under limited-data and class-imbalanced conditions, where deep learning models are prone to overfitting and often lack explicit correspondence with clinical grading criteria. To address these issues, this study proposes CRNS-Net, a clinical rule-guided neuro-symbolic network for interpretable diabetic retinopathy grading under limited-data conditions. The model uses a shared Inception-V3 backbone to jointly perform lesion segmentation and image-level grading in a multi-task framework. Lesion probability maps are converted into continuous structured descriptors, including lesion count, lesion area, and spatial distribution, through a soft statistical quantification module. These descriptors are further mapped to executable clinical rules derived from the International Clinical Diabetic Retinopathy severity scale. A dynamic knowledge base combines static clinical rules with distribution-based calibration, while a gated fusion mechanism adaptively integrates structured lesion cues with deep visual features. In addition, a Kullback–Leibler divergence constraint enforces consistency between rule-based inference and network prediction, allowing clinical knowledge to guide both training and grade decision making. On the FGADR and DDR datasets, the proposed method achieved the highest quadratic weighted Kappa among the compared methods, reaching 0.8460 and 0.8882, respectively. Ablation results suggest that gated fusion and logical reasoning provide complementary gains. These findings indicate that embedding clinical rules into the decision process can improve grading consistency and interpretability, especially in boundary-grade and limited-data scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Cui Y.; Zhang X.; Ruan J.; Ji J.; Li S.; Li T.; Huang X.
Title: Effect of ultrasound-assisted pear pomace RG-I type pectin on the structure, physicochemical properties, and digestibility of A-, B-, and C-type starches
Abstract: This study systematically investigated the effects of ultrasound (US)-assisted pear pomace RG-I type pectin (PP) on the structure, physicochemical, and digestive properties of maize starch (MaS; A-type), potato starch (PoS; B-type), and pea starch (PeS; C-type). The results indicated that hydrogen bonds and electrostatic interactions in starch-pectin complexes were associated with the coating of PP on starch granule surfaces, leading to increased particle size. Owing to varied coating effects, the extent of relative crystallinity (RC) reduction followed the order MaS-PP > PeS-PP > PoS-PP. In addition, the incorporation of PP inhibited starch pasting. The gel strength of MaS-PP and PoS-PP were reduced, whereas that of PeS-PP increased. In vitro digestion assays indicated that PP increased the resistant starch (RS) content of the three starches. Moreover, US preserved the A-type crystalline structure, as well as strengthened hydrogen bonds and improved RC in US-MaS-PP and US-PeS-PP, and further reduced their digestibility. After US-assisted PP treatment, finally, RS of US-MaS-PP, US-PeS-PP, and US-PoS-PP were increased by 200.86%, 153.12%, and 118.65%, respectively, compared with native starches. Notably, US-MaS-PP possessed the highest sum content of slowly digestible and resistant starches. These findings provide potential insights into the high-value utilization of pear pomace pectin and establish a theoretical foundation for developing low GI foods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Zhang X.; Lan J.; Wang X.; Luo J.; Zhao Y.; Leng Y.; Liang Y.; Liu H.; Wang J.
Title: Trehalose mitigates freeze–thaw-induced gluten network deterioration by modulating aggregation behavior and molecular conformation
Abstract: This study evaluated how trehalose regulates gluten aggregation behavior and molecular conformation in dough subjected to freeze–thaw treatment. At a concentration of 1% of trehalose, gluten network continuity was markedly improved, and gluten molecular chains exhibited increases in height and width of 170.8% and 78.9%, respectively, compared with the freeze–thaw control. Trehalose also inhibited gluten depolymerization, restored disulfide bond content to a level comparable to that of fresh dough, and enhanced hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic forces while reducing the solvent exposure of tryptophan and tyrosine residues. FT-IR and Raman spectroscopic analyses showed that trehalose inhibited the shift from α-helices and β-sheets toward random coil conformations and promoted the formation of more stable disulfide bridge conformations. RP-HPLC analysis further demonstrated that trehalose increased the content of HMW-GS and promoted the cross-linking of ω5-, ω1,2-, and α-gliadins with glutenin, thereby contributing to the stabilization of gluten aggregation. Molecular docking indicated that trehalose showed a stronger binding affinity for gliadin than for glutenin and that hydrogen bonding was the predominant interaction. Overall, these findings demonstrated that trehalose enhanced gluten network freeze–thaw stability by preserving molecular associations and suppressing structural destabilization, thereby providing new mechanistic insight into its cryoprotective action and supporting its application for quality preservation in frozen dough products. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Li W.; Qian C.; Luo W.; Zhu Y.; Jiang C.; Wang L.; Hu J.
Title: Robotic learning from demonstration enabled by improved gaussian mixture model and gaussian mixture regression
Abstract: Robotic learning from demonstration (LfD) can significantly minimize robotic programming difficulties due to its intuitiveness and efficiency. Gaussian mixture model (GMM)/Gaussian mixture regression (GMR) is an effective method to implement LfD. However, there are limitations in GMM/GMR, such as the requirement of creating multiple demonstrations, sensitivity to demonstration defects, and underfitting/overfitting generalization in industrial tasks. To tackle the issues, in this study, an improved GMM/GMR approach with three improvements is proposed. Firstly, a Gaussian noise scattering strategy is designed to minimize the required number of multiple demonstrations and eliminate unsmooth turning areas/jitters defects in the demonstration. Secondly, based on a new evaluation criterion of incorporating the Gaussian cluster number, Bayesian information criterion, and dynamic time warping, the particle swarm optimization algorithm is introduced to achieve an optimal balance between feature preservation and smoothness for a regression solution, thereby effectively mitigating the overfitting/underfitting issues. Thirdly, the B-spline curve-based reconstruction of the regression solution is devised to enhance the adaptability of GMM/GMR to the changes in target positions. Experiments on retired product recycling are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the approach presented in this study, providing a reliable solution to facilitate LfD in industrial environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Zhang B.-H.; Xiao F.-J.; Gu L.; Chen C.-Y.; Wen R.; Huang W.-Y.; Yang K.; Lu K.-Q.
Title: Noble-metal-free CoMoP cocatalyst anchored on ZnIn2S4 for boosted visible-light-driven hydrogen evolution
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Despite the promising application prospect of ZnIn2S4 (ZIS) in photocatalytic H2 evolution, rapid photogenerated charge recombination and insufficient active sites severely restrict its catalytic performance. Moreover, conventional noble-metal cocatalysts are costly and scarce, which prohibits their large-scale practical deployment. Herein, we rationally design a high-efficiency and low-cost noble-metal-free photocatalyst by integrating MOF-derived bimetallic CoMoP (CMP) with ZIS nanoflowers. Benefiting from the superior conductive network and abundant active sites of bimetallic phosphide CoMoP, the optimized ZIS-10% CMP composite achieves a prominent photocatalytic hydrogen evolution rate of 10,977 μmol‧g−1‧h−1, which is 5.9-fold higher than that of pristine ZIS. It also delivers a high apparent quantum efficiency of 16.55% at 420 nm and robust cycling stability over five consecutive tests, outperforming most state-of-the-art ZIS-based photocatalysts. Photoelectrochemical characterizations demonstrate that the unique bimetallic CoMoP not only provides abundant active sites for hydrogen evolution but also efficiently promotes interfacial charge transfer and inhibits photogenerated charge recombination. This work highlights the great potential of bimetallic phosphides as high-performance cocatalysts and offers a feasible avenue for the construction of cost-effective and efficient sulfide-based composite photocatalysts. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Shu Z.; Zhou J.; Hongzhao M.; Ma B.; Kang Y.; Li T.; Shen C.
Title: Ultrasensitive carbonate ion detection in water using a PANI/ZnO@PVA/CNC composite film modified Mach-Zehnder interferometer
Abstract: The reliable monitoring of carbonate ions in water is critical for assessing water hardness, buffering capacity, and potential ecological risks, yet existing sensors suffer from limited sensitivity and matrix interference. Herein, we report a highly sensitive optical fiber sensor for carbonate ion detection, constructed by coating a polyaniline (PANI)/zinc oxide (ZnO)-doped polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)/cellulose nanocrystal (CNC) composite film onto a low-cost Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) fabricated via three-segment single mode fiber offset fusion splicing. In this design, CNC serve as nano-reinforcers that crosslink with PVA through hydrogen bonding to form a PVA/CNC composite matrix, while the embedded PANI/ZnO nanocomposites enable enhanced carbonate response via ZnO coordination and the electrostatic adsorption via PANI. The sensor responds to carbonate ions over the range of 0.5-200 μg/L, with a low-concentration sensitivity of −0.21 dB/(μg/L) at 0.5-10 μg/L and a higher-concentration sensitivity of −0.008 dB/(μg/L) at 10-200 μg/L. The detection limit is 1.7 μg/L, which is about 6-fold lower than that of the reported fiber-optic SPR carbonate sensor. The response time is 10 min, and the sensor demonstrates good practical applicability, with recovery rates of 95.9-98% in pure water and 94.2-97% in tap water at spiked concentrations of 1, 10, and 100 μg/L. Experimental results demonstrate that the PANI/ZnO@PVA/CNC-coated MZI represents a promising platform for sensitive and reliable carbonate ions monitoring, which is highly applicable to environmental water quality evaluation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Santra S.; Pandey H.; Behera R.
Author full names: Santra, Sudarshan (57218712598); Pandey, Himanshu (59358494600); Behera, Ratikanta (55468237300)
Title: fI-PIDNNs: An advanced AI-driven deep learning approach for multi-term time-fractional forward and inverse problems with weak singularities
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: This study proposes a fractional integro physics-informed deep neural network (fI-PIDNN) framework for solving weakly singular integro-partial differential equations with multi-term time-fractional operators, with particular attention to singularities arising at the initial time t=0. The framework addresses both forward and inverse problems, effectively capturing the singular behavior at t=0 which commonly arises in fractional-order models. To enhance the accuracy and stability, three discretization schemes are incorporated into the network: L1-M (linear polynomial approximation), L12-M (linear-quadratic approximation), and HO-M (higher-order approximation using linear, quadratic, and cubic polynomials). The weakly singular integral operator is approximated using a modified quadrature rule that blends the midpoint and trapezoidal techniques. Among the schemes, the fI-PIDNN with HO-M exhibits superior convergence and solution accuracy. The architecture requires minimal modification to handle time-fractional inverse problems involving Volterra operators with weakly singular kernels, thereby enabling the effective identification of unknown diffusion coefficients and fractional orders. The framework is validated through comprehensive numerical experiments covering cases with bounded and unbounded temporal derivatives at t=0, confirming its robustness in tackling complex fractional models with nonlinear source terms and unknown parameters. The proposed fI-PIDNN framework provides an effective and versatile approach for solving challenging weakly singular integro-fractional models and offers clear advantages over existing AO-fPINNs and AWAO-fPINNs approaches, which fail to handle weakly singular kernels in the integral operators. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Toda K.; Miyazaki Y.
Title: Effects of soybean storage on tofu texture and its relationship with the particle size distribution and protein chemical properties of soymilk
Abstract: The mechanism underlying textural changes in tofu during soybean seed storage remains unresolved and is regarded as a central issue for manufacturers. In this study, we examined changes in the breaking stress of tofu prepared from soybeans stored for six months and 1 year at 4, 20, and 37 °C. We also evaluated the particle size distribution, protein composition and its chemical properties of the resulting soymilk. After one year of storage, tofu derived from soybeans stored at 20 °C exhibited a significantly higher breaking stress than samples stored under other conditions or prior to storage (p < 0.05). At 37 °C, breaking stress increased after six months but declined after one year, coinciding with pronounced polymerization of the 11S globulin basic subunit via disulfide bonding. The extent of disulfide bond formation progressed in the order of 37 °C > 20 °C > 4 °C. The addition of dithiothreitol to the corresponding soymilk reduced the highly polymerized basic subunits and substantially restored tofu breaking stress. Conversely, the addition of oxidized glutathione to soymilk from new-grain soybeans altered the particle size distribution and increased tofu breaking stress. These findings indicate that moderate disulfide bonding within the basic subunit initially strengthens the tofu structure, whereas excessive polymerization during prolonged storage leads to textural weakening. Furthermore, storage resulted in a decreased proportion of single oil-body particles and an increased number of larger aggregates in soymilk, likely due to protein conformational changes via disulfide bonding and degradation of 24 kDa oleosin, a key oil-body membrane protein. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Wang Y.; Wei S.; Zhang J.; Su Y.
Title: Theoretical insights into N-protonation-controlled fluorescence ON/OFF in meso-substituted BODIPY pH probes
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: BODIPY fluorescent probes containing meso substituents with a protonatable nitrogen atom commonly exhibit fluorescence OFF/ON switching upon N-protonation. This phenomenon is generally explained via photo-induced electron transfer (PET) or intramolecular charge transfer (CT). However, the detailed excited-state mechanism responsible for fluorescence quenching and recovery remains unclear. In this work, density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT (TD-DFT) calculations were performed to investigate the excited-state relaxation mechanisms of three meso -substituted BODIPY probes before and after N -protonation. The results show that the relative energy ordering of the bright locally excited (LE) state and the charge transfer (CT) state differ among the unprotonated probes at the Franck–Condon point. During structural relaxation, the CT state is stabilized and becomes a low-lying excited state. The resulting dark or weakly emissive CT state provides a nonradiative decay pathway, thereby quenching the fluorescence. N -protonation reduces the electron-donating ability of the meso substituent. It raises the energy of the CT state, suppressing the nonradiative decay through the CT state, favoring the radiative decay from the LE state. This work reveals how N -protonation regulates the LE and CT states and provides a useful strategy for the design of meso -substituted BODIPY pH probes. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zhang X.; Ma Y.; Chu L.; Li G.; Zhao Y.; Zhao S.
Title: Enhancing the antioxidant activity of peptides derived from fermented casein by ultrasonic treatment: Insights from molecular characterization and molecular dynamics simulation study
Abstract: Ultrasound-assisted fermentation has recently gained attention as an effective strategy for enhancing the functional properties of food proteins. However, the mechanisms underlying the interactions between proteases and ultrasound-treated proteins, as well as the release patterns of bioactive peptides, remain incompletely understood. This study focused on casein, a protein rich in bioactive peptides, and examined the effects of ultrasonic treatment on its structural characteristics, its interaction with the cell envelope proteinase (CEP) from Lactobacillus helveticus ATCC15009, and the release of antioxidant peptides. Computer simulations suggested that ultrasonic treatment enhanced the binding interaction between CEP and casein. Experimental characterization showed that ultrasound increased casein solubility, surface hydrophobicity, zeta-potential and random-coil content, while reducing particle size. Moreover, 400 W ultrasound promoted the generation of peptides with MW < 3 kDa and resulted in the highest antioxidant activity of the casein hydrolysates. A novel antioxidant peptide, VYPFPGPIPN, was identified through liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), bioinformatics prediction, and computational simulations. This peptide showed a strong interaction with Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (KEAP1). Cellular experiments further suggested that peptide VYPFPGPIPN enhanced antioxidant defense by regulating the KEAP1/Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway. These findings provide a promising strategy for the development of functional food ingredients. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Hu H.; Chen C.; He W.

Title: A Novel Two-Grid Finite Element Approach for Solving Nonlinear Time-Fractional Schrödinger Equation
Source title: Advances in Applied Mathematics and Mechanics
Abstract: A novel two-grid finite element method with ℱL2−1σ scheme is presented for solving nonlinear time-fractional Schrödinger equation. The finite element solution is proven bounded in the L∞-norm, with no restrictions imposed on the grid ratio. The ℱL2−1σ scheme is adopted to construct a second-order numerical scheme in the time direction, while the two-grid finite element method is applied for spatial discretization, which effectively reduces computational storage and cost. The optimal order error estimations of the two-grid solution in the Lp-norm are proved without any grid-ratio conditions. Finally, we present some numerical experiments to validate the accuracy and effectiveness of the scheme. © 2027 Global Science Press.

Authors: Guo W.-X.; Zheng H.; Lu X.-P.
Title: AN ACCELERATED MODULUS-BASED MATRIX SPLITTING ITERATION METHOD FOR SOLVING A CLASS OF HORIZONTAL NONLINEAR COMPLEMENTARITY PROBLEMS
Abstract: This paper focuses on an accelerated modulus-based matrix splitting iteration method for solving a class of horizontal nonlinear complementarity problems. First, by introducing a secondary matrix splitting based on the principles of stepwise updates and immediate utilization of the latest computational information, the equivalent modulus equation of the horizontal nonlinear complementarity problem is reformulated and thereby the accelerated modulus-based matrix splitting iteration scheme is constructed. Subsequently, under the assumption that the system matrices are H+-matrices, the convergence conditions for the proposed method are established. Finally, the computational efficiency of the new method is demonstrated by numerical experiments. © 2027 American Institute of Mathematical Sciences. All rights reserved.

Authors: Zhou S.; He Z.; Hu F.; Du L.; Zhao Y.; Fang Y.; Zou P.; Cai H.; Chu W.
Title: Intra-Matrix Flexible Optical-Electronic Configuration Algorithms for Energy-Efficient Large Language Model Inference
Source title: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics
Abstract: Low-energy, low-precision inference is an important enabler for scalable deployment of large language models (LLMs). Optical-electronic computing offers high bandwidth, low latency, and potentially high energy efficiency, making it a promising approach for future LLM deployment. However, existing optical and hybrid optical-electronic inference systems typically use uniform hardware configurations, such as fixed optical power or a fixed electronic-photonic partition across layers. Fine-grained allocation of optical power and optical-electronic computation remains underexplored for photonic LLM inference. Here, we propose three flexible configuration algorithms: Flexible Optical Power Allocation (FOPA), Flexible Weak-Column Allocation (FWCA), and Joint Optical Power and Weak-Column Allocation (JOWA). Using a diagonal Hessian estimator without constructing the full Hessian matrix, these methods jointly optimize optical-electronic resources under predefined energy budgets. Evaluations on Llama 2-7B and DeepSeek-LLM-7B-Base show estimated energy savings of 40.11%-60.85% relative to FP16 inference on the NVIDIA H100 and 5.34%-38.12% relative to uniform optical-power and weak-column baselines, while maintaining an acceptable perplexity increase. Evaluations using a Tianshu-hardware-calibrated simulator show corresponding estimated energy savings of 39.91%-53.67% and 5.02%-26.76%, respectively. These results indicate that fine-grained resource allocation can improve the energy-accuracy trade-off of hybrid optical-electronic systems for LLM inference.  © 1995-2012 IEEE.

Authors: He W.; Gong W.; Zou Q.
Author full names: He, Wenming (7402006889); Gong, Wenbo (60994157400); Zou, Qingsong (8369763900)
Title: Local ultraconvergence of post-processed finite volume element solutions over quadrilateral meshes for elliptic problems
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: This paper establishes, for the first time, the local ultraconvergence properties of post-processed high-order finite volume element methods (FVEM) for second-order elliptic problems with constant coefficients. We introduce two Richardson-type extrapolation operators-originally developed in the finite element context-and apply them to post-process both the FVEM solution and its gradient on quadrilateral meshes of degree k ≥ 1. We rigorously prove that the post-processed solution and gradient attain 2kth order convergence, up to a logarithmic factor, at interior nodes. In particular, this work provides the first theoretical proof that the FVEM gradient exhibits kth order ultraconvergence, up to a logarithmic factor, a phenomenon previously unknown in the FVEM framework. A new analytical approach is developed to overcome the lack of Galerkin orthogonality, and numerical experiments confirm the sharpness and generality of the theoretical results. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Dong Y.; Cui Y.; Guo L.; Lin S.; Li L.; Leng J.; Zhao W.
Title: Extrusion-mediated molecular reconstruction governs starch–lipid complexation and structural stability in cassava-based reconstituted rice
Abstract: Cassava-based reconstituted rice is a promising staple food alternative; however, its high digestibility and poor retrogradation resistance limit its application. Although starch–lipid assembly has been widely applied to regulate starch functionality, the molecular basis by which thermomechanical extrusion facilitates ordered structure development in amylopectin-rich cassava systems remains insufficiently understood. This study investigated how extrusion-driven molecular reconstruction governs starch–lipid assembly and functional properties of cassava-based reconstituted rice prepared with palmitic acid (PA). Extrusion substantially reconstructed the starch molecular architecture, decreasing the weight-average molecular weight from 7.71 × 105 g/mol to 4.78 × 105 g/mol, increasing the proportion of short glucan chains and the apparent amylose content, and generating molecular configurations favorable for subsequent structural assembly. PA incorporation further promoted ordered starch–lipid structures, as evidenced by the increased complex index, V-type crystalline characteristics, and enhanced thermal stability. These hierarchical structural changes significantly reduced starch hydrolysis, decreasing the digestion rate constant from 89.51 × 10−3 to 61.64 × 10−3 min−1 and estimated glycemic index from 70.61 to 60.62, while increasing resistant starch content from 17.49% to 26.86%. Furthermore, the reconstructed starch–lipid architecture restricted molecular reassociation and crystalline recovery during storage, thereby improving retrogradation resistance. Overall, this study establishes a structure–function framework linking extrusion-induced molecular reconstruction with ordered starch–lipid assembly and the nutritional and technological performance of cassava-based reconstituted rice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Author full names: Bogdanov, Fedor B. (58033153200); Fedorenko, Nikolay O. (60896029300); Rakhimov, Radmir R. (60896029400); Andreeva, Olga E. (37015258000); Piven, Yuri A. Title: Photoinduced thioxanthone/DABCO-mediated dual catalysis for the synthesis of isocryptolepine-based antitumor agents
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Herein, we report a visible-light-driven dual photoredox catalysis strategy for the efficient synthesis of structurally diverse isocryptolepine derivatives using thioxanthone and DABCO as single-electron transfer (SET) and hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) catalysts, respectively. The operationally simple protocol exhibits a broad substrate scope and compatibility with various functional groups, and provides concise access to new isocryptolepine analogs for biological evaluation. Screening against ERα-positive MCF-7, HER2-positive HCC1954, and triple-negative MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cell lines followed by cytotoxicity assessment against non-malignant human fibroblasts hFB-hTERT revealed pronounced structure–activity relationships, with subtle structural modifications producing marked differences in potency and subtype selectivity. Indoloquinolines 2j and 3a were identified as lead candidates with complementary biological profiles: 2j displayed potent and selective activity toward ER-positive breast cancer cells together with a favorable selectivity index, whereas 3a exhibited consistently high antiproliferative activity across all tested models, including aggressive triple-negative breast cancer. Both compounds effectively suppressed clonogenic survival at subnanomolar and low nanomolar concentrations, indicating sustained inhibition of long-term proliferative capacity. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Liu D.; Zhang F.; Shen Y.; Cheng Y.; Xu J.; Zhang Y.
Title: Theoretical Analysis of Liquid Lens Evaporation on Immiscible Liquid Surface
Source title: Advances in Applied Mathematics and Mechanics
Abstract: The evaporation of liquid lens widely occurs in various scientific and industrial applications. In this study, a theoretical model is set up for liquid lens evaporation under the axisymmetric toroidal coordinate, with coupled internal heat conduction and external vapor diffusion. The effect of evaporative cooling number, liquid lens shape and volume on evaporation performance is quantitatively analyzed. It is found that overall evaporation rate is determined by the competing effect of evaporation flux and area of upper surface. With the increasing ratios of upper and lower tangential angles, at high evaporative cooling numbers or large liquid volumes, overall evaporation rates decrease firstly, after reaching the minimum value, they start to increase until the asymptotic value. The ”2/3 power law” holds for transient volume variation of liquid lens over time, independent of evaporative cooling and liquid lens shape. These findings may help get insight into the liquid lens evaporation on immiscible liquid. © 2027 Global Science Press.

Authors: Li J.; Li Z.; Zhao J.; Zhang Y.; Zhang L.
Title: High-Precision Calculation of Wave-Current Forces on Offshore Wind Turbines Based on the Regularized Singular Boundary Method
Source title: Advances in Applied Mathematics and Mechanics
Abstract: The main purpose of this article is to develop a regularized singular boundary method for high-precision simulation of wave-current forces on offshore wind turbines. The engineering bottlenecks encountered in the construction of offshore wind turbines are discussed, i.e., how to effectively deal with the singularity of the Green’s function at the origin, and how to accurately calculate wave forces on offshore wind turbines. An origin intensity factor technique for marine dynamic environment simulation is proposed. Based on the origin intensity factor and the Green’s function, a regularized singular boundary method is constructed, which only requires placing source points on the wet surface of offshore wind turbines. Wave load is calculated by substituting wave parameters affected by wave-current interaction into the linear diffraction model. The wave-current force on offshore wind turbines is finally obtained by superimposing the current load and the wave load. Numerical experiments show that the regularized singular boundary method can accurately analyze the Bragg resonance of offshore wind turbines caused by wave-current force. © 2027 Global Science Press.

Author full names: Nikam, Pooja A. (61016505800); Shinde, Sarika D. (36988814600); Shinde, Mahendra (57205864411); Chaskar, Manisha (60522471300); Patil, Ganesh E. (36988843800)
Title: Ultraviolet light induced photocatalytic behavior of hydrothermally synthesized tetragonal zircon type bismuth vanadate nanoparticles
Abstract: The development of efficient and reusable photocatalyst for removal of azo dyes from wastewater remains challenging. Herein, tetragonal zircon-type BiVO4 nanoparticles were synthesized by hydrothermal route and evaluated for UV-driven degradation of Methyl Red (MR). XRD confirmed the tetragonal zircon phase, with an average crystallite size of 36.99 nm, while SEM-EDAX and HRTEM revealed porous hierarchical morphology and nanoscale particles with a 0.28 nm interplanar spacing corresponding to (112) plane. FTIR and Raman analyses confirmed the characteristics Bi-O and V-O vibrational features, and the optical band gap estimated as 2.70 eV. Under standard experimental conditions, BiVO4 nanoparticles achieved 83.8% degradation of Methyl Red after 120 min UV irradiation. After optimization of the catalyst dose, pH and initial dye concentration, the maximum degradation efficiency increased to approximately 91% at a catalyst dosage of 30 mg. The photocatalytic performance was influenced by solution pH, with maximum degradation observed at pH 3. The catalyst retained substantial activity over four consecutive cycles, demonstrating good reusability. These findings highlight hydrothermally synthesized BiVO4 nanoparticles as a promising reusable photocatalyst for UV-assisted degradation of azo dye contaminants. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Li L.; Zhang Z.
Title: Diffusion asymptotics of a coupled model for radiative transfer without thermal diffusion effects: Ill-prepared initial data
Abstract: This article studies the asymptotic analysis of a coupled model arising in radiative transfer in T3 with one-speed velocity without thermal diffusion effects. The model consists of a kinetic equation satisfied by the specific intensity of radiation coupled to a transport equation satisfied by the material temperature. We combine the moment method with Hilbert expansion to show the radiative intensity can be approximated by the sum of interior solution and initial layer. We also show the solution satisfied by the temperature can be approximated by the interior solution. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Bedre J.S.; Prasanna P.L.
Title: Adaptive facial landmark graph learning for occlusion-aware emotion recognition using optimized YOLO v11 and graph-transformer networks
Abstract: Facial Emotion Recognition (FER) is an important component of intelligent human–computer interaction and affective computing because it allows machines to learn and react to human emotional conditions. All current Emotion Recognition (ER) methods are vulnerable to several drawbacks, including occlusions, lighting differences, and lack of modeling to complex spatial relations among faces. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes a Graph Transformer (GT)-based emotion classification that effectively captures relational. The collected video data undergoes frame extraction and preprocessing to improve visual quality and consistency. The faces are detected using an optimized You Only Look Once version 11 (YOLO v11) model enhanced with the Oppositional Learning-Crested Porcupine Optimization Algorithm (OL-CPOA) for improved localization accuracy and convergence. Deep facial features are extracted using a Deep Convolutional Neural Network (DCNN) integrated with Uncertainty-Aware Self-Attention (UASA) to handle noise and uncertain representations in feature maps. Further, Rectangle-Window Cross-Attention (RWCA) is employed to capture multi-scale contextual dependencies between facial regions before feeding the refined features into the GT for final emotion classification. The experimental evaluation demonstrates that the proposed model achieves a success rate of 96%, a Positive Predictive Value (PPV) of 96.14%, a sensitivity of 96.05%, and an F1-score of 96%, indicating strong classification capability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Liang Z.; Liu Z.
Title: Double Hopf bifurcation analysis for a diffusive prey-predator model with a chemotactic term
Abstract: Interactions between chemotaxis-driven Hopf bifurcation and other bifurcations can lead to a remarkably rich array of spatiotemporal dynamics. In this paper, the stability of the positive constant equilibrium and the existence of double Hopf bifurcation for a diffusive predator-prey model with chemotactic terms are studied. For the first time, we have formulated computational methods for determining the normal forms associated with double Hopf bifurcation in a reaction-diffusion system that features a chemotactic term and adheres to Neumann boundary conditions. Especially, the developed normal form method is applicable for classifying the dynamics near the double Hopf bifurcation point. Finally, numerical simulations are provided to substantiate the results. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Mandal B.C.; Tomer D.
Title: Convergence of substructuring waveform relaxation algorithms for hyperbolic PDEs with time delay
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: This article investigates the application and analysis of two substructuring waveform relaxation algorithms namely Dirichlet-Neumann Waveform Relaxation (DNWR) and Neumann-Neumann Waveform Relaxation (NNWR) for solving hyperbolic partial differential equations (PDEs) with time delay. These equations are relevant in numerous physical and engineering contexts, such as wave propagation, biological processes, and control systems, where the system's dynamics are influenced by past states. The study emphasizes the stability, convergence, and computational efficiency of these non-overlapping domain decomposition methods when applied to such problems. Specifically, the DNWR and NNWR algorithms are analyzed using both Fourier and Laplace transforms in asymmetric domain decomposition to assess their capability to manage delayed terms in hyperbolic systems. Using Fourier analysis, we establish linear convergence estimate for the numerical errors. Laplace transform analysis enables a more in-depth study for characterizing finite-step convergence. Additionally, we derive the optimal parameters required to achieve finite step convergence in presence of heterogeneous spatial domain. Theoretical findings are complemented by numerical experiments, showcasing the methods’ effectiveness in maintaining accuracy while reducing computational complexity. Additionally, the study explores potential extensions to more complex problems and diverse applications. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: The effects of walnut protein and its polyphenol conjugates on the rheological properties and printing characteristics of potato starch
Abstract: Potato starch (PS) has strong potential for use in the three-dimensional (3D) printed food industry because of its favorable gelatinization. However, the insufficient mechanical support of native PS gel limits its use in printing. To address this, walnut protein isolate (WPI), WPI–ellagic acid conjugate (WPI–EA), and WPI–quercitrin conjugate (WPI–QCN) were incorporated into the PS system. The pasting behavior and rheological properties of the PS-based composite gels were determined, along with their structural characteristics. The results showed that WPI enhanced the viscoelastic behavior and structural support of PS, with the 30% WPI gel exhibiting the most uniform network structure. In particular, incorporating WPI–EA0.4 (WPI–EA prepared with 10 mg/mL of WPI and 0.4 mg/mL of EA) into PS exhibited the highest G′ and G″ values, suggesting that a stronger network had formed. Incorporating WPI–QCN0.4 (WPI–QCN prepared with 10 mg/mL of WPI and 0.4 mg/mL of QCN) into PS produced a relatively uniform structure. PS with 30% WPI exhibited the best 3D printing performance among the PS–WPI blends. PS with WPI–EA0.4 or WPI–QCN0.4 further improved printing accuracy compared with PS–WPI. Particularly, incorporating WPI–QCN0.4 achieved the best printing accuracy, while incorporating WPI–EA0.4 produced printed products with high hardness and adhesiveness. Title: Hardy decomposition of higher order Lipschitz classes by polymonogenic functions

Abstract: In this paper we find a decomposition of higher order Lipschitz functions into the traces of a polymonogenic function and solve a related Riemann-Hilbert problem. Title: Inside the cooling die: prediction of the flow profile of a high-moisture soy protein melt during extrusion
Abstract: The fibrous structure of plant protein-based meat analogues, manufactured using high-moisture extrusion, is determined by the flow in the cooling die. However, currently there is little understanding of how the rheological properties influence said flow. In this work, we predict how a soy protein melt flows under changing inlet temperature, cooling temperature, and pH. The model relies on a pH- and temperature-dependent dynamic yield stress and a wall slip equation, parametrised by in situ MRI velocimetry measurements in a circular die. The model predicts that the inlet velocity profile quickly transforms into plug flow for neutral and acidic pH conditions, where the dynamic yield stress is higher. Under alkaline conditions, where the dynamic yield stress is lower, the central core remains flowing, after which it transitions to plug flow. The model was validated by pressure and temperature profiles from a rectangular cooling die, measured along the length of the cooling die. The model provides insight into the link between solidification of the protein melt and the shear stress and the velocity profiles inside the cooling die. Thus, a scalable model was created that can be used to predict the pressure drops and temperature/velocity profiles over different geometries and cooling conditions. This will enable future work to more accurately model flow in the transition zone and cooling die. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. Title: Learning hidden ecological and epidemic processes in a reduced-order space
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: We study data-driven learning of ecological and epidemic dynamics governed by nonlinear reaction and reaction–diffusion systems. We consider both neural approaches for learning the underlying reaction dynamics from trajectory data and Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) for discovering sparse, interpretable governing equations. A key component of this work is a partial-learning framework for reaction–diffusion systems. The prescribed diffusion operator is projected onto a reduced-order space and explicitly retained during differentiable integration, while only the unknown local eco-epidemic reaction is learned. This enables efficient training on fine spatial grids by evaluating the neural reaction only at a small set of informative nodes. The reduced solution is then reconstructed on the original fine grid and evaluated over both the training interval and an unseen future prediction horizon. Finally, the learned neural reaction is processed by SINDy to recover a sparse, interpretable symbolic model of the underlying dynamics. Experiments with clean and noisy data demonstrate high predictive accuracy, implicit denoising, computational efficiency, and the ability to recover sparse reaction models. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Deng F.; Guo R.; Qian M.; Zhang R.; Hu Y.; Lei Y.; Mo X.; Hu J.
Title: Lightweight U-Net with depthwise separable convolutions for image reconstruction through scattering media
Abstract: Imaging through scattering media remains a challenging inverse problem in computational optics. Deep learning enables end to end reconstruction, but existing networks are often too large for portable or embedded systems. We exploited a lightweight network named DSC-U-Net, which replaces standard convolutions in the classic U-Net with depthwise separable convolutions. This decomposition into channel-wise spatial filtering followed by pointwise fusion aligns with the statistical properties of speckle patterns, extracting local textures and cross channel features while dramatically reducing model complexity. Under 600-mesh scattering, DSC-U-Net achieves an average SSIM of 0.900 and PSNR of 25.61 dB, only 1.2% and 4.3% lower than the standard U-Net, yet reduces parameters by 72%, FLOPs by 63%, and model size by 72%. Under 220-mesh, SSIM and PSNR drop by 2.1% and 4.9%. On a CPU, DSC-U-Net runs at 18.7 ms per frame, about 2.5 times faster than U-Net, approaching real time performance. Ablation studies show that computational cost is concentrated in high channel deep layers, and full replacement yields the greatest lightweighting benefit. Our method strikes an excellent balance between reconstruction fidelity and efficiency, offering a practical solution for deploying scattering imaging on resource limited platforms. © 2026 Optica Publishing Group. Title: Garlic-modified g-C3N4 for alcohol oxidation reactions in aqueous phase
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: This work explores the selective photocatalytic oxidation of p -anisyl alcohol to p -anisaldehyde under low-energy UVA irradiation (365 nm) using garlic (1–10 wt%) to modify graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4). A series of materials containing varying amounts of garlic was synthesized via thermal treatment to evaluate the effects on their physicochemical properties and photocatalytic performance. The obtained solids were characterized using structural, textural, and optical techniques. The results revealed that garlic incorporation modified the properties of g-C3N4 without significantly affecting its fundamental structure. Overall, garlic treatment induced the raise of C content, which mainly altered the optical properties. Photoluminescence results provided evidence of enhanced charge-carrier separation in the modified samples. Photocatalytic tests demonstrated that all materials were active for p -anisyl alcohol oxidation. Among them, 1 wt% garlic exhibited the best overall performance, achieving high alcohol conversion, good selectivity towards p -anisaldehyde, and a yield close to 75–80%. Scavenger experiments indicated that superoxide radicals play a key role in the reaction mechanism. Furthermore, the modified catalyst displayed good stability over four consecutive reuse cycles, maintaining high conversion, selectivity, and yield values with little alteration of solid properties. Title: Free aromatic amino acids differentially remodel x-type high-molecular-weight glutenin subunits through solvation competition and π-mediated clustering

Title: Pumpkin seed protein glycation using glucose based natural deep eutectic solvents: A sustainable approach for tailoring their structural and functional characteristics
Abstract: Pumpkin seed proteins (PSP) are promising versatile food ingredient, and their functional properties can be further improved through Maillard-induced glycation in a NADES-based medium. Title: Comprehensive characterization of regulated and emerging marine toxins by UHPLC-IM-QTOF using automated MS/MS and collision cross section measurements

Title: Reproductive numbers and traveling fronts in models of protest dynamics with police management

Title: Thermally induced instability mechanism of binary egg white protein blends: a multiscale study on foaming properties and aggregation behavior based on selective depletion

Title: Seaweed polysaccharides as prebiotic candidates: Structural diversity, gut microbiome modulation, and sustainability potential
Abstract: The human gut microbiome represents a dynamic metabolic ecosystem critically linked to health and disease. Dysbiosis, a microbial imbalance, drives metabolic disorders, chronic inflammation, and neurodegeneration, necessitating innovative dietary interventions. While terrestrial prebiotics remain the most extensively studied, marine macroalgae represent a structurally diverse and comparatively underexplored source of prebiotic polysaccharides. Seaweeds biosynthesize structurally diverse polysaccharides such as fucoidan, alginate, carrageenan, and ulvan that can undergo colonic fermentation and modulate gut microbial communities, although their effects vary with molecular structure, molecular weight, processing, and dose, and carrageenan safety remains an area of ongoing debate. Accumulating preclinical and emerging clinical evidence suggests that these marine polysaccharides may promote short-chain fatty acid production, contribute to intestinal barrier reinforcement, and modulate immune responses, although robust large-scale clinical confirmation remains an important research priority. Beyond their potential nutritional and functional applications, seaweed cultivation epitomizes sustainability: zero freshwater, zero arable land, carbon-negative farming. This review unveils the molecular architecture, fermentation biochemistry, clinical evidence, and mechanistic networks underlying seaweed prebiotics' health-promoting effects. We have critically examined the structure-function relationships, comparative advantages over terrestrial sources, and translational barriers including standardization challenges, personalized responses, and regulatory hurdles. As precision nutrition converges with environmental imperatives, seaweed-derived fibres represent a transformative dual solution, advancing gut health while addressing planetary sustainability. This paradigm shift from land to ocean positions marine prebiotics at the nexus of next-generation functional foods and climate-resilient nutrition strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Cross-modal contrastive knowledge distillation with hierarchical decomposition for kidney tumor segmentation in non-contrast CT
Abstract: Kidney cancer is one of the most prevalent malignancies worldwide, often remaining asymptomatic in its early stages, leading to frequent incidental detection during routine CT screenings. While contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) provides rich contrast information that facilitates tumor delineation, non-contrast CT (NCCT) is more commonly used in routine screenings and for patients who cannot receive contrast agents. However, NCCT suffers from low contrast differences between tissues, making kidney tumor segmentation extremely challenging for existing deep learning models. To address this issue, we propose a novel Cross-Modal Contrastive Knowledge Distillation with Hierarchical Decomposition framework for NCCT-based kidney tumor segmentation. Our framework utilizes paired CECT and NCCT data during training to transfer rich contrast information from CECT to NCCT, while requiring only NCCT images during inference. To achieve more effective contrast feature transfer, we hierarchically decompose the segmentation task by separating kidney structure knowledge and contrast knowledge for kidney-tumor differentiation. This allows us to explicitly distill contrast-related knowledge from CECT into NCCT, focusing on the features required for accurate tumor segmentation. Furthermore, we introduce a difficulty-aware cross-modal contrastive learning strategy that aligns contrast-deficient NCCT tumor features with contrast-rich tumor representations from CECT while prioritizing challenging NCCT tumor regions that are more likely to be misclassified. Title: AVT: Adhesive visual tactile sensor for anthropomorphic and precise manipulation of tiny mechanical components
Abstract: Grasping and manipulation of tiny objects have always been a significant challenge in manufacturing and industrial automation, especially in tasks such as small-part sorting, kitting, and assembly preparation. This sensor incorporates a transparent adhesive layer with a visual tactile sensor, enabling the picking of multiple pieces using adhesive force while detecting the object types and locating the positions. Title: An adaptive hybrid interpolation-based algebraic multigrid preconditioner for high-contrast and multiscale problems
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: In this paper, we develop an algebraic multigrid (AMG) preconditioner with adaptive hybrid interpolation for high-contrast and multiscale problems. Title: Trust fusion: a weighted multi-perspective framework for ECG anomaly detection in IoMT
Abstract: Continuous electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring in Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) environments faces a fundamental precision–sensitivity trade–off. Title: Quantification to Symmetry-Breaking of Rotation Invariance for Attractors in Perturbed Lorenz System
Source title: Advances in Applied Mathematics and Mechanics
Abstract: For the existence of the external perturbation on the atmospheric system, the idealized Lorenz system cannot be used to describe the local characteristics of the atmospheric system accurately. From the opinion of mathematical physics, the failure of the description for local characteristics of the perturbed atmospheric system by the idealized Lorenz system is resulted from the symmetry-breaking effects on the local structure the solutions for the system, including the Lorenz attractor. This study aims to precisely quantify the symmetry-breaking degree of the rotation invariant law for the attractors in a perturbed Lorenz system to permit the reproduction on its local characteristics accurately. The attractors of the perturbed Lorenz system are reproduced employing the second-level fourth-order symplectic Runge-Kutta scheme firstly. The structure-preserving properties of the scheme are illustrated by the tiny relative energy error in the conservative field of the Lorenz system, which verifies the validity of the simulation results indirectly. The symmetry-breaking degree for the rotation invariant law of the attractors in the system is characterized by the quantized error defined as the Euclidean distance between the points on the trajectories of the rotated part and of the unrotated part at the same moment. The symmetry-breaking phenomenon characterized by the quantized error goes through three stages in sequence, including the slow growth stage, the quick growth stage, and the oscillation stage. In addition, a pair of Lorenz attractors with the approximate rotation invariant property are observed when the quantized error is in the slow growth stage or in the quick growth stage. From the numerical results, it can be found that, the perturbation may cause the periodic step increase (the amplitudes of steps are doubling increase approximately) of the error with the time elapse even if the perturbation is tiny, which leads to more serious damage to the stability of the system. Title: Dextrans differing in molecular weight and α-(1 → 3) branching exhibit distinct fermentation dynamics by human gut microbiota in vitro
Abstract: Dextran is a structurally diverse, soluble α-glucan produced by lactic acid bacteria, but how differences in its structure influence fermentability and microbiota modulation relative to other soluble fibers remains unclear. Title: Enhancing oil-water interfacial behavior and emulsion properties of abalone protein hydrolysate-inulin conjugates by pH-shift pretreatment and Maillard reaction

In contrast, neutral wet-heating favored aggregate formation and limited effective interfacial organization. Title: Emulsifying/foaming properties of soy protein hydrolysates/peptides: A critical review

This review critically examines the current understanding of how hydrolysis strategies influence the emulsifying and foaming behavior of SPHs. Conventional hydrolysis methods are discussed with emphasis on their effects on peptide composition, molecular weight distribution, structural modifications, and functional performance. The interacting factors mentioned are discussed while particular attention is given to the molecular mechanisms governing adsorption at oil–water and air–water interfaces, interfacial film formation, and the balance between improved surface activity and reduced interfacial stability resulting from excessive hydrolysis. Title: Fusion of EEG signals with adaptive encoder network-based attention deep learning for real-time driver drowsiness detection

Title: Effects of endogenous non-starch components on structural, rheological, and functional properties of starch in quinoa flour

Title: Harnessing metal-polyphenol networks (MPNs) to regulate the digestive kinetics and enhance gel properties of whey protein gel: The influence on intermolecular interaction force and microstructure

Title: Polysaccharide-driven assembly of β-Lactoglobulin complexes: structure–function relationships and application-oriented design
Abstract: β-Lactoglobulin (β-Lg) is an important model protein for studying protein–polysaccharide interactions because of its well-defined structure and favorable functional properties. Assembly proceeds from molecular association to nanoscale, mesoscale, and macroscale structures, including soluble complexes, nanoparticles, coacervate phases, and gel networks. These structures stabilize emulsions, deliver bioactive compounds, form gels, and modulate digestive behavior. The review also summarizes challenges related to stability during food processing, large-scale production, cost control, regulatory compliance, and safety. Moreover, the deformation patterns and the failure features of the lattices were highly dependent on the radial gradients. More importantly, by appropriate design, the graded gyroid lattice could achieve an elastic modulus within the range of that of the trabecular bones from both the femoral head and proximal tibia. Authors: Sun W.; Li F.; Wang Y.; Cui P.; Wang Y.; Li G.; Li X.; Wang S.
Title: Design and energy intensification of an ionic-liquid-assisted reactive extractive distillation process for tert-Amyl ethyl ether production
Abstract: The production of tert -amyl ethyl ether (TAEE) involves a quaternary azeotropic system consisting of ethyl alcohol (EtOH)/ tert -amyl alcohol (TAA)/TAEE/Water, making conventional distillation highly energy intensive. This study proposed an ionic liquid(ILs) based reactive extractive distillation strategy through kinetic modeling, computational screening, and process simulation optimization. Five intensified process schemes were also developed to improve separation performance. First, 100 candidate ILs were systematically screened using COSMOtherm, followed by the evaluation of nine organic solvents based on relative volatility analysis. According to selectivity and viscosity criteria, four high performance ILs were identified. Quantum chemical analysis further revealed the separation mechanism and confirmed that ILs perform better than organic solvents as entrainers. Accordingly, 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium acetate([BMIM][Ac]), was selected as the entrainers. Compared with conventional distillation, the process using [BMIM][Ac] reduced the total annual cost(TAC) by 38.06%. Furthermore, Heat-integration and Intermediate heat exchange reaction extractive distillation (HI-IHE-RED) process was developed. Compared with the process using [BMIM][Ac], this intensified scheme reduced the TAC by 21.38% and gaseous emissions by 32.36%. Overall, this study establishes an integrated research framework involving reaction kinetic modeling, computational screening, mechanistic validation, and process intensification, providing a promising industrial solution for the efficient and low carbon separation of complex etherification azeotropic systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Hu Y.; Xie F.; Gao Y.; Ji H.; Mu Y.; Xu R.
Title: Tribological behavior of selective laser melted Ti-15Mo alloy for bone implantation: Atomic scale mechanism and experimental investigation
Abstract: The biomedical β-titanium alloys exhibit relatively poor wear resistance, and the atomic-scale mechanism of friction and wear behavior remains unclear. The friction-wear behavior and damage mechanism of in-situ alloyed Ti-15Mo alloy fabricated by selective laser melting are investigated combined with experimental analysis and molecular dynamics simulations. The sufficient solid solution of Mo elements can be promoted by high-energy-density lasers, significantly reducing the friction coefficient and wear rate of the alloy in a simulated body fluid environment. The alloy is mainly characterized by adhesive wear and abrasive wear. During the friction process, the deformation dominated by the {110}< 111 > slip system is induced under the synergistic effect of normal load and tangential shear. The 1/2 < 111 > dislocations are preferentially activated due to the low critical shear stress. Additionally, a BCC→HCP stress-induced martensitic transformation is triggered in the high-strain region. Simultaneously, the chemical reactions are induced on the contact surface by frictional heat and shearing effect, leading to the formation of a composite oxide film dominated by dense TiO₂ and high-hardness MoO₂. Consequently, the wear can be effectively alleviated and load-bearing protection can be provided by this film. The Ti-15Mo alloy is successfully fabricated via in-situ alloying of mixed powder by SLM, and its friction and wear mechanism is comprehensively clarified. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhang Y.; Chen J.; Wang M.; Cui T.; Liang J.; Chen S.; Wang M.
Title: High-temperature tribological behavior of laser directed energy deposition NiCrCoAlTiWCS alloy: Strength-toughness matching, precipitation kinetics and synergistic mechanism
Abstract: Ni-based alloys with superior wear resistance, self-lubrication and coordinated strength-toughness are vital for laser directed energy deposition (LDED) remanufacturing of high-temperature (800–1200 ℃) friction parts. In this work, the Ni17Cr10Co7Al5Ti3W2C1S alloy powder was prepared by vacuum induction gas atomization (VIGA), and nine alloy samples were fabricated by LDED at different laser energy densities. The effects of laser energy density (45.5–166.7 J/mm2) on the precipitation kinetics of key phase and its corresponding strengthening-toughening and wear-resistant mechanisms were systematically investigated. At the optimal laser energy density of 71.4 J/mm2, an optimal matching relationship of multiphase microstructure was obtained in the alloy, which was composed of γ/γ′ matrix phase, Ti2SC MAX phase and TiS, and carbide phases including (Ti, W)C and Cr7C3. The sample exhibited a compressive strength of 3696 MPa, a compressive strain of 56.8%, and an ultrahigh compressive strength-plasticity product up to 209933 MPa·%. The optimal alloy exhibited a tensile strength of 808 MPa, an elongation of 7.2%, and a maximum tensile strength-plasticity product of 5818 MPa·%. At 800 ℃, the high-temperature wear rate of the sample was 1.58 × 10−5 mm3/(N·m), with a friction coefficient of 0.17. Compared with the Cr28Ni48W5 substrate alloy, its tensile strength and elongation increased by 65% and 112%, while the wear resistance and self-lubricating performance were improved by 98% and 59%. The enhancement of high-temperature wear-resistant and self-lubricating properties was mainly attributed to the synergistic effect between the strengthening-toughening effect of (Ti, W)C and Cr7C3 carbides and the in-situ formed self-lubricating film derived from the Ti2SC phase. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Physics-Informed neural network approach for surface wave propagation in functionally graded magnetoelastic layered media
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: This paper investigates propagation of SH-waves in a layered composite structure consisting of a pre-stressed functionally graded magnetoelastic orthotropic layer overlying a pre-stressed functionally graded orthotropic half-space under the influence of gravity. The study introduces a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework for the dispersion analysis of SH-waves in the considered composite medium. As a benchmark, an analytical solution to the dispersion relation is derived and used to validate accuracy and reliability of the proposed PINN formulation. In the developed PINN model, the phase velocity corresponding to a prescribed wave number is treated as a trainable parameter, enabling the determination of the dispersion relation associated with the nonlinear eigenvalue problem. The Adam optimizer is employed to minimize the loss function during the training process. In addition, the effects of different activation functions and network architectures, including variations in number of hidden layers and neurons, are systematically investigated to study the performance of the proposed framework. Error analysis is carried out using several norms, namely L1, L2, RMSE, relative absolute error, and L∞, to assess the accuracy of the predictions. Furthermore, the variation of phase velocity with wave number under different material parameters is investigated. The comparison between the analytical and PINN-based results demonstrates excellent agreement, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed deep learning approach for analysing dispersion relations in complex layered composite structures. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: pH-driven conformational switch enables efficient calcium-mediated gelation of Nicandra physalodes (Linn.) Gaertn. pectin
Abstract: This study elucidates a pH-driven conformational switch regulating the calcium-mediated gelation of Nicandra physalodes (Linn.) Gaertn. pectin (NPGP). NPGP possessed a high weight-average molecular weight of 516.01 kDa, a highly linear backbone containing 79.47% homogalacturonan, and a low degree of methoxylation of 38.42%, yet remained in a flowable sol state after Ca2+ addition at its native pH of 4.06. As the pH increased from 4.0 to 7.0, the fractal parameter decreased from 2.45 to 1.49, accompanied by increases in the radius of gyration from 26.41 to 31.86 nm and the maximum dimension from 205.18 to 234.79 nm. Liquid-state 1H NMR also indicated increased segmental mobility and changes in the local molecular environment after pH adjustment. Together, these results support a transition from a compact associated organization toward a more open nanoscale structural state. Consequently, adjusting the solution pH to 5.0–7.0 converted NPGP into a calcium-responsive gelling system that formed self-supporting gels at a calcium-to-carboxyl stoichiometric ratio (R) as low as 0.1. Gels formed at R values of 0.1 and 0.2 exhibited water-holding capacities above 95%, while R values of 0.2–0.5 provided a more suitable balance among mechanical strength, deformability, water retention, and structural stability. In contrast, excessive calcium addition at R = 1.0 caused network densification, syneresis, and reduced deformability. These combined structural and functional results support a proposed conformational unmasking model, in which the compact native organization may limit the effective accessibility of potential calcium-binding groups, whereas pH-induced structural rearrangement may increase their accessibility for calcium-mediated cross-linking. Title: Flame chemistry and stability of ammonia counterflow diffusion flames: Effects of hydrogen addition and oxygen enrichment
Abstract: This study investigates ammonia (NH3) counterflow diffusion flames (CDFs) under various conditions and evaluates contemporary kinetic mechanisms against experiments. First, ammonia CDFs with hydrogen additions and air are examined; second, pure ammonia flames with oxygen-enriched oxidizers are investigated; third, the influence of H2 addition on ammonia-hydrogen-argon CDFs is studied. Argon dilution maintains identical maximum flame temperatures, thereby achieving decoupling of thermal and kinetic effects. Extinction strain rates (ESR) are used to assess flame stability and kinetic mechanism performance. Flame structure is characterized by temperature and optical diagnostics of key excited species, including OH*, NH*, NH2*, and NO*. For selected CDFs, profiles of NH3, H2, and NO are quantified using a microprobe coupled with gas-phase diagnostics. Experimental results show good agreement with numerical predictions of ESR and temperatures in ammonia-hydrogen flames. However, under oxygen-enriched conditions, all mechanisms underpredict the peak temperatures. The mechanism proposed by Konnov [Combust. Flame 253 (2023) 112789] accurately reproduces NH* and NH2* profiles, whereas deviations remain for NO*. At higher hydrogen admixtures, the local depletion of NH3 and H2 becomes spatially separated due to preferential hydrogen diffusion. The measured chemiluminescence peaks coincide with these depletion zones, forming a double-peak structure that indicates a second reaction zone dominated by H2 oxidation. Numerical predictions reproduce NH3 and H2 depletion, but fail to capture the corresponding chemiluminescence double peaks. For OH*, the reaction OH* + H2O ⇌ H2O2 + H suppresses double-peak formation, whereas the governing pathways for NH*, NH2*, and NO* remain to be identified. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: A novel investigation on oxidation behavior of crude oil during in-situ combustion based on neural networks
Abstract: In-situ combustion (ISC) was regarded as a highly prospective thermal recovery technique, and its development performance was closely related to the oxidation behavior of crude oil. To accurately predict and evaluate crude oil oxidation behavior, high-pressure differential scanning calorimetry was employed to acquire heat release data at different heating rates. A dataset was then constructed using heating rate and temperature as the input variables and oxidation heat flow as the output variable. On this basis, prediction models based on a standard back propagation neural network (BP), a genetic algorithm-BP neural network (GA-BP), and a particle swarm optimization-BP neural network (PSO-BP) were established. The correlation coefficient (R) and root mean square error (RMSE) were utilized to assess the performance of three models. Furthermore, after determining the optimal network structure and training function, the particle swarm optimization (PSO) was introduced to refine the initial weights and biases of the model. Accordingly, the final optimized PSO-BP prediction model was constructed for accurate prediction and evaluation of crude oil oxidation behavior. The results showed that in comparison with the standard BP and GA-BP models, the PSO-BP model achieved greater fitting accuracy and lower prediction errors on the training and test sets, showing that PSO effectively enhanced the capability of the model to predict the nonlinear oxidation process of crude oil. The optimized PSO-BP model still fitted the experimental results well at a heating rate of 15 ℃/min, which verified its favorable generalization ability and stability. Title: Band-gap engineering of MoS2/TiO2 coatings for simultaneous corrosion and wear protection of titanium
Abstract: Simultaneous resistance to corrosion and wear remains a major challenge for titanium. Here, MoS2/TiO2 composite coatings were fabricated by plasma electrolytic oxidation, with duty cycle used to regulate phase composition, defect chemistry, and lubricant retention. At 15% duty cycle, D1 exhibited the highest anatase fraction (73%), widest optical band gap (3.19 eV), and lowest donor density (2.0 × 1019 cm−3), together with the highest charge-transfer resistance, lowest static corrosion current density (0.042 μA cm−2), and a low friction coefficient (~0.15). Title: BMHA-Net: A two-branch multiscale hierarchical attention network for depression severity estimation from facial videos
Abstract: Depression is a prevalent mental disorder that imposes a substantial public-health and socioeconomic burden, while conventional assessments based on rating scales and clinical interviews are constrained by subjectivity and limited professional resources, hindering large-scale, low-cost, and consistent assessment. Facial-video-based automated modeling provides a non-invasive alternative for depression severity estimation and has attracted increasing attention because facial dynamics may provide informative behavioral cues associated with depression. However, depression-related visual cues are often subtle, sparsely distributed, and sensitive to head pose, illumination, and inter-subject variability, while existing multi-branch attention designs may introduce additional parameter and computational overhead, making the balance between prediction accuracy and model complexity an important issue. To address these challenges, we propose BMHA-Net, a two-branch multiscale hierarchical attention network that enhances fine-grained facial cues through high-resolution local and shifted-window self-attention, captures global spatial dependencies through low-resolution global attention, and strengthens appearance–geometry complementarity via bidirectional cross-branch interaction and adaptive multi-scale fusion. Under the same visual-only input setting, BMHA-Net achieves lower FLOPs than several recent vision-based methods with reported computational costs while maintaining competitive regression performance. Additional experiments on DAIC-WOZ further demonstrate its adaptability to pre-extracted visual descriptors under a different depression-score protocol. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Molecular and mechanic insights into stability and interfacial regulation of nanoemulsion collector for low-rank coal flotation
Abstract: Nano-emulsions outperform conventional coarse emulsions in low-rank coal flotation due to their small size and long-term stability, yet their atomic-level interfacial mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study integrates flotation electro-mechanical testing (FEMTS) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to resolve the charge-modulated adhesion kinetics and hydration film dynamics of anionic, cationic and nonionic surfactant-stabilized diesel nanoemulsions. Molecular models of surfactants and coal surfaces were established, and the adsorption configurations or interfacial arrangements between them can be obtained through MD simulations. Anionic surfactants were found to form the densest, most highly ordered monomolecular protective films at the oil–water interface, resulting in the highest recorded total system energy (−448.7 kcal/mol) hydrogen bond density (61 nm−2) and the strongest interfacial interaction energy (−102.7 kcal/mol). Within the force measurement system, the maximum repulsive forces were exhibited by the anionic surfactant nano-emulsion, quantified at approximately 31.44μN for oil-oil interactions and 35.61μN for oil-coal interactions. These phenomena were attributed to the optimal hydrophobic matching effect and intense electrostatic double-layer repulsion. Additionally, the repulsive force was observed to increase progressively with higher surfactant concentrations. However, the electrostatic repulsion was significantly attenuated by the introduction of electrolytes, a result of the Debye shielding effect. This cross-scale investigation, integrating micromechanics with molecular conformation, establishes a comprehensive theoretical framework for understanding the adhesion kinetics of nano-emulsions on low-rank coal. These findings provide a critical physical foundation for the rational design of high-efficiency, low-consumption flotation reagents tailored for the clean utilization of coal resources. Authors: Wei L.; Chen M.; Chen Y.; Zhang C.
Title: Fast density clustering via layered diffusion
Abstract: Density-based clustering algorithms often encounter difficulties when handling datasets with non-uniform density. To address this issue, we propose a novel clustering algorithm, termed Layered Diffusion Density Clustering (LDDC), which performs clustering through a layer-by-layer diffusion process from centroid points to high-density regions and finally to low-density regions. Specifically, LDDC first categorizes data points into centroid points, high-density points, and low-density points. It then propagates labels from centroid points to neighboring high-density points, after which the labeled high-density points continue diffusing labels to their high-density neighbors. During this process, clusters whose centroid points are connected by dense paths are merged, and label propagation continues until all high-density points have been assigned, thereby forming the cluster backbone. Subsequently, low-density points are incorporated into the corresponding clusters through outward diffusion from the cluster backbone, while the remaining low-density points are grouped together according to their neighbor relationships. Through this layered diffusion strategy, LDDC can effectively identify clusters with arbitrary shapes and non-uniform densities. Experiments on 9 synthetic and 10 real-world datasets demonstrate that, relative to the best-performing competing method for each metric, LDDC achieves average improvements of 16.84%, 13.31%, and 9.48% in ARI, NMI, and ACC, respectively, while maintaining high computational efficiency. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Numerical modeling of melt pool dynamics by gas-particle flow in ultrasonic-assisted directed energy deposition
Abstract: The melt pool flow behavior caused by both ultrasonics and gas-particle stream is the basic factor determining the grain nucleation and morphology in ultrasonic assisted directed energy deposition (UADED). Here, we proposed a novel heat-fluid-solid-ultrasonic coupling model incorporating the carrier gas-particle interactions to control the melt pool dynamics in UADED. The research question addressed in this study is to understand the melt pool dynamics in UADED under the combined effects of gas-particle flow and ultrasonic vibration. Ultrasonic forces and particle forces are introduced into the momentum equation to reveal the melt pool dynamics and the following microstructural evolutions. The new understanding is that the coupling model can describe the effect of process parameters on melt pool behavior under ultrasonic vibration. When the gas pressure is increased from 0.5 to 0.7 MPa, the melt pool velocity varies from 47 to 58 mm/s and the cooling rate increases by 205 K/s. This change leads to a 40 μm refinement in the average grain size. When the particle flow rate is increased from 8.15 to 10.15 g/min, the melt pool velocity rises from 49 to 61 mm/s and the cooling rate increases by 145 K/s. This results in a 17.6% increase in the nucleation rate. Title: Synergistic effect of the warm plasma discharge and the flow field on the ammonia/air premixed combustion stabilization near the lean blowout limit
Abstract: This work investigates the synergistic effect of the warm plasma discharge and the flow field on the ammonia combustion stabilization under different discharge powers and swirl numbers by a novel contribution analysis method that integrates the numerical simulation with a theoretical S-curve model. Title: Detecting cryptographic algorithm substitution attack in practice
Abstract: Algorithmic Substitution Attack (ASA) is a class of subversion attack techniques where the attacker subverts the cryptographic algorithm implementation such that the subversion is undetectable in a black-box manner, and the attacker can efficiently recover the secrets. Since the seminal work by Bellare, Paterson and Rogaway, there has been a wave of research on algorithm substitution attacks in academia, and a series of ASAs has been proposed. However, up to now, there has been no research on detecting ASAs from a practical perspective. We propose two detection methods for stateless ASAs and stateful ASAs in practice. The detection for stateless ASAs is based on a time-side channel. We transform the time samples into 0,1-bit strings and establish the correspondence between the randomness of this string and the ASA of the algorithm. For stateful ASAs, we propose a state detection scheme by analyzing the underlying code that may contain state storage operations. We also implement our method and successfully detect these ASAs implemented based on mainstream standardized cryptographic algorithms in OpenSSL, which verifies the effectiveness of our method. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Scale-armor-inspired rigid-soft-coupled heterogeneous structures: Additive manufacturing and tribological mechanisms
Abstract: Biological scale armor offers a natural strategy for reconciling lightweight design with wear resistance through rigid-soft synergy. However, the pronounced mismatch in composition and mechanical properties between rigid and soft materials often causes interfacial incompatibility and stress concentration, hindering the precise fabrication and tribological optimization of bioinspired rigid-soft coupled structures. Inspired by the wear-resistant and drag-reducing structure of desert lizard scales, we construct a bioinspired rigid-soft coupled structure (BRSCS) by multimaterial additive manufacturing and systematically investigate how structural parameters affect its friction and wear behavior. Title: Microbiologically influenced corrosion behavior of 10CrNi5MoV high-strength steel in marine environments
Abstract: 10CrNi5MoV high-strength steel may suffer from microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC) caused by sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB), posing a severe threat to structural integrity and service safety. Title: The completeness of spaces of semi-Lipschitz functions in fuzzy quasi-normed spaces
