Title: Impact of distributor zone design on flow uniformity in metal foam cooling flow fields of PEMFC
Abstract: In a proton exchange membrane fuel cell, the distributor zone of a metal foam cooling flow field directly affects coolant distribution among the cooling branches and the resulting temperature uniformity. This study systematically investigated how three key design parameters, namely distributor zone shape, circular hole diameter, and number of circular holes, regulate coolant flow uniformity. Title: Coupled convection–radiation heat transfer and optimization in microscale fin structures
Abstract: With the increasing power density of electronic devices, effective thermal management is essential for maintaining performance and reliability. Although air-cooled heat sinks have been extensively investigated, studies have primarily focused on structural optimization and convective heat transfer, while the contribution of surface radiation has received comparatively limited attention in microscale thermal management. This study investigates a backside-integrated air-cooled heat sink, with particular emphasis on the coupled effects of forced convection and surface radiation at the microscale. Comparative analysis shows that the parallel plate fin structure provides the best heat dissipation performance, while fin optimization reveals a trade-off between heat transfer enhancement and flow resistance. Furthermore, increasing the inlet velocity effectively enhances convective heat transfer and reduces the chip temperature, but the cooling benefit gradually diminishes beyond approximately 1.2 m/s, whereas flow-related energy consumption continues to increase. Meanwhile, radiative heat transfer is strongly influenced by flow conditions and input power, with surface emissivity playing an increasingly important role under low velocity and high input power conditions. At an inlet velocity of 0.2 m/s, increasing the emissivity from 0.05 to 0.95 reduces the maximum chip temperature by approximately 10.8 °C at 0.1 W and 33.3 °C at 0.3 W. At ε = 0.95 and v = 0.2 m/s, the radiative contribution reaches 32.0%, 34.3%, and 36.4% at input powers of 0.1 W, 0.2 W and 0.3 W, respectively. These results demonstrate that appropriate matching of inlet velocity and surface emissivity can effectively regulate heat dissipation while reducing reliance on excessive airflow. The findings provide a practical basis for the design and optimization of integrated thermal management systems for high power density electronic devices. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Authors: Zhang Y.; Fang Z.; Fan J.

Title: Learnability of neural networks under weak moment conditions
Source title: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the statistical performance of deep neural networks in the presence of heavy-tailed noise, including scenarios where the noise has infinite variance. Employing an information theoretic learning framework, we analyze the generalization capabilities of the empirical risk minimization estimator generated by deep ReLU networks in conjunction with Epanechnikov correntropy loss. Our findings show that these estimators achieve optimal learning rates under the condition that the regression function exhibits Hölder continuity, and the conditional noise distribution has finite p -th moment for some p>1. Notably, these learning rates exceed those typically seen in least squares regression under similar conditions, demonstrating the advantages of our method in addressing heavy-tailed noise effectively. Additionally, we explore a weaker moment condition and derive the corresponding learning rates for our proposed estimators. Interestingly, we find that these rates coincide with those of least squares regression when the stronger moment condition is satisfied. These results deepen our understanding of how non-convex loss functions can facilitate improved generalization in the presence of heavy-tailed noise. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Xie Z.; Guan J.-L.; Li M.
Title: Self-adaptive Bregman projection method based on the golden ratio technique for variational inequalities
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: This paper studies a golden ratio subgradient extragradient method with multiple sequences of parameters for solving variational inequalities in reflexive Banach spaces. By introducing an improved self-adaptive rule, not only does it avoid prior knowledge of Lipschitz constant of underlying operator, but it also accelerates the convergence rate of the algorithm. Under suitable assumptions and appropriate parameter choices, we obtain weak convergence and R-linear convergence results. In addition, we conduct numerical experiments in both Hilbert and non-Hilbert spaces, demonstrating that the proposed algorithm outperforms some existing ones in the literature. Finally, the proposed algorithm and the weak convergence result are applied to an image restoration problem, verifying the effectiveness and applicability of the algorithms. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zhang X.; Xia H.; Zhang X.; Liu J.
Author full names: Zhang, Xuerui (59147660300); Xia, Huanxiong (55386146800); Zhang, Xiumin (57221487959); Liu, Jianhua (55986543000)
Title: Vibration-induced contact response of rough interfaces: a dynamic model integrating multi-scale shoulder-shoulder contact
Abstract: The dynamic contact behavior of rough mating interfaces greatly impacts the dynamic performance of mechanical systems under vibration. However, modeling the nonlinear response induced by elasto-plastic normal contact and stick-slip tangential contact at interfaces remains challenging due to multi-scale behaviors and strong nonlinearity. This work proposes a nonlinear dynamic contact model incorporating multi-scale shoulder-shoulder contact analysis to predict the vibration-induced normal and tangential responses of rough interfaces under deterministic harmonic excitation. An improved adaptive time-step Newmark- β method matching the contact nonlinearity is derived to solve the dynamic governing equation. The model predictions agree well with experimental results for contact stiffness, damping, resonance frequency, and dynamic response, demonstrating higher accuracy than conventional tip-tip assumptions. Under vibration, the interface exhibits pronounced softening, jumping, super-harmonic, and sub-harmonic behaviors, with tangential contact showing stronger nonlinearity than normal contact. Increasing excitation amplitude intensifies nonlinear instability and promotes period-doubling and chaotic motions, whereas excitation frequency mainly regulates resonance amplification. Fractal topography strongly affects the dynamic response: larger fractal dimension and roughness intensify normal bifurcation behavior, while tangential stability shows a non-monotonic pattern with fractal dimension and low sensitivity to roughness. Moreover, increasing equivalent mass and asperity length scale suppresses the resonance response. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhang Y.; Zhang S.; Li Y.; Chen R.; Wen G.; Qin M.; Guo P.; Kim D.-E.; Li H.; Wang A.
Title: Pre-graphitized interface enables macroscopic superlubricity of Si-DLC:H coating
Abstract: Although superlubricity in silicon-doped hydrogenated diamond-like carbon coatings can enhance mechanical energy efficiency, but it is heavily dependent on special conditions, high contact loads and inert atmospheres. In this work, we proposed a strategy that combines pre-graphitization with tailored counterpart material to construct a weak chemically bonded interface for superlubricity. The fabricated Si-DLC:H coating exhibits high adhesion and mechanical properties (H=17.5 GPa, E = 130 GPa), enabling stable superlubricity (COF=0.009 ± 0.5‰) under N2. Friction-induced graphitization occurs concurrently with the formation of powdery wear debris, SiOx nanoparticles dispersed in a sp2-rich loose layer on the wear track. This debris forms a distinctive friction interface characterized by weak chemical bonding and low shear strength, ultimately leads to superlubricity. Supported by RMD simulations, this study provides a comprehensive understanding of the dynamic evolution of friction interface. It breaks through the conventional graphitization mechanism, and clarifies the macroscopic superlubricity mechanism from the perspective of weak chemical bond breaking and graphitization. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Lu W.; Ni C.; Wang Y.; Li X.; Zhu L.; Yang S.; Zhang B.; Yang Y.
Title: Tribological behavior of hierarchical ridge-pit microtextures on LPBF Ti-6Al-4V surfaces fabricated by longitudinal-torsional ultrasonic assisted milling: Anisotropy and heat treatment responses
Abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) enables near-net-shape fabrication and integrated manufacturing of complex structures. However, the non-equilibrium microstructure and poor surface integrity inherent to LPBF Ti-6Al-4V alloys limit their tribological performance. In this study, longitudinal-torsional ultrasonic assisted milling (LTUAM) was employed to improve the surface finish of LPBF Ti-6Al-4V alloys and fabricate hierarchical ridge-pit microtextured surfaces, with conventional milling (CM) serving as controls. The effects of laser scanning strategy, heat treatment, and lubrication condition on tribological behavior and wear mechanism were systematically investigated. The results demonstrate that LTUAM converts irregular machining marks generated by CM into periodic hierarchical microtextures, leading to improved surface finish and tribological performance. Under dry sliding, the hierarchical microtextures exert synergistic effects by reducing the real contact area, trapping wear debris, regulating frictional heat and strengthening the surface layer, resulting in a 36.56%-48.15% improvement in wear resistance. The wear mechanism on microstructured surfaces is predominantly mild abrasive wear accompanied by plastic deformation, whereas surfaces machined by CM exhibit a mixture of severe abrasive wear and adhesive wear. Under oil lubrication, lubricant retention, debris accommodation, and local hydrodynamic pressure further enhance tribological performance, reducing the coefficient of friction and wear rate by 23.86%-27.56% and 57.50%-65.54%, respectively. The as-built alloy exhibits pronounced tribological anisotropy, with the XOY surface outperforming the XOZ surface. Solution & aging further improve the tribological performance through microstructural homogenization and precipitation strengthening. This work provides fundamental insights into the integrated fabrication of tribological functional surfaces for additive-manufactured Ti-6Al-4V alloys. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Mishra A.; Sarkar R.B.; Faye A.; Guha S.
Author full names: Mishra, Amit (60895861200); Sarkar, Rudra Bubai (54401618000); Faye, Anshul (56006256200); Guha, Suman (55537611400)
Title: Size effects on the stretch flangeability of Dual-phase steels
Abstract: Dual Phase (DP) steels are known for their excellent combination of high strength and strain hardening capability, leading to superior formability offered by their unique microstructure of hard martensitic islands in a soft ferritic matrix. However, DP steels are among the high-strength grades that suffer from low stretch-flangeability, which is often measured by hole expansion ratio (HER). The HER depends on multiple processes as well as material parameters; hence, the correct prediction of HER has been a challenge. Additionally, size effects due to geometrically necessary dislocations are expected to play an essential role because of the shape, size, and morphology of the second-phase martensite particles in DP steels. The present work explores and explains experimental observations of the pronounced size effect of martensite island size on micro-scale deformation and failure initiation of the ferrite matrix, which significantly affects the stretch flagneability of DP steels. Towards this end, size effects due to geometrically necessary dislocations are modeled using a Conventional Mechanism-based Strain Gradient Plasticity (CMSGP) theory in micromechanics-based numerical simulations. The CMSGP model has been tailored by incorporating a failure criterion in terms of forming limit for the ferrite matrix to predict the initiation of strain localization. The experimental forming limit curve of an interstitial-free (IF) steel is used for this purpose because its mechanical properties are similar to those of ferrite in dual-phase steel. Statistically generated 2D RVEs have been used for numerical simulations. The effects of martensitic transformation and the corresponding strain gradients in the ferrite matrix, along with their implications on stretch flangeability, are explained. Findings suggest that the improved stretch flangeability can be obtained for DP steels having smaller martensite island sizes for a given volume fraction of martensite. Strain gradients play a dominant role in the improvement of HER, resulting in reduced plastic strain in the ferrite matrix with increasing length scale parameter. Furthermore, our results demonstrate that the plastic strains in the ferrite matrix generated due to martensitic transformation are important, and their consideration is essential for accurately predicting HER values using numerical simulations. A significant (≈20%) decrease in HER is observed in the presence of martensitic transformation strains. Overall, the study highlights the importance of martensite size effects at the microscopic level for better prediction of stretch-flangeability in multi-phase steels. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Masson SAS.

Authors: Huang Z.; Einaga H.
Title: Microwave–ozone coupling enables catalyst-free low-temperature carbon oxidation
Abstract: The removal of carbonaceous deposits, such as soot, typically requires high temperatures and often relies on costly noble metal catalysts, resulting in significant energy consumption and operational constraints. Herein, we demonstrate a catalyst-free approach to intensify carbon oxidation by coupling microwave irradiation with ozone activation, which enables continuous oxidation at low temperatures. Using a carbon fiber–SiC model system, the oxidation behavior was systematically investigated under conventional and microwave heating in the absence and presence of ozone. Under microwave irradiation, ozone-initiated oxidation occurred below 200 °C. The proposed mechanism is that microwave irradiation preferentially heats the solid phase while limiting gas-phase heating and ozone decomposition, thereby preserving ozone-derived oxidizing species for productive surface reactions and sustaining CO2 formation before self-sustaining combustion. The combined microwave–ozone treatment yielded the highest CO2 fraction (CO2/(CO2+CO) = 42.1 %), indicating a substantially higher degree of complete oxidation than the microwave-only and ozone-only treatments. Raman spectroscopy further supported this interpretation by showing the preferential removal of defect-rich carbon domains under microwave–ozone conditions. In addition, the microwave output power was generally lower for microwave–ozone than for microwave-only operation during the low-temperature stage before self-sustaining combustion; for conventional heating, an upper bound estimate based on the rated furnace power was provided. These findings establish a catalyst-free route for low-temperature carbon oxidation and offer mechanistic insights relevant to soot filter regeneration and carbon removal. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Liu R.; Liu Y.; Yang T.; Li P.; Meng Y.; Qiao L.; Qi J.; Yan Y.; Zheng X.
Title: Ni and C co-doping synergistically modulates the electronic distribution of MoO2 to achieve efficient hydrogen evolution in alkaline seawater
Abstract: Efficient seawater hydrogen evolution requires catalysts with high inherent activity and abundant active sites to overcome slow water dissociation and structural instability. Here, co-doping with Ni and C works synergistically to regulate electron redistribution and optimize the active sites. Supported on nickel foam, the Ni, C-MoO2 catalyst displays outstanding electrocatalytic activity for the HER in alkaline seawater. The Ni, C-MoO2 catalyst demonstrates exceptional HER performance in alkaline seawater, achieving an overpotential of 20 mV at 10 mA cm⁻2 and stability exceeding 1000 h. When paired with a Fe-MoO2 anode, the Ni, C-MoO2 cathode reached a cell voltage of 1.53 V at 10 mA cm⁻2 for overall water electrolysis. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses indicate that Ni and C co-doping synergistically modulates the electronic structure of MoO2. In this process, Ni acts as a structural activation site to drive water dissociation, while C serves as an electronic regulator to promote charge transfer. By collaboratively modulating the electronic structure of the Mo active center, they optimize the adsorption strength of hydrogen intermediates and lower the water dissociation energy barrier, thereby achieving efficient hydrogen evolution kinetics. This work offers a novel co-doping strategy and insights for scalable seawater electrolysis catalysts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Xiao S.; Li Y.; Huang Z.; Wu H.
Title: A geometry-aware operator learning framework for interface problems on varying domains
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: Solving Partial Differential Equation (PDE) interface problems on varying domains is a critical task in design and optimization, yet it remains computationally prohibitive for traditional solvers. Although operator learning has shown promise on fixed geometries, its potential for geometry-dependent interface problems has been largely unexplored. To bridge this gap, we propose an extension-based neural operator framework applicable to general linear interface problems. A key innovation of our method is the integration of the Tailored Finite Point Method (TFPM) with our base network, which reduces memory consumption and effectively alleviates the curse of dimensionality. On the theoretical front, we establish the continuity of the Helmholtz operator with respect to domain perturbations and provide rigorous error estimates for the proposed encodings. Comprehensive numerical experiments demonstrate that our framework achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and robustness. Consequently, this work provides a powerful, data-efficient tool for varying-domain simulations, offering new possibilities for real-time shape optimization. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Fe₂O₃–Mn₂O₃/CNTs reinforced hot-melt adhesive nanocomposites for the photocatalytic degradation of malachite green dye
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: The development of multifunctional polymer nanocomposites with enhanced photocatalytic performance has attracted considerable attention in recent years. In this study, 10 wt% and 20 wt% Fe₂O₃–Mn₂O₃/CNT-reinforced hot-melt adhesive (HMA) nanocomposites were successfully prepared using a solution-casting method. The films were characterized by SEM, UDF microscopy, EDX, FTIR, and XRD. Morphological analysis revealed that the nanofillers were well dispersed within the HMA matrix with average particle sizes below 250 nm. XRD analysis confirmed the formation of nanocomposites and showed a reduction in crystallite size from 28 nm for pristine HMA to 24.1 nm for the 20 wt% nanocomposite using the Scherrer equation. Photocatalytic studies demonstrated enhanced degradation of malachite green dye under UV–visible light irradiation. Pure HMA achieved 87% degradation, while 10 wt% and 20 wt% Fe₂O₃–Mn₂O₃/CNTs/HMA nanocomposites achieved 91% and 93% degradation, respectively, within 4 h. The recovered photocatalyst retained 65.6% efficiency after five cycles. Authors: Chen H.; Ning X.; Shao J.; Shu J.; Mao Y.; He F.; Ghayvat H.; Li Q.; Wang H.
Title: Unified sparse-view CT reconstruction via degradation-aware multi-view learning with residual prompts
Abstract: Sparse-view computed tomography (SVCT) is an efficient imaging technique that reduces radiation dose and shortens scanning time by limiting the number of projection angles. Nevertheless, such reconstructions have substantial artifacts arising from incomplete projection data acquisition. Existing methods typically necessitate individualized model training tailored to specific sparse-view configurations, lacking generalizability across different sparse-view settings and thereby limiting their applicability in clinical practice. In this paper, we propose a unified SVCT reconstruction framework, Residual Prompt-based Degradation-Aware Feedback Network (RP-DAFNet). Specifically, RP-DAFNet introduces a feedback regulation mechanism that utilizes preliminary reconstruction results to generate multi-scale degradation residual embeddings through the Degradation Residual Embedding Module (DREM). These embeddings are used to generate degradation-specific prompts via the proposed Degradation Residual Prompt Module (DRPM), which injects degradation-aware information into the network to dynamically guide the reconstruction process. Additionally, we introduce a Symmetry-Aware Position Attention (SAPA) block to refine symmetric anatomical structures within the reconstructed images. Experimental results on multiple datasets validate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework. The codes and models are available at https://github.com/hbchen98/RPDAFNet. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Protein nanofibrils as next-generation architectures for Pickering emulsions in food and nutraceuticals
Abstract: Amyloid-like protein nanofibrils are transformative Pickering stabilizers, potentially offering advantages over conventional particles due to their high aspect ratio, anisotropy, and tunable interfacial functionality. This review critically synthesizes advances in fibril-based emulsions, linking fibrillation pathways, morphology, interfacial mechanics, and performance. We examine thermal acid, subcritical water, ultrasonication, and enzymatic methods, showing how protein source, assembly conditions, and solvent polarity dictate fibril length, flexibility, wettability, and entanglement—governing adsorption kinetics and network formation. The anisotropic advantage can be understood through detachment energy, jamming, and rheology, which may surpass that of spherical particles under certain conditions. Emulsion architectures— oil-in-water (O/W) systems, high-internal-phase emulsions (HIPEs), oleogels, and double emulsions—are evaluated for nutraceutical encapsulation and delivery. A characterization toolbox (interfacial rheology, microscopy, oxidative stability, INFOGEST) establishes structure–function relationships. Critically, we provide an evidence-based safety assessment covering digestibility, cytotoxicity, immunogenicity, gastrointestinal fate, long-term and population-specific knowledge gaps, allergenicity, regulatory frameworks (EFSA/FDA), manufacturing scalability, and sustainability via by-product valorization, while emphasizing that safety determinations require case-by-case experimental substantiation. Harmonized reporting, predictive modeling, and integrated safety–sustainability assessments are needed for industrial adoption. Title: Nickel-incorporated Zn2In2S5 photocatalyst with S vacancies for ultrahigh-efficiency photocatalytic H2 evolution
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Element incorporation is a powerful strategy for enhancing charge separation and transfer kinetics in photocatalytic reactions. Herein, non-noble metal nickel was successfully incorporated into Zn2In2S5 nanosheets via a one-step solvothermal method for photocatalytic hydrogen (H2) evolution (PHE). The Ni-incorporated Zn2In2S5 (Ni-ZIS) exhibits a remarkable improvement in PHE performance, achieving an H2 evolution rate of 66.6 mmol g−1 h−1 compared to 3.5 mmol g−1 h−1 for pristine ZIS. This PHE rate of Ni-ZIS significantly surpasses that of previously reported ZIS-based photocatalysts. The results demonstrate that Ni incorporation optimizes the electronic structure of ZIS, enhancing visible light absorption and causing an upward shift of the conduction band edge and Fermi level. Moreover, the abundant sulfur vacancies and S-Ni bonds in Ni-ZIS play a crucial role in accelerating charge separation and transfer. Our work validates the promising potential of non-noble metal incorporation to enhance photocatalytic performance and provides a cost-effective strategy for developing high-performance photocatalysts. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Phycocyanin–chitooligosaccharide interactions drive the formation of blue soft wheat starch gels with modified digestibility: Linking multiscale structure to functional performance
Abstract: Designing starch-based soft gels with visual functionality and modulated digestibility is important for developing texture-modified foods. In this study, blue wheat starch composite gels were constructed by incorporating phycocyanin (Phy, 5% and 10%) and chitooligosaccharide (COS, 2.5% and 5%), and their formation, multiscale structure, physicochemical properties, and in vitro digestibility were systematically investigated. Phy imparted a blue to blue-green appearance to the gels, while COS further modulated their color characteristics. Phy and COS reduced pasting viscosity and viscosity rebuilding and promoted the transition from a dense, starch-dominated gel network toward a looser and more heterogeneous composite structure. Structural and thermal analyses revealed reduced short-range order, relative crystallinity, and gelatinization enthalpy, accompanied by weakened viscoelasticity and lower textural strength. The incorporation of Phy and COS also redistributed the digestible starch fractions, with increased RDS and decreased SDS and RS observed in several composite formulations. Molecular docking suggested that starch-derived glucan chains and COS could potentially recognize partially overlapping regions on the Phy surface, providing a possible molecular basis for local component association and subsequent structural reorganization. Overall, these findings demonstrate that Phy and COS regulate wheat starch gel properties through formulation-dependent structural reorganization, providing a basis for designing visually distinctive and soft-textured starch-based composite gels with modulated digestion profile. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Ratcheting instability evolution and fatigue failure mechanism in metallic chiral metamaterials manufactured by laser powder bed fusion
Abstract: Additively manufactured chiral lattice metamaterials offer unique opportunities for programmable deformation and energy absorption, yet their fatigue failure mechanisms and reliability remain insufficiently understood. Here, three representative metallic lattice metamaterials, namely non-chiral (NC), tetra-chiral (TC), and oblique-chiral (OC) structures, were fabricated by laser powder bed fusion. By integrating geometric-deviation analysis, in-situ multi-field characterization, and post-failure microscopy, this study clarifies how lattice topology modulates the load-transfer and deformation pathways through which manufacturing-induced imperfections affect structural instability and fatigue degradation. The results indicate that mechanical behavior of metallic lattice metamaterials is governed by the coupling between topology-dependent load-transfer paths and manufacturing-induced defect distribution. Under compression, NC structure dissipates energy through discrete layer-by-layer collapse, TC structure through compression–torsion-induced stress delocalization, whereas OC structure achieves the highest stiffness and peak strength at the expense of localized instability associated with manufacturing-induced imperfections. At the tested maximum stress of 9 MPa, the average fatigue lives of the TC and OC structures were approximately 48.2% and 68.9% lower, respectively, than that of the NC structure. Fatigue degradation was characterized by progressive ratcheting and a relatively stable cyclic strain range over most of the fatigue life. In-situ mechanical-acoustic-thermal characterization further resolves three fatigue failure pathways: delayed instability-induced buckling in NC, distributed buckling–torsion coupled fracture in TC, and defect-sensitive torsional-buckling collapse in OC. Title: Experimental study on the characteristics of methanotrophs in degrading coal seam methane using a RL-TW80 formulation
Abstract: Deep coal seams exhibit strong hydrophobicity and significant gas–liquid-solid interfacial mass transfer resistance, which severely limit methane degradation by methanotrophs . First, a community of methanotrophs was screened and enriched, and their growth characteristics and methane degradation capabilities in different surfactant solutions were investigated. Subsequently, experiments on wettability, interfacial tension, and quantitative adsorption were conducted to study the effects of the composite system on interfacial wetting properties and bacterial adhesion. The optimal RL:TW80 blend system (total concentration 0.048%, RL:TW80 = 7:3) improved methane degradation performance by approximately 15%, while reducing the surface tension to 41.81 mN/m and the stabilized contact angle on coal surfaces to 26.7°. The blend system also increased the maximum microbial adhesion capacity by 8.21% and significantly shortened the time required to reach the stable adhesion state. These results indicate that the primary advantage of this blend system lies in simultaneously improving microbial compatibility and gas–liquid–solid interfacial mass transfer, thereby enhancing the microbial degradation efficiency of methane and providing a new technical approach for the biological treatment of coal mine gas. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A dual-readout ratiometric fluorescence-smartphone assay for rapid preliminary screening of tetracycline-class residues in milk
Abstract: Tetracycline-class antibiotic residues in milk raise food safety concerns, requiring rapid, reliable preliminary screening of pretreated samples before instrumental confirmation. In this work, a dual-readout ratiometric fluorescence sensing platform based on a citrate-mediated biomass-derived PCDs/Eu3+ coordination sensing system (PCDs/Eu sensing system) was developed for rapid preliminary screening of tetracycline-class residues in pretreated milk samples. In this system, potato flour-derived carbon dots (PCDs) exhibit blue emission at 432 nm, while tetracycline antibiotics sensitize Eu3+ emission at 622 nm. Mechanistic studies using TC as a representative analyte supported predominantly inner-filter-related attenuation of the blue emission and coordination-assisted antenna sensitization of the red emission, generating a concentration-dependent ratio (F622/F432) and a blue-to-red transition. Under optimized conditions in buffer, the method exhibited linear ranges of 0.2-100 μM and calculated detection limits of 8.9 ± 0.1 nM (TC), 3.8 ± 0.09 nM (OTC), and 9.8 ± 0.12 nM (DOC). The assay provides dual quantitative readouts through fluorescence spectrometry and smartphone RGB analysis, while immobilization on paper strips enables portable visual and smartphone-assisted screening. Title: Ultrasound-assisted pH shifting modulates soy protein isolate-egg white protein complexes to retard corn starch retrogradation
Abstract: This study investigated the structural characteristics of a heterologous protein complex (soy protein isolate and egg white protein) prepared via ultrasound-assisted pH shifting, and its mechanism for inhibiting corn starch retrogradation was explored. The combined treatment improved the structural and functional properties of the protein complexes by enhancing hydrophobic interactions, disulfide bonds, and hydrogen bond rearrangements. Driven by electrostatic repulsion as well as enhanced hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions, the complex formed a uniform gel matrix with the starch, thereby inhibiting water penetration and granule swelling. These multiple interactions created a dense steric barrier between the protein and starch chains, hindering the orientation, entanglement, and recrystallization of amylose and amylopectin. This led to a significant slowdown in the increase of short-range order of the starch gel during storage, while the relative crystallinity only rises from 1.83% to 2.21%. These findings elucidate the intrinsic structure-activity relationship between protein structural modulation and anti-retrogradation behavior, offering mechanistic insights and a design rationale for the development of novel protein-based anti-retrogradation additives for starch-based foods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Liu T.; Cao X.; Shen M.; Yu Y.; Umar R.; Zhang Z.; Zhang L.; Li Y.
Title: A dual-biomimetic MOF integrated with a hydrogel microfluidic chip for dual-mode polyphenol detection
Abstract: The detection of polyphenols is critical for safeguarding nutritional quality and human health. A microfluidic device incorporating a dual-biomimetic sensing medium for both colorimetric and fluorescence detection of polyphenols was developed in this work. Microwave-assisted heating was employed for the synthesis of Fe-Cu MOF. Subsequently, a film of molecularly imprinted polymer was deposited onto its surface via spontaneous polymerization. Fe-Cu MOF and Fe-Cu MOF@MIP featured both excellent peroxidase-like activity and fluorescence properties. Thereafter, nanozyme hydrogels and 3D-printed microfluidic chips were prepared to design biosensors for rapid detection of polyphenols. Using this platform, total polyphenols and three individual polyphenols (GA, punicalagin and ellagic acid) in pomegranate peel (PPe) were successfully detected, with colorimetric detection limits below 32 nmol/L and fluorescence detection limits below 21 nmol/L. Title: Critical material thresholds influencing thermoelastic damping in piezoelectro-magneto-thermoelastic midspan microbeams
Abstract: A critical step in the design of high Q-factor microbeam resonators is estimating thermoelastic damping (TED). Most of the previous TED models were derived in isotropic/anisotropic beams. Those who considered smart materials did not account for midspan conditions. This work analytically investigates TED in piezoelectro–magneto–thermoelastic (PEMT) microbeams subjected to midspan (MS) symmetry and anti-symmetry constraints. The present beam is modeled as a laminate comprising identical, homogeneous, and perfectly bonded PEMT laminae. Each lamina has effective electro-magneto-thermo-mechanical properties corresponding to a two-phase BaTiO3-CoFe2O4 composite. The MS beam's first three symmetric (SM1, SM3, SM5) and first three anti-symmetric (ASM2, ASM4, ASM6) vibrational modes are analyzed. Linear Euler–Bernoulli beam theory is employed, and a comparative assessment of the Classical coupled, Lord–Shulman, and Green–Lindsay generalized thermal theories is performed. Numerical simulations are performed using the Newton–Raphson method to evaluate the eigenvalues corresponding to the MS boundary conditions. Modal shapes are derived, and the first six modal responses are characterized, providing insight into the influence of midspan constraints on damping characteristics and high-frequency applications of devices used to detect structural anomalies. Effects of thermal relaxation time, fiber volume fraction, beam dimensions, and vibrational modes on TED are also examined. Critical thickness (CrTh) and critical length (CrLt) values, where TED achieves maxima, are obtained for all modes. A critical value of fiber volume fraction is established in the range [0.4, 0.6], at which TED attains its maxima and the damping trend completely reverses. An exhaustive grid-search approach is employed to refine the estimated ranges of the critical fiber volume fraction, resulting in narrower intervals with improved accuracy. GL theory is found to produce maximum peak damping, which is traced to dual relaxation-induced phase lag between thermo-mechanical fields. The obtained outcomes provide quantitative design & development guidelines for property-tailored PEMT midspan microbeams having applications in supporting/stiffening different micro-structures, sensory analysis, MEMS/NEMS resonators, vibration suppression systems, SHM, and energy harvesting devices. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS

Authors: Zhang Y.; Wang H.; Wu W.; Wang Y.; Liu J.; Wang Y.; Zhao Y.; Li G.; Zhang G.
Title: Molten salt engineering of porous carbon materials for sustainable energy and environmental application: Mechanisms, parameter regulation, and structure-performance relationships
Abstract: Porous carbon materials are indispensable for sustainable energy conversion, energy storage, adsorption and separation, and catalytic applications because of their tunable pore structures, chemical stability, electrical conductivity, and adjustable surface chemistry. Molten salt-assisted synthesis has recently emerged as a versatile route for preparing porous carbons, as molten salts can simultaneously function as reaction media, heat-transfer media, physical templates, chemical activators, catalytic carbonization media, heteroatom-regulation platforms, and metal-anchoring environments. This review establishes a unified mechanistic theory from recent progress in molten-salt-derived porous carbon materials through the framework of “molten salt mechanism-preparation parameter-pore structure-application performance”. First, molten salt systems are classified into inert templating salts, chemically activating salts, and eutectic mixed salts, and their distinct pore-forming mechanisms, including spatial templating, redox etching, gas-evolving activation, metal-vapor intercalation, and liquid-phase mass-transfer-assisted activation, are discussed. Second, the effects of key preparation parameters, including salt-to-precursor ratio, mixing strategy, activation temperature, and activation time, are analyzed to clarify their nonlinear regulation of pore nucleation, growth, interconnection, widening, and collapse. Third, structure-performance relationships are reviewed for supercapacitors, alkali-metal-ion batteries, adsorption and separation, and catalytic applications, emphasizing application-specific requirements for pore-size distribution, surface functionality, heteroatom sites, and metal/carbon interfaces. Finally, current challenges and future perspectives are discussed, including in situ mechanistic characterization, rational salt-system design, closed-loop salt recycling, techno-economic analysis, and scalable green manufacturing. This review aims to provide mechanistic insight and design guidelines for advancing molten salt engineering from empirical porous-carbon synthesis toward function-oriented and sustainable materials manufacturing. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Qin H.; Yan F.; Su Y.; Yang X.
Title: Structural optimization and performance study of a biomimetic spiral baffle flow channel for PEMFC based on a BO-RBF surrogate model
Abstract: The bipolar plate is a key component of a proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC), and the flow channel structure on its surface directly affects the cell performance. Inspired by the spiral valve structure in the intestine of the Greenland shark, a biomimetic spiral baffle flow channel (BSBFC) is proposed in this study to achieve efficient mass transfer under low flow resistance. To perform the structural optimization and performance analysis of the BSBFC, a numerical model for PEMFC was first established via COMSOL. To reduce the computational cost of optimization, a surrogate model for predicting PEMFC net power density was developed based on a BO-RBF neural network. On this basis, Sobol sensitivity analysis was employed to quantify the influence of structural parameters on net power density, and the response surface method was used to analyze the interactions among parameters. Finally, a genetic algorithm (GA) was introduced for global optimization to obtain the optimal biomimetic spiral baffle flow channel (OBSBFC), which was comprehensively compared with a single straight flow channel (SSFC) and rectangular baffle flow channel (RBFC). The results show that, compared with the SSFC and RBFC, the OBSBFC increases the current density by 6.16 % and 3.05 %, and raises the net power density by 5.86 % and 5.32 %, respectively, and reduces the average liquid water saturation by 6.03 % and 4.38 %. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Hui W.; Xiao X.; Xu J.; Feng H.; Zhou J.; Shao X.
Title: Performance study of cascade thermal energy storage system with waste heat in hydrogen production plant
Abstract: Thermal runaway in alkaline water electrolyzers (AWE) poses critical safety risks to hydrogen production plants. Copper foam-based composite phase change materials (PCMs) demonstrate the dual functionality in AWE systems by simultaneously regulating the operational temperatures to mitigate thermal runaway risks and recovering waste heats. Moreover, the implementation of cascaded latent heat thermal energy storage (CTS) demonstrates the significant potential for improving the overall thermal efficiency. To improve the thermal matching within the CTS device, three paraffin-based PCMs with different phase change temperatures were investigated. Then a novel composite carrier material utilizing the copper foam skeleton was proposed, so as to improve the thermal conductivity of paraffin wax and prevent the leakage in its molten state. The CTS system was modeled in three dimensions using an enthalpy–porosity formulation. An exergy-based optimization methodology was established with dual objectives of achieving the maximum exergy efficiency while keeping the outlet temperature of heat transfer fluid at its rated value. The internal architecture was iteratively modified and analyzed to identify the optimal geometric configuration, which was then implemented in the energy storage unit. The thermal performances of energy storage configurations comprising one to five stages were systematically compared, and the system-level performance of the optimized CTS device was verified by TRNSYS full-link dynamic simulation. The results show that the volumetric liquid fraction of the optimized CTS device is 1.09 times that of the basic version; the three-stage CTS device achieves the most favorable trade-off between the thermodynamic performance and engineering practicability, with the highest exergy efficiency of 54.32%, a charging rate of 370.58 kJ/s, and a discharging cycle efficiency of 86.15%, avoiding the defects of two-stage, four-stage and five-stage configurations. The TRNSYS simulation verifies that the system achieves an actual Organic Rankine Cycle power generation efficiency of 7.6% and a daily net power generation of 3.10 × 105 kJ, realizing the energy self-consistency. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Title: Flat-punch contact modeling and slurry-specific removal behavior of micro-patterned pads in SiO₂ chemical mechanical planarization (CMP)
Abstract: In chemical mechanical planarization (CMP), pad structure governs slurry transport, contact-pressure distribution and abrasive–wafer interactions. However, conventional polyurethane pads exhibit stochastic and continuously evolving asperities, making their contact behavior difficult to control and limiting conventional Hertzian descriptions of flat-top micro-patterned pads. In this study, a structure-based material removal rate (MRR) model for SiO₂ CMP was developed using Sneddon flat-punch contact theory. The model incorporates designed contact area (DCA), designed inverse length (DICL) and pattern number density to describe edge stress concentration and particle-load saturation. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations were conducted to evaluate slurry velocity, pressure drop and residence time as functions of pad geometry. For silica slurry, where removal is primarily governed by mechanical abrasion of the hydrated SiO₂ surface, the calculated normalized MRR agreed well with pressure-dependent experiments. Calibration using Pad A yielded R² = 0.991 and MAPE = 2.25%, while independent prediction of Pad B without refitting achieved R² = 0.957 and MAPE = 4.76%. The model also captured the earlier particle-load saturation of Pad A relative to the higher-DCA Pad B with increasing pressure. Silica MRR increased monotonically with abrasive concentration, whereas ceria exhibited maximum MRR at 0.03 wt% for the micro-patterned pads and 0.05 wt% for the conventional pad. At higher ceria concentrations, increased ceria adsorption on the SiO₂ through Ce–O–Si bond reduced the number of abrasives effectively participating in material removal. These results clarify the coupled roles of pad geometry, slurry transport, contact mechanics and abrasive-specific interactions in SiO₂ CMP. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhao C.; Li J.; Jia X.; Li X.; Wang Y.
Title: PUIE: A physically inspired unified framework for image enhancement under complex illumination
Abstract: Images captured under complex illumination often suffer from coupled degradations encountered in low-light, backlit and underwater scenarios, which severely degrade visual quality and hinder subsequent vision applications. Although existing image enhancement methods have made substantial progress, most are tailored to specific scenarios and thus exhibit limited generalization in real-world environments. To address this issue, we propose PUIE, a unified and physically inspired framework for image enhancement under complex illumination. By analyzing the underlying imaging mechanisms, we unify diverse degradations into a common formulation involving multiplicative illumination modulation and additive perturbations, based on which the proposed framework performs sequential enhancement through transfer function-based brightness enhancement and degradation-guided image refinement. To better exploit degradation cues, we introduce a spatial-frequency degradation encoder, in which the spatial branch models non-uniform degradation distributions and structural artifacts, while the frequency branch captures spectral distortions and detail corruption. Based on these priors, a degradation-guided attention mechanism is further developed to inject degradation information into a Transformer backbone, enhancing global context modeling and facilitating content-consistent restoration. Extensive experiments on a mixed-degradation dataset and standard single-task datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves consistent and competitive performance across diverse complex illumination scenarios. © 2026

Title: Phase-resolved photoplethysmography imaging of microvascular responses to skin prick testing
Abstract: Background: Allergic skin reactions induce pronounced microvascular changes that are typically evaluated using wheal-and-flare responses. While photoplethysmography imaging (PPGI) can quantify perfusion amplitude, little is known about how local inflammation affects the temporal organization of pulsatile microvascular signals. Methods: This study is based on a secondary, cross-sectional observational analysis of data acquired during a previous clinical skin prick testing (SPT) protocol. Forearm PPGI recordings were acquired using a monochromatic camera, with simultaneously recorded fingertip photoplethysmography serving as a systemic reference. Cardiac-frequency components were extracted using wavelet ridge reconstruction, and phase shift (Δϕ), phase locking value (PLV), and phase-derived temporal offset (Δt) were computed. Linear mixed-effects models were used to assess associations with allergic reactivity. Results: Reactive SPT sites showed increased cardiac-band perfusion and a consistent phase advance relative to both references. Allergic sites exhibited phase shifts of approximately − 0.54 rad (fingertip) and − 0.52 rad (saline), corresponding to a temporal advance of about 60–65 ms, while synchronization remained high (PLV ≈ 0.81–0.91). Conclusion: Allergic inflammation is associated with local phase and temporal advance of pulsatile microvascular signals, indicating locally modified pulsatile dynamics in the skin. Phase analysis of PPGI provides complementary information beyond perfusion amplitude and may enhance objective assessment of inflammatory skin responses. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Zhang M.; Gao S.; Li W.; Gao E.; Hu N.; Chen Z.; Chen R.
Title: MoSi2-driven microstructural and passive-film synergy for enhanced tribocorrosion resistance in laser-cladded CoCrNi coatings
Abstract: Synergistic corrosion-wear critically threatens marine equipment reliability. However, conventional coatings can hardly realize synergistic tailoring of both corrosion and wear, let alone inhibit the coupled acceleration effect between them. Herein, a novel method was proposed via MoSi2-driven microstructural and passive-film synergy for enhanced tribocorrosion resistance in laser-cladded CoCrNi coatings. The corrosion, wear and tribocorrosion were investigated via in-situ measurement. The results demonstrated that incorporation of 6 wt% MoSi2 decreases the corrosion current density (icorr) by 99.41% and wear rate (K) by 48.73%, meanwhile, the strong acceleration effect between corrosion-wear is converted into weak synergistic, specifically, the icorr and K are reduced by 97.75% and 53.43% during tribocorrosion, respectively. Through molecular dynamics simulations, passive film kinetic analysis and multi-scale microstructure-performance characterizations, the mechanisms were revealed. On one hand, the Cr2O3 passive-film evolves into composite passive-film consisting of Cr₂O₃, MoO3, MoO2 and SiO2, in which, MoO3 reduces the migration barrier of O2-, diminishes oxygen vacancies and elevates the work function, thereby accelerating formation of passive-films with improved compactness. Thus, the thickness of passive-film increases by 252.17%, and the kinetic parameter n rises by 160%, enabling rapid re-passivation during tribocorrosion. On the other hand, solid-solution of Mo, precipitation of Cr5Si3 and grain refinement jointly increase coating hardness. Meanwhile, the composite passive-film possesses self-lubricating and a significantly higher elastic modulus (increased by 204.26%), alleviating the abrasion of both passive-film and coating. Working in synergy, these deliver an upgrade in corrosion and wear resistance, meanwhile quelling the coupled acceleration effect between them. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhang H.; Li G.; Fu W.; Luo Z.; Ye F.; Lü Q.
Title: A nonlinear elastoplastic subloading surface model for rock under cyclic loading-unloading with application to compressed air energy storage cavern operation
Abstract: A novel nonlinear elastoplastic subloading surface model (NEPS) is proposed for rock subjected to cyclic loading–unloading under general triaxial stress states. The model employs a modified generalized Zhang-Zhu (GZZ) criterion to describe three-dimensional nonlinear strength, introduces a plastic internal variable to characterize the evolution of rock mechanical properties with plastic deformation, and establishes a generalized subloading relation for the three-dimensional modified GZZ yield surface that evolves with the plastic state, thereby accounting for plastic evolution and loading history during stress reversal. Calibration against conventional triaxial cyclic loading–unloading tests and independent predictions under conventional and true triaxial cyclic conditions show that the NEPS model can reasonably reproduce the principal features of cyclic stress–strain response and residual-deformation accumulation. The model is further applied to the analysis of the mechanical response of compressed air energy storage (CAES) caverns during operation. The results show that the plastic state induced by excavation is carried over into the operation stage, and that the surrounding rock continues to adjust progressively with cycling even within a fixed internal pressure range. Expanding the operating pressure range intensifies irreversible deformation and promotes the outward development of plastic deformation in the surrounding rock. Interestingly, even when the operating internal pressure returns to the same level, the surrounding rock may exhibit different mechanical states, depending on the preceding cyclic process and the extrema of internal pressure previously experienced. The findings provide new insights into the evaluation of the operational state of CAES caverns. © 2026

Title: MOF-derived Co3O4/In2O3 p-n heterojunction with Core-Shell-like structure for efficient visible-light-assisted Peroxymonosulfate activation toward p-Nitrophenol degradation
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: To address the challenges of developing highly efficient visible-light-responsive peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activators, MOF-derived Co3O4/In2O3 p-n heterojunction catalysts with a core-shell-like structure (x-C/I) were constructed via an in situ growth and synergistic thermal conversion strategy employing ZIF-67/In(OH)3 as the starting material. Under visible-light assistance, the optimized catalyst (40-C/I, with a Co/In molar ratio of 40%) achieved a 98.4% removal rate of 20 mg/L p-nitrophenol (PNP) within 30 min, which was significantly superior to those of pure-phase In2O3 and Co3O4, and exhibited a TOC removal rate of 48.4%, indicating strong mineralization capability. After five consecutive cycling experiments, the catalyst retained good reactivity (removal rate of 79.8%), demonstrating its promising application potential. Mechanistic insights demonstrated that the built-in electric field, originating from the p-n heterojunction engineered at the Co3O4/In2O3 interface, substantially drove spatial charge separation and consequently expedited the Co2+/Co3+ redox kinetics. Concurrently, scavenger-trapping tests coupled with electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy identified superoxide radicals (2O•−) and singlet oxygen (1O2) as the primary reactive oxygen species (ROS) governing the catalytic process. Furthermore, the degradation pathways of PNP were elucidated via LC-MS, and T.E.S.T. theoretical calculations further confirmed that the ecotoxicity of the intermediates progressively decreased. This study paves a new avenue for the rational construction of highly efficient MOF-derived heterojunctions, offering profound insights into visible-light-elicited PMS activation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Orientation-dependent initial and fatigue-induced yield surface evolution of LPBF-fabricated SS316L
Abstract: In this study, the initial and fatigue-evolved yield surfaces of Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF)-fabricated stainless steel (SS) grade 316 L were experimentally characterised for three build orientations: horizontal (XY), inclined at 45° (ZX45), and vertical (Z). Uniaxial tensile tests revealed that XY printed specimen exhibit higher mechanical properties than those printed in other orientations. Initial yield surfaces were determined in axial-shear stress space using sixteen proportional loading paths and were fitted using isotropic (Tresca and Huber-von Mises-Hencky) and anisotropic (Hill48 and Szczepiński) yield criteria. The results demonstrated clear deviations from isotropic yielding, with the Szczepiński criterion providing the best agreement with the experimental yield points. Axial stress-controlled fatigue tests were subsequently performed with periodic interruptions at intervals of 20,000 cycles. At each interruption, the yield point was measured to capture the progressive evolution of the yield surface. The results showed orientation-dependent distortional hardening, characterised primarily by asymmetric evolution of axial tensile and compressive yield strengths, while shear yielding remained largely unchanged. Microstructural analysis confirmed that this evolution correlates with orientation-dependent changes in lattice misorientation and accumulated plastic strain. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Sr-tuned BaTiO3/NiFe-LDH heterostructured photocatalysts for solar-driven CO2-to-Fuel conversion
Abstract: Solar-driven CO2 conversion requires photocatalysts that combine strong redox power with efficient interfacial charge transfer. Here, Sr-tuned BaTiO3 was coupled with NiFe-layered double hydroxide to construct a 10BST/LDH heterostructure for selective CO2-to-fuel conversion. Among Ba1-xSrxTiO3 compositions, BST-0.15 showed the optimum structural and photocatalytic response, while 10 wt% loading on NiFe-LDH delivered the best performance. Structural, microscopic, elemental, and surface analyses confirmed the deposition of BST-0.15 nanoparticles on hierarchical NiFe-LDH nanosheets. Under irradiation, 10BST/LDH produced CO and CH3OH at 262.17 and 57.08 μmol g−1 h−1, respectively, with minor H2 and CH4 evolution of 27.01 and 2.01 μmol g−1 h−1. CO accounted for 81.61% of the carbon-containing products. Control experiments and 13CO2 tracing verified the photocatalytic origin of CO. Enhanced photocurrent, reduced impedance, irradiation-dependent ESR signals, and work-function/band-position analyses collectively indicated favourable interfacial charge redistribution, improved carrier separation, and enhanced surface redox activity. The catalyst also maintained activity during repeated irradiation and recycling. Title: Selective fractionation and valorization of maple wood using an Octadecyltrimethylammonium chloride/Ethylene glycol/Aluminum chloride ternary deep eutectic solvent
Abstract: This study developed a ternary deep eutectic solvent system (Octadecyltrimethylammonium chloride/Ethylene glycol/Aluminum chloride, abbreviated as STAC/EG/AlCl3) for efficient fractionation of maple wood (MP) and downstream utilization of carbohydrate-derived fractions, aiming to enhance the structural accessibility of lignocellulosic matrix through targeted deconstruction of MP, thereby enabling its value-added utilization. The treated MP was used as a substrate for simultaneous saccharification and fermentation (SSF) to produce ethanol, demonstrating the potential of the pretreated woody biomass for downstream bioethanol production. Meanwhile, hemicellulose was preferentially converted into xylo -oligosaccharides, achieving a maximum concentration of 4.46 g/L, corresponding to an apparent xylo -oligosaccharide mass yield of approximately 39.4 % based on the initial xylan. The substrate-normalized ethanol yield was 0.377 g ethanol/(g glucan + xylan in treated MP) via SSF. Structural analyses revealed substantial disruption of the biomass architecture, increased apparent cellulose crystallinity, and improved cellulose accessibility. Qualitative IGM analysis indicated noncovalent interaction regions consistent with hydrogen-bonding between the DES components and representative biomass models, providing supportive structural information for interpreting the observed fractionation behavior. Direct reuse experiments demonstrated that the DES retained partial pretreatment activity over repeated cycles. Overall, these results demonstrate the potential of the STAC/EG/AlCl3 system for the fractionation and downstream utilization of cellulose- and hemicellulose-derived fractions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Synergistic adhesion and hydration in aqueous lubrication enabled by PDA-TA-PAAm nanocomposites
Abstract: The widespread implementation of eco-friendly aqueous lubricants at heterogeneous interfaces (e.g., UHMWPE/copper (Cu)) remains severely hindered by water's ultralow viscosity and insufficient interfacial binding, preventing fluid-film load-bearing and exacerbating solid-state wear. To address these issues, a ternary nanocomposite suspension composed of polydopamine, tannic acid, and polyacrylamide (PDA–TA–PAAm) was fabricated through an in situ co-assembly strategy, and its tribological performance as a lubricant additive for a UHMWPE/Cu friction pair was systematically investigated. Through an in-depth analysis of the supramolecular cross-linking network, the synergistic mechanism of “bioinspired adhesion” and “hydration lubrication” at the dissimilar interfaces was fundamentally unraveled. Tribological evaluations revealed that, at the optimal concentration ratio (PDA:TA:PAAm = 50:50:50 mg/mL), the ternary system drastically reduced the coefficient of friction and wear rate by 69.68% and 78.99%, respectively, compared to the pure water baseline. Furthermore, the wear depth was significantly decreased by 47.15%. The dense supramolecular boundary film effectively prevented direct contact of the friction pair. Title: Conforming virtual element discretization of the generalized Stokes problem

Abstract: We develop and analyze a conforming Virtual Element Method on general polygonal meshes for the two-dimensional generalized Stokes equations. This parameter-dependent model provides a continuous transition between the classical Stokes problem and Darcy flow through the viscosity parameter ε. Our discretization employs enhanced virtual element spaces for the velocity, in which the normal trace on each edge is approximated by polynomials of degree one higher than those used for the tangential trace. We prove that the method is inf-sup stable with respect to the parameter ε. We provide the a priori error analysis in two different ϵ-weighted norms. In the first case, the a priori error analysis yields an optimal-order estimate for the velocity in a natural ε-weighted norm and a pressure estimate in the L2 norm also reveals the ε-dependency of the constants that appear in the priori analysis. In the second case, the weighted velocity estimate is uniform with respect to ε, which ensures robust approximation across the full Stokes–Darcy transition regime. We assess the performance of the method on several numerical tests using different families of polygonal meshes, including triangular, quadrilateral, Voronoi, and non-convex meshes. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Dual-site cooperation of Gd3+ and sulfur vacancies in CdIn2S4 for boosting photocatalytic H2O2 production
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production is recognized as a promising, eco-friendly, safe and feasible synthetic technology owing to its mild reaction conditions (room temperature and atmospheric pressure). Sulfide semiconductors are promising photocatalytic candidates. However, most sulfide photocatalysts exhibit low separation efficiency of photogenerated electrons and holes together with severe photocorrosion, which drastically lowers their performance for photocatalytic H2O2 generation. Herein, a gadolinium (Gd) and sulfur vacancy co-modified CdIn2S4 (denoted as CIS) photocatalyst were fabricated. The sites of Gd3+ and sulfur vacancies were capable of accumulating photogenerated electrons and boosting the separation and migration of photogenerated charge carriers. Title: Unveiling the critical role of g-C₃N₄ porosity in regulating donor density and Sonophotocatalytic activity of BiOCl/g-C₃N₄ heterojunctions

The g-C₃N₄ content was kept constant to isolate the effect of pore architecture. Title: Recent advances in starch-based cryogels and their hybrid systems: Production, functionalization, and applications in the food industry
Abstract: Starch-based cryogels have emerged as potentially sustainable alternatives to synthetic materials because of their renewable origin, biodegradability, and structural properties. Produced by freeze-drying, these macroporous materials exhibit high water absorption capacity, interconnected pore networks, and favorable mass transfer characteristics, supporting food preservation and packaging applications. This review examines recent advances in starch-based cryogels and hybrid systems obtained via freeze-drying. The effects of starch composition, polymer blending, and chemical modification on cryogel structure and functionality are discussed. Special emphasis is placed on the incorporation of active compounds, such as phenolic extracts, anthocyanins, organic acids, and essential oils, and their role in imparting antioxidant and antimicrobial properties. Current and emerging applications in active and intelligent food packaging are critically examined. Unlike previous broad reviews, this work integrates starch composition, processing, hybridization, active-compound incorporation, and food-application performance, while identifying key gaps in scalability, safety, regulatory compliance, and validation under real food-storage conditions. Starch-based cryogels demonstrate remarkable versatility as water- and exudate-absorbing materials capable of controlled release of active agents, contributing to extended shelf life, improved food safety, and reduced waste. Native starch cryogels can form stable networks through physical interactions without requiring synthetic crosslinking agents. However, chemically modified, hybrid, and nanocomposite systems may contain additional reagents or components whose migration, toxicity, biodegradability, and regulatory suitability must be evaluated according to their specific composition and intended food-contact application. Recent advances, including hybrid formulations and novel processing strategies, further expand their potential across the food and packaging industries. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Shen J.; Wang J.; Qian H.
Author full names: Shen, Jiebin (60988290000); Wang, Jian (59068670000); Qian, Hongjiang (57226105709)
Title: Prediction of microscopic crack initiation and macroscopic fatigue life of IN718 based on a cross-scale PI-GNN prediction framework
Abstract: The development of cross‑scale machine learning (ML) frameworks that integrate microstructural plastic evolution and macroscopic fatigue life prediction remains a challenging task. The present work proposes a physics-informed graph neural network (PI‑GNN) to predict microstructural crack initiation and be further extended to fatigue life evaluation. Material intrinsic properties, including spatial coordinate x i =(xi , yi , zi), applied load displacement Ldis , grain orientation ψ =(φ 1, φ 0, φ 2), grain size dgr and Schmid factor m , crystal plasticity parameters δ , grain boundary misorientation θ , and geometric compatibility factor η , are adopted as input features. Taking stored energy density (SED), which combines plastic work and dislocation density, as the fatigue indicator parameter (FIP), crystal plastic kinetics and dislocation density evolution theory are embedded to enable data-free prediction within the PI-GNN framework. Validated by EBSD test datasets, PI‑GNN exhibits high consistency with crystal plasticity finite element (CPFE) simulations in both the magnitude and spatial distribution of SED. The peak SED error ranges from 0.0147 to 0.0284, and its prediction performance is markedly superior to that of the physics-informed neural network (PINN). Fatigue life prediction results demonstrate that the performance of PI-GNN is very close to that of the traditional SED method but is notably superior to PINN, demonstrating its excellent predictive potential. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Duan Y.; Ma K.; Fu X.; Li S.; Chen R.; Zhao J.; Wang X.; Meng Y.H.; Zhang S.; Guo Y.
Title: Transparent and mechanically robust fish gelatin hydrogels through covalent–noncovalent interfacial regulation by dialdehyde carboxymethyl chitin nanofibers
Abstract: Polysaccharide reinforcement enhances the mechanical strength of fish gelatin (FG), narrowing its performance gap with mammalian gelatins (bovine and porcine gelatins). However, the improved mechanical strength is often accompanied by reduced optical transparency due to interfacial incompatibility-induced aggregation, phase separation, and light scattering. Herein, a covalent–noncovalent interfacial regulation strategy based on dialdehyde carboxymethyl chitin nanofibers (dCMCh-NF) was developed to optimize protein–polysaccharide interactions in FG hydrogels. At a low loading of 0.1 wt%, dCMCh-NF effectively reinforced the FG network. The FG/dCMCh8-NF hydrogel exhibited a hardness of 695.52 ± 4.51 g, significantly higher than that of pure FG (497.30 ± 19.19 g) and comparable to that of mammalian gelatin. Meanwhile, its light transmittance reached 85.70 ± 1.32%, markedly exceeding that of FG/CMCh-NF (71.37 ± 0.47%). Structural characterization and molecular dynamics simulations revealed that aldehyde groups on dCMCh-NF formed Schiff-base linkages with FG as the primary interaction, while hydrogen bonding and electrostatic interactions served as secondary stabilizing forces. This dual crosslinking suppressed local aggregation, reduced phase separation, and facilitated the formation of a homogeneous and compact network, thereby minimizing light scattering. This work establishes covalent–noncovalent interfacial regulation as an effective strategy for overcoming the inherent transparency-strength trade-off in polysaccharide-reinforced FG hydrogels. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Wang Q.; Zhang L.; Huang Z.
Title: MWG-Net: An attention-guided Multi-Scale Wavelet Gating Network for NSTEMI detection using multi-channel MCG
Abstract: Non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) may be missed during initial electrocardiographic evaluation. Magnetocardiography (MCG) is sensitive to subtle cardiac magnetic signals, but signal non-stationarity and inter-channel redundancy remain challenges for automated analysis. To address this, we propose a Multi-Scale Wavelet Gating Network (MWG-Net) for MCG-based NSTEMI classification. MWG-Net segments continuous signals into single heartbeats and applies the Stationary Wavelet Transform (SWT) to construct seven parallel input branches comprising the original signal and six SWT-derived components. Each branch employs a Multi-Scale Expert module and a 1D Convolutional Block Attention Module (1D-CBAM), followed by adaptive gating for participant-level cross-branch feature fusion. In a clinical cohort of 550 participants (243 with NSTEMI and 307 controls), 165 participants were reserved as an independent test set. MWG-Net achieved an accuracy of 93.33%, a sensitivity of 94.52%, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.9744 on the independent test set. Relatively higher gating weights for the cA5 and cD2 branches, together with branch-wise occlusion results, suggest that MWG-Net may utilize complementary multi-scale information related to slower ST–T variations and faster QRS morphological changes. Given the single-center setting, the generalizability of MWG-Net warrants further evaluation in independent cohorts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Kim K.; Pillai A.L.; Sharma D.; Xing J.; Saito T.; Kurose R.

Title: Effects of wall heat loss on flame structure and near-wall thermo-chemical interactions in laminar wall-stagnating spray flames
Abstract: This study systematically examines the effects of wall heat loss on the flame structure and near-wall thermo-chemical interactions of lean (ϕg = 0.85) and rich (ϕg = 1.30) methane/acetone/air laminar wall-stagnating spray flames. The acetone spray is represented by a fixed polydisperse size distribution with a Sauter mean diameter of 4.7 μm, using two-dimensional numerical simulations with the strain rate (K) varied through the inlet velocity. Adiabatic and isothermal (Tw = 400 K) walls are compared under otherwise identical conditions. The wall thermal boundary condition is the only prescribed difference between each paired simulation, enabling the coupled response to conductive wall heat transfer to be assessed. The sensitivity to wall heat loss reflects the spatial overlap between the reaction zone and the cooled near-wall region, characterized by the flame standoff distance (Hf). The results show that lean flames with a large Hf confine the wall heat loss to the post-flame gas, whereas rich flames stabilize close to the wall, where conductive loss reaches the reaction zone, reduces the laminar flame speed (SL), and suppresses its weak positive K dependence. Wall conduction is the dominant wall-induced additional loss, accounting for approximately 3–8% of the integrated heat release rate of the adiabatic case. By comparison, the droplet latent contribution remains small ('1%). For the rich flames, this overlap inhibits near-wall oxidation and leads to incomplete combustion, characterized by increased near-wall H2 rather than CO accumulation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Liu G.; Lei Y.; Zhang Y.; Ge H.; Zhang T.; Tan R.; Wu M.; Ma S.; Tan M.; Song T.
Title: Multiscale insights into the phase-dependent sintering of Fe2O3 and Fe3O4 under chemical looping conditions
Abstract: Iron-based oxygen carriers (OCs) are promising for chemical looping because of their low cost, high oxygen transport capacity, and inherent safety. However, their practical application is limited by severe sintering at elevated temperatures, and the phase-dependent atomic-scale sintering mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. Here, we combined reactive force field molecular dynamics (ReaxFF-MD) simulations with sintering experiments to directly compare the sintering behavior of Fe2O3 and Fe3O4 over 750–1050 °C. The results revealed that Fe3O4 exhibited lower atomic diffusion activation energies (31.8 kJ·mol−1 for bulk and 27.5 kJ·mol−1 for surface atoms) compared to Fe2O3 (49.0 kJ·mol−1 for bulk and 44.1 kJ·mol−1 for surface atoms). Consequently, Fe3O4 was identified as the kinetically more vulnerable phase, despite retaining partial crystallinity below 950 °C. Mechanistically, Fe2O3 sintering was dominated by volume diffusion, with viscous-flow-assisted sintering emerging at 1050 °C because of localized pre-melting, whereas Fe3O4 sintering was governed by coupled volume diffusion and grain boundary diffusion. Under representative redox conditions, H2 suppressed Fe2O3 sintering through surface hydroxylation and passivation, while O2 initially accelerated Fe3O4 sintering via iron-vacancy-mediated cation transport. Experimental grain-growth kinetics confirmed the higher sintering propensity of Fe3O4, which exhibited a significantly lower activation energy (98.1 kJ·mol−1) than Fe2O3 (184.0 kJ·mol−1). Overall, this work identified Fe3O4 as the critical instability window in Fe-based OCs and provided mechanistic guidance for improving their durability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Optimization of cooling efficiency over a heated block subjected to electrohydrodynamic actuation
Abstract: This study numerically investigates electrohydrodynamic (EHD)-assisted cooling of a heated block mounted in a two-dimensional channel. The coupled electric-field, flow, and energy equations are solved using the finite volume method under steady, incompressible, and two-dimensional conditions. The numerical simulations are carried out for 500≤ReDh≤1500, 14≤V0≤18kV and q″=1kW/m2. The effects of emitter-electrode position, collector-electrode configuration, and electrode spacing on thermo-electric efficiency, and thermo-hydraulic performance are systematically investigated. Heat transfer performance is highly sensitive to electrode arrangement. A major challenge is the occurrence of localized reverse heat transfer near the sharp edges of the heated block due to strong electric-field intensification and vortex recirculation. By increasing the vertical position of the emitter electrode from y=20mm to y=30mm under constant operating conditions (V0=18kV and ReDh=500), reverse heat transfer is completely eliminated, although the peak Nus decreases by approximately 32.1%. The EHD actuator is most effective at low Reynolds numbers (ReDh=500), where the ionic wind contribution is dominant relative to the flow momentum. Among the investigated configurations, the top-surface collector (Case 2) and the full-surface collector (Case 7) provide the highest heat transfer enhancement, with average Nusselt number increases of up to 515% (at x=25mm) and 578.8% (at x=32mm), respectively. However, the combined left–right collector configuration (Case 5) achieves the highest thermo-electric efficiency, reaching 137.4% (at x=25mm) while reducing electrical power consumption by 67.7%. Therefore, the optimal electrode configuration depends on the specific design objective. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Masson SAS.

Authors: Lei D.; Song P.; Li X.; Yang J.; Wang J.; Li B.; Zhang P.; Kong W.
Title: Nitrogen-doped carbon dots/glutathione-iron nanoflower enhanced fluorescent/photothermal dual-modal sensor for precision glyphosate detection
Abstract: The reliable detection of glyphosate (Gly) in complex samples remains a critical challenge due to inevitable interference of matrices and unpredictable factors. Conventional single-signal sensors are often susceptible to environmental fluctuations, leading to false-positive or false-negative results. This study aimed to develop a novel fluorescent/photothermal dual-modal sensor based on N-CDs/GSH-Fe nanoflower as the signal probe for the sensitive and accurate detection of Gly in complex matrices. A dual-modal sensing strategy was established by integrating fluorescence and photothermal signals into a single nanoprobe, enabling self-validation and mutual calibration between the two detection modes. Nitrogen-doped carbon dots (N-CDs) were synthesized via a hydrothermal method and subsequently complexed with glutathione-iron (GSH-Fe) to construct the N-CDs/GSH-Fe nanoflower probe, which exhibited excellent fluorescence and photothermal responses. The detection mechanism was investigated, and the analytical performance of both modes was evaluated under optimized conditions. Medicinal and edible malt and ginger were used as representative real samples to validate the practical applicability of the sensor. In the presence of Gly, the fluorescence signal of the nanoprobe was effectively quenched through a dynamic mechanism, while a distinct temperature change was simultaneously generated by the photothermal effect. Under optimized conditions, the fluorescent mode exhibited a linear range of 10-250 ng/mL with a limit of detection (LOD) of 2.34 ng/mL, whereas the photothermal mode achieved a broader linear range of 10-2000 ng/mL with a LOD of 3.68 ng/mL. The spiked recovery rates for the fluorescent mode ranged from 97.02% to 113.26%, while the photothermal mode achieved recoveries between 93.94% and 106.06% in medicinal and edible malt and ginger samples. The proposed dual-modal sensor offered high sensitivity, strong anti-interference capability, and operational simplicity, providing a promising strategy for the rapid and accurate detection of trace Gly residues in complex matrices and holding significant value for ensuring food quality and safety. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
