Authors: Yang H.; Yan L.; Yang S.; Zhao J.; Zhang W.
Title: Confined ZrO2 possessing triple catalytic functionality boosts luminol-dissolved oxygen electrochemiluminescence for immunoassay
Abstract: Developing high-performance electrochemiluminescence (ECL) is of great importance for trace cytokine analysis. Herein, zirconium dioxide (ZrO2) encapsulated within the silica nanochannel films (SNF) were first employed to amplify the ECL response of the luminol-dissolved oxygen (DO) system. ZrO2 nanoparticles were in-situ synthesized and confined within the SNF channels via a one-step electrodeposition strategy. Benefiting from its unique triple catalytic functionality, SNF-confined ZrO2 acts as an efficient co-reactant accelerator, resulting in markedly enhanced ECL performance. During the initial cathodic scan, the confined ZrO2 promotes the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), generating superoxide anion radicals (O2•−) and H2O2. In the subsequent anodic scan, the confined ZrO2 not only catalyzes the conversion of in-situ generated H2O2 into O2•−, but also facilitates the conversion of luminol anion (LH−) to its radical anion (L•-). These synergistic processes ensure efficient generation of abundant O2•− and L•-, ultimately boosting the ECL emission. Furthermore, an ECL immunosensor was fabricated for interleukin-6 (IL-6) detection through the oriented immobilization of antibodies on the external surface of SNF. The constructed immunosensor displays a wide linear range (1 fg mL−1 to 10 ng mL−1) and a low detection limit of 0.24 fg mL−1. This work demonstrates that SNF-confined ZrO2 holds promise as a versatile co-reactant accelerator for the construction of highly efficient ECL systems. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Xu T.; Yang X.; Dai S.; Liu B.; Xing W.; Zhu C.; Yu L.; Wu G.; Huang Y.
Title: Boosting hydrogen peroxide photosynthesis via a S-scheme heterojunction with interfacial electric field
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production provides a sustainable alternative to the anthraquinone process, but its practical application is still limited by inefficient charge separation and sluggish oxygen reduction kinetics. Herein, S-scheme BiOBr/tubular g-C3N4 (TCN) heterojunctions (BC) were rationally constructed through an in-situ growth strategy to simultaneously achieve efficient solar H2O2 production and antibiotic degradation. The synergistic effect of interfacial electronic interactions, band bending and the S-scheme charge-transfer mechanism promotes spatial carrier separation while maintaining the strong oxidation and reduction abilities of BiOBr and TCN, respectively. As a result, BC0.8 achieved a maximum H2O2 concentration of 4754.3 μM·g−1·h−1, which was 4.3 and 7.7 times higher than those of pristine TCN and BiOBr, respectively. Meanwhile, the photocatalytic system demonstrated excellent capability for simultaneous H2O2 production. During the degradation of oxytetracycline and tetracycline, H2O2 production rates of 4282.7 and 4182.2 μM·g−1·h−1 were achieved, respectively, accompanied by degradation efficiencies of 88.7% and 81.4%. These results demonstrate the feasibility of coupling solar H2O2 photosynthesis with antibiotic wastewater purification. Moreover, the photocatalyst maintained excellent H2O2 production performance in natural water matrices, including lake water and seawater, highlighting its practical applicability. Mechanistic investigations revealed that the enhanced photocatalytic performance originated from the synergistic effects of the S-scheme heterojunction, accelerated interfacial charge transfer and promoted selective two-electron oxygen reduction reaction. This work provides an effective strategy for integrating solar H2O2 production with practical water treatment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Han Y.; Wang S.; Wang X.; Li D.; He X.; Liao Z.
Title: Dry heat-treated and TGase-Modified mycoprotein emulsions: Aroma controlled release for mycoprotein-based meat analogues
Abstract: The sensory quality of meat analogues is compromised by aroma loss during thermal processing. To address this issue, high internal phase Pickering emulsions (HIPPEs) can achieve efficient aroma retention owing to encapsulation properties. Here, HIPPE aqueous phases were prepared from mycoprotein–xanthan gum conjugates and modified via dry heat treatment combined with TGase-mediated crosslinking. HIPPEs with excellent thermal stability and aroma encapsulation capacity were incorporated into mycoprotein-based meat analogues. The optimal condition is 70 °C dry heating and 4 h TGase crosslinking: the HIPPEs inhibited premature loss of meaty aroma during storage and cooking without additional off-aromas (verified by electronic nose and tongue). GC-MS quantification of beef aroma marker 4-ethyl-2-methoxyphenol confirmed chewing-triggered controlled aroma release, with low raw-state emission, a peak release of 18.15 μg/g during simulated chewing, and severe premature aroma loss in the unencapsulated control. This work provides a feasible strategy to optimize the aroma profile of mycoprotein-based meat analogues. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Wang Q.; Pei J.; Wei X.; Li Y.; Li H.; He J.; Chen B.; Li J.; Meng Y.; Yan L.
Title: Hierarchical FeCoP nanosheets array anchored on phenolic resin derived N-doped porous carbon as a high-efficiency bifunctional electrocatalyst for alkaline water splitting
Abstract: The conversion of pollutants into high-value-added energy chemicals holds considerable promise for ameliorating the prevailing fossil fuel-dominated energy landscape. Herein, we report the successful fabrication of a self-supported FeCoP/N-doped porous carbon (PC) using semi-coking wastewater derived phenolic resin-based N-doped PC as the functional scaffold, through a sequential strategy involving nitric acid hydrophilic treatment, hydrothermal reaction, and low-temperature phosphorization. Benefiting from its interconnected hierarchical porous architecture, abundant active sites, and favorable electrical conductivity, FeCoP/N-doped PC demonstrates remarkable HER and OER performance in alkaline media. For the HER, an overpotential of merely 83 mV vs. RHE is required to achieve 10 mA cm−2, with a Tafel slope as low as 76.7 mV dec−1. DFT calculations reveal that the Co-Co-bridge 3 site on the CoP (112) facet serves as the catalytically active center in the FeCoP/N-doped PC system, and the water dissociation barrier on this facet is 0.75 eV, substantially lower than the 1.24 eV calculated for the Fe2P (110) facet, thereby laying the foundation for superior alkaline HER activity from the initial reaction stage. Concurrently, FeCoP/N-doped PC also exhibits outstanding OER performance, requiring an overpotential of only 270 mV vs. RHE to deliver 20 mA cm−2, with a Tafel slope of 64.3 mV dec−1. Leveraging this exceptional bifunctional HER and OER properities, FeCoP/N-doped PC electrode pair achieves excellent overall water splitting performance, with a cell voltage of merely 1.48 V to reach 10 mA cm−2 and robust long-term operational stability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Kong Y.; Feng X.; Su X.; Bi Y.; Zhang L.; Liu S.
Title: Fe-porphyrin MOF nanozyme-based colorimetric sensor assisted by machine learning for detecting antioxidants in fruit juices
Abstract: Antioxidants (AOs) are key bioactive components governing the nutritional quality and oxidative stability of fruit juices. However, their similar reducing properties make it challenging for conventional single-signal colorimetric methods to combine individual quantitative analysis with pattern recognition in complex food matrices. Herein, an Fe-porphyrin metal-organic framework (FeP-MOF) nanozyme was constructed using iron(III) meso-tetra(4-carboxyphenyl)porphyrin chloride (Fe-TCPPCl) as the functional ligand, and further integrated into a platform for high-throughput quantification and machine-learning-assisted pattern recognition. The porous MOF framework enhanced the accessibility and catalytic efficiency of Fe-porphyrin active sites. Based on AOs-mediated inhibition of the FeP-MOF/H2O2/TMB oxidation reaction, a microplate-based colorimetric sensor was developed for quantitative detection of ascorbic acid, glutathione, cysteine, gallic acid, and tannic acid, with limits of detection of 0.52–41.54 μM. Moreover, a multi-pH cross-reactive sensor array converted single absorbance signals into composition-sensitive multidimensional fingerprints. Coupled with linear discriminant analysis and hierarchical cluster analysis, the array achieved cross-validated classification accuracies of 100.0% for five antioxidants and 98.0% for five fruit-juice categories. Results also agreed well with high-performance liquid chromatography measurements. This work integrates nanozyme amplification, quantitative analysis of individual antioxidants, fingerprint sensing, and data-driven classification, providing a versatile strategy for high-throughput AOs analysis and compositional evaluation in complex food systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Yu J.; Tang X.; Wei K.; Du Z.; Qiao X.; Li X.; Liu H.; Zhou F.
Title: Boosting methanol steam reforming performance via Fe-promoted Cu/c-ZrO2 catalysts: Experimental and theoretical insights
Abstract: Methanol steam reforming (MSR) is a promising approach for on-board hydrogen production; however, Cu-based catalysts still suffer from Cu sintering, sluggish reaction kinetics, and undesired CO formation. Herein, Fe-promoted Cu/c-ZrO2 catalysts were rationally designed to regulate Cu dispersion, electronic structure, and oxygen-vacancy chemistry. Combined experimental characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that moderate Fe incorporation (Fe/Cu = 0.25) optimizes the Cu-Fe-ZrO2 interfacial structure, generating highly dispersed Cu nanoparticles (∼11.2 nm) stabilized through interfacial Cu–O-Zr interactions. Fe promotion increases the proportion of Cu+ species from 52.1 % to 65.9 % and enhances surface oxygen-vacancy concentration from 23.8 % to 33.9 %, accompanied by the formation of mixed-valence Fe2+/Fe3+ species. As a result, Cu1Fe0.25/c-ZrO2 achieves 53.0 % methanol conversion at 473 K, a hydrogen production rate of 381.3 mmol·g−1·h−1 at 593 K, and nearly zero CO selectivity at 533 K. In situ DRIFTS, formate temperature-programmed desorption, and DFT calculations indicate that Fe-induced Cu+-oxygen vacancy synergy accelerates methoxy dehydrogenation and formate conversion through cooperative Langmuir–Hinshelwood (LH) and Mars-van Krevelen (MvK) pathways. Meanwhile, Fe modification promotes water activation and lowers the barrier for CO-containing intermediate oxidation, thereby suppressing CO accumulation. This work provides mechanistic insights into Fe-mediated electronic and oxygen-transfer regulation and offers a rational strategy for developing efficient low-temperature and CO-suppressing Cu-based MSR catalysts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Deng Y.; Han W.; Lin Y.; Chai X.; Chen F.; Liu Y.

Title: Selective partitioning of plant proteins during emulsification impairs foam stability: conformational changes of aqueous-phase residues relative to animal proteins
Abstract: The foam instability restricts the industrial application of plant protein-based whipped cream. Most current studies focus on the intrinsic properties of proteins, while there remains a lack of in-depth understanding regarding whether the emulsification process alters the protein composition in the aqueous phase and subsequently affects foaming performance. This study shows that during emulsification, aqueous-phase proteins undergo selective partitioning or depletion, altering remaining protein components and thus determining subsequent foam performance. Using animal proteins (sodium caseinate, SC; goat milk protein, GMP) as benchmarks, emulsions were formulated with plant proteins (pea protein isolate, PPI; soy protein isolate, SPI). Analysis of the results indicated that during emulsification, specific components of plant protein (66–175 kDa and 16 kDa) were preferentially depleted from the aqueous phase. Compared to animal proteins, this selective partitioning led to significant changes in the structure and surface properties of the residual protein in the aqueous phase: an increase of approximately 10% in β-sheet content, formation of more compact aggregates, and a reduction in surface hydrophobicity by over 39%. Ultimately, during whipping, the remaining plant protein exhibited lower diffusion and rearrangement rate constants at the air-water interface, resulting in slower interfacial dynamics, insufficient foam coverage, reduced whipping capacity (287%–308%), and faster foam breakdown. These results suggest that protein molecular characteristics, processing history, and non-protein components may collectively drive the selective partitioning process, with preferential adsorption at the oil-water interface potentially playing a key role. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Özen S.
Title: A non-explosive alpha-series recurrence framework for modelling mortality jump arrivals
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: Catastrophic mortality jumps disrupt long-term trends, yet existing jump models assume either constant jump probability or i.i.d. recurrence times, ignoring how jump-timing patterns evolve. The Lee–Carter framework is extended with a non-explosive alpha-series recurrence process, letting inter-jump durations shift with event order, nesting the stationary renewal process as a special case. Jump years are identified from the total-population mortality index and modelled as a common event sequence, with female and male dynamics linked through sex-specific effects and correlated innovations; the discretised likelihood uses exact recurrence-duration probabilities, including right-censoring after the most recent jump. Applied to Denmark, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, the UK, and the USA with a 2019 calibration cutoff, the model reveals substantial cross-country heterogeneity in jump recurrence and favourable forecast performance. For a term-life portfolio, alternative arrival mechanisms yield similar expected liabilities, while their relative differences become more visible in tail-capital measures, indicating that recurrence assumptions matter more for tail-risk assessment than for mean liability levels. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Bai R.; Jiang R.; Gao F.; Yuan K.; Zeng Y.; Zhang S.; Zhong Z.
Title: Construction of C-MnOx hetero-interface structure in MnOx/CNTs catalysts for enhanced NH3-SCR denitration
Abstract: Manganese oxide–carbon nanotube (MnOx/CNTs) catalysts have attracted considerable attention in low-temperature ammonia selective catalytic reduction (NH3-SCR) technology for achieving low-cost and efficient denitration of low-temperature flue gas. Herein, we report the synthesis of a series of MnOx/CNTs catalysts with varying MnOx loadings via in situ growth on CNTs to investigate the effect of the C-MnOx hetero-interface structure on NH3-SCR denitration. The C-MnOx hetero-interface structure formed between CNTs and MnOx induces the formation of a C-O-Mn structure and dual active sites in MnOx/CNTs. The C-O-Mn structure induces a strong interaction between CNTs and MnOx to regulate surface acidity, the Mn valence state and surface oxygen species, facilitating the adsorption and activation of reactants. In situ DRIFTs results suggest that the C-MnOx hetero-interface exhibits relatively separated adsorption and activation functions, where CNT-related acidic sites favour NH3 adsorption and MnOx-related sites contribute to NOx adsorption and activation, mitigating low-temperature NH3 over-oxidation. Consequently, the optimised MnOx/CNTs-0.01 catalyst exhibits outstanding activity, achieving > 95 % NOx conversion over a wide temperature range of 100–270 °C. This study highlights the critical role of interface engineering in boosting SCR at ultra-low-temperature and offers insights into designing high-efficiency catalysts for low-temperature flue gas treatment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Xie W.; Chen L.; Guo F.; Zhang T.; Abai S.; Wei B.; Ma R.
Title: Comparative study on the high-temperature corrosion mechanisms of boiler steel 15CrMoG induced by Cl2 and HCl in high-chlorine coal combustion environments
Abstract: Sha’erhu high-chlorine coal from Xinjiang contains more than 1% chlorine. Combustion of this coal releases chlorine-containing flue gas, which severely corrodes boiler waterwalls and threatens safe operation. During the corrosion, part of the HCl is converted to Cl2, however, the independent corrosive effect of Cl2 remains poorly understood. To clarify the differences between Cl2 and HCl, this study investigated the high-temperature corrosion behavior of 15CrMoG steel in O2-free and O2-containing atmospheres with HCl or Cl2 at equal molar Cl concentrations. Mass loss measurement, SEM-EDS, XRD, XPS, and thermodynamic analysis were used. A pronounced acceleration in the chlorine corrosion of 15CrMoG steel was observed between 550 and 650 °C. At 650 °C, the mass losses under HCl and Cl2 atmospheres surged by 189.55% and 164.41%, respectively, compared with those at 550 °C. Cl2, with stronger oxidizing power, preferentially forms the highly volatile FeCl3, making it more corrosive than HCl, which mainly yields FeCl2. The formation of FeCl2, FeCl3, and CrCl3 was directly confirmed by XPS. Combined XRD and EDS results demonstrated that Cl2 depleted Cr and Mo more thoroughly than HCl. O2 exhibited a synergistic effect on mass loss in both HCl and Cl2 environments. O2 played a dual role: it promoted oxide scale formation and drove a continuous chlorine cycle by oxidizing HCl to Cl2 and regenerating Cl2 from volatile chlorides, loosening the corrosion scale and intensifying spallation. This study clarifies the corrosive role of Cl2 in high-chlorine coal combustion and offers a theoretical basis for anti-corrosion design of waterwalls in such boilers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Qin X.; Wang Y.; Gong Q.; Lu Y.; Fang N.; Li W.; Ren Q.
Title: Experimental study on the effect of secondary air parameters on flame characteristics during high-temperature gas-solid combustion
Abstract: Fuel modified combustion is a key technology for the transition to clean, low-carbon energy, with high-temperature gas-solid combustion at its core. Using a 250 kW high-temperature gas-solid fuel combustion visualisation platform, experimental studies were conducted to investigate the effects of modified bituminous coal on the flame morphology, temperature distribution and pulsation characteristics of gas-solid combustion. The results indicate that secondary air velocity and oxygen concentration have a modulating effect on flame characteristics; when the secondary air velocity increased from 43.7 m/s to 87.4 m/s, the fluctuation range of the flame width increased from 94-149.5 mm to 117.5-189.5 mm, the maximum temperature decreased from 1657 °C to 1429 °C, and the amplitude of flame pulsation increased; when the oxygen concentration was increased from 44.5% to 73.9%, the range of fluctuation in flame width decreased from 100-119 mm to 71-104 mm, the maximum flame temperature rose from 1588 °C to 1775 °C, and the dynamic oscillation characteristics of the flame were further enhanced, with the pulsation amplitude showing an increasing trend as the oxygen concentration rose. In order to quantitatively characterise the evolution of jet flames, parametric fitting and model refinement were carried out on traditional empirical equations for flame width and divergence angle, as well as on the relationship between flame pulsation frequency and amplitude, based on flame visualisation data. This resulted in a model for the temporal distribution of flame width, divergence angle and pulsation amplitude that is suitable for high-temperature gas-solid combustion. This model provides a theoretical basis for characterising the flame behaviour in high-temperature gas-solid combustion and for optimising fuel modification combustion technology. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Xu D.; Zhang L.; Qi X.; Wang Y.; Shao D.; Yao Y.; He W.; Zhao Y.
Title: Ultraviolet-enhanced oxidative activation of pre-oxidized coal during storage: radical evolution and mechanistic insights into low-temperature oxidation
Abstract: Coal exposed to air and solar radiation during open storage and transportation undergoes progressive low-temperature oxidation; however, the molecular mechanism by which ultraviolet (UV) irradiation activates the radical network of pre-oxidized coal remains unclear. In this study, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, electron spin resonance, DMPO spin trapping, and DFT/TD-DFT calculations were integrated to elucidate the UV-induced generation and transformation of reactive radicals in pre-oxidized coal. Pre-oxidation reorganized oxygen-containing functionalities and aliphatic side chains, creating structurally labile sites that subsequently served as radical precursors under UV excitation. Upon irradiation, the concentration of persistent radicals increased markedly after approximately 5 min, with pre-oxidized coal exhibiting a substantially stronger radical response than weakly oxidized coal. DMPO spin trapping further identified the sequential evolution of three key reactive species. Carbon-centered radicals (R), which were scarcely detectable before irradiation, formed rapidly under UV exposure, indicating photoinduced cleavage of activated C–H and C–C bonds. The generated R subsequently reacted with O2 to form peroxyl radicals (ROO), followed by hydrogen abstraction, rearrangement, and decomposition to produce alkoxyl radicals (RO). Among these species, RO showed the most pronounced response to UV irradiation, suggesting a dominant role in sustaining radical-chain propagation. DFT/TD-DFT calculations further demonstrated that UV excitation promoted carbonyl-containing structures to the S1 and T1 excited states, weakened carbonyl-adjacent C–H and C–C bonds, and facilitated R formation and subsequent O2-involved radical reactions. The corresponding reductions in the energy barriers for O2 addition, hydrogen abstraction, and bond cleavage provide an energetic explanation for the experimentally observed R → ROO → RO sequence. These findings establish a sequential UV-activated radical mechanism in pre-oxidized coal, in which photoinduced R initiation, ROO formation, and RO-mediated propagation collectively accelerate low-temperature oxidation and increase the self-heating reactivity of coal. Authors: Sun B.H.
Title: Dimensional analysis and scaling laws with their applications in mechanics
Abstract: Dimensional analysis rests on a single requirement: physical laws cannot depend on the units in which they are expressed. This review presents its foundations, extensions, and applications in mechanics, with emphasis on its connection to symmetry. We first establish the three pillars of the method, namely the power law of dimensions, the law of dimensional homogeneity, and the Buckingham Π theorem, with proofs based on Cauchy’s functional equation and the rank–nullity theorem, and then develop similarity theory, the Π[jls-end-space/]-equality principle, and distorted models. Viewing dimensions as boundaries of discovery, we argue that Kepler’s three laws exhaust the kinematic dimensional degrees of freedom of planetary motion. We next examine the difficulties of the classical method and the extensions that address them: Huntley’s directed dimensions, Siano’s orientational analysis, Barenblatt’s incomplete similarity, Sonin’s generalized Π theorem, and allometric scaling laws. A central part of the review is the Lie group foundation of dimensional analysis. Changes of units form an Abelian scaling group, dimensionless Π groups are its invariants, the dimensional matrix is the coefficient matrix of its generators, and the Π theorem follows from the invariant theory of this group action. Sphere drag is worked through to show that the group calculation reproduces the classical one, and the simple pendulum, the West–Brown–Enquist allometric model, and the pressure drop in a pipe then show that symmetries other than changes of units supply further generators and reduce the number of invariants beyond what classical dimensional analysis can achieve. Six case studies then illustrate scaling-law mining: energy spectra of compressible turbulence, aquatic locomotion, capillary wrinkling of floating thin films, domino toppling, a generalized Kepler’s third law for classical and quantum N[jls-end-space/]-body systems, and similarity variables for Prandtl’s unsteady laminar boundary layer. In each case we distinguish what the Π theorem fixes from what must be supplied by additional physical input, calibration, or conjecture. Finally, we discuss the integration of dimensional analysis with machine learning and put forward two proposals, Dimension-Informed Neural Networks (DINN) and Scaling Law-Informed Neural Networks (SLINN), which have not yet been implemented or tested, together with their anticipated limitations and a program for their validation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Fu F.; Wang M.; Ren J.; Hu J.; Lu Z.; Xie J.; Cao Y.
Title: Construction of Ni3S2/NiFe-LDH heterostructure via in-situ sulfidation for enhanced electrocatalytic urea oxidation with overall water splitting
Abstract: Efficient, stable, and multifunctional self-supported electrocatalysts are highly desirable for advancing renewable energy conversion technologies. Herein, a two-step hydrothermal strategy combined with partial sulfidation is developed to construct tightly anchored Ni3S2/NiFe-LDH heterostructures on nickel foam. This strategy enables the in-situ integration of highly conductive Ni3S2 within NiFe-LDH nanosheet arrays. Microstructural and spectroscopic characterizations confirm strong interfacial electronic interactions, which modulate the electronic configurations of Ni and Fe active sites and strengthen the adsorption of reaction intermediates. Benefiting from the structural synergy and abundant exposed active sites, the as-fabricated electrode exhibits remarkable trifunctional electrocatalytic performance. At a current density of 10 mA cm−2, the catalyst delivers low overpotentials of 31 mV for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and 213 mV for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), while the urea oxidation reaction (UOR) proceeds at 1.312 V. Notably, urea-assisted water electrolysis only requires 1.39 V at 10 mA cm−2, which is substantially lower than the 1.48 V required for conventional urea-free overall water splitting (OWS). Authors: Li Y.; Gu T.; Long X.
Title: Resolving uniqueness in nanoindentation inverse analysis under spherical indentation using local strain fields and graph neural networks
Abstract: In nanoindentation inverse analysis, different combinations of elastic modulus and Poisson's ratio produce nearly identical applied load–penetration depth curves, resulting in a non-uniqueness problem in material parameter identification. This study focuses on spherical nanoindentation under an elastic-dominated deformation regime governed by Hertzian contact theory. Finite element simulations and graph neural networks are combined to investigate the relationship among indentation responses, local strain fields, and material parameters. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that different elastic modulus–Poisson's ratio combinations can generate virtually indistinguishable load–penetration depth curves when the effective elastic modulus remains constant. Finite element simulations further reveal that, despite nearly identical macroscopic responses, significant differences exist in the corresponding local strain-field distributions. Among the investigated strain components, radial strain exhibits the highest sensitivity to material parameters, indicating that local strain fields contain abundant parameter-dependent information that is not captured by conventional load–penetration depth curves. Based on these observations, a graph neural network framework is developed for both local strain-field prediction and material parameter inversion. By directly operating on nodal field data and preserving the spatial topology and neighborhood relationships of the deformation field, the proposed approach effectively exploits parameter-sensitive information embedded in local strain distributions. The results show that the proposed framework successfully resolves the non-uniqueness issue associated with conventional load–penetration depth curve-based inverse analysis and enables accurate identification of material parameters over a wide parameter range. In addition, the forward model achieves coefficients of determination greater than 0.95 for all strain components, demonstrating its capability as an efficient surrogate model for finite element simulations. The results indicate that the non-uniqueness problem originates primarily from the limited information content of macroscopic indentation responses. Local strain fields provide an effective source of parameter-sensitive information and offer a promising pathway for reliable material parameter identification and future integration with in-situ full-field experimental measurements. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS

Authors: Huang T.; Xiao Y.; Li D.; Chen S.; Chen S.; Wang W.; Yao H.
Title: Kinetics of natural gas hydrate formation and bed thickness evolution in wax-containing systems under multiple operating conditions
Abstract: Wax-containing multiphase systems can undergo concurrent wax precipitation and natural gas hydrate formation under high-pressure and low-temperature conditions, producing cohesive composite beds that increase flow assurance risk. However, the coupled effects of operating variables on hydrate formation kinetics and the subsequent evolution of interfacial bed thickness remain insufficiently quantified. In this study, wax-containing oil–water emulsions were investigated in a visual high-pressure reactor to determine the effects of water content (30–70 %), wax concentration (0–3 wt%), stirring speed (150–300 rpm), and pressure (3.5–5.5 MPa) on gas consumption, water-to-hydrate conversion (WTH), hydrate volume fraction (HVF), and bed thickness evolution. Increasing water content generally increased total hydrate formation but decreased conversion per unit amount of water. Wax exerted a non-monotonic dual effect: moderate wax contents promoted heterogeneous nucleation, whereas excessive wax enhanced interfacial blocking, viscosity, and mass transfer resistance. Increasing stirring speed strengthened mixing and interfacial renewal, although this benefit weakened at high wax concentration. At constant temperature and gas composition, increasing pressure increased the pressure-based thermodynamic driving force and promoted hydrate formation, with diminishing incremental gains at the highest pressures. A power-law kinetic model based on normalized thickness decay reproduced the temporal evolution of the gas–liquid interfacial wax-hydrate composite bed, with R2 = 0.9928, RMSE = 0.0688 cm, and MAE = 0.0388 cm. The model is intended for the investigated laboratory-scale system and parameter ranges and provides a quantitative basis for interpreting hydrate-deposition tendencies in wax-containing systems. Authors: Yang J.; Wang B.; Gong X.
Author full names: Yang, Jinyu (59014185200); Wang, Bochao (57203990189); Gong, Xinglong (55628578322)
Title: Large deformation visco-elasto-plastic constitutive modeling of shear stiffening elastomers
Abstract: Shear stiffening is characterized by a rapid increase in viscosity at high strain rates. Unlike shear stiffening gel and shear thickening fluid which may suffer from shape instability or require encapsulation during practical application, shear stiffening elastomer (SSE) maintains stable geometry and is easier to integrate into engineering designs. This makes SSE attractive for impact mitigation and protective equipment. However, existing studies on SSE mainly focus on material composition optimization and experimental characterization, while its constitutive modeling remains limited, particularly in capturing large deformation behavior over a wide range of strain rates, ensuring thermodynamic consistency and being supported by reliable experiments. To address this gap, we first perform systematic quantitative experiments from quasi-static to high strain rates to characterize the mechanical responses of SSE. Based on these results, we establish a novel visco-elasto-plastic constitutive model for SSE within a continuum mechanics framework. We then present a corresponding numerical implementation approach to solve the nonlinear constitutive equations and enable parameter identification. The proposed model accurately captures the mechanical behaviors of SSE. Furthermore, to facilitate engineering applications of SSE-based structures, we develop a VUMAT subroutine for the proposed constitutive model to predict the mechanical responses of structures under high strain-rate loading. Simulations show that besides shear stiffening, yielding of SSE also contributes to energy dissipation. The interplay of these mechanisms enables SSE-based composites to act as buffer components and reduce transmitted impulse under external impact. These findings provide guidance for practical design of SSE-based anti-impact structures. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS

Authors: Islam M.M.; Sheng J.J.; Hasan S.
Author full names: Islam, Md Mojahidul (58908687000); Sheng, James J. (59964347100); Hasan, Sobuj (60008131400)
Title: Effect of CO2 concentration on carbon sequestration and mechanical strength of coal-based solid waste cemented backfill
Abstract: Coal production generates large quantities of coal-based solid wastes (coal gangue, blast furnace slag, and fly ash) and significant CO2 emissions, creating severe ecological challenges in mining regions. This study integrates coal-based solid waste cemented backfilling with CO2 mineral sequestration to manage both solid wastes and CO2. The CO2 uptake and uniaxial compressive strength (UCS) of coal-based solid waste cemented backfill (CSCB) were investigated after 14 days of mineralization curing at CO2 concentrations of 0–10 vol%. Thermogravimetric analysis (TG), scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDS), and X-ray diffraction (XRD) were used to examine the sequestration mechanism and the associated strength reduction. CO2 uptake increased with CO2 concentration: raising the concentration from 1.5 to 10 vol% increased the uptake from 2.42 to 4.05 wt% (a 67.4% increase), based on a single TG measurement per group. In contrast, UCS decreased from 6.05 MPa (0 vol%) to 0.72 MPa (10 vol%), an 88.1% reduction. Microstructural and mineralogical analyses indicate that CO2 reacts with alkaline phases and hydration products (CH, MH, C-S(A)-H gel, and AFt) to form calcite, gypsum, and possible Mg-bearing carbonate (XRD peaks tentatively assigned to dolomite). The strength loss is attributed to weakening of the alkaline environment, decalcification of C-S(A)-H gel, and carbonation of AFt to gypsum. A concentration of 1.5 vol% provided a reasonable balance, with 2.42 wt% uptake and a 13.2% strength loss. These results show a clear trade-off between carbon uptake and mechanical performance in CSCB. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Effects of ultrasonication on structure and gelation of plant proteins at different denaturation states
Abstract: Changing the functionality of plant proteins can improve their applicability in food formulations. In this study, we investigated the effects of ultrasound (US; 20 kHz, 1 h, 2250 J/cm3) as a physical modification technique on faba bean protein isolate (FB, legumin-rich) and mung bean protein isolate (MB, vicilin-rich). Ultrasonication reduced particle size without causing protein degradation, but induced partial unfolding of the soluble protein fraction, altered intermolecular interactions, and decreased the denaturation enthalpy. Although G′ and G″ initially decreased after ultrasonication, subsequent heating promoted more effective structural reorganisation of the soluble protein fraction, which may have contributed to the recovery or enhancement of gel network formation, particularly in faba bean protein treated at 90 °C. Overall, these findings demonstrate that ultrasonication modulates the structure of the soluble protein fraction by promoting partial unfolding and reorganising non-covalent aggregates, with the extent of these changes depending on the protein composition and prior thermal state. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Catalytic pyrolysis of waste tires over acid–base modified paper-sludge-derived biochar for selective p-cymene production
Abstract: Waste tires (WT) and paper sludge (PS) are challenging solid wastes with limited resource utilization pathways, resulting in considerable environmental burdens. This study developed a dual-waste valorization strategy in which paper-sludge-derived biochar was sequentially modified by HCl deashing and KOH activation (HKSC) and used to selectively upgrade WT pyrolysis vapors toward p-cymene. HCl washing removed ash impurities and exposed the carbon framework, while subsequent KOH activation developed a hierarchical micro-mesoporous structure and regulated surface oxygen-containing functional groups and accessible acid sites. At 500 °C and a WT-to-HKSC mass ratio of 1:1.5, the aromatics content in the pyrolysis oil reached 76.40 %, while the p-cymene content and carbon yield reached 41.86 % and 16.04 %, respectively. Meanwhile, the carbon yield of D-limonene decreased from 16.34 % to 1.91 %, and the H2 volume fraction increased from 45.15 % to 70.33 %. The inverse trends in D-limonene and p-cymene suggest that D-limonene-derived intermediates were likely transformed into p-cymene through isomerization followed by dehydrogenative aromatization. Authors: Hao Y.; Pan Y.; Dai L.; Fan C.
Title: A refined grading evaluation method for borehole stability in gas drainage of soft coal seams
Abstract: Gas drainage in soft coal seams is often accompanied by borehole instability and collapse, resulting in reduced efficiency and an increased risk of gas hazards. Analysing borehole stability and identifying key deformation zones can guide on‑site support design to prevent collapse. Damage evolution of borehole surrounding rock increases borehole wall convergence and consequently reduces stability. We developed a mechanical model for borehole deformation and derived critical convergence thresholds for four damage characteristic points of the borehole wall, namely damage initiation, fracture propagation, fracture coalescence, and instability collapse. Using these thresholds as evaluation indices, we propose a refined grading method that classifies borehole stability into four levels (I–IV, with a higher level indicating lower stability). The stability level is then determined by comparing the measured convergence displacement against the thresholds. The method is validated with borehole deformation data from two coal mining faces. Unlike traditional empirical classification and numerical simulation, this method offers two main advantages. First, it allows dynamic adjustment of the evaluation indices to suit various geological and mining conditions, because the theoretical expressions of the thresholds have explicit quantitative relations to coal mechanical parameters, gas drainage pressure, and borehole dimensions. Second, it provides a quantitative failure potential index continuously distributed along the borehole, rather than discrete grade ratings. The grading strategy of this method avoids inadequate or excessive support design, thereby offering greater cost efficiency. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Xu J.; Meng Q.; Fan K.; Liu Q.; Ji J.
Title: 3D mesostructural modeling and DEM simulation of soil-rock mixtures using Minkowski sums
Abstract: This study presents a novel 3D mesoscale modeling framework for soil-rock mixtures (SRMs, a common type of high-volume fraction block-in-matrix rocks) integrating the Minkowski sum algorithm and the discrete element simulation method (DEM). The proposed approach with a feature of regulating the inter-particle spacing and uniformity of SRMs via Minkowski expansion, can well represent the complex concave particles through DEM clumps, and construct periodic random packings using a boundary placement algorithm. Cohesive elements are then embedded throughout the domain with distinct properties assigned to rock blocks, soil matrix, and their interfaces, enabling the simulation of completely compressive damage evolution. Numerical testing results align well with experimental data, and clearly indicate the dominant role of the cohesive element-based interface strength on the SRM's macroscopic response, e.g., with improved peak strength and ductility while with excellent ability to promote brittle failure. Parametric analyses show that the shear strength exerts greater influence on compressive resistance than the tensile strength, while increased fracture energy enhances both load capacity and deformability. Title: Pore-fracture evolution in deep coal under conventional and in situ stress- reconstructed loading–unloading paths: An online triaxial NMR study
Abstract: As mining advances to greater depths and technologies such as fluidized mining develop, understanding coal pore-fracture structure (PFS) evolution and its mechanical effects under deep in situ conditions becomes increasingly important. However, coring-induced unloading disturbs the original PFS, limiting laboratory characterization. This study combines nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), computed tomography (CT), and PFC3D simulations to compare the macroscopic and mesoscopic mechanical behavior of deep coal under simultaneous axial loading and confining pressure unloading, with and without prior in- situ stress reconstruction. During reconstruction, creep strain and pore signals stabilize concurrently, establishing a more stable initial structure representative of deep in situ stress conditions. Reconstruction increases peak deviatoric stress and produces modest, steady increases in PFS signals. Fractal dimension declines with minor fluctuations before dropping sharply near peak stress, showing a smoother trend than under conventional loading. NMRI and CT reveal shear failure under both loading paths, with reconstructed specimens developing more extensive secondary fractures beyond the main shear plane. Narrower ranges and smoother spatial variations in slice-based fractal dimensions indicate reduced spatial heterogeneity of post-failure fractures. PFC simulations reveal mixed tensile and shear cracking, with shear cracks predominating before peak stress. Crack accumulation accelerates near the peak. Stress reconstruction increases peak deviatoric stress by approximately 7% and the crack count at peak stress by 28%, with microcracks distributed more broadly beyond the main fracture band. Reconstruction delays damage localization, allowing higher peak strength to coexist with more numerous, spatially dispersed microcracks. These findings clarify stress-history-dependent PFS evolution and provide mesoscopic evidence for rock mechanics theories under coupled deep in situ conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Projected splitting methods for solving the generalized vertical polynomial complementarity problem

Abstract: For the generalized vertical polynomial complementarity problem (GVPCP), the sufficient conditions for existence of the solution are established. The relationships between solution to the GVPCP and solution to the vertical polynomial complementarity problem (VPCP) are discussed. We reformulate the GVPCP and VPCP as fixed point equations and propose projected splitting (PS) approaches, respectively. Convergence of the proposed methods is analyzed. Then we extend the PS method by using nonlinear activation functions. Finally, some numerical examples are provided to illustrate that the presented methods can solve the GVPCP and VPCP, respectively. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: A parallel projection-based method for solving variational inequality problems
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: In this paper, we propose a new method for solving paramonotone variational inequality problems on sublevel sets of differentiable convex functions. Instead of the orthogonal projection, we use the parallel projection, which is computationally more efficient. Our method involves constructing a parallel-projection-based dynamical system, which is then proven to possess a global solution that converges to the desired solution of the variational inequality problem. A discretization of this dynamical system yields a new iterative scheme. Title: Synergistic regulation of mechanical properties by gluten protein molecular matrix and micro-nano pore structure: Insights from different wheat varieties

Title: Investigation into pore structure regulation and CO2 adsorption mechanisms during PVC synergistic activation of gasification fine slag
Abstract: This study proposes a process that combines acid washing with KOH/PVC synergistic activation to prepare hierarchically micro-mesoporous carbon using coal gasification fine slag (CGFS) and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) as raw materials. When the PVC addition is 0.05 g in the co-alkali activation process, the CO2 adsorption capacity of the adsorbent(The dried HHCGFS was uniformly mixed with KOH and PVC at mass ratios of 1:2:0.05, HH-CGFS-2KOH-0.05PVC) reaches 47.63 cm3/g, and still remains at 23.65 cm3/g at 25 ℃, which is about 6 times higher than that of the unmodified slag. Title: Math-model informed neural network (MINN) for reproduction number of infectious diseases
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: Frequent pandemics of infectious diseases have had devastating global consequences. A central epidemiological metric for guiding effective public health interventions is the basic reproduction number, R0. Although mathematical models are commonly used to characterize transmission dynamics and derive R0, accurately computing this quantity remains challenging when models incorporate multiple transmission routes, time-varying parameters driven by seasonal or behavioral changes, or mobility-induced diffusion processes. Our approach leverages a neural network representation of the linearized infection subsystem, allowing for the computation of R0 without explicitly solving the system. We apply MINN to spatiotemporally homogeneous, spatially heterogeneous, temporally homogeneous, and fully spatiotemporally heterogeneous models of infectious diseases, including those with direct, environmental, and vector-borne transmission. Across all scenarios, MINN accurately estimates R0 and closely recovers previously established analytical or numerical benchmarks. This AI-augmented modeling framework provides a generalizable and efficient approach for estimating basic reproduction numbers, with potential utility in informing timely and effective pandemic-prevention policies. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Chang T.-C.; Lidz A.
Title: Line-intensity mapping
Abstract: Line-Intensity Mapping (LIM) has emerged as a powerful technique for studying large-scale structure and the high-redshift universe, enabling three-dimensional maps of line emission across vast cosmological volumes. In this review, we summarize the LIM framework, its key scientific goals, and its future prospects. We describe the landscape of emission line tracers, theoretical modeling approaches, anticipated signals, and data-analysis methodologies. We also discuss experimental challenges, particularly those posed by astrophysical foregrounds, and review possible mitigation strategies. Further, we highlight a range of cross-correlation science cases, linking LIM with other cosmological surveys. Finally, we summarize current and upcoming experiments and early results, including recent first detections, while outlining the outlook for future discoveries. Specifically, LIM may offer new insights into galaxy formation and evolution and cosmology, while revealing the Epoch of Reionization, Cosmic Dawn, and possibly the Cosmic Dark Ages. LIM enables cosmological measurements that complement other probes and provide unique access to the high-redshift universe, potentially shedding light on dark matter, dark energy, and cosmic inflation. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: Microscopic coupling mechanisms governing the tribological and corrosion performance of in-situ nano-carbide strengthened graphite/CuNiTiCrNb composite coatings
Abstract: Coupling corrosion and wear lead to the deterioration of the materials of marine moving parts. In this study, graphite/CuNiTiCrNb composite coatings were fabricated on titanium alloy substrates via laser cladding to improve tribological performance under corrosive marine environments. Title: A neural network approach to the boundary observer and control design for rotary drilling PDEs in oilwell systems

Abstract: Torsional vibrations in rotary drilling systems, particularly stick–slip oscillations, remain among the leading causes of drillstring failures, premature bit wear, and reduced penetration rates, translating into substantial economic losses and safety risks in oil and gas exploration operations. Motivated by the computational cost of gain kernel synthesis in PDE backstepping, we propose a stabilization strategy for hyperbolic PDE systems modeling torsional vibrations in rotary drilling, where the underlying dynamics are driven by a strongly nonlinear bit-rock interaction friction law. In this framework, the kernel solutions are approximated by a Deep Operator Network (DeepONet), enabling real-time control implementation. We establish the Lipschitz continuity of the kernel solution operator with respect to the plant coefficients and prove that DeepONets can uniformly approximate these operators on compact parameter sets. Title: Cryoprotective effect of fermented glutinous rice wine filtrate on the pre-fermented frozen dough quality subjected to freeze-thaw cycles: Antifreeze activity, water status, and gluten physicochemical property

Title: Oxygen recovery in a long channel PEM fuel cell using side injection: Balancing uniformity, power density, and pressure drop
Abstract: Increasing the length of proton exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cell channels attracts a lot of attention due to benefits such as enhanced reactant residence time, increased contact area and mass transfer path, and reduced edge effects. Title: Effects of reaction heat and active radicals derived from oxygen on supercritical water gasification of methanol for hydrogen production
Abstract: The role of oxygen in the product characteristics and reaction mechanism during supercritical water gasification of methanol was studied through detailed kinetic simulations. The water gas shift reaction was limited in the second stage by its own exothermic nature. Driven by the heat release and consequent temperature rise, the reactions proceeded to equilibrium more rapidly in the third stage. Furthermore, an optimal oxidation coefficient exists for maximizing the hydrogen yield. Title: Cross-modal vision transformer with energy-system priors for interpretable operational pattern discovery
Abstract: The identification of the repeating operating conditions for energy assets — namely, the limited range of states through which any turbine or building passes — forms an essential component of condition monitoring; however, since operating labels are seldom available at scale, the process has to be unsupervised. Title: Cathodic protection mitigates D. vulgaris corrosion of welded X80 steel in acidic soil
Abstract: Microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC) of welded pipeline steel in acidic soils is a critical safety concern, yet the role of cathodic protection (CP) in such inoculated environments remains largely unexplored. A counterintuitive finding is that CP induces localized alkalization and hydrogen evolution, which suppress D. vulgaris metabolic activity, resulting in shallower but far more numerous corrosion pits in inoculated solutions than in sterile ones−revealing an altered pitting propagation mechanism. Title: Interfacial heat transfer mechanism of solidified copper alloys on beryllium copper substrate for twin-roll casting
Abstract: To provide theoretical guidance and technical support for optimizing solid-substrate heat transfer in twin-roll casting of copper alloys, this study investigates the solid-state interfacial heat transfer behavior of solidified copper alloys on beryllium copper substrate surfaces. A series of heat transfer experiments were designed to simulate the thermal interaction between solidified copper alloys and substrates, in which the initial alloy temperature, substrate material, surface roughness, coating thickness, and surface treatment were varied. Complementary numerical simulations were performed to reveal the coupled thermal mechanisms across microscopic and macroscopic scales. The results demonstrate that the substrate material exerts a dominant influence on heat transfer, with beryllium copper substrates exhibiting significantly higher heat transfer performance than steel substrates. Coatings introduce thermal resistance, and the observed dual heat flux peaks clarify the origin of the plateau in the temperature-time response. The results showed that, at a depth of 5 mm below the top surface of the beryllium copper substrate, when the coating thickness increased from 58 to 125 μm, the substrate temperature decreased from 188 to 137 °C; when the surface roughness (Rz) increased from 1.122 to 3.094 μm, the substrate temperature increased from 179 to 199 °C. Under applied pressure, greater substrate surface roughness enhances heat transfer because the hardness of the solidified copper alloy decreases upon heating, thereby enlarging the effective contact area. Title: Decoupling analysis of the dynamic response of a piezoelectric laminated beam under mechanical and thermal loads
Abstract: Current theoretical investigation on energy harvesting primarily focuses on electromechanical coupling while neglecting thermal effects. Title: Oxygen-vacancy-enriched MnFeCeOx hollow nanocage catalyst with highly exposed active sites for enhanced low-temperature NH3-SCR

Title: Microstructural origins of fatigue crack growth anisotropy in thermomechanically rolled ultrafine bainitic and martensitic steels
Abstract: The fatigue crack growth (FCG) behaviour of thermomechanically rolled ultrafine bainitic (UFB) and martensitic direct-quenched and partitioned (DQ&P) medium-carbon low-alloy steels was investigated in the longitudinal–transverse (L–T) and transverse–longitudinal (T–L) orientations, primarily at a stress ratio (R) of 0.1, with additional tests performed at R = 0.5 to assess the role of crack closure. In L–T, PAGBs oriented nearly perpendicular to crack growth promote crack deflection and branching, increasing crack-path tortuosity and retarding growth. In T–L, PAGBs oriented nearly parallel to crack growth, particularly when decorated with martensite–austenite (MA) islands, facilitate intergranular crack propagation and accelerate growth. Title: Environmental fate of atrazine in surface water: The dual role of photoaged microplastics in adsorption and photodegradation

Title: Gram decay, intrinsic information dimension, and backward stability of s-step GMRES

Authors: Yin T.; Li Q.; Zhang J.; Li J.; Liu D.; Cai Y.; Dong Z.
Title: Dynamic evolution of the physical properties of low maturity shale under temperature control: implications from the Xiamaling formation shales in northern China
Abstract: The evolution mechanism of organic-rich shales during thermal maturation has always been an important research topic in the field of unconventional energy. It has important indicative significance for evaluating the gas storage capacity as well as the lower limit of exploration depth for high maturity shale reservoirs. In this study, the low mature shale samples from the Xiamaling Formation of Mesoproterozoic are used to investigate the evolution of the multi-level pore structure and mineral composition of the rocks before and after pyrolysis experiments. The results show that the development of pores exhibits a continuous decline during the initial heating stage with 400°C identified as a critical transition temperature. But both the pore volume and specific surface area maintain higher levels once the critical temperature is exceeded. The rise in temperature generally enhances the formation of gas pores, with this effect being most pronounced at 600°C. The increase in kaolinite and chlorite during pyrolysis has adverse effects on the Density Functional Theory (DFT) pore area, Barrett-Joyner-Halenda (BJH) pore volume and porosity by Mercury Intrusion Porosimetry (MIP). Furthermore, the results indicate that the range from super micropores to mesopores all exhibits the multifractal behavior. In particular, the heterogeneity degree of super micropores shows a trend of initially decreasing and then increasing during pyrolysis. For the micropore-to-mesopore, the uniformity of the target system generally declines with the rising temperature, albeit with relatively poor regularity in this variation. Overall, it is expected to provide deeper and more accurate insights into the pore-size effects and compositional evolution of organic-rich shales during thermal maturation. The findings are crucial for the in-situ prediction of natural gas. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: 3D hierarchical graphene oxide-Co LDHs composite, as a suitable platform for sensitive detecting carcinogenic antioxidant in foods
Abstract: Tert-butylhydroquinone (TBHQ) is a common food antioxidant widely applied to prolong the shelf life of food products, and its dosage must be stringently regulated to guarantee food safety. Herein, a sensitive electrochemical sensor was successfully constructed based on cobalt layered double hydroxide nanosheets anchored on graphene oxide (GO/Co LDHs). A three-dimensional (3D) hierarchical GO/Co LDHs composite with sandwich-stacked structure was fabricated through a facile one-step hydrothermal strategy. The surface morphology, elemental composition and crystal structure of GO/Co LDHs composite were systematically characterized via scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). Cyclic voltammetry (CV), differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) were employed to investigate the electrocatalytic behavior of the GO/Co LDHs composite toward TBHQ detection. The excellent sensing performance of the fabricated sensor originates from the synergistic effect between the large conductive skeleton of graphene oxide and the abundant electrochemically active sites of Co LDHs. The proposed electrochemical sensor achieved a broad linear detection range of 0.01–220 μM for TBHQ with an ultra-low limit of detection (LOD) of 2.0 nM. Real-sample testing verified that the sensor possesses satisfactory recovery rates ranging from 94.8% to 103.9%. Moreover, the sensor maintained over 91.17% of its original sensing signal after 27 days of storage, demonstrating prominent long-term stability and great application prospects in practical food safety monitoring. In addition, the sensor exhibited superior repeatability, reproducibility and anti-interference capability, which made it a reliable platform for the sensitive determination of TBHQ in complex food matrices. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Liu Z.; Wang J.; Yan Y.; Chen S.; Zhai Z.; Zhao Y.; Zhang B.
Title: Preparation of nitrogen-doped ZnIn2S4 microflowers for enhanced visible-light photocatalytic H2O2 production
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: The photocatalytic production of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) via the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) represents a sustainable alternative to the energy-intensive anthraquinone process. However, the efficiency of this approach is limited by the rapid recombination of photogenerated carriers and a lack of active surface sites. Herein, nitrogen-doped ZnIn2S4 (N-ZIS) microflowers were synthesized via a one-step solvothermal method using N , N -dimethylformamide (DMF) as the nitrogen source. The optimized N30-ZIS sample (with 30 mL of DMF) achieves an H2O2 production rate of 350 μmol g−1 h−1 under visible light irradiation (λ ≥ 420 nm), which is 1.5 times that of pristine ZIS. Nitrogen doping introduces sulfur vacancies and modulates the electronic band structure, leading to enhanced charge separation and a more negative conduction band potential. Mechanistic studies confirm that H2O2 generation proceeds via a two-electron oxygen reduction pathway involving ·O2− as the key intermediate. This work demonstrates that controlled nitrogen doping is an effective strategy to boost the photocatalytic H2O2 production performance of ZIS-based materials. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Author full names: Bubnovich, Valeri (35562140300); Henriquez-Vargas, Luis (39961464200); Alfaro, Juan (61022986800); Toledo, Mario (58984742000)
Title: Super adiabatic combustion of ultra-lean gas mixtures in inert porous media with circular gas flow
Abstract: A new design of super adiabatic burner for ultra-lean gas mixtures in inert porous media is proposed in this work. Its main objective is to minimize the fuel concentration in the gas mixture, achieve stable combustion with high temperatures in the burner, and minimize emissions to the environment. The burner consists of a round tube that forms a circle and is filled with alumina balls. The working gas is a lean methane/air mixture. Numerical simulation shows that the combustion front is trapped within the porous media, making circular movements of 360°. After performing eight rotating movements of 360° on average, the combustion wave reaches a permanent regime in which the average temperatures of both the solid and the gas with respect to the length of the porous media reach the value of 493 K and the temperature profile of the wave has the classic bell-type shape with the maximum gas temperature of 1208 K. It is demonstrated that the minimum value of the equivalence ratio can fall below the reference value of 0.1. An experimental comparison of combustion temperature and front displacements is performed in a 90° elbow geometry. The results accompanying this combustion design highlight the importance of heat accumulation by the porous media and its energy contribution to the process development under working conditions with ultra-lean mixtures. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Chkouri E.H.; Raissouni J.; Yeste M.P.; Cauqui M.Á.; Draoui K.
Title: Engineering metal-functionalized halloysite nanoclay for fundamental insights into H2-surface interactions: Effects of Mg-Ni functionalization, structural-thermodynamic characterization, and molecular interaction analysis
Abstract: This study presents the synthesis and comprehensive characterization of halloysite nanoclay (HNT)-based materials modified with magnesium (HNT-Mg), nickel (HNT-Ni), and both metals (HNT-MgNi) as model systems for investigating fundamental H2-surface interactions on metal-modified aluminosilicates. The materials were systematically characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD), X-ray fluorescence (XRF), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), thermogravimetric/differential scanning calorimetry (TGA/DSC), Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area analysis, and HAADF-STEM/EDX. Hydrogen adsorption experiments were conducted at 35, 55, and 75 °C under atmospheric pressure and evaluated using Langmuir and Freundlich models. These conditions are substantially less demanding than those generally considered for practical H2 storage, and the measured uptakes therefore remained below 0.1 mmol g−1. The thermodynamic analysis revealed positive apparent enthalpy changes of +45.51, +44.74, and +34.50 kJ mol−1 for HNT-Ni, HNT-Mg, and HNT-MgNi, respectively, indicating an apparent endothermic character under the adopted thermodynamic treatment. The corresponding entropy changes were +112.33, +92.73, and +56.79 J mol−1 K−1, respectively. HNT-Ni exhibited the highest H2 uptake, reaching 0.078 mmol g−1 at 75 °C, while its ΔG° decreased from 10.93 to 6.45 kJ mol−1 between 35 and 75 °C. Positive ΔG° values were obtained for all materials over the investigated temperature range, indicating that adsorption was not thermodynamically favorable at the adopted reference state. Hirshfeld surface and RDF analyses revealed differences in the spatial organization of H2 around the modified surfaces, including distinct H2-Ni and H2-Mg correlations. These results provide qualitative information on intermolecular proximity and local ordering but do not directly establish adsorption energies, charge transfer, chemical bonding, H2 activation, or cooperative effects. Overall, the findings show that H2 adsorption depends on the combined effects of metal identity, surface chemistry, structural organization, and accessible adsorption environments. Given the low uptake values (≤0.078 mmol g−1; <0.02 wt%), the materials are more appropriately considered as model systems for understanding H2-surface interactions than as practical hydrogen-storage sorbents. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Role of pulsation generation mechanism on the heat transfer performance of an impinging jet: A contraction-cone configuration
Abstract: Pulsating impinging jets have emerged as a promising approach for enhancing convective cooling; however, the reported thermal performance remains highly dependent on the characteristics of the pulsation-generation mechanism in addition to the operating conditions. This study experimentally investigates the thermo-fluid performance of a loudspeaker-driven pulsating jet issuing from a contraction cone nozzle. The effects of Strouhal number (0.1–0.8), pulsation amplitude (30–80%), stand-off distance (H/D = 1–6), and Reynolds number (5000–10000) on local and average Nusselt numbers are systematically evaluated. Surface temperature measurements are obtained using infrared thermography under constant heat-flux conditions. The results show that the heat transfer enhancement depends on the evolution of pulsation-induced coherent vortices. When the nozzle is positioned close to the target surface, the vortical structures remain underdeveloped, resulting in lower heat transfer than the corresponding steady jet. As the stand-off distance increases, enhanced shear-layer instability and coherent vortex evolution intensify near-wall mixing, thereby improving convective transport. The maximum enhancement in average Nusselt number reaches approximately 22–24% compared with the corresponding steady jet case. An optimal pulsation amplitude of 60% is identified, beyond which further increases reduce thermal performance due to excessive entrainment and dilution of the jet momentum. The findings demonstrate that the effectiveness of pulsating jet impingement is governed by the combined effects of pulsation frequency, amplitude, Reynolds number, and the loudspeaker-driven actuation mechanism, and provide useful guidelines for the design of high-performance jet impingement cooling systems. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Author full names: Jiménez, S. (35584464900); Herrera, A.J. (60930017900); Obras Loscertales, M. de las (60929009700); Romeo, L.M. (7003639647)
Title: Behavior of iron and mineral magnetite particles in redox cycles including direct oxidation in a high temperature reactor
Abstract: The coupling of iron oxide reduction and its subsequent oxidation is a promising technology for energy storage and recovery. The evolution of the properties of the iron particles along successive cycles is an aspect of obvious relevance in this subject. In the present work, two materials, both sieved in the 75–90 µm range, have been studied: a commercial, pure iron powder, and an iron ore from a beneficiated mineral. Three complete cycles have been performed in uncoupled facilities: a fixed bed for reduction in H2, and a flat flame reactor at high temperature and moderate oxygen concentration for the oxidation stages. The analysis of the final products of each process shows steady compositions and morphologies, except for the first reduction step of the iron ore, slightly uncomplete and improved in subsequent cycles. A number of samples were also collected at intermediate oxidation degrees in the second cycle. The fast melting of the particles at the beginning of their oxidation serves as a real ‘starting point’, effectively deleting the previous particle’s story and the variations in morphology found at the end of the first cycle, and thus leading to very similar curves for particle temperature and oxidation degree vs. residence time. The evolution of the particle size distribution from this point, where a newly narrow distribution was observed, was similar to the one previously found for the original iron. © 2026 The Author(s).

Authors: Guo S.; Wang L.; Lin E.; Deng Y.; Li H.; Han A.; Tang Y.
Title: TongueML: A multi-task learning model for multi-attribute tongue image classification based on graph convolution and transformer
Abstract: Tongue diagnosis is an important diagnostic method in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), which assesses health conditions through tongue features such as color, shape, and coating. However, it is often subjective and affected by external factors, limiting its standardization and objectivity. To address this issue, this study proposes TongueML, a multi-task learning model for multi-attribute tongue image classification. Each tongue image is annotated with five diagnostic attributes: tongue body color (shezhi), tongue body shape (shexing), tongue coating (shetai), tooth marks (chihen), and cracks (liewen). TongueML uses a pre-trained EfficientNetB0 for feature extraction, a cross-scale Transformer for local–global feature fusion, and a graph convolutional network to model spatial feature relationships. Experimental results show that TongueML outperforms baseline models, achieving a Macro F1-score of 74.56%. These results suggest that TongueML provides a promising approach for objective and standardized multi-attribute tongue image analysis and may support intelligent tongue diagnosis. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Author full names: Canales-Cortés, Luis-Daniel (60741697900); Rico-Jiménez, José-de-Jesús (55675508600); González-Barbosa, José-Joel (23396543200)
Title: Automatic glioblastoma subregion segmentation in mpMRI using a residual 3D U-Net with clinically guided multi-sequence attention
Abstract: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) segmentation from multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) remains a challenging task due to tumor heterogeneity, diffuse boundaries, and the complementary nature of MRI modalities. This work presents an enhanced residual 3D U-Net for automatic GBM subregion segmentation using the BraTS2021 dataset. The proposed framework integrates clinically guided multi-sequence attention mechanisms that independently process FLAIR, T1, T1ce, and T2 modalities before feature fusion, enabling improved preservation of modality-specific information and more effective representation of heterogeneous tumor patterns. A standardized preprocessing pipeline including isotropic interpolation, Z-score normalization, and overlapping volumetric patch extraction was implemented to ensure robust multimodal learning. The selected model reached a final training DSC of 0.9012 and achieved a whole-tumor DSC of 0.9219 on the complete hold-out test set without geometric data augmentation, while maintaining strong performance in edema and enhancing tumor delineation. Quantitative and qualitative analyses demonstrated consistent spatial agreement between predicted and reference masks across unseen patients, although necrotic regions remained the most challenging subregion due to their heterogeneous morphology and reduced contrast separation. The results indicate that combining residual learning with clinically guided modality-specific attention provides an interpretable framework for glioblastoma segmentation with potential utility for downstream radiogenomic and imaging-analysis workflows, while external validation remains necessary before broader clinical applicability can be established. © 2026

Author full names: Yadav, Neeraj Kumar (57219439916); Ambalakatte, Ajith (58070709900); Geng, Sikai (58773174500); Suja, Gagan Gopakumar (60877698300); Cairns, Alasdair (24830362900); Harrington, Anthony (57208385697); Hall, Jonathan (55860799679)
Title: The effects of ammonia-methanol blending versus co-fuelling in a lean burn spark ignition engine
Abstract: Ammonia has emerged as a promising renewable fuel for internal combustion engines; however, its adoption is hindered by inherent drawbacks such as high ignition energy, low burning velocities, narrow flammability range, and toxicity. Emulsifying ammonia with methanol provides a possible strategy to address these challenges and potentially improve fuel handling by maintaining the fuel in a bulk liquid state. Since emulsification may affect physicochemical properties in an unpredictable manner (even compared to co-fuelling of pure methanol and ammonia), detailed combustion analysis is a critical step towards any practical application. Employing chilled fuel storage to dissolve larger ammonia fractions (> 30 %) in methanol could also help achieve improved mono-fuel operation without the need for multiple fuel storage and handling systems. The work reported here concerned an experimental investigation of the impact of ammonia–methanol emulsions on combustion, performance, and emissions in a lean-burn Spark Ignition (SI) engine. Experiments were conducted on an externally boosted thermodynamic single cylinder SI engine operated under four fuelling modes: i) pure ammonia, ii) pure methanol, iii) pure ammonia/pure methanol co-fuelling, and iv) ammonia–methanol emulsion. Results revealed that both the emulsion and co-fuelling modes achieve comparable lean-burn combustion and stability limits, with similar peak combustion pressure and pressure rise rate. Engine-out NO x emissions showed a non-linear dependence on ammonia content, with the 10 % ammonia case producing the highest NO x despite a relatively low substitution ratio. Both combustion modes exhibited similar indicated thermal efficiency (>35 %) at mid-load across all tested conditions, suggesting that the emulsion can serve as a practical single-fuel alternative with a lower carbon content than pure methanol. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: A novel surface modified nano-fluid based on TiO2/Fe3O4/CAPB for extreme wettability alteration, ultra-low IFT, asphaltene stabilization, and incremental oil recovery with eco-friendly and cost-effective advantages
Abstract: Residual oil recovery from asphaltene-rich reservoirs via conventional Enhanced oil recovery (EOR) is inefficient, yet nanofluids present a promising solution for simultaneous wettability alteration, Interfacial tension (IFT) reduction, asphaltene stabilization, and enhanced production. Additionally, the synergistic effects of low-salinity water with other additives remain unexplored for asphaltenic crude oils, where asphaltene precipitation severely damages reservoir permeability and reduces production. To bridge this gap, the present study introduces a novel hybrid nanofluid composed of surface-modified TiO2/Fe3O4 nanoparticles and the amphoteric surfactant CAPB (cocamidopropyl betaine) dispersed in low-salinity brine. This formulation is specifically engineered to integrate four pivotal functions into a single sustainable system: (1) extreme wettability alteration from oil-wet to water-wet, (2) ultra-low IFT reduction, (3) effective asphaltene stabilization, and (4) enhanced oil recovery. The combination of CAPB a biodegradable, non-toxic, and cost-effective surfactant with Iron oxide (Fe3O4) and Titanium dioxide (TiO2) nanoparticles presents a green and sustainable alternative to conventional EOR agents. The novelty of this work extends beyond addressing the multifunctionality gap; it also offers new mechanistic insights into the synergistic interactions among low salinity water, modified nanoparticles, and surfactants within asphaltene-rich environments. A comprehensive suite of characterization and performance evaluation techniques including Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), Field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), Transmission electron microscopy (TEM), Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), zeta potential, Dynamic light scattering (DLS), IFT, contact angle measurements, and core flooding experiments was employed to systematically elucidate the underlying oil mobilization mechanisms. The experimental results demonstrated that the synthesized nanofluid reduced IFT to 0.95 mN/m and altered the contact angle to 18°. The coreflood test revealed that nanofluid injection at 150 ppm concentration led to a 38.7% enhancement in oil recovery over that obtained from Low salinity waterflooding alone. These findings offer a practical, scalable, and eco-friendly solution for boosting production from asphaltenic reservoirs. Overall, this work advances next-generation multifunctional EOR agents, promoting sustainable extraction through reduced chemical use, lower environmental impact, and improved efficiency in mature fields. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Tao Y.; Zhang X.; Wu L.
Title: Synergistic integration of mechanical reinforcement and graphite lubrication via TiC optimization achieves ultrahigh current-carrying durability
Abstract: In this study, we fabricated CuCrZr-graphite-TiC composites using a rapid hot-pressing sintering process and systematically investigated how TiC content (0–15 wt%) affects their microstructure, mechanical properties, and current-carrying tribological behavior. We found that adding an appropriate amount of TiC significantly improves hardness and resistance to plastic deformation. Among all compositions, CuCrZr-graphite-5 wt% TiC delivers the best overall performance. At a current strength of 9 A, it achieves a wear rate of only 6.07 × 10−6 mm3/(N·m)—nearly two orders of magnitude lower than that of the TiC-free composite—while keeping the friction coefficient stable at approximately 0.2. Finite element simulations based on a representative volume element (RVE) model show that high-hardness TiC particles construct a rigid load-bearing skeleton, effectively sharing local stresses up to 892.0 MPa and suppressing thermal softening and plastic collapse of the matrix. Joule heating further promotes the release and spreading of embedded graphite. Raman spectra reveal a reduced I  D / I  G  value (1.17) within the wear tracks, and EDS elemental mapping confirms the formation of a lubricant film with high coverage and high crystallinity. XPS analysis further indicates that TiC effectively suppresses the chemical oxidation of the graphite lubricating film, thereby stabilizing contact resistance. By optimizing TiC content, this study overcomes the failure bottleneck of conventional copper-graphite materials under high current-carrying conditions and provides both experimental and theoretical guidance for designing and applying high-performance current-carrying frictional components. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
