Title: In-situ study on the evolution of biochar–coal blended agglomerates during co-gasification
Abstract: Introducing biomass derived biochar into coal gasification provides a practical route for incorporating renewable carbon into existing high temperature conversion systems. The influence of the biochar to coal blending ratio on particle-scale evolution remains insufficiently resolved. In this study, agglomerates containing 10–50 wt% biochar were prepared from slurry droplets and gasified in 40 % H2O/60 % N2 atmosphere using a single particle laser ignition platform and in situ dual camera visualization. All agglomerates underwent swelling, shrinkage, fragmentation-dominated evolution, and residual ash melting and coalescence. As the biochar content increased, the maximum swelling ratio decreased from 1.58 to 1.24. The peak apparent average surface temperature decreased from 1670 to 1535 °C, and the residual ash volume ratio decreased from 0.191 to 0.129. The time for 95 % cumulative sub-particle generation increased from 13.4 to 18.2 s. The peak normalized generation rate and mean sub-particle size decreased from 10.99 to 8.97 %/s and from 32.4 to 25.4 μm, respectively. A fragmentation mode factor, based on body localization and relative sub-particle size, decreased from 0.623 to 0.448, indicating a transition from localized to distributed peripheral fragmentation. The biochar content was correlated with agglomerate swelling, sub-particle generation, peripheral fragmentation, and residual ash evolution. The quantified relationships between biochar content and agglomerate evolution provide particle-scale guidance for evaluating biochar blending in entrained flow co-gasification and support the modeling of sub-particle release and ash residue formation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Selenium-doped Mn-N-C single-atom nanozymes with modulated electronic structure for ultrasensitive colorimetric biosensing of total antioxidant capacity in food samples
Abstract: Herein, we report a selenium-doped manganese-based single-atom nanozyme (MnNC-Se) with engineered electronic structure, and demonstrate its application as a high-performance colorimetric sensing probe for rapid assessment of total antioxidant capacity (TAC). Comprehensive XPS characterization confirms the successful covalent incorporation of Se into the N-doped carbon matrix, which strategically increases the content of pyridinic N (from 55.55% to 68.93%). This enriched pyridinic N provides robust coordination sites that optimize the electronic structure and induce a relative shift of Mn towards lower valence states. Benefiting from this optimized electronic environment, the MnNC-Se nanozyme exhibits a remarkable 16.8-fold enhancement in peroxidase-like activity compared to its undoped counterpart, with a maximum reaction rate (Vmax) of 4.6 × 10−7 M s−1 towards H2O2. On this basis, a colorimetric biosensing platform was constructed for TAC detection using ascorbic acid (AA) as the model antioxidant. The sensor displays excellent analytical performance with a linear detection range of 2–45 μM, a detection limit of 0.721 μM, and high selectivity against common interfering substances. Practical applicability was validated through spike-recovery experiments in vitamin C beverages and supplements, yielding satisfactory recoveries of 96.78–102.57% (RSD < 3%). This work not only provides a reliable sensing tool for TAC assessment in food quality control, but also demonstrates heteroatom doping as an effective strategy for engineering high-performance single-atom nanozymes toward practical biosensing applications. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Song B.; Zhai X.; Xiao Y.; Wang K.; Ma T.; Ren L.
Title: Evolution and mechanism of oxidation characteristics of coal with different degrees of thermal damage in coalfield fire zones based on multi-method joint characterization
Abstract: Coalfield fires prevail in major coal‑producing countries worldwide, causing resource waste and environmental pollution. Thermal damage is a critical factor affecting the evolution of fire zones. However, the evolution of coal oxidation characteristics under different degrees of thermal damage remains unclear. This study systematically investigates the differences in oxidation characteristic temperatures, gaseous products, and activation energy of thermally damaged coal. It further investigates the evolution of functional groups and interprets oxidation pathways of key active groups, revealing the evolution mechanism governing coal oxidation under varying thermal damage conditions. The results show that thermal damage at 100 ℃ lowers characteristic temperatures, accelerates gas release, and reduces oxidation activation energy. Thermal damage at 200 ℃ suppresses low-temperature oxidation reactivity while imposing negligible effects on high-temperature behaviour. Severe thermal damage at 400 ℃ and 600 ℃ weakens coal spontaneous combustion propensity but increases its high-temperature oxidation susceptibility. As thermal damage temperature rises, the evolution of coal functional groups is retarded, with lower reaction rates and improved thermal stability. Aliphatic C–H and C=O are identified as the primary active groups for oxidation. Quantum chemical simulations indicate thermal damage shortens aliphatic side chains, raising energy barriers and endothermicity for oxidation of small molecular coal models. The enhanced spontaneous combustion propensity of 100 ℃-treated coal originates from water evaporation and newly exposed active sites, whereas the loss of highly reactive chemical structures accounts for the weakened propensity under high-temperature thermal damage. These outcomes offer theoretical support for coalfield fire‑zone prevention and mitigation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Dynamic weighting for boundary-aware feature selection: A directed fuzzy rough set approach
Abstract: Fuzzy rough set theory has emerged as a powerful paradigm for feature selection; however, conventional models exhibit key limitations. Specifically, they fail to account for class distribution heterogeneity and the proximity between samples and their target classes when approximating decision boundaries. To mitigate the shortcomings, we introduce a novel directed weighted fuzzy rough set (DW-FRS) framework that explicitly models fuzzy relationships among samples while quantifying the interdependencies between features and decision classes. The core innovation of this approach lies in its distance-ratio weighting mechanism, where each sample is assigned a dynamic weight according to the ratio between its distance to the target class and its distance to samples from non-target classes. This weighting strategy prioritizes samples that are topologically important for class discrimination. Building on this metric, we formulate directed weighted fuzzy rough approximation operators and establish theoretical guarantees for their key properties, such as monotonicity. Subsequently, a feature selection approach leveraging the DW-FRS model is proposed. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework can substantially reduce dimensionality while significantly improving classification accuracy. These results highlight its ability to preserve discriminative information and eliminate redundancy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Hao D.; Lv Y.; Li K.; Zhang K.; Yang Y.; Wu Z.; Li Y.; Tian G.
Title: Pretraining a dermoscopic vision foundation model via an enhanced self-distillation framework
Abstract: Dermoscopy is widely used for diagnosing skin tumors, yet automated analysis remains constrained by scarce high-quality annotations and task-specific supervised models. Existing weakly supervised or unsupervised approaches mainly rely on language supervision, teacher–student distillation, or self-distillation. Language supervision requires high-quality text annotations, whereas teacher–student methods depend on external models that may lack dermoscopy-specific knowledge. Conventional self-distillation avoids these requirements but does not explicitly address lesion-centered spatial distributions, unreliable supervision from ambiguous views, or local structural consistency. To address these limitations, we present ROSE, a visual foundation model pretrained on more than 110,000 dermoscopic images. ROSE integrates Gaussian resized cropping to concentrate global and local views on lesion-relevant regions, entropy-weighted distillation to reduce noisy supervision from semantically ambiguous views, and dense contrastive regularization to preserve local feature consistency without compromising global representations. We evaluate ROSE against state-of-the-art methods on multiple public datasets for classification, few-shot learning, segmentation, and skin-tone-stratified analysis. ROSE consistently achieves competitive or superior performance. On HAM10000, it obtains a weighted F1-score of 0.859 and an AUROC of 0.973 for classification, as well as a Dice similarity coefficient of 0.886 and a Jaccard index of 0.833 for segmentation. In a reader study, ROSE achieves a balanced accuracy of 0.809, providing diagnostic performance competitive with human experts while offering substantially greater inference efficiency. Ablation studies confirm the complementary contributions of all components. Authors: Xiao Q.; Wu Y.; Liu Z.; Li R.; Han R.
Title: FDAFusion: Fusion of infrared and visible images based on frequency-domain amplitude modulation and region-aware learning
Abstract: Infrared and visible image fusion is a critical multimodal image processing task. However, existing fusion methods primarily rely on spatial-domain feature modeling, which has limited capability to capture differences between frequency components and regional characteristics. To this end, this paper proposes a method for fusing infrared and visible images based on frequency-domain amplitude modulation and region-aware learning. This method first designs a Frequency-domain Amplitude-phase Modulation Module (FAMM), which maps the input image into the frequency domain and performs adaptive modulation processing on both the amplitude spectrum and phase information. Subsequently, a Frequency-domain Saliency Mask Module (FSMM) is constructed. By generating regional masks in the frequency domain, it guides the network to adopt differentiated feature fusion strategies across different regions, enabling effective integration of high-frequency details and global structural information. Finally, a Dual-path Feature Fusion Module (DFFM) is employed to generate a fused image that possesses both detailed clarity and structural integrity. The experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves excellent performance across multiple public datasets, with the generated fused images outperforming existing state-of-the-art image fusion methods in terms of both subjective visual quality and objective evaluation metrics. Authors: Suo B.; Jiang H.; Yuan S.; Zhang J.; Li B.; Lu K.; Song J.; Zhang C.
Title: Sequentially coupled numerical modeling of liquid-propellant-induced in-situ pyrolysis of oil shale
Abstract: The low thermal conductivity of oil shale restricts heat propagation during in-situ pyrolysis, while reservoir stimulation and heating are commonly treated as separate processes, making it difficult to capture the dynamic alteration of heat-transfer pathways after fracture creation. To address this issue, a sequentially coupled numerical framework integrating liquid-propellant deflagration pressure release, main-fracture propagation, discrete fracture-network construction and mapping, reservoir heat transfer, and kerogen pyrolysis was developed. Deflagration pressure was described using the JWL equation of state, main-fracture growth was driven by net pressure, and the resulting main and statistically generated branch fractures were mapped into a three-dimensional reservoir domain. Subsequent thermal and pyrolysis responses were calculated using Robin-type gas–rock wall heat transfer, bedding-anisotropic heat conduction, and distributed activation energy model (DAEM) kinetics, together with sensitivity analysis of the key thermal-boundary parameters and numerical verification of the heat-transfer implementation. For a single 3 kg charge, the peak gas and net pressures reached 83.78 and 77.73 MPa, respectively, and the main-fracture half-length stabilized at 1.49 m within approximately 0.3 s. The fracture network promoted preferential heat transfer from the hot gas into the reservoir, yielding 138.88 kg of cumulative primary shale-oil generation after 1800 s. Three-stage sequential deflagration substantially increased the axial thermal influence. Increasing the stage spacing from 2 to 8 m expanded the axial extent of the T ≥ 310 °C region from 12.12 to 24.12 m, whereas cumulative primary shale-oil generation decreased from 467.33 to 389.33 kg, demonstrating a trade-off between spatial coverage and inter-stage thermal overlap. These results reveal the sequential mechanism of short-duration fracturing, fracture-enhanced heat transfer, and early-stage pyrolysis, and indicate that liquid-propellant deflagration is better suited as a pre-fracturing and thermal-startup technique coupled with subsequent sustained heating rather than as an independent long-term heat source. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Sterman G.
Title: QCD for electroweak precision measurements: Foundations
Abstract: The couplings of the strong to electroweak sectors of the Standard Model enable the exploration of each using our growing knowledge of the other. In this review, we will follow the sweep of history. Starting with QED as a precision theory, deep inelastic scattering served as a gateway to the strong interactions, followed by leptonic annihilation and quark–antiquark annihilation in hadron–hadron scattering. In turn, the resulting understanding of QCD helped establish the Standard Model. The same techniques form the basis for many precision electroweak measurements at high energy and searches for signs of new physics. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Zhang H.; Zhu S.; Wang X.; Zhang J.; Wei P.; Wang H.; Zhu Z.
Title: Temperature-dependent improved UDPD modelling of thermally induced crack propagation in transparent rock-like material with prefabricated initial cracks
Abstract: High-temperature conditions in geothermal systems, radioactive-waste repositories, and other underground structures can redistribute stresses around pre-existing discontinuities and promote crack propagation, reducing the load-bearing capacity of fractured geomaterials. However, thermally induced internal crack propagation is difficult to observe directly because natural rock is opaque, and the existing UDPD model provides limited descriptions of temperature-dependent mechanical degradation and progressive damage. This study combined experiments and numerical modelling to investigate crack propagation in specimens of a transparent rock-like material, each containing a prefabricated initial crack with a specified inclination and eccentricity. Crack propagation during heating to 80, 140, and 200 °C was recorded using a high-speed camera, followed by semi-circular bending tests after cooling. Semi-circular bending tests conducted after cooling provided the Young's modulus, tensile strength, and nonlinear stress–strain response. The resulting experimental relationships were incorporated into an existing improved UDPD framework to describe temperature-dependent normal and tangential bond stiffnesses, strength-dependent stretch thresholds, and nonlinear damage before bond breakage. At 200 °C, horizontal prefabricated initial cracks produced U-shaped morphologies, whereas inclined or eccentric cracks showed earlier asymmetric propagation and developed S-shaped morphologies. The model reproduced the observed crack initiation sites, propagation sequences, and representative projected paths and was validated against independent specimen configurations. The proposed framework provides a feasible numerical tool for analysing thermally induced fracture in quasi-brittle materials under high-temperature conditions. © 2026

Authors: Li J.; Ma S.; Li Q.; Liu W.; Zhang H.
Title: Stability in distribution for a class of hybrid neutral stochastic delay systems with Lévy noise
Abstract: This paper investigates the stability in distribution of a class of neutral stochastic hybrid systems driven by Lévy noise. By constructing appropriate Lyapunov functions and employing Barbalat's lemma along with various inequality analysis techniques, the study first demonstrates that the system solutions are uniformly bounded and that solutions from different initial values share the same asymptotic behavior. A sufficient condition for the system's stability in distribution is presented. On this basis, a more concise corollary is further provided, enhancing the practical utility of the theoretical results. Finally, to verify the effectiveness of the theoretical results, the proposed stability criterion is applied to the neutral Nicholson's blowflies equation, and numerical simulations are conducted. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Author full names: Oumbarech, Layla (60010388600); Elaouzy, Youssef (57476483200); El Ghrib, Mohamed B. (59970520400); Zaabout, Abdelghafour (38562426000)
Title: Integration of electrochemical formic acid production for decarbonization of cement industry: techno-economic, energy, and carbon assessments
Abstract: The cement industry is among the largest contributors to global CO2 emissions, highlighting the need for effective decarbonization strategies. This study evaluates three integrated pathways for low-carbon cement production by coupling carbon capture with electrochemical CO2 reduction to produce formic acid, while simultaneously generating hydrogen and oxygen as valuable by-products. The process heat demand is supplied using coal and/or hydrogen under conventional air-fired and oxy-combustion configurations, with partial utilization of the generated hydrogen and oxygen, whereas electricity demand is met through a hybrid renewable energy system. The proposed pathways are comprehensively assessed through techno-economic and environmental analyses under a wide range of assumptions, including variations in capital and operating costs, electricity prices, carbon intensity, feedstock and product prices, carbon credits, and electrochemical reaction performance. The results demonstrate that the integrated systems can achieve cradle-to-gate carbon emissions avoidance of 45.2–49.9%, while revenues from formic acid, hydrogen, and oxygen can partially offset operational costs, resulting in CO2 avoidance costs of 16.2–54.97 $/tCO2e. Furthermore, the integrated scenarios supplied by the hybrid photovoltaic-wind energy configuration achieve revenue-inclusive levelized costs of heat of 5.9–39.7 $/MWh. Economic performance improves further under higher carbon-credit and product prices, and lower system costs. These findings demonstrate the potential of renewable-powered carbon capture and utilization to reduce cement sector emissions while generating valuable coproducts, thereby supporting progress toward economically viable net-zero cement production. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wang L.; Guan B.; Zhu T.; Zhuang Z.; Chen J.; Bai Y.; Gao J.; Huang Z.
Title: Green methanol production under carbon constraints: pathways, system integration, and deployment conditions
Abstract: Green methanol links low-carbon carbon sources with renewable electricity while retaining liquid-fuel handling advantages. We reviewed 155 publications covering genuinely green routes based on renewable hydrogen and sustainable carbon (CO2 hydrogenation with renewable H2 and biomass- or waste-derived methanol), transitional low-carbon retrofits of fossil-based plants, and less mature electrochemical, photocatalytic, or methane-conversion routes. Retrofits are treated as transitional, not genuinely green, because their carbon remains fossil-derived unless the feedstock is replaced. Authors adopt different system boundaries and functional units, and assumptions about electricity, CO2 supply, plant scale, and cost are rarely identical. Our comparison places each pathway in its operating conditions and avoids ranking isolated performance values. It considers technical maturity, energy demand, life-cycle emissions, levelized methanol cost, feedstock supply, infrastructure, and operating flexibility, and examines when power-hydrogen-carbon integration is justified. The review provides four outputs: a protocol for checking the comparability of techno-economic assessment and life-cycle assessment (TEA/LCA) evidence, conditional rules for evaluating integration, a qualitative regional pathway-selection matrix, and a dynamic-validation gap analysis linking demonstrated performance to availability, load-following, capacity factor, and degradation. No route is universally preferred; a defensible choice depends on consistent accounting and on regional electricity, carbon resources, industrial assets, and end use. The integration comparison distinguishes H2-to-CO2 power-to-methanol (PtM), H2-enhanced biomass/waste conversion, retrofit/carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) in fossil methanol hubs, and multi-source industrial symbiosis, and shows that no archetype is universally superior. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: COSMO-RS-assisted extraction of pectin from fingered citron (Citrus medica L. var. sarcodactylis) using natural deep eutectic solvents: Structural characteristics, antioxidant activities and pectin–κ-carrageenan gel properties
Abstract: Fingered citron is a pectin-rich citrus resource, but extraction of fingered citron pectin (FCP) using natural deep eutectic solvents (NADES) remains limited. This study combined conductor-like screening model for real solvents (COSMO-RS) prediction with experimental validation to screen NADES for FCP extraction. Thirty-five NADES systems were evaluated using monosaccharides and pectin fragments as molecular models, and five candidates were selected for ultrasound-assisted extraction. Betaine-maltose (Bet-Mal) achieved the highest yield (11.86%), followed by choline chloride-maltose (ChCl-Mal) (9.57%), both higher than water extraction (4.88%). Structural analyses showed that NADES changed the domain composition, molecular size, methyl esterification, surface charge, conformation, and aggregation behavior of FCPs. L-proline-maltose (LP-Mal), Bet-Mal, and choline chloride-fructose (ChCl-Fru) extracted galacturonic acid-rich pectins with high homogalacturonan proportions, whereas glucose-maltose (Glc-Mal) yielded a highly branched rhamnogalacturonan-I-rich fraction with the highest molecular weight (945.2 kDa), largest particle size, and strongest nanoscale aggregation. ChCl-Mal-extracted pectin showed the highest DPPH scavenging activity, while the water-soluble pectin (WSP) had the strongest superoxide anion scavenging activity. The κ-carrageenan composite gels prepared from pectins extracted with different solvents exhibited distinct textural, rheological, thermal, and microstructural characteristics. These results provide insight into the solvent-dependent structure–function relationships of FCP and offer a COSMO-RS-guided NADES extraction strategy for obtaining fingered citron pectins with distinct food-related functionalities. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Zha W.; Yao Y.; Liu Y.
Title: Programmable sound absorption and inverse design of polygonal curved metamaterials
Abstract: To address the limited low-frequency performance, fixed absorption band, and low inverse design efficiency of conventional sound absorbing structures, a Kresling inspired polygonal curved metamaterial (PCM) is proposed in this work. A tailored curved surface is used as the core cavity, and a Helmholtz-resonant absorber with a complex acoustic cavity is thereby formed. The high-efficiency sound absorption of PCM originates from the synergistic coupling among the central aperture, air cavity, and curved wall, with thermoviscous dissipation in the air domain serving as the dominant energy dissipation mechanism. Compression programming shifts the absorption peak from 342 Hz to 462 Hz. At a subwavelength thickness of 1/43λ, the PCM maintains an average absorption coefficient above 0.8, indicating its potential as an efficient sound-absorbing structure. The series configuration enables a low-frequency shift of the absorption peak, while the multi-aperture parallel configuration forms a broadband absorption region within 216-292 Hz. A Hybrid POD-DeepONet forward prediction model and an n-conditioned multi-candidate inverse design network are developed to realize rapid prediction of absorption curves and target performance driven structural inverse design. This work provides a new structural strategy and methodological framework for low-frequency absorption tuning, broadband design, and intelligent inverse design of programmable acoustic metamaterials. © 2026

Authors: Sun W.-R.; Sun X.; Cheng F.-J.; Wang Y.; Zheng H.; Pan Z.; Wu Y.-G.; Wang L.-B.; Zhao Y.-A.; Rong F.; Yu Y.
Title: Breaking the mass transfer barrier of CO2 hydrate films under static conditions via sodium lignosulfonate-amino acid synergy and temperature perturbation
Abstract: CO2 hydrate-based sequestration offers a potential route for long-term atmospheric CO2 storage, but its application under static conditions is limited by slow hydrate formation kinetics with long induction times and by hydrate films that form at the gas–liquid interface, blocking CO2 dissolution and diffusion and causing premature reaction termination. This study first examined the environmentally friendly promoter sodium lignosulfonate (SL) at 0.1–5 wt.% under static conditions. Although SL achieved gas consumption comparable to SDS, it still showed long induction times, low reaction rates, and a crystal morphology transition from mycelium-like to coral-like structures. To overcome these kinetic deficiencies, two strategies were adopted. First, SL was compounded with amino acids to shorten induction and accelerate hydrate growth through synergistic effects. Second, a dynamic temperature perturbation strategy was introduced to periodically vary subcooling, disrupt the hydrate film barrier, and restore gas–liquid contact. The results showed that compounding with L-leucine reduced the induction time by 23 %–42 % and shortened T90 by approximately 58.1 %. Temperature perturbation reactivated the mass-transfer-limited reaction, converting passive waiting time into effective reaction time and increasing the reaction rate by nearly an order of magnitude. These two strategies address the kinetic bottlenecks of the SL system through chemical promotion and physical intervention, respectively. Their synergistic application provides a feasible operational framework for advancing hydrate-based CO2 sequestration from laboratory research toward engineering scale-up. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Tan Y.; Yang F.; Luo K.; Li D.; Huo L.; Zhong H.; Li P.
Title: Built-in electric field-driven S-scheme charge dynamics in a bio-sourced/Ce-MOF heterojunction for photocatalytic oxidation
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: The sustainable remediation of antibiotic-contaminated water bodies remains a critical environmental challenge. Herein, we design a green and recyclable bio-sourced S-scheme heterojunction, Cur-X@Ce-UiO-66 (denoted as Cur-X@CeU), which integrates selective adsorption with visible-light-driven photocatalysis for antibiotic remediation. Hydrogen bonds and π-π interactions ensure the stable loading of the photosensitizer. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm that a strong built-in electric field (IEF) drives the S-scheme charge transfer. The loading process follows the pseudo-second-order and the Langmuir model. Under mild 430 nm LED (50 mW cm−2) irradiation, the optimized composite Cur-9@CeU achieved a tetracycline (TC) removal rate of 89.92% and a mineralization rate of 69.5% within three hours, demonstrating excellent recyclability and structural integrity over four consecutive cycles (as confirmed by X-ray diffraction, XRD). Kinetic deconvolution indicates that photocatalysis is the primary mechanism. The degradation proceeds mainly through hole-mediated oxidation, assisted by ·OH, ·O2−, and 1O2. Key intermediates were identified by LC-MS, and toxicity assessment using T.E.S.T. confirms a notable reduction in ecological risk compared to the parent compound. Ultimately, this work provides a green, mechanism-driven paradigm for constructing efficient MOF-based heterojunctions to control water pollution. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Author full names: Huang, Song-Jeng (55522746200); Asrate, Dawit Andualem (59761396100); Einollahi, Naser (59546459000); Kannaiyan, Sathiyalingam (56168680700)
Title: Thermodynamic descriptor-guided design of non-stoichiometric Ti26V30Mn30Cr7Ni7 high-entropy alloy for enhanced Mg-based hydrogen storage
Abstract: A descriptor-guided non-stoichiometric high-entropy alloy (HEA), was computationally designed to enhance the hydrogen storage performance of Mg. Unlike equiatomic HEAs, its composition was optimized using a constrained multi-objective Genetic Algorithm–Sequential Linear Programming framework to simultaneously maximize hydrogen affinity, thermodynamic stability, catalytic activity, and BCC solid-solution formation. The synthesized HEA exhibited a single-phase BCC structure with homogeneous elemental distribution and defect-rich nanostructures after mechanical alloying, as confirmed by XRD, SEM–EDS, and HRTEM analyses. Mg– x wt.% Ti26V30Mn30Cr7Ni7 composites (x = 3, 6, 9, and 12) showed improved hydrogen sorption kinetics and lower desorption temperatures. The Mg–6 wt% HEA composite achieved the best performance, absorbing 5.14 wt% H2 in 3.46 min at 325 °C and retaining ∼93 % of its capacity after 50 cycles, while reducing the desorption activation energy from 159.60 to 91.79 kJ mol⁻1. These results demonstrate that descriptor-guided HEA design is an effective strategy for developing advanced Mg-based hydrogen storage materials. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Lu H.; Wang X.; Ji P.; Chai L.; Wang J.
Title: A deep-neural-network-assisted framework for multi-objective optimization of compact combustion kinetic mechanisms
Abstract: Accurate yet compact kinetic mechanisms are highly desirable for combustion simulations under limited computational resources, whereas aggressive reduction often leads to substantial loss of predictive accuracy. In this work, a framework was developed for further reducing and optimizing compact combustion kinetic mechanisms by integrating reaction-level screening with deep-neural-network-assisted kinetic-parameter optimization. Redundant reactions were first removed through sensitivity-guided screening to obtain a more compact reaction network, and multi-head deep neural network surrogate models were then constructed for rapid prediction of ignition delay time and laminar flame speed. Based on these surrogates, a multi-objective optimization was performed to adjust a limited number of key kinetic parameters and recover the accuracy loss induced by structural simplification. The framework was validated for fuels with different levels of kinetic complexity, including H2, CH4, CH3OH, C2H4, C2H6, C2H5OH and NC7H16. In the present study, the initial reduced mechanisms were obtained using a previously developed RF-based reduction strategy and served as the starting point for further compact-mechanism construction. Across these systems, the additional reaction-level reduction ratio reached 59.26 % – 77.53 % relative to the initial reduced mechanisms, indicating strong further compression capability. Despite the substantial reaction removal, the optimized compact mechanisms consistently showed markedly improved agreement with the corresponding detailed mechanisms for both ignition delay time and laminar flame speed. Additional validation under conditions not included in the optimization further showed that the optimized mechanisms maintained improved predictive performance outside the optimization set, indicating good local generalization capability. Overall, the proposed framework was shown to effectively combine strong additional reaction compression with substantial recovery of predictive accuracy and to provide a practical route for developing highly compact mechanisms for target-oriented simulations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Huang Y.; Zhan X.; Liang C.; Gao R.; Li H.; Fang W.
Title: Curvature-modulated slip effects on flow and heat transfer characteristics in structured microchannels
Abstract: Efficient thermal management requires microchannel heat sinks with diverse flow-path designs, among which curved microchannels are particularly important and unavoidable in spatially constrained devices. However, heat transfer enhancement strategies based on compound structures in curved microchannels remain less explored than those in straight channels, and the coupling mechanisms are still unclear. Here, we propose a novel approach that integrates slip boundary with rib/cavity microstructures in curved channels and elucidates the curvature-modulated mechanisms governing their coupled thermal-hydraulic response. Four curved configurations with different rib/cavity arrangements: inner rib-outer cavity (IROC), both-side cavities (BC), inner cavity-outer rib (ICOR), and both-side ribs (BR) are compared with straight counterparts. The results show that curvature-induced flow redistribution makes the outer-side structure dominant in determining flow and heat transfer characteristics. Under no-slip conditions, cavity-containing curved channels exhibit better overall performance. Under slip conditions, the performance contribution of ribs increases significantly owing to the substantial reduction in flow resistance. The optimal curved configuration shifts from cavity-dominated BC ( PEC = 1.06 – 1.23), to ICOR ( PEC = 1.80 – 2.01), and to rib-dominated BR ( PEC = 2.13 – 2.21) at the moderate flow rate. These findings reveal the curvature-modulated mechanism by which the slip effect regulates momentum and thermal transport around rib/cavity structures, underscoring the potential of hydrophobic structured microchannels for high-performance thermal management. Title: Parton distribution functions and strong coupling constant: MSHT

We discuss recent methodological improvements and ongoing studies relating to closure tests of the parameterisation flexibility and the inclusion of errors on errors for experimental data. We in addition discuss recent results on the determination of the strong coupling from the MSHT fits. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier B.V. Title: A Dual-Objective Meta-Learning Physics-Informed Neural Network for multi-condition hydraulic fracture geometry prediction
Abstract: Dynamic adjustment of hydraulic fracturing operating parameters to achieve rapid and accurate predict ion of hydraulic fracture geometry (HFG) under multiple operating conditions is essential for optimizing fracturing schemes and quantitatively evaluating reservoir stimulation effects. However, existing studies on multi-condition HFG prediction remain limited. Parameterized PINNs and neural operators can reduce repetitive training to some extent, but the former may encounter optimization difficulties as the operating range expands, while the latter often suffers from accuracy degradation when training data are insufficient. Therefore, this paper proposes a Dual-Objective Meta-Learning Physics-Informed Neural Network (DOM-PINN) framework. This framework constructs a PINN model based on the PKN model for hydraulic fracture propagation and introduces two objective modules: (1) a multi-condition PINN transferable parameter initialization module; and (2) a multi-condition PINN loss weight adaptive prediction module. The proposed method adopts a bi-level meta-learning strategy. In the inner loop, PINN parameters are adapted to the current operating condition. In the outer loop, the adapted PINN parameters are used to construct the loss and jointly update the two modules. The updated modules are then used to initialize PINN parameters and assign loss weights for new operating conditions, enabling fast and accurate prediction with only a few samples and update steps. Experiments on multi-condition HFG prediction with varying fracturing-fluid viscosity and Young's modulus show that DOM-PINN achieves faster convergence and higher accuracy than baseline methods using fewer update steps. © 2026

Authors: Mu Z.; Liu X.; Li G.; Song Y.; Tian S.; Zhang P.; Tan Y.; Bai S.; Tian J.
Title: Suppressing wax deposition through N2 injection in tight oil reservoirs with variable gas-oil ratios
Abstract: Wax deposition in wellbores presents a significant challenge to production stability and enhanced oil recovery in tight reservoirs. While N2 injection is a promising mitigation technique, its interaction with wax deposition under varying gas-oil ratios (GORs) remains inadequately understood. This study establishes a wellbore thermal-fluid coupled wax deposition model that integrates both the equation of state and Rygg-Rydahl-Rønningsen deposition kinetics. The model, validated against experimental and field data, is applied to investigate the effects of N2 injection in wax-rich tight reservoirs with variable GORs. Deposition is concentrated in the upper 0–500 m, thickening toward the wellhead. Wax is dominated by C21-C36 hydrocarbons, but shifts from lighter (C21-C27) in shallow zones to heavier (C28-C36) in deeper, hotter sections. An increase in GOR significantly suppresses deposition, shifting the wax appearance temperature (WAT) to lower values, reducing deposit thickness, and enriching the deposit with heavier components C28-C36. With N2 injection, the WAT curve shifts toward higher temperatures in the low-pressure region but toward lower temperatures in the high-pressure region, resulting in an overall temperature-lowering trend that indicates wax suppression, which is an effect more pronounced in crude oils with lower GOR. Moreover, increasing N2 concentration reduces deposition thickness, and wax deposition can be essentially eliminated once N2 concentration exceeds a critical range (43.0–54.7 mol%), which itself decreases with higher GOR. This study systematically clarifies the mechanisms by which GOR and N2 injection influence wax deposition, providing a theoretical basis for optimizing flow assurance and gas injection strategies in tight oil production. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Abedi M.; Azmoodeh Z.
Title: Machine-learning-guided hydrothermal engineering of Cobalt-modified ZnFe₂O₄ for visible-light-active porous photocatalytic coating for urban infrastructure
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: This study presents a machine-learning-guided hydrothermal strategy for optimizing Cobalt-modified ZnFe2O4 (ZF–Co) photocatalysts. Moreover, a novel scalable porous inorganic coating platform compatible with retrofit implementation on existing urban infrastructures was developed for visible-light-driven atmospheric pollutant mitigation. A hydrothermal synthesis database containing 320 experimentally synthesized ZF–Co samples was generated using temperature (120–250 °C), duration (4–24 h), cobalt concentration (0–20 wt%), and urea-to-metal molar ratio (1.8–9) as input variables, while BET specific surface area (SBET) was selected as the optimization target. Linear regression, random forest, and XGBoost models were implemented for prediction and optimization. The optimized ZF–Co photocatalyst was subsequently characterized using BET, XRD, FESEM/EDS, TEM/HRTEM, FTIR, and UV–Vis analyses and incorporated into a porous lithium-silicate-based coating containing dispersant and foaming agents. The coating was deposited onto cementitious substrates and evaluated by continuous-flow photocatalytic degradation of NOx, formaldehyde, and toluene under UV-A and visible-light irradiation, along with wettability, compressive strength, and pull-off adhesion tests. Authors: Yan X.-P.; Zhang C.-H.
Title: Hopf bifurcation in a reaction-diffusion system with mixed instantaneous and nonlocal delayed density dependence
Source title: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
Abstract: This paper considers a generalized Lotka-Volterra reaction-diffusion population system with mixed instantaneous and nonlocal delayed density dependence and subject to homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. The existence and asymptotic expression of the positive steady-state bifurcating from the trivial one are established in virtue of the implicit function theorem. The associated eigenvalue problem is analyzed in detail and the local asymptotic stability and the existence of Hopf bifurcation of the positive steady-state are derived. According to the normal form method and the center manifold theorem for delayed reaction-diffusion equations, the direction of Hopf bifurcations and the stability of bifurcating periodic solutions are demonstrated. Authors: Feng L.; Dong Z.; Kexian L.; Wen X.; Cui X.; Jin G.; Huang X.; Lin G.; Zhu J.; Yan X.; Lu B.
Title: Achieving superior impact toughness-wear resistance synergy in LDED FeMnCoCrSi-WC composite coatings via crack deflection and multi-scale second-phase strengthening
Abstract: Impact toughness and wear resistance are two critical yet inherently conflicting properties required for protective coatings on critical components in petroleum and mining equipment. Improving wear resistance without sacrificing impact toughness remains a persistent challenge for protective coatings. To address this challenge, high-toughness spherical cast WC particles with a fine W2C + WC eutectic structure were incorporated into the FeMnCoCrSi high-entropy alloy (HEA) coating, which exhibits transformation-induced plasticity (TRIP) effects. Microstructural characterization revealed that coatings with varying WC contents consist of FCC, WC, W2C, and M3W3C phases. Title: Multi-label feature selection via consistent adaptive graph in feature and label spaces
Abstract: Multi-label Feature Selection (MFS) is an interpretable dimensionality reduction paradigm, which aims to identify discriminative features from the high-dimensional multi-label data. To preserve the underlying data structure, graph-based MFS approaches generally employ spectral graph learning to model structural relationships among instances. However, existing methods generally construct instance graphs based on predefined structures, which may not accurately reflect the intrinsic manifold geometry of data and overlook the potential interaction between adaptive graph learning and feature selection. Moreover, existing approaches independently construct graph structures from different spaces without considering the structural consistency, which may result in structural discrepancies. To address these problems, we propose a novel method Consistent Adaptive Graph in Feature and Label spaces, named CAGFL. Specifically, we first establish a regression-based framework to simultaneously learn feature selection matrix and low-dimensional embedding matrix. Based on these two variable matrices, a consistent adaptive graph learning strategy is developed to integrate complementary structural information from both feature and label spaces. Finally, sparsity constraints are imposed on both the adaptive graph and feature selection matrix to eliminate redundant information and enhance the robustness. By integrating the above components, the model of the proposed CAGFL is formulated as an objective function, which is effectively optimized through an alternating iterative strategy. Comprehensive experimental results on real-world multi-label datasets verify the effectiveness and superiority of CAGFL compared with representative MFS methods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Size-dependent freezing response of silty clay: an experimental study
Abstract: Specimen size can significantly affect the freezing response measured in laboratory soil tests by changing geometric heat-transfer conditions and phase-transition duration. Cylindrical silty clay specimens with a constant height of 100 mm and diameters of 50-200 mm were tested in flexible rubber molds without thermal insulation. Heat exchange occurred through the top, lateral, and bottom boundaries. Soil temperature, volumetric unfrozen water content, and vertical deformation were monitored. The results showed that as the diameter increased from 50 to 200 mm, the ratio of the nominal heat-transfer area to volume decreased from 0.1000 to 0.0400 mm−1, while the characteristic heat-transfer length increased from 10.0 to 25.0 mm. The time required for the temperature field to approach −8 °C increased from approximately 350 to 850 min, and the center-to-edge difference in apparent ice-nucleation temperature decreased from 2.2 °C for the 50 mm specimen to 0-0.2 °C for specimens with diameters of 125-200 mm. Besides, the freezing-front propagation time remained within 10-15 min for diameters of 50-125 mm and increased to 20-40 min for diameters of 150-200 mm. Additionally, the volumetric unfrozen water content exhibited freezing-thawing hysteresis, with a maximum difference of 24.0% at the center of the 125 mm specimen. Title: Construction of layered porous carbon (LPC) for supercapacitors by ice template strategy coupled with microwave activation
Abstract: Controlling the pore structure and doping with heteroatoms to construct porous carbon is an effective strategy for further improving its electrochemical performance. Title: Clay minerals in Athabasca oil sands: A review of crystal structure, specific surface area, and their impact on bitumen recovery and tailings processing
Abstract: Clay minerals in Athabasca oil sands significantly hinder bitumen recovery and tailings management due to their high specific surface area (SSA) and strong physicochemical reactivity at mineral–fluid interfaces. Fine and ultrafine clay particles increase slurry viscosity, stabilize emulsions, and impede tailings consolidation, leading to substantial operational and environmental costs. Significant efforts have focused on optimizing bitumen extraction processes, developing polymeric demulsifiers and flocculants, and improving filtration technologies to mitigate the adverse effects of fine clay particles. Despite progress, fundamental understanding of clay delamination mechanisms and nanoscale co-adsorption of asphaltenes and metal cations remains incomplete, limiting the predictive accuracy of extraction and tailings process models. Conventional bulk metrics fail to capture the mechanistic complexity of clay interactions because they do not distinguish between internal and external SSA, limiting accurate representation of their roles in crystalline swelling, adsorption, and interfacial processes. In this review, we examine the crystal structures and specific surface areas of common clay minerals and develop geometric SSA models benchmarked against literature-reported data. In particular, the effects of clay swelling and delamination on surface accessibility, asphaltene–clay–ion synergistic interactions on bitumen recovery, and the roles of swelling clay minerals in tailings filtration and dewatering are reviewed. This review also highlights directions for developing standardized delamination protocols and leveraging cation chemistry of process water to improve tailings treatment. Title: Two novel domain-preserving schemes for a class of stochastic differential equations defined in a domain
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: In recent years, the positivity-preserving schemes for stochastic differential equations (SDEs) with positive solutions have received extensive attention. Most of these schemes are often ineffective for solving SDEs with solution valued in a domain. Research in this area is relatively scarce, even for the scalar case. The transformation employed, which we refer to as the modified logarithmic transformation, maps the solution interval for the original equation to the entire real line for the transformed equation whose coefficients exhibit exponential growth. We apply two novel tamed schemes to solve the transformed equation and then transform the approximation solutions back to numerically solve the original equation, yielding two domain-preserving numerical schemes whose strong convergence rates are showed to be 1/2 and 1, respectively. Title: Microstructural evolution and tribological mechanisms of fixed agglomerated diamond abrasive pads in lapping of quartz substrates
Abstract: Balancing high-efficiency material removal with low-damage surface integrity is a critical challenge in precision machining of hard-brittle quartz substrates. Title: Effects of loading–unloading rate ratio and absolute rate level on damage and energy evolution of coal under a mining-induced true triaxial stress path
Abstract: Mining-induced stress redistribution in deep coal seams commonly involves an increase in the major principal stress and unloading of the minimum principal stress, which triggers complex damage and failure behaviors of coal masses and poses severe threats to safe underground coal extraction. In this study, true triaxial tests were conducted on coal specimens following a mining-induced stress path of “σ1 loading, constant σ2, and σ3 unloading”. The results reveal that tensile micro‑cracks dominate the overall damage process. The fraction of shear cracks shows a marked increase from 10.9 % to 21.8 % with the growth of loading‑unloading rate ratio and exhibits a stabilizing trend at higher absolute rate levels. A higher rate ratio promotes abrupt pre-peak fracture incubation and shifts macroscopic failure from distributed damage to localized failure. A higher absolute rate level mainly increases characteristic stresses and pre-peak bearing capacity. The fracture morphology evolves from regular double dominant cracks to asymmetric failure with local dislocation and edge spalling. Energy analysis shows that the rate ratio controls triaxial energy redistribution, whereas the absolute rate level intensifies energy accumulation and release. These findings clarify the rate-dependent failure mechanisms of coal under mining-induced stress paths and provide experimental insights for dynamic-hazard risk assessment and safe production in deep underground coal mines. Authors: Chen N.; Huo L.
Title: A new three-layer metapopulation networks model coupling online-offline social interactions with epidemic spread
Abstract: The dissemination of epidemic-related information can effectively enhance public awareness of preventive measures and decrease infection risks. However, information dissemination through multiple channels, including both online and offline sources, and the dynamics of information dissemination across these channels are influenced by individual mobility. To address this gap, this study develops a three-layer metapopulation network coupled model that integrates online information dissemination, epidemic spreading, and offline information dissemination. The proposed model systematically investigates the patterns of information dissemination through both online and offline channels, as well as the epidemic reaction–diffusion process driven by individual migration. Furthermore, the social interactions dynamics of both information channels are influenced by migration, manifested as migrated individuals acquire offline information in destination patches and establish online connections with individuals residing there. Theoretical analysis using the Microscopic Markov Chain Approach (MMCA) derives epidemic thresholds, while Monte Carlo (MC) simulations validate the model and examine factors influencing propagation dynamics. Results indicate that migration enhances individuals’ offline information acquisition, and accelerates cross-patch online information dissemination. Both online and offline information interactions exert inhibitory effects on epidemic spread, effectively increasing the infection threshold and reducing the outbreak scale. Furthermore, increasing the connectivity and dissemination rate of online information, particularly the information dissemination via weak relationships between patches, can effectively inhibit epidemic outbreaks. Notably, when the suppression effect of information on the epidemic is weak, population migration facilitates epidemic spread. Title: Convergence of efficient solutions for multiobjective optimal control problems and applications
Source title: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
Abstract: This paper investigates the convergence of efficient solutions for multiobjective optimal control problems (MOCPs) with affine state equations under data perturbations. Unlike most existing studies that require convexity of the multiobjective function or strong regularity of problem data (e.g., norm convergence or G-convergence), our analysis is based solely on the pointwise convergence of the system coefficients, without assuming convexity of the objective. Title: Evolution mechanisms of plugging-zone structure and force-chain network under dynamic fracture deformation
Abstract: Lost circulation is a critical drilling problem in deep fractured formations, where pressure fluctuations induce dynamic fracture deformation and destabilize plugging zones. In this study, a coupled CFD–DEM model incorporating a prescribed dynamic fracture-opening boundary was developed based on three-dimensionally scanned fracture geometries to simulate the formation, instability, and reconstruction of plugging zones in rough fractures during fracture opening. The evolution of the plugging zone structure and force chain network was systematically analyzed, and the effectiveness of a multi-stage injection method was evaluated. The results show that plugging-zone formation follows a distinct multi-stage process: coarse particles first form the bridging skeleton, while medium and fine particles fill interstitial voids and participate in load sharing, accompanied by the development of a dense interconnected force-chain network. Authors: Li J.; Liu J.; Zhu J.; Sun M.; Niu D.; Xia J.; Jiang X.Z.
Title: Cross-modal orthogonal feature distillation for gear fault diagnosis with heterogeneous multi-source information
Abstract: Gears are critical components in rotating machinery, and accurate fault diagnosis is essential for ensuring its reliability and operational safety. However, gear fault diagnosis faces challenges such as the limited fault representation capability of single-sensor signals and the difficulty of aligning and exploiting heterogeneous information from multiple sensors. To this end, this paper proposes a novel cross-modal orthogonal feature distillation network (COFD-Net). Specifically, acoustic and magnetoelectric speed signals are first fed into parallel networks to learn discriminative modality-aware fault representations. To overcome the semantic discrepancy across heterogeneous modalities, learnable mapping layers are introduced to project these features into a shared latent space, where a Cross-Fuse alignment loss is designed to promote semantically coherent and complementary cross-modal fault representations. On this basis, an orthogonal projection-based feature decoupling strategy is further developed to suppress redundant components while preserving discriminative and complementary fault-related information, thereby yielding more refined multi-modal representations. In addition, a dynamic similarity-guided distillation strategy is proposed to adaptively regulate the transfer of refined multi-modal knowledge to the vibration branch, enhancing the capability of representation and classification performance. Title: CLAS: Secure, lightweight, and constant-size convertible aggregate signcryption for multi-agent systems in 6G mission-critical networks
Abstract: Post-disaster search and rescue (SAR) operations generally rely on multi-agent systems (MAS) for collaborative sensing and rescue in hazardous environments. Our key insight is to verify each agent's contribution before aggregation, and bind all valid contributions into a constant-size collective signcryption package, simultaneously achieving confidentiality, authentication, and receiver-controlled public accountability with constant and low communication overhead. Specifically, we design a verification-before-aggregation mechanism to filter out invalid signcryption contributions preventing them from contaminating the package, a constant-size aggregate signcryption construction to minimize satellite bandwidth consumption, and a recipient-controlled convertibility mechanism to support dispute-oriented auditing. Title: Physical and chemical stability of flaxseed oil-in-water Pickering emulsions stabilized by the insoluble fraction of Persian gum

Authors: Sun Y.; Li L.; Gao J.
Title: Designing stateful enterprise control for budget commitments: Identity continuity, context-bound transitions, and controlled execution
Abstract: Enterprise information systems manage business objects with persistent control states across transactions and changing organizations, posing a stateful enterprise control problem that requires consistent alignment of object identity, valid state transitions, execution authority, and audit evidence over time. Title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon and soot formation in laminar ammonia-ethylene diffusion flames: Modeling the effects of HCN and NH2 radicals

Title: Partial approximate controllability for nonlocal fractional stochastic differential variational inequalities via sectorial operator

Title: Synergistic non-thermal plasma-catalytic reforming of toluene over hierarchical Ni/mHZSM-5 catalysts for efficient syngas production

Title: EADU-Net:A Pulmonary Nodule CT Segmentation Network Based on Local-Global Fusion and Multi-Dilated Convolutions

Title: Isogeometric analysis with C1 cubic Powell–Sabin splines
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: In this paper, we consider C1 cubic Powell–Sabin splines for the numerical solution of boundary value problems on planar and spatial surface domains. We first review the construction and basic properties of polynomial and rational C1 cubic Powell–Sabin spline representations on unstructured triangulations. Then, we discuss how these flexible representations can be exploited to create geometry mappings suited for a precise description of (classes of) surface domains. This is illustrated with several examples. Finally, the obtained domain descriptions are utilized in the isogeometric analysis framework for solving various Poisson and biharmonic problems. It is demonstrated that C1 cubic Powell–Sabin splines form a powerful alternative to C0 cubic Lagrange elements and bicubic NURBS. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Mao Y.; Guan B.; Su T.; Zhu L.; Zhu T.; Shi L.; Wu T.; Chang S.; Ma J.; Wang R.; Yang D.; Huang Z.
Title: Current research on catalysts and deactivation mechanisms for methane catalytic oxidation
Abstract: Focusing on the complex marine exhaust conditions with high water vapor, trace sulfur compounds and fluctuating operating loads, this work systematically summarizes the structure–activity relationships and anti-deactivation characteristics of mainstream catalysts for marine methane total oxidation. Among noble metal materials, Pd-based catalysts exhibit remarkable low-temperature catalytic activity, while Pt-based catalysts deliver superior sulfur tolerance under harsh flue gas environments. By contrast, the performance advantages of Rh catalysts are mainly effective for partial oxidation of methane. Beyond noble metals, low-cost transition metal oxides, perovskites, zeolites, and metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have also been comprehensively analyzed, with emphasis on their modification strategies tailored to improve low-temperature activity, hydrothermal stability and sulfur resistance. This review highlights the rational design and directional optimization of multifunctional catalysts targeting the actual demanding marine working conditions, providing theoretical guidance for the development of efficient and durable marine methane emission control technologies. Title: A hybrid higher-order interpolation/finite element technique for evolutionary groundwater-surface water problem
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: A higher-order combined interpolation/finite element approach is developed for solving the unsteady mixed Stokes-Darcy system that governs flows in karst aquifers. In the proposed higher-order scheme we approximate the time derivative with piecewise polynomial interpolation of second-order and use the finite element discretization of piecewise polynomials of degree d and d+1, where d ≥ 2 is an integer, to approximate the space derivatives. The stability together with the error estimates of the constructed technique are established in L∞(0, T; L2)-norm. The analysis suggests that the developed computational technique is unconditionally stable, temporal second-order accurate and spatial convergence of order d+1. Furthermore, the proposed approach is faster and more efficient than a broad range of numerical methods discussed in the literature for the given initial-boundary value problem. A wide set of examples are performed to confirm the theoretical studies. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Rana S.; Chauhan S.
Title: Engineering a carboxyl-functionalized etherified pine needles-derived composite hydrogel for enhanced adsorption of cationic dyes
Abstract: A carboxyl-functionalized etherified pine needles (ePNs)/sodium alginate (Alg)-grafted-poly(itaconic acid) (PIA) composite hydrogel (ePNs/Alg-g-PIA) was fabricated from forest biowaste by etherifying PNs, followed by graft polymerization with Alg and IA. Characterization confirmed a porous hydrogel for efficient adsorption of cationic dyes with removal efficiencies of 97.34% and 90.02% for malachite green (MG) and methylene blue (MB), respectively. The adsorption data followed Langmuir model, with maximum adsorption capacities of 339.36 and 329.90 mg g−1 for MG and MB, respectively. Kinetic investigations were best described by pseudo-first-order model, indicating rapid uptake governed by the accessibility of adsorption sites and mass transfer within the hydrogel matrix. Thermodynamic studies confirmed spontaneous and exothermic adsorption. The ePNs/Alg-g-PIA retained significant adsorption (>48%) after nine cycles, with cumulative adsorption capacities of 752.64 and 701.04 mg g−1 for MG and MB, respectively. The hydrogel's performance in treating real textile effluent further demonstrated its practical applicability for cationic dye removal. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Mardanov M.J.; Guliyev H.F.; Tagiyev H.T.
Title: An optimal control problem for a nonlocal boundary condition for unstable parabolic equation
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: In the paper we consider the optimal control problem for the second order unstable parabolic equation with a nonlocal boundary condition. First, the existence of an optimal pair for the given problem has been proven. Subsequently, an adapted penalty functional was introduced and it was shown that the sequence of optimal pair for the new problem converges to the optimal pair of the main problem.Necessary conditions were expressed for the sequence of optimal pairs. In the case, the equation obtained is the adjoint boundary-value problem includes the loaded term, which corresponds to the boundary condition of the original non-local boundary-value problem. For solving this boundary-value problem, an uniformly estimation is obtained for Galerkin approximations. Finally, passing to the limit with respect to the penalty parameter yields a necessary condition for optimality expressed as a variational inequality. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Yuan C.; She Y.; Zhang E.; Ogunjide S.B.
Author full names: Yuan, Chenyin (60694993200); She, Yuanliang (58352120600); Zhang, Enze (60695345800); Ogunjide, Sunday B. (59462182400)
Title: Breaking the NOx-soot trade-off in compression ignition engines at mid-load with high-percentage n-Pentanol blends through charge cooling and oxygenation
Abstract: The quest for sustainable and environmentally friendly fuel alternatives has significantly increased interest in exploring higher alcohols, particularly n-pentanol, as a promising oxygenated biofuel option for internal combustion engines. This study meticulously analyzed the combustion, performance and emission characteristics of a 60% n-pentanol/40% n-dodecane blend, designated P60D40 , and n-dodecane, D100, utilizing computational fluid dynamics simulations. Here, n-dodecane was used as a surrogate for diesel fuel. The analysis was conducted under a variety of engine operation control parameters to ensure a thorough understanding of their behaviors. The results showed that under identical operating conditions, the indicated thermal efficiency of the P60D40 blend was 47.94%, which is higher than the 44.32% for D100. Furthermore, the equivalent indicated specific fuel consumption for the P60D40 blend was 169.89 g/kWh, in contrast to the 183.77 g/kWh of D100. This represents a 7.55% reduction in fuel consumption, highlighting the efficiency benefits of using n-pentanol as a fuel component. In addition to the performance improvements, the study also found significant reductions in harmful emissions. Specifically, emissions of soot, nitrogen oxides and carbon dioxide were reduced by 91.46%, 86.18% and 12.91%, respectively, compared to D100. The utilization of a 60% n-pentanol blend demonstrates considerable potential, as it not only meets the selected Euro VI reference limits of 0.4 g/kWh and 0.01 g/kWh for NOx and soot, respectively, but also offers excellent performance characteristics. Moreover, it shows the capability to effectively address the common trade-off between NOx and soot emissions, particularly under mid-load operating conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhu Z.; Bai Y.; Cui N.
Title: Fixed-time backstepping control for overturn prevention of a trans-media vehicle during high-speed water entry
Abstract: The stable control of a trans-media vehicle during high-speed water entry is crucial for mission success. However, drastic state variations during the control process can easily trigger vehicle overturn, leading to system instability and even safety hazards. It is therefore imperative to impose strict state constraints in the controller design. Furthermore, composite uncertainties of the system can severely degrade control performance. To address these challenges, a fixed-time backstepping control scheme incorporating the overturn-prevention condition is proposed in this paper. Based on the geometric relationship between the vehicle and the cavity, the state constraint boundary for overturn prevention during the high-speed water entry process is established. By introducing a nonlinear transformation function, the control problem with full-state constraints is converted into ensuring the boundedness of error-dependent functions, thereby eliminating the dependence on feasibility conditions. A fixed-time disturbance observer is designed to estimate and compensate for the lumped disturbance, guaranteeing that the estimation error converges within a fixed time independent of initial conditions and enhancing system robustness. On this basis, a fixed-time backstepping control strategy is developed by incorporating a novel nonlinear tracking differentiator. Rigorous theoretical analysis proves that all closed-loop signals satisfy the state constraints, and the state errors converge to a small neighborhood of the origin within a fixed time. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively prevents overturn and exhibits significant superiority in both transient performance and steady-state precision. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Authors: Wu Z.; Ma Y.; Li X.; Yan Z.; Huang Y.; Wang K.; Quan W.; Mo L.; Liu S.G.
Title: CRISPR/Cas12a-powered self-sustaining catalytic nucleic acid circuit for highly sensitive detection of aflatoxin B1
Abstract: Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is a highly toxic mycotoxin and strongly carcinogenic and teratogenic to humans. Achieving CRISPR-based sensing system for highly sensitive detection of AFB1 remains a significant challenge. A CRISPR/Cas12a-powered self-sustaining catalytic nucleic acid circuit (CPSCN) is proposed for the sensitive and accurate detection of aflatoxin B1 (AFB1). In the CPSCN sensing system, CRISPR/Cas12a/gRNA1 indirectly recognizes AFB1 by aptamer and effectively triggers trans-cleavage of a pair of self-reporting single-stranded DNA-locked RNA2 fluorescence probes (named as dual-winged fluorescence probe). The released RNA2 then initiates an autocatalytic positive feedback loop, resulting in continuous probe cleavage. The CPSCN system achieves highly sensitive detection in a single-enzyme one-step process. The method exhibits excellent quantitative capability for AFB1 detection with a detection limit of 7.5 pg/mL. In real samples, the detection results of the proposed biosensor show high consistency with those obtained by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). This work not only provides a novel strategy for AFB1 detection with high sensitivity, robustness, and operational simplicity, but also offers a new insight for designing signal amplification strategies of CRISPR-based biosensors. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Li Y.; Zheng S.; Jiang Q.; Zhang H.
Title: Effects of crosslinking strategies on the structure and properties of whey protein isolate–sodium alginate oleogels: Schiff base, calcium ionic, and dual-crosslinking
Abstract: The structural and functional properties of oleogels are critically governed by their crosslinking networks. This study systematically investigated the effects of Schiff base crosslinking, calcium ionic crosslinking, and their combination on the physicochemical, stability, and digestion properties of whey protein isolate–sodium alginate oleogels. The results demonstrated that Schiff base crosslinking enhanced the stability of the precursor emulsions, while calcium ionic crosslinking enhanced mechanical strength and oil binding capacity of oleogels. Mechanistic analysis revealed that dual-crosslinking formed an interpenetrating network with a rigid Schiff base covalent backbone and tunable ionic junctions. This synergistic architecture yielded the best overall performance: superior thermal stability (24.61% residual weight), oxidative stability index (28.03 h), oil binding capacity (97.08%), and most sustained FFA release during digestion. These findings establish dual-crosslinked oleogels as a promising platform for functional fat substitutes and bioactive delivery systems. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Author full names: Wang, Xiaofeng (61005700900); Yang, Nan (58859572400); Zhang, Zheying (56068626800); Mehraj, Ali (58991197900); Scola, Pietro (61010493400); Herda, Tomas (58678912100); Hyrynsalmi, Sami (50361307000)
Title: From duality to triadic structuration: Coupling Agile agency, generative technology, and regulatory structure
Abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) increasingly permeates software development, Agile organizations face growing pressure to achieve continuous lifecycle compliance amid rapidly evolving regulatory demands. Classical Structuration Theory and its derivatives account for technology as either an instantiation of social structure or a medium for human agency; neither pole adequately captures GenAI's quasi-autonomous capacity to reshape organizational practices and give rise to new regulatory obligations. This study addresses this gap by developing Triadic Structuration Theory. Following an incremental design science research (DSR) paradigm, we develop this abstract design artifact through cycle-level intermediate artifacts, with cross-cycle knowledge accumulation. Cycle 1 derives a problem backlog of GenAI-induced tensions in Agile practice. Cycle 2 conceptualizes RegOps, showing how Agile agency adapts under regulatory pressure. Cycle 3 designs an EU AI Act-aligned model card template, showing how regulatory structure becomes embedded in generative technology. Cycle 4 explores GenAI-enabled solutions to ISO-related compliance barriers in an Agile company. Together, the evidence and knowledge accumulated within and across the cycles position generative technology as a third construct rather than a medium between agency and structure. Regulatory structure is embedded directly into it; it reshapes Agile agency through quasi-autonomous action, and its use to meet existing obligations may recursively generate new ones. The study extends Structuration Theory as a middle-range theory to Agile and GenAI contexts, and demonstrates how nested DSR with intermediate artifacts can support theory development. For practitioners, it offers guidance on leveraging GenAI for compliance, cautioning that it is a structural intervention rather than a one-off fix. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Experimental study on particle emission reduction and oxidation regeneration performance of CDPF: influence of Pt-Pd synergy and Ce modification
Abstract: Catalytic diesel particulate filters (CDPFs) combine particulate filtration with catalyst assisted soot oxidation. However, the effects of Pt-Pd synergy and Ce modification on particulate emission reduction and oxidation regeneration performance under engine exhaust conditions require further investigation. In this study, Pt, Pt-Pd, and Pt-Pd-Ce loaded CDPFs with identical substrate specifications were investigated using engine bench tests. Their PN and PM reduction efficiencies, particle size distributions, soot accumulation characteristics, pressure drop recovery, temperature evolution, regeneration rates, and particle emissions during regeneration were systematically evaluated. The results show that Pt-Pd-Ce-CDPF achieves the highest average PN and PM reduction efficiencies of 98.4% and 99.3%, respectively. All three CDPFs remove accumulation mode particles more effectively than nucleation mode particles. The average soot accumulation rates of Pt-CDPF, Pt-Pd-CDPF, and Pt-Pd-Ce-CDPF are 1.16, 1.02, and 0.87 g/h, while their regeneration rates are 1.79, 2.01, and 2.55 g·L−1/h, respectively. The corresponding complete regeneration times are 2.24, 1.99, and 1.57 h. Pressure drop recovery shows a rapid initial stage followed by a slower stage. Particle emissions during regeneration are dominated by transient nucleation mode burst windows. Pt-Pd-CDPF reduces the number and cumulative duration of significant burst windows to 10 and 91 s, while Pt-Pd-Ce-CDPF shows a lower mean PN concentration of 2.24 × 105 #/cm3 at the peak particle diameter. Under the tested conditions, Pt-Pd-Ce-CDPF provides the best overall particulate emission reduction and oxidation regeneration performance. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Tian Y.; Qiu H.
Title: PMVGD: Progressive multi-view graph distillation for health event prediction
Abstract: Graph-based methods have gained increasing attention for health event prediction from Electronic Health Records (EHRs). However, existing graph-based models face a key trade-off: complex heterogeneous graphs introduce noise and sparsity in inter-type relations, while simplified graphs overlook critical cross-domain signals. To this end, we propose PMVGD, a Progressive Multi-View Graph Distillation framework that reframes patient representation learning as iterative knowledge transfer across multiple clinical views. Specifically, PMVGD constructs a compact disease graph as the backbone, complemented by procedure and medication graphs. First, a teacher encoder, pretrained on the compact disease graph with a novel bottleneck fusion module, is developed to extract robust clinical patterns while minimizing noise. Then, a multi-view graph collaborative learning mechanism is introduced to train student encoders on the complementary graphs, guided by the teacher encoder. This mechanism employs contrastive alignment to ensure cross-view consistency and collaborative supervision to retain view-specific signals. Finally, we devise an adaptive sequential distillation strategy to refine the teacher encoder by integrating the students’ enriched perspectives, closing the loop to iteratively enhance patient representations with cross-domain insights. Extensive experiments on two real-world EHR datasets demonstrate that PMVGD consistently outperforms ten state-of-the-art baselines across two prediction tasks. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/low86/PMVGD. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Gao Y.; Liang C.; Cao Y.; Han Y.; Ji S.; Jiang F.; Yu Z.; Han X.
Title: Predicting lacustrine shale oil sweet spots: Machine-learning-derived geochemical insights into anomalous Tmax suppression and free oil enrichment
Abstract: Identifying shale oil sweet spots in heterogeneous lacustrine systems requires geochemical indicators that are continuously available along the wellbore and can be related to the geological processes of hydrocarbon generation, migration, and retention. In the Eocene Liushagang Formation of the Fushan Depression, Beibuwan Basin, pronounced lithofacies heterogeneity and the limited spatial coverage of Rock-Eval measurements on core samples have restricted the fine scale delineation of intervals enriched in free oil. Here, we integrate total organic carbon (TOC) and Rock-Eval data from 61 samples with acoustic, spontaneous potential, caliper, gamma ray, and deep resistivity logs using an ensemble artificial neural network (EANN) to predict continuous profiles of TOC, free hydrocarbons (S1), hydrocarbon generation potential (S2), and maximum pyrolysis temperature (Tmax). On the testing subset, the model yielded R2 values of 0.80, 0.86, 0.88, and 0.87 for TOC, S1, S2, and Tmax, respectively. Application to an independent blind well returned R2 values of 0.89, 0.91, 0.87, and 0.85 for the same parameters. Tmax ranges from 444 to 460 °C within an interval spanning less than 100 m of burial depth. Intervals with lower Tmax are associated with higher oil saturation index (OSI) and production index (PI) values calculated from the predicted parameters. This relationship is consistent with the retention of oil that migrated over short distances within the source rock and is unlikely to reflect a maturity gradient alone. Five candidate intervals with potential free oil enrichment were identified, among which Interval I has the highest mean OSI value of 41.87 mg HC/g TOC. By linking continuous geochemical predictions to a retained oil signature, this workflow extends well log based prediction beyond the interpolation of individual parameters and provides a practical basis for screening poorly sampled intervals in heterogeneous lacustrine shale. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
