Title: Build-direction heterogeneity and T6-induced shift in fatigue failure mechanisms of thick-wall additive friction stir deposited Al–Zn–Mg–Cu alloy
Abstract: Fatigue crack initiation in thick-wall additive friction stir deposited Al–Zn–Mg–Cu alloys is strongly governed by build-direction heterogeneity and heat-treatment-induced microstructural reconstruction. In this work, a 102-layer deposit was fabricated and tested under build-direction cyclic loading before and after T6 treatment. The as-deposited alloy exhibited severe build-direction heterogeneity in hardness, grain structure, dislocation density, and precipitation state, promoting cyclic strain localization and fatigue crack initiation from weak interlayer/soft-zone regions. T6 treatment increased the fatigue strength at 107 cycles from approximately 55 MPa to 84 MPa, representing a 52.7 % improvement, mainly due to η′-dominated precipitation reconstruction and partial homogenization of local mechanical response. Nevertheless, fatigue failure after T6 treatment was still limited by Mg–Si-rich constituent particles and residual grain-boundary η/S phases, which served as preferential crack-nucleation sites. Although T6 treatment substantially improves fatigue resistance, residual Mg–Si-rich particles and grain-boundary η/S precipitates continue to limit the fatigue performance of thick-wall AFSD components. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Bai B.; Sun M.; Qiang L.; An Y.; Wei S.; Wang F.; Ma X.
Title: Mechanistic study on the catalytic upgrading of volatiles from lignite hydropyrolysis to aromatic hydrocarbons over alkali-modified Zn/ZSM-5 catalyst
Abstract: Aromatic compounds, as important chemicals and pharmaceutical intermediates, can be obtained through catalytic hydropyrolysis of lignite. In this regard, the development of catalysts and the exploration of reaction mechanisms are crucial. In this study, ZSM-5 zeolite was synthesized, subjected to alkaline treatment, and then loaded with Zn, and its structure and composition were analyzed by using XRD, SEM, and NH3-TPD, etc. A fast pyrolysis experiment of Shengli lignite was conducted in a powder–particle fluidized bed reactor using the catalyst as the mobile phase, the results revealed that Zn loading and alkaline treatment did not alter the framework structure of the ZSM-5 zeolite but induced mesopore formation and increased total acidity, effectively increased the aromatic content of the pyrolysis tar. The AT-Zn/ZSM-5 catalyst achieved an aromatic content of up to 73.2% in pyrolysis tar under a 10% hydrogen atmosphere. The AT-Zn/ZSM-5 catalyst demonstrated satisfactory cycling stability: after ten reaction-regeneration cycles, the MFI framework was largely retained. However, the catalyst exhibited increased mesopore volume and decreased acidity, accompanied by a decline in the aromatic fraction of tar from 73.2% to 63.5%. Meanwhile, the aromatics-formation pathway was further proposed on the basis of catalyst characterization, product-distribution analysis, and DFT calculations, providing a theoretical basis for subsequent catalyst design. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Pan X.; Wang X.; Liu S.; Huang C.; Qi Y.; Huang H.; Zhang L.; Gao H.
Title: High-temperature tribological behavior of laser-clad Al0.5CoCrFeNi/TiN composite coatings: Tribolayer evolution and atomic-scale load-bearing mechanisms of TiN particles
Abstract: TiN reinforcement offers a route to improve the high-temperature wear resistance of laser-clad Al0.5CoCrFeNi coatings. However, its effects on coating microstructure, high-temperature tribological performance, friction-interface evolution, and atomic-scale deformation remain unclear. In this study, Al0.5CoCrFeNi/TiN composite coatings with 0, 5, 15, and 25 wt% TiN were fabricated on AISI 1045 steel and investigated using sliding wear tests and molecular dynamics nanoscratching simulations. Higher TiN content increased coating hardness; however, excessive TiN promoted particle agglomeration and detachment, consequently exacerbating third-body abrasive wear. The 5 wt% TiN coating showed the lowest and most stable friction coefficient at room temperature. It also exhibited lower estimated wear rates than the TiN-free coating at 200, 500 and 800 °C, with a minimum value of 5.47 × 10−6 mm3/(N·m) at 500 °C, indicating a 96.04% reduction under the adopted calculation procedure. Surface and cross-sectional SEM/EDS observations, together with XPS results, support the formation of a composite tribolayer involving TiN-containing regions, oxidation products, counterface-derived species, and compacted wear debris at 500 °C. MD results further indicated that TiN formed localized load-bearing zones, redistributed contact stress, and hindered dislocation and stacking fault propagation. Overall, the high-temperature wear resistance is closely associated with the local load-bearing capacity of TiN and the stability of the composite tribolayer. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Thermal performance of a heated tube equipped with a novel perforated V–baffle turbulator: Experimental investigation and artificial neural network prediction
Abstract: Improving the thermal performance of heat exchangers using turbulators requires balancing enhanced heat transfer against the accompanying pressure losses. In this study, conventional V-baffle turbulators were modified into a perforated V-baffle configuration, introducing physical characteristics different from those reported previously. This research examined the effects of perforated V-baffles with different orientations (upstream and downstream directions), angles of attack (30°, 50°, and 70°) and pitch lengths (25.4, 50.8, and 76.2 mm) on the thermal performance (expressed in terms of the thermal enhancement factor (TEF)) of a constant heat flux tube heat exchanger across a Reynolds numbers range of 5502-13,786. The TEF obtained for the tube equipped with perforated V-baffles ranged from approximately 0.97-1.70, depending on the baffle configuration and airflow velocity. The results indicate that the perforated V-baffles with larger pitch lengths and smaller angles of attack tended to exhibit superior thermal performance. Notably, the perforated V-baffles exhibited relatively stable TEF values across the tested airflow velocities, a key feature of this turbulator. In addition, an artificial neural network (ANN) was employed as a predictive tool to estimate the TEF. Multiple ANN models were developed using different hyperparameter settings to identify the optimal architecture. The best-performing model achieved a coefficient of determination (R2) and a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 0.999 and 0.42%,respectively, when predicting previously unknown TEF data. Furthermore, sensitivity analysis was conducted to assess the effect of independent variables on TEF, revealing that the angle of attack exerted the most significant impact. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Authors: Chen G.; Zou H.; Wang P.; Wang X.; Chen F.
Title: Reduced electron transfer from N-doping Mo2C MXene cocatalyst to CdS for enhanced photocatalytic H2 production
Abstract: As a photocatalytic cocatalyst, Mo2C MXene (Mo2CTx) shows significant potential due to its unique properties and abundant surface-active Mo sites. However, the Mo sites exhibit strong hydrogen adsorption ability, which leads to unfavorable desorption of the generated hydrogen from the Mo sites, limiting the hydrogen evolution efficiency. When Mo2C MXene is composited with photocatalyst CdS, the substantial work function difference drives spontaneous electron transfer from Mo2C MXene to CdS, resulting in the formation of stronger Mo-Hads bonds. In this work, this challenge is addressed by modulating the work function of Mo2CTx via N doping to reduce electron transfer from Mo2CTx to CdS for weakened Mo-H bond. N-doped Mo2CTx (N-Mo2CTx) is successfully synthesized by high-temperature solid-state nitridation of Mo2CTx, and CdS is in-situ grown on its surface via chemical precipitation to form N-Mo2CTx/CdS. Results reveal that N-Mo2CTx/CdS achieves a remarkable hydrogen evolution rate of 18.6 mmol h−1 g−1 in a lactic acid sacrificial system, nearly 9 and 2 times greater than that of CdS and Mo2CTx/CdS, respectively. The enhanced activity stems from the N-Mo2CTx work function and increased antibonding orbital occupancy, which suppresses interfacial electron transfer and optimizes hydrogen adsorption/desorption kinetics. This study provides an innovative strategy for designing advanced Mo2C MXene-loaded photocatalysts through doping engineering. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wang J.; Fan X.; Shang J.; Liu Z.; Li L.; Hong J.; Liu M.; Zheng X.; Liu C.
Title: Chain-length distributions and solid content determine digestion-limiting mechanisms of wheat starch gels through cross-scale fractal network assembly
Abstract: Chain-length distributions (CLDs) and solid content are known to affect starch gel digestibility. However, it remains unclear how chain architecture translates, through cross-scale network organization, into distinct rate-limiting characteristics during enzymatic digestion. Using starches enriched in long amylopectin branch chains (L-Ap), short amylopectin branch chains (S-Ap), and long amylose chains (L-Am), this study systematically investigated how CLDs characteristics and solid content (10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50%) jointly shape starch gel networks and subsequently determine the dominant rate-limiting mechanisms during enzymatic digestion. Increasing solid content reduced water mobility and advanced the transition from rapid to restricted hydrolysis from 40 to 30 min. However, the structural basis of this shift depended on chain architecture. L-Ap gel showed the greatest increase in retrogradation enthalpy from 0.33 to 0.72 J/g and was associated with a more complex and relatively open network, a structural feature consistent with restricted enzyme propagation through the gel matrix. S-Ap gel formed local aggregates and less integrated networks, suggesting that its digestion was mainly influenced by local steric hindrance during the initial stage, followed by gradual substrate exposure. At high concentration, L-Am gel retained the highest nanoscale mass filling (Dm = 1.32) and exhibited a more continuous internal skeleton. Overall, these findings clarify how starch CLDs and solid content jointly shape cross-scale gel network organization and reveal fractal structural features associated with distinct digestion constraints, providing a basis for tailoring the digestibility of starch-based gels. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Mi Y.; Guo D.; Zhao L.-C.
Title: Transient response of rotating multiscale carbon nanotube/carbon fiber annular plates for high-impact weightlifting applications
Source title: International Journal of Modern Physics C
Abstract: This study explores the transient dynamic response of rotating hybrid annular plates designed for high-impact weightlifting applications, subjected to mechanical shock. The proposed structure is modeled as a multi-scale three-phase composite, consisting of a polymer matrix reinforced with Carbon Nanotube (CNT) nanoparticles and unidirectional Carbon Fibers (CFs). The Eshelby–Mori–Tanaka scheme is adopted to incorporate the effects of CNT agglomeration, enabling accurate prediction of the enhanced isotropic properties of the nanocomposite. The governing equations, derived via First-order Shear Deformation Theory (FSDT) and Hamilton’s principle, are solved using the finite element method combined with the Newmark time integration scheme. A comprehensive parametric study is conducted to assess the influence of CNT mass fraction, distribution, agglomeration, CF volume fraction, fiber orientation, geometrical configuration and boundary conditions on the dynamic performance of the annular plate. Results indicate that the synergistic use of CNTs and CFs significantly enhances the plate’s stiffness and impact resistance. Notably, at 0.1 CF volume fraction, the central deflection under shock loading is reduced by 27.7% compared to a CNT-only system (1% CNT). A combined reinforcement of CNTs and CFs leads to a 49.2% reduction in deflection. Maximum performance is observed at 0° fiber orientation, while deflection increases by 222% at 45°, highlighting the critical role of fiber alignment in weightlifting-specific impact scenarios. The influence of the CNT distribution pattern on the dynamic response is highly dependent on the CF orientation. Title: Optimal error analysis of fully-discrete high-order semi-implicit RK-SAV/LDG schemes for the Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard equations
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: In this paper, we propose and analyze fully-discrete, high-order, linear, and energy-stable schemes for the Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard equations, combining the scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) approach with semi-implicit Runge-Kutta (RK) time integration and the local discontinuous Galerkin (LDG) method for spatial discretization. We first establish the energy stability and optimal error estimates of the semi-discrete RK-SAV scheme under an a priori H2-bound. Discrete energy stability of the fully-discrete scheme is also proved. Finally, by employing a special error splitting technique, elliptic projection, and negative norm estimates, we derive optimal L2-error estimates of the fully-discrete RK-SAV/LDG schemes for the Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard equations. Numerical experiments are presented to verify the theoretical results. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Chai Y.; Guo Y.; Jin X.; Zhang M.; Qiao J.
Title: A unified model for residual stress measurement via nanoindentation
Abstract: Accurate measurement of the residual stress is crucial for ensuring the structural integrity and service life of engineering components. Conventional nanoindentation methods heavily rely on stress-free reference samples, which are often difficult to obtain or prepare in practice. This study proposes a refined nanoindentation-based computational method that eliminates this requirement. Building upon established unloading work and stress decomposition frameworks, the model introduces two key modifications: material-dependent correction factors derived via dimensional analysis and finite element simulations, and a novel reconstruction of the stress-free indentation response using a stress-insensitive depth recovery parameter. The model is inherently semi-empirical, combining physically grounded theory with systematically calibrated simulation data—a practical necessity given the complexity of the underlying elastoplastic deformation. The model distinguishes between compressive and tensile residual stress states, and explicitly accounts for material mechanical parameters (E/σy, n). Comprehensive numerical verification, including forward/inverse prediction and stability analysis, shows that relative prediction errors are predominantly within ±15%, with good robustness against minor parameter perturbations. The assumptions underlying the finite element simulations—axisymmetric conical indenter equivalence and isotropic power-law hardening—are critically examined regarding their impact on model accuracy and applicability. Experimental validation using published data from five diverse material systems demonstrates strong agreement with reported values. The model offers reliable accuracy for the conditions tested, with promising potential for broader applicability within its defined parameter space and assumptions. This work provides a viable in-situ measurement solution for residual stress without requiring stress-free reference samples. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS

Authors: Li Y.; Wang Y.; Zhang M.; Luo X.; Zhu J.; Du S.; Hu Q.
Title: A comprehensive review of in situ characterization, phase behavior, and predictive modeling of natural gas hydrates for sustainable energy development
Abstract: Natural gas hydrates (NGHs) are widely regarded as a promising unconventional energy resource due to their high energy density and relatively low carbon emissions. However, their commercial development remains constrained by the low permeability and strong heterogeneity of hydrate-bearing sediments, complex multiphase flow behaviors, and dynamics phase transition during gas production. This study provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in NGH research, with particular emphasis on in situ characterization, phase behavior, production technologies, and predictive modeling. We first summarize recent progress in in situ sampling and characterization techniques for evaluating hydrate occurrence, reservoir properties, and fluid distributions under geological conditions. These techniques are critical for capturing reservoir heterogeneity and improving the accuracy of resource assessment and modeling. Building on this foundation, we further examine the thermodynamics and kinetics of NGH. Furthermore, major production technologies, including depressurization, thermal stimulation, CO2–CH4 replacement, and integrated production strategies, are critically evaluated with respect to their mechanisms, advantages, limitations, and engineering applicability. Recent progress in predictive modeling is also discussed, focusing on multiscale and multiphysics simulation frameworks that integrate thermal, hydrological, mechanical, and chemical processes to improve predictions of hydrate evolution and reservoir performance. Overall, this review identifies key scientific challenges and providing a roadmap for future research directions aimed at the sustainable and efficient exploitation of NGHs in the global energy transition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Shi H.; Li Z.; Wang B.; Duan X.; Li T.
Title: Acousto-mechanofluidic synergy: A GHz resonator-enhanced rotary valve system for fully automated, efficient point-of-care nucleic acid testing
Abstract: The advancement of point-of-care testing (POCT) is critical for decentralized molecular diagnostics, yet current platforms are hindered byinefficient mixing, complex workflows, long turnaround times, and operator dependency. This study presents the acoustofluidic-enhancedintegrated system (AEIS), a fully automated platform that integrates a GHz acoustic resonator with a micro-valve control system for nucleicacid testing. The resonator generates intense acoustic streaming vortices, enabling second-scale mixing and reducing nucleic acid extractiontime to under 4 min. Coupled with hydroxyl-modified polystyrene microbeads for nucleic acid extraction (98% efficiency) and automatedfluidic control via a rotary valve, the system detects EGFR L858R mutations in plasma with a limit of detection of 2.6 copies/μl and completes the sample-to-answer workflow within 30 min. This enclosed, low-cost, and portable platform minimizes contamination and operatorintervention, offering a sensitive and efficient solution for on-site testing in infectious disease control and early cancer screening. © 2026 Author(s).

Title: Differences in phase behavior of shale hydrocarbon mixtures in organic and inorganic pores
Abstract: Shale reservoirs contain complex mineral assemblages, yet the differences in phase behavior of fluids confined within different mineral nanopores remain insufficiently understood. In this study, Monte Carlo simulations combined with molecular dynamics simulations are used to compare the phase behavior of C1-nC4 mixtures confined in organic matter and illite nanopores. The organic surface is modified with oxygen atoms to match the carbon-to-oxygen ratio of kerogen in the studied formation. The results show that, owing to stronger adsorption, the phase envelope contracts more significantly in organic nanopores than in illite pores of the same size, with higher dew point pressures and lower bubble point pressures. Fluid-surface interaction energy analysis indicates that nC4 is preferentially adsorbed in both organic and inorganic nanopores. Organic nanopores exhibit deeper potential energy wells, indicating stronger fluid-surface attraction. The phase behavior of mixtures confined in micropores is further examined. In 2 nm organic pores, the superposition of surface potential fields suppresses vapor-liquid phase transition at 30°C, and the confined fluid exhibits micropore-filling characteristics. In contrast, vapor-liquid phase transition still occurs in illite pores. Stronger fluid-surface interactions promote enrichment of heavy components in the adsorbed phase near the pore wall, while light components are relatively enriched in the free phase. This compositional fractionation enhances the control of light components on dew point behavior, thereby increasing the dew point pressure. At the bubble point, adsorption-layer interactions deepen the potential well of free-phase C1 and reduce its escape tendency, increasing the difficulty of vaporization and lowering the bubble point pressure. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Cai B.; Lin S.; Pan Y.; Zheng K.; Li Y.; Chen D.; Zhu Y.
Title: Suppression of methane explosion propagation from vessels to pipes using a reverse configured Tesla valve structure
Abstract: This study evaluates the isolation effectiveness of a reverse Tesla valve against methane explosions via experiments compared with a straight pipe. The results show that the valve effectively quenches the first explosion flame via counter-flow collisions and significantly delays the secondary flame arrival at the outlet. The maximum average flame velocity reductions reach 51% and 75% for the first and secondary explosions, respectively, relative to the straight pipe, and both reductions change with higher equivalence ratios. Upstream overpressure reverses near ϕ = 1, being lower under fuel-lean and higher under fuel-rich conditions, while downstream peak overpressure is consistently lower across all conditions. The valve also exhibits excellent one-way isolation, with impulse blocking exceeding 90% under all conditions and overpressure blocking reaching 88% at ϕ = 1.12 and remaining at 58% even at ϕ = 1.42. These findings indicate that the reverse Tesla valve has potential as a passive explosion isolation device. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Synergistic modification of coal-based solid waste grouting material with SAP and nano-SiO2 for CO2 mineralization: Optimization, performance, and mechanisms
Abstract: Coal-based solid waste mineralization materials generally face bottlenecks of low carbon sequestration efficiency and poor long-term stability. While superabsorbent polymer (SAP)-based internal curing has been proven effective in cement-based materials, its applicability in solid waste-based geopolymer systems remains controversial. In this work, a multi-component coal-based solid waste CO2 mineralization grouting material was prepared using coal gangue, fly ash and desulfurization gypsum as raw materials, carbide slag and sodium silicate as activators, and SAP and nano-SiO2 as functional modifiers. Formula optimization and comparative analysis under standard and mineralization curing were performed. Under standard curing, SAP locked up the early alkaline solution and retarded geopolymer skeleton formation, reducing the 28d compressive strength. Under mineralization curing, SAP improved the strength retention ratio and achieved a maximum carbon sequestration capacity of 115.1 g/kg. SEM-EDS results show that SAP suppresses Na⁺ migration and promotes preferential reaction of CO2 with Ca2+ to form calcite. TG-DTG and XRD results further confirm lower Ca(OH)2 residue and higher calcite content, supporting the alkaline reserve slow-release function. BET and SEM results indicate that SAP retains pore water and promotes gel formation around released-water voids, as evidenced by the pore structure evolution in which in-situ-formed calcite fills mesopores while SAP-released voids and calcite growth stress reshape macropores, collectively demonstrating enhanced internal mass transfer and CO2 mineralization within the matrix. Authors: Rong W.; Hu Y.; Cao R.; Zhao F.; Yu W.
Title: The effects of long-arc plasma ignition on flame propagation and buoyancy-induced upward flame displacement of ammonia/air mixtures at elevated pressures
Abstract: Ammonia is a promising zero-carbon fuel, but its combustion is hindered by difficult ignition, low flame propagation speed, and buoyancy-induced upward flame displacement, particularly at elevated pressures. This study develops a long-arc plasma ignition strategy integrating bipolar nanosecond pulsed excitation with a specially designed electrode for spatially extended discharge. Comparative experiments were conducted in a constant-volume chamber at initial pressures of 1–7 bar with equivalence ratios Φ of 0.7–1.4. The long-arc electrode and conventional spark plug were operated under identical pulse repetition frequency, pulse number, and deposited energy, enabling direct assessment of the effect of spatial energy deposition. It was demonstrated that the long-arc strategy generated a larger initial flame kernel that could significantly enhance flame propagation compared with conventional spark ignition, thereby suppressing buoyancy-induced upward flame displacement, as quantitatively reflected by consistently higher Froude numbers. When pressure raised up to 7 bar, flame-wrinkling analysis showed that long-arc discharge promoted flame wrinkling over Φ = 0.9–1.3. Stronger buoyancy at Φ = 0.9 and 1.3 retained more wrinkles, resulting in a greater enhancement in stretched flame speed. Heat-release analysis further indicated that long-arc ignition shortened the ignition delay, weakened the double-peak heat-release-rate profile, and reduced the overall heat-release duration. It is worthy noted that the spatial distribution of plasma energy deposition plays an important role in elevated-pressure ammonia ignition and combustion, highlighting the potential of long-arc plasma ignition to address the combustion bottleneck problem in advanced ammonia-fueled internal combustion engines. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhang X.; Wei Y.; Yang K.; Guo J.; Yan C.; Lei W.; Lei Y.; Fang C.
Title: “Thiol-ene” click-enabled dual covalent network engineering for high-barrier and robust chitosan-based active packaging films
Abstract: Chitosan-based packaging films often suffer from insufficient mechanical strength, moisture sensitivity, and limited barrier performance, restricting their application in active food packaging. Herein, a dual covalent network strategy enabled by thiol-ene click chemistry and terminal double-bond self-crosslinking was developed to construct multifunctional chitosan-based films. Water-soluble methylacrylated chitosan (CSMA) was used as the matrix, while L-cysteine-derived dithiol-functionalized graphene quantum dots (Cys-GQDs) served as the multifunctional component. The thiol-ene click reaction established covalent interfacial linkages between Cys-GQDs and CSMA chains, while abundant polar groups on Cys-GQDs generated additional hydrogen-bonding and acid-base interactions, resulting in a strengthened and compact hybrid network. Consequently, the optimized films exhibited a tensile strength of 134.3 MPa) and an improved water contact angle of 80.8°. Meanwhile, the integrated crosslinked structure and nanoscale tortuous pathways effectively inhibited molecular diffusion, leading to a low water vapor transmission rate of 443.81 g/(m2·day) and a CO2/O2 selectivity of 13.55. Furthermore, Cys-GQDs endowed the films with approximately 75%ultraviolet shielding efficiency and 85% antibacterial activity against both Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus. Benefiting from these multifunctional properties, the films enabled effective and prolonged the storage quality of fresh-cut potato slices and cherry tomatoes. This study provides a molecular design strategy for developing high-performance chitosan-based active packaging materials. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: M B A.; Pradeep N.; M R S.; Girish V.; S G.; Mohan K.; P K J.
Title: Numerical investigation of the thermo-hydraulic performance of a diatom-inspired pin-fin heat sink
Abstract: The increasing heat generation in compact electronic devices necessitates the development of heat sinks capable of simultaneously enhancing heat transfer and minimizing hydraulic losses. Inspired by the streamlined external morphology of the diatom Navicula capitatoradiata , a novel diatom-inspired pin-fin heat sink (DPFHS) is proposed and numerically investigated under forced-convection conditions. The thermo-hydraulic characteristics of the proposed heat sink were numerically investigated using a three-dimensional CFD model developed in ANSYS Fluent. A sequential optimization strategy was adopted in which the influence of the fin-height ratio (h/H), fin aspect ratio (m/M), and through-holes was systematically investigated. The results demonstrate that the diatom-inspired profile effectively suppresses wake formation and significantly reduces hydraulic resistance while maintaining effective fluid–surface interaction. Among the investigated fin-height ratios, h/H = 0.9 provided the highest Performance Evaluation Criterion (PEC) of 1.45 relative to the CPFHS. Subsequent optimization identified m/M = 0.125 as the most effective fin aspect ratio owing to its superior overall thermo-hydraulic balance. Introducing through-holes into this optimized geometry further enhanced performance, with the three-hole configuration achieving the highest PEC of 1.129 among the perforated configurations. The present results demonstrate the potential of a diatom-derived external morphology as a design strategy for developing compact heat sinks with favourable thermo-hydraulic performance. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Authors: Chen W.; Yuan H.; Li S.; Ye M.
Title: DMoA: Dynamic Mixture of Adapters with Feature-Enhanced Fusion for UAV Visible-Infrared Object Detection
Abstract: Visible-infrared (RGB-IR) object detection has attracted significant attention in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based applications, such as disaster search and rescue, intelligent surveillance, and battlefield target tracking. However, the quality of RGB and IR modalities may vary substantially under different environmental conditions, causing one modality to become unreliable and leading to suboptimal feature enhancement and fusion. To address this challenge, we propose the Dynamic Mixture of Adapters (DMoA), a novel modality-aware enhancement framework that dynamically refines multi-modal features before semantic fusion through a Mixture of Experts (MoE) mechanism. Applied across multi-scale feature layers, DMoA consists of three key components. First, a Cross-Modality Feature Pre-Enhancement (CMFPE) block exploits complementary information to compensate for weak modality features. Second, the Dynamic Feature Enhancement (DFE) block employs separate four-expert pools and gating networks for RGB and IR at each scale, with no parameter sharing across modalities or scales. Each gating network sparsely activates the top two lightweight experts for input-adaptive feature refinement, thereby limiting computational overhead. Finally, a Semantic Information Fusion (SIF) block promotes cross-modal semantic consistency through mutual information optimization while suppressing redundant feature responses. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that DMoA consistently achieves competitive detection performance and a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off, highlighting its effectiveness for UAV-based RGB-IR object detection. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Wang J.; Wu H.; Feng J.; Yuan M.; Li P.; Qian X.; Liu H.; Zhou Y.
Title: Asymmetric deflagration characteristics of hydrogen-blended natural gas under multiscale conditions: The influence of ignition location
Abstract: Hydrogen-blended natural gas (HBNG) is receiving increasing attention as a practical low-carbon gaseous fuel for the transition of natural-gas-based energy systems, but its vented deflagration behavior in partially confined spaces remains insufficiently understood, especially when ignition occurs at different locations and system scale changes. To address this issue, vented deflagration experiments were conducted in three geometrically similar chambers with internal volumes of 2809 L, 281 L, and 28 L. Six representative ignition locations were considered: chamber center (LC), top center (LT), bottom center (LD), back wall (LB), right wall (LR), and quarter-diagonal intersection (LCC). The results showed that ignition location strongly affected the explosion response, but its role changed markedly with scale. As the scale decreased, the internal pressure response evolved from a clearly separated multi-peak structure to a compressed single-peak composite waveform. Under the tested conditions, the 281 L chamber generated the strongest near-field external shock, with a maximum free-field peak overpressure of 53.8 kPa at 0.5 m under LR ignition. The 2809 L chamber exhibited the most pronounced multi-peak external pressure propagation and vent competition, whereas the 28 L chamber showed highly localized near-vent external effects. Moreover, the thermal hazard zone shifted from concentration on the front and top walls at the large scale to more distributed multi-wall exposure at the small scale. These findings clarify the scale-dependent explosion behavior of HBNG and provide useful guidance for vent design and thermal-load management in enclosures and equipment associated with hydrogen use and natural gas utilization. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wang G.; Yue Q.; Dou D.; Zhao Z.; Nie X.; Ma Z.; Zhang Q.
Title: Moving-boundary wear–leakage coupling and contact-degradation-induced sealing failure of HNBR packer seals under two-way fluid–structure interaction
Abstract: Wear-induced contact degradation in packer elements is a tribological failure process. It involves temperature-dependent material removal, interfacial slip, contact-pressure redistribution, and leakage-path propagation. This failure mode is critical for expandable packers used in staged hydraulic fracturing, where high differential pressure and elevated downhole temperature accelerate wear, annular leakage, and displacement-induced seal failure. To describe this process, this study establishes a two-way fluid–structure interaction model for coupled wear–leakage behavior in an expandable packer element. The model uses a Mooney–Rivlin hyperelastic constitutive model to describe large deformation and a temperature-corrected Archard wear model to predict interfacial material removal. A moving contact boundary and ALE adaptive meshing update the worn geometry, while an overset-grid strategy and nonmatching interface data transfer achieve two-way coupling between the solid and fluid domains. Low-pressure tests at prescribed wear depths support the predicted response of specified worn geometries, with reported deviations below 10% for the compared contact and penetration measures. These tests do not directly validate transient wear accumulation or full-scale high-pressure behavior. At 50 MPa and 50 °C, worn-geometry updating increases the predicted leakage length at t sim= 3.0 s from 15.49 to 36.91 mm, corresponding to a factor of 2.38. Compared with the one-way coupling model, the full two-way model increases the predicted leakage length by 24.82%, confirming that reverse fluid-to-solid feedback further promotes leakage-path propagation. Higher pump pressure promotes degradation mainly by increasing interfacial slip and material removal, whereas elevated temperature accelerates axial slip and reduces contact pressure. For the packer configuration and HNBR material system investigated here, a leakage length equal to 50% of the initial effective sealing length is proposed as a configuration-specific provisional engineering warning level for functional sealing failure, rather than as a universal acceptance criterion. The model provides a tribology-oriented computational tool for predicting wear-induced leakage and sealing failure in elastomeric packer seals. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Tian Q.; Zhao D.; Ma X.; Ma Z.
Title: Corncob char-supported iron catalyst for hydrogen production via methane pyrolysis with carbon-iron co-utilization for steelmaking
Abstract: Catalytic methane pyrolysis (CMP) offers a CO2-free route to hydrogen, yet industrial deployment is limited by carbon-induced catalyst deactivation and poor utilization of co-produced carbon. We introduce a “carbon-iron synergy, direct steelmaking” strategy in which a corncob char-supported Fe catalyst (Fe/CC) is engineered to enable efficient methane pyrolysis for H2 generation, while the spent Fe/CC@C composite serves directly as a steelmaking feedstock without carbon separation. After Fe loading, Fe/CC achieves a specific surface area of 261.20 m2/g and an activation energy of 137 kJ/mol, which is well below that of thermal pyrolysis (356-452 kJ/mol). It exhibits uniformly dispersed Fe nanoparticles with nanoscale crystallite sizes anchored on the porous carbon matrix, as confirmed by HRTEM lattice fringe analysis. At 900 °C and 10 mL/min CH4, it exhibits an “induction period”, during which methane conversion initially decreases and then increases, due to dynamic carbon dissolution forming metastable Fe3C and C0.12Fe1.88 phases, as confirmed by XRD and XPS. Over 11 h, methane conversion stabilizes at ∼88%, yielding 12,761.9 mL H2 and 3.08 g of solid carbon. Multiscale characterization shows that deposited carbon evolves from filamentous to spherical, reflecting a shift in the dominant deactivation mechanism from diffusion-limited to encapsulation-driven. Crucially, Fe/CC@C displays superior CO2 gasification reactivity compared with raw corncob char, with an onset temperature of ∼850 °C and a peak gasification rate at ∼970 °C, thereby demonstrating its viability as a ferro-carbon feedstock for low-carbon steelmaking. This work establishes an integrated route that synergistically couples clean hydrogen production with sustainable ironmaking through the concurrent valorization of carbon and iron. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhang M.; Liu J.; Xu J.; Wang J.; Dai C.; Cai X.; Wang J.; Huang Z.
Title: Role of radial swirl number on liquid ammonia combustion in a gas turbine combustor using a multi-hole nozzle
Abstract: Direct liquid ammonia (LNH3) combustion is a promising route for ammonia-fueled gas turbines, but flash boiling and evaporation cooling impose severe challenges in its flame stabilization and emission control. In a swirl combustor, swirl intensity governs recirculation and gas–liquid interaction, thereby changing droplet dispersion, evaporation, fuel distribution, and reaction. Clarifying this coupled pathway is therefore essential for appropriate swirler design. This study examines five radial geometric swirl numbers, Sg,r=1.30–3.93, in a laboratory-scale gas-turbine combustor under single-stage and staged conditions. Blow-off limits, flame photographs, and emissions were combined with synchronous NH-PLIF/Mie-scattering and NH-PLIF/PIV diagnostics. The results identify two distinct response intervals as Sg,r increases from low through intermediate to excessive levels. From Sg,r=1.30 to 1.96, the Mie-scattering area decreased by 54–74%, while the increases in transverse transport and planar strain remained limited, showing that moderate swirl primarily promoted residual-liquid evaporation. From Sg,r=1.96 to 3.93, the residual-liquid reduction ceased and the remaining signal was redistributed toward the combustor center and downstream, while transverse transport, velocity fluctuations, planar strain, and NH-layer fragmentation continued to increase. Excessive swirl therefore narrowed the stable range and increased NH3 and N2O emissions. Under staged operation, all swirlers shared a low-emission window near φp=1.05–1.10, whereas excessive swirl increased primary-flame sensitivity to secondary air and aggravated the lean-primary NH3/N2O penalty. These findings provide a configuration-specific basis for radial-swirler selection rather than a universal optimum. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Experimental investigation of steady-state, transient and cyclic ice–water phase change in a rectangular plate-fin enclosure for cold thermal energy storage
Abstract: Ice-based cold thermal energy storage systems require reliable experimental data relating to interface evolution, stored-ice fraction and thermal response under steady, transient and cyclic operating conditions. This paper experimentally investigates ice–water phase change in a horizontal rectangular plate-fin enclosure designed to represent a module of a cold thermal storage system. The enclosure consisted of an aluminium rectangular duct with the left and right walls acting as cold and hot walls, and the upper and lower walls functioning as continuous plate fins. Calibrated Type-E thermocouples were used to measure wall and fin temperatures, while the ice–water interface was recorded using optical imaging and image processing to estimate the ice fraction. Eight steady state cases, specifically two single-step transient excursions, two cyclic operating cases and repeatability runs were considered. For the steady-state tests, the cold-wall temperature increased from −6.18 °C to −2.40 °C with the input from nominal heater increasing from 85 to 190 W. The ice fraction reduced from 43.13% to 4.53%. During the transient tests, increasing the heater input from 85 W to 130 W resulted in melting-dominant behaviour, while 130 W to 85 W led to freezing-dominant behaviour. Four cycles each lasting 7200 s generated repeatable charging and discharging during cyclic operation, with a reduction in the ice fraction during high power half-cycles and an increase during low power half cycles. The results indicated that the morphology did not develop as a planar one-dimensional front, but determined by the interaction of heat conduction through the ice, conduction along the fins normal to the flow direction, natural convection in the liquid-water phase and density inversion of water near 4 °C. Concerning the design and validation of cold thermal energy storage systems, the work provides a benchmark for steady-state, transient, cyclic and repeatability experimental data from a rectangular plate-fin ice–water enclosure. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Author full names: Lei, Yuhang (60988867700); Song, Yafei (54401630700); Ge, Chengxian (61023077200); Li, Tianpeng (16316955700); Feng, Cunqian (24767704700)
Title: Boosting adversarial transferability with gradient alignment
Abstract: In black-box transfer attacks, existing methods commonly introduce multi-view mechanisms to alleviate overfitting to the surrogate model. However, owing to the highly nonlinear decision boundaries of deep neural networks, unconstrained input transformations can lead to cross-view gradient divergence. This divergence may cause effective gradients to cancel one another during aggregation, making it difficult to extract generalizable adversarial features and causing the optimization process to become trapped in local optima. To address this issue, we propose a Gradient Alignment Attack (GAA) framework motivated by gradient consistency. Specifically, GAA introduces a plug-and-play Gradient Aggregation Module (GAM), which is trained using a composite objective consisting of three loss terms: attack effectiveness, gradient consistency, and output diversity. Through this explicit intervention, GAA preserves multi-view exploration while constraining perturbation updates to follow more consistent directions, thereby mitigating cross-view gradient divergence. Extensive experiments on ImageNet demonstrate that GAA can be seamlessly integrated with various attack methods and consistently improves the attack success rate in black-box transfer attacks against diverse models. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Li Q.; Li Y.
Title: Boundary asymptotics for a class of degenerate linearized Monge-Ampère equations
Source title: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
Abstract: In this paper, we study a class of linearized Monge–Ampère equations whose coefficient matrix is generated by a degenerate Monge–Ampère Dirichlet problem. The right-hand side is allowed to have a boundary singularity of the form h(x)d(x)−q, where d(x) denotes the distance to the boundary. Assuming that a classical solution exists, we derive boundary asymptotic estimates and show that different values of q lead to different boundary behaviors. In particular, the boundary asymptotic behavior is governed by the distance function d(x) and the singularity exponent q , rather than by the degeneracy exponent of the coefficient matrix. We further establish weighted energy estimates and a corresponding W1,2-regularity result for a suitable power of the solution in the singular regime 1<q<2. Finally, we prove the non-existence of classical solutions in the strongly singular case. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Emission reduction through fuel staging in a three-stage tangential flow ammonia combustor
Abstract: Ammonia is a promising carbon-free energy carrier due to its ease of storage and transport compared to hydrogen; however, its practical utilization in combustion systems is hindered by fuel-bound NOx formation and ammonia slip. Fuel staging has been identified as a potential strategy for NOx mitigation, but its application to pure ammonia combustion remains limited, particularly under conditions that avoid unburned ammonia emissions. In this study, a three-stage tangential flow combustor is employed to investigate the role of fuel staging in controlling NOx reduction in pure ammonia flames at a thermal input of 60 kW and global equivalence ratios ranging from 0.5 to 1.2. The configuration integrates air preheating, air staging, and distributed fuel injection to enable spatial control of local equivalence ratios. Experimental results demonstrate that fuel staging significantly reduces NOx emissions, achieving up to ∼ 85 % reduction under lean conditions and ∼ 75 % under rich conditions, while maintaining negligible ammonia slip. Large Eddy Simulations (LES) coupled with detailed chemical kinetics are used to provide mechanistic insight into the observed trends. The analysis reveals that fuel staging promotes the formation of locally fuel-rich zones, which enhance NO consumption through NHi mediated pathways. Temperature fields, species distributions, and reaction pathway analysis using a chemical reactor network (CRN) and rate-of-production (ROP) highlight the critical role of intermediate radicals in governing DeNOx chemistry. The results demonstrate that the effectiveness of fuel staging is fundamentally linked to the controlled formation of localized rich regions rather than the specific combustor geometry. These findings provide general design insights for low-NOx ammonia combustion systems based on staged combustion strategies. Novelty and significance statement. Fuel staging has been explored previously for ammonia combustion; however, its practical implementation in pure ammonia requires simultaneous achievement of flame stability, strong NOx reduction, and mitigation of ammonia slip. Title: Overcoming the strength-fatigue life tradeoff: achieving a uniform and stable ultrafine-grained Al alloy through precise regulation of nano-precipitate
Abstract: The deteriorated low-cycle fatigue (LCF) performance is the critical bottleneck restricting the prospective applications of ultrafine-grained (UFG) materials, which is ascribed to the cyclic softening behavior. Title: Cellulose nanofibers regulate nonlinear rheological behavior and structural stability of soy protein isolate emulsion gels for 3D printing
Abstract: Protein-based emulsion gels have emerged as attractive materials for 3D food printing due to their desirable nutritional value and tunable rheological properties. Authors: Widdowson D.; Kurlin V.
Title: Higher-order, generically complete, continuous, and polynomial-time invariants of crystalline materials
Abstract: This paper is at the interface between applied mathematics and numerical computations in materials science. The still open fundamental problem is to quantify the structural novelty of any solid crystalline material (briefly, a periodic crystal) whose atoms can be considered zero-sized points with or without atomic types. Several high-profile papers in Nature reported materials that turned out to be noisy disguises or near-duplicates of already existing structures. We introduce a new mathematical method to quickly and reliably find nearest neighbors of any newly claimed periodic crystal within available databases. The proposed structural invariants are strictly stronger than past descriptors satisfying the same conditions of polynomial-time computability and continuity under noise. Authors: Zhou B.; Shen Y.; Chen M.; Long H.; Wang Z.; Lin W.; Jia M.; Pan X.
Title: Online rapid detection of biomass in avilamycin fermentation process based on near-infrared spectroscopy technology
Abstract: Biomass is one of the key parameters to be monitored during avilamycin fermentation. Currently, periodic sampling is commonly employed for biomass detection, which often entails significant manpower and cost expenditure. Therefore, it is crucial to develop a method capable of real-time, online monitoring of biomass changes during avilamycin fermentation. This study selected wet weight as the biomass measurement indicator during avilamycin fermentation, and employed online near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) technology to perform rapid, non-destructive monitoring of wet weight content throughout the fermentation process. Comparing the models’ performance based on three algorithms, including partial least squares regression (PLSR), principal component regression (PCR) and support vector regression (SVR), it was confirmed that the PLSR model demonstrated optimal performance. After outlier removal, preprocessing method selection, and feature wavelengths screening, the results indicated that the dynamic biomass prediction model constructed using the SG+1st Der-i-PLSR method exhibited the optimal predictive performance. Within the validation set, the prediction set determination coefficient (R2p), root mean square error of prediction (RMSEP), residual predictive deviation (RPD), and standard error of prediction (SEP) were 0.9319, 21.19, 3.351 and 20.98, respectively. For wet weight content ranging from 109.5 to 436.5 g/L, the intuitive metric mean absolute error (MAE) was 16.30 g/L after external validation across five fermentation batches. Title: Fabrication of N/O co-doped porous carbon derived from coal liquefaction pitch for high-performance supercapacitors
Abstract: Transforming coal liquefaction pitch (CLP) from hazardous waste to high-value carbon precursors is a vital research avenue toward efficient utilization of coal. Here, a synergistic activation strategy is proposed, in which C2H10N6·H2CO3 is employed as the nitrogen source and couple with KCl to assist HCOOK activation, enabling the fabrication of N/O co-doped porous carbon from CLP. Systematic studies were executed to elucidate the influence of the nitrogen source and activator on the structural properties and electrochemical performance of the as-prepared porous carbon materials. The results indicate that synergistic effects originating from the pyrolysis interaction of C2H10N6·H2CO3 and HCOOK, the templating function of KCl, and the eutectic melting behavior of the mixed salts collectively facilitate the formation of a three-dimensional thin-walled honeycomb structure. Concurrently, N/O co-doping enhances interfacial reaction kinetics through interfacial activation and charge-transfer modulation. These multiscale cooperative effects ultimately enable the formation of a micropore-dominated porous architecture with small mesoporous contributions. This architecture maintains a high surface area while facilitating ion transport, thereby delivering superior electrochemical performance. The optimized NPC-2-2 sample achieves an ultrahigh specific surface area of 2259.69 m2/g, a microporosity of 86.54 %. Electrochemical measurements further reveal that NPC-2–2 delivers promising electrochemical energy storage performance and remarkable cycling stability, achieving a specific capacitance of 314.5F/g at 0.5 A/g, with a capacitance retention of 89.27 % after 10,000 cycles. Title: Enhancing CO2-to-methanol conversion via interfacial engineering in CuZnCeOx/Cu-foam catalyst
Abstract: Cu-based catalysts are promising for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol, but their activity and stability are often limited by Cu sintering, insufficient interfacial interactions, and inefficient heat transfer. Herein, a novel CuZnCeOx/Cu-foam catalyst was developed by growing Cu(OH)2 nanowires on Cu foam, followed by hydrothermal deposition of active species. The Cu foam provided an interconnected conductive framework for heat and mass transfer, while the nanowire layer increased the surface roughness and provided a nanostructured surface favorable for the deposition of active oxides. Furthermore, the Cu-Zn-Ce synergy regulated the catalytic interface: Cu species acted as hydrogenation sites, while Zn tuned the electronic structure of Cu and Ce introduced oxygen-vacancy-related defects to enhance CO2 adsorption and activation. Benefiting from the stable structure, improved reducibility, enriched Cu0/Cu+ sites, and abundant oxygen vacancies, CuZnCeOx/Cu-foam achieved 20.8% CO2 conversion, 76.4% methanol selectivity, and a methanol space–time yield of 326.9 mgMeOH·g−1·h−1 at 250 °C and 3 MPa, with stable operation for 120 h. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Low-load purification-combustion of high-alkali coal: Operational stability and ash deposition regimes
Abstract: The massive integration of intermittent renewable energy necessitates deep peak shaving in coal-fired power units, where stable low-load operation and ash management of high-alkali coals (HAC) remain critical bottlenecks. This study systematically investigates the purification conversion, emission characteristics, and ash deposition mechanisms of HAC across a 39 %-57 % load range on a self-constructed 200 kW purification-combustion (PC) pilot platform. Results demonstrate that the PC system achieves robust continuous operation under low-load conditions. The sequential medium-temperature activation and high-temperature reduction processes effectively reform HAC into a high-quality gaseous fuel; specifically, CO and H2 concentrations are enriched to 13.90 %-15.09 % and 4.91 %-6.12 %, respectively, yielding a lower heating value of 2.28–2.56 MJ/Nm3. Raman spectroscopy reveals a mechanistic structural activation of coal char, characterized by a decreased I G/ I All and an increased I D1/ I G, which signifies the proliferation of defect-rich, highly reactive carbon sites essential for low-load stability. Front-end liquid slag tapping remains highly effective at low loads with a mean capture rate of 47.65 %, successfully decoupling organic gasification from inorganic ash migration. In the subsequent gentle combustion unit, a combustion efficiency of 97.22 %-99.63 % is achieved with minimal NO x emissions. Differentiated ash deposition pathways are identified along the combustion path: the high-temperature zone (DP1) is dominated by refractory aluminosilicates with flow temperatures of 1352–1357 ℃, whereas the low-temperature zone (DP4) exhibits significant Ca-Na-S enrichment. The resulting FT at DP4 drops to 1175 ℃ at 39 % load, triggering a transition toward sulfate-type fouling. Title: Thermo-responsive adipose tissue mimetics stabilized by protein fibril-sodium alginate complex and enhanced by glycerolysis lipids
Abstract: Plant-based fat mimetics are increasingly needed as healthier and sustainable alternatives to animal fats. However, current emulsion gels are inherently limited in their capacity to replicate the thermal behavior of animal adipose tissue. In this study, pea protein fibril (PPF) and sodium alginate (SA) complexes were investigated for their potential to fabricate adipose tissue mimetics enhanced by glycerolized palm olein (PO). The PPF–SA complexes at mass ratios of 10:3 exhibited superior interfacial activity and a higher thermal degradation temperature compared to non-fibrillated complex. Cryo-scanning electron microscopy revealed that the PPF–SA complex coexisted around droplets forming an extracellular matrix-like network and providing thermal-responsive elasticity properties. Optimization of the oil/water ratio and Ca2+ concentration endowed the emulsion with a robust network architecture. The glycerolysis lipids provided thermal softening behavior, in which a higher monoacylglycerol (MAG) content effectively reduced interfacial tension and emulsion droplet size. The reduction consequently increased the available cross-linking sites within the PPF-SA network and significantly enhanced the oil binding capacity and freeze-thaw stability. Authors: Wu Y.; He Z.; Wang S.
Title: Carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS): From technology advances to carbon neutrality pathways in energy and industrial sectors
Abstract: Carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) is critical for hard-to-abate sectors including steel, cement, chemicals, and power generation. This review systematically synthesizes recent advances across the full CCUS chain, covering emerging electrochemical and membrane-based direct air capture (DAC), AI-enhanced monitoring, verification, and risk management with digital twins, and synergistic coupling with green hydrogen and power-to-liquid synthetic fuels. Mature capture technologies and utilization pathways are assessed alongside geological storage in saline aquifers, depleted oil and gas reservoirs, and coal seams. Operational data from million-tonne demonstration projects are distilled to bridge the gap between laboratory innovation and industrial implementation. The International Energy Agency (IEA) projects CCUS playing a key role in global emissions reductions by 2050, while the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) emphasizes its critical role in ambitious climate stabilization pathways. A conceptual system integration framework is proposed to clarify the distinct roles of CCUS in energy conversion versus industrial production. Despite persistent challenges, including high costs, energy penalties, infrastructure deficits, and regulatory gaps, future directions prioritize low-energy materials, AI-driven optimization, industrial clustering, cross-border networks, and policy incentives. Through innovation and cooperation, CCUS is transitioning from demonstration to commercial-scale deployment to support global climate goals. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Proteins in chickpea aquafaba: what is their role in foaming properties?
Abstract: Chickpea aquafaba has attracted increasing interest as a plant-based foaming agent for food applications. Given its complex composition, which includes proteins and low-molecular-weight surfactants such as saponins, this study aimed to elucidate the role of chickpea proteins in its foaming properties. To this end, four chickpea-derived samples were investigated: (i) aquafaba (AQ), (ii) aquafaba protein concentrate (CAQ), (iii) chickpea protein concentrate (CPC), and (iv) the acidic supernatant obtained during CPC production (SP). The CPC, SP, and AQ samples exhibited distinct protein profiles. In turn, the ultrafiltration process used to obtain CAQ increased the protein content by 68% and reduced the saponin content by 56% compared with AQ. Although the protein profile was preserved, the removal of low-molecular-weight compounds induced changes in protein secondary structure, reduced protein surface hydrophobicity, and increased protein size in CAQ relative to AQ. AQ and CAQ exhibited similarly high foaming capacities (approximately 85%), followed by SP (68%) and CPC (57%). However, AQ and SP displayed superior foam stabilities, whereas foams stabilized by CPC and CAQ collapsed within a few minutes. Low-molecular-weight proteins (<25 kDa) in AQ and CAQ seemed to play an important role in air entrapment, whereas higher-molecular-weight proteins adsorbed at the air–water interface were critical for foam stability. Title: Experimental study on the effect of ullage height and tank spacing on the ignition of adjacent tanks
Abstract: Preventing fire spread between tanks is essential for fuel storage facilities. Therefore, ignition behavior of tank fires with different ullage heights and tank spacings was studied, focusing on the ignition process, ignition mechanism and radiative heat transfer. A series of experiments with n-heptane as fuel was performed with two 0.4 m diameter tanks (Tank I: burning source; Tank II: ignition target) over seven tank spacings (d = 0.2 D -0.8 D) and four ullage heights (H = 0 D -0.3 D). The ignition time increased from 2 s to 597 s as the tank spacing increased from 0.2 D to 0.7 D (H = 0) and from 2 s to 455 s as the ullage height increased from 0 D to 0.2 D (d = 0.2 D). Numerical simulations using fire dynamic simulation confirmed that, near the adjacent tank upper rim, greater tank spacing suppressed flame-driven air entrainment and higher ullage height limited the fuel vapor concentrations. These results are supported by calculations showing that the view factor decreased with increasing tank spacing and ullage height. Moreover, ullage height enhances a “blocking effect” and contracts the effective flame radiation region and the effective radiation reception region, thus lowering radiative heat flux. Based on the dimensionless analysis, the quantitative relationships between the ullage height, tank spacing, tank diameter and ignition time were analyzed, and a prediction model for the ignition time of the tanks was proposed. These findings offer insights into safer design of tank spacings and provide guidance for storage tank protection strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Study on coalbed methane desorption induced by water infiltration in closed mines
Abstract: Water intrusion caused by groundwater rebound after mine closure exerts a significant influence on the gas release behavior of residual coal. To reveal the competitive desorption mechanism of adsorbed methane driven by water displacement and provide theoretical support for residual gas resource evaluation in closed mines, experimental investigations on methane desorption of typical anthracite under natural water intrusion conditions are carried out in this study. Relying on a self-developed experimental system, three initial adsorption pressures (0.74 MPa, 1.5 MPa and 2.5 MPa), four gradient water immersion conditions (water contents of 3 %, 5 %, 7 % and 9 %), and a continuous saturated water supply condition with a water content of 17 % were designed. Gradient water immersion tests ranging from 3 % to 9 % water content were carried out under 1.5 MPa and 2.5 MPa, while the 0.74 MPa condition was only used for comparative analysis of pressure responses under saturated water supply. The Helmholtz free energy is adopted to quantitatively analyze the thermodynamic mechanism of gas desorption induced by water intrusion, and an improved evaluation method for residual gas in goafs is established based on laboratory experimental parameters. The experimental results show that water infiltration can promote methane desorption from residual coal via displacement, and the desorption capacity generally increases with rising water content. As the water content increases from 3 % to 9 %, the cumulative methane desorption volume rises from 1.655 mL/g to 3.806 mL/g under 1.5 MPa, and increases from 1.823 mL/g to 4.315 mL/g under 2.5 MPa. The corresponding desorption increment ratios range from 10.65 % to 24.51 % and 9.45 % to 22.36 %, respectively. Continuous saturated water supply yields a better gas release performance than limited gradient water immersion. Thermodynamic calculations verify that methane desorption induced by water displacement is a spontaneous process, and the system free energy change varies from −3.05 J to −9.08 J under all test conditions. In double-logarithmic coordinates, the whole methane desorption process presents three evolutionary stages: initial rapid wetting, transitional attenuation, and diffusion-controlled stable stage. As the coal matrix gradually approaches saturation, the capillary effect produces retardation and imposes a certain inhibitory effect on methane diffusion. In this study, the experimentally obtained desorption increment ratio and structural correction coefficient are introduced to optimize the conventional goaf gas evaluation model, and an estimation method for residual gas resources considering the water-promoted desorption effect is established. This method addresses the deficiency of traditional models that ignore additional methane desorption triggered by water displacement, and can provide experimental evidence and theoretical reference for residual gas resource evaluation of residual coal in closed mines. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Interfacial engineering of ionic liquid functionalized g-C3N4/GO nanocomposite toward high-performance supercapacitors

The successful functionalization and nanocomposite formation were verified by complementary structural and surface analysis methods such as (XRD), (FTIR), (SEM), (EDS), (XPS), (BET), and (TGA). Title: Carbonation and CO2 sequestration potential of steelmaking slag in CO2-rich aqueous system
Abstract: Steelmaking slag is produced in large volumes and requires stabilization before broad, value-added reuse. Carbonation reactant and phase evolution were characterized by XRD, SEM-EDS, and TGA. CaCO3 formation was consistently confirmed after reaction, and carbonate formation showed systematic dependence on slag type, particle size, and carbonate loading, with the maximum TGA-derived CaCO3-equivalent formation reaching 30.59 wt% for KRS_d4_0.5. Additional experiments showed that agitation accelerated TIC depletion, sulfate/bisulfate addition did not measurably suppress TIC depletion under carbonate-excess conditions, and acetic-acid-assisted slurry pretreatment enhanced carbonate formation by increasing Ca availability. The proposed solvent-based approach was further benchmarked against CO2-pressurized carbonation reported for the same steel slag series. Title: A dual-perspective two-stage robust minimum cost consensus modeling for trust-based large-scale group decision making
Abstract: The integration of rapidly developing social networks into large-scale group decision-making has attracted growing attention, particularly regarding consensus-reaching process costs. Traditional minimum cost consensus models (MCCMs) focus primarily on minimizing total consensus cost, often implicitly assuming unconditional acceptance of opinion adjustments by decision makers (DMs) and neglecting fairness in adjustment allocation. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a dual-perspective two-stage robust MCCM. From the DMs’ perspective, fair opinion adjustment schemes are derived via cooperative game theory in the first stage. From the moderator’s perspective, the second stage determines the optimal consensus cost based on the first stage’s adjustment benchmarks, while accounting for heterogeneous risk preferences shaped by DMs’ structural positions in the trust-based network. A Gini index-based fairness measure is further introduced to ensure the second stage’s fairness level is no lower than that of the first stage. Moreover, a hybrid weighting scheme and an improved community detection algorithm are developed to jointly capture opinion deviation and trust relationships in social networks. To address uncertainty in unit adjustment costs, both classical and data-driven robust optimization approaches are incorporated, enabling the proposed framework to adapt to diverse decision-making environments. Finally, numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness, robustness, and fairness of the proposed approach. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Deciphering the adaptive rearrangement dynamics of complex Pickering emulsion interface under pH fluctuations via combined experimental and DPD simulation
Abstract: The poor pH stability of zein-based Pickering emulsions (PE), closely associated with the environmental sensitivity of particle-stabilized interfacial films, severely restricts their application in functional foods. The enhanced rearrangement of interfacial components formed a thicker and more flexible interfacial layer (>7.0 σ) with larger thickness fluctuations (7.0-7.6 σ), contributing to the structural stability of CPE under pH perturbation. Title: Programmable nuclease-based biosensors for food safety: Recent advances and perspectives
Abstract: Programmable nucleases are emerging as powerful tools for rapid and sensitive food contaminant detection. This review systematically examines five representative nucleases—Cas9, Cas12, Cas13, Cas14, and CbAgo—with emphasis on their target-recognition mechanisms, signal-transduction pathways, amplification strategies, and readout formats. The distinct analytical strengths of Cas9, Cas12, Cas13, and Cas14 are compared in terms of specificity, collateral cleavage, multiplexing capability, and suitability for nucleic acid and non-nucleic acid targets. Particular attention is given to Cas14 and CbAgo, two less extensively reviewed nucleases with PAM-independent recognition and promising potential for flexible target selection and multiplex sensing. In addition, recent advances in artificial intelligence and machine vision for fluorescence image processing, digital counting, and multiplex quantification are critically discussed. Finally, current challenges and future priorities are outlined, including one-pot integration, signal amplification, assay standardization, miniaturization, and field deployment. This review provides a comparative framework for developing practical programmable nuclease-based food-safety platforms. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Quantized output feedback control for fuzzy singularly perturbed systems subject to saturation constraints
Abstract: The focus of this paper is the design of quantized output feedback control for continuous-time nonlinear singularly perturbed systems under saturation constraints. To capture the nonlinearity, the Takagi–Sugeno (T–S) fuzzy model is adopted to linearly approximate the nonlinear singularly perturbed system. Both sensor saturation and actuator saturation, together with the quantization effects on input and output signals, are taken into account. On this basis, the resulting closed-loop control system is cast as a descriptor-type model, and its stability is investigated. The sufficient conditions are formulated for the determination of controller gains and dynamic quantizer parameters. These conditions ensure both stability and dissipativity of the system. Simulation results from two examples confirm the validity of the designed approach. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Optimal H1 and L2 error estimates for an ESAV-BDF2 finite element method with variable time steps for the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations

Abstract: Achieving optimal L2-norm error estimates for variable-step and linear schemes solving the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations remains a significant theoretical challenge. While recent works have established the suboptimal or partially optimal convergence, a fully rigorous optimal L2 error estimate under general variable time steps has yet to be attained. Authors: Zhang K.; Su H.
Title: Optimal error estimates for a decoupled, fully discrete scheme for the 2D/3D diffuse interface two-phase MHD flows
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: In this paper, we derive optimal error estimates in the L2-norms for a decoupled, fully discrete finite element method (FEM) applied to a two-phase diffuse interface magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) system. To further decouple the velocity and pressure, a pressure-correction strategy is employed. The optimal error estimates are established based on novel Ritz and Stokes quasi-projection techniques. Authors: Luo T.; Zhu X.; Zhu L.; Huang X.; Deng B.; Sun W.
Title: Efficient and robust reduced-order prediction of thermal coupling and fluid flow in cross-flow heat exchangers
Abstract: Cross-flow plate-fin heat exchangers in compact thermal systems require modeling approaches that capture channel-to-channel thermal coupling without incurring prohibitive computational costs during design iterations. To address this, a physics-based reduced-order model (ROM) is formulated from element-wise mass and energy balances. The solid wall and fin domains are represented by a two-dimensional longitudinal-conduction network, with convective terms evaluated using an effective finned surface area to account for finite fin efficiency. The physical interlayer conductance is treated separately from the numerical under-relaxation, which is used solely to stabilize the fixed-point iteration. The formulation accepts independent, prescribed mass-flow rates for individual channels and explicitly couples neighboring elements through the solid matrix. Numerical verification against a conjugate heat-transfer finite-element model gives a maximum wall-temperature deviation of 2.1 K. The selected 100×100 ROM grid requires 2.4597 s, compared with 354 s for the reference model, corresponding to a case-specific speed-up of approximately 144. Furthermore, comparison with published offset-strip-fin experiments yields mean absolute percentage errors of 1.53% for heat duty and 7.55% for pressure drop. Ultimately, these results confirm that the ROM is a highly effective tool for the rapid assessment of longitudinal conduction, prescribed channel-flow nonuniformity, and boundary heat leakage. Authors: Liu H.; Sun C.; Wu X.; Liu G.; Yu B.; Kang X.; Li Z.; Li Z.; Tao H.; Cui B.
Title: Moist-heat induced interfacial co-assembly of κ-carrageenan and soy lecithin: A chemical-crosslinker-free paradigm for physically stable Pickering emulsion
Abstract: Pickering emulsions stabilized by biopolymer-based particles have attracted considerable interest, yet fabricating eco-friendly stabilizers with simplified processes remains challenging. This study developed lipid-based particles via moist-heat treatment, a one-step preparation strategy without chemical crosslinkers, using κ-carrageenan (KC) and soy lecithin (SL) as a synergistic interfacial system. SL gradually enriches at the lipid-based particle interface and transforms the surface into a more hydrophobic structure, mainly through non-covalent interactions. The lipid-based particles exhibit good cooperative assembly behavior (minimum particle size: approximately 279.43 nm). The corresponding microgels show improved wettability for Pickering stabilization (maximum contact angle: 86.1°). Title: Lead-free X-ray shielding of multilayers composite white teak wood/BaCO3/PVA: experimental validation and Phy-X simulations
Abstract: The development of lightweight, environmentally friendly X-ray shielding materials is essential for medical and industrial applications. This study prepared and evaluated multilayer composites made from white teak wood powder, barium carbonate (BaCO3), and polyvynil alcohol (PVA) with wood contents of 90%, 80%, and 70% in single-, two-, and three-layer configurations. Authors: Wang J.; Liu K.; Xiang L.; Zhang W.; Qian T.; Lu W.
Title: Who fights best? Discovering winning personality pairings for LLM debate agents
Abstract: Multi-agent debate (MAD) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for enhancing the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs). However, most MAD systems employ personality-neutral agents and overlook the role of personality, which has been shown in psychology and behavioral science to influence reasoning styles and collaborative problem-solving. In this study, we introduce MBTI-DB, a debate framework for systematically studying the impact of personality in MAD. We design 16 distinct personality profiles and inject them into debates in a modular manner. Through experiments across four LLM families and 700 factual questions, we demonstrate that incorporating personality induces systematic and measurable accuracy shifts. Further analysis reveals that lexical density, personality-question similarity, and prompt perplexity influence these accuracy variations. We evaluate personality-pair selection strategies and find that retrospectively selecting the best-performing pair for each question yields significant gains as an oracle upper bound. However, automatically identifying the best configuration remains challenging with substantial cross-model variation, suggesting that while personality diversity offers meaningful performance benefits, its effects are complex and context-dependent. Authors: Yang Y.; Li G.; Qu S.; Yao Y.; Xu C.
Title: A molecular dynamics study of surface and subsurface damage mechanisms in 4H-SiC with different crystal orientations
Abstract: As a premier third-generation wide-bandgap semiconductor, 4H-SiC holds immense potential for high-temperature, high-frequency, and high-power electronic applications. However, its pronounced mechanical anisotropy presents substantial challenges for ultra-precision machining. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were employed to investigate the atomic-scale anisotropic deformation and damage mechanisms of 4H-SiC. Single-abrasive scratching models were constructed for the Si-face (0001) and C-face (000−1) along the [1−100], [10−10], [11−20], and [2−1−10] crystallographic directions. The coupled effects of crystal face and scratching direction were analyzed in terms of scratching forces, surface morphology, stress distribution, dislocation evolution, and subsurface damage. The [11−20] direction exhibited the highest average normal force on both crystal faces, reaching 3259.3 ± 111.5 nN on the Si-face and 3331.7 ± 88.7 nN on the C-face. The tangential response showed stronger orientation dependence in its fluctuation characteristics than in its mean magnitude. The [11−20] and [2−1−10] directions also exhibited stronger subsurface stress penetration and tended to produce longer and narrower damaged regions. On the Si-face, the maximum subsurface damage depth ranged from 43.4 Å along [1−100] to 44.9 Å along [2−1−10]. Compared with the Si-face, the C-face exhibited higher normal scratching resistance, generally higher stress levels, more active dislocation development, and deeper subsurface damage. The Si-face [1−100] combination is preferable for reducing subsurface damage under the present simulation conditions. The findings provide atomic-scale mechanistic insight for subsequent experimental studies and low-damage machining strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
