Authors: Wan Z.; Yu C.; Zhang T.; Xu K.; Shen K.; Zhang Y.
Title: Emerging valorization pathways for coal fly ash: carbon capture, strategic element recovery, and polymer composites
Abstract: Coal fly ash (CFA), a massive by-product of coal-fired power generation, poses significant environmental and health risks if improperly managed. Conventional bulk utilization of CFA in construction, environmental remediation, and agriculture is largely confined to relatively low-value-density sectors and is subject to inherent limitations. This review summarizes the physicochemical properties of CFA and discusses both conventional and emerging utilization pathways, with particular emphasis on three potential high-value routes: CFA-derived materials for CO2 capture, selective recovery of strategic elements, particularly lithium, gallium, and rare earth elements (REEs), and CFA-based polymer composites. Key mechanisms, performance characteristics, and persistent challenges such as limited long-term stability, low extraction efficiency, and poor interfacial compatibility, are discussed. Comparative considerations of technological maturity, scalability, economic feasibility, and environmental implications are further highlighted based on available literature evidence. Future development requires improved material design, scalable processing strategies, and comprehensive life-cycle and techno-economic assessments to facilitate the transition of CFA from a waste by-product to a valuable resource for sustainable technologies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Liu Y.; Xiao M.
Title: A refined kernel for d-Hitting Set
Source title: Journal of Computer and System Sciences
Abstract: The d-HITTING SET problem is a fundamental problem in parameterized complexity, which asks whether a given hypergraph contains a vertex subset S of size at most k that intersects every hyperedge (i.e., S∩e≠∅ for each hyperedge e). The best known kernel for this problem, established by Abu-Khzam (JCSS 2010), has (2d−1)kd−1+k vertices. This result has been very widely used in the literature as many problems can be modeled as a special d-HITTING SET problem. In this work, we present a refinement to this result by employing linear programming techniques to construct crown decompositions in hypergraphs. This approach yields a slight but notable improvement, reducing the size to (2d−2)kd−1+k vertices. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: The mollification regularization method for a general sideways parabolic equation

Abstract: In this study, we explore a mollification regularization approach for solving the Cauchy problem associated with a general sideways parabolic equation. By applying convolution with the measured data and the Dirichlet kernel, the ill-posed problem is reformulated into a well-posed one. Both a priori and a posteriori parameter selection methods are employed to ensure the construction of convergent estimates. Authors: Cao R.; Wu Y.; Li X.; Yu L.; Lu X.
Title: Enhancing ammonia reactivity and accelerating autoignition via off-site nanosecond pulsed discharge: strategy and mechanism
Abstract: Ammonia’s low reactivity and long ignition delay time (IDT) hinder its use in compression-ignition (CI) engines. This study proposes an off-site nanosecond pulsed discharge (NPD) pretreatment strategy to enhance ammonia autoignition through plasma-induced reforming. Reaction-path and species-removal analyses identify H2 as the dominant long-lived product responsible for ignition enhancement, whereas the combined contributions of NO, HNO, H2O2, and N2H4 are comparatively limited. Under isothermal pretreatment, decreasing pressure and increasing the initial NH3 fraction favor H2 formation. Under isothermal pretreatment of pure NH3 at an EF of 5%, the H2 production reaches approximately 3.4%. For the subsequent CI calculation at 1000 K, 20 bar, and ϕ CI = 1.0, the IDT is reduced to approximately 13.9% of the untreated value, corresponding to IDT 0/ IDT = 7.2. Chemical-enthalpy analysis further reveals distinct energy-redistribution characteristics: NH3/air discharge exhibits a negative chemical enthalpy change because of plasma-induced oxidation, whereas pure-NH3 discharge produces a positive chemical enthalpy change, indicating that part of the deposited electrical energy is retained in the reformate as H2. Under the idealized adiabatic assumption, discharge-stage heating enhances neutral-radical pathways and the maximum IDT0/IDT reaches 22. Authors: Wang Q.; Niu W.; Zheng H.; Li W.; Zhang W.; Zhang A.
Title: Influence mechanism of particle friction characteristics on seepage-induced erosion behavior of gap-graded granular systems based on CFD–DEM simulation
Abstract: To investigate the influence of interparticle friction on the seepage erosion process, a numerical model of seepage erosion in a gap-graded granular system was established using a coupled computational fluid dynamics and discrete element method (CFD–DEM). The macroscopic and microscopic responses of seepage erosion under different interparticle friction conditions were investigated, including fine-particle mass loss, particle migration characteristics, and the evolution of contact force chains. The results show that increasing the hydraulic gradient accelerates fine-particle migration and intensifies internal erosion, while also making the influence of interparticle friction on the erosion process more pronounced. Lower interparticle friction facilitates particle rolling, sliding, and detachment, thereby promoting fine-particle migration and accelerating the erosion process. In contrast, higher interparticle friction enhances the mechanical constraints between particles and promotes the formation of strong contact force chain networks, thereby inhibiting fine-particle migration and the development of preferential seepage channels. At intermediate friction coefficients, the migration behavior of fine particles becomes more complex and less predictable. © 2026

Title: A multi-interval Chebyshev collocation method for Fredholm delay integral equations
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: In this paper, a multi-interval Chebyshev spectral collocation method is formulated for addressing Fredholm delay integral equations. We begin by constructing a bidirectional locking grid for the solution domain, which significantly alleviates the mutual interference between subintervals caused by the time-delay terms, and provides a solid groundwork for both algorithm execution and error analysis. We then introduce a multi-interval Chebyshev collocation scheme for solving Fredholm delay integral equations, along with a detailed algorithm design that ensures high-precision and stable approximations. Authors: Zhang J.; Wang K.
Title: BCDQ-TCLIF: A bidirectionally coupled dendritic quadratic two-compartment LIF neuron model for time-series forecasting
Abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs), owing to their event-driven and spatiotemporally sparse nature, provide a biologically inspired paradigm for time series forecasting. However, conventional Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) neurons are constrained by their state-independent linear dynamics, restricting their ability to model nonlinear temporal dependencies. To address this issue, we propose a bidirectionally coupled dendritic quadratic two-compartment LIF neuron (BCDQ-TCLIF) inspired by biological neuronal structures. The proposed neuron consists of coupled dendritic and somatic compartments, where the dendritic compartment incorporates a quadratic integration mechanism that enables state-dependent local subthreshold nonlinear dynamics of the membrane potential, thereby enhancing temporal dependency modeling, while a binary spike-union mechanism with shared cross-compartment reset coordinates spike generation across the two compartments to improve temporal information transmission. Experimental results show that, although BCDQ-TCLIF introduces a modest increase in neuronal complexity over conventional LIF neurons, it effectively suppresses redundant spikes, yielding a lower network-level theoretical energy estimate under the adopted operation-count model. It also achieves favorable forecasting performance across the evaluated architectures and time-series datasets, with an average R2 improvement of 5.56% and an average RRSE reduction of 14.96% relative to the corresponding LIF-based models, demonstrating its capacity to capture complex temporal dependencies in time-series forecasting. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Song Y.; Yu T.; Guo Y.; Liu D.
Title: Oxygen vacancy tungsten oxide modified carbon cloth anode for enhancing microbial fuel cell performance

Title: On certain forms of transitivities for linear operators

Authors: Peng Y.; Mou J.; Lu Y.; Xu Y.; Lu P.; Gao B.
Title: A novel two-phase thermal-hydraulic-chemical two-scale carbonate matrix acidizing model and effect of CO2
Abstract: During matrix acidizing in carbonate reservoirs, the reaction between acid and rock minerals generates carbon dioxide (supersaturated CO2), resulting to multiphase flow and reducing the effective surface area available for acid-rock reaction. Under typical reservoir conditions, CO2 often exists in a liquid or supercritical state, where temperature and pressure significantly influence its physical properties. However, existing models lack the capability to efficiently and accurately simulate these complex processes. To address this gap, we develop a two-phase thermal-hydraulic-chemical two-scale model that incorporates CO2 generation. The model is solved by sequential iterative solution method for computational efficiency and convergence issues associated with strong non-linearities in fully coupled approaches. The model is validated with existing models and analytical solutions. Simulation results demonstrate that produced CO2 by the reaction leads to wormhole structures with sparser branching, shorter branch lengths, and smaller diameters. CO2 facilitates acid transport to the wormhole tip, improving wormhole propagation efficiency and reducing the pore volume to breakthrough (PVbt). Elevated injection temperatures accelerate reaction rate, further decreasing PVbt and increasing the optimal injection rate. Due to the reaction heat, the temperature around and at the top of the wormhole, as well as the surface reaction rate, are respectively 2–7K higher and increase by 20%–60% compared to those inside the wormhole. However, pressure exerted negligible effects on PVbt. Both PVbt and the optimal injection rate decrease with increasing initial average porosity. A greater horizontal-to-vertical spatial correlation length ratio enhances the directionality of wormholes. PVbt remains stable at low porosity variation coefficients but drops sharply beyond a specific threshold. Title: A Physics-Informed Neural Networks framework for simulating natural convection of Cu–water micropolar nanofluid in a porous enclosure with internal heat generation

Crucially, the impact of porosity on heat transfer is non-monotonic and dependent on the heat generation ratio; increasing porosity enhances heat transfer when fluid-phase heating dominates but reduces it when solid-phase heating prevails. Furthermore, at elevated external Rayleigh numbers, increasing nanoparticle volume fraction leads to a monotonic decrease in heat transfer performance as viscous effects outweigh thermal conductivity enhancements. Title: Hybrid bonding technology for 3D Integration: Fundamentals, challenges, and perspectives
Abstract: As Moore's Law approaches its physical limits, three-dimensional (3D) integration has emerged as a pivotal strategy for sustaining computing performance growth. Title: S-scheme Mg3Al0.5Bi0.5O4.5/EAPbBr3 heterojunction for highly efficient selective oxidation of cyclohexane

Title: Adaptive tribo-structures and multi-scale strengthening drive wear resistance in silicon-modified refractory high-entropy alloys

Title: A semi-analytical formulation for the bending theory of composite conical shells via high-order finite differences: Application to flanged structures

The formulation is subsequently extended to flanged composite conical shells by analytically modeling the flanges as orthotropic annular plates and disks. Title: A comprehensive review on ammonia-hydrogen synergistic combustion technology for engine applications: a utopia or still a challenge?
Abstract: Amid the global pursuit of carbon neutrality and energy transition, the decarbonization of engines has become an inevitable trend. Ammonia, featuring zero-carbon content and high hydrogen density, offers advantages such as easy storage and transport, a mature industrial chain and low cost, making it a promising alternative fuel for carbon–neutral energy systems. However, the inert combustion of pure ammonia severely limits its direct application in engines. Given the physicochemical differences between hydrogen and ammonia, blending highly reactive hydrogen can create novel combustion schemes for ammonia-hydrogen synergistic fuels. Notably, a critical gap remains between current fundamental reaction kinetics of ammonia-hydrogen systems and their engineering application in macro-scale engines. Therefore, this paper systemically reviews the latest technological advancements in ammonia-hydrogen synergistic fuels for internal combustion power systems, focusing on reaction kinetic mechanisms, mixture formation, advanced combustion mode adaptability, and emission generation and control strategies. In engineering applications, the realization of online hydrogen production through vehicle-mounted catalytic cracking is essential for establishing a single-fuel ammonia power system. New combustion methods, such as jet ignition and spark-assisted compression ignition, show great promise in improving the efficiency of ammonia-hydrogen combustion and reducing nitrogen-based emissions. However, ammonia-hydrogen combustion systems still face several challenges, including incomplete combustion mechanisms, unreliable materials in the injection and cracking systems, low catalytic cracking efficiency and the difficulty of controlling nitrogen-based emissions. In summary, ammonia-hydrogen synergistic combustion is a vital technical approach to achieving zero-carbon combustion in engines, but its commercial application necessitates continuous technological innovation and development. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Huang Z.
Title: Simple harmonic oscillation of strut injector on the combustor performance and flame dynamics in a model supersonic combustor
Abstract: The strut injector in a model supersonic combustor is horizontally and periodically oscillated in a simple harmonic mode. Its influences on the combustor performance and flame dynamics are studied numerically with different oscillation amplitudes and frequencies. The overall combustor performance including total thrust, total heat release rate, total pressure recovery coefficient, and final combustion efficiency (ηe) is finitely affected by strut oscillation amplitude. The overall combustor performance except ηe is improved when the strut locates at its left end and decreased near the right end. However, ηe is high near the right end. The periodical shedding of a bow shock at the leading edge of the strut becomes more pronounced with increased oscillation amplitude. The central subsonic flow zones and high temperature combustion regions are discontinuous and highly turbulent compared with the cases with a stationary strut. At low oscillation frequency, the performance parameters except ηe are stable and insensitive to the variations of strut location and oscillation period. However, ηe is dispersed at all strut locations, in all oscillation periods. At high oscillation frequency, the combustor performance except ηe is comparable with that in the low frequency cases whilst ηe is the highest. A leading bow shock is first formed and then detached periodically at the leading edge of the strut. The subsonic flow regions and the high temperature flame regions are spatially isolated, which undergo a new combustion mode different from previous observations with stationary strut. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Semi-dynamic in vitro digestion of alternative proteins: structural insights and peptidomics
Abstract: This study investigates the in vitro digestive fate of various alternative plant proteins. Findings suggest that protein secondary structure contributed to differences in the extent of digestion; the higher content of α-helix correlated with the high digestibility of SPI, PPI and PoPI, while higher proportions of β-sheet correlated with lower digestibility of HPI. Peptidomics analysis revealed that the SpPC released the highest number of peptides whilst HPI produced fewest peptides after gastrointestinal digestion. Title: Influence of stress environment on displacement-adsorption behavior during enhanced coalbed methane recovery: Insights from CT characterization of coal Pore-Fracture structures
Abstract: Inefficient methane drainage in deep, low-permeability coal seams limits mine safety and coalbed methane recovery. N2 injection can enhance CH4 desorption through competitive adsorption and pressure-driven displacement, but its efficiency under continuously evolving mining-induced stress remains unclear. In this study, a dynamic stress path was reconstructed from field stress monitoring, and N2 displacement experiments were conducted under in-situ, transition, peak, and dynamic stress conditions. Micro-CT scanning was used to quantify pore-fracture morphology and pore-throat connectivity during dynamic loading and displacement. After 12 injection-production cycles, residual CH4 concentration increased from 4.1 % under in-situ stress to 15.1 % under peak stress, indicating that high stress strongly restricts gas migration. Under the dynamic stress path, the first three low-stress cycles contributed 60.2 % of total CH4 production, confirming that the low-stress stage dominates effective recovery. However, as stress increased, the replacement ratio continuously decreased, indicating reduced CH4 production per unit N2 consumption. CT results showed that N2 injection under in-situ stress increased porosity from 0.11111 to 0.12212 and average throat diameter from 0.1281 to 0.1859 μm, whereas peak stress reduced porosity to 0.07020 and decreased pore and throat numbers to 339 and 809, respectively. Quantitative analysis showed that the replacement ratio fell by 91.7 % from cycles 1–3 to cycles 4–8, while peak stress increased mean pathway tortuosity to 1.1889. Authors: Di Y.; Qiu K.; Zou Y.; Chen C.; Yang J.
Title: Recent advances in ammonia decomposition for hydrogen production: From multiple catalytic pathways to Ru-based thermocatalysts
Abstract: Ammonia is a practical hydrogen carrier because of its high hydrogen density, mature storage and transport network, and ability to release hydrogen without direct COx formation during decomposition. However, the life-cycle carbon intensity of the ammonia-to-hydrogen pathway depends on the ammonia-production route and the energy sources used for hydrogen recovery. Several routes have been developed to recover hydrogen from ammonia, including thermocatalytic, photocatalytic, plasma-assisted, and electrochemical processes. Their operating principles are different, but the overall performance is often controlled by the same surface events: N–H bond cleavage, coupling of adsorbed nitrogen atoms, and the release of N2. Accordingly, research is shifting from isolated catalytic paradigms toward cooperative and multimodal strategies, while thermocatalysis remains the mechanistic and structural basis for most integrated systems. This review summarizes recent advances in ammonia decomposition for hydrogen production, focusing on Ru-based thermocatalysts. From a structure–electronic–kinetic perspective, bimetallic engineering, support/interface regulation, defect engineering, and electronic promotion are discussed in relation to Ru electronic structure, metal–support interactions, reaction kinetics, and catalyst stability. Future directions for low-Ru-loading, durable, and reactor-compatible ammonia-to-hydrogen catalysts are also highlighted. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhu F.
Title: Properties, modifications and uses of kudzu starch
Abstract: Kudzu starch from Pueraria spp. is a heterogeneous specialty starch whose reported functionality depends on taxon and accession, compositional purity, analytical protocol, processing history, and food-matrix context. This review evaluates isolation, multiscale structure, physicochemical properties, digestibility, modifications, and applications using a source-structure-processing-function-application framework. Across the available studies, kudzu starch is frequently, but not uniformly, associated with relatively small granules, C-type or mixed crystallinity, moderate amylose content, restrained swelling, comparatively high pasting temperature, and gel-forming capacity. Reported resistant-starch values are not directly comparable across assays or sample states. Modification can improve instant hydration, promote reassociation into enzyme-resistant domains, reinforce gels, or introduce interfacial activity; however, evidence ranges from ingredient-level measurements to formulated-food prototypes and animal studies. The current literature thus supports kudzu starch as a potentially designable, legume-like specialty ingredient, but does not yet establish broad superiority over commodity starches. Priorities are matched-method benchmarking, explicit distinction between isolated starch and root powder, sensory and shelf-life validation, standardized digestibility testing, human studies, and scale-up assessment. © 2026 The Author. Title: Thermochemical recycling of photovoltaic polymer waste: coupled equilibrium and computational fluid dynamics analysis of ethylene-vinyl acetate–backsheet co-gasification
Abstract: End-of-life crystalline silicon photovoltaic (PV) modules are generating a growing stream of polymeric waste dominated by ethylene–vinyl acetate (EVA) encapsulant and fluoropolymer-based backsheet. These materials coexist within the module and are therefore unavoidably co-processed during recycling, yet whose joint thermochemical behavior, and the implications of backsheet-derived fluorine and gasification performance, have not previously been characterised across coupled experimental, thermodynamic, and reactor-scale modelling frameworks. This study presents an experimental characterization and parallel equilibrium-CFD modelling framework to evaluate the co-gasification potential of EVA–backsheet blends recovered from end-of-life PV modules. TGA at multiple heating rates was performed on neat EVA, neat backsheet, and three binary blends (60:40, 40:60, 25:75 by mass) to establish devolatilization behavior and Coats–Redfern kinetic parameters; a Gibbs-energy-minimisation equilibrium model was used to map syngas composition and cold gas efficiency (CGE) across gasification temperatures (750–1923 K) and blend compositions; and the optimal blend was subjected to three-dimensional Euler–Lagrange CFD simulation of an oxygen-blown entrained-flow gasifier incorporating finite-rate homogeneous and heterogeneous chemistry. EVA was found to undergo two-stage devolatilization between 300 and 520 °C with negligible char ('10 wt%), while the PVF/PET backsheet decomposes in a single stage at 440–460 °C, retaining 10–15 wt% char; under co-heating, hydrogen-rich EVA volatiles lower the backsheet onset by 80–100 °C, reducing blend char to ∼ 3 wt%. The 60:40 EVA–backsheet blend achieved the highest equilibrium performance, with a CGE of 69.4% at 1300 °C and syngas mole fractions of H2 (0.36) and CO (0.40); the corresponding CFD simulation predicted a CGE of 41.4%, approximately 28 percentage points lower, attributable to finite residence time and non-uniform oxygen distribution. Title: Plasmon-enhanced photocatalytic selective hydrogenation of phenylacetylene over melamine-modified Ni/TiO2 catalyst
Abstract: Engineering of surfaces and interfaces of heterogeneous metal catalysts is both useful and important to make superior the selectivity of fine chemicals. Herein, melamine-modified Ni-based catalysts exhibit ultrahigh selectivity for the semi-hydrogenation of alkynes and possess outstanding air stability. Our experimental characterizations reveal that strong interfacial interactions between Ni nanoparticles and melamine molecules dramatically alter the interfacial structure of Ni catalysts. The melamine coating markedly weakens the adsorption of styrene on Ni nanoparticles, which is the core origin of the improved selectivity. Moreover, visible light irradiation promotes H2 activation over Ni nanoparticles, thus accelerating the overall reaction rate. This strategy offers a simple and environmentally friendly method for producing practical catalysts. Title: Interfacial engineering of carbonyl iron/c-MWCNT/hydroxyapatite composite particles for balancing tribological and magnetorheological properties of magnetorheological fluids
Abstract: The material removal capability of magnetorheological fluids (MRFs) is governed by the coupled effects of interfacial tribological behavior and field-induced rheological performance. However, the underlying competition and balance mechanisms between these two factors have not yet been systematically clarified. The simulation results demonstrated that the c-MWCNTs/HAP ratio significantly regulated the microstructural evolution of MRFs. When the mass ratio of c-MWCNTs/HAP was optimized at 1.8/2.5, the magnetic field-induced oriented structures exhibited enhanced structural uniformity and shear resistance, whereas excessive c-MWCNTs promoted the formation of aggregates and highly viscous network structures. Consequently, the CH-1.8/2.5 MRF achieved high sedimentation stability while maintaining relatively high shear stress and dynamic moduli. Tribological investigations revealed that HAP particles primarily contributed to the abrasive grinding action, whereas c-MWCNTs regulated interparticle connectivity through bridging effects and increased the effective contact area at the friction interface, thereby synergistically regulating the interfacial tribological behavior of MRFs. During friction, the dynamic reconstruction of field-induced oriented structures facilitated the continuous transport of HAP and c-MWCNTs toward the friction interface, generating a dynamic tribological mechanism involving the synergistic effects of abrasive wear, rolling friction, and structural reorganization. Title: Review of microbiologically influenced corrosion of dental metallic materials: Biofilm-mediated mechanisms, key determinants, and anticorrosion strategies
Abstract: Microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC) poses a significant threat to the integrity and service life of the surfaces of dental metallic materials prostheses and implants. Microorganisms forming biofilms alter the local environmental conditions on the surface of biomaterials and exacerbate biocorrosion processes. When oral metallic materials undergo corrosion, the leached toxic ions may cause inflammatory reactions, sensitization, and teratogenicity. However, little is known about the specific roles of different oral microorganisms in these corrosion mechanisms. A comprehensive understanding of MIC is crucial for improving the biosafety and clinical performance of dental materials. This review provides a systematic overview of MIC in the oral cavity, covering biofilm characteristics, microbial metabolites, corrosion mechanisms, typical corrosion behavior, and current preventive strategies. A major limitation of existing research is the predominant use of single- or dual-species models, which fail to reflect the complexity of the oral ecosystem; this complexity may either mitigate or exacerbate corrosion risks, and must be addressed in future research. MIC of dental metallic materials is a multidisciplinary field of research that can apply methodologies from materials science, corrosion science and biology to further investigate the mechanisms by which oral microorganisms corrode dental metallic materials, thereby guiding the development of advanced materials that combine corrosion resistance, biocompatibility and environmental sustainability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Regulation mechanism of wear and corrosion resistance of TC4 laser-cladded coating by trace boron-induced in-situ TiB precipitation

With increasing B content, both the wear and corrosion resistance of the clad layers initially improved and subsequently deteriorated, with the TC4–0.10B clad layer exhibiting the best overall performance. Title: Alkaline-thermal and enzymatic pretreatment of PLA/PBAT plastics boosts methane production from anaerobic co-digestion with food waste
Abstract: The co-treatment of food waste (FW) and biodegradable plastics in anaerobic digestion (AD) is challenged by the slow degradation of polylactic acid and poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PLA/PBAT) blends. This study systematically evaluated alkaline-thermal (AT) and enzymatic pretreatment of two PLA/PBAT plastics—starch-containing (PLA/PBAT/ST) and mineral dust-containing (PLA/PBAT/MD)—followed by anaerobic co-digestion with FW. AT pretreatment significantly enhanced methane production. The highest cumulative methane yield (223.40 ± 5.62 mL/g VS) was obtained with PLA/PBAT/MD pretreated at 140℃, a 25.2 % increase over the untreated control (CK-MD), while PLA/PBAT/ST showed an 8.6 % increase (197.60 ± 2.49 mL/g VS). Enzymatic pretreatment led to only marginal improvements. Scanning electron microscopy and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy revealed that AT at 140℃ induced extensive surface erosion, pore formation, and ester bond cleavage, thereby increasing surface hydrophilicity and microbial accessibility. Microbial community analysis indicated that AT-pretreated plastics selectively enriched hydrogenotrophic methanogens ( Methanobacterium ) and syntrophic bacteria ( Syntrophomonas ), and showed higher relative abundance of genes putatively involved in electron bifurcation and methanogenesis (e.g., K14126). In contrast, enzyme-pretreated plastics promoted hydrolytic bacteria (Synergistota) and glycolysis-related genes, causing volatile fatty acids accumulation and metabolic imbalance. Title: Novel multiscale network architecture of TiB/Ti55-0.5Si composites for superior high temperature tribological properties
Abstract: High-temperature titanium alloys are typically employed to fabricate turbine blades in aircraft engines. However, their poor tribological properties and thermal softening at elevated temperatures severely limit their service life. To address these challenges, a novel multiscale reinforced TiB/Ti55–0.5Si composite was successfully fabricated via in-situ reactive hot pressing. A unique network architecture was constructed, where in-situ synthesized TiB whiskers formed a primary quasi-continuous network along the prior β grain boundaries, while nano-sized (Ti, Zr)5Si3 phases precipitated as a secondary network at the α/β interface. This specific configuration significantly refined the matrix microstructure: the average grain size of the α phase decreased by 47.2% (from 29.0 μm to 15.3 μm), and the prior β phase was refined by 51.1% (from 64.2 μm to 31.4 μm), effectively eliminating abnormal grain growth. Title: Cyclic nutrient addition drives the evolution of coal organic matter during biodegradation and aqueous immersion
Abstract: Cyclic nutrient addition is a promising strategy for simulating in-situ hydrodynamic recharge in coal reservoirs to enhance coalbed methane production. However, the transformation mechanism of coal organic matter under the coupled effects of biodegradation and aqueous immersion with intermittent nutrient supply remains unclear. Taking high-volatile bituminous coals (C and B rank) as an example, this study applied a net-flux partitioning approach to quantitatively differentiate the contributions of abiotic and biotic processes to extractable organic matter, macromolecular structural parameters, and pore characteristics. Results show that abiotic processes primarily release pore-throat-entrapped organic matter through swelling, dissolution, and desorption, while causing aliphatic side-chain cleavage, oxygen-containing group removal, and micropore collapse. These actions serve as the prerequisite and sustained driving force for biogasification. Microorganisms rapidly utilize the released labile components to generate CH4 and CO2, and compensate for abiotic losses by releasing bound organic matter and etching new micropores on the coal surface. The coal biogasification process comprises three phases: (1) launch phase, dominated by abiotic activation and microbial compensation; (2) transition phase, featuring peak microbial degradation, consumption of labile hydrocarbons, increased aromatic condensation, and formation of micro-mesopores; and (3) maturation phase, characterized by weakened microbial activity and coexistence of abiotic pore collapse with minor biotic pore generation. Title: Combustion characteristics of a Jet-Ignited Ammonia–Hydrogen engine under Oxygen-Enriched Non-Road operating conditions
Abstract: Ammonia (NH3) and hydrogen (H2) have attracted considerable attention as promising alternative fuels. Title: Synergistic Co-Fe-Mo nanoparticles on a leaching-resistant SiO2-melamine-formaldehyde support for robust and high-performance NaBH4 hydrolysis

Title: Response of oil-water ratio on pickering emulsions of pure lemon essential oil in-situ stabilized by keratin/gelatin/xanthan gum ternary complex

Title: Frameworks for vibrational dynamics in additively-manufactured lattice cell structures for weight-optimized service components
Abstract: A significant design constraint for many industries is weight, often requiring a part to be light yet able to withstand high loads. With the rise of additively manufactured components, a new methodology for addressing these issues has gained popularity, as the introduction of complex structural geometry can be easily implemented. However, as engineers use complex geometries for their weight reduction properties, their dynamic properties are often overlooked and not fully studied when incorporated into their design constraints. Title: Optimizing operating conditions of swirl-assisted colorless distributed combustion of ammonia/hydrogen mixtures for enhanced thermal and emission performance
Abstract: The effects of hydrogen enrichment and varying equivalence ratio on ammonia fuel were investigated under Colorless Distributed Combustion (CDC) conditions, aiming to optimize the operating parameters for the lowest NOx and unburned NH3 emissions. In this context, changes in flame structures and temperature distributions, along with NOx and predicted unburned NH3 emissions, were examined both experimentally and numerically under the CDC regime. In particular, the reduction in the equivalence ratio in fuel mixtures with low H2 fractions prevented the achievement of lower O2 concentrations for CDC conditions and narrowed the operational stability range. The CDC regime resulted in more uniform thermal fields under all conditions. Furthermore, lower H2 fractions and leaner mixtures contributed to the homogenization of the thermal fields. Compared to conventional combustion conditions, NOx emissions for the 50 % NH3/50 % H2 fuel mixture at a 17 % O2 concentration were reduced by 82.2 %, 89.1 %, and 90.7 % at equivalence ratios of 0.9, 0.8, and 0.7, respectively. Under these conditions, predicted unburned NH3 emissions were minimal at an equivalence ratio of 0.9, while they were observed to be 600 ± 95 ppm and 700 ± 110 ppm at 0.8 and 0.7, respectively. Reducing the H2 fraction decreased NOx emissions while increasing NH3 slip. This paper demonstrates the CDC regime as an effective strategy for mitigating NOx and NH3 slip in the 50 % NH3/50 % H2 mixture. Implementing these strategies will enable the optimized combustion of NH3, thus expanding its use as a zero-carbon fuel. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: SalFuseFormer: A saliency-guided fusion transformer framework for clinically motivated multi-modal medical image fusion
Abstract: Multi-modal medical image fusion integrates structural and functional information from different imaging modalities to support clinical diagnosis and treatment planning. Existing transformer-based fusion methods achieve strong structural fidelity but do not address preservation of functional colour encoding in modalities such as positron emission tomography (PET) and single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), where chrominance carries quantitative diagnostic significance. This paper proposes SalFuseFormer, a saliency-guided fusion transformer that enhances a domain-fine-tuned transformer backbone with two training-free modules. The saliency-masked edge injection module selectively sharpens MRI boundaries in low-activity regions, and the adaptive chrominance fusion module preserves functional false-colour representation in metabolically active hotspot regions. Functional activity saliency is estimated from the HSV colour space without additional learnable parameters. A modality-aware design selectively applies chrominance fusion based on the diagnostic encoding convention of each modality pair. Evaluation on the Harvard Whole Brain Atlas benchmark across three fusion tasks against ten competing state-of-the-art methods demonstrates statistically significant advantages in functional information retention on MRI-PET fusion, statistically equivalent structural fidelity to the strongest competitors on CT-MRI fusion, and competitive structural fidelity on MRI-SPECT fusion. External validation on 147 MRI-PET pairs from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI-3) cohort confirms competitive performance on heterogeneous clinical data with metric-specific trade-offs. Ablation experiments confirm the independent contribution of each module, and parameter sensitivity analysis demonstrates robustness across a wide operational range. SalFuseFormer offers a balanced trade-off between structural fidelity and functional colour retention across diverse clinical imaging modalities. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Synergistic lubrication mechanism of Fe2O3-MXene heterostructured fillers in polyimide matrix composites for advanced anti-wear coatings
Abstract: Developing durable solid lubricating coatings that operate reliably under variable loads and reciprocating frequencies remains a critical challenge in mechanical engineering. Here, we construct a novel Fe₂O₃-MXene heterostructure via polydopamine-assisted assembly and incorporate it into a polyimide (PI) matrix to fabricate high-performance composite coatings for extreme tribological applications. The lowest friction coefficient and wear rate were obtained for the optimized coating with an Fe₂O₃ to MXene ratio of 0.3–1 and a total filler loading of 1 wt%. For this optimized PI coating, reductions of 15.9% in the friction coefficient and 60.9% in the wear rate were achieved compared with neat PI under 5 N and 2 Hz. These reductions were attributed to the synergistic effect. Rigid Fe₂O₃ nanosheets bear contact loads while soft MXene flakes promote interlayer shearing and repair of worn surfaces. Comprehensive variable-condition tests demonstrate that the coating maintains stable lubrication across loads from 1 N to 7 N and frequencies from 0.5 Hz to 4 Hz, with continuous transfer films enriched in Ti, Fe, and O species formed on counterfaces to prevent direct metal-coating contact. This work not only elucidates the cooperative lubrication mechanism between oxide and MXene phases but also offers a practical, scalable coating strategy for high-load reciprocating components in aerospace actuators, heavy machinery, and precision transmission systems, where both anti-friction and anti-wear durability are essential. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Ping W.; Bai Z.; Tao Y.; Wang M.; Wang Z.
Title: Knowledge-driven multimodal medical image classification
Abstract: Medical image classification is significantly hindered by the scarcity of data for minority classes, which leads to a major classification bias in models. This issue results in poor and unreliable performance on underrepresented, yet often critical, stages of disease. To address this issue, we propose a knowledge-driven multimodal classification model that integrates domain-specific images and texts. Specifically, we design a visual knowledge cache to store and retrieve representative lesion features. Meanwhile, a textual knowledge cache is proposed to dynamically select semantically relevant textual descriptions closely aligned with visual features. Furthermore, we introduce a multimodal knowledge reasoner that combines image-to-image retrieval and image-to-text alignment, leading to improved fine-grained disease classification. We evaluate our method on three public datasets APTOS2019, BUSI and COVID×CT-3 A. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our model achieves superior grading accuracy, with an average a 2.90% improvement in accuracy, highlighting its effectiveness in medical image classification. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Kong D.; Shen J.; Xiao J.
Title: Analysis of the temporal regularity of Maxwell's equations in dispersive media
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: The temporal regularity of Maxwell's equations in dispersive media, including the Cole–Cole and Havriliak–Negami models, is investigated in this paper through an exact series representation. This representation is derived by reformulating Maxwell's equations into a single integro-differential equation, which is then analyzed using the Laplace transform. For the Cole–Cole model, our analysis shows that, when the initial electric field satisfies E0≢0, the electric field E and the induced polarization field P belong to Cα in time, while the magnetic field H belongs to C1,α in time, where α ∈ (0, 1). Moreover, when E0 ≡ 0, the regularity improves to E, P ∈ C1,α and H ∈ C2,α in time. Careful numerical experiments are conducted to verify the analytical results on temporal regularity. In addition, the analysis characterizing the singular behavior near the origin is extended to the Havriliak–Negami model in the case α=1 and 0 < β < 1. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Hu J.; Chu Y.; Dong W.; Zhao T.; Han Y.; Zeng H.; Yang R.; Chen L.
Title: Size-controlled whey protein microgels enable tunable gelation in low-oil Pickering emulsions: Role of particle size and concentration
Abstract: Although many formulations have been developed to stabilize low-oil Pickering emulsions, it remains challenging to define how particle design enables the transition from a flowable emulsion to an emulsion gel. In this study, submicron-scale spherical whey protein microgels (WPMs) with tunable sizes were produced from water-in-water emulsions via a low-energy protein–polysaccharide phase-separation route. Microgels with mean sizes of ∼200 nm, ∼500 nm, and ∼1 μm were obtained. Their potential as structural building blocks for low-oil Pickering systems was then evaluated. At a WPM concentration of 4.5 wt%, all WPM-stabilized low-oil emulsions showed minimal or no creaming during 28 days of storage. However, their rheological behavior was strongly dependent on microgel size. WPM∼1 μm formed highly viscous, structured emulsions with gel-like characteristics, whereas WPM∼200 nm produced more flowable emulsions with higher mobility. The stability and structuring of these systems were governed by the coupled contributions of WPMs at the oil–water interface and in the bulk phase. Larger WPMs, especially WPM∼1 μm, exhibited lower electrostatic repulsion and more viscoelastic interfacial films. Meanwhile, their aggregation in the continuous phase promoted particle bridging and the formation of a percolated network, thereby driving the transition toward a Pickering emulsion gel and markedly enhancing system viscoelasticity. These results show that WPM size controls interfacial stabilization and bulk network formation, providing a practical route to tune low-oil Pickering systems from flowable emulsions to thick, gel-like emulsions. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Mitigating the adverse effects of free machining on the wear behaviour of large strain extrusion machined Brass260 alloy
Abstract: Conventional or free machining (FM) of Brass260 alloy typically causes inhomogeneous deformation, localized strain, and surface flaws that lower its scratch resistance. This research addresses these deficiencies by using Large Strain Extrusion Machining (LSEM), a heavy plastic deformation method designed to homogenize strain and refine the alloy's microstructure. The study evaluates the scratch and friction response of solution-annealed (SA), free machining (FM), and large strain extrusion machining (LSEM)-treated ultrafine-grained Brass260 sheets/laminates. Micro-scratch evaluations were performed under a progressive load ranging from 20 to 40 N. The findings indicate that LSEM processing substantially elevates scratch resistance and surface quality. Eventually severe grain refinement and work hardening boosted material hardness to ∼ 250 Kgf/mm². Advanced material characterization via electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and 3D optical profilometry highlighted distinct differences between the processing methods. While FM specimens exhibited unstable plastic flow, crack initiation, and severe pile-ups, the LSEM samples displayed uniform strain distribution and minimal surface damage. Friction tracking revealed a friction coefficient between 0.2 and 0.4, peaking at a 16 N force under maximum load. Detailed orientation image microscopy (OIM) based EBSD-kernal average misorientation (KAM) and grain orientation spread (GOS) analysis supported that this enhanced durability stems from increased dislocation activity and microstructural uniformity. Ultimately, this study establishes a clear relationship between the processing route, microstructural evolution, and scratch-wear response, demonstrating the potential of LSEM as an effective alternative processing strategy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zeng H.; Lin Y.C.; Tan X.-H.; Huang H.-H.; Zhou Y.
Title: Real-time reconstruction of the internal temperature field of welding using global physics-mixed long short-term memory network and physical constraint reconstruction
Abstract: Accurate reconstruction of internal welding temperature fields is essential for evaluating thermal cycles and weld quality, yet direct internal measurement is difficult. This study proposes a real-time reconstruction framework for the internal temperature field of SUS304 gas metal arc welding (GMAW) butt joints by coupling a physics-constrained mixed deep operator network (PMix-DeepONet) predictor with spatio-temporal physics-augmented plate spline interpolation (ST-PAS). In PMix-DeepONet, a global physics-mixed long short-term memory (Mix-LSTM) encoder performs physical mixing of welding current, voltage, surface molten-pool temperature, and temporal information before recurrent encoding, enabling the branch network to capture multi-source process dynamics. The DeepONet branch-trunk operator-learning structure then maps the encoded process features and spatiotemporal coordinates to the internal temperature field, while heat-transfer, boundary-condition, initial-condition, and high-temperature-sensitive constraints guide the prediction toward physically meaningful solutions. ST-PAS further combines an adaptively fitted Goldak-like thermal-shape prior with residual plate-spline correction to refine sparse reconstructed fields while preserving nonlinear heat-field morphology. Experiments show that PMix-DeepONet reduces the overall root mean square error (RMSE) from 35.78 °C to 22.09 °C compared with DeepONet. In the high-temperature region above 1000 °C, the RMSE decreases from 66.78 °C to 23.71 °C. Ablation results confirm the importance of Mix-LSTM and physical constraints for stable high-gradient prediction. For spatial refinement, ST-PAS achieves the lowest RMSE of 57.90 °C and MSE of 3352.05, reducing RMSE and MSE by 1.09% and 2.18% compared with LSM-SP. Qualitative comparisons further verify the effectiveness of the framework for real-time SUS304 GMAW temperature-field prediction. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Authors: Li Y.; Li B.; Wang B.; Shi K.; Ahmatjan A.; Tian F.
Title: Multi-scenario fire protection performance of an LDH-reinforced bio-based gel foam
Abstract: Coal spontaneous combustion, wooden building fires, and forest wildfires are typical and highly destructive fire scenarios. In this study, a flame-retardant bio-based gel foam (SK-LDH) was successfully prepared by introducing layered double hydroxide (LDH). Its fire prevention performance was systematically evaluated across multiple typical scenarios. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) showed that LDH enhanced char formation, with a char residue of 37.74% at 800.0 °C under nitrogen atmosphere. In the coal spontaneous combustion scenario, treatment with SK-LDH reduced the peak heat release rate (pHRR), total heat release (THR), and total smoke production (TSP) of coal by 15.46%, 7.71%, and 99.93%, respectively. SEM and XPS analyses of the residual char confirmed that LDH promoted the formation of a dense char layer. Under constant heating at 250.0 °C, SK-LDH reduced the coal temperature by 105.0 °C at 3600 s and delayed the expansion of high-temperature zones compared with SK. In the wooden building fire scenario, SK-LDH enabled wood to achieve a UL 94 HB rating, with the LOI increasing to 31.1%. Furthermore, no charring was observed on wooden blocks after 180 s of flame impingement. In the forest wildfire scenario, dead leaf fire-blocking tests demonstrated the effectiveness of SK-LDH as a firebreak in preventing flame spread. This study aims to provide a theoretical basis and technical support for the engineering application of gel foam in multi-scenario fire prevention and control. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: High-performance thin film nanocomposite membrane prepared from 2D ZIF-67 nanosheets and Pebax for natural gas dehydration
Abstract: Thin film nanocomposites (TFNs) fabricated with metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are considered as promising alternatives for natural gas (NG) dehydration. However, it remains difficult to realize both high water permeance and selectivity at the same time. The ultrathin selective layer of the TFN structure inherently provides higher permeance than traditional membranes. In this research, TFN membranes were fabricated via incorporating ultrathin ZIF-67 nanosheets into a Pebax 1657 polymer matrix with polyacrylonitrile (PAN) porous support. The 2D ZIF-67, characterized by their leaf-like morphology, create well-defined molecular sieving channels while maintaining excellent interfacial compatibility. A key innovation of this work is the achievement of exceptionally high separation performance. The optimized membrane with 12.5 wt% ZIF-67 loading demonstrated exceptional separation capabilities, a remarkable 38,356 GPU in water vapor permeation along with H2O/CH4 separation factor of 18,235 was documented, which surpasses most reported membranes for NG dehydration. The synthesized membranes also exhibited exceptional stability of 10 days. This work demonstrates that 2D MOF nanosheets can overcome the typical permeability-selectivity trade-off, advancing membrane based NG dehydration toward practical applications. Copyright © 2026. Title: Enhanced wear resistance of FeCoCrNiMo high-entropy alloy coatings at 600℃ by Nb-regulated evolution of tribo-induced nanocrystalline-amorphous composite structure
Abstract: During high-temperature sliding, tribo-induced microstructural evolution is a key factor determining the wear resistance of high-entropy alloy (HEA) coatings. However, there remains a lack of deep understanding regarding how refractory elements regulate the mechanisms of this evolution and tribological behavior. In this study, FeCoCrNiMo and FeCoCrNiMoNb0.3 HEA coatings were prepared using laser cladding and tested for sliding wear at 600 ℃. The influence of Nb on wear behavior and friction-induced microstructural evolution under the investigated 600 ℃ sliding condition was systematically investigated. The results show that the addition of Nb changes the coating microstructure from an FCC + σ dual-phase structure to an FCC + σ + Laves three-phase heterogeneous structure and is accompanied by redistribution of Cr and Mo. Compared with FeCoCrNiMo, the FeCoCrNiMoNb0.3 coating exhibits a lower coefficient of friction at 600℃ and a reduction in wear rate of approximately 83%, exhibiting significantly superior high-temperature wear resistance. During high-temperature sliding, a friction layer with a nanocrystalline-amorphous composite structure formed on the surfaces of both coatings. FeCoCrNiMo forms a loose friction layer approximately 2μm thick with distinct structural layering. In contrast, FeCoCrNiMoNb0.3 forms a dense, protective friction layer approximately 950 nm thick, containing an Fe- and Cr-enriched oxidized region and showing stronger amorphous features and improved retention of the nanocrystalline/amorphous composite structure. These structural characteristics improve the dynamic stability of the tribolayer and suppress repeated cracking and large-scale delamination, shifting the wear mechanism from severe oxidative and adhesive wear dominated by repeated peeling of the oxide layer to mild oxidative wear dominated by relatively thin, continuous, and dynamically stable tribolayer. This study provides a theoretical basis for the compositional design and microstructural regulation of HEA coatings for high-temperature wear-resistant applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Molecular-guided solvent selection for efficient bitumen extraction from natural rock asphalt: Integrating computational screening with experimental validation
Abstract: Solvent selection remains a major challenge in bitumen extraction from natural rock asphalt because conventional selection is largely based on empirical trial-and-error, providing limited molecular insights into solvent–bitumen interactions. This study developed a molecular-guided solvent screening strategy integrating an experimentally informed representative bitumen molecular model with density functional theory (DFT) calculations and experimental validation. Natural rock asphalt samples from the Kabungka and Lawele deposits were characterized using FTIR and SARA analysis, and the resulting compositional information was combined with literature-derived molecular structures to construct the representative model. Geometry optimization was performed using DFT/B3LYP/def2-SVP, followed by screening of nine organic solvents based on CPCM solvation energy and solvent–bitumen binding energy. Toluene exhibited the highest calculated binding-energy magnitude (76 kJ mol−1), followed by methyl ethyl ketone (75 kJ mol−1) and cyclohexane (62 kJ mol−1). Three selected solvent candidates were subsequently evaluated by laboratory-scale solid–liquid extraction. Toluene achieved the highest bitumen recovery among the tested solvents, reaching 94.07% and 85.07% for Kabungka and Lawele, respectively, compared with 88.12% and 75.91% for cyclohexane and 73.23% and 57.83% for methyl ethyl ketone. The results demonstrate that molecular-level interaction descriptors can support solvent pre-screening, while experimental validation remains necessary to account for deposit-specific composition and extraction behavior. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Pan H.; Li S.; Ji B.; Bao R.; Pan M.; Fan H.; Zhu Z.
Title: Mechanistic insights into pore structure evolution and wettability during nonionic surfactant-assisted acidification of coal
Abstract: Acidification can promote pore-structure evolution in coal reservoirs; however, its effectiveness may be limited by poor coal wettability and restricted acid accessibility within the pore network. Although surfactant-assisted acidification can improve wettability and acid transport, the relationship between pore structure evolution and wettability enhancement remains unclear. To address this issue, a CDEA-assisted acidification system was investigated, employing coconut diethanolamide (CDEA), a nonionic surfactant. X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), and contact angle (CA) measurements were employed to systematically characterize the evolution of coal microcrystalline structure, pore structure, and wettability. The results indicate that CDEA-assisted acidification promotes mineral dissolution and induces microcrystalline disorder. Micropore development is closely associated with variations in microcrystalline structural parameters, suggesting that microcrystalline restructuring provides additional space for pore development. With progressive mineral dissolution and continuous pore expansion, the pore structure of coal was significantly optimized. Total porosity increased from 6.94% to 10.81%, effective porosity increased from 3.89% to 7.98%, and the overall complexity of the pore structure decreased. The expansion of pore space and the improvement of pore connectivity were accompanied by fluid redistribution toward smaller-scale pore domains. Accordingly, T2C and T2g generally shifted toward lower values. Coal wettability was also substantially enhanced, as indicated by the decrease in contact angle from 59.9° to 26.1°. The contact angle exhibited a significant negative correlation with porosity, indicating that pore structure optimization is closely associated with wettability improvement. This study clarifies the relationship between pore-structure evolution and wettability changes during CDEA-assisted acidification and provides new theoretical insights into the permeability enhancement of low-permeability coal reservoirs. Authors: Kumar A.; Li X.; Zhao X.; Tamrakar E.
Title: Caputo-inspired stochastic gradient methods with bounded scaling for deep learning
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: Caputo-inspired optimization has attracted increasing attention because of its potential to incorporate memory-related information into gradient-based learning. However, existing fractional-order stochastic methods may encounter stability and convergence difficulties in the presence of noisy gradients and high-dimensional deep-learning models. In this work, we propose a Caputo-inspired stochastic optimization framework that decouples gradient evaluation from scalar scaling while explicitly bounding the scaling factor. Within this framework, we develop two algorithms: Extrapolated Fractional-Order Stochastic Gradient Descent (EFOSGD) and its non-extrapolated variant (VEFOSGD). Both methods replace the componentwise Caputo term with a bounded isotropic scalar based on the displacement between consecutive iterates, while EFOSGD additionally evaluates the gradient at an extrapolated point. Under standard stochastic approximation assumptions and Robbins–Monro step sizes, we establish a weighted summability result and a lim inf-type stationarity guarantee in expectation, rather than full convergence of the entire sequence. Experiments on CIFAR-10 with ResNet-18/50, CIFAR-100 with ResNet-18, and Fashion-MNIST with ResNet-18 demonstrate that EFOSGD and VEFOSGD achieve competitive performance compared with SGD, Adam, AMSGrad, Nesterov-SGD, Lookahead, and Adaptive Gradient Clipping, while exhibiting stable training behavior. These results indicate the practical potential of combining bounded Caputo-inspired scaling with extrapolated gradient evaluation for deep-learning optimization. © 2026

Authors: Li S.; Wu Y.; Zhu J.
Title: In-situ pyrolytic synthesis of MnO2/lignite-based porous carbon composite for Zn-ion batteries
Abstract: Zn-ion batteries possess the merits of good safety, cheap cost and high ionic conductivity. The δ-MnO2 cathode exhibits high capacity, however, the weak electronic conductivity and structural collapse during cycling severely hinder its practical application. Herein, a novel δ-MnO2/lignite-based porous carbon (LPC) composite (δ-MnO2/LPC) has been prepared through an in-situ pyrolysis method with lignite extract and KMnO4 as the precursor. The incorporation of LPC enables the high-value-added utilization of low rank coal, forming a hierarchical micro-/mesoporous network. The XPS and Raman results confirm the formation of Mn-O-C bonds and their regulation of Mn4+ content and crystal order. Electrochemical tests show that δ-MnO2/LPC can deliver a discharge capacity of 323.3 mAh g−1 at 0.1 A g−1 and maintain a capacity retention of 74.3 % after 1000 cycles at 0.5 A g−1. The kinetic analysis reveals that the charge-transfer resistance diminishes significantly from 394.3 Ω to 26.6 Ω, while the Zn2+ diffusion coefficient is notably enhanced. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further confirm that LPC effectively reduces the bandgap and improves the electrical conductivity of the electrode. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Du W.; Zhang C.; Wang L.; Zhu G.; Ni Z.
Title: A composite inhibitor developed through mine-water resource utilization: synergistic mechanisms for suppressing coal spontaneous combustion
Abstract: Coal spontaneous combustion remains a major safety hazard in coal mining, while large volumes of mine water generated during extraction create additional environmental pressure. This study developed a low-cost mine-water/MgCl2 composite inhibitor and evaluated its suppression of coal low-temperature oxidation and combustion. Scanning electron microscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, programmed-temperature oxidation, and cone calorimetry were used to characterize its inhibitory performance and underlying mechanisms. Compared with raw coal and coal treated separately with mine water or MgCl2, the composite-treated sample exhibited the strongest inhibition. It reduced oxygen consumption and suppressed the formation of CO, CO2, and hydrocarbon gases. At 260 °C, its oxygen-consumption rate was approximately 23% lower than that of raw coal. The composite treatment also increased the apparent activation energy to 152.08 kJ·mol−1 during the high-temperature stage and reduced both the peak heat-release rate and total heat release, with the latter decreasing by approximately 25%. Microstructural analyses suggested that Mg2+ may interact with reactive oxygen-containing structures, including hydroxyl, carboxyl, and carbonyl groups, potentially reducing the accessibility of oxidation-active sites. Inorganic ions in mine water also promoted the formation of a surface deposit layer that filled pores and restricted oxygen diffusion. The composite inhibitor therefore suppressed coal oxidation, gas evolution, and combustion through the synergistic effects of physical oxygen isolation and chemical passivation. This system integrates mine-water reuse with mine-fire prevention, offering both environmental and safety benefits. These findings provide a basis for developing sustainable technologies to control coal spontaneous combustion. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Xiao Z.; Nie X.; Wan T.
Title: Vibration isolation characteristics of a nonlinear quasi-zero stiffness metastructure based on a bistable bending beam
Abstract: To break through the limitations of the traditional vibration isolation system in the low-frequency and resonance region, this study designed a nonlinear quasi-zero stiffness (QZS) element structure composed of a negative stiffness bistable sinusoidal beam and a positive stiffness arc Euler beam in parallel. The finite element model and restoring force expression of the element structure were established by static analysis. The restoring force of the element structure and the parameter conditions with QZS characteristics near the equilibrium position were obtained. The experimental data show that the bistable QZS element structure has a wide QZS region, which verifies the accuracy of the theoretical model and finite element analysis. Based on the static analysis results, the nonlinear dynamic model of the QZS element structure is further established. The influence of system parameters and excitation amplitude on the vibration isolation performance and response stability of the system was studied using the harmonic balance method (HBM). In addition, based on the vibration isolation model of the bistable QZS element structure, a vibration isolation base with high static and low dynamic stiffness characteristics is designed. The vibration isolation performance of the base is verified by the dynamic experiment. This study provides a new design paradigm for the miniaturized and integrated vibration isolation system of special equipment, and its bistable QZS mechanism shows significant engineering application potential in broadening the effective vibration isolation frequency band. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS

Authors: Pang M.; Li N.; Liu Y.; Chen F.; Song Y.; Tang Y.
Title: A novel 1D/3D hierarchical heterojunction Bi4V2O11/In2S3 with the reinforced photocatalytic activity toward tetracycline: the synergistic modulation of S-scheme charge migration and multidimensional configuration
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Recently, the application of photocatalysis on the treatment of antibiotics contamination has been received increasing attention. Developing high active photocatalytic material is crucial to realize the efficient degradation of antibiotics. In the present work, a hierarchical 1D/3D S-scheme heterostructure Bi₄V₂O₁₁/In₂S₃ was successfully fabricated with facile hydrothermal strategy. The synthesized Bi₄V₂O₁₁/In₂S₃ was characterized by s series of measures. The combination of in-situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), band alignment, and generation of reactive species demonstrate the S-scheme charge migration mechanism of Bi₄V₂O₁₁/In₂S₃ heterojunction. The catalytic performance of Bi₄V₂O₁₁/In₂S₃ was assessed by the photocatalytic degradation of tetracycline (TC). Bi₄V₂O₁₁/In₂S₃ heterojunction exhibits significantly enhanced photoactivity relative to the bare Bi₄V₂O₁₁ and In₂S₃. The optimal heterojunction (BI-20%) shows superior photocatalytic activity toward TC degradation, achieving an TC removal efficiency of 87% after visible-light irradiation of 120 min. In addition, BI-20% demonstrated satisfactory mineralization ability, excellent structural stability, good recyclability, and strong resistance to coexisting ions, humic substances, and pH variation. The enhanced photocatalytic performance originated from the synergistic effect of multidimensional configuration and S-scheme charge migration in promoting the separation and migration of photogenerated charge carriers. As well as, the rational design of energy band arrangement of Bi₄V₂O₁₁ and In₂S₃ enables ·O₂−, ·OH, and h+ to serve as the principal active species. The current work supplies a feasible strategy for constructing efficient photocatalytic materials for the environment restoration. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Preparation of highly thermally conductive composite phase change materials based on MXene aerogel with superb electromagnetic shielding properties
Abstract: Thermal phase-change materials (PCMs) serve as highly efficient solutions to achieve thermal stored energy and thermal insulation, but their application is largely limited by issues such as poor thermal conductivity and susceptibility to leakage. Furthermore, ice-gel-based adsorbent PCMs can significantly improve thermal conductivity and reduce the leakage rate of PCMs. In this study, we have effectively integrated chitosan (CS) with a family of 2D transition metal carbides and nitrides (MXene) lamellae and introduced directed freezing to achieve an ordered arrangement of MXene nanosheets. The resulting continuous three-dimensional MXene aerogel structure, following impregnation with PCMs, markedly elevated the thermo-stability of polyethylene glycol (PEG) and reduced its leakage rate. Moreover, this composite phase-change material (PCM) features a latent heat of 174.86 J/g and delivers a heat of formation efficacy of 93.1%. With this high enthalpy efficiency, the composite material achieves a thermal conductivity of 1.446 W/(m·K) and an electro-magnetic shielding performance of 40 dB, whilst also demonstrating excellent electrothermal conversion capabilities, indicating its prospective applications in the field of phase-change energy storage. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Synthesis of Ag3PO4/WX2 (X = S, Se) layered heterojunctions for enhanced photocatalytic performance
Abstract: Visible-light photocatalysis is often constrained by fast charge recombination and limited stability, reducing dye-removal efficiency in wastewater treatment. To address this issue, layered Ag3PO4/WX2 (X = S, Se) heterojunction photocatalysts were synthesized by solvothermal preparation of bulk WX2, liquid-phase exfoliation into few-layer nanosheets, and in situ precipitation of Ag3PO4 on their surfaces. XRD confirmed the preservation of cubic Ag3PO4, while slight peak shifts, TEM/SEM observations, EDS, and XPS verified intimate interfacial coupling and charge redistribution within the heterostructures. UV-Vis DRS and Tauc analysis revealed enhanced visible-light absorption and tunable band-gap energies upon heterojunction formation. The calculated electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) increased from 6112.5 cm2 for Ag₃PO₄ to 6865 and 7072.5 cm2 for Ag₃PO₄/WS₂ and Ag₃PO₄/WSe₂, respectively, corresponding to increases of 12.3% and 15.7%. Under visible-light irradiation, pure Ag₃PO₄ achieved approximately 95% Rhodamine B degradation within 30 min, whereas Ag₃PO₄/WS₂ achieved 97% degradation in 15 min and Ag₃PO₄/WSe₂ completely degraded within 20 min. Radical trapping experiments indicated that photogenerated holes were the dominant active species responsible for the photocatalytic process. These findings demonstrate that constructing layered Ag3PO4/WX2 heterojunctions is an effective strategy to enhance the visible-light photocatalytic activity of Ag3PO4 and provide new insights into the design of high-performance photocatalysts for wastewater treatment. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Ma J.; Xia T.; Wu H.; Cheng S.; Xing Q.; Wang T.; Yuan Y.; Dong Y.; Feng F.; Wang F.
Title: In-situ grown FeP nanoparticles on Fe,P Co-doped porous carbon spheres: synergistic heterostructures for low-overpotential oxygen evolution reaction
Abstract: The surge in the need for eco-friendly hydrogen energy via water splitting has spurred intensive research into non-precious metal electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Herein, a reliable hydrothermal, carbonization and phosphorization strategy was adopted to synthesize the FeP/CS electrocatalyst, where iron phosphide nanoparticles were in-situ grown on iron and phosphorus co-doped porous carbon spheres. This unique heterostructure features Fe,P co-doping within the carbon matrix for enhanced conductivity and FeP nanoparticles anchored on the carbon surface for boosted intrinsic activity. The optimized FeP/CS exhibits superior OER catalytic activity, achieving 10 mA cm−2 at an overpotential of 273.9 mV and a Tafel slope of 68.6 mV dec−1. It also demonstrates promising long-lasting reliability, showing merely 9.2% current degradation after 50 h of chronoamperometry. Density functional theory calculations indicate that the FeP/CS heterostructure increases the density of states near the Fermi level, enhances charge transfer, and remarkably reduces the Gibbs free energy barrier of the rate-determining step (O* → OOH*) from 2.96 eV (Fe/CS) to 2.50 eV (FeP/CS). This work demonstrates that the synergistic combination of internal co-doping and in-situ interfacial engineering between metal phosphide and carbon matrix effectively boosts both the activity and stability of transition-metal phosphide-based electrocatalysts, and it can serve as a practical guideline for the rational engineering of superior OER electrocatalysts. Authors: Jiang K.; Gao H.-H.; Chen Q.-Y.; Liu Z.-H.
Title: Ru nanoparticles decorated NiFe-P nanosheet arrays and NiFe-BLDH nanosheets loading for boosting overall water splitting at high current density
Abstract: Developing efficient and durable electrocatalysts capable of operating at high current densities is critical for industrial-scale hydrogen production. Herein, based on the synergistic and interfacial engineering strategies, a hierarchical heterostructured nanocomposite, NiFe-BLDH@Ru-NiFe-P/NF, is rationally designed and fabricated by sequentially growing NiFe-P nanosheet arrays on nickel foam (NF), electrodepositing Ru nanoparticles (Ru NPs), and subsequently loading borate anion intercalated nickel–iron layered double hydroxide (NiFe-BLDH) nanosheets. The introduction of Ru NPs markedly enhances the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activity, making Ru-NiFe-P/NF with a low overpotential of only 124 ± 1 mV at 500 mA cm−2 and a Tafel slope of 87.31 ± 1.00 mV dec-1. The construction of heterointerfaces induced charge redistribution, optimized the adsorption of oxygen-containing intermediates, and also alleviated the slight dissolution of Ru in anode, endowing NiFe-BLDH@Ru-NiFe-P/NF with excellent oxygen evolution reaction (OER) performance, as demonstrated by an overpotential of 364 ± 1 mV at 500 mA cm−2 and a Tafel slope of 73.13 ± 1.00 mV dec-1. When NiFe-BLDH@Ru-NiFe-P/NF as the anode was assembled into an electrolyzer with Ru-NiFe-P/NF as the cathode, a voltage of only 1.94 V was required to deliver 500 mA cm−2 in alkaline simulated seawater (1 M KOH + 1 M NaCl), and the system operated continuously for 100 h without significant degradation, demonstrating outstanding catalytic stability and Cl- corrosion resistance. This work provides a feasible structural design strategy to develop high-performance, durable electrocatalysts for industrial-scale water splitting. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: The effect of gradient magnetic field on flow and heat transfer of burning surface of iron-doped HTPB-based propellant
Abstract: In order to reveal the effect of gradient magnetic field on flow and heat transfer of burning surface of solid propellant, a micro-scale combustion model under magnetic field effect is established based on the random particle packing model and multi-physics simulation method. The results show that compared with the case without external magnetic field, the flame height of the propellant under magnetic field is reduced, accompanied by higher O2 accumulation above the large AP particles. With the increase of the external magnetic field gradient, the height of the AP/HTPB diffusion flame decreases, which enhances heat feedback at the burning surface. Meanwhile, under the effect of magnetic field, locally high velocity region is formed near the burning surface, which enhances heat transfer to the burning surface. The increasing magnetic field gradient also leads to high concentration zones of the paramagnetic species (O2 and Fe) while the overall flame shape transitions from a sharp conical form to a full arc-like form. The combined effect of magnetic field on lateral species diffusion and the local flow structure distribution causes earlier formation of diffusion flame near the burning surface. With the increasing magnetic field gradient, the total heat transfer coefficient and Nusselt number of AP particles decrease by 1.2% and 0.8% while those of the HTPB binder increase by 5.7% and 6.3%, respectively. The non-uniform heat feedback is dominated by the lateral diffusion of paramagnetic species and the re-distribution of the flow structure above the burning surface. This study provides better understanding of the flow and heat transfer mechanism of iron-doped HTPB propellant under the effect of magnetic field. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Authors: Wu J.; Wang C.; Deng J.; Xiao Y.; Lu Y.; Liu Y.; Bai Z.; Kang F.; Shi Z.; Jing R.
Title: Preparation and properties of coal slime-based biomass composite gel——Coal mine fire prevention and control
Abstract: To improve coal spontaneous combustion (CSC) prevention while promoting the high-value utilization of coal slime (SM), a novel SM-based biomass composite gel (SA/H/X/SM) was developed. The formulation was optimized using an orthogonal experimental design, and its rheological behavior, thermal stability, sealing performance, and CSC inhibition mechanism were systematically investigated by rheological measurements, thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), air-leakage tests, temperature-programmed oxidation, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. The results show that sodium alginate (SA) and calcium lactate (CL) formed a three-dimensional gel network through ionic crosslinking, while hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC) and xanthan gum (XG) further reinforced the structure via hydrogen bonding and chain entanglement. SM particles contributed to network integrity through particle filling and interfacial interactions, improving the thermal stability and mechanical performance of the gel. SA/H/X/SM exhibited typical yield-pseudoplastic behavior and achieved an average air-leakage sealing efficiency exceeding 48.5% under different pressure and flow conditions, demonstrating excellent transportability and sealing performance. The composite gel effectively inhibited coal oxidation by delaying CO and C2H4 release and increasing the apparent activation energy by 4.97% and 29.78% during the low-temperature and accelerated oxidation stages, respectively. MD simulations further revealed that abundant hydrophilic functional groups promoted the adsorption and diffusion of water molecules on the coal surface, thereby enhancing coal wetting. Consequently, SA/H/X/SM efficiently inhibited CSC through the synergistic effects of oxygen isolation and sealing, wetting and cooling, and high-temperature carbonization for thermal dissipation. These findings provide a sustainable and scalable strategy for CSC prevention and valorization of SM in underground fire control applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
