Title: On the Wave Propagation and Dynamic Response of a Spherical Cavity in Piezoelectric Microstructures via Rabotnov Kernel-Based Moore–Gibson–Thompson Thermoelasticity Theory
Source title: International Journal of Structural Stability and Dynamics
Abstract: This study investigates the transient dynamic response and thermomechanical stability of a transversely isotropic piezoelectric medium featuring a spherical cavity. To accurately model the small-scale effects inherent in advanced structural components, a spatiotemporal nonlocal elasticity framework of the Klein–Gordon type is employed, incorporating both internal length and intrinsic time scale parameters. The governing equations of the Moore–Gibson–Thompson (MGT) thermoelastic model are reformulated using a nonsingular Rabotnov-type fractional exponential kernel, providing a robust mathematical formulation to capture memory-dependent interactions without the paradox of infinite propagation speeds. The structural boundary of the cavity is subjected to a ramp-type thermal loading and electrical grounding, simulating realistic operational conditions for sensors and actuators. Using the Laplace transform technique and the Zakian numerical inversion method, the transient distributions of temperature, displacement, stress, and electric potential are derived. The results highlight the significant influence of the Rabotnov fractional parameter and spatiotemporal nonlocality on the structural stability and wave-front characteristics. This research provides a unique medium for understanding the latest developments in fractional-order dynamics for piezoelectric micro-and nano-structures, offering practical insights for civil, aerospace, and mechanical engineering applications. © 2026 World Scientific Publishing Company.

Authors: Shi Y.; Song T.; Huo H.; Cao X.; Wu Y.; Wei Z.; Cao X.
Title: Drying condition regulated Prussian blue nanoparticles embedded in graphene fibers for accelerated thermal decomposition and enhanced combustion: from energetic components to solid propellants
Abstract: This study presents a drying-condition-regulated strategy for embedding Prussian blue (PB) nanoparticles into graphene fibers (GFs) to fabricate Prussian blue/graphene fiber (PB/GF) combustion catalysts. GFx (x = 5, 10, 20) and PB/GF10-x (x = 1, 2, 3) were synthesized by varying the graphene-solution concentration and drying protocol, followed by systematic characterization of their structural and surface properties. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) was used to assess their effects on the thermal decomposition of representative energetic components. The optimal catalyst, PB/GF10-1, was subsequently incorporated into Nitrate Ester Plasticized Polyether propellants containing RDX, HMX, or CL-20 to evaluate combustion performance. At 10 °C·min−1, the maximum reductions in decomposition peak temperature ( T p) for Cyclotrimethylene trinitramine (RDX), Cyclotetramethylene tetranitramine (HMX), and Hexanitrohexaazaisowurtzitane (CL-20), and Ammonium perchlorate (AP) were 1.3, 1.4, 1.9, and 28.2 °C, respectively. The corresponding maximum decreases in apparent activation energy ( E a) were 18.4, 31.2, 17.5, and 40.6 kJ·mol−1. The small peak shifts of the nitramines were accompanied by lower fitted activation energies, while AP showed a more pronounced peak-temperature response. In the RDX-, HMX-, and CL-20-based Al-containing NEPE propellant combustion performance tests, PB/GF10-1 increased the average burning rates by 25.5 %, 23.6 %, and 18.4 %, respectively, with reductions in the fitted pressure exponent ( n ) from 0.58, 0.60, and 0.61 to 0.55, 0.56, and 0.58 over 1–20 MPa. These results demonstrate the potential of PB/GF as a combustion catalyst and highlight the influence of drying conditions on its performance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Jin W.; Xie L.-J.
Title: Double hard thresholding pursuit: A concise and highly efficient variant of the HTP algorithm for sparse signal recovery
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: The hard thresholding pursuit (HTP) algorithm is extensively employed for the recovery of sparse signals in compressed sensing. Although powerful, it has been demonstrated that the hard thresholding operator used in the HTP algorithm should be applied to a compressible signal rather than a dense one to avoid significant information loss. This motivates us to introduce the double hard thresholding pursuit (DHTP) algorithm in this paper, wherein the hard thresholding operator is applied twice: once as in the classical HTP algorithm and another time to a dense vector generated during each iteration. We establish three sufficient conditions in terms of the restricted isometry property with three different orders to ensure the successful recovery of the DHTP algorithm. Meanwhile, we prove that the DHTP algorithm converges within a finite number of iterations and exhibits stability when handling slight changes in problem data. Extensive numerical experiments related to synthetic data and real images demonstrate the superiority of our proposed approach over existing sparse recovery algorithms. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Cai J.-Y.; Lu P.; Xia M.
Title: Dichotomy for real Holantc problems
Source title: Journal of Computer and System Sciences
Abstract: Holant problems capture a class of Sum-of-Product computations such as counting matchings. It is inspired by holographic algorithms and is equivalent to tensor networks, with counting CSP being a special case. A complexity classification for Holant problems is more difficult to prove, not only because it logically implies a classification for counting CSP, but also due to the deeper reason that there exist more intricate polynomial time tractable problems in the broader framework. We discover a new family of constraint functions L which define polynomial time computable counting problems. These do not appear in counting CSP, and no newly discovered tractable constraints can be symmetric. This family has a delicate support structure related to error-correcting codes. Local holographic transformations are fundamental in its tractability. We prove a complexity dichotomy theorem for all Holant problems defined by any real valued constraint function set on Boolean variables and contains two 0-1 pinning functions. Previously, dichotomy for the same framework was only known for symmetric constraint functions. The set L supplies the last piece of tractability. We also prove a dichotomy for a variant of counting CSP as a technical component toward this Holant dichotomy. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Li Z.; Han Z.; Lu S.; Wang H.
Title: Combustion characteristics and suppression behaviour of HTPB-based composite solid propellants by typical inorganic powder suppressants
Abstract: HTPB/AP/Al-based composite solid propellants are high-energy solid fuels whose combustion involves coupled condensed-phase decomposition, gas-phase reactions, surface regression and aluminium-particle combustion. In the event of an accidental ignition, the substance in question has the potential to undergo rapid flame development and intense heat release. This renders effective suppression a matter of paramount importance in order to ensure safety. In this study, five typical inorganic powder suppressants, Mg(OH)2, Al(OH)3, NaHCO3, NH4H2PO4, and CaCO3, were evaluated under open-combustion conditions using a self-designed suppression apparatus. High-speed imaging, infrared thermography, time-resolved emission spectroscopy, and thermogravimetric analysis were used to characterize their thermal response and suppression behaviour. The combustion process could be divided into initial combustion, developing combustion, steady combustion and extinguishment stages. After ignition, the propellant formed a continuous flame, followed by increasing apparent temperature and sustained combustion before final decay. TG results showed distinct decomposition features: NaHCO3 decomposed rapidly at low temperature, Al(OH)3 and Mg(OH)2 exhibited dehydration-dominated decomposition, NH4H2PO4 underwent broad multi-stage decomposition, and CaCO3 decomposed mainly at high temperature. After powder injection, all powders reduced the infrared apparent temperature, but their transient cooling and post-injection stability differed. NaHCO3 produced rapid initial cooling, Al(OH)3 and Mg(OH)2 showed sustained flame attenuation, CaCO3 induced gradual flame weakening, and NH4H2PO4 exhibited strong instantaneous cooling accompanied by temperature rebound and spectral fluctuation. These results indicate that the evaluation of particle-assisted intervention in HTPB/AP/Al solid-fuel combustion should encompass both transient thermal response and post-injection flame stability. Title: Gelation profiles of pulse proteins: Implications of dry and wet extraction of faba and mung bean
Abstract: In this study, heat-induced gelation was used as a model process to compare the functional properties of pulse protein concentrates extracted using dry fractionation, and isolates from wet fractionation. Faba bean and mung bean protein with contrasting storage protein compositions, particularly different legumin – to – vicilin ratios were examined. From molecular analysis of the protein, faba bean was identified to be rich in legumin – like protein and mung bean was high in vicilin – like proteins. Rheological temperature ramp measurements revealed isolates exhibited lower critical gelation temperatures and stronger gel strength than concentrates. For the first time, to our knowledge, we attempted to characterise the critical gelation point of dry fractionated pulse protein, utilising Generalised Fractional Kelvin-Voigt viscoelastic solid model to elaborate viscoelasticity, and Herschel-Bulkley model to flow behaviour of the gels. Faba bean may form more weakly connected heterogeneous gel structures than mung bean. Regarding pasting profiles, concentrates underwent continuous viscosity changes compared to the isolates, owing to the presence of carbohydrates. Faba bean isolate gel strength was higher than mung bean isolate at 120°C, but at 90°C, mung bean isolate gel was firmer due to the different denaturation temperature of the dominant storage proteins; ∼80°C for vicilin and ∼100°C for legumin. Concentrates led to comparable final gel strength between the two pulses. These findings can assist to expand the potential use of pulse proteins in industrial applications such as meat analogues or bakery products for isolates or as thickening agents for concentrates. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Complex structured meat analogues via hybrid extrusion printing by incorporation of oil-containing ionically gelling alginate binders
Abstract: Over recent decades, consumer demand has driven meat analogue development. While alternatives to minced meat products (e.g. patties and sausages) are widely available, replication of whole-cut meat products remains challenging due to their complex structure and composition including muscle fiber bundles as well as fat-rich connective tissue, which largely determine appearance, flavor, and texture. In this study, the applicability of novel a bi-stream breaker plate system in high-moisture twin-screw extrusion was investigated for the production of structurally complex, multi-phase meat analogues. An inline external gelation approach was employed using CaCl2-containing protein-mass to solidify alginate-based binders. Protein-mass temperature (100, 120, 140 °C), binder flow fraction relative to the extrudate (0, 4, 7, 13 wt%), and dispersed oil content in the binder (0, 10, 20 wt%) were varied independently. Samples were optically assessed (tearing analysis, Cryo-SEM, CLSM) and mechanical testing (texture profile analysis, cutting tests). Additionally, the rheological behavior of the protein-mass was characterized in dependence of temperature and CaCl2 concentration. Results show predominantly homogeneous binder distributions up to protein-mass temperatures of 120 °C. Increasing binder fraction did not affect its distribution across the extrudate width. Mechanical analysis revealed a continuous decrease in chewiness (up to 48 % reduction), while anisotropy increased by 40 % upon initial binder incorporation. Increasing the dispersed oil fraction reduced chewiness (up to 17 % reduction). Microstructural analysis confirmed that binder layers spatially separated protein strands, thereby inhibiting their recombination. This scalable extrusion-based process thus represents a promising alternative to 3D-printing, combining protein-rich and oil-rich layers into complex structures. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Enzymatic deamidation softens thermal-induced whey protein gels by reducing covalent crosslinking and aggregate size
Abstract: Excessive rigidity, rubbery texture, and limited lubrication remain major challenges for heat-induced whey protein (WP) gels at high protein concentrations. This study used glutaminase (PG)-induced enzymatic deamidation to soften WP gels and elucidate the underlying mechanism. WP solutions at 10% (w/v) were treated with glutaminase at 0-25 U/g protein and subsequently heated to form gels. From 0 to 25 U/g protein, gelation time increased significantly from 13.3 to 21.8 min (p < 0.05), accompanied by reduced gel elasticity. Stress-relaxation analysis showed faster stress dissipation and weaker load-bearing capacity, with the characteristic relaxation time decreasing from 2.76 to 0.33 s and the instantaneous peak stress response decreasing to 12.3% of the control at the highest PG level. Texture profile analysis showed pronounced reductions in hardness and chewiness, while water-holding capacity increased significantly from 79.2% to 98.3% (p < 0.05). Tribological measurements showed improved low-speed lubrication of deamidated gels. Scanning electron microscopy revealed fewer large aggregates and a more homogeneous gel network after deamidation. X-ray scattering showed the Rg of the small structural units decreasing significantly from 7.12 to 5.73 nm (p < 0.05) and the large-scale protein assemblies decreasing from 71.56 to 44.47 nm. Deamidation also reduced disulfide bond content from 11.4 to 7.8 μmol/g, increased protein extractability in dissociating solvents. These findings demonstrate that PG-induced deamidation provides a green approach for developing softer high protein gel-based foods with improved lubrication and water retention. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Microstructural evolution and gamma-ray attenuation performance of cement-geopolymers composites for biological radiation shielding applications
Abstract: This study presents the development and characterisation of geopolymer-mortar blends with a view to establish a correlation between the physical and microstructural attributes of the mixture with their gamma-radiation shielding performances. OPC mortar-geopolymer composites were fabricated by blending (20%, 30%, and 40%) metakaolin-based geopolymer , synthesized using NaOH/Na2SiO3 alkaline activator and locally calcined kaolin with OPC-based mortar. The resulting composites were characterized microstructurally and chemically using SEM/EDS, with bulk density determined via the Archimedes method. Gamma-ray shielding performance was assessed through the mass attenuation coefficients, (MAC) and other photon interaction cross-section-based parameters for photon energies within 10 MeV. An increase in the geopolymer content promoted physical and microstructural densification, reduced surface voids, and improved the homogeneity of the OPC mortar-geopolymer composites microstructure. For composite containing 20%, 30%, and 40% geopolymer blend, the density was 2.24 g/cm3, 2.35 g/cm3 and 2.47 g/cm3, respectively. The increase in sample density resulted in increase in the MAC of samples. MAC varied within 0.0244–13.8000 cm2/g, 0.0245–14.2100 cm2/g, and 0.0248–15.1100 cm2/g, respectively, for mortars containing 20%, 30%, and 40% geopolymer gel. The increasing proportion of geopolymer did not significantly alter the gamma buildup factors of the geopolymer-OPC mortar composites. The potential shielding performance of the mortar composite was comparable to conventional shielding materials, other geopolymer composites and OPC mortars. There was a strong relationship between density, microstructure and gamma-shielding performance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: WENO-type nonlinear reconstructions based on spline quasi-interpolation for discontinuous functions

Abstract: We introduce a novel nonlinear reconstruction framework for univariate functions exhibiting discontinuities, employing quasi-interpolating splines of degree d=2,3,4,5. A key feature of the new operators Rd is that the number of subintervals affected by the loss of accuracy is reduced to the single interval containing the discontinuity, whereas classical WENO quasi-interpolants suffer from degraded accuracy over a neighbourhood of size proportional to the B-spline support. Numerical experiments demonstrate the efficacy of our approach in various scenarios, highlighting its potential for applications in computational mathematics and engineering. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Wang Y.; Gong Y.; Song X.; Guo Q.; Yu G.
Title: In-situ study of O/C ratio effects on axial dominant thermal behaviors of particle groups in an opposed multi-burner CWS gasi fier
Abstract: Clarifying the proportion and dominant thermal behaviors of particle groups at different axial zones is critical for boosting carbon conversion efficiency and optimizing industrial gasifier operation, yet relevant quantitative in-situ observations inside gasifiers remain insufficient. This study adopted an intensified high-speed optical measurement system integrating a 650 nm narrow-band filter and image intensifier, and modified a hybrid image processing algorithm. In-situ measurements were implemented at the impinging-plug flow zone 1.5 inner gasifier diameters beneath the burner of a bench-scale opposed multi-burner (OMB) coal-water slurry (CWS) gasifier. This study aims to reveal how oxygen-carbon (O/C) ratios regulate axial dominant thermal behaviors. The results show that low O/C condition yields unimodal particle distribution dominated by char oxidation, while bimodal distribution emerges at O/C≥1.0 with volatile-combustion large particles prevailing. Light char particles flow slowly under recirculation, whereas massive volatile particles move faster under strengthened axial airflow. Char particles exhibit uniform surface temperature, while volatile particles are surrounded by fluctuating flames with obvious temperature gradients. Raising O/C significantly lifts overall particle temperature and shifts the boundary between char-dominated upper zone and volatile-dominated lower zone upward within the imaging area. Such reversed axial differentiation of dominant thermal behaviors arises from asynchronous reaction progress of fine fast-consumed particles and large delayed devolatilization droplets. Authors: Liu S.; Xiao J.; Mao Y.; Li D.; Liu H.; Li G.; Tian Y.
Title: Prediction and analysis of modal characteristics for thin-walled shells with flexible support by contact modeling
Abstract: Flexible support technology is widely used for high-quality machining of thin-walled structures in the aerospace industry. Therefore, this paper proposes a modal characteristic prediction method for thin-walled shells with pneumatic support head, which simultaneously characterizes the micro-contact mechanism and macro-dynamics behavior of the support system. First, based on the modal test results, contact characteristics between the shell and support balls are analyzed from the perspective of micro-deformation. Subsequently, a coupled dynamics model of support system is established by Rayleigh-Ritz method to predict frequency response functions and modal parameters under various support conditions. To describe the micro-contact mechanism, the semi-analytical models for the support stiffness and damping within contact interfaces are developed based on fractal contact theory. In this model, surface and deformation contact coefficients are introduced to reflect the influence of surface geometry and shell’s static deformation on the contact characteristics. Furthermore, a rapid identification method for the deformation contact coefficient and cylinder damping is proposed to enhance prediction accuracy. Finally, modal tests confirm that the proposed method exhibits excellent predictive capability, keeping the errors of the 1st- and 2nd-order natural frequencies and modal amplitudes to within 2.5% and 13.5% under multi-point support conditions. Authors: Wang Y.; Xu Z.; Luo Y.; Xu H.; Chen T.; Zhang R.; Wang Y.
Title: Zero bandgap graphene mediators enable efficient environmental remediation by interfacial electronic conduits boosting charge separation in BiOCl/graphene/UiO-66 heterojunction

Abstract: Constructing active visible-light-responsive frameworks from wide-bandgap semiconductors remains a profound challenge in solar energy conversion. Herein, a noble-metal-free ternary heterojunction, BiOCl/graphene/UiO-66 (BGU), was successfully engineered via a facile solvothermal route. Under a low-power white LED light source (400–780 nm), the wide-bandgap BiOCl and UiO-66 components remain inactive, positioning the near-zero-bandgap graphene (GN) as the exclusive visible-light harvester and electron donor. Comprehensive structural, optical, and electrochemical characterizations reveal that the strategic integration of GN establishes high-velocity interfacial electronic conduits, significantly reducing charge-transfer resistance and boosting carrier separation dynamics. Authors: Liang J.; Wang X.; Du F.; Zhang H.; Wang Y.; Rong Y.; Lin K.; Xia D.; Tao B.; Zhang J.; Yang Y.
Title: Breaking the performance trade-offs of nano-metal fuels: ammonium perchlorate-mediated high-performance energetic microspheres
Abstract: Simultaneously achieving high energy density, rapid reaction kinetics, and practical processability remains a fundamental challenge for metal fuels in next-generation solid propellants. Here, high-performance energetic microspheres (HPEMs) are established as a particle-level energetic composite by integrating nano-aluminum, nano-boron, and ammonium perchlorate into individual energetic microspheres, enabling intrinsic property complementarity to evolve into combustion synergy. Specifically, the optimized HPEMs deliver a combustion heat of 24.0 kJ g−1, 1.86 and 1.48 times higher than those of the Al@AP and B@AP counterparts, respectively. They exhibit the shortest ignition delay (577.2 ± 31.6 ms), accelerated flame propagation, and a balanced combustion duration (88.3 ± 5.0 ms), demonstrating efficient kinetic coupling between rapid Al oxidation and sustained boron combustion. The particle-level architecture suppresses nanoparticle aggregation, reducing slurry viscosity of propellant from 138.380 to 61.596 Pa·s while maintaining superior combustion performance in propellant formulations. Mechanistic investigations demonstrate that rapid Al/AP combustion establishes a self-sustained high-temperature oxidizing environment, which promotes the dynamic evolution of the molten B2O3 layer, facilitates oxygen transport to the boron core, and continuously activates boron oxidation. Consequently, the rapid reaction kinetics of nano-aluminum are effectively transferred into sustained boron oxidation, establishing a synergistic combustion pathway that combines rapid reaction kinetics with continuous high-energy release. Authors: Ren X.; Deng J.; Zhang Y.; Li Y.; Zhang Y.
Title: Study on the spontaneous combustion characteristics and synergistic effects of coal-gangue mixtures
Abstract: To investigate the spontaneous combustion characteristics and synergistic effects of the coal-gangue mixtures, liquid nitrogen adsorption, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy and thermal property testing were employed to analyse the differences in pore structure, microscopic characteristics and thermal properties between coal and gangue. Thermogravimetric analysis was conducted to investigate the mass changes, characteristic temperatures and oxidation kinetics during the spontaneous combustion process of the coal-gangue mixturess with different mass ratios. The results indicate that coal and gangue exhibit significant differences in pore structure, microscopic composition and thermal properties. Coal contains more abundant active groups and higher combustible matter content, whereas gangue possesses a more developed pore structure and superior heat transfer and thermal conductivity properties. During the spontaneous combustion process of coal-gangue mixtures, the mass changes and characteristic temperatures exhibited different degrees of variation compared with those of the individual components. With the increase in coal mass fraction, the evaporation of moisture, oxygen adsorption and combustion reactions in the mixtures were gradually enhanced. Further analysis revealed that, during the low-temperature oxidation stage, the experimental values of mass change in the coal-gangue mixtures were higher than the theoretical calculation values, whereas the experimental values of apparent activation energy were lower than the calculated values, indicating that a positive synergistic effect existed between coal and gangue, which promoted low-temperature oxidation reactions. During the combustion stage, the combustion peaks of volatile matter and fixed carbon in the mixed samples were generally shifted to higher temperatures, accompanied by an increase in apparent activation energy. However, the proportion of the volatile matter combustion peak area increased in the experimental results, whereas the combustion of fixed carbon was inhibited, demonstrating a phased synergistic effect. Principal component analysis indicated that the coal–oxygen reaction consistently dominated in coal-gangue mixtures with different mass ratios. This study elucidated the synergistic oxidation mechanisms during the spontaneous combustion process of coal-gangue mixtures, providing a theoretical basis for mine fire prevention and control and the prevention and control of spontaneous combustion in coal-gangue stockpiles. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhan L.; Deng Q.; Chen W.; Yu Y.; Li G.; Shen J.; Chen B.
Title: Analysis of two-phase flow evolution of the parallel skeleton flow field in proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers based on the volume of fluid-coupled method
Abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer (PEMWE) are regarded as one of the most promising green hydrogen production devices, boasting advantages such as zero emissions, high hydrogen production efficiency, and excellent long-term stability. The polarization performance and mass transfer characteristics of PEMWE are largely governed by factors such as the flow field configuration and the aggregation of oxygen bubbles, which remain key constraints for performance enhancement. This study focuses on investigating the two-phase flow evolution process in parallel skeleton flow field (PSFF) using the Volume of Fluid (VOF) method, aiming to improve the operational performance of PEMWE. In this paper, two structures with three-parallel skeleton flow field (3-PSFF) and five-parallel skeleton flow field (5-PSFF) are designed, and the skeleton surface is divided into upper, middle and lower sections to regulate contact angle distribution. The results indicate that among all configurations of the 3-PSFF, the contact angle gradient of 30°–50°–70° delivers the optimal oxygen discharge performance, accompanied by the lowest average pressure drop in flow channels. For the 5-PSFF, the uniform contact angle configuration of 50°–50°–50° achieves the best comprehensive performance. Through systematic analysis, it is concluded that hydrophilic contact angle layouts can effectively enhance the working performance of PEMWE. Authors: Li Z.; Yin B.; Xu Y.; Huang Q.; Zhan H.; Xiang X.; Li S.
Title: Phase transition mechanism of thermotropic-condensation protein gels induced by the concentration of lysozyme
Abstract: The mechanism by which macromolecular crowding regulates the phase transition of thermostable proteins such as lysozyme (LYS) remains unclear. In this study, the concentration-dependent (12%, 24%, and 32% w/w) gelation behavior of LYS subjected to heating (90 °C) followed by cooling was systematically characterized using multi-scale approaches including rheology, aggregation kinetics, spectroscopy, and microscopy. At 12% LYS, weak crowding leads to limited unfolding and ineffective aggregation, with hardness as low as 0.47 g and storage modulus (G′ = 0.58 Pa), and the system remains a sol. At 24% LYS, moderate crowding induces substantial pre-unfolding during heating, and cooling then triggers ordered aggregation that overcomes the gelation energy barrier, resulting in cold-dominated gelation with hardness reaching 34.31 g and G′ of 52.43 Pa. At 32% LYS, extreme crowding drives the system to reach the critical aggregation already during heating (G′ = 1836 Pa), and cooling further strengthens the network to form a dense gel (hardness = 57.95 g, G′ = 29678 Pa). Title: Development and characterization of an active and smart gelatin-alginate based packaging enriched with eggplant anthocyanin-rich extract
Abstract: Bio-functional films were developed based on a gelatin-alginate hydrocolloid matrix, incorporated with anthocyanin-rich powder extracted from eggplant peels at different concentrations (0.5-2 mg/mL). In addition, anthocyanins incorporation significantly improved the optical properties, reducing lightness (L*) and yellowness (b*), and increasing redness (a*) of the films as well as the total color difference (ΔE), and subsequently, increasing their opacity, contributing to the global enhancement of the light barrier of the films.Regarding functional properties, the incorporation of anthocyanin-powder enhanced biological properties of the films in a dose-dependent manner at multiple endpoints: increased antioxidant activities against DPPH, ABTS and reducing power, in addition to antibacterial capacities against Gram positive (Bacillus cereus and Staphylococcus aureus) and Gram negative (Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherishia coli) bacteria, which was directly associated with their phenolic content. Authors: Li J.; Fu X.; Song H.; Xia Y.; Yang Y.
Title: A timestep-based mass-scaling NCDDAM for efficient thermal–mechanical fracture modelling in rock masses
Abstract: Rock masses in deep underground engineering are commonly subjected to complex thermal–mechanical interactions induced by geological conditions and engineering disturbances. However, an explicit thermal–mechanical coupled analysis is usually restricted by the smallest stable timestep, which is often determined by the mechanical field rather than the thermal field, resulting in excessive computational costs for long-duration simulations. To overcome this limitation, this study proposes an enhanced nodal-based continuous-discontinuous deformation analysis method (NCDDAM) incorporating a timestep-based mass scaling technique. By scaling the mechanically controlled stable timestep to be consistent with that of the thermal field, the proposed numerical model substantially reduces the total number of computational steps and provides an efficient and practical tool for long-term thermal–mechanical damage and stability analysis of deep rock masses. © 2026

Title: DNN-CNN-based analysis of autoignition and combustion characteristics of DME/NH3 homogeneous mixtures under marine engine relevant conditions
Abstract: Dimethyl ether (DME)/ammonia (NH3) blended-fuel combustion has significant potential for low-carbon emissions and high-efficiency energy utilization. Zero-dimensional homogeneous combustion models coupled with chemical mechanisms can predict the autoignition characteristics of homogeneous mixtures. However, they cannot effectively describe autoignition combustion behavior under transient temperature and pressure variations. In this study, a computational program was developed using a self-established homogeneous combustion simulation model to investigate the autoignition combustion behavior of DME/NH3 homogeneous mixtures during transient temperature and pressure variations under marine engine relevant conditions. A homogeneous reactor model was used to describe the in-cylinder process, while gas exchange and heat transfer were considered. Intake temperature, intake pressure, fuel composition, intake valve closing timing (IVC), and exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) rate were used as basic operating parameters to generate the pressure-curve dataset. A dual surrogate model consisting of a deep neural network (DNN) and a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) was constructed. The DNN was used to predict peak pressure and maximum pressure rise rate, and its outputs were combined with the basic operating parameters as inputs to the 1D-CNN to reconstruct the pressure curve. By coupling the surrogate models with particle swarm optimization, using the basic operating parameters as decision variables and thermal efficiency as the screening objective, the intrinsic autoignition and combustion characteristics of the mixture and their effects on thermal efficiency were analyzed under four representative loads. Title: Meta-analysis and cross-source modeling of protein air–water adsorption kinetics
Abstract: Formulating aerated foods relies on proteins that rapidly adsorb to newly formed air–water interfaces, yet dynamic surface pressure, Π(t), has rarely been systematically analyzed across protein sources or used to predict adsorption behavior for unmeasured proteins. The study then evaluated whether complete adsorption curves could be predicted for entirely unseen protein sources using leave-one-source-out validation with two complementary approaches: a structured kinetic model and a machine-learning model, TabPFN. Authors: Turk C.G.; Dincer I.
Title: Experimental investigation of a new and more effective fuel cell stack
Abstract: Ammonium formate is a water-soluble, hydrogen-rich compound with potential application as a liquid fuel in electrochemical energy conversion systems. In this study, a passive ammonium formate fuel cell comprising an aluminum anode, a stainless-steel air-breathing cathode, and a cation exchange membrane (CMI-7000S) was experimentally investigated without external pumps, compressors, or active gas-supply equipment. The effects of operating temperature and different concentrations of Al(OH)3, KHCO3, Na2SO4, and Mg additives were evaluated. Increasing the operating temperature from room temperature to 80 °C increased the current density from approximately 27.30 to 58.71 mA/cm2 and the power density from approximately 5.61 to 27.27 mW/cm2. The corresponding energy and exergy efficiencies increased from 8.4% to 16.2% and from 7.2% to 15.7%, respectively. Over the 120-min experiments conducted at 80 °C, 1 M Al(OH)3 produced average current and power densities of 62.60 mA/cm2 and 29.87 mW/cm2, compared with 24.71 mA/cm2 and 5.05 mW/cm2 for 0.1 M Al(OH)3. Title: Fast randomized PVR-PCA for NLA-oriented leading subspace computation
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: Computing the leading k-dimensional subspace of large-scale matrices is a foundational task in numerical linear algebra (NLA), but repeated full-data products and matrix factorizations can be costly when both matrix dimensions are large. To address these issues, we propose Projected Variance-Reduced PCA (PVR-PCA), a fast randomized algorithm tailored for NLA-oriented subspace computation. PVR-PCA integrates two NLA-optimized innovations: (1) projection-enhanced variance reduction, which replaces VR-PCA's SVD-based orthogonal alignment by an unconstrained least-squares projection; and (2) QR-based orthogonalization, which replaces polar/SVD orthogonalization by thin QR factorization. Together, these changes reduce the dense-kernel per-inner-iteration cost by [Formula Presented] FLOPs compared with VR-PCA. Theoretical analysis establishes high-probability convergence to the leading subspace of the sample covariance matrix. It also gives a conditional warm-start guarantee for a Gaussian-plus-one-power-iteration initializer whenever its realized subspace error satisfies the stated threshold. Title: Cyclicity and convex-cyclicity of weighted composition operators on the harmonic Fock space

Abstract: We characterize cyclicity, convex-cyclicity, and supercyclicity for weighted composition operators and their adjoints on the harmonic Fock space. Title: Experimental and numerical investigation of dendrite fragmentation, solute concentration, and channel formation in a transparent NH4Cl-70.43%H2O solution

Title: Rotational relaxation of a torque-driven spherical particle in a micropolar fluid
Abstract: The transient rotational relaxation of a rigid spherical particle subjected to a suddenly applied constant torque is investigated in an incompressible micropolar fluid. The analysis is performed within the framework of Eringen’s micropolar continuum theory under creeping-flow conditions. Velocity-slip and spin-slip boundary conditions are incorporated to account for interfacial effects. The governing equations are solved analytically in the Laplace transform domain. The transient particle angular velocity is then recovered by numerical inversion of the transformed solution. An exact analytical solution is also obtained in the Newtonian limit and is used to validate the general formulation. The results show that the angular velocity increases monotonically toward its steady-state value, whereas the angular acceleration decays continuously with time. Increasing the particle-to-fluid density ratio delays the rotational response because of enhanced particle inertia. Stronger micropolar coupling introduces additional hydrodynamic resistance and prolongs the relaxation process. In contrast, increasing the spin parameter accelerates the transient response by reducing the resistance to microrotation at the particle surface. The slip parameter exhibits a non-monotonic influence. Moderate slip enhances the rotational response, whereas excessive slip weakens the hydrodynamic coupling between the particle and the surrounding fluid. Overall, the results demonstrate that fluid microstructure and interfacial slip jointly govern the transient transfer of angular momentum. Title: Multi-granularity dynamic spatio-temporal fusion graph convolutional network for traffic flow forecasting

Second, a spatially independent dynamic temporal graph learns node-specific and layer-specific temporal dependencies, capturing heterogeneous pattern evolution across both granularities. Title: Optimizing melt–stretch properties in yeast protein vegan mozzarella analogues through protein–starch interactions

Title: Effects of biomass composition on hydrogen yield and char formation during supercritical water gasification: A thermodynamic analysis
Abstract: Biomass is composed of cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin, whose relative proportions influence H2 production and char formation during supercritical water gasification (SCWG). Title: Optimization of wave steepness in sinusoidal-serpentine flow fields for high performance PEM water electrolyzer
Abstract: Sinusoidal-serpentine flow fields can effectively enhance the mass transfer process in proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer (PEMWE), but the impact of its wave steepness on PEMWE performance remains insufficiently understood. Herein, a three-dimensional, gas-liquid two-phase, non-isothermal numerical PEMWE model with sinusoidal-serpentine flow field was developed considering six wave steepness cases ( S = 0.1–0.6) at a fixed wavelength of λ = 10.0 mm. The results reveal a non-monotonic dependence of PEMWE performance on wave steepness. The moderate wave steepness ( S = 0.4) exhibits the best overall performance, achieving an average current density of 1.22 A·cm−2 at 2.0 V, which is 22.00% higher than the reference sinusoidal-serpentine flow field ( S = 0.1). This improvement is attributed to enhanced periodic channel curvature as S increases from 0.1 to 0.4, which promotes transverse liquid-water transport, alleviates localized product-gas accumulation, and improves the uniformity of velocity, oxygen concentration, and temperature fields. The corresponding non-uniformity indices decrease by 15.63%, 15.38%, and 4.35%, respectively. However, further increasing S to 0.5 and 0.6 causes excessive channel undulation, which aggravates local flow non-uniformity and impairs product-gas removal, reducing the average current density by 7.38% and 14.75%, respectively, relative to the S = 0.4 case. The comprehensive TOPSIS evaluation further confirms S = 0.4 as the optimal wave steepness among the investigated cases at λ = 10.0 mm, with the highest score of 0.87. Title: Computational fluid dynamics in hydrogen internal combustion engines: a review of current applications, challenges, and future directions
Abstract: Hydrogen internal combustion engines (H2ICEs) have emerged as a promising pathway toward low-carbon transportation due to hydrogen’s high energy content and carbon-free combustion characteristics. However, the implementation of H2ICEs remains challenging because of hydrogen’s unique combustion properties. These include high flame speed, low ignition energy, and wide flammability range, alongside risks of nitrogen oxides (NOx) emissions, pre-ignition, and material incompatibility. Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) has become an essential tool for understanding and optimizing H2ICE operation by providing detailed insights into hydrogen injection, in-cylinder flow development, fuel–air mixing, combustion evolution, heat transfer, and emission formation. This review presents a comprehensive analysis of the CFD modelling framework for H2ICE applications, focusing on turbulence modelling, combustion models, mesh strategies, chemical kinetics, abnormal combustion prediction, and experimental validation approaches. Advanced CFD techniques, including Reynolds-Averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS), Unsteady RANS (URANS), Large Eddy Simulation (LES), and hybrid RANS/LES methods, are critically evaluated based on their accuracy and computational requirements. While RANS/URANS approaches remain widely adopted for engineering-scale simulations, LES provides improved prediction of hydrogen jet behaviour, turbulent structures, and cycle-to-cycle variability at higher computational costs. The review further examines the challenges associated with hydrogen combustion modelling, particularly thin flame structures, thermo-diffusive instabilities, turbulence–chemistry interaction, and accurate prediction of laminar flame speed (LFS) and ignition characteristics. Furthermore, the importance of robust validation using optical diagnostics, in-cylinder pressure measurements, and heat-release-rate analysis is highlighted to improve CFD reliability. Future research directions are identified, including hydrogen-specific turbulence–chemistry interaction models, adaptive mesh refinement, machine-learning-assisted CFD acceleration, digital twin integration, and multi-physics modelling frameworks. By addressing current modelling limitations and strengthening validation methodologies, CFD can serve as a powerful approach for bridging experimental investigations and industrial H2ICE development, accelerating the transition toward efficient and sustainable hydrogen-powered engine technologies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Investigation of Sb-based perovskite-type hydrides by using first-principles calculations for advance energy storage
Source title: International Journal of Modern Physics C
Abstract: This study employs first-principles calculations based on DFT, as implemented in the CASTEP code, to conduct a comprehensive investigation of the structural, electronic, optical, mechanical and hydrogen storage properties of Sb-based perovskite-type hydrides XSbH3 (X=Li, Na, K, Rb). The GGA-PBE exchange-correlation functional was used to optimize the crystal structures, yielding lattice parameters of 4.01, 4.18, 4.26 and 4.30Å for LiSbH3, NaSbH3, KSbH3 and RbSbH3, respectively. The thermodynamic and mechanical stability of both compounds are confirmed through negative formation energy and Born stability criteria, respectively. The results reveal a zero band gap in all materials, establishing their metallic character, which is further corroborated by a detailed analysis of the total and partial densities of states. The optical properties, including the dielectric function, extinction coefficient, refractive index, reflectivity, absorption coefficient, optical conductivity and loss function, are also examined in detail. Mechanical analysis based on the elastic constants confirms that all the studied compounds are mechanically stable. All of the investigated materials are found to be ductile except LiSbH3. Further analysis of mechanical properties shows that these materials are anisotropic and harder, as evidenced by their anisotropic index and elastic moduli values, respectively. The gravimetric hydrogen storage capacity is calculated as 2.30, 2.05, 1.85 and 1.44wt.% for LiSbH3, NaSbH3, KSbH3 and RbSbH3, respectively, demonstrating that LiSbH3 is capable of accommodating a substantial quantity of hydrogen. Thus, this work represents the first theoretical and systematic study of Sb-based perovskite-type hydrides, and its findings can serve as a valuable reference for future experimental synthesis and device-level evaluation of this novel class of hydrogen storage materials. © 2027 World Scientific Publishing Company.

Title: An integrated NMR-based approach to assess hydrocarbon cleanup from fracture interfaces in shale
Abstract: The persistence of oil as thin, discrete coatings and isolated accumulations renders the direct quantification of hydrocarbons on rough, fractured shale surfaces highly challenging. Enhanced production in fracture-dominated tight formations can potentially be achieved through the effective removal of oil retained at fracture interfaces. This study presents a robust quantitative framework to evaluate fracture-surface cleanup efficiency in shale systems by integrating dynamic fluid exposure with relaxation-based monitoring techniques. An integrated and rigorous experimental methodology was developed, combining wettability assessment, Mancos shale fracture surface characterization, and sequential injection experiments monitored using proton nuclear magnetic resonance (1H NMR). Fluid-surface interactions were first established through wettability measurements on uniform shale substrates. High-resolution profilometry was employed to characterize fracture surface roughness and to elucidate the tortuous flow channels formed by geometrically superimposed fractured interfaces. Various analytical measurements were conducted to characterize the Mancos shale samples. A series of dynamic sequential injection experiments were conducted at a constant injection pressure of 2 MPa and a confining pressure of 4 MPa. The use of deuterated brine (D2O) minimized the aqueous-phase proton background and enhanced sensitivity to changes in proton-bearing fluids within the fracture system, enabling relative assessment of hydrocarbon-associated fluid evolution through cumulative T2 relaxation responses. Significant hydrocarbon retention at fracture surfaces was observed following exposure to n-Decane. Subsequent aqueous-phase injection resulted in approximately 57.30 % removal of residual hydrocarbons, while the subsequent emulsion-treatment stage produced a total NMR-derived relative cleanup efficiency of 79.96 %. This corresponds to an additional 22.66 % incremental reduction in the hydrocarbon-associated NMR response observed during the emulsion-treatment stage following aqueous treatment. These findings highlight the strong potential of emulsions for effective residual oil removal from fracture interfaces, thereby contributing to improved production performance in tight, fracture-dominated shale formations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Li A.; Cui X.; Tang J.; Yang Z.; Yang L.
Title: Photothermal-enhanced bifunctional Bi-doped CdS for coupled H2 evolution and selective alcohol oxidation
Abstract: Integrating photocatalytic H2 evolution with selective organic oxidation constitutes a sustainable strategy for coproducing clean fuel and value-added chemicals. However, this technology continues to face significant challenges, including sluggish charge separation, limited product selectivity, and restricted light utilization. Herein, we constructed a Bi-doped CdS (Bi-CdS) photocatalyst through hydrothermal method. The substitutional incorporation of Bi3+ into the CdS lattice extends the light absorption range to 800 nm, modulates the electronic structure, and induces a localized photothermal effect. Consequently, the optimized 0.5% Bi-CdS catalyst exhibits substantially reduced kinetic barriers for coupled proton reduction and alcohol dehydrogenation, exhibiting a 4.8-fold enhancement in H2 generation and a 5.1-fold improvement in benzaldehyde production relative to pristine CdS. The selectivity of benzyl alcohol oxidation to benzaldehyde approaches nearly 100%. The photothermal synergy arising from Bi3+ doping further accelerates the coupled redox reaction, resulting in an enhanced H2 evolution of 2.46 mmol g-1h−1 with a simultaneous benzaldehyde production rate of 2.42 mmol g-1h−1 over the catalyst at 313.15 K. Mechanistic studies identify the Ph(OH)CH· radical as the pivotal intermediate in the selective oxidation pathway. These findings indicate that Bi-doped CdS can function as a promising photothermal-assisted catalyst for simultaneous H2 production and alcohol upgrading, and we anticipate that this work will offer valuable insights for the rational design of dual-functional photothermal catalysts in solar-driven chemical conversion. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Compositional variation and heat-induced gelation of pea flour dispersions
Abstract: Heat-induced gelation of pea flour reflects interactions among starch, protein, fibre, and minerals, but relationships between flour composition and gelation remain insufficiently understood. In this study, 96 genetically diverse pea accessions were screened for main composition and protein profile. Based on starch content, accessions were classified as high-starch (≥40%) or low-starch (<40%), and 18 representative accessions were selected for analysis of supernatant particle size, protein distribution, and rheological behaviour. High-starch flours generally had higher amylopectin/amylose and legumin/vicilin ratios but lower protein, ash, and fibre-rich fraction than low-starch flours. Low-starch accessions generally showed larger and more heterogeneous particles in the non-heated supernatant, whereas protein distribution overlapped considerably between groups. For group-level rheological analysis, high-starch and low-starch samples were prepared at 12% and 18%, respectively, to obtain self-supporting gels. These formulations had comparable average total starch contents in the final gels (∼5.1%) but differed in amylose, amylopectin, protein, ash, and fibre-rich fraction. High-starch samples showed higher G′ at the end of heating and greater deformation tolerance, whereas low-starch samples showed higher final G′ after cooling but lower deformation tolerance. Principal component analysis showed that rheological properties were more closely associated with starch and amylopectin in the high-starch group, but with a broader combination of compositional and supernatant particle characteristics in the low-starch group. Title: Total fatigue life prediction of offshore pipeline structures based on surface integrity: crack initiation and propagation lives
Abstract: Assessing the fatigue life of offshore pipelines, which are critical infrastructure for hydrocarbon transport, is essential. This study proposes a surface‑integrity‑based total‑life prediction (SI‑TLP) method that separately quantifies crack initiation and propagation lives for X70 offshore pipeline structures. Surface residual stress and roughness are incorporated to adjust the working stress; initiation life is computed using damage mechanics, while propagation life is evaluated via fracture mechanics with the SMART adaptive remeshing technique. The framework is validated through full‑scale resonant fatigue tests. Results show that crack initiation accounts for 71.35 % of the total fatigue life in the simulation and 73.96 % in the experiment, with an overall prediction accuracy of 97.32 %. This confirms the accuracy of the proposed SI‑TLP method, and also indicates that surface integrity is a key factor determining the fatigue performance of pipelines. Additionally, a forward design approach for machined surface integrity, constrained by fatigue life, is established based on the SI‑TLP framework, offering a theoretical basis for anti‑fatigue manufacturing and life assessment of offshore pipeline structures. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Li S.; Fu X.; Chen Z.; Pan L.
Title: Reasoning-aware fake review detection via contextual integration of large language model generated rationales
Abstract: Fake reviews on e-commerce platforms undermine consumer trust and distort fair competition. Their detection remains challenging due to the subtle linguistic cues and intentional mimicry of authentic reviews. Although neural models capture surface-level semantics effectively, they often struggle to infer deceptive intent or assess commonsense plausibility, which limits the reliability of fake review detection. This work introduces LLM-Augmented Rationale Integration Network (LLM-RIN), a rationale-aware hybrid framework that integrates motivational intent and commonsense plausibility rationales generated by a large language model (LLM) into a small language model (SLM) classifier. Through rationale-level auxiliary supervision, cross-attentive review–rationale interaction, and usefulness-aware fusion, the framework improves interpretability and strengthens the ability to detect subtle deceptive patterns. A contrastive review–rationale alignment objective is further incorporated to encourage instance-level grounding and enhance robustness to noisy or drifting rationales. Experiments on YelpZip and YelpNYC-20K show that LLM-RIN consistently improves fake-class detection over competitive baselines, while class weighting provides a more recall-oriented operating point. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Luo Y.; Yu Y.; Cui X.; Luo N.; Feng X.; Cui F.; Ren P.; Tang H.; Qiao Z.; Liu W.
Title: Effect of Mo content on the tribocorrosion behavior of CoCrFeNiMox high-entropy alloys in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution
Abstract: The synergistic effect of corrosion and wear is a key factor limiting the service life of structural materials in marine environments. CoCrFeNiMox (x = 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6) high-entropy alloys were fabricated to clarify the role of Mo in tribocorrosion behavior. Quantitative synergy analysis, based on electrochemical and tribological testing, shows that Mo strongly affects passive-film stability and wear resistance. Mo0.2 exhibits the best corrosion resistance, while Mo0.6 demonstrates superior wear resistance. However, both Mo0 and Mo0.6 suffer from stronger corrosion–wear synergy due to high ΔW  C  values, associated with unstable passive films, σ-phase precipitation, and third-body abrasion. In contrast, Mo0.4 achieves the lowest total material loss by balancing hardness with a stable, self-healing passive film, thereby effectively suppressing synergy. Overall, wear dominates material removal ( ΔW > ΔC ), and moderate Mo addition (~0.4) provides the best compromise between corrosion and wear resistance. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Size-dependent in-plane shear behavior of Kevlar and Kevlar/Carbon composites with damage and hybridization mechanisms
Abstract: This study investigates in-plane shear behavior and size effects in 2D Kevlar and Kevlar/Carbon (K-C) hybrid laminates through modified lap shear tests, Digital Image Correlation, and Finite Element Analysis (FEA). Hybridization introduces marked differences in mechanical performance: K-C hybrids exhibit higher normal and shear strength than pure Kevlar laminates, attributed to the greater stiffness and buckling resistance of carbon fibers. Both material systems conform to Bažant's size effect law, with strength decreasing as in-plane dimensions increase—indicating a transition from plastic limit behavior in small specimens to Linear Elastic Fracture Mechanics (LEFM)-governed response in larger ones. Damage mechanisms transition from fiber buckling and matrix cracking to intra-laminar crack propagation. Kevlar laminates more closely approach the plastic limit due to fiber bridging, which suppresses fiber pull-out. FEA effectively captures the size-dependent response, revealing that the number of subcells between the strain concentration zone and the free edge increases with specimen size. The results demonstrate that hybridizing stiff fibers enhances shear strength but intensifies size effects. The number of subcells between the free edge and ligament is a key parameter for size effect estimation. These findings provide valuable guidance for enhancing the design and structural reliability of large-scale aerospace components. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS

Title: Modeling and steady-state limit cycles of the cardiovascular-autonomic negative feedback control dynamics: A system theoretic approach
Abstract: Understanding the dynamical interplay between the cardiovascular function and the autonomic neural control is fundamental for studying homeodynamic regulation and for clarifying the mechanisms that sustain physiological stability. This modular structure allows the individual subsystems to be combined into a unified, high-dimensional state-space model, providing a coherent system theoretic basis for formal closed-loop analysis. The model is implemented in the MATLAB/Simulink environment, and numerical simulations reveal persistent, self-sustained oscillations in the state variables. Phase-space analysis confirms the periodic nature of these oscillations and their convergence from different initial conditions, indicating that a stable limit-cycle arises from the system dynamics. By integrating a modular electrical analog with a system theoretic perspective, this framework reproduces realistic cardiovascular rhythms, highlighting emergent oscillatory patterns that are central to physiological regulation. Authors: Zheng C.; Wang Y.
Title: Chemical discrimination of wild and cultivated Dendrobium devonianum by ATR-FTIR spectroscopy and machine learning with targeted metabolomic analysis
Abstract: Wild and cultivated Dendrobium devonianum are visually similar, but their chemical differences complicate raw-material authentication. Recent spectroscopic studies of Dendrobium have focused primarily on species identification and geographical traceability, with limited chemical interpretation of wild–cultivated discrimination. Spectral differences were concentrated in the 1800–900 cm−1 fingerprint region, although unsupervised analyses showed substantial overlap between groups. Title: Transient transport of air ingress and methane dilution in negative-pressure coal mine methane drainage pipelines
Abstract: Pipeline defects in negative-pressure coal mine methane (CMM) drainage systems permit ambient air to enter under the pressure differential, causing flow redistribution, localized jet mixing, and methane dilution. Increasing the ingress-hole diameter from 50 to 120 mm intensified jet-induced momentum exchange and accelerated downstream propagation of the methane-depleted region. A greater local baseline pressure deficit produced a larger air-ingress flow rate, stronger methane dilution, and a shorter concentration–response time. Under a fixed 80 mm opening, larger pipes admitted a greater absolute air flow rate, whereas smaller pipes, associated with larger relative opening ratios d/D , exhibited stronger local mixing and faster concentration responses. Methane-concentration disturbances propagated predominantly along the main-flow direction, while upstream propagation was suppressed. These results indicate greater concentration–response sensitivity at downstream virtual monitoring locations under the investigated numerical conditions. Authors: Pan D.; Yu Z.; Qi Z.; Wu Z.
Title: A cantilevered bistable piezoelectric harvester array for broadband vibration
Abstract: This paper presents a novel magnet-free nonlinear vibrational energy harvester array to broaden the operational bandwidth and improve power distribution across the bandwidth. This array consists of cantilevered bistable piezoelectric harvesters (CBPHs) with adjacent and interlaced bandwidths, each of which is capable of operating independently. Based on the nonlinear characteristics of the static mechanical properties of CBPHs, a lumped-parameter analytical model, which is characterized by a nonlinear spring connected in series with a linear spring, is developed to predict the dynamic responses. To lay the investigation foundation for array design, comprehensive dynamic analyses are performed on a representative CBPH, using experimental testing, finite element analysis, and the analytical model. Results show that the CBPH with weak bistability, characterized by a single load-displacement path, is more likely to exhibit a hardening-type nonlinear response with high output under a relatively low excitation level, which is desirable for broadband energy harvesting. Furthermore, a parametric analysis is conducted to establish the relationship between design parameters and mechanical properties, which can serve as a guideline for designing CBPHs. Guided by these insights, an array integrating five CBPHs is designed and fabricated. Under an acceleration level of 0.5 g, all CBPHs in this array exhibit broadband hardening-type responses, achieving an operational bandwidth of 18 Hz and a relatively uniformly distributed output power across this bandwidth with an average value of 0.65 mW. Title: Adhesive collision of viscoelastic micropillar arrays: Effects of inter-fibril coupling on dissipation and capture
Abstract: Benefiting from the contact splitting principle, bioinspired micropillar array surfaces can improve contact adaptability and tune adhesion and energy dissipation, making them useful in transient contact applications such as soft robotic grasping, precision transfer, and target capture. However, dense and highly compliant designs can strengthen backing layer induced inter fibril coupling, whose effects on adhesion, delamination, and capture during transient collision remain unclear. This study develops an extended theoretical model for low-velocity adhesive collision between a rigid flat-ended indenter and a viscoelastic fibrillar array. The linear elastic force–displacement relation of the fibrillar array is extended to the viscoelastic case using the elastic–viscoelastic correspondence principle, and a rate-dependent interfacial delamination criterion is introduced to describe fibril failure during rebound. The model predicts damage-free capture, damage-involved capture, and escape. The coefficient of restitution (CoR) and the critical capture velocity vary nonmonotonically with the material retardation time. Viscoelastic dissipation and capture capability are maximized when the material retardation time is comparable to the characteristic collision time of the interface. Individual-fibril compliance and inter-fibril coupling reduce the effective contact stiffness and shift the optimal retardation time to larger values. Fibril spacing and height further regulate viscoelastic dissipation by modifying the collision time scale. Therefore, increasing the number of contacting fibrils does not necessarily increase the critical capture velocity. These results clarify the role of discrete fibril coupling in adhesive collision and provide guidance for designing viscoelastic bioinspired fibrillar arrays for dynamic capture. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Memory gradient method for robust multiobjective optimization problems
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: In this paper, we propose a memory gradient method for robust multiobjective optimization problems, where the uncertainty exists only in the objective functions and the uncertainty set is finite. We first reformulate the uncertain multiobjective optimization problem as a set-valued optimization problem. By utilizing the concept of partition sets, we derive a different vector optimization problem at each iteration to determine the search direction. The descent direction is updated by combining the current descent direction with the past multi-step iterative directions, which endows the method with the memory gradient property. Moreover, the step size is computed by the Wolfe line search. Under mild assumptions, the global convergence and convergence rate of the algorithm are established. Finally, several numerical examples are provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Resolving resin aggregation in scCO2-extracted heavy oil by topology-driven molecular design
Abstract: Supercritical CO2 (scCO2) extraction is a promising way for the recovery of heavy oil. However, the resulting raffinate heavy oil (RHO) often suffers from severe viscosity build-up. Title: Enhanced image denoising via an improved time-fractional coupled PDE system with H−1 decomposition

Authors: Li M.; Li X.; Niu Z.; Zhang J.; Li L.; Ma S.
Title: Wheat bran arabinoxylan alleviates freezing-induced starch damage: multiscale structure, pasting properties, and digestibility
Abstract: This study investigated the protective mechanism of wheat bran arabinoxylan (WBAX) on frozen starch by examining the effects of WBAX molecular weights and addition levels on multiscale structure, pasting properties, and in vitro digestibility of frozen starch. The results of granular morphology analysis showed that WBAX effectively maintained granule surface integrity and inhibited granule agglomeration. Multiscale ordered structural analysis confirmed that WBAX affected the short-range ordered structure, nanoscale lamellar structure, and long-range ordered structure of frozen starch. Specifically, WBAX induced the following changes in frozen starch: relative crystallinity decreased from 22.64% to a minimum of 15.15%; dBragg decreased from 12.57 nm to a minimum of 12.16 nm; and the 1047 cm−1/1022 cm−1 ratio decreased from 0.91 to a minimum of 0.86. These structural changes influenced the properties of frozen starch. WBAX improved the pasting properties by promoting the hydration and gelatinization of frozen starch, enhancing thermal and shear stability, and inhibiting short-term retrogradation. Furthermore, WBAX modulated the digestibility of frozen starch by maintaining granule integrity, hindering enzyme-substrate contact, and increasing system viscosity, thereby facilitating the conversion of rapidly digestible starch, slowly digestible starch, and resistant starch. Overall, this study elucidates the protective mechanisms of WBAX on frozen starch from the perspective of “multiscale structure-pasting properties-digestibility”, providing a theoretical basis for the precise development of WBAX-based frozen products. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: A viscoplastic-fatigue peridynamic model and the GPU-accelerated simulation of creep-fatigue failure in geomaterials
Abstract: A three-dimensional viscoplastic-fatigue micropolar peridynamic model is proposed for creep-fatigue failure of geomaterials, in which Perzyna viscoplasticity and fatigue degradation evolve within a unified bond-level framework. A directed-bond GPU implementation is developed to improve the computational efficiency of three-dimensional peridynamic simulations. The proposed model and the GPU acceleration implementation are validated by a cyclic compression simulation of rock salt. Results show that the proposed model can reproduce the progressive inclined damage pattern observed in the physical tests, capturing the three-stage creep-fatigue damage evolution, and obtaining fatigue lives that reasonably agree with the experimental results. Besides, the overall speedup becomes faster with material-point discretization refinement, reaching 21.19 for the finest model with 31,250 material points. An engineering-scale salt-cavern simulation is conducted, which captures the progressive development of cavern-wall damage under cyclic internal pressure, and the results indicate that the cavern-wall damage is creep-dominated. The simulations show that the proposed model can successfully simulate creep-fatigue damage in geomaterials. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Ge Y.; Liu H.; Zhu Y.; Li S.; Zhang H.; Chen H.; He J.; He Y.; Li J.; Song Y.
Title: Molecular mechanism of the impacts from coal rank and oxygen functional groups on H2 adsorption–diffusion behaviors
Abstract: Deep coal seams have significant potential for large-scale underground hydrogen storage (UHS). However, the molecular mechanisms governing the impacts of coal rank and oxygen functional groups (OFGs) on H2 adsorption–diffusion behaviors remain unclear. In this study, Grand Canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) and Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations were used to construct three coal models with different coal ranks. A series of oxygen–functionalized models (SA–OH, SA–O–, SA–C=O, SA–COOH, and SA–C) were further developed based on the SA coal model while maintaining a constant oxygen content. The coupled effects of coal rank and OFGs on H2 adsorption–diffusion behaviors were systematically investigated. H2 adsorption follows a micropore-filling mechanism under high-pressure conditions (40 MPa), and the storage capacity is primarily controlled by the effective free volume (EFV). OFGs regulate hydrogen storage through coupled adsorption–diffusion effects. Polar groups (–OH and –C=O) form localized energy traps that enhance H2 adsorption but restrict H2 diffusion. In contrast, the bulky –COOH group inhibits the stacking of aromatic layers and maintains hydrogen-accessible pore volume. H2 diffusion in coal models exhibits an overall Arrhenius-type temperature dependence, with comparable diffusion activation energies ( E a) for the HvAb and LvB models and a distinctly higher E a for the SA model, indicating stronger confinement effects in high-rank coal. Within 318–338 K, the diffusion coefficient exhibits a non-monotonic trend due to the competition between thermal activation and thermally induced structural relaxation of the coal matrix. These results indicate that low-rank coal, characterized by high EFV and low diffusion resistance, is more favorable for hydrogen storage, whereas high-rank coal may provide stronger H2 retention due to enhanced confinement effects and higher diffusion energy barriers. This study provides molecular-level insights into the impacts of coal rank and OFGs on H2 adsorption–diffusion behaviors and supports the evaluation and optimization of UHS reservoirs. Authors: Liu Q.-L.; Li Z.-W.; Lin X.-L.
Title: A fast direct solver for Toeplitz-like Hessenberg systems with application to numerical solution of a nonlocal diffusion equation
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: In this work, a novel operator-splitting scheme is proposed for a nonlocal diffusion equation with variable coefficients. By adding perturbation terms, the two-sided diffusion problems are converted into two one-sided subproblems at each time level. The coefficient matrices of these subproblems are nonsingular M-matrices that share a Toeplitz-like Hessenberg (TLH) structure, based on which a superfast recursive direct solver is proposed for solving these subproblems, which requires only O(nlog3n) operations and O(n) storage for an n × n linear system. As a result, the proposed scheme is fast and directly solvable within a linearithmic complexity in the presence of variable coefficients. Theoretically, the unconditional stability, convergence, and positivity-preserving property are established for the proposed scheme in the presence of variable coefficients. To our knowledge, this is the first fast and directly solvable scheme for the variable-coefficients nonlocal diffusion equation. Numerical results are presented to show the efficiency of the proposed method and to support our theoretical results. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Fully discrete follow-the-leader approximation of one-dimensional scalar conservation laws with vacuum
Source title: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
Abstract: We present a fully discrete particle approximation for one-dimensional scalar conservation laws. Under suitable monotonicity assumptions on the macroscopic velocity, we construct a vacuum-compatible family of time-discrete particle equations and show that an appropriate piecewise-constant density reconstruction from the particle setting converges to the unique entropy weak solution of the macroscopic scalar conservation law. © 2026 The Author(s).

Authors: Zhang W.; Zhang J.; Huang H.; Shi H.; Shi J.; Xie T.; La J.; Wang Y.
Title: Electric-field-induced electrochemical transformation of shale oil for in situ upgrading: Molecular evolution, interfacial regulation and hydrogen generation
Abstract: Simultaneous shale-oil upgrading, hydrogen evolution, and interfacial regulation through electrically induced electrochemical transformation represents a potential strategy for enhancing hydrocarbon resource utilization. In this study, a shale oil–water system was subjected to direct-current stimulation at different applied voltages, and the electrical and thermal responses, gaseous products, oil composition, molecular structure, aqueous-phase chemistry, and oil–water interfacial properties were systematically characterized to elucidate the transformation behavior and underlying physicochemical processes. At 40 V, the current reached 0.92 A and the system temperature increased to 78 °C, demonstrating pronounced electrical and Joule-heating responses. Gas analysis revealed the evolution of H2 together with C1–C6 gaseous hydrocarbons, while the liquid-phase carbon-number distribution showed enrichment of intermediate C11–C24 hydrocarbons, indicating redistribution and partial transformation of hydrocarbon components. Group-composition and Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) further revealed a decrease in saturated hydrocarbons, enrichment of resin-like polar components, and changes in aliphatic and oxygen-containing structures, collectively supporting the molecular restructuring and functionalization of shale oil during electrical treatment. Concurrently, the aqueous-phase pH increased from 6.0 to 14.0, while the oil–water interfacial tension decreased by 78.74%, from 11.95 to 2.54 mN m⁻1, demonstrating substantial electrochemically induced interfacial regulation. This work establishes an experimental connection among hydrocarbon molecular evolution, hydrogen evolution, aqueous-phase chemistry, and interfacial regulation within a unified shale oil–water electrochemical system, providing a new perspective for electrically assisted in situ hydrocarbon upgrading and enhanced resource utilization. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhao W.; Fu Y.; Ye J.; Liu Z.; Lan G.
Title: Mode transition and critical spatial aspect ratio of propane-air deflagration in long confined spaces
Abstract: Propane-air deflagration in long confined spaces depends on both the initial combustible-cloud extent and the enclosure geometry. However, the combined influence of these two factors on deflagration mode transition remains unclear. In this study, a three-dimensional CFD model was developed and validated against available deflagration experiments. The model was used to examine the effects of propane concentration, premixed-region aspect ratio L 0/ d , and spatial aspect ratio L / d on flame propagation, overpressure evolution and temperature distribution. Among the concentration cases, the highest pressure, temperature, and apparent flame-front speed occur at 4.0%, close to the stoichiometric propane concentration. During flame propagation, pressure-wave reflection and vent-induced rarefaction-wave backflow lead to multi-peak overpressure oscillations and promote flame-front deformation. The premixed-region aspect ratio is the main parameter associated with the deflagration regime transition. As L 0/ d increases from 3 to 4, the maximum apparent flame-front speed and peak overpressure move from a weak-deflagration branch to a strong-deflagration branch, and the sharpest increase occurs between L 0/ d = 3.25 and 3.5. The spatial aspect ratio further affects whether strong deflagration can develop. The critical L / d required for strong deflagration decreases from 9.0 to 4.0 as the cross-sectional width increases from 0.2 m to 1.0 m, following an empirical exponential relation. The results are interpreted in terms of the fuel volume participating in the coupling between combustion-driven expansion and flame deformation, and the delay of pressure relief from the open end. These results indicate that the transition from weak to strong deflagration is governed by the combined effect of premixed-region scale and spatial confinement, providing a reference for evaluating deflagration risk in long confined structures. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
