Authors: Klimonda Z.; Karwat P.; Dobruch-Sobczak K.; Piotrzkowska-Wróblewska H.; Litniewski J.
Author full names: Klimonda, Ziemowit (10143850100); Karwat, Piotr (35422390600); Dobruch-Sobczak, Katarzyna (56458823400); Piotrzkowska-Wróblewska, Hanna (56414859000); Litniewski, Jerzy (6602102056)
Title: Assessment of neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast tumors based on local tumor tissue response to therapy
Abstract: Breast cancer is a common cancer in women. In advanced stages and aggressive subtypes, oncologists use neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC), which precedes tumor removal surgery. The goal is to reduce the size of the tumor, which makes it easier to remove and possibly allow for less extensive surgery. The effectiveness of the NAC treatment is most often assessed by the doctor based on changes in tumor images, particularly based on changes in its size. Ultrasound imaging is one of the modalities used for this purpose. The aim of this work was to assess the local response of the tumor undergoing chemotherapy by utilizing statistical and textural parameters of ultrasound images, combined with classical machine learning methods. The optimal parameters were selected using Kullback–Leibler divergence. Probability maps of tumor tissue response to therapy were constructed and used in the tumors classification. The results presented in the article were obtained by analyzing 51 tumors over 5 cycles of neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The applied approach enabled the classification of cases with poor response to the treatment. The classification was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC). The best classification was achieved for data after the third chemotherapy cycle, when the AUC was 0.94. The presented results also indicate the particular usefulness of the gray level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) energy as a parameter for characterizing breast tumors undergoing this kind of treatment. The results suggest the potential usefulness of the proposed analysis method in evaluating the effectiveness of neoadjuvant chemotherapy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Chang L.; Deng J.; Yang J.; Song Q.; Zhang Y.; Guo B.; Li M.
Title: Concentration-dependent ternary interaction of wheat starch-arabinoxylan-ferulic acid: Multi-scale structures and digestibility
Abstract: This study investigated how arabinoxylan (AX; 2%, 4%, and 8%) and ferulic acid (FA; 1%, 2%, and 4%) regulated the multi-scale structures and digestibility of wheat starch (WS) in ternary composite systems. Here, a cooperative-competitive structural reconstruction mechanism referred to a concentration-dependent performance in which AX and FA either cooperatively promoted structural organization and digestion-resistant domain formation or competed for molecular association and restricted ordered assembly. Synchronously increasing FA concentration at 2% AX promoted gel-network reinforcement. Meanwhile, it increased short-range order, single-helical conformation, V-type crystallinity, and thermal stability. Consequently, WS-2%AX-4%FA showed enhanced digestion resistance, with the lowest rapidly digestible starch content (37.04%) and the highest resistant starch content (31.25%). In contrast, excessive AX (4% and 8%) induced antagonistic effects through molecular crowding and competitive interference with effective FA-starch association, weakening the structural benefits observed at 2% AX. Correlation analysis further revealed that the digestion resistance of ternary complexes was most strongly associated with ordered molecular and V-type crystalline structures. These results supported a concentration-dependent cooperative-competitive framework for starch-polysaccharide-polyphenol assembly, providing guidance for designing starch-based foods with controlled digestibility. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Zhao Y.; Zhao P.; Wang J.; Liu L.; Guo J.; Yang X.
Title: Improved adsorption and lubrication properties of subcritical water - treated soy protein on mucin layer
Abstract: In this study, soy protein isolate (SPI, 2-6 wt%) was subjected to heat treatment at 90 °C and subcritical water (SW) treatment at 120 °C, and the physicochemical and lubrication properties of protein aggregates were investigated to understand the structure-lubrication relationship of plant proteins. Heating at 90 °C triggered the assembly of loose protein aggregates mainly linked by intermolecular disulfide cross-linking. Compared to native SPI, heated SPI at 90 °C presented lower adsorption capacity toward mucin-coated surfaces due to high viscosity and weak bonding with mucin, thereby forming tribofilm and elevating the friction coefficient in the boundary and mixed lubrication regimes (nearly 0.85). By contrast, SW-treated SPI (SWP) contained large-sized rigid aggregates with more accessible exposed SH groups. Rigid aggregates exhibited excellent lubrication performance, attributed to higher surface adsorption and the formation of a thicker elastic tribofilm. With/without the addition of saliva, the lowest friction coefficient (around 0.45) was observed for SWP formed at high protein concentrations (6 wt%) in the boundary and mixed lubrication regime (approximately 0.1–200 mm/s). Thiol-blocking tests verified that the SPI-mucin disulfide bond possibly governed the adsorption of protein aggregates on the mucin surface and tribofilm formation, acting as a dominant reason for lubrication. This work provides theoretical guidance for alleviating the astringency of plant protein-based foods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Wang M.; Zhang M.; Yang Y.; Xing J.; Tao W.; Zhou W.; Fan L.; Li J.
Title: Stabilization of high internal phase emulsion by using soybean phosphatidylethanolamine-pectin Maillard conjugate and the application in 3D printing
Abstract: High internal phase emulsions (HIPEs) have attracted increasing attention in the field of 3D printing because of their potential to serve as structured food inks. This study aimed to develop soybean phosphatidylethanolamine (SP)-pectin Maillard conjugates (MCs) to stabilize HIPEs and evaluate their 3D printing suitability. MCs were prepared at different SP/Pectin ratios, with untreated mixtures (UMs) used as controls. Results showed that the optimal conjugation condition was obtained at an SP/Pectin ratio of 1:1, which resulted in the highest grafting degree of 38.3%. Compared with SP, pectin and UMs, MCs enabled greater reduction in interfacial tension. The higher zeta potential and water contact angle improved interfacial adsorption stability, while the expanded steric network of pectin accelerated interface saturation, collectively boosting the interfacial activity of MCs. Thus, the HIPE made by MCs exhibited smaller and more uniform droplets sizes. Moreover, the HIPE displayed improved rheology and texture, including favorable shear-thinning, higher recovery, increased gel strength, and self-supporting capability (enhanced viscoelasticity and deformation resistance). As a result, the HIPEs enabled smooth extrusion and maintained their structural integrity as well as higher-resolution patterning after printing. In addition, the HIPE remained stable after printing as evidenced by microscopic structural analysis. Overall, SP-pectin MCs showed great potential as natural stabilizers for designing HIPE-based food inks. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Author full names: Shao, Zhuangzhuang (57210338825); Wang, Haiyan (56048102200); Niu, Huiyong (54882943600); Huang, Jiliang (58573040600); Zhao, Haibo (61009850600)
Title: Study on the evolution laws of coal spontaneous combustion products and reaction pathways under different oxygen concentrations based on ReaxFF simulation
Abstract: Understanding the oxygen-dependent reaction behavior of residual coal is important for evaluating its renewed oxidation after oxygen re-entry into sealed fire zones. In this study, temperature-programmed oxidation experiments coupled with gas chromatographic and FTIR analyses were combined with reactive force field molecular dynamics (ReaxFF-MD) simulations to investigate coal oxidation under different oxygen supply conditions. The experimental results showed that decreasing O2 concentration suppressed carbon-oxide formation and altered the relative distribution of hydrocarbon products, indicating enhanced competition between oxidation and pyrolysis under oxygen-deficient conditions. FTIR analysis further revealed distinct oxygen-dependent evolution of aliphatic C–H, carbonyl-related, and hydroxyl-related structures. ReaxFF-MD simulations reproduced the overall oxygen-dependent tendency of oxidation-related products and showed that oxygen availability regulates the transformation of oxygen-containing and aliphatic structures as well as the competition among fragmentation, oxidation, and recombination reactions, thereby altering the distributions of gaseous products, tar, and residual carbon. Representative molecular pathways identified from the trajectories further elucidated the formation and transformation of major gaseous products. Overall, oxygen deficiency induces a redistribution of the oxidation–pyrolysis reaction network rather than simply reducing the reaction extent. These findings provide an experimentally supported molecular-level interpretation of the chemical behavior of residual coal under oxygen-deficient conditions and its renewed oxidation following oxygen re-entry. Authors: Zhao Z.; Feng H.; Zhu W.; Zha X.; Mao W.; Zhang Z.; Zhang L.
Title: Investigation on NO chemistry in CH4/NH3 MILD flames: Effects of NH3 blending ratio and co-flow diluents
Abstract: Ammonia is deemed a green zero-carbon alternative that can be co-fired with conventional fossil fuels to facilitate the transition toward carbon neutrality. Nevertheless, the inherent risk of high-NOx emissions severely hinders its practical deployment. Moderate or intense low-oxygen dilution (MILD) combustion offers a viable strategy to reduce NOx emissions from NH3-based fuels, though its establishment and reaction behaviors depend critically on the composition of both fuel blend and oxidizer. This study systematically investigates the detailed NO chemistry in CH4/NH3 jet flames under MILD condition, focusing on a broad range of NH3 blending ratio (0%–50%) and three co-flow diluents (FN2, CO2, and H2O). Results reveal that with the rising NH3 blending ratio, the maximum flame temperature decreases by 1.2%, 0.8%, and 1.1% under FN2-, CO2-, and H2O-dilutions, respectively, with the main reaction region shifting upstream. Both CO2 and H2O are more effective in sustaining the diffusion/kinetics-governed regime and maintaining the even temperature field. The addition of NH3 introduces fuel-N sources and leads to a linear rise in the final NO emission index. However, this promoting effect is notably mitigated under H2O-dilution, indicating its potential for achieving low‑NOx MILD combustion. Unlike other diluents, H2O uniquely promotes OH radical formation. This not only increases the predominant NH2-to-NH conversion (> 91%), but also facilitates the subsequent NH-to-HNO and NH-to-N conversions. Therefore, the pathway NH2 → NH → (N) → NO is reinforced, activating the reactivity of key intermediates and shifting the overall balance toward NO reduction rather than NO formation. The anticipated outcomes provide theoretical foundations for efficiently and cleanly realizing NH3-based fuels combustion. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: The effects of semicircular notch features and building direction on the tensile fatigue performances of laser powder bed fusion Corrax maraging stainless steel
Abstract: The roles of internal pore channels in the fatigue performances of additive-manufactured alloys are complex. This study investigated the effects of conformal cooling-channel-related semicircular notch geometry and building direction on the tensile fatigue properties of laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) Corrax maraging stainless steel. The results indicate that the fatigue performance of LPBF-fabricated Corrax steel is fundamentally governed by the interplay between building direction and surface morphology, rather than by intrinsic microstructural variations. In parallelly-built (P) specimens, the highly rough down-skin regions coincide exactly with the critical load-bearing cross-section, acting as potent micro-notches. Therefore, under cyclic loading, local stress concentrations trigger simultaneous multi-site crack initiations, leading to a lower fatigue strength at 106 cycles of 150 MPa. Conversely, vertically-built (V) specimens demonstrate significantly superior fatigue resistance, reaching a fatigue strength at 106 cycles of 300 MPa. This enhancement occurs because their maximum stress aligns with the relatively smooth intersection between the up-skin and down-skin regions, effectively delaying fatigue crack initiation. Furthermore, when semicircular notches are introduced to simulate internal pore channels, the fatigue degradation of V specimens generally adheres to theoretical stress concentration factors. However, in P specimens, the notch geometries interact adversely with the staircase effect; for instance, the P-R4D4 specimen developed a deep groove that exacerbated the reduction of the actual load-bearing cross-section. This structural degradation overrode standard theoretical predictions and further dropped the fatigue strength at 106 cycles to 100 MPa. Thus, optimizing the building direction to mitigate localized surface defects is crucial for enhancing the fatigue performance and structural integrity of LPBF components. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Novel bimetallic ZIF (Cu-Zn-ZIF-8) for enhanced and stable carbon capture from industrial moisture-laden flue gas through systematic and hierarchical material and process optimization
Abstract: Post-combustion carbon capture (PCCC) in the presence of moisture faces challenges due to competition between CO2 and H2O for adsorption sites, thereby impacting both efficiency and stability. Ten adsorbents, including metal–organic frameworks and bimetallic ZIFs, were investigated using simulated flue gas conditions: 12 vol% CO2, 10 vol% H2O, 8 vol% O2, and the balance N2. Cu-Zn-ZIF-8 demonstrated good performance among the evaluated adsorbents and was selected for further work. The adsorption process was optimized using a Central Composite Design (RSM-CCD) and an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model to confirm the results. An increase in CO2 uptake to 5.6 mmol/g was observed under optimal conditions, viz., 40 °C, 5 g of Cu-Zn-ZIF-8, flow rate of 150 ml/min, and carbonation time of 220 min. Integration of Cu2+ into the ZIF-8 framework was evidenced by Cu 2p XPS and corroborated by XRD, which showed preservation of the parent ZIF-8 framework. The Cu-Zn-ZIF-8 showed a BET surface area of 974 m2/g and a pore volume of 0.47 cm3/g. The Elovich model provided an accurate fit to the adsorption kinetics, and the Langmuir isotherm accurately fit the experimental data. A preliminary techno-economic analysis determined that the adsorbent lifetime is the key factor affecting the overall CO2 capture cost. Even under humid conditions, the adsorbent retained 80.4% of its adsorption capacity after 10 cycles, confirming its good stability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Kang Z.; Ma L.; Yang A.; Zhou L.; Duan Y.; Lu Z.; Li M.
Title: Enhancing the wear resistance of BNNSs/Al composites through interfacial design
Abstract: Boron nitride nanosheets (BNNSs)-reinforced aluminum matrix composites (AMCs) were successfully fabricated by powder metallurgy, and the interfacial structure was deliberately engineered through sintering temperature control to reveal its decisive role in tribological performance. At 600 °C, BNNSs remained physically bonded along Al grain boundaries, forming a weak Al-BN interface; at 750 °C, an in-situ reaction between BNNSs and the Al matrix generated a strongly bonded Al-AlN-BNNSs transition interface. Compared with pure Al, the 750–8 composite exhibited a 73.6% reduction in grain size (1.74→0.46 μm) and a 289.4% increase in hardness (49.1→191.1 HV). Critically, the friction coefficient (COF) dropped sharply from 0.954 (pure Al) and 0.627 (600-8) to as low as 0.492 for the 750–8 composite, accompanied by a dramatic decrease in volume wear rate from 0.0129 mm3·N-1·m-1 (pure Al) to 0.0035 mm3·N-1·m-1, a reduction of ~73%. First-principles calculations attributed this enhancement to a more than tenfold increase in interfacial shear strength from 1.4 to 1.7 GPa for the Al-BN interface to 20.3–30.0 GPa for the Al-AlN-BNNSs interfaces, confirming that the AlN transition layer continuously transfers load during friction while the strong interface effectively arrests crack initiation and propagation. This interfacial engineering shifts the wear mechanism from severe delamination in pure Al to mild abrasive wear in the 750–8 composite, providing a novel design strategy for high-performance, lightweight wear-resistant aluminum-based materials. Authors: Xu L.; Luo M.-L.; Zhu H.; Dai J.-J.; Wang J.; Yang F.-Q.
Title: Mn3O4 with multiple enzyme-like activity for differential detection of lead and copper ions
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Pb(II) can cause irreversible developmental and neurological damage, Cu(II) is an essential trace element but exhibits significant toxicity at excessive concentrations. Therefore, development of reliable detection methods for Pb(II) and Cu(II) is crucially important. In this work, Mn3O4 nanomaterial with both oxidase (OXD)-like and laccase (LAC)-like activities was synthesized using a green and mild approach. Based on the enhancing effect on OXD-like activity of Mn3O4 by Pb(II) and Cu(II), simple and sensitive fluorescent sensing methods for detecting Pb(II) and Cu(II) were developed, with the limits of detection of 0.073 μM and 0.391 μM, respectively. The developed methods were successfully applied to analyze Pb(II) and Cu(II) in various real samples. Furthermore, given that Pb(II) can inhibit the LAC-like activity of Mn3O4, a colorimetric method for Pb(II) detection with an ultra-wide linear range (1–7 μM and 7–2000 μM) was developed. By combining the fluorescence and colorimetric detection results, the differential detection of Pb(II) and Cu(II) can be realized. In addition, the substrate-dependent regulation of enzyme-like activity of Mn3O4 by Pb(II) was elucidated. Specifically, when 2,4-DP was used as the substrate, Pb(II) inhibited product formation through stabilizing the Mn3O4–2,4-DP complex. In contrast, when OPD was used as the substrate, Pb(II) promoted the generation of free radicals on the material's surface, enhancing the catalytic reaction. The findings of this study provide a reference for the discriminatory detection of different metals based on multiple enzyme-like activity of nanomaterials. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Topical advancement in electrochemical conversion of carbon dioxide to methane: recent advances, challenges, and prospects for carbon neutrality
Abstract: The electrochemical reduction of carbon dioxide (CO2) into methane (CH4) holds tremendous promise for mitigating greenhouse emissions through a sustainable pathway for carbon recycling and the storage of renewable energy as high-energy–density fuels. This review highlights recent progress on selective electrochemical CO2-to-methane conversion, with a focus on the design of advanced electrocatalysts such as copper-based materials, metal-nitrogen-carbon (MNC) structures, and metal–organic frameworks (MOFs). It deliberates the fundamental reaction mechanisms and structure–activity relationships that govern product selectivity, predominantly regarding the suppression of the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Moreover, the study highlights important innovations at the system-level, such as gas-diffusion electrodes and electrolyte engineering that can overcome mass-transport limitations and enhance current densities. Techno-economic and life-cycle analyses are evaluated to the industrial feasibility and environmental impact of these systems. Furthermore, we have considered the challenges and the future perspectives for enhanced catalyst engineering and product selectivity using in-situ mechanistic pathways. This review provides a detailed roadmap for the progress of advanced CO2 reduction technology toward global carbon neutrality and sustainable methane production by combining materials science and chemical engineering. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Xu H.; Shao Y.; Cheng J.; Cheng Y.; Li L.; Gong Z.
Author full names: Xu, Hangge (61014607100); Shao, Yabin (24491054200); Cheng, Jiarui (60054687200); Cheng, Yunlong (57037375500); Li, Laquan (57191834478); Gong, Zengtai (7201949217)
Title: Directed granular ball fuzzy neighborhood rough sets with hybrid information fusion for feature selection
Abstract: Feature selection is crucial for handling high-dimensional uncertain data, for which Fuzzy Neighborhood Rough Sets (FNRS) provide a robust framework. Traditional computational models based on point-level granularity confront efficiency bottlenecks and noise sensitivity in big data environments. Granular Ball Computing (GBC) addresses this issue by improving computational efficiency through the paradigm of granulating points into balls. However, existing granular ball generation methods exhibit “geometric rigidity” when processing class-imbalanced data and neglect directed statistical information between granules, resulting in the loss of granule-level distributional information. To address these issues, a novel feature selection method based on the Directed Granular Ball Fuzzy Neighborhood Rough Set (DGBFNRS) is proposed in this paper. First, an Adaptive Hierarchical Granular Ball (AHGB) generation method is proposed. Leveraging Gaussian Mixture Models and the Bayesian Information Criterion, it adaptively fits the multimodal topological structures of data and introduces a boundary-sensitive radius scaling mechanism to alleviate geometric overlaps between heterogeneous granules. Second, the DGBFNRS model is constructed. By defining a directed distance and a hybrid confidence measure that fuses internal and external granular information, it characterizes asymmetric semantic relationships between granules, thereby enhancing feature discriminability. Third, a collaborative filter–wrapper two-stage feature-selection strategy is designed, which combines dependency-based coarse screening with classifier-guided fine refinement to achieve coarse-to-fine feature selection. Experiments on 20 benchmark datasets show that AHGB achieves competitive clustering-validity performance across multiple complementary indices. Authors: Huang Y.; Liu Z.; Xu T.; Cai C.; Xiao X.; Ma H.; Ismail A.S.; Zhang Z.; Huang Q.
Title: Synergistic sound absorption of acoustic functional composite material with multiple dissipation mechanisms of SMA under high hydrostatic pressure
Abstract: With the advancement of underwater engineering and increasing deep-sea activities, the acoustic environment surrounding underwater structures has become increasingly complex. Consequently, acoustic material applied on the exterior surfaces of underwater structures have emerged as an important means for regulating acoustic scattering characteristics. Traditional acoustic material suffers from sound absorption degradation under high hydrostatic pressure owing to cavity compression and insufficient energy dissipation. This study proposes an acoustic functional composite material embedded with shape memory alloy (SMA) plates. A theoretical framework is developed by coupling rubber finite deformation with SMA stress-induced phase transformation. The Mooney–Rivlin hyperelastic model describes the finite deformation of rubber layers under hydrostatic pressure. For the SMA plates, an equivalent complex modulus model is established by considering the bending stress distribution and tension–compression asymmetric phase transformation under annular loading. The equivalent layering method and transfer matrix method are combined to predict the global sound absorption of the composite material. COMSOL finite element simulations and underwater acoustic impedance tube experiments validate the theoretical model. The results demonstrate that the SMA regulates the internal dynamic boundary and cavity coupling, thereby modifying acoustic-energy transmission within the coating, while the coupled vibration energy is further dissipated through multiple mechanisms involving SMA material loss, interfacial coupling, and rubber viscoelasticity. Meanwhile, the relatively high stiffness of the SMA suppresses hydrostatic deformation and contributes to maintaining the stability of these coupling and dissipation processes. Under 3 MPa hydrostatic pressure, the lower frequency limit corresponding to an absorption coefficient of 0.7 remains at 570Hz. Within [790, 6400] Hz, the functional composite material exhibits superior sound absorption performance. As the hydrostatic pressure increases from 3 MPa to 10 MPa, the SMA containing structure exhibits smaller shifts in characteristic frequency and smaller variations in the sound absorption coefficient than the structure without SMA, indicating lower pressure sensitivity and better resistance to hydrostatic-pressure-induced performance degradation. © 2026

Authors: Chen X.; Zhou J.; Chen Q.; Cai L.; Nie F.; Wang Q.
Title: Energy transport and flame attachment behavior of buoyant diffusion flames in an inclined semi-confined compartment under crossflow
Abstract: Accidental energy release events on offshore energy transportation vessels may occur under complex environmental conditions involving ambient winds, vessel heeling, and partial confinement. Under such non-ideal configurations, the redistribution and confinement of released chemical energy are governed by the coupled effects of buoyancy, crossflow-induced inertia, and surface inclination, leading to modified flame structures and intensified near-surface thermal loading. In this study, buoyant diffusion flames developing in an inclined semi-confined compartment subjected to horizontal crossflow are experimentally investigated. Heat release rates ranging from 9.24 to 27.72 kW, crossflow velocities from 0 to 3.0 m/s, and inclination angles between 0° and 30° are examined. Key flame geometric characteristics, including flame height, flame length, and flame attachment length, are quantified to elucidate the coupled influence of crossflow and inclination on energy transport behavior. The results show that flame height and flame length decrease monotonically with increasing crossflow velocity, whereas the flame attachment length increases with wind speed and exhibits a sharp increase as the inclination angle increases from 10° to 20°. All flame geometric parameters increase with both inclination angle and fuel mass supply rate due to enhanced near-surface energy confinement and reduced air entrainment. By introducing a modified buoyancy length scale accounting for surface inclination, unified scaling correlations are established for flame height, flame length, and attachment length. In addition, a boundary-layer-based correlation incorporating buoyancy–inertia competition is proposed to describe the evolution of local flame thickness in the attachment region. The present results provide predictive capability for energy redistribution and near-surface thermal loading in inclined, wind-affected, semi-confined environments relevant to offshore energy transportation vessels. Authors: Huang A.
Title: A smoothing gradient method for semidefinite programs
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: Motivated by projected gradient methods for linear and nonlinear programs, this paper presents a projected gradient method for semidefinite programming problems. Before directly applying the projected gradient method to solve standard semidefinite programs, we first modify optimality conditions of the standard semidefinite programming problem and its dual problem by using a Fischer-Burmeister function. This modification does not need to solve any matrix inequality constraints. The new method is proved to be global convergence and linear convergence under suitable stepsizes. Some numerical experiments for undirected graph problems are shown the feasibility and efficiency of the proposed approach. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Jin H.; Bai X.; Duan C.; Zhang Z.; Liu C.
Author full names: Jin, Helong (57195643557); Bai, Xiaohui (57190215119); Duan, Chengao (59341127200); Zhang, Zhongyao (57220865968); Liu, Cunliang (35210878200)
Title: Experimental and numerical studies of cross-regional coolant redistribution and film cooling superposition on pressure side of an adjustable turbine guide vane
Abstract: Thermal protection of adjustable guide vanes is essential for the efficient operation of variable geometry turbines. Changes in turning angle alter the passage aerodynamics, thereby affecting coolant distribution among film hole rows and interactions between coolant films on the pressure side. This study combines steady-state pressure-sensitive paint (PSP) measurements with numerical simulations to investigate the effects of turning angle, coolant mass flow ratio, and density ratio on pressure side film cooling performance. The findings indicate that decreasing the turning angle constricts the vane passage and alters the local pressure differences driving coolant discharge, inducing coolant redistribution across different regions and intensifying competition for coolant supply among the mid-chord film hole rows. At the three investigated coolant mass flow ratios, the area-averaged film cooling effectiveness decreases by 7.06%, 6.05%, and 4.69%, respectively, primarily due to the thinning of the near-wall coolant layer and the rapid downstream dissipation of coolant. Increasing the density ratio from 1.0 to 1.5 enhances coolant attachment to the wall, improving the area-averaged film cooling effectiveness and cooling uniformity by 9.64% and 14.99%, respectively. Furthermore, the interaction between showerhead film cooling and pressure-side film cooling improves near-wall coolant coverage and promotes downstream film development. Compared with pressure-side film cooling alone, the combined showerhead-pressure-side configuration increases the area-averaged film cooling effectiveness by 12.2% and reduces the relative standard deviation by more than 40%. These findings clarify the mechanisms governing coolant redistribution under variable geometry conditions and provide guidance for the thermal protection design of adjustable turbine guide vanes. Authors: Veliu D.; De Marchis R.; Martire A.L.; Resta M.
Author full names: Veliu, Denis (57195348602); De Marchis, Roberto (57216499820); Martire, Antonio Luciano (56228328300); Resta, Marina (56225368400)
Title: Numerical approximation in discrete portfolio optimization using DeFi as a new asset frontier: Risk contribution and correlation dynamics in a minimum-risk portfolio
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: The introduction of decentralized finance (DeFi) as an innovative asset class necessitates a reevaluation of the conventional framework for portfolio optimization. Traditional continuous-time models are challenged by the complex and non-linear features of DeFi tokens, such as discontinuous trading, high volatility, heteroskedasticity, and regime-switching behavior. The use of numerical approximation is examined in this article, optimizing portfolios with discrete techniques, including DeFi assets in a framework with low risk. We use and compare several optimization techniques, such as mean variance, Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) and a number of Risk Parity (RP) strategies are at the core of our analysis. We used a dataset of ten well-known DeFi tokens for our empirical investigation. DeFi tokens from 2021 to 2024 show a fundamental trade-off. Concentration-based models (mean-variance and CVaR) generate highly concentrated weights portfolios, leading to extreme volatility, large drawdowns, and prohibitively high portfolio turnover, which would be severely affected by real DeFi transaction fees, such as gas fees. In contrast, Risk Parity models consistently demonstrate superior practical performance. They produce well-diversified portfolios that deliver smoother results and significantly lower compound return paths and more stable rolling volatility and drastically reduced turnover. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Rong K.; Song B.; Wu J.; Lu J.; Tang J.; Zhou Y.; Zhou H.
Title: Semi-analytical contact mechanics at curvature discontinuities: Closed-form theory, Bi-modal response, and application to modified gearing
Abstract: Mechanical interfaces with discontinuous curvature can violate the local geometric assumptions of classical Hertzian contact theory. This study aims to establish a semi-analytical theory for non-Hertzian contact at curvature-mutation interfaces and apply it to the analysis and optimization of Top-rem modified spiral bevel gears. The geometric origin of curvature discontinuity is derived, showing that the studied tangency-constrained Top-rem profile preserves C1 continuity while introducing C2 discontinuity. The local formulation assumes frictionless normal line contact, linear elasticity, and small deformations. A closed-form semi-analytical solution for composite-curvature cylindrical contact is developed using a piecewise pressure distribution across the curvature-discontinuity boundary and incorporated into Loaded Tooth Contact Analysis (LTCA) through partitioned ease-off discretization. For the studied gear pair at 500 Nm, the relative error in maximum contact pressure is below 3.8% compared with FEM. A Kriging-assisted multi-objective optimization framework using NSGA-II reveals a bi-modal response in the studied gear pair. The curvature-dominant regime (S1) favors lower contact pressure, whereas the contact-ratio-dominant regime (S2) reduces the loaded transmission error (LTE) amplitude through changes in load-sharing transitions. Relative to the empirical Top-rem design, the selected solution for a contact-area margin of Δ = 0.25 mm reduces maximum contact pressure by 147.15 MPa and LTE amplitude by 1.32 μrad. For Δ = 0.5 mm, the corresponding reductions are 91.1 MPa and 6.03 μrad. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Shi X.; Liu S.; Xia M.; Li Y.; Wu H.; Ren X.; Huang X.; Liu M.; Shi B.; Cao W.
Title: Multiple explosions caused by dust entrainment from gas deflagrations: In interconnected space conditions
Abstract: The multiple explosions in the connected space have greatly restricted the safe development of industries such as coal mines. A multi-connected space experimental platform was built to study the characteristics of multiple explosions in multiple spaces. The study on multiple explosions caused by dust entrainment from gas explosions under interconnected vessel conditions was carried out. The explosion propagation and venting characteristics under different volume ratios were investigated. The flame dynamics and pressure evolution laws of explosions are studied based on high-speed cameras, pressure sensors, etc. Microscopic mechanism analysis of coal dust explosion was conducted based on molecular dynamics simulation. The results show that the explosion flame spreads from vessel A through the connecting pipe to vessel B, and the flame of the secondary explosion involving dust is vented from vessel B. The flame of the secondary explosion will also form a backflow flame in the connecting pipe. Both the backflow flame and the explosion venting flame showed unstable back-and-forth movements. With the development of the explosion, the pressure increases as the distance between the pressure measurement position and the ignition increases. The pressure balance characteristics of multi-vessel explosions were analyzed theoretically, and the multiple explosion pressures of coal dust lifted by shock waves were predicted. The main generation path of the combustion products of lignite was revealed, and the reaction mechanism with free radicals as the core intermediate was presented. The research results can provide theoretical and technical support for the safe design and control of the interconnected space in the process industry. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhang B.; Yan D.; Liu L.; Zheng A.; Liu C.; Yang X.; Zhang L.; Li K.
Title: Bottom-current reworking and diagenetic alteration of Longmaxi shale laminae: implications for three-dimensional shale-gas development
Abstract: Shale laminae in organic-rich black shale exert a dual geological and engineering control: they govern hydrocarbon enrichment by partitioning organic matter, pore systems, and source–reservoir relationships, and they dictate hydraulic-fracture geometry through pronounced mechanical anisotropy. Both controls are central to optimizing multi-layer, multi-well “cube” development. Despite their importance, the mechanisms responsible for rhythmic argillaceous–siliceous lamination in the deep-water Longmaxi shales remain incompletely understood, particularly the relative contributions of bottom-current reworking and diagenetic overprinting. This study integrates sedimentary-structure observations, optical petrography, field-emission scanning electron microscopy with cathodoluminescence imaging (FE-SEM–CL), X-ray diffraction (XRD), X-ray fluorescence (XRF), and inductively coupled plasma–mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) major-, trace-, and rare-earth-element analyses of outcrop samples from the Wangjiatang section and correlative core intervals from two wells in the Sichuan Basin. Preferred graptolite orientation, low-angle micro-cross lamination, and elevated Si/Al, Ti/Al, Ca/Al, and Sr/Al ratios in siliceous laminae collectively demonstrate that episodic bottom-current winnowing was a primary driver of laminae formation, producing systematic contrasts in redox conditions, detrital flux, and palaeoproductivity between argillaceous and siliceous intervals. Post-Archaean Australian Shale (PAAS)–normalized rare-earth-element (REE) patterns reveal a diagenetic overprint superimposed on these primary differences: light rare-earth-element (LREE) enrichment in clay-rich argillaceous laminae is attributed to clay-mineral surface adsorption and organic-matter complexation, whereas a middle rare-earth-element (MREE) bulge in siliceous laminae reflects preferential uptake by authigenic quartz and diagenetic illite during burial. The principal novelty of this work lies in integrating a bottom-current depositional model with a diagenetic REE-redistribution framework to explain, for the first time in a unified manner, the formation, geochemical signature, and mechanical implications of Longmaxi shale laminae. The resulting depositional–diagenetic architecture—brittle quartz-cemented laminae alternating with ductile clay-rich laminae—directly informs interval-specific hydraulic-fracturing strategies and provides a transferable geological framework for predicting shale quality and optimizing three-dimensional shale-gas development in heterogeneous laminated reservoirs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Chen J.; Ding Z.; Li C.H.

Title: On bi-rotary maps of negative prime power Euler characteristic
Abstract: A map is bi-orientable if it admits an assignment of local orientations to its vertices such that for every edge, the local orientations at its two endpoints are opposite. Such an assignment is called a bi-orientation of the map. A bi-orientable map is bi-rotary if its automorphism group contains an arc-regular subgroup that preserves the bi-orientation. In this paper, we characterize the automorphism group structure of bi-rotary maps whose Euler characteristic is a negative prime power. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Wang L.; Li P.; Li S.
Title: An efficient global algorithm for solving the sum of linear ratios problem on the Stiefel manifold
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: In this paper, we study the sum of linear ratios problem on the Stiefel manifold (SLRS). We first formulate a relaxation problem (EP) of (SLRS) by using Charnes-Cooper transformation, the convex hull of Stiefel manifolds and semidefinite relaxation technique. Moreover, the theoretical analysis confirms that (EP) is equivalent to (SLRS). Then we obtain an efficient linear lower bound of (EP) by leveraging the concave envelope of a single fractional term, reconstruction linearization technique and mean value theorem. Based on the lower bound and bisection branching rule, we develop a branch-and-bound algorithm and provide its global convergence and complexity analysis. Numerical results verify that our algorithm is competitive with the existing Riemannian optimization solver Manopt. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Author full names: Cheng, Yunlong (57037375500); Lv, Peinuo (60563244000); Zhang, Qinghua (57203621200); Yin, Longjun (55274361600); Shao, Yabin (24491054200)
Title: Efficient optimal scale combination selection via granular sequential three-way decision
Abstract: Optimal scale combination (OSC) selection is crucial for knowledge extraction in multi-scale decision systems (MDSs). However, existing multi-scale rough set models typically represent the three regions as unions of equivalence classes, losing the structural information of equivalence classes and hindering rule extraction. Moreover, most OSC selection algorithms adopt a fine-to-coarse backward search strategy, which not only contradicts the human coarse-to-fine cognitive mode but also is inefficient on large-scale datasets due to scale combination explosion. To address these issues, a granular sequential three-way decision model for MDSs (GrS3WD-M) is developed, and then an efficient forward optimal scale combination selection algorithm (FOSC) is designed. First, a two-step trisecting strategy is proposed to accelerate boundary region reduction, and then GrS3WD-M based on granular rough sets is developed to preserve the structural information of equivalence classes. As a result, rules can be directly extracted from equivalence classes in the positive region, while redundant computation during granulation is avoided. Second, the core scale combination is defined, an equivalent computational formula is derived, and an efficient algorithm based on GrS3WD-M and attribute grouping is proposed for its computation. Finally, the outer significance of attributes in MDSs is defined, and an efficient method for computing it is presented. Furthermore, the FOSC algorithm is proposed, which starts from the core scale combination and uses the outer significance as a heuristic to guide a coarse-to-fine forward search. Experimental results show that, compared with the state-of-the-art OSC selection algorithms, FOSC improves the average computational efficiency by more than 50 times. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Li Y.; Bai X.; Duan C.; Liu C.
Title: Experimental and numerical study of transpiration cooling in an octet-truss array structure
Abstract: To improve thermal protection under high heat flux conditions, this study investigates the flow and heat transfer characteristics of transpiration cooling structures based on octet-truss lattice (OTL) arrays through experiments and numerical simulations. Cooling performance is compared with that of square-pore structures, considering the effects of porosity, blowing ratio, mainstream Reynolds number, and inlet temperatures. Experimental results show that OTL structures achieve higher overall cooling effectiveness at the same porosity, with improvements of 8.99%–11.51% over blowing ratios of 5.12%–20.46%. This enhancement is associated with their larger internal heat transfer area and enhanced coolant–solid heat exchange, although it is accompanied by increased pressure drop. Reducing the porosity from 58.4% to 47.6% increases the cooling effectiveness of the OTL structure by 7.76% at a blowing ratio of 10.23%. Increasing the blowing ratio yields diminishing cooling benefits, whereas increasing the mainstream Reynolds number reduces cooling effectiveness, with a maximum experimental reduction of 9.55% within the tested conditions. Changes in inlet temperatures further reveal that overall cooling effectiveness and absolute wall temperature can exhibit different trends, highlighting the need to consider both quantities when assessing thermal protection. These findings provide insights into the cooling mechanisms of OTL structures and guide transpiration cooling design by considering both cooling effectiveness and flow resistance. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Authors: Wang Y.; Yu L.; Shi J.; Hao W.; Wang K.; Li F.; Wu X.; Zhang J.; Huang F.; Qian X.
Title: Investigation on the thermal runaway evolution Mechanism, gas generation behavior, and multi-medium suppression performance of lithium-ion batteries under immersion conditions
Abstract: With the rapid advancement of lithium-ion batteries, the risks of fire and explosion triggered by thermal-runaway-induced off-gassing have become increasingly prominent, particularly under overcharge conditions. Compared with conventional fire-extinguishing methods, immersion suppression offers potential in cooling, thermal propagation inhibition, and gas control, but its mechanism remains unclear. Therefore, this study examined thermal runaway evolution in 52 Ah LiFePO4 batteries under heating, overcharge, and immersion-overcharge conditions, explored the immersion suppression mechanism, and to evaluate the suppression performance differences among five immersion media (deionized water, FW-1800, water–ethylene glycol mixture, dimethyl silicone oil, and KOSTCHILL). Results show overcharge yields the highest gas (2.0591 mol) and heating the highest temperature (457 °C). Water immersion reduces gas to 1.6087 mol, peak temperature to 98 °C, and extends the thermal runaway window by 83.3 %. In terms of gas generation, immersion effectively suppresses high-temperature-dependent gases like H2 (1.185 → 0.832 mol) and CO (0.085 → 0.075 mol). Different immersion media show distinct suppression behaviors. Water-based systems perform better in temperature and gas suppression, suitable for single cells; FW-1800 performs best (Tmax = 88 °C, Vtotal = 1.1904 mol). Oil-based systems offer superior insulation (0 μS/cm), suitable for high-voltage modules; KOSTCHILL performs best (Tmax = 160.6 °C, Vtotal = 1.657 mol). This study provides theoretical and data support for developing immersion thermal safety technologies and optimizing immersion media for energy storage systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Du W.; Cao S.; Wang G.; Tang Z.
Title: Detector-view analysis of near-nozzle pulverized-coal flame organization and water-wall heat-flux exposure in a low-load tangentially fired boiler
Abstract: Near-nozzle pulverized-coal flame organization is closely linked to radiative heat transfer and water-wall exposure during deep low-load operation of tangentially fired boilers. This study investigates how detector-view flame-response structures are linked to burner-belt wall heat-flux exposure in a 350 MW pulverized-coal boiler operating at 20% boiler maximum continuous rating (BMCR). An 84-case CFD matrix was constructed by varying burner tilt, secondary-air distribution, and separated over-fire air (SOFA) pattern. The CFD-resolved combustion fields were converted into 1008 normalized burner-port flame-response maps for the active C-, D-, and E-layer burners, and flame descriptors were paired with layer-matched wall thermal-exposure metrics. The D layer forms the strongest and broadest high-response region, the E layer develops farther along the line of sight, and the C layer remains weaker and more port-sensitive. The high-response area ratio Ahigh shows the most consistent correspondence with local wall high-flux exposure. For the 95th-percentile wall heat flux q95, the full case-layer Spearman coefficient is 0.964 and remains 0.866 after adjustment for burner layer, burner tilt, SEC, and SOFA, and 0.821 after additional adjustment for wall radiative fraction. By contrast, the 95th-percentile detector-view response I95 shows a weaker and more response-formulation- and operating-state-sensitive correspondence with q95. These results support a bounded spatial-occupation interpretation of local burner-belt high-flux exposure rather than a universal area-versus-peak or causal relationship. Centroid and peak-depth descriptors support layer-scale heat-load-center migration but are not universal within-layer predictors. Limited field-image comparison provides morphology-level support. The method provides a diagnostic representation for connecting near-nozzle flame organization with burner-belt water-wall thermal exposure. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Li Y.; Ge H.; Zhang X.; Qu S.; Zhang E.; Li Z.; Wang F.; Xu D.
Title: Long-term corrosion evolution of titanium and Ti5Cu alloy in the oral environment driven by Streptococcus mutans
Abstract: Oral biomedical materials are susceptible to microbiologically induced corrosion (MIC) during long-term service, which may compromise their clinical performance and therapeutic efficacy. Herein, a 90-day experimental model was established to systematically investigate the MIC behavior of commercially pure Ti and Ti5Cu alloy under challenge of cariogenic Streptococcus mutans. Continuous electrochemical measurements revealed lower corrosion susceptibility of Ti5Cu, as evidenced by higher polarization resistance, larger capacitive arc radii, and lower corrosion current density. S. mutans biofilms induced pronounced pitting corrosion, with maximum pit depths reaching 4.3 and 3.1 μm on Ti and Ti5Cu, respectively. AFM results further revealed increased surface roughness and potential heterogeneity on Ti, suggesting enhanced micro-galvanic effects. Nevertheless, Ti5Cu effectively mitigated these effects, likely owing to its ability to suppress biofilm formation and interfacial acidification. These findings provide a theoretical basis for understanding the long-term corrosion mechanisms of titanium-based oral materials and guiding material design for their safe service. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Zhao A.-X.; Chen Y.; Liang F.; Guo X.-T.
Title: Spectral submanifold-based 3D reduced-order modeling and nonlinear dynamics analysis of spinning pipes conveying fluid
Abstract: Spinning pipes conveying fluid are critical components in drill strings and turbomachinery, etc., which are often subjected to whirling vibration and hence lose stability. Their nonlinear responses remain hard to predict owing to complex gyroscopic coupling, fluid–structure interaction (FSI) and costly full-order simulations. To address this challenge, this study proposes a novel nonlinear three-dimensional (3D) model of spinning cantilevered pipes conveying fluid accounting for outlet free boundary. New nonlinear effects arise from outlet virtual work and perturbation treatment of inertia nonlinearities, and fluid- and spin-induced gyroscopic couplings as well as Kelvin–Voigt damping are incorporated. A spectral submanifold (SSM)-based reduced-order model (ROM) is further developed, which reduces the present 16-dimensional modal system to 4- and 2-dimensional invariant-manifold representations to analyze autonomous and forced responses. Numerical examples demonstrate that the SSM-ROM accurately captures transient whirling behaviors while achieves 4 and 3.8 times speedups when combined with ode45 and ode15s solvers, respectively, compared to the full-order model, and further precisely predicts forced responses at a dramatic acceleration of two orders of magnitude. Nevertheless, the transient prediction accuracy deteriorates as a dominant natural frequency approaches zero. Nonlinear behavior exploration reveals that the gyroscopic coupling brings about vibration energy transfers between the orthogonal transverse directions, whereas the FSI effect causes complex evolution from periodic to quasiperiodic and chaotic motions. Overall, this study provides an efficient 3D modeling and reduction framework for nonlinear dynamics analysis of motional fluid structures. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Title: Long-term storage stability of duck stearin-based whipping cream governed by ZNP-ANS composites and monoglyceride: A synergistic mechanism of rigid-flexible interfacial scaffolding and fat crystal network regulation
Abstract: Using duck stearin (a low-saturated-fat lipid with weak crystallization capacity) as a model fat, this study investigated the stabilizing effect of zein nanoparticle-aminated nanosilica (ZNP-ANS) composites and their synergy with monoglyceride (MAG) in whipped cream. The ZNP-ANS composites, formed via electrostatic attraction and hydrogen bonding, constructed a continuous, “rigid-flexible” interfacial layer at the oil-water interface of the emulsion, providing critical structural support against long-term (90 days) storage stresses. Thus, the emulsion exhibited excellent colloidal stability and rheological properties. The introduction of MAG further exerted synergistic functions: it rapidly adsorbed at the air-water interface to promote bubble formation, increasing overrun to 503.63% during whipping, while regulating lipid crystallization to form a uniform fat crystal network. Through interpenetration of the fat crystal network with the ZNP-ANS scaffold, the whipped cream prepared from the emulsion after 90 days of storage maintained excellent piping firmness and low serum loss. Authors: Zhang K.; Sun K.; Huang B.; Xu Y.
Title: Tribological behavior and Ti-6Al-4V turning performance of dimple-textured YG8 tools under BP/MoS2 aqueous lubrication
Abstract: Efficient machining of titanium alloys is often limited by severe friction and material adhesion at the tool–chip interface. This study investigated the combined effects of circular dimple textures and a black phosphorus (BP)/molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) aqueous lubricant on Ti-6Al-4V/YG8 contacts through reciprocating tribological and turning experiments. Under single-component BP and MoS2 lubrication, the dimple texture reduced the mean friction coefficient by 12.25% and 18.95%, respectively, but increased Ti-6Al-4V ball wear. In the BP/MoS2 aqueous lubrication comparison, a BP:MoS2 mass ratio of 5:1 yielded the lowest mean friction coefficient (0.3985), 6.37% below that with deionized water, while increasing ball wear volume by 9.90%. Surface characterization revealed debris retention and reduced adhesion and spalling on the YG8 disk. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) results supported the formation of a tribochemical film containing oxidized P- and Mo-derived species and metal oxides. Orthogonal analysis identified dimple diameter as the most influential factor affecting friction and ball wear. In the subsequent texture-parameter study, the geometry with a diameter of 100 μm, spacing of 250 μm, and depth of 20 μm produced the lowest mean friction coefficient (0.388) but the highest ball wear volume. In turning, the dimple-textured tool under BP/MoS2 lubrication reduced the resultant cutting force by 8.47% relative to the non-textured lubricated tool and decreased surface roughness by 50.1% relative to non-textured dry turning. These results reveal a friction–wear trade-off and provide guidance for designing dimple-textured cemented carbide tools and aqueous nanolubricants for titanium alloy machining. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Liu H.; Guo W.; Xiang H.; Su R.; Chen S.; Chen L.; Deng S.
Title: In-situ catalytic hydrogen production from crude oil over Fe-based bimetallic catalysts
Abstract: In-situ H2 production technology from crude oil offers broad application prospects for clean production in low-permeability and high-water oil reservoirs. Nevertheless, its large-scale application is limited by low H2 production efficiency. To address these challenges, water-soluble composite catalysts of Fe-Ni, Fe-Co and Fe-Zn were adopted in this study for the conversion of crude oil into H2 via in-situ catalytic gasification. Compared with Fe-Co and Fe-Zn catalysts, the Fe-Ni catalyst showed the best performance. The Fe-Ni catalyst reduced the initial thermal decomposition temperature of crude oil by 30 °C, increased the mass loss rate in the LTO stage by 4.64% and effectively lowered the apparent activation energy of crude oil oxidative pyrolysis. Gas product analysis indicated that Fe-Ni and Fe-Co catalysts increased the syngas yield by 4.08 wt% and 1.75 wt%, along with an increase in H2 yield of 30.00 mL/g and 18.49 mL/g, respectively. In addition, the Fe-Ni catalyst improved oxygen utilization efficiency by 4%. Mechanism analysis confirmed the synergistic catalysis between air and the catalyst reduces thermal decomposition temperature, promotes the cleavage of C–C and C–H bonds in crude oil macromolecules and accelerates gasification to facilitate H2 generation. This study confirms the excellent performance of Fe-Ni, Fe-Co and Fe-Zn catalysts for in-situ H2 production from crude oil under an air atmosphere, and proposes an efficient in-situ catalytic H2 production method suitable for low-permeability and high-water oil reservoirs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Microwave–water effects on hydrocarbon mobility in lacustrine shale reservoirs
Abstract: Microwave irradiation provides a promising in-situ strategy for improving shale oil recovery, yet the role of abundant residual water retained after hydraulic fracturing in microwave-induced nanopore reorganization remains insufficiently constrained. To address this gap, this study employs water vapor adsorption, contrast-matched small-angle neutron scattering (CM-SANS), and SANS-based multifractal characterization to quantify water uptake and nanopore accessibility in Chang 7 lacustrine shale from the Ordos Basin and to evaluate microwave-induced pore-structure evolution in dry and water-saturated samples. The results show that 36.11%–56.61% of the nanopore volume within the 2–100 nm range is accessible to water, with preferential water occupancy in clay-related pores within the 2–3 nm interval. Water-saturated microwave irradiation increases pore volume and mean pore diameter, promotes pore enlargement and coalescence, increases pore number density in the 3–100 nm range, and reorganizes nanopore connectivity. These findings demonstrate that retained water is not merely a passive pore fluid but an active microwave-absorbing phase that participates in shale nanopore modification. By linking retained-water accessibility, microwave-induced pore-structure reorganization, and multifractal nanopore evolution, this study provides new nanoscale insights into water-assisted microwave stimulation and its potential to create more favorable transport pathways for shale oil migration. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhang L.; Zeng J.; Zhang H.
Title: Relaxed greedy randomized Kaczmarz with signal averaging for solving doubly-noisy linear systems
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: Large-scale linear systems often contain noise in both the coefficient matrix and the right-hand side. In this paper, we extend the relaxed greedy randomized Kaczmarz (RGRK) method to doubly-noisy systems by combining a relaxed greedy sampling method with the randomized Kaczmarz method. We prove that, in this doubly-noisy setting, RGRK converges linearly up to an error horizon determined by the noise. To reduce this horizon, we incorporate signal averaging over N independent measurements and propose the RGRK with signal averaging (RGRK-SA) method. We prove that RGRK-SA satisfies a conditional linear convergence bound in expectation with respect to the iteration number and that the convergence horizon decreases at the rate O(1/N) with respect to the number of repeated measurements. Numerical experiments show that, for linear systems with well-conditioned matrices, RGRK-SA attains higher accuracy than several other advanced denoising Kaczmarz-type methods. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Yang Y.; Zhang Y.; Wang J.; Hong R.; Chu H.
Title: Synergistic effects of PODE3 and ammonia on soot formation in n-heptane diffusion flames
Abstract: Soot formation in hydrocarbon diffusion flames remains a major challenge for clean combustion, and the comprehensive impact of oxygenated and carbon-free fuels on soot evolution is not fully understood. Experimental investigations were performed to evaluate the effect of ammonia (NH3) addition on soot formation in polyoxymethylene dimethyl ether (PODE3)/ n -heptane blended diffusion flames. The particle size, nanostructure, and physicochemical properties of the soot samples were comprehensively analyzed. The results showed that, at both sampling heights, the primary soot particle diameter decreased as the NH3 addition level increased. The reduction was only slight under the N20 condition, while the inhibitory effect became significant under the N40 and N60 conditions. The addition of NH3 further decreased the graphitization degree of soot, thereby leading to a more disordered arrangement of microcrystalline layers. This structural regulation effect became more pronounced during the soot growth stage. The addition of PODE3 introduced oxygen into the soot structure, while the blending of NH3 modified the influence of PODE3, significantly altering the relative atomic ratio contents of N, O, and C on the soot surface. At low NH3 blending levels, the (O + N)/C ratio slightly decreased, indicating that the functionalization of surface heteroatoms was somewhat inhibited. At high NH3 blending levels, the (O + N)/C ratio significantly increased, indicating an increase in the surface defects and the degree of heteroatom functionalization of soot. FTIR analysis further confirmed that NH3 blending resulted in a reduction in the absorption peak intensity of soot‑related characteristic functional groups. The results of this study provided experimental evidence that improved our understanding of the soot evolution mechanism during the combustion of n -heptane with PODE3/NH3. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Cao F.; Mao K.; Lei Z.; Fan M.; Zhao K.; Cheng B.; Wang M.; Hou H.
Title: Inverse design of Helmholtz array for broadband quasi-perfect sound absorption based on fully connected deep network
Abstract: Traditional Helmholtz resonators have problems such as narrow sound absorption bandwidth and complex multi-unit coupling mechanisms. At the same time, they are affected by parameter coupling, making on-demand design difficult and unable to meet the needs for efficient noise reduction in the mid-low broadband range. This paper proposes a profiled perforated-neck Helmholtz array structure (PPHAS). It achieves high-performance sound absorption over the low-frequency wideband range through weak coupling effects among its units. Addressing the shortcomings of traditional forward design, where parameter tuning relies on extensive traversals and repeated verification, resulting in high computational costs and low parameter matching efficiency, this paper first analyzes the regulation rules of geometric parameters on acoustic absorption characteristics based on forward design. It then investigates the multi-unit cooperative absorption mechanism of weakly coupled arrays, constructs a machine learning database covering the multidimensional structural parameters of PPHAS units, establishes the mapping relationship between absorption performance and structural parameters, and ultimately uses a fully connected deep neural network (FCDNN) model to achieve accurate prediction and inverse design of PPHAS absorption characteristics. The database contains 269,514 sample sets, covering five key parameters: cavity radius, neck length, neck radius, neck relative wavenumber, and neck relative roughness, spanning a frequency range of 45 Hz-1420 Hz and an absorption coefficient range of 0.1-1.0. The results of the prediction verification for two-unit, four-unit, and six-unit composite structures show that the maximum error of the FCDNN in predicting the peak absorption frequency is less than 0.80%, and the maximum prediction error of the absorption coefficient is less than 2.17%. The six-unit composite structure obtained through prediction can achieve a broadband sound absorption capability. The capacity has α>0.8 in the frequency interval of 447 Hz-574 Hz. Its bandwidth is 127 Hz. The overall thickness of the structure is only 40 mm. Experimental tests further verified the reliability of the FCDNN model, with the deviation of peak frequency between predicted and experimental values being less than 5 Hz, and the deviation of the sound absorption coefficient not exceeding 0.17. This method shortens the design cycle of PPHAS, improves the efficiency and accuracy of on-demand design, and has important reference value for the design of functional acoustic structures with multi-physical-field and multi-unit coupling. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS

Title: Visible light-induced degradation of organic pollutant using a novel g-C3N4/Fe-Mg LDH/ZIF-67 ternary photocatalyst
Abstract: Malachite green (MG) is a persistent organic contaminant that poses serious ecological and environmental hazards, underscoring the need for effective, long-term remediation techniques. In this study, a g-C3N4/Fe-Mg LDH/ZIF-67 photocatalyst was successfully synthesized via co-precipitation. Structural, optical and morphological analysis of the materials synthesized was done using XRD, FTIR, UV-DRS, BET, FESEM-EDX, XPS, PL, EIS and Mott-Schottky. A pseudo-first-order model adequately represented the dyes’ degradation dynamics. The effects of irradiation duration and catalyst dosage on the photocatalytic degradation of MG were thoroughly examined. Under visible-light irradiation, the g-C3N4/Fe-Mg LDH/ZIF-67 composite achieved a substantial degradation efficiency of 94.74%. Scavenger experiments suggest that photogenerated electrons play the predominant role in MG degradation, while holes and superoxide radicals also contribute to the photocatalytic process. The positive slope values acquired through the Mott Schottky plot suggested the existence of n-type semiconductor in the sample. The EIS analysis revealed that charge transfer occurs at the interface. The results of electrochemical and optical analyses supported the formation of a successful heterojunction and the charge transfer process. Although the individual Fe–Mg LDH and ZIF-67 materials exhibited slightly higher degradation efficiencies, the g-C3N4/Fe-Mg LDH/ZIF-67 composite demonstrated high photocatalytic activity and provides a versatile heterostructure platform for further optimization and wastewater treatment applications. Moreover, the photocatalyst showed fair reusability by maintaining photocatalytic ability during three consecutive reuses although it gradually declined in degradation performance. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Wang T.; Xu Y.
Title: Adaptive graph representation with dual-view consistency for incomplete multi-label learning
Abstract: Currently, multi-label learning faces challenges in acquiring fully annotated labels due to incomplete supervision and distorted label semantics. Existing methods often focus on limited local instance-level correlations and overlook semantic correlation, leading to suboptimal label recovery. To this end, we propose adaptive instance graph representation with dual-view label semantic consistency for incomplete multi-label learning, termed GDCIML. Specifically, an adaptive manifold graph is first constructed by integrating first-order and high-order similarities, enabling the graph to capture both local and global structural relationships. From the semantic view, we introduce a label self-representation mechanism to propagate observed labels and generate informative soft supervision. To enhance structural-semantic interaction, a dual-view consistency constraint is imposed to align graph-based feature structures with label-induced semantics. Furthermore, we present a theoretical analysis on the generalization error bound for the final linear predictor, offering an auxiliary theoretical perspective on its capacity control. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that GDCIML outperforms state-of-the-art methods under various missing-label settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Cui J.; Qing H.; Hu Z.; Wang J.; Yu Q.; Qiao L.; Ling W.; Zhou W.
Title: Laser etching of flattened copper mesh for fabricating continuous capillary channels in flexible heat pipe with high durability
Abstract: Flexible heat pipes suffer from an intrinsic trade-off between heat transfer performance and bending durability. Although thinning the flexible section can effectively reduce bending stress and improve durability, it generally compromises capillary-driven liquid transport across the wick, thereby limiting heat transfer performance. To overcome this conflict, this study proposes laser etching of flattened copper mesh for constructing continuous capillary channels in ultrathin flexible heat pipes. Ultrafast laser processing was used to generate continuous capillary channels on the surface of flattened copper mesh, and a liquid transport model was established based on three-dimensional surface topography to clarify the relationship between laser-induced morphology and capillary behavior. The results show that flattening a 200-mesh copper mesh reduced its thickness by 50% and increased wire width by 56%, creating favorable conditions for continuous channel fabrication. By regulating laser parameters, continuous V-shaped capillary channels with a depth of 35 μm and a width of 30 μm were achieved, exhibiting strong capillary pumping capability with a maximum wicking coefficient of 17.94 mm/s0.5. When applied in a flexible heat pipe, the etched flattened copper mesh enabled an ultrathin flexible section of 261 μm and a low thermal resistance of 0.84 °C/W at 5 W. A bending test platform was further developed to quantitatively evaluate durability degradation during cyclic deformation. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Masson SAS.

Authors: Yao X.; Liu X.; Shan Y.; Ma J.; Jin H.; Sun Y.; Zhang Y.; Riaz T.; Hu G.; Jin Y.
Title: Integrated hierarchical assembly of egg white proteins into nanoparticle-nanofiber composites for improved interfacial behavior and foam stabilization
Abstract: Egg white proteins (EWP) are widely used in aerated food systems but are limited by disordered thermal aggregation and weak interfacial films during processing. In this study, an integrated hierarchical assembly strategy was developed under near-neutral conditions through sequential succinylation, mild enzymatic hydrolysis, and short-time thermal induction to promote the formation of nanoparticle-nanofiber (NPs-NFs) composite structures. Succinylation provided a favorable electrostatic basis for protein conformational rearrangement, while enzymatic hydrolysis and thermal induction promoted conformational evolution toward β-sheet-enriched structures. Spectroscopic and microscopic analyses supported a transition from disordered aggregation toward ordered self-assembly and confirmed the stable coexistence of NPs and NFs. The assembled system exhibited enhanced interfacial adsorption behavior and interfacial elasticity, accompanied by improved foaming capacity and foam stability, which were further reflected by increased specific volume and a more uniform pore structure in a proof-of-concept bread model. Overall, this study provides an effective strategy for regulating the hierarchical assembly and interfacial functionality of egg white proteins under mild conditions and offers new insights into the interfacial structure design and functional optimization of protein-based hydrocolloids for aerated food applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Author full names: Buldú, Javier M. (6602820274); Latora, Vito (7003540219); Martínez, Johann H. (56529959600); Rodríguez-Sánchez, Paula (60076047600); Sampaio, Jaime (8273606200)
Title: Network science in sports
Abstract: Network science has become a central methodological framework for the study of complex systems, with applications across social, biological, and technological domains. Its strength lies in formalizing such systems as collections of interacting units, whose collective behavior depends not only on the properties of the individual components, but also on the structure, dynamics, and evolution of their interactions. In this Review, we analyze how this framework, rooted in statistical physics, is being applied to the study of sports systems. Sports provide a particularly suitable domain for network modeling, as performance emerges from interactions among agents, whose actions are constrained by spatial embedding and temporal ordering, and evolve under competitive, adaptive, and out-of-equilibrium conditions. We review the main network representations used in sports, from classical graph-based descriptions to more general frameworks, including spatial, temporal, multilayer, and higher-order networks. Particular attention is devoted to soccer, where network science has had its deepest methodological impact, while applications to other sports such as basketball, volleyball, American football, or badminton serve to illustrate the generality of the underlying principles. Network science provides sports analytics with a rigorous language for quantifying coordination, emergence, adaptation, and collective performance. At the same time, the availability of high-resolution event, tracking, and pose-estimation data makes sports an ideal testbed for validating and refining network models in realistic settings. As a result, the relationship between network science and sports, currently driven primarily by the application of network methods to sport, has the potential to become genuinely bidirectional. In this Review, we not only organize the literature on network methodologies and their applications to sports, but also discuss complementary concepts needed to capture the full picture, including entropy and complexity measures, as well as key ideas from statistical physics and nonlinear dynamics. Finally, despite the substantial progress made so far, the field remains under active development, and we highlight the main open questions that should be addressed in future research. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Multi-mode ultra-low-NOX burner for hydrogen-enriched natural gas combustion: Novel in-flame temperature diagnostics and NOX performance
Abstract: For the decarbonization of hard-to-abate industries, the use of hydrogen (H2) instead of natural gas (NG) is considered a viable and technically feasible option. However, due to potentially higher temperatures within the main reaction zone, hydrogen combustion is often linked to increased nitrogen oxides (NOX) emissions compared to state-of-the-art natural gas combustion. In this paper, a novel industrial prototype burner was investigated in a standard air-fuel combustion mode and a low-NOX staged air-fuel combustion mode. The burner power varied from 270 to 337 kW , and the oxidizer flow rate was adjusted to maintain a residual oxygen concentration of 1 Vol.-% w.b. To examine the effects of the operating modes as well as the differences between NG and H2 combustion in detail, an innovative approach for recording in-flame temperatures within the main reaction zone was developed. These temperature measurements revealed fuel-specific temperature profiles perpendicular to the burner axis. The experiments showed only minor differences in NOX emissions, measured in mg/kWh , between NG and H2 combustion under the investigated operating conditions. The low-NOX mode reduced the emissions to approximately one-third of those in the standard mode. The results support the possibility of decarbonizing hard-to-abate industries using hydrogen instead of natural gas. Low-NOX combustion modes of modern industrial burners will help to comply with strict emission regulations in the future. Furthermore, the innovative temperature measurements presented in this paper proved to be a useful tool for in-depth investigations of the main reaction zone. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Surface property descriptors governing high N2 selectivity over CuO in NH3/H2 co-combustion and its implementation in structured catalysts
Abstract: The transition toward carbon-free energy has highlighted ammonia (NH3) as a promising fuel candidate. However, its practical utilization is limited by low reactivity and undesired NOx formation during combustion. In this study, catalytic NH3/H2 co-combustion over transition metal oxides (Mn2O3, Co3O4, and CuO) was systematically investigated to elucidate the governing property-activity relationships. Among the catalysts, CuO achieved complete NH3 and H2 conversion with ' 99% N2 selectivity at 500 °C, significantly outperforming Mn2O3 and Co3O4. Characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that catalytic performance is governed by surface acidity, the electronic nature of lattice oxygen (Olat), and oxygen mobility. Co3O4, characterized by abundant oxygen vacancies and high oxygen mobility, promotes rapid NH3 activation but leads to excessive NO formation. Mn2O3, possessing strong acid sites and nucleophilic Olat, favors overoxidation pathways resulting in N2O formation. In contrast, CuO exhibits weak surface acidity, electrophilic Olat, and moderate oxygen mobility, which suppress overoxidation and drive the selective reduction of NO to N2. Furthermore, CuO was successfully implemented into structured catalysts using cordierite monoliths and copper foams, retaining high activity and N2 selectivity. These findings provide mechanistic insights and practical design guidelines for developing efficient catalysts for carbon-free combustion systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Ellipsoidal cone eigenvalue complementarity problems: Solvability conditions, reformulations and numerical experiments
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: This paper investigates two variants of the ellipsoidal cone eigenvalue complementarity problem (ECEiCP). We first derive sufficient conditions for solution existence and then establish equivalent reformulations by leveraging connections between ellipsoidal cones and second-order cones, which can be reformulated as nonlinear second-order conic complementarity problems (NSOCCPs). Numerical experiments on synthetic instances show that these counterpart complementarity problems can be solved efficiently by a customized projection method with an exact residual-based stopping rule. © 2026
