Authors: Yang J.; Liu X.; Deng J.; Wang C.; Yi X.
Title: Unveiling the inhibitory mechanism of fungi on Dananhu low-rank coal spontaneous combustion: Multi-technique analysis of coal pyrolysis behavior and structural evolution
Abstract: Green mine construction demands coal spontaneous combustion inhibitors to be eco-friendly and efficient. Fungi, with their efficient enzyme systems and excellent degradation ability for low-rank coal, are potential green inhibitors. Thus, this study systematically investigated the specific roles of the lignin-degrading fungi in inhibiting coal spontaneous combustion. Experimental results showed that all three fungi could effectively suppress spontaneous combustion of Dananhu low-rank coal. P. neostrigosus , M. verrucaria , and P. chrysosporium increased the ignition temperature of Dananhu coal by 10.98, 30.80 and 6.74 °C, respectively. M. verrucaria exhibited the optimal inhibitory effect, while P. neostrigosus and P. chrysosporium showed stronger effects on the earlier-stage characteristic temperatures. The coupled TG-FTIR and Py-GC/MS technique was employed to analyze the effects of fungal inhibition on the coal pyrolysis process and characterize the pyrolysis gas products. After fungal treatment, the release of aliphatic hydrocarbons declined at low temperatures, and the generation of aromatic hydrocarbons and heteroatom compounds was reduced at high temperatures. the release of CO and CH4 from Dananhu coal were delayed, and the release of CO2 was decreased. Combined with structure characterization methods such as FTIR and X-ray diffraction, the evolution characteristics of the molecular and crystal structures of Dananhu coal under fungal action were analyzed in depth. In addition, qualitative and quantitative analyses of liquid-phase dissociation products were performed using GC–MS. Multi scale combined technology reveals the full chain inhibition mechanism of coal pyrolysis-product distribution-structural evolution, and further elucidates the pathway of fungal inhibition of coal spontaneous combustion. Three types of fungi weaken the reactivity of active functional groups such as hydroxyl, carboxyl, and aliphatic side chains in coal, remove loose structures, and promote the enrichment of aromatic nuclei and ether crosslinking. This enhanced the thermal stability of coal molecules and suppresses the spontaneous combustion of Dananhu coal. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Kentour M.; Lu J.; Xu Q.
Title: Learn the fundamental characteristics of handwritten characters for a necessary neural network calibration
Abstract: Conventional Deep Neural Network (DNN) learning process built up the DNN architecture to fit the input space, in terms of size, structure and neural shapes. But the calibration for the input data space characterisation is never realised. This paper reports “Less is More” principle and its implementation in the development of DNN. The recent phenomenal success of artificial DNN has brought a popular but false belief: the deeper the network structure and the more training data, the better. We believe “Less is More”, as the characteristic of a problem is more fundamental than the association of statistics only. We view each input sample as a composition of linked pixels in a unique pattern, and the features of such linkage should be characterised. Technically, the necessary feature for each sample is embedded in a pixel-based graph and can be extracted, typically ∼50 features per sample pattern. With these 50 characteristic features, we extracted a neater network (size of input, hidden and output layers are 64, 6 and 7 neurons, respectively), and achieved the highest accuracy (∼99.9% against all the published DNNs regardless how deep, physical or digital they are) and a higher computing efficiency (∼58% less CPU runtime). The developed DNNs bears the features of circuitry which offers better explainability. The successful application of Less is More approach supports and promotes its wider applications; it contributes to DNN methodology. We also anticipate that the developed methodology will eliminate the waste of unnecessary computational efforts such as pruning et al. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: A long-term time series prediction model based on dynamic-order polynomial fuzzy information granules
Abstract: Navigating the big data landscape, information fusion and data mining have become essential tools for extracting meaningful insights from complex datasets, particularly in the domain of time series prediction, which is crucial for fields such as finance, power systems, and environmental studies. Traditional methods often fall short due to poor interpretability, high computational costs, and an inability to capture complex patterns. Fuzzy information granule (FIG) has emerged as a solution, but current FIGs, especially Gaussian polynomial fuzzy information granules (GPFIGs), still face challenges in accurately representing data and adapting to varying trends. To address these limitations, a novel long-term time series prediction model based on dynamic-order GPFIGs is proposed. This model combines a Savitzky-Golay filter and autocorrelation function (ACF) for time series segmentation, effectively filtering noise and identifying periodicity. Subsequently, during the construction of GPFIGs, this study proposes an FMDL polynomial order selection criterion inspired by the trade-off principle of MDL. The proposed criterion employs nonparametric entropy based on the empirical distribution of residuals to measure the fitting uncertainty and introduces a parameter-number-based penalty to quantify model complexity, thereby adaptively selecting an appropriate polynomial order for different information granules. Hierarchical clustering is integrated into the fuzzy inference system (FIS) to reduce the impact of redundant rules and improve prediction accuracy. Extensive experiments on eight datasets demonstrate the model’s superior performance, achieving lower RMSE, MAE, and SMAPE compared to advanced models. For example, on the chaotic time series dataset, the model attains an RMSE of 0.0286, MAE of 0.0224, and SMAPE of 2.72% for a prediction length of 500. These results validate the model’s effectiveness and robustness in long-term time series prediction. Authors: Zhao Y.; Chen Y.; Wang X.
Title: Oscillatory-weight formal orthogonal polynomials for numerical integration
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: The theory of formal orthogonal polynomials plays a prominent role in modern numerical analysis, with applications in Padé approximation, the QD algorithm, and convergence acceleration techniques. In this paper, we construct a new class of such polynomials by introducing an oscillatory factor. Specifically, we augment the classical Hermite weight function e−x with the factor eiξx, resulting in an oscillatory weight function and the corresponding integral ∫−∞+∞f(x)e−xeiξxdx,which defines the associated linear functional. We prove the existence of these polynomials, derive their three-term recurrence relation, and establish other properties. Furthermore, we investigate the equivalence between the Christoffel-Darboux-type identity and the three-term recurrence relation: The three-term recurrence relation for a family of formal orthogonal polynomials implies the identity. Conversely, if the identity holds for a polynomial sequence, then this sequence must satisfy a three-term recurrence relation, thereby confirming it as a family of formal orthogonal polynomials. Numerical experiments are designed for computing oscillatory integral, and our new integration method based on the constructed formal orthogonal polynomials outperforms the classical Gauss-Hermite quadrature. A quadratic-phase Gaussian integral, arising in quantum scattering and Fresnel diffraction, is used to illustrate the practical utility: the new method achieves near-machine precision with n=30, while the standard method yields errors of 10−3 even at n=500. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Rapid repassivation of multi-element solid solution binders in WC-based cermet coatings during tribocorrosion
Abstract: To address the selective corrosion of the binder phase in conventional WC-Co coatings within Cl--rich environments, four WC-based coatings with distinct metallic binders (Co, CoCrMo, CoCrW, and CoCrMoW) were fabricated using high-velocity air-fuel (HVAF) spraying to systematically investigate the influences and degradation mechanisms of multi-element solid solution design on tribocorrosion performance. Static electrochemical tests identify WC-CoCrW as the coating with the highest corrosion resistance, exhibiting a corrosion potential of −0.45 V and a corrosion current density of 2.1 × 10−6 A/cm2. This performance is primarily attributed to the combined protective effects of Cr and W. Cr promotes the formation of a dense Cr2O3 passive film that suppresses Co dissolution, while WO3 formed through the oxidation of W in solid solution facilitates rapid repassivation of the protective tribofilm. The WC-CoCrW coating exhibits the highest resistance to synergistic damage caused by wear and corrosion, with a low tribocorrosion rate of 3.7 × 10−7 mm3/N·m under open-circuit potential (OCP) conditions. This study confirms that the multi-element solid solution design is an effective approach for developing high-performance thermal spray coatings for Cl--rich tribocorrosion environments. Title: Influence of steam on nature of coke formed in thermal conversion of ethanol using Ni/SBA-15 catalyst
Abstract: In steam reforming, polymerization/cracking of reactant could take place in parallel with reforming reactions, which are important routes for coking and might form coke of distinct nature with that from reforming. This study investigated the decomposition or steam reforming of ethanol over a Ni/SBA-15 catalyst at 400, 550, and 700 °C, respectively. The results indicated that decomposition of ethanol formed more abundant carbonaceous species bearing C=C at 500–600 °C than that from steam reforming. These carbon-rich intermediates were precursors of coke, rendering production of more coke (mass ratio of coke to catalyst in decomposition versus reforming: 48.6 % versus 28.2 % at 400 °C; 86.4 % versus 57.8 % at 550 °C; 28.7 % versus 8.7 % at 700 °C), due to lack of steam to oxidize them into aliphatic oxygen-containing species. A high concentration of carbonaceous intermediates in decomposition of ethanol formed more aromatic and thermally more stable coke than that from steam reforming. Coking was the most significant at 550 °C in decomposition or reforming, because of accumulation of carbonaceous intermediates from cracking and low efficiency for their gasification. This formed coke of irregular carbon nanotubes or carbon nanobeads with abundant aliphatic structures. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Interfacial stabilization of coal particulate assemblies against wind erosion and rainfall wash-off using a multiphase emulsion-based system
Abstract: Deposited coal particulate layers in open-pit mines are susceptible to wind-induced re-entrainment and rainfall wash-off, whereas conventional water spraying cannot simultaneously provide rapid wetting, moisture retention, particle consolidation, and surface protection during drying and erosion. To coordinate these functions, an O/W emulsion-based composite dust suppressant (OWD) was formulated using OT/OP-10 mixed surfactants, xanthan gum/sodium alginate, and white oil. The formulation was selected through surfactant screening and an L9 orthogonal design based on the overall balance among coal wettability, emulsion-droplet size distribution, apparent viscosity at 35 s-1, water retention, and macroscopic stability, rather than optimization of a single indicator. Component-resolved comparisons revealed a stage-dependent functional division: OT/OP-10 primarily governed initial spreading on the coal surface, the polysaccharides restricted water loss and supported interparticle consolidation, and the white-oil phase assisted intermediate emulsion spreading and contributed mainly to later-stage surface shielding. In separate laboratory tests, the OWD-treated 10–40 mesh coal bed lost 0.80% of its dry mass at the maximum tested wind speed of 12 m/s and retained 99.90% of its pre-rainfall dry mass after 10 min of simulated rainfall. FTIR and SEM observations, together with qualitative electrostatic-potential maps, were consistent with a proposed wetting-bridging-shielding mechanism. These results demonstrate that the stabilization of deposited coal particulate layers can be enhanced by coordinating complementary functions within a multiphase system rather than by maximizing an isolated performance property. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Shape-dependent motion estimation of solid fuel particles in two-phase flows using wavelet-based optical flow velocimetry (wOFV)
Abstract: The accurate measurement of the motion of rigid solid fuel particles is important for the study of many applications in energy science. These dynamics influence the particle-turbulence interaction as well as the heat and mass transfer processes governing reactor performance and chemical conversion. While many methods for the tracking of the translational velocity of such particles are available, methods for the robust measurement of angular velocity are scarce, especially for nearly circular particles and particles with complex shapes. To address the issue, this study presents a novel methodology for computing the angular velocity of dispersed particles in two-phase flows using a wavelet-based optical flow velocimetry (wOFV) algorithm. First, the applicability of wOFV for particle velocimetry was validated against a synthetic ground-truth dataset of walnut shell fragments as a representative biomass and the influence of the regularization parameter λ was investigated. It was found that for 0.01≤λ≤5, particle rotation can be accurately determined using the presented wOFV method. Additionally, findings reveal that particle shape significantly influences the performance of both wOFV and a commonly used ellipse fit tracking method, which is used as a benchmark. While the accuracy of ellipse fit tracking correlates strongly with the particle aspect ratio, the accuracy of wOFV is more strongly determined by the ellipticity of fuel particles. The implementation of a hybrid approach that integrates wOFV and ellipse fit tracking has been demonstrated to leverage the strengths of both algorithms. This is achieved through a shape-dependent selection of the most suitable algorithm for each specific particle based on a support vector machine classification. Overall, this hybrid approach yields a reduction in the median relative error of angular velocity predictions from 4.2 % (benchmark method ellipse fit tracking) to 3.7 % (hybrid method) for the employed test set. The proposed framework demonstrates considerable potential for enhancing the precision of rotational measurements in the field of particle dynamics. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Deng C.; Ding Z.; Yang Q.; Ma H.; Cheng Y.; Feng D.; Li J.; Gu Z.; Li M.
Title: Enhancement mechanism of Ce-Ni-modified vanadium–titanium magnetite in chemical looping hydrogen production
Abstract: Vanadium-titanium magnetite concentrate (VTM) oxygen carriers suffer from inherently low redox activity and sluggish oxygen migration rate, which severely constrain their application in high-efficiency chemical looping hydrogen production. To overcome these limitations, this study introduces Ce–Ni bimetals via mechanical ball milling for synergistic modification. The enhancement mechanism of hydrogen production performance in modified VTM was systematically investigated with emphasis on phase evolution, reduction behavior, and oxygen vacancy regulation. Ni doping promoted the formation of a new NiFe2O4 phase and drove the transformation of Fe3O4 to Fe2O3, thereby optimizing the redox system of the oxygen carrier. Ce doping effectively increased the oxygen vacancy concentration through local lattice distortion. The H2-TPR and CH4-TPR results consistently show that the modified oxygen carrier exhibited a reduced reduction temperature and significantly enhanced methane activation capacity. At 900 ℃, the hydrogen yield of the 10Ce20Ni sample reached 11.39 mmol/g, approximately 10.4 times higher than that of the raw ore, with a purity of 98.32%. XPS analysis further verified that Ce-Ni co-doping optimized the distribution of oxygen species on the oxygen carrier surface. Among all the samples, 10Ce20Ni possessed the highest ratio of defective oxygen (1.61), indicating the formation of a more abundant oxygen-vacancy structure. Meanwhile, the coexisting multivalence system of Ni/Ce/Fe provides an efficient electron transfer channel for lattice oxygen migration and interfacial reactions, which serves as the core intrinsic factor for improving the activity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A novel permeable wellbore completion method for gas drainage in soft coal seams: grouting material development and coal fines control mechanisms
Abstract: Borehole gas extraction in soft coal seams frequently suffers from borehole collapse, coal fines clogging, and rapid permeability decline, severely limiting long-term gas recovery efficiency. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel permeable wellbore completion method based on in-situ grouting of a pore-tunable porous polyurethane (PU) material. A series of PU slurries were formulated and optimized through 12 iterations by systematically varying the surfactant, flame retardant, and auxiliary foaming agent contents. Three representative formulations (Groups X, Z, and D) with distinct pore architectures were selected for comprehensive evaluation. The permeability, compressive strength, pore structure, and coal fines control performance were investigated under simulated reservoir conditions, including confining pressures of 0.5–3.0 MPa and high-concentration coal fines flow. Mercury intrusion porosimetry, micro-CT three-dimensional reconstruction, and SEM-based particle size analysis were employed to characterize pore-throat alterations, coal fines deposition sites, and effluent particle size distributions. The results show that all three PU groups maintained permeabilities above 1 Darcy under confining pressure, with compressive strengths ranging from 3.80 to 4.86 MPa. Group X exhibited the highest porosity (70.37%), smallest median pore diameter (190.1 μm), and greatest interception efficiency, while Group D, with the largest dominant pore diameter (810.47 μm), showed the lowest permeability damage rate (66%). Coal fines transport and retention followed a composite mechanism characterized by selective deposition at the seepage front, agglomerate/bridge formation at pore throats, and sieve-controlled penetration of finer particles, consistent with the “1/3–1/7” particle-to-pore size criterion. Particles > 100 μm tended to be intercepted, particles < 30 μm passed through more readily, and medium-sized particles (30–100 μm) formed the main internal clogging framework. Despite 66–71% permeability impairment, post-test permeabilities remained above 1 Darcy, satisfying the high-permeability requirements for gas drainage applications. This study provides a validated material design framework for achieving balanced permeability, mechanical stability, and coal fines control in soft coal seam gas extraction, offering a scalable technical pathway for enhancing long-term borehole completion reliability. Authors: Gao D.; Lu Q.; Chen C.; Pan N.; Shen H.; Wang L.
Title: Bulk-effect-enhanced tribo-piezoelectric membrane for efficient and self-sustained pollutant degradation
Abstract: To overcome the limitations of conventional electrocatalytic wastewater treatment—including high external energy consumption, low solid–liquid interfacial charge density, unstable electrical output, and severe charge backflow—we developed an excited tribo-contact electrocatalytic (E-TCE) system. This system integrates a charge excitation module and a rectified energy-storage unit into a conventional TCE setup, enabling self-powered operation. By coupling a PTFE@MoS2 composite membrane with the bulk effect, the charge transport pathway is extended from the membrane surface into the material interior, significantly enhancing interfacial charge utilization. Under optimized conditions (dual-electrode configuration, 68 nF capacitance, 0.5 g/L MoS2 loading, 20 cm droplet height, 60° membrane inclination, and 15 mg/L crystal violet (CV)), the E-TCE system achieved a CV degradation efficiency of 94.3%, with a current output of 8.3 nA and a charge output of 9.4 nC—substantially outperforming the original TCE system. The system also demonstrated broad-spectrum efficacy, degrading methyl orange (MO), rhodamine B (RhB), and tetracycline (TC), and maintained >85% CV removal after five consecutive cycles. Radical scavenging and EPR analyses identified ·O2− and ·OH as the primary reactive species, while LC-MS-based degradation pathway and ecotoxicity assessments confirmed progressive detoxification. This work presents a self-powered, bulk-effect-enhanced interfacial charge regulation strategy for sustainable water remediation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Laminar flame propagation of propylene carbonate inhibited by TMP, TEP and BtFEC: Experimental measurements and kinetic modelling
Abstract: The laminar burning velocities (LBVs) of propylene carbonate (PC) blended with flame-retardants, i.e., trimethyl phosphate (TMP), triethyl phosphate (TEP), and bis(2,2,2-trifluoroethyl) carbonate (BtFEC), respectively, were measured in a constant-volume combustion chamber with additive ratios of 1 %, 3 %, and 5 % by mole fraction. The experiments were performed at an initial temperature (T0) of 493 K and initial pressure (P0) of 1 bar with equivalence ratios ( φ ) ranging from 0.7 to 1.4. At φ = 1.1, the experimental LBV of neat PC was 74.0 cm·s⁻1. With 5 % TMP, TEP, and BtFEC, the LBVs decreased to 47.9, 48.0, and 59.8 cm·s⁻1, corresponding to inhibition ratios of 35.3 %, 35.2 %, and 19.1 %, respectively. A kinetic mechanism calibrated and evaluated for LBV prediction under the investigated conditions was developed and shown to accurately reproduce the measured LBVs obtained in this study. Kinetic analysis using this mechanism shows that the inhibiting effects of TMP and TEP are mainly caused by radical scavenging, while BtFEC reduces the LBVs of PC via both chemical and physical effects. Sensitivity and reaction-path analyses reveal that TMP and TEP affect chain-branching reactions via phosphorus-containing intermediates, while BtFEC primarily interferes with chain-branching reactions through fluorine-based radical scavenging. This study fills the gap in the basic experimental data and kinetic mechanism of PC/flame-retardants, providing data for the development of safer electrolyte formulations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Bazirha Z.; Azrar L.
Title: Efficient finite volume schemes for the Burgers’ equations and the Keller–Segel system with additional cross-diffusion terms and a logistic source
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: A linear finite volume scheme based on the Two-Point Flux Approximation (TPFA) is developed for the coupled Burgers’ equations and the Keller–Segel (KS) model, the latter featuring novel cross-diffusion terms and a logistic source. By employing a semi-implicit time discretization, the proposed approach significantly reduces computational cost by avoiding the nonlinear systems typically associated with these models. The scheme is formulated within a general framework that accommodates both centered and upwind spatial discretizations. Under suitable temporal constraints, existence and uniqueness are rigorously established for the resulting linear systems through the properties of non-singular M-matrices. Moreover, the preservation of non-negativity is ensured through this structure: the upwind discretization yields this property unconditionally, whereas the centered discretization satisfies it only under local stability conditions. Numerical experiments validate the method's accuracy and efficiency. For the Burgers’ equations, a second-order rate of convergence is observed at high Reynolds numbers in both the discrete L2 and L∞ norms. The robustness of the scheme is confirmed by its application to a benchmark problem with mixed boundary conditions. For the Keller–Segel model, the positivity of the velocity field is numerically verified, and the method successfully simulates blow-up phenomena at various locations within a square domain. By varying parameters, we analyze the time evolution of the maximum solution value. The results demonstrate that while both the logistic source and classical cross-diffusion terms cause the maximum value to decrease over time after reaching its peak, this decrease occurs more rapidly with the novel cross-diffusion terms introduced in this work. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Du R.; Li H.; Zhang W.; Liu W.; Mai Q.; Fan M.
Title: A comprehensive review of coal gasification slag as a cementitious material: From reactivity activation to environmental implications
Abstract: Coal gasification slag (CGS), a byproduct of the coal chemical industry, possesses the potential for producing low-carbon CGS-based cementitious materials (CCMs). Its utilization is limited by low intrinsic reactivity and potential risks associated with potentially toxic elements (PTEs). This review systematically summarizes the reactivity, activation and excitation mechanisms of CGS, as well as the utilization pathways and environmental behavior of CCMs. The low reactivity of CGS is mainly attributed to its highly polymerized aluminosilicate glass network and its interlocking structure with residual carbon. Mechanical and thermal activation can enhance its reactivity, while emerging activation technologies provide alternative routes for reducing energy-intensive treatments. Alkali, salt, acid, and solid-waste synergistic excitation further promote CGS dissolution and hydration. CCMs show considerable potential in mine backfilling, concrete, non-fired bricks and ceramsites, although their application is constrained by material performance and rheological requirements. Meanwhile, CCM formation can effectively suppress the leaching of most PTEs. Overall, low-cost activation, application-oriented utilization, and long-term environmental safety are key to the large-scale deployment of CCMs. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhang J.; Li Z.; Xu L.
Title: Multidimensional reflected McKean-Vlasov mixed stochastic delay differential equation
Source title: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
Abstract: In this article, we study the existence and uniqueness of strong solutions for a class of multidimensional reflected McKean-Vlasov mixed stochastic delay differential equations driven by a combination of mutually independent Brownian motions and fractional Brownian motions with Hurst parameter H>1/2. The main challenge lies in the fact that conventional methods, such as the fixed-point theorem and the contraction mapping principle, cannot be directly applied due to the mixture of stochastic integrals and pathwise integrals, along with the non-Lipschitz drift. We establish pathwise uniqueness for these mixed-type equations through an iterative method. Building upon pathwise uniqueness, we prove the existence and uniqueness of strong solutions for the mixed equations by employing the Euler scheme and a generalized Gronwall lemma. As applications, strong convergence and convergence rate in the finite time of the Euler-Maruyama method on the particle system is discussed. Lastly, the numerical example is investigated to illustrate the theory. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Ma C.; Luo T.; Han T.; Qureshi M.F.; Liu Y.; Ma C.; Yang W.; Wu P.; Li Y.
Title: Pore-scale visualization of hydrate formation and morphological evolution in heterogeneous porous media via microfluidic chip
Abstract: Hydrate-based CO2 sequestration (HBCS) is regarded as a potential approach for achieving CO2 long-term, safe storage. Pore-structure heterogeneity in porous media can markedly affect CO2 transport, gas–liquid distribution, and hydrate nucleation and growth. Hydrate morphological evolution governs critical processes such as pore-throat blockage and thus holds significant engineering implications for HBCS. In this study, a high-pressure microfluidic visualization platform was employed to examine the formation process and morphological evolution of CO2 hydrates in heterogeneous porous media and to compare hydrate growth behavior between homogeneous and heterogeneous media, as well as between a pure-water system and 0.03 wt% L-methionine system. The results indicate the following: In heterogeneous porous media, channels with higher connectivity are preferentially invaded by CO2. Continuous hydrate clusters are initially formed by rapid expansion along these preferential pathways and, at later stages, punctate hydrate, branched hydrate, and striped hydrate are observed near local pore throats and grain boundaries. Heterogeneous media exhibit stronger spatial selectivity in gas–liquid distribution and hydrate formation than do homogeneous media. Hydrate synchronous nucleation at multiple locations within regular pore units is observed in homogeneous media, yielding an overall distribution that corresponds to the regular particle array. The principal pathway of hydrate formation along the preferential channels was not altered by the presence of 0.03 wt% L-methionine. However, fine fragmented branching and localized stripe-like morphologies at hydrate edges were accentuated during the late stages. This study provides direct pore-scale evidence of CO2 hydrate growth in heterogeneous media, with the aim of offering mechanistic insights for improving the spatial uniformity of hydrate formation in heterogeneous reservoirs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Flow boiling heat transfer enhancement on plasma-engineered copper surfaces in a macrochannel under saturated conditions
Abstract: Saturated flow boiling represents one of the most effective methods for dissipating high heat fluxes; nevertheless, the efficiency is limited by hydrodynamic instabilities and premature CHF. This study systematically examines the influence of cold atmospheric plasma surface modification of copper on flow boiling behavior in a macrochannel. Plasma treatment transformed the initially nearly hydrophobic copper surface (contact angle ≈ 90.1°) into a stable hydrophilic one (contact angle ≈ 55.8°). Surface characterization using AFM, SEM, EDX, and FT-IR showed a moderate rise in roughness (Ra ≈ 28 nm) along with oxygen-rich polar functionalities. These modifications enhanced liquid spreading, accelerated rewetting, and facilitated early activation of nucleation sites. Consequently, the ONB occurred at substantially lower wall superheats, with reductions of approximately 57–63% compared with untreated copper. Flow boiling measurements revealed substantial thermal gains: the HTC increased by about 127–155%, while the CHF was augmented by roughly 114–147% relative to the bare surface. Based on the experimental database, a new empirical correlation was developed for predicting the two-phase heat transfer coefficient, accounting for the combined effects of surface roughness, porosity, and wettability. Repeated heating–cooling cycles demonstrated that plasma-modified surfaces retain structural integrity and functional enhancements. Overall, cold atmospheric plasma treatment provides a robust, durable, and scalable route for improving CHF and HTC in high heat flux systems. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Title: Enhancement of nitrogen and phosphorus removal by coupling pyrite-based autotrophic denitrification with an electro-enhanced A2/O process
Abstract: Conventional anaerobic-anoxic-oxic (A2/O) processes often exhibit low nutrient removal efficiency and high operational costs when treating carbon-limited wastewater from highway service areas. In this study, a pyrite-based autotrophic denitrification process coupled with an electro-enhanced A2/O system (PE-A2/O) was developed to treat synthetic highway service-area wastewater. At an applied voltage of 1.2 V, the reactor configured with an anoxic anode and an oxic cathode achieved the best nutrient-removal performance. The removal efficiencies of NH4+-N, TN, and PO43−-P reached 96.89 ± 3.18%, 94.08 ± 4.99%, and 58.73 ± 3.02%, respectively, representing increases of 25.36%, 28.87%, and 20.20% compared with the control reactor. Pyrite oxidation released Fe2+ and sulfur species that supported autotrophic denitrification, while Fe2+/Fe3+ cycling promoted Fe-mediated phosphate sequestration through precipitation and surface complexation. The PE-A2/O process enriched electroactive genera, including Desulfovibrio and Sulfurospirillum, and denitrifying genera, including Thermomonas and Rhodanobacter. It also increased the relative abundances of genes associated with iron, sulfur, and nitrogen cycling, indicating enhanced functional potential for coupled Fe-S-N transformations. Collectively, this study demonstrates an A2/O-compatible PE-A2/O strategy that integrates pyrite-mediated autotrophic denitrification with electro-enhanced electron transfer, providing a mineral-electrode-microbe pathway for simultaneous nitrogen and phosphorus removal from carbon-limited wastewater. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: pH-tailored chitin nanocrystal-zein complexes as interfacial stabilizers for dysphagia-friendly 3D-printed bicontinuous bigels
Abstract: Bicontinuous bigels (BCBG) are promising semi-solid edible inks for 3D printing dysphagia-friendly foods. However, their performance is often limited by physical instability arising from poor oil–water interfacial resilience to deformation during printing. Here, pH-regulated chitin nanocrystal–zein (C-Z) complexes were prepared as food-grade interfacial stabilizers to reinforce the BCBG network while preserving printability and lubrication properties. The assembly behavior of C-Z complexes was governed by preparation pH, which regulated the electrical characteristics of chitin nanocrystals (ChNCs) and zein. The C-Z complexes were partly stabilized by electrostatic repulsion at pH 4.5–5.5 (C-Z4.5 and C-Z5.5) where both ChNCs and zein were positively charged. Compact, electrostatically associated complexes were formed at pH 6.0–6.5 (C-Z6.0 and C-Z6.5) through attraction between cationic ChNCs and anionic zein. Precipitates were formed at pH 7.5 (C-Z7.5) due to weakened electrostatic stabilization. Notably, the C-Z6.5 complexes exhibited the most compact morphology and an equilibrium interfacial tension of 9.0 mN/m. When incorporated into BCBG, C-Z6.5 was enriched at the oleogel–hydrogel interface and reinforced the bicontinuous network. The resulting C-Z6.5-BCBG systems showed improved deformation resistance and structural recovery, including creep recovery of 57.0% and thixotropic recovery of 71.1%. C-Z6.5-BCBG maintained high printing accuracy, with deformation rates of 2.46% and 1.86% for hollow irregular cube and cone models, respectively. Moreover, this formulation exhibited effective lubrication performance with the lowest friction coefficient (0.0065) and IDDSI Level 5-like textural characteristics. This work demonstrates pH-regulated protein–nanocrystal complexes as an effective interfacial strategy for dysphagia-oriented 3D-printed bigel inks. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Geng W.; Chen J.; Guo C.; Yan B.; Ren H.; Dai C.; Zhao G.; Li H.
Title: Mechanistic insights into CO2 channeling control and enhanced heavy-oil recovery using a smart CO2-reactive polymeric surfactant
Abstract: CO2 flooding can improve heavy-oil mobility, but CO2 readily channels through preferential pathways, limiting the swept volume and leaving substantial residual oil trapped in low-permeability regions and small-to-medium pores. In this work, the reservoir applicability of a frustrated Lewis pair-based CO2-reactive thickening polymeric surfactant system (PMSA/PMSB) is systematically evaluated, and its mechanisms for CO2 channeling control and residual-oil mobilization are investigated at both the core and pore scales. The results show that the PMSA/PMSB system exhibits good injectability and maintains plugging efficiencies above 85 % in cores with permeabilities ranging from 500 × 10−3 to 4500 × 10−3 μm2. The suitable injection volume, injection rate, and aging time are determined to be 0.6–0.8 PV, 0.1–0.3 mL·min−1, and 24 h, respectively. Before CO2 triggering, the PMSA/PMSB can migrate through preferential pathways and become adsorbed and retained on rock surfaces and within the pore space. Upon CO2 triggering, the system forms a covalently crosslinked thickened network that increases the flow resistance of high-permeability channels through rock-surface coverage, pore-space filling, and pore-throat bridging, thereby redirecting subsequent CO2 toward previously poorly swept regions. Low-field nuclear magnetic resonance results show that oil recovery from small pores increases from 9.09 % to 35.87 %, while the overall oil recovery increases from 29.73 % to 49.31 %, corresponding to an incremental recovery of 19.58 % after profile control. Pore-scale visualization further demonstrates that the PMSA/PMSB promotes the deformation, detachment, fragmentation, and migration of network-like, cluster-like, columnar, and film-like residual oil. This work reveals the synergistic mechanism among CO2-reactive thickening and plugging, fluid diversion, and emulsification-assisted residual-oil mobilization, providing a theoretical basis for CO2 channeling control and efficient residual-oil recovery in heavy oil reservoirs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Di L.; Zhang A.; Liu J.; Yang Y.
Title: Cadmium adsorption on iron ore in oxy-fuel combustion flue gas: An experimental and mechanism insight
Abstract: Oxy-fuel combustion is a promising technology for CO2 capture, but the release and migration of cadmium (Cd) during oxy-coal combustion pose risks to the ecosystem and human health. Cd emission during oxy-coal combustion still lacks effective control technology. In this work, four typical iron ores (hematite, ilmenite, limonite, and siderite) were used as adsorbents to systematically investigate the Cd adsorption performance and mechanism under oxy-fuel combustion. The results show that limonite exhibits the highest Cd adsorption performance, with a maximum adsorption capacity of 13.25 mg/g at 900 °C, which originates from its abundant Fe2O3 component providing sufficient surface Fe active sites to form stable Cd-O-Fe. Temperature has a significant impact on the adsorption performance. Within the range of 700–900 °C, the Cd adsorption capacity increases with the rise of temperature. When the temperature exceeds 900 °C, the Cd adsorption capacity decreases sharply. Kinetic analysis shows that the adsorption process of iron ores follows the pseudo-second-order kinetic model, and the adsorption rate is mainly controlled by chemical adsorption. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed to clarify the interfacial adsorption mechanism of CdO on the Fe2O3 surface. Structural optimization identified two stable adsorption configurations at the Fe-top site and dual-site on the Fe2O3 surface, with calculated adsorption energies of −327.98 kJ/mol and −401.17 kJ/mol, respectively. Further electronic analysis revealed the distinct interfacial electron redistribution among Cd and Fe atoms during CdO adsorption, accompanied by significant charge transfer and orbital hybridization around the adsorption sites. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Liu C.; Song Y.; Li X.; Yang C.; Wang Y.; Li W.; Yan Y.; Sun S.; Qi G.; Lu C.
Title: A biomimetic “reservoir-release-support” strategy for high-performance self-lubricating polyimide coatings
Abstract: This study went beyond the lubrication mechanisms of conventional nanofillers and liquid lubricants. Inspired by the lubrication mechanism of human synovial fluid, a biomimetic coating was designed. This study develops polyimide (PI)-based composite coatings incorporating gallium-based liquid metal (GLM) as boundary lubricant, covalent organic frameworks (COF) as controlled‑release shell, and Ti3C2Tx MXene as layered load‑bearing skeleton. In these coatings, GLM is encapsulated by COF and anchored onto MXene. The coatings are designed and fabricated via compounding with PI, yielding the final designation GLM@COF/Ti3C2Tx/PI. The optimal filler content was 0.6 wt%. Under this condition, the coating achieved a friction coefficient of 0.22. Its wear rate was 2.8 × 10−6 mm3/(N·m). These values were 35.3% and 82.7% lower than those of neat PI, respectively. In addition, excellent thermal stability and stable lubrication for over 10 h were maintained by the coating. The excellent performance was attributed to the synergistic effect among the load-bearing support of MXene, the controlled release of COF, and the dynamic lubrication of GLM. By this synergistic effect, persistent interfacial lubrication and wear protection similar to that of articular cartilage were enabled. A new strategy for designing high-durability self-lubricating polymer composite coatings is provided by the present work. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Jiang B.; Yao S.-P.; Wang W.-Z.; Li X.-Y.; Li J.; Jia H.H.; Han R.-M.; Skibsted L.H.; Zhang J.-P.
Title: Visible outshines ultraviolet light in promotion of melanin formation: the pivotal role of dopachrome as a reaction intermediate
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Melanin formation represents a fundamental research focus that bridges diverse fields, including cell biology, medicine, food science, cosmeceutical science, and materials science. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms that drive this process, particularly the common principle behind light-accelerated food browning and skin pigmentation, remain poorly understood. Using a tyrosinase-catalyzed monophenol oxidation model, we found that light exposure affects neither the initial enzymatic oxidation of monophenols to dopachrome (DC) nor the subsequent polymerization of 5,6-dihydroxyindole (DHI) and 5,6-dihydroxyindole-2-carboxylic acid (DHICA) into melanin. Instead, our findings reveal that light enhances melanin formation by specifically acting on the DC intermediate. Visible light promotes melanin formation via an excited-state proton transfer mechanism within DC. By contrast, under UV irradiation, a competing photolysis reaction involving the phenolic hydroxyl group of DC occurs at a higher excited state, which diminishes the efficiency of melanin formation. This stronger promoting effect of visible light, relative to UV light, was consistently demonstrated in both homogeneous solutions and mushroom systems. Our work elucidates a key photochemical pathway in melanin formation and provides a mechanistic basis for developing strategies to regulate photo-induced pigmentary disorders and control food browning. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Duan K.; Kang Y.
Title: Oxygen-vacancy-engineered Z-scheme In2O3/AgVO3 heterojunctions for boosted photocatalytic dye degradation: Interfacial charge separation and mechanistic insights
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: A precipitation-calcination and in-situ deposition process is used to generate a Z -scheme In2O3/AgVO3 heterojunction photocatalyst with abundant oxygen and to characterize its microstructural, compositional, and optoelectronic properties in different ways. Detailed characterizations show that the oxygen vacancies well-tuned the electronic structure and narrowed down the bandgap to 2.40 eV and red-shifted its photo-response edge to 569 nm. Optimized equimolar composite showed outstanding photocatalytic activity under visible light irradiation with a 98.95% degradation rate of methylene blue (MB) after 90 min, showing good structural stability during five cycles. Importantly, the detailed band structure analysis together with radical scavenger test revealed a direct Z -scheme charge transfer mechanism. Photo-generated electrons accumulated in the conduction band of AgVO3 whereas holes remained in the valence band of In2O3; such spatial charge separation not only suppressed the carriers' recombination but also maintained the strong redox capability. Our results emphasize the novel synergy between defect engineering and heterojunction construction, offering a solid theoretical foundation for designing high-performance indium-based photocatalysts for environmental remediation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Sun D.; Wang T.; Luo C.; Xiao R.; Yang W.; Cheng Y.; Liu M.; Xiong Z.; Zhang J.; Zhao Y.
Title: Mercury emission characteristics and control in coal-fired power plants: field evaluation of APCDs and enhanced Hg0 removal by Cu-Fe co-impregnated magnetospheres
Abstract: This study investigated the mercury emission and control characteristics of different coal-fired power plants (315 MW and 640 MW). The effects of conventional air pollution control devices (APCDs) on mercury speciation and removal were systematically analyzed by measuring mercury content in raw coal, flue gas, fly ash, bottom ash, gypsum, and desulfurization wastewater. To achieve near-zero mercury emissions, magnetospheres (MF) co-impregnated with copper chloride and ferric chloride were employed to replace commercial activated carbon (AC), and their elemental mercury (Hg0) removal performance was evaluated. The results showed that mercury was mainly present in flue gas and fly ash, accounting for 44.6–61.3% and 24.8–47.0% of the total mercury (HgT). Authors: Su B.; Wu Z.; Zhang J.; Liu L.; Tan Y.; Hao R.; Luo Z.; Wang T.
Title: Role of active components in composite dry water materials for suppressing hydrogen-blended natural gas explosions: An experimental investigation and discussion of plausible suppression mechanisms
Abstract: Hydrogen blending can significantly alter the explosion behavior of natural gas and increase safety concerns. Mixtures with hydrogen blending ratios of 0–30% and equivalence ratios of 0.8, 1.0, and 1.2 were tested to obtain the explosion pressure, pressure rise rate, and flame propagation behavior. Authors: Fu M.; Cui X.; Jin G.; Liu Y.; Zhang Q.; Chen D.; Tian S.
Title: Vanadium-regulated microstructure and temperature-dependent wear behavior of EHLA-fabricated Ni-rich multi-principal-element alloy coatings on EH40 steel
Abstract: Wear-related surface degradation limits the application of EH40 steel under ambient- and low-temperature conditions. The coatings were designated V0, V2, V4, and V6, respectively, and their microstructure, hardness, and reciprocating dry-sliding behavior at 25 and −40 ℃ were systematically investigated. Increasing the V content progressively increased the coating hardness, whereas the wear resistance varied non-monotonically. V4 exhibited the best wear resistance at both temperatures, while V6 showed increased cracking, delamination, and debris removal despite its higher hardness and lower friction coefficient. Lowering the temperature to −40 ℃ increased the friction coefficients but reduced the wear rates of all coatings. Authors: Li M.; Wang L.; Huang S.; Zhang Q.
Title: Hyperspectral image classification under label noise via multi-scale dual-view graph and dual-homogeneity
Abstract: Supervised classification of hyperspectral images (HSIs) is often degraded by label noise, which can distort class boundaries and reduce the reliability of learned models. To address this issue, this paper proposes a robust label cleansing framework termed Multi-scale Dual-View Graph with Dual-Homogeneity Constraint (MDVG-DHC). The method constructs a reliable affinity graph by jointly exploiting long-range spectral consistency and short-range spatial continuity, and further improves graph quality through a dual-homogeneity criterion that suppresses unreliable or ambiguous samples. In addition, an Edge-Robust Label Correction (ERLC) mechanism is introduced to reduce the risk of over-smoothing during label propagation and preserve fine structures and boundary details. Experiments on the Salinas, PaviaU, and KSC datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves consistently competitive classification performance under different noise levels. The results show that MDVG-DHC is particularly effective in high-noise scenarios, where it provides a favorable balance between noisy-label correction and geometric structure preservation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Li W.; Feng A.; Zeng S.; Liu Q.; Zheng X.; Hu Q.; Yang S.; Zheng B.; Chen H.
Title: Low-temperature protection mechanism of scallop protein peptides on gluten protein under freeze-thaw cycles: Quality, structural characteristics, and interaction mechanisms
Abstract: Frozen dough is highly susceptible to repeated freeze-thaw (FT) cycles during storage and transportation, which compromises the gluten protein network and deteriorates product quality. Consequently, identifying highly efficient cryoprotectants for gluten proteins is of significant importance. Microstructural analysis revealed that SPP optimized pore distribution, yielding a more intact and compact network architecture. Authors: Dai X.; Yin H.; Yang X.; Yang K.; Song Y.; Wang Z.; Yang J.; She X.; Xu H.
Title: Insights into photocatalytic CO2 reduction mechanism over a novel CdIn2S4/PCN S-scheme heterojunction

Abstract: Photocatalytic CO2 reduction technology is a highly promising green and low-carbon technology, which realizes resource-oriented conversion and utilization of CO2 by virtue of natural solar energy. Title: Group zero-norm regularized robust loss minimization: Proximal MM method and statistical error bound

Abstract: This paper concerns the group zero-norm regularized robust loss minimization problems. Title: Supercritical methane adsorption in deep high-rank coal: Implications for in situ gas content estimation
Abstract: Deep coalbed methane is a key target for unconventional gas exploration in China. However, the multiscale occurrence mechanisms of supercritical methane in deep high-rank coal and the estimation of in situ gas content remain uncertain. In this study, eight samples, comprising seven high-rank coals and one carbonaceous mudstone reference from the southeastern Ordos Basin were analyzed using low-temperature CO2 adsorption, low-temperature N2 adsorption–desorption, high-pressure mercury intrusion, and supercritical methane adsorption at formation temperatures. The supercritical Langmuir (SL), supercritical Dubinin–Radushkevich (SDR), and coupled SL + SDR models were evaluated. Theoretical methane contents based on pore-scale mechanisms were compared with field-desorption gas contents from pressure-retained sealed cores. The results show that micropores dominated the pore system, while organic-matter abundance and thermal maturity showed positive relationships with pore development. The SL + SDR model generally exhibited better fitting and predictive performance, supporting the coexistence of micropore filling and monolayer adsorption. Within 328.15–338.15 K, approximately 1 nm can serve as a practical pore-size boundary between these mechanisms. Maximum adsorption capacities calculated from full-scale pore parameters were consistent with the SL + SDR-fitted values, indicating that pore structure constrains methane adsorption capacity. Although methane remains predominantly in the adsorbed phase, the proportion of free gas is higher than that in shallow coal seams. Title: Roles of reactive radicals and alkali and alkaline earth metal forms in ambient-temperature oxidation and rapid self-heating of low-rank coal char
Abstract: The safe energy utilization of pyrolyzed low-rank coal char is limited by its rapid ambient-temperature oxidation, which may cause self-heating hazards and hazardous gas release during storage and transport. Relative self-heating risk index was further proposed to classify the relative hazards of different chars. Increasing pyrolysis temperature promoted microcrystalline ordering and was accompanied by higher radical concentrations and stronger self-heating responses, particularly for pyrolyzed chars derived from raw coal and H2O-treated coal prepared at 500-600°C. These pyrolysis-generated reactive radicals serve as initial sites for O2 attack, but their concentration alone cannot fully determine the self-heating intensity. Chemical fractionation of Raw-BRXL-derived chars revealed a clear temperature-dependent redistribution of Ca and Mg among different occurrence forms. The lower O2 consumption and temperature-rise responses observed for the pyrolyzed chars produced from NH4Cl-treated coal and HCl-treated coal further point to an additional relationship between the redistributed AAEM fractions and ambient-temperature oxidation. Authors: Uporov S.A.; Evdokimov I.V.
Title: Piezoresistive effect in complex concentrated alloys: A review
Abstract: The development of metallic strain-gauge materials capable of reliable operation under extreme thermal conditions, ranging from cryogenic environments to high-temperature aerospace applications, is among the pivotal challenges in modern materials science. Conventional strain-gauge alloys, such as Constantan and Manganin, exhibit optimal performance only near room temperature, severely limiting their utility in harsh operational settings. Recent studies have positioned multi-component body-centered cubic (BCC) solid solutions composed of Group IV and V transition metals as promising candidates for next-generation piezoresistive sensors. These complex alloys demonstrate anomalously high gauge factors, substantially exceeding those of conventional materials, while simultaneously exhibiting near-zero temperature coefficients of resistance and negligible thermopower over a broad temperature range extending down to cryogenic conditions. Moreover, most of these systems are characterized by high mechanical strength, ductility, and excellent resistance to cyclic fatigue failure under long-term deformation, making this class of solids highly favorable for sensing applications. This research provides a comprehensive overview of the available experimental data on electron-transport properties, temperature-dependent resistivity, hydrostatic compression, uniaxial tension, and high-temperature X-ray diffraction analysis of crystallographic anisotropy in a series of equiatomic alloys of the Ti–Nb–(Zr,Hf,Ta) family. Furthermore, the physical mechanisms underlying the abnormal piezoresistive effect in concentrated transition-metal alloys are discussed. This review places special emphasis on how these remarkable transport properties are predominantly governed by elastic crystal anisotropy and specific strain-induced modifications of the crystalline structure associated with pronounced anisotropic effects. In summary, we discuss the formulated fundamentals and derived theoretical models that enable a robust interpretation of the exceptional resistivity-strain sensitivity observed in most complex refractory alloys. We believe that the revealed physical principles underlying these unique electron-transport properties will stimulate further research and development in this field, thereby facilitating the design and compositional screening of advanced sensing materials for extreme-environment applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Zhang P.; Ji Y.; Yu C.; Yang Y.
Title: Theoretical study on the transition condition of operating modes in the large-diameter oscillating heat pipe
Abstract: In the large-diameter oscillating heat pipe, the effect of gravity becomes more pronounced, and the surface tension no longer dominates. There are two operating modes for the flow behavior of vapor-liquid plugs under different operating conditions. According to the visualization of the single-bend large-diameter oscillating heat pipe made of glass, this paper demonstrates that vapor-liquid plugs have two distinct operating modes: thermosyphon mode and oscillation mode. Furthermore, taking the liquid slug as the object of analysis, a mathematical model of the transition condition is established through energy conservation and force analysis, with the error relative to experimental results falling within 25%. Based on this model, the critical heating power and corresponding total heat input required for operating in the oscillation mode (transition condition between operating modes) are proposed. It is found that increasing the filling ratio or the length of the adiabatic section requires more heat input to achieve the oscillation mode, yet reduces the necessary heating power; whereas increasing the inner diameter increases both the required heat input and the heating power. Therefore, reducing the filling ratio, the length of the adiabatic section, or the inner diameter promotes the oscillation mode in the large-diameter oscillating heat pipe. Copyright © 2026. Title: T1 phase-mediated low cycle fatigue behavior and hardening/softening mechanism in a strong-ductile Al-Cu-Li alloy
Abstract: The main strengthening T1 phase plays a crucial role in mechanical properties of aluminum-copper-lithium (Al-Cu-Li) alloys. However, their fatigue behavior and properties are usually suggested to be associated with one-step shear deformation of T1 phase. Here, we studied T1 phase-mediated low-cycle fatigue (LCF) behavior and hardening/softening mechanism in a cyclic pre-deformed Al-Cu-Li alloy subjected to peak-aging. Our peak-aged alloy obtained the peak microhardness of 190 HV, yield strength of ∼570 MPa, and fracture elongation of ∼17 %. The peak-aged alloy also exhibited distinct LCF behavior of cyclic stability, hardening or/and softening at different strain amplitude, while its fatigue life decreased with the strain amplitude increasing. Experimental observations indicated that single-layer T1 phase dominated the peak-aged alloy. We found that T1 precipitates, especially those in slip bands, were subjected to severe reaction with abundant mobile dislocations during LCF, producing one-layer or multi-layer steps at T1-matrix interfaces. Importantly, initial resistance of T1 phase to dislocations provided the cyclic hardening at early stage of high strain amplitude (0.7 % or 0.8 %). With the increasing of fatigue cycles and strain accumulations, dynamic balance between resistance of T1 phase and continuous dislocation slip could lead to the cyclic stability, especially at low strain amplitude (0.5 % or 0.6 %). But, profuse T1 precipitates were sheared by mobile dislocations severely, especially those in slip bands, resulting in the cyclic softening at high strain amplitude (0.8 % or 1.0 %). Title: A novel biomimetic fish-scale flow field for mass transfer enhancement and performance optimization in PEMFCs
Abstract: The design and optimization of flow fields are critical for enhancing water management and oxygen transport in proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) at high current densities. The results indicate that the SAFF significantly improves the cell performance by enhancing oxygen transport and water management. Subsequently, a two-step sequential optimization of the key structural parameters of the SAFF is conducted under the same operating conditions: first, the number of baffles per row is optimized, and then, based on these results, the optimal number of rows is further determined, thereby deriving the optimal baffle arrangement. Finally, the optimal SAFF, consisting of 7 baffles per row and 11 rows, achieves a maximum power density that is 7.04 % and 11.52 % higher than those of the PAFF and CPFF, respectively. Title: Influence of electron beam irradiation on the textural quality of mung beans and the hierarchical structure and physicochemical properties of isolated starch
Abstract: This study investigated the effects of electron beam irradiation (EBI) on the textural properties of mung beans and the characteristics of starch isolated from EBI-treated grains, aiming to examine the association between starch modifications and textural changes. These structural changes decreased pasting viscosity, enthalpy, and swelling power while increasing solubility (from 12.14% to 32.99%) and shifting the onset and peak gelatinization temperatures to higher values. Authors: Ansari M.K.; Kumar S.
Title: Two-stage air injection for NOx reduction in ammonia-hydrogen flameless combustion
Abstract: Ammonia-hydrogen blends are emerging as promising carbon-free fuels for gas turbine and industrial combustion systems. However, lean combustion typically produces high NOx emissions due to fuel-bound nitrogen in ammonia and elevated concentrations of reactive O/H radicals, while rich combustion leads to excessive unburned ammonia and hydrogen emissions. Numerical simulations using a chemical reactor network (CRN) coupled with CFD analysis demonstrate that two-stage combustion significantly suppresses NOx formation across lean, near-stoichiometric, and rich regimes. The staged configuration substantially lowers unburnt NH3 and H2 emissions in rich mixtures. CFD results indicate improved dilution characteristics in the two-stage mode (Rdil ≈ 4) compared to single-stage combustion (Rdil ≈ 1), contributing to highly recirculated and distributed reaction zones. Title: A unified experimental-numerical assessment of Cable, Pile, and Zone solid rockbolt models in FLAC3D: bond-slip, load transfer, and model selection
Abstract: Cable, Pile, and Zone solid rockbolt models are widely used for rockbolt simulation in FLAC3D, but their differences under consistently calibrated interface conditions remain unclear. This study establishes an experimental–numerical framework for their comparative assessment. Under bilinear interface conditions, the Cable and Pile models produced similar global responses, whereas the Zone solid rockbolt model showed stronger spatial nonuniformity associated with explicit geometry and contact representation. The nonlinear relationship enabled the Pile and Zone solid models to reproduce progressive slip, stress redistribution, and post-peak degradation. Title: Experimental and numerical study of the effect of operating-parameter on steam-diluted H2/O2 micromix combustion

Title: Omni-UDG: A stable learning framework for unsupervised generalizable person re-identification

To address these limitations, we propose an offline-to-online framework, Multi-Agent Constrained Decision Transformer (MACDT), for multi-USV pursuit-evasion missions. This modeling is conditioned on historical states, actions, reward-to-go, and cost-to-go, enabling the policy to identify effective pursuit and evasion maneuvers. It further introduces a sequence-level entropy regularizer to promote strategy exploration. In the online stage, the safety-aware policy learned from offline data is deployed and refined using Multi-Agent Constrained Policy Optimization (MACPO) with prior knowledge. By updating the policy within both the trust and constraint regions, MACDT balances safety, mission success, and cooperative efficiency in highly dynamic adversarial surface environments. Title: An efficient branch-and-bound method for linear multiplicative programming using mixed-binary convex underestimators
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: We develop a branch-and-bound algorithm for linear multiplicative programming (LMP), a nonconvex problem whose product structure gives rise to multiple local optima and complicates global solution. The method reformulates LMP using a difference-of-squares transformation and constructs a mixed-binary piecewise-linear underestimator for each squared term. This underestimator is further tightened by bisecting each variable interval, and the resulting lower bounds are tighter than those obtained from standard single-secant relaxations. Based on this relaxation, we prove that the algorithm terminates within finite iterations for a given tolerance and provide an explicit bound on the iteration count. Numerical experiments on benchmark and randomly generated instances show that the proposed method requires fewer iterations than four recent methods on problems with a moderately large number of variables, although its per-node computational cost can be high for small or simple instances. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Liu J.; Gong W.; Li Y.; Wu D.; Cui H.; Yu X.; Liu W.; Wang Y.
Title: Tribological behavior and wear mechanisms of APS–FSP AlCoCrFeNi particle-reinforced AZ31 surface composites
Abstract: In this work, AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy (HEA) particle-reinforced AZ31 surface composites were fabricated by a hybrid atmospheric plasma spraying/friction stir processing (APS–FSP) route to improve the dry sliding wear resistance of magnesium alloy. HEA particles with designed volume fractions of 0, 5, 10 and 15 vol% were introduced into the AZ31 surface layer to clarify the roles of microstructure and interface stability in wear degradation. FSP disrupted the lamellar sprayed layer, reduced deposition-related defects, and redistributed HEA particles uniformly within the stir zone (SZ), producing a dense composite layer with sound interfacial bonding. A continuous interfacial transition zone with an average thickness of ~0.7 μm formed at the HEA/Mg interface, suggesting limited elemental interdiffusion without obvious interfacial debonding or particle pull-out. Meanwhile, HEA incorporation refined the stir-zone grains to ~3.66 μm and primarily increased hardness and load bearing capacity through Hall-Petch strengthening, coefficient of thermal expansion mismatch strengthening, geometrically necessary dislocation strengthening. Tribological tests indicate that, as the nominal HEA content increases, the coefficient of friction and specific wear rate first decrease and then increase. The 10 vol% HEA composite exhibited the lowest and most stable coefficient of friction (0.205), corresponding to the optimal combination of interfacial integrity, matrix refinement, and reinforcement efficiency. These results demonstrate that APS-FSP is an effective route for tailoring interface-controlled microstructures in HEA-reinforced Mg-based surface composites. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Liu S.; Xu Z.; Liao Q.; Zheng X.; Fu X.; Zhang Y.; Zhu Y.
Title: Synergism of interfacial Ti-O-Co bonds and surface Co2+/Co3+ redox couples on TiO2 for highly selective photocatalytic CO2 methanation
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Value-added conversion of CO2 using solar energy is a sustainable strategy to address the energy crisis and environmental issues simultaneously. In this work, Co3O4/TiO2 composite photocatalysts were successfully prepared by a hydrothermal method. The optimized Co3O4/TiO2 achieves a CH4 yield of 34.8 μmol·g−1·h−1 with 82.4% selectivity. The enhanced catalytic activity is ascribed to interfacial Ti-O-Co bonds that facilitate electron transfer toward Co sites, thereby modulating the Co2+/Co3+ electronic environment and creating relatively electron-rich Co sites for *CO stabilization, while the Co3O4 component facilitates the proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) process toward CH4 formation. This study provides a practical strategy for promoting the value-added photocatalytic conversion of CO2 using multivalent transition metal oxide composite photocatalysts. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Investigation on NH3‑SCR performance and low N2O formation mechanism over MIL‑100(FeMn) catalyst
Abstract: Fe-based metal–organic frameworks (Fe-MOFs) have attracted extensive attention in the field of NH3-SCR denitrification due to their environmental friendliness and tunable redox properties. In this work, the catalytic performance of bimetallic MIL-100(FeMn) catalysts was systematically investigated, and a comparative study was further conducted with conventional FeMnOx catalysts synthesized via the co-precipitation method. The experimental results reveal that MIL-100(FeMn) catalyst achieves a NOx conversion of 91% at 275 ℃, and maintains a high N2 selectivity of 94%–99% over the entire tested temperature range. Such excellent performance is attributed to the highly dispersed metal sites, moderate surface acidity and appropriate redox properties of the material. Moreover, the as-prepared catalyst can effectively restrain the side reactions of excessive NH3 oxidation and deep NO oxidation. In-situ DRIFTS characterization confirms that the NH3-SCR reaction over MIL-100(FeMn) follows the Eley-Rideal mechanism, which inhibits the formation of inert nitrate species and thereby realizes the simultaneous improvement of catalytic activity and N2 selectivity. This work provides a novel insight and experimental reference for the exploitation of high-performance low-temperature de-NOx catalysts with low N2O emission. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wu Q.; Wang H.; Li L.; Hu T.; Yao J.; Jie C.; An M.; Xie H.; Niu J.; Cao Y.
Title: Construction of dual S-scheme heterojunction in Bi2S3 QDs@ZnCdS/3DOM CaTiO3 for highly efficient photocatalytic degradation, hydrogen production and antibacterial application
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Tuning micro-morphology and constructing heterostructures are two key strategies to overcome the intrinsic drawbacks of CaTiO3-based photocatalytic systems. In this work, Bi2S3 QDs@ZnCdS/3DOM CaTiO3 photocatalysts were rationally designed and synthesized via a dual-template method combined with a hydrothermal route. The hierarchically interconnected three-dimensionally ordered macroporous (3DOM) skeleton constitutes the most prominent structural merit of the composite. Tunable macroporous channels greatly shorten mass-transport distances and reduce diffusion resistance of reactants. Meanwhile, abundant anchoring sites are provided for the in-situ immobilization of ZnCdS and Bi2S3 QDs, which effectively suppress nanoparticle agglomeration. Based on such structural substrate, the fabricated ZnCdS/3DOM CaTiO3 heterostructure integrated with well-dispersed full-spectrum-responsive Bi2S3 QDs establishes a stable and efficient dual S-scheme charge transfer pathway. The characterization results including X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy and electron paramagnetic resonance confirm the orientation of the built-in electric field within this heterojunction. While retaining excellent reduction and oxidation capabilities, this structure significantly improves the separation efficiency of photogenerated charge carriers. Benefiting from the synergistic effect of the optimized 3DOM architecture and dual S-scheme heterojunction, the Bi2S3 QDs@ZnCdS/3DOM CaTiO3 composite achieves 96.69% degradation efficiency toward methyl orange under visible light. Its amount of H2 produced is 977 times that of bare CaTiO3, with an apparent quantum efficiency of 12.45% for hydrogen production, and an antibacterial efficiency of 64.57% against Escherichia coli . This study clarifies the synergistic mechanism between 3DOM morphological modulation and dual S-scheme heterojunction, and provides theoretical guidance for simultaneously boosting pollutant degradation, hydrogen evolution and antibacterial performances under photocatalytic conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Unlocking reversible hydrogen storage in penta-hexa-hepta graphene through lithium functionalization
Abstract: A newly proposed two-dimensional carbon allotrope, penta–hexa–hepta graphene (PHH-Gr), is systematically investigated as a potential hydrogen storage medium using first-principles calculations. The thermodynamic, dynamical, and thermal robustness of PHH-Gr are verified through cohesive energy evaluation, phonon spectrum analysis, and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations. Lithium decoration is found to be energetically favorable, with Li atoms strongly anchored at heptagonal hollow sites and minimal clustering tendency due to large Li–Li separations and high diffusion barriers. Electronic structure analysis demonstrates substantial charge transfer from Li to the PHH-Gr substrate while preserving metallic characteristics. Hydrogen adsorption on pristine PHH-Gr is weak, whereas Li functionalization markedly enhances H2 binding through polarization and charge-transfer effects. Each Li species can adsorb up to four hydrogen molecules, yielding a maximum gravimetric and volumetric hydrogen storage capacities of 10.75 wt% and 91.2 g L−1, respectively. Thermodynamic analysis using differential adsorption energies reveals that while the maximum storage capacity requires cryogenic temperatures or elevated pressures, a practical working capacity of approximately 6–8 wt% is achievable under reversible cycling conditions (298 K, 30 bar for uptake; 373 K, 3 bar for release). AIMD simulations also verify that the weakly bound fourth H2 molecule per Li site desorbs at room temperature under ambient pressure. These results highlight Li-decorated PHH-Gr as a robust and efficient material for reversible hydrogen storage applications with a working capacity exceeding DOE targets. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhao Z.; Lu A.; Zhang Y.; Liu B.; Li C.
Title: Interfacial electronic regulation of Ru-functionalized bimetallic MOF/metal oxide nanozyme for multimodal detection of tetracyclines and d-penicillamine
Abstract: Tetracycline antibiotics (TCs) and d -penicillamine (D-PA) belong to typical emerging contaminants of Pharmaceuticals and Personal Care Products (PPCPs). This work constructs an interfacial electronically synergized Ru-functionalized Zr/Ce co-modified UiO-66-NH2/Mn-CeO2 heterostructured nanozyme (RZCMC), where interfacial electronic modulation accelerates reciprocal redox cycling of Mn2+/Mn3+ and Ce3+/Ce4+ metal valence pairs to endow RZCMC with prominent peroxidase (POD)-mimicking catalytic activity as well as dual-emission fluorescence for ultrasensitive quantitative detection of PPCPs. RZCMC delivers two distinct fluorescence peaks at 430 nm and 609 nm under 360 nm excitation. RZCMC recognizes TCs through synergistic interactions between exposed Zr/Ce metal nodes, –O C-O- and –NH2, thereby generating marked dual-wavelength fluorescence quenching to support ultrasensitive TC detection with an LOD as low as 0.026 μM. RZCMC displays prominent POD activity via interfacial electronic modulation accelerating reversible metal valence cycling to oxidize TMB into photothermally active oxTMB for constructing a catalytic sensing system. Fukui function analysis identifies the 9S site of D-PA (ƒ− = 0.3262) as the most electron-donating/reactive site to suppress TMB oxidation and the reductive -SH group of D-PA depletes oxTMB, collectively enabling sensitive colorimetric-photothermal dual-mode detection of D-PA with LODs of 7.45 nM and 2.94 nM. Authors: Zhang J.; Xie G.; Zhu J.; Qian Y.; Lu X.
Title: Achieving high-efficiency and clean combustion across the full-load range in an ammonia/diesel dual-fuel direct-injection engine: ICCI strategy and mode transition
Abstract: As a hydrogen carrier, ammonia is a promising zero-carbon alternative fuel for internal combustion engines (ICEs). However, existing ammonia/diesel dual-fuel (ADDF) research is mostly limited to partial-load optimization and steady-state tests, lacking a full-range combustion framework and transient mode transition verification, which hinders lab-to-engineering translation. This work performs systematic experiments on an ADDF direct-injection (ADDF-DI) engine covering an indicated mean effective pressure (IMEP) range of 2–19 bar. An optimized intelligent charge compression ignition (ICCI) strategy with ammonia energy ratio (AER) over 80% is proposed, and transient mode transition characteristics are investigated. Results show that the ICCI strategy extends the stable operating limit to IMEP of 19 bar, with a peak indicated thermal efficiency (ITE) of 53.1% and the combustion efficiency over 99%. The inherent ITE–NOx trade-off is overcome, while unburned ammonia, N2O and NOx are controlled below 2, 0.03 and 5 g/kWh at high loads, respectively, achieving nearly 80% carbon reduction versus conventional diesel combustion (CDC). The forward CDC–ICCI transition is completed within 3 cycles at IMEP of 6 bar, and the reverse transition stabilizes in 1 cycle, with the coefficient of variation of IMEP below 2% at the optimal AER of 45%. Excellent load-following performance is validated via bidirectional load step transitions between 6 and 8 bar. This study establishes a full-range ICCI control framework for ADDF-DI engines, providing theoretical and technical support for the application of the ICCI mode. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Cai F.; Zhou H.; Ren Z.
Title: Physics-enforced neural ordinary differential equation for chemical kinetics optimization in reaction-diffusion systems
Abstract: Calibrating chemical kinetics in a reaction–diffusion system is challenging because of complex dynamics governed by tightly coupled chemistry and transport, while experimental observations are often sparse and noisy. We propose a physics consistent diffusion-chemistry coupled neural ordinary differential equation (Diff-Chem Neural ODE) that embeds Arrhenius-structured reaction neurons into a fully differentiable streamline formulation and explicitly accounts for diffusion coupling. This design enables direct gradient-based analysis of kinetic parameters without sampling-based pretraining. We validate this method on burner-stabilized flat and stagnation reacting flows using mechanisms spanning different stiffness ranges. The proposed method reproduces species profiles with near-reference accuracy, whereas a pure chemistry Neural ODE that neglects diffusion coupling may misplace ignition and generate an incorrect thin reaction zone. Diff-Chem Neural ODE is more robust than pure chemistry Neural ODE and provides substantial speedups for gradient evaluation compared with fully discretized computations. In kinetics refinement, optimizing only a limited set of “primal” species reduces the loss by over 98 % and simultaneously recovers unobserved variables, demonstrating physically consistent global control. Finally, tests with 1–20 % noise in the objective show stable convergence without local overfitting, supporting its applicability under noisy measurements. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
