Title: Green hydrogen-enhanced coal-based methanol-to-aromatics and olefins system: SHAP-coupled entropy-energy-economic analysis and ANN-assisted multi-objective optimization
Abstract: A green hydrogen-enhanced coal-based methanol-to-aromatics and olefins (MTA/MTO) system offers a promising route to improve carbon utilization and reduce emissions in coal-based chemical production. However, the key variables and subsystem-level contributions affecting overall performance are not fully understood, and achieving efficient, feasible multi-objective optimization is challenging. This study develops an artificial neural network (ANN)-assisted multi-objective optimization approach based on SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-coupled entropy-energy-economic (3E) analysis. The approach integrates ANN-based Pareto region identification with hierarchical Aspen Plus re-evaluation and repair to improve both optimization efficiency and solution feasibility. SHAP-coupled 3E analysis clarifies the roles of decision variables and subsystems in thermodynamic, economic, and energy performance, and highlights trade-offs among entropy generation rate, annual energy cost, and net present value. Results indicate that methanol-related and proton exchange membrane electrolyzer operations primarily influence overall 3E performance, while electrolyzer operation and methanol separation variables are most significant for objective trade-offs. Utilizing an ANN-assisted parallel NSGA-II, a promising Pareto region is identified in surrogate space within 132 s. Following rigorous re-evaluation and SHAP-coupled 3E-informed repair, all ANN-guided solutions converge in the rigorous model, with the relative errors between rigorous objective values and ANN predictions below 1.00 %. Compared to the baseline, the selected compromise solution increases the net present value by 28.48 %, while reducing the overall entropy generation rate by 1.52 % and the annual energy cost by 0.13 %. This study provides an interpretable, efficient, and reliable optimization framework for the low-carbon upgrading of highly integrated coal-based chemical processes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wang H.; Hu X.; Ma Z.; Ma Z.
Title: Comparative study of type II and type III pea resistant starch in high internal phase emulsions: Multiscale structure, emulsion stability and probiotic delivery
Abstract: In this study, type II (PRS2) and type III (PRS3) pea resistant starches, characterized by distinct processing-induced multiscale structures, were incorporated into whey protein isolate (WPI)-pectin composite high internal phase emulsions (HIPEs) to modulate interfacial and network organization for probiotic protection. X-ray diffraction, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, size-exclusion chromatography, small-angle X-ray scattering, and scanning electron microscopy showed that PRS2 retained partial granular morphology and C-type crystallinity, whereas PRS3 formed compact aggregates with B-type crystallinity. Simplified molecular dynamics models, together with comparative denaturant and selective-solvent assays, suggested formulation-dependent differences in non-covalent association patterns. The experimental observations showed predominantly particulate organization for PRS2 and a more continuous matrix morphology in PRS3-containing composites. These observations indicate that formulation behavior varied with the processing-induced structural characteristics of PRS2 and PRS3, including differences in crystalline organization, molecular-weight distribution, hydration, nanoscale aggregation, and morphology. The HIPEs also showed distinct responses: selected PRS3 formulations showed lower short-term instability, more restricted water mobility, and greater resistance under the applied heat and freeze-thaw conditions, whereas PRS2 showed a more pronounced concentration dependence. Using Lactiplantibacillus plantarum as a model probiotic, sequential simulated gastric and intestinal exposure showed that selected PRS3-based HIPEs maintained high recoverable viability during gastric exposure, while structural analyses indicated retention of a comparatively compact matrix in gastric medium followed by reduced compactness after transfer to intestinal medium. Overall, the processing-induced multiscale characteristics of pea resistant starch help explain its organization within the WPI-pectin matrix and the formulation-specific differences in HIPE stability and probiotic survival under simulated gastrointestinal conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Experimental study on rapid formation kinetics of CO2 hydrate based on fly ash medium
Abstract: Hydrate-based marine carbon sequestration is a promising CCUS strategy because of its high gas storage capacity. However, slow hydrate nucleation and growth, together with fluctuations in formation conditions, hinder efficient carbon capture and long-term stable storage. In this study, fly ash was proposed as a medium for hydrate-based marine carbon sequestration, and the kinetics of CO2 hydrate formation were experimentally investigated in a high-pressure reactor at 3.86 MPa and 274.15 K by varying fly ash type, dosage, and water saturation, as well as temperature, pressure, and additives. Results showed that fly ash promoted hydrate formation through its porous structure and hydration/mineralization-induced interfacial regulation, where the original particle surfaces and in situ generated carbonate products may provide favorable environments for hydrate nucleation, shortening the induction time by about 80% ('20 min), and accelerated hydrate formation. Class C fly ash was more effective than class F fly ash in reducing induction time, but its stronger competition for free water and more intense chemical competition lowered gas storage capacity. In slurry systems, fly ash increased gas storage capacity by 131% to 0.14 v/v compared with static porous-medium conditions, with an optimal slurry concentration of 40 wt%. Addition of 1 wt% L-methionine further reduced the induction time to 19 min and increased gas storage to about 1.9 mol, whereas 3.5 wt% salinity inhibited hydrate formation and intensified particle floating. Under a driving force of 4.5 MPa and a subcooling of 10 K, the induction time was shortened to 11 min. hydrate cementation and gel formation enhanced particle–hydrate interactions, generating a relatively compact fly ash–hydrate composite structure with potential for improving sequestration stability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Enhancing wear resistance of HMS coatings fabricated by laser directed energy deposition via regulating WC dissolution behavior
Abstract: The problem of excessive decomposition of WC in the high manganese steel (HMS) to form continuous reticular carbides, resulting in deterioration of the coating's wear resistance, has been addressed in this study. The laser directed energy deposition ( l -DED) technology was employed to control the laser energy density (150–225 J/mm²) and the WC content (0–40 wt%), thereby preparing HMS/WC wear-resistant composite coatings with high WC content and low decomposition degree. The effects of process parameters on the microstructure evolution and tribological properties of the coatings were systematically investigated. The results show that optimizing the process parameters can effectively inhibit the decomposition of WC and cause the Fe₃W₃C formed in situ around WC to transform from a continuous reticular structure to a discontinuous dispersed structure; this Fe₃W₃C configuration is the key to enhancing the coating's wear resistance. Under the 40 wt% WC condition, compared to the coating without WC, the coating's hardness increased by 144%, the wear rate decreased by 90%, and its performance was superior to that reported in many literatures for laser additive manufacturing of WC composite coatings. The experimental results are consistent with first-principles calculations. Fe₃W₃C has high volume modulus, shear modulus, Young's modulus, high hardness, low Poisson's ratio, and significant isotropy, which can effectively bear external loads and prevent the abrasive balls from directly contacting the substrate. This study reveals the wear mechanism of the discontinuous Fe₃W₃C strengthening phase configuration, providing new process control ideas for laser additive manufacturing of high-manganese steel wear-resistant coatings under low stress wear conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: An IoT-Enabled hybrid deep learning model with optimization Driven feature selection for accurate stock price prediction

Title: Highly integrated and preloaded liquid-filled stick microextraction with in situ derivatization for determination of sulfonamides in environmental water and milk samples
Abstract: Sulfonamides (SAs) are among the most frequently prescribed antibiotic agents, and accurate surveillance of their residues in food products and environmental matrices remains essential. Authors: Zhang T.; Wu Z.; Liu Z.; Yu L.; Gao J.; Yang Q.
Title: Not all features should propagate: An interpretable role-decoupled graph transformer for traffic accident risk prediction
Abstract: Predicting traffic accident risks is crucial for urban safety management. In recent years, graph neural networks have demonstrated great potential due to their powerful ability to extract urban spatial features. However, existing graph-based methods commonly propagate heterogeneous predictive features through the same message-passing process, overlooking the fact that not all features are suitable for graph propagation. To address this issue, we propose an Interpretable Role-Decoupled Graph Transformer (IRDGT) for traffic accident risk prediction. IRDGT characterizes each input channel using four interpretable temporal and spatial statistical descriptors and softly assigns it to three computational roles: propagation, node-prior, and conditional. Propagation-oriented features are modeled through a multi-relation Graph Transformer, node-prior features bypass message passing to preserve persistent regional exposure information, and conditional features dynamically modulate existing graph relations according to the current context. Extensive experiments on two real-world datasets demonstrate that IRDGT exhibits significant advantages over comparison algorithms and offers a higher degree of interpretability. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Structural modification of Gum Arabic by β-galactosidase hydrolysis: Mechanism of saltiness enhancement and potential application in sodium reduction
Abstract: Maintaining saltiness perception while reducing sodium content remains a major challenge in low-sodium food design. Title: Performance optimization of improved rectangular baffle proton exchange membrane fuel cell through crested porcupine optimization-back propagation neural network surrogate model

Authors: Wang R.; Bao J.; Zhu J.; Wang H.; Yan X.; Shi C.
Title: Progressive compound injection strategies to combustion improvement and pollutants reduction of an ammonia/hydrogen net-zero rotary engine
Abstract: The adaptation of fixed/variable ratio compound injection technology and the application of ammonia-hydrogen zero-carbon fuels are key technical paths for high-efficiency and clean rotary engines to break through combustion bottlenecks and support the dual-carbon goals. Ammonia has become an important alternative to fossil fuels due to its full-life-cycle zero-carbon advantage, while hydrogen compensates for ammonia’s ignition delay defect with its high combustion rate and wide flammability limit. Taking gasoline rotary engine as the research object, this study established a CONVERGE multi-physics coupling simulation model, combined with the RNG κ-ε turbulence model and the SAGE detailed chemical reaction kinetics model. The influence of injection strategy on mixture preparation, combustion development, and pollutant formation was examined from two aspects, namely fixed-ratio operation and variable-ratio operation. The former mainly involves the direct injection share and split injection pattern, whereas the latter is characterized by fuel distribution ratio and split injection mode. Title: Cu-promoted CeMnOx catalysts for KCl-resistant low-temperature CO oxidation in iron ore sintering flue gas

Title: Plasma-induced fragmentation of water-in-kerosene emulsion droplets under a high-voltage pulsed discharge

Title: Experimental investigation and multi-objective optimization of key control parameters for low-emission heavy-duty hydrogen engines
Abstract: With the increasing global energy demand and the advancement of carbon neutrality goals, efficient and low-carbon power systems have attracted extensive attention in heavy-duty engine research. Title: Synergistic enhancement of CO2 capture in Li4SiO4 via Cu, K co-doping and cigarette butt-templated porosity: Synthesis, performance, and mechanistic insights

Title: Domain-decomposed antiderivative transformation iterative method: A deep learning approach for weakly and Cauchy types singular integral equations
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: Solving singular integral equations is crucial in various practical industrial systems and has long been a challenging and active research area in numerical computation. In recent years, significant progress has been made in numerical techniques for solving differential and integral equations by leveraging deep learning methods, demonstrating notable advantages in continuity and accuracy. However, the singularity of the kernel function in singular integral equations poses unique challenges for traditional deep learning methods. To address this, we propose a Domain-decomposed Antiderivative transformation Iterative Method (D-AIM) for weakly and Cauchy types singular integral equations. Title: Atomic-scale insights into synergistically enhanced scratch performance and Ni substrate protection in Al₀.₃CoCrFeNi coatings by coupling short-range order with graphene
Abstract: High-entropy alloy (HEA) coatings often face a trade-off between enhanced load-bearing capacity and reduced friction coefficient, limiting their practical ability to protect substrates. Title: A hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for high-efficiency control of turbine-assisted fuel cell air supply systems

Title: A new intelligent entropy-activated reaction-diffusion model for scale-balanced early warning of chikungunya propagation

Title: An experimental study on the flame-flame interaction of CH4/NH3/air mixtures on a twin swirl burner

Title: Citric acid-induced aqueous phase separation method in the fabrication of chitosan/nisin films for the preservation of chilled pork
Abstract: This study employed the aqueous phase separation (APS) method using citric acid buffer as coagulant to obtain high-strength and antibacterial chitosan/nisin films for the preservation of chilled pork. The tensile strength of the chitosan film prepared via the APS method using pH 5.0 citric acid buffer was 143.44% of that of the film prepared with distilled water. The addition of nisin significantly enhanced the mechanical properties and antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus of chitosan films. Specifically, the film prepared with 8% nisin (based on the dry weight of chitosan film) and designated CS-5.0@8%N was applied for preservation of chilled pork. The total volatile basic nitrogen (TVB-N) value of chilled pork packaged in CS-5.0@8%N film was 7.57 ± 0.39 mg/100 g on the 6th day, however, the TVB-N value of unpackaged chilled pork reached as high as 16.66 ± 0.46 mg/100 g on the 6th day. Notably, the storage quality of the chilled pork packaged in CS-5.0@8%N film during storage was significantly superior than that of chilled pork packaged in chitosan film in terms of total viable count (TVC), pH, and thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS). Studies indicated that the spoilage threshold of chilled pork was 6.00 log CFU/g (TVC) or 15.00 mg/100 g (TVB-N). Consequently, compared with the unpackaged group, the shelf life of the chilled pork was extended 4 d by using of CS-5.0@8%N film. This study advances the application of bio-based active packaging in the preservation of chilled pork. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Yin Q.; Zhu Q.; Yasuhara H.; Tao Z.; Yang S.; Meng B.; Wu J.; Ren S.; Shen J.
Title: Dynamic mechanisms of plugging and diverting hydraulic fracturing in tight sandstone using fiber-particulate diverters
Abstract: To address the engineering challenges of simple fracture morphology and limited total fracture area in deep hard rock hydraulic fracturing, a plugging and diverting fracturing technique integrating fibers and multi-sized particles is evaluated. Acoustic emission (AE) monitoring and three-dimensional fracture reconstruction were used to quantify the effects of material composition, injection rate, and particle gradation on fracture evolution. The results indicate that the plugging structure formed by mono-sized fine particles formed unstable bridges, frequently inducing ineffective pressure fluctuations characterized by a “bridging-collapse-rebuilding” cycle, and failed to form an effective flow barrier. The optimized particle gradation (25-, 50-, and 100-mesh at a mass ratio of 6:3:1) increased the secondary pressurization increment to approximately 128 %, promoting large-angle deflection and branch intersection of the primary fracture without chaotic near-wellbore fragmentation. Furthermore, a “high-low-high” variable-rate injection strategy (150–100-150 mL/min) effectively decoupled plug consolidation from fracture propagation, promoting plug densification before secondary fracture extension and thereby enhancing pressure accumulation and fracture network complexity. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for plugging and diverting fracturing in hard rock and support the design of hydraulic preconditioning strategies for deep hard rock excavation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wu S.; Li Z.; Xu M.; Pan J.; Wang W.; Fang H.; Wang Y.; Lv S.-W.
Title: Tailoring the electronic structure of iron by molybdenum doping to enhance peroxidase-like activity for colorimetric analysis of natural organic acids
Abstract: Accurate quantification of added organic acids with antioxidant activity in food is critical for food safety and human health. Herein, newly-designed Mo-doped Fe3C (denoted as Mo-Fe3C) as nanozyme is prepared via a stepwise self-assembly strategy. Notably, the introduction of Mo not only facilitates efficient charge transfer but also creates additional active sites. More importantly, the Mo doping can also modulate the electronic structure of Fe site in Fe3C, thereby downshifting its d-band center. This modification endows Mo-Fe3C with moderate adsorption capacity toward H2O2, which prevents the over-activation of H2O2. As a result, the Mo-Fe3C exhibits significantly enhanced peroxidase-like activity. Taking advantage of the robust peroxidase-like activity of Mo-Fe3C, a highly effective colorimetric sensing array is developed using 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethyl benzidine (TMB) as colorimetric substrate. Owing to the distinctive “molecular fingerprint” characteristic of electrophilic reactions between •OH and natural organic acids, proposed sensing array is capable of achieving colorimetric detection of four organic acids, including tannic acid (TA), phytic acid (PA), malic acid (MA), and ascorbic acid (AA). The limit of detection (LOD) values of TA, PA, MA and AA are calculated to be 0.63, 0.82, 2.40 and 2.88 μM, respectively. Even in mixed-component systems or real samples, the colorimetric sensing array still maintains high accuracy in discriminating and quantifying various organic acids. In short, the present work can provide novel insights into future research on nanozyme-based colorimetric sensing analysis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Song H.-H.; Dutta B.; Wang Y.-M.; Martínez L.
Author full names: Song, Hui-Hui (57923678600); Dutta, Bapi (55932028300); Wang, Ying-Ming (55966745100); Martínez, Luis (56215039400)
Title: Bridging structural position and behavioral heterogeneity: A clustering and variable-cost based fair consensus framework for LSGDM
Abstract: Large-scale group decision-making (LSGDM) increasingly relies on clustering and consensus-reaching processes (CRPs) to manage complexity. Existing clustering methods integrate opinions with social network information but rely on conventional indicators that overlook deeper structural characteristics, limiting their capacity to identify influential decision-makers (DMs). Furthermore, while cost minimization and fairness are recognized as critical in CRPs, the interplay between heterogeneous adjustment costs and equitable burden distribution remains underexplored. To address these gaps, this study proposes a novel clustering algorithm and consensus model for LSGDM. Firstly, a clustering algorithm is developed that jointly incorporates opinion information and social network structure via a hybrid distance metric. Network topology is captured through node embeddings, while structural hole theory is employed to identify influential DMs and initialize cluster centers, generating subgroups that are both structurally cohesive and opinion consistent. Then, within the Extended Comparative Linguistic Expressions With Symbolic Translation (ELICIT) framework, a bi-objective consensus optimization model is constructed to balance variable adjustment costs, modeled through individual tolerance levels, and fairness, quantified by the inequality of adjustment burdens among DMs. Next, a role-aware feedback mechanism is designed to provide differentiated guidance for cluster centers and non-central DMs according to their structural positions in the network. Finally, numerical experiments and comparative analyses demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior clustering quality, fairer cost allocation, and a more efficient CRP compared with existing methods. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Tang H.; Guo L.; Zheng X.; Sun L.; Luo Y.
Author full names: Tang, Haiyue (59465144400); Guo, Liangmin (24450281000); Zheng, Xiaoyao (56504205400); Sun, Liping (55492986400); Luo, Yonglong (13408204600)
Title: Social recommendation based on graph contrastive learning and preference fusion
Abstract: Contrastive learning is widely applied in graph-based recommendation systems. However, most studies rarely employ contrastive learning from multiple perspectives, failing to adequately explore diverse embedding features. Additionally, users and their social friends may differ in their preferences, leading to redundant social data. Current methods usually filter social relationships using embeddings learned from sparse interaction data, struggling to capture preferences accurately. To solve these problems, we propose a social recommendation model based on graph contrastive learning and preference fusion. Specifically, a hierarchical contrastive learning method contrasts low-order embeddings with aggregated embeddings extracted from the interaction graph using graph convolutional networks, while treating high-order embeddings of users and items as mutual contrastive views. This method enriches the embedding features of users and items. We design a social relationship filtering method based on contrastive regularization. This method leverages the user aggregation embeddings refined by contrastive learning to compute the preference similarity between users and their social friends, achieving better integration of user preferences with social relationships. Social embedding independence constraint learning is introduced to reduce redundant information in the original social graph, thereby improving recommendation accuracy. Experiments were conducted on three datasets, and the results demonstrate that our model improves recommendation performance. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Liu K.; Zhang J.; Cheng X.; Wang Z.; Li T.; Pan R.
Title: Investigation of flow-heat transfer and mechanical characteristics of three-dimensional high-temperature sodium heat pipe based on multi-physics coupling
Abstract: Investigations into the coupled flow, heat transfer and structural deformation in high-temperature alkali metal heat pipes are vital for the safety of heat pipe-cooled nuclear reactors. In this study, a three-dimensional(3D) multi-physics-coupled model of a sodium heat pipe was developed using the finite-element software COMSOL Multiphysics. Numerical simulations were performed to examine the flow and heat-transfer behavior of the working fluid, together with the thermal expansion response of the pipe wall. The results show that, under steady-state uniform heat-flux conditions, increasing the heating power from 560 W to 728 W leads to higher pipe-wall temperature, vapor temperature, vapor and liquid pressures, and total deformation of the pipe wall. The maximum thermal deformation increases by 0.19% relative to the cold state. In contrast, the vapor velocity decreases with increasing heating power, with the maximum velocity reduced by 86.40%. Under steady-state non-uniform heat-flux conditions, the temperature distribution in the evaporation section exhibits pronounced spatial non-uniformity. However, the differences in vapor velocity and total pipe-wall deformation remain small under non-uniform heat-flux profiles with different peak-to-valley values. Under transient operating conditions, the total deformation of the heat pipe increases monotonically as the heating power rises, while the vapor velocity decreases and the internal pressure increases. Moreover, the outer-wall temperature differs only slightly between simulations with and without thermal expansion. This study provides valuable insights for the analysis and safety assessment of steady-state and transient heat-pipe operation when structural-mechanical effects are taken into account. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Authors: Zhang F.-J.; Yang Z.-H.; Zhou X.-Q.; Li H.; Oh W.-C.
Title: Enhancing photocatalytic CO2 reduction via constructing a tightly contacted Bi3O4Br/Bi2WO6 type-II heterojunction photocatalyst
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: The development of efficient, stable, and highly selective catalysts is of great importance for the photocatalytic reduction of CO2. However, the inefficient separation and transfer of photogenerated charge carriers remain a major challenge for Bi-based photocatalysts. In this work, Bi3O4Br/Bi2WO6 type-II heterojunction photocatalyst via a two-step approach, and its photocatalytic CO2 reduction performance was systematically investigated. The results shin that Bi3O4Br/Bi2WO6–20 exhibits best performance, achieving CO production rate of 13.73 μmol·g−1 h−1 and is approximately 2.09-fold compared with pure Bi3O4Br and 2.05 -fold compared with pure Bi2WO6, while maintaining nearly 100% CO selectivity. Based on the experimentally determined band structures and complementary spectroscopic and photoelectrochemical results, a possible type-II charge-transfer pathway is proposed to account for the enhanced CO2 photoreduction performance. In addition, composite demonstrates excellent stability during photocatalytic process. This study provides an effective strategy for facile construction of efficient CO2 reduction photocatalysts. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Roles of crosslinks and entanglements in resisting fatigue crack growth in elastic soft materials
Abstract: In applications, materials are often required to sustain cyclic load and suffer fatigue. Here we study the roles of crosslinks and entanglements in resisting fatigue crack growth in elastic soft materials. We synthesize polyacrylamide hydrogels of different densities of crosslinks and entanglements, and swell some of the hydrogels in water to equilibrium or certain degree. For each hydrogel with precut crack, the crack growth as a function of the number of cycles is measured under cyclic stretch of different amplitudes. For each hydrogel without precut crack, the stress-stretch curves are measured under cyclic stretch of different amplitudes. Consequently, a curve on the plane of crack growth per cycle and energy release rate is obtained, giving two properties: fatigue threshold and crack growth rate. We show that crosslinks decrease the fatigue threshold and increase the crack growth rate. By contrast, entanglements increase the fatigue threshold and decrease the crack growth rate. We develop a scaling law on the fatigue threshold of a polymer network of crosslinks and entanglements. Our scaling law can well capture the trend of the experimental data for polymer networks of different densities of crosslinks and entanglements. It is further found that the crack growth rate is a power function of the energy release rate when the energy release rate is above the fatigue threshold. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Tuning the network structure and performance of pea protein–polysaccharide composite emulsion gels as bulk solid fat mimetics: Impact of biopolymer ratio
Abstract: The growing demand for low-fat and plant-based meat products has increased the need for effective fat substitutes. However, existing substitutes often exhibit limited similarity to animal fat in terms of texture and processing behavior, highlighting the need for structured alternatives with improved mechanical and functional properties. Here, pea protein isolate (PPI), konjac glucomannan (KGM), and xanthan gum (XG) were assembled into composite emulsion gels to clarify how the KGM/XG ratio regulates network formation and fat-mimetic performance. Oil droplets were entrapped within a PPI-polysaccharide matrix using a two-step homogenization process. Composite emulsion gels with KGM/XG mass ratios of 2:8, 4:6, 5:5, 6:4, and 8:2 were evaluated for appearance, texture, microstructure, rheology, thermal response, and water mobility. Among the formulations, the composite emulsion gels prepared with sequential addition of KGM and XG at a mass ratio of 6:4 exhibited the best overall performance, showing the highest hardness (448 g), storage modulus (569.9 Pa), and water-holding capacity (98.70%), together with restricted water mobility and improved heat tolerance. Confocal microscopy and electron microscopy revealed that this formulation exhibited relatively uniform oil droplet distribution and continuous network structure. These results suggest that the balanced KGM/XG ratio promoted the formation of an integrated protein–polysaccharide network through the complementary functionalities of KGM and XG, whereas excessive XG or KGM disrupted network organization and reduced gel cohesiveness. The PPI-KGM-XG composite emulsion gel therefore provides a tunable plant-based platform with potential for developing structured fat mimetics for low-fat meat products and plant-based foods. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Qi X.; Pani A.K.; Wu X.; Yan Y.
Title: Milstein convolution quadrature approximation to stochastic semilinear Volterra integro-differential equations
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: This paper investigates the strong convergence of an efficient fully discrete scheme for stochastic semilinear Volterra integro-differential equations driven by multiplicative noise. The proposed method couples a Milstein-type convolution quadrature for the temporal discretization with a finite element approximation in spatial directions. Compared with the Maruyama discretization, the Milstein approach introduces additional analytical challenges in establishing the strong convergence estimates. Rigorous proofs of the spatial and temporal strong convergence rates are provided. It is shown that the Milstein-type scheme attains an almost doubled temporal convergence rate compared with the Maruyama-type method. Numerical experiments are presented to confirm the theoretical results and to illustrate the efficiency of the proposed scheme. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Qi L.; Liu X.; Nie B.; Han W.; Hu S.; He C.; Han H.; Li Z.
Title: Mechanisms of wettability-enhanced gas displacement and nanomechanical strength weakening in coal modified by active nanofluids
Abstract: To address the limitations of conventional hydraulic fracturing in deep coal seams, this study constructed active nanofluid systems by combining SiO2 nanoparticles with three types of surfactants: the cationic surfactant dodecyltrimethylammonium bromide (DTAB), the anionic surfactant sodium dioctyl sulfosuccinate (AOT), and the nonionic surfactant alcohol ethoxylate (AEO-9). Experimental characterization and molecular simulations were integrated to systematically investigate their effects on the physicochemical structure, wettability, gas adsorption and desorption behavior, and nanomechanical strength of coal. The results showed that the addition of surfactants significantly improved the dispersion and attachment of SiO2 nanoparticles on the coal surface, enabling the composite systems to form an interfacial adsorption configuration in which hydrophobic chains were oriented toward the coal surface, while hydrophilic groups faced the aqueous phase. After treatment with active nanofluids, the response of oxygen-containing functional groups, including C–O and C==O, was enhanced on the coal surface. The total absorption peak area of oxygen-containing functional groups was negatively correlated with the coal-water contact angle, whereas the coal-water contact angle was positively correlated with CH4 adsorption capacity. As coal wettability increased, the elastic modulus and hardness generally decreased, while the maximum displacement, contact displacement, and creep displacement increased. Among the treated samples, the AOT + SiO2 group exhibited the lowest elastic modulus and hardness, which decreased by 25.21% and 25.14%, respectively, compared with raw coal, indicating that this system produced the strongest wettability enhancement and the most pronounced weakening of nanomechanical strength. This study elucidates the synergistic modification mechanism of surfactant-SiO2 composite nanofluids and provides theoretical insights and a potential approach for improving fluid injection efficiency and mitigating dynamic hazards in deep coal seams. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Effects of synergistic ultrasonic–NaClO treatment on coal microstructure at different liquid saturations
Abstract: Efficient coalbed methane (CBM) extraction is important for safe coal mining and for utilizing this gas as a relatively clean energy resource. Low–permeability coal is generally characterized by a compact matrix and poorly connected pore–fracture networks, which restrict methane desorption, diffusion, and flow. Combined ultrasonic–NaClO treatment provides a physicochemical approach to coal modification, but the role of liquid saturation in this process remains unclear. Low–temperature N2 adsorption–desorption, FTIR, and SEM were used to characterize the pore structure, functional groups, and surface morphology of coal samples subjected to combined ultrasonic–NaClO treatment at different liquid saturations. The results suggest a synergistic interaction in which ultrasonic cavitation enhanced NaClO transport within the pore–fracture system and exposed new reactive surfaces, while NaClO–induced oxidation–dissolution weakened the coal matrix and pore walls, increasing their susceptibility to cavitation and thereby promoting pore opening and microfracture development. The most pronounced pore–structure modification was observed at 50% liquid saturation. Relative to untreated coal, the BET specific surface area and pore volume increased by 36.85% and 24.39%, respectively. FTIR results were consistent with cleavage or rearrangement of aliphatic side chains and bridging bonds, reduced condensation and connectivity of aromatic units, and a less compact local macromolecular structure. SEM revealed more evident lamellar exfoliation, interparticle pores, and microfractures, together with clearer local pore–fracture connections. These findings provide a theoretical basis for synergistic physicochemical modification of low–permeability coal and enhanced CBM recovery. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Construction of travelling wave solutions to new coupled Konno–Oono equation arising in magnetic field
Source title: International Journal of Modern Physics C
Abstract: In this paper, some novel analytical solutions of the new coupled Konno–Oono equation model appearing within engineering and sciences via two vital and convenient exact approaches, namely, modified auxiliary equation method and generalized projective Riccati equation method are obtained. Furthermore, two-dimensional lines graphs, the three-dimensional surface graphs and the contour graphs to show physical nature for few of the obtained solutions are represented with the help of Wolfram Mathematica 9. Authors: Jiang H.; Lv Y.; Sun X.; Fang H.; Li Q.; Cao J.; Liu Q.; Zhang Y.
Title: Synergistic effects of “circular matrix-lattice” gas distribution zones and wavy gas-coolant channels on species distribution in proton exchange membrane fuel cells
Abstract: To achieve the synergistic enhancement of mass transport, water removal, and thermal management in graphite proton exchange membrane fuel cells, this study develops a three-dimensional multiphase model integrating “circular matrix-lattice” gas distribution zones (CMLGDZ), 34 parallel wavy channels, and dual-side cooling circuits. Particular attention is given to the coupled effects of reactant flow configuration, species transport, operating pressure, high-load operation, and cooling arrangement. Counter-flow feeding of hydrogen and oxygen improves the spatial coordination among reactant concentration, product-water distribution, and membrane hydration, thereby increasing the current–density uniformity in the cathode catalyst layer by 0.004, corresponding to an improvement of approximately 0.47%. Cross-sectional analysis indicates that the CMLGDZ combined with the multiple-inlet configuration maintains stable hydrogen supply on the anode side. However, the relative deviation in cathode oxygen concentration increases along the flow direction from 23.26% to 45.86%, representing a relative increase of 97.2%; this deterioration is further intensified by liquid–water retention in low-velocity regions. Pressurized operation increases the reactant partial pressures and membrane hydration level. When the operating pressure rises from 1.0 to 2.0 atm, the average current density increases by 0.8947 A·cm−2, corresponding to an improvement of 89.6%, although pumping-power consumption and hydrothermal non-uniformity simultaneously become more pronounced. Under high-load operating conditions, cathode oxygen depletion and localized mass-transfer polarization are further intensified. Although the net power density continues to increase, its marginal gain decreases markedly. The coolant-flow direction also restructures the coupled relationship among hotspot migration, liquid–water removal, and multiphysics-field uniformity. Specifically, aligning the cathode coolant flow with the oxygen flow direction favors instantaneous power output, whereas directing the coolant on each side along the corresponding reactant-gas flow provides a more balanced improvement in water removal, thermal uniformity, and operational stability. These findings provide a theoretical basis for the integrated design of full-plate channels, operating parameters, and cooling circuits. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Federated learning algorithm based on sigmoid kernel fuzzy rough set under privacy protection
Abstract: With the rapid proliferation of distributed data sources and increasing concerns over data confidentiality, developing effective feature selection methods that operate without centralizing sensitive information has become a critical challenge in machine learning. This research proposes a novel federated feature selection framework that enhances classification accuracy while minimizing data exposure across distributed participants. By integrating federated learning principles with a fuzzy rough set-based approach, this research aims to address the challenge of selecting optimal feature subsets from distributed data sources without compromising individual privacy. The proposed model introduces innovative techniques such as the sigmoid kernelized fuzzy rough set and the Jensen-Shannon fuzzy divergence to manage uncertain information effectively. Through a dynamic feature evaluation function and the application of the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) approach, the research seeks to demonstrate superior performance compared to existing methods, ultimately advancing the field of privacy-preserving data analysis. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Wang C.; Huang Q.; Shi Y.; Wang S.; Pan G.
Title: A Two-Phase FSI Solver for Transmedia Hydrodynamics with Geometric Flux Decomposition and Consistent Mass–Momentum Transport
Abstract: A two-phase fluid–structure interaction solver is developed for transmedia hydrodynamics by coupling an immersed-boundary method with the CLSVOF method on a staggered Cartesian grid. In cells containing both liquid and solid, the swept fluxes of the combined liquid–solid phase and the solid phase are evaluated separately, and their difference provides the liquid flux without explicitly reconstructing the triple-junction geometry. The resulting liquid fluxes are further decomposed to construct the mass fluxes required by the staggered momentum control volumes. The main advance is the extension of the established consistent mass–momentum transport framework to solid-intersected triple-phase cells, ensuring that the volume-fraction update and momentum convection use the same geometric liquid-flux information near moving immersed boundaries. The method is validated using representative water-entry, water-exit, and wave-breaking problems. The predicted free-surface evolution, body motion, and hydrodynamic loads agree well with available experimental and numerical results. Additional conservation and sensitivity tests further demonstrate the robustness of the proposed framework. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Authors: Li M.; Zhang C.; Huang D.; Wei Y.; Tao J.; Wang Y.; Wang M.
Title: A review on lateral flow immunoassay technology for mycotoxin detection: From single-signal enhancement to multi-signal synergy
Abstract: Mycotoxins are toxic secondary metabolites produced by fungi that frequently contaminate grains, nuts, and other foodstuffs. Their widespread occurrence causes significant economic losses and poses a serious threat to human and animal health. Traditional analytical methods relying on complex instruments often fail to meet the requirements for rapid on-site screening and remain limited by cost, operational complexity, and restricted on-site deployment capabilities. Lateral flow immunoassays (LFIAs) are important tool for the rapid detection of mycotoxins due to their simplicity, portability, and low cost. This review provides a critical overview of the latest development in signal readout architecture for LFIA platforms, including single-signal platforms based on colorimetry, fluorescence, chemiluminescence, and surface enhanced Raman scattering (SERS); dual-mode system integrating colorimetric-fluorescence or colorimetric-photothermal readings; and multi-mode platforms that combines three or more orthogonal signals. It also discusses the mechanism of functional nanomaterials in signal amplification, with particular emphasis on gold and fluorescent nanomaterials, nanozymes, metal organic frameworks, magnetic nanoparticles, and layered assembled plasmonic probes. The integration of portable readers, smartphone imaging, and machine learning algorithms, and high-throughput multiplexing formats is also summarized. In summary, future priorities have been identified, including multifunctional nanoprobes, intelligent on-site deployment devices, and AI assisted data interpretation. This review provides a systematic framework for the rational design of highly sensitive, reliable, and field-deployable LFIA technologies for mycotoxin monitoring. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Explicit timestamp modeling for long-term time series forecasting via pattern and residual fusion
Abstract: Long-term time series forecasting remains challenging due to the complex entanglement of deterministic periodic patterns and irregular stochastic residuals. Existing methods often utilize timestamps merely as implicit embeddings, neglecting their potential to capture global multi-scale periodicities. To address this limitation, we propose TTW, a lightweight, plug-and-play framework designed to explicitly exploit temporal cues. Specifically, the framework employs a Time Index Generator to encode multi-scale temporal attributes, guiding a Temporal Pattern Extractor to rigorously disentangle basic patterns from irregular residuals. Furthermore, a Weight Constrained Combiner adaptively fuses these components under strict constraints to ensure interpretability. Instantiated with a simple Multilayer Perceptron, TTW-MLP achieves competitive performance on mainstream benchmarks, including Electricity and Weather, with only 0.42 million parameters. This plug-and-play modularity allows TTW to seamlessly enhance various backbone networks without introducing prohibitive computational burdens. Empirical results validate the synergy among explicit timestamp modeling, residual-focused learning, and constrained fusion, demonstrating superior efficiency over complex Transformer-based architectures. Title: A novel microscopic hyperspectral imaging detection method for quantitative powdered food adulteration assessment: A comparative study of CNN-RNN attention models
Abstract: Microscopic hyperspectral imaging (MHSI) was employed to acquire particle-resolved hyperspectral information for the quantitative analysis of adulteration in powdered foods. Lotus root powder adulterated with maize starch and cassava starch was used as a model system. To characterize the complex spectral patterns associated with particle scattering, three hybrid deep sequence models, namely CNN-LSTM-Attention, CNN-GRU-Attention, and CNN-BiLSTM-Attention, were developed and systematically compared with conventional models. An optimal analytical workflow was further established by evaluating six spectral preprocessing techniques and four wavelength selection methods. Among the evaluated models, CNN-BiLSTM-Attention exhibited the best predictive performance, achieving an R2 value of 0.9457 and an RMSE value of 1.3871 on the prediction set. When combined with pseudo-color visualisation, the optimized model enabled pixel-wise mapping of predicted adulteration levels across the sample. Within regions exhibiting stable imaging quality, the pseudo-color distribution progressively shifted toward colors corresponding to higher predicted concentrations as the adulteration level increased, allowing the spatial variation in predicted adulterant concentration to be intuitively visualized. These results demonstrate the potential of MHSI coupled with deep learning for quantitative adulteration analysis and provide a promising analytical strategy for the quality control of lotus root powder and other high-value powdered food products. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Process standardization for machine learning systems: A reference model based on international standards
Abstract: Process standards have long provided a foundation for software engineering, but equivalent guidance for machine learning projects remains limited. Existing frameworks, such as ISO/IEC 5338, outline artificial intelligence lifecycle processes at a high level but lack the detail needed to guide engineering teams in practice. This paper proposes a Process Reference Model for machine learning and artificial intelligence systems that extends existing standards by providing detailed descriptions of the technical processes that define their lifecycle. The process model was developed through a structured methodology aligned with ISO/IEC 33004 and ISO/IEC 24774 and designed following the principles of Design Science Research. It focuses exclusively on technical processes, specifying their purposes, outcomes, inputs, outputs, and base practices in a consistent format. The resulting process reference model provides a standard-aligned foundation for defining, comparing, and assessing machine learning development processes, and supports future efforts in lifecycle standardization and process capability assessment. Title: CH4−H2 combustion in a divergent porous media reactor: Experimental study and chemical reactor network modeling
Abstract: Hydrogen (H2) blending with methane (CH4) is a transitional pathway toward low-carbon combustion, but its implementation in premixed burners remains limited by flashback and emission-control challenges. Divergent porous media burners (PMBs) offer a promising stabilization strategy for highly reactive mixtures, as their increasing cross-sectional area generates a decreasing filtration velocity that opposes flame propagation. In this work, lean CH4–H2 combustion in a 45∘ divergent packed-bed PMB operated at 2kW is studied experimentally and with a chemical reactor network model. Experiments are conducted for equivalence ratios between ϕ = 0.5 and 0.7, with H2 volumetric fractions up to 70% in the fuel mixture. Stability limits, axial solid-phase temperature profiles, and CO and NOx emissions are measured for all stable conditions. Results show that decreasing ϕ extends the flashback limit toward higher H2 fractions, enabling stable operation up to 70%H2 at ϕ = 0.5, while the widest stable H2 addition window is obtained at ϕ = 0.6. NOx emissions were below the 5ppm detection limit of the analyzer for most stable conditions, contrasting with the commonly expected NOx increase in H2-enriched free flames. CO emissions remained below 100ppm for ϕ = 0.6 and decreased from approximately 60ppm to 26ppm as H2 increased from 0% to 50%, whereas operation at ϕ = 0.5 produced higher CO levels due primarily to lower combustion temperatures. Overall, ϕ = 0.6 is identified as a favorable operating condition that balances hydrogen tolerance, high combustion temperature, low CO emissions, and low NOx levels. These findings provide new insights into the stabilization, thermal, and pollutant-formation behavior of high-H2 CH4–H2 mixtures in divergent packed-bed PMBs, which are promising candidates for compact and fuel-flexible heating applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Slodička M.
Title: Variable order time-fractional wave PDEs
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: We investigate a semilinear problem for a fractional wave equation with variable order Caputo fractional derivative (∂tα(t)u)(t) subject to homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. The right-hand side of the governing partial differential equation is nonlinear and contains a weakly singular Volterra operator. The whole process takes place in a bounded Lipschitz domain in Rd,d≥1 during a time-frame [0, T]. We establish the existence of a unique solution in suitable function spaces. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zhang B.; Liang Q.; Li W.; Zou S.; Wan Z.; Shen Q.; Cai Y.
Title: Effect of aging treatment on the microstructure, wear resistance, and fracture toughness of a novel Fe-based intermetallic compound alloy coating fabricated by LDED
Abstract: TC4 alloy is valued for its high specific strength, making it critical for unlubricated moving and load‑bearing aerospace components like landing gear hinges and hydraulic actuators. However, its low hardness and poor wear resistance under dry sliding severely limit the service life of components. Intermetallic alloys offer high hardness and wear resistance but suffer from room-temperature brittleness and processing difficulties. In this study, an iron-based intermetallic alloy coating was successfully prepared on TC4 alloy using laser directed energy deposition (LDED). The effects of different aging temperatures on microstructure, microhardness, wear performance, and apparent indentation fracture toughness were systematically investigated. The results reveal that the as-deposited coating mainly consists of Laves and B2 phases, forming a typical dendrite and interdendritic structure. As aging temperature increases, the B2 phase gradually transforms into Laves phase, with its volume fraction increasing from ~33.5 vol% to ~66.0 vol% after aging at 800 °C. At 800 °C, ~2.8 vol% L21 phase precipitates. The coating aged at 600 °C reaches a peak hardness of ~975.8 HV, about 2.65 times higher than that of TC4 substrate, and exhibits the best wear resistance with the lowest friction coefficient (0.455) and wear rate (1.40 × 10−5 mm3/(N·m)). The as-deposited coating shows the highest fracture toughness (5.59 MPa·m0.5), which decreases with increasing aging temperature. The incoherent Laves/B2 interface promotes crack deflection and arrest, enhancing fracture toughness. This study elucidates the correlation between aging treatment and the process–microstructure–property relationship, providing a theoretical basis for developing wear-resistant and tough protective coatings on titanium alloys. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Konjac glucomannan-modified ferrous fumarate emulsions with interpenetrating polymer networks: Physicochemical stability, microstructure, and bioaccessibility
Abstract: Ferrous fumarate (FF), a iron-rich organic fortificant, exhibits high oxidation stability; however, its poor solubility and severe sedimentation in neutral media limit bioaccessibility. This study developed an FF-loaded emulsion based on an interpenetrating polymer network (IPN) formed by whey protein concentrate (WPC), xanthan gum (XG), and konjac glucomannan (KGM). It investigated the physicochemical stability, microstructure, intermolecular interactions and iron bioaccessibility of the emulsions at different KGM concentrations. Increasing the KGM concentration reduced the emulsion particle size from 946.07 to 346.70 nm and raised the absolute zeta potential from 50.34 ± 1.17 mV to 53.34 ± 0.89 mV, thereby improving physical stability. The emulsions showed enhanced apparent viscosity with shear-thinning behavior and dominant elastic responses within the linear viscoelastic region. Microstructural analysis revealed that KGM incorporation converted a layered structure into a robust IPN architecture, confining FF near the oil–water interface and suppressing droplet aggregation. Spectroscopic results indicated strengthened intermolecular hydrogen bonding and increased β-sheet content. The incorporation of KGM effectively maintained the Fe2+ retention rate (∼95%) during thermal processing. The IPN emulsion achieved an iron bioaccessibility of 73.18%, representing an 11.86-fold increase over free FF. This study demonstrates the efficacy of IPN-structured emulsions in delivering poorly soluble active ingredients, providing a promising strategy for developing iron-fortified foods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Bao Y.; Shao S.
Title: Adaptive optimization for high dimensional interference array jet distribution: thermal-field-feedback and multi-hole-linkage
Abstract: To address engineering challenges of high-dimensional interference array jets, including the curse of dimensionality in the parameter space, high optimization cost, and difficulty in obtaining the optimum, a thermal-field-feedback-based multi-hole-linkage adaptive optimization method is proposed. This strategy transforms the high-dimensional independent search into a physics-guided adjustment and coordinates the interactions among the jet holes for hotspot suppression by adaptively updating jet-hole positions, significantly alleviating the curse of dimensionality and thus achieving an optimized engineering solution at an acceptable computational cost. The optimized configuration evolves from a uniform square to a hotspot-converging, non-uniform diamond distribution. For DJCP-16, under all inlet velocities tested (0.5 to 4 m/s), the optimized jet cooling plate reduces the maximum temperature T max by an average of 11.03 °C (21.69%) and temperature dispersion T σ by an average of 1.26 °C (32.82%), with only a 2.36% average increase in energy consumption. As the hole number increases, marginal performance gain diminishes under conventional heat flux. For DJCP-100 (250000 W/m2), the reduction in T max is only 2.47 °C (6.85%). However, under a higher heat flux (1250000 W/m2), DJCP-100 achieves a substantial T max reduction of 12.38 °C (12.31%). For the given environmental parameters, this method requires only one meshed model and one adaptive simulation to obtain an optimized distribution, greatly shortening the design cycle. This feedback-driven adaptive adjustment of the jet positions precisely matches the cooling to the hotspots, achieving efficient energy utilization at low energy cost. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Authors: Raja B.; Karuppanan S.
Title: Multifunctional AB2O4 spinel ferrites: Advances in doping and antimicrobial mechanisms
Abstract: AB2O4 spinel ferrites (where A = divalent metal ions and B = Fe) have emerged as promising materials for biomedical applications, including drug delivery, magnetic hyperthermia, and antimicrobial therapy, owing to their unique structural, magnetic, and electronic properties. This review summarizes recent advances in the synthesis of spinel ferrite nanoparticles, with emphasis on transition-metal and rare-earth doping strategies, and discusses the mechanisms responsible for their antimicrobial activity. Studies show that doped spinel ferrites containing Co, Zn, Mg, Cu, and other metal ions exhibit enhanced bacteriostatic and bactericidal effects against a broad spectrum of Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, including drug-resistant strains. Their antimicrobial performance is primarily attributed to reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, membrane disruption, and controlled ion release. Current challenges include improving biocompatibility, reducing cytotoxicity, and ensuring stability. Overall, doped AB2O4 spinel ferrites represent a platform for next-generation antimicrobial nanomaterials, with further research needed to optimize efficacy, biocompatibility, and stability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: An efficient unconditional energy-stable scheme for the simulation of the square phase-field crystal model
Abstract: In this paper, we propose a linear, second-order accurate in time, and unconditionally energy stable numerical scheme for the strongly nonlinear square phase-field crystal equation to simulate dynamical behaviors of crystals. Based on the relaxation method, an auxiliary variable is introduced to approximate the nonlinear term, which allows an algebraic system to be directly solved on a staggered grid while maintaining consistency with the original variable. The unconditional energy stability and unique solvability of the scheme are rigorously proved. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical results and demonstrate the influence of irregular confinement on the formation and evolution of square crystalline structures. © The Author(s) under exclusive licence to Sociedade Brasileira de Matemática Aplicada e Computacional 2026.

Authors: Lin Y.; Hu H.; Li B.; Li H.; Zhang Y.
Title: JCF-NMF: Automatic hierarchical multi-view clustering via Joint Convex-Fused Non-negative Matrix Factorization
Abstract: Multi-view clustering has attracted considerable attention due to its ability to integrate information from multiple sources to uncover the intrinsic structure of data. Among various techniques, Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF) has been widely employed in multi-view clustering due to its strong interpretability and effectiveness. However, most existing approaches adopt a two-stage paradigm — first learning a common representation and then performing clustering — which focuses mainly on representation-level alignment but fails to fully exploit the consistent cluster structures shared across views. Moreover, decoupling representation learning from clustering often leads to suboptimal performance, and the requirement of predefining the number of clusters further limits their flexibility. To address these issues, inspired by the idea of convex clustering, we propose JCF-NMF, a novel one-step, joint convex-fused NMF framework for automatic hierarchical multi-view clustering. The key innovation of our work is a joint convex fusion penalty applied to the representation matrices of all views. Specifically, an l2-norm regularization is imposed on inter-sample representation differences, which guides them to converge toward a shared cluster structure. This design enables a joint optimization of representation learning and clustering, allowing dynamically updated representations to iteratively refine clustering assignments. As the fusion penalty strength increases, representations from different views gradually merge, forming a multi-granularity hierarchical clustering structure that progresses from fine to coarse levels. This mechanism contributes to the interpretability of the model. Extensive experiments on five real-world datasets demonstrate that JCF-NMF consistently and significantly outperforms state-of-the-art multi-view clustering methods. © 2026

Authors: Liu S.; Yang G.
Title: Evolution of cooperation in spatial public goods games via Q-learning with random walks
Abstract: This study investigates the evolution of cooperation in spatial public goods games with overlapping local groups. Considering that learning outcomes depend not only on the update rule itself but also on the information available to learners, we introduce random walks into Q-learning to incorporate multistep spatial information, and a Random Walk Weighted Q-Learning mechanism is constructed. Secondly, under such a mechanism, we conduct numerical simulations. Simulation results indicate that the RWQ mechanism achieves higher cooperation levels than Self-Q, Direct-Q, and Global-Q, and also shows an advantage over Unweighted k-hop-Q in the low synergy region. Further analyses of social state perception and learned Q-value provide additional insight into the mechanism underlying the promotion of cooperation. Finally, we employ sensitivity analyses with respect to the state resolution, information range, random walk decay factor, exploration rate, learning rate, and discount factor, and the results further confirm the robustness of this cooperative advantage. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Guan W.; Liang D.; Zhao C.; Xiao Y.; Li D.; Wang S.; Shan R.; Yuan H.
Title: Debromination of pyrolysis oil from brominated epoxy resin by two-stage pyrolysis: roles and potential of attapulgite
Abstract: Pyrolysis is a key technology for the efficient and safe debromination of brominated epoxy resins (BERs) in waste printed circuit boards (WPCBs). However, conventional pyrolysis often suffers from insufficient debromination of the pyrolysis oil, which restricts its subsequent utilization. Herein, a two-stage integrated pyrolysis process coupling thermal debromination with catalytic pyrolysis is proposed for enhanced bromine removal and quality upgrading of pyrolysis oil. The results show that increasing the temperature in the downstream reaction zone promotes secondary cracking of volatiles, significantly reducing the bromine content while simultaneously increasing the relative content of high-value aromatics. When the temperature of second-stage reaction zone reached 700 °C, the bromine content in the pyrolysis oil decreased to 24.87%, whereas the aromatic hydrocarbon content increased to 45.31%. The introduction of attapulgite (ATP) further promoted bromine removal. Notably, alkali modification exposed the metal active sites of ATP and introduced sodium species, thereby facilitating C–Br bond cleavage and increasing the debromination efficiency to 72.94%. This method offers valuable guidance for the valorization of bromine-containing solid waste and novel insights into environmentally sound disposal of WPCBs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Stepwise loading of bimetallic Mg–Zn sites in Y zeolites for enhanced adsorption of long-chain alkylaromatics from diesel
Abstract: Long-chain alkylaromatics in diesel significantly reduce fuel quality by lowering cetane number and increasing particulate emissions, yet their selective removal remains challenging due to weak π-interactions and steric hindrance with conventional adsorbents. Here, we report a Mg-first, Zn-second stepwise loading strategy to introduce bimetallic sites into Y zeolite. The prior incorporation of Mg prevents Zn migration during calcination, largely preserving the zeolite microporosity. Moreover, Mg → Zn electron transfer reduces the positive charge on Zn, a change that would conventionally weaken cation–π attraction. Counterintuitively, the optimized adsorbent, Zn-MgY-3, exhibits enhanced n-butylbenzene (n-BB) adsorption and, in competitive adsorption with ethylbenzene (EB), the adsorption of n-BB exceeds that of EB, reversing the trend observed on monometallic Zn-NaY. Meanwhile, the n-BB/1-methylnaphthalene (1-MN) uptake ratio increases from 0.17 to 0.34, confirming enhanced selectivity for monoaromatics even in the presence of competing bicyclic aromatics. DFT calculations confirm a decrease in Zn charge upon Mg incorporation. The adsorbent also shows stable performance over multiple regeneration cycles at 180 °C without solvent, demonstrating its practical potential for diesel dearomatization. Copyright © 2026. Title: PTFE@PPy core–shell fillers enhance epoxy strength and tribological performance via interfacial anchoring and transfer-film stabilization
Abstract: Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) is a widely used solid lubricant in polymer-based self-lubricating composites. However, its low surface energy and chemical inertness often lead to three-body abrasive wear and rapid wear during sliding. To address these limitations, this work proposes an interfacial polar-anchoring strategy in which a doped polypyrrole (PPy) shell was constructed on PTFE microparticles by aqueous in situ oxidative polymerization, yielding PTFE@PPy core-shell fillers for incorporation into an epoxy matrix. The polar PPy shell bearing -NH-, -N+= , and -SO3- active species strengthens filler-matrix bonding, resulting in 12% and 10% increase in tensile and compressive strengths, respectively, over PTFE/epoxy. At a PTFE@PPy loading of 25 wt%, the steady-state friction coefficient stabilizes at 0.088 under 40 N against GCr15 steel ball, and a 40.7% lower wear rate than unmodified PTFE/epoxy. Cross-sectional FIB-TEM and elemental mapping revealed a compact transfer film approximately 145 nm thick on the steel ball, with relatively continuous coverage in the examined region. The film contained an Fe/S/O-enriched inorganic region adjacent to the steel and an outer light-element-rich organic region. These regions exhibited a diffuse and partially interpenetrating transition. The organic-rich region would provide low-shear coverage, whereas the interfacial inorganic region may promote film anchoring. Their coupled organization reduced direct counterface contact and limited tribo-oxidative damage, thereby improving the tribological performance of the epoxy composite. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Microscopic experimental investigation into the effects of silt on gas hydrate formation in sandy marine sediments
Abstract: Marine gas hydrate reservoirs are rich in fine-grained silt, which substantially affects gas hydrate occurrence patterns and sediment pore characteristics. The presence of silt is a key factor that controls gas production efficiency and sand production behavior during hydrate exploitation. In this study, cryogenic scanning electron microscopy (Cryo-SEM) was used to characterize CO2 hydrate occurrence morphologies in silt-bearing sediments. Low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (LF-NMR) was further employed to examine how silt grain size influences hydrate formation and effective pore size of sediments. The results show that silt has a pronounced effect on hydrate occurrence. Silt promotes the formation of hydrate clusters and strengthens interparticle cementation. Silt also enlarges the space available for hydrate nucleation and growth, leading to a looser pore-filling structure of hydrates. In addition, silt increases the water–gas contact area in pores, and an appropriate amount of silt enhances the hydrate formation rate. However, the presence of silt significantly reduces the effective pore size of hydrate-bearing sediments (HBS), which is unfavorable for sediment permeability. Compared with the HBS without silt, the injected-water signal intensity under the same pressure difference was reduced by about 50% and 20% for the HBS containing fine silt and coarse silt, respectively, indicating that silt reduces the effective pore size and seepage capacity of HBS. This study clarifies the roles of silt in hydrate formation and pore characteristics of HBS, and provides support for developing efficient exploitation strategies and for assessing operational safety in marine gas hydrate production. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Study on the effect of ammonia energy ratio on the combustion characteristics of ammonia-diesel dual-fuel under CO2/O2
Abstract: In order to investigate the effect of ammonia energy ratio (AER) on the ignition characteristics of ammonia-diesel dual-fuel in a CO2/O2 atmosphere, a simplified diesel-ammonia (SDA) mechanism is developed, in which five NH3-related kinetic parameters are updated on the basis of the B2PLYP/def2-TZVP method with dispersion correction, while a diesel surrogate consisting of 70 % n-heptane and 30 % toluene is adopted, and the final mechanism contains 307 species and 1763 reactions. Meanwhile, a visual rapid compression machine (RCM) system is established, and experiments are carried out at ammonia energy ratios of 0 %, 10 %, 20 %, 30 %, and 40 % under three background gas conditions, namely 47 %CO2/53 %O2, 51 %CO2/49 %O2, and 55 %CO2/45 %O2. Furthermore, ignition delay time, heat release rate, and reaction pathways are analyzed by combining numerical calculation with experimental observation. The results show that the SDA mechanism can accurately predict the ignition delay time of the ammonia–diesel dual-fuel system in a CO2/O2 atmosphere, with maximum and average relative errors of 8.49 % and 3.02 %, respectively. Under the condition with 30 %AER, the peak heat release rate (HRR) in the 55 %CO2 atmosphere decreases by about 66 % compared with that in the 47 %CO2 atmosphere, whereas the spectral width increases by about 43 %. Moreover, under high AER and CO2/O2 atmosphere, recycling and termination reactions related to NH2 and H2NO are enhanced, low-temperature hydrocarbon chain-branching reactions are suppressed, and the coupled effect finally leads to delayed ignition, weakened heat release, and lower flame luminosity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Organic–Inorganic nanocomposite microspheres with enhanced mechanical stability for deep reservoir profile control
Abstract: Polymer gel microspheres are promising agents for in-depth profile control in heterogeneous reservoirs, but conventional polymer microspheres (CPMs) are susceptible to mechanical damage during injection and repeated extrusion through pore throats, resulting in poor long-term plugging stability. Herein, we report shear-resistant organic–inorganic nanocomposite microspheres (NCMSs) prepared by inverse emulsion polymerization using a long-chain hydrophobic associative monomer and cetyltrimethylammonium bromide-modified montmorillonite. Reversible hydrophobic associations and rigid CTAB-MMT nanosheets provide complementary mechanisms for stress dissipation and structural reinforcement, respectively, thereby improving microsphere stability while preserving pore-throat deformability. NCMSs-0.5 retained 97.30 % of their initial D50 after five consecutive passages through a 12 μm micropore plate and exhibited good particle-size stability under elevated-temperature, high-salinity, and repeated pore-throat deformation conditions. After 180 days of aging, their apparent pressure-bearing strength remained 11.31 MPa, approximately 4.3 times that of CPMs. NCMSs achieved plugging efficiencies of 92.59–94.31 % and increased the liquid-production fraction of the low-permeability core from 13.83 % to 47.14 %, with its final oil recovery reaching 23.61 % compared with 14.47 % for CPMs. Microfluidic visualization further revealed deformation-assisted pore-throat passage and bridging retention. This work provides an effective organic–inorganic network design for durable deep profile control and enhanced oil recovery in heterogeneous reservoirs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Li C.; Li J.; Zhang L.; Zhou J.
Title: Dynamic modelling and uncertainty quantification of water conveyance system with bifurcated pipes in hydropower stations under coupled disturbances
Abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy introduces significant uncertainties into hydropower station operation, yet the coupling mechanisms between hydraulic parameter uncertainties and stochastic load disturbances in water conveyance systems with bifurcated pipes (WCS-BP) remain insufficiently understood. This study develops an efficient uncertainty quantification framework that integrates stochastic surrogate modeling, dynamic sensitivity analysis, and stability assessment. A dynamic model and a stochastic surrogate model for WCS-BP are first established, with the sparse grid method (SGM) employed to balance accuracy and efficiency in high-dimensional uncertainty computation. Dynamic sensitivity analysis is then performed to quantify the effects of parameter uncertainties across different operating stages. For stability assessment, zero eigenvalues are identified and excluded from the spectral abscissa statistics to enable accurate assessment of oscillation attenuation. Finally, the framework is applied to a practical engineering case. The results indicate that load disturbance dominates the system response, with time-varying sensitivity: initial head and discharge dominate the early operating stages, whereas head loss in the main pipe primarily influences the steady-state stage. Zero eigenvalues under various operating conditions mainly originate from flow balance at the bifurcation point. Furthermore, head loss uncertainty has a limited effect on the directly disturbed unit, but significantly amplifies response fluctuations in the parallel unit under asymmetric disturbances. These findings provide actionable guidance for prioritizing load disturbance monitoring, focusing on initial head and discharge during early operation and head loss during later stages, and adopting coordinated control strategies for parallel units under asymmetric disturbances. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Title: Experimental investigation and mechanistic study of coal dust wetting by [BMIM][HSO4]
Abstract: Enhancing the wettability of coal dust is of considerable importance for effective dust control in coal mines. In this study, the optimal conditions for enhancing the wettability of Huozhou coal dust (CD) using the ionic liquid [BMIM][HSO4] were determined through an orthogonal experimental design. The underlying mechanism by which [BMIM][HSO4] enhances the wettability of CD was systematically elucidated by integrating physicochemical characterization, quantum chemical calculations, and molecular dynamics simulations. The results demonstrated that the optimal treatment conditions consisted of a temperature of 40 ℃, an immersion time of 8 h, and a solid-to-liquid ratio of 1 g:10 mL. Under these conditions, the contact angle of CD decreased markedly from 79.9° to 46.2°, indicating a substantial enhancement in wettability. [BMIM][HSO4] effectively promoted the development of pore and fracture networks within CD, significantly increasing its specific surface area and thereby providing additional pathways for water adsorption and penetration. Meanwhile, [BMIM][HSO4] regulated the surface functional group composition of CD, effectively decreasing the relative abundance of hydrophobic groups while increasing the proportion of hydrophilic groups. Furthermore, [BMIM][HSO4] strengthened the interfacial electronic interactions within the CD-H2O system, significantly enhancing the ability of the coal dust surface to adsorb water molecules, increasing the thickness of the interfacial water adsorption layer, and reducing the mobility of interfacial water molecules, thereby promoting the accumulation and stable adsorption of water molecules near the coal dust surface and ultimately improving coal dust wettability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Synergistic interconnected quasi-spherical Pd-Ni nanoparticles on lignin-derived N, O-doped carbon promote selective glycerol oxidation

In addition, the catalyst maintains stable operation in an H-type flow cell with minimal current decay (≥65 mA cm−2) over 3 h. Title: Effects of MgO on the flow behavior of CaO-rich municipal solid waste slags for stable entrained-flow gasification
Abstract: Municipal solid waste (MSW) contains biogenic carbon that can be used for green methanol production. Entrained-flow gasification provides a promising pathway for the resource utilization of MSW while reducing environmental risks associated with conventional disposal methods. However, stable operation requires MSW ash to melt within an appropriate temperature range and form a continuously dischargeable slag phase. SiO2–Al2O3–CaO–MgO model slags were designed to clarify how MgO regulates the high-temperature flow behavior of CaO-rich MSW slag. Flow temperature (FT), viscosity–temperature characteristics, phase evolution, and melt structure were examined using thermodynamic calculations, XRD, Raman spectroscopy, XPS, and molecular dynamics simulations. MgO showed a composition-dependent effect rather than simple fluxing behavior. Moderate contents, particularly 2–6%, generally lowered FT and improved flowability through changes in phase assemblage and network depolymerization. Excessive MgO favored Mg-bearing or Al-bearing crystalline phases and narrowed the temperature interval corresponding to viscosities of 2.5–25 Pa·s (ΔT2.5–25Pa·s). Structural analyses showed that MgO acted mainly as a network modifier in lower-CaO slags, whereas in CaO-enriched slags, Mg2+ possibly cooperated with Ca2+ in charge compensation for Al3+, enhancing aluminosilicate network polymerization. This effect was particularly evident in slags with a lower Si/Al ratio (2.5) and was associated with poorer flow stability. Validation with real MSW ashes reduced FT, T25 Pa·s, and TCV by up to 274 °C, 135 °C, and 149 °C, respectively, while expanding ΔT2.5–25 Pa·s by 14.3-fold. These findings provide a basis for MgO control and ash-composition design for stable MSW entrained-flow gasification. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Multi-effect inhibition mechanism of CO2 on the lower flammability limit of n-butane under O2/CO2 atmospheres
Abstract: In this study, the lower flammability limits of n -butane in O2/CO2 atmospheres were experimentally determined in the condition of 5 %-70 % CO2 volume fractions at 298 K and 101.325 kPa, employing a 5 L spherical explosion vessel.
