The results indicate that the lower flammability limit of n -butane gradually increases from 1.5 % to 2.4 % with an increase in CO2 volume fraction. Further numerical analysis indicates that the inhibition effect is a process dominated by thermal effects, supplemented by radical chemical suppression, and jointly regulated by transport effects. Meanwhile, elevating the initial temperature decreases the lower flammability limit of n -butane, weakening the thermal effect while enhancing the chemical effect. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: New electrochemical biosensor for the early diagnosis of dengue virus based on a mimetic peptide immobilized on a polymeric nanocomposite
Abstract: Early diagnosis of Dengue fever is critical for effective patient management and outbreak control. This study presents an electrochemical biosensor based on a mimetic peptide (MPDV) covalently immobilized on a gold electrode modified with reduced graphene oxide (r-GO) and poly(3-hydroxyphenylacetic acid). The sensing mechanism is based on the specific binding of anti-DENV IgM antibodies by the LLRNAST core epitope-mimicking recognition motif within the MPDV peptide. This biological interaction modulates the intrinsic electrooxidation of the peptide's cysteine residues, resulting in a sensitive label-free and mediator-free signal. Surface characterization by AFM, CV, and EIS confirmed the successful layer-by-layer assembly of the sensing interface and effective peptide immobilization. The r-GO/poly(3-HPA) nanocomposite promoted a 19-fold enhancement of the electroactive charge, significantly increasing sensitivity. Molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated stable peptide orientation, ensuring the accessibility of the binding motif. The biosensor exhibited a linear response toward anti-DENV IgM in human serum over the dilution range from 1:50 to 1:10,000, with a correlation coefficient (R2) of 0.999. The limit of detection (LOD) was 0.30 ng mL−1 and the limit of quantification (LOQ) was 0.99 ng mL−1. Selectivity was validated against symptomatic negative controls and co-circulating flaviviruses, supported by preliminary immunoassay data, demonstrating negligible non-specific interactions. The biosensor retained approximately 91% of its initial response after 40 days of storage under dry storage at 8 °C. By integrating a structurally stable mimetic peptide with a nanostructured conductive interface, this study establishes a highly sensitive strategy for selective anti-DENV IgM detection. The combination of experimental and theoretical modeling provides a robust platform for early dengue diagnosis and highlights the potential of this mediator-free biosensor for point-of-care applications. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Valorization of Iraqi desert sand into functional hydrophobic silica microparticles for heavy oil upgrading in a novel digital batch baffled viscosity reducer: Experimental investigation and predictive modeling
Abstract: Heavy crude oil produced from the East Baghdad oilfield is currently transported mainly by trucks because of its high viscosity, which limits its pipeline transportation and increases operating costs. This study investigated a sustainable approach for improving the flowability of East Baghdad heavy crude oil using functional hydrophobic silica microparticles (FHS-MPs) prepared from naturally abundant Iraqi desert silica sand. The silica particles were surface-modified with 1-propanol to enhance their hydrophobicity and affinity toward the nonpolar hydrocarbon phase. The prepared particles were characterized using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and water contact angle measurements to verify the successful surface modification. The effects of particle loading (0–500 ppm), and operating temperature (10–50 °C) on crude oil viscosity were systematically investigated using a novel digital batch baffled viscosity reducer. The used reducer was allowed controlled adjustment of temperature and stirring speed and contained four vertical baffles to boost bulk circulation and particle dispersion. The experimental results demonstrated that the hydrophobic silica microparticles significantly outperformed untreated silica by promoting stronger interactions with asphaltene aggregates and disrupting the viscoelastic network responsible for the high viscosity of heavy crude oil. The optimum operating condition was obtained at a particle loading of 400 ppm, achieving a 31 % viscosity reduction at 30 °C, whereas further increases in particle concentration reduced the improvement because of particle agglomeration. Increasing temperature further enhanced viscosity reduction through a synergistic effect with the hydrophobic particles. Comparative experiments exhibited that the baffled reducer conducted a maximum viscosity reduction of 31 %, compared with 26 % for the unbaffled design under the best conditions. An empirical predictive model was developed to correlate crude oil viscosity with particle loading and operating temperature, exhibiting excellent agreement with the experimental data (R2 = 0.995). The proposed approach provides a simple and potentially low-cost strategy for boosting the flowability of Iraqi heavy crude oil. Although the present study was achieved at laboratory scale, the results create a basis for further examination of scale-up and potential pipeline applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Yin X.; Ma G.; Hu X.; Mao W.; Xu H.; Li Z.; Sun X.
Title: Synergistic mechanism of self-healing and lubrication for dynamic disulfide epoxy reinforced by CNT@2D Cu-MOF core-shell structure
Abstract: Epoxy resins are widely used in industry, but conventional thermosetting epoxies suffer from high friction, severe wear, and irreversible crosslinked networks, which limit their repairability, reprocessability, and long-term sustainable use. To address these limitations, a self-healing and reprocessable epoxy matrix (EPD) was constructed through the introduction of dynamic disulfide bonds. Meanwhile, one-dimensional/two-dimensional (1D/2D) CNT@Cu(BDC) core-shell nanohybrids with reinforcing and lubricating functions were synthesized via a solvothermal method and incorporated into the epoxy matrix. The tribological behavior, scratch self-healing capability, and repeated reprocessing performance of the resulting composites were systematically investigated, while the filler-matrix interfacial interactions were analyzed using molecular dynamics simulations. The results showed that the composite containing 0.5 wt% CNT@Cu(BDC) exhibited the best overall tribological performance. Compared with the neat EPD, the average friction coefficient of the EPD-CNT@Cu(BDC) composite decreased by 38.24% to 0.18 ± 0.05, and its specific wear rate decreased by 33.91%. Additionally, the composite retained stable tribological performance after three reprocessing cycles, which was attributed to the unique self-healing and lubrication coupling mechanism. Furthermore, it achieved satisfactory lubrication without high-precision polishing, even with a rough initial surface (Ra = 3.5 μm). Molecular dynamics simulations further revealed that the nanohybrids strengthened the filler-matrix interfacial interactions and restricted molecular-chain slippage. This study provides a viable design strategy for sustainable, self-healing, reprocessable, and self-lubricating epoxy composites. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhang X.; Chen J.; Li J.; Jing G.; Wang G.; Wang C.; An S.
Title: Cement lithofacies shape permeability evolution in sandstones during CO2-rich brine injection
Abstract: Microstructural evolution in cemented sandstones alters pore-throat connectivity and permeability, directly affecting CO2 injectivity in offshore geological storage reservoirs. However, the influence of cement lithofacies on these responses remains insufficiently understood. Here, we conducted reservoir-condition displacement experiments on natural sandstone cores to investigate the evolution of porosity and permeability associated with distinct cement reaction pathways during CO2-rich brine injection. Our results demonstrate that cement alteration involves chemical precipitation, mineral transformation, and mechanical weakening, rather than simple dissolution alone. More importantly, distinct permeability evolution patterns were observed among the three cement lithofacies, with Fe-dolomite-cemented sandstone showing an overall increase with intermittent fluctuations, clay-cemented sandstone experiencing an initial increase followed by a continuous decline, and weakly cemented sandstone exhibiting a monotonic increase. Microstructural analysis reveals that carbonate precipitation and clay transformation contribute to pore filling and restriction of flow pathways, whereas carbonate dissolution and cement weakening promote pore enlargement and connectivity enhancement. Consequently, geochemical reactions cause the porosity–permeability relationship to deviate markedly from conventional predictive models. These findings highlight the critical role of cement lithofacies in controlling sandstone petrophysical responses during CO2-rich brine injection and provide insights for evaluating reservoir-scale CO2 injectivity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Evaluating the impact of digestion pre-treatments on microplastics using NIR spectroscopy
Abstract: Microplastics represent the biggest proportion of plastic residues found in the environment. Their monitoring often requires the elimination of organic matrices through digestion treatments, as these matrices hinder their detection and identification. NIR spectroscopy is a rapid technique for microplastic analysis, however its application to chemically digested particles remain underexplored. The present study evaluates the capability of NIR spectroscopy to identify digested microplastics and to assess the impact of chemical digestion on NIR spectra. The feasibility of using single particle NIR spectroscopy to predict particle size was explored. To do so, polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polystyrene (PS), polypropylene (PP), and low-density polyethylene (LDPE) were digested with three different digestion protocols (65% HNO3, 10% KOH and 30% H2O2). Partial Least Square Discriminant Analysis (PLS-DA) enabled accurate classification of both polymer type and digestion protocol, achieving sensitivities and specificities generally above 0.9. Variable importance in projection (VIP) analysis revealed digestion-induced spectral changes in NIR region. Complementary ATR-FTIR and SEM analysis confirmed chemical and morphological alterations across all four polymers. Furthermore, PLS regression model successfully predicted microplastic particle size, further demonstrating the versatility of NIR spectroscopy. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Chen W.; Ma C.; Tan H.; Zhu S.; Chen W.; Zhu Z.; Ruan C.; Yang J.; Yang J.
Title: Tribological properties of in-situ synthesized Cr7C3-reinforced Ni-Cr-based coatings fabricated via laser cladding
Abstract: To overcome the inherent limitation of poor tribological properties in ex-situ prepared coatings, resulting from hard-phase decarburization and inferior interfacial bonding, in situ Cr7C3-reinforced Ni-Cr-based composite coatings were successfully fabricated via laser cladding. The influence of the Cr/C molar ratio on the microstructure and hardness of the coatings, as well as their tribological behavior across a wide temperature range, was systematically investigated. The results indicate that the in situ synthesized Cr7C3 strengthening phase exhibits uniform equiaxed features with a Cr/C ratio of 3:1, yielding a microhardness of 1066 HV. At room temperature, the primary mechanism is mild abrasive wear, with a coefficient of friction and a wear rate as low as 0.39 and 1.17 × 10−6 mm³ /(N·m), respectively. At elevated temperatures, the tribological performance of the coating exhibits a non-linear trend, and the wear mechanism shifts to a synergistic combination of oxidative, abrasive, and adhesive wear. At 300 °C, matrix softening leads to intensified abrasive and adhesive wear, causing an increase in the coefficient of friction (0.60) and the wear rate (6.20 ×10−5 mm3/(N·m)). However, between 600 °C and 900 °C, the coefficient of friction drops to 0.43–0.53, and the wear rate stabilizes at approximately 4.20 × 10−5 mm3/(N·m). This is due to the tribo-oxides layer formed on the worn surface. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Kim J.H.; Jung J.; Choi H.; Yun G.J.
Title: A novel multiscale intra- and interlaminar fatigue life prediction framework for CFRP laminate composites
Abstract: This paper presents a novel multiscale fatigue life prediction framework for carbon fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP) laminate composites that unifies intra- and interlaminar damage mechanisms. To describe constituent-level degradation, Mori–Tanaka’s mean-field micromechanics theory was employed, and a modified Chaboche fatigue damage model was formulated to capture nonlinear stiffness and strength reduction throughout the primary, secondary, and tertiary stages of cyclic damage evolution. Fiber–matrix interfacial degradation, which is difficult to quantify experimentally, was directly evaluated using X-ray computed tomography (CT) image processing of interrupted fatigue tests, and the resulting interfacial damage behavior was cross-validated with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Manufacturing-induced voids were characterized via CT image analysis, and their agglomeration effects on homogenized stiffness and strength were quantified using a finite-element-based representative volume element (RVE) approach. These results were further incorporated into the stochastic multiscale fatigue framework to account for microstructural variability. The complete framework was implemented in ABAQUS via user subroutines, UMAT for intralaminar behavior and UEL for interlaminar delamination, allowing direct coupling between micromechanical degradation, cohesive damage evolution, and macroscopic fatigue response. Validation was performed through fatigue experiments on T700/Epoxy laminates with various lay-ups ([0]7, [90]14, [±45]4S, [0/90/±45]2S) and stress ratios (R = –1, 0.1, 10). The simulation results showed excellent agreement with experimental S–N curves and failure morphologies, confirming the predictive accuracy of the proposed multiscale intra- and interlaminar fatigue model. The proposed multiscale framework provides a physically consistent and experimentally validated approach for predicting fatigue behavior of CFRP laminates, accounting for constituent degradation, fiber–matrix interface damage, and void agglomeration. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Dynamic-lubrication coupling analysis of bearing thermal elastohydrodynamic lubrication characteristics considering raceway surface waviness
Abstract: To investigate the engineering effects of raceway waviness on the lubrication state of angular contact bearings, a dynamic model of angular contact ball bearings is coupled with a mixed thermal elastohydrodynamic lubrication (TEHL) model. Circumferential sinusoidal waviness is used to represent the machined surface topography of the inner and outer raceways. The Newton–Euler method is employed to formulate the dynamic differential equations of the rolling elements, cage, and inner ring, while the multigrid method is used to solve the governing equations of point-contact mixed TEHL incorporating raceway waviness. The effects of waviness amplitude on film pressure, film thickness, and temperature are systematically examined under three conditions: waviness only on the inner raceway, waviness only on the outer raceway, and simultaneous waviness on both raceways. The results show that increasing waviness amplitude markedly intensifies film pressure fluctuations and local pressure concentration, thereby reducing the minimum film thickness and increasing film temperature. Under identical operating parameters, outer raceway waviness causes more severe deterioration of lubrication performance than inner raceway waviness because centrifugal force amplifies the contact load. In-phase superposition of inner and outer raceway waviness produces coincident wave crests and the strongest squeezing effect, resulting in the greatest deterioration of lubrication performance. By contrast, an anti-phase arrangement allows partial compensation between wave crests and troughs and therefore alleviates lubrication deterioration to some extent. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Experimental investigation of CH4/H2 co-firing flame structure with comparison to 1D simulation in dual-swirl injector
Abstract: This study investigated CH4/H2 flames in a dual-swirl gas-turbine injector, focusing on attached and lifted flame behaviors. High-speed OH-PLIF and PIV were used to analyze flame structures and flow fields as functions of hydrogen content and global equivalence ratio. The experiments were conducted at main bulk velocities of 10 and 15 m/s, global equivalence ratios of 0.5–0.7, and hydrogen contents of 20–80% depending on the bulk velocity. Increasing the hydrogen content promotes flame attachment, whereas increasing the main bulk velocity expands the lifted flame regime. The flame width and pilot flame liftoff height were extracted from the OH-PLIF images using the OTSU method and increased with hydrogen content. Both parameters exhibited strong correlations with the pilot-to-main momentum flux ratio. One-dimensional counterflow flame simulations using OPPDIF were also conducted, and comparable shape parameters were defined from the OH mole fraction profiles. Despite its simplicity, the one-dimensional model reproduced the experimental trends well, indicating that the momentum flux ratio is a key governing parameter and that one-dimensional analysis is a useful tool for interpreting the turbulent dual-swirl flame behavior. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Yao T.; Dong G.; Ge L.; Shi Y.; Wang S.
Title: Photochemical transformation of BTDA in the aquatic environment: mechanistic insights into molecular oxygen activation, photodegradation pathways, and ecological risks
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: 3, 3′, 4, 4′-benzophenonetetracarboxylic dianhydride (BTDA), a crucial monomer for synthesizing high-performance polyimides, is released into surface water and thus acts as an emerging pollutant. Here, we systematically elucidated its homogeneous photochemical process under simulated sunlight at the molecular level, including photoexcitation mechanism, reactive oxygen species generation, photodegradation kinetics, and ecological risks of products. Time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) calculations showed that the S1 excited state exhibited mixed local excitation and intramolecular charge-transfer character. Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) and (density functional theory) DFT calculations confirmed that BTDA produced ·OH via oxidation of water and 1O2 via triplet-state energy transfer. Photodegradation follows pseudo-first-order kinetics with k = 0.0320 min−1 ( t 1/2 = 21.66 min), and the total organic carbon removal rate within an hour is 45%. Quenching experiments indicated that ·OH (37.47%) and 1O2 (49.74%) contribute significantly to the photodegradation process. Based on Fukui function predictions and liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) analysis, six degradation products were identified, indicative of two major pathways, ·OH-induced radical cleavage and 1O2-induced anhydride ring opening followed by further cleavage. Quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR)-based toxicity screening predicted low acute toxicity and no mutagenic potential, whereas several transformation products may present potential chronic and cumulative risks to aquatic ecosystems. This study provides a scientific basis for understanding the environmental photoinduced transformation and ecological risks of the micropollutant in aquatic systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Lu Y.; Sun B.; Li L.; Yu M.
Title: Coupled effects of inclination and vertical vibration on immersion cooling performance of lithium-ion batteries
Abstract: Immersion cooling is an effective thermal management strategy for lithium-ion batteries under high-rate discharge. In electric vehicles, mechanical vibration and battery pack inclination are unavoidable and can alter coolant flow distribution and convective heat transfer around battery surfaces, yet their coupled influence on cooling performance remains unclear. This numerical study investigates the synergistic effects of vertical vibration at frequencies from 6 to 14 Hz and amplitudes from 1 to 5 mm, combined with inclination angles from 0° to 180°, on the immersion cooling of a cylindrical battery module. Vibration substantially enhances heat dissipation, but the degree of enhancement is strongly inclination-dependent. The horizontal configuration at 0° yields the largest temperature reduction: the maximum battery temperature decreases by 21.0% and the thermal equilibration time shortens by 52.6% from 390 s to 185 s relative to static conditions. However, vibration does not universally improve temperature uniformity. At moderate inclinations between 30° and 60°, it paradoxically aggravates intra-pack temperature differences. A mechanistic framework is established based on the vibration Richardson number, oscillatory wall shear stress, and the coefficient of variation of the Nusselt number. When the vibration Richardson number falls below 0.2, corresponding to an amplitude of 5 mm or higher, the influence of inclination angle becomes negligible. Vibration amplitude is identified as the dominant control parameter governing heat transfer enhancement and thermal fluctuation intensity. These findings provide a quantitative basis for understanding the coupled inclination-vibration effects on immersion cooling and offer design guidance for battery thermal management systems under dynamic vehicle conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Authors: Liu Y.; Yin Z.; Zhou L.; Li Y.; Lü K.; Wang L.
Title: MCA-SSL: A synergistic fusion-optimization-alignment loop for incomplete multi-view clustering
Abstract: The missing of views in multi-view data brings challenges to multi-view clustering, such as how to deal with missing views, how to fuse cross-view information, and how to learn clustering-oriented representation. To address these, we propose MCA-SSL, a free-imputation model for incomplete multi-view clustering (IMVC). MCA-SSL integrates mutual cross-attention mechanism (MCA), self-supervised learning (SSL), and global representation and label learning (GRLL), where MCA aims to fuse view-specific representations in a two-way mode for extracting cross-view complementary information in more detail, SSL focuses on optimizing the fused representation by combing contrastive and predictive learning for improving the quality of the view-specific representations, and GRLL is responsible for unifying the feature learning with the clustering task in a framework though contrasting the global representation and pseudo-label with view-specific representations and pseudo-labels for promoting clustering-oriented representations and improving clustering performance. The missing values of samples are initialized by random values, and their representations are iteratively optimized by SSL, which alleviates the difficulty of directly filling the missing values in original data space and enhances the robustness to view incompleteness. The entire process forms a “fusion-optimization-alignment” synergistic loop, providing an integrated learning framework and end-to-end trainable paradigm for IMVC. Extensive experiments on seven benchmark datasets demonstrate that MCA-SSL significantly outperforms baselines. More importantly, ablation studies confirm that the performance gain stems from the effective collaboration, not merely the juxtaposition of its key components. The source code is available at https://github.com/Yuanjing-03/MCA-SSL.git . © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Chen J.; Wang H.; Pang W.; Ding J.; Zhou H.; Wang Y.; Liu B.; Gao Z.
Title: Interference-resistant palm electrochemical nickel-doped-enhanced cell-free biosensor for rapid multi-scenario progesterone detection
Abstract: Composite nanomaterials-enabled USB electrochemical sensors hold great potential for on-site detection, yet achieving rapid, sensitive, and interference-free quantitative analysis across multiple scenarios through simple bioregistration modification remains to be explored. We developed an allosteric transcription factor-based nickel-doped anti-interference cell-free progesterone (ATF-Ni/AC-P4) sensor based on the structural transcription factor (SRTF), which enables efficient and simple modification of SRTF. The high affinity between SRTF and Ni@GO-MXene/SPEC provides exceptional sensitivity (0.0002 μmol L−1) and a wide detection range (0.001 μmol L−1 – 50 μmol L−1). ATF-Ni/AC-P4 sensor achieves one-step target recognition and ultra-fast signal output within 5 min across various sample matrices. Validated in matrices such as water, milk, urine, and blood, the system demonstrates excellent stability. The concurrently developed 3D-printed integrated membrane electrochemical device enables “sample-in, result-out” operation, requiring only simple pre-treatment of the sample. Compact, portable, and interference-resistant, the ATF-Ni/AC-P4 offers an innovative solution for food safety and on-site rapid detection. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Atmosphere-resolved TG-FTIR and DAEM kinetic transfer for predicting heat release dynamics of wood combustion
Abstract: Reliable prediction of transient heat-release behaviour under variable heat fluxes is important for biomass combustion modelling. Cypress wood (CW) and pine wood (PW) were characterised by TG/DTG and TG-FTIR under N2 and air. Atmosphere resolved effective kinetics were obtained using a Weibull distributed activation energy model (DAEM) and transferred as bounded priors to a reduced one-dimensional (1D) combustion model. The model was calibrated against cone-calorimeter data at 35 kW m−2 and independently validated at 25 and 50 kW m−2 without re-optimisation. Air shifted the principal degradation peak to lower temperature and introduced a distinct high temperature oxidative stage. Coincident CO2/CO evolution and secondary DTG mass loss supported the presence of a late-stage oxidative pathway involving char oxidation, while TG-FTIR was used only as qualitative mechanistic evidence. The bounded prior model reproduced mass retention, mass loss rate (MLR), heat release rate (HRR), total heat release (THR), and effective heat of combustion (EHC) for both woods. Across the six material heat flux conditions, NRMSE values were 1.77–5.31% for mass retention, 10.33–15.52% for MLR, and 7.47–16.18% for HRR, with Pearson coefficients of 0.916 or higher; EHC MAE ranged from 0.130 to 0.504 MJ kg−1. These results support a constrained route for transferring atmosphere resolved microscale degradation kinetics to bench scale heat release prediction within the investigated materials and heat flux range. Authors: Lin L.; Stone L.
Title: Efficacy versus coverage: population-level impacts of vaccination schemes
Abstract: The effectiveness of vaccination campaigns depends on vaccine efficacy, vaccination coverage, and vaccine allocation. A fundamental yet often overlooked question is whether higher vaccine efficacy or higher coverage should be prioritised. Here, within a leaky vaccine framework, we provide a theoretical analysis of their relative impact on reducing the epidemic final size in both homogeneous and heterogeneous populations, under proportional and optimal vaccine allocations. We prove that, when vaccine efficacy (in reducing susceptibility) and coverage are traded off so that their product P remains fixed but below the herd immunity threshold, the epidemic final size decreases as efficacy increases and increases as coverage increases, implying that efficacy should be prioritised. Mechanistically, under a fixed efficacy-coverage product, increasing efficacy amplifies population heterogeneity in susceptibility, which in turn reduces the final size. The difference between prioritising efficacy and prioritising coverage can be substantial, particularly when R0 is large. For example, when the basic reproduction number R0=5.0 and the product P=0.6, the final size under prioritising coverage can be 250% as large as that under prioritising efficacy, and up to 400% in heterogeneous populations. These results highlight the critical importance of vaccine efficacy and could provide useful guidance for vaccination policy and epidemic control. Copyright © 2026. Authors: Yao J.; Ning X.; Qian P.; Fu W.; Qian J.; Liu J.; Wu D.; Zhang Z.
Title: Structurally-sparse multi-task semi-supervised TSK fuzzy system for motor imagery electroencephalogram classification
Abstract: To address the challenges of limited labeled data, significant inter-subject variability, and feature redundancy in motor imagery electroencephalogram (MI-EEG) classification, this paper proposes a Takagi–Sugeno–Kang (TSK) fuzzy classifier that integrates structured sparsity, multi-task learning, and semi-supervised learning. First, a single-task semi-supervised learning TSK model is formulated, which employs a structured sparsity strategy via the ℓ2,1−2 norm for rule selection, utilizes dual graph regularization to exploit the manifold of unlabeled data, and incorporates pairwise constraints to enhance discriminability. This model is then systematically extended to a structurally sparse multi-task semi-supervised learning TSK fuzzy classifier (S3MTSK). By introducing a multi-task learning mechanism, the consequent parameters are decomposed into a shared basis and task-specific deviations, regularized by low-rank and ℓ2,1 norm sparse constraints, respectively. This structured decomposition enables the framework to effectively balance cross-task knowledge sharing and subject-specific adaptation. Experimental results on two public brain computer interface (BCI) competition datasets show that S3MTSK achieves significant performance across various labeling ratios, particularly excelling in scenarios with scarce labeled data, validating its effectiveness and practicality for MI-EEG classification tasks. © 2026

Authors: Sun A.; Zou J.; Li X.; Wu S.; Yang C.
Title: Roles of supports in Mo-based catalysts for oxidative desulfurization
Abstract: Molybdenum-based catalysts have attracted considerable attention for oxidative desulfurization (ODS) due to their reversible Mo5⁺/Mo⁶⁺ redox cycling under mild conditions. However, the role of supports is often oversimplified as passive carriers of active components. This review reframes supports from passive carriers to active interfacial components that govern Mo electronic structure, direct oxidant activation pathways, shape the local reaction microenvironment, and enhance catalyst stability through interfacial interactions. Four key support-mediated mechanisms are examined across chemically distinct support platforms, and five categories of support materials are systematically evaluated. Three outstanding challenges are identified, including the absence of quantitative frameworks for isolating the relative contributions of individual support functions, insufficient mechanistic understanding of how support properties govern selectivity between peroxo-mediated and radical-dominated oxidant activation pathways, and the lack of stability assessments extending beyond short-term recyclability to continuous operation under realistic fuel matrices. By establishing a mechanistic framework connecting interfacial support properties to catalytic outcomes, this review addresses a gap in the systematic understanding of support design for Mo-based ODS catalysts and provides a foundation for the rational development of next-generation desulfurization materials. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Rice starch-based emulsion gels containing lemon and oregano essential oils: Structure, rheology, and antimicrobial performance
Abstract: The growing demand for sustainable structured lipid systems has encouraged the valorization of agro-industrial by-products as functional food ingredients. This study prepared and characterized rice starch-based emulsion gels containing rice bran oil, rice lecithin, and essential oils (EOs). The base formulation consisted of rice bran oil (40%, w/w), water (40%, w/w), broken-rice starch (14%, w/w), and rice lecithin (6%, w/w). Sicilian lemon (Citrus limon) essential oil (LEO) and oregano (Origanum vulgare) essential oil (OEO) were incorporated at 10% and 20% (w/w, based on dry starch mass). Gas chromatography–mass spectrometry identified D-limonene (61.3%) and carvacrol (64.1%) as the major compounds in LEO and OEO, respectively. Confocal laser scanning microscopy showed a heterogeneous distribution of fluorescent lipid-rich domains in all formulations. The samples remained visually stable during refrigerated storage, whereas oil loss after centrifugation depended on EO type, concentration, and storage time. All formulations exhibited non-Newtonian shear-thinning behavior and a predominantly elastic response, with apparent viscosity data being satisfactorily described by the Carreau model. Authors: Huang L.; Li Z.; Zhao X.; Li C.; Tang J.
Title: Frequency-domain Guided Attention-Differential Enhancement Network for medical image segmentation
Abstract: Medical image segmentation remains a critical yet challenging task in pattern recognition, as extracting discriminative features is often hindered by complex anatomical structures with indistinct boundaries, low contrast, overlapping tissues, and inherent imaging noise. Consequently, these characteristics disrupt stable pattern representations, making segmentation approaches sensitive to intensity variations and anatomical ambiguities. To address these issues, we propose a Frequency-domain Guided Attention-Differential Enhancement Network (FDANet) for medical image segmentation. Our FDANet explicitly exploits frequency-domain representations, where low-frequency components preserve global anatomical layouts and high-frequency components emphasize structural details, while rich semantic information is simultaneously mined from the spatial domain. Additionally, to mitigate distribution discrepancies between the spatial and frequency domains while suppressing noise introduced during the fusion process, we design a Frequency-domain Differential Fusion Module (FDFM). Specifically, we first obtain two sets of feature embeddings in the frequency domain and spatial domain respectively, and utilize 2D Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) to embed 2D relative spatial position information into these vectors to generate position-aware feature representations. Then we perform two independent self-attention operations within the spatial and frequency domains respectively, concatenate the resulting attention weights, and apply a learnable differential mechanism to adaptively attenuate redundant and noisy activations, thereby enabling more reliable exploitation of complementary cues. Finally, Semantic Consistency Loss (SCL) is employed to enforce semantic alignment between the fused frequency-domain and spatial-domain features, further enhancing the coherence of representations. We conduct extensive experiments on the CXRS, ISIC17, ISIC18, VinDr-RibCXR, and FracAtlas datasets. Experimental results and visualizations show that our method achieves competitive performance across all five benchmarks, consistently outperforming recent Transformer and Mamba-based baselines on most metrics under the same training protocol, while remaining on par with the strongest SAM-based models, illustrating its effectiveness. Authors: Wei D.; Li T.; Ma J.; Wang J.; Tan Y.

Title: Three-dimensional in-situ stress inversion from hydraulic fracturing measurements: A physically constrained Bayesian optimization approach with SH-azimuth consistency
Abstract: Conventional in-situ stress inversion based mainly on stress-magnitude fitting may yield non-unique solutions with similar magnitude residuals but inconsistent principal stress orientations. Moreover, traditional data-driven methods usually require large training datasets, limiting their applicability when high-fidelity forward simulations are expensive. To address these limitations, this study proposes a physically constrained Bayesian optimization framework, termed SOC-BO, for sample-efficient and geomechanically consistent in-situ stress inversion from hydraulic fracturing (HF) measurements. The inversion is formulated as a constrained optimization problem in which a measurement-point-normalized objective function is constructed to reduce the scale-dominance effect caused by large spatial variations in stress magnitude, while the measured maximum horizontal principal stress (SH) azimuths are introduced as explicit physical constraints. Through the probability of feasibility, the sequential procedure allocates high-fidelity simulations to candidates having both low normalized component misfit and acceptable SH-azimuth consistency. The method was validated using HF measurements from an ultra-long, deeply buried tunnel on the eastern margin of the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau. SOC-BO identified the best feasible solution within 67 forward simulations. Compared with unconstrained Bayesian optimization under the same initial design, SOC-BO reduced the forward-simulation budget by 28.7% and the optimal objective value by 12.5%. Compared with a genetic-algorithm-optimized backpropagation neural network under the same forward-simulation budget, the stress-magnitude and SH-azimuth RMSEs were reduced by 34% and 36%, respectively. These results indicate that SOC-BO provides a physically constrained and sample-efficient approach to improve parameter identifiability and suppress SH-azimuth inconsistent non-unique solutions in HF-based inversion when the regional stress direction is sufficiently coherent and local directional uncertainty can be quantified. © 2026

Authors: Tian H.; Wang C.; Liu J.; Chen W.; Mo G.; Gao X.; Bai J.; Ma K.; Li P.
Title: A biomimetic imidazole-based hydrogen-bonded organic framework for photoelectrochemical sensing of nerve agent simulants
Abstract: Inspired by the catalytic triads of lipases that recognize organophosphorus compounds via histidine-imidazole sites, we rationally designed an imidazole-functionalized hydrogen-bonded organic framework (Im-HOF), FDU-HOF-50, as a biomimetic nanozyme for the photoelectrochemical (PEC) sensing of dimethyl chlorophosphate (DCP, a sarin simulant). FDU-HOF-50 features open nanochannels decorated with highly accessible imidazole moieties, creating a confined microenvironment precisely tailored to match the molecular dimensions of DCP. This spatial confinement enables the highly selective capture of the target through a synergistic mechanism of size-exclusion and specific N···P supramolecular interactions. Upon capture, the subsequent hydrolysis-induced protonation of the framework generates imidazolium species, which effectively narrows the band gap of the HOF and dramatically boosts its photoelectric conversion efficiency. Capitalizing on this mechanism, an electrolyte-free, portable photoelectrochemical sensing platform was constructed by integrating the Im-HOF with carbon nanotubes onto interdigitated electrodes. The resulting sensor exhibits an ultra-fast photocurrent response toward DCP, demonstrating a wide linear range of 10–350 ppm, a low detection limit of 2.3 ppm, and superb long-term storage stability (over 30 days). Overall, this work highlights the immense potential of biomimetic imidazole-based HOFs for chemical warfare agent detection, while offering a novel paradigm for engineering enzyme-mimetic framework materials with highly accessible, bio-inspired active sites. Authors: Peng S.; Liu W.; Li R.; Yang P.
Title: Airflow field reconstruction and spontaneous combustion evolution in a gob under the influence of extraction disturbances
Abstract: Gas extraction from a bottom drainage roadway can effectively reduce the risk of gas accumulation; however, it may also disturb the airflow field in the gob and aggravate the spontaneous combustion risk of residual coal. In this study, the working face in a coal mine was selected as the engineering background. Indicator gases and air leakage characteristics in the gob were tested, and a seepage-oxygen supply model under extraction disturbance was established. The evolution of air leakage pathways, the reconstruction of the oxygen supply structure, and the migration characteristics of high-temperature zones were investigated to reveal the multi-field reconstruction mechanism and the evolution of spontaneous combustion risk in the gob. The results show that: (i) extraction disturbance forms an air leakage pathway from the gob to the bottom drainage roadway, which changes the original gas migration pattern from a unidirectional “arc-shaped return flow” to a bidirectional split-flow pattern consisting of “arc-shaped return flow” and “directional flow”. The seepage velocity near the intake side is higher than that near the return side; (ii) bottom drainage roadway extraction enhances both oxygen supply and heat accumulation in the gob, thereby causing the limited to the shallow part oxidation reaction zone to extend deeply. The oxidation zone migrates 7–19.4 m toward the deep gob, the high-temperature zone expands by approximately 9 m, and temperatures in different regions increase by 2–5 ℃. (iii) extraction disturbance reconstructs the multi-field structure of the gob, forming a spatially stratified system dominated by airflow migration, oxidation reaction, and high-temperature accumulation. The overlapping area of these fields represents the high-risk zone for spontaneous combustion. This stratified structure promotes a positive feedback loop in which temperature acts back on the flow field, thereby driving the migration of the “three zones” range and increasing the risk of coal spontaneous combustion. This work contributes to guiding the coordinated prevention and control of gas emissions and coal spontaneous combustion in the gob under extraction disturbance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Choi W.-G.; Lim J.-S.
Title: Enhancing shale gas production forecasting performance using bidirectional gated recurrent unit with integration of attention mechanism and Fourier analysis networks
Abstract: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) often lose initial training information and treat all time-series data as continuously periodic, which limits their ability to account for production changes in shale gas caused by sporadic non-periodic features. This study aimed to overcome the limitations of RNNs-based shale gas production forecasting by improving the learning architecture to transform early production decline trends into series-based time-series representations, while selectively incorporating key features. To achieve this, Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) combined with the attention mechanism (AM) was applied to forecast production up to 60 months using data from Barnett Shale, including 24 months of production history, shut-in periods, monthly operation days, and decline characteristics. Furthermore, by comparing with Time2Vec, this study demonstrated the advantage of Fourier Analysis Networks (FAN) in capturing production decline from both periodic and non-periodic perspectives. Based on this capability, a novel approach, termed FAN-BiGAD, was proposed to address the limitations of RNNs-based models. Compared with the BiGRU-based model, FAN-BiGAD reduced the mean average absolute percentage error (MAPE) from 29.8% to 14.5% and the normalized root mean squared error (NRMSE) from 35% to 16.1%. In addition, an independent validation on the Marcellus Shale dataset yielded average MAPE and NRMSE values of 11.1% and 17.4%, respectively. Moreover, the cumulative production forecasts generated by FAN-BiGAD exhibited a high degree of linear agreement with the observed cumulative production in both development areas, resulting in R2 values of approximately 0.99. The proposed approach may facilitate optimizing operational planning for shale gas wells, thereby preventing supply imbalance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Xu M.; Men S.; Zheng K.; Tian M.
Title: Bimetallic FeZr-MOF with enhanced peroxidase activity via Fe-O-Zr bridging electronic synergistic effects: a three-channel sensor for organophosphorus pesticide recognition
Abstract: Organophosphorus pesticides present a notable risk to public health, making it essential to develop swift and dependable analytical techniques for food safety, yet conventional single-channel colorimetric sensors face great challenges in discriminating multiple structurally similar pesticides with high accuracy. To address these issues, a Fe-Zr bimetallic metal-organic framework nanozyme with prominently enhanced peroxidase activity was synthesized via a one-step solvothermal method. The intermetallic electron transfer through Fe-O-Zr bridges accelerates the reversible Fe3+/Fe2+ redox cycle; with a Michaelis-Menten constant ( K m) of 0.11 mM for H2O2 and a maximum reaction rate ( V max) of 9.95 × 10−8 M s−1, its catalytic efficiency outperforms monometallic analogues and the majority of previously reported MOF-based nanozymes. On this basis, a three-channel sensor array integrating absorbance, smartphone-based RGB colorimetric and photothermal signals was constructed, coupled with principal component analysis (PCA) and hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA) for chemometric pattern recognition. The sensor works effectively over a wide concentration range (5–200 μM), with excellent interference resistance and satisfactory recoveries (94.2%–107.4%) in real samples. Most importantly, the Fe-O-Zr bridging synergistic strategy offers a new approach to enhance MOF peroxidase activity, while the multi-channel architecture mitigates the limitation of single-channel sensors in differentiating similar pesticides, supporting reliable on-site food safety and environmental monitoring. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Experimental characterization of needle valve dynamics and bounce control in an outwardly opening hydrogen injector
Abstract: Precise fuel injection control is critical for realizing the full efficiency and emission potential of hydrogen direct injection engines. The low viscosity and poor lubricity of hydrogen, however, bring unique challenges for injector dynamics, particularly regarding needle valve bounce and its impact on metering accuracy and durability. This paper investigates the needle‑valve dynamics of a solenoid outwardly opening hydrogen injector and evaluates a secondary‑current strategy for controlling post‑closure bounce. By using high‑speed backlit imaging, the needle‑lift profiles, response delays, velocity characteristics, and rebound behavior were measured across a wide range of injection pressures, commanded pulse widths, and back pressures. It was found that increasing injection pressure improves linearity and reduces back‑pressure sensitivity for the injected mass. Under short pulses and low pressure (≤12 bar), the needle does not reach full lift, while under high pressure (≥16 bar), full lift can be achieved easily. Opening velocity increases with increasing pressure, and closing peaks velocity (−1.3 to −1.5 m/s) generally exceeds opening peaks, indicating strong seat impact. Needle bounce is obvious, with amplitude up to 32.8 µm. A secondary‑current strategy with a dwell interval of approximately 200 µs and a second pulse duration of approximately 300 µs reduces bounce amplitude by up to 46%, with the first bounce remaining dominant. Consistent with soft-landing control principles, this suggests reduced impact velocity during seating. However, if the secondary current is applied too late (dwell ≥ 400 µs), it re‑excites the needle after seating and amplifies rebound by 170% (to 88.5 µm). Title: Complementary mapping reassignment transform and its application for multimodal signal analysis
Abstract: Effective and accurate characterization of multimodal signals acquired under complex operating conditions has become a key research focus in the field of time-frequency analysis (TFA). Existing single-direction TFA methods are inadequate for handling multimodal signals, while mode-discrimination-based post-processing techniques still have room for improvement in time-frequency resolution. In this study, a novel TFA technique termed complementary mapping reassignment transform (CMRT) is developed. First, the intrinsic limitation of single-direction TFA methods in handling multimodal signals is elucidated from the mathematical theory. Second, a complementary redundancy elimination strategy is constructed based on instantaneous frequency and group delay estimation operators in the multimodal time-frequency plane, yielding a binarized time-frequency matrix that only retains ridge location. Finally, a time-frequency mapping operator is designed to project the binarized plane onto the original plane, generating a highly readable time-frequency representation. Numerical and experimental results validate that the CMRT yields highly concentrated TFR while maintaining strong noise robustness in multimodal signal processing, indicating its suitability for nondestructive testing and fault diagnosis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Sayyed M.I.; Rilwan U.; Sola V.; Aygün B.
Title: Bismuth-doped borosilicate glass system for enhanced gamma radiation shielding: Experimental investigation of attenuation properties and compositional optimization
Abstract: The increasing use of ionizing radiation in medical, industrial, and nuclear applications requires effective shielding materials that provide strong attenuation while reducing reliance on toxic heavy metals such as lead. This work examines bismuth borosilicate glasses with densities from 4.824 to 5.597 g/cm³ for gamma shielding. Authors: Qi Z.; Zhang Y.; Yang Z.; Wang R.; Hao D.; Du Q.; Hou Y.
Title: Diagnosing spatial hydrothermal heterogeneity in a large-area PEMFC under blocked cathode flow fields using segmented EIS measurement
Abstract: The local state of health in a large-area (370 cm2) proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) was investigated using segmented electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) technology. Parameter distributions were compared by regulating cathode stoichiometries and implementing localized cathode gas channel blockages. Results demonstrated that regulating stoichiometry induced a spatial seesaw compensatory effect. Specifically, a higher stoichiometry alleviated severe flooding in downstream regions, while excessive levels exacerbated upstream membrane drying. Meanwhile, under the normal flow field, pronounced lateral and longitudinal heterogeneity was observed: the upstream region showed a dehydration signature, whereas the downstream region exhibited the highest mass transport ASR. The geometric-core region combined suppressed current with high ohmic and charge transfer ASRs, consistent with local dehydration. Under AB blockage, the Row B ohmic ASR increased by 63.0 % and its current decreased by 39.5 %, whereas the bottom Row A retained a low ohmic ASR and high mass transport ASR, consistent with water retention. Title: Hydrogen spillover network-driven hydrodeoxygenation of lignin Oil:Ni-Ru bimetallic synergy and oxygen vacancy engineering for high-selectivity cycloalcohol production
Abstract: This study addresses the key demands for the hydrodeoxygenation (HDO) of real lignin oil to produce high-value chemicals. Commercial TiO2 was transformed into layered sodium titanate nanorod supports (denoted as TiO2-HT) through a high-concentration NaOH hydrothermal method, and Ni and Ru active components were loaded by a hydrothermal reduction method. Systematic characterizations indicated that this strategy successfully constructed a synergistic catalytic system with highly dispersed metal sites and abundant oxygen vacancies. Mechanism analysis revealed that the electron-rich Ru centers preferentially split hydrogen to generate active hydrogen atoms, which were transferred to Ni sites and oxygen vacancies via hydrogen spillover, achieving efficient activation and cleavage of C-O and C=O bonds in lignin oil molecules. The strong metal-support interaction (SMSI) formed by the Ni-Ru alloy and oxygen vacancies further enhanced the interfacial synergy of the catalyst, significantly improving its catalytic activity, durability, and product selectivity. Title: Non-destructive evaluation of equivalent interfacial transport resistance in SHJ solar cells: An engineering tool for process monitoring and optimization
Abstract: The interfacial contact characteristics between transparent conductive oxides (TCO) and microcrystalline silicon (μc-Si:H) are critical factors limiting the performance of silicon heterojunction (SHJ) solar cells. Conventional characterization methods, such as the transfer length method (TLM), require destructive sample preparation and specialized test structures, making them unsuitable for in-line process monitoring. This work proposes a practical series-resistance decomposition method based on dark current-voltage (dark I–V) characteristics, enabling non-destructive extraction of an equivalent interfacial transport resistance (RSres) associated with the TCO/μc-Si:H heterointerface in intact SHJ cells. The method subtracts contributions from the metal grid, TCO lateral conduction, metal/TCO contact, and silicon bulk resistance from the total series resistance, yielding a lumped device-level parameter intended for comparative process evaluation. Title: A theoretical and modeling study on the NH2, NO, and NO2-initiated H-abstraction mechanism in NH3/acetone and NH3/2-butanone combustion

The CCSD(T)/CBS//M06-2X/6-311++G (d, p) level was employed to calculate the potential energy surfaces for the NH2, NO, and NO2-initiated H-abstraction reactions in NH3/acetone (ACE) and NH3/2-butanone (MEK) combustion. For transition states with multiple reference features in the NO2 system, the CASSCF method was further employed to correct the barrier heights. Rate constants for all reaction pathways were determined at 300–2000 K using transition state theory (TST) in conjunction with the Master-equation. The results demonstrate that the NH2-initiated reactions exhibit the lowest barriers (7.2–11.7 kcal/mol) and are thus kinetically favored, whereas NO-initiated pathways are uncompetitive. The energy barriers for the NO2-initiated reactions lie between those of NH2 and NO. The good agreement with previously reported kinetic data supports the reliability of the current calculations. Authors: Qiu Y.; Xie J.; Qiu S.; Li J.; Liang C.; Guo S.; Chen H.; Zhao P.
Title: An interpretable large language model framework with the cokemaking-oriented prompt and fuzzy-enhanced explanation for coke quality prediction
Abstract: Although many data-driven coke quality prediction models have been proposed, existing approaches primarily rely on structured data and fail to effectively utilize the large amount of accumulated domain knowledge, such as published technical reports and scientific literature in the cokemaking field. This limitation restricts further improvements in prediction performance. Moreover, there is still a lack of a unified framework that can achieve high prediction accuracy, handle incomplete data, provide interpretability, and support interactive analysis. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel Large Language Model (LLM) framework with a cokemaking-oriented prompt and a fuzzy-enhanced explanation mechanism for predicting Coke Reactivity Index (CRI) and Coke Strength after Reaction (CSR). The input coal properties are represented as both textual tokens and graph tokens, which are further integrated within the LLM to capture complementary semantic and structural information. A total of 928 Chinese coal samples are used for model development, with the testing set entirely composed of real industrial cokemaking data. The proposed model achieves superior performance compared with mainstream machine learning approaches, with mean absolute errors of 1.72 for CRI and 2.37 for CSR, and demonstrates good generalization ability on 39 Australian coal samples. It is further found that cokemaking-oriented prompt outperforms generic prompts by activating domain-specific knowledge, leading to more compact and well-separated feature representations in the learned LLM embedding space. In addition, the fused token representations outperform single-modality inputs due to complementary information integration. The model also provides interpretable results, generating feature importance scores and explanations that are highly aligned with domain knowledge. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Effervescent-tablet-integrated derivatization and salting-out extraction for LC–FLD determination of neuropathic pain drugs in human plasma
Abstract: Reliable measurement of neuropathic pain medications in plasma is required for pharmacokinetic evaluation and therapeutic monitoring; however, their high polarity and weak intrinsic UV/fluorescence signals complicate chromatographic detection. Each preprepared tablet (8 mm in diameter and 2 mm thick) contained 2.3 mg of 6-aminoquinolyl-N-hydroxysuccinimidyl carbamate (AQC), together with 108.7 mg of Na2CO3 and 47.3 mg of NaH2PO4 (molar ratio, 2.6:1). Title: κ-Carrageenan modulates the network structure and properties of microbial transglutaminase-induced pea protein isolate gels

LF-NMR analysis revealed that the proportion of immobilized water in the PPI-0.4%KC gel reached 96.83%, indicating enhanced water immobilization within the gel network. Structural characterization further showed that appropriate KC addition contributed to the development of a more uniform and compact gel network in the composite gels. This study provides new insights into the concentration-dependent structural regulation of KC within mTG-induced protein networks and highlights the importance of coordinating covalent crosslinking and non-covalent interactions for tailoring plant protein gel structures. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Synergistic effect of mesoporosity and basicity in calcium aluminate catalysts on catalytic cracking of medium–low temperature coal tar to light olefins

Herein, four CA catalysts were fabricated via dry and wet mixing routes using AlOOH and α-Al2O3 as Al precursors, respectively. The crystal structure, pore characteristics, and surface basic sites of the as-prepared catalysts were systematically characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD), N2 physisorption, and CO2 temperature-programmed desorption (CO2-TPD). Title: Decoupling gas-phase and surface-reaction effects in ammonia-induced soot suppression: a surface-reactive PBM study
Abstract: A surface-reactive soot population balance model is developed to decouple the gas-phase and surface-reaction effects of ammonia on soot formation in ethylene counterflow diffusion flames. The model extends the conventional HACA-based framework by incorporating reactions of NH3, NH2, and HCN at soot active sites, and is solved using a moment projection method coupled with the OPPDIF-CHEMKIN flame solver. The model is applied to a series of ethylene/NH3 counterflow diffusion flames with different ammonia substitution ratios. The predicted soot profiles show reasonable agreement with experimental measurements. The strong monotonic decrease in soot formation with increasing ammonia addition is correctly captured. A decoupled analysis reveals that ammonia suppresses soot predominantly through gas-phase inhibition of aromatic precursor formation and PAH growth. Ammonia activation consumes H radicals and redirects part of the reactive hydrocarbon pool into nitrogen-containing intermediates, thereby reducing the formation of PAHs which strongly weaken soot inception. From the perspective of soot particle dynamics, the reduction in soot number density is governed mainly by decreased inception, while the reduction in soot volume is controlled primarily by weakened C2H2-based surface growth. Surface nitridation provides an additional but secondary suppression route by occupying soot active sites and indirectly inhibiting the dominant hydrocarbon-driven growth pathway. These results clarify the dominant gas-phase and secondary surface-reaction effects of ammonia on soot suppression and provide a mechanistic framework for soot modeling in ammonia-assisted combustion systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Mei Y.; Wang Y.; Wang B.; Dai A.; Sun H.
Title: Partially sharing spatial-dependence between forward and reverse sequences for 3D Human Motion Prediction
Abstract: 3D Human Motion Prediction (HMP), with the aim of forecasting future human pose sequences based on historical observations is a typical sequence-to-sequence task. Encoders of different deep models strive to learn the temporal-dependence and spatial-dependence from the observations to guide the prediction of decoders. Compared with text data for NLP or image data for image understanding, 3D human motion data is much smaller in volume, and obtaining a high-quality prediction model with limited training samples becomes a huge challenge. An effective solution to this challenge involves efficiently improving the sample efficiency. As yet, almost all HMP models have ignored the valuable information hidden in corresponding reverse sequences. Different from existing models that view the spatial-dependence as a whole, we consider that the spatial-dependence can be further semantically divided into the motion-level and sequence-level, and for a motion sequence, the motion-level spatial-dependence can be shared between its forward and reverse orders. Title: Synthesis study of formation bioavtur-type hydrocarbons from waste cooking oil-derived biodiesel (FAME) through sub-micron bubbles ozonolysis reactor
Abstract: The fossil fuel crisis has encouraged the development of biofuels as a renewable alternative fuel for the aviation sector. This study examines the ozonolysis method using a sub-micron bubble reactor to convert waste cooking oil-derived biodiesel (fatty acid methyl esters, FAME) into aviation fuel-range compounds. The average bubble diameter was 578 nm, confirming the formation of sub-micron bubbles, although not within the nanobubble range ('200 nm). Nevertheless, the bubble size distribution was relatively consistent, with stable size characteristics. Several physicochemical properties, including distillation characteristics (initial and final boiling point), complied with SNI and ASTM standards, although the smoke point and product losses remained below specification. However, the flash point of the bioavtur product was slightly higher than the conventional standard. Title: Thermodynamic simulation and mechanistic analysis of a dual-pathway biomass chemical looping gasification–steam reaction system for hydrogen production from typical aquatic invasive biomass
Abstract: The utilization of invasive aquatic biomass for hydrogen production offers a promising route for simultaneously addressing invasive species management and low-carbon energy supply. This study employed alligator weed (Alternanthera philoxeroides , AP) and water hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes , EC) as feedstocks to construct a dual-pathway biomass chemical looping gasification–steam reaction (BCLG-SR) hydrogen production system consisting of a fuel reactor (FR), water–gas shift reactor (WGSR), steam reactor (SR), air reactor (AR), and pressure swing adsorption (PSA) unit. A steady-state thermodynamic equilibrium model was developed using a process simulation framework, incorporating RYield for biomass decomposition, RGibbs based on Gibbs free-energy minimization for the main reaction equilibria, and REquil for the WGS reaction. The Peng–Robinson equation of state was used for gas-phase thermodynamic property calculations. Under the fixed dry biomass feed rate of 600 kg·h−1, the CoFe2O4 system achieved the highest H2 production rate of 58.36 kg · h−1, corresponding to 97.27 g H2 per kg of dry biomass processed. Increasing the S/B ratio significantly increased the H2 molar fraction, which reached approximately 64% in the CoFe2O4 system. Different oxygen carriers (OCs) exhibited distinct influences on system performance, with the Fe2O3 system exhibiting higher H2 selectivity (SelH2) and a higher lower heating value (LHV) of the product gas. Carbon in the system was mainly enriched in the form of CO2, with the CO2 fraction at the outlet of the water–gas shift (WGS) pathway remaining above 98% under most operating conditions. Title: Heteroatom-regulated adsorption of Cd2+, Cr3+, and Tl3+ on graphene: Surface energetics and site preference
Abstract: The substitution of heteroatoms changes the local surface environment of graphene and affects its interactions with metal ions. This study used density functional theory to investigate adsorption of Cd2+, Cr3+, and Tl3+ on pristine and B-, N-, S-, and P-doped graphene. Results show clear differences in adsorption energy and preferred configuration between dopants and ions. B-doped graphene exhibits the highest adsorption to Cd2+ and Cr3+, while Tl3+ is most favorably affected by N-doped graphene. Cr3+ is generally more strongly associated with the surfaces under investigation than Cd2+ and Tl3+. Cd2+ and Tl3+ favor similar adsorption regions in B-, and N-doped graphene, but different configurations in pristine and P-doped graphene. Analysis of the charge density also shows dopant dependent charge redistribution around the adsorption site. Title: Age-dependent molecular and dosimetric responses in human fingernails following ionizing radiation: A combined Raman spectroscopy and ESR study
Abstract: This research investigated the molecular structural changes in human fingernails induced by ionizing radiation and their dependence on donor age using a combined approach of Raman spectroscopy and electron spin resonance (ESR) dosimetry. Fingernail and toenail samples were collected from 12 healthy Asian volunteers aged ten–70 years. Each sample set was divided into irradiated (20 Gy X-rays) and control groups for analysis. ESR spectra were recorded 1 h post-irradiation, while Raman spectra were acquired in the 400–1800 inverse centimeter range to probe keratin conformation and disulfide bond integrity. The results revealed that radiation-induced ESR signal intensities varied significantly with age, with the youngest donors exhibiting the highest intensity. Raman spectroscopy showed that unirradiated fingernails from older donors had substantially greater disulfide bond intensity, indicating a higher crosslink density. After irradiation, all age groups displayed a significant decrease in disulfide bond intensity, confirming the radiation-induced cleavage of these bonds. Furthermore, the amide II band region showed greater intensity changes in younger donors, suggesting more pronounced protein structural alterations in this group. The normalized peak area ratio of the S–S bond to the C–C bond decreased significantly after irradiation across all groups, with the oldest group having the highest pre-irradiation ratio. Pearson correlation analysis revealed a strong negative association between radiation-induced ESR signal intensity and the post-irradiation S–S/C–C ratio, indicating that greater disulfide bond disruption corresponded to a higher ESR signal intensity. These findings provide a molecular basis for the age-dependent variability observed in fingernail dosimetry. The novelty of this study lies in the direct correlation between age-related keratin structural differences and dosimetric properties, demonstrating that Raman spectroscopy can identify radiation-induced molecular changes that influence ESR signal formation. This combined methodology improves the accuracy of retrospective radiation dosimetry using fingernails, a non-invasive and readily accessible biological material. Therefore, understanding these age-dependent molecular responses is critical for developing personalized dose assessment methods for nuclear and radiological emergencies, where precise dosimetry guides medical triage and treatment decisions. Title: Multiple-stage magnetic regulation of soot characteristics and emission across a wide range of oxygen concentrations
Abstract: This study explored the performance of soot reduction in inverse diffusion flames (IDF) with various oxygen concentrations by simultaneous applying magnetic fields to multiple soot evolution stages. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) and Raman spectroscopy were employed to analyze the structural characteristics of soot. Imposing an upward magnetic gradient on soot at their in-flame growth stage effectively promoted soot inception. In contrast, as soot within the flame exhaust traveled through the magnetic field, the magnetic effect significantly reduced soot emissions by accelerating soot oxidation. For flames at oxygen concentrations of 25% and 30%, multiple-stage magnetic field increased the content of disordered carbon inside soot particles. However, for flames with oxygen concentrations of 35% and 40%, multiple-stage magnetic intervention resulted in a more ordered nanostructure within the soot particles. Such oxygen‑dependent discrepancies in magnetic responses originated from the distinct regulatory effects induced by magnetic field loading in different soot evolution stage. Specifically, the imposition of an upward magnetic gradient in the flame zone expanded the high‑temperature region, which extended the residence duration of soot particles within the flame, thereby facilitating the carbonization process. Additionally, magnetic field application could strengthen the oxidation of soot within flame exhaust region by enriching local oxygen concentration. Meanwhile, as soot particles transported across the magnetic field, magnetic effect could promote the transformation from ordered carbon to disordered carbon within soot particles. Under varied oxygen conditions, the relative contributions of these coupled mechanisms differed, thus resulting in an oxygen‑dependent evolution of soot properties under magnetic regulation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Sulfur transformation behaviors and synergistic mechanism during co-pyrolysis of coal and waste tire
Abstract: Sulfur migration plays a crucial role in determining pollutant emissions, products quality and process sustainability during co-pyrolysis of coal and waste tire. However, the sulfur transformation pathways during co-pyrolysis of coal and waste tire remain unclear. In this work, the sulfur migration behaviors and transformation mechanism during co-pyrolysis of Yulin coal (YL) and waste tire (WT) were systematically elucidated by comprehensively evaluating the effects of heating rate, temperature and blending ratio on sulfur distribution in char, liquid and gaseous products on an infrared-heated fixed-bed reactor. Results showed that sulfur from YL pyrolysis was mainly distributed in liquid and char products, whereas sulfur from WT was predominantly retained in char. During co-pyrolysis, sulfur transfer from char to liquid products was promoted and sulfur release into gaseous phase was suppressed. Positive synergistic effects were mainly observed for sulfur distribution in liquid products, whereas negative synergistic effects dominated gaseous sulfur evolution. Among the S -containing gases, H2S formation was obviously inhibited at 550 – 600 °C. XRD and XPS analyses revealed that co-pyrolysis promoted the conversion of organic sulfur species into inorganic sulfides. Meanwhile, WT-derived ZnO participated in sulfur stabilization through the formation of ZnS species. These findings elucidate the coupled radical-mediated sulfur redistribution and Zn -assisted sulfur immobilization mechanism during coal/waste tire co-pyrolysis, providing insights into sulfur transformation and emission control during co-pyrolysis process. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Passivation-driven gas diffusion layer degradation in PEM water electrolyser: Mechanism, performance impact and design strategy
Abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolyser (PEMWE) is a promising technology for large-scale green hydrogen production and fuel decarbonisation. However, degradation of the anodic gas diffusion layer (GDL) significantly increases cell voltage and reduces efficiency, thereby limiting PEMWE durability and economic competitiveness for industrial deployment. Previous studies have primarily focused on mitigating GDL degradation and extending component lifetime, while the GDL degradation process itself has received limited attention. In this study, an experimentally validated multiphysics macroscale (mm-scale) PEMWE model combined with a quasi-steady state simulation framework is developed to investigate the GDL degradation process and its influence on PEMWE performance. The results reveal that TiO2 film growth at the GDL-ACL interface follows a distinct spatial evolution sequence, initiating at the edges of the GDL solid under the bipolar plate (BPP) rib, propagating towards the GDL solid junctions, and eventually extending to GDL solid under the BPP flow channel. The GDL degradation process exhibits accelerating behaviour with increasing operating time, leading to progressively increased GDL-ACL interface contact resistance (ICR), non-uniform current and oxygen generation rate distributions, local oxygen accumulation, and increasing cell voltage. Furthermore, the GDL physical structure optimisation mitigates GDL degradation and improves PEMWE long-term performance and efficiency preservation. The cell voltage increase under severe GDL degradation condition is reduced by approximately 36.9 %. Overall, this study provides mechanistic insights into GDL degradation process in PEMWE and offers practical guidance for designing high-efficiency and durable green hydrogen production systems. © 2026 The Author(s).

Authors: Dong Z.; Ling Z.; Yang Y.; Su L.
Title: Numerical study of dry rock-ice avalanche run-up against slit dams by the discrete element method
Abstract: Rock–ice avalanches are highly mobile alpine hazards of growing concern as glaciers retreat and permafrost degrades. Slit dams are regarded as a promising countermeasure against rock-ice avalanches, yet their maximum run-up height is difficult to predict, as existing models neglect the friction reduction and energy dissipation caused by the ice fraction. In this study, the interaction between rock-ice avalanches and slit dams was investigated using the discrete element method (DEM). Following calibration against flume tests, 288 simulations examined the coupled effects of the Froude number (Fr = 1 ∼ 8), ice content, expressed as the solid volume fraction (φi = 0 ∼ 100%), and blockage ratio (B = 0.1 ∼ 0.225). The results reveal a regime transition: at low Fr (≤2), a pile-up mechanism dominates and the run-up height is insensitive to φi and B; at higher Fr (≥3), a vertical run-up mechanism prevails, with the run-up height increasing with ice content and decreasing with blockage ratio. Force-chain and discharge analyses indicate that increasing Fr reorganizes the internal load-transfer network rather than monotonically strengthening it. A higher ice content reduces the continuity and occurrence of high-force paths, whereas the blockage ratio modifies their spatial organization and the transient arching and discharge behavior at the slits. Based on energy dissipation, a modified theoretical model incorporating an effective curvature coefficient keff(φi, B) is proposed, which reproduces the DEM results well (R2 = 0.888) and provides a practical tool for slit dam design. © 2026

Authors: Wei H.; Du C.; Pan J.; Li R.; Yu Y.; Lu D.; Shi P.
Title: Research on coordinated optimization and decoupling control of air flow and pressure for a 100-kW vehicular PEMFC system
Abstract: To address the strong coupling between stack inlet airflow and cathode supply pressure, along with the optimization control problem of a Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell (PEMFC) system, this paper proposes a hierarchical control scheme comprising an optimization layer and a control layer for a 100 kW vehicular PEMFC air supply subsystem. A high-fidelity model characterizing the cathode-side dynamic mass transfer process is first established based on experimental data. The air compressor is modeled using a data-driven approach, while the electrochemical parameters in the semi-empirical voltage model are identified via a hybrid Simulated Annealing-Particle Swarm Optimization (SA-PSO) algorithm. For the optimization layer, a two-dimensional objective function describing system efficiency is developed, and the Multi-strategy Enhanced Dung Beetle Optimization (MEDBO) is designed to obtain flow and pressure references that maximize efficiency under varying current densities. Optimization results show that MEDBO improves system efficiency by 0.6%–5.2% over calibration experiments, significantly outperforming the standard DBO algorithm. For the control layer, an Inverted Decoupling (ID)-based Active Disturbance Rejection Control (ID-ADRC) strategy is proposed for flow-pressure decoupling. Simulation results demonstrate that ID-ADRC achieves superior decoupling performance over Proportional Integral Differential (PID) and ID-PID, limiting coupling-induced fluctuations in airflow and pressure to 2.4 g/s and 0.94 kPa, respectively, while exhibiting stronger robustness against external disturbances. These findings offer new insights into the control and optimization of air supply management for vehicular PEMFC systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Decoupled reverse Kullback–Leibler: Rethinking knowledge distillation loss for bridging GNNs and MLPs
Abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) excel at handling graph-structured data but are often prohibitively expensive for low-latency applications. Cross-architecture graph knowledge distillation (GKD) addresses this by training efficient Multi-layer Perceptrons (MLPs) to mimic GNN performance. Interestingly, while existing methods predominantly use forward Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence, we find that the two terms of reverse KL exhibit optimization properties that are better matched to the GKD objective. However, its conventional form suffers from tightly coupled fitting and regularization terms with fixed weights, limiting its flexibility. To overcome this, we propose Decoupled Reverse KL (DRKL), which introduces hyperparameters to independently adjust the weight of each term, enabling more effective adaptation to diverse prediction scenarios. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that DRKL outperforms both standard forward and reverse KL losses across multiple metrics. Furthermore, DRKL serves as a plug-and-play loss that can enhance the GKD frameworks evaluated in this work without added computational cost, delivering improved performance, robustness, and fast inference.
