Title: Catalytic performance of metal-free ethylenediammonium salt catalysts in the thermal decomposition of ammonium perchlorate
Abstract: Ammonium perchlorate (AP) is the most widely used oxidizer in solid propellants, and its thermal decomposition directly governs the combustion performance. Consequently, extensive research has focused on developing catalytic additives to promote AP thermal decomposition. Currently, AP combustion catalysts are predominantly transition metal-based compounds such as ferrocene derivatives and iron-based catalysts, although these can improve combustion efficiency to some extent, they inevitably introduce metal impurities that compromise combustion performance. This work explores ethylenediammonium-based salts with oxidizing anions as AP thermal decomposition catalysts, synthesized three salts [enH2](ClO4)2·1/2H2O ( 1 ), [enH2](NO3)2 ( 2 ) and [enH2](BF4)F ( 3 ). Title: Advancing the near-surface mechanical characterization of polytetrafluoroethylene by indentation techniques
Abstract: The near-surface mechanical behavior of semi-crystalline thermoplastic polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) is reported at room temperature using the instrumented indentation technique (IIT). A set of four PTFE samples was tested depending on the fabrication process. First, a non-melting technique, i.e., spark plasma sintering (SPS), is used to consolidate a highly viscous PTFE micro-powder at two heating rates (100 and 160 °C/min). Second, PTFE samples prepared by conventional melting techniques, i.e., molding and extrusion, are considered for comparison. This study aims to assess how the mechanical metrics (hardness, H, and Young's modulus, E) depend on the fabrication process. The PTFE samples are characterized using XRD, FTIR, and Raman spectroscopy to identify relationships between microstructure/processing route. Next, the force-indentation depth curves are analyzed using the Berkovich technique at the nano- and microscale. Both the loading and unloading parts are successfully described by the Meyer law and the Oliver-Pharr model, respectively. The newly inverted approach is also tested, and the results agree with those obtained from the Oliver-Pharr model. Additionally, the elastic/plastic contributions during deformation are analyzed for the PTFE samples. For H and E, the results are consistent with the observed increase as the applied displacement decreases. This behavior, called the indentation size effect (ISE), is quantified according to the Meyer law. Title: A water-soluble FeNi–citrate precursor for regulating oil-shale thermal conversion under air and CO2 atmospheres
Abstract: Developing water-soluble catalyst precursors with good dispersion and thermal activity is important for enhancing the thermal reactivity of oil shale during in situ conversion. Title: Real gas effects on the laminar flame speed of hydrogen-methane-oxygen mixtures
Abstract: The laminar flame speed (LFS) of H2-CH4-O2 mixtures has been calculated over a wide range of conditions using both the ideal gas (IG) and the complete Redlich-Kwong (RK) gas models. Title: Investigation of liquid nitrogen infiltration-induced evolution of oxidative adsorption interfaces and low-temperature re-ignition mechanisms of coal
Abstract: The potential spontaneous combustion risk induced by liquid nitrogen (LN2) treatment represents a critical concern for coal spontaneous combustion prevention and control. Title: Defect-engineered lithium-coated BaTiO3 to enable high oxide-ion conduction in LT-SOFC
Abstract: Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) are emerging as transformative electrochemical energy conversion technologies owing to their superior efficiency, fuel versatility, and minimal environmental impact. Enhancing SOFCs for efficient performance at low temperatures (LT, 420–520 °C) requires electrolytes with superior ionic conductivity and extended stability. Here, we introduce lithium-coated BaTiO3 (5%, 7%, and 10%, Li@BTO), demonstrating that varying the concentration yields surfaces that function as efficient pathways for ionic transport, as validated by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), electron spin resonance (ESR), electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), and coupled distribution of relaxation times (DRT) assessments. The highest-performing 7%Li-coated BTO electrolyte delivers a peak power density of 776 mW cm−2 and remarkable ionic conductivity of 0.144 S cm−1 at a low operating temperature of 520 °C. This research emphasises interfacial defect engineering as an effective approach to address the conductivity and longevity challenges of ferroelectric/dielectric perovskite electrolytes, demonstrating exceptional electrochemical performance and a pivotal structure-defect-transport paradigm for the activation of perovskite oxides, thus establishing a foundation for the methodical design of next-generation LT-SOFCs in a scalable context. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Microscopic interactions and wetting behavior at the micro/nano-bubble water-coal interface: experiments and molecular simulations
Abstract: Coal seam water injection is a key technology for pre-wetting and dust suppression prior to mining, with its effectiveness largely dependent on the wetting capability of water on coal. As a novel wetting medium, micro-nano bubble water (MNBW) has drawn increasing attention due to the close relationship between its wettability and preparation parameters, though the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. To address this, physicochemical characterization, contact experiments, and molecular simulations were carried out. Results showed that increasing the gas flow rate during MNBW preparation enhanced its properties: scattered light intensity, interfacial potential, and dissolved oxygen content increased, while surface tension and bubble size decreased, indicating improved system stability. The contact angle on the coal surface decreased accordingly and was positively correlated with dissolved oxygen and interfacial potential but negatively correlated with bubble size. This suggests that higher gas flow rates promote wetting by increasing bubble concentration, lowering surface tension, and enhancing stability. After MNBW treatment, the oxygen content on the coal surface increased by 10.1%, accompanied by significant enrichment of oxygen-containing functional groups such as –OH and –COOH. Molecular simulations revealed stronger adsorption of water molecules in hydroxyl-rich regions, with a 45% increase in the relative concentration of water molecules at the coal–water interface, enhanced interaction energy, and a markedly reduced contact angle. These findings provide a theoretical basis for optimizing MNBW-assisted coal seam water injection technology. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Yan T.; Dai X.; Cui Y.; Wu M.; Liu T.; Zhao D.; Ye C.
Title: Tumor segmentation with incomplete MRI modalities via prototype-driven Progressive Modality Completion
Abstract: Multimodal magnetic resonance imaging enhances tumor segmentation with modality-specific features and cross-modal complementary information. However, the completeness of all desired modalities is often not guaranteed in clinical practice, leading to significant performance degradation with missing modalities. Existing approaches primarily address this problem by deriving shared multimodal representations via modality fusion. However, these methods still struggle to recover critical features of missing modalities during the integration of cross-modal information, resulting in suboptimal multimodal feature learning. To overcome this challenge, we propose Prototype-driven Progressive Modality Completion (P2MC) for tumor segmentation with incomplete modalities. It mitigates representation deficiencies caused by missing modalities with the learning and adaption of compact modality prototypes, as well as gradual recovery of missing modality information that reduces the overall recovery difficulty. Specifically, to obtain the representation of missing modalities, P2MC comprises two major components, Prototype-driven Missing Modality Recovery (PMMR) and Dually-gated Full Modality Completion (DFMC). In PMMR, we develop content-aware image tokenization and adaptive modality prototype generation for initial recovery of essential information about missing modalities. In DFMC, we propose gated channel aggregation and gated spatial aggregation to selectively extract complementary information from multimodal features, fully enhancing the feature representation of each modality. Then, DFMC uses an adaptive class-wise weighting strategy that balances the contribution of each modality to produce the final segmentation map. Experiments on two public brain tumor datasets (BraTS2020 and BraTS2018) and a private cervical tumor dataset (CervTS2024) demonstrate that P2MC achieves superior performance and robustness compared to state-of-the-art methods in tumor segmentation with missing modalities. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: A unified instance selection approach based on distributional similarity for machine learning
Abstract: In this study, we propose a unified instance selection approach, applicable to both regression and classification tasks, that selects a reduced dataset whose distribution matches that of the original, thereby preserving its key statistical and structural properties. Our central contribution is to analytically show that the instance selection problem, aiming to ensure distributional similarity measured via the Wasserstein distance, is exactly equivalent to the balanced k-medoid problem when the compression ratio is integer-valued. We further extend this equivalence to arbitrary (non-integer) ratios with explicit bounds on the resulting approximation error. This equivalence allows the instance selection problem to be addressed directly with existing balanced k-medoid solvers. To this end, we employ a Lloyd-style alternating (EM-type) constrained k-medoid algorithm, obtained by extending an existing constrained clustering method. Extensive experiments across binary classification, multi-class classification, and regression tasks confirm the method's effectiveness: it significantly outperforms the task-specific baseline at most reduction ratios on all seven multi-class datasets (Wilcoxon, p<0.05), outperforms the boundary-focused baseline on the majority of binary settings—most clearly on the higher-dimensional datasets—and attains lower error on four of five regression datasets. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: “Kill two birds with one stone” role of Ag-BC@Cu nanozyme: Orthogonal colorimetric discrimination and determination of Cr(III) and Cr(VI) in water through independently regulated dual enzyme-mimicking pathways
Abstract: Chromium predominantly exists as Cr(III) and Cr(VI) in aquatic environments, which differ markedly in physicochemical properties and toxicity. Rapid and direct discrimination of Cr(III) and Cr(VI) remains challenging because conventional chromium speciation methods often require redox pretreatment, multiple recognition elements, or indirect calculation. Herein, a new Ag/Cu-containing metal-organic nanozyme with MOF-like structural characteristics (Ag-BC@Cu) was developed. Ag-BC@Cu exhibited laccase-like and peroxidase-like activities and was used to construct an orthogonal colorimetric sensor for discrimination of Cr(III) and Cr(VI). Cr(III) selectively inhibited the laccase-like pathway, whereas Cr(VI) enhanced the peroxidase-like pathway, producing independent colorimetric responses at 510 and 652 nm, respectively. Generally, both chromium species were directly discriminated and quantified using a single nanozyme without redox pretreatment, multiple probes, or subtraction-based calculations. The detection limits of the orthogonal colorimetric sensor were 0.05 mg·L-1 for Cr(III) and 0.0047 mg·L-1 for Cr(VI). Smartphone-assisted analysis further enabled portable visual detection of chromium speciation. The colorimetric sensor exhibited good selectivity and was successfully applied to river-water samples, with results consistent with LC-ICP-MS. This work provides a simple “kill two birds with one stone” strategy for chromium speciation, with potential for portable water-quality monitoring. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Geant4 simulation study of PP/epoxy–Li2B4O7/epoxy–WO3 multilayer shielding architectures for neutron attenuation and secondary gamma reduction from a 252Cf source
Abstract: The present work investigates a multilayer shielding system based on polypropylene (PP), Li2B4O7-reinforced epoxy, and WO3-reinforced epoxy composites, aiming to enhance neutron attenuation and control secondary gamma radiation. The influence of layer arrangement on shielding performance was systematically evaluated through neutron transport and secondary gamma-ray analyses using Geant4 Monte Carlo simulations. The simulations employed the FTFP_BERT_HP physics list and a252Cf neutron source modeled using the Watt fission spectrum. A fixed total shielding thickness of 15 cm was maintained for all configurations. Three shielding designs were investigated: single-material configurations (S-group) consisting of 15 cm of each individual material; bulk multilayer configurations (M-group) consisting of three consecutive 5 cm layers with different material sequences; and periodic multilayer configurations (L-group) consisting of repeated 1 cm layers of the three materials. The repeated thin-layer configurations exhibited absorption fractions of 39% and 38% for L1 and L2, respectively, compared with 34% and 27% for M1 and M2. The M-group also showed greater sensitivity to layer sequence, whereas L1 and L2 exhibited similar absorption and identical transmission fractions of 26%. Layer architecture also influenced the secondary gamma-ray response. The emerging gamma-ray tally increased from 450,785 ± 671 for M1 to 535,450 ± 732 for M2, with corresponding mean energies of 0.570 ± 0.00114 and 0.838 ± 0.00135 MeV, respectively. In contrast, L1 and L2 produced similar gamma-ray tallies of 378,615 ± 615 and 375,300 ± 613, with mean energies of 0.650 ± 0.00134 and 0.667 ± 0.00138 MeV, respectively. These results demonstrate that shielding performance depends on both material composition and layer architecture. In particular, repeated 1 cm layering reduced the sensitivity of neutron transport and secondary gamma-ray response to the interchange of the two functional epoxy-based layers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Liu W.; Zhou M.; Gao C.; Ge H.
Title: Reliability-aware dynamic dependency graph neural network for airborne network intrusion detection
Abstract: To address the complex, nonlinear, and time-varying anomalous behaviors in airborne network intrusion data, this paper proposes a reliability-aware dynamic dependency graph intrusion detection method. The method incorporates reliability modeling into the intrusion decision process to assess prediction confidence and improve the discrimination of samples near the decision boundary. Specifically, sliding windows are used to construct window-level dynamic graphs, in which multivariate feature dimensions are treated as graph nodes and mutual information is adopted to characterize statistical dependencies for dynamic edge construction. To reduce short-window estimation noise, a structural prior learned from benign samples is used to softly regularize dynamic graph construction, while temporal consistency regularization stabilizes predictions across adjacent windows. To capture the localized instability caused by intrusions, an entropy-driven subgraph focusing mechanism is designed to identify high-entropy nodes and expand them through multi-hop neighborhoods, thereby emphasizing potentially anomalous regions. A dual-branch GCN-CNN architecture is then used to jointly capture structural dependency perturbations and local temporal patterns. Finally, predictive uncertainty, structural evolution instability, and temporal risk variation are integrated into a unified risk score for quantitative decision support. Results on MIL-STD-1553 validate RADG for airborne intrusion detection, while UNSW-NB15 and CICIDS2017 further demonstrate its generalization to conventional network scenarios. © 2026

Title: Prediction of thermomechanical coupling response of polycrystalline materials based on graph neural networks
Abstract: The mechanical properties of polycrystalline materials are determined not only by the geometric shape and crystal orientation of individual grains but also by other grains within the neighborhood. Here, we propose a graph convolutional neural network model for rapidly predicting the thermomechanical coupling response of polycrystalline materials. We adopt the Voronoi method for grain geometry modeling. By taking the degradation of the elastic modulus of the nickel-based superalloy GH4169 under unidirectional axial pressure in different temperature fields and orientation angles, we verify that the GCN model effectively learned the node characteristics and propagation laws of heterogeneous graphs. The prediction results show a strong linear fitting relationship, the root mean square errors are all less than 5%. In addition, the gradient integration method was employed to quantify the contribution of each feature parameter to the model’s prediction, the effects of different hyperparameters on the performance of the GCN model and the future application prospects of the framework are also discussed. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Inc.

Title: Polypyrrole–ferrocene–biofilm electrode for rapid BOD biosensing and energy recovery from wastewater: Bayesian calibration for field application
Abstract: Developing high-performance bioelectrodes for environmental sensing and energy recovery remains challenging. Optimal PPy loading (50 μg per 0.2 cm2) was determined by impedance spectroscopy, giving a charge-transfer resistance of 28 ± 6 Ω·cm2 for the PPy-ferrocene-biofilm system – more than 1200 times lower than that of the PPy–biofilm electrode. The bioelectrode served both as a BOD biosensor and as an anode in a 3D-printed dual-chamber microbial fuel cell (MFC). The biosensor exhibited a wide linear range of 4–600mg O2/dm3, a ∼5min response time, and 6% RSD. For the first time in a whole-cell BOD sensor, Bayesian calibration reduced the required standards from 15 to 7 while preserving accuracy and providing uncertainty quantification for the Hill equation parameters. Validation against the standard BOD5 method on real surface waters yielded R2=0.9828. Title: CO2-H2O-induced mineral-organic response and pore heterogeneity evolution in different-rank coals
Abstract: The mineral-organic structural response and pore heterogeneity evolution of coal under CO2-H2O interaction are important for evaluating coal reservoir alteration during CO2-ECBM and coalbed CO2 storage. However, the contrasting responses of coals with different coalification degrees remain insufficiently understood. In this study, two separate single-factor CO2-H2O treatment series were conducted for bituminous coal and anthracite: a time-effect series at a fixed CO2 pressure of 2 MPa for 2, 4, 6, and 8 d, and a pressure-effect series at a fixed reaction time of 2 d under gaseous CO2 pressures of 1, 2, 3, and 4 MPa. X-ray diffraction, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, low-temperature N2 adsorption–desorption, and multifractal analysis were used to characterize changes in mineral composition, functional groups, N2-accessible pore-size distribution, and pore heterogeneity. CO2-H2O treatment did not generate new crystalline mineral phases but altered their relative proportions, with dolomite showing the most evident response. Hydroxyl groups and oxygen-containing functional groups were more sensitive to treatment than aliphatic structures, and bituminous coal exhibited a stronger functional-group response than anthracite. Bituminous coal possessed a larger N2-accessible pore volume and retained a mesopore-dominated structure, although its macropore proportion increased from 8.88 % to 13.01 %-15.44 %. In contrast, anthracite exhibited more pronounced pore-size redistribution, with its macropore proportion increasing from 26.67 % to 60.00 % as reaction time increased, resulting in a transition from a mesopore-dominated to a macropore-dominated structure within the measured pore-size range. Multifractal analysis showed that the pore-size distributions of both coals exhibited multifractal characteristics. Bituminous coal maintained a relatively stable multifractal structure, whereas anthracite showed larger and non-monotonic variations in pore-volume probability distribution and heterogeneity. These findings provide a pore-scale basis for understanding the rank-related structural alteration of bituminous coal and anthracite during CO2-H2O interaction and offer implications for evaluating coal reservoir alteration associated with CO2-ECBM and coalbed CO2 storage. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Mitigation of guar gum with different viscosities on rosmarinic acid-induced gel deterioration of oxidized myofibrillar proteins
Abstract: Excessive polyphenol-protein interactions may impair the functional properties of myofibrillar proteins (MP), whereas the potential role of polysaccharides in alleviating such deterioration remains poorly understood. This study investigated the effects of guar gum (GG) with different molecular characteristics on oxidized MP gels containing excessive rosmarinic acid (RA, 0.035%). Compared with the oxidized control (OX), excessive RA further deteriorated gel properties, as evidenced by increased cooking loss from 27.48% to 29.08%, reduced water-holding capacity from 62.75% to 56.20%, and decreased hardness from 278.29 g to 189.09 g. GG supplementation (1.2%) significantly alleviated RA-induced deterioration, with high-viscosity GG (HG) exhibiting stronger protective effects than low-viscosity GG (LG). Compared with the RA group, HG + RA increased water-holding capacity by 36.80%, hardness by 60.06%, and reactive sulfhydryl by 65.8%, while reducing carbonyl content by 57.89% and cooking loss by 75.45%. Intermolecular interaction analysis showed that HG supplementation characterized as higher molecular weight and intrinsic viscosity was associated with increased hydrogen-bond interactions and reduced hydrophobic interactions and disulfide bond formation compared with the RA group. These changes were accompanied by improved protein structural stability, reduced aggregation, and a more compact gel network observed by SEM. Overall, the results suggest that GG, particularly HG, is associated with the alleviation of excessive RA-induced deterioration of oxidized MP gels, potentially through the modulation of intermolecular interaction patterns and stabilizing the protein network. This study establishes a structure-interaction-network-function relationship linking polysaccharide molecular characteristics to macroscopic gel functionality, providing new insights into the regulation of excessive polyphenol-protein interactions in complex protein-polysaccharide systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: High-dispersed NiMo on Yolk-Shell TS-1-SiO2 for enhanced dibenzothiophenes hydrodesulfurization
Abstract: With increasing energy demands and stricter environmental requirements, the design of efficient hydrogenation catalysts and the clean utilization of inferior fuel have become the priorities in the petrochemical research field. Yolk-Shell TS-1-SiO2 (YSTS) composites were prepared to handle the hydrodesulfurization (HDS) for macromolecular sulfur compounds like 4,6-dimethyldibenzothiophene (4,6-DMDBT). An innovative tetradecylamine (TDA) modification method was used to prepare a series of highly dispersed NiMo/YSTS catalysts. The unique yolk-shell architecture features a buffering space and short diffusion pathways, which significantly facilitates the mass transfer of macromolecular compounds and promotes the uniform dispersion of active metals. The resulting highly dispersed metal active sites expose a greater number of catalytic edges, which is crucial for improving overall catalytic efficiency. Building upon this advantageous support, the introduced TDA not only effectively optimized the pore structure of catalysts, but also further facilitated the deep dispersion and sulfidation of Mo species. Consequently, the MoS2 active phase with an optimal stacking morphology was formed. The desulfurization degree of the optimal NiMo@TDA-2.5/YSTS catalyst achieved 99.9% for dibenzothiophene (DBT) and 99.4% for 4,6-DMDBT. Meanwhile, the isomerization (ISO) pathway selectivity was significantly enhanced up to 43.2%, which was driven by the expanded pore structure reducing steric hindrance for macromolecules and the highly active NiMoS-II phases facilitating methyl migration. Consequently, the optimal catalyst exhibited an approximately 37% higher 4,6-DMDBT conversion than the purely microporous NiMo/TS-1 catalyst, and significantly outperformed conventional commercial NiMo/Al2O3 and other micro-mesoporous catalysts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Synergistic protection of hydrophilic coatings by bionic micro-textures and DLC films for enhanced heat dissipation characteristics and friction performance of cemented carbide under spray cooling
Abstract: Poor heat dissipation and severe friction wear are prominent defects of cemented carbide in spray cooling friction environments, which restrict its service life. This work constructed HTDC surfaces integrated with bionic micro-textures, DLC films and hydrophilic coatings on cemented carbide substrates. The morphological characteristics of all multifunctional composite surfaces were characterized, which regulated their surface wettability. HTDC surfaces achieved the minimum contact angle of 3°. Enhanced wettability further improved heat dissipation characteristics, and HTDC delivered the maximum heat flux q with the shortest droplet evaporation time. Under dry friction, the average steady-state friction temperature T fa, average coefficient of friction µ a, maximum height of scratches H max, wear rate W r and counterparts’ wear rate W rc of HTDC were nearly equivalent to TDC (bionic micro-textures and DLC films). Under spray cooling, HTDC exhibited the lowest T fa, µ a, H max, W r and W rc among all samples, and its W r was 87.6% lower than CC in the initial friction cycle. Mechanism analysis revealed that microgrooves captured wear debris to restrain three-body abrasive wear, and DLC films possessed self-lubricating property. Bionic micro-textures and DLC films jointly protected the hydrophilic coatings, thereby maintaining stable surface wettability, which enhanced q and reduced T fa. This delayed the spalling of DLC films and ultimately improved friction performance. This work provides a novel surface modification scheme for cemented carbide under spray cooling environments, and offers reference for subsequent surface structure optimization. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: From diffusion-based semantic reconstruction to identity discrimination: Hierarchical information fusion for occluded person re-identification
Abstract: Occluded person re-identification (Re-ID) requires matching identities when body cues are missing or obscured by unrelated objects. Pose and viewpoint variations further disrupt semantic correspondence between partially visible persons. We propose the Progressive Hierarchical Collaborative Perception Network (PHCP-Net), which integrates diffusion-guided reconstruction, hierarchical collaboration, and feature enhancement. A frozen pose-guided diffusion model generates reconstructed counterparts that provide complementary body cues during training. Within each branch, the Collaborative Interaction Module (CIM) recursively integrates class-token features from shallow to deep stages. The Calibration Optimization Unit (COU) uses reconstructed features as semantic anchors to calibrate intermediate features in the original branch. The Enhanced Fusion Module (EFM) combines the final Vision Transformer (ViT) token-level feature with the CIM output to produce an enhanced identity embedding. The Distribution Constraint Module (DCM) then aligns the two branches through probabilistic, statistical, and identity-conditioned constraints. Only the original branch, comprising ViT, CIM, and EFM, is retained for inference. PHCP-Net achieves 76.20% Rank-1 accuracy and 66.50% mAP on Occluded-Duke, yielding the highest Rank-1 accuracy and competitive mAP among the compared methods. On Occluded-REID, it achieves the highest compared Rank-1 accuracy and mAP, at 90.60% and 84.50%, respectively. Ablation studies support the complementary contributions of hierarchical fusion, intermediate calibration, and final representation alignment to occlusion-robust identity learning. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Hierarchical MXene-Cu hybrid interphases enable thermal-mechanical energy dissipation for high-temperature wear-resistant composites
Abstract: Friction-induced energy accumulation fundamentally destabilizes polymeric interfaces, yet regulating interfacial heat flow under dynamic loading remains a longstanding challenge. Here, a hierarchical MXene-Cu interphase is engineered on a three-dimensional (3D) woven fabric composed of aramid fiber (AF) and polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) yarns to establish a multiscale frictional energy-dissipation architecture. MXene nanosheets are first anchored onto the fiber surface as thermally conductive interfacial bridges and Cu nucleation sites, enabling the in situ growth of a continuous metallic network without conventional noble-metal sensitization. The resulting hybrid interphase integrates anisotropic thermal transport, multidirectional heat-spreading pathways, and adaptive interfacial stabilization within a single structural framework. Consequently, the modified composites exhibit an approximately 743% increase in through-thickness thermal conductivity and a 22.7% increase in tensile strength, accompanied by a 45–68% reduction in wear rate across a wide temperature range. In situ thermal evolution analysis reveals that the interconnected MXene-Cu network rapidly dissipates frictional heat, thereby suppressing matrix thermal softening and interfacial delamination during sliding. Simultaneously, the dynamic release of MXene fragments and Cu nanoparticles promotes the formation of a thermally stable dissipative tribofilm that minimizes interfacial shear resistance and stabilizes interfacial evolution under thermal-mechanical coupling. This work establishes a thermal-mechanical energy dissipation paradigm for regulating dynamic polymer interfaces, offering a new strategy for high-performance wear-resistant composites operating under extreme service conditions. Title: Ex vivo SPME-LC-MS/MS determination of carbamazepine in tissues of Arctic marine bivalve Chlamys islandica
Abstract: The Solid-Phase Microextraction (SPME) is a minimally invasive extraction technique that has gained interest in environmental studies. In this paper, we developed an SPME-LC-MS/MS protocol under ex vivo conditions to extract carbamazepine (CBZ) and its main metabolite, carbamazepine-10,11-epoxide (CBZE) from Chlamys islandica solid tissues. Optimization of SPME included selection of the stationary phase, desorption solution, desorption and extraction times. Under optimized conditions, we utilized commercially available C18 fibers, a 10 min static extraction and a 10 min desorption of CBZ and CBZE performed into 50 μL of ACN:H2O (80:20, v/v) mixture. The linear range for CBZ was 2.5-20 ng g−1 of wet mass with R2 = 0.9900; for CBZE, the linear range was 20-1000 ng g−1 of wet mass (R2 = 0.9743). Title: Multi-View tensor factorization for dynamic attributed graph embedding with graph-aware features
Abstract: Learning node representations in dynamic graphs has garnered significant attention in recent years. However, existing methods face challenges in effectively integrating topology and node attributes within individual snapshots while simultaneously capturing the evolution of graph structure and attributes across snapshots. Motivated by the above challenges, we formulate unsupervised dynamic attributed graph embedding as a coupled multi-view tensor learning problem, where topology, attributes, and graph-aware contextual features are jointly modeled by Multi-View Tensor Factorization (MV-TF) within a shared latent space. The framework explicitly models the coupling between views and incorporates a sparse subspace constraint to enhance embedding quality. Extensive experimental results on node classification tasks demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches. These results highlight its ability to effectively mine the evolution patterns of dynamic graphs and provide valuable insights for related analyses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Classification of Szeged complexity two in unicyclic graphs

Title: Study on CO2 adsorption properties of sulfur-doped porous carbon prepared from high-sulfur petroleum coke by sequential KOH-SO2 activated: GCMC calculation, experiment and kinetics
Abstract: Carbon capture is a pivotal technology for addressing CO2 emissions and promoting carbon neutrality. Porous carbons have emerged as excellent adsorbents for CO2 capture owing to their low regeneration energy consumption and economic viability. In this study, the sulfur-doped porous carbon was prepared from high-sulfur petroleum coke (PHS) via a sequential KOH-SO2 activation. The influences of sulfur functional group and pore structure on the static and dynamic CO2 adsorption performance were systematically investigated through a combination of grand canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) simulations and experiments. GCMC results revealed that thiophenic sulfur exhibits a more pronounced enhancement effect on CO2 adsorption under low-pressure microporous conditions and demonstrates superior stability in humid environments. In contrast, oxidized sulfur species contribute to a higher isosteric heat of CO2 adsorption and improved CO2/N2 selectivity. The porosity of the samples increased significantly with the rise of the KOH activation temperature. Title: Integrative analysis of physiological and metabolomic responses of Vigna mungo to Rhizobium exopolysaccharide-stabilized metal oxide nanocomposites
Abstract: Photosynthesis plays a central role in plant physiological performance and metabolic regulation, thereby influencing crop productivity. Magnesium and iron are essential micronutrients involved in photosynthetic pigment biosynthesis, and their nanoscale delivery may improve nutrient-use efficiency and sustainable crop production. In this study, Rhizobium exopolysaccharide (EPS)-stabilized magnesium oxide and iron oxide nanocomposites (EPS-MgONC and EPS-FeONC) were biosynthesized and comprehensively characterized. EPS-MgONC exhibited an average particle size of 58 nm, hydrodynamic diameter of 2216 nm and zeta potential of −32.7 mV, whereas, EPS-FeONC showed values of 60 nm, 547 nm and −38.5 mV, respectively. Foliar application of optimized formulations (50 ppm EPS-MgONC and 1 ppm EPS-FeONC) significantly enhanced biomass, photosynthetic pigments, total protein, and carbohydrate contents in Vigna mungo. Title: Pool boiling heat transfer enhancement characteristics on multi-directional dynamic micro/nano coupled shape memory alloy surfaces
Abstract: The excellent shape memory effect of shape memory alloys (SMAs) enables the adaptive optimization of boiling heat transfer performance to meet the operational requirements of different heat transfer stages. Nevertheless, previous studies have largely been limited to single-scale deformable structures; because of their fixed geometric configurations, optimal performance has been difficult to maintain across the full range of operating conditions. Based on the self-assembly technology of graphene oxide (GO) nanofluids during boiling, this study systematically investigates the effects of self-assembled nanostructured surfaces on pool boiling heat transfer performance at different deposition heat flux. Furthermore, the optimal nanostructured surface (NS-25W) is integrated with a multi-directional dynamic microstructured surface (MDS) with thermoresponsive properties to construct a novel multi-directional dynamic-nanostructured coupled surface (MDS-NS). By combining pool boiling experiments with visualization observations, the cross-scale synergistic enhancement mechanism of the coupled surface is revealed, and the boiling characteristics of each surface are systematically evaluated. The results demonstrate that the NS-25W surface exhibits a uniform structure and abundant nucleation sites, and its maximum heat transfer coefficient (HTC) and critical heat flux (CHF) are 35.7% and 43.8% higher, respectively, than those of a plain surface. Owing to the dual-enhancement mechanism, the MDS-NS surface overcomes the performance limitations of single-structure surfaces and achieves optimized boiling heat transfer performance, with a CHF of 32.6 W/cm2 and an HTC of 1.01 W/(cm2·K), corresponding to increases of 105% and 140%, respectively, compared with plain surfaces. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Title: Development of a lysosome-targeted fluorescent probe for bioimaging of hypochlorous acid in environmental and biological systems
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Hypochlorous acid (HClO) is an important reactive oxygen species involved in biological oxidative processes and environmental disinfection; however, excessive accumulation may lead to oxidative damage and potential ecological risks. Herein, we developed a red-emitting BODIPY-based fluorescent probe (BDP-FL) for selective HClO detection by incorporating an N-ethylphenothiazine recognition unit and a morpholine moiety for lysosomal targeting. The sensing mechanism is based on HClO-triggered oxidation of the phenothiazine sulfur atom, which inhibits the intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) quenching pathway and restores fluorescence emission of the BODIPY fluorophore. Upon exposure to HClO, BDP-FL exhibited an approximately 30-fold fluorescence enhancement with a detection limit of 0.46 μM and a linear response range of 0–120 μM. The probe showed good selectivity, anti-interference ability, and stable fluorescence responses over a broad pH range (4.0–10.0). In addition, BDP-FL was applied for HClO detection in environmental water and soil samples, as well as in visual sensing platforms including test strips and chitosan-based hydrogels. Fluorescence imaging experiments further demonstrated that BDP-FL could monitor HClO in HepG2 cells and zebrafish, with lysosomal localization confirmed by colocalization analysis (coefficient = 0.92). These results suggest that BDP-FL may serve as a useful red-emitting fluorescent probe for studying HClO-related oxidative processes in environmental and biological systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Effect of two-stage swirl number configurations on emission control in a centrally-staged combustor: flow structures, flame characteristics, and NOx pathways
Abstract: Swirl number selection significantly affects combustor combustion and emission performance. Three-dimensional CFD simulations are conducted to investigate a centrally-staged combustor with a two-stage swirler under various swirl number combinations. The results show that the combustion flow field is predominantly controlled by the second-stage swirl number, with the first-stage swirl number playing a secondary role. Variations in the second-stage swirl number mainly govern the radial expansion of the primary recirculation zone, while the first-stage swirl number primarily influences its axial development. Excessive swirl number in either stage alters the overall momentum balance, thereby reshaping the recirculation structures. The first-main fuel and second-main fuel exhibit stratified distributions, forming a merged “V-shaped” flame. A higher second-stage swirl number reduces the separation between staged fuels, and an appropriate first-stage swirl number regulates fuel concentration, together producing a compact merged flame with a lower flame front temperature. Merged flame intensity governs high-temperature zone formation and peak temperature, while its extent controls distribution, whereas a weak and compact flame yields lower temperatures and fewer hot spots. Increasing the second-stage swirl number while reducing the first-stage swirl number reduces ultra-high-temperature regions and improves temperature uniformity within the combustor, thereby suppressing thermal NOx formation and significantly reducing NOx emissions. At a first-stage swirl number of 0.62 and a second-stage swirl number of 0.55, the combustor achieves NOx and CO emissions of 12.91 ppm and 1.20 ppm, a uniform outlet temperature distribution with a profile factor of 12.98%, and a total pressure loss of 4.11%. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Jet-assisted single-phase immersion liquid cooling for heterogeneous chiplet packages: parametric CFD study on flow rate ratio, inlet temperature, and nozzle geometry
Abstract: This study numerically investigates a jet-assisted single-phase immersion liquid cooling (SPILC) system for high-heat-flux chiplet packages. The system integrates a primary chamber inlet for bulk flow and an auxiliary jet inlet for targeted local cooling of the CPU die (61.2 W/cm2, 7 × 7 mm2). Three-dimensional steady-state CFD simulations using the Realizable k-ε turbulence model examined the effects of flow rate ratio (β = QInlet2/QInlet1), inlet fluid temperature, and jet nozzle geometry. Relative to conventional SPILC under the same total flow rate, jet impingement at β = 1 reduced CPU temperature by 6.11 K. As β increased from 0 to 3, the maximum CPU, GPU, and memory temperatures decreased by 16.18 K, 5.08 K, and 6.97 K, respectively, while the heat transfer coefficient improved by 42.35%. PEC analysis identified β = 3 as the Pareto-optimal operating condition. A Nusselt number correlation, Nu = 3.209 · Rejet0.454 (R2 = 0.994, 3058 ≤ Rejet ≤ 6877), was derived and shown to be physically consistent with limiting-case correlations for forced convection and jet impingement reported in the literature. This correlation is valid within the ranges of Reynolds numbers, fluids, and geometric conditions tested in this study. Inlet temperature variation produced a proportional shift (∼5 K per 5 K change) without affecting flow-side performance, confirming thermal-hydraulic decoupling. The multi-nozzle configuration (Shape 2: five nozzles, d = 0.9 mm) achieved up to 17.07% higher heat transfer coefficient and 3.25 K lower CPU temperature than the single-nozzle baseline (Shape 1: d = 2 mm) under equivalent Reynolds number conditions, at the cost of up to 532% higher pumping power. These findings provide quantitative design guidelines for jet-assisted SPILC systems targeting next-generation chiplet thermal management. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Masson SAS.

Title: Synergistic optical spectral match enhanced photocatalytic degradation of thiamethoxam insecticide using Sm2O3 Photocatalyst
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: The neutralization of toxic industrial and agricultural pollutants via., photocatalysis process is gaining significant interest with the discovery and engineering of new and novel material systems. The present work critically evaluates the photocatalytic degradation efficiency of cost-effective non-toxic ultra-wide bandgap Sm2O3 photocatalyst for the remediation of Rhodamine B (RhB: industrial dye) and thiamethoxam (THMX: insecticide) pollutants. The Sm2O3 is synthesized using hydrothermal method (at 110 °C), and is calcined at different temperatures (400 °C, 600 °C and 800 °C) to yield controlled monoclinic and cubic phases. The phase-pure Sm2O3 shows minimal photocatalytic degradation efficiency (< 16%) for RhB under both ultra-violet (UV) and visible light exposure. The absence of RhB photocatalytic degradation with Sm2O3 is attributed to its high phase purity and mismatch of spectral overlap between the pollutant, photocatalyst and the illumination source. On the other hand, the ultra-wide bandgap Sm2O3 (∼ 4.9 eV) which shows an excellent absorption spectral match with THMX pollutant and illumination source results in a maximum photocatalytic degradation efficiency of 90.83% within 30 min. The THMX photocatalytic degradation showed the evolution of secondary toxic compound, whose peak intensity increased with time under neutral conditions. A systematic study of THMX degradation under different pH conditions reveals pH = 1 results in the degradation of both its intrinsic primary and secondary compound under UV exposure. The Sm2O3 photocatalyst retains its photodegradation efficiency of THMX up to 4 recycle stages, highlights its reusability for real-time practical photocatalytic degradation-based applications. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Investigation of soot formation characteristics in RP-3 aviation kerosene flames using simultaneous dual-wavelength laser diagnostics
Abstract: A simultaneous dual-wavelength laser diagnostic system using 532 and 266 nm excitation was developed to characterize LII-channel radiation, PAHs-related PLIF signals, and Mie scattering signals in RP-3 aviation kerosene laminar diffusion flames. Three cameras simultaneously recorded the same flame section at five fuel–air mass ratios, and 300 valid frames were analyzed for each channel under each condition. Axial statistical analysis, proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), and supplementary scanning electron microscopy (SEM) were used to characterize the spatial evolution of the measured fields and the morphology of the collected particulate deposits. The LII-channel response remained concentrated near the nozzle, consistent with a fuel-rich region associated with pyrolysis, initial carbonization, and early particle-related processes. In contrast, the PAHs-related PLIF field extended farther downstream, consistent with aromatic growth, transport, and diffusion, and maintained a centroid height of approximately 3.2–3.3 cm. The Mie scattering field exhibited the strongest non-monotonic response, with its effective area increasing from approximately 0.3–0.4 cm2 at a fuel–air mass ratio of 0.200 to approximately 1.4 cm2 at 0.100–0.067, before decreasing to approximately 0.5 cm2 at 0.050. This behavior suggests a competition between enhanced particle-phase development under intermediate air supply and increased oxidative consumption, together with reduced residence time, at the highest air flow rate. Across all five conditions, POD showed that the PAHs-related PLIF field consistently exhibited the most dispersed modal-energy distribution, whereas the Mie field showed increasing modal complexity with increasing air supply. The expansion and subsequent contraction of its dominant spatial mode were also qualitatively consistent with the centroid-height and effective-area trends. Multi-height SEM observations under condition c showed increasing morphological complexity from the lower to the intermediate flame region, followed by pronounced restructuring at higher positions, qualitatively consistent with continued aggregation and subsequent structural modification. Overall, the proposed dual-wavelength three-channel strategy provides complementary cross-scale information for interpreting particle-phase evolution in RP-3 flames. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Schlieren visualization of detonation diffraction and initiation in B/C2H4/O2 heterogeneous mixtures using a variable-initial pressure pre-detonator tube
Abstract: Solid powder detonation engines hold significant potential for enhancing aerospace propulsion performance, owing to the high volumetric energy density of solid fuels and the high thermal efficiency of the detonation cycle. These engines are typically ignited by a pre-detonator tube, and the initiation characteristics of the heterogeneous mixtures directly determine their reliable start-up. However, current studies on detonation wave diffraction and initiation have primarily focused on homogeneous detonations, while the discrete nature of powder fuels results in significant differences in heterogeneous systems. To investigate the initiation characteristics of B/C2H4/O2 gas–solid two-phase hybrid detonations ignited by a pressure-variable pre-detonator tube, this study therefore conducted experiments in an in-house detonation bomb with schlieren visualization. Results show that the heterogeneous nature of powder fuels enables re-initiation far from the expansion cone and tube axis, fundamentally differing from gaseous detonations, which are confined within the expansion cone. Moreover, compared with gaseous detonation (φC = 0.6), the slight addition of boron particles (φC = 0.6, φboron= 0.1) can reduce the detonation onset difficulty, whereas an excessive particle concentration (φC = 0.6, φboron= 0.7) hinders it. Furthermore, as the initial ambient pressure inside the detonation bomb increases from 48 kPa to 96 kPa, the initiation difficulty of the B/C2H4/O2 mixture decreases, and the distance from the tube outlet to the re-initiation location also shortens from 91.8 mm to 39.35 mm. These findings provide a theoretical basis for the reliable onset of powder-fueled detonation engines and contribute to a deeper understanding of gas–solid two-phase hybrid detonation initiation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Semi-supervised multi-view classification: A convex formulation and its multi-kernel extension
Abstract: Despite its widespread adoption across various fields, multi-view classification often faces performance constraints due to challenges: the scarcity of labeled data and heterogeneity across views. Motivated by this, we propose a Semi-Supervised Multi-View least squares Regression (SSMVR) method that remains effective under limited supervision while explicitly promoting cross-view consistency and complementarity. In contrast to existing approaches, SSMVR incorporates a small amount of prior information to guide semantic learning, thereby alleviating the need for extensive annotation. Furthermore, we introduce a reciprocal coupling mechanism that enables view-dependent regularization, thereby mitigating single-view dominance without an additional balancing hyperparameter. We further extend this principle to SSMKR, where the learned view weights serve as kernel weights in an adaptive composite-kernel formulation for nonlinear multi-view fusion. Both models admit closed-form alternating updates and global optimality guarantees. Extensive experiments on nine datasets against state-of-the-art methods demonstrate competitive performance across the evaluated datasets and settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Light-adaptive membrane-integrated Sm-ZnO photocatalyst for pharmaceutical and dye abatement coupled with efficient pathogen suppression

Abstract: Persistent pharmaceutical residues like doxycycline antibiotics and recalcitrant organic dyes such as methylene blue have emerged as critical aquatic pollutants, raising global concerns owing to their resistance to conventional treatment processes and their profound ecological and health implications. Herein, pristine ZnO and samarium-modulated ZnO (Sm-ZnO) photocatalysts were successfully developed through a straightforward chemical synthesis. Furthermore, a membrane-integrated 0.5 wt% Sm–ZnO system was developed to facilitate easy catalyst recovery and reuse, achieving 96.28% degradation of doxycycline within 150 min under UV-C irradiation while maintaining good stability over repeated cycles. The markedly enhanced performance of Sm-ZnO is ascribed to synergistic effects arising from band-structure modulation, efficient suppression of charge-carrier recombination, broadened optical absorption, and the creation of highly reactive surface sites. Title: Competing effects of thermal superposition and SVE-associated cooling in unsaturated soils: Controlled experiments and model-based transport decomposition
Abstract: Multi-source heating and soil vapor extraction (SVE) are commonly combined in in-situ thermal remediation, but their competing effects on heat and moisture transfer in unsaturated soils remain difficult to distinguish. This study combines large-scale physical model tests with a thermo-hydro-mechanical (THM)-coupled numerical framework adapted from a previously established granular-thermodynamic formulation. Tests were conducted under single-source heating (SHS), triple-source heating without SVE (THS-NoSVE), and triple-source heating with SVE (THS-SVE), considering two initial dry densities and two gravimetric water contents. Temperature and sensor-derived corrected gravimetric water-content histories were used for model assessment. A matched THS-NoSVE/THS-SVE test with an identical heating history isolated the net SVE response for the dense and wet soil. Across the assessed curves, the range-normalized RMSE (NRMSE) was 2.9–16.2 % for temperature and 11.3–59.3 % for water content, indicating more consistent reproduction of temperature trends than transient moisture peaks. The experiments showed that multi-source heating increased inter-source temperatures; in the matched direct-heating test, SVE reduced temperature and accelerated moisture removal. Model-based term decomposition indicated that conduction dominated without extraction, while fluid-advection-carried heat transport and pressure-gradient-driven vapor transport became the principal calculated components near the extraction well under SVE. Dense and wet soil exhibited more persistent far-field moisture accumulation, interpreted by the model as a saturation-induced reduction in gas-phase mobility. The study separates experimentally observed operating responses from model-derived internal mechanisms and supports coordinated control of heating and extraction during thermal remediation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Molecular effects of PTFE/PA composition on interfacial structure and oxygen transport in high-temperature PEM fuel cell catalyst layers
Abstract: Oxygen transport through phosphoric-acid-containing catalyst layers remains a key limitation in high-temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells (HT-PEMFCs), but how the PTFE/PA composition reshapes the interfacial molecular structure and regulates O2 transport remains unclear. In this work, an all-atom molecular dynamics model of a carbon-supported platinum catalyst layer was developed to represent the interfacial restructuring associated with catalyst-layer preparation and subsequent O2 transport. Equilibrium simulations were employed to obtain the interfacial structures formed during catalyst-layer preparation and to characterize PTFE coverage on the catalyst surface. Non-equilibrium simulations were then used to evaluate O2 dissolution, self-diffusion, and permeation in the PTFE/PA mixed phase. The results show that PA preferentially accumulates around Pt particles and forms locally structured PA-rich domains, whereas PTFE is mainly distributed on the carbon-support surface and outside the PA-rich domains. As the PTFE/PA composition changes from 2/38 to 33/7 wt%, the number of dissolved O2 molecules shows an overall increasing trend, whereas the O2 self-diffusion coefficient first increases and then decreases. Intermediate PTFE/PA compositions disrupt the compact PA-rich domains and enhance O2 mobility, whereas compositions with high PTFE and low PA contents produce more tortuous local transport pathways. Title: Effect of gamma ray and electron beam irradiation on LDPE-based active films containing α-tocopherol
Abstract: This study investigates the combined effect of α-tocopherol (Toc) incorporation and exposure to ionising radiation on the physicochemical and functional performance of low-density polyethylene (LDPE) films designed for sustainable food packaging applications. Title: Synthesis, characterization, electrical evaluation, and predictive modelling of g-C3N4–ZnO nanocomposites for memory and artificial synaptic devices

Title: Semantic drift-resistant learning for robust multimodal sentiment analysis with incomplete information
Abstract: With the rapid growth of multimodal user-generated content, multimodal sentiment analysis in real-world applications is increasingly challenged by missing modality information. Existing methods mainly focus on missing information reconstruction or representation completion, while paying less attention to the disruption of cross-modal semantic consistency caused by incomplete information, which leads to latent representation shifts and further induces semantic drift. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Semantic Drift-Resistant Learning framework (SDRL) from the perspective of semantic drift mitigation. Specifically, SDRL models the representation relationship between complete and incomplete states through semantic consistency constraints to restrict the semantic deviation caused by missing information. Meanwhile, a reliability-aware proxy compensation mechanism is introduced to generate proxy semantic representations from non-text modalities and dynamically adjust the contribution of textual and proxy representations, thereby reducing the interference of unreliable information during cross-modal representation learning. Furthermore, a hierarchical consistency optimization strategy is designed to constrain the propagation of semantic drift from multiple perspectives, including local representations, global structures, and task responses. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SDRL consistently outperforms existing methods under different missing rates and various missing modality patterns on the MOSI, MOSEI, and SIMS datasets. The results verify the effectiveness of the proposed framework in mitigating semantic drift and preserving semantic information in incomplete multimodal scenarios. Copyright © 2026. Title: Efficient pricing of derivatives under the HCIR model using an integrated Gaussian Kernel in an RBF-FD scheme

Abstract: This paper presents an efficient numerical framework for pricing options under the Heston–Cox–Ingersoll–Ross (HCIR) model. Authors: Shanmugam A.R.; Park K.S.
Title: Multi-criteria thermal–hydraulic performance analysis of channel aspect ratio in compact solar receivers using supercritical CO2
Abstract: Compact solar receivers employing mini-channel designs have emerged as an effective thermal management solution in concentrated solar power systems. Under high-temperature and high-pressure supercritical carbon dioxide (sCO2) operation, wall temperatures must remain within material limits. Hence, the geometry must be carefully selected to prevent hot spots while maintaining efficient thermal–hydraulic performance. This study numerically investigates the effects of the channel aspect ratio on the wall temperature, thermal resistance, entropy generation rate, and thermal–hydraulic performance of sCO2 in mini-channel solar receivers. Two practical design constraints are imposed: Design A (constant width and total flow area) and Design B (constant width and solid volume), with the channel parameters determined accordingly. Results show that increasing the channel aspect ratio reduces wall temperature, total entropy generation rate, and thermal resistance in both designs. However, these benefits are accompanied by increased hydraulic performance penalties, particularly in Design B, where the pumping power increases significantly. Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) analysis shows that the preferred aspect ratio range varies with design, with 5–7 being favorable for Design A and 8–10 for Design B, highlighting the strong influence of geometric constraints. The heat transfer behavior is influenced by the channel geometry and near-wall flow characteristics. At high aspect ratios, the formation of weaker counter-rotating vortices reduces cross-stream mixing, while increased near-wall shear produces higher local turbulent kinetic energy, which may contribute to the increase in the heat transfer coefficient. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Chai X.; Fang L.; Zhang Y.; Liu Y.
Title: Multi-scale mechanisms of starch retrogradation inhibition in red bean paste modulated by high-oleic peanut oil
Abstract: This study investigated how peanut oil types and contents modulate starch-lipid interactions and retard retrogradation in red bean paste. Four peanut oils: conventional (PO), refined high-oleic (HO), degummed cold-pressed high-oleic (RO), and non-degummed cold-pressed high-oleic (CO) were analyzed via RVA, TPA, LF-NMR, XRD, and FT-IR. TPA and XRD revealed that RO and CO effectively suppressed the relative crystallinity compared to polyunsaturated PO, thereby significantly retarding textural hardening with hardness reductions of 54.4% and 60.3%, respectively. FT-IR and RVA confirmed that low-steric-hindrance monounsaturated fatty acids in RO and CO formed thermodynamically stable V-type inclusion complexes, restricting amylose mobility and depressing peak viscosity. LF-NMR and oil holding capacity assessments demonstrated that native phospholipids in CO established a dense interfacial barrier, restricting water mobility and inhibiting amylopectin recrystallization. Furthermore, using RO as the model oil, macroscopic TPA and OHC assessments point out that a 50% oil addition optimally acts as a physical spacer to dilute the starch network. In contrast, a 70% addition exceeds the emulsification capacity, triggering macroscopic phase separation and free oil exudation. Conclusively, integrating high-oleic peanut oils at 50% synergistically enhances anti-retrogradation via molecular inclusion and interfacial thermodynamics. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Shen G.; Xie Y.; He F.; Yao X.; Xu Z.; Lu J.
Title: Controlling partial and deep hydrogenation of naphthalene over supported metal phosphides: kinetic and DFT insights into Ni2P/Al2O3 and MoP/Al2O3
Abstract: Selective hydrogenation of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons is vital for fuel upgrading and hydrogen-donor solvent synthesis, whereas precise regulation between partial and deep hydrogenation pathways remains a long-standing challenge. Herein, Al2O3-supported Ni2P and MoP catalysts with identical nominal loading were fabricated via a spatially confined phosphorization route and comparatively investigated for naphthalene hydrogenation. Under identical conditions (320 °C, 4 MPa H2), Ni2P /Al2O3 preferentially catalyzed deep hydrogenation: it delivered 92.8 % naphthalene conversion with 89.7 % selectivity toward decalin. By contrast, MoP/Al2O3 dominated partial saturation, affording 90.6 % naphthalene conversion and 94.9 % tetralin selectivity. Apparent kinetic measurements revealed close activation energies for initial naphthalene consumption over the two catalysts (61.16 and 65.36 kJ mol−1, reflecting similar activity for the first-ring hydrogenation. Nevertheless, the activation energy for subsequent tetralin hydrogenation differed markedly, reaching 91.59 kJ mol−1 on MoP/Al2O3 versus 66.44 kJ mol−1 on Ni2P/Al2O3. Consistently, DFT calculations confirmed similar energy barriers for naphthalene conversion to tetralin on Ni2P(0 0 1) and MoP(1 0 1), while MoP(1 0 1) possessed significantly elevated energy barriers for late-stage hydrogenation. Combined experimental and theoretical evidence identifies secondary hydrogenation of tetralin as the selectivity-determining step. This work offers clear mechanistic insights into tuning the formation of tetralin and decalin over transition metal phosphide catalysts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Yang X.; Wang L.; Yang T.; Zhang W.; Wang L.
Title: High-spatial-resolution characterization of hydroxide ion concentration in solutions: A novel strategy based on RGB color analysis
Abstract: In this work, a novel method for the quantification of hydroxide ion concentration (COH-) in aqueous solutions was developed based on RGB (color saturation) analysis, which operates on a principle fundamentally different from the Lambert–Beer law. A theoretical equation correlating the solution color saturation (S) and COH- was established as (lg(1-S)=m-nˑCOH-, m and n were constant), and the linear relationship between lg(1-S) and COH- was validated by experimental data. The quantification results exhibited RSD (COH-) 0.13% - 0.60% (n = 6), Er 1.22% - 3.34%, and LOD 0.11 μmolˑL−1. High-spatial-resolution distribution maps of COH- near the cathode surface were acquired in a non-invasive, in-situ dynamic measurement way. Under the experimental conditions, the width of the concentration polarization region (COH- 35.14 - 39.50 μmolˑL−1) was approximately 0.6 mm. In the region 1.4 - 2.2 mm away from the electrode surface, COH- decreased rapidly at a gradient of 21.31 μmolˑL−1ˑmm−1, and finally declined to the bulk concentration (<1.24 μmolˑL−1). © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Wen H.; Zhai C.; Xu H.; Xu J.; Sun Y.; Zheng Y.; Wang Y.; Tang Z.
Title: Evolution of pore and fracture structures in coal under mining stress paths: Insights from in-Situ LF-NMR
Abstract: Understanding the evolution of the pore-fracture structure of coal under mining stress is essential for coalbed methane development and the prevention and control of gas-related disasters. In this study, an in situ low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (LF-NMR) system was used to monitor real-time changes in the mechanical properties and pore-fracture structures of coal subjected to different mining stress paths. The effects of mining stress paths on the T 2 spectra, pore-size distributions and spatial evolution of the samples were analyzed. Their influences on pore heterogeneity and permeability contribution were further evaluated, and the relationship between mining stress paths and pore compressibility was established. The results showed that the peak stress and strain of the coal samples decreased in the order of no pillar mining (NM), protective seam mining (PCM) and protected seam mining (PLM). Under the NM and PCM paths, the coal underwent pore compression, microfracture initiation and macro fracture coalescence. These processes corresponded to an initial decrease followed by a recovery in the T 2 spectrum amplitude, as well as the reduction and subsequent interconnection of warm-colored regions in the NMR images. With increasing deviatoric stress, the proportion of seepage pores, mean pore size and permeability contribution first decreased and then increased, followed by a rapid increase after sample failure. In contrast, the fractal dimension of seepage pores showed the opposite trend, indicating that the complexity of the pore network decreased after sample fracture. The NM samples mainly exhibited shear failure, whereas the PCM samples gradually transformed from shear failure to tensile failure under a relatively high confining pressure unloading rate. Under the PLM path, early-stage pressure-relief expansion caused substantial changes in the internal pore structures of the samples. During subsequent deviatoric stress loading, however, the pore-structure characteristics changed relatively gradually, and the samples failed after undergoing only limited. Marked fluctuations in mean pore size and pore complexity occurred only after sample failure. The pore-compressibility results indicated that seepage pores in most samples were compressed during the initial loading stage and subsequently underwent continuous expansion, with abrupt changes occurring near failure. Among the three stress paths, the PCM path produced the most pronounced dilatancy effect. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Adhikari S.
Title: Symmetry breaking and emergent shear-normal coupling in two-point periodic lattices
Abstract: We determine the in-plane effective compliance of Y-type hexagonal lattices and identify the structural origin of shear-normal coupling. The lattice walls are modelled as Euler–Bernoulli beams with homogeneous material properties and cross-sections assigned consistently to symmetry-related members, and the effective compliance is obtained by strain–energy homogenization of the periodic unit cell under uniform macroscopic stress. The planar response is described by six independent compliances; the two shear-normal terms S13 and S23, which couple extensional and shear deformation, are the focus of this work. We show that these terms vanish if and only if the unit cell is invariant under a mirror aligned with the coordinate axes, and that this invariance requires two independent geometric ingredients: the two branches meeting at a junction must be images of one another under that mirror, a property we call branch balance, and the junctions of the repeating unit must all carry the same geometric data, a uniform decoration. Neither ingredient follows from periodicity. The closure identity of a hexagonal cell, whose boundary contains two stems and four branches, holds for every choice of branch projections and therefore constrains nothing, so a uniformly decorated lattice with unbalanced branches is admissible: it is the balanced honeycomb with successive rows slipped horizontally, it retains a single junction type, and it is generically coupled. The construction developed here instead assigns the two branch families to opposite sides at alternating junctions, giving a two-point basis, and for it we obtain closed-form expressions for all six compliances as functions of the dimensionless geometric parameters. The shear-normal compliances are then nonzero for all but a measure-zero set of geometries, vanishing only on isolated surfaces that include the symmetric one-point limit, which is recovered exactly. Because the basis size is a positive integer, two is the smallest basis supporting the alternating arrangement used here; this minimality refers to the arrangement and not to coupling in general, which the slipped lattice already reaches with a single junction type. Using the closed-form solution we map the magnitude and sign of S13 and S23 over the design space, give the loci on which each coefficient changes sign, and show that the coupling grows linearly with the geometric asymmetry near the symmetric limit, so that small departures from a symmetric cell produce first-order coupling. The four first-order sensitivities are obtained in closed form, and one of them vanishes on a curve of the geometry plane through the regular honeycomb, where S13 becomes second order in the angular asymmetry and first order in the length asymmetry alone. The results separate two roles in architected lattice design: the mirror content of the unit cell, set jointly by branch balance and by the decoration of the periodic basis, fixes which couplings are attainable, and the cell geometry then tunes their magnitude and sign. © 2026 The Author

Title: Microstructure–property relationships in nanomaterial-enhanced sustainable concrete incorporating lead–zinc tailings
Abstract: Introduction: Lead–zinc mining tailings (LZT) accumulation and concrete production impacts necessitate sustainable waste valorization. This study investigated nano-SiO₂ modification to improve LZT concrete performance and environmental safety. Methods: Mechanical properties, durability, heavy-metal leaching, hydration, pore structure, and interfacial transition zones (ITZ) were examined using SEM–EDS, XRD, FTIR, thermogravimetric analysis, and mercury intrusion porosimetry. Results: Nano-SiO₂ dosages of 0.5% and 1.0% optimized fresh-state and hardened performance, respectively. L30-N1.0 achieved compressive strengths of 56.8 MPa at 28 days and 64.9 MPa at 90 days, improving by 28.2% and 28.8% over L30. Pore volume decreased to 0.157 cm³ /g, with a critical pore diameter of 41.6 nm. Water absorption and sorptivity declined by 40.1% and 45.5%, while Pb and Zn release decreased by 94.6% and 93.1% relative to raw LZT. Conclusion: Nano-SiO₂ modification enhanced microstructural densification, mechanical performance, durability, and heavy-metal immobilization, supporting sustainable LZT utilization in concrete. © 2026

Authors: Guo L.; Zhang J.; Wang L.; Shi C.; Liu B.
Title: Study on the rheological model of waxy crude oil under various shear loading conditions
Abstract: Waxy crude oil, as an important petroleum resource, exhibits complex rheological characteristics at low temperatures. Accurately describing its shear loading response is critical for ensuring safe transportation of pipelines and predicting restart pressures. To overcome limitations of existing models in describing pre-yield viscoelasticity, yield point continuity, and the unification of various shear loading conditions, this paper establishes a full mechanical response rheological model applicable to various shear loading conditions based on structural dynamics theory. The model is built upon the Maxwell framework, where the shear modulus and effective viscosity are expressed as functions of an internal structural parameter λ , and the rate equation is used to describe the breakdown and recovery processes of the wax crystal network. The model is validated using rheological experimental data of waxy crude oil under various loading conditions, including oscillatory shear, constant shear rate, shear rate hysteresis loop, constant shear stress, and shear stress step tests. The results show that the proposed model achieves a mean of the average absolute deviations of 13.70% in oscillatory shear tests; 3.20% and 3.02% in constant shear rate and shear rate hysteresis loop tests, respectively; and 2.10% and 2.28% in constant shear stress and shear stress step tests, respectively. Compared with the Houska model and the Teng Houxing viscoelastic-thixotropic model, the proposed model demonstrates superior fitting performance across various loading conditions, overcoming limitations such as yield point discontinuity and solution difficulties. This work provides a theoretical foundation for the unified description of the rheological behavior of waxy crude oil during pipeline transportation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhang X.; Hu X.; Guo Y.; Li L.; Cao Y.; Li J.; Wu Q.; Wang Y.; Zhang P.
Title: A comprehensive review on the incremental synthesis characteristics and regulation mechanism of natural gas hydrates enhanced by porous skeleton structure: challenges, perspectives and future directions
Abstract: Natural gas has been widely regarded as a clean transitional fuel owing to its relatively low carbon intensity, high combustion efficiency and stable energy output. Hydrate-based natural gas storage and transportation has therefore attracted increasing attention as an emerging solid-state energy storage technology. However, the practical deployment remains limited by long hydrate induction times, slow formation kinetics and insufficient gas storage density. Porous skeleton systems, with tunable confinement environments and interfacial regulation capabilities, offer a promising route to intensify natural gas hydrate formation and improve storage performance. This review comprehensively summarizes the confinement effects and interfacial regulation mechanisms of porous skeleton materials during natural gas hydrate formation, with particular emphasis on their roles in promoting hydrate synthesis. The roles of key structural parameters, including pore size, specific surface area, pore volume, surface chemistry, pore topology and network connectivity, in governing hydrate nucleation, growth kinetics, and gas-storage capacity are discussed in detail. The underlying microscopic mechanisms are further examined, including gas enrichment, interfacial water restructuring, heterogeneous nucleation, mass and heat transfer, and pore-scale hydrate growth. On this basis, the kinetic laws and regulatory mechanisms of porous skeleton-enhanced hydrate formation are clarified. Finally, the deficiencies and future development directions for hydrate-based natural gas storage and transportation technology were identified. Future research should focus on artificial intelligence-assisted material design, molecular- and interfacial-scale mechanistic studies, and multiphysics coupling models. These advances will provide a scientific foundation for the rational design of porous skeleton systems and the development of hydrate-based natural gas storage technology. Copyright © 2026. Authors: Zhao Y.; Zhang P.; Xiao M.; Zeng Z.; Luo C.; Wen J.; Ding W.; Zeng F.
Title: FS-MLGB: Multi-level granular-ball representation using label distribution for multi-label feature selection
Abstract: Multi-label feature selection is important for high-dimensional multi-label data, but existing methods often rely on coarse logical labels and insufficiently exploit structural information at different granularity levels. This paper proposes a label-distribution-guided multi-level granular-ball feature selection method. Logical labels are first transformed into label distributions to provide richer supervision. Multiple purity thresholds are then used to construct level-specific granular-ball spaces, where ball centers and averaged label distributions form compact ball-level representations. Feature weight matrices for different granularities are learned, and they are connected with the global feature weight matrix through consistency constraints. At the same time, label correlation is incorporated through graph Laplacian regularization. In this way, label-distribution supervision, multi-level granular structures, and label correlation are jointly exploited. Experiments on 12 benchmark datasets show that the proposed method achieves competitive performance compared with eight representative methods. A case study on fMRI data of functional dyspepsia further demonstrates its potential for identifying functional connectivity patterns related to multidimensional acupuncture responses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Yu Y.; Huang S.; Wang X.; Guan Q.; Ullah S.; Wang X.; Wang T.; Ye R.
Title: Dual-function materials for integrated CO2 capture and hydrogenation: Materials design, reaction mechanisms and industrial prospects
Abstract: Integrated CO2 capture and utilization (ICCU) couples CO2 separation with catalytic conversion, avoiding the intermediate desorption, purification, and compression steps required in conventional capture-and-conversion processes. This review examines dual-function materials composed of Ca-, Na-, Mg-, or K-based sorbents and catalytic phases such as Ni, Ru, and Cu. The discussion links sorbent chemistry, interfacial structure, and hydrogen transfer to the formation of CH4, CH3OH, CO, and other carbon-containing products. Particular attention is given to carbonate accessibility, sorbent–catalyst proximity, cyclic stability, and performance under realistic gas feeds. Representative systems are compared using their operating conditions, capture capacity, product yield, carbon utilization, selectivity, and cyclic retention. Remaining barriers include sintering, alkali migration, impurity poisoning, particle attrition, hydrogen cost, and the limited availability of pilot-scale data. Reactor configuration and techno-economic requirements are also discussed in relation to further scale-up. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
