Authors: Wu Y.; Yu L.; Tang Z.; Cao R.; Qian Y.; Lu X.
Title: Modulating SAF reactivity with addition of iso-alkane, cycloalkane, and aromatics
Abstract: Sustainable Aviation Fuels (SAFs) are recognized as the primary pathway for decarbonizing the aviation sector, yet their higher reactivity relative to conventional kerosene poses challenges for aeroengine compatibility. To enable high-ratio substitution, effective SAF reactivity modulation is essential. This study proposes a strategic approach by introducing renewable low-reactivity components into a SAF base fuel (HEFA-SPK). To this end, the ignition delay times (IDTs) of HEFA-SPK, blended with iso -octane, decalin, and propylbenzene at 50 % by volume, were measured in a rapid compression machine (RCM) at pressures 10–20 bar and temperatures 650–980 K. Results show that propylbenzene exhibits the strongest ignition suppression, followed by iso -octane and decalin. However, a more significant finding lies in their distinct temperature-dependent behaviors. Decalin manifests the strongest negative temperature coefficient (NTC) magnitude and the highest onset temperature. Kinetic analysis reveals that decalin acts as a low-temperature reaction driver by establishing a well-developed reaction network and a robust radical pool during first-stage ignition, whereas iso -octane and propylbenzene undergo limited conversion, contributing minimally to radical generation. This work establishes a predictive framework for modulating SAF reactivity and further supports the 100 % SAF utilization in aeroengines. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Xu K.; Yang H.; Zhang L.; Liu F.; Ye Y.; Song Q.; Wang X.
Title: Tailoring Ba geometry on NiBaY ternary metal oxides to boost NO decomposition in the presence of oxygen
Abstract: NO decomposition via high-temperature catalysis is a well-established and promising approach for NOx abatement, yet its efficacy is compromised by the inhibitory effect of oxygen present in fuel combustion. By adjusting the compositional ratios of Ni, Ba, and Y as well as the calcination temperature, various Ba-containing structural geometries can be created on Y2O3, namely BaNiO3, Ni-BaO, and highly dispersed NiBa. Compared to their BaNiO3 and Ni-BaO counterparts, catalysts featuring highly dispersed NiBa demonstrate superior NO decomposition performance under oxygen-containing conditions. At identical heat-treatment temperature, the obtained NiBa catalysts possess more structural defects than the BaNiO3 and Ni-BaO configurations, manifesting as larger specific surface areas and enriched surface oxygen species. The enhanced redox capability and stronger reactant adsorption of the NiBa catalysts contribute significantly to its improved reaction activity. A nitrate-mediated pathway is proposed to elucidate the high activity of NO decomposition over the NiBa-Y2O3 catalyst, based on combined in situ transmission infrared experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The mutual reaction between NO molecules or their reaction with surface oxygen generates N atoms, NO2⁻ and NO3⁻, with O2 molecules serving as an abundant oxygen source. The high-temperature dissociation of NO3⁻ gives rise to O2 and NO⁻, followed by a direct reaction between NO⁻ and the residual N atom to yield N2. However, the oxygen-containing condition preferentially leads to N2O formation to generate N2. This work provides guidance for developing high-performance catalysts with oxygen resistance for NO decomposition, and advances the fundamental comprehension of the underlying reaction mechanism. Authors: Zhao J.; Cao X.; Sun G.; Xie Y.; Teng B.; Zhang W.; Wang S.; He P.
Title: Study on ZnCrOx/H-Beta bifunctional catalyst for butane synthesis from syngas
Abstract: Butane is an important chemical with applications as a clean fuel and solvent. The direct conversion of syngas to butane offers a promising route to the production of high-value chemicals. However, simultaneously achieving high CO conversion and butane selectivity remains a major challenge in heterogeneous catalysis. Herein, we successfully constructed a ZnCrOx/H-Beta bifunctional catalytic system for butane from syngas. By tuning the Zn/Cr ratio in the metal oxide, the surface structure and oxygen vacancy concentration were optimized. Comprehensive characterization results reveal that a Zn/Cr ratio of 2:1 leads to optimal ZnO surface enrichment and the formation of abundant oxygen vacancies (50.1%), which efficiently promote the conversion of syngas into methanol intermediates. Subsequently, these intermediates are selectively converted to butane over the acid sites of H-Beta zeolite via hydrogenation, oligomerization, and hydrogen transfer reactions. Under optimal reaction conditions, the ZnCrOx/H-Beta catalyst achieves a high butane selectivity of 53.2% with a CO conversion of 27.0%. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Effects of added pyrite on apparent kinetic responses and structural evolution during pyrolysis of clarain and durain from tar-rich coal
Abstract: This study investigated how added pyrite affects the stage-dependent pyrolysis behavior and structural evolution of clarain (XJH-L) and durain (XJH-A) from the No. 2–2 coal seam of the Xiaojihan minefield in the northern Shaanxi Jurassic coalfield, China. Samples containing 0, 3, 6, and 9 wt% added pyrite on a dry-coal basis were characterized by TG–DTG analysis, stage-resolved Doyle fitting at a fixed heating rate of 10 ℃ min−1, temperature-resolved in situ FTIR and Raman spectroscopy, and low-temperature N2 adsorption. XJH-L contained more vitrinite and had higher volatile matter and tar yields than XJH-A. Pyrite addition produced a secondary DTG feature near 550 ℃ in both lithotypes, which was more pronounced in XJH-A. Under the fixed heating program, the Doyle-fitted apparent activation-energy values decreased in S2 and S3. At 6 wt% pyrite, the fitted S3 values decreased from 45.69 to 38.07 kJ mol−1 for XJH-L and from 47.31 to 41.89 kJ mol−1 for XJH-A, while the corresponding values at 9 wt% were similar. FTIR analysis showed greater depletion of O–H, aliphatic C–H, C=O, and C–O structures after pyrite addition, with stronger aliphatic C–H and C=O responses in XJH-A. Aromatic-framework rearrangement began at lower temperatures and extended over a broader interval in XJH-L, whereas the XJH-A response was concentrated at 400–500 ℃. Differences in the measured pore response among pyrite loadings became most evident at 500–600 ℃. Overall, clarain responded earlier and over a broader temperature interval, whereas durain responded mainly at higher temperatures. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: One-step DME synthesis from CO2/H2: Promoter effects, methanol synthesis reversibility, oxygen vacancies and catalyst deactivation
Abstract: One-step dimethyl ether (DME) synthesis from CO2/H2 was investigated using physical mixtures of Hf-promoted CuZnO catalysts and FER. Methanol synthesis, the first step of DME production, was also studied using the same Cu-based catalysts. The catalysts were characterized by XRD with Rietveld refinement, XRF, specific area analysis, CO2-TPD, NH3-TPD, DRIFTS, N2O-RFC, and H2O dissociation measurements to evaluate oxygen vacancies. DFT calculations and thermodynamic analyses were also performed. Catalytic tests for methanol and DME synthesis under different reaction conditions, together with TG analysis, were conducted to investigate catalyst deactivation. Hf promotion significantly enhances catalytic performance by increasing both specific area and oxygen vacancy concentration through the substitution of Zn2⁺ by Hf4⁺ in the ZnO lattice. Consequently, methanol and DME yields increase up to an optimum Hf loading of 4 at.%, while the metallic Cu surface area remains essentially unchanged for Hf contents below 7 at.%. DFT calculations show that Hf substitution favors the spontaneous formation of oxygen vacancies in defective ZnO nanoparticles and on ZnO crystal surfaces. At higher Hf loadings, HfO2 formation blocks oxygen vacancies, active sites, and pores, leading to lower DME yield. Methanol synthesis reversibility under reaction conditions plays a decisive role in catalytic performance, favouring methanol and DME formation while suppressing CO. The proximity between methanol synthesis and dehydration sites enhances this effect. Furthermore, the acidity of the dehydration catalyst is an important factor controlling the DME formation rate. Catalyst deactivation is mainly attributed to H2O-promoted Cu sintering. Although CO is not an intermediate in methanol or DME synthesis, at high residence times CO produced by the reverse water–gas shift reaction can be re-adsorbed and hydrogenated to methanol and DME, allowing the system to approach thermodynamic equilibrium. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Zhang W.; Yang G.; Zhou Y.; Li W.; Wang R.; Wang P.; Ma C.; Li X.; Xiao X.
Title: MOF-derived CuZn/NaY@C catalysts based on zeolite induced growth: construction of multi-defect centers in ethynylation of formaldehyde for 1,4-butynediol synthesis
Abstract: Cu-based catalysts have attracted significant attention in the synthesis of highly valuable 1,4-butynediol via the coupling reaction between acetylene and formaldehyde, yet the development of highly stable catalysts remains a challenge. In this study, a novel carbon-zeolite hybrid-supported copper-based catalyst (CuZn/NaY@C) was successfully synthesized by a zeolite-induced one-pot homogeneous self-assembly method. By optimizing a series of preparation conditions, 5Cu5Zn/NaY@C-400 achieved a high yield of 86% and excellent selectivity of 96% for 1,4-butynediol (BYD). Furthermore, the catalyst maintained a yield of 73% and a selectivity of 90% after 100 h of continuous operation, with stability exceeding that of commercial catalysts. The apparent activation energy of 5Cu5Zn/NaY@C-400 is 27.5 kJ/mol equivalent to 28.6 kJ/mol of commercial catalysts, indicating its comparable reaction efficiency. Structural analysis of the catalyst, characterized by various techniques, shows that abundant carbon defects and oxygen vacancies in 5Cu5Zn/NaY@C-400 indirectly enhance C2H2 adsorption and promote the formation of active Cu2C2 intermediates. And the appropriate amount of acidic sites in the catalyst facilitates formaldehyde activation. Moreover, highly dispersed Cu2+ located in the supercages of the NaY zeolite and the strong Cu-Zn interaction formed at the CuO-ZnO interface effectively stabilize Cu2C2 during the reaction. This study provides novel strategies for the rational design of high-performance Cu-based catalysts applied in ethynylation of formaldehyde for 1,4-butynediol synthesis. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wang J.; Guan M.; Li X.; Cheng Z.; Jin H.; Guo L.
Title: Organosulfur extraction from coal in supercritical CO2-cosolvent systems: effects of molecular structure and cosolvent regulation
Abstract: Coal desulfurization using supercritical CO2 (SC-CO2)-cosolvent systems is a promising approach for clean coal utilization. However, the molecular-level mechanisms governing organosulfur extraction remain insufficiently understood. In this work, molecular dynamics simulations were performed to investigate the desorption and extraction behaviors of representative organosulfur compounds under SC-CO2 in the presence of different cosolvents. The roles of molecular structure, solvent environment, and interfacial effects were systematically examined in terms of extraction dynamics, intermolecular interactions, and spatial distribution characteristics. The results indicate that the extraction behavior of organosulfur compounds is strongly dependent on molecular structure. The extraction efficiency follows the order ethanethiol > thiophene > benzothiophene > dibenzothiophene, suggesting that increasing aromaticity and molecular conjugation enhances adsorption strength on the coal surface and hinders desorption. Among the investigated systems, SC-CO2-toluene exhibits superior performance for aromatic sulfur compounds. This enhancement is attributed to the preferential interfacial accumulation of toluene, which weakens sulfur-surface interactions and facilitates migration into the fluid phase. In mixed sulfur systems, pronounced composition-dependent competitive effects are observed. Thiophene is completely removed across all compositions, whereas dibenzothiophene exhibits limited desorption only at low thiophene fractions. Overall, the extraction behavior of the organosulfur compounds in SC-CO2-cosolvent systems is jointly influenced by molecular structure and cosolvent-induced interfacial regulation. These findings provide molecular-level insights for rational cosolvent screening and design in SC-CO2-assisted coal desulfurization. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Guo Y.; Huang X.; Bai Z.; Lu H.; Lin Y.; Wang F.
Title: Carbon nanotubes serving as fixed and flowable beds for enhanced methane storage in hydrates
Abstract: Achieving the rapid formation of methane hydrates together with high density is critical to utilize this hydrate-based energy storage technology. Herein, CNTs were adopted as the media for methane hydrate formation, which were designed as fixed or flowable beds by regulating the mass ratio between CNTs and reaction solution. The mobility of the reaction solution in the beds was confirmed as the most critical factor affecting the hydrate formation process. For flowable bed containing DI water, even though the initial hydrate growth rate was lower than that of fixed bed (R30 of 0.53 ± 0.16 vs 1.60 ± 0.19 v/v·min−1 for CNTs-2) due to fewer hydrate nucleation sites, the higher mobility of reaction solution resulted in much higher water-to-hydrate conversion (methane storage capacity of 125.2 ± 4.0 vs 83.3 ± 4.5 v/v for CNTs-2). When Leucine was coupled, the flowable bed with high mobility of reaction solution exhibited extremely efficient enhancement of hydrate formation kinetics, which achieved the synergistic effects of Leucine and CNTs beds, combining the rapid hydrate formation (t90 of 16.3 ± 0.63 min and methane storage capacity of 142.9 ± 3.4 v/v for CNTs-2) with high apparent density. Moreover, CNTs-2 bed with looser network structure and higher mobility of reaction solution performed much better than CNTs-1 bed, further verifying the significant role of the mobility of the reaction solution in achieving high-efficiency methane hydrate formation. Authors: Bao J.; Wang R.; Wang H.; Lei J.; Zhu J.; Shi C.
Title: Exploring mixture formation mechanisms and mitigating thermal inhomogeneity in a zero-carbon ammonia-hydrogen rotary engine by combined injection strategies
Abstract: Combined injection technology, through precise control of the mixture composition, can fully leverage the performance advantages of dual-fuel engines. Based on this principle, the present study investigates the impact of combined injection on combustion behavior from the perspective of mixture formation, while maintaining constant fuel mass in the cylinder prior to ignition. The results show that as the proportion of hydrogen in the direct-injected fuel increases, the high-temperature region at the flame front and the distribution of the equivalence ratio initially converge and then diverge. During this process, the second peak of the HRR curve gradually weakens, while the first peak progressively strengthens. Compared to single-fuel DI, combined injection achieves a more stable stratified combustion effect. Relative to HDI, combined injection demonstrates a significant advantage in effectively controlling combustion dead zones, with ISNH3 reduced by an order of magnitude compared to the HDI mode. Moreover, due to the more dispersed combustion hotspots in combined injection, N2O emissions are effectively controlled. However, the relatively mild combustion process in combined injection leads to an increase in the formation of thermal NOx. Additionally, the combined injection mode exhibits superior thermal stability and robustness, providing a safeguard for improved thermal efficiency while effectively mitigating the risk of knocking. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Lu X.; Li J.; Gao P.; Zong K.; Duan K.; Zhang C.; Zhu J.; Wang W.; Gao E.; Wu Z.; Yao S.; Wu N.
Title: Engineering Mn-Co oxide catalysts for energy-efficient plasma catalysis: A shift from acid-site to electron-dominated mechanisms in propane oxidation
Abstract: The development of low-temperature, energy-efficient technologies for hydrocarbon abatement is crucial for sustainable fuel processing and emission control. While non-thermal plasma (NTP) offers a promising alternative to conventional high-temperature thermal catalysis, the rational design of catalysts for such hybrid systems remains ambiguous. Here, we demonstrate a critical mechanistic shift in propane oxidation over a series of metal–organic framework (MOF)-derived MnCoOx catalysts with tailored properties. Under thermal conditions, the catalytic activity ( T 90) is strongly influenced by strong acid sites, though redox properties also play a complementary role, following the order: MnCoOx-BTC (benzene-1,3,5-tricarboxylic acid = BTC, 340 °C) > MnCoOx-MIM (2-methylimidazole = MIM, 305 °C) > MnCoOx-IDC (imidazole-4,5-dicarboxylic acid = IDC, 298 °C). Remarkably, the relative performance of MnCoOx-MIM and MnCoOx-BTC is completely inverted under plasma-driven conditions (∼227 J/L), with propane conversion ranking as MnCoOx-MIM (69 %) < MnCoOx-BTC (80 %) < MnCoOx-IDC (90 %). This striking reversal, elucidated by multi-technique characterization and operando spectroscopy, underscores a fundamental change in the rate-determining step: from C-H cleavage at acid sites to electron-transfer dynamics governed by electronic band structure. The optimal MnCoOx-IDC catalyst, featuring the narrowest band gap, superior charge-transfer kinetics and the highest oxygen vacancy concentration, achieves outstanding ambient-temperature propane conversion and energy efficiency (2.89 g/kWh). Our findings establish that effective plasma catalyst design should prioritize electronic conductivity over traditional acid-site tuning. This work provides a strategic blueprint for developing advanced, energy-saving hybrid systems for hydrocarbon oxidation, with direct implications for cleaner fuel technologies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Li Z.; Wu X.; Wang X.; Wang Y.; Tang Y.
Title: A multifunctional naphthalimide-based fluorescent probe for visual detection, environmental monitoring, and biosensing of formaldehyde
Abstract: Due to the role of formaldehyde (FA) in environmental pollutants and as an important intracellular signaling molecule, there is a pressing need to come up with highly sensitive and selective detection methods that can be applied to diverse fields. In this case, we have rationally developed and synthesized a new naphthalimide fluorescent probe Np-FA that is designed and customized to multi-scenario FA sensing. Probe Np-FA has good selectivity, very sensitive sensing capability and responds quickly (less than 10 s). The suggested sensing mechanism was verified through density functional theory (DFT) calculations and high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) analysis. Leveraging its impressive performance, probe Np-FA was effectively made into portable test strips and fluorescent sensing films to visually detect gaseous FA and aqueous FA, respectively. Moreover, Np-FA was also used successfully to measure trace FA in actual water samples. The probe has great biocompatibility and it can be used in real time fluorescence imaging of both endogenous and exogenous FA within living cells. It is important to note that Np-FA proved useful to monitor dynamic changes in FA concentrations in a drug-induced model of hepatotoxicity and therefore, it has a good potential to investigate the functions of FA in physiological and pathological states. The probe created in this work is highly versatile and trustworthy, and its application prospects are very promising, starting with environmental surveillance, and ending with sophisticated biological systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Bai K.; Shen J.; Li W.; Feng S.; Li C.; Li J.; Cheng S.; Wang C.
Title: Interpretable machine learning prediction of coalbed methane content and depth-dependent predictive contributions in shallow and medium-deep reservoirs: A case study of the Qinshui Basin
Abstract: Accurate prediction of coalbed methane (CBM) content is essential for gas exploration but remains challenging because CBM content reflects nonlinear and interacting geological controls. This study initially compiled 1072 core samples from 114 unique wells in the southern Qinshui Basin; after geological quality control and outlier treatment, 945 samples from 111 wells were retained for model development and evaluation. Samples were classified into shallow coal reservoirs (SCR, 351.3–997.4 m) and medium-deep coal reservoirs (MDCR, 1000.2–1506.9 m). K-nearest neighbors (KNN) was adopted for missing-value imputation. ReliefF was selected for both reservoir groups, retaining 12 continuous variables for SCR and 10 for MDCR. Among eight supervised-learning models, CatBoost achieved the highest mean validation-fold R2 values in 10-fold cross-validation within the model-development set, reaching 0.85 for SCR and 0.81 for MDCR. Independent blind-well validation yielded R2 values of 0.86 and 0.84, respectively. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was used to characterize model-specific predictive contributions. In SCR, maximum vitrinite reflectance ( R o,max), hydrogen content on a dry ash-free basis ( H daf), roof uniaxial compressive strength (UCSroof), and burial depth had the largest mean absolute SHAP values. In MDCR, R o,max, dry-basis ash yield ( A d), coal-seam thickness, and coal-body structure ranked highest. Furthermore, SHAP analysis characterized the predictive contributions and dependence patterns of the input parameters in the fitted CBM-content models, which may assist researchers and practitioners in identifying key predictive factors for data-informed reservoir evaluation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhang L.; Wang Z.; Li G.; Li J.; Zhang X.; Wang Y.; Yin B.; Zhou T.; Wang L.
Title: Comparative effects of acidification and Fenton oxidation on aromatic microstructures in coals of different ranks: Implications for coalbed methane reservoir modification
Abstract: Fenton oxidation is an advanced oxidation process that can modify coal organic structures under acidic conditions. To distinguish the effects of hydroxyl radical oxidation from acidification at the same pH, three coals of different ranks, long-flame coal, coking coal, and anthracite, were selected. A blank control group, an acid control group at the same pH, and a Fenton treatment group were designed. The central analysis was based on HRTEM image processing and quantification. Using a unified image-processing protocol, 27 HRTEM images were systematically analyzed both qualitatively and quantitatively to characterize the length, orientation, tortuosity, and stacking degree of aromatic lattice fringes. XRD and FTIR were further used to evaluate microcrystalline structural parameters and functional groups. The results show clear coal-rank-dependent responses to Fenton treatment. In low- and medium-rank coals, Fenton treatment weakened highly distorted and weakly connected structures, promoting local convergence, preferred orientation, and enhanced stacking of residual aromatic fragments. In contrast, anthracite showed disturbance, bending, and disaggregation of highly condensed aromatic layers, resulting in more dispersed fringe orientation, fewer long fringes, higher tortuosity, and weaker multilayer stacking. XRD and FTIR results further indicate local structural rearrangement and stacking enhancement in low- and medium-rank coals, but aromatic layer disruption and increased carbonyl contribution in anthracite. Overall, Fenton modification can be described as acid-induced loosening, radical oxidation, and coal-rank-controlled structural redistribution. This study provides nanoscale structural evidence for understanding Fenton-induced modification of coal organic matter. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: FactSage study on phase evolution and slagging of high-phosphorus and high-alkali traditional Chinese medicine residues
Abstract: To address the slagging propensity and the unclear safe operating window of high-phosphorus and high-alkali traditional Chinese medicine residues (TCMRs) during gasification, the primary phase evolution, melting behavior, and slagging risk of Shenqi Jiangtang Granules Residues (SJGR) and Schisandra Chinensis Residues (SCR) were investigated using FactSage 8.3, combined with multi-scale experimental validations (TG/DTG, FTIR, Raman, SEM, and AFT). Pseudo-ternary liquidus projections, including single-oxide sections and a basic–amphoteric–acidic (B–Am–Ac) grouping, revealed distinct regulatory mechanisms. Specifically, single-variable sensitivity analysis shows that Na2O strongly depolymerizes the network, K2O stabilizes [AlO4]⁻ tetrahedra through charge compensation, and MgO forms discrete high-melting-point silicate (M2S). Based on these mechanisms, a thermodynamic buffering index (TBI) ranked as K2O > MgO > Na2O. P/Si substitution and the CaO/P2O5 ratio jointly control phosphate crystallization. SJGR (CaO/P2O5 = 1.28) stabilizes in the KAS4 aluminosilicate region, while SCR (1.68) shifts to the tricalcium phosphate (C3P) region. Thermodynamic calculations are corroborated by multiscale experiments, including TG/DTG showing no mass loss above 600 °C, FTIR/Raman indicating network reconstruction, and SEM revealing dense adhesion versus porous foaming. These results identify 1000 °C as the engineering operating lower limit rather than a safety upper limit. The thermodynamically predicted safe operating windows are 640–733 °C for SJGR and 710–720 °C for SCR. These windows offer practical temperature boundaries, and targeted engineering control measures are proposed. This study provides a quantitative thermodynamic basis for safe operation and temperature optimization of steam gasification units using high-phosphorus, high-alkali TCMRs. Copyright © 2026. Authors: Wang X.; Lei Y.; Liu J.; Qiu T.
Title: Flow field characteristics and spatiotemporal NOx distribution from a high-pressure nitrogen jet impinging on a hydrogen premixed flame
Abstract: During hydrogen combustion in direct-injection hydrogen internal combustion engines (HICE), the impingement of a high-pressure gas jet exerts a significant impact on both flame evolution and NOx formation. Based on a constant-volume vessel (CVV) test rig, this study experimentally and numerically investigates the interaction between a hydrogen-air premixed flame and a high-pressure nitrogen jet to isolate the physical impact of the jet on the premixed flame. Results show that the jet enhances local flame-front propagation velocity (from 5.5 m/s to 45 m/s), and reduces thermal NOx via convective cooling (maximum temperature from ∼ 3200 K to ∼ 1850 K) and dilution (flame front from ∼ 1850 K to ∼ 1500 K), shifting combustion from premixed laminar to diluted turbulent mode. Because the chemical fields cannot be experimentally verified, the NOx-related quantities are treated as indicative and the discussion emphasizes qualitative trends. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Bak J.
Title: Novel guar gum agglomeration using gum arabic-based orange essential oil emulsion binder: Effect on powder, tribo-rheological, and anti-inflammatory properties
Abstract: This study introduced a fluidized-bed agglomeration approach using gum arabic (GA)-based orange essential oil emulsion as binder, and investigated its effects on the powder, tribo-rheological, and anti-inflammatory properties of guar gum (GG). Emulsion-based agglomeration significantly increased the particle size of the GG powder, and improved its flowability by reducing particle cohesiveness and increasing porosity. Although the use of emulsion binders resulted in higher span indices than the native GG powder, all emulsion-agglomerated powders exhibited a more uniform particle size distribution than the water-agglomerated control. Moreover, all emulsion-based agglomerated samples showed lower apparent viscosity and viscoelastic moduli than the control, and these parameters decreased with increasing binder concentration. Notably, the sample prepared with 12% GA-based emulsion binder exhibited significantly reduced rheological properties than the non-agglomerated counterpart. FTIR analysis suggested that these changes were associated with altered intermolecular interactions. Moreover, increasing the binder concentration led to a higher temperature sensitivity of the apparent viscosity. Although no significant difference in maximum friction coefficient was observed among samples, all emulsion-agglomerated specimens exhibited a shorter boundary lubrication regime than the non-agglomerated GG and control counterparts. Compared with the agglomeration process using GA binder, the emulsion-based agglomeration successfully imparted anti-inflammatory activity, as evidenced by reduced interleukin-6 and tumor necrosis factor-α production in lipopolysaccharide-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages, without inducing cytotoxicity. Overall, these findings demonstrate that emulsion-based fluidized-bed agglomeration may be an effective strategy to simultaneously modulate the physical properties, tribo-rheological behavior, and bioactive performance of GG, providing a versatile platform for the development of multifunctional food ingredients. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Dai W.; Chen Z.; Li B.; Fang B.; Ran R.
Title: Graph-embedded discriminative SPD autoencoder for image set classification
Abstract: As a significant class of Riemannian manifolds, Symmetric Positive Definite (SPD) manifolds have attracted widespread attention in recent years across fields such as image set classification and brain–computer interfaces. However, existing deep learning methods based on SPD manifolds often neglect the intrinsic local geometric structures of the data, have limited discriminative power, and the information of the extracted features is insufficient or inaccurate. To address these issues, this paper proposes a graph-embedded discriminative SPD autoencoder. This method achieves manifold-aware dimensionality reduction through a bilinear mapping (BiMap) layer and enhances nonlinear representational capacity via a rectified eigenvalue (ReEig) layer. Within an encoder–decoder architecture, a joint optimization model is introduced that leverages graph embedding to preserve local neighborhood structures while incorporating a label-aware class-center contrastive loss to further enhance feature discriminability. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method yields highly competitive performance across various evaluation metrics. Title: Experimental investigation of emissions and machine learning–based prediction of exhaust temperature and heat rate in a hydrogen-enriched heavy-duty internal combustion engine
Abstract: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) and hydrogen enrichment are promising approaches for improving the performance and environmental sustainability of compressed natural gas (CNG) engines. This study experimentally investigates the combined effects of hydrogen fraction, EGR ratio, spark timing, engine load, and engine speed on the exhaust characteristics and emissions of a stoichiometric hydrogen-enriched compressed natural gas (HCNG) engine. Tests were performed using hydrogen fractions of 0–20 %, EGR ratios of 0–4.5 %, spark timings of 8°–59 oCA bTDC, engine loads of 25 %, 50 %, and 75 %, and engine speeds of 900, 1200, and 1500 rpm. The experimental results show that hydrogen enrichment enhances combustion, resulting in higher exhaust temperature and exhaust heat rate. At 20 % hydrogen and 18 °CA bTDC, the maximum exhaust temperature and exhaust heat rate increased by 3.69 % and 15.27 % respectively compared with CNG operation. In contrast, increasing the EGR ratio to 4.5 % reduced the peak exhaust temperature by 1.18 % and the exhaust heat rate by 3.68 % because of charge dilution and lower combustion temperatures. Hydrogen enrichment also reduced CO, CO2, and THC emissions by promoting more complete combustion, while EGR effectively suppressed NOx formation through a decrease in peak flame temperature. To complement the experiments, five machine learning models—Interaction Linear (IL), Medium Tree (MT), Medium Gaussian Support Vector Machine (MGSVM), Bagged Tree (BT), and Exponential Gaussian Process Regression (EGPR)—were developed to predict exhaust temperature and exhaust heat rate using different input combinations and testing data ratios. Model performance was assessed using the coefficient of determination (R2), root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and training time. Among all models, EGPR demonstrated the highest prediction accuracy, achieving RMSE values of 0.7874 for exhaust temperature and 0.3394 for exhaust heat rate with a 20 % test dataset. The developed predictive model provides an efficient framework for estimating HCNG engine exhaust characteristics and can support future engine calibration, intelligent control strategies, and the design of waste-heat recovery and hydrogen-production systems. These findings contribute valuable experimental data and predictive capabilities for improving the efficiency and environmental performance of HCNG engines. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Molecular architecture and microporous structure of low mature lacustrine kerogen: A multi-parameter modeling of the Triassic Yanchang Formation, Ordos Basin
Abstract: Reliable molecular models of kerogen provide the structural basis for molecular-scale simulations of hydrocarbon generation, adsorption, and in-situ conversion. However, most existing kerogen models are primarily constrained by elemental composition and spectroscopic characterization, while structural validation is generally limited to density and 13C NMR agreement, making it difficult to evaluate whether the model realistically reproduces the microcrystalline organization of natural kerogen. In addition, the molecular architecture of low-maturity lacustrine kerogen from the Chang 7 Member, a representative shale oil source rock in the Ordos Basin, remains insufficiently constrained. In this study, kerogen from the Chang 7 Member was systematically characterized using elemental analysis, 13C NMR, XPS, FTIR, and XRD to construct representative two-dimensional and three-dimensional molecular models. Unlike conventional workflows, an “ XRD-assisted structural validation strategy ” was further established by directly comparing the calculated XRD pattern of the molecular model with the experimentally measured diffraction profile after eliminating mineral interference. This approach enables simultaneous validation of local chemical environments and medium-range structural ordering, including aromatic layer stacking and carbon microcrystalline organization. The resulting molecular model reproduces the experimental elemental composition, 13C NMR parameters, density, pore characteristics, radial distribution functions, and characteristic XRD diffraction features with high accuracy. Compared with previously reported Chang 7 kerogen models, the present model achieves closer agreement with multiple experimental constraints, including elemental ratios, carbon structural parameters, heteroatom distributions, and microcrystalline structural features, demonstrating improved accuracy and geological representativeness. Structural analysis further reveals that the Chang 7 kerogen is dominated by short-branched aliphatic chains, small aromatic clusters, sulfur-rich heteroatom functionalities, and micropore-dominated nanostructures, representing the characteristic molecular architecture of low-maturity lacustrine shale kerogen. The proposed XRD-assisted validation framework provides a more comprehensive strategy for evaluating kerogen molecular models and establishes a reliable molecular basis for future investigations of hydrocarbon generation, adsorption behavior, and in-situ conversion of lacustrine shale systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Flexible threshold multi-client secure aggregation for inner product in cloud-assisted IoV
Abstract: The cloud-assisted Internet of Vehicles (IoV) enables vehicles to outsource computation-intensive tasks to remote cloud servers, while the introduction of untrusted cloud servers brings security and privacy concerns. Although various encryption schemes have been proposed to protect data confidentiality, they do not support selective computation over encrypted data. Multi-client functional encryption (MCFE) is a promising technique for computing functions over encrypted data. Unfortunately, most of the existing MCFE schemes cannot support client dropout or flexible threshold selection, which are essential for practical IoV deployments. In this paper, we design a flexible threshold multi-client functional encryption for inner product (FTMCFE-IP) to enable secure aggregation in cloud-assisted IoV, where multiple clients generate ciphertexts independently without any interaction. In the encryption phase, clients are able to choose a threshold flexibly without reinitializing the system. Every ciphertext is related with a specific label, which resists ”mix-and-match” attacks. The decryption can be performed correctly when the number of online clients satisfies the threshold. An aggregator can aggregate ciphertexts and output the inner product of the vectors associated with his/her functional key and the ciphertexts, respectively, but cannot learning anything else. Especially, the presented scheme supports clients drop out. We provide the definition and security model of our FTMCFE-IP scheme, and propose a concrete construction. The security of the designed scheme is formally proven under the SXDH assumption. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Counterflow premixed ammonia/air flame extinction limits at elevated temperatures and pressures
Abstract: Interest in ammonia as a carbon free fuel has prompted a series of recent research efforts to increase understanding of fundamental combustion characteristics and to develop chemical kinetic models to better predict ammonia combustion behavior. Despite recent efforts, extinction limit data remain sparse with significant gaps, especially for conditions that are relevant to gas turbine combustion (elevated pressures and temperatures). Literature reaction models developed specifically for ammonia combustion remain largely untested under gas turbine relevant conditions, and existing kinetic models have shown substantial variations in predicted extinction strain rates. This paper presents results from a study directed towards improved comprehension of ammonia combustion chemistry, and acquisition of new datasets under elevated pressure and temperature conditions, providing validation data to help refine rate expressions for important reactions in ammonia combustion. Additionally, our work identifies important reaction pathways for ammonia oxidation that may be responsible for discrepancies in numerical extinction strain rate predictions, as well as elucidates sensitive reaction steps with large uncertainties that require further attention. Overall, this work provides improved understanding of ammonia combustion chemistry, particularly at elevated pressures and temperatures, and generates new experimental datasets to better constrain rate expressions for critical reaction pathways. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Numerical study of pulverized coal MILD combustion coupled with oxygen staging under O2/CO2 conditions
Abstract: Coupling oxygen staging with pulverized coal MILD-oxy combustion can further reduce NOx emissions, with oxygen concentration serving as a key control parameter. This study investigates the effects of the primary-stream and total oxygen concentrations (XO2,pri and XO2,in) on pulverized coal MILD combustion coupled with oxygen staging under O2/CO2 conditions. The results show that, as the O2 concentration in the primary stream increased from 15% to 27%, the momentum difference between the primary and secondary streams increased, causing the MILD combustion regime to develop earlier in the furnace. The proportion of the MILD combustion region varied linearly with XO2, pri - XO2, in . Heterogeneous gasification in the furnace was enhanced, and the contribution of the H2O gasification reaction increased as XO2, pri + XO2, in increased. Increasing XO2, pri promoted MILD combustion and reduced the average coal consumption rate. Increasing XO2,in inhibited gasification and thus decreased the carbon consumption rate. Both increasing XO2, pri and decreasing XO2, in promoted NO reduction. Title: Effect of ion-specific conformational changes and hydrogen-bond network reorganization on the antifreeze activity of arabinoxylan
Abstract: Arabinoxylan (AX) from wheat bran is an effective antifreeze polysaccharide, but its structure–activity relationship in ionic environments remains poorly understood. At 0.05 M, Na2SO4 markedly enhanced the antifreeze activity of AX, whereas NaCl and NaNO3 showed limited or inhibitory effects. Structural analyses revealed that AX adopts a flexible random-coil conformation in solution, while sulfate ions promoted a more compact molecular organization. Integrated mechanistic analyses suggested that ion-induced conformational rearrangement and hydration regulation collectively modulate AX–associated hydration environments and enhance its ice-affinity. Specifically, SO42-–induced AX compaction was accompanied by altered interfacial hydrogen-bonding states, stabilized local hydration interactions, and modulation of long-range hydrogen-bond network dynamics. Authors: Zhu K.-Q.; Tong X.; Wang Y.-F.; Zhang B.-X.; Zheng S.-F.; Wang X.-D.
Title: Coupled design of a bamboo-shaped cathode flow field and hybrid-porosity gas diffusion layer for enhanced performance and multiphysics transport in open-cathode PEMFCs
Abstract: The bamboo-shaped cathode flow field can enhance heat-mass transfer and improve the performance of open-cathode proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). However, its further engineering application faces two prominent challenges: 1) the effects of the key design parameters on cell performance and multiphysics transport remain unclear; 2) geometry-induced local convection enhancement may aggravate the inherent spatial nonuniformity of the physical fields within the porous electrode assembly and increase the risk of local degradation. To address these challenges, this study first studies the impacts of two key design parameters, the number of bamboo-joint units ( N ) and bamboo-joint indentation depth ( W ), on PEMFC performance and the associated heat and mass transfer in porous electrodes. Furthermore, the flow field is coupled with a hybrid-porosity GDL to improve physical field uniformity while retaining enhanced transport. The results show that moderate increases in N and W strengthen the periodic contraction–expansion effect of reactants within the bamboo-shaped configuration, thereby enhancing shear disturbance and lateral mixing. This promotes faster renewal of the thermal and concentration boundary layers in the flow field and porous electrode, thereby increasing the net water and oxygen transport fluxes and improving heat dissipation. Adjusting N and W contributes to superior open-cathode PEMFC performance by up to 8.10 % and 18.85 %, respectively. Increasing N and W also increases the ideal cathode air-supply power due to the relatively larger pressure drop under otherwise identical operating conditions, indicating a greater relative air-supply penalty. Accordingly, the flow field design requires a trade-off among performance improvement, ideal air-supply penalty, and the uniformity of key physical fields within the MEA. Guided by these mechanistic insights, a coupled design is developed by integrating the bamboo-shaped flow field with a hybrid-porosity gas diffusion layer (GDL). This novel design retains the transport and performance advantages of the bamboo-shaped flow field while further alleviating the inherent limitation of the non-uniform distribution of key physical fields within the porous electrode. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Wettability modification of long-flame coal by acid-based CO2 foam fracturing fluids: changes in mineral composition, microcrystalline structure, and surface chemistry

Authors: Qi P.; Zhao W.; Lin J.; Zhao Q.; Yin S.; Radwan A.E.
Title: Integrated controls and accumulation mechanisms of marine–continental transitional shale gas: Insights from the Benxi Formation, southeastern Ordos Basin
Abstract: For the Benxi Formation in the Ordos Basin, the coupled controls of sedimentary environment on organic matter enrichment, pore structure on reservoir capacity, and sealing conditions on gas preservation remain poorly understood. Based on systematic core observations and experimental analyses including organic geochemistry, mineralogy, and pore structure characterization, the shale of the Jinci Member in the Benxi Formation exhibit high organic matter abundance (average TOC 5.57 wt.%), high thermal maturity (average Ro 2.62%, representing the overmature dry gas stage), and predominantly II2-III kerogen types, providing a favorable material basis for gas generation. The mineral composition is dominated by clay minerals (average 60.97%), followed by quartz (average 24.13%). Various pore types are developed, including organic matter pores, clay mineral interlayer pores, and pyrite intercrystalline pores. Micropores and mesopores serve as the primary storage spaces for adsorbed and free gas, with an average porosity of 2.2% and an average permeability of 0.78 mD. The weak porosity–permeability relationship indicates significant reservoir heterogeneity and limited pore connectivity, highlighting the importance of microfractures in enhancing seepage capacity. An accumulation model of “lagoon controlling hydrocarbon generation, pore structure controlling reservoir development, overpressure controlling enrichment, and lithological association controlling preservation” has been established: anoxic lagoon environments control organic matter enrichment (thickness 5-25 m, maximum TOC 23.93 wt.%); clay mineral-dominated pore structures control reservoir capacity, with microfractures improving seepage ability; abnormal overpressure (pressure coefficient 1.2-1.4) generated by hydrocarbon generation controls gas enrichment; and the dual sealing structure of “roof coal and floor limestone” together with thin siltstone interlayers controls preservation conditions and mobility. A quantitative evaluation framework further indicates that TOC > 4 wt.%, clay mineral content of 40%–70%, pressure coefficient > 1.2, and effective roof–floor sealing constitute key thresholds for favorable shale gas enrichment. This study investigates the organic geochemistry, mineralogy, pore structure, and sealing characteristics of the Benxi Formation shales in the southeastern Ordos Basin, aiming to elucidate the main controlling factors and establish an integrated accumulation model. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Teng W.; Yu Z.; Shen G.; Ma X.
Title: Ex-situ microwave-assisted co-pyrolysis of biomass with plastics over multilamellar MFI nanosheets zeolite boosts monocyclic aromatics and suppresses coke
Abstract: High-value bio-oil rich in monocyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (MAHs) was produced via microwave-assisted ex-situ catalytic co-pyrolysis of eucalyptus wood (EW) and polypropylene (PP) over MFI nanosheet zeolite (MNZ). The effects of catalyst loading (0–200 wt%), catalytic temperature (450–650 °C), and microwave power (600–1400 W) on product yields, liquid-phase composition, and catalyst coke deposition were systematically investigated. Among the investigated conditions, the best overall performance was obtained at 100 wt% MNZ, a catalytic temperature of 500 °C, and a microwave power of 1000 W, yielding 53.5 wt% bio-oil with a relative MAHs content of 39.83 %. Under identical conditions, the relative MAHs content obtained with MNZ was 2.46 times that obtained with conventional HZSM-5, while reducing coke deposition from 2.51 to 1.23 wt%. The enhanced catalytic performance of MNZ was associated with its hierarchical pore architecture, greater mesoporous volume, and higher Brønsted/Lewis acid ratio, which improve the accessibility of acid sites and mass transport of reaction intermediates. Electromagnetic characterization further showed that, at 2.45 GHz, MNZ exhibited a higher dielectric loss tangent and attenuation constant than HZSM-5, consistent with its faster microwave-heating response. These results demonstrate the potential of MNZ for promoting MAHs formation and suppressing coke accumulation during microwave-assisted ex-situ catalytic co-pyrolysis of EW and PP within the investigated conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Tan Y.; Liu W.; Sun X.; Qin J.; Chi H.
Title: StegGuard: Authenticated multi-image steganography with key-dependent recovery
Abstract: Multi-image steganography enables high-capacity covert communication by embedding multiple secret images into a single cover image. However, existing methods mainly optimize capacity and fidelity, while providing limited protection against unauthorized recovery. In multi-receiver scenarios, mismatched authorization keys may still reveal recognizable secret-related content, causing potential information leakage. To address this problem, we propose StegGuard, an authenticated multi-image steganography framework that formulates multi-secret recovery as a key-dependent authenticated reconstruction problem. StegGuard associates each secret image with a dedicated authorization key, enabling accurate reconstruction with matched keys while forcing recovery under mismatched keys toward visually non-informative outputs. It integrates an Invertible Authentication Network and an Invertible Hiding Network for reversible secret decomposition, key-conditioned authentication, and multi-image embedding. To improve high-payload recovery, a Position-Enhanced Channel-Refined module and a Multi-Scale Fusion Predictive module are designed for spatial-channel representation and context-aware inverse recovery. More importantly, an authentication-oriented joint optimization mechanism is designed to strengthen lock–key consistency and explicitly enlarge the reconstruction gap between authorized and unauthorized keys. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of StegGuard. When embedding two secret images, it achieves up to 46.52 dB PSNR for cover/stego pairs and 38.23 dB PSNR for authorized secret recovery. Under invalid-key recovery, the recovery PSNR drops to 6.44 dB, indicating that invalid keys empirically suppress recognizable reconstruction under the evaluated setting. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Zhi P.; Li L.; Yang M.; Peng Z.; Zhang Q.; Liu Y.; Wang T.; Huang W.
Title: Predicting residual carbon distribution in coal gasification slag via hot stage microscopy by using partially reacted char as a probe
Abstract: Current understanding of residual carbon in coal gasification slag (CGS) is largely limited to bulk-average content, while its distribution heterogeneity within particle populations remain poorly resolved, hindering accurate evaluation of carbon-ash separation potential. In this work, a particle-resolved approach based on thermally induced shrinkage observed by hot-stage microscopy (HSM) was developed to predict residual carbon distribution in CGS. To decouple carbon-level effects from the complexity of industrial slag, partially reacted chars with controlled carbon levels were designed as probe materials through partial CO2 gasification and air combustion, and deashed controls were introduced to evaluate mineral interference. The results showed that with the loss on ignition (LOI) decreased, the particle size reduced continuously, the density increased monotonically, and the reactivity declined progressively. Moreover, the partially combusted char and partially gasified char with varied LOI showed almost the same trends, indicated the LOI instead the reaction affected the shrinkage behavior. Under HSM oxidation conditions, the shrinkage descriptor at 700 ℃ ( RT ) showed a strong dependence on LOI, and a unified power-law relationship between RT and LOI was established for both gasification- and combustion-derived samples. The model was validated using blended samples, yielding a mean absolute error of 1.55 % for predicted LOI distributions, and further applied to industrial Xinjiang CGS with a relative error of 2.81 %. These findings provide new insights into the distribution characteristics of residual carbon in CGS and enable rapid evaluation of carbon heterogeneity, supporting more accurate assessment of carbon–ash separation potential and process optimization. Authors: Wen P.; Duan W.; Wang H.; Chen H.; Li X.
Title: Temperature-dependent mechanistic switching in Mn-based bimetallic catalysts for NH3-SCR revealed by data-driven analysis
Abstract: Machine learning has emerged as an effective tool for understanding complex structure–activity relationships in catalytic systems. However, the temperature-dependent mechanistic evolution in NH3-SCR over bimetallic catalysts cannot be fully captured by conventional unified models due to significant variations in reaction regimes across temperature ranges. In this work, a temperature-resolved machine learning framework combined with experimental validation was developed to analyse Al2O3-supported Mn-based bimetallic NH3-SCR catalysts incorporating different transition metal promoters across multiple temperature regimes. The results reveal a pronounced regime-dependent shift in the role of promoter species within Al2O3-supported Mn-based bimetallic catalysts, where Co species dominate catalytic performance in the low- and medium-temperature regions, while Ni species become more influential at elevated temperatures. Experimental results confirm that Mn–Co/Al2O3 exhibits superior low- and medium-temperature activity, attributed to the formation of Co–O–Mn coordinated structures that enhance oxygen mobility and redox cycling. In contrast, Mn–Ni/Al2O3 shows enhanced high-temperature performance due to the formation of NiMn2O4 spinel structure, higher Mn4+/Mn3+ ratio, and abundant strong acid sites, collectively improving structural stability and intermediate adsorption. This work provides a comprehensive understanding of temperature-dependent catalytic behaviour in NH3-SCR and highlights the importance of regime-dependent structure–activity relationships for rational catalyst design. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Guo Z.; Gu R.; Liang T.; Xiong B.; Zhao Y.; Shi W.
Title: A dual-modal round-the-clock biocidal material synergizing physical piercing and photo-chemical attack based on α-Si3N4/g-C3N4 composite
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: As the growing challenge of bacterial resistance increasingly undermines the efficacy of conventional antibiotics, the development of novel antimicrobial materials that operate independently of traditional drug mechanisms has emerged as a critical research priority. In this study, we designed and synthesized a g-C3N4-based material featuring a nano-needle architecture, designated α-Si3N4/g-C3N4 composite (SiN-CN), with the aim of establishing a dual-modal antibacterial mechanism that integrates physical and chemical synergistic actions. The densely arrayed nano-needle structures on the surface of SiN-CN are capable of compromising bacterial cell wall integrity through a physical puncturing mechanism, thereby enabling rapid, broad-spectrum bactericidal activity without inducing microbial resistance. Furthermore, this material enables the in-situ generation of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) under light irradiation, conferring an additional chemical sterilization modality. Importantly, this dual-mechanism design achieves round-the-clock antimicrobial performance as follows: during illumination, the physical piercing effect acts in concert with photo-induced H2O2 production to substantially enhance bactericidal efficacy, under dark conditions, although H2O2 generation ceases, the persistent physical antimicrobial activity afforded by the stable nano-needle architecture remains operative, effectively suppressing bacterial adhesion and proliferation. Therefore, this material is capable of maintaining its antibacterial activity under both light and dark conditions, thereby enabling sustained antimicrobial performance regardless of the prevailing illumination status. In vitro antibacterial evaluation demonstrated that the material exhibits exceptional bactericidal performance under illumination, achieving sterilization rates of 91% against Escherichia coli and 90.8% against Staphylococcus aureus even at an extremely low concentration of 1.25 μg/mL. In addition, SiN-CN achieved an H2O2 production rate of 95 μmol·g−1·h−1 under illumination, representing a 4.57-fold enhancement over that of pristine g-C3N4. Collectively, this work offers a promising strategy for the development of next-generation smart antimicrobial materials characterized by high biosafety and low risk of resistance induction. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Wang D.; Wang K.; Li L.; Xia D.; Zhang Z.; Yu B.; Shen Y.; Guo Z.; Zhang W.; Xiang T.; Dong Z.; Yang S.
Title: Enhanced anisotropic magnetoresistance in La0.7-xNdxCa0.3MnO3 thin films via A-site doping
Abstract: Perovskite-type manganese oxide films have garnered significant attention due to their diverse physical phenomena and potential applications in spintronics and magnetoresistive devices. Notably, the La0.7Ca0.3MnO3 system exhibits a large intrinsic anisotropic magnetoresistance (AMR) with values exceeding 10%, making it a promising candidate for low-temperature magnetoresistive applications. In this study, we employed pulsed laser deposition (PLD) to fabricate a series of La0.7-xNdxCa0.3MnO3 (x = 0.00, 0.02, 0.04, 0.06, 0.08) (LNCMO) films on Si (00l) substrates to investigate compositions with enhanced magnetoresistance (MR) and AMR properties. The findings indicate that with increased Nd doping, the films exhibited greater lattice distortion and pronounced Jahn-Teller effects, resulting in a reduction of the metal-insulator transition temperature and an increase in resistivity. Crucially, both the MR and AMR of the films were enhanced. At x = 0.06, the film achieved a maximum AMR of −14.4% under a 1 T magnetic field, offering valuable theoretical and experimental insights for the design of high-performance magnetoresistive thin-film devices. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Cui G.; Ren Q.; Tian Y.; Zhang W.; Xie K.; Liu J.
Title: Ammonia-rich vs. Hydrogen-rich blending: A review of dual-route research progress on ammonia-hydrogen mixed combustion
Abstract: Against the backdrop of the “dual carbon” goals, hydrogen and ammonia have attracted widespread attention as typical carbon‑free fuels. Unlike previous reviews that largely focused on a single route or a single application scenario, this paper takes the dual‑route utilization of ammonia‑hydrogen blended fuels as its main thread, categorizing them into two complementary pathways—“ammonia‑rich with hydrogen addition” and “hydrogen‑rich with ammonia addition”—and systematically reviews the research progress in fuel properties, reaction kinetics, fundamental combustion behavior, nitrogen‑containing emission mechanisms, and engineering applications for both routes. The review shows that the ammonia‑rich with hydrogen addition route can significantly improve the ignition and flame propagation performance of ammonia fuel, but its application remains constrained by NOx, N2O, and unburned ammonia emissions. The hydrogen‑rich with ammonia addition route, on the other hand, can modulate the reactivity of hydrogen fuel to a certain extent, reducing the risks of auto‑ignition, flashback, and explosion propagation, thus offering a new perspective for the safe utilization of hydrogen. Further comparison reveals that the two routes have distinct technical objectives and engineering constraints in terms of fuel ratio, combustion organization, emission control, and safety boundaries. Overall, ammonia‑hydrogen blended fuels show potential application value in internal combustion engines, gas turbines, and marine propulsion, but their large‑scale development still relies on validation under high‑pressure real‑world conditions, synergistic design of power systems, and comprehensive life‑cycle assessment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Ma T.; Liu L.; Zhai X.; Song B.; Hao Y.; Hao L.; Yang H.; Xiong Q.
Title: Research on the reaction mechanism of key active groups in biomimetic antioxidant hydrogel for inhibiting coal spontaneous combustion
Abstract: Coal spontaneous combustion will reduce the fuel quality and produce harmful gases. To develop an environmentally friendly material to regulate the reactivity of coal fuel, this study developed a green, biomimetic antioxidant hydrogel inhibitor. Using proanthocyanidins modified with gallic acid as the active ingredient and a hydrogel as the carrier, a biomimetic antioxidant hydrogel inhibitor was prepared. Programmed heating experiments examined gas release at different inhibitor dosages. The inhibition rate increased with dosage and then leveled off. The optimal dosage was 5 wt%, considering both effectiveness and cost. At this level, oxygen consumption and the release of CO, CO2, C2H4, and C2H6 decreased significantly. FTIR analysis showed that treated coal had higher levels of –CH3, –CH2, C–H, –OH groups than raw coal, while C=O content in the late oxidation stage decreased by 7.78 %. Spearman correlation analysis revealed strong links between these groups and gas release, with the strongest link (0.92) between C=O and hydrocarbon gases. Using Gaussian software, simplified coal molecular models were built. Results showed that oxygen-rich areas are electron-rich, while hydroxyl hydrogens and carbonyl carbons are electron-poor. Further calculations based on ΔG and ΔH values showed that the inhibition pathway is thermodynamically more favorable than the oxidation pathway. Therefore, the hydrogel reduces the reactivity of the coal oxidation process by blocking the gas generation pathway driven by free radicals. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Torkaman asadi M.J.; Zare S.
Author full names: Torkaman asadi, Mohammad Javad (56898925900); Zare, Shahryar (57189356149)
Title: Enhanced transient thermal analysis of finite-length PDE tubes under cyclic severe internal heating using a hybrid analytical–numerical approach
Abstract: Pulse detonation engines (PDEs) are among the most promising propulsion technologies for future aerospace applications due to their potential for lower mechanical complexity and higher thermodynamic efficiency. However, their intense and cyclic thermal loading creates a unique transient heat transfer environment within the detonation tube that challenges long-term reliability and thermal design. This work presents a comprehensive analytical and numerical study of the transient thermal response of a finite-length detonation tube subjected to high-frequency, rapid, and severe internal heating representative of PDE operation. To model realistic PDE conditions, a detailed thermal loading profile based on the full engine cycle, including detonation, thrust, purging, and refilling phases, has been validated and developed. The novelty of this work lies in the verification and development of a cycle-based thermal loading model, and in providing a combined analytical-numerical solution for the transient temperature distribution across the tube wall. The analytical model, based on the separation of variables in cylindrical coordinates, provides closed-form expressions for thermal behavior under cyclic heating. These are cross-validated with finite element simulations in ABAQUS and benchmarked against experimental data reported in the literature. Validation against experimental data at an operating frequency of 3.077 Hz shows that the model accurately predicts an outer wall temperature rise of approximately 21.19°C to 22.53°C after 28 cycles, closely matching the experimental observation of 23.7°C. Results further demonstrate that while the tube temperature rises sharply without cooling, implementing external convection (h = 200 to 2000 W/m2K) effectively stabilizes the thermal response over 1000 operating cycles. The findings quantify the critical time scales for thermal penetration, showing a 1°C increase at the outer wall within approximately 2 s of operation. This hybrid modeling approach provides a precise and computationally efficient tool for the long-term thermal management and structural optimization of pulse detonation systems. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Authors: Hou J.; Zhao H.; Lan M.
Title: Target-responsive “signal-down” electrochemical biosensor based on an anti-biofouling hydrogel for glutathione detection
Abstract: Glutathione (GSH), a ubiquitous biothiol, is critical in physiological processes, and abnormal fluctuations in its level are intimately associated with various diseases. However, real-time in vivo monitoring of GSH within tissues, such as the tumor microenvironment (TME), is fundamentally hindered by severely electrode biofouling and electrochemical interference from structural analogs. Herein, we report a novel target-responsive “Signal-Down” electrochemical biosensor based on an anti-biofouling hydrogel for GSH detection, which elegantly integrates robust anti-biofouling capabilities with highly specific target recognition. This sensing interface features a highly hydrated polyacrylamide (PAM) network, crosslinked by disulfide bonds and loaded with ferrocene/β-cyclodextrin (Fc@β-CD) electroactive probes. Upon exposure to GSH, the highly specific thiol-disulfide exchange reaction triggers the macroscopic degradation of the Fc-hydrogel. This spatial disruption drives the rapid outward diffusion of the redox probes, translating microscopic molecular recognition into a dramatic attenuation of the electrochemical signal. This biosensor not only successfully differentiated abnormal intracellular GSH levels in B16 melanoma cells from those in normal L929 fibroblasts in vitro, but also achieved in situ detection of pathological redox dysregulation in a melanoma-bearing mouse model. Ultimately, by uniquely coupling macroscopic material degradation with signal attenuation, this work establishes a reliable strategy for continuous, interference-free biosensing in highly complex and fouling-prone biological matrices. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Liu K.; Tang Y.; Lin Y.; Xiong L.; Zhu M.
Title: Parallel-aligned PMX@ZIF heterostructure for enhanced tribocorrosion resistance of epoxy coating on aluminum alloy
Abstract: To enhance the tribocorrosion resistance of epoxy (EP) coatings, a layered MXene@ZIF heterostructure was synthesized and subsequently oriented into a parallel-aligned polyethylenimine-modified MXene@ZIF composite coating (PMX@ZIF/EP) on an AA2024 substrate via electric field-induced alignment. During heterostructure synthesis, the pre-anchoring of 2-methylimidazole on the Ti3C2Tx MXene surface induced high-density nucleation and confined interlayer growth of ZIF-L nanosheets, effectively suppressing MXene restacking while preserving interlayer shear lubrication. In the dry sliding test, PMX@ZIF/EP exhibited a wear rate of 3.33 × 10−5 mm3·N−1·m−1, approximately 75% lower than that of pure EP. Furthermore, the ZIF-L component increased the crosslinking density of the epoxy matrix and contributed to corrosion inhibition. After 4 weeks of electrochemical testing, PMX@ZIF/EP maintained the highest |Z|0.01 Hz value of 1.59 × 1010 Ω·cm2, demonstrating excellent long-term protective performance. Under coupled tribocorrosion conditions, the coating exhibited a progressive positive shift in open-circuit potential. Through the in situ formation of a dense, parallel-aligned tribofilm, the composite coating stabilized the friction coefficient at 0.28 and reduced the wear rate to 2.78 × 10−5 mm3·N−1·m−1. This synergistic integration of active-passive protection and interlayer shear lubrication provides an effective strategy for extending the service life of aluminum alloys in severe environments. Authors: Sasaki T.; Kubonaka T.; Morizumi S.; Mekaru K.; Uechi T.; Yasuda K.
Author full names: Sasaki, Toshikazu (61020395600); Kubonaka, Toru (61020303800); Morizumi, Shosei (61019813900); Mekaru, Kouki (58637832500); Uechi, Taisei (61020395700); Yasuda, Keita (23994491800)
Title: Energy analysis and phase equilibrium in clathrate hydrate-based simultaneous carbon capture and desalination
Abstract: To develop a technology that simultaneously performs clathrate hydrate-based carbon capture and desalination, phase equilibrium conditions of clathrate hydrate-forming systems consisting of carbon dioxide–nitrogen mixed gases and sodium chloride aqueous solutions were measured. The energy requirement associated with seawater desalination and the second stage of a multistage carbon dioxide separation process was also examined. Using mixed gases with carbon dioxide mole fractions ranging from 0.61 to 0.68 in equilibrium with sodium chloride aqueous solutions with mass fractions from 0.035 to 0.105, the measured phase equilibrium temperatures ranged from 269.8 K to 275.8 K, with corresponding equilibrium pressures ranging from 2.12 MPa to 4.02 MPa. Under the assumed operating pressure of 2.8 MPa, the sum of the energy required to supply the cold thermal energy and compress the gas corresponds to 199 kWh–220 kWh when expressed per ton of carbon dioxide captured, and 68.5 kWh–75.6 kWh when expressed per cubic meter of water obtained. A large fraction of the energy is consumed for supplying cold thermal energy to remove the enthalpy change of clathrate hydrate formation and for gas compression. Therefore, the results indicate that effective utilization of cold thermal energy from liquefied natural gas regasification, operation at lower temperatures and pressures, and the introduction of guests that enable operation at reduced pressures are promising strategies for reducing the overall energy demand. These strategies may facilitate the development of hydrate-based technologies for simultaneous carbon capture and desalination of high-salinity water streams, including produced water and seawater. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Large eddy simulation and experimental investigation of liquid ammonia diffusion combustion and emissions formation under diesel-ignited JCCI conditions
Abstract: Under the framework of powertrain carbon neutrality, the jet-controlled compression ignition (JCCI) strategy, which utilizes diesel-ignited direct injection liquid ammonia diffusion combustion demonstrates strong potential for improving the power output and reducing emissions in ammonia-fueled engines. However, fundamental insights into the liquid ammonia spray processes remain insufficient, and the mechanisms governing ammonia diffusion combustion and pollutant formation require deeper examination. This study combines optical diagnostics and Large Eddy Simulation (LES) to compare diesel prior-injection and simultaneous injection strategies under dual direct‑injection conditions. The results demonstrate that for efficient combustion of the liquid ammonia spray, the ignition source should be positioned within the well-mixed region at the spray leading edge. This enables flame propagation towards the spray periphery and tail, progressively igniting the entire flammable zone and ultimately achieving complete combustion. Conversely, if ignition occurs in the spray central region, the overly lean mixture at the spray head prevents ignition, leading to substantial escape of unburned ammonia. Regarding emissions, under the diesel prior-injection condition, NO distributes throughout the spray following flame expansion, unburned ammonia is minimal, and N2O is primarily located at the flame periphery during the late combustion stage. In contrast, the simultaneous injection condition results in incomplete combustion, confining NO to the central region, yielding higher levels of unburned ammonia, and showing negligible N2O decomposition. Based on these findings, a conceptual model incorporating the “head-priority ignition” principle is proposed, correlating pollutant distribution with combustion zones to provide a theoretical basis for optimizing engine combustion and reducing emissions. Title: Investigation of tribological behavior of CNT- and CuO-reinforced UHMWPE nanocomposites for biomedical implants
Abstract: Ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene (UHMWPE)-based composites reinforced with copper oxide (CuO) and -COOH functionalized multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) were developed to investigate their tribological and bioactive performance for orthopedic implant applications under simulated body fluid (SBF) conditions. Incorporation of 15 wt% CuO and 1.0 wt% MWCNTs into the UHMWPE matrix showed improved tribological behavior, reducing the coefficient of friction (CoF) and specific wear rate by approximately 66.0% and 49.0%, respectively, compared to neat UHMWPE with contact pressure of 4.77 MPa and sliding speed of 0.07 m/s. However, further increase of MWCNTs content in the composite resulted in a gradual deterioration of tribological performance. The optimized composite exhibited an 8.2% increase in Shore hardness over neat UHMWPE. Bioactivity assessment in SBF confirmed the formation of a hydroxyapatite layer on the composite surface. Surface wettability measurements revealed improved hydrophilicity with the incorporation of 15 wt% CuO, increasing the MWCNTs content reduced the hydrophilicity. The incorporation of CuO and optimal MWCNTs improves the mechanical, tribological, and bioactive performance of UHMWPE for orthopedic bearing applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Jia J.; Sun J.; Li J.; Wu J.; Gu M.; Tian Z.-Y.; Zhou C.; He X.
Title: Influence of ammonia blending on soot formation and nanostructure in laminar n-decane diffusion flames
Abstract: Ammonia blending with hydrocarbon fuels has drawn increasing attention as a strategy for reducing soot emissions and mitigate combustion related particulate pollution. In this study, the influence of ammonia addition on soot formation and structural evolution was investigated in laminar coflow diffusion flames of n- decane. Ammonia was blended at 0–40% volume fraction, with the carbon mass flow rate maintained constant to minimize thermal variations and emphasize chemical effects. Flame imaging and axial thermocouple measurements showed that ammonia increased the visible flame height and enlarged central dark zone, while peak flame temperatures decreased by less than 5%, indicating a limited thermal influence. Quantitative soot volume fraction measurements further confirmed that ammonia addition significantly reduced soot concentrations throughout the flame. Soot samples collected at 2, 3, and 4 cm above the burner were characterized by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and high-resolution TEM (HRTEM). Ammonia addition suppressed primary particle growth, with the mean particle diameter at 3 cm decreasing from 23 nm (N00) to 19 nm (N40). HRTEM analysis revealed that ammonia blending reduced fringe length by up to 40%, while increasing fringe tortuosity, and widened inter-fringe spacing. The increased occurrence of multicore structures and reduced internal layering indicated less ordered soot, has typically associated with higher oxidative reactivity. Numerical simulations indicate that NH3 suppresses benzene formation primarily by weakening the propargyl recombination pathway, while the increased formation of CN and HNCO reflects enhanced C–N chemistry and the redistribution of reactive carbon, thereby reducing the formation of A1 and subsequent PAH growth. These findings highlight the dual role of ammonia in suppressing soot formation and modifying soot nanostructure in ammonia-hydrocarbon combustion systems, providing insight into the development of cleaner low-emission combustion technologies. Title: Fractional delay differential fuzzy variational inequalities in banach spaces: Existence, stability, and applications
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: In this paper, we investigate a novel class of fractional delay differential fuzzy variational inequalities (FDDFVI) in Banach spaces. The proposed model is built upon a Caputo-type fractional differential equation with delay together with a fuzzy variational inequality, governed by a non-pseudo-monotone fuzzy mapping. First, we prove that the solution set of a parameterized fuzzy variational inequality is nonempty, convex and compact. We then verify that the corresponding solution mapping is upper semicontinuous. On this basis, by utilizing the measure of noncompactness, semigroup theory and fixed point theorems for condensing set-valued mapping, we establish the existence of mild solutions for the FDDFVI. Moreover, we prove the upper semicontinuity of the solution mapping for the FDDFVI, which reflects the stability of the solution set with respect to parameter perturbations. A concrete numerical example is provided to illustrate the validity and applicability of the obtained theoretical results. This research extends the existing relevant theories from finite-dimensional spaces to infinite-dimensional settings and relaxes the monotonicity constraints imposed on fuzzy mappings in previous studies. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Wu Y.; Wang Y.; Huang X.; Chen G.; Gu Y.; Wang X.; Liu Q.
Title: An aggregation-induced emission fluorescent microsphere-based intelligent lateral flow immunosensor for rapid and quantitative detection of prostate-specific antigen
Abstract: Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) is an important biomarker for prostate cancer (PCa) screening, but conventional detection methods rely on sophisticated instruments and centralized laboratories. Herein, we developed an aggregation-induced emission fluorescent microsphere-based lateral flow immunoassay strip (AIEFM-LFIS) for rapid and quantitative detection of PSA. Highly specific anti-PSA monoclonal antibodies were prepared by hybridoma technology and conjugated with AIEFMs to construct fluorescent immunoprobes, which were further integrated with a portable LumiS-1 Pro reader for quantitative signal acquisition and smartphone-based data transmission. Under optimized conditions, PSA could be detected within 20 min over a detection range of 0.5-62.5 ng/mL, with a limit of detection of 0.28 ng/mL. Clinical evaluation of 40 serum samples showed a sensitivity of 96.2%, a specificity of 100%, and a consistency of 97.5% with chemiluminescence immunoassay. Owing to its high sensitivity, portability, intelligent quantitative readout, and low cost, the developed platform provides a promising tool for decentralized PSA testing and preliminary PCa screening in primary healthcare and resource-limited settings. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
