Title: Electrospun nisin/chitooligosaccharide/fish skin gelatin nanofiber-based hydrogel membranes: water absorption-swelling behavior and application in fish preservation
Abstract: Preservation packaging is essential for reducing fish spoilage and maintaining food safety and quality. In this study, fish skin gelatin (FSG), chitooligosaccharide (COS), and nisin were used to fabricate nanofiber-based hydrogel membranes with antibacterial and antioxidant functions. The membranes were prepared by electrospinning, followed by cross-linking via the Maillard reaction and subsequent absorption and swelling treatment. The cross-linked nanofiber membrane exhibited uniform fibers with smooth surfaces, homogeneous nisin distribution, and favorable water absorption and swelling behavior. Upon hydration and swelling, the resulting NCF-H-4 formed a porous hydrogel structure, exhibiting an optimal permeability profile and excellent rheological stability. Model fitting indicated that the water absorption behavior of the hydrogel membranes was well described by the pseudo-first-order model: initial water uptake followed diffusion-driven pseudo-first-order kinetics, while the contribution of pseudo-second-order kinetics increased over time. Moreover, the NCF-H-4 demonstrated excellent antibacterial and antioxidant activities and extended the shelf life of fish by 4 d at 4 °C. Overall, the developed hydrogel membranes show promising potential for application in aquatic product preservation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Qin L.; Xiong Z.; Gong J.; Zhong Z.; Yi Y.; Song H.
Title: Multi-scale wavelet convolutional sampling and cross-stage feature enhancement reconstruction for image compressed sensing
Abstract: Deep compressed sensing (DCS) has demonstrated remarkable effectiveness in image compressed sensing (CS), owing to its superior performance and speed. However, most existing DCS methods employ simplistic sampling strategies that fail to fully exploit frequency-domain information in original images. During reconstruction, measurements are merely used to drive iterative algorithms rather than being deeply fused with evolving features. Furthermore, these methods typically concatenate reconstruction stages without establishing strong interconnections among them. To address these three challenges in both sampling and reconstruction, we propose MWCFE-Net, a multi-scale wavelet convolutional sampling and cross-stage feature enhancement reconstruction network. In sampling, the multi-scale wavelet convolutional sampling (MSWT) network decomposes multi-scale high- and low-frequency components via layered wavelet transforms, then applies a frequency-division dynamic attention mechanism to obtain measurements rich in multi-dimensional features. In reconstruction, the cross-stage feature enhancement reconstruction (CFER) module employs deep-shallow feature fusion (DSFF) and cross-stage cross-attention (CSCA) to enhance dynamic information flow across stages through measurement-guided deep features and cross-attention. MWCFE-Net integrates MSWT and CFER into an end-to-end trainable framework. Comprehensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that MWCFE-Net surpasses state-of-the-art methods with excellent noise robustness. Title: Structural transformation of hydroxyapatite into an active calcium sulfate catalyst for efficient biodiesel production from high free fatty acid feedstocks
Abstract: In this research, a sulfated hydroxyapatite (SHA) was synthesized for biodiesel production from palm fatty acid distillate (PFAD) and comprehensively characterized using XRD, DLS, FTIR, BET, SEM/EDX, NH3-TPD, CO2-TPD analyses, and Hammett acidity. Title: Boosting ambient-pressure CO2 hydrogenation to methanol: Lattice Mo doping modulates electronic structure of In2O3
Abstract: Precisely modulating the local electronic structure of oxygen vacancies is key to improving the inferior catalytic activity of In2O3 toward CO2 hydrogenation to methanol under atmospheric pressure. Herein, we demonstrate that lattice-incorporated Mo, rather than surface modification, plays a decisive role in regulating the electronic environment of oxygen vacancies in In2O3, thereby remarkably boosting the catalytic activity with a nearly two-fold increase in methanol yield compared to pristine In2O3. Both experiments and theoretical simulations substantiate that the enhanced activity originates from the synergistic promotion of oxygen vacancy generation and moderately basic sites, which cooperatively facilitate CO2 adsorption, activation, and subsequent methanol formation. By establishing a structure-activity relationship, this work identifies lattice Mo doping as the core strategy for designing highly efficient In2O3 catalysts, which can efficiently catalyze CO2 hydrogenation to methanol under atmospheric pressure, offering a promising approach for energy-saving CO2 conversion. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Unraveling the role of CaO in H2 production via sorption-enhanced steam gasification of biochar
Abstract: The integration of in-situ CO2 capture utilizing CaO-based catalyst/sorbents in conventional biomass steam gasification (SG) processes for “green hydrogen” production can address the limitations of low hydrogen yield, elevated CO levels, and inherent high endothermicity. Here, with thermodynamic analysis, online hydrogen tests, in-situ characterization and periodic density functional theory (DFT) calculations, we demonstrate that CaO-based sorbents transform the inherently endothermic SG process into a net exothermic one over a broad temperature window via thermodynamic coupling with the highly exothermic carbonation reaction, thereby markedly reducing the requirement for external heat input. Title: On trees with game chromatic number 4
Abstract: The coloring game is a two-player non-cooperative game conceived by Steven Brams, first published in 1981. In this game, Alice and Bob alternate turns to properly color the vertices of a finite graph G with t colors. Alice’s goal is to properly color the vertices of G with t colors; Bob’s aim is to prevent it. If, at any point, there is an uncolored vertex without an available color, Bob wins; otherwise, Alice wins. The game chromatic number χg(G) of a graph G is the smallest t for Alice to have a winning strategy. While the game chromatic number of trees is known to be at most four (Faigle et al. 1993), the characterization of trees with game chromatic numbers 3 and 4 remains an open problem (Dunn et al. 2015). In this paper, we extend results on caterpillars to more general trees, and establish sufficient conditions for a tree to have game chromatic number 4. The techniques developed contribute to the construction of infinite families of trees with game chromatic number 4, and clarify the relation between local configurations and global coloring strategies. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Domain-decomposition-free CF-PINN for tunnel seepage and induced ground response in layered anisotropic strata
Abstract: Steady-state seepage around tunnels in layered anisotropic soils is governed by spatial variations in hydraulic conductivity and by abrupt changes across material interfaces. Such discontinuities present a particular difficulty for strong-form, pressure-based physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), because evaluation of the governing residual may involve spatial derivatives of the conductivity field. This study develops a continuous-function PINN (CF-PINN) framework for tunnel seepage in regularly stratified ground. Known layer locations, layer-wise permeability values, and hydraulic anisotropy are embedded in a differentiable conductivity function with controlled transition widths, allowing the seepage field to be represented using a unified pressure-only network without explicit neural-domain decomposition. Hard constraints are introduced for selected boundary conditions to improve boundary satisfaction and training stability. The proposed CF-PINN-H formulation is evaluated against numerical reference solutions and compared with a hard-constrained extended PINN (XPINN-H) under non-proportional layered-permeability conditions. Field contours and pressure profiles show close agreement between the proposed formulation and the reference solutions, with converged test losses generally reaching the order of 10⁻4 or lower. CF-PINN-H also achieves accuracy comparable to XPINN-H while requiring substantially less training time. For the representative case with a tunnel burial depth of 40 m, PINN-H reduces the total training time by approximately 63.2% relative to XPINN-H. The predicted pore-pressure field is subsequently transferred to a finite element mechanical model, demonstrating the consistency of a sequentially coupled PINN–FEM workflow for obtaining representative displacement and effective-stress responses. The proposed approach provides a compact alternative to explicit neural-domain decomposition for regularly layered media. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Class-imbalance-aware wafer map defect classification via latent-space data augmentation
Abstract: Wafer map defect classification plays a critical role in semiconductor manufacturing, where accurate pattern discrimination directly affects yield analyses and process controls. However, structural noise and severe class imbalance continue to limit the reliability of existing approaches, as conventional augmentation strategies often provide limited structural diversity, while flexible generative methods or deformation methods may alter the topology of defect patterns. To address these challenges, this study proposes a convolutional network with latent space augmentation (CNN-AUG), in which a denoising and contractive autoencoder learns robust latent manifolds that are subsequently perturbed to generate diverse yet structurally coherent samples. Integrated with a lightweight convolutional architecture, the proposed CNN-AUG achieves 98.56% accuracy, a macro AUC of 0.9970, and a macro AP of 0.9925 on WM811K, outperforming conventional and recent deep models while maintaining computational efficiency. Additional topological and morphological analyses, comparisons with diffusion augmentation methods using a split by fabrication lot, external validation on MixedWM38K, and ablation studies confirm the effectiveness, robustness, and contributions of individual components to the proposed framework. Occlusion sensitivity analysis reveals that the network focuses on physically meaningful wafer regions, thereby enhancing interpretability and supporting the practical deployment of semiconductor inspection pipelines. Owing to their stable framework structure, FeMOFs can produce inherent and stable electrochemical redox peaks. Title: Design and microscopic–macroscopic study of calcium silicate/zinc oxide–modified GO/h-BN coatings for atlantoaxial joint replacement
Abstract: Ti-6Al-4V implants are severely limited by wear-induced bone resorption, stress shielding, and bacterial infection in artificial Atlantoaxial joint replacements. Title: Hybrid physics-informed neural network for axial-flow pump performance parameter prediction
Abstract: The deviation of real pump performance from ideal curves critically reduces energy efficiency at pumping stations. This deviation, caused by differences between laboratory and field conditions and long-term wear, results in unavoidable performance decline. Existing studies using CFD or neural networks trained on lab data often face limitations in physical interpretability and cross-condition applicability, restricting their use in large-scale water transfer projects.To address this, we propose a hybrid physics-informed neural network incorporating a time-dependent degradation prior for efficiency and a polynomial flow–head prior for head, and validate it using field data from the Denglou Pumping Station along the Eastern Route of the South-to-North Water Diversion Project. Results show that H-PINN achieves consistently high random-holdout accuracy across the four units, with efficiency and head R2 values of 0.9448–0.9938 and 0.9850–0.9982, respectively. For Unit 3, it yields the lowest aggregate errors among the evaluated methods, reducing the efficiency and head RMSEs by 12.3% and 9.8%, respectively, relative to the strongest competing baselines. In a separate four-fold forward-chaining evaluation of 1470 pooled off-design samples for Unit 3, H-PINN achieved efficiency and head RMSEs of 0.2484% and 0.01090 m. Authors: Gao H.; Gao H.; Wei S.; Dong A.; Xu J.; Li G.
Title: Recent advances in MOF-based non-precious metal materials for oxygen evolution reaction electrocatalysis
Abstract: The growing global energy crisis has promoted the rapid development of sustainable hydrogen production technologies, among which electrochemical water splitting is considered one of the most promising approaches. However, the performance of water electrolysis is mainly restricted by the anodic oxygen evolution reaction (OER). The slow kinetics of the four-electron transfer process leads to a high overpotential, and this process acts as the rate-determining step in the overall reaction. To overcome this issue, metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have been recognized as a suitable platform for enhancing the OER, due to their well-ordered porous structure, tunable architecture, and diverse composition. In this review, recent progress in non-precious metal MOF-based OER catalysts is systematically summarized and divided into four categories: single-metal MOFs, multimetallic MOFs, MOF-derived materials, and MOF-based composites. Particular attention is given to rational modification strategies that aim to improve intrinsic activity, electrical conductivity, and long-term stability. Additionally, the fundamental OER reaction mechanism during electrochemical splitting is discussed to provide theoretical guidance for the rational design of MOF-based catalysts. Finally, the key challenges and future development directions of non-precious metal MOF electrocatalysts are critically discussed, offering prospects for future development in high-efficiency and sustainable water electrolysis systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: From fabrication to function: Electrochemical characterization of hyaluronic acid-based biomimetic hydrogels in aqueous ethanol

Inspired by biology, we investigate a biomimetic hydrogel that combines human tongue–like properties with electrochemical responsiveness and apply it to aqueous ethanol systems. Comprehensive characterization of its structure, rheology, and biosafety confirms its suitability as a biomimetic material. Electrochemical analyses further demonstrate its capability to operate as a responsive interfacial in aqueous ethanol environments. The hydrogel exhibits solid-like viscoelastic behavior and good biocompatibility, providing a stable and secure soft interface for studies related to artificial sensory systems. Title: Si/Al ratio-regulated PdO dispersion determines methane combustion activity over Pd/H-ZSM-5
Abstract: Methane (CH4) is a potent greenhouse gas, and catalytic combustion offers an effective route for its emission abatement. Title: Al-modified SBA-15 confinement of coal tar pitch for bifunctional N/S-doped porous carbon electrocatalysts

Title: Hierarchical magnetic nano-orb-assisted fluorescence recovery aptasensor for sensitive detection of aflatoxin M1 in milk

Title: A computational approach for a class of third-kind nonlinear FIDEs based on piecewise ϕ-Jacobi cardinal functions

Title: Effects of fuel-air unmixedness on flame stability and emissions in rapidly mixed hydrogen-enriched swirling flames
Abstract: The transition to hydrogen-enriched combustion is fundamentally constrained by the challenge of simultaneously ensuring safety, flame stability, and low NO x emissions. Title: Sulfur transformation during internals-regulated pyrolysis of coal and waste tires: Characteristics and mechanisms

Title: Molecular interaction and optical properties of the acetic acid–benzene system: dielectric spectroscopy and first-principles study
Abstract: Dielectric relaxation spectroscopy is an effective approach for investigating molecular dynamics and intermolecular interactions in hydrogen-bonded liquids. The present work aims to elucidate the mechanisms of dielectric relaxation and microstructural organization in acetic acid–benzene solutions through a combined experimental and theoretical approach. The dielectric properties were investigated by dielectric spectroscopy over the wavelength range of 0.75–40 cm at temperatures from +20 to +50 °C, while temperature-dependent measurements were performed at a frequency of 1.6 MHz over the range from −80 to +50 °C. To interpret the experimental observations, first-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations were carried out to investigate the structural, electronic, and optical properties of the acetic acid–benzene complex. The results show that dielectric dispersion begins at wavelengths below 50 cm and that the relaxation behavior is most accurately described by a three-process relaxation model associated with different types of molecular associates. Dilution with benzene disrupts extended hydrogen-bonded structures and promotes the formation of specific O–H···π intermolecular complexes, leading to a redistribution of the individual relaxation contributions and corresponding changes in the characteristic relaxation times. Unlike previously reported binary organic systems, the present study demonstrates that the dielectric relaxation behavior of the acetic acid–benzene system is governed by the competition among acetic acid dimerization, hydrogen-bonded associates, and specific O–H···π intermolecular interactions, giving rise to three distinct relaxation processes. DFT calculations confirmed the weak noncovalent nature of the intermolecular interaction, and revealed pronounced anisotropy in the electronic and optical response of the complex. The calculated HOMO–LUMO energy gap, derived from the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) and the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO), is approximately 4.96 eV, indicating that the system is a wide-gap molecular system with limited low-energy electronic excitations. The combined experimental and first-principles approach establishes direct correlations among molecular structure, dielectric relaxation processes, and optical properties, thereby providing a molecular-level interpretation of the observed relaxation behavior and extending the current understanding of intermolecular interaction mechanisms in associated liquid systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhou G.; Lu Y.
Title: Burden of proof: Calibrated evidential arbitration for asymmetric decision-level fusion in vision–language recognition
Abstract: Decision-level fusion can correct a recogniser’s errors, but it can also overwrite predictions that were already correct. We study a setting in which a strong vision–language recogniser already holds a default prediction and an auxiliary source can only contest it with a challenger label. Adopting every challenger that disagrees with the default overwrites a correct answer in 18–46% of conflicts, while a fixed gate produces harm rates that vary widely across recognisers. We propose Calibrated Evidential Arbitration (CEA), a default-preserving decision-level fusion method. CEA calibrates two margins from frozen CLIP text-alignment and DINOv3 visual-support channels into belief masses, combines them with Dempster’s rule, and flips the default only when the combined pignistic margin reaches a risk-calibrated threshold. The keep-or-flip decision is evaluated through a Rescue–Hurt decomposition, which makes harmful overwrites measurable and controllable through their proportion among accepted switches (selected-hurt). Across four few-shot benchmarks and three vision–language recognisers, CEA substantially reduces harmful overwrites while preserving most of the attainable fusion gain: on the two recognisers for which challenger fusion is beneficial, held-out selected-hurt is 1.3–5.0%, and CEA closes up to 92% of the oracle fusion gap. A challenger-swap experiment yields a similar risk–gain profile after recalibration, supporting cross-challenger robustness. The method trains no neural network and fits only two monotone channel mappings and one scalar threshold. These results suggest that asymmetric fusion is better treated as calibrated arbitration, in which an auxiliary source should replace the default prediction only when its evidence justifies the risk. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Chen B.; Xue R.; Zhang X.; Liu Y.; Fang Y.
Title: LaCe co-doped Ni/MgO-Al2O3 catalyst: deactivation mechanism study for CO2 methanation
Abstract: Ni-based catalysts suffer from deactivation due to high-temperature sintering and oxidation during CO2 methanation, limiting their industrial application. Single La or Ce promotion can improve Ni dispersion and suppress sintering; however, La and Ce co-doping unexpectedly aggravates catalyst deactivation. In this study, a new deactivation mechanism of LaCe co-doped Ni/MgO-Al2O3 catalysts during CO2 methanation at 500 °C and 3 MPa is revealed. Combined characterization by XRD, H2-TPR, CO2-TPD, XPS and TEM, together with DFT calculations, suggests that the formation of a La2O3-CeO2 solid solution inhibits MgO dispersion in the support, resulting in a higher amount of free Al2O3. Meanwhile, Ce promotes the oxidation of surface Ni, and the resulting Niδ+ species are more prone to react with Al2O3 to form hardly reducible NiAl2O4 spinel, causing irreversible deactivation. Further adoption of a La-first impregnation strategy improves MgO dispersion, suppresses NiAl2O4 formation, retains more oxygen vacancies, and enhances Ni dispersion, thereby mitigating deactivation. This study reveals a new deactivation mechanism induced by LaCe co-doping, providing a theoretical basis for rational design of high-stability Ni-based CO2 methanation catalysts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Microstructure, tribological properties and wear mechanism of V2AlC reinforced multi-layer composite coatings via laser cladding
Abstract: Nowadays, titanium alloys are increasingly being utilized in automotive and aerospace manufacturing. However, limitations were presented due to their relatively low hardness and poor wear resistance. To mitigate these defects, layered MAX phase materials, known for their excellent self-lubricating properties and high-temperature stability, were widely employed for surface modification. In this study, V2AlC (VAC) was used for the first time to prepare self-lubricating coatings on titanium alloys via laser cladding. Directly depositing on TC4, the coating (VAC/TC4) was developed with needle-like, dendritic and eutectic TiCx ceramic phases. In addition, through a two-step coating method, the coating (VAC/Ni/TC4) was prepared by designing a nickel interlayer to reduce the decomposition of the MAX phase innovatively. VAC/Ni/TC4 exhibited flower-like, dendrites crystals, and MAX phase-transformation structure of VCx. The results indicated that the wear rate was 3.19 × 10−4 mm3/N·m, reducing 35.9% compared to TC4. For VAC/Ni/TC4, the wear rate (6.01 ×10−6 mm3/N·m) decreased 55.9% compared to pure Ni and two orders of magnitude compared to TC4. An in-situ protective glaze layer was formed during wear, functioning as a lubricant. At 600 °C, the wear rate of VAC/TC4 represented a rise of 178.4%, yet VAC/Ni/TC4 presented a 42.5% reduction. The performance deterioration was attributed to the three-body wear caused by the partial detachment of the glaze layer. This study explored the microstructural evolution of VAC in laser cladding processing and clarified the wear mechanism. A feasible two-step coating method was presented, which facilitated the application of VAC-based coating on the high-performance key friction parts at elevated temperature. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Huang W.; Yang Y.; He Z.; Zhang S.; Duan L.; Guo G.
Title: Visualization experimental study on transient cavitating flow and spray characteristics of methanol high-pressure direct injector nozzles
Abstract: In the context of the green and low-carbon transformation of internal combustion engines, methanol is regarded as a promising alternative fuel owing to its high oxygen content, low carbon-to-hydrogen ratio, and excellent combustion characteristics featuring minimal particulate formation, coupled with its compatibility with existing fuel infrastructure due to liquid-phase storage at ambient conditions and potential for production through carbon–neutral pathways utilizing biomass or CO2 hydrogenation. However, its low cetane number and high latent heat of vaporization present challenges to ignition stability and spray consistency during high-pressure injection. To address these issues, a high-pressure common-rail fuel injection experimental platform was developed using a prototype-based transparent nozzle model integrated with the original full-size injector. Using the backlight uniform illumination method, a systematic experimental study was conducted to investigate the effects of injection pressure and nozzle geometry (including straight orifices, convergent orifices, different SAC chamber depths, and various numbers of orifices) on the transient nozzle internal cavitation flow and near-field spray characteristics of methanol, while simultaneously characterizing the associated dynamic needle-motion response. Comparative experiments between methanol and diesel revealed that methanol injections tend to generate more pronounced aggregation of vapor structures and larger spray cone angles, while also causing more pronounced material degradation on the nozzle. Increasing injection pressure mainly affects the transient evolution of cavitation and spray during the needle-opening and needle-closing stages, while no clear monotonic effect is observed on the quasi-steady cavitation intensity or spray cone angle. The depth of the SAC chamber and the number of orifices significantly affect the needle lift and the stability of cavitation structures. Smaller-volume SAC chambers promote earlier cavitation formation, whereas larger-volume chambers contribute to sustained cavitation and prolonged tail-spray. Compared with diesel, methanol exhibits higher cavitation intensity and broader spray diffusion characteristics during stable injection. This study provides fundamental experimental evidence for understanding the transient cavitation and near-field spray behavior of high-pressure methanol injection and offers useful references for subsequent methanol nozzle optimization. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wang Y.; Ding H.; Chen L.-Q.
Title: Resonance and anti-resonance of a three rotation-joined pipes conveying pulsating fluid under dual-frequency excitation
Abstract: This study investigates the nonlinear vibration of the central pipe within a three-rotationally-joined pipe system, which conveys pulsating fluid and is subjected to local excitation. By incorporating the relevant joint constraints, the coupled nonlinear governing equations for this central pipe system are rigorously derived. The system's nonlinear vibration characteristics are subsequently analyzed using the multiple scales method under dual-frequency excitation conditions. Analytical solutions provide the time trace and amplitude envelope for the first two vibration modes of the central pipe, which are then validated through direct numerical simulation. Results reveal that the central pipe exhibits quasi-periodic motion, and resonance phenomena occur when the excitation frequencies approach its first two natural frequencies. A detailed analysis is conducted on the effects of external force and the flow's fluctuation velocity amplitude on the amplitude–frequency response. Notably, anti-resonance is observed for specific parameters, and its underlying mechanism is thoroughly analyzed. Furthermore, the frequency–amplitude response of the central pipe under dual-frequency excitation is obtained, demonstrating that the second vibration mode is almost independent of the flow's fluctuation frequency. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS

Title: Mitigation of rotational instabilities using multi-turn solenoid in induction heating-based wire additive manufacturing process
Abstract: Induction heating-based wire additive manufacturing (IH-WAM) has emerged as a promising heat source for processing high melting point materials. The Lorentz force generated by the interaction between the induced current and the magnetic field strongly influences metal transfer mechanism, often leading to delayed transfer and non-uniform deposition due to its rotational effect. In the current work, the role of magnetic flux density in controlling metal transfer dynamics to achieve favourable material deposition is targeted. The application of a multi-turn solenoid positioned near the induction coil is proposed as a novel approach to mitigate the rotational effect of Lorentz force. A simulation-based study is conducted to determine the optimal orientation of the multi-turn solenoid. A detail investigation is carried out to assess the influence of critical process parameters like wire feed rate, applied solenoid current and number of solenoid turns by analysing the temperature distribution within the fed stock wire. The magnetic field and the corresponding Lorentz force interaction between induction coil and the solenoid is performed to understand the mechanism. The baseline simulation without the solenoid exhibits good agreement with the existing experimental results, validating the developed model. However, the potentiality of magnetic field controlled by using a multi-turn solenoid at optimal design of IH-WAM, shows the way of its reliable application in additive manufacturing of high melting point metals. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Authors: Li X.; Kasama K.; Yahiro Y.; Ishikawa T.; Li Y.; Li Z.; Li F.
Title: A merging particle filter-based data assimilation for inverse estimation of soil hydraulic parameters from mini disk infiltrometer measurements
Abstract: Soil hydraulic parameters, particularly the soil hydraulic conductivity and soil water characteristic curve (SWCC), play a critical role in hydrogeological investigations and rainfall-induced hazard assessment. However, conventional measurements are often time-consuming and difficult to implement under field conditions. This study proposes a practical data assimilation framework for rapid estimation of soil hydraulic parameters, which integrates mini disk infiltrometer (MDI) tests, three-dimensional finite element (FE) seepage simulations, and a merging particle filter (MPF) approach. A sequential updating strategy is further incorporated to assimilate information from multiple measurements and improve estimation robustness. The proposed framework is validated through laboratory soil column experiments involving Toyoura sand, silica sand K-5, and Masado soil. Time-series infiltration measurements obtained from MDI tests are assimilated into transient seepage simulations based on the Richards’ equation, and the estimated parameters are compared with independently measured SWCCs and hydraulic conductivities. The results demonstrate that the framework can accurately estimate soil hydraulic parameters using only MDI infiltration measurements, while Monte Carlo simulations (MCS) successfully reproduce measured infiltration responses with all NRMSE values below 20%. Furthermore, sensitivity analyses indicate that the estimation results are relatively insensitive to assimilation sequence, whereas assimilation quantity and prior uncertainty exert greater influence on parameter identifiability and convergence. Overall, the proposed framework provides a rapid and reliable approach for probabilistic characterization of soil hydraulic parameters and shows promising potential for large-scale hydrogeological investigations. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Chen Y.; Zheng T.; Luan Y.; Feng Y.; Jiang K.; Li W.; Wang M.; Liu Z.; Lu G.
Title: Automatic design of flow channel for PEMFC based on space-weighted topology and multi-objective optimization
Abstract: To address the severe concentration polarization in Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell (PEMFC) under high current density, caused by oxygen transport limitation and water management imbalance, this study proposes a three-dimensional automatic flow channel design framework integrating topology optimization and Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II). A multi-physics coupled model is established, with average current density, current density variance, and pressure drop selected as optimization objectives. The weight space is systematically explored through Latin hypercube sampling combined with simplex mapping, and a BP neural network surrogate model is trained based on COMSOL-MATLAB high-fidelity simulation data to enable efficient global optimization. The results reveal a pronounced nonlinear trade-off among the three objectives. Single-objective optimization improves current density but significantly increases pressure drop, while conventional empirical weighting schemes fail to achieve balanced performance. The optimal compromise solution (w1 = 0.571, w2 = 0.286, w3 = 0.143), identified using the TOPSIS decision-making method, achieves a 5.04 % increase in peak power density compared to the conventional structure, while significantly enhancing oxygen distribution uniformity and water management capability. Furthermore, the lateral flow intensity ratio demonstrates a fundamental transition of oxygen transport from diffusion-dominated to convection–diffusion coupled mechanisms. This study provides a systematic and data-driven optimization framework that eliminates empirical bias in weight selection, enables automatic generation of complex flow channel structures, and the optimal structure’s discovery mechanistically reveals the embryonic form of single-channel optima, offering new insights for designing high-performance PEMFC flow fields. Authors: Zheng Z.; Zhao Z.; Jia L.; Wu L.; Tian S.; Chen L.; Liu C.; Zhang J.; Tan R.
Title: Paper-based colorimetric sensing for pesticide residue detection: Recognition mechanisms, signal transduction, and quantitative readout strategies
Abstract: Paper-based colorimetric assays offer a low-cost and portable approach for pesticide residue screening, yet reliable quantification remains a major barrier to practical deployment. Unlike previous reviews centered mainly on sensing-platform classification or individual recognition strategies, this review establishes a continuous analytical framework linking target recognition, signal transduction, and quantitative readout engineering. Representative sensing approaches are examined to clarify how variability introduced at different stages propagates through the analytical workflow and ultimately affects quantitative performance. The analysis indicates that reliability is governed by the weakest link in the sample-to-result chain, while downstream signal amplification or data modeling cannot compensate for unstable upstream recognition, sample transport, or color generation. On this basis, this review proposes a design-oriented evaluation framework to guide the development of paper-based pesticide analytical devices with improved reproducibility, standardization, and field applicability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Li Y.; Huang G.; Xu S.; Yang N.; Wu X.
Title: Explosion characteristics and flame propagation of HHO/NH3/air premixed mixtures in a closed vessel
Abstract: Brown’s gas (HHO), a highly reactive carbon-free fuel, has attracted increasing attention for hydrogen-based energy applications, while ammonia (NH3) is considered a promising hydrogen carrier. Understanding the explosion behavior of HHO/NH3/air mixtures is essential for their safe utilization. In this study, the effects of HHO fraction on explosion characteristics and flame propagation behavior were experimentally investigated in a 20 L closed cylindrical vessel under an equivalence ratio of 1.0, an initial temperature of 300 K, and an initial pressure of 101.3 kPa. HHO volume fractions of 20 %, 40 %, 60 %, 80 %, and 100 % were examined. The results demonstrate that increasing HHO fraction significantly enhances explosion severity. The maximum explosion pressure ( P max) increased from 0.60 MPa to 0.87 MPa, while the maximum rate of pressure rise ((d P /d t )max) increased from 32.06 MPa·s−1 to 702.36 MPa·s−1. The explosion index ( K St) increased continuously from 8.70 to 190.65 MPa·m·s−1, and the mixtures entered the high-hazard category according to NFPA 68 when the HHO fraction reached 40 %. Schlieren visualization revealed that flame propagation underwent a significant transition with increasing HHO concentration. Mixtures containing 60 % or more HHO exhibited significantly accelerated flame propagation, whereas lower HHO fractions exhibited slower flame propagation due to ammonia-induced dilution and reduced overall combustion activity. A noticeable change in flame propagation behavior was observed around 60 % HHO, corresponding to a transition from NH3-influenced combustion to enhanced flame acceleration associated with increasing HHO addition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhuang L.; Tian F.; Cheng P.; Ren C.; He S.
Title: Data-driven asynchronous optimal control for 2-D MJRSs with structural constraints via reinforcement learning
Abstract: This article investigates the data-driven asynchronous structured optimal control problem for discrete-time two-dimensional (2-D) Markov jump Roesser systems (MJRSs) with unknown dynamics. The structural coupling of 2-D systems motivates a structured optimal control formulation. Moreover, the proposed framework addresses the challenges associated with asynchronous mode information and unknown system dynamics. To resolve these issues, a reinforcement learning (RL) framework is established to solve the derived asynchronous discrete-time algebraic Riccati equation (ADARE) using only measurable input-state data. Two data-driven algorithms are developed to achieve this objective. First, an off-policy policy iteration (PI) algorithm is constructed to reconstruct the optimal controller. Second, a value iteration (VI) algorithm is proposed to circumvent the requirement of an initial stabilizing policy inherent in the PI algorithm. Crucially, the VI approach facilitates online learning from arbitrary initial conditions. Theoretical analyses guarantee the convergence of both algorithms to the structured optimal solution and ensure the asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework under asynchronous conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Multi-source Heterogeneous Data Fusion with Graph-Aware Dual Contrastive Learning for drug–drug interaction prediction
Abstract: Accurate prediction of drug–drug interactions (DDIs) is vital for patient safety and therapeutic efficacy. Recently, DDI prediction methods based on graph neural networks and multi-source heterogeneous drug information have made progress. However, most existing multimodal DDI prediction methods still fail to fully integrate multi-source heterogeneous drug information and effectively exploit the complementary information across different modalities, making it difficult to fully capture the sequential, structural, and semantic characteristics of drugs, thereby limiting the quality of drug representations and DDI prediction performance. To address these limitations, we propose MHGCL, a Multi-source Heterogeneous Data Fusion with Graph-Aware Dual Contrastive Learning framework, designed for DDI prediction. Initially, we construct a comprehensive drug representation by integrating four modalities: drug SMILES sequences, protein target sequences, molecular graphs, and a biomedical knowledge graph (KG) to holistically capture and incorporate the sequential, structural, and semantic information of drugs. Next, we design a graph-structure-aware adaptive subgraph extraction strategy that selects the optimal sampling method based on the structural properties of the KG, and propose a dual contrastive learning mechanism to enhance the quality of feature representations for both molecular graphs and KGs. Finally, we construct a cross-modal self-attention fusion module that achieves dynamic interaction and deep integration of heterogeneous modality features. Experimental results on three real-world drug datasets demonstrate that MHGCL significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art methods, validating its effectiveness for DDI prediction. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Chen X.; Ma H.; Wu L.; Liu C.; Mao L.; Ding J.; Qiu D.; Sun X.
Title: Study on the explosion suppression efficiency and mechanism of modified dry water material in ammonia-hydrogen-air mixture
Abstract: Ammonia-hydrogen mixture is a promising zero-carbon fuel, but its production, storage, transportation, and utilization processes carry significant explosion risks. This study aims to prepare modified dry water (KMDW) by compounding different potassium salts with melamine polyphosphate (MPP) and investigate their suppression performance on ammonia-hydrogen mixture (40 % H2) explosions at various equivalence ratios using experiments and simulations. In experiments, it can be found that all KMDW outperformed unmodified dry water, with KMDW-KCl exhibiting the best performance. With 12 g of KMDW-KCl, the peak flame temperature and explosion pressure were significantly reduced by 96.5 % and 82.6 % at φ = 1.0, and the flame was quenched 1.4 m from the ignition end. Furthermore, its suppression effectiveness was found to be applicable across a wide range of equivalence ratios. Simulation analysis revealed that the potassium and phosphorus containing active species released from KMDW-KCl decomposition interrupt the chain reactions by scavenging key radicals such as H and OH, with R968 (KOH + H = K + H2O) and R964 (KO2 + OH = KOH + O2) identified as the dominant elementary reactions for explosion suppression. These results provide critical data and a theoretical basis for the safe utilization of ammonia-hydrogen mixed fuels and offer new insights for developing highly efficient explosion suppressants. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Hu F.; Wang Y.; Tan Z.; Zhou W.; Ju T.; Li L.; Gong L.; Kawi S.
Title: Size dependence of Ni/biochar catalyst derived from chicken manure for CO2 methanation
Abstract: CO2 methanation offers a promising strategy for both reducing CO2 emissions and producing renewable natural gas, yet the development of inexpensive catalysts with high low-temperature activity and robust stability remains a major challenge. This study investigates the size effect of Ni-based catalysts supported on chicken manure-derived biochar for CO2 methanation. By tailoring the Ni nanoparticle size (11, 13, 17, and 24 nm), the influence of Ni particle size on catalyst structure, surface chemical properties, and catalytic performance was systematically examined. The results demonstrate that the 13 nm Ni/biochar catalyst exhibits the optimal performance, achieving a CO2 conversion of 70.3% at 400 °C and only ∼ 5% deactivation over a 50 h stability test. The activity order follows: 13 nm > 17 nm > 11 nm > 24 nm. Systematic characterization revealed that the 13 nm catalyst possesses moderate specific surface area, pore volume and pore size, an optimal defect density and oxygen vacancy content, as well as superior Ni dispersion and suitable metal-support interaction. Mechanistic studies reveal a temperature–dependent dual–pathway mechanism: below 350 °C, the formate pathway dominates; above 350 °C, CO dissociation occurs, and both pathways lead to methane. This work provides new insights into the value-added utilization of agricultural waste and CO2 resource recovery. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wu Q.; Wang Y.; Li J.; Tian X.; Che H.; Lu L.; Hu Y.
Title: Unified alcoholysis-GC-MS/MS for simultaneous differentiation and quantification of polyester microplastics in water
Abstract: Environmental waters now carry complex mixtures of polyester microplastics that vary in origin and biodegradability, including fossil-based and biodegradable polyesters, yet no method can simultaneously distinguish and individually quantify them. We present a unified alcoholysis method coupled with GC-MS/MS to quantify four polyester microplastics (PEMPs) in a single workflow. By selectively cleaving ester bonds in an alcohol medium, the method converts polylactic acid, polyethylene terephthalate, polyhydroxybutyrate and polybutylene succinate into four distinct, stable monomers. These monomers are directly determined by GC-MS/MS without derivatization. Under unified conditions (190 °C, 5 h), depolymerization efficiencies range from 15% to 90%. We calibrate directly between polymer mass and monomer signal intensity. Detection limits are 0.0462 μg/L for polylactic acid (PLA), 0.103 μg/L for polyethylene terephthalate (PET), 2.92 μg/L for polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB), and 0.695 μg/L for polybutylene succinate (PBS). Spiked recoveries in lake water are 90–115%. In six lake samples, PLA constitutes over 75% of total PEMPs. This fingerprint points to consumer packaging as the dominant source. By circumventing particle morphology constraints and delivering polymer-specific mass concentrations, the method opens a direct route for source apportionment of coexisting fossil-based and biodegradable polyester microplastics. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Kong B.; Xu H.; Feng X.; Duan D.; Ma L.; Zhang J.; Tan X.
Title: Study on the coupling characteristics of acoustic wave and self-potential during coal spontaneous combustion and the hazard identification method
Abstract: Addressing the challenge of accurately detecting concealed fire sources in coal spontaneous combustion, a synchronous experimental system for acoustic waves and self-potential was constructed. The study reveals that acoustic velocity increases linearly with temperature, while self-potential exhibits a staged pattern of “negative shift–positive shift–then negative shift to stability.” Although the two signals originate from different physical mechanisms, both are jointly influenced by the temperature field and the deterioration of coal structure, demonstrating an obvious coupling synergy in their temporal evolution. Based on these findings, regularized constraint methods are employed to perform acoustic velocity tomography and self-potential equivalent source inversion, reconstructing the spatial distribution of wave velocity anomaly zones and electrochemical activity zones at different temperature stages. Furthermore, a gate function is introduced to fuse the two types of information, constructing a joint hazard index that classifies spontaneous combustion risk into safe zones, dangerous zones, and high-risk zones. Validated by actual temperature data, this index effectively avoids false alarms in the low-temperature stage, while in the medium-to-high temperature stage, the high-value zones closely coincide with the high-temperature core. Compared with single-parameter indicators, the proposed index shows significant advantages in stability, sensitivity, and anti-interference capability, providing a quantitative method for the precise identification of early concealed fire sources in coal spontaneous combustion. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Stable and pH-responsive chitosan/chondroitin sulfate nanocapsules for fish oil encapsulation and controlled release with oxidative stability and antioxidant property
Abstract: Fish oil is rich in omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids that are essential for human health, but it is highly susceptible to oxidation and rancidity. In this study, chitosan (ChI) and chondroitin sulfate (ChS) were combined via electrostatic interactions to form stable pH-responsive nanocapsules for fish oil encapsulation (ChS-ChI@FO NCs), aiming to enhance stability and controlled release. XRD and FTIR analysis confirmed structural encapsulation of fish oil. The nanocapsules showed an encapsulation efficiency and loading capacity of 37.56% and 16.37%, respectively. ChS-ChI@FO NCs exhibited strong colloidal stability for over 4 months at 6 °C with no significant changes in particle size, zeta potential, and PDI. To evaluate pH responsiveness, ChS-ChI@FO NCs were assessed at pH 6, 7.4, and 8.4. The particle size of ChS-ChI@FO and ChS-ChI nanocapsules increased significantly in a pH 6.0 buffer, facilitating controlled release. The release of fish oil was gradual at pH 6, reaching approximately 90.36% after 24 h. ChS-ChI@FO NCs also exhibited antioxidant and antibacterial abilities and effectively protected fish oil from oxidation at 50 °C for 4 weeks. Overall, these findings highlight a pH-responsive, biodegradable, and biocompatible delivery system with improved stability and environment-triggered release, especially in mildly acidic environments, supporting its potential for application as a multifunctional health food delivery system. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Novel Sr3CaSi2O8 nanoparticles for lighting, anticounterfeiting, forensic, shielding and photocatalytic applications
Abstract: A novel multifunctional silicate nanomaterial, Sr3CaSi2O8 nanoparticles, was successfully synthesized via a green solution combustion method and systematically investigated for structural, electronic, optical, dielectric, radiation shielding, forensic, anticounterfeiting and photocatalytic applications. The Rietveld refined XRD analysis strongly supports the formation of an orthorhombic structure with high crystallinity, while Williamson-Hall analysis revealed an average crystallite size of 30.46 nm with a lattice strain of 6.92 × 10−4. SEM micrographs exhibited a coral-like needle-shaped morphology, and EDX analysis verified the presence of Sr, Ca, Si and O. Title: Switching charge transfer path from type-I to S-scheme via N doping for selective CO2 to CH4 photoconversion

Title: Reliability-guided hypergraph feature fusion for underwater object detection
Abstract: Underwater image degradation, such as color cast, scattering, and low contrast, introduces severe background interference and feature uncertainty, causing traditional multi-scale networks to suffer from information conflicts and error amplification during cross-scale feature fusion. Second, the multi-scale relay hypergraph fusion network (HGDFFusionHub) is constructed to operate on the middle-resolution neck feature. This module uses context-conditioned sparse hypergraph incidence for higher-order relational fusion and concurrently coordinates pyramid-anchor attention and detail compensation to aggregate abstract semantics and spatial details. Title: Flame morphology and infrared radiation of non-premixed H2-NH3 laminar flames under O2-enrichment
Abstract: Ammonia (NH3) and hydrogen (H2) are promising carbon-free fuels for decarbonizing energy-intensive industries; however, their adoption is hindered by altered flame morphology and low radiative intensity compared to hydrocarbons. This study experimentally investigates the impact of O2-enrichment on the morphology and infrared radiation heat flux of non-premixed H2-NH3 flames. Experiments were conducted in a coflow burner at constant thermal power (1 kW) and a global equivalence ratio (ϕglobal = 0.85). The NH3 volume fraction (XNH3) was varied from 0 % to 20 %, while the oxidizer composition ranged from 21 % to 100 % O2 by volume. Diagnostics included natural luminosity, OH*/NH2* chemiluminescence imaging, and radiation heat flux measurements. Under O2-enrichment, H2-NH3 flames exhibited a distinct dual-zone structure. Chemiluminescence analysis revealed that the outer zone correlates with the heat release rate (OH*), while the inner orange cone correlates with a fuel preheating zone (NH2*). As XNH3 increases, the inner cone height increases while the outer zone narrows. Notably, Roper’s classical analytical model fails to predict flame height for these blends. This is attributed to extreme disparities in molecular mass and mobility between H2 and NH3, which trigger preferential diffusion effects that render a single mean diffusion coefficient inadequate. While NH3 addition generally reduces radiation heat flux, results demonstrate that O2-enrichment can compensate for this loss. The radiation deficit between NH3-doped and pure H2 flames decreases sharply up to 30 % O2, becoming nearly independent of enrichment levels beyond that threshold. Title: Contact-configuration-dependent fretting wear of Alloy 690TT tubes against 316SS counterbodies in high-temperature pressurized water: Interfacial damage mechanisms and data-driven prediction

Title: Time-accurate and highly-stable explicit two-step Runge-Kutta methods for stiff differential equations
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: In this paper, we introduce the Time-accurate and highly-stable explicit two-step Runge-Kutta methods (TASE-TSRK) for solving stiff ordinary differential equations, inspired by the technique presented in Calvo et al. [1]. The objective of the methods is to improve the stability characteristics of explicit TSRK methods by pre-multiplying the vector field with a suitable TASE operator. In this work, the related order conditions are analyzed, and then a complete study of stability properties is carried out for TASE-TSRK methods with order k ≤ 4. Authors: Lei C.; Guo J.; Deng J.; Wang C.; Zhao J.; Cui C.; Hui C.
Title: Thermal radiation-driven coal spontaneous combustion and its risk classification and early warning
Abstract: Coal spontaneous combustion is one of the major mine disasters and also a primary trigger of secondary disasters such as mine gas and coal dust explosions. To reveal the combustion characteristics and risk evolution mechanisms of thermal radiation-driven coal spontaneous combustion, a cone calorimeter system was employed to conduct combustion tests on coal samples with four particle sizes (0.28, 0.158, 0.111, and 0.086 mm) under three heat fluxes (30, 50, and 75 kW·m−2). Furthermore, by integrating the second-order response surface methodology with a dynamic radiation absorption efficiency model, a two-dimensional classification and evaluation system for coal spontaneous combustion risk was established, centered on combustion driving force and energy utilization efficiency. The results indicate that heat flux is the dominant factor influencing coal combustion behavior. Both the heat release rate and total heat release increased critically with increasing heat flux. At a heat flux of 75 kW·m−2, the peak of heat release rate reached 31.05 kW·m−2, approximately 91.6% higher than the 16.2 kW·m−2 recorded at heat flux of 30 kW·m−2. The total heat release increased from 9.7 MJ·m−2 to 18.1 MJ·m−2, corresponding to an increase of 86.6%. The combustion mode transitioned from a heat transfer-limited regime under low heat flux to an oxygen diffusion-controlled regime under high heat flux. Particle size affected the combustion process through specific surface area effects, packing thermal resistance, and char layer formation, with finer particles effectively enhancing the thermal response rate and combustion intensity. A heat flux of 50 kW·m−2 was identified as the critical range for incomplete combustion and heavy smoke generation, whereas 75 kW·m−2 promoted complete combustion of volatiles and secondary oxidation of soot particles, thereby significantly reducing smoke production. The second-order response surface model exhibited good predictive performance, and the predicted peak heat release rate, serving as the combustion driving force, increased monotonically with heat flux, whereas the dynamic radiation absorption efficiency decreased from approximately 0.28 at 30 kW·m−2 to 0.13 at 75 kW·m−2, revealing that intense combustion under high heat flux is accompanied by severe energy utilization loss. Authors: Zhou J.; Huang S.; Jin X.; Zhang J.; Liu X.; Du H.
Title: Efficient uncertainty quantification and sensitivity analysis of straddle-type monorail vehicle system critical speed by sparse grid polynomial chaos metamodel
Abstract: Ensuring the operational safety of straddle-type monorail vehicle systems (SMVS) requires accurate reliability assessment under parametric uncertainties. This study develops a sparse grid polynomial chaos metamodel (SG-PCM) framework to efficiently quantify uncertainty propagation and global sensitivity in the critical speed of SMVS, which serves as a dynamic stability failure threshold. Traditional methods, such as Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS), suffer from prohibitive computational costs for high-dimensional problems. While SG-PCM integrates Smolyak sparse grid quadrature with polynomial chaos expansion, it effectively mitigates the "curse of dimensionality" while maintaining high accuracy. The method constructs a meta-model of critical speed by leveraging orthogonal polynomial bases and sparse grid sampling, enabling probability distribution estimation and global sensitivity analysis. Results reveal that the critical speeds exhibit significant stochastic variations under suspension parameter uncertainties. Sensitivity analysis identifies key influential parameters, including radial stiffness/damping of guiding wheel, radial stiffness of stabilizing wheel, and damping of lateral damper. Compared to MCS, SG-PCM reduces computational costs by orders of magnitude (e.g., 421 vs. 1050,000 samples for second-order analysis) with comparable accuracy (R² > 0.986). Title: Multiscale mechanisms of voltage decay and corresponding mitigation strategies for dead-ended anode PEMFCs
Abstract: Dead-ended anode (DEA) mode can improve hydrogen utilization in proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), but prolonged closure promotes nitrogen crossover, liquid–water retention and local hydrogen starvation. These coupled processes cause voltage decay and output loss. In this study, a three-dimensional transient multiphysics model was coupled with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to link cell-scale water–gas evolution with molecular-scale changes in membrane hydration structures. The results show that increasing current density accelerates hydrogen consumption on the anode side, promoting low-hydrogen, high-nitrogen, and liquid–water-rich regions near the closed end, which increases mass-transfer resistance and accelerates voltage decay. At the membrane scale, nitrogen ingress into hydrated perfluorosulfonic acid (PFSA) membranes disrupts water-cluster connectivity, weakens water-water and water-hydronium hydrogen-bond networks, and reshapes pore-size distributions, making proton-migration pathways more tortuous. These findings suggest that, under the investigated operating conditions, performance loss induced by dead-ended anode operation is associated with coupled gas dilution, liquid–water accumulation and nitrogen-related perturbation of membrane hydration structures. Periodic purging was therefore evaluated as a model-based mitigation strategy. Under the investigated single-cell model conditions, a 0.28 s purge duration combined with a 47 s interval reduced purge frequency by approximately 43 % while keeping the mean voltage loss below 0.68 %. This combination provided a favorable balance between voltage stability and hydrogen utilization within the tested parameter range, rather than a universally optimal purge strategy. Title: Interfacial engineering of Zr-MOF@Ag2S heterostructures for coupled photocatalytic pollutant degradation and hydrogen generation

Title: In-situ tracking of fatigue damage evolution at elevated temperature using grating laser nonlinear ultrasonic technique
Abstract: In-situ monitoring of high-temperature fatigue damage evolution remains challenging conventional contact sensors face significant limitations at elevated temperatures. On the basis of a systematic comparative investigation into the influences of microlens array period and excitation laser pulse rise time on the propagation characteristics of narrowband surface waves, the apparent nonlinear response index is employed to achieve the effective characterization of both surface fatigue closed cracks and subsurface buried cracks. Subsequently, an in-situ laser ultrasonic system is established and applied during fatigue tests conducted at 20, 300, and 600 °C. The fundamental-frequency amplitude, second-harmonic amplitude, and apparent nonlinear response index are tracked over the fatigue-loading process. The experimental results reveal systematic variations in the ultrasonic responses with increasing fatigue cycles and indicate that the proposed technique can distinguish different acoustic-response stages associated with fatigue damage accumulation under the investigated fatigue-testing conditions. Title: Tuning interfacial work function difference by oxygen vacancies to boost S-scheme charge transfer in BiOBr/TiO2 for photocatalytic overall nitrogen fixation
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Converting N2 to NH3 and subsequently oxidizing to NO3− offers a sustainable alternative to the Haber-Bosch and Ostwald processes. Compared with the defect-free BiOBr/TiO2 junction, introduction of oxygen vacancies into TiO2 substantially enlarges the work-function difference between the two components, thereby strengthening the interfacial built-in electric field. This enhanced field promotes spatial separation and selective migration of photogenerated carriers, while preserving the strong redox capability inherent to the S-scheme charge transfer pathway. Density functional theory calculations reveal that oxygen vacancies effectively tune the electronic structure of TiO2 and increase its work function mismatch with BiOBr, providing theoretical support for the enhanced interfacial electric field. Title: Significantly enhancing the strength of aluminum while preserving excellent electrical conductivity via single-walled carbon nanotubes reinforcement

Microstructural analysis confirmed the well dispersion of SWCNTs without micro-sized aggregations. The smaller diameter and much higher specific surface area of SWCNTs enables the formation of a greater number of clean and strong bonded interfaces with the Al matrix under the thermo-mechanical conditions of FSP, which is the key for enhancing strength and maintaining electrical conductivity of Al. Title: Synergistic effects of moisture content and freezing temperature on mechanical-desorption responses of frozen gas-bearing coal and implications for outburst prevention
Abstract: Cryogenic freezing technology can both reduce the energy storage of coal–rock mass and enhance its strength, showing broad application prospects for outburst prevention in deep outburst-prone coal seams. However, studies on the coupled effects of moisture content and freezing temperature on the mechanical strength and energy response characteristics of gas-bearing coal after freezing remain relatively scarce. Uniaxial compression tests and gas desorption experiments were conducted, and mercury intrusion porosimetry (MIP) was used to characterize the pore structure changes before and after freezing. The results show that the uniaxial compressive strength and elastic modulus first increase and then decrease with increasing moisture content, peaking near 4.5% moisture content; both continuously increase with decreasing freezing temperature. Title: A temporal-spatial-spectral Mamba for hyperspectral video reconstruction
Abstract: Hyperspectral video (HSV) is valuable for dynamic scene analysis, yet direct acquisition of HSV is challenging due to its huge data volume. Title: Conversion of sodium carboxymethyl cellulose into N-doped porous carbon as efficient CO2 adsorbent

Title: Engineering multifunctional ionic covalent organic frameworks with synergistic hydrogen-bond and nucleophilic sites for efficient CO2 fixation

Authors: Su L.; Lu W.
Title: Fractional-order fuzzy cognitive maps: A framework for long-term forecasting of multivariate time series

Title: Sustainable syngas production by photothermal dry reforming of bio-ethanol over a Ni/Mn0.1Ce0.9O2 catalyst

Title: Fast semi-supervised graph clustering by directly solving pairwise constrained problem

Title: A graph-based direct association strategy with fuzzy interpretability for linking individual coal properties in coal blending schemes to coke quality

Title: Integrated Waste-to-Energy Systems: A comprehensive review of Technologies, decision Frameworks, and sustainability metrics
Abstract: Rising waste generation and growing energy demand have driven global interest in Waste-to-Energy (WtE) systems as a pathway toward sustainable waste management and resource recovery. Title: Contrastive label enhancement-based multi-label feature selection

Title: Investigation on thermo-hydraulic performance of supercritical CO2 in heated horizontal serpentine tubes

Title: The effects of risk perception based on local or global information in suppressing the spread of infectious diseases
Source title: International Journal of Modern Physics C
Abstract: This paper aims to investigate the role of individuals’ perceptions of infection risk in suppressing the spread of infectious diseases. It also examines whether global or local information is more effective in preventing infections. We developed an agent-based model in which 100000 individuals are connected in a small-world network. Infection information for the entire population was classified as global information, and infection information for the surroundings of a specific individual was classified as local information. The degree of response to infection risk information was measured using a normalized tunable sigmoid function. Higher sensitivity to infection risk increases the implementation of preventive measures, which reduces the spread of infectious disease. The use of global information on infection risk has been shown to be more useful in suppressing infections in general. However, if infected people around us can be recognized immediately and personal quarantine is quickly followed, the use of local information has been shown to be the most cost-effective way to end infections. Our study emphasizes the importance of individuals recognizing and responding to infected people around them to effectively control the spread of infectious diseases. It demonstrates that higher sensitivity to infection risk leads to better adherence to preventive measures, which in turn reduces disease transmission. These findings suggest that individual awareness and behavior play a critical role in managing infectious diseases. © 2027 World Scientific Publishing Company.

Authors: Wang Y.; Zhang A.; Chu W.; Qi C.; Zhou T.; Pan Y.; Wang Y.; Wang C.; Liu Y.; Wang W.
Title: Nano-engineered hydrocolloid-based delivery systems for natural flavonoids: From structural diversity to bioavailability enhancement and therapeutic applications
Abstract: Natural flavonoids exhibit promising biological activities but are severely limited by poor solubility, low stability, and low bioavailability. This review systematically summarizes the structural classification of flavonoids and provides a comprehensive overview of major hydrocolloid-based delivery systems, including self-assembled nanoparticles, emulsions, hydrogels, micelles, metal–organic frameworks, stimuli-responsive systems, and biomimetic platforms. Unlike existing reviews, this work systematically summarizes and compares the applications, functional characteristics, and therapeutic outcomes of each delivery platform in flavonoid delivery, covering a broad range of disease scenarios including cancer, neurodegenerative diseases, cardiovascular diseases, metabolic disorders, inflammatory injuries, and infectious diseases. We further identify key challenges that natural flavonoids face in practical precision medicine applications and functional food, including biosafety evaluation, scalable production, standardized characterization, and clinical validation. This review aims to provide systematic guidance for rational design of flavonoid delivery systems and advances their translation into precision medicine and functional foods. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Chen G.; Jin X.; Shang Y.; Song Z.; Zhang S.
Title: A residual-correction-based panel data model for predicting dam deformation considering hysteresis and coupling effects
Abstract: In this paper, we propose a residual-correction-based panel data model that accounts for both the hysteresis effect of the water level and the spatial coupling of deformation. First, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) eliminates multicollinearity among water-level-related factors. A Least Squares Support Vector Regression (LSSVR) model tuned by random search then performs single-point prediction at each monitoring point. These predictions serve as supplementary inputs to the HPCASTC panel data model for joint multi-point prediction. Next, an eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model optimized by Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) corrects the HPCASTC residuals, and Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) are employed to quantitatively interpret the predictions. The approach is validated using initial-stage deformation measurements from six monitoring points at different elevations of a concrete arch dam. The results show that, compared with the traditional HST model, the proposed model reduces the average mean square error (MSE) by 57.32%, the root mean square error (RMSE) by 39.95%, the mean absolute error (MAE) by 40.63% and the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) by 40.62%, while increasing the coefficient of determination(R2) by 57.03%. This work offers a novel modeling approach that combines high accuracy with strong interpretability for monitoring and assessing the overall structural behavior of dams. © The Author(s) under exclusive licence to Sociedade Brasileira de Matemática Aplicada e Computacional 2026.

Authors: Liu J.; Peng B.; Wang R.; Zhang Z.; Miao Z.; Wang Z.; Jia N.; Lv W.
Title: Carbon dots stabilized CO2 micro-nanobubbles for enhanced imbibition oil recovery: Interfacial dynamics and pore-scale oil mobilization
Abstract: CO2 micro-nanobubbles (MNBs) are promising gas-dispersed fluids for enhancing oil recovery in low-permeability and tight reservoirs, but their stability-dependent imbibition performance and pore-scale mobilization mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. Building on our previous development of carbon dots (CDs)-surfactant stabilized CO2 MNBs, this study investigates the oil–water interfacial behavior, imbibition recovery, and pore-scale processes of the CAP-CDs CO2 MNBs system. CAP substantially reduced oil–water interfacial tension (IFT) and exhibited relatively rapid initial oil production, whereas adding CDs slightly increased equilibrium IFT but enhanced wettability alteration. CAP-CDs CO2 MNBs achieved the highest final imbibition recovery of 16.5 %, compared with 13.11 % for CAP CO2 MNBs and 9.29 % for CAP. A conservative scalar concentration field was coupled with the phase-field method using experimentally based IFT and contact-angle descriptions to examine concentration-dependent interfacial dynamics, including potential Marangoni effects. The results suggest that uniformly prescribing the minimum equilibrium IFT and final water-wet contact angle may overestimate oil recovery. By accounting for active-component transport and the resulting local variations in interfacial properties, the concentration-responsive model provides a more physically representative description of oil–water interface evolution. Further simulations showed microbubble migration, coalescence, and temporary retention at pore throats, accompanied by changes in active-component distributions. These processes suggest possible local flow redistribution and interfacial disturbances associated with bubble motion. Overall, the results suggest that base-fluid interfacial regulation and bubble-related transport processes jointly contribute to improved imbibition performance, with CDs contributing through enhanced wettability alteration and the improved microbubble stability established in our previous work. Title: Structural properties and radical-scavenging antioxidative potential of feruloylated sugar beet pulp pectin extracted by thermal microwave autoclaving
Abstract: Pectic substances from sugar beet pulp (SBP) were extracted by a pressurized thermal microwave-assisted extraction, TMAE (2.56 bar, 135 °C) at different pH levels (2.5, 3.5, 4.3) and compared with a non-thermal extraction, NTMAE (1.03 bar, 25 °C) at the same pH levels. Recovered SBP-pectins were characterized for extraction yield (dry basis), degree of esterification, degree of acetylation, ferulic acid content, monosaccharide composition, viscosity molecular weight (intrinsic viscosity), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and antioxidant capacity was assessed by radical-scavenging (RS) assays. TMAE obtained statistically significantly (p < 0.05) higher yields than NTMAE, reaching 19.9 % at pH 2.5 and 11.80 % for NTMAE. Across pH 2.5-4.3, SBP pectins exhibited high degrees of esterification (56.68- 64.55 %) and acetylation (14.32 -17.41 %), consistent with typical SBP pectin with solubility. Monosaccharide profiling indicated arabinose-rich, rhamnogalacturonan-I-type pectins with comparatively low molecular weight. Significantly, TMAE increased ferulic acid content (2.44 -2.71 %) relative to NTMAE (2.27 -2.34 %), supporting the enhanced RS potential of the TMAE extracts. XRD showed predominantly amorphous phases, and TGA obtained low ash residues (3.97-4.72 %), indicating adequate purity of SBP. Overall, pressurized TMAE could be explored as a green, scalable approach to produce feruloylated SBP pectin with a desirable structure and antioxidant capacity for food applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Cui Y.; Fu G.; Yang L.; Zhang J.; Sun J.
Title: Regulating the electronic environment of Co sites in UiO-66 catalysts for enhanced oxidative carboxylation of olefins with CO2
Abstract: Developing multifunctional catalysts with integrated active sites for the direct oxidative carboxylation of olefins with CO2 to cyclic carbonates remains a significant challenge. Herein, three Zr-based MOFs with missing linker defects, UiO-66-R (R = -H, –NH2, and –NO2), were synthesized using acetic acid as modulator and terephthalic acid with different substituents as linkers, followed by the incorporation of Co sites via post-synthetic metallation to afford UiO-66-R(Co) catalysts. This strategy enabled modulation of the electronic environment of Co sites through linker substituents, leading to distinct catalytic activities in direct oxidative carboxylation of styrene to styrene carbonate (SC). At 80 ℃, 1.0 MPa CO2, and 8 h, UiO-66-NH2(Co) exhibited the best catalytic performance, achieving 96.1 % styrene conversion and 78.1 % SC selectivity. This enhanced catalytic performance arose from the synergy among multiple active sites. Specifically, the –NH2 groups played a crucial dual role: enhancing the electron density of Co sites via electron-donating effects to promote styrene epoxidation, while simultaneously acting as Lewis-basic sites to facilitate CO2 adsorption and activation. Meanwhile, the redox-active Co2+ sites, Lewis-acidic Zr4+/Co2+ sites, and nucleophilic Br− species worked synergistically, collectively enabling the efficient tandem transformation of styrene epoxidation and CO2 cycloaddition to obtain SC. DFT calculations on the epoxidation pathway further revealed that UiO-66-NH2(Co) exhibited the lowest activation barrier, thereby helping to explain the linker substituent effect on catalytic activity. Moreover, the catalyst was applicable to a range of olefins and showed good recyclability over five consecutive cycles. This work establishes a feasible linker substitution strategy for tuning the electronic environment of metal sites, offering valuable guidelines for the rational design of multifunctional catalysts for CO2 fixation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wang H.; Zhan L.; Hu Y.; Xu W.; Chen Y.
Title: An equivalent model for flow and solute transport in rough fractures based on a comprehensive roughness parameter
Abstract: Accurate prediction of solute transport in rough rock fractures is critical for the long-term safety assessment of engineering systems such as deep geological disposal of high-level radioactive waste. This study develops an equivalent modeling framework for conservative solute transport in three-dimensional self-affine rough single fractures under laminar-flow conditions. High-resolution three-dimensional numerical simulations were conducted to obtain flow responses and breakthrough curves (BTCs) under different rough-fracture geometric conditions, providing the dataset used to calibrate the equivalent relationships. To characterize the coupled effects of surface morphology and aperture variability, a comprehensive roughness parameter R is introduced. A geometric tortuosity function T(H) is further used to describe the effect of surface morphology on effective diffusion. Based on these geometric descriptions, calibrated relationships are established for the equivalent hydraulic aperture, the transport velocity adjustment coefficient, and the mechanical dispersion parameter. This framework enables BTCs to be predicted from fracture geometric characteristics and hydraulic conditions, without performing repeated three-dimensional flow and transport simulations. The predictive performance of the framework was evaluated using calibration cases and a validation set. For the calibration cases, the root mean square error (RMSE) values of BTC prediction are generally below 0.06. For the validation set, both the median and mean RMSE values are below 0.04 for all aperture groups. These results indicate that the framework can predict BTCs under different rough-fracture geometric conditions with relatively low computational cost, providing a useful basis for further analysis of solute transport in rough fractures. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd
