Title: Multiparameter screening of crude oils under microwave irradiation: Asphaltene reduction, colloidal stability, and upgrading performance
Abstract: The rising global energy demand and the progressive depletion of conventional light crude oil reserves have increased interest in heavy crude oil upgrading. Microwave irradiation offers a promising alternative for viscosity reduction and asphaltene management. This study presents a systematic screening of seven crude oil samples (A–G) under 2.45 GHz microwave irradiation at 0, 30, 60, 120, and 240 s. A multiparameter approach was employed, including thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), energy dispersive Xray spectroscopy (EDAX), dielectric loss tangent, SARA (saturates, aromatics, resins, and asphaltenes) fractionation, Colloidal Instability Index (CII), rheology, and CHNSO elemental analysis. Sample A exhibits the most balanced performance—entangled morphology, high sulfur (3.15 wt%), efficient sulfur removal (–20.63%), decreasing CII (1.21→0.73), and metastable stability—making it the top candidate for microwave upgrading. Sample F ranks second, reaching metastable CII (0.86) at 30 s. Samples G, C, and D show moderate performance but remain CIIunstable. Sample B has the highest loss tangent (0.2099) but the worst stability (CII'1.65) and severe viscosity increase. Sample E achieves the highest asphaltene reduction (60.71%) due to its very low initial asphaltene (0.28 wt%) but suffers from poor thermal stability, weak microwave absorption, and an unfavorable CII trend. Notably, greater asphaltene reduction does not ensure improved colloidal stability. Based on this multiparameter screening, samples A and F are proposed for further optimization, whereas samples B and E are not recommended for microwaveassisted upgrading. Copyright © 2026. Authors: Lee J.-B.; Jeon J.-H.; Lee G.-W.; Kim J.-Y.; Kim H.-R.; Yu E.-U.; Pak S.-J.; Han S.-J.; Mazari S.A.; Mun T.-Y.; Moon J.-H.
Title: Comparative techno-economic and life cycle assessment of ammonia co-firing with different ammonia production routes in a 1100 MWe ultra-supercritical CFB coal power plant
Abstract: Ammonia (NH3) co-firing is a practical option for reducing direct CO2 emissions from coal-fired power plants while utilizing existing infrastructure. However, its overall environmental and economic feasibility depends strongly on the NH3 supply pathway and policy support. This study evaluated the process performance, cradle-to-gate environmental impacts, and economic feasibility of NH3 co-firing in a 1,100 MW ultra-supercritical circulating fluidized bed (USC-CFB) coal-fired power plant. The NH3 co-firing ratio was varied from 0 % to 50 % (HHV basis), and NH3 was supplied from fossil-based (grey), fossil-based with carbon capture (blue), and renewable (green) production routes. Life cycle assessment, techno-economic analysis, policy scenario analysis, sensitivity analysis, and Monte Carlo-based uncertainty analysis were conducted. Increasing the NH3 co-firing ratio reduced direct CO2 emissions at the power generation stage but decreased gross power output and net plant efficiency. At 50 % NH3 co-firing, green NH3 reduced global warming potential by 33.1 % relative to baseline case, whereas grey and blue NH3 increased by 18.1 % and 2.0 %, respectively. The levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) increased with NH3 co-firing ratio for all pathways in the order of grey < blue < green, mainly because of NH3 fuel cost. With policy support, the LCOE of green NH3 could be reduced to below 100 $/MWh in the range of 20–40 % NH3 co-firing ratios. Overall, the combination of green NH3, intermediate co-firing ratios, and policy support provided the most favorable balance between GWP reduction and economic performance among the evaluated cases. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: AIE-active non-traditional D-π-A organogel for sensing amine vapor via aza-Michael addition
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Fluorescent solid-state sensors are attractive platforms for the on-site detection of volatile organic amines due to the advantages of visual readout, rapid mass transfer, and device compatibility. Here, we report an AIE-active non-traditional D–π–A organogelator, MMT-PMO , constructed from a methoxyphenyl donor, a thiophene π bridge, and a dicyanovinyl acceptor. Without conventional flexible auxiliaries, MMT-PMO forms a stable supramolecular organogel in several polar organic solvents, driven by balanced slipped π–π stacking of the rigid D–π–A skeleton, and further producing ordered three-dimensional networks. The resulting xerogel functions as a solid-state amine-vapor sensor: nucleophilic primary and secondary amines, particularly piperidine, trigger pronounced fluorescence quenching and visual darkening. Mechanistic 1H NMR and HRMS demonstrate that a piperidine unit was introduced on the vinyl unit via aza-Michael addition, thereby interrupting the emissive D–π–A system. This work provides a chemically specific design strategy for a non-traditional π-organogel that translates covalent amine capture into a macroscopic optical response. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: C/C-SiC composite brake discs under high-speed service conditions: Full-scale braking fatigue tests and mechanical property evolution
Abstract: C/C-SiC composites have low density, high specific strength, excellent high-temperature resistance, and stable friction and wear properties. It is one of the preferred materials for high-speed train brake discs. Full-scale brake fatigue tests and mechanical tests of carbon-ceramic composites are carried out at speeds from 50 to 400 km/h. The evolution of braking performance, structural morphology, microstructure and mechanical properties was systematically investigated. The results show that with the increase of initial braking speed, the friction coefficient of the material decreases at low speed, rises at medium speed, and tends to be stable at high speed. Accumulated braking fatigue cycles reduce the average friction coefficient. Increasing braking pressure decreases both the amplitude and scatter of the friction coefficient. Under wet conditions, the friction coefficient exhibits higher amplitude and greater stability than under dry conditions. After fatigue service, material density and porosity exhibit significant spatial heterogeneity, and the mechanical properties show strong anisotropy. Microscopic damage modes include matrix cracking, interface debonding, and pore expansion. Macroscopic failures are dominated by warping and spalling of SiC coating as well as cracks around bolt holes, which are identified as structural weak positions. Copyright © 2026. Title: Modified lignin promotes plant development by nitrate assimilation and iron-dependent metabolic reprogramming
Abstract: In recent years, agricultural development has received considerable attention due to the growing global demand for sustainable food production and environmental stewardship. Trace elements and nitrogen are essential nutrients that critically regulate plant seedling growth. Lignin, the second most abundant natural organic macromolecule after cellulose, is abundantly present in the low-cost byproduct from industrial biorefineries. Here, the modified lignin compounds were prepared by grafting urea onto lignin via the Mannich reaction, which could promote rice seedling growth through the slow release of nitrogen during lignin degradation. The as-prepared modified lignin showed strong ion-chelating properties, which can simultaneously provide nitrogen nutrition and metal trace elements. Then, multi-technique characterization strategies for the resulting lignin-based complexes were performed to systematically evaluate their physicochemical properties, including DLS, TEM, GPC, FTIR, XPS, and 13C NMR. Multi-dimensional analytical strategies were also applied to analyze plant growing status, such as root/shoot dimensions and biomass, chlorophyll quantification and EdU staining. Last, RNA sequencing analysis unraveled the underlying molecular mechanisms of L-Urea/Fe on seedlings, including enhanced nutrient reservoir activity and significant upregulation of pathways related to nitrate transport, assimilation and response. Furthermore, α-amylase activity, iron-binding activity and FAD-binding (a key cofactor for iron-dependent oxidoreductases), were also significantly increased in seedlings. This work clarified the interactive regulatory network of nitrogen utilization, iron homeostasis and antioxidant defense of plants by modified lignin, providing solid evidence for the utilization of eco-friendly lignin-derived fertilizers to boost plants seedling growth. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Wu F.; Lan X.; Kong C.; Sun Z.; Zhou S.; Li Z.
Title: Synthesis of high-energy–density jet fuel from lignin-derived phenols and norbornene catalyzed over acetic acid modified Pd/HY
Abstract: A kind of high-energy–density jet fuel was synthesized from lignin-derived phenols and norbornene via a one-pot alkylation/hydrodeoxygenation reaction. First, HY exhibited good catalytic activity for the alkylation of guaiacol and norbornene, mainly attributed to its appropriate pore size and strong acid sites. Further, in the one-pot reaction, the bifunctional catalyst 1%Pd/HY (AA, 0.25) modified with 0.25 mol/L acetic acid (AA) demonstrated the best catalytic performance. The increased total acid density (0.153 mmol/g) and acid strength, along with the higher Pd0 proportion and binding energy of 1%Pd/HY (AA, 0.25), were beneficial for both alkylation and hydrodeoxygenation. Substrate expansion indicated that 1%Pd/HY (0.25, AA) has good applicability to various lignin-derived phenols. Finally, a high-energy–density jet fuel was synthesized from simulated soft lignin oil and norbornene in the one-pot reaction. The fuel had good properties (0.958 g/mL, 39.94 MJ/L, freezing point lower than −80 ℃). This work provided a practical route for producing high-energy–density jet fuel from the co-conversion of lignin-derived phenols and petroleum-based norbornene. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Yang T.; Wu J.; Fan J.; Tang X.; Zhao J.; Wei C.; Wang G.; Sun Z.; Peng H.
Title: Vibration-induced multiscale nonlinear tribo-dynamics for resonant piezoelectric actuators: A case study of a traveling-wave ultrasonic motor
Abstract: Piezoelectric actuators are critical in precision engineering, yet their performance is governed by complex multiscale tribological processes at the transmission interface that remain poorly understood. This paper develops a multiscale nonlinear tribo-dynamic framework for resonant-type piezoelectric actuators, integrating piezoelectric element vibration, multiscale contact mechanics, asperity-level micro-stick-slip friction, and mover dynamics. A multi-stage elasto-plastic Iwan model is proposed for tangential friction under time-varying normal load, where the distribution function of tangential yield forces is derived directly from a scale-coupling homogenized contact model that bridges microscale contact behavior with macroscopic deformation. The framework incorporates fractal surface description, linking manufacturing parameters to output performance. Compared with conventional binary stick-slip assumptions, the model predicts coexisting micro-stick and micro-slip contributions during the contact-active portions of the vibration cycle. The framework is validated by fretting tests and torque-speed measurements. Results show that surface roughness governs actuation by modulating micro-stick-slip competition. Transient simulations capture start-up, step driving, and power-off dynamics. This work provides a modeling paradigm for resonant piezoelectric actuators, offering a physics-based tool for performance prediction and interface optimization. Copyright © 2026. Title: Experimental study on biomass utilization in ammonia co-firing for carbon-neutral power generation
Abstract: Ammonia co-firing offers a practical route to decarbonize pulverized-coal power plants without major retrofitting, but its low reactivity and high fuel-bound nitrogen content promote elevated NOx emissions. Co-firing reactive biomass can suppress NOx formation, yet the combined influence of fuel reactivity and ammonia injection strategy has rarely been examined under unified conditions, and combustion data for bio-char in ammonia co-firing remain scarce. In this study, coal–ammonia co-firing experiments were conducted in a drop tube furnace (DTF) at 1300°C using woody biomass and torrefied bio-char as partial coal substitutes at blending ratios of 10–30 wt%, under both pre-mixed and staged ammonia injection (20% energy fraction). Torrefaction at 290°C raised the thermally treated biomass grindability index (TTBGI) from 6.44 to 67.85, comparable to the coal Hardgrove grindability index of 55, while shifting combustion reactivity and activation-energy distributions toward coal-like values. Staged ammonia injection consistently outperformed pre-mixing in NOx control, lowering emissions to approximately 135 ppm at a 10 wt% blending ratio, as upstream oxygen consumption by the reactive blended fuel established a stronger downstream reducing zone. These results demonstrate that pairing torrefied bio-char with staged ammonia injection provides a technically viable pathway for the phased, carbon–neutral transition of existing coal-fired power generation. Author full names: Paula, Kurzawska-Pietrowicz (57215346670); Dawid, Michalak (60934459600); Remigiusz, Jasiński (60934459700); Andrzej, Ziółkowski (60934043300)
Title: Green hydrogen and CO2 capture for synthetic aviation fuels: a review of power-to-liquid pathways, sustainability metrics, and commercial scale-up challenges
Abstract: This review provides a structured, pathway-level assessment of Power-to-Liquid (PtL) e-fuel production for aviation, covering hydrogen electrolysis (AWE, PEM, SOEC, AEM), CO2-to-syngas conversion (reverse water–gas shift vs. co-electrolysis), fuel synthesis routes (Fischer–Tropsch, methanol-to-jet, DME-to-jet, ethanol-to-jet), and CO2 sourcing strategies (point-source, biogenic, direct air capture), benchmarked against their technology readiness and EU RFNBO regulatory eligibility. A synthesis of life-cycle assessment literature shows that the well-to-wake carbon intensity of PtL jet fuel spans an unusually wide range, from below 8 gCO2e/MJ to over 100 gCO2e/MJ, occasionally exceeding the fossil Jet A-1 baseline, driven primarily by the carbon intensity of the electricity source rather than the CO2 origin. Across the studies compared, the mean reported value (21.3 gCO2e/MJ) still satisfies the ' 70% reduction threshold required under the ReFuelEU Aviation Regulation. Current PtL production costs (2.2–5.5 USD/L, up to ∼ 8 times higher than fossil Jet A-1) are projected to fall to 0.71–0.81 USD/L by 2050, driven mainly by declining electrolyzer and renewable electricity costs. A pathway-level comparison combining electrolyzer type, CO2 source, and synthesis route reveals substantial, unevenly distributed gaps in reported techno-economic data across the PtL value chain. The review further identifies the 2036 regulatory cut-off for fossil point-source CO2 eligibility and the geographic mismatch between renewable electricity and CO2 feedstock availability as underexplored constraints on long-term PtL competitiveness, while noting that commercial deployment remains limited (four operating plants as of 2025) despite a project pipeline expected to exceed 250,000 t/year of capacity in the coming years. Title: Integrated UHPLC-HRMS and field-induced droplet ionization mass spectrometry for rapid functional screening of photoactive furanocoumarins in Angelica dahurica
Abstract: Photoactive constituents in medicinal and edible plants can induce photooxidative reactions and pose potential safety risks, yet their rapid identification remains challenging. Herein, a field-induced droplet ionization mass spectrometry (FIDI-MS)-based strategy was developed to evaluate the photooxidative activity of Angelica dahurica . Ethanol extracts exhibited stronger photooxidative activity than aqueous extracts owing to their higher contents of lipophilic furanocoumarins. Six furanocoumarins, including imperatorin, isoimperatorin, psoralen, bergapten, byakangelicol, and phellopterin, were identified as the major photoactive constituents. Comparative analysis indicated that an intact furanocoumarin chromophore was essential for photooxidative activity, while lipophilicity further influenced the relative oxidation index. FIDI-MS results were consistent with conventional ROS assays. This study provides a rapid platform for identifying photoactive phytochemicals and evaluating the photooxidative risks of medicinal and edible plant resources. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Highly stable and dispersed Ni/TiO2 catalysts for CO2 Methanation: In-situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy study on active site stability
Abstract: Thermal deactivation and sintering remain critical challenges for nickel (Ni)-based catalysts in CO2 methanation (Sabatier reaction). In this study, highly dispersed Ni/TiO2 catalysts were synthesized via a citric acid (CA)-assisted solid-state method, leveraging the strong metal-support interaction (SMSI) of TiO2 to enhance catalytic stability. Optimization of the Ni:CA molar ratio revealed that a 1:2 ratio yielded superior Ni nanoparticle dispersion and strongest metal-support interaction, as confirmed by XRD, TEM, and H2-TPR, where a notable shift to higher reduction temperatures indicated strong Ni anchoring on TiO2. The optimized 20 wt% Ni/TiO2 catalyst achieved high CO2 conversion with near 100% CH4 selectivity below 350 °C and demonstrated exceptional durability with no measurable activity loss over 60 h of continuous operation. Title: Multiscale mechanisms of diamond tool wear in low-temperature ultrasonic-assisted grinding and polishing
Abstract: To elucidate the synergistic mechanisms by which low-temperature cooling and ultrasonic vibration suppress diamond tool wear, a molecular dynamics (MD) model of low-temperature ultrasonic-assisted grinding and polishing (LUGP) was established. The effects of conventional grinding and polishing (CGP), low-temperature grinding and polishing (LGP), and LUGP on tool–workpiece interfacial temperature evolution, elemental migration, atomic-structure evolution, and machined surface quality were comparatively investigated. The simulation results indicated that low-temperature cooling reduced interfacial heat accumulation and the thermal activation of tool-surface atoms. The introduction of ultrasonic vibration induced periodic contact-separation at the tool–workpiece interface, shortened the effective contact duration, and consequently further suppressed the accumulation of interfacial damage. The experimental observations were consistent with the wear-suppression mechanisms revealed by the MD simulations. The maximum tool–workpiece interfacial temperature decreased from 178.6 °C under CGP to 73.8 °C under LUGP, thereby suppressing adhesive, oxidative, and diffusion wear of the tool. Concurrently, scratching, material adhesion, and localized damage on the machined surface were markedly reduced, while the S  a  value of the mold steel decreased from 0.65 to 0.29 μm. Title: Multifidelity emulation in parameter inference problems: When low-fidelity models are better than high-fidelity counterparts
Source title: Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference
Abstract: Computer simulations are invaluable for understanding complex scientific and engineering phenomena, but their use in statistical inference can be prohibitively expensive. Emulators provide computationally tractable approximations to such simulators, yet in practice multiple emulators of differing fidelity and complexity may be available, making model selection non-trivial. In this work, we investigate multifidelity emulation for inverse problems, namely parameter inference from data, after defining the model fidelities as hierarchical approximations to a ‘gold-standard’ simulator, that is, as low- and high-fidelity emulators. We show, both theoretically and empirically, that low-fidelity emulators of multivariate simulator outputs can, despite being less accurate than their high-fidelity counterparts from a forward-prediction perspective, yield more accurate parameter inference at lower computational cost. Thus, we propose a novel multifidelity inference framework that adaptively switches between, or combines, high- and low-fidelity emulators using a classifier that identifies regions of parameter space in which each fidelity is expected to provide more accurate inference. We further introduce a combined multifidelity strategy incorporating both mechanisms and demonstrate that it can outperform inference based on single (high-) fidelity emulators. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Multiscale numerical study of Plasma-Assisted combustion in ammonia and Ammonia–Hydrogen blends
Abstract: Ammonia and hydrogen are widely regarded as promising zero-carbon alternatives to conventional fossil fuels. However, ammonia combustion presents several critical challenges, including poor ignitability, low flame propagation rates, and significant NOx emissions. Plasma-assisted combustion (PAC) has emerged as a potential strategy to address these limitations, attracting growing research interest in recent years. This study presents a numerical investigation of nanosecond pulsed plasma discharges applied to ammonia and ammonia–hydrogen combustion in air. Simulations are performed using the open-source plasma solver ChemPlasKin, both as a standalone tool and in coupled frameworks with Cantera and OpenFOAM, across a range of operating conditions. A systematic analysis is conducted on the impacts of non‑thermal plasma on ignition delay time (IDT), laminar burning velocity (LBV), and NOx emissions. In addition, the study separates plasma‑driven thermal and kinetic effects and introduces two‑dimensional simulations for plasma‑assisted ammonia–hydrogen flames. The results reveal concurrent reductions in IDT, NOx emissions, and flame thickness, alongside increases in LBV and heat release rate. Plasma enhancement is highly sensitive to both the operating regime and H2 blend fraction. Across equivalence ratios, the strongest plasma impact occurs near stoichiometric (slightly lean to slightly rich), whereas increasing pressure substantially diminishes its effectiveness. Under atmospheric pressure and lean conditions, reductions of over 99 % in IDT and 36 % in NO emissions, along with a 39 % increase in LBV, are noticed. Both plasma-driven thermal and kinetic pathways are critical for shortening IDT; in contrast, gains in LBV are dominated by thermal effects. Title: Construction of a polyoxometalate-based composite catalyst for efficient extractive and oxidative desulfurization of fuel
Abstract: A novel polyoxometalate-based composite SiO2@VTES@IL-PW11 was constructed via stepwise functionalization of mesoporous SiO2 with vinyltriethoxysilane (VTES) and lacunary Keggin-type phosphotungstate (PW11). The successful immobilization of PW11 onto the support was confirmed by FT-IR, N2 adsorption-desorption, TGA, XPS, TEM, and EDS. Catalytic tests demonstrated that the SiO2@VTES@IL-PW11 exhibits excellent desulfurization activity, achieving 99.49% DBT removal under the optimized reaction conditions. The oxidation of DBT followed pseudo-first-order kinetics with an apparent activation energy of 14.26 kJ·mol-1. The catalyst also showed good activity toward various sulfur compounds, with removal efficiencies following the order DBT > 4-MDBT > 4,6-DMDBT > BT. Notably, the catalyst maintained a DBT removal efficiency of over 94% after ten consecutive cycles, demonstrating exceptional structural stability and reusability. Title: Acid–base bifunctional MgCeO composites for efficient synthesis of dimethyl carbonate via transesterification of ethylene carbonate
Abstract: As a crucial building block, dimethyl carbonate (DMC) has been extensively applied in modern chemical industries. The transesterification reaction of ethylene carbonate (EC) with methanol is regarded as a promising route for the clean synthesis of DMC. Accordingly, the development of highly efficient and durable heterogeneous catalysts has attracted considerable attention for implementing this synthetic strategy. Herein, a series of MgO–CeO2 composites (Mg m Ce1O x ) were prepared via a facile co-precipitation method. The synthesized Mg m Ce1O x materials possessed both acidic and basic sites, and their distributions depended on the Ce contents. In the transesterification of EC with methanol, the Mg m Ce1O x materials demonstrated catalytic activity. Compared with pure MgO, Mg3Ce1O x showed not only higher catalytic activity under identical reaction conditions but also stable reusability, without leaching of catalytically active sites. A maximum DMC yield of 80.5% was achieved at 110 °C after 3 h of reaction. Meanwhile, the catalyst could be reused for at least six cycles without obvious decline in activity. Additionally, the catalyst was applicable to transesterification of propylene carbonate with methanol. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Lean limit extension Aspects of gasoline direct injection (GDI) engine with hydrogen fraction
Abstract: An experimental investigation was conducted on a spark-ignition gasoline direct injection (GDI) engine equipped with hydrogen port fuel injection (PFI) to investigate the effects of hydrogen enrichment on combustion characteristics, thermal efficiency, and exhaust emissions under lean-burn operation. Gasoline–hydrogen blends with different hydrogen mass fractions were tested at varying equivalence ratios, while spark timing was adjusted between 14° and 35° bTDC to compensate for hydrogen’s higher flame speed. However, hydrogen enrichment generally increased nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions because of higher in-cylinder combustion temperatures. Under homogeneous combustion conditions, hydrogen was supplied through port fuel injection (PFI) in the intake manifold with a start of injection (SOI) of 210° during the suction stroke, while the gasoline direct injection (GDI) SOI was set at 330° during the engine suction stroke. With a spark timing of 22° bTDC, 5.17% hydrogen by mass fraction reduced nitric oxide emissions by 0.29 g/kW-h and improved the hydrocarbon–NOx emission trade-off. Authors: Hu Q.; Yuan Z.; Zhang J.; Mi J.
Title: Multimodal anomaly detection based on multi-kernel fuzzy rough sets
Abstract: Multimodal data present significant challenges for anomaly detection due to their inherent fuzziness and uncertainty. Although fuzzy rough sets (FRS) offer a principled framework for handling uncertainty, existing FRS-based detectors may fail to preserve modality-specific structures or effectively exploit complementary information across modalities. To address this issue, this paper introduces a multi-kernel fuzzy rough set model for unsupervised multimodal anomaly detection (MKMAD). The proposed approach employs modality-specific kernel functions to extract similarity features, which are then integrated through T-norm operators to construct a unified fuzzy granular structure. Based on this fused structure, we develop multimodal fuzzy rough approximations for unlabeled data and establish their theoretical properties. The core innovation lies in characterizing anomaly degrees through granular approximation accuracy, where we define granular outlier factors that fundamentally differ from traditional sample-based approaches. Finally, anomaly scores are computed by aggregating these granular factors across different feature spaces. Extensive experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and practicality of our proposed framework in handling complex multimodal data environments. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Transfer learning-enhanced physics-informed neural network for uncertainty propagation analysis
Abstract: This paper proposes an uncertainty propagation analysis method based on transfer learning-enhanced Physics-Informed Neural Networks. The proposed method establishes an efficient framework for response distribution reconstruction by sequentially evaluating reliability information at multiple response levels and reusing previously learned physical information between adjacent response points. By leveraging the ability of PINNs to capture underlying physical knowledge, the method avoids repeated calls to the true performance function. A transfer learning-enhanced iterative mechanism is then employed, in which network parameters are sequentially inherited between adjacent response points so that the learned physical information can be continually reused, thereby reducing redundant retraining and accelerating convergence. The iteration continues until a prescribed reliability threshold is reached, after which the resulting discrete reliability information is used to reconstruct the cumulative distribution function of the response. Four examples are used to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Inc.

Title: Defect-regulated charge dynamics and ROS pathways in LaFeTiO₃ photocatalysts for enhanced antibiotic degradation under UVA irradiation
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Defect engineering can modify photogenerated charge-carrier behavior in perovskite photocatalysts without necessarily changing their optical band gap. In this study, La vacancies at the A-site were combined with Ti incorporation at the B-site to examine their effects on charge separation and reactive oxygen species (ROS) pathways in LaFeO₃ under UVA irradiation. A series of La₁₋ᵧFe₁₋ₓTiₓO₃ (x = 0.1, y = 0–0.15) photocatalysts were synthesized by a sol–gel method and evaluated for metronidazole (MTZ) degradation. The defect-engineered perovskite showed a similar optical band gap (~3.28 eV) to the reference material but higher photocatalytic activity, achieving nearly complete MTZ degradation within 70 min with an apparent rate constant of 0.2241 min−1. Photoluminescence, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and transient photocurrent measurements indicated reduced charge recombination and improved charge transfer after introducing La vacancies and Ti. Radical scavenging tests and electron spin resonance measurements showed that •OH was the main reactive species, while O₂•− also contributed to MTZ degradation. The higher contribution of •OH may be associated with electronic-structure changes caused by La vacancies, which may promote Fe3+/Fe2+ redox cycling and Fenton-like •OH generation. LC–MS analysis identified intermediates associated with hydroxylation, denitrification, and ring-cleavage reactions. The treatment achieved 44.3% TOC removal and reduced cytotoxicity based on the HeLa cell assay. The catalyst maintained its structure during repeated cycles, with low Fe/Ti leaching. Overall, the results indicate that combining La vacancies with Ti incorporation affects charge separation and ROS generation in LaFeO₃, supporting its application in photocatalytic treatment of pharmaceutical contaminants. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Thermoacoustic–flow coupling mechanism in an RP-3-fueled staged multi-swirl lean direct injection combustor
Abstract: Dynamic pressure measurements, CH* chemiluminescence imaging, hot-flow PIV and reacting large-eddy simulation (LES) were combined to investigate the combustion-mode transition with fuel–air ratio (FAR) and the associated thermoacoustic–flow coupling mechanism in an RP-3-fueled staged multi-swirl lean direct injection (LDI) combustor. As the FAR increased, the combustor transitioned from a low-fluctuation stable mode at FAR = 0.022–0.026 to a high-fluctuation unstable mode at FAR = 0.028–0.032. The normalized pressure fluctuation increased from 0.35 %–0.46 % to 3.95 %–5.02 %, while the global CH* fluctuation intensity increased from 5.6 %–6.5 % to 21.3 %–23.4 %. At FAR = 0.032, pressure and global CH* signals exhibited dominant peaks at 153.2 Hz and 153.4 Hz, respectively, indicating a well-organized thermoacoustic response. Rayleigh-like analysis showed that the main driving regions were located near the shear layers and downstream reaction zones, whereas the primary recirculation zone mainly contributed damping or weak feedback. Modal decomposition further showed that the CH* heat-release response and near-field velocity fluctuations shared a dominant frequency near 153 Hz, with coherent structures concentrated around the central shear layer, inner shear layer and recirculation-zone boundary. Reacting LES with inlet velocity forcing at the measured dominant frequency revealed that velocity oscillations periodically modified jet momentum, shear-layer position and recirculation-zone size, leading to localized flame blow-off, re-ignition and downstream propagation along the shear layer. These processes concentrated the CH response in the downstream reaction region and generated localized positive Rayleigh-like feedback. The experimental and numerical results support a localized thermoacoustic–flow coupling mechanism involving velocity-induced flame dynamics and pressure-coupled heat-release response. Title: Impact of liquid distributor design variables on film dynamics and heat and mass transfer on a horizontal flat tube falling film evaporator
Abstract: The liquid distributor plays a crucial role in controlling film formation and coupled heat and mass transfer in falling film evaporators. However, its effects on falling film behavior and heat and mass transfer over horizontal flat tubes remain poorly understood. A transient VOF model was therefore employed to investigate the effects of spray height, hole diameter, and hole spacing on film dynamics and the spatial distributions of heat and mass transfer. Based on the results, distributor-dependent correlations for heat and mass transfer were developed. The results show that increasing spray height, hole diameter, and hole spacing generally decreases film thickness and enhances mass transfer. Wave troughs, which occur predominantly over the middle and lower sections of the flat tube, are characterized by thinner liquid films and stronger mass transfer. Increasing hole spacing from 6 to 14 mm reduces the average film thickness by 28.4% and increases the average mass transfer rate by 65.6%. The local heat transfer coefficient decreases along the circumferential direction. Increasing spray height or hole diameter enhances heat transfer, whereas increasing hole spacing weakens it. Increasing spray height from 4 to 16 mm increases the average heat transfer coefficient by 58.9%. Sensitivity analysis identifies hole spacing as the dominant geometric variable. The proposed correlations predict 95.7% of the Nusselt data and 93.7% of the mass transfer rate data within ±15%. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for balancing film uniformity, heat transfer, and evaporation performance in the design of liquid distributors for horizontal flat tube systems. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Title: Thermo-responsive CO2-releasing alkali-activated low-calcium coal fly ash cementitious material for coal spontaneous combustion prevention
Abstract: CO2-loaded cementitious materials offer significant potential for both carbon sequestration and heat-triggered release for suppression of coal spontaneous combustion. However, simultaneously enhancing the active sites density and tailoring the CO2 thermal-releasing window remains a critical challenge. In this study, a high-performance CO2-loaded cementitious material was synthesized via the composite alkali-activation (NaOH/Na2SiO3) of low-calcium coal fly ash. The microstructural mechanism was elucidated through FTIR, 29Si MAS NMR, and EDS evaluations. Results demonstrate a controlled silicate supplementation effect with the composite alkali activator elevating the Si/Al molar ratio from a silicon-deficient value of 0.98 to an intermediate state of 1.35. Specifically, this 38% increase in the Si/Al molar ratio is accompanied by a 11% rise in Q3 silicate units. This stoichiometric synergy demonstrates that exogenous silicate monomers do not exclusively incorporate as surface-exposed, under-coordinated Q3 species with abundant active silanol groups (Si-OH), some of which densify into fully cross-linked Q4 networks. Title: Mechanistic insights into the effects of H2 and CO on NO removal by high-temperature reducing-zone ammonia injection
Abstract: High-temperature reducing-zone ammonia injection has emerged as a promising strategy for NOx control due to its cost-effectiveness and compatibility with existing combustion systems. Nevertheless, the effects of reducing gases on NO removal under such high-temperature reducing atmospheres, as well as the underlying mechanisms, remain poorly understood. In this work, the roles of reducing gases (H2 and CO) in the NO removal characteristics of NH3 were systematically investigated through experiments and kinetic modeling. NH3 injection into high-temperature, oxygen-deficient zone shifted the temperature window for NO removal toward higher temperatures, thereby extending the operating temperature window of conventional SNCR. Under oxygen-free conditions, H2 and CO exhibited negligible effects on NO removal, as their conversion pathways did not promote radical accumulation. In contrast, in the presence of O2, H2 oxidation pathways promote H radical generation, while CO suppressed H consumption via the chain-propagation reaction CO + OH ⇌ CO2 + H, which converted one radical species (OH) into another (H) without net radical generation. Consequently, the addition of CO and H2 facilitated rapid replenishment of the radical pool and shifted the temperature window toward lower temperatures. In particular, H2 significantly broadened the temperature window for NO removal at 0.1 % O2 but slightly narrowed it at higher O2 concentrations. In contrast, CO slightly narrowed the temperature window and reduced the maximum NO removal efficiency. Title: Mechano-thermo-chemical multi-field coupling failure life prediction of nickel-based superalloy GH4169
Abstract: In the aerospace industry, superalloys like GH4169 alloy are used for high-temperature structural components and are subject to severe conditions. Their deformation and failure are typical mechano-thermo-chemical multi-field coupling problems. To address the challenge of failure life prediction of GH4169 alloy in high-temperature and oxygen-containing environments, a mechano-thermo-chemical multi-field coupling constitutive model with damage is established. This model effectively unifies the processes of material deformation, heat transfer, mass diffusion, and chemical reactions. In high-temperature and oxygen-containing environments, the damage variable of GH4169 alloy is seen as the combined effect of creep damage, oxidation damage, and thermal-induced damage related to the change of material microstructure. These three damage mechanisms are intercoupled, and their evolution models are delved into. By coupling damage models via the weighted average approach, a mechano-thermo-chemical multi-field coupling damage evolution model is constructed. Model parameters for GH4169 alloy are determined through high-temperature pre-oxidation, anaerobic pre-heating, and creep tests, along with literature review. And the failure life and oxide thickness of GH4169 alloy under different stress, temperature, and oxygen concentration conditions are predicted. The predictions are in good agreement with the experimental results, which verifies the rationality of the proposed model. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Title: A comprehensive analysis of kinetic modeling in dry reforming of methane
Abstract: Dry reforming of methane (DRM) is a key reaction for syngas production from greenhouse gases (methane and carbon dioxide). Reaction kinetics predict reaction rates, identify and understand reaction mechanisms, and guide catalyst and reactor design. The modeling approaches are (i) empirical power law, (ii) mechanistic microkinetic, (iii) stochastic Monte Carlo, (iv) semi-empirical, and (v) AI-DFT hybrid frameworks. The analysis revealed that empirical and semi-empirical models primarily provide DRM activation energy for the catalyst. Microkinetic modeling has challenged traditional DRM understanding in notable ways. Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations explicitly resolve lateral interactions, diffusion, spatial inhomogeneity, and adsorbate correlations that mean-field microkinetics neglect, offering a mechanistically richer description of coverage-dependent chemistry. On the other hand, AI-DFT hybrid frameworks offer a data-efficient platform for screening catalyst compositions and architectures balancing methane turnover with carbon-oxidation rates. Title: Mechanism of shearer-induced CO release and its impact on oxidation activity of different rank coals
Abstract: Abnormal CO levels in the return air corner of a coal mining face do not necessarily originate solely from the oxidation of residual coal or spontaneous combustion in the goaf; the crushing, shearing, and frictional disturbances during shearer cutting operations may also induce rapid CO release. To elucidate the evolution patterns of CO release and oxidation activity in this process, lignite, bituminous coal, and anthracite were selected for study. A high-speed crusher was employed to simulate the cutting disturbances of a shearer, with varying processing times set from 10 to 50 s. The temperature rise, CO release, industrial composition, functional group structure, TG-DTG characteristics, and changes in apparent activation energy of the coal samples were systematically examined. The results indicate that the crushing-friction effect can cause a significant temperature increase and induce CO release in all three coal types within a short period. After 50 s of treatment, the maximum surface temperatures of lignite, bituminous coal, and anthracite rose to 51.9℃, 49.2℃, and 50.4℃, respectively. The CO emission concentration of lignite generally increased with prolonged treatment time, following the order of 50 s > 40 s > 30 s ≈ 20 s > 10 s; the CO emission from bituminous coal exhibited nonlinear variation; and the CO emission enhancement in anthracite was limited. Industrial analysis revealed that the moisture content of lignite, bituminous coal, and anthracite decreased from 11.24 %, 4.93 %, and 1.59 % to 6.06 %, 2.07 %, and 1.13 %, respectively, after 50 s of treatment. FTIR results demonstrated that the relative peak area of the carbonyl group in lignite decreased by approximately 91.1 % after 50 s of treatment compared to raw coal, while the phenolic hydroxyl and carboxyl groups in bituminous coal decreased by approximately 46.4 % and 55.4 %, respectively. The aliphatic structure in anthracite remained consistently low. The study reveals that CO release induced by the crushing-friction of a coal cutter is not merely a physical desorption process but rather a result of the combined effects of frictional temperature rise, pore opening, mechanochemical activation, and functional group transformation. Title: Influence of thermal oxidation on CeO2 physicochemical properties during diesel soot combustion
Abstract: The effects of thermal oxidation on CeO2 catalyst on cordierite substrate surface during diesel soot combustion have been investigated in the present study. The morphological characteristics were characterized by SEM, Raman, BET, XRD, and the surface contents and catalytic performance were tested by ICP-OES, XPS, O2-TPD and TGA. Concurrently, abundant oxygen vacancies and Ce3+ ions were generated on the cordierite surface. These thermally induced evolutions in both cordierite and CeO2 morphology significantly enhanced diesel soot reactivity and catalytic performance. The above results highlight that thermal oxidation drives a reconstruction of the surface structure and chemical composition of the CeO2 catalyst. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Zein-β-cyclodextrin composite particles for clove essential oil-loaded high internal phase Pickering emulsions: Preparation, characterization and functional fat mimicry of meat products

Title: Systematic feature selections using three-way granulation models and three-view uncertainty measures in neighborhood decision systems
Abstract: Feature selections facilitate data learning, and they resort to various uncertainty measures and granulation models. Discrimination indices in neighborhood rough sets (NRSs) ignore the informatization priority, while feature weights from partition coefficients in weighted neighborhood rough sets (WNRSs) consider only algebraic representations, so feature selections of the two factors are worth advancing via measure reinforcement and model deepening. In this paper, three-way granulation models and three-view uncertainty measures are structurally established in neighborhood decision systems, so that heuristic algorithms of feature selections are systematically acquired for learning achievements. Firstly on NRSs, new information measures and feature weights are proposed from discrimination indices; the former measures bring improvements by prioritizing informatization, while the later weights induce new WNRSs by information enrichment. Then by informational feature weights, NRSs are further optimized from similarity measures (rather than distance measures), and thus weighted similarity neighborhood rough sets (WSNRSs) emerge as the third model; there, information measures are correspondingly constructed by promoting those of NRSs, and they are combined with dependency degrees to produce algebra-information fusion measures and three-view uncertainty measures, whose granulation monotonicity/non-monotonicity is revealed. Furthermore, feature selections and their heuristic algorithms are determined by measures and models; 2 algorithms emerge by information measures on NRSs, 2 algorithms emerge by algebraic dependency degrees on WNRSs, while 3 algorithms emerge by three-view measures on WSNRSs; among the total 2+2+3=7 algorithms, 5 new ones advance 2 current baselines. Finally, weight granulations, uncertainty measures, feature selections are validated by data experiments, and our 5 improved selection algorithms outperform multiple contrast algorithms to acquire better performances for classification learning. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Fu W.; Shi M.; Li N.; Tian J.; Zhang S.; Ma J.; Jiang W.; Di J.
Title: Singlet-oxygen-mediated BNT/ZIS heterojunction for piezophotocatalytic co-production of hydrogen peroxide and benzaldehyde
Abstract: Efficient separation and use of photogenerated electrons and holes play a vital role in boosting photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) synthesis. However, conventional systems usually rely on sacrificial agents, leading to low hole utilization efficiency and poor economic viability. In this work, a (Bi0.5Na0.5)TiO3/Zn3In2S6 (BNT/ZIS) heterojunction was constructed by coupling (Bi0.5Na0.5)TiO3 with Zn3In2S6, realizing the synergistic production of H2O2 and benzaldehyde (BAL) under the combined effect of piezoelectricity and light irradiation. The optimized 10% BNT/ZIS composite delivered H2O2 and BAL formation rates of 64.05 and 85.99 mmol g−1 h−1, with approximately 99% BAL selectivity and 36% benzyl alcohol (BA) conversion. The enhanced activity originates from the intimate BNT/ZIS heterointerface, enlarged specific surface area, and charge separation driven by the piezoelectric effect. Band structure analysis, interfacial charge redistribution calculations, and photoelectrochemical measurements reveal strong interfacial coupling in the BNT/ZIS system, which effectively promotes the separation and migration of photogenerated carriers. Radical trapping experiments and ESR spectra demonstrate that O2− and singlet oxygen (1O2) are the key reactive oxygen species (ROS), among which 1O2 acts as a bifunctional ROS that participates in the O2 activation pathway toward H2O2 formation and simultaneously promotes the selective oxidative dehydrogenation of BA to BAL. In-situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (In-situ DRIFTS) further confirms the formation of oxygen reduction intermediates and BAL during the reaction. By constructing a BNT/ZIS heterojunction and utilizing the synergistic piezophotocatalytic effect, this work presents a viable approach for the coupled synthesis of H2O2 and organic products, while revealing the key role of ROS in the coupled redox process. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Fluorine-free synthesis of chlorine-terminated Nb2C MXene using CuCl: Exploring ion intercalation and electrochemical energy storage
Abstract: In this work, Cu-Nb2CCl2 MXene was successfully synthesized via a molten-salt etching strategy using CuCl as a mild etchant under an inert N2 atmosphere and its electrochemical performance was evaluated to demonstrate its energy-storage capability. Unlike conventional dichloride-based etching routes, the use of CuCl with a lower redox potential enabled the formation of uniformly layered MXene with limited lattice expansion, favourable for possible ion intercalations. Structural and surface analyses confirm the effective removal of the Al layer and the presence of Cl terminations on the surface, while Cu was attributed to metallic residues and possible partial pre-intercalation. This is supported with Ex-situ XRD before and after charge-discharge cycles. The as-prepared Sonicated Cu-Nb2CCl2 (Son. Cu-Nb2CCl2) exhibited a lower BET specific surface area than the modified MXene, potentially due to layer restacking, yet delivered a specific capacity of 119 C g−1 at 1 A g−1 in 1 M KOH electrolyte, without any further treatment. The binder free coated Son. Cu-Nb2CCl2 (Son. Cu-Nb2CCl2 - BF) delivered high specific capacity of 564 C g−1 at 1 A g−1 in 1 M KOH although the exposed substrate may contribute to the measured response. Kinetic analysis of Son. Cu-Nb2CCl2 revealed predominantly diffusion-controlled charge storage behaviour with a b value of 0.58. An asymmetric supercapacitor device fabricated using Son. Cu-Nb2CCl2 and activated carbon achieved a specific capacity of 57 C g−1 at 0.5 A g−1, an energy density of 11.7 Wh kg−1 and a power density of 375 W kg−1, while retaining 88.2% capacity and 92.48% coulombic efficiency after 10,000 cycles at 3 A g−1. These results indicate that CuCl is potential Lewis acid etchant and demonstrating the potential application of Son. Cu-Nb2CCl2 MXene, synthesized via molten-salt etching, as a promising active material for advanced ion intercalation mediated energy storage applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Zhang M.; Gou D.; Shen Y.
Title: CFD-DEM investigation of hydrogen-based iron ore reduction in a fluidised bed
Abstract: Hydrogen-based direct reduction of iron ore fines in fluidised beds is a promising route for low-carbon ironmaking, but the coupled gas–solid flow dynamics and reduction mechanisms inside reactors remain poorly understood. In this study, a GPU-accelerated CFD-DEM model is developed to simulate hydrogen-driven reduction of hematite particles in a full-scale bubbling fluidised bed. The model integrates gas–solid flow hydrodynamics, particle motion, and interphase heat and mass transfer with a multi-layer unreacted shrinking-core model for iron ore reduction, incorporating the sequential transformations from hematite to magnetite, wüstite and metallic iron. The iron ore reduction model is first validated against single-particle hydrogen reduction experiments and subsequently validated using laboratory-scale fluidised-bed experiments in terms of the overall reduction degree, which is comparable with experimental data. The validated model is then applied to investigate and quantify how particle size, gas velocity, gas temperature and hydrogen concentration jointly influence reduction behaviour and hydrogen utilisation. The results show that smaller particles and higher temperatures enhance reduction, whereas insufficient hydrogen concentration leads to incomplete conversion and low hydrogen efficiency. Increasing gas velocity improves fluidisation quality and accelerates reduction, but the benefits diminish at higher velocities and can reduce gas utilisation due to shorter residence time. The developed GPU-accelerated CFD-DEM model for iron ore reduction in fluidised beds provides an effective tool to support the design and optimisation of hydrogen-based fluidised-bed ironmaking reactors. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Sun P.; Yang T.; Zeng L.; Liu X.; Li J.; Chen J.; Wang Y.
Title: Coacervates assembled by liquid-liquid phase separation as binders for improving the quality of Fusarium venenatum-based meat analogues
Abstract: The inherent filamentous fiber structure of Fusarium venenatum makes it a promising candidate for meat analogues. However, the rigid cell wall structure results in undesirable textural properties in the final product, highlighting the necessity of a suitable binder for quality improvement. In this study, 7S vicilin and chitosan oligosaccharide (COS) at a mixing ratio of 10:1 and pH 5.5 formed liquid-like coacervate with superior viscoelasticity and strong interfacial wettability, making it suitable for binder design. In contrast, pea protein isolates and COS underwent liquid-solid phase separation (LSPS) and produced an irreversible precipitate that lacking binding functionality. Unlike LSPS, liquid-like coacervate relied on weak multivalent interactions across numerous binding sites and were characterized by a distinctive spherical droplet morphology, leading to enhanced interfacial adhesion and structural flexibility. When applied to mycoprotein-based meat analogues, the optimized binder significantly reduced cooking loss to 21.65%, compared with 29.28% for the methylcellulose-based control. Concurrently, textural properties including hardness and chewiness were markedly enhanced in the meat analogues prepared with liquid-like coacervate binder, suggesting the generation of a compact and tough protein network. Overall, this study established a functional liquid-like coacervate system, offering a viable, green, and clean-label alternative to synthetic binders for the development of high-quality meat analogues. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Liu E.; Mu S.; Zhang A.
Author full names: Liu, Ensheng (60877465200); Mu, Shengdong (57192434411); Zhang, Anqi (57725173100)
Title: Deep contrastive multi-view spatio-temporal clustering for stock volatility prediction
Abstract: Forecasting extreme stock volatility from candlestick patterns, investor commentary, and macroeconomic indicators requires reconciling views with different noise levels, temporal scales, and statistical distributions. We formulate this problem as cluster-guided multi-view forecasting: the representation and clustering modules learn latent market regimes from historical input windows, while a cluster-to-class mapping calibrated only on the training period assigns the regimes to future-return classes. We propose DCMVC-TRANS, which couples domain-adversarial low-level alignment with instance- and cluster-level contrastive objectives, Transformer-based cross-view interaction, quality-aware view weighting, and local–global assignment alignment. This coupling is designed to preserve complementary view information while preventing a noisy or dominant view from determining the consensus representation. Experiments on 238 small- and mid-cap stocks show that DCMVC-TRANS obtains the best three metrics at the 5-day horizon, the best accuracy at the 20-day horizon, and the best recall and F1-score at the 60-day horizon among the compared methods. Long-only backtests further show the highest Sharpe ratio at all three horizons. These results support the use of cluster-guided heterogeneous representation learning for robust stock volatility prediction. © 2026

Authors: Chang X.; Zhang Y.; Wang K.; Chu J.; Wang X.; Li H.
Title: Investigating the influence of dynamic adjustment on premixed methane–air combustion within porous media of varying structural configurations
Abstract: To clarify how dynamic adjustment affects porous media combustion of lean methane–air mixtures, this study experimentally compares the combustion characteristic parameters in a homogeneous structure (HS), a stepwise gradient structure (SGS), and an expanding block structure (EBS) under cold-start and dynamic adjustment conditions at identical target equivalence ratios and inlet velocities. The study reveals that dynamic adjustment lowered the lean combustion limit from an equivalence ratio of 0.50 to 0.45 at an inlet velocity of 0.10 m/s, which is attributed to retained heat compensating for insufficient heat release and sustaining reactant preheating. In addition, HS exhibited the greatest sensitivity of start-up and flame-propagation behavior to dynamic adjustment, whereas EBS was less sensitive. This is because HS, being homogeneous and weakly self-preheating, relies more on the heat retained from dynamic adjustment, whereas EBS, with pore-density gradients that inherently promote transport and heat exchange, depends less on this heat and thus responds less. Furthermore, CO emissions were lower under dynamic adjustment and lowest for EBS among the three configurations. The former is due to the heat accumulated prior to adjustment, which raised the average temperature during transient combustion and thus promoted CO oxidation; the latter arises because the axial pore-density gradient renders the temperature distribution more uniform and the thermal response less fluctuating, thereby facilitating further CO oxidation to CO2. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Author full names: Leyssale, Jean-Marc (7801481317); Obliger, Amaël (55826495500); Delhumeau, Alex Eduardo (60149421900)
Title: Misapprehending labels as types: A note to the molecular simulation community on kerogen model labeling
Abstract: In this opinion article, we recall the classification of kerogen into types I through IV using the Van Krevelen diagram. We further discuss the additional subclassification of kerogen into various subtypes based on sulfur content and/or the particular origin of the organic matter. With these foundational definitions kept in mind, we highlight several examples found in the molecular simulation literature wherein individual atomistic models of kerogen have been improperly referred to as representing different “types” or “subtypes” of kerogen. It is argued that, rather than merely being a harmless issue of semantics, such misapprehensions are concerningly detrimental to the molecular simulation community’s understanding of kerogen. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Author full names: Li, Xuecheng (57762794800); Jia, Weikuan (25121442800); Zheng, Yuanjie (23471581800)
Title: Closed-loop point-to-region optimal transport for point-supervised polyp segmentation
Abstract: Accurate polyp segmentation is essential for computer-aided colonoscopy, but dense pixel-level masks are costly to obtain. Point-supervised segmentation reduces this burden by using sparse clicks. However, a point annotation provides only a local semantic anchor and cannot determine the full lesion extent, weak boundary, or ambiguous transition region. Most existing point-supervised strategies generate pseudo masks in a single pass, providing no mechanism to refine the feature space used for subsequent supervision based on the initial point-to-pixel assignments. Consequently, early assignment errors near weak boundaries, specular highlights, and mucosa-like distractors may persist and propagate. We propose PC-CLOT, a two-pass point-to-region optimal transport framework with closed-loop prototype feedback for point-supervised polyp segmentation. PC-CLOT first uses Predictor-Corrector Skip Calibration (PCSC) to integrate multi-scale encoder features into a calibrated feature map for constructing the subsequent transport cost. Point-to-Pixel Optimal Transport (PPOT) then constructs a polyp-aware geodesic cost from calibrated features, prediction results, and sparse clicks to obtain an initial transport plan, which estimates the assignment degree between annotated points and class-specific pixels and derives an initial pseudo mask. To further refine this initial assignment, Transport-Induced Prototype Refinement (TIPR) summarizes foreground, background, boundary, uncertainty prototypes from the initial transport plan and network predictions, and uses prototype-to-pixel cross-attention to update the calibrated pixel features. The refined transport plan is then recomputed in this enhanced feature space to obtain the final prediction. Experiments on Kvasir-SEG, CVC-ClinicDB, and CVC-ColonDB show that PC-CLOT generates accurate masks from sparse clicks, achieving 0.887 Dice and 0.811 IoU on Kvasir-SEG and outperforming mainstream weakly supervised methods. Code is available at https://github.com/xuecheng990531/PC-CLOT.git . © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Global dynamics and high-order Melnikov analysis of an equivalent railway wheelset system with transverse homoclinic orbits
Abstract: During the normal serpentine motion of a railway wheelset system, small variations in running speed and track conditions may induce sudden large-amplitude chaotic responses. To investigate the underlying mechanism of such complex nonlinear behaviors, an equivalent four-dimensional non-autonomous Hamiltonian system with homoclinic orbits is derived for the railway wheelset system. Based on an extended high-order Melnikov method, analytical chaos thresholds are derived for the occurrence of Smale horseshoe chaos under a single-frequency high-order excitation. The basic Hamiltonian dynamics of the equivalent system are studied through the dissipative basin structures and global KAM phase-space structures. Subsequently, under weak dissipation and weak high-order harmonic excitations, the effects of excitation amplitude, excitation frequency and running speed on the global dynamics are investigated through threshold curves, bifurcation diagrams, phase portraits, corresponding Poincaré maps, and basins of attraction diagrams. Numerical results further reveal the evolution towards a chaotic window as the running speed increases. In particular, the evolution involves coexisting asymmetric periodic orbits induced by pitchfork bifurcations, coexisting periodic and weakly chaotic attractors induced by period-doubling bifurcations, together with other complex coexistence phenomena. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS

Title: Sustainable hydrogen production via dry reforming of biogas using M−Ni/NiAl2O4 (M = Na, K, Ca, Mg) catalysts prepared by the combustion method: Effect of alkaline and alkaline-earth promoters
Abstract: In this study, the insertion of alkaline metals (Na, K) and alkaline-earth metals (Ca and Mg) as promoters of NiO-Al2O3 catalysts, prepared by the combustion synthesis method, was studied. The catalysts were active during 8 h of reaction and with high resistance to coke deposition when compared to other catalysts in the literature, and the best results obtained were for the Ca-Ni/NiAl2O4 catalyst operating with a molar ratio CH4/CO2 = 1. The simulated biogas composition was varied (CH4/CO2 = 1, 1.5, 2) showing that the increased CH4/CO2 molar ration favors methane decomposition reaction, resulting in increased coke formation, especially for K-promoted catalyst. The characterization of the catalysts revealed that the combustion method was highly efficient to produce Ni catalysts with good stoichiometric control, and highly dispersed nickel with crystallite sizes smaller than 15 nm. The insertion of alkaline and alkaline-earth promoters result in a decrease of nickel dispersion, but no activity loss was detected. The associative mechanism was proposed by DRIFTS in situ . © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Ye H.; Yan W.J.; Zhu G.; Tao Y.B.
Title: Enhancing thermochemical heat storage of industrial waste MgCl2·6H2O with SrCl2 and modified expanded graphite
Abstract: The efficient reuse of industrial waste salts represents a crucial pathway for alleviating environmental pressure and achieving sustainable resource management. This study addresses the crucial issue of efficient reuse of industrial waste salts. We utilized magnesium chloride recovered from industrial processes and pure strontium chloride, combined with modified expanded graphite, to develop a thermochemical heat storage material, thereby providing a new pathway for recycling waste resources. The experiments focused on the composite’s water absorption capacity, heat storage performance, thermal conductivity, and cycling stability. Experimental results indicate that at a mass ratio of modified expanded graphite to magnesium chloride to strontium chloride of 20:56:24, the material exhibits optimal water uptake and thermal storage performance, achieving a heat storage density of 668 J·g−1 and a thermal conductivity of 5.11 W·m−1·K−1, along with excellent cycling stability. Furthermore, a dehydration kinetic model was established, and the apparent kinetic parameters of MEG20 were determined based on isothermal dehydration experiments. The kinetic analysis provides a quantitative basis for understanding the material-level dehydration behavior of the composite and offers fundamental parameters for future reactor-scale modelling. In summary, this study provides new insights into the viability of composite heat storage materials based on mixed chlorides and offers an effective approach for the high-value utilization of industrial waste salt in heat storage applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Yang Y.; Zhao R.; Ren H.; Zhao Y.; Liu J.
Title: Biomass-based micro-nano combustion promoter for enhanced oil recovery and carbon oxide emission reduction
Abstract: Aiming at the construction of middle-high temperature field with lower carbon oxide emission during the in-situ combustion (ISC) process, biomass-based micro-nano combustion promoter (BIO-DES-U) was prepared using paper pulp as raw materials by deep eutectic solvent-ultrasonication method. Kinetic cell (KC) combining with combustion tube experiments were conducted to investigate the oxidation behaviors and effect of BIO-DES-U on the ISC process. It was demonstrated that the ignition temperature of BIO-DES-U ranged from 181.4 °C to 211.2 °C, which was much lower than that of heavy oil (354.2–368.8 °C). Furthermore, the activation energy (Ea) of heavy oil during the low temperature oxidation (LTO) and high temperature oxidation (HTO) processes reached up to 461.4 KJ/mol and 599.3 KJ/mol, while the Ea of BIO-DES-U in VC and residue combustion (RC) stages were only 124.8 KJ/mol and 216.6 KJ/mol. The results showed that the effect of BIO-DES-U on ISC process was varied with location and concentration. The oxygen utilization ratio and oil recovery ratio reached separately the peak values of 71.57 % and 70.85 % as the 3 % BIO-DES-U was located in T3 far away from the production well, and the molar amount of COx (CO + CO2) emissions decreased to 1.22 mol with a reduction of 8.96 % compared with blank control. In addition, the oxygen utilization ratio reached 73.86 % accompanied by a 75.08 % oil recovery ratio as the 7 % BIO-DES-U was added, and the molar amount of COx emissions decreased by 11.94–1.18 mol. This work provides significant insights into the green and efficient development of ISC. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Shi L.; Jin J.; Liu H.; Wu N.; Xu C.; Bu J.; Zhao X.; Li S.; Qi Y.; Li S.; Wang H.
Title: Label-free and intelligent fluorometric array for simultaneously sensing of multiplexed metal ions based on DNA conformational diversity
Abstract: Multiplex detection of metal ions is often challenged by their similar charge states and ionic radii, which interfere with for simultaneous analysis and cause the low selectivity of conventional lock-and-key recognition elements. Herein, a label-free and intelligent fluorometric array has been developed for simultaneously probing multiplexed metal ions by utilizing the conformational diversity of DNA structures, including G-triplex, G-quadruplex, and dimeric G-quadruplex DNA. The sensing mechanism relies on thioflavin T intercalation, which converts metal-binding-induced DNA conformational changes into quantifiable fluorescence signals. The resulting fluorescence fingerprints were first visualized using principal component analysis and subsequently classified using supervised machine-learning algorithms. A comparative evaluation of multiple models reveals that the support vector machine achieves the highest classification performance for selective identification of multiple metal ions. The developed fluorometric array can accurately distinguish the samples containing various metal species (Fe3+, Co2+, Hg2+, Ni2+, Zr4+, Ag+, and Zn2+) over a wide range of concentrations (10-200 μM), with a 100% accuracy in blind validation tests. Subsequently, the feasibility of the array for detecting multiple metal ions in mixtures, as well as in lake water and tap water, is also demonstrated. As compared with most current analysis technologies, this method offers the desirable advantage of simultaneous discrimination of multiple metal ions including the heavy and non-heavy ones. Therefore, this study establishes a powerful, efficient, and cost-effective platform for the simultaneous and intelligent detection of multiple metal ions, showing strong potential as a rapid on-site screening tool for preliminary risk assessment of metal contamination. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Fan J.-X.; Hamaker B.R.; Guo X.-N.; Zhu K.-X.
Title: Understanding starch matrix remodeling and digestibility in black highland barley: Differential roles of polyphenol–glutelin assembly pathways
Abstract: Starch digestibility in whole-grain cereals is influenced not only by intrinsic starch structure but also by interactions among endogenous non-starch components. Black highland barley starch-based systems were constructed to investigate how endogenous polyphenol–glutelin assembly regulates starch matrix organization and in vitro digestibility. Non-oxidative (NPG) and oxidative (CPG) polyphenol–glutelin assemblies were incorporated into starch as NPG–S and CPG–S, respectively. SDS-PAGE under non-reducing and reducing conditions, combined with size-exclusion HPLC and side-chain reactivity assays, revealed that NPG formed a labile assembly, whereas CPG showed greater amino- and thiol-related side-chain participation and partially retained reduction-resistant high-molecular-weight species. Pasting and rheological measurements, together with scanning electron microscopy, showed that CPG-S formed a denser and more elastic matrix with restricted swelling and soluble-chain release than NPG–S. Infrared spectroscopy, iodine-binding, and chain-length analyses revealed greater helical disruption and enrichment of shorter amylopectin branches in NPG–S at high ratios, whereas CPG–S better preserved short-range order and longer branch fractions. Logarithm-of-slope (LOS)-based analysis revealed different digestogram behaviors among the systems, with some formulations exhibiting biphasic digestograms while others remained monophasic. NPG–S retained a larger slowly digestible starch (SDS) fraction, whereas increasing CPG–S ratios progressively reduced SDS and the predicted maximum hydrolysis extent while increasing resistant starch (RS) and decreasing the second-segment hydrolysis rate. These findings show that polyphenols and glutelin individually affect starch digestion, while their mode of assembly redirects starch structural evolution and hydrolysis by establishing matrix environments that govern starch rearrangement and enzyme accessibility. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Author full names: Yi, Wei (57204559982); Huang, Shuxin (58900633800); Zhang, Hongbo (60988585200); Lei, Mingfeng (35071602900); Jia, Chaojun (56549435000); Pan, Qiujing (56678265900); Xiao, Yingming (57210262334)
Title: A coupled hydro-mechanical phase-field model for mixed-mode fracture and full-stage permeability evolution in transversely isotropic rock with kinked fissures
Abstract: Understanding the coupled hydro-mechanical (HM) fracture behavior and permeability evolution in transversely isotropic rock containing kinked fissures is critical for the stability assessment and disaster prevention of deep underground engineering. Although existing phase-field models (PFMs) can effectively simulate mixed‑mode fracture and post-cracking permeability evolution, they generally neglect the energy dissipation caused by compressive stress and fail to account for the full‑stage permeability evolution, especially during the pre‑cracking stage. In this study, a coupled HM-PFM is proposed for transversely isotropic rock with kinked fissures. The model first introduces a volumetric-deviatoric strain energy decomposition framework to distinguish Mode-I tensile and Mode-II shear fracture driving forces, explicitly incorporating compressive-stress-induced energy dissipation. Second, it establishes a loading-dependent porosity evolution equation to characterize permeability variation in the entire loading process, including the pre-cracking compaction stage. The model is implemented within a transversely isotropic constitutive framework coupled with Biot's poroelasticity and Darcy's law. Real-time nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) tests are performed on layered sandstone specimens with a single kinked fissure at different bedding inclinations under triaxial hydro-mechanical coupling conditions to validate the feasibility and effectiveness of the newly proposed PFM. The results show that elastic modulus increases with bedding inclination, while peak strength exhibits a decrease-increase trend with a minimum at 60°. Maximum principal stress concentrates at fissure kinks, and maximum shear stress localizes at fissure tips, inducing symmetric shear-band failure. Permeability decreases during compaction and linear elasticity, rebounds after yielding, and increases sharply post-failure. The proposed model accurately reproduces experimental stress–strain curves, failure modes, and full-stage permeability evolution, and comparative benchmarks against existing PFMs further confirm its capability in capturing mixed-mode fracture interactions. Numerical results reveal that seepage pressure redistributes near fissures, forming high-velocity zones at crack tips, and that increasing bedding inclination deflects the seepage field and elevates peak flow velocity. The model provides a reliable numerical tool for analyzing mixed-mode fracture and hydro-mechanical behavior in transversely isotropic rock masses. © 2026

Authors: Qiu T.; Wu L.; Lei Y.; Yan F.; Zhang Z.
Title: Effect of back pressure on the ignition delay period of a diesel spray impinging on a glow plug hot surface in a spherical combustion chamber
Abstract: Ignition delay period (ID) is a key indicator for defining safe operating boundaries and evaluating combustion controllability during hot surface ignition. Back pressure is one of the most important parameters affecting the ID in hot surface ignition, and the rising back pressure shortens the ID. This study investigated diesel spray impingement ignition on a glow plug hot surface in a spherical combustion chamber with an exit channel. This study combined both experimental testing and three-dimensional numerical Large-eddy Simulations (LES) methods to investigate the diesel spray impingement ignition process on a glow plug hot surface under different back pressures. The results show that the ignition delay period of the hot surface ignition process was divided into three stages, i.e., flow, evaporation, and chemical stages, according to the local evolution of Reynolds number, evaporation rate, CH2O, and OH. When back pressure increased from 1 bar to 6 bar, ID duration decreased from 12.1 ms to 3.6 ms (reduction was 70.2% relative to the 1 bar). When back pressure increased from 1 to 9 bar, ID decreased to 2.9 ms (76.0% relative to the 1 bar). Furthermore, relative to the operation condition of back pressure = 1 bar, the chemical stage duration decreased by 85.2% at 6 bar and 88.9% at 9 bar. Meanwhile, both the flow and evaporation stages showed fewer reductions. Thus, the chemical stage causes the most important effect on the ID compared to other stages in the hot surface ignition process. Therefore, these results indicate that shortening the chemical stage is useful to reduce the ID duration and benefit the ignition process of the hot surface ignition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A multimodal diagnosis model combining multi-granularity contrastive learning and quality-aware adaptive fusion
Abstract: Significant advancements have been achieved in clinical diagnostics through the integration of 3D medical imaging with electronic health records. Despite these advancements, the diverse nature of multimodal data, particularly the often-overlooked variations in data quality, challenges the accuracy and reliability of joint diagnoses. While current methods have improved data fusion outcomes, they fall short in fully considering the multi-granularity characteristics of features. This oversight results in superficial interactions and a lack of comprehensive interaction information within individual modalities and across a global perspective. To address these issues, we introduce an innovative two-stage multimodal network. In the initial stage, we implement multi-granularity contrastive learning to achieve fine-grained alignment of cross-modal features. This is accomplished through multi-level feature interaction and label softening. Title: Comparative Analysis of waste tire pyrolysis Technologies and Advances in Key Influencing Factors
Abstract: The accumulation of end-of-life tires presents persistent environmental and resource-management challenges because vulcanized tire composites resist natural degradation. This review compares conventional thermal, catalytic, and microwave-assisted pyrolysis using the same criteria: heating mode, process severity, product selectivity, energy demand, scale-up readiness, and target application. Continuous feeding, heat and mass transfer, catalyst stability, microwave penetration, energy integration, process economics, and upgrading options for oil, gas, and recovered carbon black are also discussed. Title: Semi-implicit and Bregman parareal method for TV-nonlocal image enhancement
Abstract: The total variation nonlocal (TV-nonlocal) model integrates several advanced features, including geometric active contours, anisotropic diffusion, regularization, and nonlocal gradients, demonstrating solid mathematical foundations. Title: Material removal and damage mechanisms of SiC ceramics via hydroxyl surface modification
Abstract: Sintered silicon carbide (SSiC) is susceptible to brittle chipping during grinding owing to its high hardness and low fracture toughness. Title: Aero-optical aberration characteristics of flow over a cylinder with slit
Source title: International Journal of Modern Physics C
Abstract: The large-scale coherent structures generated in the near field of airborne optical systems are the main source of optical distortion. Comparative analyses are conducted for various dimensionless slit widths W/D, slit angle θs and multiple incident ray angles θ. Title: Tailoring porosity and surface nitrogen sites in n‑self‑doped biochar for CO2 mitigation applications
Abstract: Excessive carbon dioxide emissions have triggered severe environmental degradation.
