Thus, in this work, spirulina was used as a precursor to synthesize N‑self‑doped biochar in different calcination temperature (450, 550, 650, and 750 °C). The as-prepared biochar delivers an outstanding CO2 uptake of 5.09mmol g−1 at 25 °C and a high specific capacitance of 321.77F g−1 at 1 A g−1. Specifically, retained nitrogen functional groups (especially N-6) guarantee high CO2 uptake without excessive high-temperature activation for micropores. Title: Spatio-temporal cross attention involved dual graph convolution network for traffic flow prediction
Abstract: Traffic flow prediction is a critical task in intelligent transportation systems. The main challenge lies in the existence of complex, intertwined and dynamically evolving spatio-temporal dependencies in real-world traffic networks. Existing methods often rely on inherent static road network graph structures, lacking focus on the key time nodes and effective interaction mechanisms of spatio-temporal dimension information. To address this limitation, we propose a traffic flow prediction model named spatio-temporal cross attention involved dual graph convolution network. Our method adopts a parallel framework to synchronously extract features from both spatial and temporal dimensions. It spatially achieves enhanced learning of global and local dynamic dependencies through a dual graph convolution module, and temporally, it combines a long short-term memory network with a temporal attention module to capture continuous temporal correlations. Then through a cross attention fusion module, it dynamically integrates spatio-temporal information and establishes an interaction mechanism between them. Title: Mechanistic insights into sulfate reduction and suppression of SO2 accumulation in supercritical water gasification
Abstract: Sulfate transformation during supercritical water gasification (SCWG) is important for understanding sulfur migration, gas purification, and corrosion control, but its molecular reaction mechanism remains unclear. In contrast, the comparison with protonated sulfite-related pathways suggests that sulfite-derived intermediates can be further reduced more readily in the water-rich supercritical environment, thereby suppressing SO32- accumulation and limiting SO2 accumulation. CH4 can participate in sulfate activation, but its reduction pathway is restricted by high reaction energy barriers and difficult HSO3- conversion, especially under supercritical-water conditions. The desorption hysteresis index (HI) is introduced to quantify hysteresis magnitude, and governing equations are formulated for gas–water two-phase flow, temperature variation, coal matrix deformation and pore evolution, establishing the quantitative linkage between microscopic desorption hysteresis and macroscopic CBM extraction responses. Title: Deciphering the optical and biological profile of a chemosensor: fluorescence “Turn-Off” Ru(III) sensing, molecular docking, and in vitro biomedical assays

Authors: Khan F.; Adil M.; Roberts W.L.; Dally B.

Title: Experimental and kinetic analysis of laminar burning velocity and radical chemistry in ozone-enriched ethylene/air flames
Abstract: Lean premixed combustion of ethylene-containing fuels is proving progressively important for decarbonizing gas-fueled power and high-temperature industrial processes. Ozone (O3) serves as a highly reactive radical carrier for advanced gas-fired systems, but its impact on the structure and dynamics of unsaturated-fuel flames is inadequately characterized. Previous flame studies have focused mainly on alkanes, in which O3 acts through thermal decomposition to O atoms in the preheat zone. For ethylene, the competition between direct ozonolysis (O3 + C2H4) and radical-driven O3 consumption (O3 + H, O3 + M) inside a propagating flame has not been quantified. This study investigates the influence of ozone (O3) enrichment on laminar burning velocity and flame structure chemistry in premixed ethylene–air flames. In this study, laminar burning velocity of C2H4/air flames doped with 0–3000 ppm O3 was measured in a constant-volume spherical vessel at ϕ = 0.8 and 1.0, T0 = 300 K and P0 = 1 bar. Experiments at ϕ = 0.8 and ϕ = 1.0 show that laminar burning velocity increases approximately linearly with ozone concentration. Kinetic analysis was performed using the HP-Mech., which incorporates the Konnov mechanism and is coupled with an O3 sub-mechanism. A comprehensive investigation of one-dimensional simulations in a normalized flame coordinate (ξ) shows that the peaks of CH3CHO, H2O2, HO2, and CH2O grow monotonically with ozone enrichment while remaining anchored close to the flame front, suggesting accelerated front-centered oxidation instead of a displaced reaction zone. Despite ethylene’s distinctive ozonolysis chemistry, in-flame ozone consumption is dominated by H-abstraction (O3 + H <=> O2 + OH), exceeding the ozonolysis channel by roughly an order of magnitude; ozonolysis instead acts as a localized upstream primer for CH2O/HCO formation. Title: A comprehensive study on dynamic performance of grease-lubricated ball bearings considering thermal-mechanical coupling interactions
Abstract: This paper develops a comprehensive analysis model of grease-lubricated ball bearings focusing on thermal-mechanical coupling interactions to investigate the thermal effects on dynamic performance. The cage flexibility enhancement, grease viscosity-temperature effect, and structure deformations of rotor-bearing system are first considered, and the bearing dynamic model is proposed to analyze force and motion statuses for bearing components. Then, the heat transfer process for rotor system is deduced, and the frictional heat sources are derived based on the interplay mechanisms among bearing components and the outer ring spatial motions, so as to construct the transient thermal network model to investigate bearing temperature rise and its distributions. Further, the key parameters transfer paths between bearing dynamic behaviors and thermal properties are revealed, and the comprehensive analysis model is developed. The validation for the present model is confirmed by comparing it with bearing service performance tests. Finally, the bearing dynamic performance subjected to thermal effects is discussed. Results denote that the bearing temperature gradually increases during thermal balancing process, and the structure deformations of rotor system enlarge, causing to alter system assembly statuses. The thermal effects enhance cage flexibility and contact characteristics of ball-raceway, and diminish ball-pocket collisions and cage guiding effects, causing cage whirling trajectories to contract. The bearing skidding is suppressed by optimizing preload and system assembly statuses, and the bearing load distributions are improved, whereas the bearing temperature rises. Authors: Gao Q.; Ji X.; Du Z.; Li S.; Chen Y.; Xu K.
Title: A comparative stability analysis of spatial-temporal coupled versus decoupled compact element methods
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: With the increasing industrial demands, two families of high-order numerical schemes are widely used within the computational fluid dynamics community. One is the method of line, which relies on Runge-Kutta (RK) time-stepping applied to a semi-discrete, spatial-temporal decoupled formulation. The other is the family of Lax-Wendroff (LW)-type methods, which are inherently spatial-temporal coupled and are constructed within a multi-stage multi-derivative (MSMD) framework. This paper conducts the first comparative Fourier stability analysis of RK-type and LW-type compact element methods within the present two-moment framework to distinguish the dispersion and dissipation effects of numerical schemes respectively. Through rigorous theoretical derivation and consistent numerical validation, we draw the following conclusions: Although explicit RK-based line methods like discontinuous Galerkin (DG) and flux reconstruction (FR) schemes are straightforward, their temporal evolution is decoupled from the spatial reconstruction. This decoupling discards local space-time evolution information and necessitates small time steps. In contrast, spatial-temporal coupled compact methods, such as the gas-kinetic scheme (GKS) and the generalized Riemann problem (GRP) solver, utilize initial-value information from space far more effectively for time evolution. Even with just one additional order of spatial-temporal coupled information, they exhibit enhanced stability-related properties compared to RK-type methods. This provides new insights for CFD algorithm design, emphasizing the need for consistency between the dependence in the physical domain and that in the numerical domain. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Unraveling the CoB/Co3O4 synergistic effect in heterostructured catalysts for hydrogen production from NaBH4 hydrolysis
Abstract: Amorphous CoB suffers severe cyclic deactivation in NaBH4 hydrolysis, restricting its practical hydrogen-supply application. Herein, homologous amorphous-crystalline CoB/Co3O4 heterostructures are synthesized by chemical-reduction coupled with hydrothermal treatment to enhance the poor durability of pure CoB. The effects of CoB/Co3O4 mass ratio, NaOH and NaBH4 concentrations on hydrolysis performance are systematically studied. XRD, TEM, BET and XPS confirm the coexistence of amorphous CoB and spinel Co3O4. Incorporated CoB refines Co3O4 nanoparticles, mitigates agglomeration and realizes well-dispersed active sites. Catalytic tests show the 60 wt% Co-loaded composite reaches a peak hydrogen generation rate of 1724 mL·min−1·g−1. Owing to interfacial synergy, the heterostructure outperforms bare Co3O4 in activity and greatly improves the cycling stability of pure CoB. Low-concentration NaOH accelerates hydrolysis whereas excess alkali suppresses activity; 2.0 wt% NaOH is the optimal additive. Kinetic analysis indicates CoB/Co3O4-catalyzed NaBH4 hydrolysis follows zero-order kinetics with a low activation energy of 34.58 kJ·mol−1. Interfacial charge transfer between amorphous CoB and crystalline Co3O4 increases surface oxygen vacancies, optimizes intermediate adsorption-activation and accelerates hydrogen-evolution kinetics. This work offers a facile noble-metal-free strategy for developing heterostructured catalysts toward efficient on-demand hydrogen production. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Li X.; Chen L.; Wei B.; Ma R.; Li Y.; Guo F.; Shuang J.
Title: High-temperature corrosion and corrosion-product evolution of pure Ni in simulated HCl-containing flue gas with and without added O2
Abstract: Chlorine-containing flue gas threatens the safe operation of high-chlorine-fuel utilization equipment. Locally oxygen-deficient conditions may occur in coal-fired boiler combustion zones, where H2O becomes the primary oxidizing medium. Pure Ni was used as a model material to investigate its corrosion behavior in simulated flue gas containing 1000 ppm HCl, 4 % O2, 16 % CO2, 10 % H2O, and N2 as the balance gas at 450–650 °C for 100 h. Coupon tests, powder controls, NiCl2 conversion experiments, and thermodynamic analyses were combined to clarify the effects of H2O and O2. Without O2, HCl-containing specimens showed net mass loss, and discontinuous or porous scales with weak NiO signals formed at 550 and 650 °C. After O2 was introduced, the specimens exhibited net mass gain, and a porous scale approximately 11.37 μm thick formed at 650 °C. The mass loss of NiCl2 powder in N2 increased from 8.5 % at 450 °C to 42 % at 650 °C, while H2O promoted dechlorination and conversion into Ni- and O-rich products. Ni corrosion was governed by competition among NiO formation or repair, HCl-induced chlorination, and NiCl2 migration or volatilization. These findings provide a basis for assessing Ni-based alloys in oxygen-deficient chlorine-containing flue gas. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wang X.; Sadia H.; Ma X.-Z.; Shi L.; Liu X.; Zhang X.-X.; Peng L.-C.; Dong Z.-H.
Title: Deciphering tribocorrosion inhibition mechanisms of amino acid-based ionic liquids with mono- and dicarboxylic polar headgroups: Interfacial adsorption and tribochemistry
Abstract: Hydraulic systems are widely used in marine engineering, but seawater ingress may degrade lubricants and exacerbate tribocorrosion. Here, two surface-active ionic liquids—triethanolammonium N-lauroyl- L -alaninate (ALA-IL) and triethanolammonium N-lauroyl- L -glutamate (GLA-IL)—bearing monocarboxylic and dicarboxylic polar headgroups, respectively, were synthesized and evaluated as dual-function lubricating and tribocorrosion-inhibiting additives for AISI 1045 steel in saline medium. ALA-IL exhibits a lower friction coefficient because its low steric hindrance promotes more compact packing of hydrophobic chains. In contrast, GLA-IL exhibits lower wear volumes and maintains tribocorrosion inhibition efficiencies exceeding 80% even at 10 N and 200 rpm. Increasing load and rotational speed progressively disrupt the tribofilms, highlighting pressure–shear-induced film degradation. Surface analyses reveal differences in IL adsorption, film formation, and tribochemical behavior. ReaxFF-MD simulations reveal pressure–shear-dependent Fe–O bond exchange and mechanically adaptive interfacial coordination, while first-principles calculations identify carboxyl/carboxylate groups as primary adsorption sites and reveal deprotonation-assisted multidentate adsorption of GLA-IL. Overall, monocarboxylic ALA-IL promotes compact interfacial packing and lower friction, whereas dicarboxylic GLA-IL strengthens Fe–O coordination and tribofilm stability, thereby enhancing wear and tribocorrosion resistance. Authors: Xu Z.; Tian Y.; Yang L.; Ding L.; Wang R.
Title: Shape-invariant prompt learning with prompt relation structuring for open-vocabulary detection
Abstract: Open-vocabulary detection (OVD) aims to detect objects beyond training categories by leveraging the semantic knowledge of pretrained vision–language models. Recent studies indicate that modeling shape variation benefits OVD by making region features more adaptable to diverse object geometries. Although geometry-dependent adaptation has demonstrated the importance of shape-aware modeling, independently learning shape-specific adapters on different feature subsets may result in fragmented optimization and limited gradient sharing across shape groups, making it difficult to maintain consistent semantic alignment. Motivated by prompt-based adaptation and vision–language alignment, we propose a unified OVD framework named SIP-OVD. SIP-OVD introduces Shape-Invariant Prompt (SIP) learning, where shape-invariant prompts modulate CLIP region features according to object geometry, and a shared semantic adapter aligns the prompted embeddings with text embeddings in a shared semantic space. Furthermore, we introduce Prompt Relation Structuring (PRS), which regularizes prompt similarity to preserve smooth geometric transitions and discriminative shape boundaries. In addition, we incorporate Query-conditioned Iterative self-Training (QIT) as a complementary training module that mines reliable unseen-class regions to provide additional supervision for model refinement. Authors: Yang S.; Li Y.; He Y.; Dai C.; Zhao C.
Title: Molecular mechanism of hydrocarbon transport within kerogen nanoporous networks
Abstract: Conventional macroscopic transport theories fail in shale organic nanopores where hydrocarbons transport as discrete molecular units. Furthermore, the ultra-high specific surface area of kerogen (1.81 nm2/nm3, ∼1810 m2/cm3) implies that the impact of atomic-scale roughness and tortuosity within the porous structure is non-negligible. To resolve this breakdown of the continuum assumption, this paper establishes a 3D multi-component unsteady transport model based on the Mori-Zwanzig projection and Generalized Langevin Equation (GLE). By accurately decoupling transport resistance into topological field response (Ftopo), molecular configurational penalty (Fconfig), and internal dissipation (Ffric), we identify a fundamental transition from energy-dominated to entropy-dominated transport regimes. A “dynamic sieving” effect is quantitatively revealed: flexible long-chain molecules (e.g., octane) achieve “soft penetration” via conformational adaptation (requiring 308 ± 122 kcal/mol), whereas rigid cyclic molecules (e.g., toluene) suffer from insurmountable topological anchoring. Furthermore, we define the “solubility decoupling” mechanism—where the premature escape of light components disrupts fluid continuity, leading to the immediate immobilization of heavy fractions. The model predicts a maximum swept distance of 70 ± 10 nm for methane in 1.5 nm porous networks, marking the physical boundary where driving potential is neutralized by accumulated resistances. These findings demonstrate that shale development should be combined traditional pressure drawdown with molecular-level interfacial interventions and CO2-EOR to restore phase continuity and remobilize anchored hydrocarbons deep within the matrix. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Enhanced photocatalytic production of H2O2 by Electron modulation at the g-C3N4/Zn2In2S5 S-scheme heterojunction Interface

Abstract: The efficiency of H2O2 generation is substantially constrained by the elevated recombination rate of charge carriers in photocatalysis systems for producing hydrogen peroxide (H2O2). To address this challenge, an S-scheme heterojunction of g-C3N4/Zn2In2S5 with a 2D/2D layered structure has been designed. The remarkable catalytic efficiency arises from the close contact interface established between the 2D materials, which enhances both separation and transportation of charge carrier, while maintaining the robust redox properties of Zn2In2S5 and g-C3N4. The optimized CN/ZIS-2 composite achieved a remarkable H2O2 yield of 425.6 μmol L−1 in 2 h with excellent stability. In situ DRIFT spectra identified ·O2− as the critical reaction intermediate. The integration of density functional theory (DFT) with experimental findings supports the conclusion that the photocatalytic production of H2O2 proceeds via a two-step involving single-electron reduction of oxygen process:O2+e−→·O2−→e−H2O2. This study not only demonstrates an effective strategy for designing S-scheme heterojunctions, but also provides new insights for applying photocatalytic technology in environmental remediation and energy conversion field. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Microstructure-driven charge transport and dual relaxation dynamics in nanocrystalline Na0.5Fe2.5O4 spinel ferrite
Abstract: Understanding the interaction between crystal structure, dielectric response, and charge transport is essential for tailoring nanocrystalline ferrites for frequency-dependent functional applications. Title: Switched output feedback H∞ control for T-S fuzzy systems via privacy protection
Abstract: This paper studies the problem of dynamic output feedback H∞ control for a class of T-S fuzzy systems with time-varying membership functions. For the fuzzy Lyapunov function, this paper constructs first-order and second-order membership-dependent Lyapunov functions, and divides the system operation region into different sub-intervals according to the sign of the derivatives of the membership functions(MFs). Dynamic output feedback controller gains are designed in each sub-interval, and the corresponding controllers are adjusted accordingly. This avoids the conservatism caused by the traditional boundedness assumption while ensuring that the closed-loop system achieves the prescribed H∞ disturbance attenuation level. In addition, considering that the controller output signal may face the risk of privacy leakage during network transmission, this paper introduces an output masking mechanism to protect the privacy of the system state and output signal. Title: Design of dual-textured Mg-6.5Zn alloys with low tension–compression asymmetry by means of crystal plasticity simulations
Abstract: The stress–strain curves and the deformation mechanisms of a dual-textured Mg alloy along the extrusion direction were studied in tension and in compression by means of crystal plasticity finite element simulations of a three-dimensional representative volume element of the microstructure. The simulations were able to reproduce the experimental stress–strain curves as well as the deformation mechanisms of the dual-textured alloy, which showed very limited tension/compression asymmetry in the yield strength. In addition, the simulations were used to design an optimum microstructure with a dual texture made up of 29% of C-textured grains and 71% of E-textured grains that exhibits the same yield strength in tension and in compression and small differences in the strain hardening rates afterwards. Title: Molecular insights into aldehyde-mediated assembly and bioactivity of peptide–polysaccharide composite hydrogels
Abstract: Inflammation and oxidative stress are central pathological drivers of numerous diseases and infections, necessitating the development of bioactive peptide-based hydrogels with integrated anti-inflammatory and antibacterial functionalities. Title: The role of monovalent ions on water-in-crude oil emulsion stability
Abstract: The formation of stable water-in-crude oil (W/O) emulsions presents significant operational challenges in the petroleum industry. The role of monovalent ions in stabilizing these emulsions, which are primarily stabilized by asphaltenes and resins, remains poorly understood. This study systematically investigates the effect of monovalent cations (Li+, Na+, K+, Cs+) and anions (Cl−, Br−, I−) on the stability and rheological properties of W/O emulsions prepared with a crude oil containing a high concentration of natural surfactants. Our results demonstrate a clear ion-specific effect, consistent with the Hofmeister series. Specifically, the smallest cation, Li+, and the largest anion, I−, were the most effective at destabilizing the emulsions, leading to rapid phase separation. Rheological measurements further revealed a contrasting effect: LiCl systematically reduced emulsion viscosity, while NaCl and CsCl increased it. Because microscopic analysis showed that droplet size remained largely unchanged, the macroscopic destabilization is attributed primarily to molecular influences. Based on these observations, we propose a molecular hypothesis where highly hydrated Li+ ions disrupt the interfacial hydrogen-bonding network of the asphaltene film, while less-hydrated Na+ and Cs+ ions promote structural reinforcement through cationic clustering. Title: Thermal control of tip leakage flow for stall margin enhancement in a transonic axial compressor
Abstract: In compressible transonic regimes, the temperature field plays a fundamental role in governing local density gradients and boundary layer development, which directly dictate the position and stability of shock waves. This thermal-aerodynamic coupling is particularly critical in high-speed axial compressors, where the interaction between the passage shock and the tip leakage vortex defines the global stability limits . The present study examines the application of casing-wall cooling as a flow control strategy to modulate tip-region physics. Using numerical simulations, the stability behavior of the NASA Rotor 37 is evaluated across a range of cooling intensities. The numerical predictions are first subjected to a detailed validation against experimental data, and a full-casing isothermal boundary condition is considered for temperature ratios (TR) of 0.8, 0.6, and 0.4 relative to the inlet total temperature. The results demonstrate that casing cooling leads to a stall margin improvement of up to 26.39% for TR= 0.4. Entropy generation analysis further indicates that TR= 0.8 offers the most favorable compromise between aerodynamic benefits and thermodynamic losses, achieving 25.01% in stall margin improvement. Detailed flow field analysis reveals that casing cooling weakens the shock–vortex interaction, reduces blockage accumulation, and limits the radial migration of the induced vortex. Additionally, cooling mitigates the bow shock-boundary layer interaction at the casing wall, thereby maintaining a favorable axial momentum balance and preventing upstream displacement of the tip clearance flow. The findings suggest that casing cooling is an effective pathway for achieving gains in compressor efficiency and operational safety. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Title: Electrochemical sensing of promethazine: A critical review of detection strategies, sensor architectures, and analytical challenges
Abstract: Promethazine (PMZ) is a widely used phenothiazine drug whose accurate determination is important in pharmaceutical quality control, clinical monitoring, forensic toxicology, food analysis, and environmental surveillance. Although chromatographic and spectrometric methods remain valuable for confirmatory analysis, their dependence on sophisticated instrumentation and extensive sample preparation has encouraged the development of faster electrochemical alternatives. This review critically evaluates PMZ electrochemical detection studies published from 2010 to 2026, covering voltammetric methods, direct electrocatalytic detection, molecularly imprinted and DNA-mediated recognition, adsorptive stripping, and extraction-integrated electroanalysis. Particular attention is given to the effects of nanostructured materials, conductive composites, porous interfaces, and recognition layers on analytical performance. Comparative analysis indicates that nanostructured electrodes generally enhance sensitivity and electron transfer, whereas molecularly imprinted and DNA-modified interfaces offer greater potential for selective recognition. However, important trade-offs remain because high-surface-area and adsorption-based platforms are susceptible to fouling, affinity-based sensors often require complex fabrication and regeneration, and ultra-low detection limits frequently depend on prolonged preconcentration or sample pretreatment. Major research gaps include inadequate discrimination from structurally related phenothiazines, limited validation in authentic complex samples, poor inter-electrode and batch-to-batch reproducibility, and insufficient assessment of robustness, operational stability, total assay time, and cost. Future research should prioritize matrix- and fouling-resistant interfaces, simplified scalable fabrication, rigorous validation, and integrated sample handling. Combining reproducible disposable electrodes with microfluidics, portable potentiostats, and connected readout systems may facilitate reliable field-deployable and point-of-care PMZ analysis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Experimental studies of heat transfer regimes with boiling crisis in a vertical channel at high heat fluxes
Abstract: The results of experimental studies of heat transfer during water boiling in a vertical heated tube with a diameter of 0.013 m and a length of 2.6 m are presented. The studies were conducted in the following ranges of variation: pressure from 4 MPa to 16 MPa, mass velocity from 120 kg/m2s to 2000 kg/m2s, and heat flux from 0.13 MW/m2 to 2.59 MW/m2 and temperatures up to 800°C. Correlations have been obtained for calculating the boundaries of the onset of boiling, the transition to the equilibrium boiling regime, and the heat transfer coefficient in the non-equilibrium boiling region. The influence of flow parameters on the heat transfer coefficient is shown. In the equilibrium boiling region, the mass velocity does not significantly affect the heat transfer coefficient. The heat transfer coefficient increases with increasing pressure and gradually decreases with increasing vapor quality (steam content). In some modes, prior to the heat transfer crisis (critical heat flux, CHF), an intensification of heat transfer and an increase in the heat transfer coefficient up to 162 kW/(m2·K) are observed. Title: Metric dimension and geodetic set parameterized by vertex cover
Source title: Journal of Computer and System Sciences
Abstract: For a graph G, a subset S⊆V(G) is called a resolving set of G if, for any two vertices u,v∈V(G), there exists a vertex w∈S such that d(w,u)≠d(w,v). The METRIC DIMENSION problem takes as input a graph G on n vertices and a positive integer k, and asks whether there exists a resolving set of size at most k. In another metric-based graph problem, GEODETIC SET, the input is a graph G and an integer k, and the objective is to determine whether there exists a subset S⊆V(G) of size at most k such that, for any vertex u∈V(G), there are two vertices s1,s2∈S such that u lies on a shortest path from s1 to s2. These two classical problems are intractable with respect to the solution size, as well as most structural parameters, including the feedback vertex set number and pathwidth. The very few existing tractable results state that they are both FPT with respect to the vertex cover number vc. Specifically, we observe that both problems admit an FPT algorithm running in 2O(vc⋅nO(1) time, and a kernelization algorithm that outputs a kernel with 2O(vc) vertices. For these problems, we also prove that, unless the Exponential Time Hypothesis fails, the established running time is asymptotically the best possible. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Pan J.; Zhao M.; Li Y.; Tang F.; Fang J.; Li R.
Title: LNG cold energy driven multi-generation system integrating light hydrocarbon separation, BOG helium extraction and two-stage ORC: multi-objective optimization and comprehensive evaluation
Abstract: To achieve the cascade utilization of LNG cold energy, this paper presents a novel and efficient system known as LHS-HE-TSORC, which integrates light hydrocarbon separation (LHS), boil-off gas (BOG) helium extraction, and a two-stage organic Rankine cycle (ORC). The working fluid for the ORC and the separation membrane material used in the helium extraction system were meticulously selected. Sensitivity analysis assesses the impacts of key process variables on net electric power ( NEP ), exergy efficiency ( η ex), and net present value ( NPV ). Multi-objective optimization is conducted using the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) and Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO) to identify optimal system parameters. The results indicate that R290 is selected for the ORC subsystem, while PBO-co-PPL 28 is chosen as the membrane material for the helium extraction subsystem. The multi-objective optimization results demonstrate a performance characterized by an NEP of 12.69 × 103 kW, an η ex of 38.38 %, and an NPV of 3.67 × 109 $. Energy assessment results confirm that heat exchanger HX-3 exhibits the minimum energy loss and the highest heat transfer efficiency. Exergy assessment results indicate that the total exergy destruction amounts to 53,838.37 kW. The economic assessment reveals a dynamic payback period ( DPP ) of 2.695 years. The exergoenvironmental assessment confirms that the system shows improved environmental compatibility under colder conditions. Finally, the entropy generation assessment indicates that the highest entropy generation occurs in the heat exchanger, tower, and combustion chamber. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wen W.; Du X.
Title: Synthesis of lanthanide metal M-doped Ni3S2-based (M = La, Nb and Nd) materials and performance testing of electrolyzed seawater and urea
Abstract: H2 production through electrochemistry seawater splitting has caused much attention due to the fact that it does not consume precious freshwater resources. However, its industrial application is hindered by the slow dynamics of the anode water oxidation reaction and the corrosion problem caused by Cl−. In this study, Ni3S2-based electrocatalysts doped with different lanthanide metals (La, Nb, Nd) were firstly successfully synthesized using nickel foam as the substrate by a two-step hydrothermal method. Combining electrochemical tests with stability assessment, it was concluded that Nd-Ni3S2/NF exhibited good electrocatalytic performance in the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and urea oxidation reaction (UOR). The electrochemical test results show that the overpotential at 10 mA cm−2 is only 167 mV for the OER, which is one of the best electrochemistry performance reported up till now. However, the 15-hour timed current stability test demonstrated that the performance of the electrode declined significantly, which was attributed to the shedding of the nanosheet structure during the long-term electrolysis process and the oxidation of sulfur species to form soluble sulfates, resulting in a reduction of active sites and material loss. In addition, the electrochemical test results show that the potential at a current density of 50 mA cm−2 is only 1.38 V for the UOR, which has largely reduced the energy consumption of the reaction. This study provides experimental evidence for the design of lanthanide metal-doped nickel-based sulfides and offers a reference for the development of catalysts for alkaline seawater and urea electrolysis. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhang J.; Li W.; Huang D.; Rajic V.
Title: An intelligent and adaptive algorithm for reliability enhancement of an energy harvester under fractional-order control and stochastic excitation
Abstract: This paper proposes an intelligent adaptive algorithm for enhancing the reliability of a tri-stable piezoelectric energy harvesting system under fractional-order proportional-integral-derivative control and Gaussian white-noise excitation. The controlled electromechanical system is reduced using an equivalent decoupling procedure and an improved stochastic averaging method. The conditional reliability function is obtained from the backward Kolmogorov equation, while the mean first-passage time is evaluated using the generalized Pontryagin equation. An adaptive particle swarm optimization method combined with a Logistic basis function neural network is then developed to solve the reliability equation and simultaneously optimize the two fractional orders. For the considered parameter set, the optimized controller increases the time-averaged reliability by 6.3% and extends the mean first-passage time by 29.2% relative to the uncontrolled case. The network solution achieves a mean error of 0.0044 compared with Monte Carlo simulations. Finally, a sensitivity analysis is discussed to assess the effects of the main algorithm parameters. The proposed algorithm provides an efficient reliability-oriented tool for the optimal fractional-order control of strongly nonlinear energy harvesting systems under random excitation. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Inc.

Title: The transition from reaction control toward diffusion control of sawdust char particles gasification by the phase change of ash under non-isothermal conditions
Abstract: Biomass gasification is a key technology for efficient biomass utilization. The reaction kinetics of biomass gasification are related to the phase change of ash. The gasification reactivity of sawdust char at different heating rates (5, 10, 15, and 20 °C/min) and the regulatory effect of the phase change of ash on the reaction mechanism during gasification were systematically investigated. This was achieved through thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) and high-temperature stage microscope (HTSM) experiments, combined with iso -conversional methods (FWO and KAS methods). The results indicated that both TGA and HTSM exhibited thermal hysteresis as the heating rate increased. During the initial stage, the abundant pores in the char and the AAEMs in the ash promoted the gasification reaction. The ash gradually sintered and melted as conversion degree increased. The molten slag flowed to form a dense encapsulating layer covering the residual carbon core. The results of the kinetic analysis indicated that the activation energy decreased with increasing conversion. Based on the data fitted using the master-plot method, the apparent reaction behavior showed a gradual transition from reaction controlled characteristics toward diffusion influenced behavior, reflecting enhanced diffusion limitation in the late stage. The study elucidates the coupling relationship between ash fusion and gasification reaction kinetics, providing mechanistic insights that may support process optimization and reactor design for biomass gasification systems with similar feedstocks and operating conditions. Authors: Meng K.; Zhang X.-Q.; Qi Y.-Q.; Wu J.; Yu X.-W.; Zhang Z.; Yang Y.; Jiao S.-H.; Liu H.; Guo A.-J.; Wang Z.-X.
Title: Reaction-environment engineering by supercritical solvent coupled with Ni-Co/M-β-catalyzed hydroconversion for heavy residue into light aromatics
Abstract: The hydrocracking of highly condensed aromatic structures in heavy residue (HR) with high asphaltene content is important for the high-value utilization of heavy hydrocarbon resources. However, low hydrogen solubility and high mass-transfer resistance in viscous HR and highly aromatic asphaltene aggregates severely hinder hydroconversion efficiency. In this study, a synergistic catalytic hydroconversion strategy integrating supercritical solvent-mediated reaction-environment regulation with a Ni-Co/M-β catalyst was developed. Alkali-modified β generated a hierarchical pore structure that facilitated the diffusion of bulky molecules, while the Ni-Co bimetallic components electronically modulated Ni active centers and promoted H2 dissociation and activation. Model-compound experiments further confirmed the capability of Ni-Co/M-β to promote aromatic-ring hydrogenation and C–C bond cleavage. The hydroconversion behavior of HR was systematically investigated in different solvent systems and under different CO2 phase states. Among the investigated systems, supercritical CO2 (ScCO2) exhibited the highest asphaltene conversion and light-component yield and the lowest coke yield, reaching 55.3 %, 68.7 %, and 0.7 %, respectively. GC–MS, elemental analysis, 1H NMR, and FTIR results further indicated that ScCO2 promoted aromatic-ring hydrogenation and cracking while suppressing condensation. These results demonstrate that ScCO2-mediated reaction-environment regulation acts synergistically with Ni-Co/M-β catalysis to promote the hydrogenation-cracking pathway, providing an effective strategy for producing low-ring aromatic compounds from heavy aromatic residues. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wu J.-J.; Gui X.-H.; Wu L.-N.; Tian Z.-Y.
Title: Soot oxidation kinetics of n-C12H26 via ferrocene doping
Abstract: n -Dodecane ( n -C12H26) is an important model component of aviation fuels, and the mechanism of soot formation during its combustion is crucial for improving combustion efficiency and reducing pollutant emissions. Ferrocene (Fe(C5H5)2) exhibits unique advantages in controlling soot formation due to its excellent thermal stability and good solubility in hydrocarbon fuels. In this work, thermogravimetric (TG) technology was employed to investigate the effects of ferrocene at three concentrations (0.1 %, 0.2 % and 0.3 %) on the oxidation kinetics of soot generated from n -C12H26 combustion. The oxidation reaction stages were divided based on the soot derived from n -C12H26 combustion, and the oxidation kinetic parameters of the thermal decomposition stage (Stage Ⅱ) and the combustion stage (Stage Ⅲ) were fitted by using both the differential method and the integral method. The results show that: the Stage Ⅱ of soot oxidation for n -C12H26 conforms to the spherically symmetric three-dimensional diffusion mechanism with n = 2, while Stage Ⅲ follows a third-order chemical reaction mechanism. In Stage Ⅱ, ferrocene at concentrations of 0.1 % and 0.3 % transforms the reaction mechanism from three-dimensional diffusion to two-dimensional diffusion. In contrast, the soot reaction rate of the 0.2 % ferrocene group is significantly lower in the early stage but converges with that of other groups as the reaction proceeds. In Stage Ⅲ, ferrocene at all three concentrations exhibits the same soot suppression mode, compensating for the low reaction rate in Stage Ⅱ by consuming soot at a high rate, with relatively low apparent activation energies in this stage. Overall, ferrocene at a concentration of 0.2 % achieves the optimal soot suppression effect. © 2026 The Author(s).

Authors: Lei Y.; Cheng Y.; Wang H.; Zhang T.; Tan R.; Ge H.; Ma S.; Song T.
Title: Comparison of two- and three-step chemical looping steam methane reforming over Ni-, Cu-, or Co-doped Ca2Fe2O5 oxygen carriers
Abstract: Chemical looping steam methane reforming (CL-SMR) is a promising route for syngas and hydrogen production, where oxygen carriers are crucial. Ca2Fe2O5 enables two-step CL-SMR but suffers from low reactivity. Doping with foreign ions can improve reactivity, but its regeneration by steam alone is difficult, leading to a three-step process with air oxidation. Transition-metal-doped Ca2Fe1.75Me0.25O5 (Me = Ni, Cu, or Co) were studied in two- and three-step CL-SMR. All dopants significantly improved the CH4 conversion and H2 yield in both two- and three-step methods, and the promoting effects were ranked as Ni-doped > Cu-doped > Co-doped. In two-step method, the undoped sample achieved a CH4 conversion of 6.26 % and an H2 yield of 1.288 mmol·g−1, versus 42.3 %/5.256 mmol·g−1, 32.5 %/4.120 mmol·g−1, and 23.0 %/2.768 mmol·g−1 for Ni‑, Cu‑, and Co‑doped samples, respectively, yet doping lowered the CO selectivity and drove the H2/CO ratio below 2.0. The three-step method further improved the performance of these samples. The CH4 conversions grew by 125 % (undoped), 9 % (Ni-doped), 34 % (Cu-doped), and 40 % (Co-doped), and the H2 yields rose by 99 %, 7 %, 34 %, and 54 %, respectively. Ca2Fe1.75Ni0.25O5 and Ca2Fe1.75Cu0.25O5 performed best in three-step method; Ca2Fe1.75Ni0.25O5 delivered higher reactivity while Ca2Fe1.75Cu0.25O5 afforded better cyclic stability. The improved performance could be attributed to the increased oxygen vacancy concentration and enhanced lattice oxygen mobility, and the air oxidation stage in three-step method could promote the reincorporation of dopants into Ca2Fe2O5 lattice and greatly boost the regeneration degree of oxygen carriers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Kinetic Modeling of Oil Shale Upgrading under Subcritical and Supercritical Water: SARA Fraction Distribution in Catalytic and Non-Catalytic Systems
Abstract: The upgrading of unconventional hydrocarbons, such as oil shale, is a promising option for meeting the increasing energy demand, with hydrothermal technologies offering several advantages over conventional methods. This study develops and compares catalytic and non-catalytic kinetic models for oil shale conversion applied in subcritical (SBCW) and supercritical water (SCW) environments. For this, Bazhenov oil shale is treated with a synthesized Ni-tallate oil-soluble catalyst in a high-pressure batch reactor at 300–400 °C, employing a seven-lump reaction scheme based on organic (SARA fractions) and inorganic transformations. The findings indicate that while both models effectively predict product yields, in the non-catalytic conversion reaction, the principal pathway proceeds through the sequence Kerogen → Resins → Asphaltenes → Aromatics → Saturates, with the reactions being slow and energy demanding. On the contrary, catalytic cracking with Ni-tallate alters the pathways, favoring the Kerogen → Saturates reaction, which involves significantly less energy input. However, it can also hasten reversible aromatization reactions (Saturates → Aromatics → Resins). It was confirmed that the oil-soluble catalyst only participates in organic-phase reactions. Notably, at 400 °C, the competition between thermal and catalytic pathways begins to influence product selectivity, primarily due to the inherent limitations associated with the stability of saturates. Title: Gum Arabic-lactoferrin electrostatic complexes as natural stabilizers for cinnamon essential oil Pickering emulsions: Structure, rheology, and stability
Abstract: To address the poor water dispersibility, high volatility, and environmental sensitivity of cinnamon essential oil (CEO), a representative hydrophobic bioactive compound, gum arabic (GA)-lactoferrin (LF) composite particles were prepared by electrostatic self-assembly combined with heat-induced treatment and used as natural stabilizers for CEO Pickering emulsions. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy and intrinsic fluorescence analyses indicated that electrostatic attraction, hydrogen bonding, and LF conformational changes contributed to GA-LF particle formation. The selected particles formed and stabilised CEO oil-in-water Pickering emulsions, as confirmed by dilution tests, optical microscopy, and confocal laser scanning microscopy observations. Increasing the oil phase fraction from 10% to 50% reduced the dynamic light scattering-derived mean droplet size and narrowed the droplet-size distribution. Among the tested emulsions, the 50% oil formulation showed the lowest creaming index after 14 days (5.8%), the highest emulsifying activity index value (57.59 ± 0.72 m2/g), shear-thinning behaviour, and dominant elastic properties (G′ > G″). This formulation also exhibited better resistance to pH (3.0–11.0), heating (30–90°C), and NaCl treatments (0.1–0.7 mol/L) than lower-oil emulsions, which was attributed to interfacial particle adsorption, electrostatic/steric stabilisation, and the formation of a viscoelastic droplet network. Authors: Li P.; Chen Z.; Chen J.; Cao Z.; Chen Z.
Title: DBD plasma assisted combustion of coal and high-moisture peat: stage evolution and mechanism
Abstract: High-moisture peat is difficult to burn through self-sustained combustion because moisture evaporation suppresses heat accumulation and delays the establishment of a stable reaction stage. Coal blending can provide heat compensation, whereas dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) plasma can introduce localized energy input and enhance early-stage heat and mass transfer. However, it remains unclear how DBD energy input couples with moisture evaporation and coal-derived heat release, especially when mass decay and temperature rise are not synchronized in high-moisture blended fuels. In this study, a coaxial DBD plasma-assisted combustion system was developed for coal-high-moisture peat mixtures. Twelve representative operating conditions were designed using coal-to-peat ratio, applied voltage, and moisture content as the main factors. Discharge behavior, mass decay, and thermal response were evaluated using average discharge power, average mass-loss rate, and average temperature-rise rate. The average discharge power ranged from 8.716 to 50.241 W. During the first 800 s, the average mass-loss rate and temperature-rise rate ranged from 0.008984 to 0.017286 g·s⁻1 and from 0.4538 to 0.9709 ℃·s⁻1, respectively. Range analysis showed that applied voltage was the dominant factor, followed by coal-to-peat ratio and moisture content. Because the preferred combinations based on mass loss and temperature rise were different, a dual-indicator entropy weighting method was used to identify the preferred condition, corresponding to a coal-to-peat ratio of 5:5, an applied voltage of 20 kVpp, and a moisture content of 50 %. Validation experiments showed that DBD assistance increased the mass-loss rate and temperature-rise rate by 5.75 and 7.34 times, respectively, compared with natural combustion. These results indicate that DBD plasma promotes the transition from moisture-evaporation control to sustained combustion and provides a basis for optimizing plasma-assisted combustion of high-moisture blended fuels. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Study on zoned ignition and combustion performance induced by turbulent jet collision and entrainment for methanol direct injection engine
Abstract: Jet controlled compression ignition (JCCI) technology, employing turbulent hot jets from an ignition chamber (IC) to deliver a robust and precisely controlled ignition, presents a promising approach to enhance methanol engine performance. This study numerically investigated the effects of hot jet-methanol spray interactions on zone ignition, combustion performance, and emission characteristics. Two distinct IC nozzle configurations were compared systematically: a modified inlet orifice position (MOP) with straight nozzle holes and the fixed inlet orifice position (FOP) with swirl nozzle holes. Both nozzles were evaluated by varying orientation angles for the central (J13A) and side (J2A) jets. Jet momentum, mixing patterns, and velocity field distributions were identified as key factors controlling combustion dynamics. FOP mode demonstrates superior performance through its swirl-induced flow configuration, enabling synchronized combustion of multiple methanol sprays and reduction of local rich-mixture regions. Moreover, by precisely adjusting the methanol spray inclined angle (Ia), an effective zoned ignition mechanism is triggered through jet collision and entrainment, promoting rapid flame kernel development. The optimized configuration maintains similar indicated thermal efficiency (ITE) 45.6%, while with significantly decreasing hydrocarbons by 24% and CO by 29%, and the combustion duration (CA90-CA10) is also reduced by 19%, highlighting the potential of strategic jet-spray interactions in improving methanol engine performance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Rice Straw-derived Phosphorus/Boron co-doped hierarchical porous carbon with optimized structure–property Characteristics for high-performance supercapacitors
Abstract: Rice straw is an abundant agricultural residue, and its conversion into functional carbon materials offers a sustainable route for resource utilization and energy-storage applications. Herein, phosphorus/boron co-doped hierarchical porous carbons were prepared from rice straw through hydrothermal-assisted activation and temperature-controlled carbonization. The influence of carbonization temperature on pore architecture, surface chemistry, structural ordering, and electrochemical behavior was systematically investigated. The results show that P/B co-doping combined with optimized carbonization effectively regulated the porous structure and charge-storage kinetics. Among the obtained samples, RS-PB-700 exhibited a well-developed hierarchical porous framework with a specific surface area of 909.2 m2 g⁻1, favorable pore connectivity, and favorable interfacial charge-transfer characteristics. Consequently, RS-PB-700 delivered a high specific capacitance of 451.2 F g⁻1 at 0.5 A g⁻1 and retained 295.0 F g⁻1 at 10 A g⁻1 in a three-electrode system. The assembled symmetric supercapacitor achieved an energy density of 8.7 Wh kg⁻1 at a power density of 50 W kg⁻1, together with good rate capability and low charge-transfer resistance. DFT calculations further revealed that P/B incorporation modulates the electronic states of the carbon framework and induces pronounced local charge redistribution around the heteroatom sites. The enhanced performance is attributed to the synergistic effects of hierarchical porosity, heteroatom-induced surface chemistry and electronic modulation, and favorable ion-transport and interfacial charge-transfer behavior. Title: A fully coupled XFEM analysis of complex fracture network development during multi-cluster hydraulic fracturing in naturally fractured formations
Abstract: Multi-cluster hydraulic fracturing in naturally fractured reservoirs is often limited by non-uniform fracture propagation, yet the controlling mechanisms of NFs remain insufficiently understood. This study develops a fully coupled XFEM-based framework to simulate multi-cluster hydraulic fracturing, incorporating rock deformation, fracture propagation, fluid flow, frictional contact, leak-off, fluid partitioning, and HF-NF interactions. A unified solution strategy is introduced by incorporating a virtual pressure node and perforation flow elements, enabling the coupled problem to be solved without external iteration. The model is validated against analytical solutions for the KGD problem and benchmark cases of multi-cluster fracture propagation. Parametric analyses demonstrate that NFs promote uneven fracture growth and require higher perforation friction to compensate for the additional resistance induced by fracture deflection following NF capture. When HFs cannot cross NFs, higher stress differences increase net pressure and improve fracture growth uniformity, while smaller intersection angles enhance uniform propagation but generate simpler fracture geometries. Increasing NF aperture initially promotes balanced fracture growth and subsequently favors the development of more complex fracture networks. NF friction has a limited effect when crossing is inhibited, but once crossing occurs, fracture evolution becomes strongly controlled by HF-NF interaction patterns. Random NF distributions introduce significant uncertainty, with near-wellbore NFs playing a key role in fracture competition. These findings provide novel insights for optimizing multi-cluster fracturing designs in naturally fractured reservoirs. © 2026

Title: High-load self-lubricating EP/PTFE composites via stress-triggered solid-liquid core MoS2/PAO6@UF microcapsules
Abstract: Self-lubricating spherical plain bearings are key components in aircraft flight-control systems, and their moldable liners must provide stable lubrication under high-load conditions. However, it remains challenging to achieve low friction, low wear, and durable transfer-film protection in epoxy-based self-lubricating liner materials. The resulting microcapsules were denoted as MoS₂/PAO6@UF microcapsules. The microcapsules showed spherical morphologies, an average particle size of 6–7 μm, and good thermal stability below 200 °C. Under 1500 N and 100 rpm, the composite containing 5 wt% MoS2 in the microcapsule core exhibited the lowest coefficient of friction of 0.056, whereas the composite containing 10 wt% MoS2 achieved the lowest wear rate of 6.4 × 10−8 mm3/(N·m). Step-loading tests showed that the composites maintained effective lubrication up to 6.5–7.5 kN, indicating good high-load-bearing capability. Optical microscopy, FTIR, XPS, and Raman analyses confirmed the formation of a composite lubricating interface composed of released PAO6, a PTFE transfer film, and a MoS2 solid lubricating film. The released PAO6 continuously replenished the oil film and reduced interfacial shear, MoS2 provided solid lubrication and contributed to the formation of a tribochemical reaction film, and the PTFE-rich transfer film stabilized the lubricating interface. These results establish a stress-triggered and three-component lubrication strategy for high-load and moldable epoxy liners. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Numerical analysis of the effects of nozzle number on jet ignition mechanism and combustion characteristics in a methanol engine with a passive pre-chamber
Abstract: Pre-chamber jet ignition can improve ignition stability and accelerate flame propagation under lean-burn conditions. However, the effects of design parameters, particularly nozzle number, on the ignition process and combustion characteristics of passive pre-chamber methanol engines remain unclear. In this study, a passive pre-chamber ignition system was designed for a pure methanol engine and the effects of nozzle number were investigated by varying the number of nozzles from 1 to 6 while maintaining an approximately constant total nozzle flow area. A CFD model was established and validated against experimental data. At ignition, the one nozzle case has the highest methanol mass and average mass fraction in the pre-chamber. The six-nozzle case has the lowest values. The one nozzle case forms the earliest hot jet because of its larger nozzle diameter and weaker nozzle quenching, corresponding to a jet flame ignition mode. However, the concentrated jet impinges on the piston bowl, causing momentum and heat losses and slowing down the later flame expansion. In contrast, the smaller nozzles enhance nozzle quenching during flame discharge, so the flame enters the main chamber as separated flame kernels rather than a continuous jet. This distributed jet ignition mode improves flame coverage and shortens the flame propagation distance. Under the investigated operating condition, the six nozzle case showed the fastest pressure rise and shortest CA10–CA90 combustion duration among the four configurations. Its CA10, CA50 and CA90 were 2.5, 6.6 and 14.3∘CA ATDC, respectively. For the six nozzle case, the Borghi–Peters trajectories mainly occupy the thin reaction zones regime in the pre-chamber and move toward the corrugated flamelets regime during later main chamber combustion. Title: Mechanochemical activation of recycled glass–biogenic CaO composites: Structural evolution, hydration behavior, and silicate-network modification
Abstract: Mechanochemistry has emerged as a sustainable strategy for producing advanced materials from industrial and biogenic wastes. In this study, mechanochemically activated composites were synthesized using post-consumer recycled soda–lime glass as an amorphous support and biogenic calcium oxide (BCO) derived from waste eggshells as the active phase. Composites containing 5–95 wt% BCO were prepared by high-energy ball milling and characterized by X-ray fluorescence (XRF), X-ray diffraction (XRD) coupled with Rietveld refinement, Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The results revealed that mechanochemical activation significantly reduced the CaO crystallite size from 148.5 to 25.4 nm, while preserving the amorphous nature of the recycled glass matrix. The degree of crystallinity increased progressively with increasing BCO content, reaching 66.2% for the composite containing 95 wt% BCO; however, a substantial amorphous fraction persisted in all compositions, suggesting the formation of highly disordered crystal–amorphous interfacial regions. FTIR and Raman analyses indicated progressive modifications of the silicate network, evidenced by the formation of non-bridging oxygens and Ca–O–Si interfacial species. The Raman intensity ratio (I356/I1084) exhibited segmented behavior, revealing a critical composition of approximately 75 wt% BCO, corresponding to the transition from a glass-dominated to a CaO-dominated structural regime. Authors: Lan S.; Cai X.; Friedrich A.; Lin R.
Title: Intelligent prediction of transport properties in multicomponent-integrated gas diffusion layer
Abstract: Proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) is regarded as a promising energy source in the fields of transportation and distributed power generation. Gas diffusion layer (GDL) including macroporous substrate (MPS) and microporous layer (MPL), is a key component of PEMFC. The porous structure and multicomponent spatial distribution change the overall transport capacity of GDL. In this study, an innovative multicomponent integrated construction method is proposed, enabling controllable component distribution by morphological generation and geometric constraints. Multidimensional GDL database and multitask learning model are developed to predict the transport properties (including permeability, effective diffusivity, tortuosity) and velocity distributed images of GDL simultaneously. The effects of network, hyperparameters, and loss weights on prediction performance are systematically investigated. The results of this study show that the coefficient of determination for all transport properties are above 0.9 by the UNet-based multitask learning model. Balancing the loss weights among individual tasks can effectively improve the model convergence behavior and generalization capability. The prediction of transport properties is affected by the addition of binder and polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), while the model shows good robustness. This study provides a new research paradigm and technical support for the structural design and optimization of GDL. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Tailoring the nanostructure and graphitization of soot by metal nanoparticles in continuous nanofluid fuel pyrolysis
Abstract: Nanofluid fuel has great potential application value in the field of internal combustion engines and aerospace ramjet due to its high energy density, but the roles of metal nanoparticles in governing carbonaceous product nanostructures during the application of nanofluid fuels were still poorly unclear. In this work, the central objective was to elucidate how different metal nanoparticles actively modulate the nanostructure and graphitization of pyrolytic soot. The correlations between metal nanoparticle and soot characteristic parameters were established by integrating detailed analysis. The results indicated that different metal nanoparticles can serve as sites for soot nucleation and growth, thereby leading to varying degrees of enhancement in nanostructure ordering and graphitization degree. With the exception of the Al nanoparticle condition, soot morphology, nanostructure, and graphitization degree exhibited a positive correlation with the concentration of metal nanoparticles addition. Moreover, heterogeneous nucleation induced by the metal nanoparticles improved the uniformity of primary soot particle size. Although the addition of metal nanoparticles increased soot graphitization degree, the catalytic effects arising from the incorporation of Al, Cu, and CuO also significantly accelerated the oxidation rate of the pyrolysis products. Overall, this work was of great significance for optimizing advanced fuel systems and managing carbonaceous emissions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: High-speed characterization of spray ignition and combustion-coupled dynamics via PLIF, X-ray PCI, and broadband imaging
Abstract: This study investigates spark ignition dynamics in a liquid-fueled model combustor under ambient inlet conditions. Two hollow-cone nozzles with different inlet geometries are compared using simultaneous high-speed X-ray phase-contrast imaging (PCI) and broadband imaging to capture spray and flame behavior before and after stabilization. The spray dispersion and hollow-cone lobe structures are quantified via fuel planar laser-induced fluorescence (PLIF). Lagrangian particle tracking is performed to extract droplet size distributions, velocities, and evaporation rates, providing a micro-scale description of the spray-combustion dynamics near the nozzle. While reduced evaporation due to droplet-droplet interactions has been evidenced in simplified arrays and computational models, direct experimental quantification within sprays remains limited. The results demonstrate that dense-spray shielding significantly suppresses bulk evaporation, with combusting spray effective evaporation rates decreasing by ≈30% (0.45 to 0.30--0.32mm2/s) across the combined operational envelope of both evaluated nozzles. Theoretical models of the spray geometry further indicate that droplet-droplet interactions reduce the effective evaporation rate by at least 45% relative to isolated droplets. However, across this same combined operational envelope, the empirical ignition probability increased from 0.01 to 0.37 suggesting that successful ignition is primarily governed by localized vaporization in the immediate vicinity of the spark. Furthermore, combustion-induced thermal expansion is found to accelerate droplets and alter their trajectories, whereas the early-stage flame kernel trajectory remains essentially identical regardless of ignition success. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Cong Z.; Huang A.; Shi D.; Niu R.; Kan R.; Nie W.; Li R.; Xu Z.
Title: Laser spectroscopy diagnostics in shock tubes for high-temperature chemical kinetics
Abstract: This review summarizes recent advances in laser spectroscopy diagnostics for shock-tube studies of transient high-temperature processes. As a well-controlled high-temperature reactor, the shock tube provides a reproducible platform for probing chemical kinetics relevant to combustion, fuel conversion, pollutant formation, and non-equilibrium reacting flows. The review covers the major diagnostic families used in this field, including tunable diode and quantum cascade laser absorption spectroscopy, cavity-enhanced absorption spectroscopy, atomic resonance absorption spectroscopy, planar laser-induced fluorescence, and Raman- and grating-based techniques. Emphasis is placed on recent progress in temporal resolution, multi-parameter sensing, trace-species detection, and robustness under high-temperature and high-pressure conditions. Representative applications in fuel pyrolysis and oxidation, radical chemistry, non-equilibrium processes, and emerging pollutant systems are discussed to illustrate how laser diagnostics provide stringent constraints for chemical-kinetic model development and validation. Current limitations, including spectral interference, pressure broadening, calibration complexity, and spatial non-uniformity, are also assessed. Finally, future trends toward integrated diagnostics, intelligent spectral inversion, and broader deployment in zero-carbon-fuel and hypersonic-flow studies are outlined. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Energy management strategy for enhancing methanol economy of direct methanol fuel cell/lithium-ion battery hybrid power system
Abstract: Direct methanol fuel cell (DMFC)/lithium-ion battery hybrid power systems are promising for portable and off-grid applications because they combine the high energy density of liquid methanol with the fast power response of batteries. However, under dynamic load demand, the slow transient response and irreversible methanol consumption of DMFC systems make it challenging to achieve both stable power supply and efficient fuel utilization. In this paper, a dynamic model of a DMFC/lithium-ion battery hybrid power system is developed by considering DMFC voltage characteristics, mass transport processes, battery state of charge (SOC), and methanol level dynamics. The level of methanol (LOM) is incorporated into the prediction model to characterize methanol level variation, enabling predictive energy management considering both lithium-ion battery buffering capability and methanol level. Based on this model, an MPC-based energy management strategy is proposed to coordinate the power distribution between the DMFC stack and lithium-ion battery over the prediction horizon. Unlike conventional rule-based strategies relying on instantaneous feedback, the proposed MPC framework considers methanol economy, SOC deviation, and DMFC power variation constraints simultaneously. Simulation and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) experimental results demonstrate that the proposed strategy satisfies load demand, smooths DMFC power response, maintains battery SOC within an appropriate range, and reduces equivalent methanol consumption by 5.0 mL compared with rule-based energy management strategy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Modification of the air-water interface in soy protein foam using plasma-activated water and citric acid for egg white replacement: Foaming properties, drainage kinetics, protein structure, and rheological behavior
Abstract: Plant-based proteins generally have inferior foaming capabilities compared to animal proteins, which limits their application in bakery products. In this study, we improved the air-water interface of soybean protein foam using a combination of plasma-activated water (PAW) and citric acid (CA) and evaluated its potential as an egg white substitute. Specifically, we focused on foaming characteristics, foam release rate, rheological behavior, and protein structure. An artificial neural network was used for exploratory screening of PAW generation and processing conditions, and the selected operating region was further evaluated using response surface methodology. Foam release rate was modeled and analyzed to predict foam destabilization and evaluate foam stability (FS) over time. Analysis of particle size distribution and zeta potential revealed that combined PAW and CA treatment improved aggregation uniformity and dispersion stability compared to CA treatment alone. Free sulfhydryl content increased after PAW treatment but decreased after combined PAW and CA treatment. PAW and CA treatments reduced the density of SPI meringue and increased the overrun, while PAW treatment increased the apparent viscosity and storage modulus of the continuous phase. CD and FTIR analyses confirmed that PAW and CA treatments modified the secondary structure of SPI. Collectively, these results demonstrate that the combination of PAW and CA effectively modifies the molecular structure of SPI and significantly enhances foaming function, presenting a promising strategy for the development of EW substitutes in bakery products. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Mo S.; Lei J.; Wang D.; Zhang L.; Yao B.; Yu C.; Hu W.; Man X.; Peng N.
Title: Nonlinear dynamic characteristics analysis of spiral bevel gear transmission system with tooth breakage fault
Abstract: Tooth breakage in spiral bevel gears severely degrades transmission stability. Unlike spur gears, their meshing is spatially dependent and time-varying, complicating analytical computation of time-varying meshing stiffness (TVMS). An enhanced hybrid method integrating slice theory and the potential energy principle is proposed to compute TVMS under tooth breakage, effectively capturing the sudden stiffness reduction. The approach is validated against a finite element model. A nonlinear dynamic model with backlash and static transmission error is subsequently developed. Dynamic responses in healthy and faulty states are compared through time waveforms, phase portraits, spectra, and bifurcation diagrams. A multi-scale perturbation analysis further reveals the influences of meshing stiffness, damping ratio, and external torque on primary resonance. Results demonstrate that tooth breakage decreases effective meshing tooth pairs, causing sharp stiffness transitions. The system exhibits pronounced instability within 2600–3000 rpm, whereas higher damping markedly improves stability. Experimental spectra confirm the fault signature as amplified sidebands around the mesh fundamental frequency. The proposed framework offers an accurate and computationally efficient analytical tool for dynamic simulation and fault diagnosis of spiral bevel gears with tooth breakage. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS

Authors: Wang Y.; Yang Y.; Zhang Y.; Gao K.; Tang J.
Title: Evolution of the spontaneous combustion characteristics of thermally decomposed coal and its underlying mechanism
Abstract: Thermal decomposition is ubiquitous in underground coal mining, but its influence on spontaneous combustion characteristics (SCC) remains controversial, and the underlying mechanism has yet to be fully elucidated. This study investigated the SCC and underlying evolutionary mechanism of thermally decomposed coal (TDC) through low-temperature oxidation, TG-DSC, kinetic analysis, FTIR and ESR experiments. The results show that the TDC presented lower crossing point temperature and produced more CO and CO2 during the initial stage of low-temperature oxidation, while in the later stage it is the opposite. The TG-DSC analysis indicates that the initial mass loss of TDC is greater, and the characteristic temperature is lower. The kinetic analysis shows that the activation energy of TDC in the initial stage is 33.18 kJ·mol−1, which is lower than raw coal. But it rapidly increases to 231.97 kJ·mol−1 and remains higher than raw coal. The ESR experiments indicated that the concentration of TDC radicals after thermal decomposition at 200℃ reaches 3.27 times than raw coal. Combined with the FTIR analysis, it further indicated that the thermal effect causes the unstable functional groups decomposed and produced active sites, resulting in enhanced SCC in the early stage; while the premature decomposition of the functional groups leads to the weakened SCC in the later stage. Therefore, TDC exhibited enhanced SCC at the early stage of oxidation, but weakened later on. These findings provide possible causes and prevention strategies for re-ignition of fire area after its unsealing. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Li W.; Liu M.; Zheng S.; Li Y.; Liu Y.; Wu L.; Chen S.; Li L.; Sun C.; Zhang H.; An B.
Title: Accelerated surface reconstruction via a controllable boronization strategy for efficient water oxidation
Abstract: Efficient and stable water electrolysis is crucial for hydrogen production as a means of clean energy storage and conversion. However, the anodic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is hampered by sluggish kinetics, owing to its complex multi-step proton-coupled electron transfer process, which leads to high overpotentials and limited catalyst stability. Although the crystalline phase of electrocatalysts plays a pivotal role in determining OER activity, the fundamental relationship between phase structure and catalytic performance remains insufficiently understood. Herein, we report a controllable and mild boronization strategy to in situ construct ultrathin boron-incorporated metal–organic framework nanosheet arrays (Co-MOF/B). The mild boronization process preserves the intrinsic MOF architecture while introducing abundant crystalline-amorphous (C-A) interfaces and defect sites. These structural features facilitate charge transport and promote an early onset of surface reconstruction at 1.36 V, as directly revealed by Operando Raman spectroscopy, enabling the rapid formation of highly active oxyhydroxide species. Consequently, the Co-MOF/B catalyst demonstrates outstanding OER performance, requiring only 270 mV overpotential to achieve 10 mA cm−2, with a low Tafel slope of 67.7 mV dec-1 and excellent long-term durability. This work elucidates the critical role of precisely engineered C-A heterostructures in regulating surface reconstruction and catalytic kinetics, providing new insights into the rational design of high-performance OER electrocatalysts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wang Y.; Li M.; Wang Z.; Zhang L.; Sun B.; Ma S.
Title: Hydrothermal incubation-induced amyloid fibrillation of wheat gluten peptide: regulation of functional properties via multi-scale structural and morphological evolution
Abstract: The regulatory effects of different fibrillation conditions on the multiscale structure and morphology of gluten peptide amyloid fibrils (AFs), as well as their functional properties were investigated. The results showed that gluten peptides could self-assemble into AFs following incubation between 0 and 36 h at temperatures ranging from 60 to 90 °C. AFM images revealed that the AFs underwent a morphological evolution, changing from worm-like, long, flexible forms and dendritic, entangled networks to rigid, rod-like or amorphous aggregates. Raising the temperature can significantly accelerate the fibrillation process and increase the yield of AFs. ThT fluorescence intensity increased significantly by 55.76% following incubation at 90 °C for 36 h (p < 0.05). Circular dichroism spectroscopy confirmed that fibrillation was accompanied by conformational transition, in which α-helix and random coil were gradually transformed into a β-sheet structure. The proportion of this structure reached 36.09% after incubation at 90 °C for 36 h. Furthermore, prolonged incubation facilitated the formation of AFs with a larger particle size and a higher molecular weight. These structural and morphological differences further dominate the functional properties of AFs. The formation of AFs markedly reduced the solubility of the system. Long, flexible AFs formed after 12 h of incubation and abundant, entangled AFs networks formed after 24 h exhibited superior foaming capacity, emulsifying property and viscosity. However, prolonged incubation at high temperature (90 °C for 36 h) triggers the degradation of amyloid fibrils and impairs their functional activity. These findings clarify the regulatory mechanism of incubation conditions on the structure and function of gluten AFs, providing a theoretical basis for their diverse applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Synthesis, characterization, and DFT studies of metal-free hydrazide co-sensitizers with N719 for Pt-free DSSCs achieving 12.53% outdoor and 26.66% indoor efficiency

Abstract: Two metal-free organic sensitizers, MTP-1 and SPZ-1 , incorporating methoxytriphenylamine and phenylphenothiazine donor units, respectively, with a carboxyhydrazide-based acceptor/anchoring segment, were synthesized, characterized, and evaluated as co-sensitizers with N719 for dye-sensitized solar cells. Co-sensitization with N719 significantly enhanced the optical response of TiO₂ photoanodes, with the absorbance following the order MTP-1 + N719 > SPZ-1 + N719 > N719 , confirming complementary light harvesting between the organic ICT transitions and the MLCT absorption of N719. DFT calculations further supported the experimental findings, showing effective spatial separation between HOMO and LUMO levels, directional charge transfer from the donor moieties toward the carboxyhydrazide anchoring unit, and stable bidentate adsorption on TiO₂. To improve redox regeneration and charge transport, a Pt-free PEDOT/SnSe-rGO composite counter electrode was employed. Under AM 1.5G illumination, the MTP-1 + N719:PEDOT/SnSe-rGO device achieved the highest efficiency of 12.53%, outperforming the corresponding Pt-based device and N719 -only systems. Remarkably, under indoor illumination at 1000 lx, the same device delivered an outstanding efficiency of 26.66%, with enhanced VOC, JSC, and fill factor.
