Author full names: Jeong, Haemin (60963765400); Kim, Daniel (57208283202); Choi, Myounghyun (59467294300); Kim, Ah-Ram (55725837100)
Title: Enzyme-driven fluorescence quantification of micro and nanoplastics
Abstract: Accurate detection of micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) remains challenging due to analytical limitations, particularly for nanoplastics(<1 μm). Here, we introduce a rapid and simple fluorescence-based method for MNP quantification using a plastic-degrading enzyme. Target plastics are enzymatically depolymerized to generate specific degradation products, which are subsequently quantified via fluorescence measurement. The method enables selective detection of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and other terephthalate-releasing plastics across a broad size range, from microplastics to nanoplastics. After removal of divalent cations, the assay provides results within 6 h of enzymatic reaction with LODs of 0.43 mg/L and 0.04 mg/L for microplastics (90 μm) and nanoplastics (0.2 μm) PET standards, respectively; concentrations are reported as PET-equivalent mass referenced to these size-matched standards. Quantitative results showed good agreement with orthogonal reference methods — micro-Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy for microplastics and pyrolysis–gas chromatography/mass spectrometry for nanoplastics. This approach provides a practical alternative for rapid MNPs analysis and offers improved accessibility for nanoplastics, supporting its high throughput use in laboratories without specialized instrumentation, for aqueous samples of low matrix complexity. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Wan K.; Kou X.; Wu Y.; Zhao K.-H.; Liu J.-W.; Wang Y.; Li X.-S.
Title: Characteristics of heat transfer and secondary hydrate formation during depressurization with symmetrical well patterns in a pilot-scale simulator
Abstract: Natural gas hydrate (NGH) is a promising clean energy resource; however, efficient and sustainable exploitation remains a bottleneck for large-scale commercial production. To overcome limitations of single-well systems, multi-well pattern optimization has become a pivotal research focus. This study compared a peripheral four-spot vertical-well pattern with a central single vertical well in sandy sediments using a 117.8 L pilot-scale hydrate simulator. Hydrate dissociation, gas and water production, and heat- and mass-transfer behavior were evaluated under depressurization. The four-spot pattern exhibited a double-edged effect. During the depressurization stage, its larger gas–liquid contact area and more complex flow field intensified secondary hydrate formation; the peak secondary-hydrate proportion reached 22.7%, compared with 6.1% for the single well. The resulting blockage delayed pressure propagation, reduced early gas production, and lowered the gas-to-water ratio. During the constant-pressure stage, however, peripheral dissociation reduced the thermal resistance near the reactor boundary and enhanced inward heat transfer. Consequently, the four-spot pattern reached a final dissociation ratio of 99.9%, compared with 95.3% for the single well, and shortened the constant-pressure production period by 25.7%. These results show that increasing well density can improve late-stage recovery but may aggravate early flow-assurance risks. Multi-well design should therefore coordinate well spacing and depressurization strategy to suppress secondary hydrate formation while preserving heat-transfer benefits. Copyright © 2026. Authors: Erçek E.
Title: Multi-objective optimization of combustion, performance, and emission characteristics of diesel–MTBE–SiO2 fuel blends in a single-cylinder diesel engine using response surface methodology
Abstract: The growing need for cleaner and more efficient diesel engine operation has increased interest in oxygenated fuel additives and nanoparticle-based fuel strategies. This study experimentally investigated the effects of methyl tert -butyl ether (MTBE) and silicon dioxide (SiO2) addition on the combustion, performance, and emission characteristics of a single-cylinder compression-ignition diesel engine using response surface methodology (RSM). The experiments were conducted at 1800 rpm, considering engine load (8.24–24.72 Nm), MTBE ratio (5–15 vol%), and SiO2 concentration (50–150 ppm) as input variables. A face-centered central composite design (CCD) comprising 18 experimental runs was employed, and second-order regression models were developed for the investigated responses. Model adequacy was assessed using analysis of variance (ANOVA) and related statistical criteria. The results showed that engine load was the dominant factor influencing the investigated responses, particularly the performance and emission characteristics. Increasing engine load increased indicated mean effective pressure (IMEP) and indicated thermal efficiency (ITE) while decreasing brake-specific fuel consumption (BSFC), but resulted in higher nitrogen oxides (NOx) emissions. Moderate MTBE concentrations of approximately 9–11 vol% and SiO2 concentrations of approximately 90–110 ppm were associated with favorable performance responses. Multi-objective optimization identified 24.72 Nm engine load, 7.84 vol% MTBE, and 150 ppm SiO2 as the global optimum within the investigated experimental domain, with an overall desirability of 0.570. This condition represents a compromise among the conflicting combustion, performance, and emission objectives rather than the individually optimum condition for each response. Experimental validation under the optimized condition showed good agreement with the RSM predictions, with an average deviation of 4.71%. The findings indicate that MTBE–SiO2 blending can provide a favorable balance among the investigated engine responses under the tested operating conditions; however, the results are limited to the specified engine, operating speed, and fuel composition ranges. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Author full names: Deng, Haofeng (59665658000); Gao, Pengyu (60024493800); Zhang, Yanxi (51162336600); Gao, Xiangdong (55712057100)
Title: Microstructure and mechanical properties of resistance spot welded joints in three-layer plates of dissimilar steel
Abstract: Resistance spot welding (RSW) of dissimilar three-layer steel sheets involves complex thermal-metallurgical interactions due to material mismatch and multilayer heat transfer. In this study, the microstructural evolution and mechanical behavior of DC01, DP590 and SUS304 three-layer joints were systematically investigated using scanning electron microscopy, microhardness testing, and tensile-shear experiments. The results show that a typical fusion nugget is formed, while the intermediate layer induces pronounced asymmetry in nugget morphology, resulting in an elliptical or eccentric fusion zone. Significant elemental diffusion and microstructural heterogeneity are observed across the fusion zone and heat-affected zone (HAZ). A distinct hardness gradient is identified, with high hardness in the fusion zone dominated by martensitic transformation and reduced hardness in the HAZ associated with partial phase transformation and tempering effects. Fracture analysis reveals that the joints are primarily governed by button fracture (BF) and interfacial fracture (IF). The transition between these modes is controlled by the relative strength between the weld nugget and surrounding materials, which is strongly influenced by material combination and welding parameters. These findings clarify the coupling relationship between microstructure, hardness distribution, and fracture behavior in multilayer dissimilar steel welds, and provide guidance for optimizing welding parameters to enhance joint reliability and load-bearing capacity. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS

Authors: Lu T.; Liu H.; Wang T.; Sun K.; Lin T.; Jia Z.; Wang H.; Yu S.; Song Y.; Zhang X.
Title: Toward ammonia-to-NOx ratio control in an ammonia/diesel dual direct-injection engine under low-load conditions
Abstract: An excessive ammonia-to-NOx ratio (ANR) under low-load operation poses a challenge to the efficient operation of aftertreatment systems in ammonia-fueled engines. In this study, experiments were conducted on a single-cylinder ammonia/diesel dual direct-injection (DDI) engine to investigate the effects of ammonia substitution ratio (ASR), intake pressure, dual-fuel injection pressure, and injection timing (−28 to −12°CA ATDC) on NH3 emissions, NOx emissions, and the ANR under a low-load condition of 4 bar indicated mean effective pressure (IMEP). The results show that increasing ASR is the dominant factor driving the increase in the ANR. When the ASR was maintained below 60%, coordinated optimization of intake pressure, dual-fuel injection pressure, and injection timing under the late diesel injection strategy reduced the ANR to 1.1–1.25 while maintaining a high indicated thermal efficiency (ITE), thereby reducing the ANR to a level compatible with the efficient operating window of the aftertreatment system, and engine-out N2O emissions showed no evident deterioration. Furthermore, by substantially advancing diesel injection timing (−340 to −220°CA ATDC) to establish a thermally favorable in-cylinder environment before ammonia combustion, the ANR could be further reduced to below 1.0. However, a trade-off between ASR and ITE together with a marked increase in engine-out N2O emissions was observed under this strategy. The study systematically elucidates the regulation characteristics of key combustion control parameters on the ANR under low-load conditions and proposes practical ANR control strategies for ammonia/diesel DDI engines. The findings provide new insights into the optimization of ammonia utilization and energy conversion efficiency, and offer useful guidance for in-cylinder combustion control with aftertreatment requirements in ammonia-fueled engines. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Jiang Q.; Zhao X.-L.; Zhang H.; Wu W.-H.; Ng M.K.
Title: A convolutional low-rank continuous tensor representation for multi-dimensional data recovery
Abstract: Convolutional low-rank methods have been widely used in image processing and computer vision due to their ability to capture local spatial structure. However, existing convolutional low-rank methods are limited to rectangular meshgrids at a fixed scale, which restricts their applicability to emerging real-world spatial-irregular data, such as semantic spatial sub-regions and spatial transcriptomics. To overcome this limitation, we propose a convolutional low-rank tensor representation for spatial arbitrary-shape multi-dimensional data. Specifically, by representing the latent tensor through an implicit neural representation, we impose a new tensor nuclear norm (low-rank regularization) on the sampled domain by inferring the inside/outside data entries and develop a new ARbiTrary-shape Convolutional Tensor Nuclear Norm (ART-CTNN). Compared with classic convolutional low-rank tensor representations, ART-CTNN offers two key advantages: it unifies the exploration of the convolutional low-rank prior for spatial arbitrary-shape data, and it can exploit convolutional low-rankness at arbitrary resolutions beyond the original sampling grid, allowing regularization at a suitable scale. Extensive experiments on both regular and irregular datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves the recovery performance of complex spatial details and structures, while further enhancing downstream clustering performance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Author full names: Abraham, Ittai (7102212547); Asharov, Gilad (35101449100); Patil, Shravani (57205421438); Patra, Arpita (23036343000)
Title: Detect, Pack and Batch: Perfectly Secure MPC with Linear Communication and Constant Expected Time
Abstract: We prove that perfectly secure optimally resilient secure multiparty computation (MPC) for a circuit with C gates and depth D can be obtained in O((Cn+n4+Dn2)logn) communication complexity and O(D) expected time. For D≪n and C≥n3, this is the first perfectly secure optimally resilient MPC protocol with linear communication complexity per gate and constant expected time complexity per layer. Compared to state-of-the-art MPC protocols in the player elimination framework [Beerliova and Hirt TCC’08, and Goyal, Liu, and Song CRYPTO’19], for C>n3 and D≪n, our results significantly improve the run time from Ω(n+D) to expected O(D) while keeping communication complexity at O(Cnlogn). Compared to state-of-the-art MPC protocols that obtain an expected O(D) time complexity [Abraham, Asharov, and Yanai TCC’21], for C>n3, our results significantly improve the communication complexity from O(Cn4logn) to O(Cnlogn) while keeping the expected run time at O(D). One salient part of our technical contribution is centered around a new primitive we call detectable secret sharing. It is perfectly hiding, weakly binding and has the property that either reconstruction succeeds, or Ω(n) parties are (privately) detected. On the one hand, we show that detectable secret sharing is sufficiently powerful to generate multiplication triplets needed for MPC. On the other hand, we show how to share p secrets via detectable secret sharing with communication complexity of just O(n4logn+plogn). When sharing p≥n4 secrets, the communication cost is amortized to just O(1) field elements per secret. Our second technical contribution is a new verifiable secret sharing protocol that can share p secrets at just O(n4logn+pnlogn) word complexity. When sharing p≥n3 secrets, the communication cost is amortized to just O(n) field elements per secret. The best prior required Ω(n3) communication per secret. © International Association for Cryptologic Research 2026.

Authors: Li L.; Chen X.; Chen X.; Liu J.; Zeng J.; Pan C.; Kang F.; Yuan J.; Du Y.
Title: Symbiotic effects of high-pressure acid etching on the oxidation characteristics of coal during coal-and-gas co-mining
Abstract: Coal-and-gas co-mining involves the pre-extraction of coalbed methane (CBM) prior to coal mining, and pressurized acid injection for permeability improvement in coal mass is widely adopted to increase gas production in CBM wells. However, insufficient attention has been given to its effects on spontaneous combustion of coal in the subsequent underground coal mining. In this study, high-rank bituminous coal samples were immersed in acid pressurized at 10 MPa at six hydrofluoric acid concentrations, 0%, 3%, 6%, 9%, 12%, and 15%, and then laboratory tests were conducted to explore the influence of acid etching on the oxidation characteristics of coal. Temperature-programmed oxidation, low-temperature nitrogen adsorption, fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, and wavelength-dispersive X-ray fluorescence spectroscopy were used to characterize variations in oxidation characteristics, pore structure, oxygen-containing functional group composition, and elemental content of coal after high-pressure acidification. The research results show that (1) high-pressure acid etching altered coal spontaneous combustion tendency from spontaneous combustion of raw coal to easily spontaneous combustion of the acid-etched coal due to the obvious change in oxidation characteristics of coal; (2) compared with those of high-pressure water-immersed coal, the specific surface area and average pore diameter of acid-etched coal increased by maximums of 78.5% and 92.8%, respectively, improving coal–oxygen contact efficiency and expanding the reaction scale; (3) compared with those of high-pressure water-immersed coal, the maximum relative contents of oxygen-containing functional groups and Fe2O3 in acid-etched coal increased by 36.8% and 138%, respectively, increasing the intensity of coal–oxygen reactions. Authors: Ding C.; Han Q.; Huang H.; Zhu H.; Jiao Y.; Wu L.; Li Y.; Qin R.; Zhang X.
Title: Flame height correction model and over-wall burning criterion for pitched roof–firewall systems
Abstract: The spread of flames across a firewall is a critical process in the propagation of fires from pitched-roof buildings to adjacent spaces. This study conducted experiments on pitched-roof-firewall systems under still air conditions, varying the roof pitch (α=20°-40°) and burner-to-wall distance ( d = 0.1–0.4 m) and heat release rate (Q̇ = 30.8–61.6 kW) on an adjustable-slope platform. A total of 48 tests with firewalls and 12 baseline tests without firewalls were conducted to measure flame height, deflection angle, and the flame attachment length along the slope. The results indicate that slope angle has the most significant suppressive effect on vertical flame height, followed by heat release rate; wall distance has a weaker direct effect on flame height, primarily modulating flame deflection and the flame attachment length along the slope by altering the entrainment conditions on both sides of the flame. Using the wall-free reference height Hf,0 as the characteristic length and introducing the dimensionless wall distance η=d/Hf,0, a flame height correction model for wall-present conditions was established; furthermore, a confined-transitional-over-wall burning criterion centered on Hf/hw was proposed. This criterion agrees well with experimental observations and the frequency of over-wall burning, and can serve as a reference for the performance-based design of firewalls on sloped roofs and for assessing the risk of over-wall burning. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Nonlinear proportional-integral control for robust stabilization of a twin-rotor system
Abstract: This paper addresses the design of a nonlinear proportional-integral controller based on sliding mode control, applied to a twin-rotor system. The objective of the proposed scheme is to reduce the steady-state error in the system’s position trajectories under uncertain conditions and external disturbances. To this end, a non-conventional proportional-integral sliding manifold is introduced. Specifically, when sliding motion occurs, the position dynamics of the twin-rotor system are analyzed as a perturbed system with a proportional-integral closed-loop controller. In this context, the proportional-integral gains of the dynamics are adjusted through a convex optimization problem formulated with a set of matrix inequalities. Since the system dynamics are coupled, stability is ensured in the sense of ultimate uniform boundedness. Finally, a comparative study based on an error criterion is presented to validate the performance of the proposed control algorithm. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Title: Revealing compressive damage evolution in particle-reinforced HTPB propellant via in-situ X-ray CT and image-based mesoscale modeling
Abstract: Hydroxyl-terminated polybutadiene (HTPB) propellant is a multiphase composite widely used in launch vehicles. Investigating the evolution of its internal microstructure under loading is essential for ensuring in-service reliability. To elucidate the compressive deformation and internal failure mechanisms, this study combines in-situ X-ray computed tomography (CT) compression experiment with mesoscale modeling based on CT slices. In-situ X-ray CT tests captured the full-field damage evolution across five compression stages. From the 2D CT images, the spatial distribution and morphological features of ammonium perchlorate (AP) particles were extracted. Through reconstruction and optimization, a high-quality tetrahedral mesh of the AP particles was obtained. Subsequently, a two-phase mesoscale model of the HTPB propellant was developed by projecting the distribution characteristics of the AP tetrahedral mesh onto a hexahedral-mesh domain. The numerical simulations show good agreement with experimental observations. The results reveal that under compressive loading, failure initiates as local interfacial debonding between the matrix and AP particles, which progressively coalesces into macroscopic shear bands. This work provides a validated modeling framework for predicting the damage evolution and structural failure of particle-reinforced composites under mechanical load. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS

Authors: Zawada-Tomkiewicz A.
Title: A unified micro–macro stochastic framework for tool wear evolution and lifetime prediction
Abstract: Tool wear results from the interaction of numerous micro-scale contact regions subjected to mechanical, thermal and tribological loading. This paper proposes a physics-informed micro–macro stochastic framework linking contact-scale degradation processes with engineering-scale prediction of wear evolution and tool life. At the micro-contact level, tool degradation is represented by a population of interacting contacts undergoing wear, load redistribution and local instability. Model reduction leads to a state-dependent stochastic differential equation whose drift and diffusion terms describe macroscopic flank-wear evolution, while a jump component represents intermittent degradation events. Abrasion/ploughing, adhesion/BUE, thermal–oxidative and diffusion–chemical wear are represented as dominant degradation mechanisms, whereas coating protection and edge instability are treated as latent degradation states. Tool life is formulated as a first-passage problem with respect to a prescribed wear limit. Model parameters are identified from experimentally reconstructed wear increments, with different tribological systems represented using the same stochastic formulation through coefficient calibration. Validation is performed at three complementary levels: predictive assessment of wear evolution, statistical evaluation of degradation dynamics and independent physical validation. The framework reproduces nonlinear wear evolution and increasing degradation variability, while the inferred mechanism hierarchy and latent degradation states are qualitatively supported by independent experimental evidence. The proposed methodology bridges tribological processes at the micro-contact scale and stochastic reliability assessment at the engineering scale, integrating wear evolution, mechanism interpretation and tool-life prediction within a unified physics-informed framework. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Lin H.; Wang B.; Lin W.; Cheng X.; Bai C.; Zhang X.; Liu Z.
Title: Experimental investigation of combustion and emission characteristics of a heavy-duty direct-injection hydrogen engine with active and passive jet ignition
Abstract: Compared to traditional spark ignition systems, jet ignition in hydrogen-fueled engines shows strong potential for improving efficiency and reducing emissions. However, research on jet-ignited hydrogen engines remains limited, particularly regarding combustion behavior, emissions, and control parameter effects. This study experimentally investigates a heavy-duty direct-injection hydrogen engine with a jet ignition system under active and passive modes. The effects of spark timing, excess air ratio (λ), and pre-chamber fuel energy ratio are evaluated. Results indicate that spark timing primarily controls combustion phasing with minimal impact on combustion duration. At a CA50 of approximately 7 °CA ATDC, the maximum ITE reached 43.0 % in passive mode and 42.0 % in active mode. Over λ = 1.6–2.6, the combustion duration was 5.0–9.3 °CA in passive mode and 4.3–8.5 °CA in active mode. Active operation produced more advanced combustion phasing and higher peak pressure because of its greater ignition energy. ITE increased with λ, reaching 42.2 % and 41.3 % at λ = 2.6 in passive and active modes, respectively, while nitrogen oxides approached zero at λ ≥ 2.4. Two pre-ignition events occurred at λ = 2.7 under active operation. ITE remained approximately 41–42 % as the pre-chamber fuel-energy ratio increased from 0.8 % to 0.9 %, but decreased to approximately 36.5 % at 2.7 %, accompanied by increased NOx emissions. Thus, pre-chamber fueling should be limited to the minimum required for reliable ignition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Blocking antibiotic pollution and bacteria contamination via efficient photocatalysis using N-carbon dots doped Ni@TiO2
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Wastewater contamination from pharmaceuticals and pathogens poses an urgent global challenge that conventional water treatment processes struggle to address effectively. This research reports the multifunctionality of Ni-doped titania (Ni@TiO2) decorated with green nitrogen-doped carbon quantum dots (NCD), as a visible-light photocatalyst for drug degradation and as an antibacterial agent. To overcome the limitations of titania-based catalysts, a dual-modification strategy is proposed. The dual presence of NCD and Ni introduces localized energy levels that successfully narrow the TiO2 bandgap, promoting charge carrier separation and photo-electron transfer and optimizing photocatalytic behavior. Besides, the NCDs act as electron sinks and photo-induced electron transfer mediators, promoting charge separation and transfer at the heterojunction interface and extending charge-carrier lifetime. The presence of NCD and the Ni addition into Ni@TiO₂/NCD (NCD = 4% wt) composite achieved high paracetamol degradation (≈99%, TOC removal of 98%), ceftriaxone (70%), and vancomycin (75%) after 180 min of irradiation. Antibacterial activity of Ni@TiO₂/NCD (NCD = 4% wt) was proved, reducing the viability of S. aureus by 96.71% and 68.37%, and E. coli by 95.41% and 68.23%, at 1000 and 500 μg/mL, respectively. Finally, MIC values and residual antibacterial activity of water containing photocatalytically treated antibiotics prove the great performance of the developed composite system in achieving multiple functions, emphasizing its potential in wastewater treatment and infection control. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Yoladi M.
Title: Measurement uncertainty aware assessment of reduced order models for PIV velocity profiles downstream of rod bundle spacer grids
Abstract: A reproducible verification, validation, and uncertainty quantification workflow is presented for judging how reliably reduced order models predict measured rod bundle velocity profiles, and it is demonstrated on an open VVER 1200 spacer grid benchmark. The benchmark provides axial velocity profiles measured by particle image velocimetry (PIV) along fixed monitor lines at five distances downstream of three spacer grid variants on three measurement planes, 45 profiles in total, together with their measurement uncertainty. Three model classes are assessed: a one dimensional reduced transport model verified with the method of manufactured solutions at second order accuracy, a data driven surrogate combining proper orthogonal decomposition with Gaussian process regression, and hybrid combinations of the two. The one dimensional model is designed solely to reconstruct measured profiles along monitor lines and is not a three dimensional simulation of the reactor core. Every prediction carries distribution free conformal prediction intervals, and the comparison error is judged against the reported experimental uncertainty. Two prediction tasks are kept separate. In interpolation, where one downstream station of an already measured configuration is withheld, the surrogate is accurate: R squared of 0.951, an error of 0.142 m/s or about 12 percent of the 1.204 m/s bulk velocity, and conformal coverage of 0.978 pointwise and 0.889 per profile against a 0.90 target. In configuration transfer, where an entire spacer variant and plane combination is withheld, prediction from configuration labels alone fails in four of the nine held out cases, whereas conditioning the prediction on the velocity profile measured just downstream of the spacer restores accuracy to a mean error of 0.201 m/s, about 17 percent of the bulk velocity, with a median R squared of 0.642 and two remaining difficult cases; the conditioned operator is more accurate than a persistence baseline in all nine cases, and an independent operator reproduces the result. A projection onto the measured flow region keeps the predicted velocity at zero where the rods block the flow. Transfer errors exceed the reported experimental uncertainty, so uncertainty statements must be calibrated separately for that task. The workflow provides a transferable template for the uncertainty aware assessment of reduced order models against PIV benchmark data. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Dual-functional chitosan composite films loaded with oregano essential oil and antioxidant carbon quantum dots: A sustainable strategy for golden pomfret fillet preservation
Abstract: Functional composite films capable of retarding food spoilage are effective tools for addressing food quality deterioration. In this study, liposomes encapsulating essential oils in their hydrophobic lipid bilayer/domain and loading antioxidant carbon quantum dots (CQDs) in their hydrophilic region were synthesized and incorporated into a chitosan matrix to fabricate composite films with enhanced preservation performance. The synthesized CQDs exhibited excellent antioxidant activity, achieving 100% ABTS radical scavenging at 80 μg/mL and 90% DPPH radical scavenging at 200 μg/mL, along with strong ferric reducing capacity at the same concentration. The liposomal co-encapsulation of CQDs and oregano essential oil significantly enhanced the antioxidant and antibacterial properties of the films. Among the formulations, CS/Lip6 films (60% liposomes) exhibited the strongest antibacterial activity, with inhibition rates of 98% against E. coli and 92% against S. aureus. However, excessive liposome incorporation disrupted the film structure, leading to compromised mechanical properties. In contrast, CS/Lip4 films (40% liposomes) achieved a better balance between mechanical strength and functional performance, with a tensile strength of 2.25 MPa and an elongation at break of 96%. In terms of preservation performance, CS/Lip4 films effectively delayed lipid oxidation (TBARS reduced from 3.2 to 1.4 mg MDA/kg) and protein degradation (TVB-N reduced from 40 to 17 mg/100 g) in golden pomfret fillets. These results indicate that CS/Lip4 films offer superior overall performance for food packaging applications, and further optimization of liposome content may further enhance their preservation efficacy and broader applicability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Zhang Z.; Yang Y.; Chen Y.; Jiang B.; Du L.; Zhou P.
Title: Stable multi-view representation learning for out-of-distribution classification
Abstract: Multi-view classification is an important task in information fusion and attracts increasing attention. Although conventional multi-view classification methods have achieved promising performance, they often have an independent and identically distributed assumption on the training and test set, and thus they can only work under the in-distribution condition. However, in real-world applications, especially handling the low-quality data, the in-distribution condition is often unsatisfied, leading to the out-of-distribution (OOD) problem. To tackle the OOD problem, we propose a novel stable multi-view representation learning framework in this paper. In more detail, in the multi-view representation learning, we carefully design an adaptive dual-weighting mechanism that dynamically learns the weights of samples and dimensions simultaneously. Due to this adaptive dual-weighting mechanism, we can eliminate spurious correlations in the representation and enforce the multi-view classifier to focus on the true correlations between causal features and labels rather than spurious correlations. Extensive experiments on benchmark OOD datasets by comparing with state-of-the-art multi-view classification methods and OOD classification methods demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of our proposed method. The source code is publicly available at: https://github.com/zz978233034/stable-multi-view-classification . © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Fu Y.; Wang S.; Zhang K.; Li Z.; Song Y.; Zhang L.; Li Y.; Wu P.; Ling Z.
Title: Recycled concrete-derived aerogels with outstanding CO2 capture and storage via enhanced gas hydrate formation
Abstract: Mitigating global warming requires sustainable CO2 capture technologies. CO2 hydrates offer a sustainable route but suffer from slow formation kinetics due to limited multiphase interfaces. Herein, we report a facile freeze-drying and sodium silicate-assisted binding synthesis of robust, superhydrophilic aerogels using recycled concrete powders (RCPs, billion-ton-scale solid waste), natural clay nanofibers and multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs), serving as an ideal scaffold to accelerate CO2 hydrate formation in both water and saline solutions. The CO2 hydrate formation kinetics in the as-made aerogels exhibit distinct composition dependence, with an exceptional CO2 storage capacity of 110.56 V/V, corresponding to 95.07 mmol CO2 /mol water in real seawater (under the conditions of 3.3 MPa and 0.5 °C), which is remarkably superior to most of the reported promoters. The superior performance is attributed to the superhydrophilic surface, robust porous architecture with abundant mass-transfer channels, and the pH-modulating effect of RCPs and MWCNTs, which facilitate CO2 dissolution and transfer and enhance hydrate nucleation. Raman spectroscopy reveals that RCP hydroxyl groups weaken the aerogel–water interfacial interaction, disrupting the tetrahedral hydrogen-bonded network analogous to that in CO2 hydrate and thus prolonging hydrate nucleation. Conversely, proper MWCNT loading (10 wt%) preserves the porous structure and induces ordered water arrangement that resembles CO2 hydrate cages, significantly accelerating hydrate nucleation. The aerogels also exhibit excellent cyclic stability and substantial potential for large-scale application in CO2 hydrate formation. This work not only provides a cost-effective, sustainable solution for large-scale CO2 capture and storage using saline solutions but also offers new insights into the surface composition-dependent performance mechanisms for enhancing hydrate-based CO2 capture and storage technologies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Multi-modal knowledge-level representation learning for structure-oriented patent citation prediction
Abstract: Patent citation prediction aims to identify prior patents that challenge the novelty of new patent applications. A citation is valid when the technical components in the new application are functionally and structurally similar to those disclosed in the prior patent. This component structure is conveyed through two modalities: the claim text and the patent figures. Existing methods predominantly rely on text and struggle to capture the graph-structured nature of patent components. We propose a Multi-Modal Knowledge-Level Patent Representation Framework. First, we construct a multi-modal component graph that links text-derived triples with figure-derived visual components via reference numerals. Second, we introduce a knowledge-level attention mechanism operating at the triple level, coupled with cross-modal attention that injects figure-grounded structure into token embeddings, jointly aligning the modalities and suppressing noise arising from legal characterizations in patent text. Finally, we introduce a re-ranking module that performs structure-oriented similarity reasoning over the fused representation. We introduce PatCite, the first citation dataset categorizing samples into “tree-structured” and “graph-structured” types. Under the dynamic full-corpus protocol, our method achieves macro Recall@1/Recall@10 of 14.4%/43.8% on PatCite, with a Recall@1 gain of 5.0 percentage points over the strongest fine-tuned baseline. © 2026

Title: The saturation number of Kts
Abstract: For a given graph F , a graph G is said to be F -saturated if G contains no copy of F but for any edge uv∉E(G), G+uv contains a copy of F . The saturation number sat(n,F) is defined as the minimum number of edges among all n -vertex F -saturated graphs. The virus graph Kts, where s≥0 and t≥max⁡{3,s}, is a graph of order s+t constructed by attaching s distinct leaves to s different vertices of a complete graph Kt. Hua and Peng (2026) [13] determined sat(n,K32) and characterized its corresponding extremal graphs. In this paper, we determine sat(n,K33) and sat(n,Kt2) for all integers t≥4, together with the structural descriptions of the related extremal saturated graphs, and put forward several problems for further research. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Solid-state stabilized sage essential oil liposomes in tamarind gum beads: dual encapsulation for modulating oxidative stress and energy homeostasis in postharvest Agaricus bisporus
Abstract: This study developed a tamarind gum-liposome (TG/Lps) gel system to stabilize liposomes against aqueous instability (e.g., hydrolysis, peroxidation, fusion). This system was further applied for the liposome-gel composite of sage essential oil (SEO) to explore its delivery and sustained release properties. Results showed that incorporation of SEO improved the formability and structural integrity of the TG/Lps composite system, resulting in gel beads with a dense and uniform morphology. The TG/Lps-SEO-1 exhibited superior comprehensive characteristics, including minimal dry-wet particle size variation, high sphericity, dense morphology, encapsulation efficiency (86%), bead yield (96%), and near-native antioxidant capacity (DPPH: 83.92%; ABTS: 79.96%). In postharvest Agaricus bisporus, TG/Lps-SEO-1 suppressed browning (reduced PPO activity and browning index), maintained firmness, and mitigated membrane damage (lower lipid peroxidation/electrolyte leakage/ROS). It synergistically enhanced antioxidant defense via glutathione cycle regulation and sustained energy homeostasis, delaying senescence process. This work provides an efficient, controllable essential oil delivery strategy for mushroom preservation. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A terthiophene-based “turn-on” fluorescent probe for hypochlorite: From water/soil analysis to on-site food safety screening and bioimaging
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Hypochlorite (ClO−) is widely used as a disinfectant and bleaching agent, but its overuse threatens environmental and food safety, necessitating rapid, sensitive, and field-deployable detection methods. Herein, we introduce a new terthiophene-based “turn-on” fluorescent probe 3 TB for selective ClO− detection. 3 TB exhibits a pronounced green fluorescence turn-on upon ClO− addition, featuring instantaneous response (<30 s), low detection limit (23.7 nM), good photostability (≥6 h), and broad pH tolerance (4–10). 3 TB enables sensitive and quantitative ClO− detection in water/soil/disinfectant/bleach matrices (recoveries: 97.8–102.8%), and permits on-site visual screening of fresh produce. 3 TB -impregnated test strips further permit rapid naked-eye detection in aqueous media, while smartphone-assisted RGB analysis provides instrument-free quantitative detection on food surfaces and test strips. Moreover, 3 TB exhibits favorable biocompatibility, enabling sensitive fluorescence imaging of ClO− in HeLa cells and onion tissues. Collectively, this work affords a versatile fluorescent platform for ClO− monitoring and bioimaging, which holds significant promise for applications in environmental pollution surveillance, biological system analysis, and food safety assurance. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Low temperature dry reforming of methane over Ni/USY catalysts
Abstract: Low temperature (500-600 °C) dry reforming of methane (DRM) was studied using 5 wt.%Ni supported on USY zeolites with two Si/Al ratios (3 and 40), with or without Cs (3 wt%) addition. By combining catalyst characterization with linear programming (LP), reaction-network analysis and operando-FTIR, this work elucidates why DRM is not the dominant reaction at 500 °C and identifies the catalyst properties suppressing reactions with tendency to carbon formation. Catalyst characterization revealed a significant support effect: USY(3) stabilizes smaller, more strongly interacting Ni species and exhibits higher CO2 affinity. In contrast, USY(40) produces larger, more heterogeneous Ni particles and lower CO2 affinity. Cs addition does not generate Cs-containing phases detectable by XRD and primarily improves Ni dispersion, particularly on USY(40). At 500 °C, 5 %Ni/USY(3) offers optimal activity and stability balance (XCH4 = 30 %, XCO2 = 50 %; Coke = 2.5 % wt.%), whereas 5 %Ni/USY(40) achieves higher CH4 conversion (40 %), but with methane cracking evidence (H2/CO = 1.6) and significant coking (28.7 wt%). Cs is more beneficial on USY(40), reducing coke to 8.6 wt% and shifting the H2/CO close to 1. LP analysis and operando-FTIR reveal that at 500 °C the system operates under a mixed reaction network dominated by CDM and RWGS rather than DRM, which becomes predominant only at 600 °C. Operando-FTIR experiments reveal that the formation of carbonate-type intermediates is more pronounced on USY(3), whereas CO/Ni-carbonyl species are predominant on USY(40). Overall, stabilizing small Ni particles and promoting CO2-derived intermediates upon USY(3)-based catalysts are key to suppress methane cracking and promote DRM as dominant pathway at 600 °C. Title: Physics-informed gradient-enhanced Kriging for efficient fatigue life prediction in ultra-high-speed fixed-angle rotors
Abstract: Ultra-high-speed fixed-angle rotors experience severe centrifugal loading and may develop fatigue cracks during long-term cyclic operation. Accurate prediction of their crack-growth life requires repeated three-dimensional finite element simulations, which limits rapid assessment over varying operating and material parameters. Although surrogate models have been applied to fatigue and crack-growth problems, their use for high-cycle fatigue crack-growth prediction in ultra-high-speed rotating machinery has not been systematically investigated. This study establishes a surrogate-based prediction framework for a TC18 titanium-alloy fixed-angle rotor and develops a physics-informed gradient-enhanced Kriging (PI-GEK) model for small-sample learning. Compact-tension tests are used to identify the Paris-law parameters, and the validated finite element procedure is transferred to the rotor. Rotational speed, stress ratio, and Paris parameters define the input space. Life gradients with respect to the transformed Paris parameters are derived from the governing life integral and obtained from existing simulation histories without additional finite element analyses. Compared with conventional Kriging, PI-GEK provides more accurate crack length-life curves, more physically consistent response trends, and more stable uncertainty estimates. This work advances surrogate modelling for fatigue crack-growth assessment of ultra-high-speed rotating machinery within the prescribed computational domain and provides an efficient approach for damage-tolerance evaluation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: AIE + ESIPT active Hydroxy Benzothiazole based fluorescent spray and powder for advanced fingerprint applications

Abstract: The p -tolyl substituted hydroxyphenyl benzothiazole ( HBT-MP ) which possess AIE + ESIPT, crystallinity, spherical morphology, high quantum yield, has been utilized for well-resolved high contrast imaging of normal, physically stressed and aged LFPs after blending with SiO2 on 14 substrates (aluminium, glass, iron, lock, leaf, plastic, wood, can, tile, CD, coin, cardboard, laptop and mobile phone) using powder dusting and solution/spray based methods. Title: Temperature-dependent wear mechanism transition of plasma-nitrided TC6 titanium alloy from synergistic plastic coordination to crack-induced brittle delamination
Abstract: Plasma nitriding was conducted on TC6 titanium alloy at 820 ℃ for 10 h, and its high-temperature reciprocating sliding wear behavior was investigated at 300 ℃ and 500 ℃. Microstructural analysis indicated that plasma nitriding produced an approximately 5 μm-thick gradient architecture, consisting of an outer hard TiN/Ti2N compound layer and a nitrogen-stabilized diffusion zone. Wear tests revealed that the nitrided layer reduced the wear volume by 1–2 orders of magnitude compared to the untreated substrate, with the minimum wear occurring at 300 ℃. This superior performance is attributed to a synergistic physical-chemical mechanism: gradient plastic deformation and friction-induced amorphization accommodate the strain, while thermally driven outward migration of Al forms an in-situ Al-containing lubricious oxide film (TiO2/Al2O3). Conversely, at 500 ℃, thermal softening and stiffness mismatch generate deep vertical brittle microcracks. These cracks act as rapid diffusion channels for oxygen, inducing deep internal oxidation and catastrophic brittle spallation of the compound layer, exposing the soft Al-rich matrix to severe three-body abrasive wear. This work elucidates the temperature-driven transition from synergistic plastic coordination and chemical protection at 300 ℃ to crack-induced catastrophic failure at 500 ℃. The findings provide theoretical guidance for the surface design and safe operating temperature selection of titanium alloy components in high-temperature aerospace environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Synergistic enhancement of photocatalytic CO2 reduction to CH4 via Bi2O2S/TiO2-N heterojunction and photothermal effect under full-spectrum irradiation
Abstract: Solar-driven photocatalytic CO2-to-fuel conversion requires photocatalysts that combine broad-spectrum light harvesting with efficient charge separation. In this study, a novel Bi2O2S/TiO2-N heterojunction featuring intimate contact between TiO2-N nanocrystallites and Bi2O2S nanosheets was constructed using an ultrasound-assisted suspension method and evaluated for gas–solid CO2 reduction with water vapor, without sacrificial agents or metal cocatalysts. Photoelectrochemical measurements and DFT calculations revealed that the band positions of these semiconductors and the formation of a built-in electric field facilitated interfacial charge transfer according to a type-II heterojunction thus suppressing charge recombination and enhancing their target utilization in CO2 reduction. Semiconductor coupling also made CO2 adsorption more favorable, with a calculated adsorption energy of −1.71 eV, thereby promoting CO2 adsorption and activation on the composite. In parallel, broadband absorption by Bi2O2S extended light utilization into the near-IR region and promoted photocatalyst’s surface heating to 156 °C. Wavelength- and temperature-dependent experiments confirmed that this photothermal contribution acts synergistically with photocatalytic charge transfer during CH4 formation. Authors: Yang X.; Yang D.; Sun W.; Song Y.; Yang B.; Huang P.; Liu J.; Gao X.
Title: Decoding bacterial identity and resistance through D-amino acid metabolic fingerprinting with a cascade colorimetric sensor array
Abstract: The rapid rise of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) constitutes a global health crisis, demanding diagnostic tools capable of simultaneous bacterial identification and rapid antibiotic susceptibility testing (AST) in a single workflow. Herein, a colorimetric sensor array was developed to address this need by profiling bacterial metabolic fingerprints via a streamlined single-substrate, multi-wavelength strategy. The strategy is built upon the inherent bacteria-specific metabolism of D-amino acids (D-AAs), coupled with the enzymatic selectivity of D-amino acid oxidase (DAAO), which catalyzes the oxidation of D-AAs to generate H2O2. Differential bacterial consumption of D-Ala directly modulates the substrate available for the subsequent DAAO-coupled cascade reaction, producing varying amounts of H2O2. Consequently, H2O2 triggers the peroxidase (POD)-like activity of Prussian blue-coated gold nanoparticle (Au@PB NP) nanozyme to produce distinct multi-wavelength optical patterns from TMB oxidation. When coupled with linear discriminant analysis (LDA), this sensing platform enables clear discrimination of bacterial species based on their metabolic fingerprints. Moreover, by assessing the antibiotic-induced inhibition of this metabolic activity, the platform accurately determines bacterial susceptibility profiles, achieving 100% concordance with the standard disk diffusion method for both reference and clinical isolates, and successfully determining minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values for reference strains in full agreement with Clinical Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) breakpoint interpretation. This work establishes an integrated, rapid, and robust metabolic sensing platform for bacterial phenotyping and AST, offering a promising tool to combat AMR. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zhao W.; Zhang Y.; Wang D.; Li W.; Li X.; Niu J.; Chen X.; Wang Z.; Liu X.
Title: Molecularly imprinted dual-mode sensing of emerging contaminants in complex water matrices: A review
Abstract: Emerging and priority organic contaminants, including per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), pharmaceuticals and personal care products, endocrine-disrupting compounds, pesticides, and phenolic pollutants, are often present in natural and engineered water systems at trace or ultratrace levels. Their detection is affected by matrix components, including natural organic matter, inorganic ions, suspended particles, structurally related compounds, and background optical or electrochemical signals. These interferences hinder conventional single-mode sensors from providing stable and reliable responses in real water samples. Molecularly imprinted polymers (MIPs), with tailor-made recognition sites, chemical robustness, and compatibility with enrichment and sensing interfaces, provide a platform for improving selectivity in complex matrices. When integrated with dual-mode readout, MIP-based sensors can improve analytical reliability through signal cross-validation, internal correction, or coupled amplification. This review summarizes recent advances in molecularly imprinted dual-mode sensors for water pollutant detection, emphasizing their adaptation to complex water matrices. After outlining research trends through bibliometric analysis, we discuss MIP-based pretreatment and recognition interfaces, recognition-induced signal transduction, and the synergistic logic of representative dual-mode systems. The applications of these systems to PFAS, phenolic and halogenated phenolic compounds, pesticides and herbicides, and antibiotics are compared in terms of analytical demands, real-sample validation, signal division, and application boundaries. Authors: Hu R.; Yang B.; Gan J.; Li L.; Ye F.; Guo J.; Liu T.
Title: Dual-view contrastive learning for heterogeneous graph representation
Abstract: Representation learning on heterogeneous graphs relies on exploiting both diverse semantics and intricate structural relations. However, the common approaches struggle to simultaneously account for distant semantic interactions and fine-grained structural patterns. Therefore, we introduce a novel Heterogeneous Graph Representation Learning method via a dual-view contrastive structure (HGRL). Specifically, the Schema-aware Graph Abstraction Module (SGAM) captures relational dependencies using a type-aware graph neural network augmented with adaptive residual pathways to learn structural representations. Moreover, the Mamba-based Semantic Reasoner (MSR) utilizes a globally-enhanced Mamba backbone with multi-scale fusion and directional positional encodings to model high-order semantic dependencies. Furthermore, we design a dynamic bidirectional contrastive learning framework that aligns the semantic and structural views, where each view serves as a form of learnable augmentation and mutual supervision for the other, thereby fostering robust and mutually-enriched representations. Authors: Sun J.; Chen H.; Nie J.; Yang P.; Dong Y.; Li H.
Title: Highly efficient photothermal methanol decomposition for hydrogen production with Rh/SrTiO3 catalyst
Abstract: Methanol is an attractive liquid hydrogen carrier owing to its high hydrogen content and ease of production, while its liquid-phase handling can reduce the risks and costs associated with hydrogen storage and transportation. Herein, we report a highly dispersed Rh/SrTiO3 (Rh/STO) catalyst with mixed Rh0/Rh3+ sites and abundant oxygen vacancies for solar-driven hydrogen production via methanol decomposition. Under full-spectrum illumination at 2.0 W cm−2, the optimized Rh2%/STO catalyst produced H2 at 2.4 mol g−1h−1 and with an apparent activation barrier of 30.7 kJ mol−1. In situ characterizations and mechanistic studies reveal directional electron transfer from STO to Rh sites and hole accumulation at oxygen vacancies; which, together with photothermal heating, promote sequential methanol dehydrogenation for hydrogen production. These findings identify directional electron transfer as a key factor in photothermal MD and offer a basis for designing effective catalysts for methanol decomposition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A thermo-mechanical-material sensing framework using an external-observation-informed inverse HROM
Abstract: Real-time monitoring and reliability assessment are critical for industrial components operating under high temperature and pressure. In such environments, online state evaluation is often ill-posed because the available information is limited to extremely sparse external observations, while material properties may deviate from their nominal values because of long-term aging. Such difficulties commonly arise in industrial systems such as high-temperature rotors, where direct sensor deployment on rotating components is often impractical. To address this problem, we propose a real-time thermo-mechanical-material sensing framework (TMM-SF). At its core is an external-observation-informed inverse HROM (EOI-HROM), which combines sparse local boundary constraints inferred from external observations with physics constraints enforced on sparse internal nodes, thereby enabling direct reduced inverse inference without outer-loop inverse iteration. Built on EOI-HROM, TMM-SF further incorporates a calibrated a posteriori error-estimation model based on physics residuals for online reliability assessment and a material-property inversion model for online material-property updating. The proposed framework is demonstrated on a high-temperature turbine rotor using snapshots from only one start-up condition for offline feature extraction and a single external sensor for online input. Under multiple out-of-training testing conditions, including start-up, abnormal, and shutdown-related conditions, TMM-SF accurately infers temperature, displacement, and stress fields while simultaneously providing online error estimation and material-property inversion. The relative L2-norm errors remain below 2.1 % for temperature and 4.0 % for displacement, while the online computation is accelerated by 4.5 × 103 times relative to the full-order model. Title: FedHGA: Federated segmentation framework for heterogeneous granularity annotations
Abstract: Federated learning enables collaborative model training while preserving data privacy. Our research addresses a practical but underexplored scenario of Heterogeneous Granularity Annotations, where participants with varied resources and budgets contribute annotations of differing quality. Our empirical study demonstrates that conventional federated methods that treat all annotations uniformly fail to leverage such heterogeneous data effectively. We attribute this limitation to two issues: local model drift from sparse supervision in coarse annotations, and global model drift from the combined effect of annotation granularity differences and data distribution shifts. Therefore, we propose the federated segmentation framework for Heterogeneous Granularity Annotations (FedHGA), a novel framework incorporating two core mechanisms: a foreground semantic-guided label enhancement module that generates pseudo-labels using a pre-trained mask generator combined with a noise-tolerant loss, and an entropy-aware federated aggregation strategy that assigns client-specific aggregation weights based on Rényi entropy, which serves as a proxy for client annotation informativeness. This work provides a practical solution for collaborative utilization of heterogeneous annotation resources in privacy-sensitive scenarios, with a full framework and benchmark dataset open-sourced to facilitate further research. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Liu J.; Lu G.; Wang Y.; Wei L.; Chen D.
Title: Dynamic scene self-supervised monocular depth estimation based on multi-branch collaborative optimization
Abstract: To address the challenge of self-supervised monocular depth estimation experiencing severe performance degradation in real-world dynamic scenes due to violating the “static world assumption”, this paper proposes a unified lightweight single-frame and multi-frame fusion architecture (MDL-Depth). To effectively mitigate interference from moving objects, the method is designed at both the data and loss levels. First, we incorporate an optical flow network to precisely capture pixel-level motion. Through explicit feature warping operations, reference frame features containing dynamic objects are aligned to the target frame's viewpoint, effectively compensating for the independent motion of objects prior to feature fusion. Second, we develop an adaptive loss masking strategy tailored for dynamic foregrounds. By analyzing reprojection errors between consecutive frames, we generate dynamic masks that actively identify and filter out erroneous gradient signals caused by motion mismatches. Experiments on challenging Cityscapes and KITTI datasets demonstrate that our method achieves high accuracy (e.g., AbsRel 0.091 on KITTI) and consistent improvements in both dynamic and static regions. While ensuring high performance, the framework also prioritizes lightweight design. Title: Experimental investigation of different CO2 injection schemes to enhance oil recovery in sandstone reservoir

Title: Controlled synthesis of highly microporous O/N/P co-doped carbon for High-Performance Supercapacitors: Pore formation induced by a Phosphorus-Templated Multi-Functional flame retardant and In-Situ Heteratom doping

Title: Assessment of natural radioactivity, radon distribution, and radiological hazards in soil and groundwater of Al-Ahsa region, eastern Saudi Arabia

Title: Structure-transport-reactivity relationships for advanced SOFC cathodes
Abstract: Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) offer highly efficient electrochemical energy conversion technology. However, reducing the operating temperatures to the intermediate range of 500–700 ° C substantially increases cathodic polarization resistance because sluggish oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) kinetics reduce power output and overall cell performance. This analysis additionally explores perovskite-derived, Ruddlesden-Popper, and nanostructured SOFC cathodes, incorporating novel design methodologies and advanced fabrication techniques. Title: Revealing the thermal runaway characteristics of confined HMX-based aluminized explosives in aqueous environments of varying pH
Abstract: Thermal safety is a fundamental requirement for the application of HMX-based aluminized explosives (HAE) in complex manufacturing and storage scenarios. Furthermore, accelerating rate calorimetry (ARC) tests confirm that neutral H2O advances the trigger temperature in TR of HAE from 230.2 °C to 205.8 °C. The kinetic compensation effect (KCE) supported by the linear lnA– E a or enthalpy (Δ H‡ )-entropy (Δ S‡ ) correlations across all four environments, is first extended to the TR regime of HAE. In addition, classical MD shows that mobility of fluorine binder and H2O molecules is enhanced in neutral H2O environments, while reactive MD demonstrates the accelerated Al-F/Al-C bonds formation and Al particle fragmentation, consistent with the increased F/C contents of condensed combustion products (CCPs). Title: Assessment of CT radiation dose and optimization strategies using water-equivalent diameter: A cross-sectional study of brain, chest, and abdomen examinations
Abstract: Computed tomography (CT) is the cornerstone of modern diagnostic imaging, and protocol optimization requires institutional diagnostic reference levels (DRLs) and patient-size assessment. Title: MSA-Flow: Multi-scale adaptive normalizing flow for unsupervised anomaly detection of complex surface defects
Abstract: Unsupervised anomaly detection identifies abnormal data by learning the feature distribution of normal samples. However, when addressing complex surface defects, existing flow-based models often overlook multi-scale responses and suffer from uneven feature distribution, making them susceptible to interference from redundant background information. To address these challenges, a multi-scale adaptive fusion normalizing flow (MSA-Flow) framework is proposed. The framework achieves accurate detection of defects through cross-scale feature enhancement and interaction, adaptive feature selection and fusion, and dynamic anomaly scoring. Specifically, a cross-scale difference-aware method is introduced to capture inconsistent anomaly responses by generating attention maps from distribution shifts, enabling precise localization. In addition, an adaptive fusion flow with feature selection is developed to reduce the influence of background redundancy. By evaluating the importance of feature probability distributions, the model dynamically preserves key information for fusion while directing low-information background features to the latent space output. During anomaly scoring, a dynamic weighting strategy that combines peak saliency and spatial entropy is employed. This strategy is integrated with a Top-K aggregation mechanism to suppress false positives and improve image-level detection performance. Title: Carbon sphere-based multiscale composite lubricants: Interfacial behavior and tribological mechanisms

Title: Thermal plasma pyro-gasification of bio-oil for H2/CO-Rich syngas production
Abstract: This study investigates thermal plasma-assisted pyro-gasification as an intensified allothermal route for converting biomass-derived bio-oil and representative oxygenated compounds into H2- and CO-rich syngas. Title: Effect of the dynamic pore structure parameter changes on coal particle gas desorption during pulverization: Implications for estimation of underground gas loss
Abstract: The borehole drill cuttings sampling method is the predominant sampling method for Coalbed methane (CBM) content measurement in China owing to its operational simplicity and high efficiency. In the context of underground CBM content measurement, this high release rate implies that by the time the coal sample is collected and the on-site test begins, most of the gas has already been released. This makes it challenging to collect reliable desorption data in underground coal mines, which in turn affects the accuracy of lost gas volume calculation. Low‑pressure N2/CO2 adsorption quantitatively characterized coal’s multi‑scale pore structure. Based on this, the dual-pore series diffusion model (DPSDM) calculated dual‑pore parameters for different‑sized coal samples, revealing their rapid gas release mechanism during pulverization. Finally, we used the lost gas model to calculate lost gas for different‑sized coal samples, aiming to assess how sampling particle size affects lost gas estimation. Title: Study on the effects of ethanol and methanol blending on the explosion characteristics and flame propagation behavior of gasoline vapor
Abstract: With the widespread application of alcohol additives as clean alternative fuels in gasoline, their potential combustion and explosion safety issues have attracted increasing attention. Title: Thermodynamic and kinetic origins of micro-explosions in Al-Mg alloy nanoparticles via machine learning molecular dynamics
Abstract: Aluminum-magnesium (Al-Mg) alloy nanoparticles are promising high-energy fuels for advanced flight vehicles. While alloying enhances combustion performance, the atomistic mechanisms driving accelerated ignition and micro-explosions remain poorly understood. Authors: Lu M.; Wang R.; Miao X.; Tang T.; Li Z.; Xu D.
Title: FeCoNiZnPt high-entropy hierarchical nanosheet-assembled nanozyme with enhanced peroxidase-like activity for colorimetric glucose detection
Abstract: The poor stability of natural enzymes and the limited catalytic activity of conventional nanozymes remain major challenges in the field of colorimetric glucose sensing. In this work, a high-entropy hierarchical nanosheet-assembled nanozyme (FeCoNiZnPt-HEHN) composed of Fe, Co, Ni, Zn, and Pt was successfully constructed through a solvothermal strategy. The as-prepared nanozyme exhibits a three-dimensional hierarchical microrod architecture assembled from ultrathin nanosheets, with multiple metal elements uniformly distributed throughout the structure. The synergistic catalytic centers involving Fe2+/Fe3+ mixed-valence species and low-valence Pt0 species were established within the high-entropy framework. Steady-state kinetic analysis demonstrated that FeCoNiZnPt-HEHN possesses excellent affinity toward both hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) and 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB), exhibiting superior peroxidase-like catalytic activity compared with many previously reported nanozyme systems. These results demonstrate that the proposed cascade system (GOx + high-entropy nanozyme) holds great potential for rapid glucose detection in bioanalytical applications. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zhang L.; Quan L.; Wang M.; Zhu M.; Zhao H.
Title: Fretting tribocorrosion behavior and damage evolution of Inconel 690 after salt-fog pre-corrosion
Abstract: Pre-corroded surface evolution strongly influences the subsequent corrosion–fretting degradation of metallic components exposed to aggressive environments. In this study, the sequential degradation behavior of Inconel 690 alloy tubes after salt-fog pre-corrosion was investigated through environmental fretting tests, post-fretting electrochemical characterization, and multi-scale surface analysis. A multi-objective evaluation framework integrating response surface methodology (RSM) and the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) was developed to correlate pre-corrosion history and fretting duration with tribological and electrochemical responses. The results demonstrate that moderate pre-corrosion can temporarily modify interfacial contact behavior, whereas prolonged fretting promotes cracking, delamination, and third-body-assisted degradation of corrosion-related surface layers. Meanwhile, the corrosion activity increased by more than three orders of magnitude during sequential degradation, despite the enhanced apparent impedance response caused by surface deposits. The optimal compromise condition identified within the investigated parameter domain was 24 h pre-corrosion followed by 30 min fretting, with predicted COF, wear volume, and charge transfer resistance of 0.190, 1.425 × 10⁴ μm³ , and 3.22 × 10⁴ Ω·cm², respectively. Authors: Tu J.; Huang X.; Fan Y.; Xie P.
Title: Flash-boiling spray morphology and flow characteristics of superheated RP-3 kerosene from micro-orifice nozzles
Abstract: Improving thermal protection performance of fuel-cooled flameholders in high-performance aero-engine afterburners requires a clear understanding of flash-boiling atomization and fuel-delivery behavior under high-temperature fuel-injection conditions. Flash boiling of high-temperature, high-pressure RP-3 aviation kerosene injected through micro-orifice nozzles in a fuel-cooled flameholder was investigated experimentally using high-speed backlit imaging and flow-rate measurements. Spray morphology, cone angle, grayscale-based evaporation-region penetration length, and flow-rate characteristics were measured for straight-orifice and stepped-expansion nozzles over fuel-supply pressures of 2–5 MPa and superheat ratios of R = 1–28. Four morphology-based substages were observed: jet-like morphology at R = 1, expanding-cone morphology at R = 4–12, structured-core morphology at R = 16–20, and contracted-core morphology at R = 24–28. These substages describe distinct external features within broader literature flash-boiling regimes and are not universal thermodynamic boundaries. The cone angle increased over R = 4–20 but decreased over R = 24–28, while the grayscale-based evaporation-region penetration length continued to increase. Higher supply pressure increased axial spray momentum and extended the evaporation region. The orifice length-to-diameter ratio and stepped diameter ratio significantly altered spray expansion and the flow-rate response. Under identical operating conditions, the straight-orifice nozzle generally produced a larger cone angle and flow rate than the stepped-expansion nozzle. These results establish morphological evolution and fuel-delivery behavior of real aviation kerosene during micro-orifice flash boiling and provide experimental guidance for fuel-outlet design. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Tang J.; Wang Y.; Wang Q.; Zheng R.; Liu T.; Tao Z.
Title: Microwave assisted Bi doping engineering of PBCF cathodes for high performance solid oxide fuel cells
Abstract: Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) are considered highly efficient and environmentally friendly energy conversion devices. However, their practical application still requires highly active and durable cathodes to promote oxygen reduction reactions. A microwave-assisted Bi-doping strategy using Bi2O3 as the Bi source was developed to enhance the cathodic performance of Pr0.5Ba0.5Co0.7Fe0.3O3-δ (PBCF), with the Pr0.5Ba0.5(Co0.7Fe0.3)0.9Bi0.1O3-δ (PBCFB10), composition exhibiting the optimal electrochemical performance among the investigated samples. At 700 °C, the single cell with the PBCFB10 cathode achieves a peak power density of 1723 mW cm−2 and a low polarization resistance of 0.033 Ω cm2. Structural and surface analyses reveal that microwave assisted Bi incorporation modulates the PBCF lattice and regulates the Co/Fe valence states, thereby increasing the concentration of oxygen vacancies and accelerating surface oxygen exchange kinetics. These effects promote oxygen adsorption, oxygen-ion transport, and oxygen reduction kinetics, thereby markedly enhancing cathode activity and demonstrating microwave-assisted Bi doping as an effective strategy for developing high-performance perovskite cathodes for SOFCs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wang L.; Wu X.; Sun Z.; Dou Y.
Title: Physics-constrained spatiotemporal modeling for temporal localization in structured multichannel acoustic signals
Abstract: Temporal localization in structured multichannel acoustic signals, such as first-arrival picking in geophysical logging, is a fundamental yet challenging task. Traditional signal processing methods rely heavily on manual heuristics, while existing data-driven deep learning approaches often overlook the inherent physical priors of multichannel arrays, resulting in a trade-off among accuracy, stability, and real-time performance in field applications. To address these challenges, we propose FA-Picker, a physics-constrained spatiotemporal modeling framework for first-arrival picking. This model explicitly incorporates the depth dimension to construct a three-dimensional input data volume, enabling the capture of joint spatiotemporal features across multiple receivers and consecutive measurements. Moreover, an end-to-end multi-task architecture is designed, where coarse first-arrival segmentation guides continuous arrival-time regression. A dual-constraint mechanism is introduced, combining soft loss-based guidance with hard physical constraints, ensuring that the localized temporal points strictly comply with the underlying wave propagation laws. Furthermore, to alleviate the scarcity of high-quality labeled data, we exploit the highly structured characteristics of multichannel acoustic arrays to develop a comprehensive synthetic data generation workflow that simulates diverse formation variations and acquisition environments. Experimental results on field datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed modeling and data augmentation strategies, showing the superior performance of FA-Picker in practical first-arrival picking tasks. Authors: Liang M.; Zhang Y.; Peng Q.; Yang Y.; Dong Y.; Wang Y.; Chen D.; Liu H.; Su T.
Title: Mn-regulated Fe-N-C air cathodes for efficient oxygen reduction and stable fuel-cell operation
Abstract: Pt-free air cathodes are essential for cost-effective direct formate fuel cells, yet translating the promising oxygen reduction reaction activity of Fe-N-C catalysts into practical porous cathodes remains challenging due to performance degradation under operating conditions. Here, we develop Fe@Mn-ZIF-950, a Mn-modified ZIF-derived Fe-N-C catalyst designed for high-performance DFFC air cathodes. Aberration-corrected electron microscopy, Fe K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy and surface analyses confirm Fe-N x sites anchored in a micro/mesoporous conductive carbon framework. In alkaline ORR, Fe@Mn-ZIF-950 delivers a 0.92 V vs. RHE half-wave potential and 53.7 mV dec−1 Tafel slope, with only 24 mV decay after 1000 accelerated cycles. As cathode, it achieves 38.2 mW cm−2 peak power density, 75.2% higher than Pt/C under identical conditions, and retains 81.9% initial current after 100 h at 0.6 V. Density Functional Theory calculations reveal that Mn incorporation shifts Fe 3d states toward the Fermi level and reduces the *OOH formation energy barrier. Mn modification thus provides a viable strategy to translate Fe-N-C ORR activity into high-performance Pt-free formate fuel cell cathodes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A Hamiltonian ANCF-based method for analyzing buoyancy module arrangement to suppress tension in deep-sea towing cable systems
Abstract: The deep-sea towing cable system is critical for marine exploration, but environmental loads often cause excessive tension, compromising operational safety and efficiency. Installing buoyancy modules is an effective tension suppression strategy, and their arrangement critically influences suppression performance. This paper proposes a Hamiltonian absolute nodal coordinate formulation (ANCF)-based method to analyze buoyancy module arrangement for tension suppression. The Hamiltonian governing equations incorporate interactions among the cable, modules, and ocean currents, while a symplectic integration is derived to ensure numerical stability and energy conservation over long simulations. The proposed method is validated through numerical simulations and experiments, demonstrating its stability, accuracy, and efficiency. Compared with other layout regions, distributing modules along the upper half of the cable most effectively reduces the tension. Parametric studies examine the effects of buoyancy, drag, and inertia on tension response. Non-uniform arrangements are further investigated, and an optimized clustering scheme is identified that maintains the top tension below the safe working load while avoiding additional high-tension zones. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Authors: Su Z.; Ying Y.; Ren H.; Yu R.; Yang K.; Chen M.; Zhang G.; Liu D.
Title: Direct acoustic effects on impinging flame dynamics, soot formation and characteristics via a novel probe
Abstract: This study innovatively designed an acoustic probe, achieving for the first time the direct interaction between longitudinal acoustic wave and impinging flames. Through systematic experiments, the flame temperature fields, soot concentration fields, and surrounding flow fields were analytically compared under varying wall heights above the burner (HAB). Subsequently, the nanostructure and properties of soot deposited on the wall surface were characterized. The results indicated that acoustic wave with plane wave characteristics exerted a longitudinal force on the flame, accelerating the flow of gaseous species downstream during combustion and leading to flame necking. Simultaneously, the acoustic wave might enhance entrainment and promote the mixing of fuel and oxidizer. These consequently led to a reduction in flame temperature and soot concentration. Furthermore, the analysis of soot characteristics revealed that in the acoustically-excited flame, the total deposited soot mass was reduced, with shorter fringe length, higher fringe tortuosity, lower degree of graphitization, and enhanced oxidative reactivity. These findings collectively demonstrated that acoustic wave suppressed soot formation and growth, which was primarily attributed to three factors: (1) enhanced mixing of fuel and oxidizer, thereby suppressing soot formation; (2) acoustic acceleration of soot transport to downstream regions, resulting in reduced residence time; (3) a lower flame temperature, which adversely affected soot nucleation and surface growth. Notably, this suppressive effect became more pronounced at higher HABs, as the acoustic energy could function more effectively. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Shao P.; Xiao G.; Sun Z.; Mi H.; Wang S.; Li F.
Title: Effect of obstacle configuration on deflagration characteristics of hydrogen/methane in semi-confined channels: Implications for hydrogen infrastructure safety
Abstract: This study experimentally investigates the deflagration characteristics of hydrogen-blended natural gas (HBNG) in semi-confined domains. The study focuses on the interaction between propagating flames and downstream obstacles. Using a semi-confined duct configuration, the effects of obstacle angle ranging from 45° to 135° and arrangement including single-sided and symmetric on explosion severity were systematically analyzed. Results indicate that obstacle arrangement dominates explosion intensity. Symmetric arrangement increases peak overpressure by an average of 74.53 %, reaching a maximum of 95.48 kPa at 90°. Notably, the peak conditions for peak overpressure and total impulse do not coincide. The 90° configuration yields the highest overpressure, while the 112.5° configuration produces the maximum total impulse of 817.40 kPa·ms. Furthermore, secondary impulse induced by air backflow accounts for approximately 83 % of total impulse, highlighting the positive–negative-positive alternating pressure loading pattern that is often overlooked in current safety designs. A physically motivated regression model was developed, quantifying the contribution of arrangement effects to explosion severity at 75–82 %. These findings provide quantitative guidance for the safety assessment and structural design of HBNG infrastructure, and suggest that both impulse and peak overpressure should be considered simultaneously in the safety evaluation of semi-confined systems.
