Authors: Qin C.; Lin M.; Yu Y.; Wang K.; Zhou H.; Liu H.
Title: Scour-induced weakening effect on the lateral response for three pile types-supported offshore wind turbines in clay: A unified analytical framework
Abstract: Monopiles supported offshore wind turbines are susceptible to significant scour, which alters the surrounding soil geometry and strength, thereby affecting their lateral response. Existing p-y curve methods often fail to accurately capture the complex soil-structure interaction for large-diameter monopiles, particularly under scour condition, and a unified framework applicable to rigid, semi-rigid, and flexible piles is also lacking. This study proposes a unified analytical framework incorporating three nonlinear springs - lateral resistance, integrated moment at the rotational center, and distributed moment from shaft friction, to model the lateral behavior of three pile types under scour. The framework accounts for scour-induced weakening of clay strength through stress history effect and incorporates distinct soil failure mechanisms. Individual spring components (i.e., lateral resistance spring p-y, integrated moment spring MR-θR and distributed moment spring Mp-θp) are derived theoretically and validated against finite element results and existing solutions. The overall response is rigorously verified by centrifuge tests, field data, and 3D finite element simulations under scour and non-scour conditions. Results indicate that the proposed framework reliably predicts the lateral load-displacement response across different pile types and scour scenarios, offering a practical tool for the design and analysis of monopile foundations in scour-prone environments. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Authors: Kang X.; Wang H.; Cai G.; Ma S.; Li H.; Zhang A.; Wang X.; Liu W.
Title: A stiffness-adjustable low-frequency electromagnetic vibration energy harvesting system with inertial amplifier
Abstract: Traditional energy harvesting devices generally suffer from poor adaptability to low-frequency environments, making it difficult for them to cope with diverse conditions. This paper proposes a stiffness-adjustable electromagnetic induction energy harvesting device comprising four sets of inclined springs connected to adjustable gears, a central vertical spring, and an inertial amplifier mechanism. By altering the rotational angle of the gears, the geometric configuration and parameters of the springs are modified, thereby regulating the system's dynamic stiffness, natural frequency, and potential energy characteristics and enabling stiffness adjustment for different environmental vibration conditions. The electromechanically coupled dynamical equations are established, and the nonlinear restoring force is approximated using a ninth-order odd-polynomial fitting method. The harmonic balance method is employed to obtain amplitude-frequency response curves. Slowly varying harmonic coefficients are introduced to analyse the stability of periodic solutions. The fourth-order Runge-Kutta method is used to generate maps of RMS load voltage and average output power. Numerical results indicate that the proposed configuration can produce large-amplitude cross-well vibrations over low-frequency and broadband ranges. Coexisting responses and two-dimensional basin sections are computed for bistable, tristable, and quasi-zero-stiffness configurations to examine the dependence of steady-state responses on initial conditions. Finite-duration pulse excitation is used to investigate transitions among coexisting responses. Title: Study on early temperature inversion identification of coal spontaneous combustion based on acoustic signals
Abstract: The spontaneous combustion of coal stockpiles leads to resource depletion, safety hazards, and atmospheric pollution. Hence, reliable identification of ignition sources within loose coal beds is critical for prevention. In this study, sound waves were selected for fire-source detection. Using four coal ranks long-flame, non-caking, coking, and lean coals as experimental materials. Based on acoustic theory and wave propagation in porous media, a temperature measurement model for loose coal is established by introducing the tortuosity parameter and the conversion factor. An acoustic testing system was established to collect and analyze signals from the four coal samples during oxidative heating. The relative humidity surrounding all coal samples increased during heating, ranging from 54.84% to 92.78%. Humidity had a greater influence on sound-velocity measurement than atmospheric pressure. At ambient temperatures above 30 °C, humidity-induced temperature errors reached 8 °C, whereas errors caused by atmospheric pressure remained below 1 °C. Using the proposed model, acoustic temperatures of the four coal samples were calculated. The acoustic temperatures deviated from the measured values by at most 1.78, 1.73, −2.36, and −2.78 °C for the four coals, corresponding to maximum relative errors of −6.62%, −5.19%, −7.32%, and 8.85%, respectively. These errors mainly resulted from deviations of gas composition from the air assumption in the semi-enclosed environment, sound propagation-time measurement errors, and residuals in conversion-factor fitting. Authors: Zhang J.; Cao R.; Han A.; Han K.
Title: Multi-element XPS insights into the structural evolution of coal–spent cathode carbon co-combustion ash: From chemical speciation to critical transition
Abstract: The co-combustion of spent cathode carbon (SCC) with coal presents a promising strategy for the harmless disposal and energy recovery of this hazardous solid waste. However, SCC-derived Na, F, and Ca alter ash chemistry, affecting ash fusion and slagging behavior. While a 5 % SCC ratio improves combustion performance, the underlying microstructural evolution of ash remains unclear. This study employed XPS and XRD to investigate the chemical states of Al, Si, Ca, Fe, Ti, O, and C in ash from coal–SCC co-combustion at 1100–1400 °C, with the effect of CaO addition also examined. The results reveal a critical melt network transition at 1250 °C, evidenced by a synergistic extreme in multi-element XPS signals, which correlates well with XRD-detected bulk phase changes. CaO addition selectively modulates Fe/Ti valences and promotes carbon graphitization, as reflected in C 1 s evolution. The strong causal linkage between surface chemical states and bulk transformations provides a coupled analytical framework for interpreting ash melting behavior. These findings offer direct surface chemical evidence for ash fusion mechanisms and a theoretical basis for microstructure-oriented ash property control, with practical implications for optimizing co-combustion processes and ensuring safe boiler operation. Title: Decouple-then-align: Structural consensus for unsupervised feature selection
Abstract: Unsupervised feature selection aims to extract discriminative feature subsets from high-dimensional data, which typically exhibit intricate, multifaceted structures encompassing both local geometry and global semantics. Existing spectral-embedded methods often leverage multiple objectives to capture these distinct perspectives. However, using a single representation for manifold preservation and linear regression can lead to competing requirements on nonlinear or heterogeneous data. To address this issue, we propose a decouple-then-align framework, termed DTA-UFS, that seeks consensus between spectral embedding and pseudo-labels to coordinate their complementary structural information. The framework separates the graph-smoothed spectral representation from the relaxed cluster indicator used as the sparse-regression target. An explicit semi-orthogonal alignment parameterization records the correspondence between their latent bases, through which manifold information guides feature selection via the learned pseudo-labels. Theoretically, we derive an upper bound on the consensus offset between the learned pseudo-label representation and an ideal cluster space, linking the alignment error and manifold regularization term in the objective to the quality of the learned representation under graph perturbation. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate competitive clustering performance against representative unsupervised feature-selection baselines. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: A Ti bond layer redirects stress accommodation to mitigate failure driven by interfacial stress in hard coatings on compliant metals
Abstract: Hard coatings on compliant metals are prone to buried interface damage because of pronounced mechanical mismatch during friction. Metallic bond layers improve adhesion, but their role in accommodating contact induced stress remains unclear. In this work, multilayer hard coatings containing either a Cr or Ti bond layer were designed on phosphor bronze substrates. Atmospheric and high vacuum tribological tests, wear track characterization and molecular dynamics simulations were combined to correlate macroscopic wear behavior with subsurface mechanical responses. Under high vacuum friction at 5 N, the coating with a Cr bond layer exhibited a coefficient of friction of approximately 0.60, whereas the coating with a Ti bond layer maintained a lower value of approximately 0.43 and reduced the specific wear rate from 18.21 × 10⁻⁵ to 6.29 × 10⁻⁵ mm³ /(N·m). The architecture with a Cr bond layer developed cracking, whereas the architecture with a Ti bond layer showed more gradual deformation and localized material removal. Simulations further revealed that the Ti bond layer retained a larger compressive response and a greater fraction of plastic deformation, thereby reducing mechanical disturbance in the underlying substrate. These results identify the buried metallic bond layer as an active mechanical region that redistributes the location and mode of stress accommodation during friction. This work provides a mechanics based design principle for suppressing interface dominated failure and improving the durability of hard coatings on compliant metals. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Load-dependent tribofilm formation of solid-liquid core-shell particles as lubricant additives under boundary lubrication
Abstract: Solid-liquid core-shell particles are promising lubricant additives, however, the load-dependent interfacial response and tribofilm evolution of porous solid-liquid composite additives under boundary lubrication remain insufficiently understood. In this study, PTFE@DFNS@ILs particles, consisting of a polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) core, dendritic fibrous nanosilica (DFNS) mesoporous shell, and confined [BMIM][PF6] ionic liquids, were evaluated as additives in PAO6 base oil. Compared with PTFE, n SiO2, ZDDP, and physically mixed control formulations, P@D@ILs exhibited enhanced friction reduction and wear protection under the investigated boundary lubrication conditions. SEM-EDS, XPS, and FIB-TEM analyses revealed a pronounced load dependence of tribofilm formation. The local tribofilm increased in thickness from low to moderate loads and became thinner at the highest load, indicating a competition between tribofilm formation/compaction and shear-induced removal. XPS and cross-sectional analyses showed that the tribofilm contained FeOx, FeF2, Fe-O-P-related species. The combined results support a possible load-adaptive lubrication mechanism involving the interfacial participation of confined ILs-derived species, possible mechanical response of the composite particles, tribochemical interactions, and development of a protective tribofilm. Title: MF-IPTI: Multi-feature driven transfer identification model of incomplete wear particles for automatic wear state assessment
Abstract: Ferrography analysis has been widely employed to assess equipment wear state by examining wear particles in lubricating oils. However, the accuracy of existing methods is limited by incomplete particles resulting from agglomeration and mutual occlusion in ferrograph images. To address this issue, this paper proposes a transfer identification model for incomplete particles based on multi-feature fusion. Given the weak features of incomplete particles, a salient feature extractor is established involving a shape-texture feature branch enhanced by a grouped convolution strategy and a frequency-domain feature branch utilizing a learnable transformation method. On this basis, a transfer identification model between incomplete and complete particles is constructed with the joint maximum mean discrepancy of practical features. Through this approach, discriminative features from complete particles are adopted to guide the type identification of incomplete particles. For verification, the proposed model is tested on 128 real particle samples from coal mine machinery. The proposed model successfully identified four particle types: cutting, spherical, sliding, and fatigue, and improved the identification accuracy from 77.34% to 96.88% compared to existing methods. Furthermore, the model is applied to automatically assess the wear states of 22 coal mine machinery with a diagnostic accuracy of 95.45%. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Unravelling the kinetic and thermodynamic drivers of NO variability in ammonia-natural gas combustion based powertrains
Abstract: The deployment of ammonia–natural gas combustion in clean powertrains is limited not only by combustion instability, but also by the lack of cycle-resolved tools able to connect stochastic combustion behaviour with emissions formation and control. This work addresses this gap by developing an integrated cycle‑resolved digital diagnostic framework combining engine in‑cylinder pressure analysis, a two‑zone thermodynamic model, a digital twin for residual gas estimation, and detailed chemical kinetics to predict cycle‑to‑cycle variability (CCV) of emissions in low- and zero-carbon fuels, including ammonia (NH3), natural gas (NG) and their blends. Consequently, increasing NH3 substitution reduces NO formation under the investigated conditions, as the effects of lower peak pressures and temperatures dominate over the longer residence times in the burned-gas zone, reduced residual fractions, and the contribution of fuel-bound nitrogen. NO variability is shown to be partly inherited from combustion dynamics, increasing with NH3 due to greater flame kernel instability. The kinetic analysis further identifies oxygen-sensitive burned-gas pathways controlling NO2, N2O, CO and CO2 evolution under stoichiometric operation, providing mechanistic insight into the local nitrogen-species chemistry associated with NH3–NG combustion. These findings identify combustion temperature and species residence time as key control-relevant parameters governing emissions formation within the narrow stoichiometric window required for three-way catalyst (TWC) operation. The proposed integrated diagnostic framework provides a practical predictive solution supporting the design and control of NH3–NG combustion systems in future clean powertrains. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Consistent dilatancy-based constitutive model of rock salt for geo-energy storage applications: An open-source numerical implementation
Abstract: Accurate numerical simulation of salt cavern performance in underground geo-energy storage of hydrogen, natural gas, compressed air, and CO2 requires the integration of precise design criteria into a rigorous mechanical constitutive framework. This framework should be consistent with the design criteria, describing all mechanical loading (either short or long-term) deformations with a single parameter set. Due to methodological disconnects between the experimental derivation of design criteria and constitutive laws, only a limited number of consistent constitutive models exist in the literature. The RTL2020 model exemplifies such a mechanical constitutive law by incorporating dilatancy both as a feature in the mechanical constitutive model and as a design criterion, enabling accurate prediction of either short- or long-term mechanical deformations, including volumetric strain, with a single parameter set. This study presents a novel numerical implementation strategy for the RTL2020 model within an open-source simulator. The approach employs a stress–strain update algorithm using Newton–Raphson iterations with an adaptation of the classical implicit integration scheme (elastic predictor-inelastic corrector). This formulation ensures unconditional stability, rapid convergence, high numerical accuracy and low computational cost at the constitutive level. Validation against experimental data confirms the model's capacity to reproduce key mechanical behaviours of rock salt, including the negligible influence of mean pressure on axial and deviatoric strains and the strong sensitivity of volumetric strain to mean pressure. These results underscore the robustness of our implementation. Application of the model to numerical triaxial cyclic-loading simulations further reveals a profound dependence of deformation rate and mechanism on loading frequency and stress amplitude, which has important implications for the long-term performance of hydrogen storage caverns in rock-salt formations. The model is open-source, making it readily accessible to the geomechanics community as a reliable tool for salt cavern design in geo-energy storage. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Zhang F.; Song J.; Mei G.; Ren Y.; Deng C.; Yi J.
Title: Research on pyrolysis fluidization characteristics of oil shale
Abstract: Aiming at the inapplicability of classical fluidization theory to oil shale pyrolysis system featuring non-spherical, wide-size-distribution (0–3000 μm) and non-normally distributed shale powder and shale ash, as well as the lack of theoretical support for reactor scale-up and precise process control, this study systematically explores fluidization characteristics of shale powder and shale ash in fluidized beds and risers. Key parameters were measured via pressure drop method, differential pressure method and particle size analysis. Title: Enhanced hotspot suppression and two-phase boiling performance in groove–tapered composite microchannels for high heat flux electronics

Title: Quantifying the synergistic effect via microwave co-pyrolysis of waste tires and corn plant stalk: pollutants inhibition, fuel quality enhancement, and mechanistic insights

Title: Solvent-free hot-pressed zein films: Synergistic plasticization with glycerol, decanoic acid, and potassium hydroxide

Title: Revealing the oxygen-vacancy link to microstructural evolution and dielectric response in MgO-doped 82NaNbO3-18CaTiO3 ceramics
Abstract: Oxygen vacancies (OVs) play a decisive yet elusive role in determining microstructural evolution and dielectric response of lead-free antiferroelectric ceramics. Title: Conjugate heat-transfer performance and flow mechanisms of impingement cooling with corrugated and microchannel target surfaces
Abstract: Turbine blades in advanced aero-engines require efficient internal cooling under severe thermal loads. This study investigates conjugate heat transfer in an impingement cooling system with corrugated and microchannel target surfaces at Reynolds numbers of 5000, 10000, and 20000. Title: Radiative heat transfer and photothermal performance analysis of an MXene-Perovskite metamaterial solar absorber using machine learning and numerical modeling

In addition, parametric study results demonstrate the strong reliability and tunability of the absorber as the resonator parameters and layer thicknesses are varied. Title: Integrated CH4 joint production and CO2 sequestration: insights from various depressurization schemes and post-production partially depleted hydrate and shallow gas reservoirs
Abstract: Joint methane hydrate and shallow gas extraction can improve the economic viability of marine hydrate production. However, the gas production rate typically declines in the later stages, making it uneconomical to fully recover the remaining hydrates. Interestingly, the reservoir conditions during these later stages may favor CO2 sequestration. This study proposes an integrated approach for the co-production of marine hydrates and shallow gas coupled with CO2 storage. Various depressurization schemes were employed to extract hydrates and shallow gas, while monitoring temperature and pressure responses, as well as variations in gas and water production rates. Following joint production, CO2 was injected into the in-situ depleted reservoir for storage. Based on experimental research, further numerical simulations were conducted to reveal the characteristics of joint production and the mechanism of depleted reservoir environment in CO2 sequestration. The results indicate that residual hydrate nuclei, combined with CO2 displacement, drive the hydrate layer into a rapid CO2 storage stage. In the hydrate layer, the CO2 sequestration rate is jointly controlled by residual methane hydrates, remaining hydrate crystals, and CO2 partial pressure. In contrast, the rapid sequestration stage in the shallow gas layer occurs later and is predominantly governed by CO2 partial pressure. Stepwise and deep depressurization enhances CO2 partial pressure and sequestration efficiency by reducing residual methane. Combining stepwise and deep depressurization during dual-gas production represents an optimal strategy for improving both gas recovery and CO2 storage efficiency. Title: Synergistic dual-vacancy engineering in a Cl-doped Cu2O/Cu3SnS4 S-scheme heterojunction for selective photocatalytic CO2-to-C2H4 conversion

Title: Structural, dielectric, electrical and modulus spectroscopic investigation of Mg-doped CoFe2O4 spinel ferrites for advanced memory storage applications
Abstract: Magnesium-substituted cobalt ferrites, Co₁₋ₓMgₓFe₂O₄ (x = 0.0, 0.1, 0.3, and 0.5), were synthesized via the sol–gel method to investigate their structural, optical, dielectric, electrical, and resistive switching properties. Title: Experimental study on high-pressure constant-volume combustion of ultra-lean methane-air mixtures under different ignition delay times
Abstract: Low-concentration coal mine gas is typically characterized by low combustion rate and significant heat losses. Studies on ultra-lean methane-air combustion under high-pressure constant-volume and turbulent conditions remain limited. This study experimentally investigates turbulent combustion characteristics and heat losses under elevated initial pressures, where turbulence intensity is regulated by adjusting the ignition delay time t d. Title: Vibration suppression of beams under moving loads using a magnetically limited geometrically nonlinear absorber
Abstract: Transient peak responses and residual vibrations induced by moving loads are commonly encountered in bridges, track beams, and structures carrying moving loads. Based on the Euler–Bernoulli beam theory, a coupled dynamic model of a simply supported beam equipped with the ML-GNA subjected to moving concentrated loads is established. The governing equations are discretized using the Galerkin method, and the nonlinear time-domain responses are obtained by combining the Newmark-β method with Newton–Raphson iteration. The vibration suppression performance of the ML-GNA is further investigated under a single moving load, multiple moving loads, and accelerated/decelerated moving loads. The optimized ML-GNA reduces both the load-passing peak displacement and the post-departure residual vibration over the examined optimized mass ratio range of μ = 0.06–0.10. Abstract: With the continuous growth of global energy demand and the escalating severity of environmental challenges, the development of renewable and clean energy sources has become a global priority, among which photocatalytic hydrogen production has attracted considerable attention as a promising strategy to address the increasing global energy demand. Title: Biconvex dual PINNs for stable identification of particulate population dynamics
Abstract: The evolution of particulate systems in breakage environments is modeled by population balance partial integro-differential equations, whose predictive capacity depends on the specified breakage kernel functions. Traditional practice relies on prior expertise to assume parametrized forms for these kernels. However, inadequate assumptions for uncharacterized systems can misrepresent the underlying physics. Recent studies highlight breakage-informed dynamic mode decomposition as a means to non-parametric kernel identification, but the method remains susceptible to the practical ill-posedness of the problem as constraining the forward operator does not imply valid kernels. A distinguishing feature of our method is that it explicitly constrains the kernels while inducing a biconvex optimization structure on a typically complex PINN loss landscape. This structure admits an alternating convex search procedure with a guaranteed monotonic loss reduction property, thereby leading to fast and stable training. Extensive numerical verification on generated and real-world grinding data demonstrates the competitiveness of the dual PINN approach relative to dynamic mode decomposition and other baselines. Title: Kinetic reaction performance of methane hydrate under different unsaturated seepage scenarios in high-pressure sediments
Abstract: Methane hydrates (MH) represent a massive unconventional clean energy resource, making the understanding of their multiphase phase-transition dynamics within porous media critical for safe extraction and geological carbon storage. While macroscopic static systems and steady-state flows have been extensively studied, existing kinetic models largely rely on full-saturation assumptions, which fail to capture the complex, unsaturated multiphase seepage environments characteristic of natural MH reservoirs. To address this limitation, we investigate the deep coupling mechanisms between unsaturated multiphase hydrodynamics and crystallization kinetics by simulating the spatiotemporal evolution of MHs under designed boundary and thermodynamic conditions. Employing a comprehensive high-pressure multiphase flow-reaction framework, we integrate the kinetic model with van Genuchten soil–water characteristics (swcc) and multiphase heat and mass transfer equations. We systematically evaluate the hydrate formation process over different periods (days), analyzing the differential impacts of temperature, medium porosity, boundary fluid fluxes, and injection phase states on matrix evolution. Our results reveal that kinetic enhancement at higher temperatures (4 °C) dominates over thermodynamic subcooling, driving greater overall MH accumulation. Furthermore, high-porosity matrices sustain superior late-stage reaction rates by preserving seepage connectivity, whereas forced high-velocity gas injection overcomes capillary resistance but inhibits crystal growth by disrupting interfacial stability. Crucially, water injection into gas-bearing media tends to induce frontal self-sealing, leading to localized MH accumulation near the injection end; In contrast, gas injection into water-bearing media leverages the high mobility of the gas phase to effectively overcome pore-throat blockage, enabling extensive and deep MH formation within the porous medium. These results provide critical insights into the numerical prediction of MH formation and serve as a scientific basis for evaluating MH resource potential. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Crystal growth and scintillation properties of Dy co-doped CsI(Tl) single crystal for radiation detection
Abstract: In this work, single crystals of Dy co-doped CsI(Tl) scintillators were successfully grown using the vertical Bridgman method. Their physical and scintillation properties were investigated. Title: Prediction of coal temperature during spontaneous combustion based on the fusion of primary and auxiliary multi-gas indicators and GA-GWO-SVR: a case study of coal mines in Ningxia, China
Abstract: Accurate prediction of coal temperature is important for the early warning, prevention, and control of goaf fires. Title: Defect-engineered MIL-53(Fe)/Ag3PO4 heterojunction with Ag nanobridges: regulating charge-transfer dynamics for enhanced photocatalytic ciprofloxacin degradation and H2 evolution

Abstract: The rational design of heterojunction photocatalyst with efficient charge transfer pathways is crucial for enhancing photocatalytic performance. Title: Recursive object-centric process discovery with fitness and rediscovery guarantees
Abstract: Digitized processes are an integral part of businesses to achieve their operational goals. Process mining aims to analyze such processes based on digital track records. However, in real-life processes, it is much more common to observe multiple business objects of various types that interact with each other. If it is impossible to rediscover the full behavior of a process, the discovered model should at least be fitting for the observed behavior. We prove that our approach produces fitting models for all logs and rediscovers a subclass of processes within the used representational bias from logs that are sufficiently complete and free of incorrect recordings, unobserved or duplicated activities and loops. Title: Experimental investigation of ignition delay and laminar burning velocity of HVO/RP-3 blends as a drop-in aviation fuel under extended operating conditions

Title: Buckling–fracture interactions in triangular lattices: A combined experimental–numerical study
Abstract: Micro-architectured lattices are increasingly recognised as promising candidates for high-performance structural applications due to their exceptional stiffness-to-weight ratios. However, the governing failure mechanisms — particularly the interaction between fracture and geometric instabilities — remain insufficiently understood. Here, we present the first systematic experimental investigation of the effect of strut buckling on the fracture toughness of finite-sized triangular lattices. A combined experimental-numerical approach is employed using laser-cut polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) triangular lattices across a range of relative densities. Below a critical relative density, a distinct regime is identified in which elastic strut buckling precedes fracture and alters the governing failure mechanism. Title: Molecular-scale insight and predictive model for sulfur deposition tendency in high-sulfur gas reservoirs and wellbores
Abstract: During the development of high-sulfur gas reservoirs, variations in temperature and pressure typically reduce the solubility of elemental sulfur in natural gas and consequently induce sulfur deposition. The results indicate that sulfur deposition potential is governed by the variation of elemental sulfur solubility along the flow path rather than by sulfur solubility at a single thermodynamic condition. Moreover, both sulfur solubility and deposition vary with gas composition, suggesting that sulfur deposition is controllable by adjusting the sour gases. The molecular mechanism underlying the above changes in sulfur solubility and sulfur deposition was elucidated based on intermolecular interaction analysis. Our findings demonstrate that sulfur deposition is governed by solubility variations rather than solubility itself, thereby providing a predictive basis for sulfur deposition risk assessment during the development of high-sulfur gas reservoirs. Title: Effect of relative humidity on the desiccation behavior of bentonite buffer blocks for geological repositories

Title: Angle-weighted Visibility-based Phase Attention Entropy (AWVP-AttEn): An effective method to characterize the nonlinear time series

Title: Suppression disturbance hole configuration influence on buoyancy effect of brush seal based transient fluid-solid interaction
Abstract: To address the issue that traditional brush seal (TBS) experiences buoyancy effect due to airflow, which leads to bristles disturbance failure and reduced service life, novel suppression disturbance brush seal (SDBS) configurations were proposed, including those with straight (SDSH), oblique (SDOH), and convergent (SDCH) hole. A three-dimensional transient solution model for buoyancy effect of SDBS was established using Arbitrary Lagrange-Eulerian (ALE) fluid-solid interaction (FSI) method. Upon confirming the accuracy of numerical model, the leakage characteristics and flow-field velocity distribution of the SDBS were investigated, and the influence of different suppression disturbance (SD) hole configurations on buoyancy effect was investigated. Results demonstrate that SDBS feature SD hole on the front plate effectively mitigates airflow induced bristle bending deformation, with the SDCH configuration exhibiting superior performance in suppressing the disturbance and reducing wear. Compared to TBS, the proposed SDBS configuration (SDSH, SDOH, and SDCH) can reduce leakage by 3.27%-18.70% and decrease average deformation of bristle tip by 26.92%–37.13%. For the SDCH, increasing the SD hole angle, diameter, and height significantly diminishes the average deformation of bristle tip. Within one-factor parameter ranges investigated in this study, when each single factor is at its respective maximum ( β = 60°, D ₁ = 1.50 mm, H = 5.35 mm), reductions in average bristle tip deflection can reach 41.48%, 50.28% and 39.65%, respectively. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wang W.; Liu G.; Wei L.; Ma T.; Xu T.; Liu D.
Title: Tailoring photothermal CO2 hydrogenation by oxide-supported Pt catalysts prepared by flame spray pyrolysis
Abstract: CO2 hydrogenation provides a route for carbon utilization and renewable energy storage, but the catalytic behavior of supported Pt catalysts is strongly influenced by the oxide support. Herein, Pt-supported CeO2, In2O3, and TiO2 catalysts were prepared by flame spray pyrolysis (FSP) to compare support-dependent CO2 hydrogenation under thermal and light-irradiation conditions. The three reducible semiconductor oxides showed distinct redox properties, optical responses, and surface chemical environments, enabling a comparative evaluation of support effects. Characterization results indicate that the oxide support affects catalyst morphology, surface area, reducibility, light absorption, Pt chemical state, and surface oxygen species. Catalytic tests revealed support-dependent CO2 conversion and CO/CH4 selectivity. Under illumination, the measured light-induced temperature rise of approximately 20 °C, but CO2 conversion was markedly enhanced over all three catalysts. This indicates that the photothermal effect plays an important role in improving catalytic performance, although the extent of improvement still depends on the oxide support. In situ DRIFTS over Pt-TiO2 provided information on carbonate-, bicarbonate- and CO-related surface species under reaction conditions. This work highlights that both oxide-support selection and photothermal activation are important for optimizing Pt-supported catalysts in CO2 hydrogenation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Ding H.; Zhang R.; Zhang H.; Li T.; Shu H.; Liu G.; Gao Q.
Title: A semantic-aware dual-stream framework for spatiotemporal trajectory-user linking
Abstract: Trajectory-User Linking (TUL) aims to associate mobility trajectories with corresponding users. Current solutions rely heavily on POI identifiers and sequential dynamics, thereby providing narrow spatiotemporal insight. This paradigm yields task-specific representations that lack commonality in human mobility patterns and cross-city transferability. In this work, we propose a Semantic-Aware Trajectory-User Linking framework with city-wise transfer learning, named SATUL. In detail, SATUL leverages pre-trained semantic encoders to embed POI category texts and develops multi-frequency sinusoidal encoding to jointly capture temporal periodicity and spatial continuity. Furthermore, SATUL establishes cross-city transferability through a dual-stream mechanism that pre-trains a shared trajectory encoder across cities via joint domain optimization. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that SATUL consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines with superior data efficiency, particularly in data-scarce and cold-start scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Yin F.; Wang G.; Barinov A.A.; Liu S.; Xu K.
Title: Cove-edge-induced vibrational confinement and weakened collective phonon transport in graphene nanoribbons
Abstract: Periodic cove edges alter heat conduction in graphene nanoribbons in ways that are not fully captured by geometric boundary scattering. We investigate this effect using a graphene-nanoribbon-specific neuroevolution potential together with molecular dynamics, phonon Monte Carlo simulations, lattice dynamics, and full linearized phonon Boltzmann transport calculations. Cove-edged graphene nanoribbons exhibit lower thermal conductivity than pristine armchair nanoribbons over the length and width ranges considered. The conductivity reduction obtained from molecular dynamics is larger than that predicted by the semiclassical Monte Carlo model. The residual fraction is greatest at short lengths and small widths, whereas the Monte Carlo boundary contribution becomes relatively more important as either dimension increases. Participation ratios and real-space eigenvectors identify partially confined and strongly edge-confined modes in the low- and intermediate-frequency ranges, showing how the cove geometry reconstructs the vibrational eigenstates beyond a purely geometric boundary-scattering picture. The cove-edged ribbons also show a smaller collective correction beyond the relaxation-time approximation and a lower transport-weighted Normal-to-Umklapp scattering-rate ratio. These results indicate that cove-edge patterning changes both the vibrational eigenstates and the intrinsic scattering balance, thereby reducing the mode-coupling correction beyond the independent-mode approximation. Authors: Xia Z.; Zhang X.; Zhang W.; Liu B.; Pan J.; Song N.; Chen P.
Title: Statistics-based adaptive and hierarchical framework for underwater image restoration
Abstract: Underwater imaging plays a crucial role in marine observation and robotic perception, yet scattering and wavelength-dependent attenuation degrade contrast, color fidelity and sharpness, limiting downstream vision tasks. Although numerous restoration methods have been proposed, the statistical regularities inherent in degraded underwater images, which can characterize scattering and attenuation, remain underexplored. Moreover, it is still unclear how these statistical characteristics can be systematically exploited to inform the development of restoration methods. To address this gap, we propose a statistics-based adaptive and hierarchical framework that takes these statistical regularities as its core design principle, and operates in CIELab color space to decouple lightness and chromaticity for targeted correction. We demonstrate that adaptive tail squeezing of the lightness channel, combined with hierarchical shift estimation of chromaticity channels, yields robust contrast enhancement and natural color correction across diverse underwater conditions. For color cast, we developed a mathematical model for shift and compression of chromaticity histograms, inferred the shift direction via hierarchical detection approach, and estimated the shift magnitude through two-stage strategy incorporating fast estimation and convex optimization. We applied kurtosis- and skewness-guided asymmetric stretching to avoid over- or under-compensation. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate consistent gains in quantitative metrics and visual fidelity while suppressing artifacts. These findings indicate that distribution-aware manipulations provide a feasible and interpretable route to underwater image restoration, benefiting downstream perception. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: The role of NO2-induced sulfite oxidation in process modeling of nitrogen oxides and sulfur oxides absorption
Abstract: Simultaneous removal of NOx and SOx in a wet scrubber is simulated in a process modeling software with the addition of a proposed reaction, aiming to capture the rapid consumption of S(IV) ions (SO32- and HSO3-). Previous work has shown that the presence of NO2 drives the oxidation of S(IV) ions due to the formation of radical species, with reported oxidation rates that vary between authors. The complexity of simulating the highly reactive and complex radicals is addressed through a newly proposed mechanism which omits radical species, allowing integration into process simulation. The kinetic coefficients estimation is performed by fitting modeling results to a range of experimental data at varied operational conditions and two process configurations. A good agreement in both NO2 absorption and S(IV) oxidation is obtained in the open-loop configuration, with slight deviations in S(IV) oxidation observed at lower S(IV) concentration. Sensitivity analysis shows that S(IV) oxidation is mainly governed by nitrogen-sulfur reactions, while NO2 absorption is also influenced by mass-transfer parameters such as residence time and interfacial area. Applying the reaction to the closed-loop system requires an increase in the kinetic coefficient in order to obtain a good fit in the NO2 absorption level, showing that the proposed reaction is specific to each evaluated set-up. S(IV) oxidation in the absorber sump is investigated, where the significant effect of NO2 concentration is identified. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Predictive modeling of flash-boiling ammonia sprays using a volume expansion ratio
Abstract: Ammonia is attracting interest as a carbon-free fuel for internal combustion engines. Because it can be stored as a liquid under moderate pressure, liquid injection is often considered; under low ambient pressure, liquid injection can induce flash-boiling, which significantly alters spray morphology and affects mixture formation and combustion processes. Therefore, accurate modeling of flash-boiling sprays is necessary in computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations. This study proposes a practical modeling framework for flash-boiling liquid ammonia sprays. The model assumes that near-nozzle spray morphology is affected by vapor generation within the liquid phase and subsequent volumetric expansion during depressurization. Accordingly, a volume expansion ratio, Vexp, defined as the ratio of volumetric flow rates before and after flash-boiling, is introduced. Correlations for spray width and spray angle are formulated as functions of Vexp and used as initial conditions in discrete droplet model calculations. Because Vexp depends on fuel thermophysical properties and thermodynamic conditions, spray morphology variations with fuel species, fuel temperature, and ambient pressure can be represented through changes in Vexp. The framework was validated using spray visualization experiments for ammonia and propane under various ambient pressures and fuel temperatures. Data for the near-nozzle spray width and spray angle collapsed reasonably well when plotted against Vexp, and the proposed correlations predicted these quantities with R2 values of 0.89 and 0.75, respectively. CFD simulations reproduced the measured spray morphology reasonably without condition-specific tuning for Vexp≲200. The framework offers a practical approach for designing liquid ammonia injection systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wu Z.; Liu C.; Wang Y.; Zhu Y.; Wang X.; Jiang Y.; Nawaz H.; He A.; Hu L.
Title: Nb-Mo bimetallic catalyst facilitated efficient fractionation of corncob in alkali-alcohol solvent
Abstract: The valorization of lignocellulosic biomass is significantly hindered by the recalcitrance of lignin and the inefficiency of conventional fractionation methods. This study presents a novel niobium–molybdenum bimetallic catalyst (NMC) for the efficient fractionation of corncob and depolymerization of lignin in an alkali-alcohol solvent system. Under mild conditions of 150 °C and 2 h, the NMC-catalyzed process achieved an exceptional delignification rate of 96.8% in a NaOH-methanol solvent system (5 wt% NaOH in a 1:1 vol ratio with methanol). The yield of undepolymerized lignin was minimized to 5.2 wt%, while that of lignin depolymerization products (LDPs) reached a maximum of 35.9 wt%. Comprehensive characterization confirmed the composite structure of NMC, featuring uniformly dispersed single–atom sites and nanoclusters, which contributed to its enhanced catalytic activity. Three acetophenone derivatives, 4-hydroxy-2-methylacetophenone, apocynin, and acetosyringone were identified as the principal monomers from lignin depolymerization under this strategy. The synergistic effect of NMC, methanol and the alkaline environment effectively promote the fractionation of corncob and suppressed the condensation reactions of lignin intermediates. This work presents a scalable and mild-condition strategy for lignocellulose biorefining, underscoring the significant potential of rationally designed bimetallic catalysts in the sustainable production of high-value aromatics from renewable biomass. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Song J.; Meng Q.; Sun W.
Title: Sm3+, Bi3+ co-doped GdVO4 temperature sensing nanophosphors based on the fluorescence intensity ratios
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: In this work, hydrothermally synthesized GdVO4 nanophosphors with 5 mol% Bi3+ and varying Sm3+ (0.1 mol%, 0.2 mol%, 0.4 mol%) co-doping were prepared, and a systematic investigation was performed on their optical thermometric behavior. It is indicated by experimental findings that the Bi3+ luminescence intensity in the GdVO4 host exhibits a remarkable thermal quenching trend, whereas Sm3+ emission experiences far slower thermal quenching relative to Bi3+. This notable difference in thermal quenching trends causes obvious changes in the fluorescence intensity ratio (FIR) for Sm3+ and Bi3+ upon heating. Consequently, temperature measurement can be performed through the FIR of them, which can achieve a high relative sensitivity ( S  r ). In the case of I703.5/I541 utilized for temperature characterization, the S  r  ascends along with the increase of Sm3+ doping level, maximum is 2.38% K−1 at 442 K for the 0.4 mol% Sm3+ sample. As for the I646/I541, the S  r  likewise rises with growing Sm3+ doping level, maximum is 2.51% K−1 at 426 K for the 0.4 mol% Sm3+ sample. In addition, with temperature elevated, the nanophosphor exhibits an emission color transition from yellow-green to orange-red, which supports rough temperature evaluation via luminescence chromaticity coordinates of the nanophosphors. The GdVO4: Bi3+, Sm3+ nanophosphors demonstrated stable temperature measurement performance in the experiments, and the materials have the potential to be applied in the field of optical temperature sensing. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Bu G.; Guo C.; Gao X.; Ma R.; Wei B.; Chen L.; Wang S.; Wang J.; Yu Q.
Title: Experimental and DFT study on the mechanism of inorganic chlorine to organic chlorine during pyrolysis of high chlorine lump coal
Abstract: High-chlorine coal thermal utilization triggers severe equipment corrosion, yet the fundamental mechanisms governing the anomalous low-temperature transformation of inorganic to organic chlorine remain elusive. This study systematically investigated chlorine migration pathways during the pyrolysis of Xinjiang Shaerhu coal, utilizing both experimental characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Results reveal that the inorganic-to-organic chlorine conversion rate in lump coal peaks at 90 % at 750℃, significantly exceeding the 54 % observed for fine coal. Concurrently, the mass-transfer-limited lump coal tar yield peaks at 650℃ before rapidly declining, with chlorinated organics dominated by long-chain chlorinated hydrocarbons rather than the multi-component aromatics found in fine coal. Mechanistically, nanoconfinement within lump coal internal pores weakens Na-Cl ionic bonds to induce sub-melting-point dissociation. DFT calculations confirm that the binding energy of Cl· radicals at in-plane central vacancies (−853.5 kJ/mol) is far higher than at edge sites (−451.9 kJ/mol), while oxygen-containing functional groups lower the reaction barrier via electron-withdrawing inductive effects to facilitate stable covalent C-Cl cross-linking.This study elucidates the transformation mechanism of inorganic-to-organic chlorine from the perspectives of confined mass transfer and electronic structure regulation, providing a theoretical foundation for parameter optimization and anti-corrosion control in industrial vertical furnace lump coal pyrolysis dechlorination processes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Hou J.; Liu S.; Bie Y.; Wang H.; Tan A.; Luo L.; Chen H.
Title: Self-eXplainable AI for medical image analysis: A survey and new outlooks
Abstract: The increasing demand for transparent and reliable models, particularly in high-stakes decision-making areas such as medical image analysis, has led to the emergence of eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI). Post-hoc XAI techniques, which aim to explain black-box models after training, have raised concerns about their fidelity to model predictions. In contrast, Self-eXplainable AI (S-XAI) offers a compelling alternative by incorporating explainability directly into the training process of deep learning models. This approach allows models to generate inherent explanations that are closely aligned with their internal decision-making processes, enhancing transparency and supporting the trustworthiness, robustness, and accountability of AI systems in real-world medical applications. To facilitate the development of S-XAI methods for medical image analysis, this survey presents a comprehensive review across various image modalities and clinical applications. It covers more than 200 papers from three novel perspectives: 1) input explainability through the integration of explainable feature engineering and knowledge graph, 2) model explainability via attention-based learning, concept-based learning, and prototype-based learning, and 3) output explainability by providing textual explanations and visual counterfactual explanations. This paper also outlines desirable characteristics of S-XAI models for assessing explanation quality, while discussing major challenges and future research directions in developing S-XAI for medical image analysis. Title: Unravelling the role of built-in electric Fields in p-n SnS/NiFe-LDH heterojunctions for enhanced photocatalytic CO2 reduction
Abstract: Carbon-dioxide (CO2) photo-reduction reaction (CO2PR) offers a sustainable and cost-effective approach for transforming CO2 into value-added fuels. Nickel iron double layered hydroxides (NiFe-LDH) are promising photocatalysts for CO2PR due to their earth-abundance, tunable band gaps (∼2.1–2.3 eV) and inherent CO2 adsorption capacity. However, hasty recombination of photo-generated charge carriers confines their overall photocatalytic activity. Herein, a tin (II) sulphide (SnS)/NiFe-LDH heterojunction was engineered to enhance charge separation and catalytic efficiency. Structural analyses reveal that SnS incorporation beyond 15 wt% induces lattice strain and interfacial active sites, significantly improving the CO2 adsorption. Among the synthesized compositions, NFTS20 (20 wt% SnS) exhibits superior activity by yielding carbon monoxide (CO) and methanol (CH3OH) at rates of 60.76 and 5.76 µmol g-1h−1, respectively. This enhanced performance is attributed to suppressed charge recombination, increased surface area, and efficient interfacial charge transport. Notably, the Scanning tunneling microscope imaging and the X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy identifies sulfur diffusion into the LDH lattice, while valence band and flat band potential measurements confirms the development of a p-n (SnS/NiFe-LDH) heterojunction and its role in promoting directional charge separation. The formation of p-n junction is further corroborated with in-situ EPR studies, which demonstrated a notable increment in superoxide and hydroxyl radicals in NFTS20 under illumination, signifying the suppressed recombination and accelerated interfacial charge transfer. These synergetic structural and electronic modifications in NFTS20 result in significantly improved CO2PR activity, highlighting the potential of heterojunction engineering for solar-to-fuel conversion. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Accelerating the discovery of High-Performance multi-component thermodynamic hydrate inhibitors via Bayesian optimization with molecular insights into synergistic mechanisms
Abstract: Designing multi-component thermodynamic hydrate inhibitors is challenging due to limited experimental data and the combinatorial complexity of formulation space. To address this challenge, we propose a Bayesian optimization-based strategy for the efficient screening of multi-component inhibitors. This framework integrates machine learning (ML) models trained on 1661 experimental data points to capture the complex relationships between inhibitor compositions and methane hydrate phase equilibrium, while quantitatively elucidating the roles of key physicochemical properties in governing inhibition strength. On this basis, a suite of predictive ML models is established and subsequently coupled with Bayesian optimization to enable the intelligent exploration of the multi-component formulation space. The results suggest that the proposed strategy can assist in navigating high-dimensional formulation spaces and prioritizing promising candidate formulations for further evaluation, including multi-type and multi-component candidates that are sparsely represented in the training data. These findings suggest that the framework can capture useful patterns from predominantly single-type, single-component data and apply them to the exploration of multi-component candidate formulations. Furthermore, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations provide molecular-scale insights into the possible cooperative inhibition mechanisms. The simulations suggest that lipophilic groups may affect methane partitioning and transport near the interface, while inorganic ions can restrict water mobility through hydration. These observations offer a molecular-level interpretation of the combined effects of different inhibitor components, rather than direct evidence of synergistic inhibition. This mechanistic insight confirms that the interaction strengths among inhibitors, water, and methane molecules are critical determinants of inhibition performance and provides a molecular-level rationale for the effectiveness of the proposed model and strategy. Overall, this work provides a data-driven framework for more efficient screening and prioritization of multi-component hydrate inhibitor candidate formulations, thereby reducing the reliance on extensive empirical trial-and-error testing. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wang P.; Yu K.; He H.; Huang F.; Wu X.; Chen Y.
Title: UD-SfPNet: An underwater descattering shape-from-polarization network for 3D normal reconstruction
Abstract: Underwater optical imaging is severely hindered by scattering, but polarization imaging offers the unique dual advantages of descattering and shape-from-polarization (SfP) 3D reconstruction. To exploit these advantages, this paper proposes UD-SfPNet, an underwater descattering shape-from-polarization network that leverages polarization cues for improved 3D surface normal prediction. The framework jointly models polarization-based image descattering and SfP normal estimation in a unified pipeline, avoiding error accumulation from sequential processing and enabling global optimization across both tasks. UD-SfPNet further incorporates a novel color embedding module to enhance geometric consistency by exploiting the relationship between color encodings and surface orientation. A detail enhancement convolution module is also included to better preserve high-frequency geometric details that are lost under scattering. Experiments on the MuS-Polar3D dataset show that the proposed method significantly improves reconstruction accuracy, achieving a mean surface normal angular error of 15.12° (the lowest among compared methods). These results confirm the efficacy of combining descattering with polarization-based shape inference, and highlight the practical significance and potential applications of UD-SfPNet for optical 3D imaging in challenging underwater environments. Authors: Yang J.; Li T.; Xu J.; Gao W.; Wu M.; Wang K.; Chen Y.; Qian Y.; Wang P.
Title: Initiation and propagation of rolling contact fatigue cracks in rails: numerical prediction using an elastoplastic fatigue phase-field fracture model
Abstract: Rail rolling contact fatigue (RCF) damage evolves under multiaxial, non-proportional cyclic loading, often involving plastic accumulation, fatigue degradation, crack initiation, branching, and surface spalling or crushing. These coupled processes are difficult to describe within a unified framework using conventional stage-wise initiation and propagation approaches. In this study, a fracture phase-field model is developed by coupling elastoplastic deformation with fatigue damage accumulation. The cyclic damage, formulated based on the Basquin relation, is incorporated into the critical fracture energy through a degradation function. The staggered solution of the displacement field and the phase field is implemented in ABAQUS/Standard via a UMAT/UEL framework. The fatigue parameters are first examined against CT specimen fatigue crack-growth data and then applied to rail RCF simulations. Under moving Hertzian contact pressure combined with Coulomb frictional traction, the effects of friction coefficient and contact pressure on crack evolution are investigated. The results show that increasing the friction coefficient enhances tangential traction and drives equivalent stress and fatigue damage towards the near-surface region, shifting the dominant failure mode from subsurface crack initiation to surface spalling and reducing crack initiation life. Under non-proportional rolling contact loading, the evolving crack-tip stress state promotes mixed-mode crack-path competition, deflection, and branching. At high contact pressure, plastic dissipation increases within the near-surface plastic zone, leading to pronounced damage localization and crushing-type surface morphology. The simulated crack characteristics are qualitatively consistent with representative field observations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wang M.; Xu J.; Chen C.; Sun B.; Yang J.; Yang L.
Title: 3D nanoporous hydrogel-integrated portable platform for pretreatment-free, rapid multiplexed detection of small-molecule biomarkers in whole blood
Abstract: Point-of-care testing (POCT) demands rapid, user-friendly solutions for instant medical diagnosis. Traditional colorimetric whole-blood analysis faces challenges from red blood cell and hemoglobin interference, often necessitating complex pretreatment. Herein, we introduce a three-dimensional (3D) nanoporous hydrogel-integrated portable platform designed for pretreatment-free, rapid multiplexed detection of small-molecule biomarkers directly from whole blood. The platform utilizes a polystyrene Eppendorf (EP)-tube as a miniaturized laboratory, featuring a TiO2-sodium alginate hydrogel-modified cap with a 3D nanoscale porous architecture. This innovative structure serves dual roles: embedding enzymatic systems for cascade reactions and excluding macromolecules (e.g., hemoglobin, erythrocytes) through size-selective exclusion. Small-molecule biomarkers (e.g., glucose, uric acid, lactate) diffuse into the hydrogel matrix, triggering concentration-proportional colorimetric signals via enzymatic cascade reactions. A 15-min "flip-and-scan" protocol-comprising tube inversion for biomarker diffusion and smartphone RGB analysis for quantitative readout-enables simultaneous quantification of three biomarkers with detection limits of 0.11 mM for glucose, 16 μM for uric acid, and 20 μM for lactate. The clinical validation with diverse patient samples (diabetic, gout, and composite metabolic cases) demonstrates that the tri-marker detection strategy enables precise differential diagnosis of overlapping metabolic syndromes by distinguishing biomarker patterns. Clinical validation with 15 diverse patient samples (5 diabetic patients, 5 gout patients, and 5 patients with composite metabolic abnormalities) demonstrated strong concordance with a commercial clinical biochemistry analyzer, with Pearson correlation coefficient > 0.95 and negligible bias in Bland-Altman analysis with all data points falling within the 95% limits of agreement. Compared with conventional microfluidic and paper-based sensors, this approach eliminates pretreatment steps, reduces assay time, ensures closed-loop biosafety, and prevents cross-contamination, offering a versatile and accessible analytical platform that represents a significant step toward practical multiplexed biomarker detection in POCT. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Solar pyrolysis of poplar wood Biomass: Effect of feedstock particle size and physical form
Abstract: Solar pyrolysis offers a sustainable pathway for converting lignocellulosic biomass into value-added products using concentrated radiative heat. In this study, solar pyrolysis experiments were conducted using poplar wood biomass in three feedstock forms-powder (<75 μm), chips (1–3 mm), and cylindrical pellets (approximately 6 mm diameter and 20–40 mm length) to investigate the influence of feedstock size/form and the associated thermal history on product formation and pyrogas characteristics. The pyrogas composition exhibited a strong temperature-dependent evolution, with H2 concentration increasing with increasing biomass-bed temperature and reaching a maximum of 55.65 vol% for pellets. Authors: Xue Y.; Chen D.
Title: A multi-scale modeling approach for infectious disease: Integrating within-host dynamics to network-based transmission
Abstract: Infectious disease transmission is shaped by tightly coupled biological processes within hosts and social contact patterns between hosts, making cross-scale modeling essential for understanding epidemic dynamics. We develop a data-driven multiscale framework that links within-host viral kinetics to between-host transmission on a dynamic multilayer contact network. Using influenza virus, SARS-CoV-2, and SARS-CoV as representative pathogens, we infer infection-age-dependent infectiousness from longitudinal viral-load data and integrate the resulting profiles into a stochastic individual-based model with contact layers constructed from empirical demographic and contact data. By comparing infectiousness profiles within the same multilayer transmission framework, we show that epidemic trajectories depend not only on overall transmission potential but also on the timing and duration of infectiousness. Early, concentrated infectiousness produces earlier epidemic peaks and shorter outbreaks, whereas later or prolonged infectiousness delays and extends transmission. Layer-resolved analyses show that setting-specific contributions arise from interactions among contact volume, contact intensity, and infectiousness profiles. Intervention simulations highlight the importance of temporal alignment: case isolation and vaccination are most effective when implemented before or during the pathogen-specific period of high infectiousness, whereas physical distancing reduces epidemic burden by lowering contact opportunities. This framework provides a flexible approach for linking viral-load-derived infectiousness with network-mediated transmission and evaluating targeted epidemic control strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Authors: Ma Y.; Wei J.; Yu A.C.H.; Qin P.
Title: Characterization and modulation of directly and delayed ultrasound-activated cells under single-pulse exposure
Abstract: Low-intensity ultrasound offers therapeutic promise through noninvasive, precise neuronal activation. Advancing its clinical translation requires a clear understanding of its biophysical mechanisms. However, due to intercellular communications, directly ultrasound-activated cells inevitably trigger delayed activation in neighboring cells. Accurate identification of these activation types is therefore essential for understanding ultrasound-cell interactions and improving ultrasound neuromodulation. Under continuous-wave ultrasound excitation, using the onset time of intracellular Fluo-4 fluorescence and the change in intracellular propidium iodide, directly ultrasound-activated cells, delayed-activated cells, and ultrasound-permeated cells were accurately characterized. For directly ultrasound-activated cells, the activation efficiency, amplitude, and time-to-peak of intracellular Ca2⁺ transients correlated positively with acoustic pressure but not pulse duration, suggesting acoustic radiation force may play a crucial role in cellular activation. Longer pulse intervals increased the probability of repeated cellular activation, with a ∼ 5-min interval significantly strengthening the temporal coupling between ultrasound pulse and cellular activation. Gd3⁺ and 2-APB treatments reduced activation efficiency and intracellular Ca2⁺ response levels, suggesting involvement of TRP family ion channels in direct activation. For delayed-activated cells, the propagation velocity of intercellular Ca2⁺ wave increased nearly linearly with the proportion and degree of directly ultrasound-activated cells, but decreased with longer time-to-peak of intracellular Ca2⁺ transients in those cells, demonstrating delayed activation originated from directly ultrasound-activated cells. The reduced propagation velocity in delayed-activated cells after Gd3+, 2-APB, and BAPTA treatment indicates involvement of gap-junction-dependent pathways and ATP-mediated paracrine signaling in intercellular Ca2⁺ propagation. This information facilitates the differentiation between directly ultrasound-activated cells and delayed–activated cells, advancing understanding of the mechanisms governing each activation type. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Structure-preserving methods for two-dimensional stochastic nonlinear wave equations with Stratonovich multiplicative noise

Abstract: This paper proposes a structure-preserving numerical method for a nonlinear wave equation driven by Stratonovich-type multiplicative noise. Title: Risk-aware heterogeneous multimodal fusion with structured discrete tokens for task-oriented robotic grasping
Abstract: Task-oriented grasping (TOG) is a multi-source heterogeneous fusion problem, requiring the selected grasp to be physically stable, semantically consistent with the intended task, and reliable under noisy evidence. Recent vision-language-action (VLA) approaches address this challenge by integrating visual observations, point clouds, language instructions, and candidate grasp actions within a unified multimodal framework. However, most existing methods compress visual scenes into continuous embeddings and score candidates in isolation, weakening fine-grained semantic alignment under clutter and yielding overconfident decisions under ambiguous instructions. Both failures leave the ranking head with evidence that is too coarse for part-level discrimination or too ambiguous for a reliable point estimate, motivating a joint treatment of representation structure and residual ambiguity. To address these issues, we propose UM-VLA-Grasp, an uncertainty-aware multimodal VLA framework for task-oriented grasp selection that discretizes visual scenes into structured visual tokens, jointly reasons over competing grasp candidates, and ranks them according to predictive uncertainty. RGB observations are quantized into a learned codebook and merged by byte-pair encoding (BPE), whose pair priority combines frequency with spatial consistency to produce tokens that preserve fine-grained scene patterns. These tokens are fused with point-cloud geometry, language instructions, and grasp action embeddings, while relational reasoning across the candidate set captures dependencies among grasps. For each candidate, the model outputs a task compatibility score and a predictive uncertainty, combined into a risk-aware utility that suppresses overconfident yet unreliable selections. Title: Non-ordinary state-based peridynamics method for predicting excavation damage zone of deep tunnels with initial in-situ stress equilibrium reconstruction
Abstract: The in-situ stress state before deep-tunnel excavation governs the unloading path and the formation of the excavation damage zone (EDZ). Peridynamic (PD) tunnel-excavation simulations commonly establish this state by boundary loading with dynamic relaxation. Because this procedure reaches equilibrium through externally induced deformation and numerical damping, artificial pre-deformation can be introduced, while the prescribed in-situ stress field and the discrete force equilibrium of free material points may remain inconsistent. To address this issue, a discrete reconstruction method for the pre-excavation in-situ stress state is developed and implemented within non-ordinary state-based peridynamics (NOSBPD). The method incorporates the prescribed in-situ stress into the initial stress state through an initial-stress–incremental-stress decomposition, evaluates the discrete residual on the unconstrained degrees of freedom, and solves for an initial-equilibrium correction force subject to pairwise antisymmetry and stress-preserving constraints. The correction force is introduced solely to enforce initial discrete equilibrium, and the corresponding correction is released when material points are removed by excavation or interactions fail. Comparisons with prescribed stress fields and the Kirsch solution verify target-stress recovery, residual-force reduction, and stress redistribution after excavation. The circular-tunnel excavation-damage case, compared with finite-element method (FEM) predictions and experimental reference data, validates the predicted EDZ, displacement field, and monitoring-point responses. Analyses examine equivalent burial depth, a linearly varying target in-situ stress field, and full-face, two-bench, and three-bench excavation of a horseshoe tunnel. Title: A least-squares weak Galerkin finite element scheme for cauchy problems in Helmholtz

Title: Development of a high-throughput proteome sample preparation workflow based on efficient protein extraction to empower rational design of yeast cell factories
Abstract: Mass spectrometry-based proteomics provides a powerful tool for the rational design of yeast cell factories. However, the rigid yeast cell wall architecture and the fast-growing scale of strain libraries present certain challenges for efficient protein extraction and high-throughput proteomic profiling. Conventional protein extraction methods either demand lengthy incubation periods or specialized equipment, leading to limited sample throughput and low efficiency. Herein, we report an efficient protein extraction strategy using a solvent combination of ionic liquid, guanidine hydrochloride, and lithium acetate under heat treatment (IGL-H). This method enables rapid protein extraction and is compatible with diverse yeast species across different growth phases. Compared with the classical glass bead grinding method, the IGL-H method affords higher protein yield and comparable or superior proteome coverage, and recovers higher proportions of integral membrane proteins of the endomembrane trafficking system. Furthermore, this method is readily amenable to liquid handling workstations for high-throughput proteome sample preparation by using magnetic solid-phase alkylation (mSPA) materials in less than 1.5 h, achieving Pearson correlation coefficients exceeding 0.97. Applying this pipeline to study proteome dynamics of Candida utilis under different nitrogen sources revealed an adaptive strategy involving carbon flux-specific allocation. Title: Precipitation mechanism and regulation of metallic iron from high-alkali slag revealed from chemical bond evolution
Abstract: The entrained-flow gasification of high-alkali coal is significantly hindered by high contents of CaO, MgO, and Fe2O3, which lead to elevated liquidus temperatures and metallic iron precipitation, causing severe slag tapping issues. Consequently, a comprehensive understanding of the iron precipitation mechanism in high-alkali slag systems is essential. However, this mechanism remains unexplored from the perspective of chemical bond structure of slag, impeding the effective regulation of such slags. This study elucidates the metallic iron precipitation mechanism by analyzing chemical bond evolution via thermodynamic modeling and proposes corresponding regulation strategies. Results indicate that the metallic iron was precipitation in the Shell gasification condition. The metallic iron content was decreased with the increasing SiO2 content, or Al2O3 content, or S/A ratio, or Ca/Mg ratio. Increasing AAEMs content of slag improved metallic iron precipitation. The iron in the liquid of CGS primarily exists as Si-O-Fe and Al-O-Fe bonds within the slag. The competition between Si-O-M (M=Na, K, Ca, Mg) and Fe-containing bonds facilitates iron precipitation. Specifically, the stability of Si-O-Mg exceeds that of Si-O-Ca, while Si-O-Na is stronger than Si-O-K. While increasing Ca2+ or Mg2+ content decreases Si-O-Fe bond content, Na+ and K+ ions interact with Si-O-Fe/Al-O-Fe through charge compensation, forming Si-O-NaAl or Si-O-KAl structures. Finally, blending high-alkali coal with 40–50 wt% coal gasification slag effectively lowers the liquidus temperature and prevents iron precipitation at a tapping temperature of 1350 °C, ensuring the slag viscosity meets the operation requirements for entrained-flow gasifiers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Gao P.; Cheng J.; Fei C.; Ren S.; Fan Y.; Zhang P.
Title: CoDIF: Conditional diffusion fusion with soft alignment for robust multimodal 3D object detection
Abstract: Dense bird’s-eye view (BEV) fusion has been widely adopted in multimodal 3D object detection for autonomous driving. However, most existing methods rely on calibration-based associations between sensors. This requires strict spatial alignment across modalities. Such rigid dependency restricts deep interactive learning and adaptive reasoning. Detection performance becomes highly vulnerable to heterogeneous noise and environmental perturbations. To address this challenge, we introduce a soft alignment mechanism and propose CoDIF, a multimodal detection framework built upon conditional diffusion fusion with few steps. CoDIF overcomes the above limitations through two core innovations. (1) Diffusion-driven Soft Fusion (DSF) realizes soft alignment via a prediction–reconstruction process: it learns to associate modalities without exact spatial correspondence, replacing rigid calibration with learnable cross-modal matching. (2) Patch-Global Gated fusion (PGG) orchestrates a local-to-global progressive control scheme. It employs a gating mechanism to adaptively balance multimodal features, achieving deep feature equilibrium. Extensive experiments on KITTI, nuScenes, and nuScenes-C benchmarks demonstrate that CoDIF surpasses state-of-the-art methods. These results validate the effectiveness of soft alignment and subsequent fusion. Under the disturbance of sensor misalignment on the nuScenes-C dataset, CoDIF exhibits outstanding robustness, improving the baseline by 3.78%. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: A novel red-emissive CDs-based aptasensor for sensitive detection of Pb2+ via fluorescence resonance energy transfer in vitro and in vivo
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Sensitive and efficient detection of lead ions (Pb2+) is important for protecting public safety and human health. In this study, a Pb2+-specific aptamer (Pb2+-apt) was covalently immobilized on the surface of red-emissive carbon quantum dots (R-CDs) through peptide bonds to produce the R-CDs@Pb2+-apt composite. This composite was combined with graphene oxide (GO) to construct a fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET)-based aptasensor (R-CDs@Pb2+-apt/GO). π–π stacking between R-CDs@Pb2+-apt and GO brought the two components into close proximity and quenched R-CD fluorescence through FRET. Upon Pb2+ addition, preferential binding of Pb2+-apt to the target ions disrupted its interaction with GO, interrupted FRET, and restored the fluorescence signal, enabling sensitive Pb2+ detection in serum samples. The red emission also reduced interference from endogenous fluorescence in wheat and supported in vivo imaging of Pb2+ in wheat plants. Under the optimized conditions, the aptasensor exhibited a linear response over 0.5–180 nM and a limit of detection of 0.03 nM. Because its aptamer sequence is exchangeable, the platform may be adaptable to the in vitro and in vivo detection of other metal ions. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Clark D.E.
Title: Topological cumulants of point-process currents
Abstract: A random population of trajectories can be viewed as a point process whose points are entire paths. When the spatial domain contains holes or obstacles, a path also carries global route information, such as how many times it winds around an obstacle. We represent this information by line integrals against a finite family of smooth one-forms supplied by Hodge–Morrey theory; on an annulus, the resulting coordinate is the usual winding number. The main result expresses the cumulant generating function of the aggregate coordinate vector directly in terms of the factorial cumulant measures of the path process. Differentiation yields an all-order partition formula for these topological cumulants. The covariance separates single-trajectory variation from non-Poisson dependence between trajectories. The construction is independent of the chosen closed-form representatives and transforms naturally under a change of coordinate basis. For Poisson path populations the law reduces to compound Poisson, and balanced clockwise and anticlockwise populations give a centred Skellam law. © 2026 The Author.

Title: An efficient high-fidelity medical image storage simulation based on a Gd2O3/Ta2O5 bilayer memristor with noise-tolerant binary readout
Abstract: Reliable readout under electrical noise is essential for memristor-based image-storage systems, particularly for medical images where small reconstruction errors may degrade diagnostic information. However, how device-level resistance-state separation translates into noise-tolerant, high-fidelity medical image storage remains insufficiently understood, particularly under experimentally calibrated rea dout conditions.
