The bilayer device exhibits a substantially enlarged resistance window and improved resistance-state stability within the evaluated 100 switching cycles, enabling well-separated resistance states for reliable binary storage compared with single-layer devices. The enhanced resistance-state separation is tentatively associated with the introduction of the Gd2O3/Ta2O5 heterointerface, which may modify the local electric-field distribution and defect-assisted transport, thereby influencing conductive-path formation and rupture. Experimentally calibrated simulations further show that the enlarged resistance-state separation of the bilayer device enables noise-tolerant binary image readout, yielding a BER of only 0.18% under 15% resistance-proportional read noise. More importantly, multiview CT image-storage simulation preserves high grayscale fidelity, yielding a BER of 0.17 ± 0.01%, PSNR of 32.17 ± 0.64 dB, SSIM of 0.9974 ± 0.0006, and MAE of 0.45 ± 0.05. Title: Seismic response of underground structures in layered unsaturated–saturated poroelastic sites under varying groundwater levels
Abstract: In this study, an explicit finite element method is developed for seismic response analysis of underground structures in layered unsaturated–saturated poroelastic sites under varying groundwater levels. The soil above the groundwater table is modeled as a layered unsaturated poroelastic medium, with saturation and properties varying with depth, while the soil below is modeled as a saturated poroelastic medium. The structure and bedrock are treated as single-phase elastic media. After finite element discretization, local nodal systems are constructed to derive explicit recurrence formulations for responses at any node. Seismic input is realized by combining one-dimensional site response analysis with transmitting artificial boundaries. The method is verified through degenerate cases and then applied to a subway station under varying groundwater levels. The effects of groundwater level, incident-wave characteristics, initial porosity, burial depth, and soil conditions above the groundwater table are examined. Results show that groundwater level variations change the unsaturated and saturated areas, thereby modifying site stiffness and wave propagation. These changes affect the surrounding-soil motion and consequently change the structural response. Incident-wave characteristics, porosity, and burial depth can further influence the response. Model comparisons indicate that simplifying the soil above the groundwater table as a single-phase elastic medium or a single-layer unsaturated poroelastic medium with fixed saturation may either underestimate or overestimate the structural response. The proposed method provides an efficient approach for seismic analysis of underground structures in layered unsaturated–saturated poroelastic sites and shows that groundwater level variations should not be neglected. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Electronic origin of catalytic methane pyrolysis on NiMoM-Bi alloys: a bader charge descriptor
Abstract: Methane pyrolysis can produce hydrogen without direct CO2 emissions, but catalyst deactivation by solid carbon remains a central barrier. Bader charge analysis shows that a more positive Ni charge is associated with shorter first C–H cleavage times (R2 = 0.8505), supporting its use as a correlational screening descriptor. Title: Beyond decontamination: Investigating the effect of gamma irradiation on natural dyes in a historical wool carpet
Abstract: This study investigates the viability of gamma irradiation as a treatment process for historical textiles, focusing on the dyes of a 19th–century wool carpet. Dye characterization using the LC-PDA-MS method revealed the presence of indigo carmine in the blue fibers, cochineal in the red fibers, and a mixture of weld and cochineal in the yellow fibers. The irradiation at 10 kGy significantly decreased the extractability of red and yellow color components. As no new peaks corresponding to degradation products were detected in the chromatograms, the reduced extractability was attributed to radiation-induced solid-state molecular reorganization, consistent with the Raman and SEM findings. Furthermore, theoretical evaluations of the experimental findings were performed using global reactivity descriptors, charge distributions, and local reactivity regions obtained via optimized geometries, MEP mapping, and Fukui functions, respectively. Title: Mixture formation and combustion characteristics in a heavy-duty hydrogen DI Engine: Impact of tumble and injector configuration
Abstract: This study investigates improving in-cylinder fuel mixing and combustion stability in a hydrogen-fueled direct-injected heavy-duty optical engine with flat-deck cylinder head by changing the injector outflow geometry and using tumble plates to alter in-cylinder flow. The test matrix included two injector outflow boundaries defined by injector protrusion. For each of these, three levels of tumble were tested while varying the start of injection timing. Title: A damage model for full-stage mechanical behavior of rocks and application to excavation response analysis of deep-buried tunnels
Abstract: A full-stage damage model for rock is proposed by accounting for the intermediate principal stress, strain-rate effects, and nonlinear deformation characteristics. Three independent characteristic strength surfaces corresponding to the initial, peak, and residual states constrain damage initiation, peak load-bearing capacity, and residual load-bearing capacity, respectively. Stress-state-dependent deformability and damage-induced stiffness degradation are incorporated into a unified stress–strain relation, allowing continuous representation of rock behavior from the undamaged state through strain hardening and strain softening to the residual state. The model is further applied to excavation analysis of a deep-buried circular tunnel, and a finite-difference iterative semi-analytical solution is developed. At each radial node, the initial, peak, and residual characteristic deviatoric stresses, damage variable, and stress state are determined iteratively, maintaining consistency between damage evolution and stress updating and avoiding stress oscillations in the strain-hardening zone caused by explicitly lagged updating. Results show that the extent of the excavation damaged zone alone is insufficient to characterize damage severity in surrounding rock; the internal state composition and transition process must also be considered. Increasing the support pressure ratio reduces tunnel-wall unloading, the extent of the excavation damaged zone, and convergence deformation, while progressively shifting the dominant internal state from the residual and strain-softening states toward the strain-hardening state. Increasing the initial in-situ stress enlarges the excavation damaged zone, increases tunnel-wall displacement, and promotes the development of the strain-softening and residual zones. The results advance understanding of excavation-induced damage evolution in deep-buried tunnels. © 2026

Title: Robust reversible image watermarking based on the zeros distribution of orthogonal moments
Abstract: Robust reversible watermarking (RRW) has emerged as a promising technique for sensitive applications such as medical imaging and judicial forensics, as it enables reliable watermark extraction against complex attacks while guaranteeing perfect image recovery in attack-free environments. However, balancing robustness and visual imperceptibility in current RRW schemes remains a key challenge. Specifically, Jacobi-Fourier moments (JFM) and fractional-order Jacobi-Fourier moments (FJFM) are employed as carriers, and an attack-driven zeros distribution strategy is integrated with dynamic error compensation. The radial zeros distribution of the kernel functions is optimized within a unified parameter space to select robust moment carriers for different images. Dynamic error compensation is then introduced to mitigate computation errors of JFM/FJFM on discrete images, reducing the reversible information required for subsequent embedding and improving the visual quality of the final watermarked image. Finally, residual distortion caused by robust embedding is encoded as binary reversible information and embedded into the robust watermarked image for lossless recovery. Experiments show that the proposed scheme maintains a low reversible information payload while achieving strong robustness against noise, compression, filtering, and geometric deformation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Dynamics of hydrocarbon fuel coke particle deposition in curved channels: from discrete particle migration to macroscopic prediction of coking characteristics

Title: Analysis of a fully discrete EAVF method for the conservative Allen-Cahn equation

Abstract: In this paper, we develop and analyze a fully discrete exponential average vector field (EAVF) method for the conservative Allen-Cahn equation with nonlocal constraints. Starting from the stabilized equivalent formulation of the model, we derive the fully discrete EAVF scheme by adopting the EAVF integrator for temporal discretization and the central finite difference method for spatial discretization. Rigorous theoretical analysis demonstrates that this iterative algorithm unconditionally preserves the MBP and converges under certain time-step constraints, which ensures that the proposed EAVF method admits a unique MBP-preserving numerical solution. Title: Investigation of the wave propagation response of FG porous nanobeams under longitudinal magnetic field
Abstract: This study investigates the wave propagation characteristics of functionally graded porous nanobeams subjected to a longitudinal magnetic field within the framework of nonlocal strain gradient theory. Effect of longitudinal magnetic field is incorporated into formulation through Maxwell's equations and the resulting Lorentz force. Governing equations of motion are derived using Hamilton's principle together with nonlocal strain gradient constitutive relations. Subsequently, harmonic wave solutions are introduced to obtain dispersion relations and phase velocities associated with longitudinal, shear, and bending wave branches. Wave propagation characteristics are systematically investigated by varying the nonlocal and strain gradient parameters, magnetic field intensity, porosity volume fraction, power-law index, and adopted beam formulation. Title: Experimental investigation of a novel hydrogen nanobubble water injection in a hydrogen direct-injection spark-ignition engine
Abstract: Hydrogen offers a credible route to zero-carbon combustion in internal combustion engines and can deliver high thermal efficiency, but its physical and combustion properties create persistent challenges in fuel delivery, storage, and NOx control. This work reports experiments on a boosted single-cylinder spark-ignition engine running on hydrogen direct injection (DI) as the primary fuel, with intake-port water injection used as a NOx mitigation strategy and further enriched with hydrogen-charged nanobubbles. Relative to conventional water, nanobubble water raised indicated thermal efficiency by about 4% and torque by about 5%. Title: Doping-induced redox-vacancy-bands engineering in ceria electrolytes for proton-assisted ceramic fuel cells
Abstract: Efficient charge transport in ceria at lower temperatures depends on controlling defects, redox reactions, and interfaces. In this work, Mg-Pr co-doping (10% Pr-Mg-CeO2 (Ce0.80Mg0.10Pr0.10O2-δ; PMCO-10)) modifies the transport behavior of ceria through combined oxygen-vacancy formation, engineered energy bands, and redox effects. Moreover, the optimized composition (PMCO-10) shows a reduced band gap of 2.38 eV and a shift in the band-edge positions illustrated by energy-band alignment, making oxygen-vacancy related states more accessible. As a result, the PMCO-10 electrolyte-based cell delivers a peak power density of 993 mW cm−2 and ionic conductivity of ∼ 0.179 S cm−1 at 550 °C. Interestingly, the PMCO-10 shows dominant proton conductivity of 0.156 S cm−1. Further, time-dependent distribution of relaxation times (DRT) analysis shows faster transport processes, especially those involving protons, and reduced bulk and grain boundary resistances under hydrogen conditions. Title: Molecular structure model construction and quantum chemical calculations for weakly caking coal: a case study of Huangling coal in Shaanxi, China
Abstract: The characteristics of coal organic macromolecular structures affect the physicochemical properties and reaction behavior of coal. To clarify the molecular structural characteristics of weakly caking coal from Huangling (HL) and construct its molecular structure model, this study employed coal quality analysis, ultimate analysis, scanning electron microscopy-energy-dispersive spectroscopy (SEM-EDS), solid-state 13C nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (13C NMR), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and X-ray diffraction (XRD), combined with molecular dynamics and quantum chemical calculations to investigate its physicochemical properties. The results showed that HL coal was characterized by low ash, low sulfur, high oxygen content, and weak caking properties, with relatively well-developed surface micropores and fractures. The aromatic ring carbon content was 57.31%, the ratio of aromatic bridgehead carbon to peripheral carbon (XBP) was 0.178, and the average methylene chain length was 2.15. The molecular formula of the average molecular structure model was C158H124O38N2. Quantum chemical calculations showed that the electronic structure and molecular electrostatic potential (MEP) distribution of HL coal molecules exhibited pronounced heterogeneity. The reactive sites were mainly concentrated in oxygen-containing functional groups and their adjacent regions, aliphatic CH2, cycloalkane C–H structures, and aromatic edge bridging regions. The results can provide a theoretical basis at the molecular scale for understanding the structural characteristics and low-temperature oxidation reactivity of HL coal. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Activating cellulose with filtrate from washing active carbon of previous round of activation for maximizing utilization efficiency of activators and minimizing liquid waste
Abstract: Activation of biomass with K2C2O4 or KOH requires post-treatment of resulting activated carbon (AC) via acid (i.e. HCl) pickling to leach potassium derivatives (i.e. K2CO3 and K2O) in form of KCl, which generates liquid waste. Water washing offers an alternative route to recover K2CO3 and K2O, which can serve as activators in second-round activation, maximizing utilization efficiency of activator while minimizing formation of liquid waste. Such a hypothesis was verified herein by conducting activation of cellulose with K2C2O4 or KOH, recovering potassium derivatives in filtrate via water washing and performing second-round activation of cellulose with the filtrate. The results showed that recycled K2CO3 exhibited higher capability than K2C2O4 for generating pores, forming AC with comparable specific surfacer area (1094.9 versus 1057.9 m2/g from K2C2O4 activation), larger pore diameters (2.2 versus 1.9 nm) and special hollow honeycomblike surface structure. This was attributed to superior activity of the recycled K2CO3 for gasification/cracking reactions. The recycled K2CO3 from first-round KOH activation delivered AC with improved pore development (1168.8 m2/g) compared with AC directly prepared by fresh KOH activation (729.1 m2/g). Inserting K into the carbon skeleton structures during activation with KOH blocked partially pores of resulting AC, while the activation with recycled K2CO3 did not. The life cycle assessment showed that the use of filtrate via water washing of AC for next-round activation could effectively diminish environmental impact. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Mechanism of spontaneous ignition of high-pressure hydrogen release in arc-shaped confined space
Abstract: High-pressure hydrogen storage is one of the mainstream ways of hydrogen storage currently. However, its propensity for spontaneous ignition can pose challenges to the safe application of hydrogen energy. It has been recognized that the spontaneous ignition usually takes place when it is released through tubes. However, this study demonstrates that the spontaneous ignition can still take place when it is released directly into the atmosphere and impinges on an arc-shaped wall afterwards. This paper presents a numerical investigation by using LES, RNG, EDC models and detailed hydrogen/air combustion mechanisms. The evolution of the shock wave/vortex and the flame induced by the spontaneous ignition are clearly captured and interpreted. A new mechanism of spontaneous ignition is proposed: the spontaneous ignition induced by the shock wave after the reflection of under-expanded shock by the confined walls. The effect of release pressure (30–70 MPa) and wall distance (100–300 mm) are considered. It is found that higher release pressure promotes earlier ignition and larger flame areas. Shorter wall distances accelerate flame development, but excessive shortening would lead to local flame quenching. The proposed mechanism offers a new perspective for the hydrogen combustion community. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Han X.; Liu Y.; Shang J.; Bai Y.; Wang Y.; Zhang Q.
Title: Reliability-aware feedback learning for scribble-supervised 3D multi-organ segmentation
Abstract: Sparse scribbles significantly reduce annotation costs for 3D multi-organ segmentation but often result in unstable feature learning and poor performance in unlabeled regions due to severe under-supervision. These unreliable regions reveal limitations in discriminative representation learning and remain a key obstacle to reliable segmentation. Therefore, we propose a reliability-aware feedback learning framework. Unlike existing methods that rely only on uncertainty estimation or pseudo-label refinement, it explicitly models feature-space reliability and uses reliability-based feedback conditions, enabling more stable representation learning in unreliable regions. Specifically, (1) we represent each class as a multivariate Gaussian in the embedding space and measure sample-to-class discrepancy using Mahalanobis distance. With triplet loss promoting intra-class compactness and inter-class separability, the resulting distance maps provide a reliability estimate. (2) A feature-perturbed decoder produces complementary predictions, which are fused via distance-based reliability masks to generate robust pseudo-labels. (3) The resulting low-reliability discrepancy map, together with the pseudo-labels, is fed back as an additional conditioning signal to focus learning on hard regions. Extensive experiments on two public 3D multi-organ benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over existing advanced methods in accuracy, cross-dataset generalization, and noise robustness. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Intelligent photoelectric dry separation for low-rank coal upgrading
Abstract: Air dense medium fluidized bed (ADMFB) dry separation represents a key technology for achieving the clean and efficient utilization of coal resources. However, it still faces critical technical bottlenecks, including the difficulty of online identification of mismatched materials and the lagging regulation of separation parameters. In this study, an intelligent separation control strategy integrating an improved YOLOv13 model with Model Predictive Control (MPC) is proposed, and a closed-loop control framework of “visual perception–feature quantification–MPC decision–parameter execution” is established. A dual-channel image dataset of dry separation products, termed ADMFB-G3K , was constructed, covering separation conditions under six representative combinations of operating parameters. An improved target detection algorithm, SCU-YOLOv13, was developed by integrating a Lightweight Multi-Head Self-Attention module (LMHSA), a Multi-Scale Convolution–Attention Fusion module (MSCAF), and an Adaptive Intersection-over-Union loss function (AIoU). The LMHSA module reduced computational complexity by 68 % while improving recall by 3.5 %; the MSCAF module increased mAP@0.5 by 5.5 %; and the AIoU loss reduced bounding-box localization error by 40.2 %. Through the synergistic effect of the three modules, the model achieved a precision of 93.4 %, a recall of 92.5 %, and an mAP@0.5 of 97.8 %. Furthermore, an intelligent regulation system based on Model Predictive Control was established, in which the MPC controller was designed with a prediction horizon of Np = 20 and a control horizon of Nc = 10 . Experimental results demonstrate that MPC regulation increased the clean-coal yield by 1.79 %, reduced the ash content of clean coal to 9.97 %, and increased the ash content of tailings to 59.64 %. Title: Wear evolution and nonlinear dynamics of gear system with rough surface interactions in mixed EHL
Abstract: The wear evolution of tooth surface asperities under mixed elastohydrodynamic lubrication (EHL) significantly alters surface topography and contact states, thereby affecting the dynamic response of gear system. To investigate the effects of wear evolution on rough tooth flanks and system dynamics, this study integrates fractal theory and EHL theory to construct a time-varying mesh stiffness (TVMS) model that couples asperity contact stiffness with oil film stiffness. Subsequently, a modified Archard wear model and power spectral density (PSD) analysis are introduced to predict the evolution of tooth surface wear depth across meshing cycles and the corresponding fractal parameters at different evolution stages. Furthermore, an 8-degree-of-freedom dynamic model of a spur gear system is established, incorporating motor and load inertia as well as modified mesh stiffness and wear induced dynamic backlash, to investigate the evolution of the system's dynamic response during the wear process. The results indicate that increased surface roughness significantly elevates flash temperature and wear rate. As wear cycles accumulate, the synchronous degradation of solid and fluid contact stiffness causes a reduction in mesh stiffness amplitude accompanied by intensified fluctuations. Additionally, the deterioration of tooth surface morphology amplifies load-sharing fluctuations in the double-tooth contact zone, inducing an earlier occurrence of system bifurcation points and a significant increase in the dynamic transmission error. Title: Sulfur-doped graphitic carbon nitride/cerium tungstate nanocomposites for ultrasensitive dopamine sensing in mouse striatal tissue
Abstract: Following the COVID-19 pandemic, the demand for rapid diagnostic tools for the highly specific and sensitive detection of disease-related biomarkers has increased significantly. Title: Ag NPs@MXene-mediated electrochemical-SERS dual-mode microfluidic array for multiplexed breast cancer-associated miRNAs detection
Abstract: Breast cancer-associated miRNAs are promising liquid-biopsy biomarkers, but their low serum abundance, short sequences and matrix interference hinder sensitive and multiplexed detection. Authors: Lv X.; Jiao X.; Du C.; Zhang S.; Huang Y.
Title: Lignin for hydrogen production: A comprehensive review of technologies, catalysts, and future perspectives
Abstract: Lignin, the second most abundant natural aromatic polymer, remains a promising yet severely underutilized feedstock for sustainable green hydrogen production. As a low‑cost industrial byproduct generated at hundreds of millions of tons annually, lignin contains a hydrogen content of approximately 5–6 wt% and abundant reactive functional groups, enabling the co‑production of high‑purity hydrogen and value‑added aromatic compounds. This review provides a critical, systematic overview of state‑of‑the‑art lignin‑to‑hydrogen technologies, including electrochemical, photoelectrochemical, thermochemical, endogenous hydrogen, photocatalytic, and biological routes. Emphasis is placed on reaction mechanisms, catalyst design principles, performance benchmarks, and cross‑technology comparisons. Key challenges hindering industrial translation are rigorously analyzed, including feedstock heterogeneity, catalyst durability and cost, energy efficiency, product separation, and scalability. Among all pathways, photoelectrochemical coupling, supercritical water gasification, and methoxy‑directed endogenous hydrogen production are identified as the most promising, owing to their balanced energy utilization, feedstock compatibility, and economic potential. Future research priorities are proposed to advance lignin valorization toward industrial‑scale green hydrogen applications, focusing on non‑precious bifunctional catalysts, green pretreatment, and integrated biorefinery systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Enhancing hydrothermal stability of polysulfone-based solid acids via electronic effects for cellulose saccharification
Abstract: The hydrothermal instability of –SO3H groups severely limits the application of sulfonic acid-functionalized solid acids in biomass conversion. With bisphenol A polysulfone (PSU) employed as the precursor, the abundant aromatic rings of PSU were “knitted” into a robust three-dimensional porous network via Friedel–Crafts hypercrosslinking, and a series of polysulfone-based solid acid catalysts (PSU-HCSAs) were subsequently obtained through sulfonation. The catalysts were characterized by XRD, FT-IR, BET, SEM, XPS, TG-MS, and acid–base titration, and the electronic modulation mechanism was elucidated by DFT calculations. The catalytic performance was evaluated in microcrystalline cellulose hydrolysis. A glucose yield of 76.5 mol% was achieved over the optimal catalyst, with approximately 85 % of the initial activity retained after five hydrothermal cycles, significantly outperforming the control sample and the catalysts reported in the literature. Notably, two distinct –SO3H species with different thermal stabilities were identified and quantified within the same catalyst for the first time, whereby the decisive role of the local electronic environment of –SO3H groups in their stability was revealed. Title: Elucidating the mechanism of catalytic cracking reactions by integrating microscopic and macroscopic research methods: a combined analysis of radical formation and thermogravimetric kinetic data

CaAl selectively activates C–O bonds to yield oxygen radicals for heteroatom removal yet triggers aromatic polymerization side reactions. mixed catalysts deliver combinatorial effect: they reduce cracking temperatures and activation energy, coordinating bond cleavage, radical generation and small-molecule release. This framework integrates microscopic bond breaking, free radical behavior, and macroscopic thermal responses, demonstrating that the kinetic differences stem from free radical transformations. Title: Frequency-dependent damping behavior of AB-stacked multilayer graphene: A molecular dynamics investigation
Abstract: Graphene-based nanostructures are increasingly employed in nanoelectromechanical systems, resonators, sensors, and advanced nanocomposites, where vibration damping strongly influences dynamic performance and reliability. Although the damping behavior of monolayer graphene has been extensively investigated, the influence of graphene layer number on energy dissipation remains insufficiently understood. In this study, molecular dynamics simulations are performed to investigate the frequency-dependent damping behavior of AB-stacked graphene nanoplates containing one to five graphene layers subjected to localized out-of-plane harmonic excitation. A prescribed sinusoidal displacement is applied to the central region of the upper graphene layer, while the corresponding vertical reaction force is monitored throughout the excitation cycle. The equivalent damping ratio is determined from the phase lag between the imposed displacement and reaction force using a cross-correlation approach. The influence of excitation frequency, ranging from 1 GHz to 1 THz, is systematically examined for a displacement amplitude of 5 Å. The results demonstrate that excitation frequency dominates the damping response, whereas increasing the number of graphene layers substantially modifies the energy dissipation mechanism through interlayer mechanical coupling. At low frequencies, the equivalent damping ratio increases moderately with layer number, whereas at higher frequencies multilayer graphene exhibits lower damping ratios despite developing larger reaction forces and stronger through-thickness load transfer. Title: Direct injection and automated pressurized extraction coupled to high-resolution mass spectrometry for the quantification of organophosphate flame retardants in water, soil and dust

Title: DDENet: Dual-Domain Enhancement Network for low-light light field
Abstract: Low-light enhancement for light field (LF) images is challenging due to the difficulty in leveraging cross-view information under noisy conditions and the inherent coupling between illumination recovery and noise suppression. First, existing methods suffer from angular inconsistency, where noise disrupts the geometric structure, hindering effective utilization of angular correlations. Second, the coupled nature of brightness enhancement and denoising makes it difficult to exploit LF-specific geometric cues without introducing artifacts. To address these issues, we propose a dual-domain enhancement strategy. Motivated by the need for decoupled processing, we utilize the wavelet domain to substantially separate illumination from noise and compress disparities, enabling noise-robust, angularly-consistent brightness recovery. Subsequently, we employ the pixel domain to independently reduce noise and refine details, exploiting the rich spatial locality and epipolar geometry information. Based on this strategy, we develop a Dual-Domain Enhancement Network (DDENet), featuring a Wavelet-Domain Illumination Enhancement (WDIE) module and a Pixel-Domain Detail Enhancement (PDDE) module. Title: A fast construction method for ellipsoid model-based interval fields with stationary characteristics and applications

By combining the multivariate spline and convolution-based kernel method and stationary characteristics, the large-scale constrained optimization problem originally required to be solved for ellipsoid model-based stationary interval fields construction is transformed into a small-scale unconstrained optimization problem, which achieves efficient construction of ellipsoid model-based stationary interval fields with limited samples. Title: Reproducing and benchmarking behavioral similarity methods for business process models

Title: Life cycle analysis and multi-objective optimization of CCUS-integrated methanol reforming PEMFC-CCHP systems
Abstract: Distributed methanol steam reforming (MSR)-proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) systems have attracted attention due to their high efficiency, flexibility, and cost-effectiveness. Title: An ab initio kinetic study on competitive pathways in H-abstraction reactions from γ-valerolactone
Abstract: γ-Valerolactone (GVL) has been regarded as a promising oxygenated biofuel and fuel additive, as it shows high energy density and can achieve more complete combustion compared to conventional hydrocarbon fuels. However, as a cyclic methyl ester, its unique molecular structure makes the combustion chemistry more complex than that of small linear esters, which remains still not fully understood. In this work, the potential energy surfaces of H-atom abstraction from GVL by H, CH3, C2H5, O, OH, CH3O, O2, HO2, and CH3OO were systematically investigated using high-level ab initio calculations, while the temperature-dependent rate coefficients were calculated using conventional transition state theory or RRKM theory over 500–2500 K. For a specific H-abstraction site, the barrier heights follow the order of OH < O ≈ CH3O < H < CH3 ≈ C2H5 < CH3OO ≈ HO2 < O2. For a given abstractor, the barrier heights generally increase in the order of Cγ < Cα < Cβ < Cmethyl, identifying the tertiary Cγ site as the most reactive abstraction site. OH-initiated abstraction exhibits the highest rate coefficients at low and intermediate temperatures due to its very low barriers, including a submerged barrier for the Cγ channel. However, its total rate coefficient shows relatively weak temperature dependence, whereas the reactions initiated by O and H atoms increase more rapidly with temperature. Consequently, the total rate coefficients by O atom and H atom exceed that by OH radical when the temperature increases beyond 1200 K and 1800 K, respectively. H-abstraction reactions by O2 remain the slowest pathway throughout the investigated temperature range, because of its exceptionally high barriers. These newly calculated rate coefficients are observed to improve the prediction performance of GVL kinetic model in literature, which better reproduces the mole fractions of methane and 1-butene during GVL pyrolysis in a plug flow reactor. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A comprehensive review of liquid bio-oil upgrading in batch vs. flow reactors
Abstract: Catalytic hydroprocessing is a key strategy for upgrading fast pyrolysis bio-oils into renewable fuels and value-added chemicals. While previous reviews have primarily focused on catalyst development and hydrodeoxygenation mechanisms, the influence of reactor configuration on process performance, catalyst stability, kinetics, and scalability has received less systematic attention. This review critically compares batch and continuous-flow hydroprocessing of model compounds, bio-oil fractions, and whole bio-oils, with emphasis on reaction mechanisms, product distribution, kinetic modeling, catalyst deactivation, and techno-economic considerations. The analysis shows that batch reactors are well suited for catalyst screening, mechanistic studies, and intrinsic kinetic investigations owing to their operational flexibility, whereas continuous-flow reactors better represent industrial operation by enabling steady-state processing and long-term catalyst performance evaluation. However, direct comparison between reactor configurations remains challenging because differences in conversion, selectivity, and catalyst stability are often affected by catalyst properties, feedstock composition, and operating conditions rather than reactor design alone. The review identifies key knowledge gaps, including the lack of standardized protocols for reactor comparison, limited studies under comparable experimental conditions, and insufficient long-term catalyst stability data. By critically assessing the advantages and limitations of both reactor types, this review provides guidance for selecting appropriate reactor configurations and outlines priorities for future research and industrial bio-oil upgrading. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: How structure shapes function in mushroom-derived β-glucans: Implications for gastrointestinal functionality, gut microbiota modulation, and immunomodulation

Title: An efficient numerical approximation for spatial fractional viscous Cahn-Hilliard equation
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: This paper presents an efficient numerical approximation for the spatial fractional viscous Cahn-Hilliard equation with the Ginzburg-Landau polynomial potential. A numerical scheme is established based on the stabilized Crank-Nicolson scheme in time and the pseudo-spectral method in space. Theoretically, we rigorously prove the mass conservation and energy dissipation in the fully-discrete sense. The bound of the numerical solution under the H1 norm is a direct conclusion of the unconditional energy stability. Making use of the boundedness and the Sobolev embedding theorem, we provide the convergence analysis and derive the optimal error estimate. Several numerical experiments are carried out to testify the theoretical results and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Lie symmetry classification and exact solutions of a diffusive Lotka–Volterra system with convection
Abstract: A mathematical model for description of the viscous fingering induced by a chemical reaction is under study. This complicated six-component model is reduced to a three-component diffusive Lotka–Volterra system with convection by introducing a stream function. The system obtained is examined by the classical Lie method. A complete Lie symmetry classification is derived via a rigorous algorithm. In particular, it is proved that the widest Lie algebras of invariance occur when the stream function generate a linear velocity field. The most interesting cases (from the symmetry and applicability point of view) are further studied in order to derive exact solutions. A wide range of exact solutions are constructed for radially-symmetric stream functions. These solutions include time-dependent and radially-symmetric solutions as well as more complicated solutions expressed in terms of the Weierstrass function. It was shown that some of exact solutions can be used for demonstration of spatiotemporal evolution of concentrations corresponding to two reactants and their product. © The Author(s) under exclusive licence to Sociedade Brasileira de Matemática Aplicada e Computacional 2026.

Title: Hybrid MPI/OpenMP parallel implementation for simulating the water-exit and ice-breaking process of a ventilated underwater vehicle
Abstract: Large-scale numerical simulation of the ice-breaking and water exit process of underwater vehicles requires substantial computational resources due to the strong coupling among multiphase flow, vehicle motion, and ice fracture. The parallel performance is evaluated over a wide range of process and thread configurations. Title: Electrospray preparation of Fe-PMMA films for one-drop analysis of thiocyanate a tobacco biomarker as a case study

Title: Semi-Asynchronous Efficient Hierarchical Federated Learning for heterogeneous resources
Abstract: With the rapid proliferation of cloud–edge–device collaborative computing, Hierarchical Federated Learning (HFL) has become a promising paradigm for large-scale distributed model training. Title: Mild continuous-flow methanol extraction coupled with formic acid assisted catalytic hydrogenolysis of corn stover
Abstract: Fractionation of lignocellulosic biomass is important for efficient utilization of both lignin and carbohydrates. Conventional one-pot reductive catalytic fractionation (RCF) can effectively depolymerize lignin, but challenges remain in balancing lignin monomer yield, carbohydrate retention, and external H2 demand, as well as in separating the heterogeneous catalyst from carbohydrate-rich solids. Herein, a decoupled route for corn stover valorization was developed. Mild continuous-flow methanol extraction was first used to obtain lignin fragments while preserving the carbohydrate-rich solids. The extracted lignin fragments were subsequently subjected to formic-acid-assisted catalytic hydrogenolysis to produce lignin monomers. The extraction conditions were optimized to balance lignin-fragment recovery and carbohydrate preservation. Subsequently, the extracted lignin fragments were hydrogenolyzed under H2 and H2-free atmosphere. Under optimal extraction conditions, yield of lignin fragments reaches 17.3 ± 0.5 wt%, while the carbohydrate retention remains above 95%. The lignin fragments can preserve a part of chemical structures in raw lignin, while carbohydrate-rich solids retain cellulose I. In the subsequent hydrogenolysis step, the addition of 10% formic acid gives a lignin monomer yield of 21.0 wt% without external H2. Compared with one-pot RCF, the decoupled route reduces the monomer yield by 8.1 percentage points, but makes carbohydrate retention increase from 24.1% to over 95%. The work could provide a competitive process-design option for high-efficiency utilization of lignocellulosic biomass. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Low-temperature deposition and wide-temperature tribological performance of Ti-interlayered DLC films on PEEK
Abstract: Carbon films are one of the most effective approaches for improving the tribological performance of PEEK. Meanwhile, systematic studies on the tribological behavior of carbon films modified PEEK has yet to be systematically investigated. In this study, a Ti-interlayered DLC composite coating was deposited on PEEK substrates at an ultra-low temperature (60 °C) using a custom-designed hybrid MS and PECVD system. The tribological performance of the coated PEEK was systematically evaluated under a constant load across a wide temperature range. Compared with unmodified PEEK, the Ti/DLC-coated PEEK exhibits an approximately 80% reduction in friction coefficient and a 27.6% decrease in wear rate under 5.0 N. At 200 °C, these improvements reach 86% and 95%. The combined MS/PECVD technique is thus established as a viable low-temperature route for PEEK surface modification, with the Ti interlayer playing a critical role in adhesion and service life enhancement of hard coatings on flexible substrates. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Recent advances in hybrid power systems for engineering vehicles
Abstract: In the face of energy scarcity and worsening air pollution, energy-intensive engineering vehicles demand rapid efficiency gains and emission reductions. Title: MPA-Net: An enhanced feature aggregation with Pixel-Shuffle for non-cooperative low-altitude small object detection

Title: A comparative kinetic investigation of ethyl acetate and n-propyl acetate as ester-based electrolyte solvents: Integrating quantum chemical calculations with kinetic modeling
Abstract: Ethyl acetate (EA) and n -propyl acetate (PA) are promising electrolyte solvents for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) owing to their low melting points and reduced viscosity. Understanding their chemical kinetics is essential for assessing fire and explosion hazards during thermal runaway (TR). By combining quantum chemical calculations and kinetic modeling, this work compares the pyrolysis, oxidation, ignition, and laminar flame propagation characteristics of EA and PA under TR-relevant conditions. Quantum chemical calculations were performed to characterize the unimolecular decomposition pathways of PA. A high-temperature kinetic model for EA and PA was constructed based on the calculated rate constants and validated against available experimental data. Kinetic analyses were performed to identify radical-driven pathways and reaction channel competition between EA and PA across various regimes. Simulations reveal that EA and PA exhibit similar three-stage pyrolysis behaviors, with fuel consumption dominated by the six-center intramolecular elimination channel. Under oxidation conditions, PA shows marginally higher intrinsic reactivity during initial fuel decomposition, whereas EA exhibits earlier radical buildup, leading to faster consumption of primary products. Consistent trends are observed in ignition delay and flame propagation. EA displays shorter ignition delay times than PA owing to stronger pre-ignition heat release and enhanced radical generation, while its higher laminar burning velocities stem from a more reactive radical pool. Title: Oxidation reaction-mass transfer coupling and compositional evolution during thermal air flooding in light oil reservoirs

Title: MOF-derived partially hydrated P’2-type layered oxide with enlarged interlayer spacing as a high-performance cathode for sodium-ion batteries

Title: Co-firing of upgraded biomass towards flexible CO2 reduction for coal-fired power plants in China

Authors: Lin J.; Wen J.; Wan W.; Liu M.
Title: Pose2Point: Bridging human poses and point clouds for unified action recognition
Abstract: Pose and point cloud representations are inherently complementary for human action recognition: pose provides compact structural priors, while point clouds offer flexible geometric modeling. Although multimodal approaches attempt to combine these advantages, existing dual-input architectures often suffer from a strong reliance on paired data and complex cross-modal alignment. To address these issues, we propose the Pose2Point (P2P) framework, which reformulates pose sequences into a Pose Point Cloud (PPC) representation. By achieving data-level unification at the source, P2P deeply integrates pose structural priors with point cloud geometric flexibility within a single-modality paradigm. The framework introduces a Transfer2PointCloud module to convert pose sequences into point clouds encoding 3D spatial coordinates and spatiotemporal topology, enabling the joint preservation of pose semantics and motion dynamics. By selecting points based on joint distribution, the proposed Uniform Mixed Sampling (UMS) strategy circumvents the structural and temporal destruction inherent in standard downsampling, ensuring the preservation of pose topology and motion continuity. On the resulting PPCs, hierarchical neighborhood aggregation is employed to capture fine-grained local interactions and high-level action semantics. In addition, a Multi-CLS loss and PPC-Specific Training Strategy strategies are incorporated to enhance optimization and robustness. Extensive experiments on NTU RGB+D, NTU RGB+D 120, and NW-UCLA demonstrate that Pose2Point achieves state-of-the-art performance, validating the effectiveness of the proposed unified point cloud representation for pose-based action recognition. Authors: Peng Y.; Hao F.
Title: An electro-chemo-mechanical coupling model in the Eulerian description for contact behaviors of electrodes in lithium-ion batteries
Abstract: The electrochemical performance of batteries is critically influenced by evolving interparticle contact in composite electrodes. While significant contact stresses trigger structural degradation and capacity fading, the reestablishment of electrical contact between active particles facilitates capacity recovery. Herein, an electro-chemo-mechanical coupling model in the Eulerian description is developed to investigate the effects of contact behaviors on the electro-chemo-mechanical responses in electrodes. The proposed model simultaneously describes mechanical and electrical contact among active particles, and the Eulerian description accommodates the associated geometrical changes. Crucially, the model reproduces the capacity recovery phenomenon. The results show that significant contact stress suppresses lithium accumulation in the contact region. It is found that the electrically isolated particle is activated due to interparticle contact. At the early stage of contact, lithiation is transiently reversed into delithiation and then suppressed in the highly lithiated particle, whereas lithiation is promoted in the low lithiated particle. Ultimately, the two particles evolve with a uniform degree of lithiation. This concurrent lithiation of both particles contributes to an increase in the total amount of lithium intercalated, leading to capacity recovery. The proposed model provides insights into the complex interplay among interparticle contact behaviors, interfacial reaction kinetics, and electrode capacity evolution. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS

Title: Continuous hydrogenation of phenol to cyclohexanol over Co/γ-Al2O3 catalyst
Abstract: Cyclohexanol is a key intermediate for high-value chemicals, but its current production relies heavily on petroleum, driving demand for sustainable alternatives. In this work, hydrogenation of phenol to cyclohexanol was investigated in a continuous fixed-bed reactor considering temperatures (140–200 °C), hydrogen (H2) pressures (1–3 MPa), weight hourly space velocity (WHSV 0.3–0.6 h−1), and H2 to phenol molar ratio (15.7–47.2). Temperature exerted the most pronounced effect on product distribution, and elevated temperatures facilitated the further conversion of cyclohexanol to cyclohexane. H2 pressure significantly influenced product selectivity, with cyclohexanol selectivity reaching a maximum of 83.8 % at 2 MPa. WHSV minimally affected cyclohexanol selectivity, whereas increasing the H2 to phenol ratio improved apparent H2 availability and phenol conversion. At 160 °C, 2 MPa, 0.4 h−1, and H2 to phenol ratio of 31.5, 5 wt% Co/γ-Al2O3 achieved > 99 % phenol conversion, whereas 10 wt% Co/γ-Al2O3 afforded the highest cyclohexanol selectivity (91.92 %). The observed product distribution was consistent with a step‑by‑step hydrogenation pathway for phenol conversion from phenol to cyclohexanol, then to cyclohexene and finally to cyclohexane. During 120 h on stream, 5 wt% Co/γ-Al2O3 maintained 98.3 to > 99 % conversion, and 90.3–91.7 % cyclohexanol selectivity. Title: SpikeHSA: Heterogeneous Space-Aligned Spiking Hashing for cross-modal retrieval
Abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer a promising paradigm for cross-modal hashing (CMH) due to their biological plausibility and energy efficiency. However, sparse spike-driven representations can limit semantic encoding, while conventional single-space alignment is insufficient to capture complementary fine-grained cross-modal semantics. To address these issues, we propose SpikeHSA, a Heterogeneous Space-Aligned Spiking Hashing framework for Cross-Modal Retrieval. Inspired by neuronal threshold diversity, SpikeHSA introduces the Heterogeneous Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (H-LIF) neuron, which assigns dimension-specific thresholds to diversify spiking responses and improve the information density of spike-based representations. We further develop a Heterogeneous Space Alignment (HSA) strategy that projects image, text, and fused multimodal representations into multiple heterogeneous spaces and aligns each unimodal representation with the fused semantic reference. Extensive experiments on three widely used benchmarks demonstrate that, with convolutional image encoders, SpikeHSA improves mAP by up to 4.6% over ANN-based baselines and 4.3% over the SNN-based method, while requiring as little as approximately one-eighth of the estimated inference energy of non-spiking baselines Code will be available at https://github.com/whisper233/SpikeHSA. © 2026

Authors: Yang W.; Liu Z.
Title: GeoPHiT: A physics-informed hierarchical discrete transformer for multi-scale geological sequence prediction
Abstract: Geological sequence prediction in industrial drilling is a heterogeneous information fusion problem, because gamma ray, resistivity, porosity, and density logs jointly describe subsurface states across multiple depth scales while obeying approximate petrophysical relations. Existing deep models improve temporal modeling but generally fuse channels without a petrophysical residual on decoded outputs. This paper presents GeoPHiT, a physics-informed hierarchical discrete Transformer for multi-scale geological sequence prediction. GeoPHiT maps each five-log local depth block to one depth-indexed discrete token, regularizes decoded Stage-1 reconstructions, and forecasts coarse-to-fine token transitions. Experiments on the Volve, Tarim Basin, and FORCE 2020 Carbonate datasets show 20-run mean RMSE reductions of 4.0–5.4% relative to HDT and 8.7–9.9% relative to PINNsformer. On Volve, all paired RMSE and GCI comparisons remain significant after Holm correction ( p Holm ≤ 0.001701). The loss-external GR–NPHI-derived porosity-proxy check also favors GeoPHiT, whereas MRPR and CVR remain diagnostics of agreement with the in-loss Archie proxy. Title: Experimental and chemical kinetic modeling study on the ignition and flame propagation characteristics of ethanol/N2O mixture
Abstract: Ethanol(C2H5OH)/nitrous oxide (N2O) hybrid propellants show promising application prospects in the aerospace field. A detailed understanding of their autoignition and flame propagation characteristics is essential for developing reliable chemical kinetic models and ensuring the safe operation of propulsion systems. In this study, a high‑pressure shock tube is used to measure the ignition delay times (IDTs) under wide combustion conditions (i.e., temperatures 1300–1600 K, pressures 5.0/10.0/20.0 bar, equivalence ratios 0.5/1.0/2.0). The effects of temperature, pressure, and equivalence ratio on IDTs are systematically analysed. Additionally, laminar burning velocities (LBVs) are measured using a constant‑volume combustion vessel with N2 dilution ratio of 50%, at initial temperatures of 373 K and 423 K, and at initial pressures of 1.0 and 2.0 bar. Based on the C3MechV4.0 mechanism, an improved chemical kinetic model is proposed by updating the ammonia/NOx sub‑chemistry. This model demonstrates good performance in predicting the newly measured LBVs and IDTs of ethanol/N2O mixtures. Detailed flux and sensitivity analyses based on the proposed mechanism reveal that the N2O decomposition reaction (N2O (+M) = N2 + Ö (+M)) and its reaction with Ḣ atoms (N2O + Ḣ = N2 + ȮH) are the key reaction pathways governing both the ignition process and flame propagation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: NiFeSn alloy-enhanced microbial electrosynthesis for carbon dioxide conversion to butyric and caproic acids

CO2 conversion and chain elongation were substantially increased in the NiFeSn cell. Title: NH3-assisted pyrolysis-induced differentiation of nitrogen configurations and selective Na/K regulation of biomass char oxidation
Abstract: Ammonia, typically treated as a supplementary fuel in solid-fuel co-firing, has received limited investigation into its chemical interactions with the solid matrix, particularly how it regulates biomass-char structure during pyrolysis. In this study, real biomass feedstocks and model compounds (cellulose and lignin) were used to compare direct NH3 co-combustion with staged NH3-assisted pyrolysis-oxidation. Multi-feedstock screening, model-compound decoupling, and alkali-metal loading experiments reveal that staged pyrolysis-oxidation is more effective than direct co-combustion, and the promoting effect is related to the cellulose/lignin composition and the Na/K contents of the biomass feedstock. Model-compound experiments revealed that NH3-assisted pyrolysis of cellulose preferentially formed embedded graphitic nitrogen, which inhibited char oxidation, whereas lignin favored the formation of edge pyridinic and pyrrolic nitrogen, shifting the main mass-loss peak from 763.6 °C to 364.7 °C. Mayer bond-order and interaction region indicator (IRI) analyses showed that Na decreased the relevant bond orders in edge pyridinic and pyrrolic nitrogen structures but increased oxygen-related bond orders at graphitic-nitrogen sites. Title: Assessing the techno-economic performance of membrane-based carbon capture and storage in South African coal-fired power plants
Abstract: South Africa relies heavily on coal for electricity generation, making its power sector a major contributor to carbon dioxide emissions. Carbon capture and storage (CCS) technologies have been proposed as pathways to mitigate carbon dioxide emissions and environmental impacts. This study presents a techno-economic evaluation of a membrane-based carbon dioxide capture system tailored for a South African coal-fired power plant. This study presents a techno-economic evaluation of a membrane-based carbon dioxide capture from a South African coal-fired power plant. The work involves firstly simulating a supercritical coal power plant with a capacity to produce a gross power of 804 MW. Coal characteristics and local ambient conditions in a specified region of South Africa are considered. The resulting flue gas composition and state are determined from the simulation. In a second stage, a membrane system is proposed for carbon capture from the power plant flue gas. To optimise the process, a superstructure-based model is applied. The capture efficiency is set at 90% whilst the product stream consists of 95% carbon dioxide. The cost of the membrane process, transport and storage and ultimately the cost of electricity, is determined. Authors: Xue H.; Xu W.; Gao W.; Shang C.; Kolditz O.; Wang J.; Zhan L.; Chen Y.
Title: Reactive transport mechanisms and homogenization for americium in rough-walled fractures
Abstract: Americium (Am) is a typical long‑lived radionuclide of major concern in deep geological disposal, whose transport behavior in fractured media is one of the critical issues in repository safety assessment. Given the lack of systematic understanding, this study develops a comprehensive framework for numerical simulation and parameter homogenization in rough‑walled fractures, integrating fracture characterization, precipitation kinetic modeling, reactive transport simulation, two‑stage homogenization and sensitivity analysis. Results show that Am precipitation in open‑flow fractures cannot reach instantaneous equilibrium, and thermodynamic equilibrium models tend to underestimate dissolved Am concentrations at the core scale; a kinetic model is therefore essential for such systems. Fracture heterogeneity and precipitation processes jointly govern Am transport, with preferential channels dominating solute breakthrough and precipitation distribution. To quantify the precipitation‑induced retardation effect, the theoretical evolution law of the equivalent retardation factor Req is derived, and an adaptive feature‑point selection strategy is proposed accordingly. The established homogenization method achieves both high accuracy and efficiency across various scenarios, and the obtained equivalent parameters can elucidate the mechanism of Am transport. Furthermore, the homogenization method shows stable performance for extrapolation across large spatiotemporal scales, and the developed stepwise upscaling strategy further markedly enhances homogenization efficiency. This study also systematically clarifies how fracture geometric characteristics, boundary conditions, chemical reactions, and transport parameters govern Am transport. © 2026

Authors: Bai D.; Huang T.
Title: ReaxFF molecular dynamics simulations of methane hydrate: from low-temperature melting through high-temperature combustion to flame extinction
Abstract: For natural gas hydrates, as a type of energy mineral deposit, combustion is undoubtedly one of the main energy utilization methods. In this paper, we have studied the total process of methane hydrate combustion from decomposition to extinction in various oxygen dosage systems by using ReaxFF molecular dynamics simulations, and also evaluated the applicability of ReaxFF for low-temperature non-reactive processes. The results indicate that ReaxFF can qualitatively provide the phase diagram of hydrate and the diffusion coefficients of each component, but it underestimates the strength of hydrogen bonding between water molecules. The combustion of the hydrate and oxygen two-phase system begins with the melting and decomposition of hydrate from the interface. After ignition, oxygen first reacts with water to generate OH∙. In the early combustion stages, keeping the system in a fuel-lean state can yield more OH∙; and in the subsequent rapid combustion stage, reducing the oxygen dosage can enable the generated H∙ to participate in the radical activation process, both of which are beneficial for accelerating the combustion of methane. During the extinction stage, the flame goes out when the temperature drops to about 800 K. For hypothetical CH4/O2 binary hydrates without oxygen mass transfer resistance, there will be a surge in OH∙ during the early combustion stages, and oxygen will be more thoroughly consumed. Under fuel-lean conditions, methane can be oxidized to CO and CO2 by three oxidant species O2, OH∙, and HO2∙; while under fuel-rich conditions, methane can only be oxidized to CO by OH∙. The difference in initial oxygen dosage determines whether CO2 is mainly generated before or during the extinction stage, but has little effect on the final CO2 production. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: CaH2-improved CO2 methanation performance of Ni/TiO2 catalyst through adjusting oxygen vacancy and electronic structure
Abstract: Regulating the oxygen vacancy concentration and active site electronic structure by introducing additives is an effective strategy to improve catalyst activity for CO2 methanation. A series of characterizations confirmed that CaH2 promoted catalyst surface oxygen vacancy generation and modulated the Ni electronic state, thereby facilitating the adsorption and activation of H2 and CO2 on the catalyst surface. In-situ Fourier transform infrared (In-situ FT-IR) spectroscopy and density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that CO2 tends to dissociate directly into CO* and O* species at oxygen vacancies on the CaH2-modified Ni/TiO2 catalyst surface. This study highlights the critical role of metal hydrides in regulating the electronic structure and surface defects of the Ni/TiO2 catalyst. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: CFD optimization and fluid modeling of a Venturi flowmeter for downhole CO2 flow measurement
Abstract: Accurate measurement of downhole CO2 mass flow rate is essential for efficient CO2 injection in CO2 enhanced oil recovery (CO2-EOR) and carbon geological storage. This work establishes a Venturi flow measurement framework coupled with the Peng–Robinson (PR) equation of state to describe real-fluid thermodynamic behaviors. The PR-based flow inversion achieves an overall mean relative flow-rate deviation of 1.13%. Dimensionless analysis shows that the optimized Venturi maintains stable differential-pressure response within a moderate Reynolds number range, while CO2 real-fluid and compressibility effects still introduce measurable deviations at high Reynolds numbers. Title: The perceived legitimacy of costly punishment in the evolution of cooperation under private reputation
Abstract: Indirect reciprocity promotes cooperation by allowing reputation to serve as a social currency for future benefits. However, the role of costly punishment under private reputation remains less understood. Under private reputation, independent assessments may lead observers and punishers to hold different views about the same recipient. This raises the question of how an observer evaluates punishment when the punished recipient appears to have a good reputation. We introduce the perceived legitimacy of costly punishment into a private-reputation model of indirect reciprocity. We first analyze the core dynamics among unconditional cooperators, unconditional defectors, and discriminating punishers, and then test whether the cooperative state is stable against the full set of action-rule mutants, including antisocial punishers. Our results show that costly punishment promotes cooperation only when its perceived legitimacy lies within an appropriate range. In this regime, discriminating punishers and unconditional cooperators can coexist stably, producing high cooperation and social payoff. However, insufficient legitimacy prevents punishers from disciplining defectors, whereas excessive legitimacy allows strategies that punish high-reputation individuals to invade, linking the model to antisocial punishment. Finite-population Markov analyses further confirm that the main qualitative dynamics are robust to small punishment execution and assessment errors. These findings show that, under private reputation, the perceived legitimacy of costly punishment determines whether punishment sustains cooperation or facilitates antisocial punishment. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Encapsulation of gallic acid in alginate composite microgel by impinging aerosol and xerogel technique

Title: A simulation model of atomic force microscope and its guidance for scanning surfaces with multi-material properties
Abstract: A virtual platform for modeling tapping mode atomic force microscopy (TM-AFM) based on Simulink is proposed. Title: Aptamer-CRISPR/Cas as a tool in point-of-care testing of infectious diseases

Title: Effects of substrate component proportions on dark fermentative hydrogen production from food waste: performance, process parameters, and mechanistic Insights

Title: Comparative evaluation of H2O2 and peroxydisulfate (PDS) activation by Fe3O4/g-C3N4 composite under visible light for methyl orange degradation

Title: Global-local information fusion via contrastive learning and optimal transport for weakly paired H&E-to-IHC stain transfer
Abstract: Virtual staining offers a computational alternative to conventional chemical staining by synthesizing histological stains from routine microscopy images. Furthermore, a WSI-Guided Consistency (WGC) module leverages slide-level representations extracted from a pathology foundation model to align patch-wise synthesis with global tissue characteristics. By adopting a contrastive learning strategy, the WGC module preserves inter-slide distinctiveness, providing strong global context for patch-level translation. Extensive experiments on six benchmark datasets with diverse IHC staining types demonstrate that PCSC-StainNet consistently achieves superior synthesis quality and pathological consistency compared with state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: He Y.; Ding W.; Cao J.; Di X.; He J.; Xu R.; Qi H.
Title: Intrusion detection for Internet of Vehicles using Global spatio-temporal Representation with multivariate knowledge distillation
Abstract: With the rapid development of vehicle intelligence and Internet connection technology, various network attacks threaten driving safety. IoV intrusion detection has become crucial. However, previous studies have primarily relied on local spatial features and local temporal correlations of message sequences for intrusion detection, without fully considering global features. Meanwhile, IoV requires lightweight detection mechanisms due to the real-time and fast characteristics. Existing inaccurate and inefficient intrusion detection makes IoV vulnerable to undetected attacks. To extract global features for intrusion detection, this paper proposes an IoV intrusion detection method using Global spatio-temporal Representations (IoVGR), which broadens the scope of analysis using attention mechanisms and applies adaptive feature fusion to extract global representations. Furthermore, to achieve lightweight detection, this paper adopts multiple knowledge distillation (MKD), which introduces teacher assistant models and intermediate layer mapping to compress the detection model. We conduct extensive experimental evaluations on the VeReMi Extension dataset, which show that the average F1-score of multi-classification and bi-classification attack detection for IoVGR are higher than the best baseline method by 2.31% and 4.16%, respectively. The compressed IoV intrusion detection model reduces the number of parameters by 93.92% and the amount of calculation by 99.44% while ensuring accuracy. Moreover, IoVGR is executed on the UNSW-NB15 dataset and the ORACLE RF fingerprint dataset with an improved F1-score of 1.22% and 3.81%, demonstrating the universality of the model. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Li L.; Ye Y.; Chen Z.; Xia Y.
Title: Unified start, personalized end: Progressive pruning for efficient 3D medical image segmentation
Abstract: High-performance 3D medical image segmentation models are often limited in practice by their high computational and memory costs. Existing lightweight methods usually rely on static, manually specified architectures, whose capacity is fixed before training and therefore cannot adapt to the heterogeneous complexity of different anatomical targets and imaging datasets. To address this limitation, we propose PSP-Seg, a progressive pruning framework that learns task-specific network topologies during training. PSP-Seg follows a “unified start, personalized end” paradigm: it starts from a common over-parameterized backbone constructed with Parallel Redundant Modules (PRMs), and dynamically evolves into a compact topology by progressively removing task-irrelevant branches. To support stable in-training structural adaptation, we introduce a Functional Decoupling (FD) Loss that encourages complementary roles between semantic representation learning and spatial localization. We further design a reversible masked-then-prune strategy that temporarily masks candidate branches and validates their removal before permanent pruning, reducing the risk of irreversible performance degradation. Experiments on five public 3D medical image segmentation benchmarks across CT and MRI modalities show that PSP-Seg reduces GPU memory by 42%–45%, training time by 29%–48%, and parameter count by 83%–87%, while maintaining segmentation accuracy comparable to strong baselines such as nnU-Net. Additional analysis shows that the compact architectures obtained through the redundant-to-compact training trajectory outperform the same architectures trained from scratch, confirming the importance of dynamic structural evolution for efficient medical image segmentation. These results indicate that PSP-Seg provides an effective framework for jointly achieving high accuracy, practical efficiency, and task adaptability in 3D medical image segmentation. Authors: Chen Z.; Liao H.; Chen J.; You D.
Title: Complementary recommendation with abductive correction in incremental development
Abstract: Complementary cloud API recommendation, which suggests APIs frequently co-invoked with a given set of APIs, plays a crucial role in enabling efficient incremental development. Existing approaches primarily model API complementarity from co-invocation behaviors but often overlook weak complementary relationships revealed through functional co-occurrence. Moreover, most methods follow a one-step paradigm, directly generating recommendations from learned relationships without further abductive refinement, thereby limiting accuracy. To address these issues, we propose a Complementary Recommendation method with Abductive Correction, named CRAC. CRAC is built on three key ideas: (1) developing a path-based modeling approach that unifies both strong complementary (from co-invocation) and weak complementary (from functional co-occurrence) relations into a unified framework; (2) introducing complementary projection and higher-order reasoning modules that capture complementary and non-substitutable relationships while enforcing complementary-but-not-substitutable constraints; (3) designing an abductive correction mechanism that refines recommendation results through abductive tasks and losses, with an over-correction strategy to ensure effective correction. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that CRAC significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Further ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of weak complementarity modeling and abductive correction in enhancing complementary recommendation performance. The implementation of CRAC is publicly available on: https://github.com/lhnngp/CR_AC. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Injectable bioactive chitosan/silk fibroin hydrogels containing in situ formed magnetic nanoparticles for bone tissue engineering
Abstract: Irregularly shaped bone defects caused by trauma or tumor excision are difficult to fill with preformed scaffolds, motivating injectable materials that conform to complex geometries. Here, an injectable magnetic chitosan/silk fibroin/bioactive glass hydrogel containing in situ formed Fe3O4 nanoparticles was developed for bone tissue engineering, avoiding separate nanoparticle synthesis and incorporation. The formulation containing 3 wt% chitosan and 3 wt% bioactive glass showed favorable injectability and shape fidelity. Characterization confirmed Fe3O4 formation, porous morphology, and inorganic phase incorporation. Rheological analyses showed G′ > G″, shear-thinning behavior, and thixotropic recovery. The hydrogel exhibited a compressive modulus of 18.0 ± 0.5 kPa, 720 ± 18% swelling after 24 h, and 80 ± 5% mass loss after 7 days in PBS. Hydroxyapatite formed after 21 days in SBF. MG-63 metabolic activity reached 239.65 ± 12.47% on day 3, with SEM confirming attachment. These findings support the hydrogel's potential for bone repair applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Author full names: Yao, Xiaoxin (57216871538); Xia, Dengchao (57211313251); Cai, Jiajun (60808585700); Zeng, Gangwei (59657134600); Huang, Zuohua (8550071700); Tang, Chenglong (59902116200)
Title: Multi-hole spray morphologies and auto-ignition characteristics of liquid ammonia + diethyl ether blends
Abstract: Based on high-speed schlieren imaging and an optically accessible rapid compression machine, this study experimentally investigates the spray morphology and auto-ignition characteristics of liquid ammonia + diethyl ether (DEE) fuel blends, with a focus on classifying and elucidating the mechanisms underlying flash-boiling collapsing and autoignition combustion behaviors. The results show that the degree of spray collapsing intensifies with increasing ammonia blending ratio. Conditions featuring a high ammonia blending ratio, elevated ambient temperature, and low ambient pressure are particularly favorable for promoting rapid flash boiling and collapsing in multi-hole sprays of ammonia + DEE blends. As temperature decreases and the ammonia blending ratio increases, the auto-ignition of ammonia + DEE blended fuels becomes progressively more difficult, accompanied by a transition in combustion mode from diffusion-controlled to premixed combustion. For ammonia volume fractions exceeding 90 %, autoignition is essentially unattainable at temperatures below 890 K. Under high ammonia blending ratios, achieving rapid combustion at low temperatures remains challenging; stable and rapid ignition and combustion require the temperature to exceed 820 K, with notably longer ignition delay times. This work offers essential experimental evidence and theoretical support for the understanding of spray morphologies and auto-ignition characteristics of ammonia + DEE blends. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Guan Q.; Zheng L.; Cao S.; Xue C.; Chang Y.
Title: An enzymatic glycomics strategy for quantifying structural units in κ- and ι-carrageenans using the bifunctional carrageenase and UPSEC-HRMS
Abstract: The κ- and ι-carrageenans are widely used as food hydrocolloids for their gelling, thickening, and stabilizing properties. However, their structural heterogeneity and highly hybrid compositions hinder the characterization and quantification of structural units, rendering product quality evaluation and functional studies difficult. In this study, an enzymatic glycomics strategy was developed for the quantitative analysis of κ- and ι-carrageenan structural units. The bifunctional carrageenase Cg82Mf was used to simultaneously release κ- and ι-type oligosaccharides from carrageenan chains, and the hydrolysates were analyzed by ultra-performance size-exclusion chromatography coupled with high-resolution mass spectrometry (UPSEC-HRMS). Five structurally defined oligosaccharide standards were enzymatically prepared to establish calibration curves, including neo-κ-carrageenan di- and tetrasaccharides and neo-ι-carrageenan di-, tetra-, and hexasaccharides. Application to 12 commercial carrageenan additives revealed marked differences in composition and structural-unit contents, with the total contents of quantified structural units ranging from 5.84% ± 1.32% to 76.44% ± 8.45%. Principal component analysis further distinguished κ- and ι-dominant carrageenans and visualized differences in composition and content among samples. This study establishes a quantitative glycomics workflow for κ- and ι-carrageenans and provides a practical tool for quality assessment and standardization of commercial carrageenan products. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Sun C.; Zhang N.; Wang Q.; Li Q.; Wang X.
Title: An improved differentiable finite element method for saturated–unsaturated seepage with time–stepping, parallel, and inverse strategies
Abstract: Physics–informed neural networks (PINNs) integrate physical laws with the advantages of data–driven methods. However, achieving the strict precision required by PDEs is hindered in scenarios such as unsaturated seepage, not only by the non–convexity and non–uniqueness of neural networks, but also by loss balancing, time marching, and the inherent nonlinearity of the PDEs. To address these challenges, this study proposes an improved differentiable finite element method (DFEM) framework for steady and transient saturated–unsaturated seepage analysis. The governing equation is formulated in a Galerkin weak form of Richards’ equation, and the resulting residuals are embedded into a differentiable optimization framework. Thereby, the nodal pressure heads are directly optimized, neural-network parameter redundancy is avoided, and the Dirichlet boundary conditions are exactly satisfied. A vectorized implementation is developed to evaluate Gauss–point residuals in parallel and assemble the global residual efficiently within neural–network computing frameworks. A time–marching scheme is incorporated to model transient seepage evolution, respecting the structure of parabolic PDEs rather than treating time as an additional entangled network input. For inverse analysis, the DFEM solver is coupled with Bayesian optimization to identify saturated hydraulic conductivity from pressure–head observations. Numerical examples, including Poisson flow, 1D and 2D infiltration, irregular–domain seepage, layered–soil seepage, and hydraulic–conductivity identification, demonstrate that the improved DFEM achieves stable convergence and superior accuracy compared to PINN. © 2026
