Authors: Meng J.; Li C.; Lan P.; Xie J.; Wang Y.
Title: An improved multi-fidelity neural network for surrogate modeling of mechanical responses of irregularly shaped granular materials
Abstract: High-resolution discrete element method (DEM) simulations are essential for accurately capturing the mechanical behavior of irregularly shaped granular materials; however, their high computational cost limits practical applications in large-scale engineering analyses. Data-driven surrogate models alleviate this burden, while multi-fidelity learning further enhances data efficiency by incorporating inexpensive low-fidelity (LF) simulations. Nevertheless, existing multi-fidelity approaches remain constrained by the limited parameter-space coverage of scarce high-fidelity (HF) samples. This study develops an improved multi-fidelity neural network (IMFNN) with a projection-based data enhancement strategy to predict the critical-state macro–mesoscopic responses of irregular granular materials. First, a dedicated multi-fidelity DEM dataset is established, where fidelity levels are defined by particle-shape resolution and controlled by the number of sub-spheres in the clumped-particle representations. A feedforward neural network is pretrained using abundant LF data to capture dominant nonlinear response trends. Subsequently, a projection neural network is trained using HF samples together with their LF-level predictions to learn the LF–HF correction relationship. The learned relationship is then propagated to LF samples to generate pseudo-HF labels, thereby extending the effective coverage of HF-level supervision. The real and pseudo-HF samples are integrated to train the final surrogate model, which enhances the utilization of multi-fidelity information and improves predictive performance. The IMFNN accurately predicts critical-state macroscopic and mesoscopic responses and outperforms a pooled feedforward neural network and a conventional multi-fidelity neural network under the considered HF-data availability levels. The trained IMFNN surrogate model further enables efficient parametric studies and probabilistic analyses, providing a computationally efficient alternative to repeated high-resolution DEM simulations of irregular granular materials. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Segmental pin and endwall heat transfer for a staggered pin fin array in a stationary and rotating channel
Abstract: An experimental study is conducted to separate the heat transfer contributions of the pin surfaces and endwalls in a staggered circular pin fin array subjected to straight flow ejection in a low aspect ratio rectangular channel, representative of gas turbine trailing edge cooling passages. The array has a height-to-diameter ratio of 2, a streamwise pitch of 2.5D (where D is the pin diameter), and a spanwise pitch of 2D. Two geometrically identical test sections, one with copper pins and the other with perspex pins, are used to isolate the pin and wall heat transfer contributions under identical operating conditions. Experiments are performed over a Reynolds number range of 3000 - 25000 under stationary conditions, while rotating experiments cover Reynolds numbers of 3000 - 5000 and rotation numbers up to 0.26. Under stationary conditions, both wall and pin Nusselt numbers increase with Reynolds number. The pin Nusselt number is approximately 50% higher than the wall Nusselt number in the second row. However, the overall wall and pin heat transfer contributions are comparable because of the larger endwall area. Separate correlations are developed for the average wall and pin Nusselt numbers under stationary conditions. At Re = 3000 and Ro = 0.26, the average pin Nusselt number increases by approximately 70% relative to the stationary value, while the average wall Nusselt numbers remain close to their stationary values. These results indicate that the two surfaces should be treated separately in thermal analysis of rotating pin fin channels. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Title: Critical stability evaluations of different types of solid amine sorbents in DAC processes
Abstract: Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology plays a pivotal role in mitigating climate change by capturing CO2 directly from the atmosphere. Solid amine adsorbents are highly regarded in the DAC field for their superior CO2 adsorption capacity and relatively low energy consumption. In practical industrial operations, adsorbents will undergo cyclic adsorption–desorption operations and their stability performances are important concerns. In this study, we carried out a comprehensive stability evaluation for three solid amine adsorbents (SiO2-PEI, SiO2-APTMS and DRC-I), which were representative of the three typical classes, i.e. impregnation (Class 1), grafting (Class 2), and in-situ polymerization methods (Class 3). All the degradation mechanisms that may encounter in practical DAC operations were included in these tests, i.e. cyclic stability, oxidative stability, water immersion stability, thermal stability, and hydrothermal stability. The experimental results indicate that DRC-I, prepared via in-situ polymerization, exhibits the best stability across all tests, a performance consistent with robust amine-phase stability as indirectly evidenced by non-detectable nitrogen loss in elemental analysis. In the presence of water, a shift in the reaction pathway leads to an increasing trend in CO2 adsorption capacity, but its working adsorption capacity remains lower than that of the other two adsorbents. Conversely, the impregnated SiO2-PEI and grafted SiO2-APTMS adsorbents showed much poorer stability performances under aqueous conditions, i.e. in water immersion and hydrothermal stability tests. Overall, considering their CO2 adsorption capacities and stabilities, all three adsorbents remain inadequate for large-scale industrial CO2 capture. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Gao S.; Yang M.; Wu F.; Jia K.; Zhang L.
Title: Hollow microspheres with CoP/MoCoO heterointerfaces for enhancing the hydrogen storage performance of NaBH4
Abstract: Sodium borohydride (NaBH4) is a promising solid-state hydrogen storage material due to its high theoretical gravimetric capacity (10.8 wt%) and ambient stability. Herein, we synthesize a hollow microsphere catalyst composed of CoP/MoCoO heterointerfaces via a one-step hydrothermal method followed by phosphorylation, exploiting the molybdate-ion-induced Ostwald ripening mechanism. When combined with NaBH4 via a solution impregnation method, the resulting CoP/MoCoO@NaBH4 composite exhibits a greatly reduced initial dehydrogenation temperature (60.6 °C), compared to 403 °C for pure NaBH4 and 127.5 °C for CoP@NaBH4. This is attributed to the abundant active sites provided by the catalyst’s hollow structure, as well as the strong electronic coupling induced by the CoP-MoCoO heterointerface, which optimizes the electron density at Co sites, thereby weakening the Co-H bond strength and promoting hydrogen desorption and release. The dehydrogenation activation energy of CoP/MoCoO@NaBH4 is 60.2 kJ·mol−1. Isothermal testing at 440 °C showed that the hydrogen release reached 8.70 wt% within 6 h, far exceeding the 1.32 wt% released by pure NaBH4 under the same conditions. Moreover, the composite achieves a reversible capacity of 5.03 wt% after three cycles at 400 °C, retaining 72 % of its initial capacity. This work demonstrates that integrating bimetallic heterointerface engineering with hollow morphology control is an effective strategy to boost the dehydrogenation kinetics and cycling stability of NaBH4 for solid-state hydrogen storage. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Yang E.; Xu Z.; Xu X.; Xing P.; Ma Y.; Li Z.; Zeng D.
Title: HyCo-IAD: Hyperbolic collaborative reinforcement fine-tuning for multimodal industrial anomaly detection
Abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) offer a promising avenue for Industrial Anomaly Detection (IAD) by enabling complex reasoning beyond simple numerical scoring. However, with the limited anomaly data available in industrial settings, standard Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) may overfit the training samples and generalize poorly to unseen defects. Reinforcement Fine-Tuning (RFT) provides an alternative by optimizing task-level rewards and encouraging solution exploration. Its application to IAD nevertheless remains challenging: Euclidean visual representations do not explicitly account for the hierarchical structure of industrial defects, while sparse reward supervision may provide limited feedback to earlier visual layers. Motivated by these considerations, we propose HyCo-IAD, an RFT framework that integrates hyperbolic visual adaptation with tensor-based cross-layer collaboration. Specifically, we introduce a Low-rank Hyperbolic Adaptation (LHA) strategy, which performs low-rank Lorentz transformations on visual representations to model the hierarchical structure of industrial defects. We further devise a Cross-Layer Collaborative Optimization (CCO) mechanism that stacks the layer-wise adaptation coefficients into a third-order tensor and applies a learnable relation matrix along the mode indexing the visual layers and adaptation branches. Extensive experiments on the MMAD benchmark indicate that HyCo-IAD achieves strong performance under the standard 1-shot evaluation protocol, supporting its effectiveness in a data-scarce adaptation setting. Authors: Wang T.; Li H.; Wang Y.
Title: Asymptotic stability for variable-order short-memory fractional systems via event-triggered impulsive control
Abstract: This work establishes a framework for global asymptotic stability of variable-order fractional systems with short memory under an event-triggered impulsive control strategy. Through the fusion of the short-memory principle with variable-order fractional operators, the proposed approach leverages their inherent dynamic order adjustability. This enables the system to accurately characterize time-varying memory properties and respond effectively to its dynamic evolution. Sufficient criteria are deduced to guarantee global asymptotic stability while explicitly excluding Zeno behavior. Finally, a numerical simulation is provided to verify the theoretical results. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Extracellular manganese as a redox mediator and matrix binder in cyanobacterial photoelectrochemistry
Abstract: The model organism Synechocystis sp. PCC6803 is routinely employed in biophotoelectrochemical systems for the study of extracellular electron transport and the production of solar electricity, chemicals and fuels. The precise mechanism of electron export in Synechocystis is still under debate; NADPH has previously been proposed as the endogenous mediator, whilst others suggest the involvement of metal ions such as Mn and Fe species. Here, we first tested the hypothesis that NADPH acts as an electron mediator during biophotoelectrochemistry of Synechocystis cells on indium tin oxide (ITO) electrodes. We found that under standard conditions NADPH does not exhibit properties of an electron mediator between the cyanobacteria and electrode. Second, we investigated the role of extracellular Mn ions in cyanobacterial photocurrent production. The ability of endogenous and exogenous Mn ions to enhance photocurrents was tested, and up to 40-fold enhancements of were observed following the electrochemical production of localised oxidised Mn pools. We observed the contraction of the extracellular polymeric matrix upon oxidation of Mn ions, marked by increased cell-cell and cell-electrode interactions. These results provide future directions for increasing cyanobacteria-electrode adhesion and overall photocurrent output in these bioelectrochemical systems. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Wang S.; Sun S.
Title: Rational design, fabrication, performance, and challenges of intermediate temperature CO2 adsorbents: A review
Abstract: Carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) are widely recognized as an effective approach to mitigating the climate impacts of rising CO2 emissions. Among the various technologies developed for CCUS, solid CO2 adsorbents have been widely applied. Intermediate-temperature solid adsorbents have attracted significant attention due to their compatibility with industrial CO2 emission conditions. However, intermediate-temperature adsorbents are constrained by their performance and stability, which are largely determined by their design and fabrication. Herein, we present a critical review of intermediate-temperature CO2 adsorbents, including a systematic evaluation of fabrication strategies for solid CO2 adsorbents, along with a critical analysis of their CO2 interaction mechanisms, sorption performance, potential applications, and remaining technical challenges. Finally, we look forward to the industrial-scale application of these adsorbents and the application of machine learning to enhance the efficiency of material development. Collectively, this work provides actionable guidance for the rational design and scalable production of high-performance intermediate-temperature CO2 adsorbents for industrial applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Physics-informed neural network for predicting high-temperature flow stress of 3Cr-1Si-1Ni ultra-high-strength steel
Abstract: In this work, a first application of physics-informed neural network (PINN) to predict the high-temperature flow stress of an ultra-high strength steel is proposed, in which the accuracy, robustness and data efficiency are enhanced. Physical embedding and physical constraints are incorporated into the PINN as guiding physical principles, enabling superior generalisation ability and accuracy compared with the conventional artificial neural network (ANN) and the Johnson–Cook (J–C) model. The PINN also demonstrates significantly improved data efficiency when only small amounts of training data are available, requiring only three datasets for training. In terms of robustness, the PINN is shown to tolerate higher levels of random noise than the ANN. When the standard deviation of added random noise increases from 0 % to 10 %, the absolute prediction error of the PINN rises by only 5.5 MPa, compared with a 30.0 MPa increase for the ANN. These results demonstrate that PINNs provide a powerful framework for the development of constitutive models for metals with improved accuracy, data efficiency, and robustness. Authors: Xiong C.; Lin W.; Huang H.; Mu Q.; Li K.
Title: Unified task profiling and performance interference-aware Makespan and energy scheduling for cloud robotics tasks driven by an improved genetic algorithm
Abstract: Cloud robotics systems offload heterogeneous, computation- and data-intensive tasks to shared cloud nodes, yet suffer from severe performance interference caused by co-located contention for shared physical resources. Such interference renders idealized execution times unreliable and degrades both Makespan and energy efficiency in conventional schedulers. To enable interference-aware scheduling, it is first necessary to quantitatively characterize the resource demands of diverse tasks and to measure how co-location affects their execution. Therefore, this paper proposes a unified task profiling approach that characterizes CPU, I/O, and memory demands and other key differentiating attributes of eight representative cloud robotics tasks spanning perception, planning, control, and execution. Lightweight, tunable benchmarks are then designed to emulate these resource-access patterns, enabling controlled co-location experiments that construct a quantitative interference-sensitivity matrix. On this foundation, an interference-aware integer programming model is formulated to minimize the weighted sum of Makespan and energy consumption. The main novelty lies in connecting task profiling, benchmark-calibrated interference measurement, and joint Makespan-energy scheduling into a unified interference-aware optimization method. To solve the resulting NP-hard problem, we propose an Improved Genetic Algorithm for Cloud Robotics Task Scheduling (IGA-CTS), which jointly searches task allocation and execution order over the interference-aware scheduling model. In benchmark-calibrated simulation experiments against seven evaluated baselines, no baseline simultaneously achieves lower median Makespan and energy consumption than IGA-CTS at any scale; although some baselines perform better on an individual objective, these advantages are accompanied by inferior performance on the other. An objective-weight sensitivity analysis further shows that this overall trade-off is largely maintained under varying optimization preferences. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Wu X.; Wu Z.; Xu X.; Cui W.; Zhao R.; Zhou E.
Title: A 2D MPLBM-FDEM method for modeling two-phase displacement in porous media under fluid-solid interaction conditions
Abstract: This paper develops a two-dimensional (2D) numerical framework by coupling the multi-component pseudopotential lattice Boltzmann method (MPLBM) and the combined finite-discrete element method (FDEM) to investigate the process of two-phase displacement in porous media under fluid–solid interaction (FSI) conditions. The MPLBM is used to simulate two-phase displacement processes, while the FDEM simulates the mechanical response of solids, and the immersed moving boundary (IMB) scheme is employed to achieve bidirectional coupling between MPLBM and FDEM. To prevent artificial pore-channel closure under confining pressure in 2D simulations, an algorithm for equivalent 3D pore connectivity in 2D simulations (E3PC-2D) is developed via the introduction of an outer ghost layer (OGL) element strategy. The MPLBM-FDEM coupling framework is verified through four benchmark cases, while the mechanical and hydraulic consistency of the E3PC-2D algorithm is further assessed using stress-dependent porosity and permeability responses. Then, the MPLBM-FDEM method is adopted to investigate the evolution of water–oil displacement under varying capillary numbers and confining pressures. Numerical results indicate that the saturation (Sw) and fractal dimension (Df) of the invading water phase decrease as confining pressure increases, and Sw is more sensitive to changes in confining pressure than Df. At the pore scale, quantitative analysis of throat-width reduction and capillary-entry-threshold variation shows that increasing confining pressure enhances local entry resistance and invasion selectivity, thereby producing narrower preferential invasion pathways. In addition, this study proposes a theory of displacement pattern transition that accounts for the effects of confining pressure and develops a corresponding phase diagram. The phase diagram is generally consistent with the simulated regime distribution and predicts a widening trend of the crossover-zone interval with increasing confining pressure. Overall, this study provides a robust methodology for analyzing multiphase displacement mechanisms under FSI conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: A carbonate/H2O2 surrogate for representing thermal runaway and state-of-charge effects in lithium-ion battery fires
Abstract: For fire hazard assessment of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), the autoignition of carbonate/H2O2 mixtures in a transient constant-volume reactor was numerically simulated to investigate their potential as simplified reactive surrogates for selected LIB fire characteristics. The effects of replacing air with hydrogen peroxide as the oxidizer on the ignition behavior of carbonate fuels, the autoignition and rapid self-heating behavior of the carbonate/H2O2 surrogate at elevated initial temperatures, and the feasibility of phenomenologically representing state-of-charge (SOC)-dependent thermal behavior were systematically investigated. Compared with carbonate/air mixtures, the ignition delay times (IDTs) of carbonate/H2O2 mixtures were reduced by enhanced reactivity. Reaction-pathway and sensitivity analyses of DMC/H2O2, employed as a representative single-carbonate fuel, revealed that OH was the primary radical promoting ignition, whereas HO2 played an increasingly important role as the mixture became more fuel-rich. Comparison with the ARC measurements was used to identify phenomenological equivalence-ratio bounds associated with the thermal behaviors of fully charged and fully discharged LIBs. These results suggest that the proposed carbonate/H2O2 surrogate provides a simple reactive framework for examining selected thermal-runaway and SOC-related characteristics of LIB fires. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Low-temperature catalytic steam reforming of phenol for hydrogen production over Co-K/Al2O3 catalyst
Abstract: Hydrogen production via catalytic steam reforming of biomass-derived phenolic compounds attracted significant attention, but catalyst deactivation caused by coking and sintering remains a major challenge. Title: Smartphone-assisted upconversion nanoparticles–aptamer-based probe functionalized hydrogel microneedles for rapid interstitial fluid lactate profiling
Abstract: Rapid assessment of lactate dynamics is important for evaluating tissue hypoxia, metabolic stress, and exercise-induced physiological responses. However, conventional lactate measurements predominantly rely on blood sampling and enzyme-based assays, making them poorly suited for rapid and minimally invasive assessment of localized lactate dynamics in interstitial fluid (ISF). Here, we developed a rare-earth nanomaterial–aptamer probe-functionalized composite hydrogel microneedle patch for rapid ISF lactate profiling. The sensing system integrates fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET)-based signal modulation with smartphone-assisted imaging, enabling portable lactate quantification within 20 min. The hydrogel microneedles facilitate minimally invasive ISF access while providing an integrated interface for analyte recognition and optical signal transduction. In vitro, the patch exhibited a concentration-dependent fluorescence response over a lactate range of 2–20 mM (R2 = 0.961), with a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.47 mM. In a rat model with elevated lactate levels, ISF lactate concentrations measured using the microneedle patch showed a strong correlation with simultaneously determined blood lactate concentrations obtained using a commercial assay kit, supporting reliable in vivo lactate assessment. Collectively, this work presents an integrated, minimally invasive, and portable strategy for rapid ISF lactate profiling and provides a versatile platform for the timely evaluation of exertion-related metabolic biomarkers and personalized physiological assessment. Authors: Guo Y.-Y.; Zhu L.-N.; Zhang Z.-Q.; She D.-S.; Wang H.-D.; Kang J.-J.
Title: Effects of heat treatment and titanium modification on the microstructure and tribological properties of CMT-processed 2024 aluminum alloy
Abstract: Lightweight drilling tools require materials combining high strength and wear resistance, yet the limited surface hardness of 2024 aluminum alloy restricts its use under severe sliding and abrasive conditions. In this study, Al-Cu-Mg and Ti-modified Al-Cu-Mg cladding layers were deposited on 2024-T4 aluminum alloy by cold metal transfer, and the effects of Ti addition and heat treatment on microstructure, mechanical properties, and tribological behavior were investigated. The results show that with the addition of 1.27 wt% Ti, the average grain size can be reduced from 57.4 micrometers to 10.4 micrometers, and the porosity can be decreased from 0.521% to 0.321%. Thermally stable Al₃Ti particles promoted heterogeneous nucleation and weakened crystallographic texture, while heat treatment partially dissolved continuous Al₂Cu and Al₂CuMg phases and redistributed Cu and Mg within the α-Al matrix. The Al-Cu-Mg-Ti-HT cladding layer achieved the highest microhardness of 149.49 HV₀.₂, 38.3% above that of the as-deposited Al-Cu-Mg cladding layer. Heat treatment increased tensile strength from 295–300 MPa to 440–445 MPa and elongation from 4.5%–5.5% to 7.0–7.5%. The optimized cladding layer exhibited a wear rate of 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ mm³ ·N⁻¹ ·m⁻¹ and a maximum wear depth of 22 μm, representing reductions of 60% and 51%, respectively. The dominant mechanism shifted from severe abrasive, adhesive, and oxidative wear with fatigue delamination to mild abrasive-oxidative wear with limited adhesion. These findings provide a feasible approach for improving the mechanical and tribological performance of CMT-fabricated 2024 aluminum alloy components for lightweight drilling applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Gao J.; Chen Y.; Feng J.; Li M.; Yan W.; Wang H.; Zhang W.
Title: Synergistic electronic modulation in C@NiCoP-Fe/NF accelerates intermediate adsorption kinetics for enhanced oxygen evolution
Abstract: Water electrolysis has emerged as a sustainable method for clean hydrogen production. Nevertheless, the intricate four-electron nature and sluggish kinetics of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) at the anode persist as significant impediments. Despite the evident potential of transition metal phosphides, their propensity for the adsorption of the *OH intermediate, as well as the consequent high RDS energy barrier, remain pivotal concerns that necessitate resolution. This work proposes a dual electron regulation strategy to construct a transition metal phosphides OER catalyst. The resulting C@NiCoP-Fe/NF catalyst delivers remarkable OER performance with overpotentials of only 267 mV (10 mA cm−2) and 363 mV (100 mA cm−2), exceeding most existing NiCo-based counterparts. A 1000-h constant-current test at 10 mA cm−2 also ascertains the stability. In-situ characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that phosphorization (P) carbonizes the organic framework, forming a conductive carbon layer. Mechanistically, the high electronegativity of P induces electron-deficient NiCo sites to promote OH− adsorption, while Fe doping triggers metal–metal interactions that modulate the d-band center to lower the energy barrier of the rate-determining *O to *OOH step. This work provides comprehensive insights into the dual electron regulation mechanism for OER through phosphorization and Fe doping. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Revolutionizing Control in Fractional Delay Systems with Minimum Energy
Abstract: This study focuses on determining the minimum energy control for fractional delay systems. The optimal energy performance index for such systems is derived using solutions obtained through the Laplace transform. The proposed control strategy ensures the system transitions from its initial state to the desired final state with minimal energy consumption. The approach is further extended to accommodate various control types. Title: Reactive molecular dynamics combustion simulation of sustainable aviation fuel alternative components
Abstract: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), constituting an important technological pathway for the aviation industry to achieve carbon neutrality goals, has attracted significant attention due to its potential to substantially reduce carbon emissions. However, the complex multi-component nature of SAF has resulted in unelucidated competitive/synergistic reaction mechanisms between components and unclear pollutant generation pathways during its combustion process. Existing ReaxFF-MD studies on SAF mainly focus on single-component surrogates, lacking systematic exploration of multi-component interaction mechanisms under actual aero-engine high-temperature conditions. In this paper, based on the reactive molecular dynamics (ReaxFF-MD) simulation method, a kinetic model of the high-temperature combustion process was constructed for the alternative components of a typical SAF multi-component mixture system, and pyrolysis and oxidation reaction paths alongside free radical generation were systematically investigated. Through comprehensive comparison of potential energy (PE) changes, combustion rates, intermediate product distributions, and final products at different temperatures and oxygen contents, the microscopic mechanism of SAF multi-component synergistic combustion was uncovered, while the regulatory effects of temperature on bond cleavage pathways and radical evolution, as well as the influence of excess air coefficient ( λ ) on combustion efficiency and product distribution, were revealed. Simultaneously, the reaction mechanism of SAF was obtained by analyzing the reaction paths. The results show that, compared with the low-temperature conditions, under high-temperature conditions, SAF has a faster combustion rate, a greater total number of species, and higher generation and consumption rates of free radicals. Furthermore, oxygen content exerts a significant effect on combustion efficiency and product distribution. Increasing the excess air coefficient enhances the reaction rate to a certain extent but offers no substantial benefit when the excess air coefficient exceeds 1.5. Notably, most PE attains its maximum during the cleavage of C–C and C–H bonds, indicating that bond scission is the rate-determining step in the initial stage of SAF combustion. This study provides fundamental theoretical support at the microscopic level combined with reaction path analysis for optimizing the combustion performance of SAF alternative components and developing clean combustion technology, thereby accelerating the decarbonization process of aviation fuels. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Liu C.; Wu W.; Liu X.; Wang B.; El Naggar M.H.; Liu H.; Zhang Y.; Frah M.A.
Title: A novel theoretical model for dynamic response analysis of inclined pile groups in layered soil
Abstract: This study proposes a novel theoretical model to efficiently and accurately evaluate the dynamic pile-soil-pile interaction of inclined pile groups in layered soil by coupling the finite element method (FEM) and thin-layer method (TLM). The dynamic governing equations for the inclined pile group are formulated based on the three-dimensional Euler-Bernoulli beam theory and a local-global coordinate transformation. Subsequently, the TLM is adopted to describe the complex wave propagation within the layered soil, while Perfectly Matched Layers (PMLs) are incorporated to simulate the underlying semi-infinite elastic space to eliminate spurious reflections at the truncated boundaries. The dynamic Green’s functions of the layered soil are efficiently derived based on this coupled TLM-PMLs framework. By enforcing strict displacement compatibility and force equilibrium conditions at the pile-soil interface, the coupling of the inclined pile group and the layered soil is achieved, allowing for the solution of the dynamic impedance. The proposed model is validated by comparing its predictions with results of existing numerical solutions. An in-depth investigation is further conducted to reveal the influence of the geometric parameters on the dynamic bearing characteristics of the inclined pile group. The obtained conclusions can not only deepen the understanding of the spatial dynamic synergistic behavior of inclined pile groups, but also provide a reliable theoretical basis for foundation configuration optimization and refined anti-vibration design in practice. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Authors: Fu Z.; Zhang Z.; Chen F.; Yao H.; Shan X.; Gou R.; Nie Z.; Zhou J.; Chen G.; Dong S.; Zhao K.; Zheng M.; Ma Y.; Yue C.
Title: Effect of reactor environment on free-radical evolution and product selectivity during pyrolysis of coal liquefaction pitch (CLP)
Abstract: Coal liquefaction pitch (CLP) contains abundant aromatic carbon resources. However, its complex molecular architecture and highly condensed nature severely restrict potential high value applications. The present study proposes theoretical models for reactor dependent free radical evolution. We aim to infer their impact on the selective conversion of this pitch. Pyrolysis experiments were comparatively conducted in a fluidized bed, a fixed bed, and an autoclave operating under elevated pressure. Multiphase product distributions and free radical reaction pathways were systematically investigated by integrating pyrolysis kinetics with gas chromatography mass spectrometry and gas phase analysis. The results demonstrate distinct multiple stage characteristics during the pyrolysis process. The apparent activation energy escalated dynamically from 95.36 to 218.74 kJ/mol as conversion increased. This escalation reflects a clear mechanistic transition. The reaction shifts from the initial scission of aliphatic side chains to the profound cleavage of aromatic skeletons. The distinct macroscopic environments across the three reactors effectively drove three divergent radical evolution patterns. Intensified heat transfer and rapid stripping driven by gas flow in the fluidized bed effectively suppressed the secondary polycondensation of volatiles. This kinetic advantage yielded a maximum oil recovery of 24.06 wt% at 560 °C. The GC–MS detectable light and medium components of the resulting oil were predominantly enriched in moderately condensed polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons like pyrene and benzofluorene derivatives. It is important to note that non-volatile heavy asphaltenes are beyond this analytical scope. However, ultimate analysis provides complementary information on the elemental characteristics of the analyzed fractions. Prolonged vapor residence time in the fixed bed system exacerbated secondary cracking and polycondensation reactions. Consequently, the oil yield was slightly lower than that observed in the fluidized bed. Elevated pressure within the autoclave thermodynamically suppressed volatile desorption and prolonged the retention of intermediates within the liquid phase. This closed environment promoted a synergistic interplay between dehydrogenative polycondensation and hydrogen transfer. The oil yield declined drastically to 7.11 wt%. However, the resultant liquid was uniquely enriched in branched alkanes, hydrogenated aromatics, and highly condensed pyrene structures. The liquid product also maintained a higher degree of oxygen retention. Ultimately the reactor configuration governs the selective conversion pathways by modulating heat and mass transfer behaviors. This physical modulation fundamentally redistributes the intricate competition among radical cracking, polycondensation, and hydrogen transfer. Reactor environments regulate heat transfer, volatile residence time and free radical evolution, thereby redistributing the competition among cracking, condensation and hydrogen transfer reactions, which ultimately determines the selective conversion of CLP. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Author full names: Buitrago-Tello, Rodrigo (57195058901); Lee, Uisung (55344751100); Amar, Vinod (55007055600); McVay, Jesse (60607938800); Menegay, Matt (60969339100)
Title: Life cycle carbon, energy, and water impacts of isobutanol and sustainable aviation fuel from pea starch
Abstract: The rapid expansion of plant-based food markets has increased the importance of pea protein production in the food industry, while generating large quantities of pea starch as a low-value co-product. Pea starch is currently used in applications such as animal feed, but these outlets may be insufficient to absorb increasing co-product volumes. Improving pea processing systems requires identifying higher-value and lower-impact applications for this starch, and converting it into isobutanol (IBA) and sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) offers such an outlet while serving aviation, a sector expected to continue relying on liquid fuels to meet increasing demand. This study presents a life cycle assessment of U.S. pea starch-derived IBA and SAF covering the full life cycle, including pea cultivation, protein-starch fractionation, and fuel production. Carbon intensity (CI), fossil energy consumption, and water consumption are quantified. To evaluate the influence of separation technology, IBA purification is modeled using conventional distillation and membrane solvent extraction, with the latter as an alternative designed to reduce process heat demand. Results show that agricultural impacts are primarily driven by nitrogen fertilizer production and N2O emissions from soil, while energy requirements dominate CI and fossil energy consumption in downstream stages. Replacing distillation with a membrane system reduces natural gas demand, resulting in a 43 % decrease in CI, and a 51 % reduction in fossil energy use for IBA relative to gasoline (52.1 vs 92.1 gCO2e/MJ and 0.59 vs 1.22 MJ/MJ, respectively). These improvements are associated with lower thermal energy requirements and credits from renewable natural gas generated from process waste streams. Compared with conventional jet fuel, starch-based SAF shows lower CI (75.0 vs 89.0 gCO2e/MJ) and fossil energy demand (0.96 vs 1.11 MJ/MJ), improving overall environmental performance. However, pea starch-derived fuels have higher life cycle water consumption than their fossil counterparts. Overall, pea starch shows potential as an additional feedstock for fuel production derived from a low-value co-product, particularly when process energy demand is minimized, although increased water consumption remains an important tradeoff. © 2026 The Author(s), Argonne National Laboratory,.

Authors: Tan J.; Nie Q.; Li Y.; Zou Y.; Xu J.; Lu L.; Tana D.; Peng Z.; Jin H.
Title: Performance assessment of a solar-driven system for polyethylene terephthalate supercritical water gasification integrated with seawater desalination to produce hydrogen-electricity-heat
Abstract: Residents of islands surrounded by the ocean need a sustainable supply of fresh water and energy. Meanwhile, the enormous amount of plastic waste dumped into the ocean poses a serious threat to the environment and human health. This study proposes an integrated technical framework that combines solar-driven supercritical water gasification (SCWG) and supercritical water desalination (SCWD) to treat ocean plastic waste (PET) for the generation of hydrogen-electricity-heat. Thermodynamic analysis and life cycle assessment (LCA) were adopted to evaluate the system performance from multiple perspectives. Increasing slurry concentration while reducing gasification temperature and system pressure can improve energy efficiency (ηENE) and exergy efficiency (ηEXE). Under the operating conditions identified as optimal within the investigated parameter ranges via sensitivity analysis and response surface methodology (RSM), the system yields hydrogen at 130.52 kg/h, freshwater at 962.59 kg/h and steam at 1500 kg/h, with a power output of 808.15 kW. The corresponding ηENE and ηExE reach 75.46 % and 66.85 %, respectively. Exergy analysis reveals that the SCWG reactor has the largest exergy loss, which is 13396.41 kW, accounting for 76.29 % of the total loss. The environmental performance of the system was quantified using the global warming potential (GWP), abiotic depletion potential (ADP), acidification potential (AP), and eutrophication potential (EP), the relevant GWP per tonne of PET treated reaches 990.38–1118.64 kg CO2-eq. Under the idealized CCS assumption considered in this study, deploying carbon capture and storage (CCS) may exhibit a negative GWP value (−550.89-(−122.22) kg CO2 equivalent per tonne PET). This work may offer a feasible energy management strategy for ocean plastic treatment and seawater desalination. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Li Z.; Qin B.; Shi Q.; Ma D.; Shao X.; Wang X.
Title: Methane-involved thermal restructuring of coal enhances low-temperature oxidation reactivity: Experimental and theoretical insights
Abstract: Igneous intrusion into coal seams creates a high-temperature, high-pressure methane-rich geological environment that substantially modifies coal structure and elevates its spontaneous combustion tendency. Yet the active role of CH4 during coal thermal restructuring remains poorly understood. In this study, coals were thermally treated under pressurized N2 and CH4 atmosphere, respectively. Functional group evolution was characterized by Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and pyrolysis gases were analyzed by gas chromatography. Quantum chemical calculations were performed to elucidate the reaction mechanisms and low-temperature oxidation behavior. The results demonstrate that the CH4 atmosphere facilitates coal pyrolysis and significantly increasing aliphatic hydrocarbon content. After treatment at 300 °C, aliphatic content reaches 31.95 % under CH4, considerably higher than the 26.45 % observed under N2. This arises because highly active coal-derived radicals can abstract hydrogen from CH4 with a low energy barrier. CH4 progressively serves as a hydrogen donor as the temperature rises, promoting sustained hydrodeoxygenation, enabling exogenous hydrogen and methyl groups to be incorporated into the coal structure. In addition, comparison of the low-temperature oxidation characteristic temperatures derived from thermogravimetric (TG) analysis shows that coals pretreated in a CH4 atmosphere possess greater low-temperature reactivity. Consequently, CH4-involved thermal restructuring enriches aliphatic hydrocarbons and enhances low-temperature oxidation reactivity. These findings reveal the effect of a CH4 atmosphere on coal thermal restructuring, providing a theoretical basis for assessing the spontaneous combustion risk in coal seams subjected to magmatic intrusion. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Combinatorial lutein, zeaxanthin, and spearmint extract attenuated intense LED-induced intraocular pressure elevation and oxidative stress in the retina and anterior segment
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Prolonged exposure to high-intensity light-emitting diode (LED) illumination can provoke retinal dysfunction accompanied by intraocular pressure elevation. We evaluated whether an oral formulation containing lutein, zeaxanthin, and spearmint extract attenuated the impairing effects caused by intense LED exposure in mice, using topical latanoprost as a pharmacological benchmark for lowering intraocular pressure. Female ICR mice (6 weeks) were assigned to control, LED damage, combined lutein-zeaxanthin-spearmint (0.25× or 1.0×), lutein-zeaxanthin, spearmint extract, or latanoprost groups. All supplements were administered daily by oral gavage, and latanoprost was instilled daily (days 1–37). LED exposure (5000 lx, 24 h/day) was applied on days 17–37. Intraocular pressure was measured on days 15, 22, 29, and 36; scotopic electroretinography (ERG) was measured on days 16, 23, 30, and 37. Whole-eye sections were analyzed for retinal thickness and immunostaining for RPE65, 8-OHdG, and 4-HNE. Cornea, iris, ciliary body, and trabecular meshwork were assessed for 8-OHdG, 4-HNE, AQP1, and AQP4. The results showed that LED exposure reduced ERG a- and b-wave amplitudes and retinal thickness, particularly in the outer nuclear layer, which none of the treatment regimens prevented. However, the combined lutein-zeaxanthin-spearmint attenuated LED-induced retinal 8-OHdG and 4-HNE upregulation and mitigated RPE65 loss. LED exposure elevated intraocular pressure on days 29 and 36, which the combined lutein-zeaxanthin-spearmint attenuated. The combined lutein-zeaxanthin-spearmint also reduced oxidative injury in the cornea, iris, ciliary body, and trabecular meshwork but did not prevent LED-associated AQP1 and AQP4 downregulation in the ciliary body. Collectively, the combined formulation attenuated oxidative injury in the retina and anterior segment and partially stabilized intraocular pressure under intense LED exposure, but did not rescue retinal dysfunction or thinning. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Biogas separation employing sII and sH promoters coupled with kinetic additives: Investigation of hydrate formation/dissociation kinetics
Abstract: Biogas separation is essential for producing high purity CH4 as a clean fuel while enabling CO2 capture within carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS). However, insufficient separation can result in methane losses and incomplete CO2 capture, undermining climate benefits by high impact CH4 emissions with continued CO2 release. Hydrate based gas separation (HBGS) can be a potential solution for this purpose. The successful application of hydrate-based biogas storage depends on resolving the challenge of slow formation kinetics by developing methods that can effectively accelerate hydrate onset and growth. Thermodynamic additives (Tetrahydrofuran (THF), Cyclopentane (CP), 1,3 Dioxolane (DIOX) [forming sII structure] and Tetrabutyl methyl ether(TBME) [forming sH structure] at their stoichiometric concentrations alongside combinations with kinetic additives were employed to separate 24.8 mol% CO2 / 74.2 mol% CH4 (biogas) mixture at 4.7 MPa and 283.2 K. Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) and piperazine were also tested in combination for their effect on formation kinetics and separation efficiency. Highest gas uptake of 102.72 ± 5.12 mmol/mol was obtained using 2.86 mol% TBME with 0.1 wt% l-leucine. Selective separation ability of TBME forming sH hydrate was found to be higher compared to THF, CP and DIOX (structure sII hydrates) as it demonstrated highest separation factor of 2.45 ± 0.1, employing 2.86 mol% TBME with 5 wt% piperazine. DIOX sII mixed hydrate showed better performance compared to THF and CP in terms of gas uptake and rate of hydrate formation specifically in combination with l-methionine. Dissociation study of mixed hydrates with morphological observations show case higher thermodynamic stability of CP compared to THF and DIOX, other sII promoters. Overall, this work provides the systematic comprehensive evaluation of sII and sH promoters integrated with different bio-additives, advancing HBGS as a viable strategy for simultaneous methane enrichment and CO2 capture with reduced environmental impact aligning with United Nations sustainable development goals (SDGs) of 7 and 13. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Ding S.; Deng Y.; Sun J.; Liu J.; Yuan G.; Zheng J.
Title: HGMamSurv: a hypergraph mamba network for cancer survival prediction on whole slide images
Abstract: The complex correlations within whole slide images (WSIs) are crucial for cancer survival prediction, as they reveal intricate interactions between tumors and their surrounding microenvironment. However, current graph-based methods for WSI analysis primarily focus on pairwise correlations, leading to the loss of high-order information. Although hypergraph-based approaches can model such higher-order interactions, they remain constrained by local message-passing mechanisms, which limit the overall representational capacity of WSIs. In this work, we propose HGMamSurv, a novel hypergraph Mamba network for cancer survival prediction on WSIs. HGMamSurv pioneers the incorporation of the Mamba architecture into hypergraph networks, enabling efficient modeling of comprehensive high-order correlations while capturing both local details and global contextual patterns in complex WSIs. Specifically, we design a Hypergraph-Mamba Block (HMB) that orders node and hyperedge features by topological degree and employs Mamba to dynamically capture long-range dependencies across the hypergraph. Furthermore, we introduce a Cross Fusion Mamba Block (CFMB) to enhance the interaction and fusion between node and hyperedge representations, thereby enriching high-order feature learning from multiple perspectives for improved survival prediction. Extensive validation experiments were conducted on six public cancer cohorts from TCGA. The results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches. We also present interpretable analyses of HGMamSurv and highlight its potential applications in pathological image analysis, underscoring its clinical relevance for survival prognosis. © 2026

Authors: Yang Y.; Li Y.; Wu Z.; Li H.; Zhang Y.; Shi S.; Yang Y.; Zhao Q.; Guo Z.; Peng Q.; Zhu F.
Title: Dual-metal interfacial engineering of reduced graphene oxide for strengthening and friction reduction in Cu12Sn2Ni bearing composites
Abstract: Simultaneously improving the load-bearing capacity and tribological performance of Cu12Sn2Ni bearing alloys remains challenging because graphene-based reinforcements often suffer from poor dispersion and weak interfacial bonding. Here, reduced graphene oxide (rGO) was modified with Ni, Ag and Ni-Ag coatings and incorporated into a Cu12Sn2Ni matrix by spark plasma sintering. The dual-metal coating was designed to separate the functions of interfacial strengthening and friction regulation. NiAg@rGO/Cu12Sn2Ni exhibited the best combined performance, with a compressive strength of 1087 MPa, 70.9% higher than that of the Cu12Sn2Ni matrix. Its average friction coefficient decreased from 0.86 to 0.32, and its wear rate decreased to 1.19 × 10−5 mm3/(N·m), representing a 69.3% reduction. Microstructural observations and density functional theory calculations show that Ni promotes a metallized rGO-Ni-(Cu,Sn)-Cu transition interface, enhancing interfacial anchoring and load transfer. In contrast, Ag mainly contributes to low-shear lubrication during sliding. Worn-surface analyses further reveal the formation of a carbonaceous/oxide composite tribofilm containing rGO-derived carbon, Ag and Cu/Sn oxides, which suppresses direct metal-to-metal contact and severe delamination. This work demonstrates a dual-metal interfacial design for Cu-based bearing composites with coupled strengthening and friction reduction. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Liu T.; Guan B.; Shen C.; Liu M.; Wen Y.; Hu S.; Chen Y.; Liu G.-S.; Chen Z.; Meng J.; Chen L.; Luo Y.
Title: Particle swarm optimization algorithm assisted general rule metamaterial SPR biosensor design for MMP-9 detection
Abstract: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensors offer in situ, label-free, and real-time detection. They are essential tools for quantitative detection. However, achieving the high sensitivity required for detecting small biomolecules remains highly challenging, particularly in the efficient design of optimized metamaterial-based SPR sensors. This study presents a design framework for general rule metamaterial SPR sensors. The framework transcends the constraints of current metamaterial designs. It enhances design flexibility and minimizes fabrication inaccuracies. The framework requires only the optical properties of 10 materials as input. It then efficiently selects the structure with optimal sensitivity from 1.07 × 1027 possible combinations. The sensitivity improves by 42.5%. The designed metamaterial SPR sensor reduces the detection limit for matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9) from 6.5042 to 0.083 fg/mL. This value is two orders of magnitude lower than that of traditional gold sensors. This design framework provides a universal and cost-effective approach for designing SPR sensors with optimized performance. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zhao X.; Zhang X.; Yang Y.; Luo M.; Li X.
Title: PW9V3 confined in MIL-101(Cr) via V–O–Cr interfacial linkages for enhanced photocatalytic nitrogen reduction
Abstract: Photocatalytic nitrogen fixation can convert N2 to NH3 under mild conditions. However, the high bond energy of the N≡N bond, the tendency of photogenerated charge carriers to recombine, and a lack of active sites severely limit the reaction. POM@MOF composites, which combine tunable electronic structures with spatial confinement effects, have been used in research on photocatalytic nitrogen fixation. In this study, vanadium-substituted Keggin-type polyoxometalates (POMs) PW12−XVX were synthesized to regulate the electronic structure of phosphotungstic acid and were subsequently confined within the cages of MIL-101(Cr) through an in-situ encapsulation strategy. The optimized PW9V3@MIL-101(Cr) photocatalyst achieved an NH3 production rate of 38.31 μmol g-1cat h−1 under simulated sunlight irradiation in air without sacrificial agent, approximately 5.8 times that of pristine MIL-101(Cr). In-situ XPS, EPR, and PL/TRPL measurements confirme that S-scheme heterojunction formed in this system, photoelectrochemical measurements suggest promoted interfacial charge redistribution and charge separation. IR spectroscopy, ground-state XPS analysis, and DFT calculation indicate that PW9V3 preferentially interacts with MIL-101(Cr) through a V–O–Cr interfacial linkage, and the V site shows stronger N2 adsorption, larger electron donation, and greater N–N bond elongation than W sites. Differential charge density and Bader charge analyses suggest electron transfer from the V-centered interfacial region to adsorbed N2, resulting in N≡N bond weakening. In situ DRIFTS measurements provide spectroscopic evidence for possible nitrogen-reduction intermediates and support the proposed photocatalytic N2 reduction pathway. DFT calculations also indicate that the energy barrier for the first-step hydrogenation of the V site is low, whereas the energy barrier for the formation of N2H4 at the V site is high, further confirming that the reaction follows a long-range reaction pathway. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Combustion mode transitions in methanol-diesel partially premixed combustion under varying injection intervals: CNN-enhanced schlieren quantification
Abstract: Diesel-methanol partially premixed combustion (DM-PPC), characterized by prior mixing and controlled auto-ignition, is a promising strategy for improving combustion controllability and extending methanol utilization in compression-ignition engines. However, the spatiotemporal evolution of ignition and flame development under different injection intervals remains insufficiently quantified. In this work, diesel–methanol dual-fuel direct-injection jet flame tests were conducted in a constant-volume chamber at 750 K and 40 bar. Title: Boosting photoelectrocatalytic degradation of tetracycline hydrochloride via rationally designed dual S-scheme g-C3N4/WO3/BiVO4 heterojunctions
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: The efficient remediation of antibiotic contaminants remains a formidable challenge, constrained by their inherent structural stability and resistance to degradation. While photoelectrocatalysis (PEC) represents a potent strategy for degrading refractory organics, its efficacy is frequently limited by sluggish charge carrier separation and deleterious electron-hole recombination. In this work, we report the rational design of a dual S-scheme g-C3N4/WO3/BiVO4 (CN-W-BVO) photoanode with a pore-confined architecture, in which WO3 and g-C3N4 are predominantly confined within the BiVO4 pores via conformal electrodeposition and precursor-derived calcination, respectively. The equilibration of Fermi levels across the dual interfaces induces synergistic built-in electric fields (BIEFs), which drive the selective recombination of low-energy photogenerated carriers while promoting the spatial separation and accumulation of high-potential redox carriers at the distal reactive surfaces, with WO3 serving as the oxidation photocatalyst and BiVO4/g-C3N4 as the reduction photocatalyst. This spatial separation mechanism ensures superior charge-transfer kinetics, as evidenced by the PEC degradation of tetracycline hydrochloride, achieving a degradation efficiency of 89.02% within 120 min at 1.0 V vs. RHE, significantly outperforming both pristine BiVO4 and binary counterparts. Furthermore, the CN-W-BVO architecture demonstrates broad-spectrum efficacy in mineralizing diverse phenolic derivatives. Authors: Yao L.; Li Y.; Cao W.; Zhao Y.
Title: Stabilizing instance-conditioned modality fusion for multi-modal entity alignment
Abstract: Multi-modal entity alignment (MMEA) identifies equivalent entities across different knowledge graphs by fusing multiple sources of information, including graph structure, relations, attributes, and images. Existing work primarily focuses on generating or calibrating entity-level fusion weights, while paying less attention to how these weights evolve and remain stable during joint training. We propose an Instance-Conditioned Modality Fusion (ICMF) framework. The framework assigns a separately parameterized ModalityGate to each modality, generates a fusion score for every entity–modality pair from its uni-modal representation, and normalizes these scores into entity-level fusion weights. To limit excessive polarization of fusion scores during training, we further introduce Dual-Variable Dispersion Control (DVDC), which imposes a budget constraint on the dispersion of fusion scores and adaptively adjusts the penalty strength. Experiments show that ICMF achieves strong alignment performance, exceeding the strongest baseline by 1.4 and 2.3 mean reciprocal rank (MRR) points under low-supervision heterogeneous knowledge-graph settings. In terms of efficiency, its parameter count, representation-generation latency, and inference latency are all the lowest among the evaluated methods. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Guan Y.; Dong H.; Shen Z.; Wu Z.; Hou W.; Piao Z.; Guo Y.; Piazzese J.; Dialami N.; Chiumenti M.; Guo S.; Yan S.; Liang D.; Li H.
Title: Temperature-dependent magneto-tribological behavior and interfacial instability of NdFeB/FKM elastomers
Abstract: Magnetorheological elastomers (MREs) offer a promising route for actively regulating frictional interfaces through magnetic-field-induced changes in stiffness and contact deformation. However, their magneto-tribological response at elevated temperatures remains insufficiently understood because thermal softening of the elastomer matrix and attenuation of magnetic properties occur simultaneously. In this study, isotropic NdFeB/FKM MREs with different magnetic-particle contents were fabricated, and their thermo-magneto-mechanical and tribological responses were investigated over 20–120 °C under magnetic fields up to 400 mT. Dry reciprocating sliding tests against a non-magnetic ceramic counterface showed that increasing temperature reduced hardness, tensile strength, storage modulus, saturation magnetization, remanence, and coercivity, while increasing the mean friction coefficient, friction fluctuations, and wear volume. Applying a magnetic field generally reduced friction and wear and improved sliding stability throughout the investigated temperature range. MRE-70 exhibited the strongest field-induced regulation, with reductions of approximately 10–12% in friction coefficient and 9–13% in wear volume under 400 mT. Nevertheless, the regulation efficiency decreased progressively with temperature. This deterioration resulted from the combined effects of matrix softening, which enhanced interfacial deformation and adhesion–slip behavior, and magnetic attenuation, which weakened field-induced reinforcement and load-bearing support. Surface observations further indicated that elevated temperature increased the extent and continuity of Schallamach-wave-related deformation, whereas the magnetic field disrupted such deformation and mitigated frictional instability. These findings clarify the competing roles of thermal softening and magnetic reinforcement in governing the temperature-dependent tribological behavior of NdFeB/FKM MREs and support the design of actively tunable friction interfaces for thermally variable service conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Enriched finite element method for Poisson equations
Abstract: We develop an enriched finite element method for the Poisson equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Starting from the standard linear Lagrangian finite element, the local approximation space is enriched by three functions associated with edge-average degrees of freedom. The construction is presented within the Ciarlet framework, and the conditions ensuring local admissibility and global conformity are examined. Two new two-parameter families of weighted enrichment functions, based on Jacobi-type weights, are introduced, and explicit expressions for the corresponding local basis functions are derived. For one of these families, an explicit L2-error estimate is obtained for the enriched interpolation operator, with a constant depending on the enrichment parameters. For conforming enriched spaces containing the standard linear finite element space, the error of the enriched Galerkin approximation in the energy norm is proved to be no greater than that of the standard linear approximation. The numerical study compares the proposed enriched elements with the standard linear and quadratic Lagrangian finite elements on regular and nonuniform triangulations. The numerical results show that the most effective enrichment, as well as the choice of the Jacobi weight parameters, depends on the problem under consideration. The numerical examples include heat-conduction problems and a prescribed-crack problem with a singular solution at the crack tip. © 2026 The Author(s). Published by Elsevier Inc. Authors: Salari E.; Dai L.
Title: 3D-printed architected sandwich spherical meta-shells with bamboo fiber reinforced PLA composite face-sheets: Snap-through instability and dynamic performance
Abstract: Understanding snap-through instability and dynamic behavior is vital for designing lightweight, damage-tolerant components and preventing catastrophic failure in structural applications. This study presents a comprehensive analytical, experimental, as well as numerical investigation of the nonlinear snap-through instability and dynamic behavior of 3D-printed architected sandwich spherical meta-shells with bamboo fiber-reinforced polylactic acid (PLA) composite face-sheets. The proposed structure combines lightweight architected star-shaped cellular cores with sustainable bio-composite face-sheets to achieve enhanced stiffness, stability, and vibration performance. Using Hamilton's principle, a nonlinear shell model is established within the framework of the First-Order Shear Deformation Theory (FSDT), while geometric nonlinearity is represented through the von-Kármán formulation. The governing equations are solved through the Ritz method employing Chebyshev polynomial expansion, while the cylindrical arc-length technique is adopted to accurately trace complex snap-through equilibrium paths. The present work investigates the influence of two practically important loading conditions, namely concentrated loading (CL) and uniformly distributed loading (UDL), on the nonlinear snap-through response of architected spherical meta-shells. The analytical model is first verified against benchmark solutions available in the literature. Additionally, a 3D finite element model is developed to capture the true physical dynamic behavior of the complex architected geometry, which is evaluated experimentally through impact hammer modal testing on a baseline pure PLA fused deposition modeling (FDM)-fabricated specimen. Following these evaluations, an extensive parametric study is carried out to examine the influence of shell geometry, architected core characteristics, thickness ratio, fiber volume fraction, loading scenarios, and support conditions on nonlinear vibration and snap-through responses. The developed bio-inspired architected sandwich meta-shells offer an efficient lightweight alternative for multifunctional structural systems that demand enhanced stability, excellent energy absorption, and outstanding dynamic performance. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Pan Y.; Yan M.; Li D.; Yang J.; Qian J.
Title: Multi-view collaborative consistency for light field depth estimation
Abstract: Light field (LF) depth estimation recovers scene geometry from densely sampled views. Recent methods can achieve low mean squared error (MSE) while retaining a high bad-pixel rate (BPR) in difficult regions. Occlusion, weak texture, and view-dependent reflectance make cross-view matching unreliable in these regions. We use Multi-view Consistency Collapse (MCC) to denote this localized loss of reliable cross-view matching. To reduce the resulting errors, we propose CARNet (Collapse-Aware Refinement Network), a coarse-to-refined model with three components. The Consistency-Sensitive Feature Module (CSFM) combines adaptive low-pass filtering with high-frequency residual enhancement. The Multi-view Collapse Risk Map (MCRM) derives view-specific confidence weights from forward-warp residuals, reverse-warp residuals, and local texture. These weights scale the corresponding warped features during residual cost-volume construction. The Collapse-Prioritized Supervision Objective (CPSO) combines global L1, a differentiable BPR surrogate with stochastic pixel weighting, and spectral consistency at both prediction stages. We evaluate CARNet on the HCI 4D Benchmark and UrbanLF-Syn, and test CPSO as a training-only objective on two LF depth backbones without changing their inference architectures. On the HCI 4D Benchmark, CARNet records the lowest average BP1, BP3, BP7, and MSE among the compared methods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Song M.; Zhang S.; Dai W.; Chen J.; Zhang X.; Yin C.; Yuan W.
Title: Effects of coexisting H2 and CO in O2 atmosphere on microscopic combustion reaction characteristics of bituminous coal molecules via ReaxFF MD simulation
Abstract: Injecting gases rich in H2 and CO into blast furnaces offers a promising pathway for low-carbon ironmaking by significantly reducing carbon emissions. However, previous macro-scale computational fluid dynamics simulations have indicated severe oxygen competition between the injected gases and coal, yet have failed to capture the underlying molecular-level interactions. Crucially, the coupling impacts of coexisting H2 and CO on key oxidizing species and the surface chemical environment during coal combustion remain entirely unexplored, leaving the microscopic competitive combustion mechanism of gases and solid carbon unclear. In this study, weight loss, non-bonding interactions, radical evolution, and reaction frequencies during coal combustion were investigated using ReaxFF MD simulation, thereby revealing the synergistic mechanism underlying the influence of injected H2 and CO on coal combustion. Results show that adding CO suppresses early-stage coal combustion via consuming ⋅OH, which inhibits ring-opening and oxidation of coal and via non-bonding interactions that form a steric hindrance on the coal surface to block effective O2 collisions. In the H2, CO and O2 mixed atmosphere, increasing the H2 ratio mitigates ⋅OH depletion. Nevertheless, the steric hindrance exerted by CO persists, resulting in a lower initial burn rate compared to pure O2 conditions. This study provides theoretical insights for co-injecting gas and pulverized coal in blast furnaces. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Environmental performance of hydrogen production via eucalyptus biomass gasification and natural gas steam reforming: A life cycle assessment approach
Abstract: A life cycle assessment (LCA) was conducted to compare hydrogen production via steam methane reforming (SMR) of natural gas and eucalyptus biomass gasification under Brazilian conditions. Three scenarios were evaluated for the production of 1 kg of hydrogen: (i) SMR, (ii) SMR with carbon capture and storage (SMR-CCS), and (iii) Gasification-WGS (eucalyptus gasification with water–gas shift reaction). The ReCiPe 2016 midpoint method was applied, with normalization used to identify the most relevant impact categories. Global warming potential (GWP) was confirmed as the most critical category by both midpoint and endpoint results. SMR generated 10.13 kg CO2-eq, SMR-CCS 6.40 kg CO2-eq, and Gasification–WGS 1.30 kg CO2-eq per kg of hydrogen, corresponding to reductions of 36.8% and 87.2% relative to conventional SMR, respectively. Carbon capture reduced the climate impact of the fossil route but did not result in net-negative emissions. SMR-CCS showed higher burdens than conventional SMR in seventeen of the eighteen impact categories assessed, most markedly in water consumption (14.1-fold) and land use (8.5-fold), the latter arising from the biomass-fired cogeneration supplying MEA regeneration heat. Gasification-WGS achieved the lowest climate impact but did not dominate across all indicators: it outperformed conventional SMR in nine of the eighteen categories and underperformed in the remaining nine, most notably in land use (37-fold), water consumption (3.8-fold), marine eutrophication (2.3-fold) and freshwater ecotoxicity (2.2-fold). The comparison therefore describes a trade-off in which the biomass route exchanges carbon and fossil resources for land, water and nutrient pressure. Overall, the results indicate that the preferred pathway depends on which environmental priority dominates in a given region: eucalyptus gasification offers the largest climate and fossil-resource benefit, while carbon capture on the fossil route delivers a smaller climate gain at the cost of increased impacts in nearly every other category. By addressing both climate mitigation and resource sustainability, this study provides guidance for policymakers and industry in developing low-carbon hydrogen pathways adapted to regional conditions. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Investigation on the performance of bimetallic catalysts for methanol-to-aromatics: Active site regulation and enhancement of formaldehyde-mediated reaction pathways
Abstract: Methanol-to-aromatics (MTA) technology represents an important approach for the efficient utilization of coal resources; however, conventional ZSM-5 zeolites suffer from low BTX selectivity and susceptibility to coking deactivation. This paper proposes a bimetallic co-impregnation strategy that directs methanol conversion toward a formaldehyde-mediated Prins aromatization pathway by tuning the distribution of active sites and the reaction pathway. The optimized ZnNi/Z5 catalyst exhibits excellent performance in a fixed-bed reactor: BTX selectivity reaches 56.54%, methanol conversion remains at 100% for 32.0 h, total lifetime extends to 45.3 h, and coke deposition is only 9.79%, significantly lower than that of monometallic Zn/Z5 (24.03%). Combining density functional theory (DFT) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, the microscopic mechanism of the bimetallic synergy is revealed: the introduction of Ni promotes the formation of highly active Zn(OH)+ species (increasing their proportion from 61% to 70%), optimizes the acid strength distribution, and regulates the adsorption and diffusion behaviors of key intermediates such as CH2O and C2H4O, enhancing CH2O diffusion capacity and tuning the d-band center position, thereby supporting the formaldehyde-mediated selective aromatization pathway. This study provides new insights into metal synergy and reaction pathway engineering, as well as a theoretical basis for the design of high-performance MTA catalysts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Rajamani R.P.; Deepankumar K.
Title: Intelligent pH-responsive colorimetric films based on κ-carrageenan/grape peel extract for real time monitoring of food freshness
Abstract: The need for innovative packaging solutions have fuelled the research in indicator films from natural sources. In this study, an intelligent pH-responsive colorimetric film has been developed based on κ-carrageenan, Myristica fragrans extract (MFE) and grape peel extract (GPE). The κ-carrageenan act as a biopolymer matrix, GPE, composed of anthocyanin rich compounds act as the main pH indicator and MFE imparts color stability which helps to maintain the anthocyanin compounds present GPE in flavylium cation form, enabling swift response to pH change induced by volatile amine groups released from the spoiled food. The indicator films showed excellent UV protection and water barrier properties. The incorporation of MFE aided in enhancement of mechanical properties and hydrophobicity of indicator films enabling its storage at 25°C and 4°C. The film exhibited distinguishable color changes from pale red to red or violet and to blue or green, clearly indicating the distinct phases of food condition. The indicator film showed visual color changes for packaged shrimp, tuna, mushroom and milk stored at 25°C and 4°C. The TVB-N values, microbial load, MDA content and pH of packaged samples were in accordance with the color change of indicator films giving conclusive information on the status of food real time. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Investigation of a rapid coking formation mechanism based on conjugated stable radicals
Abstract: To elucidate the kinetic pathways of aviation fuel pyrolysis and coking formation, a new kinetic mechanism designated as CKL-Soot is developed based on high-level electronic structure calculations and elementary reaction analysis. The mechanism is initiated by acetylene addition to conjugated cyclopentadienyl radicals generated under pyrolytic conditions, and proceeds stepwise toward the formation of a fundamental carbonaceous structural unit, denoted as ST1R. Subsequently, ST1R undergoes aggregation processes that lead to the growth of larger carbonaceous structures, where weak intermolecular interactions between aggregates are explicitly considered. The CKL-Soot mechanism is constructed using a set of 16 reversible elementary reactions involving exclusively conjugated radical species, which enables carbonaceous intermediates to achieve both chemical stability and sustained reactivity while maintaining computational efficiency for engineering-scale simulations. All reaction pathways are validated through high-level electronic structure analyses, including the characterization of π–π stacking interactions between two ST1R units (interaction energy: 115.00 kJ/mol), wavefunction analysis of conjugated radical species, thermodynamic data acquisition and processing, and systematic evaluation of kinetic parameters. Experimentally, a constant-volume chamber system is established, in which the mass of carbonaceous products formed during bulk-phase coking is measured using the light extinction method. The experimental results show that coking yield increases monotonically with temperature from 1000 K to 1200 K. With increasing reaction time, the coking yield rises and approaches a steady state after approximately 500 ms. Comparison between simulations and experiments demonstrates that at 1000 K, the coking amount predicted by the CKL-Soot mechanism agrees with experimental results in both magnitude and temporal evolution. Title: Insights into product regulation and catalyst deactivation mechanisms during catalytic fast pyrolysis of cotton stalk: The influence of molecular sieve topology
Abstract: Molecular sieve represents one of the most promising catalysts for producing high‑value sustainable chemicals from biomass via catalytic fast pyrolysis (CFP). To elucidate how molecular sieve topology influences product distribution and catalyst deactivation in biomass CFP, this study systematically investigated the performance of 10 molecular sieves with different pore apertures (small-, medium-, large-pore, and mesoporous) and channel dimensionality (1D, 2D, and 3D) during the CFP of cotton stalk. Results indicate that pore aperture size is associated with variations in the distribution of pyrolysis products, particularly the composition of bio‑oil. Compared to 8-membered ring (MR), 12‑MR and mesoporous, the 3D 10‑MR channel structure exhibited the highest relative GC–MS peak-area fractions of monocyclic aromatics (MAs, 70 %), benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylenes (BTEX, 63.2 %), along with the lowest coke deposition (2 %). To further probe these complex conversion behaviors, we integrated Py-GC/MS analysis using cellulose and lignin model compounds with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. The MD results indicate that the dimensionality and connectivity of the zeolite channels significantly influence the diffusion behavior of biomass pyrolysis volatiles within the pores. TG and GC–MS analyses further indicated that spent molecular sieves with different topologies contained similar extractable coke species, suggesting a similar terminal aromatic condensation tendency. Title: Fuzzy logic-enhanced membership Mamba for hyperspectral and LiDAR data classification
Abstract: In recent years, the Mamba framework, with its ability to balance long-range dependency modeling and low-complexity feature learning, has attracted increasing attention in the field of joint classification of hyperspectral images (HSI) and LiDAR data. However, existing Mamba-based methods tend to introduce interference from heterogeneous pixels at class boundaries when dividing patches centered on target pixels, and their robustness to noise remains limited, making it difficult to maintain reliable classification performance in complex scenarios. To this end, we propose a fuzzy logic-enhanced membership mamba network (FLEMamba) for HSI and LiDAR joint classification. Specifically, FLEMamba extracts global features through a multi-scale membership Mamba module and weights the pixels within each patch according to their membership values, thereby enhancing target-class representations while suppressing interference from heterogeneous pixels. Subsequently, local features are extracted through a fuzzy convolution module, which, combined with fuzzy activation and fuzzy pooling mechanisms, further enhances the model's robustness against noise interference and data distribution variations, thereby reducing the risk of overfitting. Finally, the extracted features are employed for classification, effectively improving both robustness and accuracy. Extensive experiments on three public datasets demonstrate the superior classification performance of the proposed method compared with several state-of-the-art methods. © 2026

Title: A bi-objective optimization model to plan vaccination campaigns aided by temporary centers
Abstract: Vaccination campaigns have saved thousands of lives and reached even the world's most remote areas. However, the COVID-19 pandemic significantly changed the strategies for such campaigns. It is now crucial to rigorously consider new factors when planning the operational aspects of these campaigns, particularly for last-mile vaccine dispensing. First, a large share of the population must be vaccinated, with emphasis on vulnerable groups at higher risk. Second, if the virus is highly contagious and capable of asymptomatic transmission, implementing public health measures at vaccination sites becomes paramount. To address these challenges, we propose a bi-objective optimization model to support healthcare decision-making. It defines a schedule for locating temporary vaccination centers and assigning populations to permanent and temporary sites over a planning horizon. Moreover, we formalize and validate a minimum set of properties for a function-based prioritization mechanism to ensure consistent prioritization. One objective prioritizes vaccinating vulnerable groups according to our novel function-based approach, while the other minimizes the operational costs of temporary centers. In the complex environment of a pandemic, the strategic integration and use of temporary and permanent vaccination centers is vital for creating a robust and responsive vaccination strategy. Temporary centers, whose locations are determined by the model, improve access for hard-to-reach groups, contribute to minimizing crowding at permanent sites, and lower infection risks. Our results, demonstrated through a case study, show that the model effectively allocates resources and generates various vaccination plans that cater to different priority levels assigned to each objective, thereby offering valuable decision support. © 2026 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.
