Title: Two-step activation of MoS2 basal plane via P-doping and conducting polymer interface enabling tunable multilayer HER electrodes
Abstract: Molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) is a promising non‑precious electrocatalyst for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER); however, its catalytic activity is largely confined to the edge sites, leaving the abundant basal plane inert. Herein, we report a two‑step strategy to activate the basal plane of MoS2 by combining phosphorus (P) doping with conducting polymer interface engineering. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that P doping modifies the electronic structure of MoS2, and subsequent interfacial coupling with conducting polymers (polyaniline (PANI) or polypyrrole (PPy)) induces directional electron transfer, enriching the basal plane with electrons. This synergistic modulation significantly optimizes the hydrogen adsorption Gibbs free energy (ΔGH*) on S, Mo, and P sites within the basal plane. To translate this intrinsic activity enhancement into macroscopically tunable electrodes, we employed layer–by–layer (LbL) assembly to fabricate flexible (conducting polymer/P@MoS2)n multilayer films on carbon cloth. The HER performance exhibits a strong dependence on the number of bilayers (n), initially increasing with n and reaching an optimum at n = 16. The optimized (PANI/P@MoS2)16-CC and (PPy/P@MoS2)16-CC electrodes deliver low overpotentials of 168 and 164 mV at 10 mA cm−2 in 0.5 M H2SO4, with small Tafel slopes of 47 and 45 mV dec−1, respectively. Electrochemical surface area analysis confirms high double-layer capacitance values (58.8 and 67.4 mF cm−2), indicating abundant accessible active sites. Moreover, both electrodes exhibit acceptable long-term durability, retaining over 90% of their initial activity after 1000 cyclic voltammetry cycles and maintaining stable current output during 50 h chronoamperometric measurements. When integrated into a solar-driven thermoelectric device, the system enables steady H2 production. Authors: Lv M.; Lu P.; Zhao Y.; Li Z.; Wu L.; Wang S.; Li S.; Wang C.; Shi X.; Gao J.; Lan X.
Title: Simulation study of mass-heat transfer matching in gas-solid fluidized beds
Abstract: Against the background of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, Fluid Catalytic Cracking (FCC) is being driven toward enhanced production of light olefins. This requires improving catalytic cracking efficiency while suppressing undesired thermal cracking. However, gas–solid flow, heat and mass transfer, and reactions are strongly coupled in FCC reactors, and product distribution is significantly affected by the reactor flow regime and transport performance. Conventional risers operate in the transport-bed regime, where non-uniform radial temperature and concentration fields make it difficult to achieve both high cracking severity and favorable product selectivity. Therefore, clarifying the relationship between hydrodynamics and transport mechanisms in different reactor types is important for advanced FCC reactor design. In this study, the gas–solid flow, heat transfer, and mass transfer characteristics in a riser, a fast fluidized bed (FFB), and a turbulent fluidized bed (TFB) were systematically investigated. A radial uniformity index (RUI) and radial uniformity rate index (RURI) were proposed to quantify radial transport performance. The results show that transport in the riser is dominated by axial convection, leading to insufficient radial transport, while the core-annulus structure restricts radial heat transfer. In contrast, enhanced gas–solid mixing in the FFB and TFB promotes radial mass and heat transfer, and higher solids holdup further strengthens heat transfer. As a result, the radial heat-transfer RUI is slightly higher than the radial mass-transfer RUI in both the FFB and TFB. Based on RURI evaluation, the FFB shows the highest radial mass-transfer performance, whereas the riser is the lowest. Compared with the riser, the radial mass-transfer RURI values in the FFB and TFB are 71% and 63% higher than that in the riser, respectively. The FFB and TFB show comparable heat transfer performance, with their radial heat-transfer RURI values nearly 120% higher than that of the riser. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Dual-mode microfluidic RELS-QCM platform for label-free profiling of mitochondrial preparations from a graded stress model
Abstract: Rapid comparison of fragile isolated organelles requires consistent sample handling and concentration normalization. We present a polycarbonate microfluidic platform that sequentially combines resonance elastic light scattering (RELS) and quartz crystal microbalance (QCM) sensing of the same unstained mitochondrial suspension. Title: Tribo-dynamic coupling effect on transient transmission efficiency of fixed-axis three-split reducer
Abstract: A fixed-axis three-split reducer (FTSR) with high-load capacity, compactness, and high power density, is used in some equipment. The proposed efficiency model is validated against the bench-test efficiency measurement. The numerical results demonstrate that the tribo-dynamic coupling effect significantly reduces the meshing friction power loss and attenuates high-frequency fluctuations of FTSR efficiency compared with the dry-dynamic coupling state. The transmission efficiency varies non-monotonically with input speed, input power, and lubricant viscosity, whereas it decreases with increasing surface roughness. Title: Dissimilar autogenous electron beam welding for nuclear applications:316L joined to 10CrMo9-10
Abstract: This study investigates the micromechanical characteristics and behaviour of an autogenous electron beam welding between AISI Type 316 L stainless steel and 10CrMo9-10 ferritic steel. Conventionally, the dissimilar joints for these materials, which are prevalent in thermal energy generation plants, use a nickel-based alloy filler to reduce the adverse effect of thermal expansion mismatch observed between austenitic and ferritic steels. However, traditional welding technologies have disadvantages, including large fusion and heat-affected zones, unpredictable defects, and human factors that influence the weld quality. Some of these disadvantages can be mitigated using advanced welding methods such as electron beam welding (EBW). The fundamental question this paper contributes to answering is assessing the risk associated with the structural integrity of dissimilar welds produced using autogenous EBW processes. To this end, microstructural analysis on the 316 L to 10CrMo9-10 weld revealed well-defined interfaces with minimal elemental diffusion and distinct grain morphologies across the welding zone and parent metals. This analysis is completed with the residual stress measurements across the weld using neutron diffraction, impacted by the dissimilar properties of both base metals. Mechanical testing, including tensile and creep-fatigue tests with local strain measured using digital image correlation, quantified the thermomechanical behaviour across the weld and parent materials. Tensile testing revealed a strain gradient distribution related to the differences in the microstructure and the thermomechanical stability of the fusion zone. Failure was notably located outside the fusion and heat-affected zones, within the parent 10CrMo9-10 material. Creep-fatigue tests performed at 550 °C demonstrated acceptable weldment performance at elevated temperatures, with no failure observed within the cycles to failure predicted for this joint using conventional design code limits. Authors: Csató L.
Title: How to optimise tournament draws: The case of the FIFA World Cup
Abstract: The organisers of major sports competitions use different policies with respect to constraints in the group draw. Our paper aims to rationalise these choices by analysing the trade-off between attractiveness (the number of games played by teams from the same geographic zone) and fairness (the departure of the draw mechanism from a uniform distribution). A parametric optimisation model is formulated and applied to the 2018 and 2022 FIFA World Cup draws. A flaw of the draw procedure is identified: the pre-assignment of the host to a group unnecessarily increases the distortions. All Pareto efficient sets of draw constraints are determined via simulations. The proposed framework can be used to find the optimal draw rules and justify the non-uniformity of the draw procedure for the stakeholders. © 2026 The Author(s). Authors: Xiong S.; Guo Q.; Wang M.; Li R.; Li Q.; Zhou J.; Guo H.
Title: Fluorescent molecularly imprinted nanoparticles-based paper sensor for rapid detection of Staphylococcus aureus
Abstract: A fluorescent molecularly imprinted polymer (FMIP)-based paper sensor was constructed for rapid detection of Staphylococcus aureus ( S. aureus ). The FMIP nanoparticles were prepared by the boronate affinity imprinting strategy based on the interactions between the cell-surface biomolecules and the functional monomer with phenylboronic acid groups. Then, such FMIP nanoparticles were modified with amino groups for subsequent covalently grafting onto the aldehyde-functionalized paper surface, enabling its specific recognition capability to S. aureus . The paper sensor can specifically recognize the target bacteria in 5 min with an imprinting factor as high as 14.0. Such paper sensor can quantitatively detect S. aureus in the range of 102-106 CFU/mL with a detection limit of 77 CFU/mL, and gave spiked recoveries of 87%-116% in real samples. Title: Fusion-driven geometry-constrained latent flow learning for robust AUV motion anticipation from heterogeneous 3D observations
Abstract: Reliable motion anticipation for autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) is challenging when heterogeneous observations are sparse, asynchronous, corrupted, or intermittently unavailable, and when sensing statistics differ between simulation and real deployment. This paper proposes PIG-Dyn, a reliability-aware geometry-constrained latent flow framework for AUV motion anticipation from heterogeneous 3D observations. Timestamped observations are transformed into a common ego-centric frame and assigned learned reliability scores according to availability, acquisition age, and observation quality. Masked reliability-aware attention then fuses the observations into functionally differentiated latent subspaces representing scene geometry, vehicle–environment interaction, ego-motion, and disturbance-related residuals. In parallel, a local geometric belief field preserves occupancy, free-space, directional, and traversal-risk cues and directly conditions the continuous latent vector field. The latent dynamics employ skew-symmetric conservative and positive-semidefinite dissipative operators within a port-structured parameterization. The conservative term contributes zero power to a learned storage function, whereas dissipation is non-positive in the autonomous unforced case. Control, disturbance, and geometry-conditioned effects are modeled as external ports and softly regulated through a finite-step storage-balance objective. Latent uncertainty is propagated through the discrete transition map using a first-order diagonal Gaussian approximation and decoded into future position, orientation, and velocity. Sim-to-real transfer is encouraged by aligning predictive latent moments and batch-averaged transition sensitivities rather than raw sensor appearance. Title: Comprehensive performance assessment of proton exchange membrane fuel cells with fractal gas distribution zones and non-aligned wavy gas-cooling channels
Abstract: Enhancing the performance and durability of proton exchange membrane fuel cells requires a comprehensive understanding of the coupled transport, thermal, and electrochemical processes occurring within the cell. The simulations reveal that the hydrogen distribution in the anode FF remains nearly homogeneous, with a maximum concentration variation of only 1.69%. By contrast, the wavy cathode FF induces pronounced spatial heterogeneity in oxygen transport, with concentration variations of 8.51%-19.45%, while also increasing the likelihood of water accumulation near the outlet. Compared with the co-flow mode, the counter-flow arrangement causes only a negligible voltage loss of 0.0001 V, yet promotes a more uniform water distribution in the cathode through enhanced cross-convective transport, which is favorable for sustained stable operation. Elevating the operating pressure to 3.0 atm increases the net power density by as much as 30.2%; however, it simultaneously aggravates localized reactant depletion and non-uniform membrane hydration. When the coolant flow direction is aligned with the oxygen flow direction, heat dissipation from the bipolar plates is strengthened, high-temperature regions within the membrane are reduced, and liquid water retention in the cathode channels is mitigated, leading to a voltage improvement of 0.0021 V. Title: Adversarial contrastive multi-view clustering via representation enhancement guided by reconstruction
Abstract: Deep multi-view clustering (DMVC) learns unified and discriminative representations from multiple views to reveal consistent clustering structures. However, existing DMVC methods face two challenges: (1) many operate directly on original views, making learning highly dependent on view quality and limited by the information in the inputs; (2) contrastive learning methods for DMVC usually rely on batch negatives, which are not sufficiently challenging and thus provide limited guidance for learning discriminative decision boundaries. The reconstruction error is used as a relative cue to indicate how well the current latent representation preserves the structural information of each view, and this cue guides the construction of an enhanced latent representation that complements the original views. The enhanced representation is trained jointly with the original views under reconstruction and contrastive objectives, improving consistency learning. In addition, a generator synthesizes view-specific hard negatives to strengthen discriminability, while distribution alignment preserves semantic coherence across views. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of ACRE-MVC in improving clustering performance. The code is available at https://github.com/anhuiyanglihao/ACRE_MVC. © 2026

Title: Low-valence NbOx-supported Ni3P for furfural hydrogenation and rearrangement to cyclopentanone
Abstract: The catalytic hydrogenation and rearrangement of furfural to cyclopentanone is of considerable industrial relevance, yet achieving high performance with cost-effective catalysts remains challenging. Detailed characterization indicates that Ni3P sites exhibit superior activity compared to metallic Ni. Phosphidation of the active nickel metal enhances surface acidity, which facilitates the ring-opening step, while the reduced NbOx provides abundant oxygen vacancies. Under mild conditions (130 °C, 2 MPa H2, 4 h), the catalyst achieves complete conversion of furfural and a cyclopentanone yield of 94.8%, which is among the best reported values. Title: A hybrid framework for cetane number prediction: integrating a novel cetane index formula with explainable machine learning

Title: Biomass-derived N-doped hollow carbon nanospheres anchored PdAu nanoparticles for efficient hydrogen generation via formic acid decomposition

Title: Pressurized H2O/O2 coal partial gasification for H2/CH4-rich syngas: Multi-objective optimization via autothermal Aspen plus modeling and response surface methodology

Title: A data-driven surrogate framework for predicting axial dynamic-pressure distributions at resonant modes in a model gas turbine combustor

Title: Implementation and verification of a thermal-hydraulic-mechanical model based on fractional seepage theory in ABAQUS

Title: Effects of CO2 jet injection on methane explosion dynamics and flame propagation in a confined pipeline
Abstract: Methane explosions in confined environments often occur under spatially inhomogeneous methane–air mixture conditions. As the injection pressure increases, the flame front becomes progressively unstable, showing deformation and fragmentation. Title: High interfacial shear resistance and controlled wear of shear-adaptive mixed-valence MoOx interfaces in entangled metallic networks

Title: Insights into the nanopore characteristics and synergistic effects of coal, biomass, and co-pyrolysis chars using very small-angle neutron scattering

Title: Multi-behavior popularity-aware recommendation
Abstract: Recommender systems (RSs) face a persistent challenge known as popularity bias, which is characterized by the systematic over-recommendation of popular items and under-recommendation of long-tail or new items. This issue has been addressed in existing single-behavior recommendations, which mainly focus on mitigating popularity bias in the final interaction (such as purchasing). Multiple behaviors of users typically exhibit sequential dependencies across multiple stages (e.g., browsing → adding to cart → purchasing). However, existing multi-behavior recommendations fail to sufficiently leverage these relationships to effectively address popularity bias. In this paper, we propose a multi-behavior popularity-aware recommendation to alleviate the above problem. We explore the role of user sequential behavioral relationships in alleviating popularity bias from two perspectives: items and users. From the perspective of items, we redefine popularity under multi-behavior. We calculate the item popularity by counting the number of user-item interactions, such as browsing, adding to cart, and purchasing. From the user’s perspective, we calculate the user’s attention to the item popularity and divide all users into conservatives and trend-followers by their attention. Subsequently, we design a popularity-matching loss to influence the recommendation probability. It represents the matching degree between the two kinds of followers’ preferences and the popularity of the target item. Finally, we rank the probabilities of all target items and provide a recommendation list for the user. Elevated temperature (750 °C) and load (5 N) jointly trigger cracking, spallation, and subsequent oxidative wear of the oxide film. As the temperature increased from 150 °C to 750 °C, the slope of the E d-wear rate fitting line gradually increased, implying a decreasing resistance of the material to wear. MD simulations and radial distribution function (RDF) analysis demonstrate that elevated temperature and normal load synergistically aggravate the breakage of interfacial chemical bonds and lattice distortion, endowing the worn zone with the characteristic amorphous structure of short-range order and long-range disorder. Authors: Lin Y.; Li S.; Ma Y.; Shao D.; Jiang W.; Yang J.; Wang P.
Title: Conformational restriction-engineered near-infrared fluorescent probe for tracking viscosity dynamics during ferroptosis in sepsis
Abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening inflammatory response to infection and is increasingly linked to dysregulated iron metabolism and ferroptosis. Monitoring the viscosity dynamics during ferroptosis is crucial for understanding sepsis progression. This work presents a novel near-infrared fluorescent probe ROBN for highly selective and sensitive detection of microenvironmental viscosity. Due to the conformational restrictions imposed by the rigid plane formed by the julolidine group, ROBN is regulated by the twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT) mechanism and exhibits a significant 44-fold fluorescence increase in high-viscosity environments. This probe exhibits low cytotoxicity and could effectively monitor viscosity changes in various cell lines, especially in mitochondria. Furthermore, ROBN enabled the visualization of elevated viscosity associated with ferroptosis in the inflammatory model of cells and zebrafish induced by LPS. Importantly, it was successfully employed in monitoring sepsis progression and organ-specific viscosity changes in the mouse sepsis model. This probe provides a powerful tool for real-time tracking of viscosity alterations during sepsis and offers valuable insights into ferroptosis mechanisms and potential diagnostic strategies for sepsis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Guo J.; Cui M.; Yang H.; Long K.; Li X.; Qin M.; Yu H.; Zhang T.

Title: A Multi-task Sparse Adversarial Training framework for autonomous driving in harsh conditions
Abstract: Autonomous driving has emerged as one of the most transformative applications of artificial intelligence and computer vision, offering the potential to improve transportation safety, efficiency, and sustainability. Despite remarkable advances, ensuring reliable perception under adverse weather conditions and defending against adversarial perturbations remain major challenges. Moreover, the limited computation resources of resource-aware perception platforms demand efficient yet robust models capable of real-time performance. To address these issues, we propose a novel Multi-Task Sparse Adversarial Training (MTSAT) framework that unifies multi-task learning, adversarial training, and dynamic sparse training into a single end-to-end paradigm. The core idea is to simultaneously enhance model robustness and efficiency through a constrained min–max optimization strategy that enforces sparsity during adversarial training. Specifically, MTSAT jointly minimizes multi-task losses while maximizing resistance to adversarial perturbations, enabling the model to learn robust shared representations across perception tasks such as semantic segmentation, part segmentation, and disparity estimation. Furthermore, a dynamic sparse training mechanism adaptively prunes and regrows network connections to achieve compact and computation-efficient models that are suitable for resource-constrained environments. Experiments on Cityscapes, Foggy Cityscapes, and Rainy Cityscapes demonstrate that MTSAT achieves improved overall multi-task performance over the evaluated baselines, while maintaining high model sparsity. These findings highlight the importance of balanced multi-task adversarial modeling and provide critical insights into evaluating, diagnosing, and strengthening autonomous driving systems under different weather conditions. Future work will further validate the proposed framework on real-world datasets by leveraging proxy annotations and unified multi-task evaluation protocols. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: An innovative UBFEM–ANN approach for slope stability evaluation and slip surface prediction of frictional soil slopes
Abstract: To address the limitations of existing machine learning approaches in simultaneously predicting slope stability and failure characteristics, this study proposes an efficient framework for slope failure characteristic prediction by integrating upper-bound finite element limit analysis (UBFEM) with an artificial neural network (ANN). A local six-node, sixfold-path discontinuous triangular mesh is employed to exploit the complementary advantages of plastic elements and velocity discontinuities in critical slip surface identification. The sliding body is subsequently identified based on velocity discontinuities, enabling the construction of a high-fidelity dataset of primary slope failure characteristics. A dataset comprising 1008 parameter combinations of classical homogeneous frictional soil slopes is used to train the machine learning models. The results demonstrate that the optimized model maintains excellent predictive performance across different slope geometries and soil strength conditions, achieving an R2 of 0.999 and an RMSE of 0.356 for critical unit weight prediction, while the mean relative error MRE of the sliding body area prediction is only 0.036. Furthermore, the Hausdorff distance is employed to quantify error propagation during the reconstruction of the critical slip surface, while permutation feature importance (PFI) and SHapley additive explanations (SHAP) are combined to quantitatively evaluate the effects of input parameters on slope stability and slip surface geometry. The proposed UBFEM–ANN framework therefore provides an effective and interpretable approach for predicting slope stability, critical slip surface geometry, and sliding body area. © 2026

Title: Domino synthesis of an AIE-active pyrazolo[3,4-j][1,7]phenanthroline for reversible Hg2+ binding and fluorescence sensing in aqueous media
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: An aggregation-induced emission (AIE)-active heteroaromatic fluorophore, 2-amino-4-(4-( tert -butyl)phenyl)-10-methyl-8-phenyl-6,8-dihydro-5 H -pyrazolo[3,4- j ][1,7]phenanthroline-3‑carbonitrile ( PPCN ), was synthesized via a green one-pot domino strategy and evaluated as a fluorescent probe for Hg2+ detection in aqueous media. PPCN exhibits pronounced solvent-dependent emission with positive solvatochromism and large Stokes shifts, consistent with an intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) mechanism. Under AIE conditions, fluorescence is significantly enhanced due to restriction of intramolecular motions. The probe demonstrates excellent selectivity toward Hg2+ with negligible interference from competing metal ions and enables rapid, real-time fluorescence monitoring of Hg2+ under aqueous sensing conditions. Fluorescence quenching is predominantly attributed to ground-state complex formation between PPCN and Hg2+. Owing to the strong heavy-atom character of Hg2+, enhanced spin-orbit coupling and intersystem crossing may also contribute to non-radiative deactivation after complex formation. Stern-Volmer analysis performed using a revised experimental calibration yielded a quenching constant of 1.003 × 105 M−1 with excellent linearity (R2 = 0.99886) and an experimentally determined limit of detection (LOD) of 119 nM and limit of quantification (LOQ) of 397 nM. FT-IR, HRMS, and time-resolved fluorescence studies confirm 1:1 binding. Furthermore, a cotton-based sensing platform enabled rapid, visual, and reversible Hg2+ detection with efficient EDTA-assisted regeneration. The combination of AIE-enhanced emission, strong binding affinity, real-time sensing capability, and operational reversibility establishes PPCN as a promising fluorescent platform for practical environmental monitoring of Hg2+ contamination. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Ding Y.; Li B.; Zhu Y.; Zhang Y.; Qu B.; Wang X.; Guo Q.
Title: ReAlignHDR: Region-constrained alignment for ghost-free HDR imaging
Abstract: Multi-exposure High Dynamic Range (HDR) imaging reconstructs an HDR image from bracketed Standard Dynamic Range (SDR) exposures. Although recent dynamic HDR deghosting methods employ alignment or attention-based fusion to handle object motion, they implicitly assume that cross-frame feature interaction remains valid under motion, using semantic or motion priors mainly for region awareness or soft regulation. However, under large foreground motion and occlusion, we observe that region-inconsistent cross-frame interaction can contribute to structural artifacts, as soft regulation may still leave residual aggregation across semantically inconsistent regions and weaken local structural consistency. To address this issue, we propose ReAlignHDR, a region-constrained framework for ghost-free HDR imaging. Specifically, the proposed Structure Anchoring Branch (SAB) establishes a reliable structural foundation by enforcing region-constrained attention under explicit region priors, reducing structural corruption caused by cross-region aggregation. To further handle large-motion scenarios, we introduce a Texture Compensation Branch (TCB), which transports semantically consistent textures from spatially distant regions into the reference frame through explicit alignment. A Progressive Refinement Module (PRM) is then employed for structure-preserving integration. Moreover, we develop a privileged interaction distillation strategy that internalizes the feasible cross-frame interaction space defined by explicit region priors into an implicit prior, thereby enabling region-consistent HDR reconstruction in a mask-free manner. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ReAlignHDR effectively suppresses structural ghosting, yielding competitive performance on challenging dynamic scenes. Author full names: Raman, Roshan (57210530861); Garg, Akhil (55482431700); Caliskan, Hakan (57200234321); Shukla, Neeraj Kumar (57216301033); Sharma, Virendra (60697366400); Barmavatu, Praveen (57213565363); Garg, Aman (57208735083)
Title: Machine Learning-Assisted optimization of acetylene Dual-Fuel combustion using Copper oxide (CuO) Nano-Enhanced waste Plastic Oil in Compression Ignition (CI) Engine
Abstract: In this study, an experimental and machine learning-assisted investigation was conducted on a modified single-cylinder direct-injection Compression Ignition (CI) engine operating in acetylene dual-fuel mode using copper oxide (CuO) nanoparticle-enhanced waste plastic oil (WPO) blends. The proposed approach integrates waste-to-energy fuel utilization, catalytic nano-additives, high-reactivity gaseous combustion, and data-driven predictive modelling within a unified sustainable combustion framework. Experimental investigations were performed using WPO10 and WPO20 blends containing 50 and 100 ppm CuO nanoparticles under acetylene flow rates of 5 and 10 LPM. Among all tested fuel combinations, A5WPO10Cu100 exhibited the best overall performance, achieving a maximum brake thermal efficiency of 33.12 %, corresponding to an 8.27 % improvement over diesel, together with a 21.03 % reduction in brake specific energy consumption. The optimum fuel also reduced HC, CO, and smoke opacity by 41.46 %, 47.62 %, and 43.58 %, respectively, while A10WPO10Cu100 produced the highest combustion intensity with a peak heat release rate of 68.9 J/°CA, maximum cylinder pressure of 90.5 bar, and minimum ignition delay of 8.75 °CA, indicating enhanced premixed combustion and catalytic oxidation. Although NOx emissions increased under higher acetylene induction due to elevated combustion temperatures, the overall combustion efficiency and emission trade-off were significantly improved. To further establish predictive capability, Linear Regression, Decision Tree, and Random Forest models were developed using the experimental dataset. Among these, the Random Forest model demonstrated the highest prediction accuracy with R2 values ranging from 0.995 to 0.999 and prediction accuracy exceeding 98 %, confirming its robustness in predicting nonlinear combustion, performance, and emission characteristics. The integrated experimental and machine learning framework demonstrates that CuO nano-enhanced WPO coupled with acetylene induction is a promising strategy for improving CI engine efficiency while simultaneously advancing intelligent combustion optimization for sustainable transportation applications. To further enhance predictive capability and intelligent engine diagnostics, advanced machine learning (ML) algorithms including Linear Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), and Random Forest (RF) were developed using experimentally measured combustion, performance, and emission parameters. The Random Forest model demonstrated superior nonlinear prediction capability with prediction accuracy exceeding 98 %, coefficient of determination (R2) approaching 0.995–0.999 for major engine responses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Caliari M.; Cassini F.
Title: A tensor-based exponential integrator for diffusion–reaction equations in common curvilinear coordinates
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: In this paper, we study a tensor-based method for the numerical solution of a class of diffusion–reaction equations defined on spatial domains that admit common curvilinear coordinate representations. Typical examples in 2D include disks (polar coordinates), and in 3D balls or cylinders (spherical or cylindrical coordinates) as well as spheres for problems involving the Laplace–Beltrami operator. The proposed approach is based on a carefully chosen finite difference discretization of the Laplace operators that yields matrices with a structured representation as sums of Kronecker products. For the time integration, we introduce a novel split variant of the exponential Euler method that effectively handles the stiffness and avoids the severe time step size restriction of classical explicit methods. By exploiting the peculiar form of the obtained discretized operators and the chosen splitting strategy, we compute the needed action of the φ1 matrix function through suitable tensor-matrix products in a μ-mode framework. We demonstrate the efficiency of the approach on a wide range of physically relevant 2D and 3D examples of N-coupled diffusion–reaction systems generating Turing patterns with up to 106 degrees of freedom. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Sun Y.; Zong M.; Zhang Y.; Su H.; Xia Z.
Title: A noise-aware physics-informed neural network method for nonlinear consolidation with non-Darcian flow and continuous drainage boundary
Abstract: Accurate characterization of soft soil nonlinear consolidation with non-Darcian flow and complex boundary conditions is fundamental to assessing foundation stability. This study presents a Noise-Aware Physics-Informed Neural Network (NA-PINN) framework for one-dimensional nonlinear consolidation problems involving a continuous drainage boundary and non-Darcian flow. Multiple nonlinear couplings can cause gradient imbalance in standard PINNs. Furthermore, when measurement noise and sparse data are present, the inversion of the flow index is susceptible to ill-posedness. To address this problem, the PDE residual weight is prescribed based on the assumed noise level of the observation data, ensuring that the governing equation can provide stronger constraints during inverse training under noisy conditions. In addition, a differentiable variable transformation is used to keep the identified flow index within prescribed physical bounds. Benchmark comparisons with finite difference solutions show that, in eight repeated inverse runs under the nominal setting with 10 % measurement noise, the relative errors of the identified flow index remained below 0.1 %. The continuous excess pore water pressure field was also reconstructed from 15 noisy temporal observations of the average degree of consolidation. The proposed framework captures the nonlinear evolution of excess pore water pressure dissipation and average consolidation response under time-dependent loading, and provides a useful tool for consolidation analysis when monitoring data are sparse or noisy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Liu Y.; Bao Y.; Liu C.; Wang Y.; Wang J.; Li J.; Li X.
Title: Properties of DHA algal oil liposomes coated with different deacetylation degrees chitosan: preparation, physicochemical characterization and in vitro release
Abstract: This study investigated the effects of chitosan coating with varying deacetylation degrees (DD) on the physicochemical properties, stability, in vitro release of DHA algal oil liposomes, through multiple characterization techniques. With chitosan coating, the encapsulation rate of liposomes increased significantly to 92.87%, exceeding that of unmodified liposomes (89%). Transmission electron microscopy revealed the more uniform dispersion and more regular morphology of chitosan-coated liposomes. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analyses confirmed the successful adsorption of chitosan onto the liposomal surface, with enhanced adsorption at higher deacetylation degrees. Antioxidant assays demonstrated that compared with unmodified liposomes, those coated with 90% DD chitosan exhibited 1.2 times greater scavenging activity against DPPH and ABTS radicals. Liposomes coated with 90% DD chitosan showed superior stability under acidic, ionic, and thermal stressors. After 28 days of storage at 4°C, the encapsulation efficiency remained at approximately 87%. In contrast, the liposomes coated with 50%, 70%, and 80% DD chitosan showed a significant increase in particle size and a decrease in encapsulation efficiency. Furthermore, the stability of the liposomes decreased under alkaline conditions due to chitosan deprotonation. In vitro release experiments showed that the chitosan coating could delay the release of DHA algal oil, as evidenced by the 60.87% release rate of the 90% DD group after 48 h, and all liposomes conformed to the first-order kinetic model. In vitro simulated gastrointestinal digestion experiments indicated that chitosan coating significantly improved the liposome bioaccessibility, e.g., the 90% DD achieved bioaccessibility 2.5 times that of uncoated liposomes. These findings indicate that coating DHA algal oil liposomes with 90% deacetylated chitosan significantly enhances their stability, providing a theoretical basis and technical support for the efficient delivery and stabilization of functional bioactive components. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zheng L.; Li Y.; Yu R.; Zhang K.
Title: Efficient dual-domain image dehazing with haze prior perception
Abstract: Transformers offer strong global modeling for single-image dehazing but incur high computational costs. Most methods rely on spatial features to capture long-range dependencies, making them less effective under complex haze conditions. Although some integrate frequency-domain cues, weak spatial-frequency coupling limits their performance. To address these issues, we propose the Dark Channel Guided Frequency-aware Dehazing Network (DGFDNet), a dual-domain framework that explicitly aligns degradation across spatial and frequency domains. At its core, the DGFDBlock consists of two modules: (1) Haze-Aware Frequency Modulator (HAFM), which uses the dark channel prior to generate a haze confidence map for adaptive frequency modulation, achieving global degradation-aware spectral filtering. (2) Multi-level Gating Aggregation Module (MGAM), which fuses multi-scale features via multi-scale convolutions and a hybrid gating mechanism to recover fine-grained structures. Additionally, the Prior Correction Guidance Branch (PCGB) incorporates feedback for iterative refinement of the prior, improving haze localization accuracy, particularly in outdoor scenes. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that DGFDNet achieves state-of-the-art performance with improved robustness and computational efficiency. Authors: Gheshlagh S.M.; Bahrami A.
Title: Calcium-decorated C4B32 heteroborospherene as a promising lightweight platform for potentially reversible hydrogen storage: A DFT study
Abstract: The C4B32 heteroborospherene has attracted significant interest as a potential lightweight platform for clean energy storage. In this study, the hydrogen adsorption characteristics of pristine and Ca-decorated C4B32 are systematically investigated using density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The computational results indicate that pristine C4B32 exhibits weak interactions with H2, showing positive adsorption energies at the carbon sites. In contrast, decoration with calcium atoms enhances the adsorption performance. Up to seven H2 molecules can be accommodated on each of the four decorated Ca atoms, yielding a Ca4@C4B32-(H2)28 complex with a calculated gravimetric density of 9.24 wt%. The calculated average adsorption energy is −0.22 eV per H2, falling within the commonly reported range for reversible molecular hydrogen adsorption. Furthermore, Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules (QTAIM) and Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) analyses characterize the noncovalent nature of the Ca-H2 interactions and clarify the electronic properties of the cluster. These findings suggest that Ca-decorated C4B32 may serve as a useful model for the design of boron-based nanomaterials for hydrogen storage applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Guo E.; Shi B.; Guo J.; Chen H.; Shan L.; Song S.; Gong J.
Title: A multi-scale transient multiphase flow model for hydrate particle formation-aggregation-deposition in pipeline
Abstract: Hydrate blockage critically impacts the safety and efficiency of deep-water oil and gas exploitation. Under low-temperature and high-pressure conditions, hydrates tend to form and disperse as solid particles within the multiphase flow. Hydrate aggregation and deposition are widely recognized as the dominant blockage mechanisms. While few quantitative models exist to describe this entire complex process due to the intricate coupling among hydrate phase-change kinetics, particle agglomeration, deposition, and multiphase fluid interactions. This work proposes a novel multi-scale particle–fluid coupling transient multiphase flow model, comprising one Main-core-model and three Sub-models describing hydrate formation, aggregation, and deposition, respectively. To link micro- and meso -scale particle behaviors to macro-scale flow dynamics, new transport equations for the concentration and average diameter of hydrate particles are introduced to characterize the population effect. By resolving the forces acting on the hydrate aggregates, the critical particle size is derived as a function of multi-scale parameters, from which a log-normal distribution of aggregate size is obtained. The model further predicts deposition probability and layer thickness to quantitatively describe hydrate deposition state in the multiphase system. Comparing with experimental data from a high-pressure flow loop, the model demonstrates exceptional reliability and engineering applicability. Through simulation of a horizontal gas-condensate pipeline, the behaviors of hydrate particle formation, aggregation, and deposition are elucidated and the coupling relationship with multiphase flow is clarified. Thereby, this work advances the fundamental understanding of hydrate blockage and provides a reliable basis for flow assurance control strategies in submarine multiphase pipelines. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Ce-doped BiF3@Pt nanocatalyst enhanced CHA-based electrochemical biosensor for sub-femtomolar detection of miRNA-21
Abstract: The sensitive detection of disease-related microRNAs in clinical samples remains a challenge requiring robust signal amplification strategies. Herein, we report an electrochemical biosensor for ultrasensitive miRNA-21 detection by integrating a catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA) circuit with a rationally designed cerium-doped bismuth fluoride-supported platinum nanoparticle composite (BiF3(Ce)@Pt). Cerium doping strategically reconstructs BiF3 into a porous architecture, enabling high-density, anti-aggregation loading of Pt nanoparticles and significantly enhancing heterogeneous electron transfer at the electrode interface. The BiF3(Ce)@Pt modified electrode exhibits exceptional electrocatalytic activity toward H2O2 reduction, as evidenced by enhanced cathodic current density and accelerated electron transfer kinetics. Serving as a powerful signal tag, BiF3(Ce)@Pt is anchored onto the electrode surface via target-initiated CHA, where each miRNA-21 recognition event triggers the assembly of multiple nanocatalysts, converting a single binding event into a substantially amplified current response. This dual-amplification strategy achieves a wide linear range from 10 fM to 5 nM and an ultra-low detection limit of 0.38 fM. Authors: Si X.; Wang J.; Huang H.; Yang Z.; Yu J.; Han Y.; Zhang S.; Wang Z.; Ming D.
Title: BCF-CDAN: bidirectional cross-modal fusion and conditional domain adversarial network for multimodal cross-subject emotion recognition with EEG-fNIRS
Abstract: Emotion recognition is essential for affective brain-computer interface (BCI), yet poses significant challenges. Specifically, emotion processing involves complex temporal dynamics and spatial brain networks. Therefore, it’s difficult to decode human emotions. Furthermore, individual differences limit the generalizability of cross-subject emotion recognition. In addition, the feasibility of EEG-fNIRS for fine-grained emotion recognition remains underexplored. To address the above issues, this study proposed an interpretable multimodal cross-subject emotion recognition model—the bidirectional cross-modal fusion and conditional domain adversarial network (BCF-CDAN). The proposed framework explicitly exploited the high temporal resolution of EEG and the high spatial resolution of fNIRS. Specifically, modality-specific convolutional neural networks were first employed to emphasize the temporal information of EEG and the spatial information of fNIRS. A multi-stream module and a one-stream module were then designed to achieve cross-modal fusion. The multi-stream module employed bidirectional cross-attention to capture interactive correlations between EEG temporal features and fNIRS spatial features, while the one-stream module used self-attention to learn a global discriminative representation. Subsequently, a conditional domain adversarial network (CDAN) combined with maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) loss was applied to achieve cross-subject distribution alignment. Results on the two self-collected EEG-fNIRS datasets, TMVED3 (three-class task) and TMVED8 (fine-grained eight-class task), showed that BCF-CDAN achieved cross-subject accuracies of 80.14% and 53.13%, respectively, outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Moreover, the interpretability analysis revealed cross-modal dependencies between EEG temporal features and fNIRS spatial features. Overall, the approach leveraged modality-specific strengths, offering a generalizable and interpretable strategy for brain signal integration. Title: Revealing the Microscopic Regulatory mechanism of CO2 in in situ oil shale pyrolysis and the subsurface Oil-Gas conversion efficiency through ReaxFF MD simulation
Abstract: To elucidate the mechanism and energy conversion efficiency of CO2 as a thermal fluid in in-situ oil shale development, this study employed ReaxFF molecular dynamics simulations to compare the pyrolysis behavior of kerogen under vacuum, Ar, and CO2 atmospheres, revealing the mechanism by which CO2 regulates the kerogen pyrolysis network. Furthermore, going beyond the limitations of conventional ex-situ uniform heating models, we simulated, for the first time, the in-situ CO2 injection process under simulated formation conditions, characterized the subsurface heat-transfer behavior of CO2, and quantitatively compared, at the molecular scale, the influence of subsurface non-uniform heat transfer on product conversion. Results show that pyrolysis under a CO2 atmosphere exhibits distinctive kinetic features of early initiation, deep cracking, and strong coke suppression, featuring the lowest onset temperature (1500 K) and the minimum coke residue (3.3 wt%). Unlike the vigorous secondary reactions in vacuum and the physical caging effect in Ar, CO2 can instantly capture highly active radicals and small fragments, suppressing heteroatom-involved cyclization and polycondensation to improve oil and gas quality. In-situ heating simulations further show that, due to thermal-front propagation, local thermal lag, and non-uniform temperature distribution, the conversion of valuable oil and gas under in-situ heating reaches 67.85 %, lower than the 77.95 % obtained under ideal ex-situ uniform heating. Title: Color image restoration based on nonlocal saturation-value similarity
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: In this paper, we propose and develop a novel nonlocal variational technique based on saturation-value similarity for color image restoration. In traditional nonlocal methods, image patches are extracted from red, green and blue channels of a color image directly, and the color information can not be described finely because the patch similarity is mainly based on the grayscale value of independent channel. The main aim of this paper is to propose and develop a novel nonlocal regularization method by considering the similarity of image patches in saturation-value channel of a color image. In particular, we first establish saturation-value similarity based nonlocal total variation by incorporating saturation-value similarity of color image patches into the proposed nonlocal gradients, which can describe the saturation and value similarity of two adjacent color image patches. The proposed nonlocal variational models are then formulated based on saturation-value similarity based nonlocal total variation. Moreover, we design an effective and efficient algorithm to solve the proposed optimization problem numerically by employing bregmanized operator splitting method, and we also study the convergence of the proposed algorithms. Numerical examples are presented to demonstrate that the performance of the proposed models is better than that of other testing methods in terms of visual quality and some quantitative metrics including peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity index (SSIM), quaternion structural similarity index (QSSIM) and S-CIELAB color error. © 2026

Title: Secondary-reduction-induced Pd0-Pd2+/Co3+ interfacial synergy enables efficient and stable dehydrofgenation of dodecahydro-N-propylcarbazole
Abstract: Liquid organic hydrogen carriers (LOHCs) face severe kinetic bottlenecks during the deep dehydrogenation stage due to sluggish final aromatization. Title: Combustion behavior and mechanism of levitated single MgB2 particles in air
Abstract: Simultaneous decomposition and oxidation of MgB2 strongly influence its combustion behavior and energy release efficiency, yet the detailed mechanism at the single-particle level remains insufficiently understood due to the lack of high-resolution diagnostics. In this work, the combustion of individual micrometer-sized MgB2 particles was investigated using an electrodynamic levitator combined with high-speed microscopic imaging, with a calibrated object-plane sampling interval of 0.70 μm/pix. Results showed that MgB2 particle combustion proceeds through three distinct stages associated with sequential decomposition and oxidation of Mg–B intermediate phases. Four combustion modes were identified: single-stage combustion, micro-explosion, and two types of three-stage combustion. Evaporation analysis further shows that the oxidation of boron-rich phases is diffusion-controlled. High-resolution observations reveal previously unobserved phenomena, including particle expansion, localized rupture and self-healing of the oxide layer, and a transient BO2-induced green flash marking the transition to the final combustion stage. These findings provide new insight into the role of magnesium in boron combustion, showing that magnesium improves the combustion process of boron, specifically through the promotion of the formation of a porous oxide layer and the exothermic oxidation. Title: Tribological performance of laser-powder bed fused Ti-6Al-4V: Role of texture geometry and modified surface layers
Abstract: Ti-6Al-4V fabricated via Laser-Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) exhibits superior mechanical properties and a refined microstructure compared to conventionally forged alloys; however, its tribological performance remains limited. To address this issue, square and circular micro-textures were generated on LPBF-fabricated and conventionally forged Ti-6Al-4V using multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT)-assisted micro-electrical discharge machining (micro-EDM), maintaining a texture density of 10.5%. Title: Uncertainty-aware multimodal fusion for change detection via hyperdimensional prototype reasoning
Abstract: Multimodal change detection aims to identify land-cover changes by fusing complementary information from heterogeneous remote sensing observations. Although different modalities provide richer and more robust change cues than a single sensor, reliable multimodal fusion remains difficult because of differences in imaging mechanisms, spatial textures, and noise patterns. Most existing methods focus on learning discriminative cross-modal change features, but they offer limited explicit modeling of prediction reliability. Title: On fractional discrete-time spatio-temporal SIR models
Abstract: Mathematical modeling is an essential tool for studying and controlling disease transmission. We derive the model’s equilibrium points, compute the basic reproduction number R0, and investigate the local stability of both the disease-free and endemic equilibria. Using appropriately constructed Lyapunov functions, we further prove the global asymptotic stability of each equilibrium. Title: An innovative coupled system with p(x)-growth conditions and regularized Perona–Malik diffusion applied to image denoising

Title: Stochastic inertial projection-extrapolation method: A damped approach with applications to machine learning

Abstract: We introduce and analyze a novel stochastic algorithm for monotone variational inequalities under uncertainty, a class that includes convex–concave saddle-point problems and convex optimization problems as special cases. Unlike classical inertial methods that employ positive momentum for acceleration, our damped inertial momentum serves as a smoothing mechanism that stabilizes iterates against stochastic noise. Title: Controlling high-temperature exposure and product selectivity in pulsed microwave plasma methane coupling

Title: Transformation of Lignocellulosic biomass into green hypergolic rocket fuels using highly dense Cu(II) hypergolic promoters
Abstract: The valorization of biomass waste into biofuel has the potential to meet the rapidly increasing global energy demand, along with substantially reducing environmental waste and the cost of waste management. Still, the biomass waste conversion is mostly restricted to fuels for land and marine transportation. Title: Co-assembly SERS strategy for trace detection and intelligent recognition of controlled-drug mixtures
Abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is promising for trace chemical analysis, drug detection, and illicit-substance screening. However, conventional assembly-based substrates generally rely on post-assembly soaking, which limits analyte access to nanoscale hot spots and compromises sensitivity and mixture recognition. Title: Class-specific branch attention for mitigating gradient interference under class imbalance
Abstract: Deep neural networks trained under severe class imbalance often exhibit degraded performance, typically attributed to statistical bias. In this work, we identify a complementary optimization-level pathology: inter-class gradient interference within shared representations, where gradients from majority classes suppress minority-class learning. To analyze this phenomenon, we introduce a diagnostic framework based on layer-wise gradient flow analysis and a Gradient Conflict Matrix, which quantifies interference using cosine similarity between class-specific gradients. Using this framework, we study multi-branch convolutional architectures and propose a lightweight modification, Class-Specific Branch Attention (CSBA), that enables branch-specific channel reweighting to reduce gradient coupling. This mechanism promotes implicit feature decoupling across branches while preserving architectural simplicity. Empirically, CSBA improves minority-class performance, increasing the F1 score for the Physical-Damage class from 0.261 to 0.522 under severe imbalance, while maintaining comparable overall accuracy. These results suggest that mitigating gradient interference is associated with improved minority-class representation. Title: Aptamer-grafted amino-functionalized covalent organic frameworks for simultaneous exceptional selectivity and high-capacity adsorption of four aflatoxins

Title: Integrated field test and modeling study of CO2 geological storage with enhanced water recovery in Eastern Junggar Basin of Xinjiang
Abstract: Xinjiang, a primary energy export hub in China, faces substantial carbon emission pressure and severe water scarcity, making CO2 geological storage combined with enhanced water recovery (CO2-EWR) a win–win strategy to foster regional development and bolster national energy security. Title: A constitutive model for large-strain elasticity of incompressible, isotropic soft materials
Abstract: Constitutive models facilitate numerical simulations that support the design and optimization of soft-material-based components, reducing reliance on costly, time-consuming trial-and-error experiments. Commonly used constitutive models often balance between simplicity and predictive accuracy: simple models have limited predictive power, while complex models face challenges in parameter identification and numerical stability. This study introduces a simple two-parameter phenomenological model, formulated in terms of the principal stretches, for incompressible, isotropic soft materials undergoing large deformations. The model’s admissibility is established analytically via the Baker-Ericksen inequality and polyconvexity; its recovery of the classical linear-elastic limit at infinitesimal strain is demonstrated; and an extension to the nearly incompressible case is presented. Material parameters were identified using a hybrid differential evolution and trust-region reflective optimization strategy under two calibration scenarios: uniaxial tension (UT) data only, and simultaneous fitting to uniaxial tension, equibiaxial (EB), and pure shear (PS) data. Title: A harmonic-oscillator analogy for elastic wave localization in piezoelectric metamaterial beams
Abstract: Locally resonant piezoelectric metamaterials can localize elastic energy at defects, but conventional defects rely on abrupt changes in the lattice that trap the field in isolated cavities and impose sharp spatial constraints. Here we replace the abrupt defect with a smooth piecewise-quadratic modulation of the electrical resonance across an array of inductively shunted unit cells, forming a distributed trapping region whose location, width, and depth are set electrically rather than by geometry. This graded profile maps the slowly varying wave envelope onto the quantum harmonic oscillator, so the trapped modes are Hermite–Gauss envelopes whose spatial localization length and descending frequency sequence are predicted in closed form from the modulation depth and width alone. A coupled electromechanical eigenvalue analysis, an inverse participation ratio, and transient simulations establish the trap. A resonance maximum traps a Gaussian fundamental and a family of higher modes while a minimum expels the field, the depth and the width act as independent controls over the confinement and the spread, and the localized mode relocates anywhere along the beam without altering the structure. Title: Ex-situ catalytic pyrolysis of lignin over derived biochar catalysts into the typical components of sustainable aviation fuels: Effects of single transition metals on aromatic hydrocarbon generation

Title: Decoupling time scales and environments in equivariant graph neural networks for spatio-temporal dynamics

Title: The gelation mechanism and network structure of polysaccharide food gels as studied from macroscopic, microscopic to molecular levels — A review of methodologies
Abstract: Owing to their high-water contents, low calorie density, easy-to-swallowing properties, polysaccharide gels have attracted increasing attention in the food industry and almost exist in our every day's life. Gelation is one of the most important properties for polysaccharides, which describes a process of chain-chain aggregation and the formation of a three-dimensional network structure that finally leads to a drastic change in the macroscopic mechanical properties, i.e., from a solution with good fluidity to a gel with self-supporting property. Moreover, the gelation process is also considered to cause remarkable changes in the microenvironments in the interspatial network and in the polymer chain's mobility as well as the polymer-water interactions. Therefore, it is important to have a fundamental understanding of how polysaccharides form gels from macroscopic, microscopic to molecular levels. In this review article, we have summarized the application of bulk rheology, particle tracking, light scattering, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) and some other tools in elucidating the network structures and gelation mechanism of typical gelling polysaccharides gellan and carrageenans. It has been demonstrated that these techniques are powerful to provide important information on the gelation mechanism and network structure at different length scales. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Weng P.; Du H.; Jiang L.; Ding H.; Yin X.; Bai H.
Title: A unified explicit unloading relation for elastic–plastic flattening contact and spherical indentation
Abstract: Elastic–plastic unloading is commonly described by Hertzian-type relations, empirical fitting expressions, or finite-element-based regression models. However, these approaches usually cannot simultaneously represent the coupled evolution of contact force, contact radius, and indentation within a unified framework. Based on the cohesionless unloading framework proposed by Mesarovic and Johnson, this study establishes an explicit unloading relation among contact force, contact radius, and indentation, and further examines its direct applicability to flattening contact and its extension to spherical indentation using finite element (FE) simulations and available experimental results. The results show that, for flattening contact, the theoretical predictions agree well with the FE results in the small-deformation regime, whereas a finite-deformation correction is required in the large-deformation regime to improve the prediction of the recovered deformation distribution, recovered indentation, and unloading relations. For indentation contact, although the pressure state at the onset of unloading does not strictly satisfy the assumptions of the original theoretical framework, the proposed unloading law still maintains good predictive accuracy and agrees well with FE results and published results for power-law hardening materials. Overall, the explicit unloading law developed in this study provides a unified description of the evolution of contact force, contact radius, and indentation during elastic–plastic unloading, and offers a concise theoretical basis for predicting key unloading responses in both flattening and indentation contacts. © 2026

Authors: Cheng R.; Zhuo L.; Chen H.
Author full names: Cheng, Ruiqin (59560561800); Zhuo, Lijun (55936735500); Chen, Hongchu (57189690546)
Title: A physics-informed calibration method for transient surface heat flux prediction under complex radiative heating
Abstract: Monitoring surface heat fluxes of materials is crucial in engineering and is a prerequisite for thermal system design. However, the thermophysical properties of most engineering materials are temperature-dependent, which undoubtedly increases the difficulty of surface heat flux estimation. In this paper, a data-driven calibration integral equation method was proposed to solve these problems. Additionally, an experimental heating system was designed based on quartz lamps, and the system was used to test this calibration-based inverse prediction method. Due to the complexity of the quartz lamp heating system, the difference between the incident surface heat flux and net surface heat flux are considered. In addition, the time delay caused by the heating system was also discussed based on mathematic analysis. Then, a new equation was derived for surface heat flux estimation without the impact of the delay time. Subsequently, stainless steel 304 and Inconel 600 were selected as test samples to validate the accuracy of surface heat flux predictions. In this process, the thermal conductivities of the materials were no need to be provided. The results show that the predictions of the calibration integral equation are accurate, with a relative root mean square error of less than 12%. By comparing the prediction accuracy with space marching method, the integral equation is weakly parameter-dependent, which decreases the system uncertainty. This outcome indicates that the involved inverse method can provide guidance for thermal system design. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Authors: Paul M.; Soman S.; Phan N.; Shao S.; Shamsaei N.
Title: Fatigue crack growth behavior of additively manufactured aluminum alloys: A comparative investigation
Abstract: This study investigates the fatigue crack growth (FCG) behavior of three aluminum alloys, namely AlSi10Mg, QuesTek Al, and Scalmalloy, using compact tension specimens fabricated via laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF). Among these, AlSi10Mg specimens are manufactured with two feedstocks from different suppliers. The materials exhibit different fracture surface roughnesses due to variations in their microstructures which correlated with threshold stress intensity factor range, ΔKth . Scalmalloy exhibited the highest ΔKth , followed by QuesTek Al, with both AlSi10Mg materials being comparable but the lowest. Vertical specimens had higher ΔKth values (except Scalmalloy), while higher R resulted in lower ΔKth due to reduced crack closure effects. Stable crack growth behavior was comparable among both AlSi10Mg materials and Scalmalloy although their microstructures were different. However, QuesTek Al had significantly higher FCG rates due to its limited ductility. In the unstable region, the maximum stress intensity factor at failure, Kmax,failure correlated broadly with ductility obtained from tensile tests. Scalmalloy exhibited the highest Kmax,failure whereas QuesTek Al exhibited the lowest due to its limited plastic deformation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Dong A.; Dou J.; Yang Y.; Xing K.; Dong S.; Li H.
Title: Embedding slope-failure mechanics in E-PINN for co-seismic landslide susceptibility assessment
Abstract: Data-driven models for co-seismic landslide susceptibility assessment (LSA) can discriminate unstable terrain effectively, but their predictions remain weakly connected to slope-failure mechanics. This limits assessment of whether high susceptibility arises from reduced material resistance, greater seismic loading, or their interaction. We develop an Explicitly Constrained Physics-Informed Neural Network (E-PINN) that embeds a differentiable slope-stability pathway within a deep learning architecture. The framework is evaluated for landslides triggered by the 2018 Hokkaido Eastern Iburi earthquake, Japan. Parallel SE-ResNet trunks learn bounded adjustments to weak lithology-conditioned strength anchors. The adjusted strength variables then enter a white-box chain linking Ta-d-informed soil thickness, wetness-adjusted infinite-slope stability, Newmark-type critical acceleration, terrain-modulated PGA–PGV seismic demand, and susceptibility. E-PINN achieves a ROC-AUC of 0.866; its gain over the architecture-matched SE-ResNet baseline is greatest with 100 training samples per class (0.051). The model also concentrates 54.6% of the mapped landslide area within 18.0% of the study area. Sensitivity, displacement-based, and pathway tests show stable discrimination under alternative instability representations and substantial dependence of the final prediction on the physical states. These model-conditioned variables exhibit the expected ordering: landslide pixels have lower effective strength and stability but higher seismic demand. E-PINN thus combines predictive discrimination with an inspectable mechanical pathway, supporting regional post-earthquake screening and field-inspection prioritization. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Li J.; Jiao W.; Zhang C.; Xie G.; Zhang J.
Author full names: Li, Jie (59748727700); Jiao, Wenpei (57927646500); Zhang, Chunyan (58641567900); Xie, Guangming (7202981443); Zhang, Jianlei (36146538300)
Title: Open long-tailed sonar image recognition via sparsity-aware tail memory learning
Abstract: Open long-tailed recognition for sonar images (Sonar-OLTR) is critical for autonomous underwater perception systems. However, Sonar-OLTR remains challenging due to data scarcity, long-tailed class distributions, and real-world distribution shifts. Existing methods typically synthesize pseudo-unknown samples to improve class boundary learning. However, these strategies are mostly adapted from optical image domains, overlooking the unique textural and structural characteristics of sonar data, and thus struggle to fit sonar image feature distributions. To address these limitations, we construct a real-world open-set sonar image dataset with over 9 K multi-sensor images and complete image information collected from underwater scenarios. Based on this dataset, we propose sparsity-aware tail memory learning (SATML), a unified framework for pseudo-unknown sample synthesis and long-tailed known-class representation learning. Specifically, sparsity-aware pseudo feature synthesis (SAPFS) fuses target foreground semantics with heterogeneous contextual semantics from other samples in the feature space, generating pseudo-unknowns that are semantically close to known classes but weakly affiliated with any known category. Prototype-guided tail memory contrastive learning (PTMCL) complements tail-class positives through class-wise memory banks and uses prototype-based dynamic filtering and class-balanced reduction to suppress noisy memories and head-class bias, improving intra-class compactness and inter-class separability. Experiments on three sonar datasets show that SATML achieves state-of-the-art performance, while additional results on SAR and terahertz datasets suggest potential transferability. Notably, both modules are training-only and add no inference cost, making SATML practical for deployment. © 2026

Authors: Li Z.; Chen Z.; Zhou R.; Lu P.; Liu X.
Title: Co-packed metal hydride and phase change pellets enable rapid hydrogen storage and release
Abstract: Solid-state magnesium-based hydrides provide a promising route toward high-density, safe, and reversible hydrogen storage. However, their practical application is severely limited by inefficient thermal management: heat accumulation during exothermic hydrogenation suppresses reaction kinetics, while continuous external heat input is required to drive endothermic dehydrogenation. Here, we present a simple co-packed strategy that integrates metal hydride and phase change pellets to enable rapid hydrogen storage and release. The phase change pellets dynamically absorb and release latent heat, effectively removing excess heat during hydrogenation and supplying heat during dehydrogenation. As a result, the co-packed system exhibits markedly accelerated hydrogen uptake and release kinetics, with total storage and release time reduced by 39% and 33%, respectively, compared with conventional packed beds. More notably, at 90% conversion, the hydrogen storage and release rates are enhanced by 600% and 400%, respectively. Mechanistic studies reveal that particle-level thermal coupling shortens heat transfer pathways and enables rapid thermal response, thereby accelerating reaction kinetics. This work establishes a simple but effective strategy to mitigate thermal limitations in solid-state hydrogen storage, enabling rapid hydrogen storage and release. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Xu S.; Liu Y.; Cao X.; Zhang Y.; Bu C.
Title: Milder solar thermochemical water splitting for hydrogen production: Coupling CH4-assisted reduction with Zr4+ doped CeO2
Abstract: Solar-driven two-step thermochemical H2O splitting offers a viable pathway toward hydrogen production. CeO2 has emerged as a leading material candidate. Nevertheless, the practical deployment of CeO2-based systems is constrained by the high temperatures required for reduction in the redox cycle. To overcome this limitation, a strategy combining CH4-assisted reduction with Zr4+ doping was examined to enhance cycle performance under milder conditions. An integrated experimental and density functional theory (DFT) study reveals the mechanism at the atomic level. In a fixed-bed reactor, Ce0.75Zr0.25O2 (25 mol% Zr4+ doping) is found to be optimal, achieving a peak H2 yield of 1.21 mmol g−1 at 900℃, attributed to improved oxygen exchange capacity and redox cycling stability. DFT calculations elucidate the complete H2O-splitting pathway on the doped surface, identifying OH* cleavage as the rate-determining step; the dopant lowers the energy barrier of this step and facilitates H2O adsorption, thereby enhancing overall efficiency. These results provide a mechanistic understanding of how doping modulates H2O splitting and offer guidance for the design of more efficient oxides for solar-fuel generation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Li F.; Chang J.; Zhu C.; Bai H.; Huang W.
Title: Tuning donor–acceptor interactions via electronic modulation in Ga-doped ZnO for carbon chain growth from syngas
Abstract: Higher alcohol synthesis from syngas over conventional CuZn catalysts often encounters a trade-off between total alcohol selectivity and C2+ distribution. Here, we show that Ga-doped ZnO enables precise electronic modulation to balance donor and acceptor reactions through controlled Ga doping. Electron-deficient Znδ+ sites serve as key active centers, facilitating non-dissociative CO adsorption and CO insertion for carbon chain growth. At low doping, substitutional Ga acts as a donor, promoting C-O bond activation. At 1 mol% Ga, substitutional Ga and the resulting electron-deficient Znδ+ sites effectively balance the electron donation-acquisition relationship, achieving 63.5% liquid C2+ alcohol content. Excessive doping (13 mol%) causes Ga clustering and electron-rich states, over-dominating acceptor reactions and suppressing CO insertion. This work establishes that balancing donor–acceptor reactions via electronic modulation is key to overcoming this trade-off, offering a design principle extendable to other electronically tunable catalytic systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wang M.; Zhu L.; Fan R.; Zhang J.; Yang B.; Xiong Z.; Shi Z.
Title: Regulation of precipitation order on the physical–chemical properties of MgCo2Oz catalyst for AP thermal decomposition: catalytic performance and mechanism
Abstract: Herein, two different precipitation sequences were proposed to fabricate layered Co/Mg hydroxide catalyst (Denoted as MgCo2O z ) in order to regulate the catalytic performance for ammonium perchlorate (AP) thermal decomposition. The results demonstrated that the change of precipitation sequence markedly altered the morphology, crystallinity, pore structure, and surface chemical states of the as-fabricated layered Co/Mg hydroxide catalysts. Compared with the as-synthesized MC-NH3·H2O catalyst by dropping metal precursor solution into precipitating agent, MC-NH3·H2O* synthesized by the opposite titration sequence produced greater reductions in the high-temperature decomposition temperature and apparent activation energy of AP, reaching 156.4 °C and 32.4 kJ mol−1, respectively. And MC-NH3·H2O* exhibited a microflower-like morphology, higher crystallinity, more abundant interlayer ionic species, and a higher average oxidation state of surface Co than MC-NH3·H2O. Furthermore, the formed MgCo2O4-related or other Co/Mg mixed-oxide species from Co/Mg hydroxide precursor during heating up also played important role on AP catalytic thermal decomposition. Kinetic analysis indicated that AP/MC-NH3·H2O and AP/MC-NH3·H2O* composites generally exhibited nucleation-and-growth characteristics, with the dominant mechanism evolving from an L2-like random-fragmentation mode at low conversion to F2- and F3-like reaction-order modes at high conversion, respectively. DFT calculations showed that MgCo2O4 (311) surface provided energetically favorable adsorption and activation sites for NH3 and HClO4, while the synergistic effects of Co, Mg, and adjacent O sites facilitated intermediate conversion, alleviated the reaction stagnation between the LTD and HTD stages, and promoted the earlier onset and partial merging of HTD and LTD stages. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Lu S.; Xue Y.; Liu L.; Zhang Y.; Dong Q.; Ding W.; Hua K.; Guo Z.; Zhang Y.; Chen Z.
Title: Ultrafast synthesis of Fe-ZSM-5 for energy-efficient catalytic amine regeneration in CO2 capture
Abstract: The conventional amine-based carbon capture technique is constrained by low reaction kinetics and high energy requirements in the amine regeneration process. Transition metal-zeolite catalysts with numerous Brønsted and Lewis acidic sites have been extensively utilized, however, the active metal species are prone to leaching and deactivation, and the long crystallization time leads to high synthetic costs, which is due to a discrepancy between the rapid precipitation of metal species in alkaline conditions and the long crystallization time of zeolites, resulting in the difficulty to uniformly disperse metal species within the zeolite framework. Herein, we present a facile and ultrafast synthesis strategy to fabricate Fe-ZSM-5 catalyst in 15 min, which involves aging followed by crystallization in a high-conductivity tubular reactor with a long-to-diameter ratio. Some Fe is substituted for partial Al in the ZSM-5 framework, and the well-dispersed FeO x nanoparticles are also confined on the surface of ZSM-5. Fe-ZSM-5 enhances proton, electron, and mass transfer due to an increase in the number of acidic sites and pore structures. The Fe-ZSM-5 catalyst with the Fe/Al molar ratio of 1.23 exhibited optimal catalytic CO2 desorption activity and long-term stability, demonstrating an increase in desorption amount and rate of 26% and 81.75%, along with a 26% reduction in regeneration heat duty compared to the non-catalytic condition in the CO2-rich MEA solution. Additionally, Fe-ZSM-5 enhanced the CO2 desorption kinetic efficiency and facilitated the decomposition of MEACOO- and HCO3– in the MEA-MDEA and MEA-DEEA blended amine solutions. Fe-ZSM-5 exhibited commendable stability during amine regeneration. This straightforward and effective synthesis approach of metal-modified ZSM-5 catalysts possesses significant potential for large-scale industrial applications in energy-efficient CO2 capture. Title: Polyamine-modified porphyrin magnetic nanoconjugates for antimicrobial photodynamic water disinfection in a continuous-flow reactor
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Waterborne pathogens are a major public health concern, driving disease transmission and persistent contamination of water resources. Photodynamic inactivation (PDI) using immobilized photosensitizers is a promising approach for microbial control. Here, Fe3O4 magnetic nanoparticles (MNP) covalently functionalized with 5,10,15,20-tetrakis(pentafluorophenyl)porphyrin and further modified with polyethylenimine (MNP-PEI) or spermine (MNP-SPM) were synthesized and evaluated as photodynamic antimicrobial materials.
