Title: Large deformation and snap-through buckling of bimodular deep-or-shallow opening and non-opening spherical shells
Abstract: Bimodular materials exhibit different mechanical properties in tension and compression, yet this effect is often neglected in existing studies due to its complexity in analysis. Based on the principle of minimum potential energy, this paper establishes a large deformation theoretical model for thin-walled spherical shells that considers the bimodular effect, and also investigates the mechanical response and snap-through instability behavior under normal loads simulating an underwater environment. The main research objects are opening spherical shells and non-opening deep spherical shells; the analytical relationship between normal load and deflection is derived, and a user material subroutine (UMAT) for bimodular materials applicable to spherical shell structures is developed for the first time, using numerical iterations to simulate the actual structural response. Furthermore, for the non-opening deep spherical shell, the proposed theoretical model is also applicable to shallow spherical shells with reduced half apex angle, enabling a unified analysis of deep-or-shallow spherical shells and yielding the critical geometric parameters and critical loads for snap-through instability. The results indicate that the shape, boundary conditions, and bimodular effect significantly influence the deformation behavior of spherical shells; at higher load levels, a decrease in the half apex angle or an increase in the base radius-thickness ratio enhances the bimodular effect’s influence on deformation. From the perspective of nonlinear large deformation, this study reveals the influence of the bimodular effect on the mechanical behavior of spherical shells, providing a theoretical basis for the design and optimization of pressure-resistant spherical shell structures. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Title: Machine learning-assisted Ti3C2Tx-PANI-SnO2 heterojunctions for real-time monitoring of NH3 released from food spoilage
Abstract: Ammonia (NH3) released during food spoilage is an important indicator of food freshness, yet its accurate monitoring remains challenging because of high humidity and interference from coexisting volatile amines. In this study, an intelligent sensing platform integrating a Ti3C2Tx-polyaniline (PANI)-SnO2 multidimensional heterojunction sensor with Transformer -based signal analysis was developed for reliable, real-time NH3 monitoring. The synergistic combination of Ti3C2Tx, PANI, and SnO2 enabled efficient signal transport, selective NH3 adsorption, enhanced interfacial charge transfer, and improved structural stability. The optimized Ti3C2Tx-PANI (50) -SnO2 (30)  sensor exhibited a response of 12.6 to 200 ppm NH3 over a wide detection range of 0.2-200 ppm. It maintained stable sensing performance at 20%-90% relative humidity and retained approximately 80% of its initial response after 60 days of storage, demonstrating good humidity tolerance and long-term stability. To mitigate interference from dimethylamine and trimethylamine generated during food spoilage, a Transformer model was employed to analyze the dynamic sensing signals. The model achieved a classification accuracy of 97.51% for mixed-gas samples and enabled reliable quantitative determination of NH3 under complex interference conditions. The sensor and embedded model were further integrated into a portable device for real-time monitoring of NH3 released during the spoilage of shrimp, fish, and pork. The measured NH3 concentrations deviated from the actual values by less than 10%. This multifunctional intelligent sensing platform provides a practical approach for on-site, intelligent food freshness assessment in complex high-humidity environments. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Analysis of medical isotope yield based on 232Th(p, x)225Ac reaction
Abstract: Actinium-225 (225Ac) has emerged as a premier medical isotope for targeted alpha therapy (TAT), yet its large-scale production remains impeded by multiple technical challenges. This study aims to develop an optimal thick-target scheme for 225Ac production via proton beam irradiation of thorium targets. Specifically, the FLUKA code was employed to quantify and analyze the impacts of thorium target thickness and incident proton energy on both 225Ac production yield and the maximum deposition power density within the target, thereby identifying the optimal proton energy and corresponding target thickness parameters. The results indicate that irradiating an 18-cm-thick thorium target with 500 MeV protons maximizes 225Ac production efficiency under the constraint of constant proton beam power. This work achieves an optimal trade-off among 225Ac yield, proton energy, and target heat load, thereby providing a critical technical reference for the efficient and scalable production of this pivotal medical isotope. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Unraveling the mechanism of programmable heating and quenching in enhancing tar yield from PVC pyrolysis: a ReaxFF MD study
Abstract: The conventional continuous heating (CCH) method for recovering polyvinyl chloride (PVC) has limitations that result in a low tar yield. The programmable heating and quenching (PHQ) method can increase the tar yield of PVC, but the underlying mechanism was still unclear. In this study, the Reactive Force Field molecular dynamics (ReaxFF MD) simulations were used to systematically investigate the effect of the PHQ method on the tar yield of PVC. First, the PVC was pyrolyzed using the CCH method to determine the effective temperature range suitable for the PHQ method, which includes the maximum temperature ( Tmax ) and the minimum temperature ( Tmin ). Subsequently, within this temperature range, the effects of different heating and cooling time ratios ( th / tc ) on the product distribution were compared. The results showed that a smaller th / tc could significantly increase the tar yield. Additionally, when th / tc was set to 1/9, the effects of changes in Tmax and Tmin on the product distribution of the thermal decomposition were studied. Finally, by comparing the product distributions of PVC pyrolysis in the PHQ and CCH modes, it was found that the PHQ method significantly increased the tar yield. Through in-depth analysis of the reaction pathways, the intrinsic mechanism of PHQ in increasing the tar yield was revealed: (1) The cooling process effectively inhibited the condensation reaction of tar, (2) Reducing the generation of organic gas molecules indirectly promoted the accumulation of tar, (3) Pulsed heating promoted the breakage and decomposition of carbon chains. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Dual-view visual-semantic fusion for cursive Urdu HTR: Compact CRNN with confidence-gated zero-shot LLM verification
Abstract: Offline handwritten text recognition (HTR) for Urdu is difficult due to the right-to-left cursive script, context-dependent character shapes, and limited annotated handwriting. Several recent Urdu recognizers use transformer-based encoder–decoder architectures, while post-correction with large language models (LLMs) has shown mixed effectiveness. We present DualView-HTR, a two-stage framework that fuses visual and semantic information. In Stage 1, the line image is reflected along its width to follow the reading direction, and a compact convolutional recurrent neural network (CRNN) is trained with connectionist temporal classification (CTC). CTC prefix beam search with a character 5-gram language model produces a transcription hypothesis. In Stage 2, a zero-shot LLM verifier, instructed to make only local character corrections, proposes a candidate for each handwritten line. A confidence gate based on the minimum emission confidence of the CTC posterior then selects between this candidate and the hypothesis. The method is evaluated on a benchmark that combines synthetic printed-style (MMU-OCR-21) and handwritten (NUST-UHWR) lines, with baselines retrained under the same evaluation protocol. The proposed method achieves a character error rate of 4.02% and a word error rate of 13.87%, the lowest among the compared methods. Ablations show that hybrid training on synthetic and handwritten lines, right-to-left reflection, and language-model decoding provide most of the error reduction. Title: Numerical solution of fractional volterra integral equations by Bernstein-Durrmeyer type approximation operators
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: In this article define a new numerical technique for solving fractional Volterra integral equations of first and second kind by using the Bernstein-Durrmeyer operators. An extensive theoretical framework is presented including moment identities, Korovkin's theorem-based uniform convergence, and a Voronovskaya-type asymptotic equation. The corresponding numerical methods convert the fractional Volterra equations into a system of linear algebraic equations which can be computed efficiently. We prove the error and convergence results under the stated assumptions of regularity and stability. Further, numerical tests demonstrate the performance of the proposed method for fractional Volterra equations with weakly singular Riemann-Liouville kernels. Finally, the approximation results show that the Bernstein-Durrmeyer operator provides a precise approximation framework with high accuracy at moderate polynomial degrees, while the numerical performance is influenced by the conditioning of the resulting algebraic systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: SFD-Mamba2Net: Structure-Guided Frequency-Enhanced Dual-Stream Mamba2 Network for Coronary Artery Segmentation

Long-range spatial dependencies and complex vessel topology are modeled via an Axial-Alternating Dual-Stream Mamba2 (AA-DS Mamba2) module. Title: Intrinsic stochasticity in soil-rock mixtures: Meso-to-macro mechanisms and random elastoplastic damage model
Abstract: The mechanical behaviour of soil-rock mixtures (SRMs) under shear is governed by meso-structural transitions driven by spatial heterogeneity in particle arrangement, geometry, and force chain topology—a source of non-negligible intrinsic stochasticity within SRM structure that remains poorly captured by existing constitutive models. This study establishes an integrated stochastic framework that links fabric evolution to constitutive response through discrete element simulations and a meso-structurally informed elastoplastic model. We identify rock content (Rc) and its shape as the two dominate factors: characteristic Rc demarcates soil- from rock-dominated fabric, while irregular particles enhance geometric interlocking, shifting the dominant mechanism from contact sliding to skeletal stability control. These meso-scale transitions are embedded into a damage-plasticity constitutive model, where damage-softening and plastic dilatancy emerge as co-manifestations of meso-structural instability, quantitatively regulated by fabric parameters. Crucially, the macro-scale shear stress response exhibits intrinsic uncertainty arising directly from the meso-stochasticity of SRMs, rigorously decomposed into two components: (i) structural stress fluctuations—abrupt, event-like changes due to force chain reorganization and geometric locking during shear; and (ii) stochastic stress noise—irreducible background variation from contact sliding and particle motion. Notably, intermittent stress bursts (6–10% of peak strength) intensify with increasing Rc and may trigger shear localisation. The framework provides, for the first time, a unified interpretation of SRM behaviour spanning coupled stochastic fabric evolution and constitutive response, along with physically meaningful stress uncertainty, establishing a physically grounded basis for reliability-based geotechnical analysis of SRMs. © 2026

Title: Radiation induced changes in polymer materials used in medical devices and implications for sterilization technologies
Abstract: The sterilization of medical devices represents a critical step in ensuring patient safety and device functionality. Among various sterilization modalities, ionizing radiation technologies including gamma irradiation, electron beam processing, and X-ray irradiation have gained widespread adoption due to their effectiveness, scalability, and compatibility with terminally sterilized products. However, the interaction between ionizing radiation and polymeric materials can induce significant physicochemical alterations that may compromise device performance, biocompatibility, and shelf-life. This narrative review takes a critical look at recent evidence on radiation-induced changes in polymer materials commonly employed in medical devices, asking what that evidence implies for the selection and optimization of a sterilization technology. Sources were chosen for relevance and, wherever possible, for direct comparison of radiation modalities; no formal systematic-review protocol was followed. Literature published between 2018 and June 2026 was emphasized, with attention to mechanistic insights into polymer degradation pathways, comparative analyses of radiation modalities, and strategies for mitigating adverse effects. Our analysis reveals that radiation effects are highly polymer-specific and dependent on factors including crystallinity, molecular architecture, additive composition, and processing history. When absorbed dose is matched, gamma, electron beam, and X-ray irradiation are reported to produce broadly comparable changes in several polyolefins and multilayer films, with the exceptions concentrated in particular polymer-property combinations; dose rate and atmosphere appear to account for much of the residual difference between sources. While polyolefins such as polypropylene exhibit complex responses involving both chain scission and crosslinking, biodegradable polyesters like poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) demonstrate pronounced molecular weight reduction under irradiation. Emerging evidence highlights the potential of low-energy electron beam irradiation and optimized dose protocols to balance sterilization efficacy with material preservation. We conclude that a comprehensive understanding of radiation-polymer interactions, coupled with systematic material characterization and process validation, is essential for advancing safe and effective sterilization practices in medical device manufacturing. Rather than proposing a new methodology, the review appraises how strong the existing comparative evidence is, identifies where it remains thin, and sets out what regulators and industry can reasonably expect when a product moves from one radiation modality to another. Title: A novel hybrid SPH-DEM scheme with spatiotemporal porosity evolution for cross-scale particulate flows

Title: Experimental study on gas–liquid two-phase transport characteristics in an alkaline water electrolysis for hydrogen production system

Title: Enhancing learning efficiency in spiking neural networks via expanded representation and neuronal heterogeneity
Abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) remain limited by three coupled deficiencies in existing neuron models: binary spikes collapse continuous membrane states into 0/1 events, causing severe quantization loss; fixed or homogeneous thresholds cannot adapt to instantaneous inputs and neuron-wise dynamics; and conventional hard/soft reset rules either discard useful residual membrane information or retain excessive residual potential, leading to redundant firing. For stable optimization of multi-valued firing, we further design a threshold-dependent surrogate gradient (TdSG) and an accelerated variant (T2TdSG). To preserve event-driven efficiency during inference, we introduce an integer-to-binary (I2B) conversion scheme and binary-based energy metrics. Experiments on static and neuromorphic benchmarks show state-of-the-art performance, achieving 82.8% on CIFAR100, 69.89% on Tiny-ImageNet, and 89.4% on CIFAR10-DVS, while I2B reduces synaptic operations by 21%–36%. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: The effect of tributyl phosphate on the oxidation of hydrocarbon diluents under electron beam irradiation in the circulation-emulsion mode
Abstract: Electron beam-induced oxidation in circulating water-hydrocarbon emulsions was investigated. Title: Bile salts govern protein bioaccessibility and nanostructural assembly during digestion of Nori seaweed

Authors: Tang C.; Ge Z.; Ma W.; Yang X.; Lai C.; Huo J.; Liu S.
Title: Construction of magnetic self-assembled electrochemical biosensor with TiO2@Co/C@Au nanocomposite for sensitive detection of PIK3CA gene
Abstract: PIK3CA gene mutations are key drivers in various malignant tumors, and their highly sensitive detection is crucial for tumor diagnosis. This study aims to develop a label-free electrochemical biosensor based on a TiO2@Co/C@Au nanocomposite for highly sensitive detection of the PIK3CA gene. By optimizing the synthesis conditions of the composite, electrode modification process, and hybridization detection parameters, the synergistic effects of multiple components are utilized to enhance electrode conductivity and biomolecule loading capacity. Leveraging the magnetic properties of cobalt enables simple, controllable electrode modification, establishing a “signal-off” detection platform. The sensor has a linear range of 1 fM to 1 μM and a detection limit of 2.26 fM, enabling low femtomole detection of the PIK3CA gene with excellent specificity, reproducibility, and stability. In real serum sample testing, the sensor demonstrated good recovery rates (99.92%–117.75%), and the measured values closely matched the added concentrations, confirming its reliability and practicality in complex biological matrices. This provides a cost-effective, simple, and reliable new strategy for point-of-care detection of tumor-related genes. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Li X.; Feng M.; Liang M.; Zhu S.; Wang Q.; Chen P.; Jiao M.; Qiao Y.; Li L.
Title: A ppb-level H2S photoacoustic sensor with highly accurate and robust resonance frequency tracking using phase characteristics of acoustic excitation
Abstract: Photoacoustic spectroscopy (PAS) systems that employ a resonant photoacoustic cell (PAC) require accurate tracking of the resonance frequency to maintain optimal photoacoustic detection sensitivity. However, conventional frequency scanning relies on amplitude-peak searching, which is slow and susceptible to amplitude fluctuations and peak-position uncertainty. To address this, a photoacoustic gas sensor with highly accurate and robust resonance frequency tracking using the phase characteristics of acoustic excitation is proposed. A loudspeaker integrated into the PAC provides acoustic excitation independent of laser modulation and gas concentration. The resonance frequency is identified from the zero crossing of the corrected phase response, providing a highly accurate and robust resonance criterion. The method was experimentally demonstrated for H2S detection in an SF6 background. When the gas flow rate was changed from 75 to 50 sccm, phase-based resonance frequency correction increased the H2S sensitivity from 0.0318 to 0.0547 V/ppm, an improvement of approximately 72%, and the minimum detection limit was reduced from 349 ppb to 203 ppb at an optimal integration time of 277 s. The proposed method advances PAS resonance tracking from amplitude-peak searching to phase-criterion-based identification and is well suited for real-time closed-loop frequency control. It is readily extensible to other resonant photoacoustic systems, paving the way for continuous and unattended PAS operation in field environments. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Cheng T.; Wang X.; Wen P.; Zhang Z.; Jian W.
Author full names: Cheng, Tiancai (57216648144); Wang, Xiaoyu (57218518574); Wen, Pengyun (60933880200); Zhang, Zhuo (60934072900); Jian, Weiran (60434981500)
Title: Topology optimization of proton exchange membrane fuel cell flow fields with interface enhancement and morphology-robustness constraints
Abstract: Conventional density-based topology optimization is mainly driven by global flow and heat-transfer metrics. The fluid–solid interface is usually formed indirectly as the density field evolves, and thin and threshold-sensitive features can remain. To address these issues, an interface-enhanced and morphology-robust topology optimization method is proposed for the cathode flow field of proton exchange membrane fuel cells. In the flow–heat-transfer bi-objective framework, an active-interface enhancement term is constructed by coupling local interface density, a positive temperature-difference driving force, and a velocity-utilization factor. Local heat-transfer conditions can therefore directly influence interface placement. A morphology-robustness constraint is also constructed from the difference between eroded and dilated projections to suppress thin, isolated, and threshold-sensitive features. The interface-enhanced and robust topology-optimized flow field (IERTO-FF) is generated through two-dimensional thermofluid optimization and then reconstructed in three dimensions. It is compared with conventional, parameterized, and other topology-optimized flow fields using a steady, non-isothermal gas–liquid two-phase PEMFC model and 25 cm2 single-cell experiments. The IERTO-FF exhibits a pressure drop of 79.77 Pa, which is 91.39 % and 64.27 % lower than those of the serpentine and parallel flow fields, respectively. Its average liquid–water concentration is the lowest among the eight flow fields. At 0.5 V, the net power density reaches 0.6866 W/cm2, 16.04 % higher than that of the parallel flow field. The proposed method preserves the basic thermofluid performance while producing a clearer and more stable topology. Lower flow loss, improved liquid–water management, and higher electrochemical output are also achieved. The method provides a useful approach for inverse design of PEMFC cathode flow fields. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Hu W.; Ji G.
Title: Maximum bound preserving and energy stable exponential time differencing schemes for blue phase liquid crystals
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: The Landau-de Gennes theory provides a rigorous framework for modelling the blue phases of chiral liquid crystals, which exhibit complex defect structures. In this paper, we develop and analyse first- and second-order exponential time differencing (ETD) schemes for the associated gradient flow model, which unconditionally preserve the maximum bound principle and the energy dissipation process at the time-discrete level. For spatial discretization, we employ the Fourier spectral method. Subsequently, we construct a novel matrix-valued symmetric trace-free basis to diagonalize the curl operator, thereby extending the applicability of ETD-type methods to general coupled linear differential operators. Furthermore, for the fully discrete schemes, we establish the l∞ boundedness of the numerical solutions, verify the discrete energy dissipation law and derive optimal error estimates in the l2 norm. Various numerical experiments are presented to validate the theoretical results, verify that the eigenvalues of the Q-tensor remain bounded within the interval [−1/3,2/3], and demonstrate the effectiveness of simulating the dynamics of blue phases. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zhu X.; Song S.; Xu X.; Shi S.; Jiang C.
Title: Red luminescence and enhanced blue luminescence of BPO4-based phosphors and their applications in light-emitting diodes
Abstract: In this study, building upon our previous work on phosphate host materials, we developed red- and enhanced blue-emitting BPO4-based phosphors. BPO4 was selected as the host matrix due to its unique rigid tetrahedral framework, excellent thermal stability, and low phonon energy. By introducing MnSO4·H2O and MgCO3·Mg(OH)2·3H2O as dopants, we achieved distinct luminescent properties in the prepared phosphors. The Mg-doped system formed a BPO4/Mg2P2O7 composite, exhibiting significantly enhanced blue emission compared to pure BPO4. When integrated into cold white LED devices, this phosphor demonstrated outstanding performance with a high color rendering index Ra = 92.5, CRI = 91.1) and a correlated color temperature (CCT) of 6032 K. The Mn-doped phosphor retained a single-phase BPO4 structure, with Mn2+ ions successfully incorporated into the host lattice, enabling efficient red emission. This material was subsequently utilized to fabricate high-performance red LEDs. Our findings offering a promising approach for developing rare-earth-free luminescent materials. © 2026

Authors: Chen Q.; Zhou X.; Chen F.; Sun Z.
Title: A stochastic BSMPM-derived causal multi-task U-Net surrogate model for quantitative risk assessment of spatially variable slopes
Abstract: Spatial variability in soil strength controls both slope instability and post-failure runout, but quantitative risk assessment (QRA) remains exceptionally resource-intensive when each Monte Carlo realization requires a strength-reduction large-deformation simulation. Existing surrogates predict scalar indices or output fields in parallel without enforcing the mechanical sequence of failure. A Causal Multi-Task U-Net (CMT-UNet) surrogate model is developed from stochastic B-spline Material Point Method (BSMPM) simulations. Here, Causal refers to physics-causal decoder ordering implemented by gradient isolation between the equivalent plastic strain (PEEQ) and displacement branches, while Multi-Task denotes the three output heads (the strength reduction factor Ks, PEEQ, displacement). The model embeds mechanics-driven coupling: PEEQ is reconstructed as the precursor of slip-surface formation and is passed to the displacement decoder as a detached feature input, forcing displacement prediction to depend on the formed failure surface without backpropagating errors. Given slope geometry, initial stress, and heterogeneous shear-strength fields, CMT-UNet jointly predicts Ks, PEEQ, and displacement fields using a target-adaptive PEEQ loss, total-variation regularization, and a simplified Mohr–Coulomb form shear-strength regularizer. On an independent test set of 2054 samples, the model predicts Ks (R2=0.9795, MSE=0.0010, MAE=0.0240). Sliding volume (V), runout distance (L), and maximum crest settlement (H), extracted from the predicted fields, have MAPE values below 9% and Pearson r values of 0.807–0.896 against the SR-SBSMPM references. For 300 Monte Carlo simulations, the surrogate-assisted workflow reduces total computational time from 126.33 h to 16.18 h (87.2% saving). In a same-node hardware-normalized benchmark, the complete surrogate prediction chain accelerates the replaced large-deformation stage by approximately 2.4×103 on a 32-thread CPU and 2.8×103 on the GPU. The surrogate further enables Sobol sensitivity analysis across random-field generation algorithms and their discretization parameters. The results separate the controls on instability and post-failure response: Ks is dominated by mean cohesion and slope height, whereas V, L, and H depend more strongly on geometric driving potential and random-field interactions. Pairwise second-order indices were smaller and less certain than the dominant first-order and total-order effects. The proposed framework provides an efficient field-resolved route for quantitative risk assessment of spatially variable soil slopes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Zhang Y.; Su W.; Du R.
Author full names: Zhang, Yulin (58873271500); Su, Wenkang (56898394800); Du, Ruizhong (7103156747)
Title: DensePSA: Robust image watermarking framework with cross-scale dense structure and patch-wise self-attention mechanism
Abstract: While recent architectural advances in image watermarking have yielded notable performance improvements, they often introduce substantial model complexity and computational overhead, thereby impeding real-world deployment. To address this trade-off, we propose a robust yet lightweight image watermarking framework that integrates cross-scale dense connection with a self-attention mechanism. Specifically, we design a multi-scale dense-connected encoder/decoder architecture that systematically reuses intermediate features across resolutions, enhancing both feature utilization and representational capacity for reliable watermark embedding and extraction. Complementing this design, we incorporate a Patch-wise Self-Attention (PSA) module between convolutional stages. By partitioning high-resolution feature maps into non-overlapping patches and applying an adaptive re-weighting strategy, PSA effectively captures global dependencies with reduced computational cost. This patch-based design preserves global contextual information without incurring the prohibitive complexity associated with conventional attention models on large tensors. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of both imperceptibility and robustness against common signal-processing attacks, all while supporting real-time inference. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Liu Z.; Liu H.
Title: Escape operator-based competitive CSA with imitated gradient descent and integer planning for large-scale global optimization problems
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: To make Crow Search Algorithm (CSA) applicable to large-scale global optimization problems, this paper proposes a variant named Competitive Crow Search Algorithm (CCSA), which based on the ideas of competitive grouping and imitating gradient descent method. Firstly, a variant of opposition-based learning strategy is used to generate better initial solutions. Secondly, designing two adaptive parameters used in the original algorithm as well as a selection operator. They can make the population dynamically balance exploration and exploitation, improve convergence accuracy and prevent trapping in local optimum. Then, a grouping strategy is adopted to divide the population equally into two groups and a new formula for updating the position of the crows is designed separately, which greatly accelerate the convergence speed and accuracy. In addition, iteration phase is carried out in segments, and different update formulas are selected for different phases. It can allow the algorithm to be further balanced for exploration and exploitation. Finally, an accurate revision strategy based on the gradient descent and integer planning was integrated with CSA. It improves the convergence accuracy. CCSA is compared with the standard CSA, one advanced large-scale variant of CSA, and eight state-of-the-art evolutionary algorithms on 19 benchmark functions and the CEC2017 test set. The experimental results show that CCSA outperforms these comparative algorithms, demonstrating good results in low and high-dimensions. Applied to four engineering design problems, the results show that CCSA is also effective for real constrained optimization problems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zhao T.; Xie X.; Ye J.; Yang Z.
Title: Numerical modeling on the undrained cyclic liquefaction behaviors of imperfectly saturated sand
Abstract: In natural environments, the pore fluid of sand often contains a certain amount of gas, either in the form of closed bubbles or dissolved gas. As a result, even sand below the groundwater table may be in an imperfectly saturated state. Existing experimental studies have shown that the sand liquefaction resistance increases under imperfectly saturated conditions. However, numerical models describing the cyclic liquefaction behaviors of imperfectly saturated sand are still lacking. In the present study, a finite element model considering the effects of imperfect saturation was developed, and element-scale simulations were conducted to further investigate how this condition affects the cyclic liquefaction behaviors of sand: (1) First, a fully explicit finite element model was established based on the two-phase Biot’s theory. The pore water containing gas was treated as a homogeneous fluid, in which the effects of free and dissolved gas were described by Boyle’s and Henry’s laws, respectively. An advanced constitutive model was employed to represent the cyclic behaviors of the soil skeleton. (2) Subsequently, the proposed algorithm and self-developed FEM program was validated through comparisons with analytical solutions as well as laboratory monotonic and cyclic undrained tests, confirming that the mechanical responses of fully and imperfectly saturated sands can be reasonably captured. (3) Finally, the developed numerical approach was employed to investigate the distinctive cyclic liquefaction behaviors of imperfectly saturated sands under conventional triaxial conditions. The influences of degree of saturation, dissolved gas content, and cyclic stress path were examined, and the effect of dynamic evolution of saturation due to volumetric strain was also discussed. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Authors: Tahmasebi E.; Abdi M.
Title: A high-surface-area mesoporous carbon synthesized using porous hydroxyapatite nanostructures template: an efficient adsorbent for solid-phase extraction of parabens
Abstract: Herein, a mesoporous carbon material was prepared via pyrolysis of a melamine-resorcinol formaldehyde copolymer synthesized in the presence of mesoporous hydroxyapatite (HA) nanostructures, as a hard template. The porous HA nanostructures were prepared through a novel strategy that involved synthesizing calcium carbonate nanostructures on CTAB micellar aggregations as a soft template, followed by carbonate-phosphate replacement under hydrothermal conditions. This approach yielded microspheres composed of rod-like nanostructures featuring ordered approximately 1 nm nanochannels, exhibiting a BET surface area of 51.17 m2 g−1 and a BJH-derived characteristic pore diameter of 18.46 nm. The XRD analysis of the carbon product indicated the presence of a graphitic carbon structure, consistent with the Raman spectroscopy results. Additionally, the presence of oxygen and nitrogen heteroatoms and their related functional groups in the carbon framework was confirmed by elemental analysis and FT-IR spectroscopy. Based on BET analysis, the carbon product exhibited a high specific surface area of 882.78 m2 g−1, a large pore volume of 3.944 cm3 g−1, and a characteristic pore diameter of 32.58 nm obtained from BJH analysis. BET analysis highlighted the role of CTAB and carbonate in the synthesis of the HA template, enabling the achievement of high-surface-area mesoporous carbon. The combination of high porosity, graphitic domains, and oxygen- and nitrogen-containing species makes the material a promising adsorbent for the extraction of relatively polar aromatic compounds. The synthesized carbon material was employed as an effective adsorbent for the dispersive solid-phase extraction (SPE) of some parabens, preservatives with endocrine-disrupting effects, with detection using HPLC-UV. The experimental design methodology efficiently determined optimal extraction conditions while minimizing the number of experiments and analyzing parameter interactions. Under the optimized conditions, a good analytical performance for the proposed method was achieved with a linearity of 0.1-100.0 μg L−1 (R2 ≥ 0.998) and preconcentration factors ranging from 84 to 116 for the target analytes. The applicability of the proposed method was assayed in real samples with different matrices, yielding satisfactory relative recoveries (89-111%) and RSD values (n = 3) ranging from 2.4% to 7.9%. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Guo J.; Xiao K.; Guo M.; Huang J.; Fillon M.; Han Y.
Title: Transient wear prediction of planet gear journal bearings under mixed thermo-elastohydrodynamic lubrication using an entropy-degradation-based wear model
Abstract: This paper coupled a mixed thermo-elastohydrodynamic lubrication framework (TEHD) with a transient entropy-degradation-based wear model to quantitatively investigate the transient mixed lubrication and wear (TML-wear) behavior of planet gear journal bearings (PGJBs) under quasi-steady gear meshing conditions. The model accounted for planetary gear misalignment, thermal and elastic deformations of the pin bushing layer, as well as variations in surface roughness and lubricant temperature during operation. The predictive capability and reasonable transferability of the model were validated through comparisons with equivalent experimental data and available numerical results. Subsequently, the influence of key model parameters, including thermal effects, surface roughness, and degradation coefficient, on the predicted transient performance of the PGJB was investigated. The results highlighted the importance of incorporating thermal effects and surface roughness evolution for accurately predicting TML-wear performance, particularly the evolution of wear. The comparison with the classical Archard model further demonstrated the good parameter robustness of the adopted wear model for transient wear prediction within the investigated range. On this basis, the TML-wear performance of PGJBs under different loads was further explored, and the effectiveness of a symmetric semi-parabolic profile modification method in bearing performance improvement was evaluated. It was found that under the prescribed constant moment, reducing the applied load within the investigated range weakens hydrodynamic effects and reduces temperature rise but aggravates edge wear. Appropriate edge profile modification can effectively enhance the hydrodynamic lubrication of the PGJB and, more importantly, substantially suppress or even eliminate wear under the investigated operating and profile-modification conditions. However, excessive modification requires careful consideration, as it may induce local pressure concentration and secondary wear. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhang J.; Li S.; Chen J.; Luo C.; Ding Y.
Title: Construction of a bimetallic MOF-derived nanozymes with enhanced peroxidase-like activity for colorimetric detection of hydroquinone
Abstract: Hydroquinone (HQ) is a typical toxic phenolic pollutant that can severely disrupt the ecological balance of aquatic ecosystems and threaten human health. Therefore, it is imperative to develop simple and portable analytical techniques for the rapid on-site monitoring of HQ in aquatic environments. Here, the carbon-supported cobalt-nickel oxide nanozymes (CoNiOx@C) with enhanced peroxidase-like activity was synthesized using a CoNi bimetallic metal-organic framework (CoNi–MOF) as a precursor followed by annealing process. The significantly enhanced peroxidase-like activity of CoNiOx@C was derived from the synergistic effect of highly exposed Co/Ni–O–C bimetallic active sites and the in situ constructed carbon layer network, which effectively overcomes the inherent performance limitations of conventional nanozymes. Meanwhile, a catalytic signal amplification strategy was proposed based on the peroxidase-like mimetic mechanism of CoNiOx@C and the reducibility of the phenolic hydroxyl group, enabling the colorimetric detection of HQ. The colorimetric sensor developed showed good linearity in the range of 0–200 μM, with a detection limit as low as 0.068 μM. Interestingly, a portable visual detection platform was developed by integrating paper-based chips with smartphone, which achieves the sensitive the detection of HQ in real water samples. This study not only provides a facile synthetic route for MOF-derived bimetallic nanozymes but also offers a new approach for the development of low-cost, easy-to-operate visual on-site detection strategies. Authors: Wu J.; Xu H.; Huangfu Z.; Huang G.; Deng J.; Cao Y.; Li S.; Cui J.; Li J.
Title: Coal macerals separation technology: current status, mechanism, and development trends of resource utilization
Abstract: Coal is the most carbon-rich substance in nature, except for diamonds and graphite. Due to its abundant functional groups and defect sites, it is increasingly being utilized as a high-value-added chemical raw material. However, the inorganic mineral components in coal not only hinder its high-value development but also lead to resource waste and environmental pollution. Consequently, a comprehensive analysis of the various methodologies and intrinsic complexities involved in the separation of macerals from coal and rock is imperative to elucidate the future developmental trajectory in this domain. The present article commences with an examination of the sources and physical/chemical properties of each maceral (vitrinite, inertinite, liptinite, and huminite) in coal. A detailed analysis of the properties of each maceral was conducted, forming the basis for subsequent discussions of application methods and mechanisms. The discussions employed physical separation enrichment techniques (density gradient centrifugation (DGC), float-and-sink, dense medium separation (DMS), flotation, and friction electrostatic separation) and chemical separation enrichment techniques (chemical oxidation, chemical leaching, and solvent extraction). Meanwhile, the extant problems and application prospects of the current process separation technology are summarized and projected. Finally, after discussion, an economically feasible technical path was evaluated: The comprehensive processing of one ton of coal can yield a return of 18.7∼ 246.2 US dollars. Under the best conditions, the net profit per ton of coal can reach 246.2 US dollars, indicating a promising economic potential. This review aims to provide a solid theoretical foundation for the high-end, low-carbon, and eco-friendly utilization of coal resources. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Yao X.; Ma S.; Yuan L.; Duan H.
Title: A variational neural constitutive update with a conditional convex pseudo-potential for pressure-sensitive geomaterials
Abstract: Pressure-sensitive geomaterials, such as soils, rocks, and rock-like materials, often exhibit constitutive updates governed by path dependence, non-associated flow, dilation or contraction, and post-peak strength degradation. Conventional neural constitutive models based on direct stress regression generally lack an explicit incremental update structure and provide limited capability for dissipation diagnostics. To address these limitations, a thermodynamics-informed variational neural constitutive update framework is proposed. Instead of predicting stress directly, the framework introduces an equivalent irreversible correction variable in principal-stress space, whose optimal value is determined through an inner minimization problem; the updated stress is then recovered through an elastic return relation. To promote structural stability of the inner update, a partially input-convex neural network is used to construct a state-conditioned incremental dissipation pseudo-potential, which remains convex with respect to the equivalent correction variable when the trial state and history variables are fixed. During training, a component-normalized stress error, an equivalent return-correction consistency term, a penalty on negative algorithmic discrete dissipation, and a first-order stationarity residual are further introduced to jointly constrain the stress response, the equivalent irreversible correction, and the variational consistency of the inner problem. Validation using data generated by a non-associated Drucker–Prager softening model shows that the proposed model can accurately recover stress evolution under different confining pressures and loading paths. The predicted equivalent irreversible corrections are also broadly consistent with the equivalent return corrections inferred from the reference stresses, and the accumulated equivalent dissipation exhibits stable evolution along representative paths. These results indicate that the proposed framework preserves stress-prediction accuracy while providing a neural constitutive update method for pressure-sensitive geomaterials with an explicit variational structure, interpretable equivalent corrections, and dissipation-diagnostic capability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Thickness Gradient Design Enhances Bending Performance of Multilayer Beams through Slip Homogenization
Abstract: Multilayer structures are ubiquitous in both natural and engineered systems, with interlayer interactions governing their mechanical behavior. This study investigates the bending behavior of symmetric multilayer composite beams with interlayer slip, with particular emphasis on the critical role of thickness gradient design in optimizing structural performance. A comprehensive analytical framework is developed to predict interlayer slip distributions and global deflection in multilayer beams featuring arbitrary layer counts and continuous geometric gradients. Through combined analytical modeling and finite element validation, parametric analyses reveal that the bending response is predominantly governed by two key parameters: the layer thickness gradient and interfacial shear stiffness. Building on this foundation, this work establishes a quantitative design relationship linking “interfacial stiffness-thickness gradient-slip homogenization”, which is applicable to symmetric gradient beams with arbitrary layer counts. By proposing an optimized thickness gradient that achieves uniform interlayer slip, the design achieves a synergy between structural compliance (flexibility) and load-bearing capacity (strength). This optimization strategy enhances the structural reliability by mitigating localized interfacial damage, allowing for higher external loads before reaching interfacial capacity. Furthermore, this research reveals a dimensionless scaling law for the optimal thickness gradient, providing a practical foundation for the performance-driven design of functionally graded laminated composites. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Title: Enhanced flotation of coal gasification fine slag: mechanistic insights into functional group-regulated interfacial behavior of polar–nonpolar compound collectors
Abstract: Carbon–ash separation of coal gasification fine slag (CGFS) is essential for its resource utilization. However, oxygen-containing groups and a developed porous structure of residual carbon limit the selectivity of conventional nonpolar collectors such as kerosene (KER). In this study, polar–nonpolar compound collectors were constructed by introducing esters, ketones, aldehydes, and ethers into kerosene. The effects of functional group type and blending ratio on CGFS flotation were systematically investigated, and the interfacial regulation mechanisms were elucidated through interfacial characterization and flotation kinetics. The results showed that appropriate polar modification significantly enhanced carbon–ash separation, with esters, ketones, and aldehydes exhibiting stronger synergistic effects, whereas ethers showed limited enhancement. Comprehensive evaluation revealed that the KER–10% ethyl laurate (EL), KER–5% ethyl benzoate (EB), KER–10% 2,5-hexanedione (2,5-HD), and KER–10% undecanal (UDA) systems exhibited relatively favorable performance. KER–10% EL reduced the concentrate ash content to 55.99%, while KER–10% 2,5-HD increased the tailings ash content to 94.38%. The introduced polar functional groups reduced the surface tension, improved reagent dispersion, regulated interfacial charge distribution, and enhanced selective adsorption onto residual carbon. Among them, KER–5% EB exhibited the highest flotation rate constant (0.0148 s−1), selectivity index (1.5709), and wettability modification capability, achieving a relatively balanced flotation performance. Furthermore, KER–10% EL was more effective for concentrate upgrading, while KER–10% 2,5-HD favored deep decarbonization of tailings. Authors: Su T.; Wang P.; Wang P.; Liu J.; Zhuang H.; Ju W.; Liu J.; Lu X.
Title: Numerical investigation on the flow and heat transfer characteristics of impingement cooling in narrow channels under the influence of film hole aspiration
Abstract: Double-wall cooling structures in modern turbine blades demand increasingly refined design as the coupling between impingement and film-cooling elements intensifies. Yet the mechanism by which film-hole suction alters the impingement-cooling flow field remains insufficiently understood. This work presents a numerical investigation of jet-impingement cooling subjected to film-hole suction, examining how film-hole layout, jet Reynolds number (Re j ), and jet-to-target distance ( h/d ) govern the internal flow and heat transfer of the “impingement–film” system. Film-hole suction rapidly evacuates the spent coolant after impingement, substantially weakening the crossflow-induced shear and deflection of downstream jets; this improves the spatial uniformity of target-surface heat transfer and raises overall heat transfer intensity by 7 %–10 %. The enhancement is greatest when film holes and jet holes are arranged in a staggered configuration. Increasing Re j  thins the thermal boundary layer and augments turbulent kinetic energy (TKE), producing a secondary heat transfer peak away from the stagnation zone. Varying h/d from 0.5 to 4 allows more complete jet development and stronger mixing between the coolant and the ambient medium, raising relative thermal efficiency by up to 20 %. From a mechanistic perspective, heat transfer in the stagnation region is jointly affected by velocity gradient and temperature gradient, while heat transfer in the wall jet region is dominated by turbulent kinetic energy (TKE). Film-hole suction modulates both the spatial extent and intensity of these two mechanisms by reshaping the flow field. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Authors: Huang F.; Wang C.; Kong W.
Title: The effect of pressure on the characteristics of pure propane jet diffusion flame at sub-atmospheric pressures
Abstract: Sub-atmospheric pressure significantly influences the combustion stability of non-premixed jet flames at high-altitude conditions. This work conducts experimental and numerical simulation studies to investigate the flame stability of non-premixed propane jet under pressures ranging from 40 kPa to 101 kPa. The results show that the height of laminar jet flame increases linearly with volumetric flow rate. The flame flickering frequency decreases with increasing Reynolds number, while the flickering amplitude increases with Reynolds number. Pressure reduction advances the onset of the laminar-turbulent transition, yields wider radial flame expansion and facilitates flame liftoff. The height of attached laminar flame exhibits non-monotonic pressure dependence. It slightly decreases with rising pressure below a critical threshold, followed by a rebound increase. At a fixed Reynolds number, the laminar liftoff height increases monotonically with pressure drops, and a parallelogram stability regime is identified for stable laminar lifted flames. Based on edge-flame stabilization theory, a pressure-corrected correlation is proposed to predict the laminar liftoff height over the pressure range of 40–101 kPa. For all tested nozzle diameters, the flame blowout velocity increases with increasing pressure. Numerical results reveal that lower pressure weakens jet momentum dissipation, leading to faster axial flame penetration and greater flame length. By contrast, higher pressure intensifies shear layer instability, triggers more frequent flickering and larger-amplitude oscillations. The soot emissions increase as pressure decreases, whereas NOx formation shows a continuously increasing trend. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Comprehensive optimization of a detailed NH3/H2 combustion kinetic mechanism
Abstract: Over the last decade, numerous detailed NH3/H2 combustion kinetic mechanisms have been published, but none of the available models are accurate enough across a wide range of experimental conditions. In our previous study (Szanthoffer et al., 2026), the NUIG-2024 mechanism (Zhu et al., 2024) exhibited the best overall performance against a large collection of NH3 and NH3/H2 indirect experimental data, including shock tube ignition delay times, laminar burning velocities, and concentration data measured in various reactors. However, even NUIG-2024 could not reproduce the data points within their 3 σ uncertainty limits, on average, where σ is the standard deviation of the experimental data. This study focuses on optimizing a modified NUIG-2024 mechanism against our collection of NH3/H2 indirect experimental data (7,259 data points in 578 data series) using a mean-squared objective function. The most impactful reactions in the initial mechanism were identified using local sensitivity analysis results and uncertainties of rate coefficients and indirect experimental data. The model parameters selected for optimization comprise 25 sets of Arrhenius parameters (A , n , E) and the third-body collision efficiency of NH3 for the H + O2 (+M) = HO2 (+M) reaction. Authors: Zhu Z.; Li J.; Zhu G.; Duan P.; Hou J.; Wang R.; Xu K.; Cao Y.
Title: Structural evolution of coal vitrinite during coalification revealed by in situ synchronous Infrared-Raman spectroscopy and molecular imaging
Abstract: Accurately characterizing coal vitrinite molecular structure is crucial for understanding coalification and enabling efficient utilization. FTIR and Raman spectroscopy require separate measurements, preventing analysis of the same microregion, and conventional FTIR microscopy suffers from the Abbe diffraction limit, which restricts its lateral resolution. Here, optical photothermal infrared spectroscopy enables in situ synchronous infrared-Raman analysis and high-resolution molecular distribution imaging across six vitrinite samples of varying maturities. O-PTIR overcomes the infrared diffraction limit (∼500 nm) and acquires both infrared and Raman spectra from the same microregion with matching lateral resolution, reducing errors caused by coal heterogeneity. With increasing maturity, the infrared A-factor and C-factor decrease, suggesting progressive removal of aliphatic structures and oxygen-containing groups. Aliphatic chain length and Raman AD1/AG show variations with coal rank, implying aliphatic decomposition and reconstruction influence carbon skeleton ordering. No strong correlation between the C-factor and AD1/AG was observed, indicating oxygen functional group removal may have limited impact on the carbon skeleton. High-resolution molecular imaging generates hundreds of thousands of data points per microregion at submicron scale. Pseudo–Van Krevelen analysis shows distribution centers of the A-factor and C-factor shift toward the origin with increasing maturity, while data points progressively converge—statistically reflecting deoxygenation, decarbonization, and structural condensation, alongside microscale heterogeneous molecular evolution. This integrated approach offers a valuable tool for investigating micro- to nanoscale organic structures and provides spectroscopic insights into coalification mechanisms and heterogeneity assessment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Shah N.
Title: Resilient edge-mesh federated learning for LPWAN-based urban flood monitoring
Abstract: Urban flooding risk is rising, and centralised monitoring systems are prone to network congestion during disasters. This paper presents a four-tier edge-mesh federated framework for resilient disaster sensing in smart cities with limited infrastructure. The framework integrates real and physically derived multi-modal sensing—rainfall, water level, and a recession-time-based soil moisture index (SMI)—GRU-based edge intelligence, and Byzantine-robust federated learning with gradient sparsification, gossip-based pre-consensus, and sample-weighted Krum aggregation. Performance is evaluated on real INDOFLOODS flood gauge data from 15 Maharashtra stations (749 events, 1965–2019), objectively selected by highest event count, with all three modalities weakly correlated ((Formula presented) ). All results are mean± std over 5 seeds and 30 communication rounds. Multi-modal fusion achieves lower MSE (0.092 ± 0.012) than unimodal sensing (0.108 ± 0.017). The proposed Krum-Mesh aggregator achieves lower MSE than FedAvg across all corruption scenarios (e.g., 0.093 vs. 0.119 under 20% Byzantine extreme-value poisoning), supported by a formal (Formula presented) guarantee satisfied at 20% and 26% Byzantine ratios. Krum-Mesh retains an advantage over FedAvg under the adaptive “A Little Is Enough” attack, though the margin compresses relative to oblivious attacks; the aggregation mechanism scales empirically as (Formula presented) up to 100 synthetic wards with the safety condition preserved throughout. Physical-layer analysis confirms a LoRa duty cycle of 0.2551%, well within the 1% regulatory limit, and energy analysis confirms a (Formula presented) improvement, with an estimated transmission-only battery lifetime of 2288 days under sparsified updates. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: DME as a challenge for commercial Pt/Pd-series diesel oxidation catalysts
Abstract: This paper examines the stationary dimethyl ether (DME) oxidation behavior of state-of-the-art diesel oxidation catalysts (DOCs) under both model conditions and scenarios that closely resemble real-world application. The study investigates the implications of new hydrocarbon (HC) mixtures present in the exhaust gas matrix of DME-fueled combustion engines, focusing on the potential application of series-production DOCs within exhaust aftertreatment systems. Utilizing a synthetic gas test bench (SGB), gas mixtures are designed to simulate realistic operating conditions, including one scenario with 100% DME fuel and another where DME is blended with Diesel fuel, leading to varying HC mixtures. Experimental findings reveal that 2 out of 5 DOCs convert <50% of the raw DME emissions reaching temperatures of 374 °C. Under these realistic conditions, also 0 out 5 DOCs convert <80% until reaching 379 °C. Notably, while DME partly inhibits NO oxidation at intermediate temperatures, it does not promote N2O formation as propene does. The experiments further reveal distinct temperature-dependent patterns of secondary emissions, including formaldehyde, formic acid, carbon monoxide, methanol, and methyl formate. These secondary emissions are strongly affected by the exhaust gas composition and are substantially reduced or shifted under conditions representative of DME-containing engine exhaust. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Notes on trace characterizations via inequalities concerning different versions of the geometric mean and relative entropies

Authors: Xi R.; Xie L.; Fang B.W.
Title: Learning fuzzy measures for multi-distance fusion in ordinal classification
Abstract: Ordinal classification aims to predict discrete labels with an inherent order, where different prediction errors may imply different ordinal deviations and practical costs. Although existing methods have modeled ordinal label structures from various perspectives, the fusion of heterogeneous geometric relations among samples remains insufficiently explored. In distance-based ordinal classification, different distance measures may produce inconsistent local neighborhood orders, suggesting that, particularly in high-dimensional settings, a single distance is often inadequate for describing ordinal sample relations. To address this issue, this paper proposes a multi-distance fusion method via Choquet integral for ordinal classification. The method constructs five diverse base distances, including Euclidean, Manhattan, Canberra, Bray–Curtis, and cosine distances, under a unified standardization scheme. The Choquet integral is then used to aggregate these distances nonadditively, enabling the model to capture both individual distance contributions and interactions among distance subsets. To align the fused distance with the ordinal label structure, ordinal triplet ranking constraints are introduced and fuzzy measure learning is formulated as a linear programming problem. In prediction, the learned fused distance is incorporated into an ordinal nearest-neighbor rule with distance-adaptive weighting and ordinal cost minimization. Experiments on 31 public ordinal classification datasets show that our method achieves competitive and stable performance in terms of ACC, MAE, C-index, BA, AMAE, Kendall’s τ , and MMAE. Ablation results further confirm the benefits of multi-distance representation and nonadditive fusion based on fuzzy measures over linear weighted fusion and single-distance variants, and the ordinal decision rule is shown to be more effective than simple majority voting. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Extending the operating range of HCCI engines with the rhombic drive mechanism: A novel concept
Abstract: Homogeneous charge compression ignition (HCCI) engines offer high thermal efficiency and very low nitrogen oxides (NOx) and soot emissions, but they have significant challenges such as a limited operating range, knocking at high loads, and misfiring at low loads. In this study, the use of a rhombic drive mechanism as an alternative to the conventional crankshaft mechanism was numerically investigated for the first time to extend the operating range of HCCI engines. A total of 301 computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations were performed using CONVERGE CFD, employing an HCCI engine model validated with experimental data. The simulations were conducted at engine speeds of 800–2600 rpm, within a λ range of 1.3–3.4, using fuels with research octane numbers of 20 and 40 (RON20 and RON40). The results showed that the rhombic drive mechanism extended the compression phase, allowing the piston to remain near top dead center (TDC) for a longer duration. This increased the average cylinder temperature, facilitating auto-ignition and enabling stable HCCI combustion near the low-load limit at higher engine speeds. With the rhombic drive mechanism, heat release was more concentrated around TDC, the combustion duration was shortened, and the combustion process approached a constant-volume character. The principal contribution of the rhombic drive mechanism was extending the upper engine-speed limit of naturally aspirated HCCI operation. The low-load improvement was secondary, while higher MPRR under identical engine-speed and lambda conditions showed no direct extension of the high-load limit at a fixed speed. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Interface-aware adaptive layer-wise physics-informed neural networks for multilayer large-strain consolidation: a benchmark of architectures, training strategies, and trade-offs
Abstract: Multilayer large-strain consolidation in stratified soils involves nonlinear pore-pressure dissipation, evolving deformation, and material discontinuities, which pose significant challenges for physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). This study develops a layer-wise adaptive PINN framework in which soil layers are represented by neural subnetworks coupled through pore-pressure and Darcy-flux continuity conditions. A controlled three-layer benchmark is used to evaluate MLP and KAN architectures, adaptive activation, adaptive weighting, and parameter sharing over three independent random seeds. The framework is further extended to four- and five-layer profiles using Shared MLP, layer-wise MLP, and KAN. Results demonstrate that no single architecture is optimal across all physical responses: parameter sharing improves mean global and settlement accuracy, KAN-based models better control selected local errors, and adaptive strategies alter pressure, settlement, and interface behavior in a metric-dependent manner. The successful four- and five-layer calculations further support the applicability of the same physical formulation as the number of internal interfaces increases, although the preferred architecture changes with the layer arrangement. Overall, pore-pressure accuracy, settlement prediction, interface consistency, and computational cost involve distinct trade-offs, so model selection should reflect the target physical quantity and profile complexity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Xu K.; Chen D.; Luo Y.; Tong Y.; Mao Z.; Xu X.
Title: Performance evolution and adaptability improvement method of fuel cell systems at variable altitudes based on multi-dimensional bubble map
Abstract: The performance of proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) systems at high altitudes is severely constrained by low atmospheric pressure and hypoxic conditions, resulting in a decrease in net power and a sharp increase in the air compressor consumption . This study investigates a 150 kW commercial vehicle fuel cell system through environmental chamber tests (0–5000 m) and a high-fidelity model with flow and pressure errors within 1.5 %. To analyze performance evolution and enhance adaptability, a multi-dimensional bubble mapping (MDBM) method is proposed, constructing a four-dimensional parameter space of current density, altitude, oxygen excess ratio (OER), and inlet pressure. Results identify 3000 m as a critical turning point where the air compressor approaches its rated operating boundary. At 5000 m and 2.0 A/cm2, the net power decreases by approximately 23 % compared to the plain level. The proposed “loss degree” indicator reveals a maximum power loss of 23.5 % with a low current densities at 5000 m. Through multi-parameter collaborative optimization of inlet pressure and OER for the 3000–5000 m range, a performance improvement of at least 2.66 % is achieved across the operating range, with an average improvement of 5.5 %. Specifically, at 5000 m and 760 A, the optimized net power gain reaches 17.64 kW, a 14.99 % increase over the original strategy. The MDBM method effectively elucidates the nonlinear trade-off between net output and parasitic power, supporting efficient fuel cell operation across wide altitude ranges. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Label- and- enzyme free electrochemical DNA biosensor for ultrasensitive detection of breast cancer prognostic marker ESR1
Abstract: Breast cancer is a complex heterogeneous disease that continues to impose a substantial global burden on women's health. Analysis of ESR1 gene expression using non-invasive liquid biopsy has significant prognostic value, serving as an indicator of poor prognosis and overall survival (OS) in patients with ER+/HER-2− (Estrogen Receptor+/Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor-2−) breast cancer. This underscores the need for a reliable detection method for disease monitoring. UV laser induced graphene (UV-LIG) electrodes were produced by laser scribing of polyimide sheets subjected to UV-ozone treatment, providing a hydrophilic, activated surface that enhances cationic PLL adsorption. The successful fabrication of the UV-LIG-based DNA biosensor was confirmed by SEM, TEM, and XPS analyses. Under optimized conditions, chronoamperometric measurements exhibited a well-defined linear relationship between current density response and the logarithm of ESR1 target concentration over a range of 10 aM to 1 nM, with a detection limit of 2.5 aM and a quantification limit of 8.3 aM, without requiring any labeling procedures. Title: Er3+/Yb3+ codoped multicomponent NBiBSA glass for upconversion and NIR broadband applications
Abstract: The Er3+/Yb3+ co-doped glasses of composition, 20 Na2O - 10 Bi2O3 - 15 B2O3 - (50-x-y) SiO2 - 5 Al2O3 - x Er2O3 - y Yb2O3 (NBiBSAErYb) were prepared by conventional melt quench method. The non-metallic behaviour was known by evaluating the metallization factor. Considerably low reflection loss makes NBiBSAErYb glass suitable for 1533 nm laser gain medium. The measured Ω2 parameters reveal an asymmetric environment around Er3+ and Yb3+ ions. The studied glasses were characterized for 1533 nm (Er3+: 4I13/2 → 4I15/2) emission upon 980 nm leaser excitation. The emission intensity was effectively sensitized by Yb3+ codoping by Yb3+ → Er3+ energy transfer. The emission cross sections found from J-O theory were found close to those obtained from the McCumber theory. The Yb3+ → Er3+ energy transfer was confirmed through excited state decay measurements. The NBiBSAErYb glass shows a better flat gain coefficient with a population inversion of ≥ 50%. The laser characteristics such as full width at half maximum (78.3 nm), stimulated emission cross-section (9.20 ×10−21 cm2), gain bandwidth (7.20 ×10−26 cm3) and figure of merit (2.07 ×10−23 cm2s) corresponding to 4I13/2 → 4I15/2 transition show the potentiality of NBiBSAErYb glass for the emission of 1533 nm luminescence. Title: Recent advances in graphene/metal oxide composites for high-performance electrochemical energy systems. A review
Abstract: The growing need for sustainable energy storage and conversion technologies has accelerated the development of advanced and efficient electrode materials. Graphene/metal oxide (G/MO) composites have become a promising new generation of hybrid materials that combine the high electrical conductivity and high surface area. G/MO composites also integrate high mechanical strength of graphene with the high redox activity and high theoretical capacity of transition-metal oxides in a synergistic. This review critically reviews recent advances in the design, synthesis, and use of these composites for electrochemical energy systems, such as lithium- and sodium-ion batteries (LIBs and SIBs), supercapacitors, electrocatalysis, and photoelectrochemical (PEC) devices. Despite great progress, the systems are still limited by the challenges of restacking of graphene, poor control and limited interfacial scalability, and the instability of the metal oxides. This review offers a balanced view of the prospects and limitations of G/MO composites through discussions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Chowdhury S.; Adhikari S.
Title: Nonlinear rolling rod viscoelastic damper inerters: Closed-form expressions under structural uncertainty
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel nonlinear rolling rod viscoelastic damper inerter (NRRVDI) for vibration mitigation of uncertain structural systems. The device integrates rolling rod dynamics, inerter induced inertia enhancement, nonlinear Coulomb friction, and viscoelastic hereditary damping within a unified passive control framework. A nonlinear mathematical model is derived using Lagrange’s energy method, and bounded structural uncertainties are incorporated through stochastic modelling. Closed form expressions for the optimal tuning frequency ratio, damping ratio, and equivalent friction damping ratio are analytically derived using both H∞ and H2 optimisation criteria. The developed formulations eliminate iterative numerical optimisation and provide direct physical insight into the influence of inerter coupling and nonlinear damping mechanisms. Frequency domain and nonlinear time domain analyses are performed to evaluate the vibration mitigation performance under deterministic and stochastic structural conditions. The results demonstrate excellent agreement between deterministic predictions and Monte Carlo simulation responses. NRRVDI achieves 76.6% and 52.9% additional vibration reduction relative to benchmark FTMD and TMDI systems, respectively, in the frequency domain. In the nonlinear time domain, NRRVDI further achieves 2.77% and 10.64% additional vibration reduction relative to FTMD and TMDI systems, respectively, under stochastic structural conditions. The nonlinear responses also demonstrate faster transient attenuation and smaller residual oscillations compared with the benchmark dampers. Overall, NRRVDI demonstrates robust and broadband nonlinear vibration suppression capability under uncertain dynamic environments. © 2026 The Author(s). Published by Elsevier Inc. Title: Markov chain-based mixed traffic flow modeling incorporating platooning willingness in connected vehicle management
Abstract: This study develops a Markov chain framework to characterize mixed traffic flow composed of connected vehicle platoons and regular vehicles, incorporating connected vehicle penetration rate, user platooning willingness, and maximum platoon size into an analytical capacity model. Theoretical derivations reveal that mixed traffic capacity increases monotonically with both penetration rate and platooning willingness, though the relationship with willingness is neither globally convex nor concave. The capacity also increases with maximum platoon size at a decreasing rate, implying the existence of an optimal size for capacity management. Numerical results demonstrate that neglecting platooning willingness overestimates capacity by up to 32.2%. The proposed optimal management strategy for maximum platoon size improves capacity by up to 66.9% and, compared with the upper-bound strategy, reduces platoon size by over 10% with a capacity loss of <1.4%. These findings suggest that optimal platoon size management can substantially enhance capacity while improving operational feasibility. Title: An efficient spectral clustering algorithm based on adaptive granular ball anchors
Abstract: Anchor-graph spectral clustering is widely adopted for large-scale clustering, yet existing anchor-based schemes suffer from two practical limitations: clustering quality is highly sensitive to anchor representativeness, and the anchor count must be manually predefined. Drawing on granular ball (GB) computing, we propose GB-ASC, an efficient spectral clustering method based on adaptive granular ball anchors. Our method automatically determines both the number and distribution of anchors from the intrinsic data structure, faithfully preserving complex data topology. Specifically, compact granular balls are adaptively generated via intra-ball distance minimization; their centers serve as anchors to construct a sparse anchor graph, and singular value decomposition (SVD) derives spectral embeddings for clustering. Title: Cryo-EM structure of oat amyloid fibrils reveals ordered histidine arrays on the surface
Abstract: Oat globulin, the major seed storage protein in Avena sativa, has recently been shown to form amyloid fibrils with exceptional iron-stabilizing capacity, yet the atomic-level structural basis remains unknown. The atomic model reveals a compact hydrophobic core devoid of charged residues, while two histidine residues (His418 and His427) per layer are stacked along the fibril axis to form two parallel rows on the solvent-exposed surface. These surface histidine arrays offer a possible molecular-level explanation for the exceptional iron bioavailability of oat fibrils observed clinically. Title: Multi-level Synergy Alignment Framework for weakly supervised visible-infrared person re-identification
Abstract: Visible-infrared person re-identification (VI-ReID) is an important task for all-weather surveillance, but it remains challenging due to significant modality discrepancies and the high cost of annotating cross-modality identity correspondences. To reduce annotation dependence, this paper focuses on weakly supervised VI-ReID, where only intra-modality identity labels are available and explicit cross-modality identity correspondences are absent. In MSAF, the Cross-Spectral Consensus Block (CSCB) performs frequency-domain decomposition and adaptive fusion to integrate complementary low- and high-frequency cues and enhance cross-spectral structural representations. The Self-Organized Semantic Anchoring (SOSA) module discovers discriminative local semantic anchors with learnable prototypes and constructs a global-local pedestrian representation. The Uncertainty-Driven Expert Synergy (UDES) mechanism estimates sample-level reliability and modulates cross-modality prediction scores to reduce the influence of noisy pseudo labels. Title: A differentiable energy minimization framework for massive parallel analysis of laterally loaded piles
Abstract: Current design objectives of laterally loaded piles are increasingly shifting from deterministic calculations to reliability-based analysis to consider various uncertainties, which requires extensive sample evaluations and brings great computational challenges to conventional analytical frameworks. This study proposes a Differentiable Energy Minimization framework for Pile Analysis (DEM-PA), which enables the rapid parallel analysis of a massive number of samples without sacrificing accuracy. Based on the principle of minimum total potential energy, DEM-PA discretizes the pile and directly treats the nodal degrees of freedom (DOFs) as optimizable variables, minimizing the global energy functional via backpropagation and optimization algorithms. By employing localized Gaussian quadrature, the framework effectively decouples the simulation of pile deformation and soil resistance. This allows it to accurately capture complex local soil fluctuations with minimal active DOFs. By structuring all computations into standardized tensor formats, DEM-PA leverages Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) parallelization for the simultaneous evaluation of massive samples. Title: High-order flexoelectric beams and bars with transversal strain and axial voltage
Abstract: Flexoelectric beams become electromechanically active at small scales, but most one-dimensional models neglect through-thickness electric and strain boundary layers, transverse deformation, and the longitudinal electric field. The solutions are validated against fully resolved two-dimensional finite-element simulations. The analysis shows that the effective transverse response is thickness-dependent: at the nanoscale, lateral contraction can become as large as the axial strain, with the effective Poisson-like ratio increasing from the bulk value (≈0.49) to a flexoelectric plateau of (≈0.91) as the thickness-to-length-scale ratio t/ℓμ decreases across four orders of magnitude, in close agreement with two-dimensional finite-element results. Bending and axial loading also behave differently: bending produces no net voltage along the beam, whereas axial loading admits a net end-to-end potential difference. Title: Square ℓ2-norm based Angle principal component analysis
Abstract: Angle PCA represents a significant advancement in robust PCA research, as it enhances the robustness of PCA by incorporating the geometric structure information of data and employing the sparse ℓ2-norm. In this paper, we aim to analyze the main reason of Angle PCA with robustness to noise, and proposed that Angle PCA should adopt the square ℓ2-norm instead of using the sparse ℓ2-norm constraint. More specifically, a generalized Angle PCA framework is proposed, which first analyzed the geometry structure information lacking by the classical PCA model, and then proposed the square ℓ2-norm model and extended it to p-power of ℓ2-norm. The proposed model effectively captures the underlying geometry structure of the original data and leads to the conclusion that the p-power of ratio form carrying the geometry structure information is the key factor responsible for noise robustness. In the experimental section, we first explore the importance of geometric structure information under clean and noisy data conditions. More specifically, the proposed model is compared with both PCA and Angle PCA on clean and noisy datasets. The experimental results show the proposed method outperforms the classical PCA on the clean dataset and outperforms Angle PCA method on the noisy datasets, and thus the contribution of the ratio form with the square ℓ2-norm is more robust to noise than Angle PCA. Title: Regime shifts in shallow lakes: Modeling nonlinear feedbacks in submerged macrophyte-epiphyte-snail system
