Abstract: A three-dimensional dynamical model is formulated to investigate the interactions among submerged macrophytes, epiphytes, and snails in shallow lake ecosystems. The model incorporates key processes such as shading effect, selective grazing behavior, and nonlinear predation pressure from higher trophic levels. Title: Photocatalytic degradation and detoxification of tetracycline by magnetic nano TiO2-SiO2/Fe3O4 photocatalysts evaluated with integrated chemical, antibacterial and phytotoxicity assessment

Abstract: Tetracycline (TC), a major antibiotic, has a severe impact on plants via inhibition of chloroplast, making its removal from aquatic systems an urgent issue. The degradation rate significantly depended on the initial TC concentration, which could be explained by UV light absorption by TC molecules themselves. The antibacterial inhibition zone test with Lactobacillus casei showed the decrease in zone area over photocatalytic treatment time, indicating the reduction of residual antibacterial activity. The phytotoxicity test using Pak choi seeds revealed that leaves did not turn green in TC solution—that is, reduction in chlorophyll content. As the photocatalytic treatment time increased, the leaves turned green, and, they were close to those in water after two hours of treatment, indicating the reduction of chlorophyll-inhibitory effect. Authors: Yang X.; Guo K.; Cheng P.; Du Q.
Title: Ratiometric fluorescence sensor based on molecularly imprinted lanthanide metal-organic framework for specific and sensitive detection of uric acid
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: The early diagnosis of hyperuricemia urgently demands highly selective and sensitive analytical methods for uric acid (UA). To this end, via the combination of a luminescent lanthanide metal-organic framework (Eu-MOF) and molecularly imprinted polymers (MIPs), this study facilely constructed a sensitive ratiometric fluorescence sensor, designated Eu-MOF@MIP, for the specific recognition and rapid detection of UA in complex samples. Here, Eu-MOF serves as the dual-emission ratiometric signal unit, while the surface imprinted layer provides tailor-made recognition cavities for UA, enabling efficient discrimination of UA from its structural analogues and common coexisting substances. Mechanistic investigation indicated that the UA-induced ratiometric response is primarily governed by specific recognition of UA by the imprinted cavities, while the inner filter effect may affect absolute fluorescence intensity but contributes negligibly to the ratiometric signal. Under the optimized experimental parameters, satisfactory linearity toward UA was observed over the 1–20 mg/L range, with a detection limit of 0.007 mg/L (3σ/slope). The proposed sensor was successfully employed for UA detection in human urine, giving spiked recoveries of 97.94%–107.62% with relative standard deviations (RSD) below 3.55%. Overall, the developed Eu-MOF@MIP ratiometric fluorescence sensor provides a simple, rapid and highly selective analytical tool for routine UA monitoring, and also provides a new approach for constructing high-performance sensing platforms targeting other disease biomarkers. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Thi Le N.; Kieu Linh N.; Tuan Viet T.
Author full names: Thi Le, Nguyen (60986169800); Kieu Linh, Nguyen (56845067000); Tuan Viet, Tran (60985650800)
Title: A fast constructive algorithm for large-scale generation of orthogonal polygonal structures with applications to benchmarking geometric algorithms
Abstract: Efficient generation of large-scale structured data plays an important role in simulation and performance evaluation of algorithms. However, constructing complex geometric instances with guaranteed validity and a prescribed size remains computationally challenging. In this paper, we propose a simple and efficient constructive algorithm for generating orthogonal polygonal structures with a fixed number of vertices. The algorithm incrementally evolves a seed configuration using local transformations, while ensuring structural validity and exact control over the number of vertices. The method runs in polynomial time, and its correctness and complexity are formally analyzed. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method substantially outperforms the two baseline algorithms, Inflate-Cut and Inflate-Paste (Tomas and Bajuelos, 2004), in both runtime and memory consumption. For instances with n=50,000 vertices, the proposed method requires approximately 11.45 s, whereas Inflate-Cut takes about 38 min, corresponding to a speedup of approximately 200 times. Under the same experimental environment, in which all three algorithms were evaluated on the same computer configuration, the proposed method remains computationally feasible for instances containing up to one million vertices. In contrast, Inflate-Paste becomes impractical beyond approximately 5, 000 vertices, while Inflate-Cut is limited to approximately 50, 000 vertices. The proposed method also requires substantially less memory than the baselines across the tested instances. Furthermore, nearest-neighbor-based uniformity measures indicate that the generated vertices are more evenly distributed over the normalized spatial domain. In addition, the generated datasets are used to benchmark representative algorithms for orthogonal hull computation and minimum-area rectilinear convex hull computation, providing empirical insights into their performance on large-scale inputs. These results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm is an effective tool for large-scale data generation, simulation, and benchmarking of geometric and computational algorithms. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Sotoodeh K.
Title: Tribology of industrial valves: Contact interfaces, degradation mechanisms, and surface engineering strategies—A review
Abstract: Industrial valves operate under severe tribological conditions involving high contact stresses, sliding motion, particulate erosion, and corrosive environments. Their reliability and service life depend on friction, wear, and lubrication at critical interfaces, particularly the closure-member-to-seat, stem-to-packing, and dynamic sealing contacts. This review provides a comprehensive assessment of industrial valve tribology by linking valve-specific operating conditions, degradation mechanisms, material selection, and surface engineering solutions. It examines the principal tribological interfaces across major valve types and discusses the mechanisms governing friction, lubrication, and wear under severe service conditions. The influence of lubrication regimes and contact mechanics on valve performance is evaluated together with the tribological behaviour of engineering materials and protective coatings, including cobalt-based hardfacing alloys, thermal spray coatings, and PVD/CVD coatings. Finally, current engineering challenges and emerging research directions, including advanced coatings, digital technologies, and sustainable valve engineering, are discussed to support the development of more reliable and durable industrial valve systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zheng J.; Niu M.; Zhong H.; Niu B.; Ma B.; Xu C.
Title: Modification of coal tar with turpentine for the production of a coal–biomass hybrid high-density fuel
Abstract: Co-upgrading coal tar with biomass-derived compounds via alkylative cyclization provides a potential strategy for tailoring the molecular structure and fuel-related properties of complex hydrocarbon feedstocks. In this study, an alkylative cyclization process was developed to convert biomass-derived turpentine and low-temperature coal tar into higher-molecular-weight polycyclic products. Catalyzed by metal trichlorides, the reaction resulted in substantial reconstruction of the carbon-number distribution and molecular structures of the feedstocks. A combination of GC, GC–MS, GC × GC-TOF-MS, FT-IR, HRMS, 1H NMR spectroscopy, and DFT calculations was employed to investigate the product composition, structural evolution, and possible reaction mechanism. After hydrorefining under optimized conditions, a coal–biomass hybrid high-density hydrocarbon product with a density of 0.9398 g/mL and a gross calorific value of 45.98 MJ/kg was obtained. These results demonstrate the potential of this strategy for producing high-density fuel components. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Jamalabadi S.; Schwiegelshohn U.
Title: An improved lower bound for the online preemptive single-machine weighted completion time problem
Abstract: We address the problem of online preemptive single-machine scheduling to minimize the total weighted completion time. We improve the lower bound on the competitive ratio of deterministic algorithms from 1.0730 to 1.1038. Based on this approach and the worst-case instance for the WSRPT (Weighted Shortest Remaining Processing Time) algorithm, we describe a new adversarial strategy that enables the determination of even better lower bounds. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Luys L.; Ghose P.; Verbeke M.
Author full names: Luys, Lara (60633422800); Ghose, Prangon (61011925400); Verbeke, Mathias (55332189100)
Title: Efficient drift detection and model adaptation for edge MLOps leveraging class separability in the latent space
Abstract: When machine learning (ML) applications are deployed in real-world settings, the dynamic nature of these environments often leads to a gradual degradation in model performance over time. This is called drift, which is one of the challenges the Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) paradigm tries to solve using drift detection techniques. At the same time, there is an ongoing trend of moving ML models onto edge devices, closer to the source of the data, avoiding latency issues of inference on the cloud. However, these devices have limited resources making it challenging to employ MLOps techniques like drift detection, which often require large amount of data and processing power. This paper introduces LSDD+ as a robust and efficient drift detection technique with an incorporated model adaptation strategy. This strategy makes it possible to implement new concepts whilst also recognizing previously known concepts. LSDD+ is evaluated against several other state-of-the-art drift detectors on three semi-synthetic datasets. It shows a significant increase in efficiency compared to the most accurate drift detectors whilst still being on par with these detectors in the ability to detect drift. This proves the method’s suitability for MLOps on the edge. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies.

Authors: Lyu C.; Han K.; Chen J.; Zhang J.; Teng Q.; Xu W.; Liu Z.
Title: A unified medical incomplete multimodal diagnosis framework based on optimal feature disentanglement
Abstract: Multimodal disease diagnosis integrates diverse clinical data for comprehensive results but faces challenges due to missing modalities. Existing methods that reconstruct missing information often suffer from significant noise and high training costs. To address these issues, we propose Uni-IMD, a unified medical incomplete multimodal diagnosis framework based on optimal feature disentanglement. Uni-IMD employs optimal transport to efficiently disentangle multimodal features, extracting high-quality common features that serve as a bridge for reconstructing missing information while minimizing noise. Uni-IMD integrates both complete and incomplete modality learning into a single architecture, reducing computational overhead and enabling close interaction between them. The framework is robust to any modality input situation during both training and testing. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate that Uni-IMD efficiently handles varying degrees of modality missing under a unified multimodal diagnosis architecture, offering a novel and promising solution for complex clinical deployment of multimodal diagnosis models. © 2026

Authors: Guo F.; Li Y.; Liang J.; Guo X.; Liu R.; Nie J.
Title: Damage-ignition mechanism of composite energetic materials with different densities under multi-pulse loading
Abstract: Ignition of composite energetic materials (CEMs) may occur under multi-pulse loading, involving a complex interplay between damage and hotspot accumulation. The ignition mechanism is not clear due to the heterogeneous structure and complexity of the loading. In this study, multi-pulse dynamic compression tests were conducted on CEMs with different initial densities. The deformation, damage evolution, ignition behavior and temperature field were quantitatively characterized using a high-speed camera and an ultra-high-speed electro-optical framing camera. A coupled damage-ignition constitutive model for CEMs was established, including tensile failure, shear fracture and an ignition criterion governed by cumulative plastic dissipation. The results showed that ignition occurred during the third loading pulse. The ignition threshold and ignition delay time of CEMs are strongly dependent on the initial density and loading condition. The ignition and burning processes exhibited spatial heterogeneity. The hotspots first appeared near the outer region of the specimen, where shear strain rate was highly concentrated, and then rapidly propagated outward. Stress concentration and shear localization are more likely to occur in specimens with lower initial density, resulting in shorter ignition delay times and higher peak hotspot temperatures. The ignition mechanism of CEM samples with different densities under dynamic loading was revealed. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Saenz S.; Trujillo J.M.; Alvarez L.F.; Akkerman V.; Dumitrescu C.E.
Author full names: Saenz, Stefany (60339323100); Trujillo, Juan M. (60339880300); Alvarez, Luis F. (58852696000); Akkerman, V’yacheslav (60162732100); Dumitrescu, Cosmin E. (23484731500)
Title: Nitrogen-based emissions in a spark ignition engine fueled with neat NH3, Part I: phenomenological model
Abstract: Decarbonization of internal combustion engines (ICEs) intensified the interest in ammonia (NH3). This work extends prior works that focused on just giving possible explanations for observed experimental results. Part I presents the development of a novel 0D modeling framework calibrated on thermodynamic parameters (i.e., in-cylinder pressure, volume, heat transfer, etc.) suitable for predicting emissions from a SI engine operating with neat NH3, with the focus on investigating the contributions of thermal and fuel bound NO mechanisms to the NH3, NOx, and N2O engine-out emissions. The model is well suited for the systematic exploration of various engine operating strategies (e.g., the effect of equivalence ratio, spark timing, engine speed, etc.) and, once the root cause of the observed behavior is identified, the model’s sub‑systems can capture key emissions formation metrics by resolving the influence of individual reaction pathways, as will be shown in Part II of this study that focused on the model’s predictive capability. The model provided useful insights into the formation of nitrogen-based emissions when the SI engine is fueled with NH3. The sample results presented in this paper showed that the use of numerical simulations developed almost exclusively for and validated with hydrocarbon fuels will provide inaccurate results when modeling NH3 combustion inside a SI engine. The addition of flame chemistry via a sequence of 0D homogeneous reactors, a reactor that modeled the chemistry inside the pockets of unburned mixture initially trapped in crevices, and a reactor that modeled the chemistry during the exhaust blowdown allowed the detailed tracking of NH3 chemistry, explained N2O formation, and predicted DeNOx effects on the final exhaust composition. Under engine relevant conditions, the model showed that NO production was primarily governed by HNO chemistry and that the conventional assumption of Zeldovich reactions always producing NO was incorrect for NH3 combustion. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Jin C.; Qiu L.; Zhou N.; Zhang C.; Wu Y.; Xue F.; Dai Z.; Xiong Y.
Title: Metal-coordination cross-linked poly(ionic liquid)s as bifunctional heterogeneous catalysts for efficient CO2 conversion under mild conditions
Abstract: Rising CO2 emissions into the atmosphere has posed major environmental challenges. Among various utilization strategies, the cycloaddition of CO2 with epoxides to cyclic carbonates represents a particularly attractive and atom-economical solution. This study introduces a family of novel bifunctional heterogeneous catalysts (c-PIL-Mt) based on metal-coordination cross-linked poly(ionic liquid)s, featuring porous structures and multiple active sites. The catalysts were comprehensively measured and evaluated in CO2–epoxide cycloaddition under mild conditions. Notably, c-PIL-Co2+ achieved 99.99 % conversion and > 99 % selectivity for CO2–epichlorohydrin under mild conditions (100 °C, ambient pressure, 20 h). The catalyst exhibited a high turnover number (TON) of 223.54 and turnover frequency (TOF) of 9.31 h−1, comparable to many leading systems, and maintained stable activity and > 99 % selectivity over five cycles. On the basis of in situ FT-IR results and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, the synergistic effect of Lewis acidic metal centers and basic nitrogen sites, together with the coordination environment, underpins the enhanced activity of c-PIL-Mt. This work thus provides a robust, recyclable, and highly efficient heterogeneous catalyst, offering a promising pathway for sustainable CO2 utilization. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Fu J.; Yang Z.; Zheng Y.
Title: Density-based topology optimization with cost restrictions for laser powder-bed metal additive manufacturing
Abstract: This paper presents a manufacturing cost-constrained topology optimization method for laser powder-bed metal additive manufacturing (MAM). The density-based topology optimization framework is adopted and an explicit cost model is established based on the voxel geometric model. Modeling the cost model in a derivable form is emphasized as the core contribution. For material volume-constrained topology optimization, the metal powder consumption is a constant, while the evolving part height plays a key role in affecting the manufacturing cost, since the layer-based powder recoating process is time consuming. Therefore, a smoothed maximum function is adopted to estimate the part height and iterative corrections are made to remedy the estimation errors. It is also disclosed that support volume is proportional to the part height and thus, restricting the part height simultaneous suppresses the support material cost. A detailed sensitivity analysis about the optimization model is performed and the full optimization setup is detailed. A few 3D numerical examples are studied to prove the effectiveness of the proposed method, realizing the design effect for cost-effectiveness. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Authors: Zheng S.; Xue X.
Title: Energy-based machine learning models for predicting soil liquefaction potential
Abstract: This study presents a hybrid model that combines the extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) algorithm with the Newton–Raphson–based optimizer (NRBO) to predict the normalized energy capacity (NEC) in the energy-based liquefaction assessment. 217 sets of soil liquefaction data collected from laboratory cyclic triaxial tests were used to build the proposed model. The performance of the NRBO-XGBoost model was compared with that of three other machine learning models optimized by NRBO, namely the light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM), support vector machine (SVM), and artificial neural network (ANN) models. The coefficient of determination, root mean squared error, mean absolute error and Willmott's index of agreement values of the NRBO-XGBoost model are 0.988, 0.063, 0.048 and 0.997, respectively, for the training set and 0.927, 0.159, 0.125 and 0.982, respectively, for the test set. Subsequently, by combining the predicted NEC with the calculated normalized energy demand (NED), a deterministic liquefaction assessment was conducted for the on-site seismic conditions, and a probabilistic liquefaction model was established based on the predicted NEC using logistic regression. The results show that the accuracy of the deterministic liquefaction assessment reaches 0.852 under actual site seismic conditions, and the probabilistic liquefaction model demonstrates strong overall discriminative ability. Additionally, the SHapley additive explanations (SHAP) method was used to analyze the importance of each parameter in the energy-based liquefaction assessment for NEC prediction. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Sun Y.; Li X.; Huo Z.; Chen Z.; Liu Z.; Tang Y.; He C.; Zeng L.
Title: Boundary-aware geometric learning for time-consistent malware open-set recognition
Abstract: Open-set malware recognition (OSR) in evolving environments requires models to distinguish known families while rejecting samples from emerging unknown families. Since malware distributions change over time, this task should be evaluated under a time-consistent protocol that excludes future samples from training to avoid temporal leakage. Under this setting, we propose OMT (Open-set Malware recognition under Temporal constraints), a multi-stage information fusion framework for time-consistent family-level OSR on Windows malware. OMT couples three complementary components: boundary-aware proxy generation, geometric representation learning, and local-neighborhood rejection. During training, the classifier learns closed-set family prediction, compact hyperspherical embeddings with fixed orthogonal prototypes, and feature-level separation. The generator constructs class-conditional boundary-aware proxy features that serve as hard negatives for open-set training. At test time, OMT rejects unknown families using a class-conditional k -nearest-neighbor ( k -NN) rule that measures local neighborhood density relative to the predicted seen family. Experiments on two public Windows malware datasets with time-consistent splits show that OMT achieves the strongest seen/unseen separability across all six evaluated splits and the best or highly competitive final open-set recognition performance. Ablation studies further examine the roles of proxy-based open-set training, class-wise scale-adaptive Gaussian perturbation, and class-conditional local-density k -NN rejection. These results demonstrate that OMT provides an effective solution for malware OSR under evolving distributions by fusing boundary-aware generation, geometric representation learning, and local-density rejection. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Chen Q.; Pei C.; Lu F.; Zhang Q.; Zou B.
Title: Influence of soil arching mobilization on localized surcharge identification in a shallow trapdoor system
Abstract: Localized surcharge identification above shallow buried structures depends on soil-arching state and the reliability of sparse monitoring channels. We examine an active trapdoor at H/B=1.5 using three pre-displacement states and five observation sets combining surface settlements and support-reaction features. A 117-response plane-strain Mohr–Coulomb finite-element database was divided into training, development, independent numerical evaluation, and independent numerical confirmation sets. State-specific quadratic-trend Matérn-5/2 Gaussian-process surrogates were trained on the training set, while channel-wise discrepancy was calibrated on the development set and applied to the independent sets. Training-set leave-one-out cross-validation underestimated the out-of-sample discrepancy of the signed reaction moment. In the independent evaluation set, its normalized forward root-mean-square error was 8.56 and its mean contribution to the inverse objective at the true parameters was 62.7%. Development calibration reduced these values to 1.30 and 11.8%, respectively, eliminating the associated opposite-boundary solutions. With the calibrated scale, median combined errors across the five observation sets ranged from 0.302 to 0.359. The reaction-distribution scale improved width recovery in some states but provided no general combined-error advantage. In the confirmation set, median combined errors ranged from 0.493 to 0.511; the same feature reduced median width error from 47.35% to 35.14%, although 16 of 24 estimates still reached a parameter boundary. Observation design should therefore account jointly for arching state, parameter-specific information, and surrogate discrepancy. Width recovery remains limited in sparsely covered parts of the nominal load domain. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Wang M.; He M.; Nan K.; Chen B.; Hu B.
Title: Synthesis of the desthiobiotin-phenylarsenic oxide probe for identification and analysis of arsenic-binding proteins in MCF-7 cells
Abstract: A novel organoarsenic probe, desthiobiotin-phenylarsenic oxide (DesBiotin-PAO(III)), was synthesized by coupling desthiobiotin with p-aminophenylarsenic acid (PAO(III)) via a mixed anhydride method. This probe enables the in situ capture of intracellular arsenic binding proteins, which are subsequently adsorbed onto streptavidin-coated magnetic beads (SA-MBs) through the desthiobiotin–streptavidin interaction, thereby achieving selective separation of arsenic-binding proteins from other intracellular components. Because the binding affinity of desthiobiotin for streptavidin is considerably weaker than that of biotin, free biotin can be employed as a competitive displacement agent to gently release the captured arsenic-binding proteins from the SA-MBs. Comprehensive characterization of the synthesized probe confirmed the successful preparation of DesBiotin-PAO(III). Using reduced bovine serum albumin (rBSA) as a model arsenic-binding protein, the capture performance of DesBiotin-PAO(III) was systematically validated. Building on this, DesBiotin-PAO(III) was employed for the in situ capture of arsenic-binding proteins in MCF-7 cells, and the captured proteins were identified by high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC)- electrospray ionization tandem mass spectrometry (ESI-MS/MS) (separated using C18 column with gradient elution (H2O-CH3CN containing 0.1% formic acid) and detected in positive mode). In total, 153 arsenic-binding proteins were ultimately identified in MCF-7 cells. Compared with previously reported methods based on organoarsenic probes, the present approach identified the greatest number of arsenic-binding proteins to date. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Qin Y.; Deng S.; He Y.; Ding W.; Wu Y.; Ding W.
Title: Analogue-twin interpretation of bandgap broadening in piezoelectric metamaterials
Abstract: With the development of piezoelectric metamaterials, increasingly complex shunt circuits have improved tunability and broadband attenuation performance, but they also make repeated multiphysics simulations expensive and obscure how circuit design parameters govern attenuation-band evolution in finite structures. To address these issues, this study develops an impedance-based analogue-twin reduced-order model (AT-ROM) for a piezoelectric metamaterial beam with periodic patches shunted by parallel negative-capacitance (NC) and synthetic-inductance (SI) circuits. Based on the electromechanical analogy, the host-beam compliance, piezoelectric coupling, intrinsic blocked capacitance, NC and SI are condensed into a characteristic-branch impedance. Two anchor frequencies follow from this impedance: a zero that locates the low-impedance attenuation valley and a pole that bounds the negative-stiffness window, whose stiffness–weighted combination gives the bandgap edge of the actual cell. Their ratio is independent of the inductance, so the SI places the anchors on the frequency axis while the NC sets their separation, which yields an explicit two-parameter tuning rule and a nonlinear broadening trend of the bandgap. Unit-cell dispersion analysis, finite-element frequency-response comparison and experiments on a free–free steel beam with eight piezoelectric patches consistently confirm this behavior: the attenuation valley stays locked to the target mode while the attenuation band broadens with NC, and the model reproduces the finite-element response at about three orders of magnitude lower computational cost. This study provides a rapid and physically interpretable impedance-level bridge between shunt-circuit parameters and finite-structure attenuation-band evolution. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS

Authors: Jiang N.; Li H.; Teng X.; Hu Z.
Title: Comprehensive review of GANs and diffusion models in multimodal 3D medical image conversion
Abstract: This review summarizes recent advances in Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Diffusion Models (DMs) for multimodal transformation of 3D medical images. GAN-based methods enable nonlinear cross-modality mapping, while architectures such as CycleGAN reduce reliance on paired data. DMs improve generation stability and anatomical consistency. Hybrid GAN–diffusion frameworks further enhance synthesis quality and robustness. These methods have been applied to missing magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) sequence completion and translation among computed tomography (CT), MRI, and positron emission tomography (PET). These applications support diagnosis, radiation dose reduction, and treatment planning. However, challenges remain in annotation cost, physiological credibility of generated images, computational complexity, and clinical deployment. We therefore outline future directions in large-scale multimodal pre-trained models, physically constrained generation, privacy-preserving federated learning, and real-time interactive systems. These directions aim to facilitate reliable clinical translation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Energy, exergy, and direct engine-out emission impact assessment of an ethyl acetate–diesel dual-fuel engine under different EGR rates
Abstract: This study experimentally investigates the energy, exergy, and direct engine-out emission impacts of ethyl acetate (EA)–diesel dual-fuel operation under exhaust gas recirculation (EGR). Tests were conducted on a single-cylinder direct-injection diesel engine at 1800 rpm and 25–100% loads. EA injection durations of 1, 2, and 3 ms and EGR rates of 0%, 5%, 10%, and 20% were investigated. Energy and exergy balances were established, and direct emission impact was calculated from CO, CO2, HC, and NOx mass-flow rates derived from the measured exhaust-gas concentrations and intake-air flow. At full load, EA(2 ms) + 20% EGR increased energy and exergy efficiencies by 39.1% and 38.4%, respectively, and reduced exergy destruction by 42.5% relative to diesel operation without EGR, representing the thermodynamically preferred condition. EA(3 ms) without EGR produced the maximum pointwise direct emission-impact reduction of 72.5% at 25% load, whereas EA(3 ms) + 20% EGR provided the greatest average reduction of 35.8%. Condition-mean ANOVA showed that engine load accounted for 84.81%, 84.61%, and 91.70% of the variations in energy efficiency, exergy efficiency, and direct emission impact, respectively. Load-resolved TOPSIS identified EA(2 ms) + 20% EGR as the highest-ranked balanced compromise, with a mean closeness coefficient of 0.7781; however, EA(3 ms) + 20% EGR became preferable when direct emission impact received greater weight. The results demonstrate metric-specific optima and support load-dependent coordination of EA injection and EGR. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Huang Y.; Mao X.; Guo W.; Bao F.
Title: In situ generation of NiFeOOH mitigates metal-organic framework degradation for ampere‑level oxygen evolution reaction and anion‑exchange membrane water electrolysis
Abstract: NiFe-based metal–organic frameworks (NiFe-MOFs) require reconstruction into metal (oxy)hydroxides to achieve oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity. However, during the OER process, deep electrochemical reconstruction can lead to the degradation and structural collapse of the organic framework, thereby reducing the activity and stability of the electrocatalyst. Herein, we immerse the Ni-MOF precursor in a mixed salt solution of Ni2+ and Fe2+ to in-situ form NiFeOOH/Ni-MOF. In-situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) reveals that the formation of NiFeOOH significantly reduces the interfacial charge transfer resistance and enhances the OER interfacial kinetics. In-situ Raman spectroscopy indicates that NiFeOOH, as the OER active phase, significantly enhances the activity. Furthermore, in-situ / ex-situ Raman spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy demonstrate that NiFeOOH can mitigate the degradation of the organic framework (O=C–O, C=C) in the MOF. After operating for 810 h at 1.0 A cm−2, the organic framework is only partially degraded, thereby enhancing the structural stability of the electrocatalyst. As a result, NiFeOOH/Ni-MOF achieves OER stability for over 810 h at 1.0 A cm−2 and overall water splitting for over 1000 h at 1.5 A cm−2. In 6.0 M KOH at 60 °C, it requires only 1.92 V to drive 1.0 A cm−2 (243.9 A g−1) and maintain anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) durability for 210 h. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Tang R.; Ma S.; Zhang J.; Xiong J.; Zuo H.; Song P.; Jiang W.; Di J.
Title: Fe polarization site in Bi19S27Cl3 promotes near-infrared photocatalytic reduction of nitrate to ammonia
Abstract: To address the issues of weak response in the near-infrared spectral region and slow NO3− reduction kinetics of traditional photocatalysts, this paper successfully synthesized a Fe-doped Bi19S27Cl3 photocatalyst via a solvothermal method and applied it to the photocatalytic NO3− reduction to ammonia synthesis. The effects of Fe introduction on the crystal structure, surface morphology, and photochemical properties of the material were systematically investigated using XRD, HRTEM, XPS, and UV–Vis-NIR spectrophotometry. The results show that the introduction of Fe did not alter the bulk crystal structure of Bi19S27Cl3, but effectively modulated its surface chemical state and photoelectric properties. Under simulated sunlight irradiation, the optimized Fe-Bi19S27Cl3 catalyst exhibited excellent photocatalytic ammonia synthesis activity from NO3− reduction, achieving an ammonia yield of 253.5 μmol g-1h−1, and also exhibited an activity of 105.3 μmol g-1h−1 and high stability under near-infrared light irradiation. Photoelectrochemical tests confirmed that the introduction of Fe induced efficient interfacial charge migration and effectively suppressed the recombination of photogenerated electron-hole pairs. Authors: Liu C.; Hu F.; Quan B.; Li M.; Li L.; Zhi Z.; Zhang Y.; Zhu W.; Huang C.
Title: Metal organic framework UiO-66 functionalized terahertz metasurface for detection of biomarker 2-pentanone
Abstract: 2-Pentanone has attracted increasing attention as a potential biomarker for several diseases, highlighting the demand for rapid, selective, and noninvasive detection. Here, we present a UiO-66-functionalized terahertz metasurface comprising two S-shaped split-ring resonators and an antenna, which supports three physically distinct resonance modes. Simulation results reveal high sensitivities of 52.5, 85.5, and 99 GHz/RIU (refractive index unit) at the respective resonances. To enhance analyte uptake and generate measurable multimode responses, the metasurface was functionalized with UiO-66 through a robust multilayer assembly strategy. Across the investigated 20–200 ppm range, all three modes exhibited concentration-dependent red shifts, with a maximum shift of 14.62 GHz at 200 ppm. Authors: Li K.; Shi H.; Mi C.; Qiang Y.; Huang R.; Chen S.; Zhang H.; Ni X.; Chen W.
Title: Deformation-dependent oil-film force modeling and high-dimensional stability analysis of a spiral bevel gear system with elastic-ring squeeze film damper support
Abstract: High-speed spiral bevel gear transmissions are prone to orbital instability when time-varying mesh stiffness, transmission error, backlash, eccentric excitation, and nonlinear support forces act simultaneously. Although an elastic-ring squeeze film damper (ERSFD) can provide passive vibration attenuation, its use in gear transmissions requires more than evaluating response-amplitude reduction; the key issue is how the deformation-dependent damper force changes the route to instability. Existing damper-level and rotor-system studies do not fully connect elastic-ring deformation, inner- and outer-oil-film pressure, and high-dimensional gear-system stability. The results show that the ERSFD suppresses the early Neimark–Sacker route observed without ERSFD support, maintains stable period-one motion over a wider low- and medium-speed range, weakens high-speed period-doubling and aperiodic responses, and narrows the strongly complex-response region. Title: Deployment-dependent vibration attenuation in a telescopic laminated beam with evolving resonator distributions
Abstract: This study investigates the deployment-dependent vibration attenuation characteristics of a telescopic laminated beam equipped with distributed local resonators. A time-varying dynamic model is developed by combining Euler–Bernoulli beam theory, classical laminate theory, and deployment-dependent resonator configurations. Title: Composite surface reinforcement and tribological mechanisms of 40Cr gear steel via micro-flame-assisted laser texturing synergized with graphene coating
Abstract: High-speed, heavy-duty gears frequently suffer severe tribological failures under extreme-pressure conditions. To transcend the limits of monolithic modifications, we propose a multi-scale solid-liquid synergistic surface strategy (MLG) integrating micro-flame-assisted laser texturing with a graphene coating. Structural characterizations reveal that MLG induces a martensitic transformation, providing exceptional fatigue stiffness. Concurrently, the grid microtextures and graphene coating promoted lubricant retention and transport at the contact interface. This tribolayer may have reduced interfacial shear and direct metal-to-metal contact, thereby contributing to the mitigation of adhesive wear. Title: A synergistic intelligence framework for decoupled hierarchical identification of RBF-network-based NARMAX systems
Abstract: Additive NARMAX models have been widely used in industrial process modeling and biomedical signal analysis. Specifically, an adaptive step-size matrix based gradient iterative algorithm is developed for dynamic parameter estimation using the auxiliary model identification method, while a particle swarm optimization assisted gradient iterative algorithm is proposed for hyperparameter optimization. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm achieves faster convergence and more accurate parameter estimation than the conventional gradient iterative algorithm. The mean parameter estimation error is reduced by more than 90%, and the median estimation error remains below 5% under low noise and below 15% under high noise. Title: Development of a reliable microwave plasma-atomic emission spectrometry (MP-AES) method for the determination of total arsenic in groundwater using l-cysteine as a reducing agent

The effectiveness of the reduction process was verified by high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (HPLC-ICP-MS) analysis. The developed method provides reliable and accurate determination of total arsenic in groundwater and offers a practical analytical approach for the routine monitoring of arsenic-contaminated water resources. The method achieved a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.49 ppb and a limit of quantification (LOQ) of 1.47 ppb. Spike recovery values for groundwater samples ranged from 98% to 107%, while the relative standard deviation (RSD) was below 5%, demonstrating excellent accuracy and precision. Title: The analysis of 2D complex scale-sensitive bar structures in the framework of space-fractional non-local mechanical model

Title: P2L-CA: An effective parameter tuning framework for rehearsal-free Multi-Label Class-Incremental Learning
Abstract: Multi-label Class-Incremental Learning (MLCIL) aims to continuously recognize novel categories in complex scenes where multiple objects co-occur. The P2L module leverages class-specific prompts to disentangle multi-label representations while incorporating linguistic priors to enforce semantic–visual alignment. Meanwhile, the CA module utilizes lightweight adapters to bridge the domain gaps between pre-trained models and downstream tasks, thereby enhancing model plasticity. Extensive experiments across standard and challenging MLCIL settings on MS-COCO and PASCAL VOC demonstrate that P2L-CA achieves substantial improvements over state-of-the-art methods, while also showing strong generalization in class-incremental learning scenarios, all while requiring minimal trainable parameters and eliminating the need for memory buffers. Title: Development of CALF-20-based MWCNT and MXene composites for dynamic CO2/CH4 separation in biogas upgrading
Abstract: Biogas has garnered significant attention as the world transitions toward renewable energy, driven by the depletion of fossil fuel resources and concerns over climate change. The composites retained the crystal structure of the parent MOF, CALF-20. The adsorption isotherms recorded at 298 K and 100 kPa showed that CALF-20 exhibits a CO2 adsorption capacity of 3.37 mmol/g, while its composites, CALF-20@MWCNTs and CALF-20@MXene, exhibit capacities of 4.53 mmol/g and 4.22 mmol/g, corresponding to increases of 34.42 % and 25.22 %, respectively. Title: Physics-Informed neural operator hybrids for Multi-Scale inverse problems

Abstract: We develop a hybrid physics-informed neural operator framework for efficient and uncertainty-aware multi-scale inverse problems in subsurface flow. The proposed methodology combines neural operator architectures with embedded partial differential equation (PDE) constraints, hierarchical coarse-to-fine training, and Bayesian uncertainty quantification to improve reconstruction accuracy while preserving physical consistency across multiple spatial scales. The principal contributions are threefold. First, we develop constrained neural operator models that incorporate governing PDE information through physics-informed loss functions and conservation-aware formulations. Second, we introduce a multilevel training strategy inspired by multigrid principles that efficiently captures multi-scale features while reducing computational complexity. Third, we integrate approximate Bayesian inference into the operator-learning framework to quantify epistemic uncertainty associated with inverse parameter estimation. Theoretical analyses establish error propagation bounds, posterior stability, and identifiability properties of the proposed hybrid framework, providing insight into the influence of surrogate approximation errors on inverse reconstruction. Efficient training and inversion algorithms are further developed by combining neural operator learning with selective physics-based solver refinement. Extensive numerical experiments on heterogeneous elliptic PDEs, Darcy flow inverse problems, and the SPE10 permeability benchmark demonstrate that the proposed framework accurately reconstructs fine-scale permeability fields, provides well-calibrated uncertainty estimates, and significantly accelerates repeated inverse analyses compared with conventional PDE-constrained optimization methods. Title: Catalytic transformation of CO2 with propylene oxide catalyzed by ZnBr2 supported on boron-doped carbon nitride materials
Abstract: The cycloaddition of CO2 with propylene oxide (PO) to synthesize propylene carbonate (PC) is a sustainable strategy for the catalytic transformation of CO2. Title: Turbulence generation and evolution mechanisms induced by herringbone ribs in supersonic mixing layer
Abstract: To investigate how herringbone ribs modify turbulence generation and evolution in a supersonic mixing layer, large-eddy simulations (LES) are performed for a splitter-plate configuration. The numerical framework is first validated against classical experimental data by comparing normalized velocity and turbulence-intensity profiles obtained using Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS), LES without synthetic inlet turbulence, and LES with synthetic-eddy-method (SEM)-generated turbulent inflow. The downstream evolution of the baseline mixing layer and the local variations in mixing-layer thickness associated with shock–shear-layer interactions are then examined. Herringbone ribs are introduced on the splitter plate, and the baseline and herringbone-ribbed configurations are compared in terms of flow structures, vortex evolution, mean-velocity profiles, turbulence intensities, and dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) characteristics. The results show that the rib-induced geometric perturbations generate periodically distributed near-wall vortical structures and secondary motions. Compared with the baseline configuration, a distinct canonical two-dimensional roll-up stage is not clearly identified in the ribbed case, while three-dimensional vortical structures emerge farther upstream. Recirculating motions downstream of the rib trailing edges are accompanied by enhanced velocity fluctuations, with the initial streamwise turbulence intensity increasing by 60% relative to the baseline configuration. DMD analysis further shows that the herringbone ribs excite high-frequency small-scale disturbances through localized forcing of the shear layer, while sustaining low-frequency large-scale coherent motions with longer temporal persistence. Title: Photoinduced weathering of plastics and implications for spectral inclusion into matching database for laser direct infrared spectroscopy identification
Abstract: Microplastics are a ubiquitous environmental contaminant that can be found virtually every habitat and water source around the world. Therefore, there is great interest in developing efficient and reliable methodologies for the identification and enumeration of microplastics from environmental media. However, only pristine spectra of plastics are currently used in the identification process. To test if weathering influences identification of microplastics by LDIR, nine different plastics were irradiated to simulate weathering from 3 to 13 years in the sun. The physical and chemical changes of the plastic were measured by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and attenuated total reflectance Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR) respectively. The weathered polymers were analyzed by LDIR-transflectance spectroscopy and resulting spectra were loaded into the LDIR matching database. This updated database was used to analyze samples from a local wastewater treatment plant with and without the inclusion of weathered spectra. This manuscript shows the inclusion of weathered transflectance spectra into the LDIR matching database can increase polymer identifications by 9.6 – 10.2% in wastewater samples on average. Title: Ethanol-dependent multiscale transitions in zein–lutein encapsulation: From predicted monomer compaction to path-dependent thermal stability

However, suspension experiments showed that these lower-scale transitions were not directly reflected in lutein protection. Title: AI-enabled cyberbullying detection from a cyber-physical-social-thinking space integration perspective: Theories, technologies, and challenges
Abstract: Cyberbullying has emerged as a pervasive threat to digital well-being, evolving into a multidimensional phenomenon that spans multiple interconnected spaces. Despite significant progress in detection techniques, existing approaches predominantly rely on textual analysis, limiting their ability to capture the full spectrum of cyberbullying behaviors and contextual dependencies. To address this limitation, this study presents a systematic review with qualitative synthesis of AI-enabled cyberbullying detection through the lens of Cyber-Physical-Social-Thinking (CPST) space integration. Based on 120 included studies, the review develops three principal outputs. First, it develops a fusion-mechanism taxonomy of AI-enabled cyberbullying detection research across cyber, physical, social, and thinking dimensions, organizing how content, contextual, relational, behavioral, and cognitive information is combined to support more comprehensive and context-aware detection. Second, it establishes a quantitative and descriptive landscape of the reviewed literature across CPST-space coverage, modalities, model families, publication trends, social media platforms, dataset characteristics, and evaluation metrics. Third, it develops a four-level conceptual taxonomy that organizes cyberbullying-related information into observable evidence, latent states, behaviors, and outcomes. Building on this evidence-based output, the study synthesizes a CPST-based conceptual reference architecture that organizes heterogeneous data sources, feature representations, information-fusion strategies, and decision-making processes, while distinguishing the differing empirical maturity of the four spaces. The review further synthesizes state-of-the-art AI technologies, including natural language processing, computer vision, network analysis, affective computing, and multimodal learning, in relation to their roles in cross-space information integration. Title: Leveraging unlabeled data via semi-supervised contrastive learning for enhanced monocular depth estimation
Abstract: Accurate monocular depth estimation with limited annotations remains a critical challenge in real-world scenarios. Existing supervised approaches heavily rely on large-scale dense annotations, the acquisition of which is costly and difficult to scale, while self-supervised methods often depend on restrictive geometric assumptions and additional information such as camera parameters or multi-view consistency, thereby limiting their generalization under sparse or noisy supervision. To bridge this gap, we propose TriConDepth, a novel semi-supervised framework that leverages contrastive learning (CL) to explore both labeled and unlabeled data effectively. The method comprises three stages: unsupervised image-level CL to extract global geometry-invariant structures from unlabeled images, empowering the embedding space with global contextual awareness; supervised pixel-level CL performed on labeled images to enhance local depth-aware feature discriminability; and a consistency-based semi-supervised strategy to align intermediate embeddings and ensure robust predictions under perturbations. To address incomplete annotations within labeled data, we design a window-based contrastive loss that fully exploits sparse and invalid depth regions. Extensive experiments across varying label ratios on the KITTI and NYU datasets demonstrate that TriConDepth consistently surpasses state-of-the-art alternatives, achieving significant improvements and showcasing the model's robustness and effectiveness in real-world depth estimation. Title: Folic acid self-assembly-assisted ultrafine Ru nanoparticles on highly graphitic N-doped carbon for co-electrolytic H2 generation paired with hydrazine oxidation
Abstract: Overall water splitting (OWS) for H2 production is limited by the sluggish kinetics of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Title: A Physics-Guided Transformer–LSTM prediction Model with dynamic feature weighting for NOx emission prediction in CFB boilers

Title: Effect of cellulase on methane production and its mechanism during anaerobic digestion of coal

Title: Iron-based metal–organic frameworks in analytical chemistry: Synthesis, characterization, structure-property relationships, and analytical applications
Abstract: Iron-based metal–organic frameworks (Fe-MOFs) represent a unique class of porous materials for advanced analytical sensing. Their high surface area, tunable pore structures, intrinsic catalytic activity, excellent stability, and remarkable biocompatibility have made them highly attractive platforms for a wide range of analytical applications. This review provides a novel and critical perspective on recent advances in Fe-MOF-based analytical platforms by systematically evaluating their synthesis strategies, functionalization approaches, sensing mechanisms, and analytical applications in spectrophotometric, fluorimetric, surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS), and electrochemical techniques. Unlike previous reviews, this work establishes clear relationships between Fe-MOF structure, catalytic activity, and analytical performance through a comprehensive comparative analysis supported by standardized analytical performance metrics. The review further highlights the impact of structural engineering and hybrid Fe-MOF architectures on sensitivity, selectivity, and practical applicability in real-sample analysis. In addition, the current challenges and future perspectives for developing sustainable, high-performance Fe-MOF-based analytical sensors are critically discussed. This review provides valuable design insights and a practical framework to guide the rational development of Fe-MOF analytical sensing platforms. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: DMSFNet: Dual-stage modality-guided frequency suppression and semantic fusion for visible-infrared person re-identification
Abstract: Visible-Infrared Person Re-identification (VI-ReID) is a modeling task that aims to accurately retrieve images of a given pedestrian across visible and infrared modalities by using query images from the complementary modality. Most existing methods hinge on projecting visible (VIS) and infrared (IR) images into a unified pseudo-modal embedding space. As a result, such methods frequently overlook intrinsic cross-modality discrepancies that become particularly pronounced under challenging conditions (e.g., severe background clutter and low-contrast environments), ultimately leading to degraded performance. To address these issues, we propose a novel Dual-stage Modality-guided Frequency Suppression and Semantic Fusion Network (DMSFNet) for the VI-ReID task, which integrates a Dual-stage Modality-guided Strategy (DMGS), a Low-Frequency Suppression Module (LFSM), and a High-Frequency Semantic Fusion (HFSF) module. Specifically, the DMGS generates a more diverse and discriminative pseudo-modality embedding space, thereby reducing domain discrepancies between VIS and IR images. On the other hand, the LFSM effectively suppresses low-frequency noise features (e.g., background interferences or low-contrast regions) by leveraging spatial self-attention combined with Haar wavelet-guided processing. Finally, the HFSF module enforces intra-and inter-modality consistency constraints while highlighting and fusing personalized high-frequency semantic cues (e.g., clothing textures and accessories). Extensive experiments, ablation studies and visualizations conducted on three public VI-ReID datasets (SYSU-MM01, RegDB, and LLCM) demonstrate that DMSFNet achieves competitive performance against existing state-of-the-art methods. Title: Multimodal fusion for precision livestock behavior monitoring: A systematic review of deep learning, pose estimation, and sensor integration strategies
Abstract: Animal behavior analysis is a cornerstone of precision livestock farming, providing non-invasive insights into health, welfare, and productivity through continuous behavioral monitoring. Traditional approaches, including manual observation, sensor-based systems, and rule-based modeling, are limited by labor intensity, observer subjectivity, and low temporal resolution. This systematic review (PRISMA 2020; 2020-2026 literature) presents a comprehensive synthesis of deep learning and multimodal artificial intelligence approaches for animal behavior recognition in precision agriculture. Deep learning architectures, including convolutional, recurrent, and transformer-based models, achieve reported accuracies of 85-99% across livestock species, with transformer-based models reaching a mean of 94.4% (95% CI: 91.96-96.76%). Critically, multimodal fusion systems demonstrate a mean accuracy gain of 10.3 percentage points over single-modality baselines in an exploratory analysis of four independent source-level comparisons (95% CI: 4.9-15.8%; paired t(3) = 6.01, p = 0.009, Cohen’s d = 3.01), with peak detection sensitivities exceeding 90% for health-critical conditions, including lameness and metabolic disorders. This review evaluates early, late, and hybrid fusion strategies; the role of pose estimation in fine-grained movement analysis (with 94-100% accuracy in lameness detection); and the contribution of wearable and environmental sensors to continuous monitoring. Explainable AI methods are assessed for their role in improving model transparency and stakeholder trust. Key challenges, including data scarcity, annotation heterogeneity, multimodal synchronization, and limited cross-domain generalization, are critically discussed, along with six directions for future research. This review uniquely positions adaptive multimodal fusion as the central paradigm for next-generation, deployable precision livestock behavior monitoring systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: An D.; Xie X.; Tian J.; Zhang K.
Title: Construction of defective STO/g-CN S-scheme heterojunctions for efficient photocatalytic NO removal
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Low-concentration NO can be converted using photocatalytic technology because of its favorable solar energy usage and moderate reaction conditions. Photocatalytic materials are the key to improving the photocatalytic conversion efficiency of NO. In this paper, oxygen vacancy-containing SrTiO3 prepared by the solvothermal method and intrinsic defect-containing g-C3N5 prepared by high-temperature calcination were subjected to high-temperature treatment, and the STO/g-CN heterojunction photocatalysts were created. Under visible light irradiation, the NO removal rate of STO/g-CN reached 63%. The presence of intrinsic vacancies in g-C3N5 and oxygen defects in SrTiO3 was verified by EPR, and high-temperature treatment considerably raised the defect concentration in STO/g-CN. Because vacancy and heterojunctions work in concert, the modified material extended its photo response range, which is beneficial to enhancing the effectiveness of photogenerated carriers' migration and improving the photocatalytic NO conversion efficiency of the material in the presence of light. In addition, the mechanism of photocatalytic NO removal over the modified materials was investigated using EPR, trapping experiments, and in-situ diffuse reflectance Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy. This study proposes a strategy combining defect engineering and heterojunction synergistically, which provides a reference for the preparation of highly efficient photocatalysts for NO conversion. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Fu T.; Wang X.; Li X.; Cao Y.; Fu N.; Wang Y.
Title: DRNet: Parallel two-branch network with fusion-enhancement and channel-pixel attention for color image steganalysis
Abstract: Image steganalysis is a hot topic in the field of information security, and researchers have recently proposed a series of methods. However, existing color image steganalysis methods tend to extract features indiscriminately from different channels and regions, which fails to focus on steganographically relevant channels and texture-rich areas where stego signals are concentrated. In addition, most methods lack effective mechanisms to aggregate and amplify steganographic information across the three color channels, leaving weak stego signals dispersed and undetected. To address these issues, we propose a parallel two-branch network with fusion-enhancement and channel-pixel attention for universal color image steganalysis. In the main branch, we design a stego signal fusion-enhancement block that performs multi-channel information fusion and first introduces detail-enhanced convolution to amplify weak stego signals. In the auxiliary branch, we design a channel-pixel attention mechanism that jointly performs attention across channel and pixel dimensions, enabling precise localization of steganographic regions via multiplication-based fusion with main branch features. Experiments on the Alaska II dataset demonstrate that the proposed network achieves superior detection accuracy and generalization over state-of-the-art methods. Ablation studies validate the contribution of each component, and visualizations confirm that the channel-pixel attention mechanism effectively guides the model to focus on steganographic regions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: A wearable sensor integrating a MXene-PLL-GOx-modified electrode and a Janus nanofibrous membrane for electrochemical monitoring of sweat glucose
Abstract: MXene is a two-dimensional transition metal carbide with large specific surface area, good conductivity, and outstanding biocompatibility, which can be integrated with electrochemical devices, significantly enhancing the sensing performance. Herein, we present a wearable electrochemical sensor based on MXene composites modified electrode and Janus nanofibrous membranes for active sweat collection and precise detection of sweat glucose. Poly- l -lysine (PLL) is highly positively charged because of the -NH3+ groups, which acts as the crosslinker to bond MXene and glucose oxidase (GOx, containing -COO- groups) both negatively charged, forming a functional composite with high catalytic activity for glucose sensing. In this way, GOx was efficiently immobilized on the MXene nanosheets and then deposited on the screen-printed carbon electrode (SPCE). The intermediate H2O2 from enzymatic glucose oxidation was catalytically decomposed by MXene into H2O and O2. The recycled O2 further accelerated the enzymatic reaction on the SPCE. PU/PVA Janus nanofibrous membrane was prepared through electrospinning for active and effective sweat collection due to the unidirectional moisture conduction from its hydrophobic/hydrophilic side. The modified SPCE was integrated with the Janus nanofibrous membrane to fabricate a wearable sweat sensor, with the sensitivities of 16.70 μA mM−1 cm−2 for 0∼300 μM glucose levels, with a detection limit of 24.35 μM. The sensor also showed good stability, selectivity, and reproducibility, providing a new strategy for non-invasive sweat glucose monitoring. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Techno-economic and life cycle assessment of a tandem CO2 and plastic waste-to-fuels system
Abstract: The transition towards a circular and low-carbon economy requires integrated solutions that enable the simultaneous valorization of waste streams and carbon dioxide. In this context, this study investigates a tandem system combining an electrochemical reactor (PV-EC) and a photo-electrochemical reactor (PEC) for the conversion of CO2 and ethylene glycol derived from plastic waste into fuels and valuable chemical products (including glycolic acid). The planned research includes an economic analysis, encompassing capital expenditure estimation and investment profitability assessment using the Net Present Value (NPV) method, as well as a Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) aimed at evaluating the environmental impact of the proposed technology. Economic analysis revealed that profitability is mainly determined by the selling price of glycolic acid and the cost of renewable electricity, with glycolic acid accounting for nearly 85 % of total revenue. However, n-propanol is prioritized as the main target product and basis for the Functional Unit because the process was specifically designed for CO2 reduction into high-density liquid fuels. LCA shows that ethylene glycol dominates the environmental footprint, while the PV-EC configuration outperforms PEC due to lower glycol demand and reduced electricity consumption. These results highlight the system as a dual-purpose platform where n-propanol serves as the primary energy carrier while glycolic acid provides the required economic viability. Additionally, reducing ethylene glycol use via low-impact supply chains further improves environmental performance. This approach highlights the potential of the tandem reactor system for sustainable fuel and chemical production within a low-carbon, circular economy framework. © 2026 The Author(s).

Authors: Jiang J.-H.; Zheng H.
Title: Finite element force method for joint and material nonlinearity problems
Abstract: For geotechnical structures such as slopes and tunnels, their deformation and strength are characterized by both joint nonlinearity and material nonlinearity. Here, joints refer to various geological and artificial interfaces that obey Coulomb's friction law. The properties of joint nonlinearity and material nonlinearity differ significantly: the former belongs to state nonlinearity, while the latter to process nonlinearity. Directly coupling these two types of nonlinearities during programming is highly likely to cause iterative entanglement, thereby impeding the convergence of iterations. In this study, the contact stress on the joint surface is taken as the primal unknown quantity. The behaviors of both joints and elastoplastic materials are described using variational inequalities, and the iterations are conducted uniformly by means of process iteration. This approach avoids the introduction of any artificial parameters, including Kn/Ks of joints (normal and shear stiffness coefficients). The convergence of the two types of nonlinearities is theoretically guaranteed, thereby completely resolving the issue of iterative entanglement between state nonlinearity and process nonlinearity. Although the proposed solution is implemented within the framework of the force method, most of the involved matrices are identical to those employed in the traditional displacement method, facilitating its straightforward transplantation into displacement method-based programs. The analysis of highly challenging problems has demonstrated that the numerical performance of the method proposed herein is far superior to that of those popular methods including those mature software products. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Catalytic ozonation of VOC over high-entropy MnCePrZrY oxide: unveiling the role of high-entropy configuration in ozone activation
Abstract: High-entropy oxides (HEOs) have emerged as promising catalytic materials owing to their unique multi-metal synergy and tunable defect structures. However, their application in the catalytic ozonation of gaseous volatile organic compounds (VOCs) remains largely unexplored. Herein, a novel fluorite-type HEO, (MnCePrZrY)O2, was synthesized via a self-propagating combustion method and employed for the low-temperature catalytic ozonation of acetone. The HEO achieved complete catalytic ozonation of acetone at 90 °C while maintaining stable activity over an 18 h test. Comparative experiments using O2 and O3 as oxidants revealed that the promotional effect of the high-entropy structure was substantially more pronounced in catalytic ozonation than in conventional catalytic oxidation, highlighting the critical role of the HEO in amplifying the promoting effect of O3. Mechanistic investigations demonstrated that the local lattice distortion induced by the high-entropy configuration lowered the oxygen-vacancy formation energy, thereby promoting the generation of oxygen-deficient structures and enhancing ozone adsorption. Meanwhile, multimetallic coupling induced pronounced electronic redistribution and reduced the charge-transfer resistance, facilitating the activation of adsorbed ozone and its conversion into ROS, particularly highly oxidative hydroxyl radicals, which accelerated the oxidation of acetone-derived intermediates. This work elucidates how high-entropy configurations enhance ozone activation and promote the low-temperature deep oxidation of VOCs, providing new insights into the rational design of efficient catalysts for catalytic ozonation. Title: Evaluation of gasification agent strategies for underground coal gasification in post-ECBM reservoirs: A coupled thermo-hydro-chemical numerical simulation approach
Abstract: Implementing underground coal gasification (UCG) in post-ECBM reservoirs, namely coal reservoirs after CO2-enhanced coalbed methane (CO2-ECBM) recovery, provides a potential pathway for residual energy recovery. However, the pre-existing CO2-rich environment alters reservoir conditions and introduces additional constraints on gasification agent selection and process control. In this study, an in-house coupled thermo-hydro-chemical (THC) simulator was developed to investigate UCG under CO2-rich post-ECBM reservoir conditions. The gasification performance of different gasification agent strategies, including pure O2 injection, CO2–O2 co-injection, and water co-injection with O2, was systematically evaluated under various injection rates, together with a simplified screening-level cost assessment based on the assumed cost parameters. The results demonstrate that UCG can be initiated and maintained under the investigated reservoir, operating, and kinetic conditions. During gasification, the CO2 distribution evolves dynamically with cavity development, suggesting its potential to reflect reaction-zone evolution. For pure oxygen injection, increasing the injection rate accelerates coal conversion and reduces unit gas cost, but decreases syngas lower heating value and combustible component fraction. Compared with pure oxygen injection, CO2–O2 co-injection increases residual coal mass and results in lower syngas quality and higher unit gas cost under the investigated conditions. In contrast, moderate water co-injection improves syngas quality and reduces unit energy cost at low-to-moderate oxygen injection rates by promoting steam-related gasification reactions. Among the simulated cases, an oxygen injection rate of 3 × 10−4 m3/s combined with a water injection rate of 3 × 10−6 m3/s exhibited the most favorable overall performance within the investigated parameter range. Overall, this study provides insights into the thermochemical response of UCG under post-ECBM conditions and offers a numerical basis for comparative evaluation of gasification strategies prior to experimental and engineering-scale investigations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Hierarchical Ce-UiO-66 with tailored mesopores for efficient upgrading of biomass-derived carboxylic acids via ketonization

Compared with the original microporous Ce-UiO-66, the modified materials successfully introduced ∼ 8 nm mesopores, with the mesopore volume remarkably expanding to 0.312 cm3/g. This well-developed micro-mesoporous network not only overcomes mass transfer barriers, but also promotes the formation of abundant active sites, Ce3+ species, and oxygen vacancies while improving thermal stability. Among all samples, Ce-UiO-(100), synthesized with 100 mg F127 in 6 mL H2O, displayed the highest Ce3+ proportion (41.3 %) and the optimal thermal stability, attributed to optimal templating conditions that balance crystallinity and defect formation. Catalytic conversion of n-octanoic acid at 500 ℃ demonstrated that Ce-UiO-66 outperformed conventional CeO2, and mesoporosity further enhanced activity. Authors: Wei J.; Zhong Y.; Wang X.; Xu Y.; Zeng Y.; Li W.
Title: Chemical evolution of DMC-diesel soot during oxidation: Effects of NO concentration on surface and bulk functional groups
Abstract: Dimethyl carbonate alters diesel soot properties, yet how NO concentration regulates its chemical evolution during oxidation remains unclear. This study investigates the oxidation behavior and surface and bulk functional group evolution of soot from a DMC-diesel blend (DMC7) versus pure diesel (D100) across varying NO concentrations using thermogravimetric, X-ray photoelectron, and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy. NO concentration governs a mechanistic transition from site-blocking effect to NO2-enhanced oxidation. Low NO levels induce site-blocking effect between NO and O2 on active sites, elevating peak oxidation temperatures, whereas higher NO levels activate carbon-NO2 reaction, triggering formation of C=O and COO⁻ groups. D100 soot with ordered graphitic structure and higher graphitic nitrogen content undergoes surface-dominated oxidation with pronounced nitrogen functional groups reorganization and sp3/sp2 fluctuations. DMC7 soot featuring disordered nanostructure and abundant pyridinic nitrogen facilitates internal oxidant penetration and exhibits bulk-dominated oxidation with lower activation energy and moderate surface chemical evolution. Bulk –ONO2 evolution is distinct in that DMC7 soot shows higher initial abundance but is significantly suppressed under NO atmospheres, while D100 soot exhibits extended detection under NO conditions. Aliphatic C–H groups show an anomalous mid-oxidation increase for DMC7 soot due to C=C bond cleavage, whereas higher NO concentration enhances their consumption. Collectively, DMC blending shifts soot oxidation from surface-limited to bulk-penetrated regimes while NO concentration acts as a critical switch between competing pathways, providing a basis for optimizing aftertreatment strategies. Authors: Leite D.
Title: Granular incremental learning for uncertain data streams: A unifying conceptual and methodological overview
Abstract: This paper presents a conceptual and methodological synthesis of incremental machine learning under uncertainty. It connects the foundations of incremental learning with granular computing through interval, probabilistic, and fuzzy-possibilistic representations as canonical forms of information granules. A unified framework is introduced to organize existing approaches according to data representations, model structures, locally valid functions, information fusion mechanisms, and underlying optimization principles. The resulting classifiers, predictors, or controllers account for input-output, parametric, structural, and representational uncertainty. At their core, granular incremental learners balance multiple regularization criteria—including prediction error, interpretability, coverage-specificity equilibrium, structural compactness, stability, and semantic coherence—that guide how granules and local models are created, adapted, merged, and removed over time. Their outputs are combined through aggregation operators that allow cooperation among localized models without fully interconnected architectures. By systematizing the relationships among granular and structure-adaptive learning methods, this work provides a foundation for extending incremental learning toward interpretable, safe, and autonomous systems operating in complex and multimodal environments. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Tribological and sealing performance of working-fluid self-sealing interfaces for magnetorheological damper rod seals
Abstract: As new-energy vehicles and intelligent chassis systems advance, magnetorheological (MR) dampers have become important actuators in intelligent suspension systems because of their rapid response and continuously adjustable damping. However, conventional contact rod seals are prone to friction, wear, and leakage, particularly in particle-containing MR fluids. This study proposes a working-fluid self-sealing method in which the damper's internal MR fluid simultaneously serves as the damping and rod-end sealing medium. A permanent magnetic field confines the MR fluid within the piston-rod clearance, while the connected working-fluid region enables replenishment and magnetic re-capture after reciprocating disturbance. A self-sealing MR damper was designed, and magnetic-field analysis was used to evaluate compatibility between the sealing and damping magnetic circuits. A mechanistic framework combining field-dependent MR-fluid rheology, porous-media seepage, and working-fluid balance was then developed to interpret the physical processes governing pressure retention and motion resistance. Full-scale prototype tests evaluated static and dynamic pressure retention, apparent motion resistance, and damping performance. The self-sealing interface maintained stable static pressure retention over 0.30–0.70 MPa. After reciprocating motion, the pressure decrease was only about 1.0–1.3 kPa and did not progressively increase as peak piston-rod velocity rose from 15.7 to 47.1 mm/s. Compared with a conventionally sealed MR damper, the self-sealing damper reduced apparent motion resistance by about 51–73% while preserving stable current-dependent damping. Title: Hamiltonian dynamics of Boolean networks

Additionally, a family of unate Boolean networks capable of describing these three Hamiltonian behaviors is introduced, highlighting their specific properties and limitations. Title: Passivity-based adaptive integral control for underactuated mechanical systems and its application in tower cranes
Abstract: This study proposes a novel adaptive integral controller integrated with the interconnection and damping assignment passivity-based control framework for underactuated mechanical systems, and applies it to tower cranes. Title: A vaccination model for COVID-19 with asymptomatic transmission, waning immunity, and outbreak calibration
Abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has posed unprecedented challenges to global public health, revealing critical gaps in our understanding of transmission dynamics, particularly the roles of asymptomatic spread and waning immunity. This decomposition enables quantification of the contribution of asymptomatic spread to disease persistence. Calibration of the model to an outbreak in Nanjing, China, yields excellent fit ( R 2 = 0.9617) and reveals that asymptomatic transmission accounts for approximately 53.7% of the modeled transmission potential. Title: An intelligent control strategy based on improved LSTM prediction model for improving gas extraction efficiency in boreholes
Abstract: In order to break through the technical bottleneck that current coal mines are unable to accurately and dynamically increase the gas concentration in essence. First, the “gas-air” migration model in coal seam fissures is constructed from the perspective of the air leakage mechanism in boreholes. And the numerical simulation of gas extraction effect under different extraction conditions is carried out. Subsequently, the CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) and Attention mechanism are introduced to optimize the LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) model. The intelligent control strategy for enhancing gas concentration in boreholes is proposed. Finally, the proposed control strategy in this paper is applied in field practice to verify the strategy’s reliability. The study results indicate that there is an obvious correlation between concentration and negative pressure, and the extraction concentration’s attenuation rate is obviously different with varying negative pressure conditions. In addition, it can also enhance the predictive model’s ability to capture the gas concentration attenuation law under different extraction parameters.
