Authors: Zhu J.; Sun W.; Li Q.; Xu B.
Title: Koopman Re-ID: Modeling invariant and variant features for person re-identification
Abstract: Person re-identification (Re-ID) aims to identify pedestrians across multiple cameras over times, which can be conceptualized as a time-series problem. The Koopman operator provides a framework to model the evolution of nonlinear system by transforming this nonlinear time-series task into a linear representation, simplifying the analysis and prediction of underlying patterns. However, challenges remain in addressing the complex dynamics of pedestrian behavior and variations across different camera views. To overcome these challenges, we propose a novel Koopman-based model that extracts both invariant and dynamic features in Re-ID. The model consists of three key components: the Koopman Camera Block (KCB), the Koopman Person Block (KPB), and the Coarse-to-Fine (CF) fusion strategy. The KCB captures camera-specific features, learning inter-camera differences, while the KPB extracts person-specific features to account for dynamic variations in pedestrian attributes. The CF fusion strategy integrates and refines these features, ensuring a balance between robustness and accuracy. The proposed approach leverages Koopman operators to distinguish invariant features from dynamic variations, enabling the model to learn context-aware person attributes and handle cross-camera differences. By incorporating both camera- and pedestrian-specific features, the model strikes a balance between precision and generalization, improving Re-ID performance across diverse real-world settings. Extensive evaluations demonstrate the method's effectiveness, outperforming state-of-the-art approaches by 3.2% mAP and 5.1% rank-1 on the MSMT17 dataset. Title: GO-TSC composite integrated with EDXRF for ultrasensitive determination of trace Hg(II) in water via solid-phase preconcentration

Although Energy-Dispersive X-ray Fluorescence (EDXRF) is a promising field-deployable technique, its direct application to liquid samples faces three critical challenges: (1) strong absorption and scattering of X-rays by the aqueous matrix severely reduce excitation efficiency, limiting detection limits to only the mg L−1 level—far above the 1 μg L−1 regulatory requirement; (2) complex and variable water matrices cause pronounced matrix effects that compromise quantitative accuracy; (3) mercury's volatility and chemical instability in liquid samples complicate preservation and introduce bias. Carboxyl dimine-grafted S/N ligand-modified graphene oxide (GO-TSC) adsorbent selectively captures Hg2+ via HSAB soft-soft coordination. Enrichment followed by vacuum filtration forms a uniform thin film, eliminating water attenuation. Optimized conditions (pH 3, 70 °C, 40 min; Rh target 9 W, 300 s) with Compton-scattering normalization effectively correct for deposition nonuniformity. The method exhibits a linear range of 10–8000 μg L−1 (R2 > 0.9928) and an LOD of 0.26 μg L−1 (≈3 orders of magnitude lower than direct measurement). RSD < 3.2%, strong anti-interference (coexisting ions at 4 ppm yield < 5% signal change), and 7-day signal loss < 4.5%. Notably, the LOQ of 0.87 μg L−1 is below the WHO permissible limit of 1.0 μg L−1, confirming that the method can accurately quantify Hg(II) at the regulatory borderline. Wastewater spike recoveries are 96.55-102.84%, in agreement with ICP-MS. Authors: Sheng Y.; Wang P.; Wu Y.; Jing Q.; Zhang L.
Title: Investigation of deflagration characteristics and kinetic mechanisms for refined oil vapors in confined space
Abstract: To systematically investigate the explosion characteristics of single oils and their blended systems, experimental studies were conducted using the modified 20 L spherical explosion vessel. The explosion pressure and flame propagation characteristics of vapor mixtures of 95# gasoline, naphtha, −35# diesel, and 0# diesel, including both single oils and mixed oils, were measured at 353 K with volume fractions of 2%, 6%, and 10%. In addition, chemical kinetic simulations were performed to analyze the adiabatic flame temperature, key heat release reactions, and sensitivity coefficients of laminar burning velocity. The results indicate that the maximum explosion pressures of naphtha, gasoline, −35# diesel, and 0# diesel were achieved at volume fractions of 6%, 2%, 6%, and 6%, respectively. Among them, gasoline reached its peak explosion pressure at a relatively low concentration and exhibited the widest explosion limit range. Significant coupling enhancement effects were observed in the mixture systems, and the gasoline–0# diesel (1:1) mixture exhibited a markedly higher explosion intensity than both the 2:8 mixed oil systems and pure gasoline. The deflagration times (Tc and Tb) exhibited an inverse relationship with explosion pressure. Naphtha showed the fastest reaction rate, whereas the explosion durations of 0# diesel were approximately 1.72 and 1.83 times those of naphtha, respectively. Under the maximum explosion intensity conditions, the dominant key heat release reaction for gasoline, 0# diesel, and their blended vapor systems was R499, which governed the heat release process by promoting H radical generation. Sensitivity analysis of laminar burning velocity indicated that R432 was the key reaction affecting the laminar burning velocity of the system, synergistically influencing the evolution of macroscopic explosion pressure through regulation of laminar flame propagation and endothermic processes. Authors: Zhao W.; Zhang B.; Wang Y.; Li B.; Liu K.
Title: Mitigating feature degradation in deep Forward–Forward networks
Abstract: The Forward–Forward (FF) algorithm is a promising alternative to Backpropagation (BP) using layer-wise optimization. However, due to its local learning nature, FF suffers from feature degradation, which can be more severe than in BP for deep networks. To bridge this gap, we propose Sustained Forward (SF), which employs a dual-mechanism approach to achieve sustained feature propagation. Specifically, Cross-layer Gradient Momentum (CGM) propagates cross-layer gradient momentum to enrich the learning signal, and Local Feature Reconstruction (LFR) reconstructs local features to compensate for information loss. Extensive experiments on common benchmarks demonstrate that SF achieves significant performance improvements (e.g., over 6% on CIFAR-100), substantially narrowing the gap to BP. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Monophonic position sets of Cartesian and lexicographic products of graphs
Abstract: The general position problem in graph theory asks for the number of vertices in a largest set S of vertices of a graph G such that no shortest path of G contains more than two vertices of S. The analogous monophonic position problem is obtained from the general position problem by replacing “shortest path” by “induced path.” In this paper the monophonic position number is studied on Cartesian and lexicographic products of graphs. It is proved that in Cartesian products, a monophonic position set can only be in one of three canonical forms, named layered, varied, and cliquey. The monophonic position number of an arbitrary Cartesian product is bounded from below and above. The two bounds coincide if neither of the factors has simplicial vertices. A formula for the monophonic position number of a lexicographic product is given which only contains the clique number and the structure of monophonic sets of the second factor. © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Sun Q.; Zhu B.; Sun Y.
Title: Transient combustion behavior and oxidation characteristics of iron particles under ammonium perchlorate-assisted conditions
Abstract: To support carbon neutrality and carbon peaking goals, recyclable metal fuels have attracted considerable attention owing to their clean combustion characteristics and energy storage capability. Among them, iron (Fe) particles exhibit significant advantages due to their abundant availability and high potential for cyclic utilization. However, the transient combustion response of Fe particles and oxidation characteristics remain insufficiently understood. In this study, the combustion behavior of Fe particles under ammonium perchlorate (AP)-assisted conditions were investigated using a CO2 laser ignition platform. By combining high-speed imaging with X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and particle size analysis (PSA), the particle evolution, final phase composition, product morphology, and particle-size distribution were systematically elucidated. The combustion of Fe particles exhibits unsteady and multistage evolution characteristics. The particle remains largely intact during the initial stage, followed by oxide-shell instability-induced micro-explosions and particle fragmentation, and ultimately transitioned into a molten state in the combustion stage. High-temperature oxidation experiments further demonstrate the oxidation of Fe particles in air. Fe oxides with different valence states and residual metallic Fe under different temperatures coexist due to oxygen diffusion limitations and localized non-equilibrium oxidation. This study provides experimental evidence for understanding Fe particle combustion in heterogeneous reactive environments and establishes a foundation for their application in clean thermal energy systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Fan H.; Zhu B.; Dong X.; Guo J.; Li J.; Chang J.; Zhou Y.; Chu X.
Title: Low-crystallinity bimetallic NiCr phosphides with modulated electronic structure toward accelerated urea oxidation reaction
Abstract: Developing highly active and stable non-precious metal catalysts is a key challenge faced by the urea oxidation reaction (UOR), with the difficulty lying in the slow formation of high-valent Ni3+ active sites and a narrow effective potential window. Inspired by this, by employing NiCr layered double hydroxide as a precursor, a low-crystallinity bimetallic phosphide (Ni1.5Cr-P(30)) catalyst is constructed through a low-temperature controllable phosphidation strategy. The introduction of P optimized the local electronic structure of Ni/Cr, expanded the potential window of the charge transfer control region from 1.17-1.27 V to 1.17–1.32 V, and broadened the steady-state reaction potential window of γ-NiOOH from 1.27-1.32 V to 1.32–1.42 V. Electrochemical tests show that Ni1.5Cr-P(30) exhibits superior UOR performance in 1 M KOH and 0.33 M urea, with the onset potential of 1.28 V vs. RHE, a potential of 1.31 V vs. RHE at 10 mA cm−2, and a Tafel slope as low as 38.6 mV dec-1. This study provides a new approach for designing efficient UOR catalysts through electronic structure regulation and potential window expansion. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Si L.; Li L.; Yuan W.; Ma Z.
Title: Link prediction in multiplex social networks based on information transmission graph neural networks
Source title: International Journal of Modern Physics C
Abstract: Social networks are omnipresent graph-structured data where entities and interactions between them can be modeled as nodes and edges, respectively. In recent years, graph neural networks (GNNs) have evolved as a mainstream and powerful model for handling graph data. Link prediction, which can foretell missing or potential links, is a crucial task in social network analysis. However, most existing methods focus on monolayer networks and usually ignore that multiplex networks have richer information, which often results in poor performance on link prediction. Therefore, this paper proposes an information transmission-based GNN (IT-GNN) model for link prediction in multiplex social networks. IT-GNN first learns the representation of each node in a multiplex network from itself and its neighborhood. Specifically, the neighborhood information of a node is learned from its 1-, 2- and 3-hop neighbors in combination with the three new ways of information transmission. Then, the embedding of a node pair is obtained based on these representations. In this regard, the final representations of potential links in the target layer, which are used to determine the existence of potential links, are generated by fusing their embeddings from all layers. Extensive experiments on seven real-world networks demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed model. © 2027 World Scientific Publishing Company.

Authors: Chen R.; Xiao F.; Zhu H.; Liang P.; Kong D.
Title: Thermometric inversion of dynamic specific absorption rate for bioheat temperature prediction in microwave ablation
Abstract: In the bioheat model, the specific absorption rate (SAR) quantifies mass-specific power deposition and is a key factor influencing temperature simulation accuracy in microwave ablation (MWA). Conventional thermometric SAR estimation is based on early-time temperature slopes, which can miss the temporal evolution of effective deposition over the entire heating interval. We propose a physics-constrained thermometric inversion framework to identify an effective dynamic SAR using a fast semi-analytical forward solver for stable full-duration prediction. The recovered SAR adopts a compact, mechanism-informed form that combines a baseline spatial envelope with a constrained spatiotemporal modulation to capture heating dynamics. Phantom experiments demonstrate substantially lower global errors and markedly improved cross-sensor consistency than the early-time slope baseline and two electromagnetic-based SAR models. A model-component ablation study further indicates that spatiotemporal modulation is necessary to reproduce the observed build-up and late-stage heating behavior. The dynamic SAR provides a practical and compact heat-source description for rapid temperature prediction in MWA and related thermal therapies. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Authors: Sahu N.K.; Gulati R.; Dewan A.; Kumar M.
Author full names: Sahu, Nitesh Kumar (57211023053); Gulati, Rakshit (60968535700); Dewan, Anupam (7006876749); Kumar, Mayank (56647323300)
Title: Critical swirl number for the onset of vortex breakdown in isothermal confined swirling flows: Roles of swirl-generation strategy and reference location
Abstract: Swirl number characterizes swirl-strength and is widely used to correlate vortex-breakdown (VB) onset, yet reported critical values vary, likely because studies differ in swirl-number formulation, its axial evaluation location, Reynolds number (Re), expansion ratio (ER), and swirl-generation-strategy. This work investigates the most appropriate swirl-number formulation and suitable evaluation location, its critical value for stable-VB onset in non-reacting flows, and how swirl-generation strategy affects these aspects. A baseline isothermal-flow in a single-stream model dump-combustor with ER=2.0, Re≈2.0×10⁴, and a 45° axial-vaned swirler is first simulated using an LES-based solver and validated against available experimental mean-flow and coherent-dynamics measurements. Then the validated solver setup is applied to other combustor cases differing from the base-case only in vane-angle or swirler-configuration: four axial-vaned swirler cases with 17°, 25°, 40°, and 45° vane-angles, and four tangential-vaned swirler cases with 45°, 55°, 68°, and 75° vane-angles. Stable-VB is absent in the 17° axial and 45° tangential cases, and appears from 25° and 55° onwards, respectively. The generic swirl-number, SNg, including mean-velocity, velocity-fluctuation, and pressure contributions in a radius-normalized ratio of axial angular-momentum to axial-momentum fluxes, emerges as the most appropriate swirl-strength measure. However, meaningful comparison across different swirl-combustor cases using SNg also requires its evaluation upstream of the expansion-plane, sufficiently close to the swirler. Using this criterion, critical SNg lies between 0.22 and 0.35 for axial-swirler cases and between 0.25 and 0.37 for tangential-swirler cases, suggesting near-independence from swirl-generation strategy under the investigated isothermal conditions at fixed values of Re, ER and downstream geometry. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Authors: Li Y.; Wang Q.; Liu C.; Li C.; Meng Q.; Zhang J.; Zhang Y.; Yang X.; Du M.; Wang X.
Title: Well-dispersed CuZn catalysts supported on mesoporous alumina for efficient methanol steam reforming via EDTA-assisted impregnation
Abstract: Methanol steam reforming (MSR) is a promising hydrogen production technology, but conventional Cu-based catalysts suffer from insufficient activity and stability. Herein, mesoporous Al-TUD-1 with large surface area and three-dimensional porous structure was prepared by using a facile sol–gel route. A series of CuZn/EAT-x catalysts with different EDTA/Cu molar ratios were fabricated by EDTA-assisted impregnation method and applied in MSR for the first time. Characterization results demonstrated that appropriate EDTA dosage improved metal-support interaction and active species dispersion. Compared to CuZn/Al-TUD-1, EDTA-modified CuZn/EAT-x catalysts displayed enhanced physicochemical properties and catalytic performance due to the strong Cu-EDTA coordination. The CuZn/EAT-1 catalyst featured the smallest Cu particle size and abundant Cu0/Cu+ active species, delivering promising activity and stability. Notably, it achieved 94.9% methanol conversion at 275 °C while maintaining near-zero CO selectivity across a wide temperature window (200–300 °C), indicating effective suppression of the reverse water–gas shift reaction. The catalyst also retained 95% of its initial methanol conversion after 60 h on stream, with its H2 production rate remaining essentially stable. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Liu Y.; Wan Y.; Xin Q.; Liang X.
Title: GC-RIO: A geometry-conditioned resolution-invariant operator for cross-geometry generalization on complex domains
Abstract: Parameterized boundary value problems on complex local domains are central to engineering analysis and inverse design, where repeated evaluation of structural responses under varying loads, geometries, and discretisations is required for safety assessment and decision-making. However, existing neural-operator methods remain difficult to apply in such settings because they are often sensitive to discretisation changes, limited in handling irregular complex geometries, and weak in generalising across heterogeneous local domains. To address these challenges, we propose GC-RIO, a geometry-conditioned operator learning framework for parameterized boundary value problems on complex local domains with varying finite-element discretisations. The framework combines graph-based geometric encoding, latent regularisation of variable-cardinality point clouds, and geometry-conditioned spectral operator learning to construct transferable solution representations for unseen structures. In addition, a learnable geometric context module extracts cross-domain geometric priors and modulates the spectral operator, while engineering priors are incorporated to couple field prediction with stress exceedance assessment and structural risk ranking, thereby extending surrogate modelling toward engineering decision support. The proposed method is validated on a benchmark 2D Darcy flow problem and multiple real 3D aerospace structural cases, including wing and fuselage local domains from different aircraft platforms under diverse loading conditions. Results show that GC-RIO consistently outperforms DeepONet, FNO, and NORM in prediction accuracy, cross-resolution robustness, and cross-geometry generalisation, demonstrating its effectiveness as a computational modelling framework for engineering-oriented operator learning on complex geometries. Our code and dataset are available at https://github.com/jaixlu/GC-RIO.git. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Inc.

Title: Comments on “Review of the applications of different fractional models in engineering”
Abstract: In this paper, we analyse the choices made in the article “Review of the applications of different fractional models in engineering”, particularly with regard to the derivatives used. It is shown that many pioneers in the applications of fractional calculus have been overlooked. The use of Riemann-Liouville and Caputo derivatives is criticised and it is shown that they are not suitable for engineering system definitions, namely because they do not allow the construction of time-invariant systems. © 2026 The Author(s). Authors: Geng X.; Quan Y.; Li L.; Ren J.
Title: New insights into “Two birds with one Stone” effect of Cu in CoxCu/ZrO2 catalysts for furfural hydrogenation to 2-methylfuran
Abstract: A series of CoxCu/ZrO2 catalysts with different Co/Cu molar ratios were prepared by a complexation impregnation method and applied to the liquid-phase hydrogenation of furfural (FFA) to 2-methylfuran (2-MF). The catalytic performance varied markedly with the Co/Cu molar ratio, and Co5Cu/ZrO2 achieved complete FFA conversion with a 2-MF selectivity of 90.2 % at 195 °C and 2.0 MPa H2, remarkably outperforming Cu/ZrO2 (24.8 %) and Co/ZrO2 (57.0 %). The excellent catalytic performance was mainly attributed to the synergistic effects of metallic Co0 sites and oxygen vacancies based on the linear relationships between 2-MF selectivity and them, which are responsible for H2 dissociation and may promote the formation of a vertical adsorption configuration of FFA molecules, respectively. It has been verified by H2-TPR that the realization of the lower-temperature reduction of CoOx species required the introduction of Cu species to form a strong Cu-Co interaction, in spite of Co0 possessing the stronger ability of dissociating H2 than Cu0 species. Larger Co0 concentration was generated due to the modification of Cu with appropriate Co/Cu molar ratio, accompanied by the formation of more oxygen vacancies via hydrogen spillover to ZrO2 as confirmed by the O 1 s XPS and EPR results. This work innovatively proposed that Cu modification is an effective strategy for constructing active species-oxygen defect synergistic double metal catalysts, providing new insights into the rational design of catalysts for the selective upgrading of biomass-derived furanic compounds. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Modeling of gas-water transport in the porous transport layer of a proton exchange membrane electrolyzer
Abstract: In this work, the mechanism of gas invasion into a saturated thin porous medium, specifically the Porous Transport Layer used in a Proton Exchange Membrane electrolyzer, is investigated. The phase-field model based on the Cahn-Hilliard theory is employed to capture the dynamics of the water-air interface in the presence of solid surfaces within the porous material. Numerical simulations are performed on 2 mm× 6 mm domain geometries composed of cylindrical solid grains, characterized by different pore sizes from 10 to 30 µm and porosities from 0.47 to 0.59, to examine the influence of pore architecture and inlet air velocity on two-phase distribution. Additionally, mesh dependency, relative tolerance, and mobility sensitivity studies are conducted to identify the optimal simulation parameters. Quantitative evaluation of the phase distributions reveals that increasing inlet air velocity shifts the system from capillary-dominated to viscous-dominated flow. The boundaries of this regime transition depend on the Capillary number, pore microstructure, sample thickness, and fluid properties. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Title: Azo-carbazole-containing layer-engineered DNA multilayer films for polarization holography
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: The realization of dynamic and rewritable holographic media is essential for advancing next-generation optical data storage, information security, and display technologies. In this work, we report for the first time a study on multi-layer DNA-CACzE-CPC films. Natural DNA was combined with an azo-carbazole chromophore (CACzE) and a cetylpyridinium chloride (CPC) surfactant and the samples were prepared using a sequential solution-casting method. Three types of films were prepared: (a) a 1-layer film consisting of a single DNA-CACzE-CPC layer; (b) a 2-layer film consisting of a DNA-CPC layer at the bottom and a DNA-CACzE-CPC layer on top; and (c) a 3-layer film consisting of a DNA-CACzE-CPC layer sandwiched between top and bottom DNA-CPC layers. The effects of multiple layers were studied through a) response time, b) retention behavior and c) diffraction efficiency by conducting polarization holographic recording and reading experiments. It was found that the tested 3-layer film showed the highest diffraction efficiency and short-term retention among the investigated architectures, although its response time was modestly longer. The observed performance may reflect DNA–CACzE–CPC molecular association and interfacial confinement, while the greater nominal film thickness may also contribute. Moreover, for the first time, we report a DNA based holographic material that exhibits performance comparable to other existing rewritable materials using the 3-layer film. We also report for the first time that the polarization selective properties of the recorded hologram deviates from the conventional theory of polarization holography, for which DNA chirality represents one plausible, but unproven, contribution. This handedness-dependent response may be relevant to polarization-multiplexed holography, although its mechanism requires further study. This work establishes DNA-based layered composites as a versatile, sustainable, and mechanically robust platform for rewritable holography, bridging biopolymer ordering with synthetic chromophore functionality and scalable fabrication. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Malik M.I.; Abatzoglou N.
Title: Methane dry reforming for sustainable syngas production: thermodynamic constraints, thermal catalyst design, and alternative energy-input strategies
Abstract: Dry reforming of methane (DRM) and autothermal dry reforming (ATDR) are promising technologies for converting methane and carbon dioxide into syngas (H2 and CO), an important feedstock for the production of fuels and value-added chemicals. However, their industrial implementation remains challenging because of the highly endothermic nature of DRM, heat management issues during autothermal operation, and catalyst deactivation caused by carbon deposition, metal sintering, oxidation, and poisoning. Although numerous studies have reported advances in catalyst development, an integrated understanding of thermodynamic constraints, catalyst stability, and emerging energy-input technologies remains limited. This review discusses the thermodynamics of DRM and ATDR, together with the catalytic aspects of DRM. Particular emphasis is given to the influence of operating conditions on equilibrium conversion, gas composition, carbon formation, and hotspot development. Recent advances in thermal catalytic systems are discussed, highlighting the roles of catalyst supports, promoters, and active metals, together with strategies for mitigating catalyst deactivation. Furthermore, photothermal and microwave-assisted dry reforming are critically evaluated as alternative energy-input technologies for overcoming the thermodynamic and kinetic limitations of conventional thermal reforming. Overall, this review provides a comprehensive framework for optimizing reaction thermodynamics, catalyst design, and reactor operation to enable efficient, stable, and sustainable syngas production. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Synergistic Fe(II)/Co(II) bimetallic MOF with Tunable oxidation states for visible-light photocatalytic tetracycline hydrochloride degradation
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Water pollution from medical antibiotics such as Tetracycline Hydrochloride (TCH) necessitates the development of novel photocatalysts to degrade them photocatalytically under visible light. In this study, Fe-Co bimetallic metal organic frameworks (Fe-Co BMOFs) photocatalyst with terephthalic acid linker was developed, and its properties were engineered via tuning the Fe:Co metal ratios of 1:1, 1:3, 1:5, 3:1, and 5:1. All metal compositions exhibited crystalline structure; however, varying the metal ratio showed distinct morphological and textural features, with a maximum surface area of 58.4 m2/g. The optimized Fe-Co BMOFs photodegraded TCH with 87% efficiency within 300 min under visible light with a maximum reaction rate constant of 0.34 h−1. The ligand to metal charge transfer occurs from π-conjugated TA to Co2+ and Fe3+ nodes, which initiate the Fe2+/Fe3+ ↔ Co2+/Co3+ redox cycle. Interaction between Fe3+ and Co2+ centres via oxygen linkers governs the degree of 3d orbital overlap and charge-transfer efficiency. The enhanced photocatalytic activity is attributed to high porosity, mixed valence states of Fe, and favourable charge-transfer characteristics. Hydroxyl radicals were primarily responsible for the increased activity. The degradation occurred via hydroxylation, demethylation, and ring cleavage. These catalysts exhibited excellent stability and recyclability. Most importantly, the study shows the significance of the Fe:Co ratio in determining the physicochemical and photocatalytic properties of Fe-Co BMOFs, which demonstrates it to be a potential candidate for antibiotic degradation and sustainable environmental remediation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Chen W.; Li R.; Wang W.; Yin K.; Hou X.; Wu L.
Title: Synergistic Ag/Cu-TCPP MOFs–based plasmonic SERS platform for non-invasive and time-resolved monitoring of salivary uric acid
Abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) methods offer high sensitivity for uric acid (UA) detection, but efficient molecular enrichment and reliable analysis in complex biological matrices remain challenging. Here, we developed an Ag/Cu-TCPP SERS platform for noninvasive determination of UA in saliva. The platform combined the electromagnetic enhancement provided by Ag nanoparticles (Ag NPs) with the molecular enrichment capability of Cu-TCPP. Density functional theory calculations further indicated that UA can be enriched on Cu-TCPP through weak Cu···O quasi-coordination between the UA carbonyl oxygen and exposed Cu centers, accompanied by interfacial charge redistribution. Consequently, the platform achieved a low detection limit of 0.04 μM and a wide linear range of 0.1–1000 μM. Beyond conventional single-point determination, the platform enabled time-resolved assessment of salivary UA concentration, revealing temporal fluctuations under physiological and feeding-related conditions. These results highlight the potential of MOF-integrated SERS platforms for noninvasive monitoring of small-molecule biomarkers. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Chi J.; Li Z.; Jiang R.; Sun D.; Ma Z.; Fang F.
Title: Facet-inheritance strategy to enrich Cu(1 0 0) in Cu/ZnO catalyst for high-efficiency CO2 hydrogenation to methanol
Abstract: Increasing the content of the Cu(1 0 0) facet in Cu/ZnO-based catalyst is an effective strategy for boosting their catalytic performance in CO2 hydrogenation to methanol. However, the Cu(1 1 1) facet rather than the Cu(1 0 0) facet has the lowest surface energy for both CuO and metallic Cu, making it challenging to enrich Cu(1 0 0) facet through traditional preparation methods. Herein, leveraging the intrinsically lowest surface energy of the (1 0 0) facet in Cu2O, we proposed a scalable solid-phase synthesis method starting with Cu2O/ZnO composites, proceeding via CuO/ZnO composites as an intermediate, and then reduced to prepare Cu/ZnO catalysts with high Cu(1 0 0) facet content. Due to the facet inheritance behavior of Cu during redox processes under mild conditions, the Cu(1 0 0) facet content in the synthesized Cu/ZnO catalyst was 1.7-fold higher than that of the catalyst prepared by the traditional preparation method. The increased Cu(1 0 0) facet facilitates CO2 bridge adsorption as well as hydrogen activation and spillover, thus enhancing catalytic performance. Under 260 °C and 3 MPa, the methanol selectivity and space–time yield of the optimized Cu/ZnO catalyst reached 64 % and 920 mg·gcat−1·h−1, respectively. The facet engineering strategy significantly improves catalytic performance of Cu/ZnO catalysts and holds great potential for industrial-scale applications. Copyright © 2026. Title: Experimental investigation and RSM-based optimization of combustion characteristics in an ABE-fueled HCCI engine
Abstract: Homogeneous charge compression ignition (HCCI) combustion is an advanced low-temperature combustion (LTC) strategy that combines the high thermal efficiency of compression ignition (CI) engines with the low nitrogen oxide (NOx) and soot emission advantages of spark ignition (SI) engines. However, difficulties in controlling self-ignition timing and a narrow operating range are among the main issues that limit the practical application of HCCI engines. In this study, the effects of n-heptane and acetone-butanol-ethanol (ABE) blends on the combustion, performance, and emission characteristics of an HCCI engine were investigated both experimentally and statistically. In the experiments, ABE mixtures at 20%, 40%, and 60% ratios were added to n-heptane fuel, and engine tests were conducted at engine speeds ranging from 800 to 1200 rpm and lambda values ranging from 2.5 to 3.5. In the experimental design and analysis processes, response surface methodology (RSM) based on the central composite design (CCD) was employed, and a total of 15 experimental combinations were conducted. The variable response parameters evaluated were engine torque, brake specific fuel consumption (BSFC), exhaust temperature, maximum pressure rise rate (MPRR), start of combustion (CA10), combustion phase (CA50), combustion duration (CD), indicated thermal efficiency (ITE), as well as carbon monoxide (CO) and hydrocarbon (HC) emissions. As a result of RSM optimization, the optimal operating conditions were determined to be an ABE ratio of 51.64%, an engine speed of 800 rpm, and a lambda value of 2.65. Based on the validation tests conducted under optimal conditions, the maximum deviation for the response parameters was found to be 2.63%. The findings indicate that n-heptane/ABE blends increase combustion stability in HCCI engines, reducing fuel consumption and providing highly efficient combustion behavior. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zou Y.; Pan Z.; Lin X.; Cai C.; Zhou X.
Author full names: Zou, Yu (58612072500); Pan, Zhigeng (59109223200); Lin, Xianxuan (57203802022); Cai, Chuangxin (57209021175); Zhou, Xianchun (60341559800)
Title: LDOFormer: Low-rank and Decorrelation-regularized Transformer for 3D human pose estimation
Abstract: Transformer-based 2D-to-3D human pose lifting is accurate but often relies on large parameter budgets (15–50 M). Although factorized spatio-temporal attention reduces computation, it does not ensure complementary spatial and temporal representations; an important and under-explored axis for improvement is therefore representational redundancy rather than scale. We identify two sources of representational inefficiency: (i) high cross-stream correlation between spatial and temporal attention streams, which leads to redundant feature encoding; and (ii) limited use of the low-dimensional structure of natural human motion. We propose LDOFormer, a lightweight spatio-temporal Transformer with a structured redundancy-suppression design. At the input level, a unified spatio-temporal adaptive embedding (USTAE) fuses spatial, temporal, kinematic (velocity and acceleration), and global context cues via data-dependent weights. At the operator level, a low-rank enhanced spatio-temporal block (LeST-Block) parameterizes the Q/K/V and FFN projections as the sum of a full-rank matrix and a rank-r branch trained from scratch. At the feature level, a multi-source complementary learning strategy (MCLS) regularizes cross-stream Pearson correlation during training. On Human3.6M with CPN-detected inputs, LDOFormer reports 37.5 mm MPJPE (Protocol 1) and 29.8 mm PA-MPJPE (Protocol 2) using 3.7 M parameters, approximately 9× fewer than comparable methods. These results indicate that structured redundancy suppression is a useful design choice for efficient 3D pose estimation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Incorporating Mg into Al-based supports to modulate metal-support interactions for enhanced H2 productivity and selectivity in Ni-catalyzed aqueous-phase reforming
Abstract: Aqueous-phase reforming (APR) of biomass-derived oxygenates provides a sustainable route for hydrogen production. Owing to their multifunctionality, Ni-based catalysts have been widely studied; however, these catalysts are still limited by methanation side reaction that decreases H2 selectivity and agglomeration that reduces activity. Herein, we demonstrate that these issues can be tackled by regulating the metal-support interaction (MSI) in the supported Ni catalysts. Specifically, Mg is incorporated into Al-based supports to precisely modulate the MSI between Ni and Al-based support to enhance selective hydrogen production from APR of ethylene glycol. A volcano-type dependence of H2 productivity on Mg content is observed, with an optimal Mg/Al ratio of 1:3 achieving an H2 productivity of 4.43 mmol/gNi/min, approximately twofold higher than that of Ni/Al2O3 (2.20 mmol/gNi/min), while completely suppressing methanation. Complementary characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal that Mg strengthens MSI, promoting the dispersion of Ni species and partially depleting the electron density of Ni, which increases the density of active sites to enhance apparent activity and suppresses hydrogen-consuming side reactions. However, excessive Mg induces overly strong MSI, stabilizing Ni in an electron-deficient and poorly reducible state, thereby inhibiting decarbonylative C–C bond cleavage and drastically reducing activity. This work demonstrates MSI modulation as an effective strategy to balance geometric and electronic effects in Ni catalysts for efficient hydrogen production via APR. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhang W.; Dong L.; Fang Y.; Yang X.; Chen Z.; Li Z.; Chen G.; Ning S.
Title: Multi‑objective optimisation and experimental validation of a compact energy‑efficient active regeneration burner for diesel particulate filter regeneration
Abstract: Active regeneration burners are essential for diesel particulate filter (DPF) regeneration. However, they are often constrained by low flow utilisation, excessive gas velocity, and inadequate mixing between combustion products and exhaust gas, leading to poor thermal efficiency and degraded regeneration performance. To tackle these challenges, this study focused on achieving a compact and lightweight burner design via iterative and dimensional optimisation. A multi‑objective optimisation framework incorporating Response Surface Methodology (RSM), Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III (NSGA-III), and Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to an Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) was then established to enhance the combustion performance. The effectiveness of this optimisation approach was verified through regeneration experiments. The optimised design reduced burner volume and mass by 57.7 % and 39.5 %, respectively, while maintaining outlet velocity uniformity above 97 % across three investigated exhaust-flow conditions. Outlet temperature uniformity increased from 82.8 % to 92.2 %, the maximum measured outlet temperature at the five-point thermocouple plane increased from 865 °C to 970 °C, and thermal efficiency increased from 38.8 % to 51.1 %. The time required for the DPF upstream temperature to reach 600 °C decreased from 200 s to 172 s, while the regeneration efficiency increased from 92 % to 94 %. Smoke opacity, HC, and CO decreased from 3.9 % to 3.1 %, 28 ppm to 8 ppm, and 0.205 vol% to 0.100 vol%, respectively; however, NOx increased from 104.5 ppm to 117.0 ppm, indicating a trade-off between oxidation completeness and NOx formation. These results demonstrate the practical potential of the burner for compact and energy-efficient diesel aftertreatment systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Yu F.; Xu H.; Xia C.; Zong Z.; Tan G.
Title: Deflickering vision-based occupancy networks through lightweight spatio-temporal correlation
Abstract: Vision-based occupancy networks (VONs) provide an end-to-end solution for reconstructing 3D environments in autonomous driving. However, existing methods often suffer from temporal inconsistencies, manifesting as flickering effects that compromise visual experience and adversely affect decision-making. While recent approaches have incorporated historical data to mitigate the issue, they often incur high computational costs and may introduce noisy information that interferes with object detection. We propose OccLinker, a novel plugin framework designed to seamlessly integrate with existing VONs for boosting performance. Our method efficiently consolidates historical static and motion cues, learns sparse latent correlations with current features through a dual cross-attention mechanism, and produces correction occupancy components to refine the base network's predictions. We propose a new temporal consistency metric to quantitatively identify flickering effects. Extensive experiments on two benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method delivers superior performance with negligible computational overhead, while effectively eliminating flickering artifacts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Li F.; Dong J.; Chu M.; Tang J.; Tian H.
Title: Effect of vertical cooling furnace structure on hydrogen cooling behavior of oxidized pellets
Abstract: Hydrogen cooling of hot oxidized pellets not only recovers the sensible heat of the pellets but also produces prereduced pellets, thereby reducing the energy load and reduction burden in subsequent smelting processes. This study investigates the hydrogen cooling process of high–temperature oxidized pellets in a vertical cooling furnace through numerical simulation, with a focus on the effects of key parameters—including bed height, shaft angle, and central baffle angle—on cooling efficiency, metallization rate, exergy efficiency, and gas utilization rate. A multiphase mathematical model is developed based on mass, momentum, and energy conservation equations, accounting for compressible gas flow, pellet reduction reactions, and heat transfer. The results show that increasing the bed height extends the residence time, which improves the metallization rate, exergy efficiency, and cooling gas utilization rate, with an optimal bed height of 5.62 m. A furnace angle of 157° promotes reaction uniformity and enhances process efficiency, while a central baffle angle of 134° optimizes gas distribution and reaction homogeneity. Under the optimal configuration, the process achieves a metallization rate of 32.55%, an exergy efficiency of 23.84%, and a cooling gas utilization rate of 27.56%. Copyright © 2026. Title: MLDN: Multi-layer diffusion network for recognizing malicious (Deformable) handwritten text through restoration
Abstract: Although many handwritten text recognition systems have been successfully developed, open challenges remain, particularly in accurately grading descriptive answers. This is because the handwriting of descriptive answers may contain unreadable words called malicious text, including various types of struck-out words, overwriting, scribbling, deformation, and degradation. Such words are often used when students are uncertain about their answers and to add more detail to meet the requirements of the question. Recognizing such words accurately is important and an open challenge for the present OCRs. Restoring actual information in such malicious words can help improve the automatic grading of descriptive answers. This paper presents a new technique to improve recognition performance through the restoration of malicious words. We take advantage of the high-quality image generation capability of diffusion models and propose a Multi-Layer Diffusion Network (MLDN), which comprises three modules considering the characteristics of malicious text. Module 1 combines U-Net and GAN to generate noisy images and to perform denoising. Module 2 employs a diffusion-Transformer to restore the structure of characters using feature maps derived from the input and generated samples. Module 3 introduces a pretrained Tr-OCR that utilizes dual decoders for recognizing the text. The performance of the MLDN is validated through experiments on our datasets and benchmark datasets. A comparative analysis with state-of-the-art models shows that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art models. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Fast tempered fractional physics-informed neural network for nonlinear tempered time-fractional subdiffusion equations: Forward and inverse problems
Abstract: We develop FT-fPINNs, a fast physics-informed learning framework for nonlinear tempered time-fractional subdiffusion equations (tTFSEs) that couples a tempered fast L2-1θ discretization of the tempered Caputo derivative with a neural surrogate trained in an end-to-end manner. The time-fractional operator is enforced through its time-discrete fast representation embedded directly into the physics-informed residual, which reduces the memory and computational cost associated with long-history evaluation while retaining the higher temporal accuracy of the L2-1θ scheme. To enhance optimization efficiency, we employ a stagewise training strategy that progressively expands the effective time horizon, thereby stabilizing the learning dynamics and concentrating updates on informative residual structures. The resulting approach is mesh-free in space, uses automatic differentiation for spatial derivatives, and is applicable to forward simulation and inverse parameter identification in tempered fractional-order dynamics. We validate FT-fPINNs on one-dimensional and two-dimensional benchmark problems for nonlinear tTFSEs in both forward and inverse settings. The numerical results demonstrate accurate reconstruction of the solution field and reliable recovery of the unknown parameter set from terminal observations. Robustness is further examined by contaminating only terminal measurements with additive Gaussian noise at representative levels, under which reconstruction errors remain controlled and the inferred parameters remain close to their reference values. These results indicate that FT-fPINNs provides an effective and computationally efficient physics-informed learning framework for nonlinear tTFSEs with tempered memory. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Recent developments in nickel/copper electrodes using polymer ink catalyst and their synergies for hydrogen production
Abstract: The growing demand for sustainable energy has accelerated the development of efficient hydrogen production technologies, particularly electrochemical water splitting. This review highlights the recent progress in nickel/copper (Ni/Cu) electrode systems enhanced by polymer ink catalysts, focusing on their synergistic effects in improving hydrogen production. Ni/Cu bimetallic electrodes offer a cost-effective and stable alternative to noble metals, in which nickel facilitates water dissociation and oxygen evolution, while copper improves hydrogen desorption and electrical conductivity. Their combined effect optimizes adsorption energies, enhances charge transfer, and boosts catalytic efficiency in both acidic and alkaline media. The role of polymer ink catalysts is emphasized in enabling uniform catalyst distribution, strong adhesion, and controlled nucleation during electroless deposition, leading to improved electrode morphology and performance. Various synthesis strategies, including electrodeposition, hydrothermal methods, and hierarchical nano-structuring, are discussed for enhancing surface area, active sites, and durability. Additionally, advances in doping, hybrid nanostructures, and porous architectures are reviewed for further performance optimization. Despite remaining challenges in scalability and long-term stability, Ni/Cu electrodes integrated with polymer ink catalysts demonstrate significant potential as scalable, low-cost, and high-performance systems for sustainable hydrogen production and future energy applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Numerical investigation of gas void fraction measurement in gas-liquid slug flow at a Venturi throat using ultrasonic time of flight
Abstract: Ultrasonic void-fraction measurement in gas-liquid slug flow is challenging because the received time-of-flight signal is strongly affected by the spatially non-uniform phase distribution at the measurement section. This study investigates an intrusive direct-contact ultrasonic pulse-transmission method installed at the throat of a Venturi tube. A one-way flow-acoustic numerical framework was developed. The gas-liquid slug-flow field was first simulated using a phase-field model, and representative throat-local snapshots were then frozen and mapped to a transient pressure-acoustics model. The arrival time of the first dominant positive peak of the received acoustic-pressure signal was extracted to determine the ultrasonic time of flight and the corresponding TOF-derived equivalent propagation speed. The results show that the TOF-derived equivalent propagation speed varies non-monotonically with the representative throat-local gas void fraction and exhibits an overall trend consistent with the separately calculated homogeneous Wood reference. However, the simulated values remain higher than the corresponding Wood values for all investigated two-phase slug-flow snapshots. This difference is associated with the cross-throat non-uniformity of the gas-volume-fraction distribution and the path-dependent formation of the received dominant peak. The results provide a numerical basis for interpreting direct-contact ultrasonic time-of-flight measurements in Venturi-throat slug flow. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Yu J.; Xie Y.; Chen H.; Ni S.; Zhang N.
Title: SALiT: A structure-aware lightweight Transformer for multi-task remote sensing interpretation
Abstract: On-board optical remote sensing (RS) interpretation requires lightweight visual backbones that maintain strong representational capacity under stringent resource constraints. Although Vision Transformers (ViTs) excel at modeling long-range dependencies, their inherent structural complexity makes compact design challenging, as aggressive compression often leads to substantial performance degradation. To address this issue, we propose SALiT, a structure-aware lightweight Transformer that integrates redundancy-driven compression with hierarchical structural distillation. Specifically, a structure-aware dual-driven compression (SAD2C) strategy is developed based on structural redundancy analysis. By exploiting the high intra-stage similarity among Transformer blocks and the observed coupling between Query (Q) and Key (K) branches, SAD2C combines stage-wise weight sharing with an Integrated Attention formulation, while retaining effective global interaction modeling for complex RS interpretation. Furthermore, a global hierarchical knowledge distillation (GHKD) framework is introduced to provide comprehensive structural guidance beyond local feature supervision. GHKD facilitates the transfer of structural modeling capabilities tailored to RS-specific characteristics, enabling the lightweight model to maintain strong discriminative power despite its compact structure. Extensive evaluations on public RS benchmarks demonstrate that SALiT provides competitive representational capability with substantially lower backbone complexity, requiring only 10.5 M parameters and 4.0 G FLOPs, establishing SALiT as a versatile backbone for efficient multi-task RS interpretation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Hu Z.; Wang Q.; Xiao L.; Tang J.; Wang Y.; Xu X.; Wang D.; Yang X.; Tu Y.
Title: Synergistic thermochemical conversion behavior and mechanism for ultra-low concentration methane-coal gangue mixtures in an oxygen enriched fluidized bed
Abstract: During coal mining operations, large amounts of ultra-low concentration methane are vented directly into the atmosphere because they cannot be efficiently utilized, resulting not only in a waste of resources but also in an exacerbation of the greenhouse effect. Co-firing highly diluted methane alongside coal refuse in a fluidized bed offers a viable “waste-treating-waste” solution; however, it still faces challenges like sluggish reaction kinetics and elevated CO emissions under standard atmospheric conditions. Building on previous research, this study introduces oxygen-enriched combustion technology into this fluidized-bed system. By integrating a self-developed fluidized-bed thermal oxidation experimental platform with the Chemkin Pro chemical kinetics model, the study systematically investigates how an oxygen-enhanced environment influences the combustion behavior and reaction pathways when co-firing highly diluted methane with coal refuse. The results show that an oxygen-enriched atmosphere significantly lowers the critical conversion temperature of methane and significantly reduces CO emissions. Furthermore, combustion efficiency increases with rising oxygen concentration, whereas the discharge of contaminants like SO2 and NOx initially intensifies before stabilizing alongside further oxygen enrichment. Kinetic simulations confirm that an oxygen-enriched atmosphere increases the concentrations of O and OH radicals, accelerates chain oxidation reactions, and promotes the conversion of CO to CO2. However, the accelerated NO conversion pathway contributes to NOx formation to some extent. When the oxygen concentration exceeds 35 %, the NOx formation rate tends to stabilize, consistent with experimental results. By combining experimental investigation with chemical kinetic simulations, this study clarifies the self-sustaining combustion mechanism and energy conversion behavior of a gas–solid coupled system under complex oxygen-enriched atmospheres. The findings provide a theoretical basis for the efficient utilization of ultra-low concentration methane and the development of oxygen-enriched thermal conversion technologies for coal-derived solid waste. These findings have important implications for greenhouse gas mitigation and the achievement of carbon neutrality targets. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Assessing and refining user stories using large language models: a replication study in a real-world organizational software-development setting
Abstract: Specifying and maintaining high-quality user stories is challenging because project contexts evolve, natural-language artifacts are ambiguous, and manual assessment requires substantial effort. The INVEST criteria provide a structured framework for evaluating whether user stories are Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, and Testable. This study examines run-to-run variability and model–expert alignment through a two-phase design. The first phase comprised a dependent replication in which 60 original Spanish-language user stories were evaluated by three experts, GPT-5.1 Thinking (ChatGPT interface), and GPT-5.1 (API-based). The second phase extended the design through structured refinement of the original stories followed by reevaluation of the refined versions under the same Likert (1–5) scale and INVEST rubric. Results were criterion- and execution-condition-specific. Evaluator-related differences in the initial evaluation were detected in a limited subset of comparisons. Across all criterion–condition combinations, paired analyses generally indicated smaller absolute expert–model discrepancies after refinement and reevaluation, although magnitudes were heterogeneous and zero changes were frequent. In the initial evaluation, model ratings more often fell below the expert median when ratings differed; this pattern persisted less uniformly after refinement. Agreement for the average of the three expert ratings was high under ICC(2,3), while ordinal agreement varied by criterion in one refined condition. Overall, the findings are consistent with a potential complementary role for large language models in INVEST-based evaluation and structured refinement, but they do not establish causal improvement, model superiority, or equivalence with expert judgment. However, human oversight remains essential for contextual validation, interpretation, and backlog prioritization. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: An M.; Sun Y.; Peng X.; Jie C.; Yang J.; Li F.; Zhang J.; Li H.
Title: Removal of elemental mercury from flue gas by biochar from copper enriched calamus and life cycle assessment
Abstract: In this study, copper (Cu)-contaminated phytoremediation biomass of Acorus calamus was utilized as a feedstock to prepare Acorus-derived biochar containing Cu active sites (Cu-SBC) for the removal of elemental mercury (Hg0) from flue gas. The results showed that Cu-SBC pyrolyzed at 500 °C (Cu-SBC500) exhibited favorable Hg0 removal performance at a reaction temperature of 100 °C, achieving a removal efficiency of approximately 99%. It was revealed that the captured mercury species on the Cu-SBC500 surface mainly existed in the forms of HgS and HgO. Cu-SBC500 possessed a relatively large specific surface area, abundant short-chain sulfur species, and highly dispersed Cu species. During Hg0 removal, short-chain sulfur species and Cu2+ sites played key roles in mercury capture. Flue gas components also influenced the mercury removal performance: SO2 exhibited a slight inhibitory effect on Hg0 capture by Cu-SBC500, whereas NO showed a slight promotional effect. Furthermore, the environmental impacts of Cu-SBC500 were quantified using the eFootprint platform across multiple impact categories, and life cycle cost analysis estimated the production cost of Cu-SBC500 to be approximately 4.51 CNY kg−1. Compared with other materials, Cu-SBC500 features a simple preparation process, low production cost, and relatively low environmental impact. This work provides a promising pathway for the resource utilization of phytoremediation biomass and offers new insights into mercury emission control in coal-fired power plants. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Duan L.; Wang K.; Tang J.
Title: Positive–negative complementarity disambiguation with semantic–visual calibration for partial label learning
Abstract: Partial label learning (PLL) is an important weakly supervised paradigm where each candidate label set contains exactly one ground-truth label, with all other labels being noise. Although existing deep PLL methods achieve competitive performance, they primarily focus on increasing the probability of the ground-truth label without explicitly suppressing candidate noisy labels, which results in inefficient disambiguation and elevated sensitivity to label noise. To tackle this issue, we propose a Positive–Negative Complementarity Disambiguation with Semantic–Visual Calibration (PNCS) method for robust label disambiguation. First, we design a positive–negative complementary learning strategy that simultaneously increases the probability of the true label and suppresses spurious labels, enabling accurate label identification. Furthermore, we provide a gradient-based analysis to validate and interpret its effectiveness. Second, to enhance fine-grained discriminability, we introduce an adaptive margin calibration loss that progressively distinguishes between candidate and non-candidate labels based on semantic–visual representations. In addition, we design a dual consistency regularization term to further improve the model's robustness against noisy labels. Finally, we derive a theoretical upper bound on the generalization error of PNCS, thus providing a formal guarantee for its robustness and transferability to unseen data. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets validate the effectiveness of PNCS. The code will be released at: https://github.com/JY-LY/PNCS. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Electrocatalytic depolymerization and valorization of lignin in a Dual-Acid deep eutectic solvent over a Corrosion-Resistant RuO2-SnO2/Ti heterojunction
Abstract: Acidic deep eutectic solvents combined with electrocatalysis enables green and efficient lignin depolymerization into value-added chemicals through hydrogen-bond activation and radical-mediated selective bond cleavage. In particular, the dual-acid DES composed of choline chloride, lactic acid, and acetic acid provides synergistic enhancement of both acidity and the hydrogen-bond network, thereby promoting lignin dissolution and facilitating more efficient bond cleavage during electrocatalytic depolymerization. However, conventional metal electrodes often suffer from severe electrochemical corrosion in dual-acid DES systems, which limits their practical application. Here, we design a corrosion-resistant RuO2-SnO2/Ti heterojunction catalyst for electrocatalytic oxidation of lignin in a choline chloride-lactic-acetic acid DES. Using 4-benzyloxyphenol as a model compound, the catalyst achieved 97 % conversion and a 22 % benzoquinone yield within 3 h at 5 mA cm−2. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that selective C-O bond cleavage occurs on the heterojunction surface, elucidating the reaction pathway. When applied to alkali-extracted lignin , the system produced valuable aromatic aldehydes, including syringaldehyde (0.82 wt%) and vanillin (2.37 wt%). The generated aromatic products also show potential as renewable fuel-related chemicals and fuel precursors, further highlighting the relevance of this strategy to sustainable energy and biomass valorization. This work demonstrates a sustainable and efficient strategy for lignin valorization in electro-catalytic double-acidic DES media through the development of durable electrocatalysts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Synergistic oxidative conversion of methane and carbon over V2O5 toward C1 and C2 oxygenates
Abstract: Efficient utilization of fossil energies into value-added chemicals is highly desirable for sustainable fossil energy conversion. Herein, we report a synergistic conversion of CH4 and activated carbon (AC) catalyzed by V2O5 in aqueous media, enabling the simultaneous utilization of gaseous and solid carbon resources. Additionally, various raw coals could also serve as carbon source with even higher activity. Mechanism investigations revealed that V4+ species were generated by AC-assisted reduction of V2O5, and H/D exchange experiments further confirmed that the reduced V site facilitated C–H bond activation. Hydroxyl radical (·OH) was identified as the reactive oxygen species. AC served not only as a co-reductant to promote catalyst reduction but also as a carbon source for oxygenate formation. Isotopic labeling experiments further showed that CH3OH was primarily derived from reaction of CH4 with O2, while HCOOH, CH3CHO, and CH3COOH were derived from reaction of AC with H2O. CO and CO2 were derived from AC rather than CH4. Title: Coupling wide-size fuel high-temperature activation with load-adaptive staging for CFB flexible combustion
Abstract: Deep peak shaving in circulating fluidized-bed (CFB) boilers is constrained by interacting losses in thermal uniformity, burnout, and NOx control at low load. We tested a 65-kW system coupling an activation-modification device (AMD) to a CFB, with fixed AMD output supplying 10 % of rated thermal input. However, injection at 2500 mm gave the lowest temperature dispersion at both loads. Dual injection at 1500 + 2500 mm maintained stable 20 % operation with 11.99 % fly-ash carbon, whereas 1500 + 3500 mm was unstable. At 20 % load, a 30 % secondary-air ratio through S3 reduced NOx from 478.48 to 139.64 mg·m−3 at 6 vol% O2. All tested multi-level cases at that ratio produced higher emissions. It was obtained using a 20 % secondary-air ratio split equally between S2 and S3 and was 80.51 % below baseline. Title: Flow effects on laser-induced ignition of ammonia-hydrogen mixtures: minimum ignition energy and third-lobed flame kernel dynamics
Abstract: Laser-induced ignition experiments were conducted on ammonia-hydrogen mixtures under different flow velocities using an advective flow ignition platform. The effects of flow velocity and Lewis number (Le) on ignition probability, minimum ignition energy (MIE), flame kernel morphology, and flame development were investigated. The results show that, for mixtures with Le ' 1, the MIE exhibits a non-monotonic variation with increasing flow velocity, decreasing first and then increasing as the flow evolves from the low Reynolds number to the high Reynolds number regime. This indicates that flow facilitated ignition (FFI) behavior can occur in laser-induced ignition even for Le ' 1 mixtures. Mechanism analysis shows that, in the low Reynolds number regime, ignition is mainly governed by the positive and negative curvature regions induced by the characteristic third-lobed flame kernel generated during laser ignition. As the flow velocity increases, flame surface wrinkling, vortical deformation, and flame kernel fragmentation become increasingly important, while flow enhanced heat loss becomes dominant in the high Reynolds number regime and leads to a rapid increase in MIE. The early and later stage flame development results further show that moderate flow promotes flame kernel growth by increasing the projected flame area and supporting third lobe development, whereas excessive flow destabilizes the third-lobed flame kernel and weakens its ignition promoting effect. In addition, asymmetric third lobe development reduces favorable curvature effects for Le ' 1 mixtures and may split the main flame kernel for Le ' 1 mixtures, increasing the risk of quenching before a self-sustaining flame is established. These findings clarify the competing promoting and inhibiting effects of flow on laser-induced ignition of ammonia-hydrogen mixtures and provide guidance for optimizing laser ignition under practical flowing conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Multi-criteria kinetic modeling of kerogen hydrothermal conversion: assessing network complexity and model selection
Abstract: The kerogen-rich oil shale deposits constitute a strategically vital unconventional resource base. However, suitable kinetic studies that represent the reactions for developing appropriate technologies are scarce. This study systematically evaluates the predictive accuracy of kinetic models for kerogen conversion under hydrothermal conditions through the interplay among reaction network complexity, objective function selection, and stoichiometric constraints. These simulation choices, while often treated independently, have a cumulative impact on model fidelity. By benchmarking a three-pathway parallel reaction scheme against a single global reaction model across both catalytic (nickel tallate) and thermal systems, the investigation reveals that considering the complexity of kerogen reduces prediction errors by 16–45%. It also highlights a key choice between two optimization methods: average absolute error focuses on overall accuracy, while the sum of squared errors emphasizes precision for the most significant components. Lastly, the study emphasizes the importance of adhering to stoichiometric constraints to ensure physical consistency and prevent overfitting. Title: A review on chalcogenide-polymer based flexible thermoelectrics for power generation
Abstract: Flexible thermoelectric (TE) materials and devices are attracting growing interest because they are lightweight, bendable, and well-suited for power generation from low-temperature waste heat. Over the past few decades, researchers have made significant progress in improving the efficiency of flexible TE materials through advances in material synthesis, device design, and generator integration. The demand for eco-friendly, stable, and compact long-lasting power sources is also driving interest in flexible TE technology, especially for integrated electronics. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent developments in chalcogenides-polymers such as PANI, PVDF, Nylon and PEDOT:PSS based on their fabrication methods, TE properties and real-time applications. It has summarized the most important processing routes keeping an eye on its reproducibility and room-temperature TE properties enhancement. In addition, the review highlights applications of flexible TEs in textiles, wearable electronics, biomedical implants, low-grade waste heat recovery, sensors, and health monitoring. Overall, this work aims to outline current challenges, identify promising directions, and guide researchers in selecting potential chalcogenide-polymer based flexible materials and the appropriate processing route to advance flexible TE technology. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Zhou A.; Zhao Y.; Zhang X.; Wu S.; Liang H.; Liu H.; Deng S.; Zhang J.; Guo X.
Title: Decoupling the effects of spatial acid distribution and pore architecture of MFI core@shell zeolites toward benzene-methanol alkylation
Abstract: Benzene alkylation with methanol over ZSM-5 zeolite catalysts is a promising route for toluene and xylene production. However, rapid catalyst deactivation and unsatisfactory target product selectivity remain major drawbacks originating from uncontrolled spatial distribution of acid sites and severe mass transfer limitations. Herein, a series of MFI-type core@shell catalysts (ZSM-5@S-1 and S-1@ZSM-5) were constructed to decouple the effects of acid site distribution and pore architecture. By varying the type and calcination state of the core, we precisely prepared catalysts with tailored acid gradients (Al-rich core vs . Al-rich shell) and distinct pore textures (microporous vs. hierarchical/hollow structures). Comprehensive analysis reveals that the synergy of an inert S-1 shell and hierarchical porosity boosts catalytic activity, target aromatic selectivity, and anti-coking capacity. The inert S-1 shell eliminates surface coke-forming centers and improves surface hydrophobicity, whereas mesopores accelerate the diffusion of bulky aromatics, enhance the accessibility of internal acid sites, and expand the coke accommodation capacity of the catalyst. This work provides a universal structural design strategy for high-performance zeolite alkylation catalysts. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Effects of ambient temperature on flame propagation characteristics of methanol spray-hydrogen explosions
Abstract: Methanol-hydrogen fuel forms explosive spray droplet clouds during storage and transport. Therefore, understanding the propagation characteristics of spray flames is crucial for safe application. This study systematically investigates the impact of ambient temperature, methanol concentration, and hydrogen addition on flame propagation characteristics and reaction kinetics. A spray combustion model was developed and validated against experimental data. The results indicated that hydrogen addition played a dominant role in the variations of flame structure and explosion intensity. Compared with pure methanol spray combustion, the flame with 10.0 % hydrogen addition exhibited a smooth and symmetric structure, resembling that of a premixed gas‑phase flame. Its average propagation speed reached 3.04 times that of the pure methanol case, and the explosion index increased by 223.38 %. Ambient temperature had a non‑monotonic effect on flame propagation. At excessively high temperatures, the evaporative cooling of methanol suppressed combustion. Chemical kinetic analysis showed that the H-abstraction pathways R84 and R85 dominated methanol consumption, while R1 and R30 had the strongest inhibitory effect on flame temperature. This paper clarifies the combined effects of ambient temperature and hydrogen addition on methanol spray explosions, providing a theoretical basis for the safe storage and risk management of blended fuels. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Experimental investigation and theoretical modeling of gas expansion energy during coal and gas outburst based on multi-source emission
Abstract: Coal and gas outbursts are severe dynamic disasters in underground mining, primarily driven by gas expansion energy. However, accurately quantifying this energy remains challenging due to the complex, instantaneous, and multi-source nature of gas emissions. This study proposes a novel theoretical model to evaluate gas expansion energy by decoupling the participating gas into three sources: free gas in the outburst coal, rapidly desorbed gas from pulverized coal, and gas effused from the outburst cavity wall. An equivalent gas desorption particle size model was derived by integrating fractal size distribution with fractional decay diffusion kinetics, while the cavity wall gas emission was quantified using a fluid–solid coupled numerical approach. The theoretical framework was validated through a self-developed large-scale three-dimensional physical simulation experiment and historical field cases, yielding relative errors of only 6.53% and less than 10%, respectively. Furthermore, an iterative reverse-estimation model based on energy balance was established to back-calculate the actual gas pressure at the moment of outburst. Crucially, energy evolution analysis at varying mining depths (down to 1108 m) revealed a transition in the dominant triggering factors. In deep mining, the contribution of elastic strain energy sharply increases to 35.07%, transitioning the disaster mechanism from a “gas-dominated” to a “stress-gas coupling-dominated” type and dynamically lowering the critical gas pressure required for initiation. These findings demonstrate that traditional static gas thresholds are inadequate for deep mines, highlighting the urgent need for a coupled stress-gas evaluation system and a strategic shift toward active in-seam pressure relief. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Bai B.; Yu X.; Fu C.; Song H.; Nie Q.; Jin H.
Title: Synergistic degradation of waste agricultural plastic film in supercritical water-CO2 mixed fluid with high CO2 concentration: Gasification characteristics and reaction pathways
Abstract: To mitigate environmental pollution from waste plastic mulch films and improve their resource utilization efficiency, this work proposes an efficient recycling strategy via supercritical mixed fluid gasification composed of supercritical water (SCW) and a high concentration of supercritical CO2 (SCCO2) at a level comparable to water. The effects of gasification temperature, residence time, and mixed fluid ratio on gasification performance are systematically investigated. The results show that elevated temperature significantly improves gasification efficiency. At 700 °C, the carbon and hydrogen conversion efficiencies reach 65.28% and 91.08%, respectively, which are approximately 1.76 and 1.59 times those in pure supercritical water, since high temperature promotes complete cracking of long-chain alkanes. The optimal gasification performance is achieved at a SCW-SCCO2 ratio of 2:1, with a faster reaction rate than the single SCW system. Extending residence time facilitates complete PE depolymerization and deep conversion of light hydrocarbons and active intermediates via secondary cracking and reforming reactions. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations reveal that increasing temperature and CO2 concentration accelerate PE fragment migration and increase the diffusion coefficient. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further elucidate that CO2 introduction provides additional carboxylation pathways, promotes the formation of formic and acetic acid intermediates, and facilitates the generation of H2 and CO small-molecule gases. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Lu J.; Gao W.; Huang Q.; Du L.; Li H.; Hu X.; Wang C.; Zhao Y.; Yu J.; Tang K.
Title: Online chiral derivatization coupled with CE-MS for baseline separation of 16 proteinogenic amino acid enantiomers
Abstract: Amino acid (AA) enantiomers influence protein function through their distinct spatial structures, making their precise separation essential for elucidating physiological and pathological pathways. In this work, a novel method for the efficient separation of AA enantiomers based on on-line chiral derivatization with (S)-N-(4-nitrophenoxycarbonyl) phenylalanine methoxyethyl ester ((S)-NIFE) coupled with CE-MS has been developed. The method utilizes the ultrafast reaction kinetics of (S)-NIFE with AA enantiomers to facilitate their efficient separation. The online strategy eliminates time-consuming offline derivatization by permitting immediate injection upon simple mixing of derivatization reagent with AA enantiomers, enabling a streamlined analytical workflow. By optimizing experimental parameters, baseline separation of 16 chiral proteinogenic AA enantiomers has been achieved with resolutions ranging from 1.5 to 11.03. The relative standard deviations of migration time and peak area for intraday and interday measurements are less than 5%, and the limits of detection (LOD) and quantification (LOQ) are as low as 40 nM and 80 nM, respectively. Furthermore, the method was further applied to comparative analyses of AA enantiomers in serum samples from healthy controls and patients with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease and atrial fibrillation. The baseline separation of three AA enantiomers was consistently achieved. The LODs and LOQs for three ᴅ-AAs in complex matrix were as low as 180 nM and 600 nM. The intraday and interday precisions were both below 11%, and the average recoveries range from 87.60% to 95.51% with low standard deviations. All these results confirm the effectiveness of the approach in separating AA enantiomers in complex matrices. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Beyond surface reconstruction: a critical review and unified mechanistic framework for dynamic self-activation across electrocatalytic energy conversion reactions
Abstract: A growing body of work shows that the true catalyst often forms and reshapes itself under operating conditions. This phenomenon, where a material transforms to become more active, selective, or stable, can be called “self-activation” or “dynamic surface reconstruction.” The surface that forms during the oxygen evolution reaction is described in one language. The restructuring of a copper catalyst during carbon dioxide reduction is described in another. A common conceptual framework is missing. This separation hides the universal design rules that nature is showing us. In this comprehensive review, we survey the landscape across five major reactions, HER, OER, ORR, CO2RR, and NRR (with the self-activation literature dominated by NO3RR), and demonstrate that a common thread of dynamic self-activation runs through them all. From these insights, we extract a set of general design strategies for what we term “proactive catalyst engineering,” designing starting materials programmed to transform into their optimal state under operating conditions. We also provide a comprehensive overview of the operando techniques and theoretical tools needed to capture and predict this dynamic behavior, including X-ray absorption spectroscopy, vibrational spectroscopies, electron microscopy, mass spectrometry, and advanced computational methods ranging from density functional theory to machine learning potentials. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd
