Authors: Wang Y.; Su J.; Lei B.; Huang X.; Sun T.; Li P.
Title: Stress degradation modeling and reliability analysis of flight-vehicle folding wings based on Tweedie exponential dispersion process
Abstract: Folding wings of a flight vehicle may experience progressive surface-stress accumulation under normal tensile loading, leading to failure once a critical threshold is exceeded. To characterize this stochastic degradation and support safety assessment, this study proposes a displacement-based degradation modeling and reliability framework based on the Tweedie exponential dispersion (TED) process. Finite element analysis in ANSYS Workbench predicts the surface-stress response and guide strain-gauge placement. Normal tensile tests are conducted on deployed folding wings to obtain surface-stress degradation data, which are modeled using the TED process. Since the TED increment density has no closed form, a saddle point approximation with a dual-branch reparameterization strategy is introduced to enable robust maximum likelihood estimation. Reliability is evaluated using a hybrid scheme that combines fine displacement-grid Monte Carlo simulation with a Birnbaum–Saunders (BS) representation to estimate the first-hitting displacement distribution and reliability. Results show that the TED model achieves higher fitting accuracy than the Gamma-process benchmark, while the MC–BS method provides more conservative reliability predictions. The proposed framework offers a practical and physically interpretable tool for reliability assessment of folding wings and related deployable aerospace structures under tensile loading. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Title: Preparation of silicon tetrachloride from fly ash by chlorination-volatilization and recovery of phosphorus from water using fly ash and chlorinated residue
Abstract: Converting silicon (Si) and aluminum (Al) compounds into valuable resources is essential for promoting the sustainable utilization of fly ash from coal- and biomass-fueled power plants. Transforming Si and Al into volatile chlorides enables their application as high-value raw materials for fumed silica and catalysts. While heating pure Si and Al oxides with solid carbon in chlorine gas yields SiCl4 and AlCl3, complex minerals in fly ash, such as quartz and mullite, exhibit distinct reactivities. This study investigated the effects of reaction temperature and time on Si and Al release by treating bituminous coal fly ash mixed with solid carbon under chlorine gas flow. Significant Si and Al volatilization occurred at 1000 °C, yielding high recovery proportions of 83 % for Al and 99 % for Si in the gas cooling and condensation zones. Additionally, calcium-rich fly ashes derived from sub-bituminous coal and woody biomass were evaluated as phosphate recovery materials. The volatilization of Si and Al elevated Ca concentrations in the residue up to 29.8 % and 38.7 % as CaO, respectively, thereby enhancing overall phosphate capture capacities. The resulting chlorinated residues achieved efficient removal performance with high equilibrium capture capacities (q e = 36.2 and 42.4 mg-P/g for sub-bituminous coal and woody biomass ash residues, respectively). Mechanistically, structural and extraction analyses confirm that calcium compounds in the residues immobilize phosphate primarily as CaHPO4 via a coupled surface adsorption and localized precipitation process. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Transient mixed thermoelastohydrodynamic lubrication-wear-cavitation interaction characteristics at the textured slipper/swashplate interface of aviation fuel piston pumps
Abstract: Laser surface texturing (LST) has attracted attention as an active method for regulating tribological performance. Although LST improves the lubrication performance and suppresses wear at the slipper/swashplate interface of aviation fuel piston pumps, it induces cavitation. To investigate the influence laws of LST on interfacial lubrication and wear characteristics under the fluid–solid-thermal-cavitation interaction, this study extends the transient mixed thermoelastohydrodynamic lubrication and wear coupled model by incorporating spherical textured dimples, Gaussian surface roughness, and mass-conserving cavitation effects. The Fischer–Burmeister–Newton with a Single Unknown algorithm, combined with a semi-coarsening multigrid technique, is employed to solve the average Reynolds equation containing the cavity fraction and roughness factors, the Fischer–Burmeister equation, the energy equation, and the heat conduction equation. This constructs a transient mixed thermoelastohydrodynamic lubrication-wear-cavitation coupled model. The model captures the cavitation induced by the diverging wedges of the spherical textured dimples, with a maximum cavity fraction of 0.52. Furthermore, the local micro-hydrodynamic effects (7.68–14.64 MPa) generated by the converging wedges elevate the interface to a full-film lubrication state (2.11–5.72 μm). This eliminates asperity contact wear, achieves a temperature reduction of 96.65 °C, and reduces the friction coefficient and energy dissipation by 0.05 and 679.19 W, respectively. Comprehensive analysis indicates that the spherical texture configuration comprising dimples with a radius of 150μm and a depth of 6μm, with 64 dimples uniformly distributed in the circumferential direction and positioned radially at 8.3, 8.8, and 9.3 mm, exhibits the best overall tribological performance among the configurations investigated in this study. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: VLKD-YOLO: A semantic-aware visual-language distillation framework for lightweight underwater object detection
Abstract: Underwater object detection can facilitate marine exploration and conservation by enabling accurate identification. However, color distortion and low contrast in underwater images pose significant challenges to accurate object recognition. Moreover, the limited computational capacity of underwater detection devices hinders the practical deployment. In this paper, we present a Visual-Language Knowledge Distillation (VLKD) method to address the trade-off between detection accuracy and efficiency. Specifically, to enhance model adaptability for underwater imagery, we propose a Cross-Modal Text Alignment (CMTA) module that integrates textual data to improve the semantic comprehension ability of the model. Additionally, we design the Visual Lateral Inhibition Knowledge Distillation (VLIKD) module, which guides student models to focus on critical learning regions, thereby minimizing model parameters while maximizing detection accuracy. Evaluations on the DUO and RUOD datasets demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance on underwater object detection accuracy benchmarks. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Qiu X.; Fan D.; Huang Y.; Chen Y.; Wei L.
Title: Hierarchical prototype-based domain priors for multiple instance learning in multimodal histopathology analysis
Abstract: Digital pathology has fundamentally altered diagnostic workflows by enabling the computational analysis of gigapixel Whole Slide Images (WSIs), yet effectively deciphering their complex tumor microenvironments remains a formidable challenge. Existing Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) frameworks typically treat Whole Slide Images as unstructured bags of patches, discarding critical morphological semantics and spatial geometry. This lack of inductive bias often leads to overfitting on background noise and fails to align visual features with high-level diagnostic knowledge. To overcome these limitations, we propose the Hierarchical Prototype-based Domain Priors (HPDP) framework, a unified multimodal approach applicable to diagnostic and prognostic tasks in histopathology. HPDP enhances conventional MIL models by introducing a Morphologically Anchored Prototype System (MAPS), which uses reference centroids derived from clustering training patch features to regularize learnable Prior Experts, together with a Sinusoidal Positional Encoder (SPE) to incorporate two-dimensional absolute positional information. Furthermore, a Hierarchical Cross-Modal Alignment (HCMA) module incorporates Large Language Model (LLM)-generated auxiliary descriptions to modulate visual representations. Experiments across seven cancer cohorts demonstrate competitive classification and survival prediction performance, with the highest mean classification metrics among the evaluated methods and cohort-dependent performance in survival analysis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Aluminum-modified lignin-derived sulfonated hydrochar for the conversion of levoglucosan to 5-hydroxymethylfurfural in a biphasic system
Abstract: Levoglucosan (LG), a major anhydrosugar in cellulose-derived pyrolysis oil, is a promising feedstock for the production of value-added chemicals. Herein, an aluminum-modified lignin-derived sulfonated carbon solid acid (LCSA98-Al) was developed for the one-pot conversion of LG to 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) in a NaCl-H2O/THF biphasic system. Under the optimized conditions, an HMF yield of 65.9% was achieved at complete LG conversion. Physicochemical characterization revealed an amorphous carbon framework bearing sulfonic acid groups and highly dispersed Al species. 27Al MAS NMR showed that Al existed predominantly in a hexacoordinate environment. Recycling tests showed that LG conversion remained above 97% over five recycles, although the HMF yield gradually decreased. Positive-ion ESI-MS combined with D2O isotopic labeling suggested that water-derived protons participate mainly in LG hydrolysis and subsequent proton-transfer processes, whereas little solvent-derived deuterium is retained in HMF after dehydration and furan-ring formation. This work presents a lignin-derived bifunctional catalytic strategy for the sustainable conversion of pyrolysis-derived LG into a key platform precursor for biofuel and bioplastic production. Title: Texture-preserving Caputo fractional-order telegraph diffusion model for SAR and ultrasound image despeckling
Abstract: Multiplicative speckle noise is a major challenge in coherent imaging modalities such as synthetic aperture radar (SAR) and ultrasound imaging, where effective noise suppression must be achieved without compromising structural and textural details. In this work, we propose a texture-preserving Caputo fractional-order telegraph diffusion model for image despeckling. The proposed formulation incorporates a Caputo time-fractional derivative into a nonlinear telegraph diffusion framework, combining nonlocal temporal memory effects with wave-like propagation behavior. The resulting fractional dynamics provide enhanced control of the diffusion process while reducing numerical dissipation compared with classical integer-order models. Furthermore, the telegraph diffusion mechanism preserves oscillatory structures and high-frequency image features, mitigating the excessive smoothing commonly encountered in standard parabolic diffusion approaches. We establish a maximum-principle property that guarantees the solution remains bounded by the initial image data and develop a semi-implicit finite difference scheme based on the Caputo L1 approximation, which is proved to be unconditionally stable. Extensive experiments on natural, texture, SAR, MRI and ultrasound images demonstrate that the proposed method effectively suppresses multiplicative speckle noise while preserving important image features. Quantitative and visual comparisons show that the proposed approach reliably outperforms several classical PDE-based methods and relevant recent despeckling approaches. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Authors: Zhen J.; Xiaofan H.E.; Hongna D.; Ting Z.; Yu L.
Title: Fatigue life analysis under random load spectra based on the relative miner rule and a load spectrum shape factor correction
Abstract: Random load spectra associated with complex aircraft missions exhibit nonlinear interactions between high-low loads. The lack of effective fatigue damage models capable of capturing these interactions results in inaccurate fatigue life predictions, with serious implications for aircraft operational safety and economic efficiency. Fatigue life predictions based on the relative Miner rule may still exhibit considerable errors when the load spectra differ in shape. Therefore, a damage-equivalent load spectrum shape factor (SSF D ) is employed to characterize the differences among load spectra and further correct the predicted fatigue life. First, a fatigue life analysis method is established using the Smith-Watson-Topper (SWT) equivalent-damage conversion relationship and the relative Miner rule. whereby the fatigue life under a target random load spectrum is estimated from the experimental life under a reference spectrum using the ratio of their calculated damage sums. Next, SSF D is adopted to quantify spectrum similarity. A second calibration spectrum is used to construct the relationship between the life calculated error E and SSF D , while the other spectra are reserved for independent validation. A “calculated life-similarity characterization-error correction” fatigue life correction framework is then developed, and the calculated life is corrected using the E - SSF D relationship. Finally, the method is experimentally validated using open-hole flat-plate specimens of 7050-T7451 aluminum alloy subjected to five random load spectra. The results show that the proposed correction method provides substantially higher accuracy than conventional fatigue analysis methods, with fatigue life prediction errors within 10%. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Bismuth-stabilized perovskites with water-boosted fluorescence for accurate quantification of high-concentration chloride in wastewater
Abstract: The rapid anion exchange between chloride (Cl−) and bromide (Br−), accompanied by remarkable photoluminescence (PL) shifts, enables CsPbBr3 perovskites to exhibit excellent selectivity for Cl− detection. However, CsPbBr3 nanocrystals stabilized by organic ligands usually exhibit limited applicability for Cl− detection in water, because the hydrophobic ligands prevent direct contact with aqueous Cl− and restrict interfacial ion-exchange kinetics. Ligand-free CsPbBr3-based perovskites synthesized by solid-state methods generally suffer from poor stability in aqueous environments and weak fluorescence, arising from their intrinsic ionic nature, abundant defect states, and large grain size, which severely limit their application in fluorescence sensing. Herein, metallic bismuth (Bi) with strong affinity toward Cl− was introduced to form composites with ligand-free CsPbBr3/Cs4PbBr6 perovskites, constructing multi-branched CsPbBr3/Cs4PbBr6/Bi composites (CPB-Bi) for Cl− detection in ethanol-water environments. The incorporation of Bi provides a robust structural framework and interfacial protection, significantly improving the stability of perovskite components in polar solvent environments. Additionally, the amount of water in ethanol induces partial reconstruction of Cs4PbBr6 into CsPbBr3 nanocrystals and passivates surface defects, resulting in enhanced radiative recombination and greatly improved PL intensity. Owing to the rapid reaction between the nanosized perovskite materials and chloride ions, the detection time was significantly reduced to 10 min. Based on the Cl−/Br− anion exchange mechanism, a linear relationship between PL peak positions and Cl− concentrations was established. The optimized CPB-Bi10 (10 mmol Bi) sensor achieved a chloride detection accuracy of 95.65% in wastewater samples at Cl− concentrations up to 10,000 ppm. The sensor exhibits outstanding sensitivity, high selectivity, and robust anti-interference capability, offering a facile strategy for designing ligand-free perovskite-based fluorescent sensors for environmental ion monitoring. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Alkali lignin/plastic composite-derived catalysts for ball-milling-assisted transesterification with enhanced performance and kinetic insights
Abstract: A series of K2CO3-loaded heterogeneous solid base catalysts (designated K2CO3/AL-P) were developed via co-pyrolysis of waste alkali lignin and plastics, used as carriers. Among the catalysts synthesised, the polypropylene (PP)-derived variant (K2CO3/AL-PP) showed improved performance in a ball-milling-assisted transesterification reaction, achieving a 100% fatty acid methyl ester (FAME) yield, as determined by the GC internal standard method within 30 min. Characterization techniques revealed that the unique interaction between PP and lignin facilitated the formation of a carbon matrix with tailored porosity and abundant defects, which promoted the dispersion and stabilization of potassium species derived from the K2CO3 precursor. DFT calculations further confirmed that the defective carbon support enhanced methanol adsorption on the potassium species (from −0.371 eV on K2CO3/AL to −0.685 eV on K2CO3/AL-PP). Further kinetic analysis revealed the decisive influence of the energy input method on the reaction mechanism. Although the apparent activation energies were comparable (74.56 kJ/mol for ball milling versus 71.87 kJ/mol for magnetic stirring), the reaction kinetics diverged significantly: the process followed apparent second-order kinetics under ball-milling conditions, in contrast to the pseudo-first-order kinetics observed with magnetic stirring. This divergence suggests that mechanochemical force, potentially through synchronous multi-bond cleavage or by mitigating steric hindrance, alters the rate-determining step. The findings of this study provide new insights into the valorization of waste materials and the efficient synthesis of biodiesel. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Liu W.; Qiu Z.; Liang M.; Yu Y.; Zhang Q.; Kong W.; Qu T.; Zhang K.
Title: Effect of pyrite on shale fracture development under triaxial compression revealed by micro-CT technology
Abstract: This study investigates the impact of pyrite grains and veins on the mechanical properties and fracture characteristics of shale through triaxial compression tests combined with X-ray computed tomography (CT). Shale samples with diverse pyrite content and occurrence forms were collected from the Lower Silurian Longmaxi shales, analyzed to reveal the coupling effect of pyrite on shale mechanical behavior and fracture evolution; these samples cover three pyrite occurrence types (pyrite-absent, nodular, veined) and span a wide content gradient. Integrated triaxial compression tests and high-resolution X-ray CT were employed to quantify key mechanical parameters, including triaxial compressive strength (TCS), Young’s modulus (E), and Poisson’s ratio (ν), as well as to characterize the initiation, propagation, and connectivity of fractures. Results demonstrate that pyrite occurrence type and content induce variations in shale mechanical properties; stress–strain curve analysis reveals that TCS decreases from 145.22 MPa (pyrite-absent shale to a minimum of 109.72 MPa (shale with veined pyrite) due to stress concentration at pyrite-matrix interfaces. X-ray CT imaging further reveals distinct fracture evolution mechanisms: pyrite-absent or low-pyrite-content shale (0.12 %) develops single shear fractures due to uniform deformation of the shale matrix; shale with high pyrite content (8.3 %) and scattered nodular pyrite exhibits stress concentration at pyrite-matrix interfaces, which guides crack bifurcation and the formation of complex fracture networks; shale with pyrite veins forms a continuous rigid network that blocks crack extension, resulting in short fractures with limited connectivity. These findings enrich the understanding of pyrite’s dual regulatory role in shale mechanics and fracture development, offering critical insights for optimizing hydraulic fracturing operations in analogous pyrite-bearing shale reservoirs. Laboratory triaxial results provide mesoscopic reference, further hydro-mechanical coupling simulation is required for field-scale fracturing design. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Curvature-dependent contact-angle errors in a static phase-field lattice Boltzmann model
Abstract: In the present study, a static D2Q9 Cahn–Hilliard lattice Boltzmann benchmark has been developed to quantify equilibrium contact-angle and liquid-area errors on convex and concave circular boundaries. Intentionally, momentum transport is suppressed to isolate the compound effect of geometric wetting, ghost-node extension, curved-wall reconstruction, and normal-based angle measurement from the hydrodynamic influences. The bulk formulation reproduces the analytical hyperbolic-tangent profile; increasing the interface thickness from ξ=2 to 5 reduces the normalized L2 and maximum chemical-potential residuals by factors of 6.2 and 5.8 in sequence. For a planar wall, the contact angle is underpredicted by 0.4° at θset=30° and by 6.0° at θset=150°. In the concave cavity, 74 of 75 cases (98.7%) yield positive errors, with an estimated maximum hitting 21.8°; the only negative error is −2.0° at R/Δx=36, ξ=4, and θset=60°. For the convex cylinder, the 30° cases remain positively biased, with errors of approximately 8°–16° over the investigated parameter range, whereas intermediate and obtuse angles are predominantly underpredicted. The maximum relative liquid-area drift is 4.85×10−2 for the concave geometry and 1.8×10−2 for the convex geometry. Neither signed contact-angle error nor relative liquid-area drift collapses uniquely with the curvature Cahn number (Cn=ξ/R), demonstrating non-monotonic relationships of curvature sign, wall radius, interface thickness, and prescribed wettability. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Title: Electron beam-induced structural modification of SiO2/C anodes from biomass power plant waste
Abstract: SiO2/C anodes, derived from rice husk ash (RHA) waste generated during thermal and electrical energy production in biomass power plants, offer a sustainable solution for repurposing waste. RHA is abundant in Thailand. However, the crystalline structure of SiO2/C limits its reactivity with lithium due to strong Si–O covalent bonds, which restrict electrochemical reactivity. Electron-beam (e-beam) irradiation is a promising method for modifying the structure of such crystalline materials. This study investigates the impact of varying e-beam irradiation doses on the structural and electrochemical properties of RHA-derived SiO2/C material. While the overall long-range crystallinity and particle morphology remained largely unchanged, e-beam treatment was found to successfully introduce local structural disorder and distortion within inter-tetrahedral Si–O–Si bond angles without disrupting the fundamental SiO4 structure. Although overall crystallinity and particle size remained unchanged, irradiation was found to modify the SiO2/C structure by increasing local structural disorder and inducing changes in the Si–O–Si network while retaining the first-shell Si–O local coordination environment. Among the irradiated conditions, the SiO2/C-20 anode demonstrated a sustained capacity improvement of over 23% after 400 cycles compared to the pristine SiO2/C-0 sample. This work establishes a facile radiation-based approach for the structural modification of SiO2/C materials, which is associated with improved electrochemical performance for lithium-ion battery anodes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wang R.; Ma T.; Qin X.; Liu Q.; Cui Q.; Li L.
Title: Cation-π interaction engineering non-conjugated imidazole-based photodynamic antibacterial agents
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: π-Conjugation extension has long dominated the design of organic fluorescent materials, yet increases synthetic complexity and biotoxicity. We demonstrate cation-π interaction engineering as an alternative paradigm in which non-covalent cation-π contacts govern photophysical output. Two non-conjugated imidazole-based molecules including BTIM (methylene linker) and BTIMP (propylene linker) were facilely synthesized via one-step nucleophilic substitution. In water, both molecules can self-assemble into uniform nanoparticles via cation-π and hydrophobic interactions. Aggregation restricts non-radiative decay and promotes intersystem crossing, yielding aggregation-enhanced fluorescence with BTIM exhibiting five-fold higher emission than BTIMP. Under white light irradiation, both nanoparticles can efficiently generate •OH via a Type I pathway. Against Escherichia coli , BTIM achieves 97% photoactivated killing with IC50 of 5.3 μM, while BTIMP displays intrinsic dark antibacterial activity with IC50 of 4.2 μM due to its longer hydrophobic alkyl chain. This work establishes cation-π engineering as a platform in which a single non-covalent interaction simultaneously governs self-assembly, fluorescence emission, photodynamic behaviors, and biological function. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Isaabadi M.; Tahsini A.M.
Title: A dual-channel micro-combustor with isolated catalytic hydrogen combustion for efficient ammonia/hydrogen utilization
Abstract: To overcome the storage and safety challenges associated with hydrogen, ammonia has emerged as a practical carbon-free fuel for power systems. However, its sluggish kinetics and low reactivity hinder stable and efficient combustion. Although catalytic hydrogen combustion can effectively promote gas-phase ammonia oxidation through thermal and chemical coupling, the accumulation of nitrogen-containing surface intermediates can inhibit catalytic activity on noble-metal surfaces, limiting the effectiveness of direct catalytic ammonia combustion. To circumvent this limitation without increasing geometric complexity, a novel dual-channel planar micro-combustor is proposed, in which a fuel-lean hydrogen/air mixture undergoes catalytic combustion in an adjacent upper channel, while a fuel-rich ammonia/hydrogen/air mixture flows through the center channel without contacting the catalyst. Numerical simulations using a validated coupled hetero-homogeneous kinetic model reveal that the heat and reactive radicals generated in the catalytic channels enhance and support gas-phase flame anchoring within the downstream blending zone, where the two streams merge. Parametric investigations covering side-channel equivalence ratios of 0.35–0.55, center-channel equivalence ratios up to 7.5, blending ratios of 0.1–0.5, and center-channel inlet velocities of 1.7–2.5 m/s demonstrate that the proposed combustor can reproduce the thermal performance of a pure-hydrogen baseline (outlet temperature of 1457 K). Under the best-performing investigated condition (φ1=0.5,φ2=3.1,X=0.3), both ammonia conversion and combustion efficiency exceed 95 %, while the total hydrogen mass flow rate is reduced by 34.6 %. These findings demonstrate an effective strategy for minimizing hydrogen dependence by exploiting hetero-homogeneous coupling while completely avoiding direct ammonia catalyst interaction. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Thermal performance of a packed bed spherical alumina ball regenerative heat exchanger under varying porosity and mass flow rate
Abstract: Regenerative heat exchangers are extensively employed in industrial energy recovery systems for their ability to store and reutilise thermal energy, thereby enhancing overall process efficiency. Among various configurations, fixed-bed and packed-bed regenerators offer advantages including high surface-area-to-volume ratio, mechanical simplicity, and operational flexibility. Despite considerable research on metallic packing materials such as stainless steel and wire mesh, the use of alumina (Al2O3) spheres as heat storage media in fixed-bed regenerators remains relatively unexplored. In the present work, a compact fixed-bed regenerative heat exchanger with housing dimensions of 60 mm × 40 mm × 40 mm, packed with spherical alumina balls, is designed, fabricated, and experimentally investigated to evaluate its thermal and hydraulic performance under cyclic heating and cooling conditions. The bed porosity is systematically varied by employing three packing configurations — 6 mm spheres (ε = 0.62), 10 mm spheres (ε = 0.56), and a mixed arrangement of 6 mm and 10 mm spheres (ε = 0.52), and experiments are conducted at three air mass flow rates ranging from 0.0025 to 0.005 kg/s. The Nusselt number, thermal effectiveness, pressure drop, friction factor, and NTU are evaluated as functions of porosity and mass flow rate. Results show that the Nusselt number increases with Reynolds number and peaks at ε = 0.56, while effectiveness decreases with increasing mass flow rate due to reduced residence time. Experimental pressure drop values agree with Ergun equation predictions within 15–30%, and an empirical Nusselt number correlation is proposed. The findings confirm alumina balls as a viable, cost-effective alternative to metallic packings for fixed-bed regenerators. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Masson SAS.

Author full names: Kamboj, Varun (59560229800); Twinkle (60381956000); Kumar, Mukul (59204741100); Singh, Arun Kumar (56122757500); Sharma, Gyaneshwar (56160296900); Kumar, Sanjeev (57213856324)
Title: Thickness-modulated high electrostrain response in microwave-sintered lead-free piezoceramics
Abstract: The combination of advanced fabrication techniques and sub-millimeter geometrical scaling offers new possibilities for enhancing the functional response of ferroelectric ceramics. Here, we synthesize (Na0.5Bi0.485Eu0.015)0.94Ba0.06Ti1–1.5x(ZnSn0.5)xO3 (x = 0.01–0.03) ceramics via solid state technique. The synergistic effect of microwave-induced dense microstructure and high field operation enabled by thickness scaling induces pronounced polarization evolution, as confirmed by P–E loops and Arrott plot analysis. We achieve a high electrostrain ~0.74% leading to a high d33* ~741 pm/V at 99.89 kV/cm for the microwave sintered x = 0.02 ceramic. Compared to conventional processing, the microwave sintered samples exhibit notable enhancements, with electrostrain and d33* increasing by ~39% & ~11%, respectively. A simple yet effective synthesis strategy is presented, enabling high electrostrain for next generation functional materials, while highlighting the need for further optimization to reduce the required driving field. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Yan T.; Guo Q.; Mi J.-X.; Lai Z.; Li W.
Title: Tensorized specificity and consistency for latent multi-view subspace clustering
Abstract: Latent multi-view subspace clustering (LMVSC), which learns a shared latent representation from multi-view data, has achieved promising clustering results. However, existing LMVSC methods often neglect the unique characteristics inherent to each view and fail to explicitly capture high-order correlations across views due to their reliance on matrix representations. To overcome these limitations, we propose Tensorized Specificity and Consistency for LMVSC (TSCL-MVSC), a novel model designed to simultaneously learn both view-specific and consistent latent representations. This allows TSCL-MVSC to leverage the distinct information present in each view while maintaining a coherent understanding of the underlying data structure. TSCL-MVSC constructs specific and consistent self-representation matrices from the learned latent representations and forms a third-order tensor by stacking them. By imposing a low-rank constraint on this tensor, TSCL-MVSC effectively captures high-order correlations among views, a capability lacking in traditional matrix-based LMVSC methods, while promoting synergistic interactions between specificity and consistency. Furthermore, we develop an iterative algorithm to optimize the objective function of TSCL-MVSC. Experimental results on eight datasets demonstrate that TSCL-MVSC achieves superior or competitive clustering performance compared with fifteen state-of-the-art methods. The implementation for TSCL-MVSC is available at https://github.com/TH-Yan/TSCL-MVSC. © 2026

Authors: Zhou T.; Jiang J.; Li Y.; Zhan L.; Qi R.; Bai L.
Title: Semantic-guided data augmentation for self-supervised visual pattern learning: Leveraging foundation model priors
Abstract: Self-supervised visual representation learning depends critically on semantically meaningful data augmentations. However, current strategies either disrupt semantic structure through random transformations or suffer semantic drift when using generative models. We present Semantic Data Inflation (SDI), a framework that leverages pre-trained foundation models as “semantic oracles” to guide augmentations while preserving object identity. SDI extracts multi-scale semantic cues and employs an adaptive mechanism to dynamically select guidance granularity based on image characteristics. Experiments indicate that SDI improves over baseline and generative methods across multiple contrastive learning frameworks. On ImageNet-1k, SDI achieves 72.35% linear probe accuracy (+2.44% over baseline). On ImageNette, SDI reaches 95.75% accuracy, improving over standard (+3.88%) and generative (+3.65%) methods. Analysis indicates that SDI produces more discriminative features with improved semantic consistency, supporting an efficient approach for visual pattern recognition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Highly active Ni-Co catalyst on hybrid MWCNT-Graphene nanoplatelet catalysts for ammonia decomposition
Abstract: Ammonia decomposition offers a promising route for on-demand hydrogen production. However, the large-scale use of non-noble metal catalysts is limited by their low activity and poor stability at low temperatures. In this study, a series of monometallic Ni, Co and bimetallic Ni-Co catalysts supported on a hybrid multi-walled carbon nanotube-graphene nanoplatelet were synthesised via impregnation. This study examined how changes in the Ni-Co ratio affect the properties and performance of the catalysts. The catalysts were carefully analysed using XRD, N2 physisorption, CO chemisorption, H2-TPR, H2-TPD, N2-TPD, NH3-TPD, SEM, and TEM. They were then tested for NH3 decomposition at a weight hourly space velocity of 12,000 mL/gcat.h. The results showed that increasing Co content increased the surface area, metal dispersion, and reducibility, while lowering the adsorption and desorption energies for H2, N2, and NH3. The 2.5Ni-7.5Co catalyst had the highest surface area (166.8 m2/g), the best metal dispersion (8.39%), the smallest crystallite size (7.27 nm), and the lowest desorption temperatures and energies for H2, N2, and NH3. It reached 78% NH3 conversion at 500°C and 99% at 550°C, and remained stable for 24h. These findings show that the combination of Ni and Co, along with conductive carbon supports, is important for making efficient, long-lasting, non-noble-metal catalysts for low-temperature NH3 decomposition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Ren Z.; Liu H.; Ben G.; Hao Q.; Wang B.; Wang Y.
Author full names: Ren, Zhengqun (60624869700); Liu, Huan (57898551800); Ben, Guangli (57195509421); Hao, Qisheng (60625250300); Wang, Boxiao (59974485800); Wang, Yongcheng (56437944700)
Title: Visible–infrared remote sensing image fusion for object detection based on hybrid-level dual-input Mamba fusion
Abstract: Existing visible–infrared fusion detectors often struggle to balance cross modal complementarity, redundancy, and conflict. Most multimodal Mamba methods pre-fuse the two modalities before state space modeling, causing complementary and conflicting cues to be jointly encoded and obscuring their sources and reliability during state evolution. To address this issue, we propose hybrid-level dual-input Mamba fusion framework (HDMF) for UAV based vehicle detection. At the feature level, dual-branch SimAM–wavelet attention (DSWA) identifies regions with significant cross modal differences and performs complementary or modality specific enhancement to suppress noise amplification and spurious responses. Binary fusion Mamba (BFMamba) then treats visible, infrared, and explicit interaction features as independent inputs to the state equations, enabling cross modal fusion to directly guide hidden state evolution while modeling long range dependencies with linear complexity. At the decision level, the tri-branch aware decision fusion head (TDFH) combines illumination priors and cross branch consistency to fuse predictions from visible, infrared, and fused branches, mitigating residual modal mismatch and prediction inconsistency. HDMF achieves COCO style mAP@0.5:0.95 scores of 56.62%, 69.82%, and 48.11% on DroneVehicle, LLVIP, and FLIR, respectively. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Liu W.; Yang B.; Zhu Q.; Xiao R.; Huang S.; Li Q.
Title: CSG4Rec: Collaborative-similarity guided semantic IDs tokenization for generative sequential recommendation
Abstract: Sequential recommendation focuses on capturing users’ interests from their historical interaction sequences. Conventional sequential recommendation models use Numeric IDs, including item Numeric IDs and user Numeric IDs. Recently, Semantic IDs have been introduced in sequential recommendation models, resulting in improved model performance. Existing works align quantized embeddings with collaborative filtering embeddings, despite the fact that they reside in two respective spaces. Moreover, most existing works only utilize item Semantic IDs or user Numeric IDs, without constructing or leveraging user Semantic IDs, which limits the ability to capture users’ semantic information. In this paper, we propose CSG4Rec, a Collaborative-Similarity Guided Semantic ID Tokenization for Generative Sequential Recommendation. In CSG4Rec, a Collaborative-Similarity Contrastive Learning strategy is proposed, which aligns quantized embeddings within a single quantized space. Furthermore, we propose to construct user Semantic IDs by aggregating the semantic embeddings of items that each user has historically interacted with and quantizing them with collaborative-similarity guidance. The constructed user Semantic IDs are then combined with item Semantic IDs and fed into a generative model to produce recommendations. Incorporating the proposed modules above, CSG4Rec is constructed as a novel generative sequential recommendation model. Experimental results on three widely used benchmark datasets show that CSG4Rec consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. The source code of the proposed CSG4Rec is available at: https://github.com/yangbo1973/CSG4Rec . © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zhu L.; Bao Y.; Huo J.; Wu J.; Lai Y.-K.; Li W.; Gao Y.
Title: Training-free video editing via optical flow-enhanced score distillation
Abstract: The rapid advancement in visual generation, particularly the emergence of pre-trained text-to-image and text-to-video models, has catalyzed growing interest in training-free video editing research. Mirroring training-free image editing techniques, current approaches preserve original video information through video input inversion and manipulation of intermediate features and attention during the inference process to achieve content editing. Although they have demonstrated promising results, the lossy nature of the inversion process poses significant challenges in maintaining unedited regions of the video. Furthermore, approaches based on feature and attention manipulation during inference can lead to unintended over-editing and face challenges in both local temporal continuity and global content consistency. To address these challenges, this study proposes a score distillation paradigm based on pre-trained text-to-video models, where the original video is iteratively optimized through multiple steps guided by editing gradients provided by score distillation to ultimately obtain the target video. The iterative optimization starting from the original video, combined with a content preservation loss, ensures the maintenance of unedited regions in the original video and suppresses over-editing. To further guarantee video content consistency and temporal continuity, we additionally introduce a global consistency auxiliary loss and optical flow prediction-based local editing gradient smoothing. Experiments demonstrate that these strategies effectively address the aforementioned challenges, achieving comparable or superior performance across multiple dimensions, including preservation of unedited regions, local temporal continuity, and global content consistency of editing results, compared to that of state-of-the-art methods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Gao M.; Song W.; Pan J.; Huang F.
Author full names: Gao, Mingliang (26634962800); Song, Wenhao (57865380700); Pan, Jinfeng (8985450700); Huang, Fei (60877932000)
Title: Multi-scale attention-gated recurrent unit network for image fusion
Abstract: The objective of infrared and visible image fusion is to produce an image that combines thermal radiation information from the infrared image with fine-texture details from the visible image. However, existing deep learning-based methods generally rely heavily on cascaded convolutional operators or transformer blocks, which limit their capacity to capture long-term dependencies across scales and levels. Additionally, these methods often overlook the multi-scale information that represents objects at various sizes in the original images. To tackle these problems, we propose a Multi-scale Attention-Gated Recurrent Unit Network (MA-GRUNet) for infrared and visible image fusion. The MA-GRUNet utilizes dilated convolutions with varying rates to extract multi-scale information from the original images. Furthermore, we incorporate an Attention Gated Recurrent Unit (AGRU) to enhance interaction between multi-scale and multi-level features, effectively addressing the long-term dependency issue. Additionally, we introduce a multi-stage loss function to guide the network in preserving valuable information while processing the original images. Comprehensive experiments conducted on three public datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art fusion methods, both quantitatively and qualitatively. © 2026

Authors: Zhuo X.; Lu F.; Huang D.; Ma X.; Chen J.; Lei P.; Wang Z.
Title: Tool influence function prediction in robotic bonnet polishing through coupled robot compliance–viscoelastic contact modeling
Abstract: Industrial robots offer large workspaces and flexibility for optical polishing, but their low and pose-dependent stiffness causes load-induced end-effector deformation. This deformation reduces the effective tool offset and thereby changes the boundary condition governing the transient viscoelastic contact between the bonnet and workpiece. Existing TIF models generally treat robot compliance and bonnet contact behavior separately, limiting their ability to predict position-dependent material removal. This study establishes a coupled robot compliance-viscoelastic contact framework for TIF prediction. Pose-dependent normal stiffness is first mapped to end-effector deformation and effective bonnet offset through force-displacement equilibrium. The corrected offset is then introduced into a transient contact model based on generalized Maxwell viscoelasticity and coupled with Greenwood-Williamson microscopic contact theory for material-removal prediction. Reduced robot stiffness decreases the actual bonnet tool offset, contact force, and contact pressure, whereas stress relaxation and delayed recovery produce asymmetric leading and trailing side pressure distributions. Spot polishing experiments at different robot poses validate the model. Across nine polishing positions, the mean maximum depth prediction error decreases from 17.77% to 4.12%. The model establishes a direct mechanistic link between robot pose, contact boundary conditions, transient pressure evolution, and spatial TIF variation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhang D.; Huang M.; Jiang X.; Tu N.; Zhao C.; Chen Y.; Chen C.; Huang X.; Zeng R.; Nie X.
Title: The structure and properties of the solid solution of high temperature piezoelectric ceramics: (1-x)Li0.5Bi2.5Nb2O9-xBi3TiNbO9
Abstract: Bismuth layer-structured piezoelectric ceramics have long faced an inherent trade-off between piezoelectric performance and Curie temperature. A novel solid solution (1-x)Li0.5Bi2.5Nb2O9-xBi3TiNbO9 (denoted as (1-x)LBN-xBTN) was designed and fabricated via a conventional solid-state reaction method to achieve a synergistic improvement in both properties. With increasing BTN content, the rotation angle of the oxygen octahedra within the a-b plane increased, resulting in a more pronounced orthorhombic distortion. The Curie temperature rose from 833 °C to 896.3 °C. Furthermore, the refined grain size and increased relative density synergistically enhanced the breakdown electric field. The ferroelectric domains were more fully oriented under high electric fields, significantly improving the remnant polarization and piezoelectric response. The (1-x)LBN-xBTN series of ceramics achieved optimal overall performance when x = 0.5: TC = 861 °C, d33 = 13.0 pC/N, ρdc (at 500 °C) = 2.39 × 107 Ω·cm, demonstrating its promise for high-temperature applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Liu Y.; Tian Y.
Title: Influence of threshold-activated linear decay behaviors on information propagation in social networks
Source title: International Journal of Modern Physics C
Abstract: The social propagation of behaviors is influenced not only by interpersonal interactions, but also by individual psychological dynamics. This study presents a threshold-activated linear decay behaviors (TALDB) that incorporates both social and psychological factors to investigate propagation phenomena in social networks. Through edge-based partition theory and numerical simulations, the results demonstrate that TALDB can induce a range of phenomena, including continuous phase transitions, discontinuous phase transitions, and static behaviors. As the values of behavioral parameters increase, the behavioral intensity weakens, leading to a shift from continuous to discontinuous to static phase transitions. The findings reveal a phase transition crossover in how TALDB changes: the high-intensity behaviors promote the propagation of behaviors, while the weak behaviors delay propagation, decreasing gradually and more slowly. These insights extend the theoretical understanding of how individual psychology affects propagation dynamics in social systems, providing a mechanism for targeted interventions in complex networks. © 2027 World Scientific Publishing Company.

Authors: Ouyang C.; Zhang H.; Lee E.; Meng Y.; Ma L.; Tian Y.
Title: Beyond adsorption: Amino-acid-assisted interfacial radical chemistry enables ultralow friction
Abstract: Amino acids are widely investigated as environmentally compatible additives for water-based lubrication, yet their lubricating action is commonly attributed to adsorption, hydration, or conventional tribochemical reactions. Here we investigate an alternative mechanism in which amino acids participate in radical-mediated polymerization with unsaturated compounds at sliding interfaces. Valine (Val) and leucine (Leu) were evaluated in a PEG 200/water mixture (50:50, w/w) in combination with C C-containing monomers using a four-ball tribometer. The combined additives exhibited a pronounced synergistic effect: after a running-in period of approximately 33 min, selected amino acid–monomer formulations reduced the coefficient of friction (COF) to below 0.001, whereas either component alone provided substantially poorer lubrication. The position of the amino group strongly affected the tribological response: α-Leu outperformed its β- and γ-isomers, whereas replacing the amino group with a hydroxy or methyl group progressively reduced lubricity, consistent with the proposed involvement of reactive intermediates. Addition of the radical scavenger TEMPO suppressed the friction reduction and eliminated the characteristic decrease in COF, providing evidence for the involvement of radical intermediates. These results are consistent with a contribution from radical-mediated interfacial reactions and suggest a strategy for pairing amino acids with unsaturated additives for environmentally compatible lubricant additives. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhang H.; Xia J.; Zhang J.; Guo C.; Shen H.
Title: Event-triggered adaptive practical finite-time control of p-normal nonlinear systems with multiple uncertainties
Abstract: Focusing on a type of p-normal nonlinear systems involving multiple uncertainties, this paper presents an investigation into their event-triggered adaptive practical finite-time stability (PFTS) problem. The Nussbaum function is modified, and a novel lemma is established by introducing the class K∞ functions, which will relax the conservatism of the Nussbaum parameter and augment the applicability of the control algorithm. By embedding the event-triggering mechanism into the adaptive finite-time control design, the proposed framework reduces unnecessary control updates while preserving the desired transient behavior. The presented control methodology ensures that the closed-loop system achieves PFTS, which improves the existing results that merely ensure boundedness or asymptotic stability. Leveraging the contradiction augment and Lyapunov theory, it is established that the Zeno phenomenon is avoided in the event-triggered mechanism. To demonstrate the efficacy of the presented control approach, two simulations are ultimately performed. © 2026

Authors: Wang H.-R.; Zhou Y.-G.; Ma Q.
Title: Analytical solutions and numerical verification of small-strain moduli for granular materials: From unary to binary media
Abstract: The small-strain moduli are key parameters for characterizing the physical properties of granular materials and for engineering design. To investigate its variation under complex gradation conditions, theoretical derivation and simulation-based verification were conducted. In this study, the theoretical small-strain modulus equations considering the finite friction for unary media were derived. By using the contact information of contact probability, contact participation proportion, sliding proportion, and tangential stiffness reduction coefficient, the theoretical small-strain modulus equations for binary media were further derived. Numerical models of unary/binary media were created by the Discrete Element Method (DEM) to obtain the contact information and determine the specific formula parameter values. The macroscopic moduli of the samples were measured by simulated triaxial compression tests and wave velocity tests based on DEM to further verify the modulus formulas. This study reveals that all the macroscopic modulus equations can be derived from the microscopic contact information and the contact parameters can be obtained by DEM simulation. For example, the modulus formulas for unary media align well with the simulated values, whereas the formulas align well for binary media of fine‑dominated skeletons and coarse‑dominated skeletons. The mechanism of the load-bearing skeleton in binary media is influenced mainly by the coarse particle content and contact participation proportion, which is reflected by the modulus formulas. © 2026

Authors: Zhen X.; Liu Z.; Tian Z.; Liu D.; Feng X.; Wang Y.
Title: Coupling effects of engine speed and injection timing on spray dynamics, combustion and emissions in direct-injection spark-ignition n-butanol engine
Abstract: N-butanol is considered one of the most ideal alternatives for reducing carbon emissions in the transportation sector. However, its inherently poor atomization and low volatility pose significant challenges for mixture preparation and combustion control in engines. To elucidate the intrinsic coupling between injection timing and engine operating conditions, this study numerically investigates the effects of injection timing on in-cylinder flow characteristics, fuel–air mixing, combustion behavior, and pollutant formation of a pure n-butanol-fueled engine under different engine speeds. The results reveal the transition of the dominant mixture-formation mechanism from spray-momentum-dominated mixing at low speed to intake-tumble-dominated mixing at high speed, and link this transition with the speed-dependent recommended injection timing. The recommended SOI timings are −300 °CA at 1200 and 2600 rpm, and −320 °CA at 4000 rpm under the present combustion-emission compromise. At 1200 rpm engine speed, spray momentum dominates mixture formation because of the weak intake-induced flow, whereas at 4000 rpm engine speed, the strengthened tumble flow becomes dominant and requires earlier injection to provide sufficient evaporation and mixing time. Quantitatively, at 2600 rpm, −300 °CA increases IMEP by up to 4.85 % compared with the excessively delayed −260 °CA case, while at 4000 rpm, −320 °CA increases IMEP by 9.59 % and ITE by 3.46 percentage points relative to −260 °CA. In terms of emissions, at 1200 rpm, −300 °CA reduces soot and HC emissions by 9.5 % and 90.0 %, respectively, compared with −320 °CA. However, at 4000 rpm, excessively delayed injection at −260 °CA increases CO, soot, and HC emissions by 199.4 %, 839.3 %, and 7843.1 %, respectively, relative to −320 °CA, although NOx emissions decrease by 51.7 %. The combustion and emission characteristics are found to be strongly correlated with mixture homogeneity: a more uniform mixture significantly improves combustion efficiency but simultaneously increases NOx formation due to elevated combustion temperatures. This study elucidates the underlying mechanism governing the interaction between engine speed and injection timing optimization for n-butanol, providing theoretical guidance for achieving clean and efficient combustion of n-butanol fueled engines. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Xiao X.; Sang L.; Xie K.; Zhang Q.; Wang K.; Chen L.; Ding T.; Zhang S.
Title: An energy-driven micro breakage approach for aggregates by coupling ball kinematics with shape-based contact correction
Abstract: Micro breakage, characterized by continuous spalling at the corners and edges of aggregates, leads to fines generation, progressive particle rounding, and degradation of the load-bearing skeleton. Nevertheless, conventional discrete element methods (DEM) still face difficulty in representing micro breakage and the associated shape evolution under repeated loading. To address this limitation, an energy-driven micro breakage approach for aggregates is proposed. Specifically, Ball elements are used as kinematic carriers for particle motion, whereas particle-specific spherical-harmonic radial functions r(θ, φ) are used to represent irregular particle morphology. The breakage criterion is established by relating the contact elastic energy accumulated in local high-curvature regions to the fracture energy required to create equivalent new free surfaces. When the instantaneous or cumulative energy condition is satisfied, the particle radial function is updated according to the breakage volume. This update modifies the contact curvature and contact-scale geometric information, which are then fed back to the rolling-resistance Hertz contact model, thereby enabling continuous coupling among contact response, shape evolution, and micro breakage. The proposed approach is examined through numerical examples and compared with available laboratory results at the single-particle, multi-particle abrasion, and assembly scales. The results show that it can reasonably reproduce the multi-peak force-displacement response induced by micro breakage, together with the coupled evolution of abrasion ratio, particle shape, energy, and assembly degradation. The proposed approach provides a particle-scale framework for analyzing contact-induced micro breakage, particle rounding, and load-bearing skeleton degradation of graded aggregates under compression-dominated repeated loading. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Chenovick C.
Title: Grace, the Spirits of the Blood, and Mystical Marriage in Aemilia Lanyer-s Salve Deus Rex Judaeorum
Abstract: Aemilia Lanyer-s relationship to the prospective patronesses of her Salve Deus Rex Judaeorum has been the subject of much scholarship. The sheer number of dedicatory verses in Salve Deus have led some to read the volume-s devotional elements as a cynical cover for worldly ambition. At the same time, scholars interested in the potential erotic bonds Lanyer depicts between women have also given the poem-s social ends primacy over its devotional discourses. This essay reevaluates these assumptions by drawing out how Lanyer persistently unifies social and spiritual grace in Salve Deus. Showing how Lanyer draws on spirit-based physiologies to describe the operations of grace in both the patronage poems and in passages on the Passion of Christ, I argue that Lanyer uses physiological beliefs about the spirits of the blood to position divine grace as an embodied force that constitutes the social bonds she creates through her poetry. Title: Tracking fitness, comparing bodies: Social comparison and exercise activity among college students
Abstract: Wearable fitness trackers are widely used by college students to monitor exercise and promote healthy habits. Previous research has predominantly identified the positive role that fitness trackers have in users' exercise behavior. Guided by Bandura's Social Cognitive Theory, this study explored both positive and negative behaviors associated with wearable fitness trackers. A total of 253 college students completed a cross-sectional survey that examined associations among exercise tracking, exercise-related social media use, social comparison, exercise-related outcomes, mental health, and disordered eating. This study found students who tracked exercise behavior reported higher levels of exercise involvement, motivation, and positive exercise outcomes. Tracking was also associated with increased upward and downward social comparison, which can be harmful for some students, particularly for those who have been treated for an eating disorder. How often students share tracked exercise behavior on social media was not significantly related to most outcomes, suggesting frequency alone may not capture its relationship to mental health. Title: Simulating Shape Variation in Material Culture: The Simumorph R-package
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Archaeologists have devoted a significant amount of effort to define their types, or units of analysis. However, strong disagreements persist even after years of debate. This may occur for many reasons, some intrinsic to the archaeological record itself—since different technocomplexes may involve distinct and not always comparable types—and others related to the discipline’s epistemology, where interobserver bias and differences in theoretical schools and training traditions can play a key role. As a result, most archaeological analyses, usually based on type presence/absence or type frequencies, present uncertainty levels from the start, which are not always due to the archaeological record itself, but to how we analyse that record. In this work, we adopt a materialist view to present an alternative approach where we analyse purely artefact shape without the need for previous categorisation. To do this, we resort to Geometric Morphometrics, widely used in archaeology, and we develop a simulation framework for stepwise artefactual change. We provide the software tools to do this, which have been compiled in the R-package Simumorph, and we showcase its performance in four simulated archaeological scenarios. Here, we base our simulations on the geometric microliths found during the Early and Middle Holocene in the Western Mediterranean, but the framework can be applied to any context where shape variation matters. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Analysis of retail resilience in Seoul's neighborhood commercial districts Amidst the COVID-19 shock
Abstract: This study examines the economic resilience of neighborhood commercial districts in Seoul in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic. Moving beyond static before–after comparisons, we employ a Panel Interrupted Time Series (Panel ITS) design to separately identify (i) the immediate level shift at the onset of the shock, conceptualized as resistance, and (ii) the subsequent change in the growth trajectory as conditions transitioned toward the endemic phase, conceptualized as recoverability. The results show that structural diversity, operationalized via Shannon's entropy, functions as a key buffering mechanism: it attenuates initial revenue losses and is associated with a steeper post-shock recovery trend. Importantly, we also document pronounced spatial heterogeneity across Seoul's five major sub-markets. Central business districts exhibit heightened exposure and larger initial downturns, while recovery trajectories vary across sub-markets. Taken together, these findings imply that urban management should complement place-based physical upgrading with ecosystem-oriented strategies—specifically, “portfolio diversification” approaches that strengthen sectoral complexity and reduce systemic vulnerability within local commercial ecosystems. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Human-Elephant Conflict and its Impact on the Social Vulnerability of Subsistence Farmers in the Chure Terai Madhesh Landscape, Nepal
Abstract: Asian elephants (Elephas maximus) mainly inhabit fragmented landscapes within their range and frequently clash with humans, rendering subsistence farmers socially vulnerable. However, the extent of this vulnerability in Nepal is not well understood. In this study, we explored the social aspects of human–elephant conflict (HEC) and its impact on subsistence farmers by interviewing 1,060 affected households in Nepal’s Chure Terai Madhesh Landscape. Data were analyzed using the Social Vulnerability Index based on the five capitals of the Sustainable Livelihood Framework. 60% of respondents perceived an increase in HEC. The most common impacts reported were crop damage (47%), property losses (38%), and human casualties (15%). Among the 19 districts studied, Bardia and Jhapa showed the highest exposure and sensitivity to HEC. Farming households faced moderate to high vulnerability to crop loss caused by elephants. Of the five livelihood capitals, physical capital was the most vulnerable, followed by financial capital; social and human capitals showed the lowest vulnerability. The greater vulnerability of financial and physical capital indicates a reduced adaptive capacity among subsistence farmers. We recommend implementing tailored mitigation strategies, such as physical barriers for protecting crops and property, improving financial support systems, and promoting community-based adaptation measures to diminish the vulnerability of affected subsistence farmers. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Authors: Tunc H.; Unal E.
Title: Newly graduated nurses' experiences in internal medicine and surgical clinics after the earthquake
Abstract: Aim: To explore the experiences of newly graduated nurses working in internal medicine and surgical units in earthquake-affected regions. Background: The 2023 earthquakes in Türkiye severely disrupted healthcare services and increased the need for healthcare professionals in affected regions. Little is known about the experiences of newly graduated nurses as they begin their careers in disaster-affected settings. Methods: This qualitative descriptive phenomenological study used semi-structured interviews with 10 newly graduated nurses working in internal medicine and surgical units between February and August 2025. The interviews were conducted online, recorded, transcribed, thematically analysed, and reported in accordance with the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research guidelines. Results: Six main themes and 14 sub-themes were identified: (1) assignment process and decision-making, involving perceived ease of appointment, obligation, family guidance, and social responsibility; (2) physiological and environmental challenges, including health, housing, basic needs and transportation problems; (3) psychological challenges, including adaptation difficulties, post-traumatic fears, and empathic burden from traumatic narratives; (4) social life challenges, characterised by limited social opportunities and gradual development of a new social life; (5) professional experiences, including inexperience, working with disaster-affected colleagues, and caring for earthquake-affected patients; and (6) recommendations for supporting newly graduated nurses. Conclusions: Beginning professional practice in a disaster-affected region created substantial environmental, psychological, social, and professional challenges for newly graduated nurses. These findings support the need for structured preparation and support to facilitate their adaptation to such settings. Implications for nursing and health policy: Newly graduated nurses assigned to disaster-affected regions should receive disaster preparedness training, structured orientation, and psychological and institutional support. Workforce planning should also ensure access to experienced nurses who can support newly graduated staff in high-risk settings. Title: Emotions in flipped and lecture-based math courses
Abstract: Background: Emotions play an important role in learning. Activating teaching methods, such as flipped learning, can provide positive learning experiences but also pose emotional challenges to students. Aims: This intensive longitudinal study investigated 1) how students’ emotional valence before a learning event, learning mode (individual, peer, teacher-led), teaching implementation (lecture-based vs. flipped), and physiological arousal (electrodermal activity, EDA) during the learning event related to emotional valence after a learning event, and 2) how EDA varies across within-event segments and teaching implementations during learning events. Sample: Participants were 69 students enrolled in an engineering mathematics course implemented either as lecture-based (n = 34) or flipped learning (n = 35). Methods: Students reported their emotional states via a smartphone application and wore smart rings to measure EDA. A series of multilevel binomial logistic regression and linear mixed-effects models were analyzed across 546 learning events, totaling 827 h of data. Results: Positive pre-event emotional valence predicted positive post-event emotional valence. Teacher-led events were associated with more positive post-event emotional valence than individual events, particularly in the lecture-based group. The main effect of the teaching implementation was not significant. EDA did not show robust associations with post-event emotional valence; however, lecture-based events showed a clearer decline in EDA across event segments than flipped learning events. Conclusions: The results highlight the importance of supporting social and individual learning processes and examining physiological arousal as a temporal learning-event process rather than a simple proxy for post-event emotional valence. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Physiological and behavioral modeling of stress and cognitive load in web-based question answering
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: Time pressure and question difficulty can trigger stress and cognitive overload in web-based surveys, compromising data quality and user experience. Most stress detection methods are based on low-resolution self-reports, which are poorly suited for capturing fast, moment-to-moment changes during short online tasks. Addressing this gap, we conducted a 2 × 2 within-subjects study (N = 29), manipulating question difficulty and time pressure in a web-based multiple-choice questionnaire. Participants completed general knowledge and cognitive questions while we collected multimodal data: mouse dynamics, eye tracking, electrocardiogram, and electrodermal activity. Using condition-based and self-reported labels, we used statistical and machine learning models to model stress and question difficulty. Our results show distinct physiological and behavioral patterns within very short timeframes. This work demonstrates the feasibility of rapidly detecting cognitive-affective states in digital environments, paving the way for more adaptive, ethical, and user-aware survey interfaces. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Newcomers help most after being helped, veterans do not: Evidence from Stack Overflow
Abstract: Whether people who receive help online go on to help others is an open question. Prior observational studies report mixed results, and designs that ignore prior user activity may overstate reciprocity. We develop a matched difference-in-differences survival analysis of over 21 million Stack Overflow questions, comparing users whose questions were answered with propensity-score-matched users whose questions were not. We don't ask broadly whether reciprocity works in general, but locate the narrow conditions under which it affects user behavior. Users whose questions were answered helped others slightly more often (increment at answer arrival, hazard ratio [HR] = 1.049, 95% CI [1.044, 1.054]). The response depended on tenure: new users responded most (HR = 1.071 in the first week, 95% CI [1.056, 1.086]), while the longest-tenured users did not respond measurably. The tenure gradient is the most robust pattern we find. Timing mattered too, though far more fragilely: users answered within 30 to 60 min responded most strongly, while answers under 30 min show no elevation. Most of our data predate 2020, and the generalized reciprocity effect among new users does not survive a split at 2020, so these estimates largely reflect a pre-generative-AI baseline. We review gratitude, moral obligation, social expectation, and incentive displacement as possible psychological mechanisms but cannot measure them. On Stack Overflow, generalized reciprocity is less a general driver of cooperation than a recruitment channel for contributions from new users: designers gain most by getting newcomers’ questions answered. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Do negative emotions mediate the association between negative appraisals and dysfunctional reactions to involuntary musical imagery? Testing an OCD-analogue cognitive model of distressing earworms
Source title: Journal of Behavior Therapy and Experimental Psychiatry
Abstract: Purpose: Distressing involuntary musical imagery (INMI) or “earworms” are often experienced but rarely studied. Due to their similarity with obsessions, research can draw on models of obsessive-compulsive disorder. The present study followed a cognitive model and tested the hypothesis of a positive relationship between negative appraisals and dysfunctional reactions, mediated by negative emotions. Methods: Individuals with OCD (n = 79) and students without OCD (n = 298) completed the Characteristics of Earworms Questionnaire (CEAR). The central hypothesis was tested using a mediation analysis. Results: The analysis revealed a significant direct effect of negative appraisals on dysfunctional reactions to INMI, but no mediation by negative emotions. Conclusions: These findings support the applicability of the cognitive OCD model to INMI, particularly the relationship between negative appraisals and dysfunctional reactions. However, the results question whether negative emotions mediate this relationship. Title: Factors associated with installed photovoltaic capacity in Australia across small, medium, and large-scale systems
Abstract: Australia, as a global leader in photovoltaic deployment, has attracted significant research attention, has attracted significant research attention into factors associated with PV installation patterns. Previous studies have highlighted the role of early adopters, family wealth, and education, and have identified financial parameters (such as investment cost, internal rate of return, and net present value), social parameters (including household income and demographics), and environmental factors as relevant correlates of PV adoption. However, how these correlations vary across different system sizes, small, medium, and large, has not been systematically examined using historical data. In this study, historical time-series data on installed PV capacity in Australia, categorized by system-size groups across five states from 2013/14 to 2024/25 are collected, and the correlation of 4 groups of economic, market, financial, and affordability variables with PV installed patterns is examined. The results indicate that different system-size categories exhibit distinct association patterns. Small-scale adoption shows higher correlations with electricity prices and unit costs, medium-scale systems are more correlated with income and affordability indicators, and large-scale systems are more correlated with long-term financial returns and market incentives. Title: Health-promoting effects of sky gardens in high-density cities: Evidence from subjective restorative evaluation, eye tracking, and machine learning
Abstract: Sky gardens are increasingly recognized as health-promoting potential strategies in high-density urban environments, yet how specific spatial elements contribute to restorative benefits remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates the relationships between spatial composition, visual attention, and psychological restoration by integrating subjective assessments, eye-tracking data, and machine learning analysis across nine sky gardens in Singapore. The results reveal that restorative effects are primarily driven by natural landscapes, public facilities, and waterscapes, while urban landscapes and high-rise elements tend to undermine restoration. Different spatial elements exhibit distinct restorative roles: natural landscapes support both immediate visual attraction and sustained engagement, whereas waterscapes and people presence mainly enhance short-term attention, and public facilities contribute to longer-term restorative experiences. Importantly, these effects are nonlinear, with identifiable threshold ranges beyond which restorative benefits may diminish. These findings provide evidence-based insights for designing health-promoting sky gardens, emphasizing the need to balance natural landscapes, functional facilities, and visual openness to optimize restorative effects. This study deepens understanding of restorative mechanisms in vertical urban spaces and offers practical guidance for improving environmental quality in dense cities. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Negotiation impasses as meaningful outcomes: How AI is changing the cost structure of walking away
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is often expected to improve negotiation by strengthening information processing and analytical consistency. We argue that its effects on impasses are more selective. Extending the impasse cause, type, and resolution (ICTR) model, we distinguish two pathways. The first pathway is analytical augmentation: AI can reduce unwanted impasses caused by misunderstanding, poor option generation, and coordination failure. The second pathway runs through behavioral flexibility: Humans sometimes reach mutually acceptable agreements through aspiration adjustment, face-saving, and relational repair. Systems configured to apply stable decision thresholds and optimize focal-party outcomes without relational objectives reduce this flexibility and can thereby increase forced impasses. Which pathway dominates depends on AI's role as advisor or counterpart; its objective, training, and prompt; and whether agreement primarily requires analytical problem solving or interpersonal flexibility. These predictions concern system behavior, not whether AI experiences fatigue or social pressure: systems can be designed to respond to relational cues without experiencing them. Wanted impasses depend on both parties' underlying preferences, which AI does not change; AI instead helps negotiators recognize incompatibility sooner and justify walking away more openly. AI therefore changes the composition and meaning of impasses rather than uniformly increasing or decreasing agreement. Remaining impasses may reveal genuine incompatibility, but they may also reflect misspecified objectives or failures to encode principals' relational and economic costs. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Spatio-temporal heterogeneity in the built environment-urban vibrancy nexus of rail transit station areas and its implications for targeted management: Case study of Xi’an, China
Abstract: Urban Rail Transit (URT) station areas are pivotal nodes for shaping urban structure and fostering Urban Vibrancy. However, the spatio-temporal heterogeneity of the built environment’s impact on urban vibrancy remains underexplored, as existing research predominantly relies on spatially invariant global models, which overlook how the effects of the built environment vary across geographical locations and temporal contexts. To address this gap, this study uses Xi’an Metro Line 2 in China as a case study. Employing multi-source big data, including Location-Based Service (LBS) population heatmaps and Points of Interest (POIs) at a fine-grained grid scale, we utilize a Geographically Weighted Regression (GWR) model to quantitatively deconstruct the spatially varying interactions between built environment’s variables and urban vibrancy across different time periods (morning, noon, and evening).The results first statistically confirm the significant spatial non-stationarity of the built environment’s impacts. Based on this, the study identifies three distinct vibrancy generation archetypes: (1) "endogenous service-oriented" vibrancy, driven by localized built capacity and public services; (2) "exogenous attraction-based" vibrancy, defined by city-level functional synergies and public space quality; and (3) "nodal absorption-oriented" vibrancy, characterized by the efficient absorption of commuter flows through high-density development and functional diversity.These findings empirically challenge the universal applicability of principles within Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) theory. The core contribution of this study, therefore, is its advocacy for a paradigm shift in planning-from a "prescriptive framework" that applies standardized principles to a "diagnostic framework" predicated on the precise identification of local, dominant driving mechanisms. This conclusion provides a solid scientific basis and theoretical guidance for formulating place-based and time-sensitive strategies to enhance station area vibrancy. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Understanding preferences for explainable AI: A study on LIME variations
Abstract: The current research aims to empirically examine user preferences of four variations of visual explanations from an image classification model. Title: Introducing a Conditional Support Framework: How young residents view the Olympic games
Abstract: While cost-benefit frameworks have dominated resident support research, they struggle to explain why governance quality increasingly shapes acceptance.
