Title: Financializing the subsoil: Technical disclosure, extractive governance, and asymmetrical accountability in an emerging copper project in the Ecuadorian Amazon
Abstract: This article examines how technical disclosure frameworks contribute to the financialization of mineral resources and shape forms of information disclosure within contemporary extractive governance. Focusing on the Warintza copper project in the Ecuadorian Amazon, the study analyzes how geological information, investor-oriented valuation, environmental considerations, and community relations are structured within corporate disclosure practices. The research is based on qualitative documentary analysis of 18 publicly available disclosure documents produced between 2015 and 2024, including a NI 43–101 technical report, investor presentations, corporate reports, and sustainability-related documents. NI 43–101, a Canadian securities regulation designed to inform investors, structures highly detailed technical disclosures while offering only limited treatment of social and environmental dimensions. The findings show that disclosure systems prioritize geological and investor-oriented information through highly structured quantitative frameworks. Resource classification, drilling results, and corporate narratives of project potential translate geological uncertainty into investor expectations and position the deposit within global investment networks. By contrast, environmental and social dynamics are primarily represented through narrative descriptions that remain only partially integrated into investor evaluation. Rather than framing this as a problem of asymmetrical accountability, the article conceptualizes these dynamics as a condition of asymmetrical information disclosure across distinct governance domains. Different regulatory systems produce differentiated informational outputs, structuring what is disclosed, to whom, and with what level of precision. The findings also indicate that the limited disclosure of social conflict and Indigenous opposition may constitute a material gap in the representation of project-related risks within investor-oriented disclosure systems. By examining disclosure practices in an emerging mining region, the study contributes to debates on extractive governance, transparency regimes, and the financialization of natural resources. Title: Do users trade performance for eco-visibility? Digital pollution awareness and stated preferences for social media platform configurations
Abstract: Digital platforms face growing pressure to demonstrate environmental responsibility, yet users’ preferences for eco-visible features remain underexplored relative to functional attributes. Title: Collective communication behavior driven by emotion: A systematic meta-analysis of the relationship between emotional arousal and rumor spreading
Abstract: This meta-analysis aimed to quantify the relationship between emotional arousal and rumor spreading. To this end, it integrated 30 empirical studies (55 effect sizes, N = 32,082) and employed a three-level meta-analytic model. Meta-regression examined the moderating effects of emotional valence, rumor-spreading channel, measurement dimension, and participants’ country, gender, and educational background. Authors: Deshpande A.
Title: Why identity matters for development
Abstract: This paper argues that while development economics has moved beyond income-based metrics toward a broader capabilities framework, it remains insufficiently attentive to the role of social identity in shaping life chances. Identities such as caste, race, gender, and ethnicity structure access to resources, opportunities, and power in ways that conventional and multidimensional indices fail to capture. Drawing on evidence from global gender disparities and caste-based inequalities in India, the paper demonstrates how identity-blind policies risk reinforcing structural hierarchies. Authors: Wang Y.; Liu X.; Liu Z.; Chen J.; Jatowt A.; Kim K.; Kando N.; Yu H.-T.
Title: Event-centric human value understanding in news-domain texts: An actor-conditioned benchmark across multi-scope event contexts
Abstract: This work presents NEVU, a benchmark for actor-conditioned, event-centric, and direction-aware human value recognition in news-domain texts. NEVU evaluates whether models can infer values from event-structured evidence, attribute them to the correct social actors, and determine their aligned or contradictory direction. Built from 2865 English news articles, NEVU represents news at four semantic levels, from subevents to composite events and full articles. Using a hierarchical taxonomy of 54 fine-grained and 20 coarse-grained values, the benchmark contains 46,589 semantic units, 72,905 annotated unit–actor pairs, and 168,061 directed value instances. NEVU is constructed through a staged LLM-assisted annotation and verification pipeline, with targeted human verification for unresolved cases. Candidate-level acceptance and agreement are further examined through a multi-group assessment. The experiments show that prompting-only models remain limited, whereas LoRA-tuned open-weight models substantially improve performance, with overall Micro-F1 gains of 29.77 and 8.21 percentage points over the strongest prompting-only open-weight and proprietary baselines, respectively. These gains primarily reflect learnability under the NEVU reference-label setting. NEVU provides a structured benchmark for systematic evaluation and supervised adaptation of actor-conditioned human value recognition in English news. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Sacco P.L.; Fancourt D.
Title: Operationalising the arts exposome
Abstract: A recent arts exposome framework identified 50 transdiagnostic causal mechanisms (emotional, cognitive, self-referential, arousal–stress, inflammatory–epigenetic, social, and behavioural) by which arts engagement may affect mental health, organised around patterned daily exposure to active ingredients across diverse modes of arts engagement. Translating this structure into testable predictions depends on two operational prerequisites that current research has under-addressed. First, the active ingredients must be decomposed into mechanism-aligned exposure dimensions: aggregating activities as varied as receptive consumption, active participation, and cultural attendance under “arts engagement” averages mechanistically different effects and yields findings that the framework cannot localise to specific processes. Second, mechanism tractability is unevenly distributed across measurement modalities. Stress–HPA–immune mechanisms are well-served by peripheral measurement, including transcriptomic markers such as the Conserved Transcriptional Response to Adversity. Aesthetic and reward mechanisms are tractable through central measurement and autonomic indices of aesthetic emotion, but not through peripheral biomarkers. Affiliative mechanisms face validity challenges in peripheral measurement that may require pharmacological probes or behavioural proxies. Neither prerequisite suffices alone: a valid biomarker linked to a heterogeneous exposure measures something the framework cannot interpret, and a well-specified exposure linked to an inappropriate modality deteriorates evidence quality. These refinements are best understood as minimum conditions for identifying the core ingredients that matter most for each mechanism, since individual and contextual variation continue to moderate activation in real-world settings. Together, they identify where mechanism research can deliver near-term advances, where alternative methods are needed, and how the framework can move from theoretical mapping toward ecologically grounded testable inference. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Anggara A.
Title: Evaluating land price effects of zoning policy adjustment in Bekasi's TOD area: A regression discontinuity design analysis
Abstract: The expansion of Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) and associated zoning adjustments in Bekasi, Indonesia, has reshaped urban land markets, yet their causal effects on land prices and social outcomes remain insufficiently examined in developing-city contexts. This study estimates the impact of zoning regulation changes on land prices around TOD areas using a sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) with dual distance cutoffs at 500 and 750 m. Based on 905 geo-referenced land price transactions from 2017 to 2024, the results reveal a statistically significant discontinuity at the 750-m threshold, corresponding to an average increase in land value of approximately 107 percent. In contrast, no significant effect is detected at the 500-m cutoff, suggesting that land prices in the immediate TOD core had largely internalized accessibility benefits prior to the formal zoning adjustment, resulting in a pre-existing price premium. Covariate balance and robustness tests support the validity of the causal estimates. The findings indicate that zoning-induced land value capitalization is most pronounced in transitional TOD zones rather than in fully matured TOD centers. While the results empirically support the use of a 750-m TOD planning radius, the magnitude of land value appreciation also raises concerns regarding housing affordability and potential gentrification. These outcomes highlight the need for complementary policy instruments to ensure that TOD-driven zoning benefits contribute to inclusive and socially balanced urban development. Copyright © 2026. Authors: Zhou D.; Liu J.; Li H.; Fan F.; Yan L.; Zhang J.
Title: AI-assisted analysis of creative thinking opportunities in new Chinese elementary mathematics textbooks
Abstract: Developing students’ mathematical creative thinking has become a central goal of mathematics curriculum reform worldwide. This study examines opportunities for mathematical creative thinking in the three Grade 1 Chinese mathematics textbook editions first implemented under the Compulsory Education Mathematics Curriculum Standards (2022 Edition). Drawing on the Opportunities-to-Learn framework, the study localizes Hadar and Tirosh’s (2019) analytical framework by refining the operational indicators of divergent, convergent, and lateral thinking and extending the framework through the incorporation of cognitive complexity. A human–AI collaborative coding approach was used to analyze 1,473 mathematical tasks. The findings indicate that approximately half of all textbook tasks provide opportunities for mathematical creative thinking, with convergent thinking emerging as the dominant dimension across all three editions, although each edition places emphasis on different indicators of mathematical creative thinking. This study contributes a localized analytical framework for evaluating mathematical creative thinking in curriculum materials and provides implications for textbook design, curriculum reform, and future research on mathematical creative thinking. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Li B.; Kim N.; Zhang H.
Title: Virtual reality as a catalyst for change: Promoting communication intention, policy support and interaction with migrant workers in Singapore
Abstract: Migrant workers are vital to the host country's development, yet they often remain socially invisible and face barriers to social integration. Drawing on narrative persuasion and indirect contact perspectives, this research examines how immersive storytelling relates to empathy and supportive orientations toward migrant workers through two laboratory experiments in Singapore. Study One (N = 125) compared narrative delivery via virtual reality (VR), 360-degree video, and text. VR generated the highest immersion, and a sequential path indicated that greater immersion was associated with stronger identification with the protagonist, followed by greater empathy; empathy was associated with stronger willingness to interact with migrant workers, greater policy support, and higher future supportive behavioral intentions. Study Two (N = 87) focused on a key VR design choice, avatar perspective, by comparing self-versus other-embodiment in the VR experience. Self-embodiment increased self-presence, while greater self-presence was sequentially associated with immersion, identification with the protagonist, and empathy, followed by the same pattern of supportive outcomes. Together, the studies show that both modality and within-VR self-representation shape empathy-based pathways toward supportive orientations, offering actionable guidance for designing immersive interventions that promote understanding and support for marginalized groups. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Li X.; Bai H.; Wang X.; Li Y.; Hu W.
Title: Imagery ability dimensions: Effects on scientific creativity in multimedia learning
Abstract: Many forms of scientific learning require students to understand abstract concepts, spatial relations, and dynamic processes. Multimedia learning can support these processes by providing coordinated verbal and visual representations, but its effectiveness may vary according to students’ ability to construct and manipulate mental representations. Imagery ability, defined as the capacity to generate and process mental images, may be an important source of such individual differences. However, the specific mechanisms by which imagery ability influences multimedia learning outcomes and scientific creativity remain unclear. To address this gap, this study explored the effects of different dimensions of imagery ability (clarity, manipulation ability, and imaginativeness) on learning performance and scientific creativity in multimedia learning environments, as well as the underlying neural mechanisms. Four experiments were conducted, including three behavioural experiments and one neuroimaging experiment using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). The results showed that although pictorial multimedia learning facilitated knowledge retention, its effects on knowledge transfer and scientific creativity depended more on students’ imagery manipulation ability and imaginativeness than on imagery clarity. Furthermore, the fNIRS results revealed that activation in the right middle temporal gyrus (MTG) and medial prefrontal cortex (MPFC) mediated the association between multimedia learning and scientific creativity. Notably, only imagery imaginativeness positively moderated the pathway from multimedia learning to right MPFC activation. These findings suggest that the generative construction and novel reorganisation of mental representations may be particularly important for transforming knowledge acquired through multimedia learning into original scientific ideas. This study provides empirical evidence for the design of personalised multimedia instruction and the development of strategies for fostering scientific creativity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Gong Y.; Huang J.; Bao L.; Li H.; Liu J.; Jing P.; Xiong J.; Tang X.
Title: Teacher emotional support, question openness and student oral participation: The role of positive emotion across stages in AI-observed STEM and non-STEM classes
Abstract: Background: Student oral participation is essential for engagement and learning, yet participation tends to decline in large-class and STEM contexts where social risk and cognitive demands are higher. Existing studies often relied on self-reported or small-scale observations, which may introduce subjective bias and are labor-intensive, limiting large-scale evidence on how instructional practices influence participation across contexts. Aims: This study examines how teacher emotional support and question openness influence student oral participation through student emotion, and whether these effects vary across educational stages and disciplinary contexts. Sample: Data were collected from 1455 face-to-face classes in China. Methods: Artificial intelligence-based techniques were used to capture fine-grained classroom interactions. Structural equation modeling and multigroup analyses were conducted to examine the mediating role of student positive emotion and to compare pathway patterns across educational stages and disciplinary contexts. Results: Teacher emotional support was primarily associated with student oral participation via student positive emotion, whereas question openness showed a more direct association with participation. The indirect role of emotional support through positive emotion became stronger across educational stages, suggesting a compensatory function in secondary education where baseline participation tends to decline. Students in STEM classes were less emotionally responsive to teacher support but showed a stronger association between positive emotions and oral participation. Conclusions: Emotional support is a context-sensitive intervention rather than a universally effective strategy. By combining large-scale AI-based observation with cross-stage and disciplinary comparisons, this study contributes methodological advances for classroom interaction research, although cross-cultural validation of AI-based measures is needed. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Contreras S.A.
Title: Making critical-mineral sourcing visible: recorded-origin evidence from U.S. federal procurement
Abstract: Critical-mineral security depends not only on extraction and processing capacity but also on state visibility. Governments struggle to govern a mineral dependence they cannot observe in their own records, even when fragments of that information are held privately across agencies. This article asks how far the United States federal government’s recorded sourcing of the critical-mineral commodities it buys can be seen in its own contract data. Using approximately one thousand federal contract awards for selected critical-mineral commodity classes over fiscal years 2018–2026, we measure domestic-versus-foreign sourcing at the contract level in USAspending / Federal Procurement Data System (FPDS) records. Country of product origin is recorded for about 94% of awards and for nearly all obligated dollars, enough to support a bounded sourcing profile in this narrow universe. Among awards with recorded origin, foreign sourcing is a minority, about 9%, but it is policy-relevant: China is the largest foreign source by dollar value, concentrated in two large manganese awards, while Germany is the most frequent by award count. Bullion and coinage flows must be separated from strategic-materials procurement, or they inflate the universe twenty- to forty-fold. Two preliminary findings, a selective-onshoring trend and a defense-logistics sourcing effect, do not survive the complete data. The analysis covers U.S. federal procurement only and measures recorded procurement sourcing rather than upstream mine origin or total national dependence. Its contribution is to make one layer of critical-mineral governance, the state’s own recorded purchasing, observable, and to clarify what that layer can and cannot show for public oversight. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Hutson S.R.
Title: Uncorrelated Inequalities: A Multiproxy Measure for Household Archaeology
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Inequality has received increased attention in the social sciences since the 1990s, in part because of the harm it causes and because massive inequality is avoidable. Bolstered by the Gini coefficient, a quantitative measure of unevenness in a distribution that enhances comparative studies across time and space, archaeologists have expanded the study of inequality in recent years. Many of these investigations use multiple variables to assess inequality. A challenge of such multi-proxy studies is that simply averaging Gini coefficients for multiple variables can over-represent inequality in societies where variables for inequality are not correlated. This paper provides an experimental measure—the Domain Sensitivity Gini (DSG)—and applies it to a sample of Maya archaeological case studies with extensive domestic excavations. The DSG helps disambiguate societies where wealth variables are aligned from societies where such variables are not aligned. In cases where variables do not align, different forms of wealth are not strongly correlated: a household that is poor in one domain might be wealthy in other domains. The DSG also suggests that inequality is lower than estimates based on averaged variables. This finding is valuable when set within a broader comparative context because it shows that high inequality seen today is not natural and that ancient case studies are relevant. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Authors: Saldıray A.
Title: Experiencing expanded minds in higher education: Critical thinking–based discussion sessions in the context of Hannah Arendt’s political thought
Abstract: The uncertainties and multidimensional crises faced by today’s society also shape the civic qualities individuals should possess. Critical thinking skills, along with their public qualities, are the civic skills required by today’s society. There is limited educational sciences research on Hannah Arendt’s treatment of thinking as political action with moral responsibilities. This case study examined argument-based discussion sessions held by university students regarding Turkey’s social problems, based on Hannah Arendt’s understanding of citizenship. The analysis covered six argument-based discussion sessions on Turkey’s social problems, a discussion session based on general evaluations, written evaluation forms, and individual interviews. Participants included 44 teacher candidates enrolled in the education faculty of a university in Central Anatolia. Data collection was conducted during the researcher’s Critical and Analytical Thinking course. The findings suggested that discussions based on critical thinking had transformed into a pluralistic forum by creating a public context where individuals could express their uniqueness through words and actions. In the discussions, students—within their experience of political existence—tried to form ideas while expressing their individual identities and also being nourished and tested by the views of others. Plurality-based interaction supported establishing connections and clarifying personal opinions. The effort to understand different ideas entailed visiting the mind of another and thinking with an expanded mindset. Participating in discussions as a listener also provided important gains. The students who listened used their metacognitive thinking skills throughout the whole research process. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Iqbal M.
Title: Critical minerals and the U.S. industrial strategy: resource security, environmental justice, and the contradictions of decarbonization
Abstract: The United States has rapidly implemented a critical minerals industrial policy to support the clean energy transition and to advance national and economic security, using the Inflation Reduction Act, Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, and Defense Production Act to strengthen domestic supply chains and reduce reliance on China. This review examines whether this strategy represents decarbonization, a new phase of green industrial policy, green extractivism, a geopolitical resource-security approach, or a contradictory project that advances climate goals while perpetuating inequalities. Drawing on 65 peer-reviewed articles, books, and policy reports, the Critical Minerals Justice Dilemma framework clarifies persistent tensions among decarbonization, supply security, industrial competitiveness, environmental justice, and geopolitical resilience. Evidence from Indigenous sovereignty research, conflict mapping in the Americas, and political economy analysis shows that U.S. policy accelerates green extractivism, overrides Tribal consent through crisis-driven measures, uses techno-legal solutions that undermine democratic governance, and shifts environmental and social burdens to Global South sacrifice zones. The analysis identifies three main gaps: limited theorization of racial capitalism and settler colonialism in domestic contexts, insufficient attention to epistemic justice, and a lack of demand-side political economy. The findings suggest techno-optimistic views on green transitions do not address structural inequalities. Achieving a just strategy requires prioritizing Free, Prior, and Informed Consent, Indigenous co-governance, and demand reduction as central political imperatives rather than technical solutions. Decarbonization within racial capitalism continues to reproduce extractivist inequalities. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: An integrated framework for total nitrogen load allocation and multidimensional assessment reconciling equity and environmental efficiency in large river basins
Abstract: Total nitrogen (TN) load governance is crucial for safeguarding river and nearshore water environments. However, translating basin reduction goals into equitable and efficient spatial targets remains challenging due to socioeconomic, hydrological, and biogeochemical heterogeneities. This study develops an integrated framework coupling process-based water quality modelling (SWAT) with Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) to reconcile environmental efficiency with regional equity. Applying this framework to the Liao River Basin in China, this study generated multiple allocation schemes reflecting different socioeconomic priorities and evaluated their performance across TN compliance, abatement costs, food production, and social equality. Results show that under the 30% reduction target, schemes integrating efficiency reduced total basin abatement costs by 0.1%–6.5% and increased crop yields by 0.4%–2.4% relative to the equity-only scheme, although they widened regional disparities in economic and livelihood burdens. Sensitivity analyses indicate that the economic advantages of efficiency-integrated schemes weaken under the 40% reduction target due to nonlinearly escalating marginal abatement costs, and remain sensitive to source allocation within individual catchments. The scheme performance assessment accounting for multiple uncertainties reveals that the optimal schemes depend on the total reduction target and specific policy priorities, including objective weighting and policy-weighted scenarios prioritizing food security, cost control, or social equality. Ultimately, this framework explicitly quantifies multidimensional tradeoffs and provides a practical basis for formulating load management strategies across varying reduction targets and policy priorities. © 2026

Author full names: Ginsburg, Golda S. (7005246778); LoCurto, Jamie (56928203200); FitzGerald, David (60811991300); Chan, Grace (37044631800)
Title: A pilot randomized controlled trial of the feasibility and acceptability of a school-based intervention to reduce student anxiety during the transition to middle school
Source title: Journal of Behavioral and Cognitive Therapy
Abstract: This study evaluated the feasibility and acceptability of a school-based intervention to reduce anxiety and related impairment during the transition to middle school. Thirty-eight students were randomly assigned to receive the Transitioning Emotionally and Academically to Middle School Successfully (TEAMSS, n = 20) program, a group cognitive behavioral intervention, or Enhanced Usual Care (EUC, n = 18), a study generated resource list and usual school counseling. Students (mean age 10.4; 85.7% White; 50% female) had elevated anxiety symptoms and/or a primary anxiety disorder. Feasibility and acceptability were assessed via recruitment, retention, attendance, intervention satisfaction, and intervention adherence. Exploratory student outcomes of anxiety and constructs targeted in TEAMSS (e.g., behavioral avoidance, academic organizational and social skills) were assessed at post intervention (10 weeks after the initiation of treatment) and at the end of the academic year (follow-up). Results revealed student recruitment challenges; enrolled participants found the intervention acceptable and helpful. Student attendance at the group meetings was high. Clinician adherence to the intervention indicated room for improvement. At post and follow-up assessments, students in both groups showed significant reductions in anxiety and improvements in functioning, but there were few statistically significant between-group differences. Within group effect sizes were medium to large and favored TEAMSS on several measures assessing changes in areas targeted in TEAMSS (e.g., maladaptive cognitions, social skills); however, these findings should be interpreted with caution given the overall absence of group differences on most measures. Implementation challenges and future directions are discussed. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive. Published by Elsevier Masson SAS. Authors: Guo X.; Ta R.; Li X.; Peng C.; Hu W.
Title: Associations between teaching approaches, epistemological beliefs, utility value, and science-related career choice: A study across different metacognitive levels
Abstract: This study utilized survey data from 1,257 Chinese eighth-grade students to examine the associations among teaching approaches (i.e., inquiry-based teaching and teacher-directed instruction), epistemological beliefs, utility value, and science-related career choice. Crucially, these relational patterns were analyzed within different levels of metacognitive ability (high, medium, and low). Specifically, the present study employed multi-group structural equation modeling to examine group-specific patterns of associations among variables across students with different levels of metacognitive ability. Results indicated that positive associations between inquiry-based teaching and the examined variables were mainly observed within the high-metacognitive group, whereas teacher-directed instruction demonstrated positive associations with certain variables across groups. In addition, indirect associations involving utility value in the relationship between teaching approaches and science-related career choice were identified in the high-metacognitive group, while comparable patterns were not observed in the other groups. These findings suggest that the association patterns involving teaching approaches, epistemological beliefs, utility value, and science-related career choice may differ across metacognitive groups. Authors: Jung E.H.; Chae J.
Title: Sharing for better health: Exploring age, health data sharing behavior, and relatedness needs in mobile health apps
Abstract: Drawing on socioemotional selectivity theory and self-determination theory, this study investigated associations of age and future time perspective (FTP) with mHealth users' target-specific health data sharing and related psychological experiences. An online survey of 613 adults aged 20 to 95 years assessed their behaviors of health data sharing in their personal networks and with healthcare professionals, along with their satisfaction of relatedness needs, enjoyment, and well-being. Structural equation modeling indicated that age was negatively associated with FTP and that FTP was positively associated with both types of health data sharing. Unexpectedly, sharing with healthcare professionals, but not sharing within personal networks, was positively associated with satisfaction of relatedness needs. Satisfaction of relatedness needs was positively associated with enjoyment, and enjoyment was positively associated with well-being. These findings highlight the importance of mHealth designs that are responsive to users’ varied social, privacy, and technological preferences. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: The complex role of perspective taking in negotiations
Abstract: To reach an agreement, successful negotiators typically need to understand two things: what they themselves are willing to accept, and what the other side is willing to accept. Understanding the other party's threshold requires perspective taking. In negotiations over goods or services, these judgments shape perceptions of the bargaining zone: the range of outcomes both parties would prefer to walking away without an agreement. The present paper examines how negotiators form perceptions of the bargaining zone. These perceptions have important downstream consequences, influencing everything from the offers negotiators make to the agreements they reach. We review work on how negotiators form perceptions of what their counterpart is willing to accept. Perspective taking can help negotiators estimate the lowest price a seller would accept or the highest price a buyer would pay. However, it can also lead negotiators to erroneously internalize the other party's perspective as if it is relevant to their own valuation. As an example, we demonstrate that buyers are willing to pay more for the same good when the seller gives up an entire endowment rather than only part of it, although the seller's end state should not affect buyer's willingness to pay for the good. These findings show how taking the other party's perspective can shape valuations, fairness judgments and negotiations outcomes. We conclude by discussing implications for multi-issue bargaining and strategic framing, highlighting how psychological heuristics and social context interact to shape outcomes in complex real-world situations, such as salary negotiations and real estate transactions. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: How Sociodemographic Factors Shape Community Well-Being in Sustainable Tourism Destinations
Abstract: Tourism significantly contributes to the livelihoods of host communities, influencing their social, environmental, and economic development. However, residents’ diverse demographics and attitudes often shape their perceptions of tourism, affecting the level of support or opposition within these communities. Such demographic factors may influence how individuals perceive tourism’s benefits and drawbacks, leading to regional variations in engagement. This study examined the relationship between sociodemographic factors, New Silk Road (NSR) infrastructure, community well-being, and tourism sustainability in destination areas. Specifically, it analysed correlations among NSR infrastructure, demographic variables, tourism impact (TI), quality of life (QOL), place image (PI), and support for tourism development (STD). Data were collected during the NSR infrastructure project in Turkistan, Kazakhstan. The findings indicated that 24 of 28 relationships between variables were statistically significant, demonstrating strong associations. Additionally, post-hoc analysis revealed significant differences in satisfaction with non-material aspects of life—affected by respondents’ income, occupation, and parental status—providing valuable insights for policymakers to develop targeted strategies. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Vocabulary Size of Children Aged 5 – 9: The Contribution of Shared Reading and Screen Time
Abstract: Language development is shaped by children’s exposure to linguistic input, which increasingly comes from both caregiver–child interaction and digital media. Although shared reading is a well-established predictor of vocabulary growth, less is known about how different forms of shared reading and temporally differentiated screen exposure jointly contribute to language development. This study examined the relative contributions of shared book reading, shared poetry reading, weekday screen time, and weekend screen time to passive vocabulary in children aged 5–9 years (N = 636). Children completed a standardized passive vocabulary test, while parents reported literacy practices and screen exposure. Hierarchical regression analyses controlling for age revealed distinct and context-dependent associations. Weekday screen time was negatively associated with vocabulary, whereas shared book reading showed the strongest positive association. Shared poetry reading also made a smaller but significant positive contribution. In contrast, weekend screen time showed a weak positive association with vocabulary. The findings demonstrate that children’s vocabulary development is differentially shaped by both the type of literacy input and the temporal context of screen exposure. The study advances current research by integrating differentiated forms of shared reading and screen use within a single model, highlighting the importance of context-sensitive approaches to children’s digital and linguistic environments. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. Title: Navigating blue economy research conflicts for improved societal outcomes
Abstract: The Blue Economy aims to balance economic prosperity, environmental stewardship, and social equity through sustainable ocean development. Its rapid expansion—spanning fisheries, aquaculture, maritime transport, and energy—has intensified competition for marine resources and space, often generating conflict and cumulative impacts on ecosystems and communities. These tensions are driven by uncertainty about outcomes, as well as differing stakeholder values and perceptions. To realize the goals of the Blue Economy, robust research is needed. However, research institutions working in contested marine spaces may face reputational, ethical, and strategic risks. These include navigating tensions among ocean users, developers, policymakers, and the public. From an organisational perspective, deciding whether to engage in such research requires balancing potential benefits against risks to integrity, partnerships, and long-term goals. This paper introduces the Conflict Navigation Grid, a decision-support framework that enables research organisations to systematically evaluate the risks and benefits of proposed projects. The Grid helps identify initiatives that provide strong organisational, community, environmental, and policy value while also assessing whether reputational, operational, or personal risks are manageable. It distinguishes projects that align with institutional values and capacities from those where the potential harms outweigh uncertain returns. By adopting this systematic decision framework, organisations can confidently make decisions in the face of conflict, thereby managing risk and achieving improved societal outcomes. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Shiny by Design: Establishing Diagnostic Criteria for Intentional Burnishing on Prehistoric Bone Artifacts
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: The identification of intentional burnishing on prehistoric osseous artifacts remains a persistent methodological challenge. Bone surfaces are highly reactive and readily record microwear traces but are susceptible to taphonomic alteration. This study investigates how the use of different burnishing materials affects the morphology of bone surfaces and the formation of diagnostic microwear traces to develop a methodologically grounded classification for identifying intentionally burnished surfaces on archeological osseous artifacts. Experimental observations are evaluated in relation to existing knowledge of use-related, manufacturing, and postdepositional surface modifications. The analysis is based on a microwear framework that integrates multiscalar observations (low- and high-magnification microscopy and scanning electron microscopy) with quantitative three-dimensional surface texture analysis. Both microscopy and quantitative data derived from confocal microscopy reveal clear differences among bones burnished with different agents, highlighting agent-specific topographic patterns. The experimentally derived reference dataset was subsequently applied during microwear analysis of selected prehistoric bone points from Lake Lubāns (Latvia) and the Wiele 33 site (Poland) to assess the analytical applicability of the proposed protocol. The results of our study demonstrate the diagnostic potential of the created classification of wear traces to distinguish intentional burnishing on archaeological osseous artifacts and to discriminate between intentional, use-related, and taphonomic surface modifications. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Direct Technology Diffusion in Higher Education: Evidence from Doctoral Students
Source title: ASEAN Journal of Educational Research and Technology
Abstract: This study compares direct and indirect technology diffusion in higher education, focusing on plagiarism detection software in Indian doctoral education. Using a quantitative survey of research scholars, the study finds that direct diffusion significantly improves outcomes. Similarity levels decreased substantially under direct diffusion, indicating more accurate application of plagiarism rules. Additionally, direct diffusion reduced the time required and lowered costs considerably. The findings suggest that direct access empowers users, minimizes intermediary-related inefficiencies, and enhances both effectiveness and efficiency. The study highlights cost-effectiveness as a key enabler and recommends that policymakers and institutions promote direct technology diffusion to improve adoption and strengthen academic integrity in higher education. © 2027 Bumi Publikasi Nusantara.

Authors: Jedinger A.
Title: A dual-process motivational approach to understanding antisemitism: The role of authoritarianism, social dominance orientation, and conspiracy mentality
Abstract: Antisemitism remains a persistent challenge in contemporary societies, yet its psychological underpinnings are not well understood. Building on the dual-process motivational (DPM) model of ideology and prejudice, this study examined the extent to which antisemitism is rooted in broader ideological dispositions - right-wing authoritarianism (RWA), social dominance orientation (SDO), and conspiracy mentality. Using a nationwide online survey of German adults ( N = 457), bivariate and multivariate analyses indicate that conspiracy mentality is the strongest correlate of antisemitic attitudes, followed by individual differences in SDO. These findings support the view that antisemitism is embedded within a broader ideological belief system characterized by anti-egalitarian and conspiratorial worldviews. The role of conspiratorial worldviews as a potential distinct motivational pathway to prejudice within the DPM model is discussed. © 2026 The Author.

Author full names: Brady, William J. (57222282207); Yu, Chen-Wei (57941423800); Ornstein, Nicholas (60896643700); Sun, Bolun (60895903900); Jackson, Joshua Conrad (57056837000)
Title: Artificial intelligence systems distort upstream selection in human social learning
Abstract: Humans are social learners who depend on observing others to acquire knowledge, norms, and behaviors, a capacity that underlies cumulative cultural evolution. Social learning unfolds in two stages: upstream selection determines what information becomes visible, and downstream selection determines what learners copy from that visible sample. Downstream selection occurs through biases such as conformity bias (copying what appears common) and prestige bias (copying those who appear highly respected). These downstream biases can be adaptive when upstream selection yields a sample that reflects the population's true distribution, so that what appears common is actually common and those who appear respected are actually competent. We argue that digital technologies disrupt this condition, creating an upstream selection problem. Engagement-based algorithms amplify the tails of the distribution, surfacing rare and extreme content, whereas generative AI collapses it toward the mode (of the population or the user), erasing the surrounding diversity. Crucially, in each system the optimization signal shapes both visibility and prestige. For engagement-based algorithms, the signal is engagement: creators who post extreme content become more visible and, through the likes, shares, and followers, appear more prestigious. For generative AI, the signal is statistical typicality: it makes a modal answer dominant and, with no alternatives shown, makes the model that produced it appear more prestigious. These distortions can give rise to emergent group-level phenomena, including pluralistic ignorance and illusory consensus. Synthesizing evidence across psychology, cultural evolution, and computational social science, we provide a framework for how digital technologies disrupt social learning and outline interventions for restoring functional cultural transmission. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Zhou W.; Kim Y.
Title: Long-term impact of ChatGPT-4 on music students' creative and analytical skills: A follow-up study
Abstract: The rapid integration of generative AI into education has raised important questions about its long-term influence on higher-order thinking. Building on our earlier study that examined the one-off impact of ChatGPT-4, the present follow-up study investigated its sustained effects on music students’ creative and analytical skills. A quasi-experimental design was employed with 74 undergraduate music students assigned to an experimental group ( n = 36) and a control group ( n = 38). Across a 24-week intervention, creativity and analytical skills were assessed at 12 repeated measurement points. Data were analyzed using latent growth modeling, multivariate analysis of covariance, cross-lagged panel modeling, epistemic network analysis, and a first-order Markov chain model. Results indicated that the experimental group began with higher initial levels and demonstrated steeper growth trajectories, reflecting a Matthew effect, while the control group displayed compensatory tendencies. Cross-lagged analyses revealed that analytical reasoning strongly predicted subsequent creativity in the experimental group, and network analysis confirmed stable co-occurrences between creative and analytical moves. Transition modeling further showed recursive cycles of idea generation, revision, evaluation, and structural reasoning. These findings suggest that ChatGPT-4 fosters an integrated interplay of creativity and analysis, offering music educators worldwide practical strategies for designing AI-mediated learning that balances innovation with critical rigor. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Parcero-Oubiña C.; Solana-Muñoz A.
Title: Exploring the Inherent Affordability for Movement in Past Landscapes
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: The aim of this paper is to demonstrate a method for exploring the conditions inherent to mobility within a landscape, as a means of broadening our understanding of the role of human movement in archaeology. Specifically, it is based on the application of a tool, Omniscape, developed in the field of ecology, which to date has barely been utilised in archaeology. As we shall attempt to demonstrate, it holds great potential to overcome some of the common limitations in the digital modelling of mobility in archaeology. After briefly reviewing these limitations, we outline the operating principles of Omniscape and illustrate the type of results it produces using three ideal control surfaces. Finally, an archaeological case study regarding the distribution of burial mounds in an area of NW Iberia is presented, to illustrate possible ways of utilising the results for tackling specific archaeological questions. © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Li M.; Guo L.
Title: Critical thinking in generative AI use: Development and validation of the GAICU scale for university students
Abstract: The widespread adoption of generative artificial intelligence is reshaping higher education, calling for responsible engagement with AI tools to maintain students' agency as learners. Grounded in Facione’s six core reasoning skills, this study contextualizes critical thinking competencies to address the distinct cognitive and behavioural demands of AI engagement. The Generative AI Critical Use Scale (GAICU) was developed and validated in three sequential phases. In Phase 1, a literature-informed synthesis of 46 studies, student interviews, and expert review produced 22 items. In Phase 2, exploratory factor analysis with a pilot sample (N = 166) yielded a stable four-factor structure of 16 items. In Phase 3, confirmatory factor analysis with a large sample (N = 1515) finalized a 15-item scale with acceptable model fit. The final scale demonstrated strong reliability and multiple sources of validity evidence, including composite reliability, convergent and discriminant validity, criterion-related validity, and measurement invariance across academic disciplines and educational levels. The GAICU introduces a behaviourally grounded, four-dimensional framework: (1) analysis and understanding of the task, (2) evaluation and judgement of AI content, (3) control and optimization of AI use, and (4) self-regulation and reflection on AI results. These dimensions function as a sequence: task analysis initiates the sequence, evaluation and optimization form the interactive core, and reflection serves as the metacognitive review. The GAICU thus provides a theoretically grounded and empirically validated instrument to measure university students’ critical engagementwith generative AI in academic settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Key attributes for industry 4.0–enabled occupational safety and health management in modern methods of construction: a Delphi–VAHP approach
Abstract: The adoption of Industry 4.0 technologies presents significant opportunities to enhance occupational safety and health (OSH) management within modern methods of construction (MMC). However, organisations often lack clarity on which factors are crucial for the adoption of Industry 4.0 technologies for OSH improvement in MMC. Existing studies have mainly investigated individual technologies, adoption barriers, or organisational capability factors, without systematically identifying and prioritising the comprehensive set of people, organisational, technological, and infrastructure attributes that enable effective Industry 4.0-enabled OSH management in MMC. This study addresses this gap by identifying, validating, and prioritising the key attributes for effective Industry 4.0-enabled OSH management in MMC using a four-stage methodological approach comprising SLR, expert verification, Delphi method, and voting analytic hierarchy process (VAHP). Through a combination of systematic literature review (SLR) and expert verification, 21 attributes were identified and grouped into four clusters: people, organisation, technology, and infrastructure. The 21 identified and validated attributes were then ranked by a group of experts through a two-round Delphi survey. Following this, the weights and importance of attributes were determined using the voting analytical hierarchy process (VAHP). The results indicate that organisation and people clusters achieved the highest relative priorities; Management support, workforce competence, and technology acceptance were identified as the highest-priority attributes. These findings reveal a sociotechnical hierarchy in which organisational and human capabilities are prioritised above technological and infrastructural capabilities, suggesting successful Industry 4.0-enabled transformation for OSH improvement depends more on social-subsystem capability than on technology deployment alone. © 2026 The Author(s).

Authors: Xiang R.; Deng S.; Wang F.
Author full names: Xiang, Rongrong (59145700000); Deng, Shengli (36968080200); Wang, Fan (56380796500)
Title: Evolution and lifecycle mapping of research methods based on the Boston Matrix in library and information science from 1995 to 2025
Abstract: Developing an evolution framework for research methods is essential for advancing Library and Information Science (LIS), but existing research method schemas remain fragmented and limited. This study proposes an automated framework combining AI-driven methods to mine, classify, and a temporal analysis based on the Boston Matrix to map the lifecycles of research methods. Using a comprehensive dataset of 31,913 articles from 21 LIS journals (1995–2025) as a validation corpus, the framework integrates semantic clustering for bottom-up entity extraction with generative top-down ontology mapping. This approach dynamically maps methods into a four-stage lifecycle schema: mainstream, emerging, marginalized, and mature, revealing distinct evolutionary trajectories and the broader computational turn within LIS. Validated through quantitative threshold testing and qualitative evaluation, the proposed framework significantly reduces manual coding subjectivity and enhances replicability. By empirically comparing the subfields of librarianship and information science, this study accounts for inherent thematic variations and uncovers their distinct paces of methodological adoption. Ultimately, this study offers a robust automated framework for longitudinal methodological tracking, theoretically demonstrating how diverse AI-driven and traditional methods synergistically coevolve and assume distinct scholarly roles within the emerging AI4Science paradigm. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Han L.; Qiao Y.; Jia F.; Zhao Y.; Jia C.
Title: RumorGAL: Graph-anchored LLM for domain-generalized rumor detection
Abstract: Rumor detection models must remain robust to breaking events that are unseen during training. Although large language models (LLMs) offer strong generalization potential, their text-centric nature makes them vulnerable to spurious textual patterns in noisy social media discussions and leaves them without explicit awareness of how rumors propagate through conversation threads. To address these limitations, we propose RumorGAL, a graph-anchored LLM framework for domain-generalized rumor detection. The framework first employs a graph neural network (GNN) to derive graph-anchored structural prefixes from the propagation graph, providing structural guidance for the LLM. It then identifies high-quality textual evidence from noisy discussions through an evidence density-guided mining strategy. Finally, a hierarchical reasoning mechanism organizes both the structural prefixes and textual evidence into a unified reasoning process, enabling the LLM to ground its predictions in both propagation patterns and informative content. Across the three transfer settings, RumorGAL achieves robust performance, improving average accuracy over the strongest baseline, zero-shot GPT-4.1, by 5.27 percentage points under the domain generalization setting. When compared with domain adaptation methods, it surpasses the best domain adaptation method in two out of three tasks, with improvements of 3.1 and 0.5 percentage points in F1 score for the rumor class, respectively. These findings suggest that an LLM-as-primary, GNN-as-auxiliary design, which couples structure-aware guidance with evidence-grounded reasoning, is a promising approach to robust and interpretable rumor detection. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Muthia A.; Utari D.; Soesilo T.E.B.
Title: Environmental health conditions associated with childhood stunting during the first 1000 days of life
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Child stunting is increasingly recognized not only as a nutritional disorder but also as a complex environmental health issue. Household environmental determinants, particularly safe potable water and advanced sanitation infrastructure, exert a fundamental influence on minimizing children's susceptibility to environmental health hazards that compromise linear growth trajectories. Using the transtheoretical model as a behavioral framework, the study objectives were to examine how household environmental conditions, including access to improved drinking water and sanitation, together with maternal environmental health-related behaviors, are associated with child stunting during the first 1,000 days of life in Indonesia. METHODS: This cross-sectional study used nationally representative data from the fifth wave of the Indonesian Family Life Survey. Maternal behaviors related to nutrition, healthcare utilization, and environmental conditions were operationalized as proxies for advanced stages of behavioral change. Child stunting was defined using height-for-age z-scores based on the World Health Organization Child Growth Standards. A binary logistic regression model was utilized to evaluate the multivariate associations linking maternal behavioral patterns, socio-environmental covariates, and socio-demographic indicators to the latent risk of linear growth retardation in children. FINDINGS: The prevalence of stunting among children aged 0 to 23 months was 30.32 percent. Low birth weight and higher birth order significantly increased the odds of stunting. Maternal behaviors reflecting progression to the action and maintenance stages were protective, including routine antenatal care attendance, with an odds ratio of 0.642, and delivery assisted by a skilled birth attendant, with an odds ratio of 0.707. Findings indicate that higher maternal educational attainment, improved sanitation facilities, and safe drinking water sources significantly decreased the likelihood of stunting. In contrast, maternal under nutrition elevated the associated risk by 26.5 percent. CONCLUSION: Household environmental conditions constitute fundamental determinants of child stunting during the first 1,000 days of life. Maternal progression toward advanced stages of stunting prevention behavior, reinforced by adequate health services and enabling environments, plays a critical role in reducing stunting during the first 1,000 days of life. The findings underscore the efficacy of the transtheoretical model as a robust conceptual paradigm for mitigating childhood stunting. By integrating maternal behavioral stages of change with healthcare access and environmental determinants, the research delineates a nuanced, stage-sensitive and contextually grounded architecture for analyzing early childhood growth dynamics. © 2027 The author(s). Title: Prioritizing resilience criteria and indicators in urban disadvantaged areas using the Best-Worst Method (BWM)
Abstract: Urban disadvantaged areas are highly vulnerable to natural hazards due to physical, social, economic, and institutional deficiencies. These areas-such as historic residential area, decayed residential areas, informal settlements, and social housing-experience distinct challenges that necessitate tailored resilience strategies. Considering Iran's high hazard proneness, strengthening resilience in such areas is an urgent priority. Existing resilience literature often adopts a generalized, city-wide perspective, lacking the granularity for effective local-level resource allocation in diverse disadvantaged areas. This study aims to identify and prioritize resilience criteria and indicators across the four types of disadvantaged areas. A comprehensive literature review extracted potential resilience criteria, refined and validated using the Delphi method with 16 experts engaged via snowball sampling. The Best-Worst Method (BWM), an MCDM approach, weighted and ranked criteria for each area type. Results show economic capacity is most critical in informal settlements. Physical-environmental aspects (building quality, infrastructure) dominate historical and decayed areas. Institutional dimensions (governance, accountability, policy support) are most influential in social housing resilience. Cross-area comparison reveals shared and context-specific determinants, underscoring the need for integrated, area-sensitive resilience planning. Findings offer a framework for urban planners to prioritize targeted interventions, balancing physical upgrades with social empowerment, economic capacity building, and institutional strengthening for sustainable and inclusive resilience. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Lemmens A.
Title: Algorithmic fairness as a human–technology interaction problem
Abstract: Algorithms shape high-stakes decisions across society. While promising efficiency, algorithms also raise fairness concerns. This article proposes that algorithmic fairness is best understood as a human–technology interaction problem rather than a purely technical challenge. Algorithms can reproduce human biases, amplify them through feedback loops, or create new forms of unfairness through objectives, proxies, and seemingly neutral variables. Yet they can make decision processes more explicit, disparities more visible, and actively mitigate discrimination. Fairness depends not only on statistical properties but also on how algorithms are designed, used and experienced by those affected by their decisions. This article therefore offers an interdisciplinary perspective that integrates insights from social justice, psychology, computer science, judgment and decision-making, and management. © 2026 The Author

Authors: Chen J.; Xia S.; Ma Z.
Title: The role of attention and norm perception in online comments’ impact on attitudes toward sunscreen: An eye-tracking approach
Abstract: Social media platforms have become a major source of health information, where user-generated comments often shape attitudes toward health behaviors. Yet, the mechanisms underlying these effects remain unclear. This study examines the role of selective attention and perceived norms in the influence of online comments on attitudes toward sunscreen use. Using a between-subject eye-tracking experiment (N = 177), participants viewed a simulated YouTube live-stream video promoting sunscreen misinformation accompanied by either pro- or anti-sunscreen comments. Attention to comments was measured objectively (time viewed, fixation counts) and subjectively (self-reported attention). Results reveal that prior attitudes and behaviors predict selective attention in distinct ways: individuals with more positive attitudes attended more to pro-sunscreen comments, whereas more frequent sunscreen use was associated with more attention to anti-sunscreen comments. Mediation analyses indicate that attention to comments influences perceived norms differently across conditions. In the pro-sunscreen condition, greater attention predicted stronger perceived proximal network norms, which were strongly associated with attitude change. In contrast, in the anti-sunscreen condition, attention predicted weaker perceived social media norms but did not alter proximal norms. Across models, changes in proximal network norms were the most robust predictor of attitude change. Findings highlight the importance of examining selective attention to better understand online comment effects and reveal nuanced normative pathways. The study advances selective exposure and social norm literature in online comment contexts and underscores the value of eye-tracking for objectively measuring visual attention to online comments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Local Knowledge for Ecological Restoration: Motivations and Barriers in Urban Protected Areas in Mexico
Abstract: Local knowledge is recognized as an important part of ecological restoration, and local communities have become more actively involved in recent years. Because participants hold diverse worldviews, their experiences can support ecological restoration. This study explored motivations and barriers to restoration based on the experiences of local participants in urban protected areas in the Valley of Mexico. We collected data through a survey and interviews. Local participants in restoration were mainly motivated by nature conservation and air purification. The main barriers to restoration were drought and fires. Participants’ restoration goals varied and were less aligned with protected-area objectives. Additionally, more experienced participants were more likely to identify restoration goals than less experienced participants. Overall, participants acquired knowledge through experience and undertook diverse efforts to address constraints. This suggests that learning from restoration activities, as a form of local knowledge, is important for identifying context-based barriers. From a socio-ecological perspective, this research discusses the need to establish context-based ecosystem targets and shared goals among stakeholders, as well as the importance of local knowledge for improving ecological restoration. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Authors: Dehghani A.; Salaripour A.
Title: From design attributes to social life: Modelling conviviality in urban underground spaces
Abstract: From being infrastructure utilities, urban underground spaces (UUS) have developed into multipurpose public spaces that combine commercial, cultural, and transit functions. While their technical and spatial contributions to compact urbanism are evident, their capacity to foster conviviality, the experiential quality of inclusiveness, sociability, and shared belonging, is less understood. This study develops and empirically tests a conceptual framework that operationalizes conviviality in UUS by linking seven spatial-perceptual dimensions (safety and security, identity and meaning, accessibility, functionality, environmental comfort, aesthetics, and structure and form) to behavioral mediators of willingness to use and social interaction, culminating in perceived conviviality. Using the Theatre-Shahr underground complex in Tehran as a case study, data were collected through structured surveys and analyzed via Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that although environmental factors generally have a positive indirect effect on perceived conviviality, social interaction emerges as the primary mechanism shaping conviviality in urban underground spaces, while willingness to use plays only a complementary and limited mediating role in this process. Among the environmental factors, accessibility, environmental comfort, and safety and security show the strongest effects. In contrast, some variables, particularly identity and meaning and structure and form, do not demonstrate statistically significant effects in certain pathways. These findings suggest that planning and design strategies for urban underground spaces should prioritize environmental qualities that support social interaction, to enhance perceived conviviality. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Peterson B.
Title: Aemilia Lanyer and the Body
Abstract: Scholars have consistently turned to representations of the body in Salve Deus Rex Judaeorum to consider issues of genre, religion, gender, race, social status, poetics, and poetic authority. Yet, despite scholars- frequent attention to topics of corporeality and embodiment, “the body” has not been recognized in Lanyer studies as a central subject of inquiry. The introduction to this special issue surveys how the corpus naturale has undergirded Lanyer scholarship over the past fifty years. Whereas previous studies have identified the body-s importance at discrete moments or in specific mechanisms in Lanyer-s poetry, this introduction emphasizes how the form and content of Salve Deus is fundamentally rooted in the body and bodily experience. This special issue, thus, reconceptualizes the categories of “women writers” and “women-s writing,” highlighting how we might consider the female body not as a historical identity but rather as a formal model in early modern English literature. Title: Learn AI with AI: Designing conversational agents to support older adults in learning about AI
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: Older adults are motivated to develop AI literacy and consider it important. Prior research suggests that conversational agents can support older adults’ AI literacy learning by simplifying AI concepts and providing interactive learning experiences. However, little is known about how such agents should be designed to address the learning challenges older adults face. To address this, we interviewed nine older adults to explore their challenges and identify design opportunities. Findings revealed affective barriers related to confidence and engagement, emphasizing the importance of peer-like characteristics in agents, such as reciprocal knowledge sharing. Guided by these insights, we designed a peer-like agent and compared it with a website and an assistant agent in a between-subjects study with 45 older adults learning about deepfakes. Results showed that the peer agent fostered higher engagement and supported confidence more than the others. We conclude with design recommendations for conversational agents to support older adults’ AI learning. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Bansah K.J.
Title: Mechanization, gender, and livelihoods in artisanal and small-scale mining: a technofeminist political ecology perspective
Abstract: This study examines the gendered impacts of mechanization in artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM), a sector increasingly shaped by excavators, washing plants, motorized pumps, trommels, and leaching techniques. Drawing on field investigations in mining communities in southwestern Ghana, the study shows that technological adoption in ASM is not gender neutral. While mechanization has improved efficiency and productivity, it has simultaneously displaced women from core mining activities where they historically played essential economic roles. As a result, women are increasingly relegated to ancillary and informal tasks that generate lower and often unsustainable incomes while exposing them to heightened environmental and health risks. These intersecting experiences show how mechanization can simultaneously produce economic displacement and continued environmental vulnerability for women in ASM. To explain these dynamics, the study develops and applies a Technofeminist Political Ecology (TPE) framework as an original analytical lens. Integrating insights from technofeminism and feminist political ecology, TPE conceptualizes technology not as a neutral tool of progress but as a social and political force that restructures labor, redistributes environmental risk, and reconfigures gendered vulnerabilities within extractive economies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Reconstructing the Life History of Double Perforated Ivory Beads from the Swabian Aurignacian: A Combined Traceological and Experimental Approach
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Aurignacian ivory beads provide valuable insights into ivory-working techniques, labour investment, production organisation, and the symbolic behaviour of Early Upper Palaeolithic people. Although decades of research have led to a detailed understanding of the chaîne opératoire of these iconic beads, systematic approaches for identifying and interpreting manufacturing- and use-related traces remain limited. Using 74 double perforated ivory beads (DPIBs) from Archaeological Horizon IV at Hohle Fels Cave as a case study, we integrate taphonomic, typological, morphometric, and traceological analyses with experimental replication to develop an analytical framework for reconstructing the manufacture and use of archaeological ivory beads. Our results suggest that DPIB production followed a broadly shared production sequence while allowing flexibility in the order and execution of individual manufacturing steps. The archaeological evidence indicates that the beads were produced, used, and discarded on site. Experimental replication further provides a basis for evaluating labour investment and identifying surface modifications associated with manufacture and use. The observed morphological variability may reflect differences in production practices related to variation in skill, individual behaviour, and the involvement of multiple craftspeople. The analytical approach presented here is transferable and can be applied to other archaeological ivory bead assemblages. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Analysis of environmental and social impacts of quarry mining for bridging stakeholder perception gaps–a case study from Padukka, Sri Lanka
Abstract: This study investigates stakeholder perceptions of the environmental and social impacts associated with the China Harbour Aggregate Quarry in the Padukka Division of the Colombo District, Sri Lanka. Despite growing concerns about the impacts of quarrying on host communities, limited empirical evidence exists regarding how different stakeholder groups perceive and experience these impacts in the Sri Lankan context. A mixed-methods case study design integrated qualitative and quantitative approaches to examine stakeholder perspectives. The study involved 31 community members near the quarry, 3 quarry site professionals, and 4 officers from a technical services company, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through semi-structured in-depth interviews with all stakeholder groups and structured questionnaires comprising open- and closed-ended questions administered to community members. Thematic analysis was used to analyze interview and open-ended questionnaire data, while descriptive analysis was applied to closed-ended questionnaire responses. Findings indicate that vibration was the dominant impact, reported by all community participants (100%), with concerns about noise, water dry out, dust, and occasional flyrock events. Community responses revealed high perceived annoyance (93.5%) and opposition to the mining site (87.1%), although all respondents were unwilling to relocate, highlighting sociopsychological constraints. Comparative analysis revealed convergence and divergence between community perceptions and quarry personnel perspectives, with mitigation measures implemented but challenges persisting due to spatial constraints, communication gaps, and disputed compensation claims. The study contributes context-specific evidence on stakeholder perceptions of quarrying impacts and provides practical insights for strengthening community engagement, impact mitigation, and socially responsible quarry management in Sri Lanka. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Old scrap metal recycling management under industrial decarbonization: A comprehensive review
Abstract: Industrial decarbonization is increasing the demand for metals, creating a growing challenge for material supply and may lead to an increase in carbon emissions associated with primary metal production. Old scrap recycling can help address these pressures by supplementing primary metal supply. It may also reduce greenhouse gas emissions when recycled metals effectively substitute for primary metal production. An effective management of old metal recycling thus takes a central role in improving the potential of old scrap processes from collection, recovery, and reintegration into the production systems. This study systematically reviews 92 articles published between 2000 and 2023 to examine the development of management research on old scrap metal recycling and its relevance to industrial decarbonization. The review shows that contemporary research varies substantially across metals relevant to decarbonization and across different domains ofrecycling management. Sustainability implications are also unevenly examined, with environmental implications receiving greater attention than economic and social implications. Methodologically, existing studies offer valuable insights into various components and levels of recycling systems; however, there is still a need for better integration of multi-level processes and dynamic feedback. Future research on old scrap recycling should align more closely with decarbonization needs, diversify management interventions and their combinations, broaden economic and social assessment, strengthen integrated sustainability evaluation, and advance multi-level dynamic modeling. Policy development should further promote collection of valuable old scrap, its responsible and traceable recycling, and improve energy and emissions performance of recycling activities. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Teng J.; Cho S.
Title: Mental imagery and visuospatial processing in visual communication design education: Examining relationships with creative performance and academic achievement in university students
Abstract: This study investigated the relationships among mental imagery, visuospatial processing, creative performance, and academic achievement in university visual communication design students. A sample of 156 undergraduate students majoring in visual communication design completed the Mental Imagery Test (MIT), Raven's Standard Progressive Matrices (RSPM), and Torrance Tests of Creative Thinking (TTCT), while their academic performance in design studio, typography, digital imaging, and visual theory courses was assessed through course grades. Results indicated significant positive correlations between mental imagery abilities and both creative performance and academic achievement across all design-related courses. Visuospatial processing, operationalized here as figural-inductive visuospatial reasoning, partially mediated the relationship between mental imagery and academic performance in design studio and digital imaging courses, while creative self-efficacy emerged as an additional mediator for typography performance. Gender differences were minimal, with males showing slight advantages only in spatial transformation tasks. These findings underscore the importance of developing mental imagery and visuospatial skills within visual communication curricula and suggest that targeted cognitive training interventions may enhance both creative output and academic success in design education contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
