Authors: Damalas C.A.
Title: The role of personal norms in farmers’ safety practices: Protective equipment use in pesticide handling
Abstract: Farmers’ use of personal protective equipment (PPE) during pesticide handling has been studied, but factors shaping this behavior can vary considerably. Farmers’ intention to use PPE in pesticide handling and observed protective behavior were studied using the norm activation model (NAM). Data analysis was conducted using descriptive statistics, Spearman’s correlation, multiple linear regression, and binary logistic regression models. Almost fifty-nine (58.9%) of farmers showed unsafe behavior regarding PPE use. Intention to use PPE was low (mean: 2.415 on a 1–5 scale) and positively associated with observed protective behavior. Regarding NAM constructs, farmers showed moderate personal norms (mean: 3.027), slightly lower awareness of the consequences associated with not using PPE (mean: 2.888), and relatively weak ascription of responsibility (mean: 2.741) for reducing those consequences. Personal norms significantly predicted both intention and observed protective behavior (P < 0.01). In turn, awareness of consequences and ascription of responsibility were significant positive predictors of personal norms, supporting the applicability of NAM for understanding PPE-related behavior. Further analysis indicated that personal norms were negatively associated with age and farm size (P < 0.01), suggesting weaker norms among older farmers and those managing larger farms. Conversely, education was positively correlated with personal norms (P < 0.01). Overall, personal norms played a central role in shaping PPE use, with their relationship influenced by recognition of the risks of non-use and acceptance of responsibility for mitigating them. Enhancing communication about pesticide risks and emphasizing the importance of PPE may help strengthen personal norms and promote safer PPE-related practices. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Managing Perils at Sea: a diagnostic analysis of occupational hazards among small-scale fishers in India’s southern coasts
Abstract: Marine fishing is a high-risk occupation that sustains the livelihoods of coastal communities worldwide. This study highlights the occupational hazards associated with marine fishing, drawing on an empirical case study of the high-intensity, multi-day offshore fishing sector in southern India. Following the FAO/ILO/IMO joint framework on occupational health and safety of fishers, our research revealed significant deficiencies in the adoption of safety devices, communication technologies, and navigation systems by sample fishers in the study areas. These gaps, compounded by weak regulatory enforcement and low insurance coverage, pose substantial risks, exacerbated by climate change. The findings underscore the need for targeted interventions—including awareness campaigns, training, and financial aid—to foster a robust safety culture and mitigate economic barriers, leading to improved fisher safety and well-being in the coastal regions of India. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: “Feminine” strengths, “masculine” costs: Rethinking gender gaps in negotiation research
Abstract: The impact of gender on negotiation outcomes has been an important aspect of the negotiation literature for decades. This literature has primarily focused on “masculine” attributes, such as assertiveness, as ideal negotiator characteristics, manifesting in gender research focused on men's economic advantages in negotiations, to the detriment of both women and men. Yet recent research has begun to examine gender gaps in “feminine” attributes, highlighting women's strengths in negotiations, particularly in relational outcomes. Future work is needed to fully unpack these results, understand the impact of intersecting identities, and explore partner effects. We also emphasize the importance of replication efforts and conducting this research in naturalistic settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Narratives of workplace conflict: A mixed-methods analysis of HEXACO and Dark Triad personality predictors
Abstract: Workplace conflicts are common, yet most evidence links personality to broad conflict management styles rather than to how concrete episodes unfold. We used a mixed-methods design to examine whether Dark Triad and HEXACO traits predict the content and course of real conflicts. Hungarian employees ( N = 318, 31.1% male, 68.9% female, M age = 35.24, SD = 10.34) completed personality measures and provided written narratives of a workplace conflict in which they were directly involved. Personality traits were more strongly related to how conflicts unfolded and were interpreted than to their structural features, such as who was involved or what triggered the conflict. Interpersonal traits from the HEXACO model showed the most consistent associations with conflict dynamics, emotional responses, and relationship outcomes. Dark Triad traits showed selective but limited associations with conflict processes, offering little evidence for broad predictive advantages beyond broader personality dimensions. Overall, the findings suggest that workplace conflict is not only enacted but also interpreted through the lens of personality, highlighting the importance of integrating dispositional and situational perspectives in research on organizational conflict. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Water footprint of low-tech digesters for bioenergy recovery from waste
Abstract: This study aimed to assess the water footprint of plastic tubular digesters to treat organic waste and recover bioenergy. Different scenarios in a small-scale dairy farm in Colombia were considered: i) scenario without the digester in which cow manure is piled up, and dairy wastewater is directly discharged into the environment, ii) scenario with a plastic tubular digester treating cow manure, and iii) scenario with a plastic tubular digester co-digesting cow manure with dairy wastewater. Results showed that, in terms of water quality degradation, the co-digestion scenario exhibited impacts 10% to 45% lower than those of the other scenarios, depending on the impact category. In terms of water scarcity, the co-digestion scenario exhibited approximately 10% lower water scarcity than the other scenarios, which showed a similar water scarcity footprint. This indicates that implementing plastic tubular digesters, even under mono-digestion conditions, does not worsen water availability. These benefits are greater if co-digestion of different agri-food waste is applied, since it helps preserve water quality by valorising the intrinsic water content of food wastewater. It also decreases environmental impacts by reducing synthetic fertiliser use through the production of a higher-quality digestate. Overall, plastic tubular digesters provide a low-water footprint alternative to the direct discharge and uncontrolled storage of livestock waste and food-production wastewater in small-scale farms. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Robust decision-making for minimizing building life-cycle GHG emissions and costs under uncertainties: Application to office buildings in China's cold regions
Abstract: Uncertainties can substantially affect building life-cycle assessment (LCA) results. Existing optimization methods commonly adopt certainty assumptions and limited variables without sufficient robustness interpretation. This study develops a probabilistic decision-making framework for minimizing life-cycle greenhouse gas emissions (LCGHG) and life-cycle costs (LCC) under deterministic, mean, and 90th percentile (P90) risk metrics, which is applied to multistorey office building design in China's cold regions. The life-cycle performances of nine stock-derived form prototypes, combined with envelopes, HVAC, and rooftop photovoltaics, are explored under uncertain future climate, grid mix, discount rates, and component lifespans. Pareto-diagrams show that solutions obtained from different robustness criteria fall into two performance clusters mainly distinguished by HVAC energy sources. Yet deterministic and mean-based Pareto-fronts demonstrate materially higher upper-tail values of LCGHG and/or LCC. P90-based optimal ground-source heat pump solutions achieve LCGHG(90%) of 22.79–23.57 kg CO2-eq./(m2·a) and LCC(90%) of 4558–5518 CNY/m2, whereas air-source heat pump solutions reduce costs by approximately 50% but increase emissions by about 30%. Within each cluster, building forms further differentiate performances, while envelopes and photovoltaics fine-tune outcomes. Design ranking consistency and performance distributional analyses indicate that solutions with lower P90 values generally correspond to lower medians and narrower variations. Moreover, P90-optimal solutions show similar operational emissions with trade-offs between equipment-related embodied emissions and costs. Sensitivity analysis identifies grid mix and HVAC lifespans as key drivers of LCGHG uncertainty, whereas discount rates and HVAC lifespans govern LCC variability. Although numerical findings are specific to the case, the proposed workflow and design guidance are transferable to other contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Associations of job satisfaction, AI literacy, innovation capability, and innovation behavior among nursing interns: A cross-sectional study
Abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming increasingly embedded in clinical care, decision support, and nursing education. Nursing interns therefore need not only foundational AI literacy, including the capacity to appraise AI-generated information critically and ethically, but also the capability to identify and implement improvements in care. How work-related experience and these capability-related factors are associated with innovation behavior during clinical internship remains important for nursing education. Aims: To examine the associations among job satisfaction, AI literacy, innovation capability, and innovation behavior among nursing interns. Design: A cross-sectional study. Participants: 349 final-year nursing interns. Methods: Data were collected between November 2024 and February 2025 from a convenience sample of final-year nursing interns from one medical university undertaking clinical rotations at five tertiary teaching hospitals in China. A latent-variable structural equation model was used to estimate a theory-informed sequence linking job satisfaction, AI literacy, innovation capability, and innovation behavior. Innovation behavior was modeled using its seven items. Bias-corrected bootstrapping with 5000 resamples was used to estimate direct and indirect associations. Results: The model demonstrated acceptable fit: χ2/df = 2.81, CFI = 0.947, TLI = 0.935, RMSEA = 0.072 (90% CI: 0.065–0.080), and SRMR = 0.027. The indirect association through AI literacy and innovation capability was significant (β = 0.053, 95% CI [0.008, 0.089], p = 0.018) and represented 45.0% of the total indirect association. The indirect association through AI literacy alone was significant (β = 0.033, p = 0.043), whereas the direct association between job satisfaction and innovation behavior was non-significant (β = −0.013, p = 0.682). Conclusions: In this sample, AI literacy and innovation capability showed stronger associations with innovation behavior than did job satisfaction. Job satisfaction showed comparatively modest associations with the other study variables. Longitudinal and intervention research is needed to determine how these factors develop and whether educational approaches improve innovation-related outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: A latent counterfactual disentanglement framework for implicit hate speech detection
Abstract: Implicit hate speech often conceals hateful intent through semantic camouflage, such as sarcasm and metaphor, causing core toxicity features to remain hidden beneath the surface text. Existing models tend to jointly encode core toxicity and camouflage style during feature extraction, thereby leading to spurious decision shortcuts dominated by camouflage-style cues. To alleviate this problem, this paper approaches implicit hate speech detection from the perspective of camouflage-style removal and proposes a latent counterfactual disentanglement (LCD) framework for implicit hate speech detection. Specifically, LCD decomposes textual latent representations into a core toxicity subspace and a camouflage style subspace through causal feature disentanglement. It further constructs counterfactually augmented representations using a feature-level multiple counterfactual intervention mechanism, thereby reducing the model’s dependence on camouflage style. Meanwhile, a latent semantic reconstruction module is introduced to mitigate the risk of information loss during disentanglement. Experimental results on three challenging public benchmark datasets, namely IHC, SBIC, and DYNA, show that LCD achieves Macro-F1 scores of 79.20%, 91.09%, and 83.43%, respectively. Further experiments and visualization analyses demonstrate that LCD can reduce the leakage of label-related information into the camouflage style branch and improve prediction consistency under style perturbations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: GenAI-supported internal feedback intervention for writing improvement: The roles of evaluative judgment and student-AI interaction in a cluster-randomized experimental study
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) enables scalable feedback provision. While GenAI has commonly been examined as a source of external feedback, its role in supporting internal feedback remains underexplored. The study involved 368 students (experimental: n = 169; control: n = 199) at a university in China. Data included pre- and post-test writing scores, comparison sheets, and student-AI interaction logs. Students in the GenAI-supported internal feedback condition achieved higher adjusted post-test writing performance than those in the control group. Within the experimental group, evaluative judgment (a cognitive indicator) and prompt complexity (a behavioral indicator of interaction quality) were more strongly associated with better writing performance, whereas the contribution of interaction quantity was weaker. While both quantity and quality of student-AI interactions increased over time, evaluative judgment showed limited development across the intervention. The findings suggest that GenAI can support internal feedback processes within a student-centered learning framework, while behavioral engagement with GenAI may develop without corresponding growth in evaluative judgment. Title: Culturally responsive cognitive-behavioral therapy for black populations: a scoping review

Abstract: This scoping review aimed to map and synthesize the contributions of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) to culturally responsive clinical practice addressing racial and ethnic issues, with an emphasis on the mental health of Black populations. The review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute and PRISMA-ScR guidelines and included systematic searches across multiple databases and complementary sources, resulting in 22 included publications. Conceptual heterogeneity emerged regarding how the cultural contextualization of CBT is defined and implemented, ranging from structured adaptations of standard protocols to culturally responsive therapeutic stances integrated into case conceptualization and clinical interactions. The most frequently reported intervention domains included cognitive restructuring, coping skills training, psychoeducation, and engagement in valued activities, often accompanied by explicit validation of racism-related experiences. The literature emphasized the centrality of culturally responsive therapeutic relationships and identified structural racism and healthcare mistrust as key barriers to access and engagement. Although the field demonstrates growing methodological and clinical maturity, theoretical fragmentation and the absence of integrative conceptual models remain significant gaps, underscoring the need for further empirical research in diverse sociocultural settings. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive. Authors: Suh S.
Title: Is it abundance or scarcity? Reassessing freshwater resources and civil war onset (1960–2023)
Abstract: Popular policy arguments indicate freshwater scarcity leads to civil wars. Yet, studies are unclear about this relationship with arguments based on scarcity, abundance, and human adaptation competing. In this article, I clarify this debate by conducting survival analysis with global data from 1960 to 2023. I construct a short-term freshwater shock variable – separated by positive (flood) and negative (drought) – that addresses the methodological limitations of the literature. My results show that both positive and negative shocks increase the likelihood of civil wars but with different temporal patterns. Negative shocks have immediate same-year positive association with conflict hazard, whereas positive shocks have a one-year delay. Interaction models further indicate that this relationship is not moderated by level of democracy, agriculture-dependence, or ethnic division contexts, while arid conditions amplify the hazard from negative shocks. Conclusions indicate policy must accentuate freshwater concerns to mitigate potential civil wars, as climate change brings drastic freshwater crises. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Instructional approaches and content knowledge in teaching computational thinking: A large-scale study
Abstract: With the ongoing digitalization of society, educational curricula increasingly emphasize the development of learners' computational thinking. Yet, there is little consensus on how best to achieve this goal in classroom practice. This study investigates patterns in teachers' use of instructional approaches to foster computational thinking, focusing on approaches identified in the literature as effective: problem-based learning, cooperative learning, and direct instruction. Using data from the 2023 cycle of the International Computer and Information Literacy Study in Flanders, the analysis focuses on lower secondary school teachers teaching eighth-grade students. Latent profile analysis is used to identify teacher profiles. Three profiles are identified, distinguished primarily by the frequency rather than the type of instructional approaches employed. Direct instruction is most prevalent, though often combined with problem-based and cooperative learning. The study further examines the extent to which teachers' computational thinking content knowledge accounts for variation in their use of specific instructional approaches. To address this, a regression analysis is conducted. The findings reveal a significant negative association between teachers' computational thinking content knowledge and the use of problem-based and cooperative learning approaches, suggesting that teachers with higher levels of content knowledge tend to apply these approaches less frequently. No significant relationship is found between content knowledge and the use of direct instruction. Title: XAI in the human-agent-environment loop: how do task, explanation strategy, and AI literacy shape user engagement?

Abstract: This study explored how tasks, explanation strategies, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) literacy levels collectively influenced human interaction with Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in a single-target prediction task. Using a within-subjects experiment with 70 participants, the study examined combinations of four AI-assisted prediction tasks—varying in prediction target (human-related vs. human-unrelated) and stakes (high vs. low)—and six explanation strategies (model-based, comparison-based, input influence-based, sensitivity-based, demographic-based, and case-based), across participants with varying AI literacy (AIL). Results showed that explanation strategies had the most significant impact on human-XAI interaction in most aspects, especially on prediction change with XAI assistance. Additionally, explanation strategies significantly affected all perception and experience indicators, except for curiosity. Compared to the scope of explanations, the content provided by strategies had a greater influence on user predictions. Strategies with trends and ratios, such as case-based (CA) and demographic-based (DE), were more effective. Conversely, strategies lacking trends and ratios, such as model-based (MO) and comparison-based (CO), were generally the least effective. For users, AI literacy influenced all performance metrics, especially re-prediction time. Higher AI literacy was significantly associated with longer re-prediction time. Tasks had moderate impacts on the XAI interaction process, especially experience measures. In the human-related tasks (recidivism and shipwreck survival prediction), participants reported lower subjective experience ratings among the tasks examined, particularly regarding perceived justice. In the high-stakes, human-unrelated task (wine quality prediction), participants gave the most favorable experiential ratings among the tasks in the study. Furthermore, second-order effects related to explanation strategies had significant impacts on various metrics. On the one hand, the interaction between explanation strategies and task characteristics influenced prediction changes. Global explanations, such as the input-influence-based (IN) and MO strategies, performed better on human-related tasks than on human-unrelated tasks. In contrast, local explanations, such as the sensitivity-based (SE) and CO strategies, showed the opposite pattern. On the other hand, the impact of explanation strategies on user perception and experience was moderated by AI literacy. Users with lower literacy tended to prefer local explanations, while users with higher literacy preferred global explanations. The content of the XAI explanation significantly affected the quality, while the scope had subtle interactive effects with different tasks and users. These effects with XAI, majorly interpreted through the Elaboration Likelihood model (ELM), provide evidence supporting adaptive XAI within the human-agent-environment loop. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Urbanization through the eyes of a spreading semi-aquatic mammal: contributions of multi-scale analysis to management decisions
Abstract: Anthropogenic processes modify the environment, influencing species distribution. In urban settings, wildlife persistence depends on the interaction between landscape patterns, local habitat characteristics, and species-specific traits. Despite habitat fragmentation, many wildlife species manage to adapt and thrive within the urban matrix. An example of this is the coypu (Myocastor coypus), which has increased its presence in urban habitats due to its high ecological plasticity. Although native to Argentina, it is considered one of the most harmful invasive mammals worldwide. Its expansion and population density can impact vegetation and create conflicts with humans. In the conurbano bonaerense, in central Argentina, coypus are frequently associated with gated communities, where they have become increasingly common. This study analyzed the influence of habitat characteristics measured at the microhabitat, macrohabitat, and landscape scales on coypu occurrence, abundance, and use intensity in urban environments of the conurbano bonaerense. Sampling was conducted at 31 sites between 2021 and 2023, covering 7,216.7 km2. Signs of activity were recorded in 397 transects along permanent water bodies, and habitat variables were quantified through field surveys, photointerpretation, and remote sensing using scale-specific spatial extents. The results showed that coypu occurrence, abundance, and use intensity were associated with anthropogenic disturbance, aquatic habitat configuration, and the availability of short herbaceous vegetation. Landscape-scale variables explained most of the variation in the three response variables, although habitat characteristics measured at macro- and microhabitat scales also contributed to explaining species responses. These findings identify habitat characteristics associated with spatial distribution of coypu that can support future conservation initiatives where the species is of conservation interest and management strategies where it generates conflicts. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Wang D.; Sun M.; Li Y.; Liu M.
Title: Co-developmental trajectories of internalizing symptoms and psychotic-like experiences among adolescents: The predictive role of sleep disturbance
Abstract: Background Internalizing symptoms and psychotic-like experiences (PLEs) are common among adolescents. However, few studies have explored the longitudinal co-development of internalizing symptoms and PLEs in this age group. Methods A total of 7529 adolescents (M age at baseline = 13.89 years, SD = 1.34; 50% girls) participated in this three-wave longitudinal study. A parallel-process latent class growth analysis identified joint trajectories of internalizing symptoms and PLEs, and multinomial logistic regression examined the effect of sleep disturbance. Results Three distinct trajectories were identified: a low-risk group (74.0%), a pure-internalizing symptoms group (13.5%), and a chronic co-occurring group (12.5%). After controlling for sample characteristics, negative life events during follow-up, and sleep duration, baseline sleep disturbance was significantly associated with both the pure-internalizing symptoms trajectory (OR = 3.41, 95% CI = 2.84–4.08) and the chronic co-occurring trajectory (OR = 3.69, 95% CI = 3.06–4.46). Conclusions These findings indicate that sleep disturbance independently associated with the heterogeneous co-developmental trajectories of internalizing symptoms and PLEs. Early assessment and treatment of sleep disturbance may be an important strategy for the prevention and intervention of psychopathology development. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Love, faith, and cognitive dissonance in interfaith relationships: A CBT-informed analysis of Indonesian digital narratives on the song Mangu
Source title: Journal of Behavioral and Cognitive Therapy
Abstract: Interfaith relationships in Indonesia involve negotiations among romantic attachment, religious commitment, moral and spiritual identity, family belonging, and sociocultural expectations. Although interfaith relationships have been widely examined from sociological, theological, and legal perspectives, less is known about how these tensions are cognitively, emotionally, and spiritually narrated in naturally occurring digital spaces. This study examined Indonesian YouTube users’ narratives concerning interfaith relationships, religious conversion, hidayah, sociocultural pressure, and separation in comments surrounding the song Mangu by Fourtwnty featuring Charita Utami. An exploratory corpus analysis using Voyant Tools was first conducted on a broader corpus of 16,356 Indonesian-language YouTube comments to identify lexical patterns and support data familiarization. Subsequently, qualitative content analysis was conducted on 51 criterion-selected comments through inductive thematic analysis, followed by a bounded, non-diagnostic CBT-informed interpretation. Five themes were identified: struggles in maintaining interfaith relationships; religious conversion as a pathway to relational and spiritual alignment; sociocultural and familial pressure; hidayah and changes in belief; and firmness of belief followed by relational separation. Across the narratives, similar contexts of religious difference were assigned different meanings and followed by multiple pathways, including continued negotiation, maintenance of separate religious identities, conversion, reconciliation, and separation. A CBT-informed reading suggests that these pathways may be understood through interactions among cognitive appraisal, core and intermediate beliefs, emotional responses, coping processes, and meaning reconstruction. However, conversion, hidayah, and separation were not treated as inherently adaptive, pathological, or clinically verified processes. The study contributes a context-sensitive framework for interpreting digital narratives at the intersection of religion and intimacy and highlights the need for ethically neutral counseling support that addresses intrapersonal, interpersonal, and sociocultural dimensions. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive. Title: A self-supervised approach to malware classification using hybrid VAE-Swin Transformer models
Abstract: Malware detection and classification are critical in cybersecurity, where accurate identification of malware families enhances threat response and mitigation. Despite significant advances in malware image-based classification, challenges such as limited capture of local and global contextual dependencies, loss of spatial information, and high computational complexity continue to hinder robust malware family classification, particularly for diverse and imbalanced datasets. This paper introduces MalVEIT, a hybrid deep Variational Autoencoder (VAE) using an attention mechanism in the bottleneck of the model for malware classification under a self-supervised learning paradigm. Malware binaries are transformed into image representations, where the selected RGB formulation is adopted based on comparative evaluation against grayscale and other channel-construction alternatives. The VAE encoder then compresses these patches into a compact latent representation parameterized by learned mean and variance. Within the bottleneck layer of the VAE, shifted-window based self-attention mechanism is implemented using Swin Transformers for hierarchical feature extraction, enabling effective capture of both local structural patterns and global contextual dependencies. The refined features are sampled and reconstructed through a VAE decoder enforcing Kullback–Leibler divergence regularization to maintain a smooth distribution. The aggregated feature maps are then passed to a fully connected layer for malware family classification. The proposed model is evaluated on six benchmarked datasets, viz., Malimg, Malevis, Big-2015, Blended, Packed PE, and Obfuscation. It consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating robust multi-family malware classification across diverse datasets with data imbalance and outliers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Wassiliwizky E.
Title: What are we measuring when we measure attractiveness?
Abstract: Facial attractiveness ratings are widely used as indicators of mate value and sexual preference in evolutionary aesthetics. Yet recent large-scale evidence reveals a robust Gender Attractiveness Gap (GAP): female faces are rated as more attractive than male faces across cultures, sexual orientations, age groups, and methodological contexts. This structural asymmetry has remained largely invisible despite being embedded in facial-attractiveness datasets for decades. It challenges the assumption that explicit attractiveness ratings map straightforwardly onto sexual desire. Rather, the GAP suggests that attractiveness judgments are outputs of a broader evaluative system in which female appearance occupies a privileged position. This article discusses the conceptual and methodological implications of this finding for measurement, theory construction, and future research on human aesthetic cognition. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Design, development, and evaluation of STI Shield: A multi-chatbot mobile application for sexual health education and behavior change in African young adults
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) remain a significant public health concern among African young adults, driven by limited knowledge, high-risk behaviors, stigma, and inadequate access to care. While mobile health (mHealth) interventions offer potential, many existing tools lack cultural relevance, theoretical grounding, and adaptability. This study presents STI Shield, a multi-chatbot mobile application designed to enhance STI awareness and encourage safer sexual behaviors. The app integrates rule-based and large language model (LLM)-based chatbots to deliver structured education and personalized counseling, drawing on the Health Belief Model and Persuasive System Design principles. A two-phase evaluation involving African participants living both in Africa and outside Africa, comprising pilot and in-the-wild studies, demonstrated high usability and acceptability, strong educational impact, high persuasiveness, and positive shifts in key behavior change determinants. This work contributes to the fields of mHealth, conversational artificial intelligence, and human-computer interaction by offering a novel chatbot-based system model for delivering personalized, culturally relevant, and theory-driven digital health support in under-resourced settings. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Sleep quality and its associated factors among community-dwelling patients with severe mental disorders in Minhang District, Shanghai: A cross-sectional study
Abstract: Background Sleep disturbances are common in severe mental disorders (SMD), but community-based epidemiological data in China are scarce. This study examined the prevalence and correlates of poor sleep quality and tested the indirect pathways of psychological distress in the association between social support and sleep. Methods Using 2022 baseline data from a community survey in Shanghai, we included 3797 SMD patients (mean age 54.9 years; 51.6% female; 64.1% schizophrenia-spectrum). Sleep quality was assessed with the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI; poor defined as >5), social support with PSSS, anxiety with GAD-7, and depression with PHQ-9. Hierarchical multivariable regression, bootstrap mediation (5000 resamples), and K-means clustering were applied. Results Mean PSQI was 5.14, and 39.3% had poor sleep. The full model explained 27.8% of variance. PHQ-9 was the strongest independent correlate of poor sleep. Comorbidity (OR = 1.48, 95% CI: 1.23–1.77) and lower household income were associated with higher odds of poor sleep, whereas no hospitalization history was associated with lower odds of poor sleep. The indirect effect via depression accounted for 81.4% of the total association between social support and sleep, while that via anxiety accounted for 57.8%; the PSSS×PHQ-9 interaction was significant. Three sleep phenotypes were identified: mild (36.1%, mean PSQI 2.7), moderate (43.4%, mean 4.8), and severe (20.5%, mean 10.2), with PHQ-9 as the strongest discriminator. Conclusions Poor sleep is highly prevalent in community SMD patients. Depression appears central in the indirect pathway from social support to sleep. Integrating depression management, social support enhancement, and phenotype-based stratification warrants further investigation to improve sleep. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: Aligning risk frameworks with fieldwork realities: extending Rasmussen’s model to scientific research settings
Abstract: Scientific fieldwork is an essential component of research across many academic disciplines. Fieldwork entails numerous risks, ranging from interpersonal to environmental risks, and can often result in physical and mental injury or illness. Despite these potential harms, standardized frameworks for understanding, managing, and responding to incidents in fieldwork remain underdeveloped. A limited understanding of incident causation in fieldwork contexts compounds this gap. In this article we propose that fieldwork, like other workplaces, operates as a complex socio-technical system in which people, cultural beliefs, governance, equipment, and the environment interact to create both safe and unsafe outcomes. To better understand the scientific fieldwork system, we conducted four focus groups to identify the people and institutions that constitute a fieldwork system and to characterize how these actors are organized within hierarchical levels. Through these sessions, we developed a classificatory scheme of variables that together influence safety outcomes. In total, 91 different actors across seven hierarchical levels and a contextual domain were identified. The resulting ActorMap and associated contributory factors offer a foundational framework for operationalizing safety and risk approaches, such as AcciMapping, in fieldwork settings. By incorporating these insights, we can enhance training, policy development, and institutional support structures to better equip researchers for the challenges of fieldwork. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: García-Hombrados J.; Novak L.
Title: The economics of abduction marriage: Evidence from Ethiopia
Abstract: A sizable share of marriages in several Asian and African countries are initiated by the man abducting the woman he wishes to wed. In this paper, we use quantitative and qualitative methods to characterize the practice of abduction marriage in Ethiopia. We first present the results from in-depth qualitative interviews with community leaders and abducted women in the Gambella region of Ethiopia to gain a deeper understanding of how the practice functions in these communities. These interviews suggest that abduction is typically used to overcome the refusal of the woman's family. Second, we use Demographic and Health Survey along with ethnographic data to characterize women and ethnic groups affected by this practice in Ethiopia. Finally, we empirically examine the central hypothesis about the persistence of this practice and find evidence consistent with the hypothesis that men often use abduction to improve bargaining power in marriage negotiations and reduce the size of the bride price payment. Specifically, we demonstrate that droughts—a proxy for income shocks in this setting—increase the probability of abduction marriage only for women from ethnic groups that traditionally exchange a bride price. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Childhood adversity and digital deviance: Adverse childhood experiences and offline and online offending among active hackers
Abstract: Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) are consistently associated with emotional dysregulation and externalizing behavior, yet their relevance for technologically mediated forms of deviance remains underexplored. Guided by developmental trauma research and General Strain Theory (GST), this study examines whether cumulative and specific ACE exposures are associated with offline and online offending among active malicious hackers. Data were drawn from an international sample of 238 individuals, spanning 45 countries, identified through Zone-H, a public repository of verified website defacements, ensuring that all participants had engaged in at least one confirmed act of illicit system intrusion. The study proceeded in three stages. First, we documented the prevalence and distribution of ACEs within this population. ACE exposure was high, with a substantial proportion reporting four or more adversities. Second, we tested whether cumulative ACE exposure was associated with violent crime, property crime, and engagement in more serious cyber offending beyond baseline defacement activity. Individuals reporting high ACE exposure exhibited significantly greater odds of all offense types. Third, item-level models assessed whether specific ACE categories demonstrated differential associations with offending outcomes. Emotional abuse demonstrated the most consistent ACE-specific associations across offense domains. These findings suggest that developmental vulnerabilities documented in offline contexts may extend into adult cyber offending populations. By situating malicious hacking within developmental and strain-based frameworks, this study contributes to interdisciplinary research examining how early adversity intersects with digitally mediated environments to shape heterogeneous offending patterns. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Ibrahim M.R.
Title: Optimising construction health and safety training: the role of training design and firm size
Abstract: Background The construction industry is one of the most hazardous sectors globally, responsible for a disproportionate share of work-related injuries and fatalities. Construction health and safety (H&S) training is widely recognised as a critical component for improving workers’ H&S competence and reducing accident rates. Despite extensive investment in training programmes, research indicates that learning effectiveness varies across construction firms and may be associated with differences in training design and organisational context. However, empirical understanding of whether firm size moderates the relationship between specific training design dimensions and learning effectiveness is limited. Objective This study investigated the relationships between training design dimensions (training content relevance, facilitator competence, opportunity for practice, and learning environment) and learning effectiveness in construction H&S training while assessing the moderating role of firm size. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted with 80 construction professionals from medium- and large-scale firms. Data were collected using 5-point Likert scales to measure training design dimensions and learning effectiveness. Correlation analysis, multiple regression analysis, and moderation analysis using PROCESS were performed to test the hypothesised relationships. Results Multiple regression showed that the four training design dimensions jointly explained 64% of the variance in learning effectiveness ( R2 = 0.64, adjusted R2 = 0.62), with all four dimensions showing significant positive associations. Moderation analysis showed that firm size significantly moderated the relationship between training design quality and learning effectiveness (interaction B = 0.19, p = 0.033), with a stronger conditional effect among large firms ( b = 0.62) than medium-sized firms ( B = 0.43). Conclusions This study extends the training effectiveness literature by showing that the relationship between training design quality and learning effectiveness varies according to organisational context, with firm size representing a potential boundary condition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Chen Z.; Hu X.; Liu W.; Shi Y.; Zheng S.
Title: Supply-chain transmission and shared responsibility for multi-gas footprints across Chinese urban agglomerations
Abstract: Urban agglomerations connect the production, consumption, and governance of greenhouse gas emissions through interregional supply chains, yet existing studies often separate footprint accounting, emission drivers, supply-chain transmission, and responsibility sharing. This study examines 18 Chinese urban agglomerations comprising 204 cities using an integrated framework of environmentally extended multiregional input–output analysis (EE-MRIO), exact structural decomposition across all 120 factor-order permutations (SDA), structural path analysis (SPA), multi-gas emission-state diagnostics and a Shapley cooperative game. Consumption-based footprints of carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide and aggregate greenhouse gases were assessed for 2012, 2015 and 2017. Per capita final demand increased emissions across all gases and periods, while the main mitigation source shifted from improvements in resource and emission intensity in 2012–2015 to changes in production structure in 2015–2017. For nitrous oxide, the −51.98% intensity effect in the earlier period was substantially offset by production restructuring and an expansion in final demand. Supply-chain pathways were gas-specific: carbon dioxide and aggregate greenhouse gases were transmitted mainly through electricity–industry–investment chains, whereas methane and nitrous oxide were more closely associated with agriculture, fuel exploitation and waste treatment. In 2017, eastern final demand induced 22.7–36.6% of the corresponding source-side footprints in western China, with the highest share for methane. Strong inter-gas coupling did not necessarily imply coordinated mitigation. Under the baseline Shapley allocation, five leading agglomerations accounted for 50.66% of total responsibility, while cross-scenario tests identified a stable four-agglomeration core and a policy-sensitive boundary. These findings support a differentiated, gas-specific and adaptive framework for shared supply-chain responsibility. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Contextual and temporal determinants of injury severity in electric micromobility: a comparative analysis of E-bikes and E-scooters
Abstract: The rapid adoption of electric micromobility has reshaped urban transport while introducing significant and evolving safety challenges. Despite a growing volume of injury data, existing research has largely examined e-scooters and e-bikes in isolation, and conventional analytical approaches have routinely failed to account for the spatial and temporal structure of injury events. This study provides a comparative analysis of injury patterns and severity determinants among e-scooter and e-bike users in the United States, using 2,413 emergency department cases from the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System for 2021 and 2022. Cases were identified through product-code screening and reproducible narrative-based classification. Injury patterns were examined descriptively, followed by binomial logistic regression incorporating demographic, clinical, behavioral, temporal, and location-context characteristics. Cluster-robust standard errors accounted for dependence within NEISS location groups, while interaction terms examined whether the association between motor-vehicle involvement and severe outcomes varied across injury environments. Title: Clarifying environmental responsibility for consistent absolute environmental sustainability assessment: A global sector-level analysis
Abstract: Absolute Environmental Sustainability Assessment (AESA) aims to determine whether a system operates within its allocated share of Carrying Capacities (CCs). Initial guidelines have been proposed to establish a methodological framework. This paper proposes methodological recommendations to address three key requirements for a consistent implementation of AESA, i.e., i) additivity in the CCs downscaling, ii) no double-counting issues in environmental assessment, and iii) consistency of system boundaries between environmental assessment and downscaling steps. Proposals are based on the concept of environmental responsibility. Three environmental accounting approaches, which consider different types of actors responsible for a system's environmental impacts, are employed. These are the production-based approach (PBA), the consumption-based approach (CBA) and the income-based approach (IBA). Furthermore, identifying the responsible actor makes the CCs allocation step more transparent. The adapted AESA method is implemented across country-level economic sectors using Exiobase, an input-output database. Results obtained using the three accounting approaches and two theories of distributive justice are then compared. Similar to the choice of theory of distributive justice, AESA results are sensitive to the chosen accounting approach. Both are normative choices. Based on these preliminary findings, recommendations and further research perspectives are proposed for the AESA community. Finally, a focus on a single sector makes it possible to explore in further detail the relevance of the proposed recommendations for decision-making. © 2026 The Authors

Title: How do I measure emotion regulation repertoire? Let me count the ways: The sum index, distinct index, diversity index, and latent profiles

Title: Regionalized life cycle assessment of NMC and LFP batteries across China-EU supply chain configurations under the EU Battery Regulation
Abstract: The EU Battery Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 introduces stringent life cycle carbon footprint requirements that are expected to influence the regional organization of battery production. However, the carbon footprint implications of alternative China-EU supply chain configurations remain insufficiently understood. This study develops a regionalized life cycle assessment framework to evaluate the life cycle carbon footprints of lithium nickel‑manganese‑cobalt (NMC) and lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries under alternative regional supply chain configurations between China and the EU. The analysis follows the latest EU methodological guidance and combines proprietary industrial data from leading Chinese electric vehicle (EV) battery manufacturers. The boundary analysis showed that the calculated carbon footprints were sensitive to the life cycle stages included. Under the EU baseline, the carbon footprints of NMC and LFP batteries were 96.2 and 51.6 gCO2e/kWh under the Directive 91/157/EEC-informed reference boundary, 95.9 and 81.3 gCO2e/kWh under the Directive 2006/66/EC-informed reference boundary, and 142.9 and 128.3 gCO2e/kWh under the Regulation (EU) 2023/1542-aligned full life cycle boundary, respectively. Scenario analysis further indicated that regional supply chain reconfiguration can substantially narrow carbon footprint differences relative to Baseline-EU. For NMC batteries, the difference decreased from 59.3 gCO2e/kWh under the export (EX) scenario to 49.3 and 47.7 gCO2e/kWh under the overseas battery production (TB) scenario and partial material pre-processing in the EU (TBM) scenario, respectively. For LFP batteries, the corresponding values decreased from 74.1 to 49.4 and 47.1 gCO2e/kWh. These findings suggest that the regulatory context may encourage supply chain configurations with lower life cycle carbon footprints by altering the regional allocation of production stages. The findings highlight the importance of aligning regional production characteristics with decarbonization potential and provide policy-relevant evidence for coordinated China-EU battery supply chain strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: From black carbon reduction to coordinated fuel adoption on a trans-Arctic shipping corridor
Abstract: Arctic sea ice loss is opening trans-Arctic routes, but black carbon (BC) from conventional marine fuels amplifies climate risks in ice covered environments. This study evaluates whether lower BC fuel pathways can move from environmental advantage to coordinated deployment on a representative 14,000 km Murmansk-Shanghai corridor. The analysis integrates life cycle assessment (LCA), BC emission inventories, life cycle cost analysis (LCC), a resource–environment–economy (REE) evaluation, and a tripartite evolutionary game involving governments, ports, and shipping enterprises. Relative to heavy fuel oil (HFO) and very-low sulfur fuel oil (VLSFO), LNG and methanol reduce modeled onboard BC mass by 93.9% and 79.0%, respectively. Standard 100-year Global Warming Potential (GWP100) values are 64.68 kg CO2-eq per functional unit (FU) for LNG and 70.53 kg for CO2-methanol, compared with 81.61 kg for HFO/VLSFO. Title: Hard-work orientation as an individual difference: Passion and subjective vitality as sequential mechanisms of student engagement
Abstract: Effort has a well-documented dark side: excessive work has been linked to burnout, and persistence after failure to hopelessness. Effort is also an individual difference, in that people vary in how strongly they believe effort is valuable and necessary for achievement. Drawing on self-determination theory, this study asks why an effort-oriented disposition might generate psychological resources rather than deplete them. Passion and subjective vitality were tested as a sequential motivational and energetic process linking hard-work orientation to student engagement, using three-wave time-lagged data from 524 students in northern India. Hard-work orientation was positively associated with passion, subjective vitality, and engagement. Both mediators carried significant indirect associations, and the serial indirect pathway through passion and subjective vitality was also significant. The findings locate the bright side of effort in how effort is regulated rather than in how much of it is expended. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Ecohydrological conceptual models and impact pathway diagrams for identifying and communicating environmental impacts in an arid landscape
Abstract: Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs) are critical for evaluating the potential environmental consequences of proposed developments. However, their effectiveness is often hindered by lengthy, technical, and fragmented documentation that limits accessibility for regulators and interested parties. To address this challenge, we developed an approach that uses ecohydrological conceptual models (ECMs) and impact pathway diagrams (IPDs) to integrate and communicate complex interdisciplinary information more effectively. The approach was applied to a pilot case study in an arid region of South Australia to identify potential ecohydrological impacts associated with mining development. Engagement with interested parties throughout the project using ECMs and IPDs was designed to provide an intuitive and accessible means of exploring development-related impacts, support trust-building and provide a transparent understanding of impacts across multiple stakeholder groups, with visual representations intending to lower participation barriers. Authors: McClanahan W.P.; Dickinson T.
Title: A criminological mixed-methods analysis of university policies and strategies against AI cheating: A case study of novel deviance and cultural lag
Abstract: University policies regarding AI-facilitated cheating are premised on classic criminological notions of rational choice positing that individuals will refrain from actions, such as academic dishonesty, because of the risks of being caught and punished. In the present study, we examine the efficacy of such policies and the applicability of Rational Choice Theory (RCT) to AI-facilitated cheating with a large scale, mixed-methods experiment (N = 3298 college students). In support of RCT, we find that students' perceived likelihood of getting caught and perceived severity of punishment significantly reduced their likelihood of using AI to cheat. However, we do not find that the tested university practices and policies influence students' perceptions of these risks. Our analysis suggests that this is due to the novelty of AI. First, there is a “cultural lag” among AI use and its regulation in society. As such, students’ decisions to use AI to cheat are primarily driven by various personal factors, rather than the situational elements such as school policy. These include their own moral assessments of cheating and their personal definitions of what constitutes cheating with AI. Secondly, as using AI to cheat is a novel form of deviance, there is no consensus on what constitutes a high (low) risk situation. We discuss implications for RCT more broadly and make suggestions for university administrators and instructors for addressing this growing form of academic misconduct. © The Authors

Title: Beyond tasks: Environment and interaction as active components in virtual reality interventions for dementia
Abstract: Dementia presents a major global health challenge, and virtual reality (VR) offers an emerging platform that combines therapeutic potential with engaging human-computer interaction. Research has often emphasized task design or exercise-based training, yet the roles of the environment and interaction within VR interventions remain underexplored. This systematic review synthesized 48 empirical studies published between 2010 and 2024, encompassing 1944 participants across 23 countries. Literature was identified through searches in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, CNKI, and Elsevier, and study quality was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool. Findings indicate that natural, cultural, and personally meaningful environments were linked to reducing anxiety, depression, and behavioral symptoms in individuals with moderate to severe dementia, while task-oriented and gamified environments enhanced memory, attention, and executive function in those with mild impairment. Modes of engagement also shaped outcomes, with whole-body interaction producing greater improvements in balance, coordination, and daily functioning than passive viewing. Intervention frequency further influenced results as high-frequency short-term programs supported rapid emotional and physical benefits, whereas low-frequency long-term programs promoted sustained cognitive stability. By framing environments, engagement, and frequency as active design variables, this review positions VR dementia interventions within a broader human-computer interaction perspective that can inform future technologies for aging populations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Urbanization effects and contributions on surface thermal trends: Diurnal and climatic differences across urban gradients in Asian cities
Abstract: Urban expansion and internal densification reshape urban surface structures and thermal conditions, yet their effects and contributions across development intensity gradients remain unclear. This study examined land surface temperature (LST) conditions and trends across urban gradients in Asian cities from 2000 to 2023. Impervious surfaces were classified into low, medium, and high density urban zones, with rural reference areas included. Daytime LST, nighttime LST, and day–night temperature difference was derived. Long-term trends were estimated, and urbanization effects and contributions were quantified from urban density trend differences. Mean daytime and nighttime LST rose consistently with impervious surface density, increasing by 2.10 and 1.58 °C, respectively, from rural to high density zones. In contrast, long-term LST trends showed no consistent monotonic gradient across density classes, while the day–night difference exhibited negative trends in all spatial classes. Daytime urbanization effects increased from 0.0167 to 0.0217 °C/year, with relative contributions rising from 0.1772 to 0.2614. Nighttime effects and contributions shifted from negative values at low and medium densities toward zero at high density, whereas effects on day–night difference shifted from positive to near zero. Title: Comparison of visual tasks for assessing attentional bias in cannabis users and non-users
Abstract: Attentional bias toward substance-related cues is a key feature of addiction and may contribute to the continued use of substances, such as cannabis. However, the sensitivity of different paradigms for detecting this bias remains underexplored. This study compared three visual attentional bias paradigms: dot probe (DP), eye movement (EM), and MouseView.js (MV) in detecting cannabis-related attentional biases among cannabis users and non-users. Thirty-one participants (i.e., 16 users and 15 non-users) completed all measures: DP (reaction time to probes replacing cannabis or neutral stimuli), EM (measured via eye-tracking), and MV (cursor-based dwell time). Linear mixed-effects models examined the effects of stimulus type, group, craving, and cannabis use severity. The EM and MV tasks revealed significant stimulus effects, with non-users showing greater attention to neutral images, while cannabis users exhibited more evenly distributed attention across stimuli. In the EM task, a significant stimulus × severity interaction indicated reduced attentional differentiation with increased cannabis use severity. MV results followed a similar, but less precise pattern. In contrast, the DP task showed minimal group or interaction effects and lacked sensitivity to detect attentional differences. These findings suggest that EM-based measures are more sensitive for detecting cannabis-related attentional biases, particularly when accounting for cannabis use severity. MV showed some alignment with EM patterns but demonstrated weaker effects. The DP task, despite its widespread use, may be insufficient for capturing cannabis-related attentional differences. Results highlight the importance of task selection in attentional bias research and the potential influence of individual differences in cannabis use severity. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Ventral striatal and caudate contributions to episodic retrieval
Abstract: Striatal activity during episodic memory retrieval is a robust phenomenon observed across various stimulus types and experimental paradigms. Previous research suggests that the ventral striatum and the caudate contribute differentially to retrieval processes: ventral striatal activity is posited to vary with the intrinsic reward of successful retrieval, whereas caudate activity is attributed to effortful cognitive control. The present fMRI study aimed to test the overarching hypothesis that these striatal subregions make distinct contributions to episodic retrieval and to further specify their functional roles. To this end, we employed a word–picture paired-associates learning paradigm in which words served as cues in two consecutive cued-recall tests that were separated by 24 h. Participants indicated the specificity of their associative memories, enabling characterization of striatal response profiles as a function of associative memory specificity and treatment of memory specificity as a proxy for the intrinsic reward associated with retrieval success. Rather than being not readily compatible with a role of the caudate in effortful post-retrieval control, the results suggest that elevated caudate activity during successful recall reflects pre-retrieval control or involuntary orienting to salient mnemonic information. In contrast, rather than reflect intrinsic reward itself, ventral striatal activity varied with the discrepancy between expected and actual intrinsic reward elicited by retrieval outcomes—that is, a metacognitive reward prediction error. Moreover, ventral striatum signaled the relevance of retrieved information and modulated its re-encoding to facilitate future retrievals. © 2026

Title: Negotiating your way to the top: Conflict management by women leaders in family businesses
Abstract: Family businesses are a fertile ground for women to take up different leader roles. The way up as well as functioning at the nexus of the business family and family business offer unique negotiation challenges. Women leaders play a central role in preserving family harmony while safeguarding business performance, acting as mediators in cases of intra-family conflict and developing their career as leaders. Traditionally oriented succession dynamics, inequality, and lack of legitimacy as business leaders and family leaders require specific and high-level negotiation competencies. Title: Assessing agrammatic speech: Insights from perceptual ratings, statistical metrics, and lesion-symptom mapping
Abstract: The perceptual recognition of expressive agrammatism in aphasia is rapid and readily apparent by seasoned and novice researchers alike. However, in recent years much work on agrammatism has relied on statistical quantification of agrammatic speech through variables such as mean length of utterance and proportion of grammatical elements. An agrammatic/non-agrammatic perceptual classification based on audiovisual recordings of discourse samples was drawn from previously published analyses. Behavioral analyses showed significant correspondence between the perceptual groupings of agrammatic and non-agrammatic individuals and several linguistic variables, including mean length of utterance, use of past tense, and percent nouns. Despite a general correspondence between perceptual and statistical linguistic measures, only the perceptual approach revealed robust lesion correlates. LSM of perceptual classification revealed a strong lesion correlate primarily in the frontal lobe, spanning the middle frontal gyrus and the precentral and postcentral gyri, consistent with previous research, in both voxel and ROI analyses. Title: Cannabis detection in postmortem toxicology among suicide decedents in the Federal District, Brazil, 2009–2019

Title: Strict phonics instruction outperforms mixed phonics: Evidence from a large-scale study
Abstract: Background: Learning to read is a foundational milestone in formal education, and a large body of research supports the effectiveness of systematic phonics instruction in early literacy development. However, much less is known about whether different implementations of phonics instruction influence children's reading outcomes. This study investigates whether variation within phonics-based instruction—specifically, strict versus mixed phonics approaches—is associated with differences in early reading development. Methods: We combine survey data from more than 9000 first-grade teachers with longitudinal assessment data for over 139,000 pupils in France. Teachers were classified according to the instructional approaches they reported using and the characteristics of the reading materials employed in their classrooms. Pupils’ reading fluency and reading comprehension were measured using nationally administered standardized assessments conducted during Grade 1 and at the beginning of Grade 2. Results: Multilevel analyses showed that pupils taught using strict phonics approaches achieved higher reading fluency and reading comprehension than those taught with mixed phonics approaches, with differences corresponding to approximately 0.11–0.16 standard deviations. These effects were substantially larger among pupils with weaker pre-reading skills and those attending socioeconomically disadvantaged schools. The findings remained robust across multiple complementary analyses designed to address potential selection effects and omitted-variable bias. Conclusion: The findings demonstrate that meaningful differences in reading outcomes may arise not only from whether systematic phonics instruction is provided, but also from how it is implemented. They further suggest that optimizing the coherence of early phonics instruction may be particularly beneficial for pupils most at risk of reading difficulties. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Association of artificial intelligence literacy with moral distress and moral resilience among nursing interns: A cross-sectional study
Abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into healthcare and nursing education, requiring new forms of digital competency among nursing interns. However, the associations of AI literacy with ethical and psychological outcomes among nursing interns remain unclear. This study examined the associations of AI literacy with moral distress and moral resilience among nursing interns. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 300 nursing interns from three tertiary hospitals in China between December 2025 and April 2026. AI literacy was assessed using the 12-item AI Literacy Scale adapted by Reinhardt et al. Moral distress and moral resilience were assessed using the Moral Distress Scale–Revised and the Rushton Moral Resilience Scale, respectively. Multivariable linear regression models and exploratory subgroup analyses were performed. Results: The mean (SD) age of the participants was 22.0 (1.2) years, 234 (78.0%) were female, and the mean (SD) AI literacy score was 3.98 (1.29). Higher AI literacy was associated with lower moral distress in both the unadjusted model (β = −0.64; 95% CI, −0.73 to −0.55; P < .001) and adjusted model (β = −0.63; 95% CI, −0.72 to −0.54; P < .001). Title: Consensus on components of psychological treatment for depression to reduce symptoms and target relapse risk factors in young adults: A modified Delphi study
Abstract: Background Depression is increasingly prevalent in young adults and relapse is common. This study aimed to obtain consensus on Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT)-based treatment components considered important by experts for reducing symptoms and targeting relapse risk factors in young adults (18–25 years). Academics/clinicians (n = 46) and young adult experts-by-experience (n = 24) rated treatment components, therapist competencies, relapse risk factors and interventions, content of relapse-prevention sessions, and post-treatment relapse-prevention strategies. The Academic/Clinician panel rated experiments targeting negative automatic thoughts highest (97%, n = 30) while the Young Adult panel rated those targeting rumination highest (71%, n = 24). Title: A multilevel framework for distinguishing psychopathy from related disorders
Abstract: Although psychopathy is not a standalone diagnosis in current psychiatric classification systems, it remains widely used in forensic contexts and can have significant consequences for individuals within the legal system. Consequently, it is critical that the field be able to distinguish psychopathy from other mental disorders with over=lapping symptom presentations. This review proposes a multilevel theoretical framework for understanding how psychopathy differs from related disorders when mechanistic and dispositional factors are considered alongside behavioral symptoms. It illustrates how disorders overlapping with psychopathy at one level of analysis (e.g., chronic antisocial behavior and aggression) diverge from it at others, particularly the mechanistic level (e.g., attentional functioning, threat reactivity, empathy processing) and dispositional level (e.g., callous-unemotional traits). It further considers how contextual factors modulate whether psychopathic features are rewarded or criminalized and how this may affect their interpretation. By identifying features that distinguish psychopathy across levels of analysis, the framework clarifies what makes psychopathy a distinct construct, with implications for case formulation, treatment, and forensic assessment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: IGPC: Multi-domain multimodal fake news detection via Info-Gini Weight Adaptation and Prototypical Multi-level Contrastive Learning

Title: Debunking decisions for dynamically emerging topic-associated rumors
Abstract: In public emergency events, topic-associated rumors typically erupt in a streaming, multi-wave fashion, requiring authorities to continuously produce debunking decisions as new rumors keep emerging, all under unknown diffusion-model parameters. Title: Good listening as a wise negotiation tactic
Abstract: Listening is a foundational interpersonal skill. Effective listening is central to managing the dual demands of negotiation: competing over limited resources while sustaining cooperation and trust. Nevertheless, limited research has shed light on how to listen effectively in negotiation. Integrating research from psychology, communication, and negotiation, we identify three common listening traps that undermine negotiation effectiveness: negotiators tend to focus too much on: (1) the self (and too little on others); (2) resolving disagreement (and too little on exploring it); and (3) what is said (and too little on what remains unspoken). We propose three approaches for effective listening in negotiations: (1) listening to understand rather than persuade; (2) listening for movement and change; and (3) making listening observable through concrete verbal and nonverbal behaviors. We argue that high-quality listening improves both informational and relational outcomes by facilitating deeper information exchange, increasing trust, and supporting integrative agreements. Title: Aesthetic taste in humans and machines
Abstract: Aesthetic taste remains an elusive phenomenon that has been comparatively underexplored in psychology. We argue that taste integrates four dimensions: sensitivity to fine-grained differences within a domain; valence, through which these differences come to matter affectively; orientation, the selective tendency to seek encounters that may further transform one's sensibility; and normativity, through which judgments of taste become shareable and contestable. These are not separate dimensions but faces of a single underlying capacity: continuously monitoring one's grip on the world and letting that monitoring modulate what happens next. This makes human engagement non-uniform. Throughout, we use current artificial intelligence as a contrast case, exploring how far it can model or replicate human taste. Machines can be sensitive to fine-grained distinctions, predict human preferences, generate apparently tasteful outputs, and shape the environments in which human taste develops. But they do not yet possess taste in the full human sense, because they lack the stake that makes human processing non-uniform: self-directed exploration, online self-transformation, and genuine normative vulnerability. The upshot is a systematic framework for the study of human taste and for assessing how AI may transform its formation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: QESM: A Quantum-Inspired Network with Dynamic Fusion and Entangled Measurement for multimodal emotion recognition
Abstract: Multimodal emotion recognition in conversation (MERC) integrates textual, acoustic, visual, and contextual cues to identify each utterance’s emotion. Classical models encode temporal and cross-modal relations through recurrence, graphs, or attention, whereas quantum-inspired models largely retain static states and separable measurements, leaving operator-level evolution and coherence-aware joint readout under-modelled. To address these limitations, we propose QESM, which integrates Unitary Temporal Evolution (UTE), OTOC Cross-Modal Scrambling (OCS), and Entangled Born Measurement (EBM). UTE propagates speaker-aware emotional context through norm-preserving unitary phase evolution. Title: Gone with the wind: Productive response to agricultural shock
Abstract: Weather-induced agricultural shocks are geographically selective, as exposure reflects both exogenous atmospheric dynamics and predetermined local geography. We exploit the knowledge of shock determinants to isolate the exogenous component, relying on counterfactual simulations to measure medium-term farmers’ adaptation strategies. Title: From search results to generative answers: A mixed-methods study of credibility assessment and trust formation in AI Overviews
Abstract: Generative search shifts information evaluation from comparing ranked documents to assessing synthesised answers. Title: When and why women ask (or do not): Taking stock of research on gender differences in negotiation propensity, behavior, and outcomes
Abstract: Evidence first emerged several decades ago that women are less likely than men to initiate negotiations and perform less competitively than men in negotiations. Researchers also have discovered moderators of these effects, including structural ambiguity, representation role, and gender salience and relevance. Furthermore, the anticipation of backlash has emerged as a potential mechanism to explain gender differences in negotiations. Yet, more recent research has revealed varied findings concerning whether gender differences, underlying mechanisms, and moderators have shifted, as well as the role of intersectionality. We review the research in this area and find that the nature of gender differences in negotiation is complex, with some recent research replicating certain past findings (e.g., gender gaps in negotiation behavior) but not others (i.e., gender gaps in negotiation propensity or moderation by representation role). Still other recent research has even revealed a reversal of gender gaps in negotiation propensity, with women being more likely than men to negotiate in certain cases, and that female negotiation counterparts are liked more than male negotiation counterparts, leading to greater counterpart satisfaction. We also consider the role of statistical power given the small-to medium-sized effects typically reported: Sample size may be another important reason for inconsistent findings in the gender and negotiation literature. Finally, we consider the potential for changing gender roles. Overall, we conclude that gender differences in negotiation performance outcomes persist and are influenced by situational nuances, but that these differences have been mitigated for propensity to initiate negotiations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Capability, opportunity, and motivation for healthy eating: Exploring gender-specific pathways
Abstract: Women generally consume a healthier diet than men; however, both fall short of dietary guidelines. Health behaviour theories are often applied in a gender-neutral manner, implicitly assuming that explanatory models operate similarly across groups. This conceptual replication tested the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation and Behaviour (COM-B) model for dietary behaviour, originally evaluated in a female-dominant sample, in a male-dominant sample (N = 1358; 67% male). Using the same measurement battery and a closely aligned analytic approach, structural equation modelling indicated acceptable overall fit, with the COM-B model explaining 22% of the variance in diet quality. As in the original study, capability and opportunity were associated with behaviour indirectly through motivation, which was the strongest predictor of diet quality. At the indicator level, the male-dominant model retained action control and habits (capability), descriptive norms and the home food environment (opportunity), and self-efficacy, intentions, affective attitudes and perceived behavioural control (motivation), whereas identity, decision-making barriers, instrumental attitudes and the shopping environment indicator were not retained during trimming. These differences, relative to the female-dominant model, suggest potential variation in how COM-B constructs are operationalised across gender-dominant samples and should be treated as hypothesis-generating. Discriminant validity concerns (habits–action control; self-efficacy–intention) further indicated overlap between conceptually distinct constructs in the male-dominant sample. Title: Physical fatigue increases shipboard firefighting simulation completion time and perceived workload
Abstract: Firefighting involves physically demanding tasks performed under high heat and time pressure. While previous research reports the physical load involved, the extent to which physical fatigue impedes firefighting performance, especially in shipboard environments remains underexplored.
