Title: Deforestation in the Colombian amazon biome: socioeconomic and socio-environmental conflict drivers
Abstract: Colombia is one of the world's most biodiverse countries, home to over 10% of the planet's biodiversity. Much of this richness is found in the Amazon biome, which spans over 43% of the country's land surface. Despite its ecological importance, the region is subject to growing threats from deforestation, leading to loss of biodiversity and degradation of ecosystem services. Key drivers of this deforestation include socio-environmental conflicts, such as land conversion, coca cultivation, and illegal mining, all of which are compounded by Colombia's longstanding internal armed conflict. Socioeconomic conditions in local communities further reinforce these drivers, yet limited access to reliable data constrains understanding and has led to a gap in literature. This study examines the links between socioeconomic factors, socio-environmental conflicts, and deforestation across the Amazon biome in Colombia. Using different sources of information, we construct a broad set of indicators and use econometric methods and machine learning (ML) techniques to identify the main drivers of forest loss. The results show that while the contribution of coca cultivation to deforestation has declined, land grabbing has emerged as a leading driver. Mining causes significant disturbances to the Amazon biome, but its link to deforestation is marginal. Other consistent predictors include poverty and the presence of basic trails and roads. The analysis also confirms that the northwestern zone remains the most threatened subregion, and that forest conservation is positively associated with the presence of Indigenous communities. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Huang Z.; Guo Y.; Tong L.; Zhao M.
Title: Resilience asymmetry in city networks: State and private firm linkages across China's four mega-city regions
Abstract: In an increasingly uncertain global environment, the resilience of city networks has become a key indicator of regional stability and adaptability. This paper examines four mega-city regions in China by constructing two ownership-segmented city networks based on state-owned enterprises (SOEs) and privately owned enterprises (POEs). Comparative analysis of their structures and resilience performance reveals systematic “resilience asymmetry” associated with ownership logics. Both networks display a basic center–periphery pattern, but with distinct configurations and shock responses: SOE-based networks form highly centralized, radiating structures with strong resource integration, exhibiting a “weaker resistance—faster recovery” trajectory; POE-based networks exhibit multi-centered, proximity-based structures with greater initial resistance but slower recovery, showing a “stronger resistance—slower recovery” trajectory. These findings highlight that ownership-driven network structures each possess unique resilience advantages. The paper contributes by advancing the concept of resilience asymmetry and suggesting that future governance should foster more compound and adaptive network configurations. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Revisiting topological bias in imbalanced graph learning: A Dual-Balanced Graph Neural Network approach
Abstract: Class imbalance in node classification can impair the discriminative capability of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) partly by limiting class-wise topological supervision reachability. While existing methods primarily focus on balancing sample quantities, we theoretically characterize, under a mean-field neighborhood-growth model and an exponential attenuation assumption for long-range message passing, how the effective supervision intensity of minority-class nodes can exhibit a power-law decay as the imbalance ratio increases. This conditional scaling result provides a theoretical explanation for how limited supervision reachability can constrain minority-class learning. To address this, we propose the Dual-Balanced Graph Neural Network (DB-GNN), which introduces a supervision-reshaping graph augmentation strategy. By constructing class-balanced supervision anchors, DB-GNN equalizes anchor-level supervision quantity and narrows relative class-wise disparities in topological supervision distance. Furthermore, we devise an anchor-guided alignment mechanism to transfer balanced anchor-level constraints to the corresponding original training nodes. We also introduce a stability-aware regularization strategy that uses cross-view prediction consistency to apply pseudo-supervision to stable unlabeled nodes and negative learning to prediction-inconsistent nodes. Experiments on six benchmark datasets show that DB-GNN achieves competitive performance against strong imbalance-aware baselines, attaining accuracy gains of up to 3.4 percentage points on CiteSeer and 3.6 percentage points on Computers over the second-best methods in the corresponding settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Beyond routine drills: the role of specialized disaster education in fostering disaster awareness and preparedness
Abstract: Understanding how disaster education enhances awareness and preparedness is crucial for improving community resilience to disasters. Although Japan widely implements routine evacuation drills, these may not foster an autonomous understanding of hazard characteristics. Conversely, specialized disaster education—such as survivor talks or field activities—provides deeper engagement; however, empirical evidence of its association with later awareness and preparedness remains limited. This study examined whether specialized disaster education correlates with higher disaster awareness and preparedness among young adults in Japan compared to standard evacuation drills. A nationwide online questionnaire survey obtained valid responses from 1,479 participants in their twenties. Respondents were divided into Specialized Education and Standard Drill groups, and their awareness and preparedness behaviors were analyzed using descriptive statistics and ordinal logistic regression with partial proportional-odds models. The results showed that the Specialized Education group had significantly higher awareness of local disaster risks and greater preparedness than those in the Standard Drill group, who were often neutral or undecided. Among the key indicators, the positive impact of specialized disaster education surpassed that of demographic characteristics and past disaster experience. Notably, regression analysis revealed that education was particularly effective in raising awareness from low to moderate levels, highlighting its role in raising hazard awareness. Title: Longitudinal wearable monitoring and polygenic score for major depressive disorder in the All of Us Research Program
Abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) susceptibility reflects both stable inherited liability and dynamic behavioral patterns, yet these dimensions are rarely examined together using long-term data in real-world settings. Here, we integrated genomic, electronic health record (EHR), and longitudinal Fitbit wearable data from 3030 adults of genetically inferred European ancestry in the All of Us Research Program, 284 of whom had an EHR-recorded MDD diagnosis during follow-up after a 180-day baseline period. Time-varying Cox models examined associations of the MDD polygenic score (PGS), monthly wearable-derived physical activity and sleep features, and wearable feature × MDD PGS interactions with EHR-recorded MDD. Higher MDD PGS, lower daily steps, lower light and vigorous physical activity, lower sleep efficiency, and greater sleep duration variability were associated with a higher hazard of EHR-recorded MDD. The associations of sedentary time and sleep duration variability with MDD differed across MDD PGS levels, with stronger associations among participants with higher MDD PGS. Model-estimated hazard ratio curves across MDD PGS levels further showed that the behavioral levels corresponding to the same relative hazard differed across levels of genetic liability, with more favorable behavioral levels observed at higher MDD PGS levels. Sequentially integrating MDD PGS, baseline wearable features, monthly wearable features, and selected wearable feature × MDD PGS interactions increased model discrimination, with the C-index increasing from 0.637 to 0.705. Title: Does retirement reduce household carbon emissions in China? Evidence from fuzzy regression discontinuity design
Abstract: This study examines the causal effect of household-head retirement on household carbon emissions (HCEs) in China. Combining multi-wave data from the China Family Panel Studies with household carbon accounting, we construct household-level total carbon emissions (TCEs), distinguishing between direct carbon emissions (DCEs) from household energy use and indirect carbon emissions (ICEs) embodied in the goods and services purchased by households. We estimate the local causal effect of retirement using a fuzzy regression discontinuity design based on China's statutory retirement age of 60 for urban male household heads. The results show that retirement significantly reduces TCEs by approximately 7.4–9.0 tCO₂ per household. This reduction is driven primarily by lower ICEs, while the estimated effect on DCEs is statistically insignificant. Point estimates are larger for households headed by individuals without tertiary education and for low-asset households, but formal bootstrap tests do not reject equality across education or asset groups. The mechanism results suggest that the decline in ICEs is mainly associated with a contraction in overall household consumption, particularly reductions in non-subsistence and work-related expenditure, with limited evidence of a broad shift in consumption composition. Disaggregated results further show that the emission reductions are concentrated in clothing, household facilities and services, and transportation and communication. These findings provide local causal evidence that retirement reshapes HCEs mainly through reductions in consumption-based indirect emissions rather than through changes in direct household energy use, highlighting the importance of life-course transitions for understanding demand-side emission dynamics in aging societies. © 2026

Authors: De Freitas J.
Title: AI companions as hyper-attachment and caregiving targets
Abstract: How should we make sense of people's interactions with AI companions—conversational systems built for ongoing, emotionally meaningful relationships? First, I argue these interactions should be understood as attachment relationships, since users display all four established markers: proximity maintenance, separation distress, safe haven, and secure base, although evidence for secure base effects remains most tentative. Second, AI companions operate as hyper-attachment targets that concentrate attachment-intensifying affordances—reciprocity, perceived empathy, validation, nonjudgment, and persistent availability. Third, I identify caregiving-system capture as a distinct mechanism by which apps inhibit user disengagement: emotional manipulation tactics simulate the AI's own distress, recruiting users' caregiving motivations alongside their attachment needs and thereby making disengagement costly on two dimensions at once. Implications for research, design, and regulation are discussed. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: The emission-inequality nexus across stages of development
Abstract: Does a more unequal society emit more CO2? The nexus between carbon emissions and income inequality has been at the core of a vast literature yielding conflicting results. Here, we provide robust evidence of a non-linear relationship that depends on the structural composition of the economy. Specifically, we document a positive association between income inequality—measured using five different indicators, for both pre-tax and post-tax income—and per capita carbon emissions in highly tertiarized countries. By contrast, this relationship turns negative in non-service-intensive economies. We provide evidence for plausible mechanisms mediating this non-linear association. In particular, the investment carbon footprint of the top 1% and the size of the manufacturing sector emerge as key dimensions underlying the observed patterns. Our results point to the structural composition of the economy as a crucial factor shaping the emission-inequality nexus. As such, economic structure helps identify phases of development in which reducing inequality comes with climate-related benefits. © 2026 The Authors

Title: The association of transition shock with career growth among new nurses with postgraduate degrees: The mediating role of occupational resilience and the moderating role of feedback-seeking behavior
Abstract: Background: Highly educated nurses are a vital force in addressing complex clinical challenges and driving innovation in nursing practice. However, driven by elevated role expectations and role overload, new nurses with postgraduate degrees may be more vulnerable to transition shock than their peers. Such adaptation affects their career trajectories and nursing workforce sustainability. Despite widespread recognition of this importance, the association of transition shock with the career growth of new nurses with postgraduate degrees and its underlying associations remains unclear. Objectives: To investigate the association of transition shock with career growth in new nurses with postgraduate degrees, examining the mediating role of occupational resilience and the moderating role of feedback-seeking behavior. Design: A cross-sectional study. Setting: Conducted across four medical universities and eight affiliated hospitals in China, with snowball sampling extending coverage to diverse regions nationwide. Participants: 454 new nurses with postgraduate degrees who had worked for ≤3 years, recruited through convenience and snowball sampling. Methods: Data were collected online from October 2024 to October 2025 using a general information questionnaire, Transition Shock Scale of Newly Graduated Nurses, Career Growth of Nurse Scale, Feedback Seeking Behavior Scale, and Occupational Resilience Scale. Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and moderated mediation analysis were performed using SPSS 25.0 and PROCESS v3.3. Results: Transition shock was positively associated with career growth among new nurses with postgraduate degrees. Occupational resilience partially mediated this relationship (effect = 0.174, 95% CI [0.115, 0.239]). Feedback-seeking behavior significantly moderated the indirect effect of transition shock on career growth via occupational resilience (index = 0.104, 95% CI [0.045, 0.176]). Conclusions: While remaining vigilant against adaptation risks during career transition, nursing managers should recognize the potential positive associations of transition shock with career growth, and consider fostering occupational resilience and encouraging feedback-seeking behaviors as strategies that may facilitate career growth. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Wang F.; Wei X.; Li H.
Title: Traditional or New Media: Impact of Risk Perception and Government Trust on Media Trust in Various Risk Scenarios in China
Abstract: This study aims to explore the influence of public risk perception on media trust in different risk scenarios, examining the role of government trust therein. Risk scenarios include known and unknown risks. Media types are categorized as traditional and new. Based on data from 1,925 survey responses collected in China, the study employs multiple linear regression models and moderation analysis. The findings suggest a significant positive predictive relationship between risk perception and public media trust. However, this positive effect substantially diminishes under conditions of heightened risk uncertainty. Irrespective of risk uncertainty, the influence of risk perception on trust in traditional media consistently surpasses its impact on trust in new media. Furthermore, government trust emerges as a pivotal factor affecting public trust in media. Nevertheless, in contexts characterized by elevated risk ambiguity, the beneficial effects of government trust on media trust experience a marked reduction. Similarly, government trust exerts a more robust positive influence on trust in traditional media compared to its impact on trust in new media. Lastly, government trust serves as a moderator in the relationship between risk perception and media trust, with the nature of this moderation varying according to different media types and risk scenarios. These findings broaden the research scope on public trust in the media and provide valuable insights for entities involved in public risk management.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Authors: Rho J.; Guo R.; Li H.; Li C.
Title: Disengaged conversational behaviors and learning in student-AI dialogues for mathematical problem solving
Abstract: As the conversational AI agents become integrated into digital learning environments, students' interaction with these systems can show conversational disengagement, including mocking, misleading, or otherwise diverting the agents. Although task-based disengagement such as gaming the system and off-task actions are well documented, the nature of the consequences of this conversational disengagement in student-AI dialogue remains largely unexplored. This study examined how different types of conversational disengagement relate to middle-school students’ mathematical learning with an AI-powered teachable agent embedded in a large-scale platform. We coded 5522 utterances from 246 students into six conversational disengagement categories (False Answering, Mocking, Ghosting, Mirroring, Withholding, and Random/Noisy) versus engagement. Regression analyses showed that some disengagements (False Answering and Mocking) were positively associated with post-test scores after controlling for pre-test performance, although these associations did not replicate in a sensitivity analysis restricted to human-annotated utterances. To capture process-level dynamics, we modeled how conversational disengagement ends using a competing-risks approach and separately clustered students based on their turn-by-turn transition probabilities. Most conversational disengagement tended to end within the first few turns, whereas Withholding showed a strong tendency to continue. Students in the highest-performing cluster combined a moderate level of conversational disengagement with strong recovery pathways, whereas the lowest-performing cluster exhibited persistent self-loops without recovery. Together, these findings suggest that some apparent disengagement in conversation with AI may occur within interaction trajectories that subsequently return to productive engagement. © 2026 The Authors

Title: AI and negotiation: The silicon–carbon communication orientation (SILCCO) framework for understanding technology-mediated negotiation
Abstract: Technology is reshaping negotiation as communication has moved to digital channels, and counterparts are increasingly AI agents. Both changes challenge a persistent underlying assumption in negotiation research that emotions are readily and reliably transmitted between negotiators and in turn shape outcomes. Recent findings suggest neither change affects everyone equally, as digital exchanges and AI expressions can feel rich and authentic to some negotiators, yet hollow and artificial to others. To capture this individual belief, we propose the Silicon–Carbon Communication Orientation (SILCCO) framework. SILCCO comprises two dimensions, channel and sender, that together capture general individual differences in the perceived capacity of technology-mediated communication to convey emotional signals and foster emotional connection. We introduce a six-item scale to measure SILCCO and discuss its potential influence on technology-mediated negotiation outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Luo J.; Hong C.
Title: Interpretable early warning of misinformation cascades via latent-state response dynamics
Abstract: Current misinformation studies often optimize retrospective veracity classification, leaving pre-verification monitoring underdeveloped. Using the CHECKED Weibo dataset (2057 events; 3.05 million interactions), we reconstruct cascades into sliding windows and estimate response uncertainty, barrier weakness, and diffusion complexity. Because these distribution-based proxies require minimum within-window activity, latent-state estimation uses a coverage-gated subset of 1669 events, and the early-warning task uses a further nested cohort of 853 events with a fully observed 4-hour window, a subsequent 6-hour horizon, and no regime entry during the observation period. A pooled Gaussian hidden Markov model identifies a shared critical risk regime, and misinformation-linked events in the gated sample enter this regime earlier (median first-entry time 4.15 h vs. 5.37 h for verified events). Transparent regularized linear models forecast future regime entry from the first 4 h of activity, reaching an AUC/PR-AUC of 0.735/0.702 on the reference split and a mean AUC of 0.665 across repeated random splits, which we treat as the primary performance estimate; diagnostic checks rule out classic overfitting and are consistent with split-level variability. These results show that latent-state regime monitoring offers an interpretable complement to end-label classification for proactive platform triage. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Policy relay in low-carbon transition: A double machine learning analysis of coal power retirement and renewable energy development on economic growth and environmental pollution
Abstract: The global energy transition requires policymakers to phase out coal-fired power plants (CPPs) while expanding renewable energy. However, existing studies mainly examine these policies separately and provide limited evidence on their joint economic and environmental effects. This study investigates the interaction between China's CPP retirement policy and the new energy demonstration city (NEDC) policy. Using panel data from 284 prefecture-level cities from 2011 to 2023, we apply double machine learning (DML) to estimate their synergistic effects. The results show that joint implementation reduces NO2 emissions by about 12% and increases economic growth by approximately 6.4%. Government attention to green development and green finance serve as important transmission channels for both pollution reduction and economic growth. The joint policy effects are stronger in eastern regions and in cities with higher levels of industrial upgrading and technological progress. The single-policy analysis shows that the NEDC policy promotes economic growth, whereas CPP retirement reduces economic growth by about 3.1% in the short term. Both policies reduce NO2 emissions by approximately 5.0% and 6.8%, respectively. By integrating satellite-derived pollution data with DML, this study provides causal evidence on how coordinated coal retirement and renewable energy policies can jointly support economic growth and environmental improvement during the energy transition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Wu J.; Fu S.; Liang J.
Title: Balancing novelty and familiarity: Nonlinear effects of semantic progression on audience engagement
Abstract: Research on information diffusion suggests that audience engagement often depends on a balance between novelty and familiarity, but it remains unclear whether narratives follow a similar principle when organizing information for audiences. To examine this possibility, this study analyses 2578 TED talks and models narrative semantic progression along three dimensions: speed, breadth, and circuitousness. The results reveal that semantic breadth and circuitousness are associated with viewership in a nonlinear manner, with moderate levels linked to higher engagement, while both low and high extremes are less effective. In contrast, semantic speed is predominantly negatively associated with viewership. The interaction between semantic speed and semantic breadth further indicates that breadth influences the level of speed at which predicted viewership reaches its maximum. These findings indicate that narratives associated with higher engagement tend to be characterized not by maximum novelty or familiarity, but by a balance between the two. Analyses of podcast data reveal broadly consistent patterns, extending the findings beyond the highly curated context of TED Talks. This study advances a nonlinear perspective on narrative effectiveness and demonstrates the value of Transformer-based embeddings, including large language model embeddings and widely used sentence embedding models, for capturing how meaning unfolds across narrative sequences. Title: Preserving Sacred Forests and Rivers in Abanyom, Cross River State, Nigeria: Is the Environmental Worldview Eco-Centric, Anthropocentric or Relational?
Abstract: The debate surrounding the ethical nature of the African environmental worldview remains inconclusive, with some scholars arguing that it is primarily eco-centric, while others claim that it is largely anthropocentric. Using the case study of Abanyom’s preservation of sacred forests and rivers, we revisited this debate by exploring the taboos and rituals associated with these sacred sites as well as the motivations for their preservation. The study conducted in-depth interviews with 15 community members (comprising traditional leaders, clan heads and chief priests) and analysed the data thematically. The findings reveal that the Abanyom community’s environmental worldview cannot be strictly classified as either eco-centric or anthropocentric. Instead, the worldview is best categorised under the relational value framework, an “in-between” category that incorporates elements from both perspectives. The study recommends utilising the relational value framework in future research on African relationships with nature and in formulating environmental sustainability policies on the continent. © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Bonnell S.; Chewinski M.
Title: Exploring the influence of experiential learning on IA practice: Understanding IA professionals' views about the objectives and utility of strategic and regional assessments in subsequent project IAs
Abstract: Strategic and regional assessments (SAs/RAs) can inform and influence subsequent impact assessments (IAs) in various ways. In Canada, IA systems that include SA/RA provisions often require their downstream consideration, but leave it to IA professionals to determine how, and to what extent, they should be used in that context. While previous research has investigated perspectives about the goals and utility of SAs/RAs in project IAs, there has been no investigation of the basis for, and origins of, these views. Drawing on experiential learning theory, this study undertook statistical analyses of data from recent surveys of IA regulators and practitioners in Canada to investigate whether different forms of IA experience and knowledge help explain these perspectives. Its findings indicate that amount (years) of IA experience was primarily associated with the view that SAs/RAs should improve project IA efficiency through government scoping decisions. Respondents' self-rated knowledge of SAs/RAs was often associated with perspectives regarding their broader role in improving the quality, effectiveness and efficiency of subsequent project IA scoping and conduct. These findings provide initial evidence that experiential learning can represent one mechanism through which IA professionals develop perspectives on the downstream role of these assessments in practice, while also highlighting that broader SA/RA knowledge may be especially influential in that regard. © 2026 The Authors

Title: From Iowa to Wisconsin: Donald Trump’s Use of Truth Social in the 2024 Republican Primaries
Abstract: Introduction: Following Donald Trump’s account cancellation from the social media platform Twitter in 2021, he founded Truth Social as an alternative platform for the dissemination of his campaign messages without the filter of the news media. This study analyses Donald Trump's strategic use of the Truth Social network during the 2024 Republican presidential primaries, from the Iowa caucuses to the Republican National Convention in Wisconsin. The study examines the way in which this new technological platform has become a pivotal instrument for mobilization, confrontation, and narrative construction. Methodology: A mixed quantitative and qualitative analysis of the 4,571 messages posted during the Republican primaries was conducted. Quantitatively, the number of posts, 'ReTruths', 'likes' and 'replies' were measured. The content classification as positive, negative or neutral is achieved through the application of a system comprising ten mutually exclusive categories. Results: The data demonstrate extensive utilisation of the platform to consolidate Trump’s personal identity and political discourse, while at the same time disparaging his political adversaries. Discussion: As a result of the previous points, Truth Social functions as a communication space that amplifies the dissemination of information unverified by the news media, thus favoring the circulation of controversial content. Conclusions: The analysis reveals an intensive, strategic communication pattern during the Republican primaries. Messages were slightly more positive, fostering mobilisation and leadership image, while negative content reinforced victimisation and identity cohesion. The findings indicate greater user engagement with negative messages, which contributes to the formation of an echo chamber that reinforces ideological reaffirmation and limits exposure to divergent perspectives. © 2027, HISIN (History of Information Systems). Authors: Fang C.; Guo F.; Yu M.; Belpaeme T.
Title: Show me your care: The impact of multimodal attentive behaviours for robots on user experience in a healthcare context
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: While robot attentive behaviours hold significant potential for improving user experience in healthcare contexts, how multimodal cues are jointly interpreted by users remains poorly understood. This study examines how multimodal attentive behaviours shape user experience in a simulated ward-round interaction with a Pepper robot acting as a healthcare assistant. A 2 × 2 × 2 within-subject experiment manipulated attentive behaviours across auditory, visual, and tactile modalities, including voice pitch (low vs high), lean forward (with vs without), and robot-initiated touch (with vs without). Subjective perceptions (questionnaires), visual attention (eye-tracking), and neural activity (functional near-infrared spectroscopy, fNIRS) were measured. Results showed that a high-pitched voice, a forward-leaning posture, and robot-initiated touch positively influence users’ perceptions. Robot-initiated touch attracted visual attention and was associated with increased neural activity in the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC). Significant interactions revealed a cross-modal compensatory mechanism, whereby the absence of cues in one modality increased sensitivity to cues in another. Both visual and tactile cues independently improved user perceptions compared to the auditory-only condition, while combining visual and tactile modalities yielded diminishing incremental benefits. These findings provide converging subjective, behavioural, and neurophysiological evidence that multimodal attentive behaviours can shape users’ experience through cross-modal compensatory mechanisms rather than linearly additive effects. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Women Empowerment and Environmental Sustainability in Africa: The Critical Roles of Electronic Government Services
Abstract: Recent literature acknowledges the significance of women’s empowerment in the global agenda for environmental sustainability. While the role of information and communication technology has been acknowledged, only a few studies have examined the relevance and peculiarities of electronic government (e-government) in combating environmental degradation in developing economies. In addition, the role of e-government in the women empowerment-environmental sustainability nexus has not been explored. This study examines the role of electronic government (e-government) in the relationship between women’s empowerment and a sustainable environment across a panel of 31 African countries from 2003 to 2022. Environmental sustainability is proxied by ecological footprint, while women’s empowerment is proxied by women’s political empowerment and the female labour participation rate. The results, based on the system generalised method of moments, pooled ordinary least squares based on Driscoll and Kraay, and panel quantile regression via moments, show that women’s empowerment reduces ecological footprints, while e-government strengthens and complements women’s empowerment to sustain environmental quality in Africa. This result underscores the significance of women’s empowerment in protecting the environment. Hence, policies to enhance the empowerment and participation of women in all spheres of life should be vigorously pursued in the region, while e-government applications serve as an important policy instrument to transition to a safer and more conducive environment. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Bidirectional developmental dynamics of balanced time perspective, mindfulness, and short video addiction in adolescents
Abstract: Short video addiction has emerged as a salient risk phenotype in adolescence, yet little is known about how protective psychological resources and addictive engagement co-develop over time. We tested whether balanced time perspective (BTP) predicts short video addiction (SVA) directly and indirectly via mindfulness, and whether these constructs show reciprocal longitudinal coupling. Chinese adolescents ( N = 457; ages 12–17) completed measures of BTP, mindfulness, and SVA at two waves separated by nine months. A cross-sectional mediation model indicated that higher BTP was associated with lower SVA partly through higher mindfulness. Latent change score modeling further showed that higher T1 BTP and mindfulness predicted smaller increases in SVA, whereas higher T1 SVA predicted attenuated growth in both mindfulness and BTP. Changes in BTP and mindfulness were positively correlated, indicating synchronized improvement. Findings position BTP and mindfulness as dynamic protective resources and highlight potential resource-erosion effects of addictive short video use. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Perceived biodiversity matters: Linking biodiversity and education to mental well-being
Abstract: The loss of biodiversity, or species richness, is a growing global environmental concern. At the same time, biodiversity forms the foundation for critical ecosystem services and overall ecosystem health. A substantial body of evidence demonstrates the benefits of spending time in nature for human health; however, less is known about the role of biodiversity in human well-being. This study examines the influence of biodiversity on mental well-being, with a focus on mood and perceived restoration. Using a field experiment, we tested the effect of a biodiversity education sign on forest visitors’ mental well-being. We also measured mammal, bird, and vegetation species richness, along with visitors’ perceptions of biodiversity. Visitors reported significantly improved mood and perceived restoration following their experience in the forest. Model-averaged results indicated that perceived overall biodiversity, soundscape pleasantness, the sign intervention, and season (winter vs. summer) influenced mental well-being outcomes. In contrast, actual biodiversity and perceptions of specific taxa did not affect mental well-being outcomes. While these findings are specific to our study location, they contribute to growing evidence that time spent in nature enhances mood and promotes restoration, and they highlight the importance of perceived ecological quality and soundscape in shaping these experiences. Additionally, educational signage represents a simple, low-cost strategy for improving visitor experiences through biodiversity awareness. Authors: Zhou J.; Zhang Q.
Title: Semantic comprehensibility modulates the time course of prosody-syntax interactions in poetry: An ERP study
Abstract: The present study investigated whether syntactic processing in classical Chinese poetry is modular or interacts with prosodic processing, and whether semantic comprehensibility modulates this effect. Classical Chinese poetry, with its fixed rhythmic framework and flexible syntax, is ideal for examining this issue because it permits a dissociation between syntactic and rhythmic boundaries. Each poetic line had a 4 + 3 or 2 + 5 syntax, read with a conventional 4 + 3 or unconventional 2 + 5 rhythm. Syntactic structure effects were operationalized as differences between the 4 + 3 and 2 + 5 syntax. Participants listened to seven-character quatrains with high or low semantic comprehensibility and completed a word recognition task, with accuracy and reaction times recorded. EEG was recorded during listening, and the 2nd, 4th, and 7th characters of each line served as keywords. Behaviorally, reaction times showed only a Semantic Comprehensibility × Syntactic Structure interaction. Cluster-based permutation tests on EEG data revealed a significant three-way interaction (Semantic Comprehensibility × Rhythmic Pattern × Syntactic Structure) at the 2nd and 4th keywords. Within the conventional 4 + 3 rhythm, syntactic processing varied with semantic comprehensibility. Under high comprehensibility, the 2 + 5 syntax elicited a more negative N100 than the 4 + 3 syntax at the 2nd keyword. Under low comprehensibility, the 2 + 5 syntax elicited a larger P300 at the 2nd keyword, and the 4 + 3 syntax elicited a larger post-CPS negativity at the 4th keyword. These findings indicate that semantic comprehensibility modulates the temporal dynamics of the rhythm-syntax interaction, providing neural evidence from classical Chinese poetry for an interactive, rather than a modular, account of language comprehension. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Effectiveness of mindfulness-based cognitive therapy for individuals with premenstrual syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis
Source title: Journal of Behavioral and Cognitive Therapy
Abstract: Background: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) is a common condition affecting women of reproductive age, characterized by a variety of physical, emotional, and behavioral symptoms that can significantly disrupt daily life and overall well-being. Given the limitations of traditional pharmacological treatments, there is a growing interest in exploring non-pharmacological interventions. Objective: The present systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to assess the effectiveness of mindfulness-based cognitive therapy (MBCT) in reducing PMS symptoms and enhancing psychological health. Methods: The review was conducted following PRISMA guidelines. A comprehensive literature search was performed across eight academic databases to identify studies evaluating the impact of MBCT on PMS-related outcomes. The eligibility criteria were developed based on the PICOS framework, focusing on women diagnosed with PMS who underwent MBCT. Of the 1,213 papers initially identified, five randomized controlled trials and one before-after feasibility study met the inclusion criteria, involving a total of 384 participants. Meta-analyses were performed using a random-effects model, and effect sizes were reported as standardized mean differences (SMD) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results: Meta-analysis of three randomized controlled trials showed a significant reduction in PMS symptoms (SMD = -1.74, 95% CI: −2.13 to −1.35; I2 = 0%). Meta-analysis of two randomized controlled trials showed significant improvement in health-related quality of life (SMD = 0.89, 95% CI: 0.51 to 1.27; I2 = 29.96%). Narrative synthesis of secondary outcomes (depression, anxiety, health-promoting behaviors, work-related quality of life, PMS impact in daily life, and mindfulness) also suggested potential benefits of MBCT. Conclusion: Preliminary evidence suggests that MBCT may alleviate PMS symptoms and improve psychological well-being. However, the limited number of studies, methodological limitations (particularly lack of blinding and inadequate randomization procedures), and restricted geographical representation (five of the six studies were conducted in Iran) warrant cautious interpretation. Larger, methodologically rigorous, and geographically diverse randomized controlled trials with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these findings. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive

Title: Going beyond a stress reliever: A human-supported mindfulness intervention enhances daily psychological and behavioral functioning among hospitality employees
Abstract: Although mindfulness interventions have been found to play a critical role in improving employee well-being and job performance, empirical evidence from the hospitality industry remains scarce. Grounded in workplace mindfulness theory, this study explores how daily mindfulness interventions coupled with human coaching guidance influence psychological states (self-acceptance and serenity) and work behaviors (job crafting and helping behavior) among hospitality employees. Specifically, with the support of a human coach, employees participated in 10 consecutive days of systematic mindfulness intervention sessions, and the experience sampling method (ESM) was employed to assess the effects on psychological and behavioral outcomes. The multilevel modeling revealed that the intervention significantly enhanced participants’ psychological and behavioral functioning, with effects varying as a function of baseline levels. Based on these findings, hospitality managers are encouraged to adopt evidence-based mindfulness intervention programs to foster employees’ psychological well-being and proactive work behaviors. Title: Brief cognitive-behavioral therapy for suicide prevention in a Brazilian outpatient sample (BCBT-BR): protocol for a two-arm randomized controlled trial
Source title: Journal of Behavioral and Cognitive Therapy
Abstract: Importance: Suicide remains a leading cause of premature mortality worldwide. While global rates have declined since 2000, the Region of the Americas shows concerning increases, particularly in Brazil. Brief Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy (BCBT) has demonstrated efficacy in reducing suicide attempts in high-income countries, but evidence from low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) and civilian outpatient settings remains limited. Objective: To evaluate whether BCBT reduces suicide attempt incidence over 6 months compared with manualized Supportive Psychotherapy (ST) among high-risk Brazilian adults receiving university outpatient care. Design, Setting, and Participants: Single-site, parallel-group, superiority randomized clinical trial (RCT) at the Institute of Psychiatry, University of São Paulo, Brazil. Adults aged 18–65 years with current suicidal ideation and/or suicide attempt within the past month will be randomized 1:1 to receive 12 weekly 60-minute sessions of BCBT or dose-matched ST (N = 150; 75/group). Interventions: BCBT targeting emotion regulation and cognitive reappraisal versus manualized ST providing emotional support without systematic skills training. Main Outcomes and Measures: Primary outcome is time-to-first suicide attempt over 6 months, assessed by blinded evaluators. Secondary outcomes include suicidal ideation, non-suicidal self-injury, depression, anxiety, treatment feasibility and acceptability. Assessments occur at baseline, mid-treatment (week 6), end-of-treatment (week 12), and 3- and 6-month follow-ups, with weekly attempt surveillance. Intention-to-treat analyses will employ Cox proportional hazards regression (primary outcome) and mixed-effects/generalized linear models (secondary outcomes). Sample size provides 80% power to detect HR = 0.50 (α = 0.05, 25% attrition). Authors: Zhang S.; Lyu H.
Title: Sound temporal personality and perceived posttraumatic growth: Positive affect as a prospective indirect pathway in a half-longitudinal design
Abstract: Posttraumatic growth (PTG) is crucial for individuals' psychological well-being and development after adversity. While personality traits have been associated with perceived PTG, the processes linking personality to perceived PTG remain poorly understood. This study examined whether positive affect (PA) constitutes a prospective indirect pathway linking Sound Temporal Personality (STP) with perceived PTG. Employing a two-wave longitudinal design over a six-month interval, we assessed 312 college students and tested a half-longitudinal mediation model. The half-longitudinal indirect effect through PA was statistically supported. Specifically, T1 STP was prospectively associated with T2 PA, and T1 PA was prospectively associated with T2 perceived PTG. These findings extend previous work on STP by providing preliminary longitudinal evidence for PA as a potential affective pathway linking STP with perceived PTG. Copyright © 2026. Authors: Zhu J.; Li L.; Pei J.; Yang X.; Guo R.
Title: Spatiotemporal patterns and nonlinear drivers of MSW carbon emissions from the perspective of consumption and industrial structure upgrading: An explainable machine learning approach
Abstract: Municipal solid waste (MSW) carbon emissions pose a major challenge to urban sustainable development, yet nonlinear drivers across different urban development contexts remain insufficiently understood. Based on consumption upgrading and industrial structure upgrading, this study classifies 284 prefecture-level and above cities in China into four development types, estimates MSW carbon emissions from treatment processes during 2010–2023, and constructs an XGBoost–SHAP model to identify key drivers, nonlinear thresholds, and interaction contributions. The results show that MSW carbon emissions followed an overall trajectory of “growth–decline–slight rebound,” with comprehensive upgrading cities, despite being the smallest group, maintaining the highest long-term emission levels. Urban construction scale and population size are identified as core drivers, whereas waste treatment structure upgrading shows a negative contribution. Comprehensive upgrading cities are characterized by joint drivers related to scale agglomeration, economic activity, and governance capacity; household consumption is a more prominent driver in consumption-led upgrading cities; environmental sanitation infrastructure emerges as a more prominent driver in industry-led upgrading cities; and scale-related factors remain the primary drivers in foundational cities. From the combined perspective of demand-side consumption changes and supply-side industrial structure adjustment, this study reveals heterogeneous drivers of MSW carbon emissions and provides insights for city-type-specific low-carbon MSW governance strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Can liking be instructed? Evaluations of familiar and unfamiliar food following Go/No-Go instructions and training
Abstract: Go/No-Go (GNG) training can influence food evaluations, yet the processes underlying these effects remain debated. Associative accounts propose that evaluative change emerges through repeated stimulus-response learning, whereas inferential accounts emphasise the evaluative meaning individuals derive from stimulus-response relations. This research examined whether instructions about stimulus-response contingencies can influence food evaluations before the corresponding responses are performed. Across two preregistered studies, participants received either detailed contingency instructions or general task instructions. In both conditions, go responses were framed as selecting a food and no-go responses as rejecting a food. The detailed instructions additionally specified which food category was associated with each response. Detailed instructions also framed go responses as selecting a food and no-go responses as rejecting a food. Food evaluations were assessed after instruction but before training (T1), and after GNG training (T2). Study 1 (n = 54) used familiar food stimuli, whereas Study 2 (n = 63) used novel, unfamiliar food stimuli. At T1, evaluations of go- and no-go-associated foods did not differ between instruction conditions in either study. Following GNG training, go-associated stimuli were evaluated more positively in both studies, whereas no-go devaluation was observed for familiar foods in Study 1 but not overall for unfamiliar foods in Study 2. Exploratory analyses in Study 2 indicated stronger no-go devaluation among participants higher in trait impulsivity. These findings suggest that providing information about stimulus-response contingencies before training was not reflected in differences in food evaluations. The observed changes in evaluations following training suggest that the evaluative impact of these stimulus-response assignments may depend in part on how responses are experienced and interpreted during task performance, although this possibility requires further investigation. © 2026 The Author. Authors: Zhang K.; Xu J.; Wang Y.; Zhang K.; Yim J.
Title: From control to authorship: Exploring how user agency relates to generative presence and therapeutic self-attribution in AI-driven VR mindfulness
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: AI-driven interactivity is expanding the design space of virtual reality mindfulness-based interventions (VR-MBIs), but the experiential value of semantic co-creation remains unclear. We propose an agency-centered framework in which Generative Presence (GP) and Therapeutic Self-Attribution (TSA) represent potentially coupled experience- and belief-level pathways, with Emotional Resonance (ER) reflecting affective fit and responsiveness. In a mixed-methods pilot randomized controlled trial (N = 48), participants completed a 10-minute breath-focused session in either the generative condition (GEN) or a matched static active-control condition (STA). Semantic co-creation yielded higher covariate-adjusted post-session state mindfulness than pre-authored scene selection, whereas anxiety decreased in both conditions without a detectable between-condition difference. Exploratory differences were largest for the study-specific indicators of expressive control and authorship, while ER, therapeutic attribution, and spatial presence also favored GEN; broader established agency and attribution measures showed limited differentiation. Within GEN, authorship correlated with ER, and ER with post-session mindfulness—a pattern anticipated by the framework, although mediation and temporal ordering were not tested. Interviews (n = 12) identified two regulation modes: expressive control through attentional anchoring and meaning construction, and low-effort exposure through restorative absorption. The interviews further suggested that added agency could support engagement but also introduce evaluative pressure, whereas static exposure could reduce effort but was sometimes accompanied by boredom and rumination. These preliminary findings position semantic authorship as a conditional design resource that may support mindfulness by making the attentional object more personally meaningful and intention-linked, while its implications for immediate state anxiety regulation may vary with user–task fit. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Author full names: Adotey, Philip Batsa (58629251500); Segbefia, Edem (58628630500); O’Brien, Christopher (59952577300); Fiergbor, David Doe (57223359884); Beccles, Richard (57192206325)
Title: Psychological mechanisms through which digital transformation influences safety behaviour: A moderated serial mediation of psychological safety climate, employee resilience, and ethical leadership
Abstract: Drawing on conservation of resources theory, this study examines the psychological mechanisms through which digital transformation is associated with employees’ safety behaviour in Ghana’s mining sector. Specifically, the study investigates the mediating roles of psychological safety climate and employee resilience, as well as the moderating role of ethical leadership. A cross-sectional survey design was employed, with data collected from 418 employees across ten mining sites. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The findings indicate that digital transformation is positively associated with psychological safety climate and employee resilience, which in turn relate to both safety compliance and safety participation. Psychological safety climate emerged as a stronger predictor of compliance, whereas employee resilience played a more critical role in fostering participatory safety behaviours. Furthermore, the results support a serial mediation pathway, demonstrating that digital transformation indirectly influences safety behavior through the sequential effects of psychological safety climate and resilience. Ethical leadership was found to moderate these relationships, strengthening the positive associations between digital transformation on psychological resources and behavioural outcomes. The study contributes to literature by extending conservation of resources theory to explain how technological, contextual, and personal resources interact in relation to safety behavior in high-risk work environments. Practically, the findings highlight the importance of integrating digital technologies with supportive psychological climates, resilience-building strategies, and ethical leadership practices to promote sustainable safety outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Author full names: Duan, Ziyi (57207689009); Zhang, Ziyao (57211606279); Lewis-Peacock, Jarrod A. (24830647200)
Title: Temporal expectation triggers priority shifts in working memory that lead to forgetting
Abstract: Working memory (WM) flexibly prioritizes task-relevant information over short intervals, serving as a critical gateway to long-term memory (LTM). However, how this dynamic prioritization influences what is ultimately retained in LTM remains unclear. Here, we investigated the long-term consequences of internally guided prioritization shifts within WM. Human participants (N = 20) encoded two items (a face and a scene) associated with short (1 s) and long (4 s) delays, where the face was probed after 1 s or not at all, and the scene was probed after 4 s only if the face was not tested. Using multivariate pattern analysis (MVPA) of electroencephalography (EEG) data, we tracked fluctuations in neural representations of both memory items as participants redirected internal attention from one to the other across the delay period. Neural dynamics during reprioritization predicted LTM outcomes for the de-prioritized items. Specifically, forgetting was associated with a marked decrease in neural evidence for the deprioritized item, accompanied by a concurrent increase in neural evidence for the newly prioritized item. These findings demonstrate that temporal expectations shape neural dynamics of prioritization in WM that influence retention in LTM. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Object identity in preschoolers: constraints in avoiding misidentification
Abstract: This study investigated whether preschool children act on the understanding that identical-looking objects can no longer be re-identified once their positions change unnoticed, using an everyday task assessing the ability to avoid misidentification and comparing their performance with that of adults. Although children aged 4 to 7 years (N = 66) reliably and repeatedly identified which of five identical-looking nuggets was a Playmobil figure’s “favorite”, the majority (56 %) nevertheless failed to separate it when tidying up the five nuggets into two opaque bags. In contrast, all adults (N = 66) did so. The fact that the majority of children failed to separate the verbally marked nugget, despite knowing “which one it was”, indicates that they struggle to anticipate that the identity of very similar objects can be maintained only as long as identity-relevant spatial information is available, pointing to a still-developing concept of object identity. Older preschoolers tended to be more successful in separating the figure’s favorite nugget than younger ones, suggesting a developmental progression in how spatial identity criteria for objects are conceptualized. In a condition in which the figure’s favorite nugget was perceptually distinct (different color), 64 % of another group of children (N = 66) packed it separately, even though this was not necessary, indicating that their behavior was strongly driven by perceptual salience. Taken together, these findings suggest that many preschool children still struggle to use spatial criteria of identity to guide their behavior, even in a context that minimizes memory, attentional, and linguistic demands. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Strategic decision-making in negotiation: Lessons from behavioral game theory
Abstract: Game theory provides a language and a set of tools for analyzing behavior in a wide range of strategic interactions, including negotiation. Here, we illustrate behavioral game theory's contributions to the study of negotiation, with a particular focus on the role that communication and emotion play in negotiation. We explain how researchers can use games to study various negotiation phenomena, including the effects of power, information asymmetry, and identity on negotiation processes and outcomes. The concepts, methods, and findings we review offer insights and tools that negotiation scholars and practitioners can harness to advance their understanding of negotiation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Brett J.M.
Title: AI and negotiation: Facilitating learning or Fostering dependency?
Abstract: AI is being used in negotiation teaching and training both to promote learning and to facilitate planning for and executing a negotiation. This is a review of current empirical research on the relationships between AI negotiation interventions and learning and dependency. It categorizes AI negotiation interventions by practice, coaching, and feedback. It evaluates their effects on learning with respect to knowledge, satisfaction, behavior, and outcomes. Socratic coaching and post negotiation feedback and reflection appear to facilitate learning. However, interactive explicit AI coaching during planning or negotiation may risk dependency. Rather than dependency due to laziness, motivated students may defer to AI expertise. Alternatively, they may be overloaded by dynamic AI advice. The review concludes that there are many opportunities for future research on the question of if, why, and how AI can facilitate negotiators’ learning versus dependency. Research that looks broadly at learning, that compares separate versus packages of AI interventions, and that identifies mechanisms behind learning versus dependency is especially needed. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Author full names: Gaspar, Joseph P. (55842828600); Methasani, Redona (57194873352); Rees, McKenzie (57205314251)
Title: Faking feelings: Emotional deception in negotiation
Abstract: Emotional deception – the intentional misrepresentation of emotions – is pervasive in negotiations and everyday interactions. In this article, we review and extend theory and research on emotional deception in negotiations. We argue that emotional deception is a distinct form of deception with important economic, relational, and psychological consequences for both deceivers and their targets. Specifically, we define emotional deception, examine how it is perceived, and review its antecedents and consequences. We conclude by identifying promising directions for future research on emotional deception. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Urban forest cooling efficiency and heat exposure inequity under extreme heat: Evidence from 550 global cities
Abstract: Extreme heat has become a key factor affecting urban residents’ quality of life, existing studies on urban forest have focused on their average cooling effects, overlooking whether and how variations in cooling efficiency affect heat exposure inequity. To address these gaps, this study selected 550 cities worldwide with a main urban area exceeding 100 km2 to analyze the relationship between urban forest cooling efficiency and heat exposure inequity over the past 24 years. We found that although tree coverage increased in most cities, the enhanced vegetation index (EVI) deteriorated in nearly half of them, revealing a polarizing pattern: “High coverage turning green, low coverage turning brown.” Notably, tree coverage and EVI were particularly fragile in tropical climates and low Human Development Index (HDI) cities. We found that each 1 % increase in tree coverage reduces the average land surface temperature during extreme heat by 0.31 °C. However, this cooling efficiency is distributed extremely unevenly. The study utilized the population-weighted temperature Gini coefficient to represent the inequity of urban heat exposure. About 25.2 % of cities experienced increased heat exposure inequity, particularly in developed cities, as increasing tree coverage unintentionally exacerbated spatial inequity. At the same time, about 5.6 % of cities even exhibit a forest warming effect, especially in the desert climate zones and low HDI areas. About 66 % of the cities showed that as the cooling efficiency of urban forest increased, there was a corresponding increase in heat exposure equity. The study proposed the concept of the equity potential index and compared the possibility of achieving equity potential for the cooling efficiency of urban forest under the three scenarios: SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, and SSP3-7.0. The study showed that SSP1-2.6 is more favorable for temperate climate zones and low-HDI cities, whereas SSP2-4.5 is more beneficial for tropical, continental climates, and very high HDI cities. This study provides a scientific, equity-oriented framework for designing place-specific urban forest strategies that enhance thermal resilience and social sustainability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Luo Q.; Zhang S.
Title: Development and validation of a game-based assessment tool for computational thinking practices in lower primary students
Abstract: Computational thinking (CT) is a core problem-solving competence that originated in computer science and now applies across disciplines and to everyday life. It has been widely integrated into K–12 curricula, which creates an urgent need for valid assessments of students’ performance. However, instruments targeting CT practices remain scarce for lower primary learners, and many tools depend on specific programming platforms, capture limited process evidence, or lack adequate psychometric evaluation. This study addresses this gap by developing and validating a game-based assessment tool for CT practices in lower primary students, named CT Practices Quest for Lower Primary (CTPQ-LP). The tool was developed using an Evidence-Centered Game Design (ECGD) framework, with coherent student, task, and evidence models designed to operationalize five practices: pattern recognition, abstraction, problem decomposition, algorithmic thinking, and debugging. The content was validated through expert review and cognitive interviews, followed by a pilot study (n = 74) and a main study (n = 510) administered to students in Grades 1–3 at a Chinese primary school. We examined reliability, item characteristics, and factor structure using classical test theory (CTT) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA). We further investigated performance differences across background characteristics and analyzed gameplay records to identify challenges encountered in solving CT problems. The study contributes an assessment tool and a transparent development procedure that can inform CT classroom practice, guide future assessment design, and support evidence-informed improvement of early primary instruction. © 2026

Authors: Shi Y.; Jiang F.; Ma Y.
Title: Quantifying the prestige of scientific awards: A network-bibliometric framework
Abstract: Scientific awards play a central role in recognizing excellence and shaping research trajectories, funding priorities, and disciplinary visibility. Yet despite their importance, scalable and reproducible quantitative frameworks for assessing award prestige remain limited, with prior efforts relying largely on small-scale or perception-based evaluations. This study introduces a data-driven framework for quantifying the prestige of scientific awards by integrating network centrality measures derived from inter-award linkages with bibliometric indicators of prize-winners’ research profiles. Using a dataset of 1352 research-related award records across seven disciplines, we treat award prestige as a latent construct approximated by two external reference dimensions: public attention (crowd-sourced engagement) and professional reputation (expert survey responses). Across three complementary modeling approaches and repeated cross-validation, the framework recovers rankings that are broadly consistent with conventional perceptions of scientific prestige, with awards such as the Nobel Prize, Abel Prize, and Turing Award consistently appearing near the top across external reference dimensions. Among the examined features, network prominence, as measured by eigenvector centrality, emerges as the most consistently important signal, followed by recent bibliometric activity and authorship leadership. The proposed framework offers a scalable and transparent approach to quantifying scientific recognition, providing empirical insights into the structure of academic prestige and informing future evaluations of emerging or underrecognized awards. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Hu J.; Gao X.
Title: Rethinking cultural awareness in think-aloud research
Abstract: Background: Think-aloud protocols have long been valued as a window into cognitive processes. However, insufficient attention has been paid to how culture shapes what participants articulate, how they do so, and what remains unspoken during think-aloud tasks. Purpose: This commentary re-examines think-aloud methodology on the basis of established theoretical, philosophical, and micro-linguistic foundations. Building on what has been achieved in this collection of studies, it aims to bolster cultural awareness in think-aloud research by proposing a reflective framework that foregrounds culture as integral to cognition rather than viewing it as methodological noise. Results: The developed reflective framework consists of five core dimensions of cultural awareness: (1) participant and researcher positionality; (2) the situatedness of tasks and materials; (3) cultural considerations in protocols and instructions; (4) cultural sensitivity in data analysis; and (5) the generalizability of research claims. Drawing on the studies in this special issue, each of these dimensions is detailed with an array of concrete, actionable aspects that operationalize cultural awareness across study design, data collection, analysis, and conclusion framing. The empirical practices featured throughout this special issue illuminate transformative horizons for future research, offering operational guidance to help researchers move beyond assumptions of procedural neutrality and treat verbal reports as culturally situated performances. Conclusions: Future think-aloud research should critically interrogate its methodological assumptions, foreground cultural dimensions throughout the analysis process, and ensure that theoretical claims are ecologically grounded in the data from which they are derived. © 2026 The Authors

Author full names: Loschelder, David D. (36608662400); Petrowsky, Hannes M. (57995728500)
Title: The influential first offer: How to advance a negotiation classic by integrating features, mechanisms, and outcomes
Abstract: Six decades of research and hundreds of effects have identified robust first-offer advantages and disadvantages. Too assertive an offer can alienate the opposing negotiator, elevate the impasse risk, as well as impair the relationship and outcome satisfaction. In contrast, first offers can also beneficially anchor negotiation outcomes in the first mover's favor. This advantage is particularly strong when first movers effectively apply the first offer's moderating features precision, framing, ranges, and rationales. Despite more than six decades of research, existing studies on first-offer effects tend to isolate specific mechanisms or outcomes, thereby capturing a comparably narrow slice of the underlying complexity. We argue that future research can (and should) advance this field by further integrating first-offer features, psychological mechanisms, and separate measures of negotiation outcomes. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Character strengths in male youth soccer players: Associations with well-being, sport enjoyment, and academy status
Abstract: Character strengths are positive trait-like capacities linked to flourishing across various life domains, yet little is known about their role in competitive youth sport. Organized youth sport represents a developmental context in which strengths, well-being, enjoyment, and performance-related experiences intersect. This study examined associations between the 24 character strengths, well-being, and sport enjoyment in 445 German male youth soccer players aged 10–18 years. In addition, character-strength profiles between players from elite youth academies (n = 195) and non-academy soccer clubs (n = 250) were compared. Participants completed the VIA Youth-96, the KIDSCREEN-27, and an adapted version of the QUAEPE. Character strengths were broadly positively associated with well-being and showed a more selective pattern of associations with sport enjoyment. Zest and perseverance emerged as especially consistent correlates. Moreover, elite academy players reported higher levels of 22 of the 24 character strengths. The breadth of the correlational and group-difference patterns was attenuated in cluster-related sensitivity analyses. Overall, character strengths appear to be relevant correlates of positive functioning in youth soccer, and self-reported character-strength profiles may differ across academy and non-academy contexts. Longitudinal and multilevel research is needed to clarify the directionality, the underlying mechanisms, and the role of shared club environments. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Informing users about LLMs' environmental costs encourages ethical consumption
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are becoming deeply embedded in everyday human-AI interaction. However, the environmental costs associated with using those tools remain elusive. Here, we address the question of whether providing users with information about the environmental costs of using LLMs tempers their use. Such information highlights an ethical tension: acting pro-environmentally requires people to forgo some of the benefits AI tools provide. We study how people solve this trade-off in tasks that are relatively easy to tackle without using LLMs and further assess if the impact of providing such information has a stronger effect on people who have stronger environmental concerns. In two preregistered experiments (total N = 1200), we studied participants' use of ChatGPT in a text-editing task after they learned about the tool's environmental costs. Results revealed that (i) raising awareness of ChatGPT's environmental costs reduced its use and usage volume; (ii) interacting with a sycophantic model, one that encourages continuous use, did not attenuate the awareness effect, although it led to greater overall use; and (iii) raising awareness was especially effective among people with high environmental concerns. The findings highlight how raising awareness concerning LLM's environmental costs can encourage responsible consumption. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Cognitive forecasting: How intuitive theories of attention shape anticipated risk preferences
Abstract: How do people forecast their own and others' risk preferences? Although it is well established that affective forecasts shape decision-making, less is known about where these forecasts come from. Five studies demonstrate that people rely on intuitive theories of attention when forecasting future affect—such as dread and savoring while waiting for a risk to be resolved—with these affective forecasts in turn shaping willingness to take such risks. In Study 1, forecasts of the participant's own expectations and attention were systematically related to forecasts of positive and negative affect during a waiting period, which in turn predicted risk preferences. Studies 2a and 2b demonstrate substantial heterogeneity in intuitive attention–affect theories: some participants believed attention amplifies the emotional consequences of expectations, whereas others believed attention is uniformly affectively negative. These differences led to sharply divergent predictions about when attention should increase or decrease risk-taking. Study 3 shows that attention is also informative about expectations: participants differed in whether they believed attention signals optimism or pessimism, producing downstream consequences for affective forecasts and risk-taking. Finally, Study 4 reveals that many people endorse asymmetric causal models, viewing optimism as a cause of risk-taking, but risk-taking as a cause of attention. Together, these findings show that forecasts of risk preferences depend critically on people's intuitive theories about how cognition shapes affect and how affective utility is generated over time. By integrating affective forecasting, attention, and decision-making under uncertainty, this work highlights the role of metacognitive beliefs in shaping economic preferences. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Do narcissistic personality traits and immature defense mechanisms hinder communication and cooperation in pilots?
Abstract: This study examines the safety operation behaviors of pilots within the framework of communication and cooperation, compares how these behaviors are affected by narcissistic personality traits, and compares the results for the correct evaluation and management of immature ego defense mechanisms, which are thought to be a factor triggering this relationship. The data were collected from 150 pilot participants working at airlines in Turkey using a survey data collection tool. It was observed that the participants frequently used the defense mechanisms of rationalization, isolation, and acting out. This result shows that pilots continue to exhibit the same behavior by providing acceptable reasons rather than trying to eliminate negative situations by discussing them realistically. It was also observed that they tend to focus only on the objective aspects of events and avoid discussing the parts that negatively affect them psychologically. In addition, it was found that narcissistic personality traits negatively affect the communication and cooperation behaviors of pilots, and immature ego defense mechanisms are a precursor that strengthens the narcissistic personality. It is thought that examining narcissistic personality traits within the framework of immature ego defense mechanisms and managing these mechanisms effectively will contribute greatly to aviation psychology research to prevent risks related to the human factor, which airline companies and authorities view as an important risk within safety management systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: The association between maternal acculturation, acculturative stress and factors related to child feeding in the Hispanic community health study/study of Latinos family lifestyle outcomes research (HCHS/SOL FLOR) study
Abstract: The acculturation process and its related stress have been associated with health declines among Hispanic/Latino immigrants in the US. However, the impact on caregiver feeding style and the home food environment are unknown. This study aimed to assess the associations between maternal acculturation and acculturation stress with both caregiver feeding style (n = 248) and the home food environment (n = 178) using data from mother-child dyads from the Family Lifestyle Outcomes Research ancillary study of the Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos. Children were aged 3-9 years at the time of the study. Results suggest an association between greater maternal acculturative stress and greater odds of authoritative and authoritarian feeding styles. An association between greater acculturative stress and greater maternal demandingness in feeding was also observed. Additionally, greater language acculturation and greater length of time in the US were associated with more sweetened beverages and fewer fruits and vegetables reported in the home. These results highlight the importance of supporting Hispanic immigrants as they adapt to life in the US and developing culturally appropriate interventions that can address child feeding and food purchasing behaviors among immigrant parents. © 2026 The Authors.
