Title: Application of XR in nursing skills training for nurses and nursing students: A scoping review
Abstract: Background: Proficient nursing skills are essential for patient safety, yet limited clinical resources restrict hands-on training for nursing students and nurses. As a promising technical tool, extended reality (XR) holds great potential for nursing skills training, though a comprehensive synthesis of its applications, outcomes and barriers remains lacking. Objective: This scoping review aimed to map the applications of XR in nursing skills training, summarize training outcomes and barriers, evaluate outcomes using the Kirkpatrick Model, and describe their use across the three XR modalities. The Kirkpatrick Model classifies training outcomes into four levels: Level 1 Reaction, Level 2 Learning, Level 3 Behavior, and Level 4 Results. Methods: Following Arksey and O'Malley's framework, nine databases were searched for studies published between 2015 and 2026 on XR-based nursing skills training for nurses and nursing students. Outcomes were mapped to the Kirkpatrick Model. Results: A total of 128 studies were included. Virtual reality (VR, n = 105, 82%) dominated XR application, with augmented reality (AR, n = 15, 11.7%) and mixed reality (MR, n = 8, 6.2%) underrepresented, covering fundamental, specialized and emergency nursing skills. Skill level (n = 87, 67.9%) and satisfaction (n = 81, 63.2%) were frequently reported outcomes, with skill level corresponding to Level 2 Learning and satisfaction falling under Level 1 Reaction of the Kirkpatrick Model, while data regarding Level 3 Behavior and Level 4 Results remained scarce. Technical issues (n = 33, 25.7%), realism gaps (n = 23, 17.9%) and physical discomfort (n = 22, 17.1%) were the three most frequently reported barriers that undermine the effectiveness of XR training. Conclusion: This scoping review maps current evidence on XR-based nursing skills training, with VR representing the predominant modality and AR and MR remaining comparatively underrepresented. Applications primarily focus on fundamental nursing skills, and reported outcomes are concentrated at Kirkpatrick Levels 1 and 2, whereas evidence at Levels 3 and 4 remains scarce. Technical issues, realism gaps, and physical discomfort are among the most frequently reported barriers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Constructing a time-varying network to observe the spatiotemporal evolution characteristics of intra-city migration
Abstract: Studying the long-term migration network within cities effectively reveals changes in urban spatial structures. This paper focuses on intra-city migration activities, introducing a method for dynamic network construction and analysis based on spatiotemporal data, offering a new perspective for examining the dynamic characteristics of residential migration within cities and their relationship to urban development. Migration behaviors are aggregated at the community level in the form of migration flows, and a time-varying network model of migration flows is constructed. Community detection and dynamic evolution analyses are conducted to uncover migration behavior characteristics. Using Shenzhen, a megacity in China, as a case study, a migration network spanning six consecutive years (2018–2023) was constructed using mobile phone signaling data. Our findings reveal that the gravitational pull of communities in the northern and eastern sub-center areas has increased. The dynamic evolution of community structures is closely related to the city's polycentric structure. Smaller network communities are more susceptible to changes, while strengthened regional connections have led to community mergers. The time-varying migration network proposed in this study provides an effective method for observing the development patterns of urban spatial structures from a mesoscopic perspective by tracking and analyzing migration flow patterns between different areas within a city. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Vaheddoost M.; Özbay A.
Title: Personality, resilience, and educational recovery after disaster: A 12-month longitudinal analysis of mediation and cross-lagged associations
Abstract: Individual differences in personality may shape educational adaptation following natural disasters. This 12-month longitudinal study examined Big Five personality traits, academic resilience, and four adaptation outcomes among 884 Turkish university students following the February 2023 earthquake. Latent growth curve models indicated that conscientiousness (β = 0.34) and emotional stability (β = 0.28) showed the strongest associations with adaptation trajectories. Academic resilience accounted for approximately 32–38% of these associations, although concurrent T1 assessment of personality and resilience precludes causal interpretation of the indirect effects. Confirmatory factor analyses and the Fornell–Larcker criterion supported the empirical distinctiveness of personality and academic resilience. Cross-lagged analyses showed prospective associations between resilience and subsequent adaptation across academic performance, online learning adaptation, psychological well-being, and life satisfaction, with resilience-to-adaptation paths generally stronger and more consistent than reverse paths. These associations should be interpreted cautiously because traditional CLPMs do not separate within- and between-person variance. A robustness analysis using verified pre-earthquake GPA records ( n = 648) indicated that the principal personality associations with academic recovery persisted when performance was modeled relative to pre-earthquake achievement. Person-centered analyses supported three prototypical trajectories: Resilient Adapters (63.7%), Gradual Improvers (26.7%), and Struggling Students (9.6%). The findings are organized using the Dynamic Personality–Resilience–Adaptation framework as a heuristic, educationally specific extension of existing personality-adaptation accounts rather than as an independently validated theory. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Strengthening strategic environmental assessment through ecosystem service valuation and public preferences: evidence from Ireland
Abstract: Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) is a key instrument for integrating environmental considerations into plans and programmes at an early stage of decision-making. However, effectiveness reviews highlight a significant gap in the systematic quantification of SEA benefits, particularly regarding non-market values and ecosystem services (ES). To address this deficiency, this study, conducted in the Republic of Ireland, adopts a sequential research design in which expert workshops and focus groups were used to develop a nationally representative discrete choice survey (n = 970) to estimate willingness to pay (WTP) for environmental improvements and to enhance the effectiveness, legitimacy, and practical uptake of SEA. Our findings reveal strong public support for planning scenarios that include greater public participation, substantial increases in local green space (10–30%), and acceptance of short procedural delays (1–2 years) in SEA processes to ensure comprehensive environmental assessment. Model estimates indicate that respondents expressed a WTP of approximately €48–€63 per year for a 30% increase in green space, with the lower estimate derived from the multinomial logit (MNL) model and the higher estimate from the random parameters logit (RPL) model. Results also indicate limited public familiarity with SEA instruments and relatively low trust in governmental environmental decision-making. The study presents a methodological framework for integrating ecosystem service valuation and measurable forms of public participation into SEA processes to support more effective and legitimate environmental decision-making. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Marine ecosystem extent accounting in a deep-sea-dominated nation
Abstract: The global economy is heavily reliant on healthy ecosystems, which provide humanity’s foundation for prosperity, resilience, and well-being. This interdependence has driven growing international interest in developing frameworks to assess and account for the value of natural capital to humanity, society, and the economy. In response to this need, the United Nations developed the System of Environmental-Economic Accounting - Ecosystem Accounting (SEEA EA), and, in late 2024, the European Parliament adopted Regulation (EU) 2024/3024, which establishes ecosystem accounts as a core component of the European Union’s environmental-economic accounting system. This Regulation mandates Member States to compile data for three key physical accounts: ecosystem extent, ecosystem condition, and ecosystem services flows, covering both their terrestrial and marine territories. It provides a comprehensive framework that allows countries to move beyond GDP, enabling a systematized and coherent assessment of Member States' natural capital. Marine ecosystem accounting represents an innovative and data-driven approach for integrating ecological, economic, and social information into decision-making processes. This paper presents the methodological approach and preliminary results of Portugal’s Marine Ecosystem Extent Account, which showed that 99% of the Portuguese maritime space is deep-sea (' 200 m). Results show that, particularly for deep-sea dominated nations, greater detail is needed, beyond classes defined solely by depth and slope, in order to support useful and actionable ecosystem accounting. The paper also discusses the methodological challenges encountered during the compilation of Portugal’s marine extent account and highlights its policy relevance as a decision-support tool for evidence-based marine management and sustainable ocean governance. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Suppressed inquiry: The hidden toll of working with satisfaction-optimized AI
Abstract: LLMs have become thinking companions for hundreds of millions worldwide, and they often do remarkable work. But their satisfaction-optimized design produces suppressed inquiry: the tendency for LLMs to inhibit rather than facilitate users' questioning process. LLMs appear fluent, confident, and seemingly all-knowing, their near-instant and polished output making non-LLM work feel unacceptably tedious and less eloquent. They affirm rather than interrogate users' assumptions, producing output that is deceptively adequate—shallower, less original, and less carefully reasoned than it appears. Seemingly competent systems also reduce vigilance and the monitoring impulse that independent judgment requires. Their responses also confine users within the frame they establish, narrowing what users think to ask. These costs are self-concealing: detecting them requires the very engagement that they suppress. And repeated delegation gradually atrophies users' capacity to reason independently. Three converging pressures make correction difficult: commercial incentives that reward satisfaction over substance, LLMs’ tendency to revert to satisfaction-optimized defaults even when users push back, and a societal drift toward less-effortful engagement. We propose a research agenda to deepen the understanding of suppressed inquiry and how to counter it, to move closer to the remarkable thinking partners LLMs promised to be. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Temporal dynamics of mixed symptom configurations in bipolar disorder: An intensive longitudinal study
Abstract: Background Mixed symptom presentations in bipolar disorder (BD) are clinically consequential, but their short-term temporal organization remains poorly understood. Using ecological momentary assessment (EMA), we mapped transitions across depressive, hypo/manic, co-symptomatic, and mixed symptom configurations and examined the symptom context surrounding mixedness. Methods Fifty adults with BD were recruited for the BADAS Study and completed the Bipolar Disorder Symptom Scale (BDSx) twice daily over 123 days on average (3 to 14 months). Symptom presentations were classified into 10 mutually exclusive configurations spanning asymptomatic, depressive, hypo/manic, co-symptomatic, and mixed symptom configurations. We characterized 9627 consecutive within-person transitions, modeled predictors of entry into mixedness, and examined prospective associations between the underlying continuous symptom dimensions. Results Overall, 42.3% of transitions remained in the same symptom configuration. Mixedness showed increasing short-term continuity with severity: 60.1%, 68.4%, and 75.0% of assessments remained mixed following low, moderate, and clinical-range mixedness, respectively. Depression-containing configurations accounted for 88.6% of 925 entries into mixedness and 88.6% of 932 exits. Among 493 complete nonmixed–mixed–nonmixed sequences, 77.7% were depression-containing on both sides. In prospective analyses restricted to transitions within 12 h, within-person elevations in depression predicted subsequent hypo/ mania after accounting for prior hypo/mania and elapsed time (standardized β = 0.077, 95% CI [0.048, 0.106], p < .001). The reciprocal association was smaller (β = 0.026, 95% CI [−0.003, 0.055], p = .077), and the two pathways differed significantly ( p = .019). Conclusions Mixed symptom configurations showed structured short-term persistence and occurred predominantly within depression-containing symptom contexts. Prospective dimensional analyses additionally identified modest temporal asymmetry between depressive and hypo/manic symptoms independent of the categorical definition of mixedness. Copyright © 2026. Title: Locus of morphological processing during visual L2 compound recognition: An ERP investigation
Abstract: The extent to which second language (L2) speakers process morphologically complex words through morphem-based processes remains debated, with conflicting evidence from behavioral studies suggesting that L2 learners may rely primarily on orthographic overlap rather than morphological structure. The present study employed morpho-semantic priming paradigm and event-related potentials (ERPs) to investigate whether and how Chinese-English bilinguals engage in morphological decomposition and morpho-semantic integration during real-time English compound word recognition. We manipulated two factors: Relatedness (primes semantically related vs. unrelated to the first constituent morpheme of the compound word) and Semantic Transparency (transparent vs. opaque compound words). In the N400 time window, a significant main effect of Relatedness emerged, with both transparent and opaque compound words showing comparable N400 attenuation, indicating early semantically blind morphological decomposition. In the late negativity window (800–1200 ms), a significant main effect of Semantic Transparency emerged, with opaque compounds eliciting greater negativity than transparent compounds, reflecting the late morpho-semantic integration process. These findings demonstrate a biphasic pattern of L2 morphological processing encompassing early obligatory morphological decomposition followed by late morpho-semantic integration. Overall, our findings suggest that Chinese-English bilinguals can engage in native-like morphological processing during recognition of English compound words. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Effects of orthographic consistency on spoken word recognition and production in L1-Spanish children
Abstract: Learning to read reshapes spoken language processing by establishing systematic mappings between phonemes and graphemes. One robust manifestation of this interaction is the Orthographic Consistency Effect (OCE), whereby spoken words containing phonemes with a single possible spelling (consistent spellings) are processed more efficiently than those with multiple possible spellings (inconsistent spellings). The present study investigates whether early L1-Spanish readers show phoneme-level OCEs in spoken word perception and production. L1-Spanish second graders of around seven years of age completed three tasks: an auditory lexical decision task, a picture naming task, and a reading aloud task. Stimuli could contain either consistent phonemes or inconsistent phonemes. Results revealed OCEs in both perception and production. In the auditory lexical decision task, children responded more accurately to items with consistent than inconsistent phoneme-to-grapheme mappings. In reading aloud, consistent items were named both faster and more accurately than inconsistent items. In contrast, no consistency effects were observed in picture naming, a task that does not overtly involve orthographic input. These findings demonstrate that, even in a highly transparent orthography, early readers are sensitive to phoneme-level orthographic inconsistencies during spoken word recognition and production. L1-Spanish early readers appear to rely on phonological decoding strategically, suggesting that the impact of literacy on speech perception and production in Spanish is present but task-dependent at the onset of reading acquisition. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Bridging the Human-AI preference gap: A persuasion-oriented tripartite framework
Abstract: The remarkable performance of artificial intelligence (AI) systems on a wide variety of complex tasks has fueled its rapid adoption in recent years. Yet, many individuals still exhibit a human-AI preference gap, such that they prefer human-generated over AI-generated outputs and follow recommendations made by generative AI (GenAI) less than human advice. We conceptualize the rejection of a superior AI system in favor of an inferior human as a persuasion failure that necessitates psychological rather than technological resolution. Recent research has identified various interventions that compress the human-AI preference gap. We codify these interventions by introducing a persuasion-oriented tripartite framework that delineates three distinct paths by which the preference gap between humans and AI systems may be narrowed: (1) AI-centric interventions, which directly bolster perceptions and evaluations of AI systems; (2) human-centric interventions, which reduce the (often inflated) perceptions and evaluations of humans; and (3) hybrid interventions, which offer an integrated or reformulated alternative that combines human and AI elements. Ultimately, our tripartite framework illustrates how different persuasion tactics fundamentally reshape beliefs and attitudes about both AI and humans, thereby informing system design elements and communication strategies that can bridge the human-AI preference gap. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Using physiological measures to assess and diagnose team performance: An interrogative approach
Abstract: Physiological measures have the potential to capture the dynamic nature of teamwork as it unfolds. Despite this potential, relatively few studies have applied physiological data in team contexts, leaving a gap in theory and practice. To address this gap, this work examines the following question: What are the emerging principles for using physiological measures to assess and diagnose team performance? To explore this question, we present an interrogative approach that structures the key considerations for applying physiological measures in team research. Specifically, this approach organizes considerations related to the purpose, context, personnel, timing, measurement selection, and implementation of using physiological measures to assess team performance. Building on prior guidance, we propose a set of emerging principles that synthesize best practices while introducing new considerations specific to the use of physiological data in team contexts. These principles provide practical guidance for researchers and practitioners seeking to leverage physiological measures, while emphasizing that their effective use depends on rigorous methodology, ethical safeguards, and integration with other validated assessment approaches. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Recent clinical encounters for suicidal thoughts and behaviours: Disclosure, assessment, missed opportunities, and implications for practice
Abstract: Objective Many individuals who die by suicide have contact with healthcare services in the months preceding their death, making these interactions critical opportunities for identification, intervention, and support. However, little is known about how individuals experiencing suicidal thoughts and behaviours (STBs) perceive recent clinical encounters, including how these experiences are discussed and managed. Method Australian adults (N = 266; M  age  = 32.9; range = 18–71 years) who had experienced STBs and consulted with a mental health professional within the past two weeks completed an online survey examining suicide-related enquiry, disclosure experiences, clinician responses, and satisfaction. Results Psychologists were the most commonly consulted clinicians (49.2%), and 90.8% reported having seen the same clinician previously. Although 95.7% of participants considered discussing their STBs at least somewhat important, only 67.9% reported discussing these experiences with clinicians. Among those who did not discuss STBs, 50.0% reported that they had not been asked. Participants also reported that clinicians more frequently enquired about general emotional wellbeing (80.6%) than directly about STBs (55.3%). Among participants who did discuss STBs, 52.1% reported withholding information, while 46.2% reported feeling hesitant to disclose. Safety planning (36.9%) and follow-up (37.4%) were reported infrequently despite being viewed as important and helpful. Nevertheless, 75.4% reported being satisfied with their recent interactions. Conclusions Despite generally positive experiences with these interactions, the findings highlight opportunities to strengthen suicide prevention by creating opportunities to discuss STBs beyond initial clinical encounters, supporting disclosure through compassionate care, and ensuring that suicide-specific care is provided where appropriate following identification. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Unequal sanitation in the Global South: infrastructure and governance shortfalls in northern Minas Gerais, Brazil
Abstract: The universal provision of public utilities, such as basic sanitation, remains a critical challenge in the Global South, where infrastructure disparities and governance failures perpetuate the exclusion of vulnerable populations. This article analyses the disparities in the provision and management of water, sewerage, solid waste and drainage services in the Brazilian semi-arid region, comparing a regional hub (Montes Claros) with 19 peripheral municipalities in northern Minas Gerais. Using microdata from the National Sanitation Information System (SINISA – 2024), the study develops a matrix of institutional compliance and integrated indicators of coverage and inefficiency. The results confirm the persistence of a deep centre-periphery infrastructure divide and identify severe ‘statistical invisibility’ — characterised by an absence of official data — in localities with lower governance capacity. Furthermore, the study highlights the lack of coordination between sanitation policy areas, with a serious historical neglect of stormwater drainage and solid waste management. It is concluded that current funding metrics and the expansion of privatisation in the sector are insufficient without a regulatory framework that addresses territorial inequalities. The study provides recommendations for improving public policies, highlighting the need to review federal coordination mechanisms and subsidies to ensure water and sanitation security in peripheral regions. © 2026 The Authors. Title: A systems analysis of fatal railway level crossing crashes
Abstract: Fatal railway level crossing crashes represent a public safety challenge. Existing data on these crashes is limited, mostly focusing on frequencies rather than providing an in-depth understanding of the underlying causes. This study aimed to demonstrate the utility of using coronial findings, supplemented with reports from investigation agencies, to understand the system-wide factors contributing to railway crossing crashes and to explore the proposed recommendations. A systems thinking accident analysis approach, the AcciMap technique, underpinned the analysis. Over a 20-year period, 151 cases were identified, involving a range of road user types. Of these cases, 135 included sufficient detail to extract contributory factors and recommendations. A total of 483 contributory factors were extracted and used to develop an aggregate AcciMap. Most factors were associated with road user behaviour and/or individual characteristics, as opposed to systemic issues. Unique contributory factors were identified for crashes occurring at active crossings (those with dynamic warnings present) versus passive crossings (those with signage only). A total of 184 recommendations were extracted and mapped using the AcciMap framework. Recommendations tended to take a system-wide view of preventing future occurrences, acknowledging the complexity of managing risk at the interface of two transport modes. The analysis provided important information to support crash prevention efforts, including a set of common systemic recommendations identified from the data that require collaborative efforts across road and rail stakeholders. Mechanisms for supporting this collaboration should be further explored. The study also provided learnings regarding the nature of coronial investigations and areas for potential improvement. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Evaluating university campus open spaces through a resilience-based urban system lens: Integrating ecological, spatial and adaptive dimensions
Abstract: This study conceptualizes university campus open spaces as socio-ecological systems and develops an integrated evaluation framework combining spatial elements, ecological services, and adaptive capacities. Addressing the tendency for campus open spaces to be assessed through site-specific criteria, the study applies a resilience-based urban systems perspective to capture the interdependencies among environmental, spatial, and functional performance attributes. Using a case study at a Hong Kong university campus, questionnaire-based surveys were conducted with 220 users across ten open-space types, and Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) was employed to examine how perceived importance of performance attributes shapes satisfaction with different open-space settings. The results reveal two distinct satisfaction pathways. For passive open spaces (courtyards, cafés, squares), satisfaction is predominantly driven by spatial elements (β = 0.507), indicating that perceptions of openness, scale, and aesthetic quality play a decisive role in shaping user experience, with ecological services exerting an indirect influence through spatial elements. In contrast, satisfaction with active open spaces (sport places) is primarily shaped by adaptive capacities (β = 0.268), such as accessibility, safety, and sociability, reflecting a more function-oriented appraisal. Across both pathways, ecological services emerge as a foundational dimension, significantly influencing spatial elements and adaptive capacities, and being directly associated with satisfaction in ecologically intensive settings such as rooftop gardens. By revealing differentiated satisfaction mechanisms and their structural relationships, this study advances the understanding of campus open spaces as integrated and resilient systems. The findings provide actionable guidance for campus planning and management, suggesting that investments should prioritize spatial quality in passive spaces while emphasizing functional accessibility and safety for active environments. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Does AI encourage lax thinking, or does the human preference for validation make it that way?
Abstract: We offer a different perspective on whether AI encourages lax human thought. Specifically, we propose an “enjoyment-engagement tradeoff”: the type of chatbot that people most enjoy interacting with may be the type that encourages less cognitive engagement. We examined this possibility in the context of chatbot congeniality, expecting that people would prefer interacting with a congenial chatbot (one that consistently validates their views) over an uncongenial chatbot (one that consistently challenges their views); furthermore, we expected that people would show greater signs of enjoyment when interacting with a congenial chatbot but would show greater signs of cognitive engagement when interacting with an uncongenial chatbot. We tested this idea in an experiment wherein participants (N = 438) interacted with either a congenial chatbot, an uncongenial chatbot, or a default-model baseline chatbot that exhibited the default behavior of a popular AI chatbot. Results, based on self-reports and linguistic analyses of conversation transcripts, suggested that participants who interacted with the congenial (vs. uncongenial) chatbot showed greater attraction toward the chatbot (e.g., desire to interact again) along with signs of greater enjoyment (e.g., more positive affect) while participants who interacted with the uncongenial (vs. congenial) chatbot exhibited various signs of greater cognitive engagement (e.g., enhanced perceived learning, higher word counts). The default-model baseline chatbot closely resembled the congenial chatbot in its effects on attraction, enjoyment, and cognitive engagement. Findings suggest a novel perspective on whether AI chatbots encourage lax human thought: People's preference for congenial (vs. uncongenial) chatbots may, ultimately, undermine cognitive engagement. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Can visibility-based metrics predict soundscape perception in cities?
Abstract: Context plays a central role in soundscape perception within the ISO 12913 series framework. However, there is a lack of empirical evidence on how to identify operational, standardised proxy metrics for capturing ‘context’ in soundscape assessment and prediction. The study addresses this gap by deriving a set of visibility-based metrics from Isovist and Visibility Graph Analysis (VGA) and evaluating their effectiveness in a soundscape predictive model. An on-site soundscape data campaign was conducted in Bloomsbury, Central London., Isovist and VGA metrics were computed for each soundscape observation to obtain a high-resolution, geospatial soundscape dataset (N = 787). Key findings stand out: (1) Isovist and VGA metrics correlate strongly with pleasantness (PISO) but weakly with eventfulness (EISO); (2) four ‘visual-spatial’ clusters (ViSpID) are derived from the selected Isovist and VGA metrics: Highly connected streets, Moderately connected streets, Open spaces & poorly connected streets, and Enclosed spaces; and (3) a linear multilevel model predicting PISO that incorporates these clusters (ViSpID) with psychoacoustic predictors (R2 = 0.51) outperforms a psychoacoustics-only baseline model (R2 = 0.15). These findings demonstrate that Isovist and VGA metrics provide practical proxies for the structural visibility and spatial configuration dimensions of physical context and support a systematic and reproducible framework for integrating these effects into predictive modelling. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Adaptive Learning-based Semantic Enhancement for Multimodal Dialogue Discourse Parsing
Abstract: Dialogue Discourse Parsing (DDP) aims to identify dependency structures and relation types among utterances in conversations. Title: On the role of perception in the psychology of art: More than meets the eye of the beholder
Abstract: Perception is a cornerstone of aesthetic experience and the psychology of art, providing the primary means through which people engage with artworks and generate emotional and cognitive responses. Across theories of aesthetics, perception is the key process connecting the classic psychological triad of stimulus, person, and context, by integrating sensory information with situational influences. It encompasses factors ranging from low-level visual features, such as natural image statistics with broad appeal, to high-level influences related to familiarity with particular contents and artistic styles shaped by individual experience and sociocultural background. Title: Psychometric properties and validity of the Family Accommodation Scale–Patient Version (FAS-PV) in adults with obsessive compulsive disorder: A French adaptation

Abstract: Background: Family accommodation (FA) is a common phenomenon in obsessive–compulsive disorder (OCD) and is associated with greater symptom severity, functional impairment, and poorer treatment outcomes. Patients completed the French FAS-PV alongside measures of OCD severity (Y-BOCS), relative-reported accommodation (FAS-SR), psychological distress, functional impairment, and family functioning. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses were conducted, and internal consistency, test–retest reliability, and convergent and divergent validity were examined. Authors: Bonnell S.; Blakley J.
Title: Proactivity vs. specificity: Addressing cumulative effects through planning - not prediction - in strategic and regional assessments
Abstract: Strategic environmental assessments (SEAs) and regional assessments (RAs) are often seen as more effective means of assessing and managing cumulative effects compared to project-level impact assessments (IAs) alone. Inevitable uncertainty about future development activities during these assessments is, however, sometimes treated as a constraint – rather than an opportunity - which can affect whether, how and the degree to which cumulative effects are being addressed. Drawing on several recent Canadian SEA and RA examples, this article illustrates and investigates these matters, including the at times limited analysis of cumulative effects in these assessments, associated attempts to have these issues pushed to later assessment tiers, and a resulting lack of planning outputs and influence in practice. The cases illustrate that uncertainty about future development and limitations in data, time and resources are often raised as key reasons for this, reflecting a continued emphasis on effects prediction rather than on achieving a type and level of analysis appropriate to the scale and timing of these assessments, and importantly, capable of informing broader planning outcomes. Case studies also suggest that the latter may be constrained by a lack of institutional willingness to develop or use planning outputs that may affect future development based on potential cumulative effects. © 2026

Authors: Wang Z.; Long X.
Title: The health effects of genetically modified crops
Abstract: Public debates on genetically modified (GM) crops center on environmental and health risks, yet evidence remains limited and focuses largely on herbicide-tolerant varieties or on local exposure, leaving the broad consequences of insect-resistant crops unclear. Insect-resistant crops can reduce pesticide use and generate health effects beyond directly exposed farmers. Yet their net effects are ambiguous, as any environmental gains may be offset by crop substitution, pest resistance, industrial expansion, and land-use change. We exploit the staggered approval of Bt cotton across China, combined with river networks that link cotton-growing areas to downstream residents. Bt cotton approval leads to significant downstream reductions in under-five mortality by 4.2%, driven by reduced pesticide use and improved water quality. In aggregate, Bt cotton approval reduces national pesticide use by 3.2%. The findings show that the social value of insect-resistant GM crops can be significantly underestimated, as they generate positive health externalities through environmental spillovers. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Colors of perfectionism - How experimental feedbacks change physiology using Mandalas
Abstract: Although the link between perfectionism, performance, and feedback has been widely studied, findings remain inconclusive, partly due to the lack of objective assessment methods. Title: Crowd evacuation dynamics in a multi-exit room under the presence of simulated attackers: An experimental study
Abstract: In recent years, knife and axe violent attacks in crowded public places worldwide have occurred frequently. Such incidents easily trigger large-scale crowd physiological stress and stampede accidents, and have become one of the primary public safety risks threatening urban crowd. To reveal the physical-physiological coupling mechanism of crowd evacuation under knife attack scenarios, this study investigates evacuation dynamics in a multi-exit room under simulated attacker-induced threats through controlled experiments. Sixty-two participants completed 54 repeated runs across 27 experimental combinations, including 3 simulated attacker scenarios (0, 1, 2 simulated attackers) and 3 exit layout configurations (1, 2, 4 exits). High-precision trajectories were extracted using PeTrack software, and continuous physiological data were recorded by Apple Watch S7 devices. Results show that simulated attackers significantly exacerbate exit bottleneck deadlocks and the classic “faster-is-slower” effect with markedly prolonged peak time headway. They significantly increase crowd detour ratio by forcing evacuees to take longer alternative routes, reduce overall mean speed despite initial individual acceleration, elevate flow field turbulence intensity, and cause the fundamental speed-density relationship to deviate substantially from classical pedestrian flow laws. A distinct “physiological lag effect” is quantitatively verified, with peak heart rate consistently occurring after the completion of evacuation in most high-stress trials, and crowd danger increases stepwise with increasing attacker count. The findings of this study reveal the unique evacuation characteristics under dynamic threat conditions, providing critical scientific basis and empirical support for multi-exit architectural layout optimization, targeted emergency evacuation plan formulation, and proactive crowd safety management under violent attack scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Adapting to linguistic innovations: the role of language contact in bilingual and monolingual speakers
Abstract: Contact between speakers and languages may play a key role in driving language change. During interaction, speakers tend to adapt to their interlocutors' speech, which can cumulatively lead to longer-term changes. Yet it remains unclear how innovations emerge, and who drives their adoption. These questions are addressed through two experiments on Italian motion-events framing. Study 1 examines German-Italian bilinguals with varying cumulative German contact, exploring whether exposure to innovative satellite-framed constructions triggers adaptation within Italian and across languages. Study 2 tests Italian monolinguals to assess adaptation in the absence of cross-linguistic influence. Results show that both bilinguals and monolinguals adapt to innovative structures at an abstract level, but only bilinguals with a high degree of German contact maintain these changes in a post-test, highlighting the role of bilingual experience. Findings suggest language contact may enhance the uptake of innovations, providing insight into the cognitive mechanisms underlying language change. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Cooperative operation of networked virtual power plants in low-carbon distribution systems
Abstract: Networked virtual power plants can create coordination gains while their emission and participation outcomes depend on the governing carbon and settlement rules. This study develops a DSO-coordinated mechanism that couples feeder-constrained two-stage stochastic dispatch, carbon-policy accounting, and coalition-stable settlement. The dispatch model coordinates renewable output, dispatchable generation, stationary storage, mobility-coupled electric vehicles, reserve, and scenario recourse. Risk is represented by six clustered empirical scenarios and one explicit tail scenario, with a 95% conditional value-at-risk term. The policy layer separates physical operational emissions, allocated allowances, carbon-valued accounting cost, and internal settlement. The settlement layer uses standard Shapley values to calibrate weighted-Nash gains and evaluates every coalition through core and least-core diagnostics. In a 168 h CAISO-eGRID case, cooperation under the same tiered carbon rule reduced total accounting cost from 52,566.65 to 50,349.19 USD and created 2217.47 USD of surplus. Physical emissions changed from 141.3554 to 144.5849 t CO2, an increase of 3.2294 t CO2 under the matched policy. The integrated results identify the operating and governance conditions that support cost efficiency, carbon accountability, and stable participation. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Teachers’ language-promoting questions in primary classroom discourse: Relations with teacher expectations and student learning
Abstract: Background: Enhancing student learning with the use of cognitively and linguistically challenging questions is considered key for fostering student learning in classroom discourse. Theoretical models suggest that teachers’ use of questions is related to their achievement expectations for students. Methods: First, we coded the language-promoting quality of teacher questions based on video recordings of whole-classroom discourse. Second, we employed multilevel modeling to examine links between teachers’ (inaccurate) expectations, teacher questions, and later student achievement. Results: Teacher questions were mostly of low language-promoting quality. Teachers asked significantly more questions in mathematics, including more open-ended questions. For mathematics, (inaccurately) low expectations were linked with higher frequencies of questions that promote elaboration and description. Title: Auditing TikTok’s recommendations: Understanding the prevalence of misinformation on the platform

Abstract: Short video platforms have rapidly increased in popularity, bringing forth a concerning trend: widespread dissemination of misinformation partially owing to the persuasive nature of the rich media these platforms support. We explore the prevalence of misinformation in TikTok’s auto-complete suggestions, search results, and For You Page (FYP) recommendations. Title: A dispatch-aware framework for resource-efficient distributed electrification: A case study of photovoltaic-battery streetlights
Abstract: The rapid deployment of distributed electrification infrastructure requires assessment approaches that jointly consider operational carbon benefits, life-cycle environmental burdens, and public investment. Title: A sight for restored minds: examining the impact of nature image exposure on perceived restorativeness and healthy food choices
Abstract: Nature exposure (including through images) offers physical and psychological benefits, including cognitive restoration. Title: Automatic binary security classification of arabic mobile app reviews using transformer models and active learning
Abstract: Mobile application user reviews provide valuable insights into user-reported issues, including security concerns that are critical for software engineering activities such as requirements analysis and system design. To construct a high-quality labeled dataset, we developed an annotation approach combining keyword-guided sample selection, expert annotation, and iterative dataset refinement using active learning. During the active learning phase, semantic feature representations were generated using Low-Rank Adaptation-enhanced sentence transformers and combined with machine learning classifiers within an agreement-based active learning strategy to identify candidate samples for expert validation. The process was conducted over ten iterations, starting with 300 expert-annotated reviews and terminating when classifier performance stabilized. Following the stopping criterion, the final classifier-agreement samples were expert-validated and used to construct a held-out test set rather than being added to the training data. Title: Personalizing AI voice agents: How voice agents with similar voices shape trust, self-congruency, and behavior

Authors: Qian J.; Ji Y.; Dang R.; Wu Y.
Title: Enhancing flood resilience in critical communication infrastructures: empirical analysis and software-defined architecture design
Abstract: Mobile communication systems serve as a lifeline for disaster response, yet catastrophic floods—exemplified by the Beijing 23·7 and Zhengzhou 7·20 events—have exposed profound vulnerabilities that trigger cascading failures in emergency command and rescue operations. While existing interventions predominantly focus on temporary hardware deployments (e.g., UAVs), the potential of software-defined optimization within existing 5G terrestrial communication infrastructure remains critically underexplored. This study addresses this gap through a dual-layered research design that bridges technology and disaster management practice. First, we establish an empirical foundation by applying an LLM-assisted mixed-methods analysis to a comprehensive multi-source corpus. This corpus integrates academic literature, official disaster reports, and original interviews with personnel from emergency management departments and technical experts from telecommunications operators. This analysis identifies and characterizes five core communication failure modes in real-world flood scenarios, clarifying the critical infrastructure vulnerabilities that precipitate decision-making paralysis and systemic governance failures. Second, grounded in these empirical findings, we develop an integrated theoretical framework and a dynamic operational architecture for 5G base station (gNB) resilience. This architecture systematically maps specific 5G software-defined capabilities to the identified disaster challenges. The results provide a cost-effective, scalable strategy for enhancing critical infrastructure resilience without requiring extensive hardware modifications. This research offers actionable guidelines for policy makers and emergency planners to maintain information pathways during extreme climate-related risks, directly contributing to the modernization of urban safety governance. Authors: Zhao Q.; Wu X.; Luo L.; Zhang Y.
Title: Teachers' attitudes toward students' mistakes and students’ mathematical creativity: The mediating role of diagnostic skills in a multi-level model based on organizational creative theory
Abstract: Background: Although the importance of mathematical creativity is increasingly recognized, the relationships between teacher-related factors and students' mathematical creativity remain unclear. Teachers' attitudes toward students' mistakes and their diagnostic skills have been identified as potentially relevant factors; however, their relationships with students’ mathematical creativity have not yet been fully examined. Objective: Drawing on Organizational Creativity Theory, this study examines teachers' diagnostic skills as a mediator in the relationship between teachers' attitudes toward student mistakes and students’ mathematical creativity, assessed through problem-posing tasks in terms of fluency, flexibility, and originality. Sample: This study employed purposive sampling and included 81 middle school mathematics teachers from different regions of China and 2046 students from their classes. Methods: Teacher questionnaire data and student mathematical creativity task responses were analyzed using multilevel structural equation modeling. Results: Teachers' attitudes toward student mistakes significantly and positively predicted teachers' diagnostic skills (β = 0.42), and teachers' diagnostic skills significantly and positively predicted students' mathematical creativity (β = 0.85). Teachers' diagnostic skills significantly mediated the association between teachers' attitudes toward student mistakes and students’ mathematical creativity (indirect effect β = 0.36). Conclusion: These results help clarify how (i.e., through teachers' diagnostic skills) the effects of teachers' attitudes toward students' mistakes on students’ mathematical creativity are strengthened. The findings are also consistent with the proposition in Organizational Creativity Theory that group-level processes are important for understanding the association between contextual factors and individual creative outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Cao Z.; Ling L.; Li S.; Chen X.; Robinson G.M.
Title: Spatiotemporal evolution and driving mechanisms of rural human settlement quality in China: Based on a Kernel-Driver analytical framework
Abstract: Improving rural human settlements is essential for enhancing rural residents' well-being and achieving SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities). This study develops a Kernel-Driver analytical framework to investigate the spatiotemporal evolution, driving mechanisms, and future trajectories of rural human settlement quality (RHSQ) in China from 2005 to 2024. Results show that: First, RHSQ improved substantially, with an average annual growth rate of 6.10%, exhibiting a stable east-central-west gradient and gradually narrowing regional disparities. Second, rural development investment, farmers' income, rural industrial upgrading, urbanization, and rural digitalization promoted RHSQ improvement, although their marginal effects weakened over time. Rural hollowing and terrain slope constrained RHSQ, while rural population aging showed a weak positive effect overall, with declining intensity and negative effects in some regions. These drivers exhibited pronounced spatiotemporal heterogeneity. Third, RHSQ is projected to improve under all scenarios, with the enhanced rural revitalization scenario generating the greatest improvement. However, spatial equity remains challenging, as policy strengthening has limited capacity to reshape long-standing regional disparities. By revealing the dynamic mechanisms underlying RHSQ evolution, this study provides insights for developing more targeted and adaptive rural governance strategies to promote equitable and sustainable rural development. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Stünz G.V.; Strauß N.
Title: Media representations of corporate sustainability communication: German news coverage of lithium mining in Chile
Abstract: Introduction: The global shift toward e-mobility has intensified scrutiny of raw material procurement, particularly lithium mining in Chile–essential for the automotive industry. However, less is known about how German news media portray and evaluate the sustainability of lithium mining and how corporate messages by the automotive sector are represented in this debate. Methodology: This study analyzes how German news media frame the sustainability of lithium extraction in Chile, focusing on ideological differences across outlets, representations of automotive companies in news coverage, and their implications for industrial and environmental priorities surrounding the debate. A qualitative content analysis of 192 articles from five major outlets (2009-2024) reveals distinct narratives. Results: The left-leaning news outlet Zeit Online and the tabloid Bild emphasize socio-ecological consequences, while the financial newspaper Handelsblatt and liberal outlet FAZ foreground economic risks; the conservative newspaper Welt combines environmental and geopolitical concerns. Findings highlight temporal shifts whereby articles after 2020 reflect global awareness of geopolitical issues. Discussion: The findings suggest that German news coverage increasingly frames lithium mining through interconnected environmental, industrial, and geopolitical concerns, while automotive companies occupy uneven positions of visibility within these mediated sustainability debates. Conclusions: By identifying how automotive companies are represented in news coverage, the study highlights patterns that are consistent with agenda-building dynamics in the interaction between automotive companies and news media. © 2027, HISIN (History of Information Systems). Authors: Li B.; Dykeman C.
Title: Aggregate convergence and constituent divergence in incel-related online communities: A mentalizing-theory lens on cross-platform linguistic patterns
Abstract: The “incel” (involuntary celibate) subculture comprises an online ecosystem spanning mainstream-hosted, independent, and recovery-oriented communities. Using Fonagy's mentalizing framework, we derived four community-level Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC-22) patterns: rigidity–flexibility (Psychic Equivalence-inspired), goal–affect balance (Teleological Mode-inspired), cognitive-affective elaboration (Pretend Mode-inspired), and counter-positioning–curiosity (Epistemic Mistrust-inspired). Study 1 compared 2261 incels.is discussion-thread documents with 15 LIWC-22 Test Kitchen reference corpora and the overall benchmark. Incels.is generally showed higher Psychic Equivalence-inspired scores and consistently higher Epistemic Mistrust-inspired scores; Teleological Mode-inspired differences were reference-dependent, whereas Pretend Mode-inspired results were heterogeneous across reference genres. Excluding text from the top 1% of identifiable contributors retained 61 of 64 comparison directions. Study 2 analyzed 28,980 platform-specific user aggregates across five communities. Although platform differences were supported, their magnitude was modest (η2 = 0.037–0.055), with most user-level linguistic variation remaining within platforms. Relative to IncelExit, active-incel platforms generally scored higher on the Psychic Equivalence- and Teleological Mode-inspired patterns and lower on the Pretend Mode-inspired pattern. IncelExit had the highest Epistemic Mistrust-inspired score despite high curiosity, showing that the composite did not isolate epistemic closure from counter-positioning. Across all four patterns, community means showed a consistent ordering, although adjacent contrasts were not uniformly supported. The three-platform portion of the ordering persisted in temporally matched and year-adjusted analyses. Evidential support was clearest for PE, partial for TM, limited for EM and PM. The latent ecological or psychological basis of the ordering remains unresolved, and the linguistic patterns are descriptive rather than validated measures of mentalizing. © 2026

Authors: Ballot C.; Zesiger P.
Title: Development of mental imagery strategy in a recall task as a function of word imageability and grade level in elementary school children
Abstract: Objective: This study investigated the development of mental imagery strategy in episodic memory as a function of word imageability and grade level in elementary school children. Method: A total of 62 first-grade children, 61 third-grade children, and 60 fifth-grade children performed a free recall task involving high- and low-imageability words. A test of word memory was conducted using either a mental imagery strategy or a rehearsal strategy. Results: The results showed that the benefit of the mental imagery strategy over the rehearsal condition was lower for first-graders than for third- or fifth-graders. Furthermore, word imageability influenced word recall to a greater extent in the mental imagery condition than in the rehearsal condition. Finally, the effect of word imageability did not interact with the children's age. Conclusion: The findings are discussed in light of theories on the development of mental imagery and the cognitive processes underlying episodic memory. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Kokkinos C.M.; Voulgaridou I.
Title: Beyond openness: Mapping need for cognition across Big Five domains and facets in university students
Abstract: Need for cognition (NFC) is closely associated with openness-related personality traits, but broad domains may obscure a more selective facet-level pattern. We examined NFC in 1551 university students using the Big Five Inventory–2 and a split-sample discovery–validation design. In discovery, three domains (Open-Mindedness, Conscientiousness, and Extraversion) and four facets (Productiveness, Intellectual Curiosity, Assertiveness, and Creative Imagination) met the selected magnitude threshold. In held-out validation, all three domains remained independently associated with NFC, whereas at the facet level only Assertiveness, Intellectual Curiosity, and Productiveness did so. Complementary latent models indicated positive associations of NFC with both Intellectual Curiosity and Assertiveness, although a bifactor decomposition of Open-Mindedness was inadmissible and correlated-factor model fit was mixed. Overall, the findings support the particular importance of intellectual openness while indicating that NFC is also embedded in a selective cross-domain configuration involving agentic and goal-directed characteristics. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: The residential food environment, financial constraints, and dietary behavior in Dutch adults with low socioeconomic position: a test of the EnRG framework
Abstract: Socioeconomic disparities in dietary behavior are often partially attributed to differences in the residential food environment, yet evidence linking food outlet availability to diet quality remains inconsistent. The Environmental Research framework for weight Gain prevention (EnRG) proposes that environmental influences operate through both a cognitive pathway, mediated by Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) constructs, and a direct, automatic pathway. In this secondary analysis of cross-sectional data from 1033 adults with oversampling of low socioeconomic position, we tested both pathways while additionally examining the role of food insecurity and financial scarcity. Outlet density and distance to nearest fast-food and fruit and vegetable outlet were measured at the postal code level. Dietary behavior, TPB constructs, food insecurity, and financial scarcity were assessed by self-report. Path analyses tested cognitive mediation; subgroup and moderation analyses examined whether food insecurity altered food environment effects. The residential food environment showed minimal associations with dietary consumption: only one of eight direct associations reached significance (fast-food distance and fast-food consumption), and was attenuated in path analyses. All paths from food environment characteristics to TPB constructs were non-significant, indicating no support for cognitive mediation. Food insecurity did not moderate food environment effects. In contrast, food insecurity and financial scarcity were consistently associated with lower fruit and vegetable consumption and poorer diet quality, but not with fast-food consumption. These findings do not support the hypothesis that the residential food environment plays a large role in shaping dietary behavior in low-SEP populations, while financial constraints were more consistently associated with dietary outcomes supporting evaluation of policies aimed at affordability alongside environmental interventions. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Adoptability of PPP Models to Overcome Procurement Issues in Affordable Housing Projects
Source title: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction
Abstract: Urbanization has caused severe housing issues related to affordability in urban areas. In Colombo, Sri Lanka, middle-income earners are more vulnerable to housing issues due to housing unaffordability and demand supply imbalances, and structural and distributional issues. However, public-private partnership (PPP) models have been successfully initiated in addressing urban housing affordability issues worldwide. Hence, this research aimed to investigate the adaptability of PPP models to overcome procurement issues in state-sector middle-income housing projects in Sri Lanka. The aim was accomplished via a three rounds of the Delphi approach by collecting data through semistructured interviews from experts. Collected data were analyzed through manual content analysis via three-phase coding. Findings revealed that PPP models, joint venture, concession, design-build-finance-operate-maintain (DBFOM), build-own-operate-transfer (BOOT), lease-develop-operate, design-build-finance-operate (DBFO), mixed PPP, and build-lease-transfer (BLT) offer viable alternatives for addressing challenges in delivery of affordable housing in Sri Lanka through conventional public-sector procurement methods. Key PPP features identified as critical to overcoming existing procurement issues include partnership and collaboration, shared risks and responsibilities, private funding, innovation and efficiency, value for money, and digital transformation. However, weak regulatory frameworks, lack of sector-specific PPP policies, bureaucratic inefficiencies, and absence of a central authority were highlighted as barriers to implementation of PPPs. The findings offer a foundation for countries that share similar socioeconomic backgrounds, particularly for developing countries, to consider PPP models in delivery of affordable housing.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: Companion Animals' Influence on Guardians' Disaster Risk and Impact Perception and Willingness to Evacuate: Atlantic Canadian Focus
Abstract: This study examines whether companion animal guardianship characteristics have an association with disaster risk perception, impact perception, and evacuation willingness among Atlantic Canadian guardians. While previous research often treats guardianship as a binary measure, this study considers the count, type, health status, and role of companion animals. Based on 936 valid survey responses, proportional odds logistic regression models show each additional companion animal reduced the odds of higher risk perception (OR = 0.872, p<0.01), impact perception (OR = 0.910, p=0.016), and evacuation willingness (OR = 0.876, p<0.01). Animal type was associated with odds ranges of 0.70-1.52 for risk perception, 0.68-1.71 for impact perception, and 1.00-1.92 for evacuation willingness. Guardianship of animals with chronic health conditions or emotional-support or service animals was associated with higher perceived impact but lower evacuation willingness. Findings suggest preparedness should address multianimal households and species-specific evacuation needs.  © 2026 This work is made available under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International license,.

Title: Temporal organization of negative affect shapes reciprocal feedback with psychotic-like experiences in daily life
Abstract: Background Negative affect and psychotic-like experiences (PLEs) reinforce each other in daily life, but which temporal properties of negative affect differ between individuals with PLEs and controls and shape this coupling is unknown. Methods 201 adults (99 with PLEs, 102 controls) completed 7-day experience sampling. Person-level mean negative affect, variability (SD), lability (RMSSD, MASD), and inertia were compared between groups, adjusting for mean negative affect. In participants with PLEs, lagged multilevel models tested whether these indices moderated reciprocal negative affect–PLEs associations, joint models separated amplitude from temporal dependency, and a continuous-time simulation quantified the moderation expected from persistence alone. Results Participants with PLEs showed larger fluctuations of negative affect beyond its higher mean level (adjusted d = 0.63–0.80), whereas their higher inertia depended on mean negative affect. Within participants with PLEs, only inertia moderated the lagged associations: coupling was absent at low and substantial at high inertia. Lability effects reflected its inverse relation to inertia and vanished once inertia was accounted for. Persistence alone accounted for the moderation of the PLEs-to-negative-affect effect and about half of the reverse effect, which operated through carry-over. Limitations Observational design; young, predominantly female, non-clinical sample; inertia estimated from one week with low split-half reliability. Conclusion Between persons, PLEs are associated mainly with the amplitude of negative affect fluctuations; within persons, the persistence of negative affect, not its intensity or amplitude, tracks the strength of its coupling with PLEs. Studies of affective dynamics along the psychosis continuum should therefore distinguish amplitude from persistence. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Using substances while playing: Players’ motivations, perceptions, and experiences with psychoactive drugs during recreational gaming
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: Research on psychoactive substance use during video game play has traditionally adopted a medical lens, focusing on the addictive potential of licit and illicit drugs and their pathological impacts on players. This framing highlights negative outcomes of the co-occurrence between excessive gaming and substance use, leaving the motivations, meanings, and perceptions that players themselves attach to substance use during recreational play under-examined. In this article, we explore a first-person perspective on substance-involved play through a qualitative study with 24 participants (11 Italians and 13 Americans) who reported using psychoactive substances during gameplay. Semi-structured interviews were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis, which led us to develop three themes: first, adult players describe a “lost immersion”, an effortless absorption they remember from youth and no longer attain spontaneously, which leads them to deploy a repertoire of strategies, including substance use, to re-enter it; second, participants engage in “situated modulation”: they use substances as precise, context-sensitive levers for shaping experience, emotion, and cognition, aligning substance choice with game genre, in-game task, and the stakes of the session; third, participants perform legitimacy work around fairness, treating the same substance as benign in casual play and suspect in competitive play, and practicing situational rather than categorical self-restraint. Substance use also produced unintended effects that sometimes diminished, rather than enhanced, players’ agency over play and over their internal states. By foregrounding first-person accounts, this article contributes to HCI scholarship on digital games, altered states, and player agency in ways that complement the medical lens. © 2026 The Author(s). Authors: Zhang L.; Ma X.; Cai C.; Yu H.
Title: How institutions shape adaptation: Evolution and mechanisms of local residents’ behaviors in rural tourism
Abstract: Local residents' adaptive behavior is a key determinant of sustainable tourism. Nevertheless, the institutional mechanisms driving its formation have received insufficient scholarly attention. Using Yinxi Village in China as a case study and the Institutional Analysis and Development (IAD) framework, this research explores the evolution and mechanisms of residents' adaptive behaviors. The findings show that: first, residents' adaptive behaviors evolve from silent adaptation to supportive adaptation and then to resistant adaptation. Second, the high mobility of tourism development weakens the constraint effect of informal institutions, thereby creating an institutional environment in which residents adopt resistant adaptation as a ‘weapon of the weak.’ Based on these findings, the “mobility-institutional effect-adaptive behavior (MIEA)” framework is proposed. This study distinguishes three types of adaptive behaviors in rural tourism and offers an institutional perspective on their evolution. The results provide practical insights for improving residents' well-being and promoting the sustainable development of rural tourism. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Overbye-Thompson H.; Hamilton K.A.; Fisher J.
Author full names: Overbye-Thompson, Hannah (58722982700); Hamilton, Kristy A. (57192013589); Fisher, Jacob (57196390864)
Title: Understanding human detection of algorithmic bias through drift-diffusion modeling
Abstract: Algorithms increasingly make high-risk decisions that impact individuals' lives, from loan approvals to medical diagnoses, but can exhibit problematic biases that require human oversight. Despite regulatory moves toward human-in-the-loop systems, little is known about a person's ability to detect algorithmic bias or how cognitive processes influence detection accuracy. Across two experiments, we show that human detection of algorithmic bias is limited, even when bias is pronounced and participants evaluate decisions across multiple trials. Detection accuracy is shaped by individual differences in gender and moral reasoning, and was not improved by a single warning ahead of time that bias may be present. Participants who are better at detecting bias tend to engage in more deliberative decision-making, taking longer to reach conclusions and requiring more evidence before responding. Modeling detection as a process of evidence accumulation allows us to locate where in the decision oversight may break down rather than only assessing whether it breaks down or not. These findings highlight the potential and limits of human oversight in algorithmic systems, suggesting that effective human-in-the-loop designs must support careful, reflective judgments and account for variability in users' monitoring abilities. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Berihun Tenessa D.
Title: Alignments and Trade-Offs in Multidimensional Household Diversification: A Pseudo-Panel Analysis of Standard Practices and Public Programs in Rural Ethiopia
Abstract: In rural Ethiopia, multidimensional household diversification (MDHD) has become a vital element in strengthening livelihood resilience. While earlier research addressed how household-level standard practices (HLSPs) and public income-generating initiatives (PIGIs) influence diversification, their direct impact on resilience was not fully understood. This study analyzed data from five waves of the Ethiopian Living Standards Measurement Study from 2011 to 2021 to clarify these relationships. Households were classified into 15,191 cohorts based on birth year, location, and household head gender. Using a weighted Herfindahl-based method, the analysis found that 51.33% of households were highly diversified. The results indicated that public income-generating initiatives significantly enhanced diversification, increasing it by 6.88 points on a 0-100 scale. Other important factors included land tenure arrangements, gender dynamics, access to extension services, and participation in nonfarm enterprises. A key insight was that public income-generating programs are most effective when aligned with existing household strategies. Among households already engaged in traditional livelihood practices, involvement in government initiatives led to the greatest improvements, adding 6.88 points to diversification levels. For policymakers, the study suggests that the Ministry of Agriculture should require regional offices to evaluate household practices before implementing income-generating programs. Additionally, District Rural Development Offices should supplement these efforts with agricultural training and enhanced extension services. Such an integrated approach would enable rural households to develop more diverse income sources and better withstand economic shocks. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Authors: Engen O.A.; Jore S.H.; Hansen S.T.
Author full names: Engen, Ole Andreas (22834151500); Jore, Sissel Haugdal (25646522500); Hansen, Susanne Therese (57187615400)
Title: Polycentric risk governance across safety and security risk logics
Abstract: The regulatory regime governing the Norwegian petroleum sector changed significantly in response to new geopolitical conditions following the war in Ukraine and the sabotage of the Nord Stream I and II pipelines. New legal security requirements and security risk logics were introduced into a sector whose traditional regulatory regime and risk logic had been intrinsically oriented toward safety. This shift altered the balance between safety and security considerations within the sector. This article explores the implications for regulatory regimes and risk logics when transitioning from safety-oriented to security-oriented regulatory models. Our ambition is primarily conceptual and theoretical, with the Norwegian petroleum industry serving as an illustrative case. The article analyses the emerging interface between safety and security, emphasizing the ontological, epistemological, and procedural divergences that complicate the integration of security concerns − focused on intentional, adversarial threats − into established safety regimes that manage unintentional harm. Anchored in a polycentric governance framework, the article examines how geopolitical developments have created tensions between rule-based and risk-based regulatory models, and the implications for organizational practices, regulatory oversight, and tripartite cooperation. It concludes by proposing a model of enforced self-regulation that reconciles safety and security logics, highlighting the need for adaptive, resilient, and knowledge-driven approaches to risk management in complex and evolving threat landscapes. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Cognitive performance and self-reported physical exercise in bipolar disorder: A cross-sectional analysis of pre-randomization screening data from an ongoing randomized controlled trial
Abstract: Background Bipolar Disorder (BD) is frequently associated with persistent cognitive deficits that significantly impair functionality and quality of life. While physical exercise (PE) has shown promise in improving cognition in healthy individuals and those with other psychiatric conditions, most consistently in major depressive disorder and schizophrenia, its specific impact on individuals with BD remains under-investigated. This study aimed to investigate the association between self-reported regular physical exercise and cognitive performance in individuals with Bipolar Disorder. Methods This study consists of a cross-sectional analysis of pre-randomization screening data from an ongoing randomized controlled trial. The analysis included 108 euthymic BD individuals (aged 18–55) recruited from the outpatient clinic at the University of São Paulo Medical School (PROMAN). Participants were allocated into either the Exercise Group ( n = 48), defined by self-reported engagement in regular structured physical exercise at least twice a week, and the No-Exercise Group ( n = 60); exercise status was ascertained with a brief in-house checklist. Cognitive performance was assessed using the Screen for Cognitive Impairment in Psychiatry (SCIP). Secondary measures included mood symptoms (MADRS and YMRS) and pharmacological treatment profiles. Effect sizes were estimated with Cohen's d, and a Bonferroni-corrected threshold of α = 0.0033 was applied to the 15 comparisons performed. Results The Exercise group demonstrated significantly higher SCIP Total Scores compared to the No-Exercise group (64.63 ± 9.19 vs. 56.50 ± 7.84; p < 0.001, d = 0.95). Significant advantages for the exercise group were observed in sub-domains related to verbal learning ( p = 0.010) and working memory ( p = 0.002); the total score and working memory remained significant after Bonferroni correction, whereas verbal learning did not. Notably, the No-Exercise group had a significantly higher usage of stimulants (27.5% vs. 4.5%, p = 0.029), while the Exercise group had a higher prevalence of anticonvulsant use (45.5% vs. 20%, p = 0.035); neither medication difference survived correction. Limitations: Exercise status was self-reported and dichotomous, with no data on intensity, duration or modality, and no demographic or clinical covariates were available for adjustment. Conclusion: Regular physical exercise appears to be associated with superior global cognition, verbal learning, and working memory in individuals with BD. These findings, derived from the screening phase of an ongoing trial, suggest that PE may be a promising adjunctive strategy for neurocognitive rehabilitation, although the cross-sectional design precludes any causal inference. Title: Topography-specific white matter hyperintensities, hippocampal atrophy, and gait slowing as independent and interrelated correlates of late-life depression
Abstract: Background Late-life depression (LLD) has been linked to cerebrovascular disease, neurodegeneration, and physical dysfunction. This study aimed to investigate the independent and interrelated associations of topography-specific white matter hyperintensities (WMH) burden, hippocampal volume, and gait speed with LLD. Methods We evaluated 366 older adults (LLD n = 112; non-depressed n = 254) using 3 T MRI, neuropsychological testing, and gait speed assessment. WMH were segmented into juxtaventricular (JVWMH), periventricular (PVWMH), and deep (DWMH) regions. Multivariable logistic and linear regressions and structural path analysis were performed. Results JVWMH (OR = 2.98, 95% CI 1.58–5.63, p = 0.001) and PVWMH volume (OR = 2.60, 95% CI 1.61–4.18, p < 0.001), together with slower gait (OR = 0.96, 95% CI 0.95–0.98, p < 0.001) were associated with LLD, whereas DWMH was not. In linear models, JVWMH (β = 0.184, P = 0.001), PVWMH (β = 0.197, P < 0.001), smaller hippocampus volume (β = −0.115, p = 0.038), and slower gait (β = −0.322, p < 0.001) were independently associated with increased depressive symptom severity, whereas DWMH was not. Path analysis demonstrated that JVWMH exerted both direct (β = 0.17, p < 0.001) and indirect effects on depression via gait slowing (β = 0.044, p = 0.007), whereas PVWMH showed only direct effects and DWMH showed no significant pathways. Conclusions This study reveals that LLD is independently associated with regional WMH, hippocampal volume loss, and gait slowing, via topography-specific direct and indirect WMH pathways. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Narrative identity awareness as a regulatory pathway between rumination and reflection and personality functioning
Abstract: Personality functioning reflects individual differences in self and interpersonal capacities. This study examined whether narrative identity awareness mediates the associations of rumination and reflection with personality functioning. In a community sample of 424 adults, participants completed self-report measures of personality functioning, rumination, reflection, and narrative identity awareness. Cross-sectional mediation analyses (complete cases, N = 405) showed that rumination was associated with greater impairment, whereas reflection showed a more selective pattern. Narrative identity awareness was associated with lower impairment, and significant indirect associations were observed for both rumination and reflection in the simultaneous model; sensitivity analyses indicated that the indirect association was more robust for reflection than for rumination. Indirect associations were most evident for identity and self-direction, smaller for intimacy, and not statistically detectable for empathy. Component-level analyses indicated that coherence-related facets, particularly causal coherence, showed the most consistent indirect associations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
