Title: Identifying technological problems and exploring potential solutions to support R&D: Tech-mining with multi-LLM applications
Abstract: The shortening of technology lifecycles and growing technological complexity have made the rapid identification of technical problems and exploration of solutions a critical challenge. Patent analysis can serve as a crucial tool for supporting R&D activities by extracting problem–solution pairs from patent documents. However, current patent analysis methods have several limitations. They focus primarily on extracting technical problems from patents without providing a systematic framework for transforming fragmented problems into comprehensive technological intelligence. Moreover, they remain heavily dependent on technical experts, with supervised learning models struggling to achieve the expected performance on unseen data, which is a particularly critical issue given the accelerating technological change. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a systematic framework that converts fragmented technical problems into actionable technological intelligence. The framework performs target–symptom decomposition, inter-problem causal analysis, and solution portfolio development, while employing a multi-large-language-model (multi-LLM) architecture with few-shot learning capabilities to reduce the dependence on technical experts and enhance analytical reliability. A case study of hydrogen storage technology with cross-domain demonstrations in the semiconductor and biopharmaceutical fields demonstrates that the framework can systematically identify technical problems, trace their root causes, and explore potential solutions to support R&D planning with improved cost efficiency and domain-independent applicability. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Guo Y.; Lin P.; Hou C.-T.; Xu H.; Zhao W.-W.; Wang X.; Ji J.-J.; Chen Z.-H.
Title: Associations between parenting styles, problematic smartphone use, and depression severity in adolescents with depressive disorder
Abstract: Background Adolescent depression represents a significant public health issue in China. Parenting styles and problematic smartphone use (PSU) are closely associated with adolescent depression. Consistent with the I-PACE model, depression is considered a distal vulnerability factor for PSU; however, among adolescents already diagnosed with depressive disorder, whether PSU is associated with increased symptom severity remains unclear, and the potential indirect role of parenting styles warrants further investigation. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among adolescent patients diagnosed with depressive disorder. From December 2023 to October 2024, 451 participants were recruited from a tertiary psychiatric hospital in Nanjing, with data from 403 participants included in the final analysis. Parenting styles were assessed using the short Chinese version of the Egna Minnen av Barndoms Uppfostran (S-EMBU-C), problematic smartphone use was measured with the Mobile Phone Addiction Index (MPAI), and depression severity was evaluated using the 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-17). Data were analyzed using LASSO regression and structural equation modeling. Results LASSO regression retained maternal emotional warmth, maternal rejection, paternal rejection, and all four dimensions of problematic smartphone use as significant correlates of depression severity. Maternal emotional warmth was negatively associated with depression, whereas parental rejection and problematic smartphone use dimensions showed positive associations. In structural equation models, problematic smartphone use statistically accounted for part of the associations between maternal rejection and depression (indirect effect β = 0.144, 95% CI [0.070, 0.232]), between paternal rejection and depression (indirect effect β = 0.090, 95% CI [0.020, 0.165]), and between maternal emotional warmth and depression (indirect effect β = −0.099, 95% CI [−0.166, −0.040]). Conclusion In this clinical sample of adolescents with depressive disorder, PSU was associated with higher depression severity, suggesting that PSU may have an exacerbating role in adolescents already in a depressed state. Parenting styles were indirectly associated with depression severity through their associations with PSU. These findings underscore the potential value of addressing both family environment and maladaptive digital behavior in the assessment and intervention of adolescent depression. Given the cross-sectional design, the temporal direction of these associations cannot be determined, and longitudinal validation is required. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wierzbicki A.; Kukulska-Kozieł A.; Hernik J.
Author full names: Wierzbicki, Artur (60829231100); Kukulska-Kozieł, Anita (57202718944); Hernik, Józef (15725136900)
Title: Implementing municipal standards for soft infrastructure accessibility: A spatial diagnosis of Kraków in the context of urban planning reforms
Abstract: Dynamic urbanisation processes in Poland, including land development pressure and oversupply of buildable land, pose increasing challenges in ensuring equal access to soft infrastructure for local populations. These problems are addressed in the 2023 amendment to the Act on spatial planning and development. It allows for defining municipal standards for soft infrastructure accessibility in master plans. The study diagnoses the spatial accessibility of the infrastructure in Kraków and evaluates the compliance of the existing soft infrastructure with the new statutory standards. Its novelty lies in being the first attempt at operationalising the new regulations in an empirical analysis that uses network-based GIS methodology. The analyses were performed with the QNEAT3 plugin for QGIS using the statutory distance limits. The results show that 77% and 93% of parcels in Kraków conform to school and public green spaces accessibility criteria, respectively. However, only 56% of the city area has access to both types of soft infrastructure simultaneously; eastern and peripheral parts of the city are clearly disadvantaged. Overall, Kraków is relatively well prepared to implement soft infrastructure accessibility standards, but the findings revealed an integration gap across housing, transport, and environmental policies. The evidence can serve as a reference for other municipalities in Poland and internationally, including in Eastern European countries, following the sociopolitical transformation for implementing new spatial planning tools. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Xu P.; Zhang Y.
Title: Belief updating across information ecologies: The trade-off between information gain and noise filtering
Abstract: This paper investigates the ecology of belief updating in environments with varying reliability structures, focusing on how individuals navigate the trade-off between information utility and noise filtering. Combining computational simulations with behavioral experiments, we examined how belief-updating strategies ranging from discrete gating to continuous discounting performed across environments differing in source credibility and heterogeneity, and how frequently participants' behavior was best captured by each strategy. A simulation study mapped the performance landscape of these heuristics and showed that threshold-based strategies exhibit a relative advantage in long-sequence environments with low-to-moderate credibility, whereas performance differences across strategies are attenuated in high-credibility settings. Two behavioral experiments using a sequential estimation task revealed substantial between-participant heterogeneity: rather than a single strategy characterizing all participants, threshold-based, discounting, and Bayesian strategies each best described a subset of participants, with the prevalence of each strategy differing across informational environments in a manner broadly consistent with the simulations. Among participants best fit by the threshold model, fitted threshold values were also higher under conditions of greater mean source credibility, offering preliminary, population-level evidence that the decision criterion underlying threshold gating may be sensitive to the average reliability of the environment. Together, these findings highlight the importance of environmental context in shaping belief updating under uncertain source reliability. © 2026

Title: Income inequality as a barrier to the CO2-reducing potential of public investment: evidence from Latin America
Abstract: This paper aims to empirically analyze the association between public investment and carbon emissions relative to Gross Domestic Product (GDP) for a panel of Latin American countries from 1994 to 2019. Given that reduced income inequality can enhance the effectiveness of environmental policies, the estimations are carried out under two income inequality regimes: higher and lower. A nonlinear Local Projections model with a threshold is employed, dividing the sample into two groups based on the Gini index. The results show that, during periods of relatively low income inequality, the estimated response of carbon-intensity growth to changes in public investment is negative over time. In contrast, under conditions of relatively high income inequality, the estimated association is not statistically significant at the 10% level. Our estimates suggest that a 10% increase in public investments is associated with an approximately 4.40% reduction in the growth rate of carbon intensity in the low-inequality regime, as measured by the Gini index, until the fourth year following the increase in public investment. These empirical findings support existing literature highlighting the positive association between income inequality and carbon emissions. © 2026

Author full names: Goddard, Alex (58103285800); Reader, Tom (17135545500); Gillespie, Alex (8326676500)
Title: Analysing hospital responses to patient-reported safety incidents online using large language models
Abstract: Patient experiences reported online can reveal safety incidents in healthcare organisations, but they can only translate into quality improvement if organisations engage with them. Accordingly, healthcare organisations’ responses to online feedback offer a new data source on corrective culture, namely, the norms and practices for identifying, interpreting, and acting on safety incidents. This study explored the feasibility of using a large language model to reliably code these responses for two candidate indicators of corrective culture: engagement and organisational learning. We manually coded 600 feedback-response pairs for engagement (κ = 0.90) and organisational learning (Gwet’s AC1 = 0.84), and used this gold standard to develop and evaluate a GPT-5-mini classifier. The classifier coded engagement with high agreement (F1 = 0.86), but was less reliable for organisational learning (F1 = 0.70). To assess construct validity, we analysed human disagreements and classifier misclassifications. Organisational learning was harder to code because it is a reported behaviour, whereas engagement is an observed behaviour. We then used the classifier to code 157,051 responses (2011–2023) across 844 healthcare organisations. Our results indicate that large language models can reliably code engagement in these responses, while their ability to code organisational learning remains inconclusive. Organisational culture in healthcare is usually assessed with staff surveys, which rely on self-report. Large language models could complement surveys by measuring observed behaviour in naturally occurring data, although whether engagement reflects corrective culture requires external validation. Authors: Torres Castro U.E.
Title: When engagement matters: Agentic engagement, expressive behavior, and academic performance in higher education
Abstract: This study examines whether agentic engagement (AE), understood as students’ observable contributions to instructional interaction, can be measured reliably and comparably across women and men and how it relates to academic performance in higher education. Using data from 1713 final-year undergraduate students from six Colombian universities, the study assesses the psychometric properties of the Agentic Engagement Scale (AES) and analyzes its association with grade point average (GPA), which is used as an institutional indicator of academic performance, controlling for gender and academic discipline. The results support the reliability, unidimensional structure, and measurement invariance of the AES across women and men, indicating that AE scores can be meaningfully compared between these gender groups. Regression analyses revealed a positive but modest association between AE and GPA. At the item level, however, the association was identified for AES2, which captures students’ expression of preferences and opinions. This pattern indicates that the AES total score should not be interpreted as showing a uniform association with GPA. Instead, the AE–GPA relationship depends on specific measured instructional behaviors through which student initiative becomes visible in teaching interactions. By showing that the AE–GPA association was concentrated in students’ expression of preferences and opinions, this study supports a behavior-specific and context-sensitive interpretation of AE in higher education. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Supporting young children impacted by trauma: A mixed-methods study of early childhood professionals’ trauma-informed knowledge, confidence and wellbeing
Abstract: Despite growing awareness of the prevalence and impacts of childhood trauma, the understanding of early childhood professionals’ preparedness to work with trauma-impacted children is limited. This study aimed to explore early childhood professionals’ professional capacity (knowledge and confidence) and psychological capacity (wellbeing) in the context of working with trauma-impacted children, and the supports required to strengthen their capacities. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was employed, integrating quantitative survey data from 135 educators and qualitative data obtained via follow-up interviews with 15 participants. Findings revealed a substantial mismatch between the high reported presence of children impacted by trauma in Early Childhood Education and Care (ECEC) settings and the capacity of early childhood professionals to respond. There is a need to clarify early childhood professionals’ role responsibilities and professional boundaries when supporting trauma-impacted children. Higher perceived trauma-informed knowledge and confidence, along with better service’s Australian National Quality Standard rating, were associated significantly with greater psychological wellbeing of early childhood professionals. Authors: Zhou J.; Bai Y.; Fu C.; Sun M.; Xu X.; Zhang L.
Title: Land tenure as a catalyst: Synergizing gender equality and agrobiodiversity conservation for sustainable development in Asian vulnerable areas
Abstract: Agrobiodiversity, as an important land use pattern, plays a critical role in enhancing ecological resilience, promoting sustainable food production, and facilitating adaptation to climate change, especially for smallholder farmers in vulnerable areas. Although literature often incorporates land tenure into broader indices of women's empowerment in agriculture, the direct relationship between women's land tenure and agrobiodiversity remains underexplored. Using species and variety richness as indicators of household-level agrobiodiversity, this study examines the effect of women's land tenure on household crop diversity and explores whether women's intra-household decision-making regarding crop choice constitutes a potential pathway and assesses heterogeneity across socioeconomic and geographic contexts. Using primary data collected from 1089 households across 12 vulnerable sites of four distinct geographic ecosystems in five Asian countries (Cambodia, China, Myanmar, Nepal, and Thailand), this study employs a Negative Binomial regression model and the Inverse Probability Weighted Regression Adjustment method. The results consistently demonstrate that women's land tenure significantly increases the diversity of crop species and varieties cultivated by households on average, with notable effects on both staple and non-staple grain crops, but it varies across countries. The positive effects on crop species diversity are more evident in the countries with initially low crop diversity such as Cambodia, Myanmar, and Thailand, while the effects on variety diversity are strongest in Cambodia and Thailand. In Nepal, where baseline crop diversity is high, the effect of women's land tenure is negligible, whereas the effect is more concentrated in staple and non-staple grain crop species in China. Women possessing land tenure are more likely to make crop choice decisions independently, a pattern consistent with decision-making power as a potential pathway to greater crop diversity. In addition, the positive effects are more pronounced in the freshwater and dryland ecosystems, and among the households with higher income. These findings provide implications for land governance and land use policies, showing that strengthening women's land rights effectively support household agrobiodiversity and synergies Sustainable Development Goals: gender equality (SDG 5), agrobiodiversity conservation (SDG 15), and equal access to control over land (SDGs 1 & 2). © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Lee S.Y.
Title: Uneven benefits of long-term study abroad: English use, job pathways, and earnings in Japan
Abstract: Outbound student mobility is widely promoted as a core component of higher education internationalization, yet evidence remains mixed regarding how extended study abroad translates into durable graduate outcomes. This study examines whether long-term university study abroad is associated with employability outcomes at labor market entry and later in the career in Japan, a context where outbound mobility remains limited and institutionally constrained. Drawing on a nationwide survey of bachelor’s degree holders, the analysis focuses on individuals who studied abroad for more than one year during university and compares them to non-mobile peers. Earnings are measured at two stages: annual income in the first post-graduation job, deflated to 2017 yen, and current annual income measured in 2017, both inclusive of bonuses. To address differences in background characteristics between mobile and non-mobile graduates, the study applies propensity score matching and models first-job and current-job outcomes within a two-period framework. Results indicate that long-term study abroad is positively associated with earnings at both career stages under baseline adjustment. However, the association diminishes substantially after accounting for university academic level and becomes statistically indistinguishable from zero once English proficiency and job pathway characteristics are considered. Further analyses reveal systematic sorting of study abroad participants into internationally oriented departments and workplaces, suggesting that the employability value of mobility is concentrated in career tracks where English and related international competencies are actively used. These findings suggest that the benefits of long-term mobility are conditional rather than universal and depend on the alignment between educational experiences and subsequent labor market contexts. The study contributes to research on internationalization and graduate outcomes by clarifying the pathways through which mobility may shape early and mid-career trajectories, with implications for the design and targeting of outbound study abroad initiatives. © 2026 The Author.

Authors: Wu Y.
Title: Supporting shared mental models: How an AI facilitator shapes interprofessional team cognition in collaborative learning
Abstract: Background: Effective interprofessional collaboration is critical for patient safety. Fostering the underlying cognitive coordination of teamwork remains a significant challenge in health professions education. Traditional approaches often prioritize outcome assessment rather than actively facilitating the collaborative process itself. Objectives: This study investigated whether a novel artificial intelligence (AI) facilitator, acting as a metacognitive guide, was associated with team performance and differences in the collaborative discourse structure of interprofessional student teams. Methods: In an explanatory sequential mixed-methods randomized controlled trial, thirty three-person teams (N = 90) of final-year clinical medicine, nursing, and pharmacy students were randomized to solve a complex clinical case with or without the AI facilitator. While blinded experts assessed the primary outcome of team performance, this study utilized epistemic network analysis (ENA) on collaborative discourse to map discourse-based proxies for cognitive coordination, followed by reflexive thematic analysis of post-task interviews to identify underlying interactional mechanisms. Results: Teams in the experimental group showed higher clinical performance and reported greater collaboration satisfaction and lower cognitive load. ENA revealed distinct structural differences, with the experimental network showing stronger connections among professional contribution, hypothesis generation, and synthesis and integration. Thematic analysis suggested three perceived interactional mechanisms: functioning as a non-directive cognitive guide, supporting cross-professional perspective-taking, and providing a metacognitive framework that helped organize complex reasoning. Conclusion: An AI facilitator may support interprofessional teamwork by scaffolding metacognitive regulation during collaboration. These findings suggest that AI may serve as a process-oriented pedagogical scaffold, supporting human interaction and collaborative cognition beyond content delivery. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Yan C.; Sun T.; Qian M.
Author full names: Yan, Chunshun (60109736500); Sun, Tianyi (60109615400); Qian, Mengting (58897332300)
Title: Universities as regional innovation anchors: Pathways of engagement and mechanism building
Abstract: Universities are increasingly framed as regional innovation anchors, yet the literature explains less clearly how anchoring capacity is built beyond discrete projects, technology-transfer outputs, or engagement intensity. Starting from the public-purpose conception of the university, this study develops a five-stage, mechanism-based model of anchoring. It analyzes 139 publicly available Innovation and Economic Prosperity (IEP) case narratives from 36 U.S. public and land-grant universities in the Association of Public and Land-grant Universities (APLU) network between 2013 and 2023, using storyline analysis and systematic qualitative coding. The findings identify five connected stages: (1) needs recognition and problem framing; (2) engagement pathway formation across place-based partnerships, education/workforce development, research translation, cross-boundary collaboration, and entrepreneurship support; (3) mechanism building through partnership governance and cross-sector coordination, talent and technical support, resource and funding architectures, ecosystem infrastructure, and operational routines; (4) outcome generation in innovation-system and public-value domains; and (5) diffusion and scaling through organizational expansion, geographic scaling, horizontal replication, ecosystem building, and benchmarking or demonstration. In this corpus, mechanism building functions as the central explanatory stage because it shows how episodic initiatives are represented as repeatable coordination capacity. The study contributes to anchor institution and regional innovation scholarship by theorizing anchoring as a staged institutional accomplishment grounded in public value, rather than as a simple accumulation of projects or outputs. It also shows how recognition-based institutional narratives can reveal the otherwise hidden coordination work through which universities build durable ecosystem roles. Policy implications point to investing in coordination capacity, governance infrastructures, and diffusion mechanisms for inclusive regional innovation. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: He J.; Tang J.; Zhang H.; Zhang L.; Wang Q.
Title: Assessing comprehensive impact of autonomous electric taxis via an integrated modeling framework
Source title: Transportation Research Part D: Transport and Environment
Abstract: Autonomous electric taxis are a crucial technology for the sustainable urban transport transition, yet the multidimensional impacts of large-scale deployment and differentiated policy effects remain insufficiently assessed. This paper proposes a framework integrating BERTopic, Bass diffusion, parameterized binary Logit and system dynamics to analyze autonomous electric taxis’ penetration in the on-demand mobility market of Guangzhou, a representative Chinese megacity, and their accident-related economic, environmental and employment impacts. Results show that autonomous electric taxis will reach approximately 70% penetration by 2050, and save roughly 88.4 million yuan in socioeconomic costs from fewer traffic accidents. However, new travel demand will lift cumulative carbon emissions by around 760,000 tons and displace about 61% of traditional mobility jobs. Moreover, policy trade-offs emerge: price subsidies best promote penetration and promotional campaigns best lower accident costs, but both exacerbate carbon emissions and employment impacts; opening operating areas has limited market effects yet mitigates environmental impacts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Author full names: Applin, Jessica B. (57205464714); Kibbe, Melissa M. (42661413500)
Title: An agent’s partial knowledge of a hidden array impacts infants’ representations of object quantity
Abstract: Infants can represent the quantity of a set of hidden objects, but if the number of objects hidden in a location exceeds three, infants experience “catastrophic forgetting”, failing to represent even a subset of the objects. Infants’ representations of an object also are impacted by other agents’ visual access to an object; infants represent what an agent observed about an object instead of what they themselves observed. Here, we asked whether an agent’s partial visual access to a set of objects would impact infants’ representations of the set’s quantity, and if so, whether this impact would apply when infants’ own representational limits are exceeded. Ten-14-month-olds (n = 85) completed an ordinal choice task in which they watched an experimenter distribute different quantities of crackers across two containers, and were allowed to crawl to one of the containers to obtain its contents. We manipulated whether the quantities hidden were within or outside of infants’ capacity limits (1 vs. 2 or 1 vs. 4) and whether a second experimenter, who infants saw had also observed the crackers being distributed, had partial knowledge of the arrays (observing 1 vs. 1 or 1 vs. 2, respectively) or no knowledge. Infants’ container choices suggested that they used the observing agent’s perspective to represent quantity whenever she had partial knowledge of the arrays. Our results suggest that an agent’s quantity representations may mandatorily supplant infants’ own, and this may allow infants to represent a subset of objects in situations in which they would normally experience catastrophic representational failure. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Jia A.Y.; Gilbert D.
Title: Designing the temporal architecture for safety in heat: An ethnographic study of the practice of acclimatisation in a megaproject
Abstract: Time is an essential dimension in safety management and a conceptual lens for understanding risks. By strategic structuring and ordering of actions into time, hazards can be designed out, mitigation measures designed in an organisation’s temporal architecture. However, the temporal approach to safety management has not been systematically explored so far. Heat stress on construction site, as both a natural hazard inherent in the hot weather and a work hazard of metabolic heat from the heavy physical work, is a temporal risk characterized by rhythmic variance across seasons and hours, coupled with the timing and speed of work-life activities. A construction project organisation is a socio-technical system structured by the temporal institutions such as work hours, work-rest regimens, task deadlines and their resulted norms of rhythms and work paces. In hot weather, the temporal architecture acts as a mediating platform to facilitate workers’ acclimatisation, or exacerbate the heat hazards. In this study, we analyse the practices of acclimatisation and the temporal architecture of a project organisation, drawing on ethnographic data from a megaproject in a tropical climate zone in Australia. We explicate a set of temporal concepts that are actionable for safety management and generalisable to a broader industry context. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Association between adverse childhood and adolescence experiences and chronic nociplastic pain: A meta-analysis of observational studies
Abstract: Background: Chronic nociplastic pain is defined by persistent alterations in central pain processing, typically occurring without identifiable tissue damage. Existing evidence indicates that adverse childhood experiences (ACEs), including physical, emotional, and sexual abuse and neglect, may increase susceptibility to the development of these conditions across the lifespan. Objective: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate and synthesize evidence regarding the association between ACEs and chronic nociplastic pain. Participants and Setting: The review included observational studies involving individuals with a history of childhood or adolescent abuse, conducted in various countries and clinical settings. Methods: The protocol was registered with PROSPERO, and the review followed Cochrane and PRISMA 2020 guidelines. We searched PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, PsycINFO, and LILACS. Two independent reviewers performed data selection, extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment. We used a random-effects model for meta-analysis. We assessed heterogeneity using the I2 test and publication bias using Egger’s test. Results: The systematic search initially identified 617 records. After screening and eligibility assessment, eight studies, comprising 120,616 participants in total, were included in the systematic review and meta-analysis. The pooled prevalence of chronic nociplastic pain among individuals exposed to ACEs was 24.86% (95% CI: 7.53–48.01). Substantial heterogeneity was observed (I2 = 99.7%). Egger’s test indicated small-study effects consistent with possible publication bias; however, this result should be interpreted with caution due to the limited number of studies and extreme heterogeneity. Conclusions: Current evidence indicates a high pooled prevalence of nociplastic pain among individuals exposed to ACEs. Nevertheless, given the extreme heterogeneity, this estimate should be regarded as a descriptive aggregation rather than a definitive clinical measure. Additional research employing standardized designs and more homogeneous samples is warranted. These findings underscore the potential importance of trauma-informed care in chronic pain management. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Assessing the security risks of China's solar PV industry chain
Abstract: As a strategic emerging industry with international competitive advantages, China's solar photovoltaic (PV) industry plays a critical role in its industrial and national security. However, limited literature has been targeted on the security risks for China's solar PV industry chain. To address this particular issue, firstly, this study constructed a risk assessment index for China's solar PV industry chain by adopting the improved Delphi expert method and the cloud model for a comprehensive indicator weighting. Next, it evaluated the security risks from 2016 to 2024 by using the matter-element extension model. The results indicate that: (1) during the study period, the security risks of China's solar PV industry chain were mostly at low or medium-low levels, with high-risk in 2018 and 2024. (2) The security risks for the upstream fluctuated significantly due to the tight supply of critical mineral resources, imbalanced supply and demand and high concentration of silicon resources. (3) The overall risks in the midstream for each dimension show a decreasing trend, except for the market competition dimension, the technological level of solar PV cells still requires innovation and improvement. (4) In the downstream, the risks of the uncertain market environment are at a high level. Finally, this study proposes corresponding risk prevention strategies and policy implications. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Jadhav B.N.; Gowri S.; Abdul Azeez E.P.; Farsana K.P.
Title: Women's encounters with street sexual harassment in India: A photovoice study
Abstract: Street sexual harassment (SSH) is a global public health and gender inequality problem. It appears in many forms, disproportionately affecting young girls and women in public places, but scholarship lacks a comprehensive understanding of women's SSH experiences, especially in India. This study examined young women's experiences and perspectives of SSH in Southern India. A photovoice qualitative method was employed to collect data from 19 young women who captured photographs representing what it was like to experience SSH, followed by interviews to understand the phenomenon in detail. The photos, captions, and interview transcripts were analyzed thematically. The analysis revealed several themes. The findings imply the need for policy interventions, public awareness, family support, and strengthening women's trust in the legal system to address the issue and promote women's health and well-being. Making public places safer and accessible to women should be a policy priority. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Mukherjee S.; Mandal S.
Title: Subverting gendered vulnerability of sex trafficking through resilience in Ruchira Gupta's I Kick and I Fly
Abstract: Women and girls are the most vulnerable to exploitation, constituting approximately sixty to eightypercent of identified trafficking victims (UNODC, 2020). Yet scholarship on trafficking fiction remains largely confined to a victimhood paradigm, leaving the transition from vulnerability to resilience under-theorized. This article addresses the gap through Ruchira Gupta's I Kick and I Fly (2023), which depicts the intergenerational prostitution and trafficking of Nat girls in a small village of Forbesganj, where such exploitation is normalized as women's inevitable destiny. Contesting generational norms, the narrative traces the transformation of girls from vulnerable subjects to resilient survivors through martial arts training and collective female solidarity. The study first reads Judith Butler's concept of precarity alongside Kimberlé Crenshaw's intersectionality to show how colonial criminalization of the Nat community and its postcolonial neglect produce a caste and gender specific susceptibility of women to trafficking. It then develops a framework of embodied resilience, joining Martha McCaughey's theory of physical feminism with bell hooks' feminist sisterhood to theorize self-defense training and female solidarity as practices that subvert exploitation. Read together, these frameworks trace a single arc from structural vulnerability to embodied and collective resilience, moving beyond the conventional trafficking narratives that dwell on suffering to account for the conditions under which vulnerable girls reclaim agency. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Si H.; Liang J.; Zhang M.; Duan X.; Zhao Y.
Title: Understanding young consumers’ purchase intention for autonomous vehicles: Evidence from China
Abstract: Understanding consumers' purchase intention for autonomous vehicles (AVs) is a prerequisite for the sustainable diffusion of this technology. Existing research focuses on general acceptance or usage intention and rarely examines purchase intentions for ownership, particularly among young consumers who represent the core future market. This study develops and empirically tests an integrated framework explaining young consumers' AV purchase intention by combining psychological factors, perceptions of the external environment, and product/brand attributes. Survey data were collected from 1259 young consumers in China. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and multi-group analysis were used to estimate the model and explore subgroup heterogeneity. The results show that attitude and perceived value are central factors related to AV purchase intention. Perceived value is positively linked to purchase intention both directly and indirectly via attitude. Attitude is mainly explained by perceived value, perceived policy support, technology cognition, brand trust, and risk preference, while perceived value is mainly predicted by technology cognition, face consciousness, preference for personalization, hedonistic orientation, and usage-cost concern. Risk preference is not only positively related to purchase intention but also weakens the relationship between attitude and purchase intention, whereas usage-cost concern strengthens the relationship between perceived value and purchase intention without showing a significant direct link with purchase intention. Multi-group analysis further reveals heterogeneity across gender, education, age and driving license status. These findings enrich AV adoption theory and offer segment-specific implications for policymakers and firms seeking to foster young consumers’ AV purchase intention and accelerate AV market deployment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Deciphering leader decision-making patterns from open-source information: A temporal knowledge graph-based approach
Abstract: In an era characterized by complex geopolitical and economic volatility, analyzing leader decision patterns is crucial for strategic foresight and organizational risk assessment. While leaders’ decision-making footprints are increasingly captured in massive open-source information, deciphering these patterns presents significant challenges. Traditional decision-making analysis heavily relies on subjective expert judgment and struggles with large-scale unstructured data, whereas modern data-driven deep learning models often operate as uninterpretable black boxes lacking theoretical grounding. Furthermore, the inherent sparsity and temporal dispersion of open-source data complicate effective modeling. To address these limitations, this study proposes a theory-grounded computational framework that integrates a Temporal Knowledge Graph with a Decision Pattern Neural Network. The Temporal Knowledge Graph structures fragmented open-source information into temporally ordered semantic quadruples, enabling the dynamic representation of decision-related entities, relations, and contextual factors. The Decision Pattern Neural Network further models decision-making as a hierarchical process in which external environmental factors are filtered through leader-specific individual factors before producing action tendencies. In a case study of Saudi Aramco, we construct a Temporal Knowledge Graph containing 153,267 quadruples from more than 440,000 open-source records and evaluate the framework on 352 annotated decision events of CEO Amin Nasser. The proposed model achieves an overall prediction accuracy of 83.02%, with a precision of 86.49% and a recall of 88.89%. This study provides a theoretically sound and computationally scalable solution for deciphering leadership logic, effectively bridging the gap between qualitative decision theory and quantitative data analytics. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Dong H.; Pan H.; Yu M.
Title: Electric vehicle use, travel behavior, and driver perceptions in the context of aging communities: Evidence from a car owner survey in the Yangtze River Delta cities
Abstract: Against the dual background of transport electrification and population aging, this study examines electric vehicle (EV) use from the perspective of vehicle users. Drawing on survey data of private vehicle users in cities across the Yangtze River Delta region, this study addresses two core questions: (1) does EV usage contribute to stronger automobile dependence, and (2) do EV users and non-EV users differ in their perceptions of the potential inconvenience caused to older residents and in self-reported yielding behaviors? The results indicate that EV users currently report lower annual mileage than internal combustion engine vehicle (ICEV) users. However, EV use is also associated with a greater self-reported increase in overall travel frequency, a stronger reduction in active travel, and, among households with prior ICEV ownership, a higher likelihood of reporting an increase in annual mileage among respondents who replaced an ICEV with an EV than among those in dual-vehicle households. EV users report weaker perceived negative impacts of their vehicle use on older residents, whereas no significant difference is found in self-reported yielding frequency, indicating a possible perception-behavior gap. These findings highlight the need to integrate age-friendly objectives into urban transport electrification and strengthen driver awareness interventions. A behaviorally informed transition that considers travel patterns, subjective risk perceptions, and pedestrian-oriented conduct may better align low-carbon mobility with age-friendly and inclusive community development. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Determinants of electric vehicle adoption intention in Bangladesh: Policy-Relevant evidence from an extended UTAUT2 model using PLS-SEM and fsQCA
Abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) adoption remains limited in Bangladesh despite growing policy attention to transport electrification. This study examined Behavioral Intention toward EV adoption among 428 EV-aware respondents across Bangladesh's eight administrative divisions using an extended Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2) framework incorporating Environmental Concern, Perceived Risk, Institutional Support, and Attitude. Cross-sectional survey data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), importance-performance map analysis (IPMA), and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA). The structural model explained 59.5% of the variance in Behavioral Intention. Performance Expectancy (β = 0.233) and Perceived Risk (β = −0.240) showed the strongest positive and negative associations, respectively, with comparable absolute path coefficients. Environmental Concern and Institutional Support were positively associated with intention. Environmental Concern and Perceived Risk also exhibited statistically significant but small indirect associations through Attitude, whereas Institutional Support showed no significant association with Attitude. Although Attitude was positively associated with intention, its three specified antecedents explained only 8.2% of its variance, indicating a limited evaluative pathway. IPMA identified Perceived Risk as having the greatest absolute importance, while fsQCA revealed alternative within-sample configurations associated with high Behavioral Intention. Together, the findings highlight the relevance of anticipated ownership-related uncertainty alongside expected EV benefits, clarify the empirical limits of the proposed attitudinal pathway, and distinguish individual structural associations from alternative configurational patterns. Title: Dual illusion of informational self-sufficiency and its implications for verification and truth recognition: The interplay of news-finds-me and third-person perceptions

Using two-wave panel data (N = 896), we examine their independent and interactive associations with verification and truth recognition. Results partially support the proposed synergy: NFMP alone does not deter verification, but combined with perceptual bias, it predicts lower verification. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: de Jong E.; Grunwald A.
Title: Visions of quantum computing: An ethical assessment
Abstract: Visions of future technologies shape their development trajectories, making them important objects of ethical analysis. This paper examines contemporary visions of quantum computing and the futures they project. First, we analyse vision statements by key actors in the field, focusing on anticipated technical affordances, the applications these give rise to, their associated domains, and the value-laden terms used to describe these projections. Drawing on these insights, we distil four main visions of quantum computing, each framing its societal relevance differently: as a contributor to the public good, a scientific tool, an economic asset, or a geopolitical advantage. Second, we highlight ethically salient patterns and presuppositions embedded within these visions, including a pervasive techno-optimism paired with techno-solutionist reasoning; the prevalence of promissory language used to legitimise innovation agendas; and a morally ambivalent discourse shaped by the interests of a narrow group of powerful actors. Taken together, these features form a figurative heatmap of potential ethical concerns in contemporary visions of quantum computing that warrant closer ethical scrutiny and point to avenues for further research. Authors: Paasch R.; Mau G.
Title: Understanding risk acceptance in performance enhancing substance use: A cluster randomized prevention study among recreational fitness athletes
Abstract: Background: The use of performance-enhancing substances such as pre-workout supplements has become increasingly common in recreational fitness environments. Although behavioral interventions aim to reduce enhancement-related substance use, little is known about whether such interventions operate similarly across different psychosocial athlete profiles and which psychological mechanisms may underlie behavioral change. Methods: Data were analyzed from a cluster-randomized prevention trial conducted in ten fitness studios in Germany, including 602 recreational fitness athletes. Cluster-adjusted logistic regression models examined intervention effects on booster use at follow-up (T3). Risk acceptance decreased more strongly among motivationally ambivalent athlete profiles, whereas comparable moderation effects were not observed for booster use. These reductions were consistent with a partial mediation pathway linking the intervention to reduced booster use. Conclusions: The findings suggest that behavioral interventions in recreational fitness settings may operate differently across psychosocial athlete profiles rather than producing uniform effects. Title: Media exposure and local economic transformation: Evidence from place-based anime broadcasting in Japan
Abstract: This study examines whether media exposure can drive local economic development using the case of anime “holy lands” in Japan—real-world locations depicted in animated works. Title: Within-person associations between fear of missing out and cyberbullying victimization: An ecological momentary assessment study
Abstract: Several psychological factors (e.g., personality, mental health, and behavioral problems) have been linked to cyberbullying victimization. However, relatively little research has examined fear of missing out (FoMO) in relation to cyberbullying victimization. Existing studies have largely relied on cross-sectional designs focusing on between-person differences, providing limited insight into how this association unfolds within individuals in daily life. To address this gap, the present study employed a 14-day ecological momentary assessment (EMA) design with four prompts per day to examine their momentary association in community adults (N = 301). Title: Are nudges suitable to combat health inequalities? The efficacy of default nudges in people with lower versus higher socio-economic position
Abstract: Nudging is assumed to be particularly effective among lower socio-economic position (SEP) subpopulations and thus to have the potential of combating health disparities. However, empirical evidence for this proposition is scarce. In two studies, we examined the efficacy of a default nudge in stimulating healthy food choices and whether this effect is moderated by SEP. In both experiments, a default nudge (versus a no-nudge control condition) was applied in a hypothetical online supermarket among UK participants with lower and higher SEP. Study 2 involved a more realistic supermarket setting by manipulating the presence of price information. SEP-indicators and related SEP-variables were measured. Across both studies, the default nudge was efficacious in stimulating healthy choices. This effect was not consistently moderated by SEP, with the effect being present among lower and higher SEP groups. Study 2 demonstrates that these effects are not impacted by the presence of price information. We conclude that default nudges are also efficacious among lower SEP populations, even when processing additional price information, but that this technique does not combat health inequalities. Future nudging studies in real-life settings, where financial factors matter, are needed to learn whether default nudges can actually benefit lower (versus higher) SEP groups. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Are domestic long-distance travel and international flying complementary? Evidence from England's National Travel Survey, 2015–2019
Abstract: Research on the demand and climate impacts of domestic and international long-distance travel (LDT) has expanded rapidly, yet comparatively little is known about whether these two domains are behaviourally interlinked; that is, whether participation in one is associated with participation in, or the intensity of, the other. This paper addresses that gap by examining the relationship between domestic LDT and international flying at both the extensive (participation) and intensive (frequency) margins within a common analytical framework. Using pooled National Travel Survey data for England (2015–2019), the study estimates zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) models of annual trips per person with cross-domain participation as a key explanatory variable and a control-function correction for potential endogeneity across both domains. Conditional mixed process (CMP) simultaneous-equation models provide a broader robustness check. Descriptively, among respondents aged 16 and above, those who had taken at least one international flight in the previous year (fliers) were substantially more mobile domestically than those who didn't. Fliers travelled around 50 % further in total but nearly twice as far in domestic long-distance trips, generating proportionally higher emissions than non-fliers, suggesting the main divide lies in longer-distance rather than everyday travel. ZINB models show a positive bidirectional association between domestic LDT and international flying at the extensive margin, where participation in one domain is associated with a higher likelihood of participation in the other. At the intensive margin, however, the association becomes asymmetric, as international flying participation is not associated with higher LDT frequency among its participants. CMP models point to modest shared unobserved drivers of entry across both domains and identify another directional asymmetry, as domestic LDT frequency is not associated with international flying participation. Together these patterns indicate asymmetric co-variation rather than symmetric patterning and support treating domestic and international long-distance travel as interconnected components of individual mobility. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Exploring the perceived awareness–behaviour gap in AI-enabled phishing: a socio-technical perspective informed by complex adaptive systems
Abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping phishing by enabling increasingly personalised, scalable, and psychologically persuasive attacks. Although cybersecurity awareness remains important, knowledge may not consistently translate into protective action when users encounter contextual pressures or insufficient institutional support. This study examines the perceived awareness–behaviour gap in an AI-enabled phishing context through a complex adaptive socio-technical systems perspective. A cross-sectional survey of 300 university students was analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). The individual-level analysis captured students’ perceptions of system awareness, institutional support, feedback and reinforcement, adaptive response capacity, and self-reported protective behaviour. System Awareness was positively associated with Adaptive Response Capacity (β = 0.612, p < 0.001), as was Perceived Institutional Support (β = 0.441, p < 0.001). Perceived Feedback and Reinforcement was positively associated with Self-Reported Protective Behaviour (β = 0.536, p < 0.001). These findings provide exploratory, perception-based evidence that students’ reported cybersecurity responses are associated with both individual awareness and perceived institutional conditions. The cross-sectional design does not directly capture temporal adaptation, co-evolution, system emergence, actual behaviour, or responses to experimentally presented AI-generated phishing attacks. Complex Adaptive Systems theory is therefore employed as an explanatory perspective rather than as a directly tested dynamic model. The study extends socio-technical cybersecurity research by integrating awareness, perceived institutional support, feedback, adaptive response capacity, and reported protective practices within a unified framework relevant to university-based cybersecurity interventions. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Longer lives, longer-lived buildings: Implications of population aging and low-demand scenarios for Japan's residential sector decarbonization
Abstract: The residential sector is a major contributor to Japan's emissions and plays a pivotal role in achieving net-zero targets. As operational emissions decline with power-sector decarbonization, embodied emissions from building materials are becoming an increasingly critical component of mitigation efforts. However, the predominance of short-lived buildings and the evolving housing demands associated with an aging population present significant, and yet insufficiently examined, challenges for building-sector decarbonization. This study assesses the mitigation potential of low energy and material demand (LEMD) strategies in Japan's residential sector, explicitly incorporating demographic aging within the MESSAGEix-Buildings framework. Results show that population aging may increase building material demand through higher per-capita floor area consumption, a factor often overlooked in decarbonization modeling. The moderate sufficiency measure, reducing per capita floor space among elderly households through a shift toward compact multi-family housing, achieves a 10% reduction in embodied carbon emissions relative to the Reference scenario in 2050. When combined with other LEMD measures, total avoided embodied emissions reach 25–40%. Although extending building lifetimes may increase operational energy use by retaining less efficient structures, the net mitigation effect remains positive, as the reduction in embodied emissions outweighs the additional operational emissions. Overall, deep decarbonization of Japan's residential sector requires aligning LEMD strategies with aging-sensitive demand trajectories and accelerated electrification powered by cleaner electricity. © 2026

Title: Efficacy of immersive virtual reality reminiscence for older persons living in the community in Singapore: A multi-centre study
Abstract: Background: With the global population aged 60 and above expected to reach 2.1 billion by 2050, interventions promoting mental health in older adults have become increasingly important. Objective: This study compared the effects of immersive Virtual Reality (VR) reminiscence with traditional photograph-based reminiscence on subjective happiness, loneliness, and quality of life among older adults, while additionally examining technology acceptance factors. Methods: A randomized controlled trial was conducted with 60 community-dwelling older adults (mean age 78.57 years) recruited from multi-centre design in Singapore. Participants were randomly allocated to either VR reminiscence (n=30) or traditional photograph-based reminiscence (n=30) groups. Both groups participated in 4 weekly 30-minute sessions featuring culturally-relevant content including Singapore landmarks, and traditional festivals. Outcomes were measured using validated scales for subjective happiness, loneliness, quality of life, and technology acceptance at baseline and post-intervention. Semi-structured interviews provided qualitative insights. Results: The VR group showed significant improvements in subjective happiness (Cohen's d=0.45, p=0.034) and technology acceptance, with large effect sizes for attitudinal beliefs (d=0.67, p=0.002) and control beliefs (d=0.53, p=0.009). A positive correlation between subjective happiness and loneliness was observed (ρ=0.559, p<0.001), more pronounced in the VR group (ρ=0.623) than controls (ρ=0.445). Qualitative findings revealed that culturally-relevant content was most emotionally engaging, with facilitator support is crucial for technology acceptance. Conclusions: This study suggests that VR reminiscence may show promise in enhancing subjective happiness and technology acceptance among the sampled older adults © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Aging knowledge, geriatric care attitudes, and career choice motivation among nursing students: A latent profile analysis and mediation analysis
Abstract: Background: The global aging population has intensified the demand for geriatric care, yet a critical shortage of professionals persists, partly due to nursing students' low motivation to pursue careers in this field. Knowledge of aging and attitudes towards geriatric care are key antecedents to career choice motivation, but their complex interrelationships and the heterogeneity in attitudes remain underexplored. Aim: To identify latent profiles of geriatric care attitudes, examine differences in knowledge of aging and career choice motivation across profiles, and investigate knowledge of aging's mediating role between attitudes and career choice motivation. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 429 third-year nursing students recruited via convenience sampling from a single university in Chongqing, China (May–July 2025). Participants were included if they majored in nursing, voluntarily participated, and could communicate fluently in Mandarin. Data were collected using the Facts on Aging Quiz (FAQ), Perspectives on Caring for Older Patients (PCOP) scale, and Career Choice Motivation Questionnaire for Geriatric Nursing (CCMQ-GN). Latent profile analysis (LPA) was used to identify attitude profiles, and mediation analysis examined the role of knowledge of aging between attitudes and career choice motivation. Results: Three distinct attitude profiles were identified: ambivalent-coexistent (12.12%), moderate-balanced (27.97%), and positive-pure (59.91%). The positive-pure group showed the most favorable attitudes but not the highest career choice motivation. The ambivalent-coexistent group, despite conflict, exhibited the strongest motivation. Knowledge of aging mediated the relationship between attitudes and career choice motivation only in the moderate-balanced group (indirect effect: β = −1.1068, 95%CI [−2.1281, −0.2945]); no mediation was found in the positive-pure group. Conclusions: Three distinct attitudinal profiles exist with differential career choice motivation. Knowledge of aging plays a conditional mediating role, effective only for the moderate-balanced group. Tailored interventions are warranted: a. for the moderate-balanced group, priority should be given to systematic knowledge training to build care confidence; b. for the positive-pure group, interventions should focus on optimizing professional environments and career prospects; c. for the ambivalent-coexistent group, empowerment training can help resolve cognitive conflicts and leverage their high motivation. Tailored interventions are needed. Trial registration: Not applicable. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Author full names: Mukhopadhyay, Rishika (57666172700); Prajapat, Kanika (61010777100); Varvarousis, Angelos (57214675688)
Title: Crafting post-growth? A support-structure diagnosis of Jaipur’s craft economy
Abstract: Post-growth scholarship has often celebrated craft as a privileged site for imagining postcapitalist and post-growth transitions. Yet this discussion remains largely Global North-centred and empirically underdeveloped, drawing mostly on small-scale, elective and niche craft economies rather than large craft sectors where artisanal labour constitutes a major livelihood system. This paper addresses this gap through the case of Jaipur’s craft economy, one of the world’s largest concentrated craft economies. The study draws on semi-structured interviews with craft-sector experts, field visits to craft fairs and markets, participant observation at a socio-ecological enterprise, and documentary analysis conducted between 2023 and 2024. We examine how Jaipur’s craft sector enables, constrains and complicates post-growth-compatible forms of territorial development. To do so, we develop a support-structure diagnosis, understood as an analysis of the institutional, material, financial, cultural, geographical and historical conditions sustaining, transforming or absorbing craft economies into dominant growth-oriented circuits. We map three interrelated support structures operating across multiple scales: top-down institutional structures, bottom-up and intermediary structures, and local conditions. The article shows that Jaipur’s large-scale, decentralised and historically embedded craft economy unsettles simple distinctions between local and global, formal and informal, traditional and entrepreneurial. It requires a more situated understanding of relocalisation, alterity and market integration in post-growth debates. We identify four dynamics through which support structures interact: encouragement, collaboration, suppression and friction. Theoretically, equity, central to post-growth economies, remains a concern for Jaipur. Scale, heterogeneity of informalisation and decentralisation, and multiple axes of power in Jaipur’s craft ecosystem open up a productive challenge for post-growth scholarship. Authors: Wang C.; Du R.; Liu H.
Title: Resilient or relocating? Migrants' settlement responses to climate extremes in Chinese cities
Abstract: Climate extremes are increasingly disrupting urban systems and reshaping mobility, with migrants among the most exposed and least protected. However, the mechanisms linking extreme weather to migrants' settlement decisions remain insufficiently explored. This study examines how exposure to extreme heat, extreme cold, heavy rainfall, and extreme drought affects long-term settlement intentions in Chinese cities. We develop a multi-perspective framework that integrates neoclassical, new economics, behavioural, and structural theories, and test it using multilevel logistic regression models with data from 151,706 migrants across 154 cities (2014–2018). The results indicate that exposure to extreme heat and cold significantly reduces the likelihood of permanent settlement, while drought and rainfall exert more context-dependent influences. These impacts are heterogeneous across population groups: older migrants and long-term residents are especially sensitive to climatic stress, whereas higher education and income enhance adaptive capacity. Male migrants show greater sensitivity to heat stress, potentially reflecting higher occupational exposure in outdoor labour sectors. In addition, a composite climate risk index demonstrates limited explanatory power, suggesting that aggregate measures may obscure subgroup-specific vulnerabilities. Overall, climate extremes not only influence urban settlement patterns but also exacerbate inequalities. The findings extend beyond China and offer broader insights into how migrants can be more effectively integrated into urban climate adaptation strategies in rapidly urbanizing regions of the Global South. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Settler colonialism and community protection from redistricting
Abstract: Much research on the urban racial politics of redistricting focus on the period of the “redistricting revolution” after 1965. This study takes a more historical approach to this topic by asking: how have select communities within cities managed to avoid ever being redistricted from their founding in the 19th century to the present? Using digitized ward boundaries from Chicago and Milwaukee from their founding to the present, we discovered the importance of the legacy of settler colonialism for answering this question. Specifically, logics of settler colonialism have protected select communities in Chicago and Milwaukee from ever being redistricted through three mechanisms: 1) settlement formation, 2) state law protection, and 3) litigation protection. We conclude by discussing the implications for studying the urban racial politics of redistricting. © 2026 The Author(s). Published by Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Choi S.C.; Suh T.
Title: Rural Migration in Korea: Patterns and Implications Under Rapid Fertility Decline
Source title: Journal of Population and Social Studies
Abstract: Studies on South Korea’s population have primarily relied on aggregate data or focused exclusively on urban areas. However, rural population dynamics differ significantly from national trends, making it challenging to apply national population projections directly to rural and agricultural populations. This study estimates the in-migration and out-migration rates of rural areas using municipality-level statistical data from 2012 to 2022 and forecasts regional net migration rates. The population is categorized by gender and age group, and in-migration and out-migration rates are estimated for each cohort. Given that regional migration rates are non-negative, the Tobit model is employed for the estimation. The analysis reveals heterogeneity in migration behaviors across different demographic groups. In particular, young adults in their twenties exhibit the highest out-migration rates, mainly due to limited access to higher education and employment opportunities in rural areas. In contrast, for individuals in their thirties and early forties, the availability of childcare and family-supportive environments plays a significant role in migration decisions. These findings highlight the need for differentiated policy strategies tailored to the specific needs of each age group. This study enhances understanding of rural population dynamics and provides evidence to inform the formulation of regional revitalization policies. © 2027 Mahidol University, Institute for Population and Social Research. Title: A New Method for Detecting and Explaining Local Irregularities in Spatial Synthetic Data
Abstract: Spatial synthetic populations are increasingly used in agent-based models, spatial microsimulation, and other forms of place-based analysis. Their usefulness, however, depends not only on reproducing aggregate patterns but also on maintaining plausible local distributions. This creates a difficult validation problem when independent benchmarks are limited and validation cannot proceed beyond checking the technical implementation of model constraints. We develop a moment-based validation framework for detecting and interpreting local irregularities in spatial synthetic data. Local distributions are characterized through their first four moments and we combine hierarchical clustering with SHapley Additive exPlanations to identify and explain areas whose modeled distributions depart from expected local patterns and contextual variables. The framework is demonstrated using modeled salary distributions from the Synthetic Population Catalyst in West Yorkshire, a setting in which fine-scale synthetic populations are assembled from sources observed at coarser spatial and substantive resolutions. The application identifies locally unusual areas, shows how these can be interpreted against contextual characteristics and local knowledge, and illustrates how the framework can support judgments about whether synthetic data are fit for intended use. More broadly, the article argues that local coherence should be treated as a central criterion in the validation of spatial synthetic populations. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: How do substance use behaviors change across housing hardship transitions? Asymmetric effects on smoking, binge drinking, and marijuana use in young adulthood
Abstract: Housing hardship is increasingly recognized as a risk factor for substance use, yet little is known about whether entering and exiting hardship are differentially associated with addictive behaviors or whether these associations vary by gender. Drawing on stress-coping theory and the self-medication hypothesis, this study examines how housing hardship transitions are associated with smoking frequency (number of days smoked in the past 30 days), binge drinking frequency (days per month), and marijuana use (any use in the past 30 days) among young adults. Using data from Waves III (aged 18–27, M = 21.9) and IV (aged 24–34, M = 28.4) of the National Longitudinal Study of Adolescent to Adult Health (N = 12,965), we employ asymmetric fixed-effects models that separately estimate associations for entering and exiting housing hardship and formally test whether they differ in magnitude. Standard fixed-effects models indicate positive associations between housing hardship and all three substance use outcomes. However, asymmetric models reveal significant asymmetry for smoking: entering housing hardship is associated with increases in smoking, whereas exiting is not associated with corresponding reductions, consistent with the persistence of nicotine dependence. Binge drinking and marijuana use display largely symmetric responses. Gender interaction analyses indicate that increases in smoking and marijuana use associated with hardship entry are more pronounced among men, while reductions in binge drinking associated with hardship exit are stronger among men. These findings suggest potential substance-specific differences in the reversibility of stress-induced use and may inform gender-responsive approaches to addiction treatment and housing support. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Retirement-related grief symptoms: The role of neuroticism, time perspective, and occupational regret
Abstract: Retirement represents a significant life and identity transition that may be associated with a sense of loss. Individuals differ in their adjustment; however, the psychological and cognitive factors contributing to maladaptive adaptation, including prolonged grief symptoms, remain underexplored. In this study, 359 retirees (M = 68.89, SD = 3.63; 31.8% men, 68.2% women), who had retired within the past five years, completed measures of neuroticism, time perspectives (past negative, present fatalistic, and future), occupational regret, and prolonged grief symptoms. Pearson correlations and regression analysis were conducted. Higher neuroticism was positively associated with prolonged grief symptoms ( r = 0.30, p < .001). In the regression model, past negative and present fatalistic time perspectives, as well as occupational regret, and reason for retirement significantly contributed to prolonged grief symptoms. The future time perspective was not significantly associated with prolonged grief symptoms. Overall, negative personality and cognitive predispositions play a critical role in emotional responses to retirement, underscoring the importance of identifying at-risk individuals and developing targeted interventions to support adjustment. Title: Differences in Toddlers’ inhibitory control performance across phases with and without sound-absorbing materials in a nursery classroom: a field-based intervention study
Abstract: Objective To examine whether toddlers’ IC-related performance differed across classroom periods with and without sound-absorbing materials. Methods A field-based alternating intervention was conducted in a Japanese nursery classroom (N = 30; age = 24.3–39.3 months). Sound-absorbing materials were installed during two phases and removed during an intervening phase. Existing classroom recordings from four days in each phase were analyzed to characterize sound levels and reverberation times were measured across two phases. Teachers also completed the Self-Regulation Assessment Scale for Early Childhood for a subset of children. Results Modest reductions in reverberation time and sound levels were observed during the phases with the sound-absorbing materials installed. Children showed significantly higher odds of task success during both With-installation phases than during the Without-installation phase, although individual response patterns were heterogeneous. The proportion of children waiting successfully for 300 s was lowest during the Without-installation phase, but substantial individual variability was observed. Teacher ratings collected for a limited subset of children showed a broadly similar pattern. Title: Health information–seeking behavior for gastric cancer in Japan: Analysis of temporal changes and regional differences using Google Trends
Abstract: Introduction: Gastric cancer remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality in Japan. Digital search data such as Google Trends have been increasingly used to capture population-level health information–seeking behavior and may complement traditional surveillance systems. However, it remains unclear whether gastric cancer awareness campaigns are associated with measurable changes in online search activity and whether search interest reflects regional disease burden. Aim: This study aimed to evaluate changes in national online search activity during the Gastric Cancer Awareness Month and to assess whether prefecture-level search volume was associated with regional gastric cancer incidence. Methods: We conducted a population-level ecological study using publicly available Google Trends data for Japan from 2012 to 2021. Interrupted time series analysis was applied to evaluate monthly changes in search activity during the awareness month. Prefecture-level associations between annual mean search volume and age-standardized gastric cancer incidence were examined for 2017–2021. Results: At the national level, search activity related to gastric cancer remained relatively stable, with no significant changes in level or trend during the awareness month. In contrast, prefecture-level analyses revealed positive associations between search volume and gastric cancer incidence, although several high-burden regions showed comparatively low search interest. Title: Role-play training based on conversational artificial intelligence and immersive virtual reality: Platform, proof-of-concept, and user study
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: Role-play is an effective method for training conflict resolution skills. However, traditional programs relying on theoretical models, such as the Thomas-Kilmann Conflict Mode Instrument (TKI), often employ questionnaire-based exercises or human-led role-plays, which can limit ecological validity and scalability. To address these limitations, we developed the AI-based Immersive Role-Play Experience Platform (AIRPEP), which integrates large language models (LLMs) and immersive virtual reality (IVR) to simulate realistic training scenarios. AIRPEP features virtual characters, natural interactions, immersive environments, multimodal data collection, and LLM-driven assistants for role-play and personalized feedback. We also proposed a Thematic Content Creation Workflow to create AI-driven scenarios on AIRPEP and applied it to create the Student Conflict Simulator VR, designed for Korean university students. This tool incorporates TKI’s five conflict styles (Collaborating, Competing, Avoiding, Compromising, Accommodating) and the Six Steps of the No-Lose Method. To evaluate the system’s feasibility and user experience, we conducted a pretest-posttest user study with an experimental group (n=32) and a control group (n=23) comprising Korean university students. The experimental group demonstrated a significant improvement in self-expressive communication skills and significantly decreased scores for the Collaborating, Competing, and Avoiding conflict resolution styles. In contrast, the control group’s results indicated a significant decrease in communication skills, with significantly decreased Avoiding conflict resolution style. While the satisfaction and usability ratings of the experimental group were high, the absence of avatars negatively affected their sense of self-presence. Finally, we proposed ten design principles for developing AI-driven role-play training IVR applications. Overall, the initial feasibility and user experience evaluation results indicate that the AIRPEP platform can be used to develop immersive, engaging, and repeatable role-play training interventions, but its long-term effects remain to be evaluated. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Towards continual stance detection via Dual Prototype Aware Mixture of Experts Network
Abstract: Stance detection identifies an author’s stance towards targets. However, real-world scenarios involve constantly emerging targets, causing models trained on static datasets to quickly become outdated and less effective. To address this issue, we propose a new task, Continual Stance Detection, which explores how models can continuously learn to detect stance towards new targets while retaining performance on previously seen targets. We present the first continual stance detection evaluation benchmark, ConStance, comprising the ConDoc dataset (25,492 samples across 8 targets) and the ConTwitter dataset (11,003 samples across 10 targets). Additionally, we propose an effective Dual Prototype Aware Mixture of Experts Network (DP-MoE) method. During continual training, DP-MoE maintains stance-class and expert prototypes, utilizing prototypical contrastive learning and dynamic soft routing to dynamically adapt to new tasks while effectively preserving prior knowledge. Extensive experiments show that DP-MoE achieves the best performance among the evaluated BERT-based continual learning baselines on both datasets under the same continual learning protocol. Specifically, DP-MoE outperforms the best competing method by improving the Macro-F1 score by 2.05% on ConDoc and 3.26% on ConTwitter, while substantially mitigating catastrophic forgetting by reducing the Forgetting Rate by 1.05% and 1.31% across the respective datasets.
