Title: Relationship between driving behaviors and capacity drop using empirical trajectory data
Abstract: Capacity drop, referring to the reduction in bottleneck discharge rate, is a primary contributor to freeway delays. This paper aims to provide empirical evidence of how driving behaviors trigger capacity drop through the analysis of vehicle trajectory data collected before its onset. By quantifying the spatiotemporal impacts of driving behaviors on the discharge rate, we find that the impact of lane-changing (LC) on the discharge rate increased significantly before the onset of capacity drop. Gaps produced by LCs in the anticipation phase contribute most significantly to capacity drop, followed by gaps in the relaxation phase. In contrast, gaps left in the original lane are filled by other vehicles, thereby increasing the discharge rate. The contribution of car-following (CF) behavior to capacity drop is relatively limited. However, after capacity drop occurs, CFs gradually reduce the discharge rate within the bottleneck segment. These empirical results are further validated using several trajectory datasets. © 2026

Title: Serial mediating role of belonging and state mindfulness in the relationship between clinical learning environment and caring behaviors in nursing students
Abstract: Aim: The study aimed to examine the relationship between clinical learning environment and caring behaviors in nursing students and to test the serial mediating roles of belonging and state mindfulness in this relationship. Background: The psychosocial mechanisms linking the clinical learning environment to caring behaviors remain unclear, particularly the combined roles of belonging and state mindfulness. Design: The study had a cross-sectional design and was conducted in line with the STROBE guidelines. Methods: The sample consisted of 452 undergraduate nursing students studying at a state university in Turkiye. The data were collected between December 2025 and January 2026 using the Personal Information Form, Clinical Learning Environment Scale, Nursing Department Belonging Scale, State Mindfulness Scale, and Caring Behaviors Inventory. Results: The clinical learning environment was found to be positively correlated with sense of belonging (B = 0.412, p < .001). Sense of belonging significantly predicted both State Mindfulness (B = 0.607, p < .001) and caring behaviors (B = 0.857, p < .001). State mindfulness is also a significant predictor of caring behaviors (B = 0.734, p < .001). Indirect effects analyses indicated that the clinical learning environment was associated with caring behaviors through sense of belonging and through the sequential pathway involving both sense of belonging and state mindfulness. Additionally, the indirect effect of the clinical learning environment on caring behaviors through state mindfulness alone was not significant. Title: Transport affordability and automobile debt in the United States
Abstract: Rising transportation costs have sparked widespread concern, with media headlines questioning whether the era of inexpensive automobility is over. Existing analyses often rely on sticker prices and aggregated sales data, failing to account for the full range of ownership costs such as insurance, fuel, and debt payments. This study bridges that gap by providing a fuller accounting of transportation affordability relative to incomes and total expenses, as well as with respect to automobile debt burdens. We examine transportation affordability using aggregate Consumer Expenditure Survey data from 1984 to 2024 and household-level records from 2024 to 2025, analyzing long-term trends in transportation spending and modeling recent predictors of affordability and automobile debt using beta, logistic, OLS, and GLM regressions. Real transportation expenditures have risen since 2020 but remain within their historical range, while transportation's shares of household income and total expenditures remain below their 1980s levels. We find that demographic and geographic predictors of transportation expenditure vary depending on whether costs are modeled as a share of income versus as a share of total expenses. Most notably, Black and Hispanic households spend more on transportation as a share of total expenditures but not income. Further, predictors of auto debt paint different portraits of who experiences higher costs compared to expenditure models. Households in the West devote smaller shares of both income and expenditure to transportation, while auto debt levels are higher in the South. These findings demonstrate that expenditure and debt burdens are distributed differently across households and highlight the limitations of relying on any single expenditure-based measure of transportation affordability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Shared processing in familiar and unfamiliar face matching
Abstract: Large performance benefits in face processing for familiar compared to unfamiliar faces are often interpreted as reflecting qualitative changes in processing. However, directly testing this claim has proven difficult because of variation in tasks, stimuli and performance scales used to measure unfamiliar and familiar face recognition. Here we introduce a new method to compare familiar and unfamiliar face identity processing abilities, using the same task, and the same faces across experimental conditions. Familiarity was manipulated naturally, based on participants' viewing history for one of two popular TV shows, such that characters from one show were familiar, and the other unfamiliar. Prior exposure to characters led to improved identity matching performance for actors on that show, confirming effective manipulation of familiarity, but our method avoided floor and ceiling effects which have made previous research hard to interpret. Across two experiments, we report strong and reliable associations between viewers' accuracy on familiar and unfamiliar face matching. We conclude that despite the considerable accuracy differences typically observed between tests of familiar and unfamiliar faces, they appear to share underlying processes. We discuss these results in terms of the debate about the degree to which quantitative or qualitative differences best characterise the relationship between familiar and unfamiliar face processing. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Urban–Rural Differences in the Determinants of Depression Among Mothers of Children Under Five in Indonesia
Source title: Journal of Population and Social Studies
Abstract: Mothers of children under five are vulnerable to depression, which may adversely affect child growth and development. This study examined urban–rural differences in the biopsychosocial determinants of maternal depression in Indonesia. Data were obtained from the 2023 Indonesia Health Survey and included 70,851 mothers with children aged 0–59 months. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview, and determinants were analyzed using multiple logistic regression. In urban areas, maternal depression was associated with younger maternal age (15–19 years; adjusted odds ratio (AOR) = 4.14, 95% CI [2.15, 7.94]), current pregnancy (AOR = 2.30, 95% CI [1.54, 3.43]), and chronic disease (AOR = 2.87, 95% CI [2.08, 3.95]), unintended pregnancy (AOR = 3.50, 95% CI [2.76, 4.44]), divorced status (AOR = 2.61, 95% CI [1.59, 4.27]), unemployment (AOR = 1.80, 95% CI [1.43, 2.28]), and lower educational attainment. In rural areas, depression was associated with chronic disease (AOR = 2.24, 95% CI [1.37, 3.66]), unintended pregnancy (AOR = 2.66, 95% CI [1.79, 3.95]), unemployment (AOR = 1.51, 95% CI [1.15, 1.98]), and divorced status (AOR = 3.45, 95% CI [1.94, 6.14]). These findings demonstrate distinct urban–rural patterns in the determinants of maternal depression, highlighting the importance of context-specific maternal mental health interventions. © 2027 Mahidol University, Institute for Population and Social Research. Title: Evolution of sentiment orientation for Chinese commercially autonomous ride-hailing: An online review–based analysis
Abstract: Baidu Apollo Go, launched in Wuhan, marks the first large-scale commercial deployment of autonomous ride-hailing in China. Before such services are rolled out more broadly, there is an urgent need for an objective assessment of public acceptance. However, existing studies largely rely on hypothetical scenarios and short observation windows, so their findings may deviate from real-world dynamics. This study focuses on a full year following the surge in public attention surrounding Apollo Go and uses related comments posted on Weibo as the empirical basis to investigate the evolution of public sentiment orientation. Specifically, we collect 41,009 comments containing references to Apollo Go and autonomous ride-hailing from 7 July 2024 to 6 July 2025 via a web spider, apply Latent Dirichlet Allocation for topic modelling, and employ the Baidu Smart Cloud Sentiment Analysis API for sentiment classification. By situating these comments in the context of major events and regional differences, we explore how public attention and sentiment toward key topics evolve over time. The main findings are as follows. (1) Public attention exhibits a clear stage-wise shift. In the early stage, discussion mainly focuses on the employment impact on ride-hailing drivers, whereas, as commercial operations progress, public attention gradually shifts toward passenger safety and ride experience. (2) Although the overall sentiment score for the full study period is only 0.35, public sentiment exhibits a fluctuating upward trend over time. (3) Major events lead to pronounced fluctuations in public sentiment. Technological breakthroughs, disclosures of safety performance, and positive industry-development signals generally improve public sentiment, whereas safety accidents and corporate operational risks tend to reduce it. (4) Public sentiment also exhibits clear regional differences. Among provinces where autonomous ride-hailing services operate over an area of at least 100 km2, those with per capita GDP above USD 20,000 generally exhibit lower overall sentiment scores. © 2026 Hong Kong Society for Transportation Studies

Authors: Gruda D.; Jonason P.K.
Title: There's no place like home: Stayers are more psychopathic than movers
Abstract: Recent evidence links residential mobility, moving away from one's childhood region, to higher Dark Triad scores. We ask the mirror-image question. In a U.S. adult sample with known childhood and current state ( N = 3958), respondents still living in their childhood state (stayers) scored higher on psychopathy than those who had moved away (movers). The difference was small and survived comparisons within origin state and birth cohort with the current state held fixed. Machiavellianism and narcissism showed no statistically significant adjusted difference. The stayer difference did not depend on sex or on how far movers had gone, and a state-level education proxy gave no sign of socioeconomic selection. Among movers, higher scorers on all three traits went to denser destinations, and higher psychopathy scorers to states with more homicide and inequality. Lifetime immobility and recent mobility thus relate to psychopathy in opposite directions, which is consistent with interstate moves being pulled by opportunities that reach high scorers less often. Individual socioeconomic status and reasons for moving were unmeasured. © 2026 The Author(s).

Authors: Kim B.-J.; Jung J.
Title: The AI safety paradox: how the threat of displacement erodes safety behavior and the buffering role of servant leadership
Abstract: While organizations increasingly adopt artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance operational efficiency and minimize errors, this study examines a critical strategic irony: the potential for AI-induced job insecurity (AIJI) to undermine the very safety behaviors it aims to augment. Drawing on Conservation of Resources (COR) theory, we propose a comprehensive model wherein AIJI acts as a distal threat that triggers a resource loss spiral, directly reducing safety behavior and indirectly eroding it through the sequential mechanisms of diminished psychological safety and heightened job stress. We further posit that servant leadership functions as a protective boundary condition that can interrupt this deleterious process. To test these hypotheses, we employed a four-wave time-lagged design with data collected from 365 employees in South Korea. The structural equation modeling results confirmed that AIJI exerts both a direct negative influence on safety behavior and a significant indirect effect transmitted sequentially through reduced psychological safety and increased job stress. Furthermore, the analysis revealed a significant moderated mediation effect; high levels of servant leadership effectively buffered the negative impact of AIJI on psychological safety, thereby attenuating the subsequent chain of resource depletion and behavioral withdrawal. These findings contribute to the literature by elucidating the sophisticated psychological pathways linking technological threats to operational risks and by establishing servant leadership as a strategic human shield essential for maintaining safety reliability in the algorithmic era. Title: Experiences of ageism in palliative care: Nursing students' perspectives
Abstract: Background: Increasing life expectancy is associated with greater dependency among older adults due to the rising prevalence of chronic diseases. Therefore, prejudice, stigmatization, and discrimination against older adults become more pronounced as individuality decreases. Aim: This study aimed to examine the views and experiences of nursing students, as future healthcare professionals who may play a role in shaping attitudes toward older adults, regarding ageism in clinical practice. Methods: A qualitative descriptive research design was employed to explore how nursing students experienced and made sense of ageism in palliative care. The study was conducted in October – December 2024 with 18 nursing students at a university in the Black Sea Region who had begun practice in the palliative service. Data were collected using a personal questionnaire and a semi-structured interview form. Ethics committee and institutional approvals were obtained for the study. Results: The mean age of the students was 21.83 ± 1.79 years. Three main themes were identified: “Traces of Passing Time: Looking at Old Age”, “Reflections of Ageism in Nursing Care”, and “Self-Awareness.” Students reported that communication, holistic care, and professional commitment are essential for quality care for older adults; however, these aspects were often influenced by age-related biases in clinical practice. Conclusion: Participants noted that systemic barriers in clinical settings (particularly excessive workloads) and ageist attitudes are key constraints to providing quality care for older adults. The findings highlight the need for practice-based early educational interventions that combat ageism in clinical settings, minimize the negative effects of systemic barriers on care, and strengthen students' preparedness to provide holistic care to frail older adults. © 2026

Authors: Dang H.; Lü D.; Li J.; Lü Y.; Feng Q.; Fu B.
Title: A spatially-explicit framework for landscape optimization integrating nonlinear trade-offs and critical thresholds of ecosystem services
Abstract: Clarifying the impact of landscape patterns on ecosystem services (ESs) and the trade-off relationships among them, as well as exploring adaptive landscape optimization schemes, is of crucial importance for landscape pattern planning and management, as well as maximizing the value of ecosystem services. However, current research on the relationship between landscape patterns and ecosystem services is still insufficient, especially in mountainous regions. The response mechanisms between different landscape patterns and ecosystem services also need to be further explored. The traditional landscape planning methods usually only consider a single type of ecosystem service and lack clear spatial orientation. To address these critical knowledge gaps, this research presents an integrated spatially explicit framework that combines interpretable machine learning and multi-objective optimization. The five key ESs in the Qinling Mountains, China's central ecological shelter, were quantified. A random forest model coupled with partial dependence plot analysis was employed to disentangle the nonlinear and threshold-dependent relationships between landscape metrics and ESs, while the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm-II was applied to generate Pareto-optimal landscape configurations under multiple policy constraints. The results indicate that forest land dominated the landscape from 2000 to 2020, with relatively high spatial stability. The landscape pattern indices and ecosystem services exhibit nonlinear and staged characteristics. Compared with the current landscape pattern, the optimal scheme not only complies with policy requirements but also comprehensively enhances water yield (0.05%), carbon sequestration (0.02%), and soil retention (0.26%). The research protocol provides a verifiable and scalable planning method, offering a reference for formulating scientific ecological protection strategies for mountainous areas and cross-scale sustainable landscape management. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Empirical analysis of perceived inaccessibility in the Netherlands
Source title: Transportation Research Part D: Transport and Environment
Abstract: A growing body of research examines how people perceive accessibility, typically drawing from small-scale surveys in either urban or rural areas. The novelty of this study lies in analysing the heterogeneity in the perceived inability to reach different destinations, accounting for differences across population segments, regions, and transport modes at a nationwide scale. We apply destination-specific ordered logistic regression models and negative-exponential impedance functions, with data from the Dutch National Travel Survey (n = 81,182) alongside a dataset of nationwide cumulative opportunity accessibility measures. Results show that household income, employment, car or E-bike availability, and frequency of biking and driving are associated with lower perceived inaccessibility. Conversely, migration background and use of public transport are associated with higher perceived inaccessibility. The study findings highlight the importance of incorporating people’s capabilities in transport policy to improve accessibility and overall wellbeing. Title: Neurodiversity and generative AI in higher education: A sequential multi-method qualitative study of students’ interactions, motivations, and strategies
Abstract: Neurodivergent students have been largely overlooked in research examining student experiences with generative AI (GenAI) in higher education, creating critical knowledge gaps about inclusive educational technology use. This sequential multi-method qualitative study examined how neurodivergent students (NDS) and neurotypical students (NTS) interact with and experience GenAI in academic contexts. Using a sequential design, we employed a virtual revisit think-aloud protocol with 24 university students (12 NDS, 12 NTS) completing an academic task using Microsoft Copilot, followed by focus groups with 14 participants (7 NDS, 7 NTS) to contextualise these task-based behaviours through broader GenAI perceptions. A neurodivergent research advisory board co-designed all procedures. Three themes emerged: approaching the task efficiently, evaluating and refining output, and maintaining academic integrity. While both groups demonstrated strategic GenAI use, neurodivergent participants in this sample explicitly described their cognitive processing needs, using GenAI to manage energy, and humanising some AI interactions. In the neurodivergent focus group, students described GenAI as essential scaffolding for managing academic demands, though this created complex tensions around authenticity and over-reliance. Interface design challenges seemed to particularly disadvantage users with executive function differences. As institutions rapidly integrate these technologies, inclusive design principles and empirical evidence regarding diverse student needs are essential to ensure equitable access to AI-supported education. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: EmoLoop: An adaptive VR biofeedback system for stress regulation
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: Virtual reality (VR) and biofeedback offer new opportunities for regulating affective states. This study investigated an adaptive VR-based biofeedback system that modulated participants’ field of view (FOV) based on breathing rate, embedded within a restorative, nature-based VR environment. Participants completed baseline and stress-inducing Stroop tasks, followed by a restorative VR session. Physiological responses (heart rate, electrodermal activity, breathing rate) and subjective stress ratings were recorded. The Stroop reliably induced stress, while the restorative VR environment reduced physiological arousal. While between-group differences did not reach statistical significance, the adaptive biofeedback group exhibited greater physiological reductions on average during VR exposure, alongside lower usability and higher anxiety. These findings highlight a central HCI challenge: adaptive physiological feedback can support stress regulation but may undermine usability if mechanisms are overly subtle or opaque. A methodological contribution of this work is error-triggered retraining strategies for stress classification models to address temporal drift in physiological signals. Error-triggered retraining analysis using live VR data demonstrated effective adaptation to physiological drift, establishing the foundation for online implementation during VR biofeedback. Overall, this study underscores both the promise and the challenges of integrating adaptive biofeedback and machine learning into VR. Future VR interventions should balance immersion with transparency and leverage adaptive ML to ensure personalization, usability, and sustained effectiveness in stress regulation. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: How Innovative Financial Technologies Can Foster Equity and Sustainability in Cities and Regions
Abstract: Fintech has become a powerful tool for cultivating equitable and sustainable development within cities and regions. One of the significant contributions of fintech lies in its ability to extend financial services to previously underserved populations, thereby narrowing the financial gap between different socio-economic groups. As financial exclusion has plagued societies for centuries, particularly in marginalised communities, fintech came with the potential to alleviate this problem by empowering individuals through innovative solutions. Moreover, by utilising data analytics and artificial intelligence, fintech can create tailored financial solutions for individuals with limited financial literacy, enabling them to make informed decisions and improve their financial status. While the potential benefits of fintech in creating equitable and sustainable cities and regions are vast, certain considerations should not be overlooked. Privacy and data protection concerns must be addressed to ensure users’ personal and financial information remains secure. This chapter aims to explore the diverse potential of these technologies in promoting equitable and sustainable development within cities and regions. By examining the crucial role of fintech in bridging financial gaps, promoting financial inclusion, and enhancing resource management, we can gain valuable insights into how these technologies can contribute to building more equitable and sustainable societies. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: Regional place attachment and meat reduction: The role of perceived availability of traditional vegetarian meals and attachment to culinary traditions
Abstract: Meat consumption is among the most environmentally impactful human activities. Therefore, reducing meat intake represents a crucial step in addressing climate change. While researchers increasingly recognize that meat consumption is influenced by individual, environmental, and socio-cultural factors, the latter remain underexplored. The present study examined the association between regional place attachment and intentions to reduce meat consumption, focusing on the mediating roles of perceived availability of vegetarian dishes at the regional level and attachment to regional culinary traditions. The proposed model was tested using path analysis on a representative sample of 4066 Italian individuals (Mage = 51.05, SDage = 16.57, range = 18-89, 51.50% women). Although regional place attachment was not directly associated with intentions to reduce meat consumption, the mediation analyses revealed two indirect effects operating in opposite directions. Regional place attachment was linked to a greater intention to reduce meat-based dishes through the perceived regional availability of vegetarian options. At the same time, regional place attachment was associated with stronger attachment to regional culinary traditions, which in turn was linked to a lower intention to adopt a sustainable diet. Overall, these findings underscored the complex role of regional place attachment in shaping intentions to reduce meat consumption and pointed to potential avenues for innovative, community-based interventions. © 2026 The Authors. Title: What determines the adoption of space cooling technology in households? Evidence from regions in Belgium and Poland
Abstract: Frequent heatwaves are common, especially during the climate crisis. Hence, the topic of mitigating the impact of hot summer days is attracting increasing attention, and the demand for cooling solutions is rising. This research aims to identify and assess the factors that individuals in the Antwerp Province of Belgium and the Kuyavian-Pomeranian Voivodeship of Poland might consider when adopting a cooling solution. These regions are experiencing heatwaves during the summer, which are becoming more frequent, intense, and prolonged due to climate change. These two regions are characterized by similar population sizes (∼2 million) but differ in climate, urbanization, and economic roles, making them suitable for comparative analysis. This study employs a discrete choice experiment to examine households' preferences for cooling options, considering the following characteristics: thermal comfort, air quality, sound level, environmental impact, lifespan, and cost. The results indicate that in the Polish region, which is in a more extreme climate zone, households are much more willing to invest in cooling technology than those living in Antwerp Province, which has a milder climate. The Willingness-to-Pay analysis revealed that reduced noise is the most valuable feature of household cooling solutions in the Belgium region, which is much more densely populated. The air quality improvement feature is most valued in areas where people perceive poor air quality. The study suggests that the business sector should design cooling devices to be silent and more environmentally friendly, and that policymakers should make cooling systems more affordable and accessible. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Exploring the micro-foundations of local green co-creation: challenging the myth of a Global North-Global South divide?
Abstract: Scholars are displaying increasing interest in how to ensure the success of co-creation efforts intended to foster green solutions. Authors: Ziegert R.F.
Title: When governments shift, do policies follow?Tracing policy change in Brazil's land use regulatory framework
Abstract: Land degradation and native vegetation loss in Brazil have persisted despite a comprehensive land use regulatory framework. This study examines how Brazilian federal land use policies changed between 2000 and 2025 and how these changes relate to institutional government change. Drawing on historical institutionalism, qualitative policy analysis, and process tracing, the research analyzes 239 laws and decrees across eight environmental and agricultural policies over eight administrations. The findings show that policy goals persisted across governments, while rules, instruments, budgets, and institutional capacities shifted. Two critical junctures, Dilma Rousseff's impeachment in 2015 and the start of Bolsonaro's presidency in 2019, coincided with environmental policy replacement, institutional dismantling, and weakened enforcement. However, prior layering and conversion of environmental policies created resilience, enabling institutional recovery under Lula's third administration beginning in 2023. Agricultural policies exhibited greater stability, reflecting entrenched economic and political coalitions. Linking policy change processes to vegetation loss data shows that periods of weakened implementation were associated with increased vegetation loss, whereas restored institutional coordination was associated with reduced deforestation. Targeted strategies, especially the Action Plans for the Prevention and Control of Deforestation, were highly effective when supported by institutional capacity. This study calls for greater integration between agricultural and environmental policies, using cross-compliant financial and technical instruments to combat land use change driving vegetation loss, matched with continued whole-territory monitoring and targeted actions across biomes. The findings underscore the critical role of stable interministerial coordination and long-term institutional foundations in sustaining conservation policy amid political volatility. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Conditional Cash Transfer and Food Insecurity: Evidence from Low-Income Households With Children in Indonesia

Title: Network members can hide from group centrality measures
Abstract: Group centrality measures assess the relative importance of a set of nodes within a network. In many settings, certain groups may have a strong incentive to evade such analysis—either to avoid detection, obscure their role, or limit exposure. While evasion has been studied in the context of individual centrality, no prior work has investigated how groups might strategically rewire a network to minimize their group centrality. In this work, we address this gap by analyzing the computational aspects of hiding from three fundamental group centrality measures, namely degree, closeness, and betweenness. We show that the problem of finding an optimal rewiring strategy can be solved in polynomial time for degree group centrality, but is NP-complete for closeness and betweenness group centrality measures. Furthermore, we provide a mixed-integer linear program for computing an optimal hiding strategy against closeness group centrality in networks of moderate size. We complement our theoretical findings with an extensive empirical evaluation comparing optimal and heuristic strategies across various network topologies and evader distributions. Our results demonstrate that evasion is often possible even when the evading group has access only to information about its immediate network neighborhood, and that certain heuristics perform consistently well across a range of scenarios. This work provides a foundation for understanding and mitigating the risks posed by groups seeking to conceal their centrality in complex networks. Title: Suicidality profiles among Korean adults: Ideation recency, lifetime behavioral history, and current psychiatric morbidity
Abstract: Lifetime suicidal ideation encompasses different combinations of recent thoughts and behavioral history. We examined suicidality profiles and their psychiatric and psychosocial correlates in the 2021 National Mental Health Survey of Korea ( N = 5511). Among 574 lifetime ideators, latent class analysis used five binary indicators: past-year ideation, current ideation, lifetime plan, lifetime attempt, and lifetime nonsuicidal self-injury. Class differences in psychiatric and psychosocial characteristics were examined using survey-design-based analyses, with classification-error correction for continuous outcomes. Three profiles were retained: remote ideation with limited behavioral history (78.0%), lifetime plan and attempt with low current ideation (15.3%), and current ideation with intermediate lifetime planning (6.7%; modal n = 32). BCH-corrected mean counts of positive 12-month diagnostic indicators were 0.20, 0.35, and 0.92 (omnibus P = 0.024); the current-ideation class exceeded the remote-ideation class (adjusted P = 0.039; d = 0.91). Resilience and loneliness also differed overall across profiles, whereas life satisfaction did not. These profiles suggest that ideation recency and lifetime behavioral history provide complementary clinical information among adults with lifetime suicidal ideation. Separate assessment of current suicidal thoughts and lifetime behavioral history may therefore improve clinical characterization. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Fractured consent and disrupted desires: Decoding the representational politics of marital rape and cohabitant sexual abuse in Malayalam Cinema from India
Abstract: While marital rape has been a subject of legal dispute in Indian society, non-consensual sexual abuse within a cohabiting relationship also makes the issue complex and debatable. This research examines marital rape and cohabitant partner rape of females in Kerala, India, and their representation in Malayalam cinema. Any non-consensual sexual acts committed by an intimate partner or spouse cause psychological and physical harm and trauma to the survivor. Title: Teachers learning to guide classroom discussions on controversial issues: a study of a professional development program
Abstract: Classroom discussions on controversial issues are widely regarded as an essential part of democratic citizenship education, yet there is limited knowledge about how teachers can be supported in facilitating them. This study evaluates a professional development program (PDP) aimed at supporting in-service teachers in guiding classroom discussions on controversial issues. The program involved peer-coaching sessions where teachers experimented with discussion strategies and reflected on their experiences. The study adopted a mixed-methods design, combining a quasi-experimental study (N = 54) to assess effects on teachers’ self-efficacy regarding an open and safe classroom climate, co-construction, and content quality, with stimulated recall interviews (N = 8) to explore how teachers experienced the PDP and applied it in their classroom practice. The results showed that participation in the PDP was associated with significantly greater growth in teachers’ self-efficacy for supporting an open and safe classroom climate and co-construction, compared to a control group. No significant effects were found for teacher self-efficacy with respect to promoting content quality. The qualitative findings mirrored these results and provided further insight into teachers’ perceptions of how the PDP supported their approaches to classroom discussions, while also highlighting persistent challenges, particularly in balancing neutrality with normative guidance during discussions. Authors: Yu K.; Wang X.; Shi Y.
Title: The major transfer decision-making process among nursing undergraduates: A grounded theory
Abstract: Background: The global nursing workforce faces a projected shortage of 4.5 million by 2030, exacerbated by high attrition rates among nursing undergraduates transferring to other majors. Studies indicate that 76.7% consider transferring upon enrollment, and 23.3% ultimately do so. Existing research tends to treat this decision as a static outcome, with limited attention to the process by which it unfolds. Objective: To develop a theory explaining the process through which nursing undergraduates navigate the decision of whether to transfer out of their major. Design: Constructivist grounded theory. Participants: Twenty-seven nursing undergraduates from three Chinese universities who had considered or had already transferred to a non-nursing major. Methods: Purposive and theoretical sampling were used. Data were collected through semi-structured remote interviews and analyzed using constant comparative methods, focusing on processes, meanings, and psychosocial interactions shaping participants' decision journeys. Results: Analysis produced the Dynamic Deliberation Process Model of Nursing Major Transfer Decision, comprising four stages: intention formation, intention latency, intention weighing, and decision execution. The process is driven by interplay among triggering, underlying, inhibiting, and promoting factors. The outcome, whether a student transfers, abandons the intention, or remains in active retention, passive retention, or postponement, reflects ongoing negotiation among these factors throughout the decision journey. Conclusion: The major transfer decision is a protracted psychosocial process. Findings advocate shifting from reactive, generalized support to proactive, stage-specific interventions. By identifying signs of each phase and understanding underlying factor dynamics, educators can transition from gatekeeping to navigating students' decision processes. They can foster professional identity early, provide emotionally aware counseling during conflict, and ensure supportive pathways for all outcomes. © 2026

Title: End of life legislation and implementation for the recycling and reuse of solar e-waste, Kenya
Abstract: Solar energy is critical for achieving universal, affordable energy access. As solar energy becomes increasingly popular across the world, with uptake in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) growing significantly in recent years, how to deal with the waste from these products and systems is of high importance, to avoid an e-waste crisis. However, legislation and infrastructure tackling the end of life of solar e-waste is insufficient, especially in SSA. This paper addresses this limitation and argues for stronger legislation and implementation of end of life management. Title: Exploring the relationships of eWOM with distance and traditional attractiveness: evidence from Shanghai
Abstract: In retail geography, the mechanisms through which traditional attractiveness influences shopping mall visitation have been widely studied. However, how the online attractiveness represented by electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) affects visitation, and how this effect varies with distance and traditional attractiveness, remain unclear. Using suburban shopping malls in Shanghai as the case, this study draws on online review data and visitors’ location-based services (LBS) data and applies principal component analysis (PCA), negative binomial regression, and mixed-effects negative binomial regression with natural spline functions to address these gaps. The results show, first, that eWOM provides explanatory power for shopping mall visitation beyond that offered by traditional attractiveness and significantly increases visitation. Second, the relationship between eWOM attractiveness and visitation distance is significantly nonlinear, rising sharply at first and then declining gradually. Finally, the traditional attractiveness of shopping malls does not significantly moderate the attractiveness of eWOM to visitation. This study reveals the mechanism through which online attractiveness, represented by eWOM, influences shopping mall visitation. The findings offer insights for refining retail gravity mechanisms and provide practical implications for shopping mall operators and urban planning authorities. © 2026 Hong Kong Society for Transportation Studies

Title: Expected foreign military intervention and demand for state-building: Evidence from Mali
Abstract: We study how the announcement of a foreign military intervention, which improves expectations about the state's future functioning, can raise citizens’ willingness to participate in state-building processes. We analyze the impact of the 2012 United Nations Security Council resolution that authorized intervention in Mali to reunify the country and restore democracy during a profound institutional crisis on individuals’ attitudes toward the state. Consistent with a prospective-beliefs channel, respondents interviewed after the announcement report higher tax morale and more favorable tax-related attitudes across a broad range of outcomes. While optimism about future democracy increases widely, the increase in tax morale appears concentrated in areas with low state capacity, limited ethnic diversity, and individuals who do not perceive discrimination against their ethnic group. Title: Resilience and Adaptability to Climate Challenges in Cold Desert of Ladakh (India)
Abstract: The Ladakh region faces escalating socioeconomic and environmental challenges due to climate change, increasing the vulnerability of local communities to risks such as water scarcity and glacial retreat. These changes exacerbate the region’s susceptibility to extreme weather events, necessitating urgent adaptation strategies to ensure sustainable livelihoods and environmental resilience. Unregulated grazing and the introduction of exotic species have accelerated pasture degradation, with Changthang’s rangelands experiencing overstocking, leading to forage competition. This has prompted nomadic communities to migrate in search of better adaptation measures. Title: From collaborative evidence generation to trustworthy detection: A foundation model-based framework for medical misinformation verification
Abstract: Medical misinformation propagates rapidly across digital platforms, posing substantial risks to public health decision-making. Traditional content-based detection approaches exhibit limited effectiveness when confronting the nuanced language and domain-specific terminology inherent in health-related claims. While foundation language models demonstrate remarkable semantic understanding capabilities, their direct application to medical misinformation detection encounters two fundamental obstacles: hallucination-induced evidence unreliability and insufficient explainability in high-stakes health contexts. Rather than treating foundation models as monolithic end-to-end predictors, we reconceptualize them as modular evidence generators and verifiers within a collaborative reasoning architecture. We propose Medical misinformation GUard via multi-model Adversarial Reasoning and Dimensional evidence (MedGUARD), a two-stage framework that leverages foundation model collaboration for explainable detection. The evidence generation stage employs adaptive in-context learning and multi-model adversarial negotiation to synthesize reliable multidimensional evidence, effectively mitigating hallucination artifacts. The semantic fusion stage integrates claim representations with evidence-augmented features through multimodal factorized bilinear pooling. Experiments across four medical misinformation benchmarks demonstrate that MedGUARD achieves improvements of 3.2 to 4.5 F1 points over 25 baseline methods, with all advantages confirmed by McNemar’s significance test. Adversarial negotiation reduces hallucination rates by 66% to 70% while generating transparent reasoning trails across seven evidential dimensions. Authors: Yu Q.; Li S.
Title: When physical activity becomes a personal choice: How psychological ownership in physical activity motivates sustained participation among college students
Abstract: College students’ participation in physical activity is often unstable and interrupted. Existing research has mainly explained this through motivation, autonomy, or exercise identity, but has paid less attention to why individuals experience exercise as their own activity. This study introduces psychological ownership as a complementary perspective and examines whether it is associated with autonomous choice, personal investment, and self connection, and whether it is related to sustained exercise intention through agency and affective commitment. Study 1 (N = 350) showed that autonomous choice and personal investment were positively associated with psychological ownership, whereas self connection was not significant in the natural setting. Study 2 (N = 209) provided experimental support for the proposed antecedent pathways, showing that self connection also increased psychological ownership under isolated experimental manipulation. Study 3 (N = 228) showed that psychological ownership was prospectively associated with later exercise intention and record-verified exercise behavior, with a small but significant indirect association through affective commitment. Taken together, the findings provide a psychological ownership perspective on the early development of sustained exercise participation and suggest that decision involvement, personal investment, and longer term relational support may be relevant for promoting more stable exercise participation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Measuring the influence of stress on eating: Taking stock of the Salzburg Stress Eating Scale
Abstract: The Salzburg Stress Eating Scale (SSES) was developed in 2018 to measure stress-related changes in food intake. The questionnaire consists of 10 items that depict stressful situations and responses are recorded on a five-point scale ranging from 1 = I eat much less than usual to 5 = I eat much more than usual (with the middle of the scale indicating no change in food intake when being stressed). In this narrative review, we provide an overview of studies that have used the SSES thus far, which includes a description of adaptations of the SSES (e.g., translations into other languages and versions for other health-related behaviors) and its psychometric properties. Findings generally support reliability and validity of the SSES in multiple languages. However, whether the SSES exhibits predictive validity (i.e., accurate prediction of naturalistic and experimental data) remains an open question for future research, as findings of naturalistic studies have been mixed and laboratory studies are absent. Future avenues include developing alternative scoring procedures, combining the scale with adapted versions for other health behaviors—such as alcohol consumption, smoking, and physical activity—and promoting its use in trans-cultural, longitudinal, and clinical studies. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Mapping the longevity horizon: a 5-wave random-intercept cross-lagged panel analysis of subjective life expectancy, depressive symptoms, functional disability, exercise frequency, and skipped meals in an aging population in Thailand
Abstract: Objectives: To examine within-person longitudinal pathways linking Subjective Life Expectancy (SLE) with depressive symptoms, Activities of Daily Living (ADL) limitations, exercise frequency, and skipped meals in ageing adults in Thailand. Methods: Longitudinal data from 5259 older adults across five biennial waves (2015–2024) of the HART study were analyzed using a joint multivariate latent Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model (RI-CLPM). Robust maximum likelihood estimation was used to account for non-normality, while longitudinally metric-invariant latent item parcels represented depressive symptoms. Measurement error for the single-item SLE indicator was incorporated using an established reliability estimate (α = 0.80). Continuous-time scaling was applied to account for unequal wave spacing. Inverse Probability of Attrition Weighting (IPAW) was used as a sensitivity analysis for potential attrition-related bias. Results: Model fit was generally acceptable to excellent (robust RMSEA ≤0.051; SRMR ≤0.102). At the within-person level, increases in depressive symptoms consistently predicted subsequent declines in SLE (B = −0.336, SE = 0.055, z = −6.152, p < 0.001). Title: Braking or accelerating? Conditional associations of rural educational and public transport facilities with village courtyard vacancy
Abstract: Rural educational facilities are becoming concentrated in central places while public transport facilities continue to extend into villages. These facilities serve different functions, making their joint configuration central to understanding village courtyard vacancy. Using survey data from villages in Xintai, Shandong Province, with 415 villages in the regression sample, this study measures educational-facility conditions through the presence and accessibility of primary schools and kindergartens and public transport provision through bus-stop presence. Beta regressions, joint-configuration models, population-status models, historical information, spatial models, and multiple-imputation analysis provide mutually reinforcing evidence. Our findings show: (1) The absence and lower accessibility of primary schools and kindergartens are associated with higher courtyard vacancy rates; lower primary-school accessibility also corresponds to more out-migrants and fewer in-migrants. (2) Bus-stop presence is generally associated with lower vacancy, mainly through its association with fewer out-migrants, but its residential association varies with primary-school configuration. Configurations that include a primary school show the most stable association with low vacancy. (3) Greater village-level private-car ownership weakens the positive association between primary-school absence and courtyard vacancy. The results identify service function as the missing link between facility supply and residential outcomes. Title: Brain network localization of delusions
Abstract: Background Delusions constitute a cross-diagnostic core symptom of schizophrenia spectrum disorders and correlate with poor functional outcomes. Despite much recent effort successfully mapping neuropsychiatric symptoms to specific brain networks, investigations focusing on network localization of delusions are still scarce. Methods We initially conducted a systematic review of 44 published neuroimaging studies to identify brain regions exhibiting structural and functional alterations associated with delusions. By applying functional connectivity network mapping to normative functional connectomes derived from two independent resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging datasets, we mapped these affected brain regions to three delusion networks. Results The delusion morphology and task-induced activation abnormality networks were both broadly distributed and had some spatial similarities. In addition to their shared spatial overlap with the ventral attention and somatomotor networks, the delusion morphology abnormality network showed greater spatial overlap with the frontoparietal and dorsal attention networks, while the task-induced activation abnormality network overlapped more extensively with the subcortical and limbic networks. Concurrently, the delusion resting-state activity abnormality network showed the greatest spatial overlap with the default network. In addition, the right opercular part of the inferior frontal gyrus, the right anterior agranular insula complex, and the right anterior portion of the superior temporal gyrus exhibited functional connectivity profiles with the highest spatial similarity to these delusion network probability maps and were therefore considered potential neuromodulation targets. Conclusions Aside from elucidating the neurobiological mechanism underlying delusions from a network perspective, our findings potentially inform the development of reliable biomarkers and targeted treatments for delusions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: A Spatially Weighted Relative Deprivation Index: Incorporating Spatial Structure Into Regional Inequality Measurement
Abstract: Regional inequality is conventionally assessed based on the distribution of economic outcomes across regions. However, regional disparities are spatially structured because regional economic outcomes are interdependent across space. Existing approaches generally capture either the spatial dimension of inequality at an aggregate level or unit-specific disadvantage without incorporating spatial relevance. This study proposes a Spatially Weighted Relative Deprivation (SWRD) index that combines the one-sided upward-gap rule of relative deprivation (RD) with an empirically calibrated spatial weighting structure. Using real gross regional domestic product (GRDP) for 229 Korean districts from 2015 to 2021, the study estimates the distance decay of spatial dependence and constructs annual SWRD values. The empirical comparison shows that SWRD produces spatial patterns and regional rankings that differ from conventional RD. Spatial permutation tests indicate that high SWRD values are unlikely under random spatial reassignment. Monte Carlo simulations on a uniform lattice further show that the divergence between RD and SWRD increases with stronger spatial dependence, steeper distance decay, and greater dispersion and right skewness. These findings show that incorporating spatial structure can change assessments of regional disadvantage under varying spatial and distributional conditions. © 2026 The Ohio State University.

Title: Factors associated with patient safety competency and configurational pathways among master's nursing students: A cross-sectional study using PLS-SEM, NCA, and fsQCA
Abstract: Aim: To examine the associations of organizational support (OS), patient safety culture (PSCul), adverse event risk perception (AERP), self-efficacy (SE) and professional identity (PI) with self-reported patient safety competency (PSC) among master's nursing students, and to investigate the corresponding indirect associations, necessary-condition constraints and configurational pathways. Design: A cross-sectional online survey. Setting: Multiple regions of China. Participants: A total of 326 master's nursing students with at least 3 months of clinical practice experience. Methods: Data were collected from June 2025 to February 2026 using convenience and snowball sampling. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was used to estimate the direct and indirect associations between the study factors and PSC. Necessary condition analysis (NCA) was used to evaluate the necessary-condition constraints for attaining higher levels of PSC, whereas fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) was used to identify configurations associated with high and non-high PSC. Results: OS, PSCul, AERP, SE and PI were each positively associated with PSC (β = 0.110–0.344, all P ≤ 0.005). OS, PSCul and AERP were also significantly associated with PSC indirectly through SE and PI (β = 0.040–0.104, all P ≤ 0.003). The structural model accounted for 59.2% of the variance in PSC. NCA showed that each antecedent represented a statistically significant necessary constraint (d = 0.105–0.246, P < 0.001). fsQCA identified four configurations associated with high PSC (solution consistency = 0.917; solution coverage = 0.648), with SE present as a core condition in all four configurations. Four distinct configurations were associated with non-high PSC (solution consistency = 0.888; solution coverage = 0.736), indicating configurational asymmetry. Conclusions: PSC among master's nursing students was associated with organizational and individual psychological factors through multiple, asymmetric pathways. Nursing educators and clinical preceptors may combine supportive learning environments and a positive patient safety culture with efforts to strengthen SE, PI and AERP. However, given the cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported data, these findings require further verification in longitudinal studies using multisource assessments. © 2026 Churchill Livingstone

Title: Evaluating the reliability of collaborative problem solving performance among Chilean students: A Generalizability Study
Abstract: Drawing on Generalizability Theory, the study examines how communication, creativity, as well as critical thinking manifest in students’ problem solving processes, and how these skills can be consistently captured in performance-based assessment. Title: Simulation-based training for child helpline counsellors: Impact of simulation, feedback, and reflection in a randomised controlled trial

Abstract: Child helplines require well-trained counsellors to support children in need. Such training typically involves role-playing, which is effective but costly and difficult to organise at scale. A promising addition, therefore, is simulation-based training, where trainees interact with a conversational agent that mimics a child contacting the helpline. However, interacting with a simulation alone may not be sufficient, as augmenting it with feedback and reflection can provide more guided learning. The learning effects of sequentially adding these elements—simulation, feedback, and reflection—to training systems are not yet fully understood. Participants interacted with the interventions in five sessions over fourteen days. Compared with the no-intervention condition, simulation training improved participants’ task knowledge and reflective-writing capability. Adding feedback led to further gains in knowledge and conversational outcomes (performance). Title: Consumer reactions to AI enabled surveillance of drivers. the case of Pay-how-you-drive insurance products

Following Holland and John (2023), we use the term AI-enabled to refer to the ensemble of machine learning techniques that are at the heart of the HUK-COBURG scoring pipeline. Title: Assessing the triple effects of artificial intelligence at the corporate level in China: New insights from productive efficiency, salary gap, and financial risk
Abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) integrates into China's corporate sector, it significantly transforms operational paradigms. While existing studies have explored the individual impacts of AI on productive efficiency, salary gap, and financial risk, how AI simultaneously affects these three dimensions in an integrated manner remains insufficiently understood. Title: Land Triadic Nexus: A conceptual framework for land governance through the strategic adaptive alignment of land use, rights, and values
Abstract: Land governance persistently fails to achieve its stated objectives, producing unintended outcomes, coordination failures, and inequality. This paper argues that a major reason is the treatment of land use, land rights, and land value as parallel administrative domains rather than as mutually constitutive components of one recursive governance structure. The Land Triadic Nexus, developed here, explains governance outcomes as a function of the degree of alignment among these three domains. The framework is constructed through a targeted review of existing land governance frameworks, from which four theoretical foundations are developed and four propositions derived. Three foundations are analytical, drawing on institutional economics and property rights theory, game theory, and adaptive governance theory. The fourth is normative, grounded in political philosophy and critical land studies, and establishes land as a shared trust defining what alignment is for. Together these traditions yield three claims. Configurations of land use, rights, and value are strategically produced and defended by actors. Alignment among the three domains is the condition under which planning interventions achieve their intended outcomes. And land governance is an ongoing institutional search for better alignment, constrained by path dependence, capture, and culturally institutionalised models of governance. The propositions are conjectures rather than validated findings, and define the empirical agenda of the research programme the paper opens. Title: From text to development outcomes: China's fisheries policy text intensity from 1986 to 2024
Abstract: The Chinese government has issued a series of economic development and resource conservation policies for fisheries since it implemented the Fisheries Law in 1986. However, quantitative research on China's fisheries based on policy texts remains limited. Therefore, this study evaluates 657 central-level policy documents issued between 1986 and 2024 based on criteria developed across three dimensions: policy hierarchies, policy objectives, and policy measures. We assess the documents' text intensity and use a ridge regression model to explore the associations between policy text intensity and economic and environmental outcomes. The analysis reveals that China's fisheries policy system has evolved through four stages, shifting from supply expansion to an orientation toward ecological quality. Changes in policy instruments reflect adjustments in strategic priorities in response to external constraints. The ridge regression results indicate that policy text intensity is positively associated with economic growth, whereas text intensity for policies on technological innovation and regulation is negatively associated with carbon emissions intensity. These findings align with the Chinese government's efforts to promote economic development and environmental protection for fisheries. The study's results provide practical insights useful for optimizing policy mixes and building a sustainable fisheries governance system. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Unveiling the core factors of internet addiction in adolescents: A machine learning and network analysis approach
Abstract: The high prevalence and detrimental effects of internet addiction among adolescents have led to a growing research focus on this mental health issue. To more comprehensively identify its risk factors and explore their interrelationships, this study employed machine learning and network analysis to investigate the development of internet addiction and potential associated factors. Candidate variables were selected based on the I-PACE model, and surveys were conducted among 3380 Chinese secondary school students (50.2% male; Mage = 13.96, SD = 1.31). After data collection, Latent Profile Analysis was performed to categorize internet addiction profiles. Subsequently, the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithm was applied to predict the LPA outcomes, with the top 15 most influential features selected from an initial set of 28. Finally, a Mixed Graphical Model was employed to construct and visualize the interrelationships among these 15 influential predictors. The XGBoost model demonstrated good predictive performance (AUC = 0.86). Among the top 15 features, depression ranked first, indicating the strongest predictive power for internet addiction. Network analysis further revealed that the Behavioral Inhibition System (BIS) was the most central node in the network, positively correlated with intolerance of uncertainty, and rumination. Authors: Njenga M.
Title: Clean cooking stacking: A stark reality for a just energy transition
Abstract: During two decades of my research and development in bioenergy systems I have come to understand the importance of how people are mixing, matching and improvising to meet their cooking energy needs. By layering and/or stacking energy strategies, people use their ingenuity to take what is also a pragmatic approach to “clean cooking”. These energy strategies involve choosing fuels such as woodfuel (charcoal and firewood/fuelwood), briquettes, kerosene, liquid petroleum gas (LPG), biogas, and electricity based upon their values, constraints, and local realities. Household budgets, appliance availability and the rhythm of daily life all shape whether an induction stove or an electric pressure cooker becomes a staple or a distant dream. Using scientific evidence and lived experiences, this publication shares examples of cooking energy stacking in different contexts. It presents arguments for a paradigm shift to cleaning the stack and a move away from the denialist view of funders, private investors, development agents, policy makers and researchers that energy stacking stands in the way of a clean cooking transition. This new view emphasizes that failure to improve the traditional methods that persist in the stacking undermines the health and environmental benefits of a clean cooking transition. It presents lessons about how to achieve a just and inclusive transition to clean cooking stacking that will support governments' policy making and implementation plans toward meeting multiple sustainable development goals. © 2026

Title: When place becomes a brand: Creating values and benefits for rural people and places in a whisky region
Abstract: As rural development becomes increasingly shaped by industries that draw on place-based identities, cultures, and environments, understanding how their benefits are distributed within host communities is increasingly important. This paper examines the interconnected whisky and food-and-drink tourism sectors in Speyside, Scotland, where both industries derive value from the symbolic and material qualities of place. In such contexts, place itself becomes part of the product, forming what we conceptualise as a brandscape. We argue that a mismatch can emerge between the value extracted from rural places through branding, production, and tourism, and the benefits retained within those places. To explore this issue, we combine value chain analysis with a brandscape perspective to develop a new conceptual framework for understanding the relationships between large rural industries, communities, and place. Drawing on multiple sources of qualitative data, we examine the economic, socio-cultural, and environmental values and benefits associated with the interconnected whisky and tourism sectors in Speyside. Our findings demonstrate that while these industries generate substantial benefits for the region, the distribution of those benefits is uneven and does not always reflect the contributions made by local communities and environments. We therefore argue for a more reciprocal relationship between industry, community, and place, in which the value generated through place-based branding is more effectively retained within rural areas. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Volumetric Waste: Containing Polymorphous Plastic in Bangkok’s Circular Economies
Abstract: This paper examines how volumetric reasoning permeates everyday practices in Bangkok’s circular economies. While circular economies calculate, value, and contain plastic waste, mobile waste flows are hidden from view and often evade regulation. As a result, circular economy initiatives struggle to account for low-value waste, microplastics, and chemicals that proliferate through land, water, air, and blood in bodies. In these instances, waste travels and transforms volumetrically without a traceable latitude and longitude. Similarly, the actual dimensions of plastic objects impact their ability to be valued in the circular economy. Drawing on seventeen months of ethnographic fieldwork in Bangkok, Thailand, this paper documents how circular economy practitioners manage waste that takes on new materialities as it moves through plastic circularity loops. Nonstate waste practitioners invoke volumetric reasoning as they grapple with circular economy solutions (e.g., recovering, repurposing, and upcycling plastics). My argument is twofold: first, I argue that practitioners’ everyday volumetric practices expose the limits of formal circular economy policy. Second, I argue that volumetric reasoning gives practitioners a set of techniques for reclaiming agency over the everyday management of waste. By attending to commonplace yet novel spatial dimensions of plastic circularity, this paper contributes to emerging scholarship at the intersection of political ecology and volumetric analyses of plastic pollution in Asia. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: The NU-HOME RCT home food environment, family meal frequency, meal quality and children's dietary intake and physical activity outcomes
Abstract: Introduction: The assessment of secondary outcomes in childhood obesity RCTs is important to understand programmatic impacts and precursors to weight-related changes. Study design: RCT. Baseline and post-intervention (9 months, 86% retention) data were collected (2017-2019) and analyzed (2022) for 114 7-10-year-old participants in the New Ulm at HOME (NU-HOME) study, which aimed to prevent obesity in rural children. The NU-HOME intervention engaged whole families in 7 monthly in-person, interactive sessions promoting healthful home food environments (i.e., frequent family meals, home availability of fruits and vegetables (FV), high quality of foods served at meals), children's dietary intake (i.e., diet quality via HEI and FV and low SSB intake), and children's physical activity (PA; i.e., moderate-to-vigorous PA (MVPA) and reduced screen time). Main Outcome Measures: Family home food environment; child dietary intake and PA outcomes. Results: Compared to families in the wait-list control group, families in the intervention group showed significantly greater improvement in the availability of vegetables in the home (p < .05) and the quality of foods and beverages served at the evening meal (p < .05). Although not statistically significant (p = .07), children in the intervention group demonstrated a 1/3 cup increase in fruit consumption compared to children in the control group, a clinically meaningful outcome. No significant treatment group differences were seen for family meal frequency, home availability of fruit, intake of vegetables, SSB intake, or minutes of MVPA and screen time. Title: On-road driving performance in older drivers with subjective memory concerns
Abstract: Introduction Cross-sectional studies have reported associations between subjective memory concerns (SMC) and self-reported crashes in older drivers; however, the effect of SMC on driving performance remains unknown. The aim of this study was to explore the differences in on-road driving performance characteristics (error types and context of errors) by the severity of SMC among older drivers. Method This study used a cross-sectional dataset of 277 non-demented current older drivers (age, 75.7 ± 6.1 years; 40.8% female; and years of education, 15.7 ± 3.9) recruited through the community and primary and tertiary care clinics in Canberra, Australia. An on-road driving test along a 20 km route by a driver-trained occupational therapist assessed error types (such as observation and lane position) and traffic contexts of errors (such as roundabout and straight driving). SMC was scored using a Memory Complaint Questionnaire (MAC-Q). Results For error types, multiple regression analysis showed no linear associations with MAC-Q score were found. For traffic context, in exploratory analysis by multivariate analysis of covariance considering each question separately, there was a significantly higher percentage of reversing errors in those who perceived their memory as poorer compared to their high school age than those who perceived as the same or better memory, even after Bonferroni adjustment within the question's domain; however, this was a hypothesis-generating finding (adjusted mean difference [95% confidence interval] = 20.0% [6.6% to 33.4%], P = 0.004). Conclusions SMC assessed using MAC-Q had no statistically significant associations with poorer driving performance across a range of measures. An exploratory MAC-Q item-level analysis identified a possible association between SMC and more errors on the reversing task. Practical applications These findings may help guide future research examining the relationship between SMC and driving performance. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A nurse-guided ChatGPT-assisted dietary learning program and self-efficacy for avoiding high-phosphorus foods in peritoneal dialysis patients
Abstract: Objective: To examine longitudinal changes in self-efficacy for avoiding high‑phosphorus foods (SE-AHPF) before and after a nurse-guided ChatGPT-assisted dietary learning program among peritoneal dialysis (PD) patients and the associations of health learning intention (HLI) and ChatGPT-assisted phosphorus-related information-seeking behavior (CPISB) with subsequent SE-AHPF. Methods: In this prospective longitudinal study, 85 PD patients were assessed for SE-AHPF at T1 (June 2024), T2 (January 2025), and T3 (September 2025). A 3-month nurse-guided ChatGPT-assisted dietary learning program involving reminders, ChatGPT-assisted dietary information seeking, and nurse feedback was conducted between T2 and T3. HLI and CPISB were assessed before T3. Longitudinal changes in SE-AHPF and the associations among HLI, CPISB, and subsequent T3 SE-AHPF were examined. Results: SE-AHPF increased significantly over time, with higher scores at T3 than at T1 and T2 (both ps < 0.001, ηp2 = 0.76). Higher HLI was associated with higher CPISB (β = 0.56, p < .001). Higher CPISB was associated with higher subsequent T3 SE-AHPF after adjustment for demographic characteristics, serum phosphorus levels, T2 SE-AHPF, and HLI (β = 0.51, p < .001). Authors: Korsgaard S.; Thrane C.
Title: Entrepreneurial agency in mission oriented innovation policies
Abstract: Policy makers have recently turned to mission-oriented innovation policies (MOIPs) to direct entrepreneurial activity towards societal goals. Yet, while entrepreneurial experimentation is a key component of missions, there has been limited exchange between the MOIP literature and recent entrepreneurship research, leaving the theoretical foundations of entrepreneurial agency in missions underdeveloped. To address this, we draw on current debates in entrepreneurship research to articulate two distinct views of entrepreneurship, a discovery view and an expanded view. Both perspectives can be useful for MOIPs, although an expansive view stands out in its ability to provide an account of how entrepreneurship can contribute to advancing fully the transformative potential of missions through reflexive revision of problem-solution spaces and resource structures. Conceptual and practical implications are outlined and discussed emphasising the need for experimentation with new governance structures and instruments to leverage entrepreneurship in MOIPs. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Independent and joint predictive value of Lipid Accumulation Product and estimated Pulse Wave Velocity for incident depressive symptoms: Evidence from CHARLS
Abstract: Background Depression is a major public health concern worldwide, associated with considerable emotional, social, and economic burdens. Emerging evidence suggests that metabolic dysfunction and vascular aging may contribute to the pathogenesis of depression. However, large-scale population studies examining these associations remain limited. Objective To investigate the associations of Lipid Accumulation Product (LAP) and estimated Pulse Wave Velocity (ePWV)-markers of metabolic and vascular health-with incident depressive symptoms among Chinese adults. Methods Data were obtained from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS, 2011–2020). A total of 5216 participants aged ≥45 years without depression at baseline were included. LAP and ePWV were calculated using standard formulas. Incident depressive symptoms were assessed using the CES-D-10 (score ≥ 10). Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals across progressively adjusted models. Dose–response relationships were examined using restricted cubic spline models, and subgroup analyses were conducted to assess potential effect modification. Receiver operating characteristic curves were used to evaluate predictive performance. Results During follow-up, 1927 participants developed incident depressive symptoms. Higher levels of both LAP and ePWV were significantly associated with increased depression risk. In fully adjusted models, LAP was positively associated with incident depressive symptoms (HR = 1.04, 95% CI 1.03–1.05), while ePWV showed a stronger association (HR = 1.73, 95% CI 1.66–1.80). Quartile analyses demonstrated significant dose–response relationships (all P for trend <0.001), with the highest quartiles conferring the greatest risk. RCS analyses revealed nonlinear associations for both indicators, with a more pronounced risk increase at higher ePWV levels. Subgroup analyses indicated that the associations were generally consistent across population strata, although the effect of ePWV appeared stronger in certain subgroups such as females and older individuals. ROC analysis showed that ePWV had better predictive performance than LAP (AUC: 0.727 vs. 0.627 in fully adjusted models). Conclusions Higher LAP and ePWV were associated with incident depressive symptoms among middle-aged and older Chinese adults. ePWV showed better discrimination than LAP; however, the incremental predictive value of adding LAP was limited. Title: Deservingness and backlash: How gendered advantage is built and defended in equity-accredited universities
Abstract: Despite sustained investment in gender-equity initiatives, hierarchies of authority, legitimacy and reward remain entrenched in higher education. This paper synthesises two staff surveys conducted in Athena Swan-accredited institutions in the United Kingdom and SAGE Athena Swan-accredited institutions in Australia. We develop a processual account of how gendered advantage is accumulated and defended within institutions recognised for equity progress. Across the studies, encouragement, sponsorship, workload protection and recognition operated as informal judgements of deservingness that shaped who entered formal evaluation with credibility and institutional momentum. Resistance became more visible when equity initiatives rendered these arrangements contestable, appearing through appeals to merit, reverse-discrimination claims and institutional withdrawal. We theorise these mechanisms as operating at different organisational speeds: deservingness is slow, cumulative and ordinarily obscured, whereas backlash is faster, reactive and more visible. Backlash is therefore treated as diagnostic evidence of the status, resources and authority being defended. This framework explains how accreditation can generate substantial activity while leaving informal distributions of legitimacy comparatively intact. © 2026 The Authors.
