Authors: Nguyen M.; Zhang Y.; Cao T.T.
Title: The right endorser for the right stay: How human and AI endorsers shape accommodation booking
Abstract: This research examines how endorser presence and endorser type influence consumers’ accommodation booking intention. Drawing on Embodied Cognition Theory, it shows that endorsers shape booking intention by activating embodied mental simulation. It further examines two hospitality-specific factors, booking purpose and service mode, that influence when human and AI-generated endorsers are more effective. Across five experimental studies, we demonstrate that endorser presence increases booking intention via embodied mental simulation. Human endorsers generally produce stronger embodied mental simulation and booking intention than AI-generated endorsers. However, this pattern reverses in high-privacy booking and self-service environments, where AI-generated endorsers are better aligned with the accommodation experiences consumers are imagining. This research extends Embodied Cognition Theory by showing that the effectiveness of embodied cues depends on the match between endorser type and the accommodation experience consumers mentally construct. It also offer practical guidance for hospitality marketers seeking to align endorser strategies with different booking contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Zhou Y.; Lyu Y.; Wu L.-Z.; Chen M.
Title: Why and when customer-related social stressors impair service performance: A conservation of resources perspective
Abstract: Building on the conservation of resources theory, we investigate how customer-related social stressors impact service performance among hospitality employees. To explore this, we gathered data from 350 supervisor-employee pairs across twelve hotels in China through a three-wave survey. The results show that customer-related social stressors detrimentally affect work engagement, which in turn reduces service performance. Furthermore, job social support and employees’ social skills emerge as two key moderators, buffering both the direct impact of customer-related social stressors on work engagement and the indirect effect on service performance via work engagement. These findings provide a nuanced understanding of the interactions among customer-related social stressors, work engagement, and service performance, offering significant implications for both theory and practice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Digital service nudges and consumer adoption of reusable packaging in online retailing: From convenience to circular responsibility
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Online retailers increasingly offer reusable express packaging, but adoption remains difficult because sustainable options can conflict with the convenience expectations that define online retailing. This article examines reusable packaging adoption as a circular retail service conversion problem. Across three studies with adult online shoppers, we test how digital service nudges and responsibility framing influence adoption through perceived service friction, perceived environmental efficacy, and sustainable service trust, and how these effects depend on return convenience. Study 1 uses a quota-based, post-stratification-weighted survey to show that decision-relevant service nudges reduce perceived service friction and increase adoption intention, while responsibility framing increases perceived environmental efficacy and sustainable service trust. Study 2 uses a discrete choice experiment to estimate trade-offs among nudge timing, return convenience, deposit/refund rules, delivery delay, environmental benefit visibility, and responsibility framing. Study 3 uses an incentivized simulated checkout task to test behaviorally consequential reusable-packaging choice at the decision point. The results show that return convenience and deposit clarity are stronger adoption drivers than generic environmental claims, and that consumers penalize delivery delay more strongly than they reward verified environmental-benefit information. Decision-point nudges increase reusable-packaging checkout choice more than post-checkout reminders, especially when return convenience is high. The findings contribute to retail service convenience, digital nudging, and circular retailing research by showing that sustainable retail adoption depends on service-touchpoint design, not only on environmental attitudes. Title: Decarbonization pathways for the dust-proof nets industry
Abstract: Plastic dust-proof nets (DPNs) are widely used for mitigating construction fugitive dust to safeguard urban air quality. Authors: Chen Z.
Title: Toward vulnerability-friendly destinations: A relational framework for inclusive destination governance
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Tourism research has generally located vulnerability in particular travelers and treated inclusion as an extension of accessibility provision. This paper reframes vulnerability as a relational destination-level condition produced, intensified, or reduced through interactions between heterogeneous human capacities and destination-system demands. A structured integrative conceptual synthesis connects public health equity, human factors engineering, and tourism management. The resulting framework explains how unequal exposure creates person-system mismatch, how destination arrangements produce vulnerability through recurring interfaces, and how inclusive-governance capability operates both preventively by shaping system properties and responsively by coordinating intervention. Risk redistribution is specified as a distinct mechanism that follows risk reduction and the allocation of responsibility, workload, and cost, and concerns the pooling, transfer, or absorption of residual risk by actors with greater capacity. Five recurring exposure interfaces and four intervention dimensions are organized in an analytical matrix. The framework distinguishes proximal outcomes (participation, safety, dignity, trust, and wellbeing) from conditional destination outcomes such as legitimacy, loyalty, and competitiveness. The paper extends relational vulnerability logic to the destination-system level and provides a research agenda for inclusive destination governance. © 2026

Title: Motivations in Chinese costume travel photography: An evolutionary psychology perspective
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Tourist photography has shifted from passive sightseeing to active narrative construction. Existing research has revealed the proximate motives of such behavior centered on identity construction, but the ultimate motives remain underexplored. Using a qualitative research design, this study explores motivations in Chinese costume travel photography by applying three interpretive lenses derived from evolutionary psychology, namely performative affiliation, temporary status, and scripted exploration. The findings indicate that participants' motivations are satisfied in Chinese costume travel photography as follows: temporary immersion and affiliation are gained from symbolic imitation and contextual co-performance; contextualized status enhancement is acquired by enacting ideal identities and collecting digital validation; and novelty seeking is met through experiences grounded in symbolic imagination and pre-arranged scripts. This study provides insights into the ultimate drivers of tourists’ surface motivations and the possible satisfaction mechanisms of deep evolutionary motives in Chinese costume travel photography. It also offers practical insights for tourism experience design and marketing by focusing on the satisfaction of deep motives. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Organizational Memory for Agentic Business Process Execution

Title: Turning adversity into opportunity: Managerial interventions and employee responses to observed customer mistreatment
Abstract: Customer mistreatment is a pervasive challenge in hospitality settings, affecting not only directly targeted employees but also those who witness encounters. Title: From image to action: How social proof turns brand image into repurchase intention
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: This study examines how social proof shapes the relationship between brand image and repurchase intention in an emerging digital marketplace, distinguishing three forms that operate through different mechanisms: user-generated content, brand ambassadors, and testimonials. Because online markets involve considerable information overload, consumers rely heavily on others' evaluations to reduce decision risk; however, forms of social proof vary in authenticity and persuasive effectiveness, and prior research has largely treated them as a single, uniformly positive construct. A two-study, mixed-methods design set in Vietnam addresses this gap. Study 1 applies a Vietnamese-optimized RoBERTa (Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach) model to social media comments to surface authentic consumer sentiment, providing exploratory, triangulating context without constituting a direct hypothesis test. Study 2 tests the proposed relationships using moderated regression on survey responses from 394 active Vietnamese online shoppers. Results show that brand image exerts a strong positive direct effect on repurchase intention. Title: Justifying membership fees through quality and pricing in a competitive supply chain

Title: Is Europe a laggard? Comparing the EU and the US using an interdisciplinary well-being framework

Title: From academic integrity to credential integrity: What does management education certify once artificial intelligence can produce the work?
Abstract: The debate on generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) in management education has centered on whether students may use AI, yet the larger question is what student work can still prove. This article calls the resulting problem credential integrity (i.e., whether a business school can defend what its degree certifies when AI may have produced the graded work). Abstract: This paper examines whether local exposure to extreme weather affects support for national climate and energy policies in Switzerland. Title: Multimarket contact, excess capacity, and low-cost carrier competition: A dual-channel model of mutual forbearance in international airline markets
Abstract: Research on the relationship between multimarket contact (MMC) and firm performance has produced mixed results. To help reconcile this discrepancy, we examine how firm-level excess capacity and low-cost carrier (LCC) competition condition the MMC–performance relationship in international airline markets. Drawing on mutual forbearance theory, we disaggregate total multimarket contact into contacts through strong resource-sharing markets (routes sharing endpoint cities) and weak resource-sharing markets (routes without shared endpoints), and we theorize a dual-channel model in which excess capacity determines which type of contact drives forbearance. Our analysis of 2979 firm–market–year observations spanning 82 airlines across 265 route markets serving Taiwan over the period 2009–2018 reveals three principal findings. First, total MMC exhibits an inverted U-shaped relationship with subsequent market share. Second, excess capacity channels the significant concave MMC profiles through different contact types: strong resource-sharing contact among high-excess-capacity firms (where idle capacity is visible at shared airports) and weak resource-sharing contact among low-excess-capacity firms (where network breadth sustains competitive awareness); in both cases the estimated downturn lies in a sparsely populated right tail and is interpreted cautiously. Third, LCC entry disrupts the forbearance equilibrium: the inverted U-shape is absent in markets with LCC competitors, and an exploratory positive linear pattern in those markets suggests that multimarket contact functions there as a competitive resource rather than as a forbearance signal. Accordingly, our study contributes to the multimarket competition literature by shedding light on how firm resources and competitive context jointly determine the mechanism and viability of mutual forbearance, helping to reconcile the inconsistent findings in prior research. Title: Weaving lived experiences into strategy: A multi-stakeholder framework for vulnerability-friendly big health tourism
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Growing attention to patient-centered care and transformations in health management systems, accelerated by the pandemic and global aging trends, are driving the development of big health tourism. However, a systematic understanding of its determinants remains underdeveloped. This study employs a multi-perspective Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA) to explore the determinants of big health tourism destination development. Through 50 interviews with tourism, health, and government stakeholders and guided by the PESTLE framework, this study identifies five key dimensions: sociological, technological, economic, environmental, and political-legal. Unlike traditional medical tourism focused on treatment, big health tourism encompasses integrated, lifelong wellness ecosystems spanning prevention, treatment, and lifestyle management. The findings further show how accessible, affordable, and coordinated destination services can jointly address barriers faced by vulnerable groups at the destination level. Theoretically, it contributes a multidimensional analytical framework that integrates PESTLE dimensions with multi-stakeholder perspectives for vulnerability-friendly big health tourism destination development. Practically, it provides guidance for healthcare, tourism, and government stakeholders. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Ullah O.; Tan B.; Zeb A.; Gui H.
Title: When do sustainability-related fashion reviews become helpful? The credibility role of verified purchase in online retailing
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Online reviews are an important source of information in digital retailing, yet not all reviews are equally useful to consumers. This study examines whether sustainability-related content is associated with online review helpfulness and whether verified purchase status conditions this relationship. Using 1,680,956 Amazon Fashion reviews, sustainability-related content is identified through a two-stage procedure combining a keyword pre-filter with large language model–assisted semantic classification and is integrated with review-, product-, and reviewer-level information. The main analysis employs a full-sample Negative Binomial model with product-level clustered standard errors, review-age exposure and review-specificity controls, and an empirically estimated NB2 dispersion parameter. Sustainability-related content is negatively associated with expected helpfulness among unverified reviews (β=−0.763), whereas verified purchase status is positively associated with helpfulness (β=0.596). The interaction between sustainability-related content and verified purchase status is positive and statistically significant (β=0.958). A formal linear-combination test shows that the combined sustainability effect among verified reviews is positive (β,=0.195p=0.023), corresponding to approximately 21.5% more expected helpful votes. Binary Logit and OLS models, year and month fixed effects, and product-type proxy fixed effects support the same credibility-contingent pattern. The findings indicate that sustainability-related user-generated content is not uniformly associated with greater helpfulness; its informational value is contingent on the transaction-based credibility cue attached to the review. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Tsui P.-L.
Title: Trust in algorithmic governance: How algorithmic control and fairness shape justice perceptions and employee voice in luxury hotels
Abstract: Algorithmic management is increasingly embedded in hotel operations, raising questions about how employees interpret managerial authority and voice concerns. Drawing on organisational justice and trust perspectives, this study examines relationships among perceived algorithmic control, perceived algorithmic fairness, and employee voice intention. An explanatory sequential mixed methods design combined structural equation modelling with semi-structured interviews. Perceived algorithmic control was negatively associated with procedural justice, interactional justice, and voice intention, whereas perceived algorithmic fairness was positively associated with trust in the employer and voice intention. Procedural justice, interactional justice, and trust were positively related to voice intention. The indirect-association analysis showed that algorithmic control was negatively associated with voice through procedural and interactional justice, while algorithmic fairness was positively associated with voice through trust. Qualitative findings highlighted explainability, reviewability, and managerial discretion. The study positions algorithmic management as relational governance and distinguishes control and fairness as separate pathways associated with employee voice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: How can hotels strategically enhance competitive performance? Investigating the dynamic roles and impacts of service attributes on customer satisfaction and dissatisfaction
Abstract: This study examines the asymmetric impact of service attributes on customer satisfaction (CS) and dissatisfaction (DS) in the luxury and upper upscale hotel segments, utilizing Impact Asymmetry Analysis and Impact Asymmetry Competitor Analysis. Grounded by the two-factor theory, this study integrates insights from online review ratings and textual sentiment to gauge customer evaluations. The findings reveal that attributes have discrete impacts on CS and DS when comparing high and low performance consistency brands. Hotels exhibiting low performance consistency are advised to prioritize managing attributes such as rooms, followed by value and cleanliness in rating-based evaluations. Additionally, location is identified as a key competitive disadvantage requiring urgent action in sentiment-based assessments. This study extends the understanding of the two-factor theory by examining the distinct impacts of attributes on CS and DS under varying performance consistency, providing actionable insights for hoteliers to strategically enhance attribute-level performance that strengthens customer experience and competitive standing. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Shokeen S.; Khattar A.
Title: Net Zero, Full Strategy: Integrating Environmental Goals with Business Strategy as Growth Engines
Source title: Contributions to Environmental Sciences and Innovative Business Technology
Abstract: Sustainability is not optional for businesses anymore, considering the growing constraints and challenges posed by climate change, environmental degradation, and stakeholder demands. In order to make environmental stewardship a driver of innovation, resilience, and competitive advantage, this chapter discusses how environmental goals can be effectively incorporated into business strategy. The chapter charts the evolution of business cases for sustainability, beginning with cost cutting and legal obligations and ending with increased investor appeal and brand value. It also provides helpful advice on incorporating sustainability into operations, product design, marketing, supply chain, and corporate governance through strategic models, namely the Triple Bottom Line, Shared Value Model, and the circular economy principles. Successful integration and the lessons learned are of actual business practices of powerhouses such as Patagonia, Hindustan Unilever Limited (HUL), and Tech Mahindra. This chapter also discusses practical issues such as balancing short-term profitability with long-term sustainability and the dangers of greenwashing. Ecological goals are now an element of company growth and have grown synonymous with it as the environment changes. It also presents responsible environmental integration as a basic necessity for companies which are value-driven and future-ready, apart from being legal requirements. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Authors: Liu Y.; Lv X.; Yuan R.; Fu X.; Hu L.
Title: Fixed or flexible: How product formats affect consumer redemption behavior for live-streamed food and beverage (F&B) products
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: With the rapid growth of live-streaming e-commerce in the food and beverage industry, low redemption rates despite high sales volumes have become a critical challenge for merchants. This research investigates how product formats and familiarity affect consumer redemption behavior and identifies the underlying psychological mechanisms and boundary conditions. Through five studies using one archival-data study, three scenario-based experiments, and one field experiment, we find that: product formats and familiarity interact significantly: set meals yield higher redemption under low familiarity, while vouchers perform better under high familiarity. This relationship is mediated through a dual-pathway mechanism: at low levels of familiarity, a loss-avoidance pathway prevails through perceived risk, whereas at high levels of familiarity, a gain-seeking pathway dominates through perceived preference fit. Purchase type further moderates this interaction, such that the effect emerges only under impulse purchase conditions. This research extends the theoretical understanding of the “purchase-redemption” process in live-streaming commerce and offers actionable insights for F&B firms to optimize product strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Adult-only: When excluding children reveals a flaw in hospitality management approach
Abstract: This research note explores social servicescape in hospitality settings, considering recent regulatory debates questioning the exclusion of children. Although children are often positioned as either sovereign consumers or a marginalised group, their impact on guest satisfaction remains largely unexplored. Drawing on 90,045 TripAdvisor reviews from 72 international resorts, we applied advanced natural language processing techniques, including BERT-based sentiment analysis and child-reference classification using a local Large Language Model to examine whether references to children influence customer evaluations. By comparing satisfaction scores across reviews that mention or omit children, we explore whether these differences reflect broader managerial, academic, and policy-related challenges. This study contributes to ongoing debates on adult-only vs inclusive hospitality by highlighting how children's presence is addressed in guest feedback, and by raising questions about the potential limitations in current hospitality management practices. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Hu Q.; Pan Z.
Title: Helpfulness and enjoyment in eWOM: A dual-value perspective for hedonic digital products
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: As the digital economy increasingly pivots toward the experience sector, electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) serves not merely as a decision-support tool but as an intrinsic source of entertainment. Yet, the literature remains overwhelmingly anchored to a unidimensional metric: review helpfulness. Challenging this utilitarian bias, this study establishes a dual-value evaluative paradigm that encompasses both diagnostic helpfulness and enjoyment to decode peer evaluations of hedonic digital product reviews. Grounded in processing fluency theory, we investigate how cognitive stimuli (product informativeness) and affective stimuli (emotional richness) synergistically yet distinctly drive these dual dimensions. Leveraging a dataset of 12,823 reviews from Steam, we deploy a rigorous methodological triangulation: extracting deep semantic features via Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and VADER sentiment analysis, estimating causal mechanisms via Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial (ZINB) regressions, and validating predictive robustness using Random Forest algorithms. The empirical findings reveal that review breadth and thematic distribution divergence concurrently enhance both outcomes. Review thematic density exhibits an inverted U-shaped relationship across both dimensions. While the negative sentiment rate enhances utilitarian risk-mitigation but severely disrupts hedonic gratification. The study advances eWOM literature by establishing a dual-value evaluative paradigm, providing actionable guidelines for digital platforms to optimize content distribution for review helpfulness and enjoyment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Chowdhury F.; Swaminathan S.
Title: Political activism and indulgent preferences: Perceived moral contribution and deservingness
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Political activism is commonly conceptualized as a form of collective action that promotes individual empowerment, collective efficacy, and societal well-being. However, this research demonstrates that activism focused on the pursuit of a collective goal can also have paradoxical consequences by increasing subsequent indulgent preferences. Drawing on moral licensing theory, when high-effort, in-person activism is grounded in moral conviction, actors may interpret their effortful involvement as a morally meaningful contribution to a collective cause, enhancing a sense of perceived moral contribution, which heightens perceived deservingness and, in turn, indulgence. Across four experimental studies (n = 852) in emerging and developed economies, the results highlight that participants exposed to high-effort, in-person activism scenarios subsequently demonstrated higher levels of indulgence than those in low-effort online actions or the control condition. These effects are moderated by consumer type in emerging markets, with the effect of high-effort activism on indulgence being stronger among bottom-of-the-pyramid (BOP) consumers. Our findings caution advocacy organizations against assuming that effortful civic participation consistently reinforces prosocial behavior. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Fan G.; Deng Z.; Fang H.
Title: EXPLORING THE HEALTH KNOWLEDGE CO-CONSTRUCTION ON SHORT VIDEO PLATFORMS
Abstract: Short video platforms have become an important channel for doctors to conduct health science popularization. This study aims to explore the factors influencing health knowledge co-construction on short video platforms. Based on arousal theory, we develop an empirical model to examine the effects of video vividness, video complexity, emotional attitudes, and doctor popularity on health knowledge co-construction. We collected data from the largest short video platform in China, comprising a total of 4,009 videos and 1,040,230 comments for empirical analysis. This study combined machine learning, large language models, and econometric models to test the theoretical model. The results show that: (1) video vividness has a significant positive effect on health knowledge co-construction; (2) video complexity has a negative effect on health knowledge co-construction; (3) there is an inverted U-shaped relationship between emotional attitude and health knowledge co-construction; (4) doctor popularity positively moderates this curvilinear relationship. This study contributes to the literature on knowledge co-construction, expands the understanding of health knowledge co-construction on short video platforms, and provides practical guidance for platform managers and doctors. © 2027 California State University, Long Beach. Title: Barriers and Facilitators of Utilizing Real-World Evidence to Support Policy Decisions in Central and Eastern Europe
Abstract: Objectives We aimed to identify drivers and solutions to overcome the barriers of the effective use of real-world data (RWD) and real-world evidence (RWE) in Central and Eastern Europe. Methods First, a targeted literature review was followed by an experts’ workshop aiming to refine and complement the identification of current barriers and drivers. Next, we performed a gap analysis on the barriers based on their importance and actionability. The scores of importance and actionability for each barrier were determined through a questionnaire completed by the experts. Finally, a second experts’ workshop was held to develop recommendations to overcome the most important actionable barriers and to collect case studies of RWD/RWE utilization. Results A total of 22 publications were included in the data extraction phase of the targeted literature review. After the first experts’ workshop, 16 barriers and 9 drivers were identified. At the second workshop 9 solutions were proposed in 4 main intervention areas. In addition, 13 case studies were provided from the 4 countries, where RWD/RWE was used effectively. Conclusions The effective use of RWD/RWE in health-policy decision making still faces several barriers in Czechia, Hungary, Poland, and Slovakia. This research highlighted the most important barriers and collected recommendations by key experts on how to improve the utilization of RWD/RWE. In addition, we have identified several drivers for the use of RWD/RWE, alongside with 13 case studies, in which RWD/RWE was used effectively. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Europe at the crossroads: trading strategic autonomy for resilience under degrowth
Abstract: This paper reviews the economic interpretations of strategic autonomy, which has been reintroduced, and sheds new light on it from the perspective of the European economy using a systems approach. The paper uses the zombie phenomenon to demonstrate the flawed nature of quantitative economic growth-based strategic autonomy and the necessity of a degrowth transition that replaces autonomy with resilience, which necessitates the fundamental reassessment of the role of zombies. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: A probabilistic approach to reliability assessment of inventory management strategies in an MRP environment with random yield
Abstract: Although there are several strategies for planning production or replenishment in a material requirement planning (MRP) environment, they are all designed to calculate planned stock parameters. Other metrics, such as more precise probabilistic estimates of safety stocks, shortages and the reliability of the entire inventory management system, are rarely considered. Improving the accuracy of probabilistic estimates of these indicators is necessary to enhance the reliability of describing production processes under conditions of uncertainty. The article proposes calculated dependencies that allow determining the safety stock level based on analytical calculations rather than practical experience or arbitrary assumptions. A general algorithm was developed for selecting an inventory management strategy under random yield that takes safety stocks and random yield into account. This algorithm includes estimates of efficiency (order costs, on-hand stock holding costs and safety stock holding costs) and material planning reliability indicators in the form of failure-free probability during the planning period. Analysis of the results revealed that more precise probabilistic consideration of safety stocks in MRP under random yield leads to a change in the production planning or replenishment strategy. © 2025 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

Title: Resource flows in the UK’s foundation industries
Abstract: The UK foundation industries supply essential materials but remain difficult to decarbonise because of high-temperature processing and process emissions. This study implements a gate-to-gate resource flow mapping, integrating material and energy inputs and outputs, by-products, and direct emissions, for selected cement, ceramics, chemicals, glass, metals, and paper products in 2019, benchmarked against global averages and product-mix-adjusted energy best practice. These products totalled 33 Mt/yr, used 330 PJ/yr of fuels and purchased electricity, and emitted 27 MtCO2/yr (Scope 1): 12.5 Mt from process reactions, 12.3 Mt from fossil fuels, and 2.1 Mt biogenic. Recovered materials (e.g., scrap), not counting by-products (e.g., slag), supplied 14% of material inputs excluding water and oxygen. UK energy intensity was 13% above the global benchmark. The gap to energy best practice is 28% in energy use but only 15% in direct emissions, mainly due to process-reaction emissions. Title: The evolution of Italian airport ownership
Abstract: The ownership of commercial airports is increasingly essential for national competitiveness and regional economic development. Airport ownership directly influences the planning of airport infrastructure and air transport policies at both a local and national level. In Italy, historically, tight control by the state permitted the implementation of long-term development plans and ensured that the needs of local communities were addressed, but today, there are very few airports, and among the larger ones, almost none, without an equity share held by the private sector. In light of current debates surrounding the future viability of Italian airports following the COVID-19 pandemic, this paper aims to examine the evolution of Italian airport ownership compared to significant international experiences, such as the UK, in which airport privatisation followed the 1986 Airports Act. This paper critically examines the evolution of Italian airport ownership, focusing on the underlying drivers and consequences of these changes and comparing them with the UK case, by considering different ownership models, the nature of the private entities involved, the proportion of passengers flying through airports with different ownership structures, and the number of owners per airport. The analysis involves the main 33 Italian airports, controlled by 25 airport companies, and covers the period 1997-2024, which is analysed in three specific phases: 1997/2008-2009/2019, and 2020/2024. Among the primary outcomes of this research, there is a better understanding of how airport ownership has evolved in Italy compared with other international settings and whether airports can be considered public utilities or private assets to provide valuable recommendations for airport management and policymakers regarding the industry's future viability. Title: Turning climate concern into climate courage: Female parliamentarians, environmental taxation and SDG13
Abstract: Environmental issues, including climate change, biodiversity loss, and air pollution, have received heightened international attention following the adoption of the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), which aim to promote global sustainable development. The presence of women in parliament has proven to be highly effective in advancing environmental tax policies that help reduce vulnerability to climate change. Using panel data from G20 and N11 economies between 2002 and 2022, this study provides evidence that women's presence in parliament is a critical determinant of achieving environmental sustainability. The models' results show that female parliamentarians with significant representation are more effective, and they reach the ‘Climate Action’ goal by reducing CO2 and GHG emissions, among other environmental targets. Notably, the country's ecological achievements can be intensified by implementing more efficient environmental taxation policies. We mitigate endogeneity by using Lewbel-IV and GMM estimation. Moreover, this study also highlights the significance of this relationship when the government invests more in renewable energy, emits less CO2, has a significant forest reserve, and offers better employment opportunities. © 2026 The Authors. Title: A reciprocal perspective on internationalization and ESG in EMNEs: The role of digitalization
Abstract: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) has become a critical measure of multinational enterprises’ global competitiveness, yet emerging market multinational enterprises (EMNEs) face distinct legitimacy challenges due to weak home-country ESG regulations, known as the liability of home origin. Although prior studies have examined the relationship between internationalization and ESG, they have largely treated the two directions separately, leaving unclear whether they operate as competing explanations or as mutually reinforcing processes. Drawing on legitimacy theory, this study conceptualizes internationalization and ESG performance as exhibiting mutually reinforcing associations over time. Using longitudinal data from 2460 Chinese listed firms between 2009 and 2020, we examine the reciprocal relationship between internationalization and ESG performance, and the moderating role of digitalization. Findings indicate that internationalization is consistently associated with stronger ESG performance, suggesting EMNEs use ESG to mitigate liabilities of origin and build legitimacy abroad. The reverse association is weaker but most robust for foreign-country scope, indicating that ESG performance may support international expansion by signaling alignment with international sustainability expectations. The moderating associations of digitalization are uneven and are concentrated in visible foreign organizational and geographic presence, such as overseas subsidiaries and foreign-country scope, rather than overseas revenues. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Wang L.; Jia J.; Zhou L.; Li S.
Title: Perceived placeness in creative tourism: Conceptualization, scale development and implications for transformative experiences
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Creative place-making combines cultural heritage, spatial design, creative symbolism, and experiential affordances to cultivate distinctive destinations, yet what tourists holistically perceive in these places remains underexplored. Drawing on atmospheric aesthetics theory, this study conceptualizes perceived placeness in creative tourism as tourists' holistic perception of the environmental and atmospheric qualities that make creative tourism destinations experientially distinctive. To operationalize this construct, content analysis was used to identify its dimensions and initial items. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses refined these items into a 20-item, five-dimensional scale comprising environmental qualities, historical-cultural embeddedness, creative-symbolic ambiance, restorative affordance, and emotional affordance. The nomological relevance of the scale was further established by examining its implications for transformative experiences via authenticity. Theoretically, this study positions perceived placeness as an integrative perceptual field between place-making and tourists’ psychological responses, and contextually elaborates atmospheric aesthetics theory in creative tourism. Practically, the scale provides a timely tool for evaluating and planning creative place-making efforts and curating meaningful tourist experiences. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Business Process Analysis and Re-engineering by Synthetic Expert Panel and Human Expert Collaboration
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: This study presents a synthetic expert panel employing four large language models as synthetic experts for business process automation assessment. The framework implements a six-stage pipeline: process decomposition, multi-model solution generation, cross-model evaluation, optimal solution selection through voting mechanisms, process optimization, and documentation generation. Empirical validation with 140 business professionals across diverse domains demonstrated the framework’s practical applicability across three successive model generations. The framework proved most effective for production-related fields (M = 4.41) and marketing & sales processes (M = 4.28), while administrative workflows showed the greatest variability. At the activity level, Anthropic’s models produced the highest-rated automation suggestions, and Sonnet 4.6 was the highest-rated model overall (M = 4.46), though newer model versions did not consistently outperform predecessors across all providers. The synthetic expert panel approach reduces single-model biases and provides a systematic, scalable methodology for AI-driven process transformation in business information systems. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Going green to compete: Male-biased operational sex ratio, status motivation, and men's relative green product preference
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Motivating men to choose environmentally preferable products remains an important challenge. Across six studies, this research examines how operational sex ratio (OSR), defined as the ratio of reproductively available men to women, is associated with men's relative preference for green products over conventional alternatives. OSR can characterize a broader demographic environment or serve as a population cue in a local social setting. A cross-level analysis in China showed that men living in provinces with more male-biased OSRs assigned greater priority to environmental protection, whereas women showed no corresponding association. Randomized experiments showed that perceived male-biased OSR increased men's relative green product preference; perceiving a female-biased OSR did not produce a corresponding increase among women. Among men, the subsequent studies provided complementary evidence consistent with mediation by status motivation, linked male-biased OSR cues more closely to intrasexual competition motivation than to mate-attraction motivation, and showed that audience publicness moderated the indirect effect through status motivation. Title: Biodiversity risk and hotel stock returns: Global evidence from wavelet analysis
Abstract: This paper aims to examine the dynamic correlation mechanisms between the S&P Global LargeMidCap Biodiversity Index (GBIO) and share prices of nine major global hotel groups. Based on daily data spanning from June 2019 to July 2025, the research utilises advanced econometric methods including wavelet local multiple correlation, wavelet coherence, wavelet quantile correlation, and rolling window wavelet correlation to reveal that biodiversity risk and hotel industry stock returns exhibit significant non-linear, time-varying, and frequency-dependent characteristics. Empirical results demonstrate that the two maintain a strong and stable positive correlation from a long-term investment perspective (exceeding 64 days), with correlation coefficients generally surpassing 0.8, whilst correlation weakens considerably at short-term scales (2–16 days). Cross-regional comparisons reveal that American hotel groups exhibit the strongest positive correlation with the biodiversity index (averaging 0.56), followed by European enterprises (averaging 0.45), with Asian enterprises showing the weakest correlation (averaging 0.27), reflecting the heterogeneity in ESG factor pricing efficiency across different capital markets. Title: Experiential and symbolic pathways to luxury fashion brand equity: The contingent role of brand attachment and subjective norm

Title: Descriptive or injunctive? The interactive effects of influencer type and social norms on alternative protein purchase intention

Abstract: As alternative protein products attract increasing attention, understanding how social norm messages and influencer type jointly shape consumers’ purchase intention has become increasingly relevant. Title: Measurement scale for push and pull factors of Chinese pedestrian streets

Abstract: The concepts of push and pull theory have been proposed and extensively discussed in various studies, particularly in tourism research. Title: Product visual form and customer satisfaction: Multimodal evidence on affective value and functional diagnosis
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Product visual form conveys important aesthetic, quality, and use-related cues for functionally complex products. Title: The joint effects of organisational learning and CEO cognition on cross-border acquisition pace

Title: Green power markets in selected Latin American countries: Experiences and trends
Abstract: Latin America is undergoing a significant transformation of its electricity systems as countries strive to advance their energy transitions through cleaner technologies, new business models, and strengthened policy frameworks. Despite long-standing reliance on hydropower, the region has experienced both a rapid expansion of non-hydro renewable capacity and, unexpectedly, a parallel growth in thermal generation. However, comparative understanding of how renewable energy policies and emerging green power markets have evolved across the region remains limited. This paper addresses this gap by analyzing the emergence and evolution of green power markets across twelve Latin American countries, examining renewable energy policies, green electricity products, and the mechanisms that shape market development. Our findings reveal convergence in the types of policy instruments adopted, but substantial differences in their implementation and green power market development. Overall, market development remains limited and fragmented. Title: When ads look worth keeping: Screenshotable design increases ad saving and Facebook ad liking
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: As social media advertising increasingly competes in fast-scrolling feed environments, an important but understudied question is whether some ads succeed by functioning less as transient persuasive messages and more as saveable information objects. Title: When plateware shape matters: The congruence effects between food pungency and plateware shape on food preference

Title: Land-based climate policy, land prices, and the green transition trilemma: Evidence from Bolivia
Abstract: Land-based climate policies in forest-rich developing economies are often assessed separately, overlooking how land scarcity, land prices, and macroeconomic constraints shape feasibility. This paper examines the macro-financial challenges of sustainable agriculture and forest conservation in Bolivia, where deforestation is high and fiscal and external constraints bind. Overall, the NDCs improve economic activity and environmental outcomes while worsening fiscal and trade imbalances. Fiscal consolidation and exchange-rate adjustment mitigate some imbalances but entail inflationary pressures or lower output and employment. Environmental gains may therefore come at the cost of macroeconomic fragility. The paper shows how conservation-induced land scarcity and land price dynamics interact with fiscal and balance-of-payments constraints to determine the feasibility of land-based transitions in resource-dependent economies. Title: The duty to rescue at sea and Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS): Implementation under the IMO MASS code
Abstract: Under the international legal framework governing Search and Rescue (SAR) at sea, flag states are required to ensure that ships flying their flag render assistance to persons in distress, while coastal states must establish and coordinate adequate SAR services within their areas of responsibility. Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS) pose challenges for ensuring compliance with rescue obligations due to difficulties in designating a master and limited embarkation and accommodation capabilities. This paper argues that autonomy does not justify an exemption from, or relief from, the duty to rescue. Against this background, the article examines how Chapter 21 (SAR) of the International Code of Safety for Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS Code) translates the duty to rescue for MASS into a goal-based structure comprising goals, functional requirements, and expected performance, aligned with SOLAS. It further delineates the respective implementation responsibilities of flag states and coastal states, with a view to ensuring that MASS can render effective assistance to persons in distress at sea. On the one hand, flag states should implement Chapter 21 by survey, certification, and approval processes and oversee compliance through classification societies. On the other hand, coastal states must integrate MASS into SAR coordination arrangements and fulfil their obligation to coordinate the disembarkation of survivors to a “place of safety,” thereby completing the ship-side rescue duty upon delivery. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Allocation of foreign aid in emerging economies: Investment in new vs maintenance of old infrastructure
Abstract: This paper analyzes the growth and welfare effects of allocating public resources — both domestic tax revenues and foreign aid — between investment in new public capital and the maintenance of existing public capital in emerging economies. Title: Semantically-Guided LLM Pipeline for Business Architecture Modelling with Incremental Knowledge Acquisition

Title: Beyond the accession event: Joint regional membership duration and completion of cross-border acquisitions
Abstract: Cross-border acquisition (CBA) completion is often hindered by institutional barriers, imposing substantial costs on deal participants. Title: The double-edged effect of realism design in AI-powered digital streamers: The moderating role of social evaluative threat in livestreaming commerce

Abstract: AI-powered digital streamers have emerged as a powerful tool for e-commerce livestreaming due to their cost efficiency, stable performance, and high customizability. Title: A Malatya Centrality-based algorithm for optimal solutions to maximum independent set and minimum vertex cover problems in lattice graphs
Abstract: A lattice graph constitutes a fundamental graph type utilized across various domains and for addressing distinct challenges. Subsequently, it ascertains the optimal solution set for MVCP based on the solution derived for MISP. It offers an efficient and robust solution in polynomial time across different lattice graph categories. Mathematical analysis and empirical studies on prevalent lattice graphs in the literature affirm that the algorithm yields optimal and effective resolutions for MISP and MVCP. Title: Should generative AI be responsible to users? Developing and validating the user-generative AI psychological contract scale

Abstract: As GenAI becomes increasingly embedded in AI-enabled service interactions, users' evaluations of AI are extending from functional performance to expectations regarding responsibility and obligation. Study 1 used purposively recruited interviews (N = 26) to identify the construct content domain. Study 2 used two nonprobability online-panel samples of active GenAI users (N = 507 and N = 506) to develop the items and examine the factor structure, reliability, and construct validity. Title: Recommend or not? Investigating the effectiveness of personalized algorithmic recommendations in micro-donation advertising
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Online charitable platforms are important channels through which the public participates in micro-donations, and these platforms have increasingly leveraged algorithmic recommendation technologies to deliver personalized charitable advertisements to potential donors. Nonetheless, whether personalized algorithmic recommendations enhance or undermine consumers’ micro-donation intentions remains unclear. Drawing on moral identity theory, our research addresses this gap through five online scenario-based experiments. The results show that consumers exhibit lower micro-donation intentions when exposed to micro-donation advertisements with personalized algorithmic recommendations, and that this negative effect is driven primarily by perceived identity value threat. Furthermore, we find that the negative effect of personalized algorithmic recommendations in micro-donation advertising is attenuated in the presence of legitimization cues or among consumers with low scores on the moral identity scale. Title: Perceived business value of digital freight platforms: Evidence from small and medium-sized enterprises in Poland
Source title: Research in Transportation Business and Management
Abstract: Purpose: This study examines how SMEs operating in the Polish transport, shipping and logistics (TSL) sector perceive the business value of digital freight exchanges, and how they associate platform use with operational efficiency, empty vehicle movements, transport resource utilization and competitive positioning. The sample is therefore not representative of the broader Polish SME road-freight population. Factor stability was assessed using bootstrap analysis. Authors: Kang I.; Wei S.
Title: Persuasive triggers and psychological pathways: Unplanned purchase behavior in live-streaming blind box commerce
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Unplanned purchasing is increasingly embedded in digital experiences in which consumers encounter commercial opportunities without a prior intention to shop. This study examines how such opportunities become valued and actionable in live-streaming blind-box commerce. Using survey data from 231 Chinese consumers with experience purchasing blind boxes through livestreams, we test a process model linking scarcity messages, time pressure, economic benefits, and fear of missing out (FOMO) with perceived value, emotional and cognitive self-efficacy, and unplanned purchase behavior (UPB). All four conditions were positively associated with perceived value, which was positively associated with both forms of self-efficacy; emotional and cognitive self-efficacy were, in turn, positively associated with UPB. Streamer persuasiveness strengthened the relationships between all four antecedent conditions and perceived value. The findings show that an unplanned purchase need not arise simply from impulsive responding. Consumers may encounter an unexpected opportunity, judge it to be worthwhile, and feel capable of acting even when the purchase was not previously planned. Title: When loyalty points become donations: The effects of redeemability, point expiration, and descriptive norm information
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Although loyalty programs and checkout charity are widely implemented across retail industries, the integration of reward point donations into online checkout charity remains rare, and consumer behavior in this context is not yet fully understood. While a few studies have explored reward point donations and generally reported positive consumer responses, to the best of our knowledge, little research has examined how reward point characteristics and situational factors influence consumers' willingness to donate. Study 1 shows that consumers exhibit higher donation intention when their reward points are non-redeemable than when they are redeemable. Study 2 demonstrates that the interaction between point redeemability and point expiration significantly influences donation intention, while Study 3 shows that the interaction between point redeemability and descriptive norm information also significantly affects donation intention. Title: Sustainable production and export performance of globe artichoke in Egypt: evidence from 2000 to 2023
Abstract: The globe artichoke is one of the major vegetable crops cultivated in the Mediterranean Basin, with global production reaching nearly 1.6 million tons in 2023. Egypt is among the world’s leading producers, contributing almost one-fifth of global production; however, its export performance remains relatively limited compared with its production potential. This study examines the production dynamics, geographical distribution, and export competitiveness of globe artichoke in Egypt during 2000–2023 within the framework of sustainable agricultural development. Both quantitative and qualitative approaches were used to analyze trends in cultivated areas, productivity, and exports, in addition to major competitiveness indicators in international markets. The results indicate that production growth was driven mainly by horizontal expansion rather than improvements in yield. The cultivated area increased to 50.4 thousand fed in 2023, with an average annual growth rate of about 8%, whereas yield increased only marginally during the study period. Expansion was more pronounced in new lands than in old lands, reflecting the crop’s adaptability to new production areas but also indicating limited progress in productivity efficiency. Despite the increase in production, globe artichoke exports declined by approximately 1.4%, largely due to rising competition from Mediterranean countries, export market concentration, and price fluctuations. Italy, France, and Spain remained the main importers of Egyptian artichokes while simultaneously representing major competitors in international markets. The findings suggest that improving productivity efficiency, promoting value-added products, and diversifying export markets may contribute to strengthening export competitiveness and enhancing the long-term sustainability of globe artichoke production in Egypt. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Authors: Karichalil R.A.
Title: Circular economy transition pathways for AI adoption in Indian municipal waste management: Scenario-based forecasts to 2050

Title: The allure of imperfection: How ugly-cute aesthetics drive purchase intentions
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: The rise of social media has increased both aesthetic diversity and consumer attention to product appearance and emotional appeal. This research examines the commercially successful yet under-researched “ugly-cute” aesthetic, exemplified by products like Pop Mart's LABUBU. Title: Political career incentives and the environmental costs: Evidence from China's promotion tournaments
Abstract: This paper shows that promotion incentives for county-level cadres in China are an important driver of air pollution deterioration. Building on the multi-winner tournament model proposed by Clark and Riis (1998), we predict an inverted-U-shaped relationship between the number of counties within a prefecture and the promotion incentives for county-level cadres. Using the length of small rivers as an instrumental variable for the number of counties within a prefecture, our empirical analysis identifies a robust inverted-U-shaped relationship between the number of counties and air pollution levels, suggesting that promotion incentives significantly exacerbate air pollution. Further analysis reveals that, in pursuit of economic growth, local cadres tend to relax environmental regulations and attract more pollution-intensive firms. In regions where cadres’ performance evaluation places less emphasis on economic growth, the inverted-U-shaped relationship does not exist. These findings suggest that local cadres’ career incentives stimulate economic growth at the expense of the environment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Can stablecoin instability threaten emerging tourism payment infrastructure?

Evidence from tourism payment activity suggests that severe depeg events may reduce the use of stablecoin-based payments within crypto-native tourism ecosystems. Title: Emotional interaction and conversion value in live streaming E-commerce

Abstract: Multi-agent emotional interaction constitutes a core characteristic of live streaming e-commerce. Title: The punctuality stability of the Nash equilibrium: the advantage of a late player in potential and aggregative games
Abstract: In a Nash equilibrium, no player can gain by unilaterally deviating. Title: A study analyzing factors retarding digital transformation and configuration pathways: Based on the perspective of digital transformation acceptors
Abstract: The high-touch service nature of the hospitality industry highlights that the success of digital transformation depends primarily on human factors rather than technology itself. Title: The potential for coordination between air and ocean transport in advancing Net Zero policies

Title: Do platform and seller cues improve price prediction? A study on online food delivery platforms using machine learning

Title: When does AI design help or hurt? Brand positioning and the dual effects of homogeneity and trend relevance in fashion retailing
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in fashion design to generate product aesthetics and forecast trends. While prior research has separately examined algorithmic homogeneity risks or efficiency gains, how consumers simultaneously process these opposing signals, and whether this processing differs from human-generated design, remains unclear. Title: Reinventing the package holiday: Consumer preferences and optimal pricing for hotel room upgrades

Title: Who eats matters: How eating-agent identity in short-form retail videos influences consumers’ purchase intentions

Title: Using vertical integration to safeguard against unfavorable bargaining position
Abstract: This paper examines the effect of a change in bargaining power on the decision to engage in vertical integration. Title: An agent based model to support secondary critical materials markets development
Abstract: The development of Secondary Materials Markets (SMMs) is a promising approach to diversify and strengthen critical materials supply chains. SMMs involve the recovery of valuable materials from discarded products and reintroduce valuable materials into the economy through cooperative business partnerships. Title: Virtue re-coding: How institutional voids shape ethical practice in international business
Abstract: Shared moral vocabularies recur across the Arab world, yet senior executives enact them differently across institutional settings. Drawing on a comparative case study of 45 interviews with Muslim and Christian executives in Lebanon, Iraq, and Egypt, we ask how shared moral resources are re-coded across distinct institutional voids. Title: Shared value vs plural values. Contesting renewable energy projects of the Enel Group

Title: Examining the evolutionary patterns of open-source software projects

Title: Inter-class co-movement of retail electricity tariffs and the residential adjustment gradient: evidence from a new Latin American panel

Title: Material use and its relationship with per capita income. A panel data analysis at the global level
Abstract: Global use of materials has significantly increased over recent decades, causing a wide range of environmental and social concerns. Title: From sound to resonance: Club anthem attractiveness and fan–brand relationships

Abstract: Auditory branding plays an increasingly important role in sensory service experiences; however, limited research has examined how recurring auditory brand cues relate to consumer–brand relationship outcomes. Title: Secondhand fashion subscription boxes: A necessary condition analysis of purchase intention determinants

Title: Toward sustainable oceans: Redirecting fisheries subsidies through cleaner production in Chile
Abstract: Fisheries subsidies are often linked to overcapacity, overfishing, and environmental harm. Title: The fantasy of digital immateriality: AI, ecologically unequal exchange, and appropriation of lived human time

Title: Exemption or backfire? The double-edged effect of AI attribution strategy on brand trust in digital content moral crises

Abstract: Human-AI collaboration has become central to brand content production, but AI's black-box nature obscures responsibility in digital content moral crises. Title: Attribution of causality following service failure on online retail platforms: The roles of governance structure and recurring failures

This research extends contingency theory in tourism by incorporating governance quality as a moderating contextual factor and introducing cultural decoupling as a mechanism explaining how governance contexts shape service outcomes across contexts. Title: From Classroom to Practice: Bridging BPM Education and Industry Expectations Through a Process Mining Tool Comparison Project
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: This paper presents an innovative assignment approach implemented in the Business Process Modelling, Mining, and Automation course for Master’s students at theUniversity of Ottawa. The course integrates Active Learning principles to train industry-ready business analysts, capable of supporting modern business process management, mining, optimization, and automation initiatives. The assignment approach involves a project-based process mining tool comparison project, where students evaluate industry-relevant tools using real event logs to address a concrete business problem. The assignment design integrates experiential learning, formative feedback, and peer review activities to support both technical and professional skill development. The assignment is structured around a set of guiding principles. First, it emphasizes the development of real-world skills aligned with the evolving demands of digital business processes. Second, it encourages students to critically challenge their assumptions, tool limitations, and existing practices through a data-driven, evidence-based mindset. Finally, it promotes continuous self-reflection and the active exchange of constructive feedback among peers to reinforce deeper learning and professional growth. These guiding principles offer a practical framework that can support other educators in the BPM community in designing effective and practical assignment strategies that help bridge the gap between academic learning and industry expectations. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Systematic and Automated Diagnosis of Process Models Using Reference Frameworks
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Reference frameworks in Business Process Management (BPM) are generic best-practice templates used to design, analyze, benchmark, and improve business processes (BPs). They promote consistency in BP structure and terminology and support BP model diagnosis by revealing gaps and weaknesses through comparison with a reference structure. Despite extensive research on the development and adaptation of reference frameworks, the BPM literature offers limited methodological support for their systematic application to existing BP models, leaving much of the analysis to manual work by domain experts. However, this analysis typically demands significant time, human, and financial resources and does not scale well to enterprise-wide BP sets, limiting its practical use for BP diagnosis. In this paper, following a Design Science Research (DSR) methodology, we analyze existing approaches that leverage reference frameworks for BP diagnosis to identify their key characteristics, and propose a maturity model to systematically guide their application to existing BP models. To demonstrate feasibility, we use a Large Language Model (LLM) to automate the application of the maturity model, generating suggestions across all diagnostic levels. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Zisgen Y.; Koschmider A.
Title: Differentially Private HeuristicsMiner
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Process discovery aims at extracting process models from prior recordings of process executions stored in information systems, called event logs. These process models may reveal sensitive information about unique traces and about the process stakeholders. Although a differentially private process discovery algorithm exists, it does not lend itself well to handling noisy event logs. This paper proposes the Differentially Private Heuristics Miner (DPHM), an algorithm that considers Differential Privacy at the discovery step while handling noise efficiently. We provide proof of the property of Differential Privacy and evaluated our approach on four real-world event logs against three other process discovery algorithms. The evaluation results indicate that unique traces can be protected with a slight loss of utility. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Song M.; Dai F.; Wang Z.; Lu T.; Zhu Q.
Title: Youngism at work: How age discrimination against younger employees fractures psychological sense of community
Abstract: Age discrimination against younger employees has become increasingly prevalent, yet its psychological consequences remain underexplored. Grounded in the rejection-identification model and social identity theory, we examine how youngism shapes younger employees’ psychological sense of community (PSOC). Using a daily diary design across 10 working days with 63 Chinese employees (≤ 3 years’ tenure, 546 daily observations), we find that daily age-based discrimination strengthens younger employees’ identification with their peer group, which in turn enhances their in-group PSOC while diminishing their organizational PSOC. We refer to these opposing outcomes as an “identity trade-off”. Furthermore, a growth mindset moderates the relationship between discrimination and age-group identification, such that this relationship is weaker among individuals with stronger growth mindset. By focusing on younger targets of ageism, we elucidate a dual-pathway mechanism through which youngism erodes workplace community and identify a boundary condition that mitigates this process. Theoretical and practical implications are discussed. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Xie W.; Shan W.
Title: Competing for attention: Exploring the impact of video cover features on clicks with machine learning and generative AI
Abstract: Under scarce viewer attention, video covers serve as critical previews to drive engagement. Despite extensive research on titles or thumbnails, their joint and interaction effects remain largely unexplored, especially in destination marketing. Drawing on the model of attention capture and transfer, this study integrates machine learning and generative AI to analyze 13,037 tourism video covers, examining how cognitive, aesthetic, and emotional features affect video views. In between-cover attention competition, the results show that title readability is positively associated with clicks, whereas thumbnail fit follows a U-shaped pattern. Thumbnail colorfulness, thumbnail complexity, and negative sentiment in titles and thumbnails are linked to more views. In within-cover attention competition, aesthetic and emotional features condition the effects of cognitive features through attention transfer between the title and the thumbnail. Additional analyses consider attraction type and text overlays. The findings contribute to the marketing literature and offer practical insights for creators, marketers, and platforms. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Author full names: Kardani Malekinezhad, Mona (57219845120); Rahimnia, Fariborz (35219188600); Eslami, Ghasem (57200936073); Farahi, Mohammad Mahdi (57214804224)
Title: Unveiling the dynamics of data driven innovation in human resource analytics: A grounded theory of strategic approach to HRM
Abstract: Data-driven innovation (DDI) in Human Resource Analytics (HR Analytics) presents a significant potential for strategic organizational change. A persistent gap exists between the theoretical promises of HR Analytics and its practical, value-generating implementation within organizations. This study aims to develop a conceptual model for the effective implementation of HR Analytics within private-sector organizations in a developing economy (Iran), framed through the lens of DDI. Employing a Grounded Theory (GT) approach, specifically the systematic coding methodology of Strauss and Corbin, this research gathered rich qualitative data through in-depth, semi-structured interviews with HR Analytics and Business Analytics experts operating within the Iranian organizational context. Data analysis, facilitated by MAXQDA, involved rigorous open, axial, and selective coding until theoretical saturation was achieved, with study rigor confirmed via Lincoln and Guba's criteria. The resulting conceptual model elucidates the complex interplay of causal conditions (e.g., transformation in human resource management, data-driven approach), context (e.g., technology adoption, cultural contexts), strategies (pre-adoption, decision-making, adoption phases), intervening obstacles, and possible outcomes. By highlighting the contextual features of the Iranian economic environment, this model offers a coherent framework to assist private enterprises in comparable settings to more effectively navigate their transition toward data-driven HR management, offering insights for organizations aiming to leverage HR Analytics as a driver for strategic innovation and business value enhancement. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Sarısoy Ö.; Kurt G.
Title: Rethinking Accounting Culture: Classical Theories and Contemporary Debates
Source title: Accounting, Finance, Sustainability, Governance and Fraud
Abstract: This study analyzes the theoretical foundations of the concept of “accounting culture” and its evolution over time. Using a theoretical analysis and a comparative approach, this methodology reveals the paradigmatic shifts that have occurred within the literature on the relationship between culture and accounting. The research identifies an evolution from early models that viewed culture as a “direct determinant” of accounting systems to models in which culture’s influence becomes “indirect,” mediated by variables such as “corporate governance” or the “external environment.” It further analyzes how this evolution has continued with economic–institutional approaches, in which the role of culture in the adoption of global standards such as IAS/IFRS has become “secondary,” giving way to “economic rationality.” The research also discusses how current global developments have accelerated this paradigmatic transformation. These new dynamics have been found to challenge local cultural tendencies while increasing the explanatory power of economic and institutional models. In conclusion, the study demonstrates that accounting culture is not a static determinant but a dynamic concept that continually evolves through interactions with global economic and social dynamics. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Authors: Mukherjee S.; Mukherjee S.; Cheng T.C.E.
Author full names: Mukherjee, Soumyatanu (56349236300); Mukherjee, Sayan (57950748800); Cheng, T.C. Edwin (60239632300)
Title: Operational disruption, resource reconfiguration, and AI integration in hospital equipment-as-a-service operations
Abstract: This study examines how disruption exposure relates to adaptive responses in hospital Equipment-as-a-Service (EaaS) operations, focusing on resource reconfiguration and the depth of AI workflow embedding. Drawing on the dynamic capabilities view, supported by resource orchestration logic and a behavioral theory of the firm lens, we test a disruption-to-adaptation framework in which disruption exposure is associated with resource reconfiguration and AI integration, while technical complexity and trust condition these relationships. We use a field-grounded, between-subjects, scenario-based role-playing experiment with 320 hospital decision-makers from India-based hospitals across Bihar, Maharashtra, and West Bengal. The scenarios were developed from field engagements documenting disruption episodes involving CT outages, network delays, patient surges, staffing bottlenecks, and vendor coordination. The results show positive associations of disruption exposure with resource reconfiguration and AI integration. Resource reconfiguration is, in turn, positively associated with AI integration, and a supplementary indirect-effect analysis identifies it as a significant complementary pathway that accounts for approximately 18.6% of the total association linking disruption exposure to deeper AI embedding. Technical complexity strengthens the relationships of disruption exposure with both resource reconfiguration and AI integration. Trust strengthens the direct relationship between disruption exposure and AI integration but does not significantly alter the relationship between reconfiguration and AI integration. The findings contribute to production and service operations research by showing that AI-enabled service platforms support disruption response not merely through technological sophistication, but through timely reconfiguration of workflows, roles, and coordination routines. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Li T.; Lu Y.; Zhang M.M.; Yang M.M.; Wang Y.; Yi L.
Title: From institutional pressures to employee involvement in organizational sustainability: The role of common good HRM
Abstract: Employee involvement in organizational sustainability is critical to achieving long-term environmental, social, and economic goals, yet the drivers of such involvement remain underexplored. Drawing on institutional theory and social exchange theory, this study develops a cross-level serial mediation model to explain how institutional sustainability pressures may become associated with employee involvement in organizational sustainability. We propose that institutional pressures, as perceived by senior executives, are associated with employee-experienced common good human resource management (CG-HRM), which in turn relates to perceived organizational support and, subsequently, employee involvement in organizational sustainability. Using time-lagged, multisource survey data from 96 firms in China, we find support for the proposed model. The findings contribute a more micro-foundational account of how institutional sustainability pressures, as perceived by senior executives, may become meaningful at the employee level through organizational and psychological processes, and clarify the role of employee-experienced CG-HRM in explaining employee sustainability-related behavior. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Wilson M.S.
Title: The crypto risk puzzle
Source title: North American Journal of Economics and Finance
Abstract: I compare Ethereum and Bitcoin. Ethereum is too tightly correlated with Bitcoin to be a good hedge. It is also riskier than Bitcoin and often fails to generate a higher rate of return. With a Dynamic Conditional Correlation (DCC) GARCH model, I demonstrate that there are predictable periods when Ethereum’s expected risk is higher and its expected rate of return is lower. This happens in about half the sample. Nevertheless, Ethereum is still a popular asset and it has the second highest market capitalization of all cryptocurrencies. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Inc.
