Authors: Liao R.; Rao H.R.
Title: Was I scammed? Understanding consumer scam reporting behavior through cognitive appraisal
Abstract: Underreporting has been hampering regulatory efforts due to consumers’ hesitance to report ambiguous unsatisfactory transactions, particularly in online marketplaces or consumer services where deceptive business practices are uncertain or difficult to prove. This study examines how consumers appraise harm, effort, and resolution uncertainty when deciding whether to respond to potential scams. Drawing on Cognitive Appraisal Theory and Consumer Complaint Behavior, we develop and test a dual-pathway model that explains when victims pursue private action (e.g., contacting the seller) or public action (e.g., filing a complaint). Using nationally representative data from the U.S. Federal Trade Commission's 2017 fraud survey, we show that financial loss, perceived effort, outcome uncertainty, and their interactions jointly shape complaint behavior. We find that private action is driven by restitution motives and is amplified in high-loss or online scenarios, where it is perceived as a low-cost first step. Public action, by contrast, is less influenced by financial stakes and more by confidence in evidence, reflecting a justice-seeking mindset. This research contributes to the theoretical understanding of consumer behavior after perceived scam experiences by adopting long-standing marketing and consumer behavior theories and offers practical managerial insights by shifting the focus from victim profiling to behavioral process modeling. Our findings highlight the need for system-level interventions such as standardized dispute mechanisms, centralized complaint portals, and structured evidence logs to reduce harm and improve reporting confidence in scam-prone “gray areas.” © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: A Hybrid LLM-Based Framework for Automated Security Annotation Generation in Business Process Models
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: The modelling and analysis of secure business processes require the incorporation of security annotations into process models. Although BPMN extensions, including SecBPMN2, exist for this purpose, the derivation of accurate and complete security annotations from natural-language specifications remains a manual, expert-intensive, and error-prone task. This paper presents a hybrid framework that takes a BPMN process model and a security requirements document as input and automatically generates security annotations adhering to the SecBPMN2 specification. The approach combines Large Language Model (LLM)–based semantic extraction with schema-constrained mapping, rule-based normalization, and deterministic validation. The framework is evaluated comprehensively on a curated dataset of 27 process models from various domains. The results indicate that it consistently produces structurally valid SecBPMN2 annotations with high schema completeness. Compared to human security analysts, the system achieves substantially higher precision (0.58 vs. 0.29) while maintaining comparable recall (0.52 vs. 0.50) and reduces erroneous or misplaced annotations by nearly 50%. In addition, annotation generation is significantly faster than manual annotation. These findings demonstrate that hybrid LLM- and rule-based automation can reduce modeling effort while improving consistency and reliability, thereby providing a scalable foundation for security-by-design BPM. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Qi Y.; Agag G.
Title: Empowered generative artificial intelligence in retail service recovery: Recovery justice, customer effort reduction, trust restoration, and purchase behaviour
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Retailers increasingly deploy generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) to handle complaints, yet evidence remains limited on when these agents restore purchasing rather than merely improve immediate evaluations. We develop a configuration model in which recovery agent identity (GenAI versus human) is separated from recovery agent empowerment, defined as authority to complete a remedy during the encounter. Across a qualitative study, two pretests, two randomised experiments, and two secondary-data studies in United Kingdom retailing, we examine perceived recovery justice, customer effort reduction, and trust restoration as mechanisms linking recovery configurations to subsequent behaviour. The experiments capture an incentivised purchase choice, whereas the field studies observe repeat purchase, spending, time to next purchase, and churn. GenAI was not inherently superior to a human agent. Its advantage emerged when it had visible and executable authority to issue refunds, replacements, delivery upgrades, or account credits. Empowered GenAI improved justice, reduced effort, and restored trust, and generated the strongest purchase outcomes. Failure severity weakened this advantage, while customer relationship strength amplified both the penalty for low-empowerment GenAI and the reward for empowered GenAI. The study contributes an authority-identity decoupling perspective: customers respond not only to who communicates, but also to whether the recovery architecture gives that agent the data access, decision rights, and operational capability required to act. The findings support selective empowerment for routine failures and accountable hybrid escalation for severe or data-constrained cases. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Peer benchmarking and digital upgrading: Field experiments on business websites
Abstract: Can low-cost comparative information trigger firms to improve the performance of a digital asset they already own? Using two large-scale randomised controlled trials with approximately 7000 UK firms in the distilling and retail sectors, we study whether peer benchmarking of website performance prompts measurable improvement. Firms receiving benchmarked website metrics and targeted recommendations exhibit modest average improvements, with more favourable effects among initially underperforming firms, consistent with partial convergence towards the industry frontier. The catch-up dynamic is strongest on mobile metrics, including as a spillover in the first experiment, in which reports contained desktop metrics only, a pattern consistent with firms focusing improvement efforts where performance gaps are greatest. Treated firms also show suggestive report-aligned increases in the adoption of mobile-optimisation and content-delivery technologies. These patterns are consistent with comparative performance information helping firms identify and respond to performance shortfalls. The findings position peer benchmarking as a scalable, low-cost instrument for narrowing the digital divide among SMEs: informational aspiration cues generate more favourable responses among firms furthest behind than among firms nearer the frontier. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Object-Centric Process Querying in SQL: Translation Rules and In-Database Execution
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Object-Centric Process Querying (OCPQ) is a visual query language and accompanying tool for expressing queries and constraints over Object-Centric Event Data (OCED). Such queries span multiple object and event types that case-centric query languages cannot natively address. Its existing execution engine processes data in memory: Dataset size is capped by host memory, and the relational database systems that organizations already operate cannot serve as backends, forcing data export or migration. In this paper, we present a translation from OCPQ to SQL, defined as a recursive mapping over the OCPQ query tree with a rule per construct, emitting SQL for SQLite, DuckDB, and PostgreSQL. An OCEL 2.0 Virtualization Layer accommodates source schemas that diverge from the OCEL 2.0 layout via direct rewrite or VIEW generation, so the translation can target them without data migration. We evaluate using three types of workloads: Seven queries from prior work, an automatically generated corpus of 6919 OCPQ trees, and a non-OCEL Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) database schema queried through the virtualization layer. The resulting query outputs match the in-memory engine across all queries, demonstrating that the translation preserves its semantics. Our evaluation also shows the memory decoupling enabled by the translation: SQL backends scale to support large datasets on which the native OCPQ engine runs out of memory. When data fits in memory, the in-memory OCPQ engine remains fastest, with DuckDB roughly 3–12× slower and PostgreSQL 14–71× slower as drop-in replacements. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Green debt for nature-based solutions: aligning municipal budgeting and banking practices
Abstract: Local governments face growing risks from climate change, which require substantial investments in climate adaptation to safeguard future generations. Nature-based solutions (NBS) have been recognized as a cost-efficient strategy to redevelop public space, to create greener and more climate adaptive urban environments. However, development of NBS is hindered by a lack of financial resources to fully scale up the transformation. To overcome this barrier, literature calls for clear sustainable finance frameworks and business model approaches to include private financing in the development of public NBS. In our research we consider the perceptions of municipalities and banks, as institutional lenders, towards using green debt-financing to finance NBS. We draw on sustainability transitions literature to theorize NBS as a niche innovation within established banking-municipal relations. Using qualitative interviews with Belgian banking experts and urban and financial planners from Flemish cities, we reveal competing financial logics between municipal financing practices and banking requirements, limiting the uptake of green debt for NBS. While NBS are mostly absorbed in traditional municipal deficit financing, this conceals their value and prevents market development. Alternatively, project finance remains difficult due to capacity constraints and differing valuation logics. Emerging sustainable finance frameworks create opportunities but shift administrative burdens onto municipalities. Overall, current practices mainly support NBS to fit and conform, rather than transform established debt-practices. Substantial upscaling of NBS will require changes in both banking practices and municipal financing approaches, including explicit integration of physical climate risk and collective financing mechanisms. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Rethinking conscientiousness in supervisor-subordinate dynamics: impacts on employee thriving
Abstract: Organizations prize Conscientiousness, yet our research reveals a paradox: pairing two highly conscientious individuals may undermine employee thriving. Drawing on Dominance Complementarity Theory and Goal-Setting Theory, we conducted two multi-wave, multi-source field studies involving 157 supervisors and 584 subordinates. Cross-level polynomial regression and response surface analyses revealed three key findings. First, high–high Conscientiousness alignment consistently suppressed subordinate vitality, indicating a potential relational cost. Second, thriving was highest under asymmetric complementarity: subordinates high in Conscientiousness thrived most when paired with low-Conscientiousness supervisors. Third, the effects of Conscientiousness alignment on learning varied across contexts, with high–high alignment constraining learning in structured work (Study 1) but enhancing learning in less structured roles (Study 2). Goal clarity mediated linear alignment effects but did not explain vitality suppression, suggesting alternative interpersonal mechanisms. These findings challenge the assumption that “similarity is always beneficial” and highlight the importance of a contingent, dyadic approach to Conscientiousness. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Title: Digital transformation and supply chain Resilience: Inverted U-shaped effect and mechanisms with dual Moderation—Evidence from China’s A-share listed firms
Abstract: Against the background of rising global supply chain risks and deepening digital transformation, this study draws on the resource-based view and dynamic capabilities perspective and uses data from Chinese A-share listed firms from 2013 to 2023 to examine the effect of digital transformation on supply chain resilience. Findings reveal a significant inverted U-shaped effect: moderate levels of digital transformation strengthen supply chain resilience, whereas excessive levels of digital transformation weaken it. Absorptive, innovative, and adaptive capabilities partially mediate this nonlinear effect. Further analysis shows R&D intensity steepens the inverted U-shaped curve, whereas firm size flattens it. Moreover, the inverted U-shaped effect is more pronounced among firms in regions with higher factor market development and among firms with higher supply chain concentration and lower financing constraints. These findings help firms identify an effective range of digital transformation based on their capabilities and resources and inform differentiated government support policies. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Inc.

Title: Deployment-Sovereign AI Infrastructure for BPM Education: An Open-Source Stack from Document Analysis to Process Execution
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: This paper investigates whether deployment-sovereign AI infrastructure can support BPM education without dependence on commercial LLM APIs. We assembled an open-source teaching stack combining PCSS-hosted open-weight models, Flowise/Qdrant retrieval-augmented generation, n8n workflow orchestration, and the CIB Seven BPMN engine. In the tested PCSS deployment, all five open-weight models completed the high-sensitivity corpus without API errors or policy refusals. A preliminary, non-blinded expert assessment found no obvious quality deficit for routine BPM documentation tasks, but does not establish statistical equivalence to commercial models. Title: Understanding the dark side of relative mindfulness: The moderating roles of job demands and job control
Abstract: Mindfulness benefits employee functioning in the workplace. However, little is known about whether relative mindfulness (i.e., an employee’s mindfulness compared to the average mindfulness in the work team) influences focal employees’ interpersonal behaviors. To address this knowledge gap, we draw on social comparison theory and the job demands-control model to suggest that higher relative mindfulness is positively related to focal employees’ hostility towards coworkers. In turn, hostility would trigger their negative interpersonal behaviors (i.e., counterproductive work behavior towards coworkers and incivility towards customers). Job demands and job control play a moderating role in the above relationships, such that a higher level of job demands and a lower level of job control strengthen the positive effect of relative mindfulness on hostility towards coworkers and its indirect effects on behavioral reactions. Title: How virtual reality presence experiences engage online visitors in actual destination: a dual-path model
Abstract: While virtual reality (VR) presence experiences have transformed how online visitors engage with destinations, their psychological mechanisms remain underexplored. Drawing on the elaboration likelihood model, we develop a dual-path model to reveal pathways of two presence experiences (realistic and immersive) that are elicited by distinct visualization modes (panoramic and modeled). Study 2 (n = 205) further supported the proposed dual-path model. For the direct realism path, panoramic VR generates higher realistic presence that promotes visit intention directly. As for the indirect immersion path, modeled VR creates greater immersive presence, influencing visit intention indirectly, mediated by psychological closeness. This contributes a nuanced perspective on how VR shapes visitor behaviors. Practically, we offer a strategic framework for enhancing VR experiences that align with specific persuasion goals, whether to facilitate decision-making directly or to engage visitors through psychological closeness. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Title: Inside out: cutting-edge methods to decode external opportunities for startup growth
Abstract: We examine how both internal resources and the external environment influence startup growth, addressing the challenge of measuring the knowledge structure in which the startup operates. Title: From classroom confidence to workplace readiness: Reimagining future skills development in higher education
Abstract: Global megatrends such as demographic change, digitalization, and climate change are transforming the nature of work and increasing the importance of future skills and lifelong learning. These transferable, often non-technical skills enable individuals to navigate complexity, uncertainty, and continuous change.Despite their recognized importance, a persistent gap remains between what higher education develops and what employers expect. This study investigates that gap by comparing students’ self-assessments of future skills with qualitative evaluations from internship supervisors. Using a mixed-methods design and a scenario-based self-assessment tool grounded in real-world work situations, we examine both perceived readiness and demonstrated skill application.The findings show that students are confident in performing clearly defined tasks, particularly those involving information processing and communication, but are less prepared to take initiative, apply skills in complex contexts, and act proactively. The key challenge lies not only in possession of skills, but also in their activation, application, and transfer to real-world contexts. These findings suggest that higher education should move beyond structured learning environments and incorporate more complex, unstructured, and practice-oriented experiences to foster proactive capability.This study contributes to futures-oriented research by shifting the focus from skill possession to how individuals actively engage with and shape uncertain and evolving work environments through proactive behaviour. Authors: Řepa V.
Title: The Logic of Processed Events in Human Processes
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: The paper investigates the logical structure of event processing in human processes, emphasizing the unique characteristics of events defined by their meaning, temporal ordering, and exclusivity. Drawing on the framework of MMABP (a methodological approach prioritizing event granularity based on purpose-driven semantics), the paper formalizes the equivalence between event implication (ε ⇒ φ) and logical equivalence (ε ≡ φ) in human-centric processes. This conclusion arises from the necessity of exclusive, time-ordered resolution in human processes, where disjunctive decisions are modeled as XOR logic. The paper further contrasts this logic with OntoUML’s system-centric event modeling, highlighting key differences in event uniqueness, exclusivity, and human-centric focus. By establishing a rigorous, human-centric framework for event processing, the paper provides theoretical foundations for designing event-driven algorithms, ensuring unambiguous resolution in workflows, business processes, and human-machine interactions. The paper also explores implications for process modeling, emphasizing the integration of temporal constraints, exclusive event relationships, and human intent in system frameworks. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Li H.; Yang Y.
Title: Can linguistic vagueness in annual reports predict supply chain risk?
Abstract: Annual reports serve as a critical information channel for corporate stakeholders, especially for supply chain partners. We argue that linguistic vagueness in these reports can function as an early-warning signal for predicting supply chain risk. To test our proposition, we develop a theory-grounded measure of linguistic vagueness by integrating communication vagueness theory with the Word2Vec method. Our analysis of publicly listed companies in China reveals a robust positive association between linguistic vagueness and subsequent supply chain risk. Heterogeneity analyses indicate that this predictive capacity varies under different reputational pressures. Furthermore, by employing interpretable machine learning approaches within an out-of-sample predictive framework, we validate the consistent directional predictive signal via SHAP analysis and solidify the indicator’s predictive robustness. Ultimately, this study establishes linguistic vagueness as an incremental signal that carries significant out-of-sample predictive value for supply chain risk, providing stakeholders with a data-driven approach for proactive risk monitoring. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Title: Co-creation in sustainable family entrepreneurship
Abstract: This study examines how co-creation unfolds in sustainable family entrepreneurship across nine co-creation cases in two family firms in Mexico and Colombia. The findings identify three aggregate dimensions of sustainable family co-creation: family sustainable drivers and motivations, family sustainable management and control, and family co-created sustainable outcomes. These dimensions operate through six mechanisms: generating a shared view, conveying different interpretations, family coupling, family decoupling, family inclusion, and family separation. Title: Upframing customer vulnerability through a circle of strength
Abstract: This editorial introduces the Circle of Strength framework to move beyond an individual-deficit view of vulnerability toward understanding the circumstances in which customers experience susceptibility to harm. Title: AI-Based Data Analytics in Public Administration: A Conceptual Model of Organizational Constraints
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: The increasing integration of AI-based data analytics in public administration is significantly transforming organizational decision-making, knowledge management, and public service delivery. Title: Simulating Dynamic Relationships in Object-Centric Processes
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Several Business Process Simulation techniques have been proposed to generate case-based event logs. However, an accurate description of many real-world processes requires modeling the interdependent objects that participate in them, leading to the rapid growth of object-centric process mining. Title: Teaching Declarative BPM: Where, When and to Whom it Matters

Title: Managing geopolitical risk in global supply chains: A qualitative study of European multinational enterprises
Abstract: Geopolitical risk has emerged as a major disruptive risk to global supply chains and the operations of multinational enterprises (MNEs) today. Drawing on a qualitative content analysis of the annual reports of 20 European MNEs across five industries, supported by a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline, this study examines how companies strategically manage geopolitical risk in their supply chains. We extend an established supply chain risk framework by conceptualizing geopolitical risk management (GRM) as a distinct strategic risk management dimension centered on reducing geopolitical exposure, in contrast to supply chain risk management (SCRM), which enhances operational resilience within existing supply chain structures. Applying this distinction, we identify seven key GRM strategies, including localization, decentralized procurement and R&D, direct sourcing, supplier diversification, geographical production diversification, circular economy initiatives, and political engagement. Furthermore, applying the Triple-P framework in a disclosure-based setting suggests that companies facing different forms of supply chain complexity across the partnership, product, and process dimensions disclose distinct portfolios of GRM strategies. The findings of this study provide cross-industry insights into the strategic orientation of large European MNEs and support managerial decision making to strengthen resilience in the face of supply chain and geopolitical risk. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Digital twins for operations and supply chain management: definitions, theoretical foundations and avenues for further study
Abstract: The burgeoning discourse surrounding digital twins (DTs) has reached a critical point that requires the careful examination of the disparity between their conceptual idealisation and empirical reality. Title: Using Process Mining to Generate AI Agents from Software Engineering Process Records
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Integrating AI agents into Software Engineering (SE) raises an important challenge: how can we specify and realize AI agents that work effectively alongside humans in hybrid SE teams? Title: Product social currency: Conceptualization, measurement and nomological validity
Abstract: The marketplace increasingly values products that function as social currency, yet the existing literature lacks a blueprint for understanding the attributes that characterize these products. PSC also predicted word-of-mouth within a broader nomological network. Title: State ownership, media sentiment, and the completion of cross-border acquisitions
Abstract: Media sentiment plays an important but underexamined role in shaping the completion of cross-border acquisitions (CBAs) by state-owned enterprise (SOE) acquirers. Title: A Conflict Index Based on Inducement Correspondences and Its Application to 2 × 2 Game Classification
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Two-person, two-strategy games provide a simple yet powerful framework for analyzing situations in which the interests of the parties can be partly aligned and partly opposed. Title: Bridging the pitch and the canvas: Synergistic insights for advancing empirical research a pre-registered report
Abstract: High-quality empirical research depends on guidance tools that are structured, coherent, and lifecycle-spanning. Abstract: Front-of-Pack Nutritional Labels (FOPLs) are usually examined as consumer information tools or public-health disclosures. Title: Does public data openness mitigate asset mispricing?

Title: Low-carbon economic transition uncertainty and corporate financialization
Source title: North American Journal of Economics and Finance
Abstract: This study explores the intricate relationship between low-carbon economic transition uncertainty (LETU) and corporate financialization. Title: How government data openness mitigates policy uncertainty effects on corporate investment

Title: When employees mistreat service robots: Customer moral reactions, behavioral contagion, and service provider evaluation

Abstract: Service robots are increasingly visible in frontline service encounters, yet little is known about how customers respond when they observe employees mistreating these robots. The findings further show that robot anthropomorphism attenuates the erosion of perceived injunctive norms, whereas customer moral identity weakens the translation of weakened norms into mistreatment intentions. Title: Semantic similarity score: A new method for mapping intellectual structures in business research

Title: The power of the present in building organizational resilience
Abstract: Organizational resilience scholars increasingly recognize that time matters; however, the operative present in which executives anticipate, absorb, recover from, and learn from adversity remains underspecified. Title: Toward sustainable maritime logistics with electric reach stackers: A spherical fuzzy decision-making framework

Title: Lending in Need: Natural Disaster Shocks and Online Borrowing in Indonesia

Title: Out of space? How human density influences satisfaction in premium services
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Purpose: This study examines how human density in premium servicescapes influences customer satisfaction through two opposing routes, using airport lounges as the empirical setting. At the same time, density retains a smaller positive association with satisfaction, consistent with the possibility that the presence of others may generate social value in premium settings. Title: Aggregate fluctuations from firm comovement

Title: Uncertainty and tail spillovers: Dynamic connectedness between DeFi tokens and BRICS equity markets
Abstract: This paper investigates the dynamic connectedness between four decentralized finance (DeFi) tokens (LINK, MKR, SNX, and BAT) and BRICS equity markets from March 15, 2018, to June 30, 2023, covering the pre-COVID period, the COVID-19 pandemic, and the Russia-Ukraine conflict. Title: How digital human capital investment drives AI innovation in tourism and hospitality firms: The roles of data assets and TMT stability

Title: Does concentrated ownership structure affect ESG disclosure? Role of corporate life cycle and market competition

Title: Editorial Introduction: Designing Lives: The Rise of Entrepreneurial Life Design

Abstract: This editorial introduction positions Entrepreneurial Life Design (ELD) as an emerging interdisciplinary field at the intersection of entrepreneurship education, Life Design, and human development. Title: Process-Aware Design of Just-In-Time Adaptive Interventions: An Object-Centric Perspective

Title: The direction of generosity: The effect of ascending versus descending tip displays on gratuities

Title: Entrepreneurial bankruptcy as a career-sorting event: income trajectories, re-entry, and risk-taking
Abstract: Entrepreneurial bankruptcy is a salient failure event, yet little is known about its association with subsequent income trajectories and career paths. Title: From breakdown to breakthrough: How entrepreneurs craft vulnerability narratives on social media
Abstract: Entrepreneurial narratives are widely understood as strategic tools for building legitimacy and mobilizing resources. Our analysis reveals that women entrepreneurs hold multiple and coexisting motivations for disclosure - self-oriented, relational, and normative - oscillating between them as needed, while developing narrative-crafting tactics that sustain the benefits of sharing while managing interpersonal risks. Title: Comparative Analysis of Volatility in Green Cryptocurrencies Versus Conventional Cryptocurrencies

Abstract: By introducing decentralised financial systems as a critical factor, cryptocurrencies have altered and enhanced the financial industry dramatically. Authors: Lin Q.; He L.
Title: Is competition good or bad for employee innovation? Examining the double-edged sword effect of team and individual responses
Abstract: Amid an increasingly competitive environment, fostering innovation among employees has emerged as a central concern for both academia and the business community. Drawing upon the conservation of resources (COR) theory, this study develops a multi-level framework to examine the underlying mechanisms and boundary conditions of competitive psychological climate (CPC) on employees' innovative work behavior. By gathering data from 386 hotel employees and their leaders spanning 60 teams throughout four provinces along China's southeastern coast, the results indicated that CPC facilitated employees' innovative work behavior by increasing team cooperative orientation (i.e., resource-gain pathway); simultaneously, it inhibited innovative work behavior by eliciting workplace anxiety (i.e., resource-depletion pathway). Furthermore, psychological capital buffered the resource-depletion pathway, while error tolerance reinforced the resource-gain pathway. The results advance theoretical insight into CPC's dual influence mechanism and offer practical guidance for motivating employees to innovate in the highly competitive hospitality sector. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: When automation hurts and when it helps: A context-contingent model of emotional burden and uplift across unmanned retail formats

Abstract: Why does the same unmanned retail technology produce different emotional responses across formats? Title: U.S.-China tensions and systemic risk transmission across asset classes: New evidence from a TVP-VAR connectedness framework
Abstract: This paper examines how U.S.-China bilateral tensions have evolved in the transmission of systemic risk across major asset classes. However, in the trade war and COVID-19 pandemic period, the Chinese market and gold emerged as the dominant transmitters of systemic risk, while the UCT Index transitioned from a shock originator to a more passive role, suggesting that it reflects periods of systemic financial stress more than it directly drives them, with its influence remaining generally mild and time-dependent. Title: AI-Driven Automation in Knowledge-Intensive License Management: An Empirical Analysis of Enterprise Constraints and Automation Potential
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Software License Management (SLM) is a complex, Knowledge-Intensive Process (KiP) in which fragmented data, heterogeneous IT landscapes, and frequent vendor audits contribute to significant process governance gaps, reducing organizational agility and increasing contractual and financial risk exposure. The findings reveal that traditional rule-based systems fail to address the dynamic nature of license governance, leaving the SLM undermanaged despite growing financial exposure. To bridge the design–emergence gap, this study presents three process governance-oriented design principles for Agentic BPM: lifecycle visibility, cross-functional coordination, and human-in-the-loop oversight. Title: From social disconnection to brand voice: Identity reconstruction and consumer engagement in brand activism
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Brand activism is a major way companies are getting involved in societal issues, but the conditions on the consumer side that drive engagement are not well understood. Title: The DNA of Accounting Culture: The Role of Auditor Profiles in Ethical Decision-Making Behaviors
Source title: Accounting, Finance, Sustainability, Governance and Fraud
Abstract: The present study employs a person-centered analytical approach to examine the influence of accounting culture values on auditors’ ethical decision-making. Title: Ontology-Guided Hybrid Intelligence for Diagnosing Underspecification in Reporting Standards

Abstract: Business reporting standards such as International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) are high-impact business-rule artifacts whose clauses often compress evidence, institutional structure, recognition, measurement, and presentation into single surface labels. Title: Is the relationship between climate policy uncertainty and cash holding nonlinear?

Abstract: As climate-related risks intensify and environmental policy becomes increasingly uncertain, understanding how firms adjust their financial policies to climate policy uncertainty has become increasingly important. Title: Consumer vulnerability in artificial intelligence-driven marketing: A paradox theory lens
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming marketing through hyper-personalization, predictive analytics and enhanced customer experience, yet its ethical implications for consumer vulnerability remain undertheorized. Title: The power of virtual identities: How priming actual and ideal selves shapes cool brand preference

Abstract: Consumers increasingly use virtual identities to represent their actual or ideal selves on social media platforms. Title: Consumer decision patterns in sustainable mobility: A cross-cultural digital perspective

Title: Measuring Inequalities in Well-Being: A Three-Way Approach with Applications to Italy and the European Union

Title: Process Externalities: A Missing Construct for Responsible BPM

Abstract: Responsible Business Process Management (RBPM) asks the discipline to account for the effects of processes on stakeholders, society, and the environment. Title: Investment irreversibility in a granular world

Title: Unveiling the black box: How source transparency shapes GenAI-driven hotel recommendation adoption
Abstract: The proliferation of GenAI in hotel recommendation services has spurred inquiries into the impact of source transparency on consumers. This research investigates how GenAI hotel recommendation source transparency influences consumer adoption, focusing on the roles of perceived authenticity, perceived manipulation, regulatory focus, and negative e-WOM. Employing a multi-method approach involving a field experiment collaborating with a hotel and two online experiments, we find that higher source transparency increases recommendation adoption through greater perceived authenticity and reduced perceived manipulation, especially for prevention-focused consumers. Furthermore, when negative content is present in recommendations, high transparency enhances adoption regardless of regulatory focus, whereas this effect diminishes when no negative content is shown. These findings offer theoretical insights into the psychological mechanisms underlying GenAI-driven hotel recommendations. From a practical perspective, they offer actionable strategies for hotels and recommendation system designers to refine their services, thereby improving consumer acceptance in the context of GenAI-powered hotel recommendations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Dai L.; Tu R.; Li J.
Title: How AI service persona drift erodes consumer trust through relationship discontinuity
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Conversational agents are becoming a central interface for retail customer service. As these systems are updated and reconfigured, consumers may perceive the same branded AI service interface as communicating less continuously across service episodes. We define this phenomenon as service persona drift perception, or perceived changes in an AI service interface's persona cues across encounters. Expectancy violation theory is used to explain why such perceived drift becomes psychologically consequential. We propose a service interface-based mechanism in which persona drift undermines consumer trust by increasing relationship discontinuity. Relationship discontinuity refers to the perception that the current service episode no longer follows the interaction pattern established in prior encounters with the same branded AI service interface. Evidence from three studies with adult online shoppers supports this account using controlled service episode stimuli that hold factual information, service process, and solution outcomes constant while varying persona cues. Study 1 shows that persona drift increases relationship discontinuity and reduces trust, with discontinuity carrying the indirect effect. Study 2 demonstrates that these effects are stronger among consumers with higher customer relationship investment, defined as accumulated behavioral, resource based, and psychological stakes in the brand relationship. Study 3 extends the findings to behavioral outcomes by incorporating a simulated decision task. Persona drift increases the likelihood of choosing human handoff and elevates exit intention, with the latter operating through the sequential process linking discontinuity and trust. Overall, the results show that perceived persona discontinuity can weaken trust and increase escalation and withdrawal responses even when service outcomes remain unchanged. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Ju C.; Li K.; Xu C.; Liu H.
Title: A patent-driven SCOR-IFCM framework to prioritize generative AI adoption for supply chain resilience
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI) has considerable potential to enhance supply chain resilience (SCR), but its effective adoption remains subject to technological uncertainty. This study integrates BERTopic, the Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) model, intuitionistic fuzzy sets (IFS), and clamped intuitionistic fuzzy cognitive map (IFCM) simulation to develop a patent-driven framework for screening and prioritizing potential Gen AI applications. Based on 139,661 Gen AI patent abstracts associated with Chinese listed firms, the framework identifies 870 fine-grained technology topics, maps them onto 29 SCOR-oriented nodes, and uses patent-text evidence to construct a technology propagation structure and a 29×5 technology-performance allocation matrix. Four main findings emerge. First, patent portfolio analysis focuses on enabling, data-processing, and infrastructure capabilities, with semantic evidence linking these capabilities to SCR dimensions such as reliability, responsiveness, agility, cost, and asset management. Second, counter- and unresolved evidence reveal constraining pathways, with negative propagation concentrated in limited cross-node relationships. Third, sustained support for selected driver nodes creates selective spillovers rather than uniform gains; under the soft-clamped scenario, engineering quality and progress management, order lifecycle management, and intelligent logistics path planning achieve the highest non-driver activation. Fourth, SCOR contributions depend jointly on steady-state activation and patent-semantic associations, so strong semantic support alone does not guarantee high modeled contribution. Overall, the framework provides patent-evidence-based decision support for screening candidate technologies, prioritizing staged evaluation, and comparing conditional SCOR performance profiles. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Beyond psychology and environment explanations: a linguistic microfoundation approach to entrepreneurs’ anxiety
Abstract: We offer a novel theoretical account of why entrepreneurs experience anxiety and how entrepreneurs cope with anxiety. We integrate insights from linguistic theories into entrepreneurship literature to propose that entrepreneurs’ linguistic architecture—particularly the vocabulary their language provides for identifying and describing emotions (i.e., its emotion lexicon)—is an essential linguistic microfoundation that systematically shapes how entrepreneurs process and experience anxiety. As moderators, we examine how bilingualism and entrepreneurial experience can systematically alter how entrepreneurs’ linguistic architecture influences their anxiety. Our final sample was 1,251 entrepreneurs speaking 14 different languages, supplemented by an experimental study with 202 bilingual entrepreneurs in Hong Kong. We find that entrepreneurs with a richer vocabulary for identifying and describing emotions (i.e., a richer emotion lexicon) heighten anxiety due to more precise and vivid emotional processing, and bilingualism weakens, yet prior entrepreneurial experience strengthens the positive effect of emotion lexicon on anxiety. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Natural Language Querying for Large Declarative Rule Repositories
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: In organizations, business processes are constrained by a large number of business rules that can, for example, be represented as process models, declarative constraints, or textual descriptions. When executing, auditing, or managing these processes, users may face specific questions that can only be answered by the declarative business rules that apply in this exact scenario. Non-technical users may only be able to specify their requirements in natural language queries, which need to be answered by specific business rules. However, the efficient matching between the natural language user query and the appropriate declarative business rules is not trivial because rules should be identified based on semantic similarity to the query, which may include synonyms and domain-specific technical terms. In this paper, we propose a system design that combines state-of-the-art technologies, namely Large Language Models, Vector Databases, and Retrieval Augmented Generation, to support cost-efficient natural language querying on large declarative rule repositories to identify appropriate rules. Title: Beyond reviews: Operating-environment cues and consumer decision making on digital service platforms
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: As consumers face growing uncertainty about the credibility of online reviews, an important question is how they continue to evaluate service providers on digital platforms. This study examines how consumers make booking judgments on restaurant platforms when the credibility of peer-generated evaluative cues is weakened. Two studies test the proposed conditional cue-use logic. Study 1 uses Yelp archival data to examine how PEC credibility, operational information disclosure, environmental cleanliness, and environmental orderliness relate to booking-intention-related archival responses. Study 2 uses a 2 x 2 scenario-based experiment manipulating PEC credibility and FOECs and tests the role of Perceived Diagnosticity of FOECs. Title: The Transformative Impact of Prosthetics on Well-being of Consumers with Disabilities
Abstract: Technologies that restore or substitute human functions increasingly shape how consumers with disabilities access and navigate service systems. Yet marketing and service research has largely focused on human enhancement or interpersonal encounters, overlooking technologies as active enablers of well-being. Integrating insights from Transformative Service Research, disability research, and Human Enhancement Technology research, this paper advances a prosthetic perspective that conceptualizes technologies as service-enabling systems supporting self-directed action in physical and virtual servicescapes. Distinguishing physical, hybrid, and virtual prosthetic service realities reveals how these configure transformative mechanisms (i.e., empowerment, participation, and inclusion). A focus on more virtual prosthetic service realities further demonstrates how these mechanisms extend in scale and scope and can enable spillover from virtual to physical well-being. The paper concludes with a research agenda that invites scholars to examine how prosthetic service realities may mitigate structurally disabling servicescapes and promote individual, collective, and societal well-being. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Mind your breath: Air pollution and return manipulation
Abstract: This study examines the causal effect of air pollution on mutual fund managers' portfolio pumping using a large sample of Chinese mutual funds. We find that higher air pollution significantly increases portfolio pumping. Mechanism test shows that pollution induces short-term opportunistic behavior through elevated portfolio turnover, which facilitates return manipulation. This effect is stronger when peer monitoring is weaker, managerial workload is higher, reputational pressure is lower, and stakeholder attention is limited. Causal identification relies on thermal inversions, the Beijing Olympic Games, and the Qinling-Huai River heating policy. Our findings highlight how environmental conditions shape managerial behavior and financial market outcomes. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Organizational citizenship behavior (OCB)-informed performance evaluation: the role of organizational and cultural factors
Abstract: Organizational citizenship behavior (OCB) plays a significant role in an organization’s success, and encouraging such behavior is therefore one of managers’ primary goals. Similarly, managers in innovative organizations place greater importance on OCB. Title: Feature Attribution-Based Explainability Analysis of Deep Learning Models in Predictive Process Monitoring
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Predictive process monitoring supports the optimization and control of operational business processes by forecasting the future state or outcome of ongoing cases. While deep neural networks have achieved strong performance for these tasks by modeling sequential dependencies in event logs, their black-box nature limits trust and practical adoption. The method relies on a control-flow-aware segmentation algorithm that partitions a trace into meaningful segments and supports the computation of segment-level SHAP explanations. This makes it possible to identify which parts of a trace influence a prediction and which change points steer the case toward the predicted outcome. Title: Does circular transformation matter for firm value?

Title: A Knowledge Management Method for Frascati-Compatible R&D Conceptualization in Multi-project Software Engineering Organizations
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Software engineering organizations claiming benefits under national R&D tax incentive schemes built on the OECD Frascati Manual face structural barriers in producing acceptable evidence. Software work is intangible, novel and routine components share the same codebase, operational documentation is rarely written for evidential purposes, and consultant interpretive knowledge is largely tacit. Claim quality therefore depends heavily on individual consultant experience. This paper presents a six-step concept-mapping method, designed within a Design Science Research framework, that addresses these barriers. The method is grounded in Nonaka and Takeuchi’s externalization concept and in Novak and Gowin’s concept-mapping methodology. It produces structured evidence packages through a fixed sequence of steps and five supporting artifacts: a Legal Concept Map, a Software Engineering Knowledge Map, an Activity Classification Table, an Employee-Activity Linkage Table, and an Epistemic Drilling Protocol. All artifacts are realized as tables in standard office software. The method is applied to two contrasting national schemes – the Irish R&D Tax Credit and the Swedish Forskningsavdrag – through anonymous project scenario analysis and assessed through a structured expert practitioner evaluation. Initial validation indicates that the method produces complete and reproducible evidence structures for both schemes, with scheme differences absorbed primarily by the Legal Concept Map. The expert evaluation (n = 4), while confirming the method’s component-level credibility, constitutes a thin evidential basis; strengthening this validation is a priority for future research. The contribution is a transferable method that reduces, but does not eliminate, the dependence of claim quality on individual consultant experience. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: When and how hyperbole hurts: the effects of hyperboles in advertising on perceived brand authenticity and purchase behavior
Abstract: In today’s information-saturated media environment, hyperbolic rhetoric is widely employed in advertising for its capacity to enhance creativity, yet its effectiveness remains uncertain. Title: Market dispersion and localized competition in peer-to-peer accommodation markets
Abstract: This study investigates how localized competition, measured through service and spatial differentiation, influences price and demand dispersion among Airbnb listings in London. Title: The endorsement paradox: Unpacking the mechanisms of brand betrayal and consumer retaliation in the digital era
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: While celebrity endorsement is widely regarded as a protective asset for brands, its role during product failures remains underexplored. Furthermore, perceived betrayal is the core psychological mechanism driving consumer retaliation. Crucially, loss aversion serves as a boundary condition, exacerbating negative responses when consumers face actual health or financial risks. Title: Reassessing the airline quality rating: Reporting units, fixed weights, and alignment with passenger satisfaction
Abstract: For over three decades, the Airline Quality Rating (AQR) has used the same expert weights to preserve longitudinal comparability. Title: The effect of environmental concern on green product choice under different cognitive loads
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Green consumption constitutes a critical pathway to mitigating environmental threats and advancing carbon emission reduction. Title: The Cultural Role of Accounting Practices in the Formation of Corporate Identity

Abstract: This chapter explores the cultural foundations of accounting practices and their strategic role in shaping corporate identity. Title: Mindfulness in organizations: how and when mindfulness shapes perceptions of distributive justice in society

Across four field studies involving European managers, we investigate how mindfulness influences managers’ perceptions of distributive justice in society (PDJS). Three results emerge. Title: Crafting Lives That Do Not Fit into One Job Description: Entrepreneurial Life Design Through Hybrid Entrepreneurship

Abstract: Drawing on in-depth interviews with 14 German hybrid entrepreneurs, we develop a six-phase cyclical model of Hybrid Entrepreneurial Life Design (HELD). Title: Co-founder selection from a marriage market perspective: How the dark triad shapes judgments of interpersonal attraction, resources, and equity demand
Abstract: Co-founder selection is a pivotal decision in new venture formation, yet how lead founders evaluate potential partners remains underexplored. Drawing on insights from marriage market theory, we conceptualize co-founder selection as an act of individuated judgment guided by cooperative logic and associated joint utility projection, wherein lead founders assess co-founder candidates based on social-emotional, instrumental, and distributive considerations reflected in interpersonal attraction, resource contributions, and equity demand. We further propose that lead founders' dark triad shifts this judgmental process from joint utility logic to personal utility maximization. Using a conjoint experiment with 206 entrepreneurs making 3296 co-founder selection decisions, we find that interpersonal attraction and resource contributions positively influence willingness to select a co-founder candidate, whereas higher equity demand reduces candidate attractiveness. Critically, lead founders higher in the dark triad display distinct patterns: they discount interpersonal attraction and display heightened sensitivity to equity dilution—assessments that indicate their prioritization of personal over joint value creation. Taken together, these findings reveal how dispositional tendencies influence the judgments underlying co-founder selection, indicating a shift away from the cooperative logic assumed in marriage market theory and co-founder selection toward greater emphasis on personal utility considerations. Title: Work with or work alone? How AI involvement in healthcare consultations shapes consumer responses to service failure

Abstract: Leaders increasingly face decisions about what inclusion requires in settings where formal guidance is incomplete or unevenly applied, a situation this study conceptualizes as institutional ambiguity. Title: A multi-product operations-emission cost optimization model with stochastic demand

Title: Corporate digital responsibility (CDR): Enhancing employees’ perceived justice and organizational outcomes

Title: Board gender diversity, cultural logics, and corporate tax behaviour

Title: Managing airport operational resilience through dynamic relational diagnosis: A multi-airport graph-based study

Abstract: Multiexperience (MX) describes users’ perceptions and responses when an interactive system distributes activity across multiple devices and modalities. Title: The green credentials of benefit corporations and sociétés à mission: Property rights and the prevention of greenwashing
Abstract: This research inquires whether the property rights templates of US benefit corporations (BCs) and French sociétés à mission (SaMs) are credible protections against greenwashing. This vulnerability is further exacerbated by ambiguous missions and third-party assessments weakened by the freedom BCs and SaMs have to select and pay auditors. Rooted in the tradition of institutional ecological economics, this research emphasizes institutional realism by leveraging a mechanism-based methodology. Title: Ownership structure and the international expansion of German firms

Title: Pre-positioning relief supplies subject to uncertain probability estimates

Title: Digital Trust in Health Data Sharing: A Value Sensitive Design Approach

Title: Multimodal Process Monitoring with On-demand Disambiguation
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Process monitoring is increasingly supported by Internet-of-Things (IoT) environments. However, the abstraction of sensor data into process events often leads to ambiguity. Existing approaches that leverage IoT data do not address how to resolve such ambiguity dynamically. To address this challenge, we present MMPMOD, a novel architecture for multimodal process monitoring that detects ambiguity in IoT-based events and orchestrates contextual sensing modalities on-demand to resolve it. Upon ambiguity detection, it activates cameras to capture the visual context, and applies scene understanding to disambiguate events. Authors: Liu H.; Wang Z.; Zhang T.; Fang Z.; Xie S.
Title: From user reviews to budget strategy: Optimizing hotel app resource allocation via deep learning and game theory
Abstract: Mobile applications have evolved from simple booking interfaces into critical service touchpoints in the hospitality industry. Although hotel managers possess vast amounts of online customer reviews, translating these unstructured textual insights into precise financial decisions remains a complex challenge. This study proposes a quantitative decision-support framework to optimize strategic resource allocation for hotel mobile app development. Methodologically, the study first utilizes aspect-level sentiment analysis based on deep learning to extract fine-grained customer preferences from online reviews. Subsequently, the app development process is modeled as a non-cooperative game where distinct functional modules (e.g., functionality, aesthetics, security) compete for limited budgetary resources. This approach mirrors the internal departmental competition for resources within hotel organizations. The model identifies a unique Nash Equilibrium, providing an optimal investment strategy that maximizes overall customer satisfaction while mitigating the “diminishing returns” effect. By analyzing 36,902 reviews from 7 major hotel brands, this study reveals a counter-intuitive insight: features with the highest user attention often represent “Investment Traps” due to saturation, where additional resources yield negligible returns. Conversely, the optimal strategy dictates reallocating surplus budget from these saturated areas to “Investment Dividend” features—those with high strategic weight but lower current satisfaction—thereby maximizing the marginal utility of digital assets. Title: When public meets private: How dual digital channels reshape subscription E-commerce
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Leveraging online private-domain channels, retail-controlled platforms accessible only to designated customer segments, for subscription commerce has become a cornerstone for many retailers seeking stable revenue streams and deeper customer engagement. In pursuit of an omnichannel presence, however, an increasing number of retailers have begun to roll out subscription offerings through online public-domain channels: third-party platforms open to all users. The impact of this strategic expansion on their existing private-domain subscription business remains ambiguous. Drawing on Decision Field Theory and granular subscription-order data from a leading subscription retailer, we employ a multi-period difference-in-differences design to assess how the introduction of public-domain channels affects subscription volume and subscription cycle length in private-domain channels. Our findings reveal that public-domain entry negatively affects both subscription volume and subscription cycle in the private-domain channel. However, these adverse effects are attenuated for products whose consumer bases exhibit higher pre-treatment subscription frequency or longer prior subscription cycles. Title: From Principles to Practice: Embedding GEDSI in Process Design
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: This paper investigates the integration of Gender, Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) principles into process design, highlighting their significance in promoting equitable processes. Title: Big-data-driven decision-making capability and corporate bond spreads: The complementary role of local digital financial inclusion
Abstract: We examine whether corporate bond issuance spreads reflect firms’ disclosed data-driven decision-making practices and whether this association varies with the local digital financial environment. Using Chinese bond data from 2011 to 2022 and a textual proxy for big-data-driven decision-making (BDD), we find that the BDD–spread association becomes more negative as local digital financial inclusion increases. This conditional association is economically meaningful and persists across alternative measures and specifications. The time-sequenced evidence is consistent with an information-based interpretation: higher BDD disclosure is associated with lower absolute accruals in the following year, while lower absolute accruals are associated with narrower issuance spreads in the subsequent year. Subsample point estimates are more negative for asset-light issuers and for firms with lower peer BDD, smaller boards, or non-Big-4 auditors. Authors: Feng Q.; Mei L.; Yang Y.; Liu Q.
Title: The impact of China's new-generation artificial intelligence innovative development pilot zone policy on firms' investment–financing maturity mismatch: Evidence from Chinese listed companies
Abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies has profoundly reshaped firms' investment and financing decisions, making it important to rigorously evaluate the effects of related public policies. Title: More to gain, less to lose? Chinese firms’ US patenting strategies amidst decoupling
Abstract: US-China geopolitical tensions have produced decoupling policies that restrict Chinese firms’ access to most assets within strategic industries in the US. Yet Chinese firms in strategic industries can still legally obtain patents in the US, though doing so poses political risks and even this access may be restricted in the future. How do Chinese firms seek assets abroad in this new geopolitical environment? Drawing on the Attention-Based View, we argue that decoupling redirects attention of managers at Chinese firms in strategic industries to significantly increase US patenting because restrictions on alternative assets heighten patents’ relative value, reduce the perceived costs of exploiting them aggressively, and create urgency to secure them before access is potentially restricted. In contrast, managers with lived experience in the US or politically similar markets are theorized to perceive greater political risks of this strategy, leading their firms to increase patenting less. Using a difference-in-differences approach analyzing USPTO patent filings by publicly-listed Chinese firms from 2013–2023, we find support for our hypotheses. Robustness checks, including tests showing no comparable increase in patenting by the Chinese firms in other major foreign markets, corroborate these results. Further, supplementary analysis indicates that the increase in patenting is associated with fewer claims per patent — a pattern consistent with the strategic use of patents, potentially as weapons and transactable assets, rather than proportionally greater inventiveness. Title: WARP: Worktime-Aware Representation for Predictive Process Monitoring
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Predictive Process Monitoring leverages historical event logs to generate data-driven forecasts about the future development of ongoing process instances, such as the time until the completion of the next event. Recent research has focused on enhancing predictive performance through advanced deep-learning architectures and feature engineering. In this context, existing approaches typically model time as a continuous calendar-based feature. This design choice overlooks an important characteristic of real-world business processes: process execution is often constrained by organizational working patterns, including business hours, shift schedules, and weekends. In this paper, we investigate the integration of organizational working constraints into the predictive pipeline through a worktime-based transformation of the temporal axis. We propose a methodology that maps event timestamps from a conventional clocktime axis to a worktime-based axis, effectively excluding periods of scheduled resource unavailability. This transformation allows predictive models to learn temporal patterns based on active process execution rather than elapsed calendar time. We evaluate the approach using both synthetic and real-world event log data. The results show that the worktime-based transformation improves prediction accuracy, particularly in scenarios characterized by temporal gaps between discrete working intervals. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Çavuş G.; Önce S.
Title: Whistleblowing and Silence in Accounting Irregularities and Fraud: The Role of Cultural Norms
Source title: Accounting, Finance, Sustainability, Governance and Fraud
Abstract: Accounting irregularities and fraud are described as the intentional misrepresentation of a company’s financial statements to hide its true financial status. The detection of accounting irregularities and fraud activities is important for both companies and the national economy. A significant proportion of accounting irregularities and fraud appears through the whistleblowing behavior of employees. If employees do not engage in whistleblowing, their tendency to remain silent increases and a culture of silence prevails in the company. This culture of silence can lead to accounting irregularities and fraud going unnoticed and becoming normalized over time. Consequently, whistleblowing serves as an important tool for the early detection and prevention of accounting irregularities and fraud. However, whistleblowing is not just an individual-focused behavior; it is also influenced by environmental factors such as cultural types. National culture and accounting culture are among the most significant types of culture that influence individuals’ decisions to report accounting irregularities and fraud to the relevant authorities or to remain silent. The primary objective of this study is to investigate how the dimensions of national and accounting culture values affect the willingness of accounting professionals in Turkish companies to report or conceal accounting irregularities and fraud. For this purpose, semi-structured interviews were conducted using specially developed scenarios based on Hofstede’s national culture dimensions and Gray’s accounting cultural values related to accounting irregularities and fraud. Thematic analysis of the interview data was performed using NVivo software. The research findings attempt to identify key points for developing a healthy whistleblowing culture to prevent accounting irregularities and fraud. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: From Algorithms to Advisors: Exploring AIs Dual Disruption in Trading and Wealth Management

Authors: Li Y.; Chai S.
Title: Explainable medical artificial intelligence: The impact of agent and explanation types on health persuasion
Abstract: Despite the rapid advancements in medical artificial intelligence (AI), little is known about how different types of explanations influence user compliance in healthcare settings. Title: The Impact of Pre-trained Language Models for Success Prediction in Digital Negotiations - A Comparative Analysis

Title: Extreme environmental distance and global sustainability engagement: Evidence from the United Nations Global Compact
Abstract: In the face of increasingly polarized environmental regulations, MNEs struggle to respond strategically to divergent environmental contexts. We introduce the concept of extreme environmental distance, capturing the most pronounced environmental discrepancy within the firm’s global operation, and argue that such salient extremes heighten stakeholder scrutiny and redirect headquarters’ attention toward coherent firm-level strategies. Using a large global sample, we show that extreme environmental distance significantly motivates MNEs’ engagement with a supranational sustainability initiative, the United Nations Global Compact (UNGC). This effect is amplified when stakeholder pressures are more salient, such as in economically significant host markets, highly competitive industries, and contexts of elevated reputational risk. Additional analyses indicate that extreme environmental distance also facilitates MNEs’ alignment with the United Nations’ 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and that both UNGC engagement and SDG alignment are associated with stronger international financial performance. Overall, our findings underscore how global sustainability frameworks enable MNEs to pursue sustainable value creation amid environmental inconsistencies across international markets. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: When assurance fits the risk: Platform and third-party assurance in circular retail
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Circular retailers use platform-backed protections and independent third-party assurance to reduce uncertainty about refurbished products, yet these sources are often treated as interchangeable trust cues. This pattern emerged across purchase intention, hypothetical product choice, choice confidence, and stated willingness to pay. Study 1 further found corresponding shifts in perceived diagnosticity, assurance-source trust, and perceived risk, yielding conditional statistical indirect-effect patterns consistent with the account. Study 4 directly measured perceived provider-role relevance and added no-additional-assurance and dual-assurance benchmarks. Matched single-source assurance improved responses relative to no additional assurance, whereas dual assurance did not consistently improve responses beyond the matched source. These findings qualify the view of assurance as a generic trust signal and show that assurance design in circular retailing depends on matching the assurance provider to the risk consumers are evaluating. © 2026

Title: From trust to retirement preparedness: the mediating role of financial behavior and financial resilience

Abstract: Population ageing and demographic shifts in the European Union are placing increasing strain on traditional pension systems, shifting greater responsibility to individuals to ensure their own retirement preparedness. The results show that trust in financial advisors is positively associated with retirement preparedness, both directly and indirectly through financial behavior and financial resilience. Title: Automation-Induced Complacency as a Dual Suppressor of Hybrid Intelligence: Evidence from GenAI Literacy and Critical AI Evaluation Among Citizen Developers
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Hybrid Intelligence (HI) depends on humans who can engage AI systems critically, not merely fluently. This paper addresses whether automation-induced complacency, the tendency to accept AI outputs uncritically, undermines HI at its foundation by suppressing the very competencies, GenAI literacy and critical AI evaluation, that HI requires, rather than only degrading interaction outcomes. This gap matters for business informatics because current IS alignment and training strategies assume literacy growth is sufficient for effective human-AI collaboration; if complacency instead erodes literacy itself, that assumption fails. Complacency is negatively associated with both GenAI literacy and critical AI use, and its effect on analytical self-efficacy is partly transmitted through reduced literacy (29.8% of the total effect), supporting a cascade suppression mechanism. Notably, GenAI literacy is not significantly associated with critical evaluation, suggesting that functional competence and critical judgment may develop as separable capacities. These findings reframe complacency as a competency-development risk, not only a performance risk, with direct implications for how HI systems, IS alignment strategies, and citizen-developer training should be designed to explicitly cultivate critical evaluation rather than assume it follows from functional fluency. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Learning Process Modelling in BPMN Through Real-Life Process Observation

Title: Ex-post customer reference effects of lead-time quotation in an online waiting experiment

Abstract: Retailers and service providers routinely quote waits for deliveries, collections, appointments, and digital support. Title: Prioritising seafood diversification in Sweden: Integrating biological screening with stakeholder constraints
Abstract: Diversifying seafood production and consumption has been proposed as a strategy for improving the sustainability and resilience of food systems. Title: Intergenerational Change in Türkiye and Its Effects on Accounting Professionals in Terms of Knowledge Transfer

Title: Customer ducation in sales: A ystematic iterature eview
Abstract: Customer education in sales (CEd) is an emerging research area, yet the literature remains fragmented across multiple fields with inconsistent terminology and conceptualizations. This fragmentation has hindered the development of cumulative knowledge and left fundamental questions about CEd’s effectiveness, mechanisms, and theoretical foundations unanswered. We conduct a systematic literature review of 42 journal articles, examining CEd research across four dimensions: (1) industry contexts and business settings, (2) delivery modes and their outcomes, (3) mechanisms and boundary conditions, and (4) the application of pedagogical theories. Our analysis reveals that across seven distinct delivery modes, CEd generally produces positive, sales-supporting outcomes, such as customer loyalty. Frontline interactions are the most studied mode, while formal programs show the strongest return on investment. However, significant gaps remain: B2C research predominates, direct financial outcomes are understudied, and few studies engage with pedagogical theory. Authors: Gong Y.; Zhao L.; Guo W.; Yao R.; Hu F.
Title: “Beauty” versus “threat”: how awe influences the desire for luxury goods
Abstract: Luxury brands often incorporate threatening natural imagery that evokes negative awe into marketing communications to shape consumer perceptions of the brand. Can such imagery actually make luxury products more appealing to consumers? Across six studies, we find that negative awe elicited by threatening imagery enhances consumers’ desire for luxury products. This occurs because negative awe induces loss of control. Furthermore, the enhancing effect is stronger when marketing communications emphasize symbolic (vs. functional) value or when the products are public (vs. private) goods. These findings highlight the unique role of negative awe in shaping luxury consumption and provide practical guidance for luxury brands to strategically leverage natural imagery in their marketing communications. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Authors: Kataria V.; Kaur T.
Title: Investigating Transgender Inclusion in White-Collar Employment: Implications for Workplace Diversity Policies and the UN SDG Charter 2030
Source title: Contributions to Environmental Sciences and Innovative Business Technology
Abstract: Transgenders are a marginalized section of the society who are inappropriately clubbed in the LGBTQIA+ collective. Literature confirms that transgenders have their unique set of challenges that are much distinct from other members of the collective and yet they are brought together in this collective. By drafting a conceptual framework, this paper investigates the constructs to facilitate considerations of transgender inclusion in white-collar employment, in the specific context of early applicant or job-seeker stage. This conceptual paper also provides a foundation for an impending empirical investigation by drawing coherence by first establishing the rationale for considerations of transgenders as a unique entity that should not be a part of a collective. It then establishes the rationale for investigating transgender inclusion under the lens of societal and management considerations with the objective of extending workplace diversity policies taking into account considerations of recruitment practices at the early applicant or job seeker stage. The proposed research investigation also establishes the rationale for underpinning the research in the construct of the signaling theory. This paper is novel as it proposes a conceptual understanding for a novel empirical investigation of transgender inclusion in white-collar employment with implications for workplace diversity policies and considerations for UN SDGs 8 and 10 thereby impacting academia, society, and management practices. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: Who are my people and what can I do? Community remapping for entrepreneurial venturing after forced migration
Abstract: Scholarship on post-disruption adaptation largely assumes conditions of partial disruption—situations where despite losing access to one or multiple domains, other important domains remain intact. Yet wholesale disruptions pose a qualitatively different challenge for entrepreneurship. We explore how experiences of wholesale disruption shape actors' reconstruction of their contextual structure, perceived scope of their entrepreneurial possibility space, and the long-term trajectory of their ventures. We conduct an inductive study of the venturing efforts of refugees following their wholesale disruption caused by forced migration to the USA. We develop a grounded theoretical model of community remapping for venturing after wholesale disruption that explains why some refugees enact dynamic, growing ventures while others enact more stable, static ventures and eschew growth aspirations. Our findings and theorizing contribute to literatures on venturing in response to wholesale disruptions and on refugee entrepreneurship. © 2026 The Authors.
